proof_strategy: Use bellBasis_expansion to represent B by a 4 × 4 unitary coefficient matrix; unitarity of each B k forces the coefficient vectors to be null for the Minkowski-type quadratic form coming from det; classify these configurations by an explicit case analysis.
title: Uniqueness of the Pauli Unitary Error Basis

description:
For triangle-free graphs Shearer's bound beats the Caro-Wei greedy bound by a logarithmic factor. The conjecture is that this gain is still purely greedy: a weighted version of the relative Caro-Wei induction proved in this thread, with a concave weight satisfying Shearer's recursion, should reproduce it. This would de-randomise the source of the classical R(3,k) lower bound.

Every triangle-free graph with maximum degree D >= 2 satisfies alpha(G) >= n*(D*log D - D + 1)/(D-1)^2, provable by the minimum-degree deletion recursion with a concave weight function.

Generalize caro_wei_finset to an arbitrary concave weight f satisfying the Shearer recursion, instantiate f, and check numerically on Petersen, Kneser and random triangle-free graphs.

The logarithmic gain over greedy, hence the R(3,k) lower bound, becomes constructive and verified.

A triangle-free graph forcing the greedy recursion to lose the log factor shows analytic averaging is essential.
proof_strategy: Delete the closed neighbourhood of a minimum-degree vertex; use triangle-freeness to note the neighbourhood is independent, giving a two-term credit; solve the resulting recursion by concavity of the Shearer weight.
title: Shearer Gap Above the Greedy Independence Bound

description:
The two envelope theorems proved here are stated for an arbitrary envelope H but a fixed increment 1/m - log(1+1/m). Abstracting the increment to a general analytic g with g(x) = O(x^2) would make the principle applicable to Stieltjes constants, log Gamma, and tails of zeta partial sums. This would supply Mathlib with effective error bounds where currently only qualitative convergence exists.

If s(n+1) - s(n) = g(1/(n+1)) with g analytic, g(x) = O(x^2), and H telescopes against g in the sense H(m) - H(m+1) >= g(1/m) with H >= 0, then lim s - s(n) <= H(n+1); dually for the lower bound.

Generalize tail_le_envelope / envelope_le_tail by replacing the explicit increment with a hypothesis s(n+1) - s(n) = g(1/(n+1)), and instantiate at the first Stieltjes constant gamma_1.

A single reusable lemma yields explicit sharp error bounds for a whole family of classical constants without any integral remainder theory.

The telescoping principle depends on monotonicity special to the harmonic increment, isolating what makes gamma easier than gamma_1.
proof_strategy: The existing proofs use only monotone induction plus a limit comparison; replace the concrete increment lemma eulerMascheroniSeq_succ_sub by a hypothesis and check nothing else is used.
title: Envelope Transfer Principle for Log-Type Limits

description:
Robustness has two finite-sample axioms: resisting explosion (breakdown) and reproducing an uncontaminated majority (exact fit). The conjecture is that for equivariant estimators the exact-fit point never exceeds the breakdown number, with equality for every order statistic. The approach reuses the general predicate-count transfer lemma with an equality predicate in place of an order predicate.

For every translation-equivariant T and non-empty xs, exactFitPoint T xs <= breakdownNumber T xs, and for T = orderStat j both equal min(j+1, n-j).

Define exactFitPoint via IsLeast {k | exists a k-contamination on which T differs from the majority value} and prove the order-statistic case; then search for a gap by testing piecewise-defined equivariant estimators on ratios8.

The two classical robustness axioms are formally comparable and coincide on the whole order-statistic family.

A gap exhibits an estimator that resists explosion but misreports a clean majority, separating the axioms at finite sample size.
proof_strategy: Apply countP_le_countP_add_diffCount with the Boolean predicate (fun x => decide (x = v)) for the majority value v; combine with orderStat_le_of_countP and le_orderStat_of_countP to sandwich the estimator at v, and dualise via contaminate for the sharpness half.
title: Exact-Fit Point versus Breakdown Point

description:
Every tested carrier of the per-modulus quadratic-sieve yield residual has been an N-property: a function of N modulo a fixed factor base, or of the local factorisation around N. This direction conjectures that the residual is carried by run-level statistics of the sieve process (partial-relation graph structure, per-sample j-window occupancy) which are not measurable with respect to any N-property sigma-algebra. The measurable ceiling makes the claim falsifiable: a genuine carrier must strictly lower the within-cell energy of the joint N-property feature.

There is a run-level statistic S of the sieve process such that withinSS y (dial, neighbourhood, S) < (1 - 0.4) * withinSS y (dial, neighbourhood), while no N-measurable feature achieves any such reduction.

Instantiate QRResidual.withinSS at the joint feature with and without the run-level statistic and compare; formally, exhibit the strict inequality as a theorem about a concrete finite design.

The residual is a property of the algorithm, not of the modulus, and yield prediction must be online rather than a priori.

Some N-property class still untested carries the residual, and the coverage claim is incomplete.
proof_strategy: Use rss_measurableClass to reduce both sides to within-cell energies, then refinement monotonicity (withinSS_mono_of_refines) to isolate the extra explanatory power of the run-level statistic.
title: Sieve-Process Carriers for the Quadratic-Sieve Yield Residual

description:
The semantic optimum is now known: the nodes of a downset containing the support are a minimum-cardinality uniqueness set. What is missing is a syntactic invariant computing that downset from the expression tree. The conjecture is that a compositional Newton-downset recursion is both sound and, for cancellation-free expressions, tight, giving certificates that are never worse and usually far better than the simplex one.

There is a computable compositional map newton : NExpr n → Finset (Fin n →₀ ℕ) whose value is a downset containing the support of toZ e, equal to the downward closure of that support whenever no coefficient cancellation occurs in the products; the induced certificate uses #(newton e) evaluations, which is minimal for that support.

Define newton by recursion with a downward-closure operator, prove support containment and closure under ≤, derive NewtonCert from downset_unisolvent, and check that #(newton e) < C(n + deg e, n) for cubeLHS, symLHS and quasiLHS.

Identity checking in the chart calculus becomes support-adapted end to end: the number of evaluations is dictated by the Newton polytope of the identity rather than by its degree.

Either downward closure of Minkowski sums overshoots the true support systematically, or cancellation is generic, in which case optimal certificates cannot be read off the syntax and must be computed from coefficients.
proof_strategy: Induct on the expression using MvPolynomial.support_add and support_mul, exactly as in wsum_le_wdeg; for tightness, show that the leading coefficient at each maximal exponent of the Minkowski sum is a product of nonzero leading coefficients in a domain.
title: Syntactic Newton Downsets for Optimal Certificates

description:
The exact box-kernel deflation k w^2 / 12 is the curvature times the variance of the box kernel. We conjecture the same formula with Var(K) for every symmetric unimodal kernel, with the vertex exactly preserved. This identifies the single number any binning-free shape test must report.

For symmetric non-negative unimodal K with unit mass and f symmetric and concave about u*, argmax (f * K_h) = u* and (f * K_h)(u*) = f(u*) + (1/2) f''(u*) Var(K_h) + o(Var(K_h)).

Generalise slidingAvg_quadratic from the box kernel to an arbitrary kernel by second-order Taylor expansion under the integral, and re-derive w^2/12 as the box variance.

Bin width, kernel bandwidth and wavelet scale become interchangeable through a single scalar, making cross-method comparison exact.

Kernel shape enters at leading order and histogram results cannot be compared with density-regression results without recalibration.
proof_strategy: Expand f to second order about u*, integrate against K using symmetry to kill the first moment, and control the remainder by the modulus of continuity of f''.
title: Kernel-Variance Universality of the Deflation Law

description:
The feedback recursion proved here gives the harmonic value H_u for a deck of distinct cards. For a deck with repeated card types we conjecture that stagewise fair odds still give value zero, and that under unit scoring the greedy 'call a most-frequent remaining type' strategy is optimal with an explicit stagewise value. This covers real card counting, where suits repeat.

For a deck given by a multiset of multiplicities r_1,...,r_m, the stagewise-fair-odds value is 0 for every admissible strategy, and the greedy strategy maximises the unit-scoring value, whose value is the expected sum over stages of (max remaining multiplicity)/(cards remaining).

Generalise expScore from Finset alpha to a multiset state, reprove expScore_step, and check optimality by exhaustive dynamic programming for all multiplicity vectors with total size at most 7.

Card counting with repeated ranks is fully solved at the level of exact expectations, and the fair-odds invariance is confirmed to be independent of deck composition.

Greedy is not optimal, which would mean that deliberately naming a rarer type buys information worth more than the immediate hit probability.
proof_strategy: Exchange argument on the recursion tree: swapping the first call to a maximal-multiplicity type can only increase the immediate term while leaving the successor states majorised.
title: Greedy Optimality for Multiset Decks with Feedback

description:
Two obstructions to the existence of a dimension were isolated: the origin may be missing (odd rules) and the cardinality may fail to divide 2^n (Lagrange). The conjecture is that these are the only two, so that every stationary locus is linear, an affine torsor, or detectably neither, giving a complete trichotomy of the 256 rules.

For every rule r and every n, the locus V(f_r, n) is either a linear subspace, or a coset of one, or has cardinality not dividing 2^n; moreover the coset case occurs exactly for the odd rules whose window relation is the graph of an affine map.

Enumerate all 256 rules at n = 6 with kernel-checked decision procedures, classify each locus by the trichotomy, and formalise the general statement that an affine locus is a coset of the linearised locus.

A complete classification of the 256 stationary loci as algebraic objects, refining the falsification into a positive taxonomy.

A third obstruction exists, presumably from rules whose window relation is not the graph of a partial function, indicating richer scheme structure.
proof_strategy: Split the local rule into affine and non-affine parts over F2, show the affine part yields a torsor, and apply the Lagrange bound ncard_dvd_of_isAffineSubvariety to the remainder.
title: Origin-Freeness Obstruction Class for the 256 Loci

description:
The generating function of the proved trace counts should equal minus the logarithm of det(I - uB), and for regular graphs factor through the Ihara polynomial. The counting theorem reduces the identity to a bijection between cyclic non-backtracking words and multisets of primitive cycles.

For every finite simple graph, sum_{n>=1} trace(B^n) u^n / n = -log det(I - uB), and for (q+1)-regular graphs det(I - uB) = (1-u^2)^{|E|-|V|} det(I - uA + q u^2 I).

Use the proved rotation stability of nbCycles to define the rotation action, prove that each orbit is generated by a primitive cyclic word, and compare coefficientwise with the power-sum expansion of the determinant.

A fully formal Ihara zeta function with its Euler product becomes available over Mathlib.

Some rotation orbits fail to be free, indicating that the primitive-cycle decomposition needs a stabiliser correction.
proof_strategy: Compute orbit sizes of the rotation action on nbCycles as divisors of n, and identify the resulting Dirichlet-type convolution with the logarithmic derivative of a determinant.
title: Ihara Determinant Identity via Cyclic Word Counting

description:
The calibrated model predBase rho = 4*ceil(4*rho) turns the measured bases into disjoint density intervals for code, English and German. The conjecture is that tokenizer statistics measured directly on the corpora land in those intervals, and that a language above density 3/2 must need at least 28 keys. This tests the mechanism without training any model.

Measured relative token densities satisfy rho_code in (1/2,3/4], rho_EN in (3/4,1], rho_DE in (1,5/4], and any corpus with rho > 3/2 has base at least 28 keys at ctx 512.

Compute tokens-per-aligned-sentence ratios on the four corpora and compare with Catalog.NET71.net71_density_intervals; run one sweep for a high-density agglutinative language and compare with high_density_forces_seven_steps.

The tokenizer tax becomes predictable from corpus statistics alone, so cache budgets for a new language can be set before any sweep is run.

The base is not a function of token density, and the four-domain ordering must be explained by attention structure rather than by tokenisation.
proof_strategy: Formalise the density-to-budget map as the grid closure of a linear functional (predBase_eq_gridUp), invert it on each measured base (predBase_eq_iff), and derive the threshold prediction from monotonicity of the ceiling.
title: Corpus-Only Falsification of the Density Mechanism

description:
This cycle proved that the optimal m-ary Bayes error equals 1 - Cs/m, identifying the universal-coding Shtarkov sum with the multi-hypothesis testing optimum. The conjecture extends the identity to list decoding: outputting k candidate hypotheses should cost 1 - Cs^(k)/m, where Cs^(k) sums the k largest likelihoods at each message. This would give a full interpolation between perfect identification and pure guessing.

For a finite source class with m members and uniform prior, the least average error of a rule outputting k hypotheses equals 1 - Cs^(k)/m with Cs^(k) = sum over x of the sum of the k largest values of p_theta x; the sequence k -> Cs^(k) is concave with Cs^(1) = Cs and Cs^(m) = m.

Define the top-k envelope by sorting the finite family of likelihoods at each x, mirror the argmax exchange used in isLeast_mAryError, and check the endpoints against shtarkovSum_le_card and shtarkovSum_eq_card_iff_mutuallySingular.

Universal-coding rigidity theorems transfer wholesale to list-decoding and top-k classification error, a directly practical machine-learning quantity.

The failure point would identify ties in the order statistics as a genuine obstruction, isolating where randomized list rules beat deterministic ones.
proof_strategy: Pointwise optimality of the top-k selection rule; concavity from the discrete derivative of order statistics; endpoints from the existing rigidity analysis.
title: List-Decoding Hierarchy of Truncated Shtarkov Sums

description:
The optimal stratified weighting is q/p = sqrt(kappa_g), irrational for g = 2. Conjecture that the shortfall of the best integer weighting with p,q <= N decays exactly like N^-2, with the continued-fraction convergents of sqrt(7) as extremisers. This turns a qualitative suboptimality theorem into a design rule.

There are constants 0 < a < A with a/N^2 <= min_{1<=p,q<=N} (kappa* - stratCeiling p q) <= A/N^2, and the minimiser is a convergent of the continued fraction of sqrt(7).

Prove kappa* - stratCeiling p q is comparable to (q - p sqrt 7)^2 / (p+q)^3 using the cubic weight identity, then invoke the classical theory of best rational approximation to a quadratic irrational.

Integer weight budgets for the dial can be chosen optimally by continued fractions; 37/14 is provably near-extremal.

Approximation of the optimum is governed by something other than Diophantine quality, e.g. the discrete 1/n^2 correction dominates.
proof_strategy: Use cubic_weight_identity to factor the deficit as (v - s u)^2 times a positive linear form, then apply Liouville/Hurwitz bounds for sqrt 7.
title: Irrational Optimum Barrier for Integer Weightings

description:
The interval matrix of a melody window is idempotent in the min-plus matrix semiring, hence equal to its own Kleene star. We conjecture a full tropical Perron-Frobenius description: eigenvalue zero, eigenspace spanned by the columns, and a transposition-invariance classification of melodies with equal eigenspaces.

For every window, the tropical eigenvalue of the interval matrix is the tropical unit, its eigenspace is the tropical span of its columns, and two windows share an eigenspace iff their digit multisets agree up to a common additive shift.

Formalize tropical eigenvectors for Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (Tropical (WithTop N)) and prove A * v = v for columns v of A using intervalMatrix_idempotent.

Melody windows acquire a canonical tropical invariant, independent of any temporal lag statistic.

Idempotency is not enough to pin down the eigenspace and additional metric hypotheses on the digit alphabet are needed.
proof_strategy: Columns of an idempotent min-plus matrix are fixed vectors by A * A = A; classification then reduces to reconstructing a distance matrix from its Kleene star, i.e. to a one-dimensional embedding argument.
title: Min-Plus Spectral Theory of Interval Matrices

description:
The conjectured mean-based meta-analytic decorrelation budget is false, and fails only through a missing ordering hypothesis: decorrelation must antivary with headroom across replications. This turns the ordering into an empirical diagnostic of a dial cell. The conjecture is that clean cells antivary while count-parity cells monovary, with a quantifiable over-credit factor.

For a uniform dial cell the sequences (1 - c_i) and (1 - a_i b_i) over seeds are antivarying, so the mean-based budget holds; for a count-parity cell they are monovarying and the mean-based budget over-credits the pooled advantage energy by a factor at least 1 + Var(c)/(1 - cbar)^2.

Recompute per-seed mutual correlations c_i and reading products a_i b_i from the recorded seeds, evaluate the rank correlation of (1 - c_i) against (1 - a_i b_i), and compare the two budgets against the measured pooled energy.

Meta-analysis of dial cells acquires a validity precondition that can be checked from the same data, and count-parity verdicts become explainable as budget-allocation failures.

The ordering is an artefact of the counterexample and the mean-based budget fails for a different, still unidentified reason.
proof_strategy: Use aggregated_budget_chebyshev in the antivarying case; in the monovarying case bound the Chebyshev defect from below by the covariance and convert to the stated variance ratio.
title: Antivariation Test for Dial Meta-Analysis

description:
The quadratic sieve needs π(B)+1 smooth relations, which is proved sufficient here. The number of candidates needed is that quota divided by the smooth density ρ(u). We conjecture the required candidate count always exceeds the profitable batch size, so the testing phase can never be the bottleneck at cryptographic sizes.

For N ≥ 2^40 and every B ≥ 2, (π(B)+1)/ρ(log N / log B) > √(A/q) for the empirically calibrated A, q of the product-tree cost model.

Combine the proved quota BatchYield.exists_square_subproduct with a proved lower bound ρ(u) ≥ u^(−u) and the proved optimum BatchYield.blockCost_eq_opt_iff.

Batch smoothness testing is permanently a constant-factor optimisation for QS at these sizes; effort should move to the finding phase.

There is a parameter window where batching changes the asymptotic balance of the sieve — a much stronger claim than the measured +0.104.
proof_strategy: Bound the quota below by π(B) ≥ B/(2 log B) and the density above by u^(−u); compare with the square-root batch optimum.
title: Yield-over-Quota Dominance for Bit-Length-40 Sieving

description:
Define the defect of a complex Hadamard matrix as the dimension of the space of first-order deformations modulo dephasing, and prove that in order two it is zero, i.e. F₂ is isolated. The proved dephasing theorem gives the full orbit, so isolation becomes a rank computation on the linearized orthogonality constraints.

The tangent space at F₂ to the set of order-two complex Hadamard matrices equals the tangent space of its dephasing orbit; equivalently the defect of F₂ is 0.

Formalize the linearized constraint 'H + εK Hadamard to first order' as a real-linear system in K and compute its solution space, comparing with the 3-parameter diagonal orbit produced by flat_sharp_dephase.

Gives a formal, dimension-two base case for the Hadamard defect theory and a template for order four, where a genuine one-parameter family exists.

There would be a deformation of F₂ not obtainable by phases, contradicting flat_sharp_dephase and signalling an error in the equivalence classification.
proof_strategy: Differentiate the equations |H_ij| = 1 and rows orthogonal at H = F₂, solve the resulting real-linear system in 8 real unknowns, and match the solution space with the image of the derivative of the diagonal action.
title: Zero Defect of Order-Two Complex Hadamard Matrices

description:
The trace formula turns the return sequence walkCount S n 1 into the moment sequence of the adjacency spectrum. For abelian G that spectrum is the multiset of character sums over S, so reconstructing S becomes a Fourier-uniqueness question. The non-abelian case is expected to fail, with a small explicit counterexample.

For finite abelian G, two inversion-closed connection sets with equal return sequences are related by an automorphism of G; for non-abelian G this fails for some group of order at most 16.

Compute return sequences for all inversion-closed subsets of small abelian groups and search for collisions; formalise the abelian direction using the discrete Fourier transform.

The identity column of a census determines the connection set up to symmetry, so censuses are a faithful fingerprint for abelian Cayley graphs.

There are cospectral non-isomorphic circulant graphs whose spectra coincide as multisets, recovering classical circulant cospectrality inside this framework.
proof_strategy: Use trace_adj_pow plus Newton's identities to pass from moments to the spectrum, then invert the character-sum map by Fourier inversion on the dual group.
title: Moment Reconstruction of Abelian Connection Sets

description:
Census equivalence provably preserves being an involution. The conjecture is that this is one instance of a general descent principle for functorial group-theoretic invariants, and that these invariants are jointly complete for the relation. This would give a decision procedure for census equivalence that avoids searching Aut(G).

Every invariant of group elements that is preserved by inversion and by all automorphisms in Aut(G,S) is constant on census-equivalence classes, and the family of such invariants separates distinct classes.

Formalise a general descent lemma parameterised by an invariant, instantiate it at orderOf and at derived-series membership, and test completeness computationally on groups of order ≤ 16.

Census equivalence becomes decidable by evaluating a finite list of invariants, replacing an automorphism search.

There are census-inequivalent elements agreeing on all definable invariants, which would be an interesting rigidity failure.
proof_strategy: Generalise the three-case induction used in CensusEquiv_sq_eq_one_iff to an arbitrary invariant closed under inversion and S-preserving automorphisms.
title: Definable Invariants of Census Equivalence

description:
The KL bridge proved here inherits Pinsker's sqrt(KL/2), which exceeds 1 and becomes vacuous for KL >= 2. The Bretagnolle-Huber bound sqrt(1 - exp(-KL)) is always non-vacuous. Both follow from the same Bernoulli reduction already performed in the catalog's Pinsker proof.

For all finite Q absolutely continuous with respect to P, d_TV(Q,P) <= sqrt(1 - exp(-KL(Q||P))), and this is strictly better than sqrt(KL/2) exactly for KL above a universal threshold in (1,2).

Reuse klFinDist_block_ge to reduce to the Bernoulli case and prove the scalar inequality for klBernoulli by calculus (derivative comparison), then re-derive bayesError_ge_of_kl with the new bound.

Every KL-based Le Cam bound in the catalog becomes non-vacuous, and PAC-Bayes generalization bounds inherit a strictly better distinguishability floor.

The Bernoulli reduction must lose information, which would itself be a notable failure of the standard two-point method.
proof_strategy: Alphabet collapse along {P <= Q}; one-dimensional analysis of h(t) = 1 - exp(-klBernoulli(a,b)) - (a-b)^2.
title: Bretagnolle-Huber Refinement of the Pinsker Bridge

description:
Equilibria carry no complexity information, but the space-time diagram does. The conjecture is that the ideal generated by the n(T-1) defining cubics of the space-time variety has a Hilbert function and Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity that do correlate with Wolfram classes, with Rule 110 maximal among the 256 rules.

The space-time variety ST_T(f_r, n) has dimension n for every rule, but the graded ranks of the ideal generated by its defining cubics separate the Wolfram classes, and Rule 110 attains the maximal regularity at fixed (n, T).

Formalise ST_T as the graph of iterated evolution, prove the dimension statement for all rules, and compute the ranks of the linear spans of the cubic generators for all 256 rules at n = 6, T = 3.

An algebraic-geometric invariant of cellular automata that finally correlates with computational complexity.

Complexity is not a finite-window algebraic invariant, a strong negative result constraining all Grothendieck-style approaches to automata.
proof_strategy: Show ST_T is the image of a section of the projection to initial conditions, giving dimension n, then study the defining ideal degreewise and bound its regularity rule by rule.
title: Space-Time Ideal Regularity as a Complexity Invariant

description:
Return dominance says the identity maximises the census at even lengths. The conjecture is a quantitative strengthening: the gap between the identity and any other element grows monotonically in the even length. The odd-length behaviour is genuinely different, as a D3 counterexample at length three shows.

For inversion-closed S, the sequence n ↦ walkCount S (2n) 1 − walkCount S (2n) g is nondecreasing for every g.

Verify by direct computation on dihedral and cyclic groups up to order 12 and lengths up to 12, then attempt a proof by iterated Cauchy–Schwarz on the convolution identity walkCount_add.

The census admits a Lyapunov-type monotone quantity, giving mixing-time estimates for random walks on Cayley graphs directly from counting data.

Even-length return dominance is not a monotone phenomenon and the ℓ²-decay of the walk is not uniform in the target element.
proof_strategy: Write the deficit as an ℓ²-distance using walkCount_two_mul_one_eq_sum_sq and apply the semigroup law to compare consecutive even lengths.
title: Monotone Even-Length Return Deficit

description:
This cycle brackets the envelope Lipschitz constant in [2.96, 4.1]: a conservation-aware displacement lemma gives the upper bound and two explicit 52-bit profiles give the lower witness. Conjecture that the sharp constant is exactly 3, attained by transferring mass out of a dominant tie class.

For profiles of equal length and mass on n points, |rho^2(L) - rho^2(L')| <= 3 tau + O(tau^2 + 1/n), and 3 is attained in the limit by a dominant-block transfer; the proved bracket is [2.96, 4.1].

Replace the square-sum bound by the profile-dependent weight sum, optimise under mass conservation and the l1 budget, and compare with the explicit dominant-block family already formalised.

The deployment envelope tightens by a further 27 percent and becomes optimal, pinning every robustness claim in the dial series to a sharp constant.

The worst case spreads over many blocks, meaning envelope robustness degrades with resolution and must be stated K-dependently.
proof_strategy: Localise the perturbation to two coordinates by a rearrangement/exchange argument, then optimise the resulting one-variable rational function.
title: Sharp Three-Lipschitz Envelope Constant

description:
Generalise the bottom-merged and tip-merged blindness ceilings from an interval of dyadic tie blocks to an arbitrary union of 2-adic valuation classes. For each blindness pattern S the surviving between-group sum of squares is an explicit sum over the retained blocks, so the recorded dial value cuts out a down-set of admissible patterns. This upgrades a one-parameter threshold into a full classification of what the response must resolve.

For every S ⊆ {0,…,b-1}, the response constant on the merged classes outside S satisfies ρ² = (Σ over the retained blocks of an explicit block term)/((8^b − 1)/14), and the set of S compatible with ρ² ≥ 0.7192² is an up-set under inclusion.

Formalise ssR of a general block-merge partition of dyadicBlocks b (generalising ssR_bottom_merged_gen and ssR_tip_merged), then prove monotonicity in S via ssR_coarse_le.

The recorded dial certifies a precise minimal set of valuation classes the statistic must separate.

Blindness cost is not additive over classes, which would mean the coarsening order and the dial order genuinely disagree.
proof_strategy: Telescope ssR over the partition using ssR_append, ssR_shift_parallel and ssR_affine; monotonicity from ssR_coarse_le applied blockwise.
title: Valuation-Class Resolution Spectrum

description:
RLHF.audit_invariant_of_cov_zero shows that an audit statistic uncorrelated with the reward has o(1/β) drift. The conjecture computes the next term: a third-moment (skewness) pairing, giving a hierarchy of orthogonality conditions that a statistic must satisfy to be robust to alignment pressure at every order.

If Cov_p(r,f) = 0 then β²(𝔼_{π_β}f − 𝔼_p f) → 𝔼_p[(r − 𝔼_p r)²(f − 𝔼_p f)]/2, and f is unmovable at all orders iff f is p-a.s. constant on each level set of r.

Expand RLHF.audit_gap_eq_centred to third order using Real.exp_bound with n = 3, exactly as in RLHF.abs_tiltNorm_sub_quad; verify numerically on a 3-point space with an audit statistic orthogonal to the reward.

Alignment robustness of a monitor is a checkable finite hierarchy of moment conditions, not a single correlation test.

The second-order term is not a pure third moment, meaning normalisation effects (W_β) survive at second order and audits can be hacked through the partition function.
proof_strategy: In 𝔼_{π_β}f − 𝔼_p f = 𝔼_p[(e^s − 1)(f − 𝔼f)]/W_β substitute e^s = 1 + s + s²/2 + O(s³) and W_β = 1 + Var/(2β²) + O(β⁻³); the s-term vanishes by hypothesis and the s²/2 term gives the claim.
title: Second-Order Hackability Hierarchy for Uncorrelated Audits

description:
Tensoring budgets is additive on depth up to two levels, and both ends are attained. We conjecture an exact arithmetic criterion for the excess and a positive limiting density for the extremal case, tying composition to the deficit statistics.

foamDepth B (T1*T2) - foamDepth B T1 - foamDepth B T2 = 2 iff both T1 and T2 lie in the lossy part of their scale blocks and T1*T2 >= foamCells B (d1+d2+2); the set of such pairs has positive density.

Cross the interval descriptions of Deficit.lossy_filter_eq for the two factors with the multiplicative bounds foamCells_add_le_mul and foamCells_mul_le; verify exhaustively for B <= 5 and budgets up to 10^4.

Composition of holographic budgets gets a complete combinatorial classification, sharpening the +2 into an exact rule.

The excess depends on finer arithmetic of T1, T2 than block position, suggesting a genuinely two-dimensional phenomenon.
proof_strategy: Write T_i = foamCells B d_i + s_i with explicit remainders and expand the product against the repunit identity (B-1)S+1 = B^(d+1).
title: Arithmetic of the Two-Level Composition Gap

description:
Peak height 2T and sidelobe decay 2/|omega| are the two halves of a time-bandwidth statement. The conjecture is that no window supported on [-T,T] with unit sup-norm can simultaneously beat the rectangular peak and its sidelobe decay by more than bounded factors.

If w is supported in [-T,T] with |w| <= 1 then |w-hat(0)| <= 2T and the integral of |w-hat|^2 is at most 4 pi T, with equality in both iff w is the rectangular window almost everywhere.

Prove the two inequalities from the triangle inequality and Plancherel, then characterize the equality case via strict convexity of the L2 norm on the unit ball of L-infinity.

The rectangular window is the unique extremizer, so the sinc law is the universal model for windowed resonance.

Some window beats the rectangle in both peak and energy, contradicting Plancherel; more likely the equality case is non-unique, revealing a family of extremal windows.
proof_strategy: Plancherel for compactly supported L2 functions plus the equality case of the L-infinity-vs-L2 comparison on a finite-measure set.
title: Window Uncertainty Principle Beyond the Rectangle

description:
The alternating witness has lag-1 autocorrelation 0 and lag-2 autocorrelation 1 while sharing any prescribed prefix. We conjecture that the set of achievable autocorrelation profiles of irrational numbers equals the set of profiles of periodic words, transported by a lacunary perturbation that is invisible to densities.

A function A from positive lags to {0,1} is the autocorrelation profile of an irrational number with prescribed decimal prefix if and only if it is the profile of some periodic word.

Formalise the profile of a periodic word combinatorially, then transport it with Pyth.card_exceptional_le, which already bounds the exceptional sets uniformly in the lag.

Autocorrelation laws of real constants are combinatorial shadows of periodic words, never arithmetic facts.

Some profile is realisable only by rationals, which would give the first arithmetic obstruction of this kind.
proof_strategy: Write digits as periodic base plus lacunary bump; agreements and disagreements coincide with those of the base except on O(log M) positions.
title: Autocorrelation Profile Realisation Theorem

description:
Within one modulus, position and magnitude coincide; identification comes only from cross-modulus variation. The conjecture quantifies that variation and predicts it vanishes exponentially in the bit length, so positional kernels are asymptotically unidentifiable at fixed bit length. It matters because it sets a hard information-theoretic limit on the whole positional-layer programme.

For a pooled design of M moduli of common bit length b, the Fisher information for a positional kernel parameter, orthogonalised against all magnitude kernels, is O(M 2^{-b/2}).

Compute the orthogonalised Fisher information numerically for b = 24, 32, 40 and fit the exponent; then formalise the O(2^{-b/2}) upper bound.

No experiment at cryptographic bit lengths can detect a positional kernel; the layer must be probed at small b.

Positional structure is detectable at scale and the search should be re-opened with larger M.
proof_strategy: Expand the cross-modulus separation j - isqrt N at fixed v, bound its spread by O(1/s), and propagate through the score function.
title: Exponential Decay of Positional Identification Power in Bit Length

description:
Cycle 8 made the primitivity threshold effective in the reflexive cases: card - 1 for a lazy frame (sharp) and 2*(card - 1) from a single self-loop. The remaining case is loopless aperiodicity, where the conjecture is Wielandt's bound n^2 - 2n + 2. The approach bounds the approach and exit legs by the diameter principle and the residual cost by the conductor of the cycle monoid.

For a finite irreducible KFrame F with n = card F.W >= 2 and an aperiodic world, iterR F k u v holds for all u, v and all k >= n^2 - 2n + 2; the Wielandt digraph on n vertices attains this exponent.

Prove by excision of closed paths that the cycle monoid at an aperiodic world is generated by simple cycle lengths at most n with gcd 1, prove a quadratic conductor bound for numerical semigroups with generators at most n, then absorb the two legs bounded by exists_iterR_lt_card; check sharpness by computing powers of the Wielandt digraph for n = 3, 4, 5.

exists_uniform_primitive_of_aperiodic becomes fully effective and the modal path calculus reproves Wielandt's classical matrix bound.

Some frame exceeds the classical exponent, which would locate an error in the identification of matrix-power positivity with iterR, i.e. in stepPow_pos_iff.
proof_strategy: Adapt exists_shorter_iterR to closed paths so that the cycle monoid is generated by simple cycle lengths at most n; aperiodicity gives gcd 1; bound the conductor of such a numerical semigroup quadratically in n (the two-generator case is Chicken McNugget); then pad with iterR_of_aperiodic_pad. The shortcut via two consecutive return lengths at most n is refuted by the figure-eight of 5- and 8-cycles on 12 worlds, whose return monoid has first consecutive pair (15,16).
title: Wielandt Exponent for Aperiodic Modal Primitivity

description:
When the connection set is a union of conjugacy classes the adjacency operator is central in the group algebra, so its powers are class sums. The conjecture is that in this regime no census coincidences beyond the forced ones occur. This would identify exactly when the orbit bound card_census_image_le is sharp.

If S is closed under conjugation and inversion, then walkCount S n g = walkCount S n h for all n implies that g and h are census-equivalent.

Formalise the class-sum expansion of adj S in the group algebra and compare with character-theoretic separation; check computationally on all normal connection sets in groups of order ≤ 24.

card_census_image_le is an equality for normal Cayley graphs, giving an exact orbit count.

Even central connection sets admit hidden symmetry, sharpening the ℤ/8 phenomenon.
proof_strategy: Expand walkCount in irreducible characters via the central idempotents, then use linear independence of characters to separate classes.
title: Census Completeness for Normal Cayley Graphs

description:
The cut rank of a codebook is provably not submodular, while Shannon entropy always is. Formalising submodularity of the cut entropy would separate the two invariants sharply and explain why the entropic Singleton bound dominates the counting one.

cutEntropy C S + cutEntropy C T ≥ cutEntropy C (S ∪ T) + cutEntropy C (S ∩ T) for every finite codebook and all cuts.

Prove it in Lean from a conditional grouping inequality; cross-check numerically against the 24 rank-violating codebooks on three bits.

The entropy profile is a polymatroid and the counting profile is a strictly coarser shadow of it.

Marginals of uniform code distributions would violate a basic information inequality, which would indicate an error in the fibre model.
proof_strategy: Decompose H(S ∪ T) - H(S) as an average of conditional entropies over the fibres of the projection to S, then dominate each by the corresponding conditional entropy over S ∩ T using the grouping inequality.
title: Entropy Submodularity versus Rank Non-Submodularity

description:
The unrestricted count of complement-stable assembly spaces was settled this cycle at 2^(2^(n-1)), the square root of the total. The open refinement asks for the density of self-duality among puzzles of bounded description size, where the assembly space is no longer an arbitrary subset of the cube. The conjecture is that the density still vanishes and that stability is detectable syntactically from the piece multiset.

For fixed m and k, the fraction of framed puzzles with at most m clause pieces of at most k literal inputs each whose assembly space is complement-stable tends to 0 as n grows, and such puzzles are exactly those whose piece multiset is invariant under polarity reversal up to reordering.

Enumerate all puzzles with small m, k, n and compare the syntactic invariance criterion with complement-stability of the computed assembly space.

Self-duality is syntactically decidable in bounded families, giving a fast filter for the parity law.

There are semantically self-dual puzzles with asymmetric piece multisets, so stability is a genuinely semantic property.
proof_strategy: Use card_stableSpaces as the unrestricted baseline, then bound the number of bounded-size puzzles realising a stable space via the gauge parameterisation.
title: Bounded-Description Density of Self-Dual Framed Puzzles

description:
Depth is squeezed between log_3(m+n) - 1 and (m+n-3)/2, both tight only on extremal words. The conjecture asks for the typical constant, testing the reported slope 1.211 against the circulating 1.4.

For nodes drawn uniformly from those with m+n <= X, depth / log_2 X converges to a constant c with c in [1.12, 1.31]; in particular c is not 1.4.

Enumerate nodes with m+n <= X for growing X, regress depth on log_2 X, and formalise a two-sided bound of the form a log_2 X <= depth <= b log_2 X on an explicit density-one subfamily.

The corrected dP law gets a proof-backed constant and the 1.4 folklore value is formally excluded.

Depth is not concentrated and the dP law must be restated as a distributional, not a pointwise, statement.
proof_strategy: Sharpen sum_step_le and sum_step_ge to letter-dependent growth factors, then apply a law of large numbers to the letter sequence of a random word.
title: Exact Constant in the Price Depth Law

description:
The map S ↦ surfaceOf S is uniformly definable and sends the finiteness of S to the triangulability of a surface. Every Π₂ arithmetic statement of the form 'infinitely many n satisfy P' therefore has an exactly equivalent geometric form, and the base theory needed for the equivalence can be measured.

For every arithmetic predicate P, surfaceOf {n | P n} is transfinite-dimensional iff {n | P n} is infinite, provably in a weak base theory.

Formalise the equivalence for a general decidable predicate and inspect the axioms used by the resulting bridge theorems.

A uniform dictionary translating Π₂ number theory into fractal geometry, with the twin prime instance already formalised.

The translation needs strength beyond the base theory, which would itself be a striking reverse-mathematical fact.
proof_strategy: dimH (surfaceOf S) = sup S already holds; combine with the fact that a subset of ℕ is infinite iff unbounded, and track the induction principles used.
title: Arithmetic Surfaces Detecting Goldbach-Type Statements

description:
Every test on a finite dish space has a batch length N > 0 whose residue map is idempotent, so verification stabilises. The current proof yields a quadratic N. The conjecture asks for the sharp bound in terms of the functional graph of the residue map, where the relevant quantity is the least common multiple of the cycle lengths beyond the longest tail.

For every finite D and test t there is N with residue-iterate^N idempotent and N at most g(n) + n, where g is Landau's function and n = card D; and N <= n cannot be improved to a sublinear bound.

Formalise tail length and cycle decomposition of an endofunction on a Fintype, define N as lcm of cycle lengths rounded above the tail length, and prove idempotence; then evaluate the minimal N by exhaustive enumeration for n <= 6 and compare with Landau's function.

Stabilisation of repeated verification has an explicit, essentially optimal cost, and the plain bound N <= n is exposed as false whenever Landau's function exceeds n.

Some endofunction has idempotent power strictly beyond lcm of its cycle lengths plus tail, contradicting the standard functional-graph picture and indicating an error in the tail analysis.
proof_strategy: Decompose the functional graph into the eventual image (a permutation, hence a disjoint union of cycles) and transient trees. Take N a common multiple of the cycle lengths that is at least the maximal tail length; show iterate^N maps everything into the eventual image and acts as the identity there.
title: Idempotent Batch Length of a Verification Transition

description:
Identify the minimizing and maximizing m-dimensional central sections of a diagonal ellipsoid. The Gram determinant governing the section volume is, by Cauchy-Binet, a weighted sum of squared m x m minors of A^{-1} iota, so the extremal subspaces should be spanned by the extreme semiaxes. The codimension-one case, including its equality case, is now proved and serves as the base case.

For A = diag(d) with 0 < d_0 <= ... <= d_{n-1}, the minimum of vol_m(E A ∩ V) over m-dimensional subspaces V equals (prod_{j<m} d_j) vol(B^m) and the maximum equals (prod_{j>=n-m} d_j) vol(B^m), both attained at coordinate subspaces, and only there up to multiplicities.

Prove Cauchy-Binet for det((A^{-1} iota)^T (A^{-1} iota)) in Lean, compare the resulting sum of squared minors against the extreme coordinate terms, and sample random orthonormal frames numerically for n <= 5, m <= 3.

Upgrades volume_centralSection_sandwich from crude lo^m/hi^m bounds to the exact extremal values, with explicit extremizers and uniqueness.

Some non-coordinate subspace beats every coordinate one, revealing that the compound matrix of A^{-1} is not diagonally extremal and requiring a genuinely new majorization argument.
proof_strategy: Establish Cauchy-Binet for Gram determinants; observe that the minors of a diagonal-times-frame product factor as (prod_{i in S} d_i) times a minor of iota; bound the resulting convex combination using the orthonormality relation sum_S (minor_S iota)^2 = 1, and import the equality case from volume_centralSection_eq_max_iff in codimension one.
title: Cauchy–Binet Extremality of Coordinate Sections

description:
Recast the Moser–Tardos analysis as a finite injective encoding of resampling logs by witness trees, avoiding infinite random sequences entirely. The existing finite weighted probability framework supplies the LLL side; only the combinatorial encoding is missing. This would make the constructive LLL fully formal with an explicit running-time bound.

For instances with e*p*(d+1) <= 1 there is an injection from non-terminating Moser–Tardos logs of length T into a set of size 2^n * (d+1)^T * p^T, forcing T = O(n*d*log(1/p)).

Formalize the witness-tree encoding of logs in Lean, prove injectivity, derive the length bound; sanity-check on random 3-SAT instances by evaluation.

The probabilistic method becomes algorithmic with a verified complexity bound.

Randomness is essential to Moser–Tardos and the constructivization is only semi-effective.
proof_strategy: Encode each resampling step by the index of the resampled event and the witness tree of its cause; injectivity by replaying the log; count encodings and compare with the number of logs.
title: Entropy-Compression Certificates for Moser–Tardos

description:
The Berggren tree fails to be Lorentzian because it lives on the null cone, where all distinct rays are spacelike. Move to Pythagorean quadruples a^2+b^2+c^2=d^2 and order the integer points of the closed future cone of R^{3,1} by the Minkowski relation itself. The conjecture is that this yields a locally finite poset acted on by the quadruple analogue of the Berggren moves.

The set of integer vectors v in Z^4 with Q(v) = v1^2+v2^2+v3^2-v4^2 <= 0 and v4 > 0, ordered by u <= v iff Q(v-u) <= 0 and v4 >= u4, is a locally finite poset, and the quadruple Berggren generators act on it by order automorphisms.

Formalise the order, prove antisymmetry via the reverse triangle inequality for future-directed vectors, prove local finiteness by bounding the coordinates of points in an interval, and check that the quadruple generators preserve Q and future-directedness.

A genuinely Lorentzian Pythagorean causal set with intervals of polynomial (volume-like) growth, i.e. the moonshot realised one dimension up.

A precise theorem that integrality plus the cone condition still forces degenerate interval growth, sharpening the obstruction found in this cycle.
proof_strategy: Reverse Cauchy-Schwarz for future timelike vectors gives antisymmetry; interval finiteness follows from the bound on the time coordinate plus the compactness of the spatial slice of a bounded interval; equivariance is a matrix computation as in wordMat_lorentz.
title: Quadruple Causal Cone in (3,1) Signature

description:
The No-Free-Lunch theorem proved here uses a label-flip involution and the uniform prior over targets. For a general prior we conjecture that the maximal achievable off-training edge equals the expected total-variation distance between the posterior label distribution and its flip. This turns a qualitative impossibility result into an exact quantitative one and identifies flip-invariance as the precise obstruction to learning.

For any prior P on targets X -> Bool, any training set T and any x not in T, the supremum over learners depending only on the T-labels of the expected +-1 score at x equals E_{labels on T} |P(f x = true | labels) - P(f x = false | labels)|.

Formalise the conditional posterior for a finite prior, prove the upper bound by the flip pairing and the lower bound by the plug-in MAP learner, and verify numerically on all priors supported on at most four targets over X = Fin 3.

Learnability off the training set is exactly measured by the flip-asymmetry of the prior, unifying No Free Lunch with Bayes-optimality in one identity.

The optimal learner extracts more than the pairwise flip defect, indicating that higher-order structure of the prior is exploitable.
proof_strategy: Pair each target with its flip at x: the learner is constant on the pair, so its score on the pair is the signed mass difference; summing gives the upper bound, and the MAP learner attains it pairwise.
title: Total-Variation Law for the No-Free-Lunch Edge

description:
Any stage-one elliptic-curve computation using t point operations forms multiples at most 2^t, so it can only detect base points of order at most 2^{t+1}. Conjecture: this converts into a per-curve success probability at most c·2^{2t}/p, making every fixed-t curve budget essentially linear in p. The doubling ladder should be extremal.

For every addition chain of length t and every prime p, the probability that a uniformly random curve over F_p with a uniformly random base point is detected by that chain is at most c·2^{2t}/p for an absolute constant c.

Formalize the reach bound (done: addChain_le_two_pow) and the order bound (done: detected_order_le_two_mul_max), then bound the number of points of order at most 2^{t+1} in a cyclic group (done: card_lowOrder_le_sq) and average over group orders in the Hasse interval.

No reordering or reshuffling of stage-one multiples can produce sub-linear curve budgets without growing t like log p; the lite arm's exponent 1 is structural.

There exists a short chain with anomalously large detection mass, which would be a genuinely new stage-one design.
proof_strategy: Chain reach bound by strong induction; detection window via the elliptic involution; counting by the truncated totient sum; averaging over the Hasse interval.
title: Smoothness-Free Addition-Chain Barrier

description:
This cycle proved max over events equals min over couplings by exhibiting both optima. The conjecture is that the identity is an instance of finite LP duality, with complementary slackness forcing the maximal coupling's support. A duality proof would generalize the statement from the Hamming cost to arbitrary costs, i.e. to a finite Kantorovich-Rubinstein theorem.

For every cost c : X x X -> R the minimum of sum c(x,y) k(x,y) over the transport polytope of (p,q) equals the maximum of sum phi p - sum psi q over the dual polytope {phi x - psi y <= c(x,y)}, and for c = indicator of inequality the dual optimum is attained at phi = psi = indicator of {q <= p}.

Formalize the two polytopes as Finset-indexed linear systems and prove duality by Farkas / Fourier-Motzkin elimination in the finite case, then specialize to c = 1 - delta and compare with isLeast_disagreeProb.

The catalog gains a reusable finite optimal-transport toolkit; total variation, Wasserstein and Kantorovich distances become one theorem.

A degeneracy in the transport polytope would show that attainment needs the explicit construction, isolating exactly which vertices are missed.
proof_strategy: Finite Farkas lemma; identify vertices of the transport polytope with spanning forests; complementary slackness against the Neyman-Pearson indicator.
title: Linear-Programming Duality for the Transport Polytope

description:
The discrete Gabor transform of spectral data has a position spread and a frequency spread whose product is conjecturally bounded below by 1/(4π), with equality exactly on the Heisenberg orbit of the Gaussian window. The approach is to combine the already-formalised Fourier intertwining relations with the second moment of the Gaussian integral. It matters because it identifies the Gaussian window as the unique optimum rather than merely a convenient choice.

For every normalised window w with finite second moments, Δa(w)·Δξ(w) ≥ 1/(4π), with equality if and only if w lies in the gaborAct-orbit of gaussC s for some s > 0.

Formalise the second moment ∫ x² exp(-b x²) dx = (1/2b)√(π/b) in Lean, define Δa and Δξ for the Gabor transform of Algebra.SmoothWindows.HarmonicGaborWindow, and prove the inequality via the Cauchy-Schwarz/commutator argument; check the equality case against gaborAct_gaborAtom.

The Gaussian window becomes the canonical, provably optimal window for the catalog's harmonic-sum detector, and the equality locus is a Heisenberg orbit, giving a group-theoretic classification of optimal windows.

Either the discrete spreads are not the right invariants (the sums are not integrals) or the optimum is a non-Gaussian discrete window, which would be a genuinely new phenomenon for multiset-supported data.
proof_strategy: Commutator identity [position, frequency] = i/(2π) transported through heisRep; Cauchy-Schwarz on the resulting quadratic form; equality forces a first-order ODE whose solutions are Gaussians; fourier_gaussC identifies the fixed ray.
title: Gaussian Extremality of the Discrete Gabor Uncertainty Product

description:
The Combinatorial Nullstellensatz reduces the whole problem to a coefficient nonvanishing statement for L_1^{p-1} L_2^{p-1} in characteristic p, where L_1, L_2 are the two coordinate forms of the direction family. The degree budget matches the conjectured threshold exactly; the counterexamples show that with zero slack all admissible coefficients can vanish simultaneously. The conjecture is that one unit of slack already forces a nonzero coefficient.

If v_1,...,v_k are pairwise independent and sum_i (p-|S_i|) <= (k-2)(p-1) - 1, then some e with e_i <= |S_i|-1 and |e| = 2(p-1) satisfies coeff_e(L_1^{p-1} L_2^{p-1}) != 0 in F_p.

Symbolic computation of the coefficient sums over F_p for p=5,7 and k=4,5 for all admissible exponent vectors; then a Lean proof of the multinomial identity plus a Lucas-type nonvanishing argument.

Proves the corrected sharp threshold (k-2)(p-1)-1 for all k, completing the problem and giving a purely algebraic proof of the triple criterion as a special case.

The polynomial method is not tight for this problem and the corrected threshold must come from a combinatorial (Kneser / Pollard) route instead.
proof_strategy: Write coeff_e as sum over splittings e = f+g with |f|=|g|=p-1 of multinomial(p-1;f) multinomial(p-1;g) prod a_i^{f_i} b_i^{g_i}. Use the slack to choose e so that exactly one splitting has both multinomials nonzero mod p (Lucas), which makes the sum a single nonzero monomial in the pairwise determinants.
title: Slack-One Nonvanishing for Bilinear Power Coefficients

description:
Classical sequential growth builds a causal set one event at a time subject to Bell causality and discrete general covariance. The Berggren tree is a deterministic 3-fold growth process whose labelled invariants are now all exactly known, making it a concrete test case for the covariance axioms.

The Berggren growth process, viewed as a labelled sequential growth with birth rates supported on the three Berggren moves, satisfies discrete general covariance (the induced measure on unlabelled posets is independent of the labelling order) if and only if the three branch weights are equal.

Formalise finite labelled growth histories to depth k as words, define the induced measure, and compare the measures of relabelled histories; the free-monoid theorem wordMat_injective makes the history space explicitly a ternary tree.

A fully formalised, exactly solvable example of a covariant sequential growth model with computable interval and antichain statistics.

An explicit obstruction showing that tree-like growth is incompatible with discrete general covariance, which sharpens why physical growth models produce non-tree posets.
proof_strategy: Because levels are antichains and intervals are chains, every unlabelled poset arising has a unique automorphism-free presentation, so the covariance condition reduces to a symmetric-function identity in the three weights.
title: Deterministic Sequential Growth of the Berggren Poset

description:
The N-independent shape counts b(r,L) of surjective even closed walks should satisfy a finite linear recursion in L for fixed r, with an algebraic bivariate generating function. The shapes are Eulerian circuits of doubled connected multigraphs on r labelled vertices.

For each r there are constants c_1, ..., c_d with b(r, L+d) = c_1 b(r, L+d-1) + ... + c_d b(r, L) for all large L.

Compute b(r,L) for r ≤ 4 and L ≤ 10 by exhaustive evaluation of the formal definition, fit a recursion, and prove it by a transfer-matrix argument on edge-multiplicity vectors.

All moments of the ensemble become effectively computable in closed form, order by order, with no new combinatorial input.

The shape counts are transcendental in nature and the moment polynomials must be attacked one order at a time.
proof_strategy: Encode a walk shape by the vector of edge multiplicities modulo two together with the current vertex, giving a finite automaton whose transfer matrix has the shape counts as its trace-like statistics.
title: Shape Generating Function for Even Closed Walks

description:
The max-cut averaging bound was proved this cycle both by counting and by local search, with an explicit iteration bound. The conjecture is that the Edwards improvement m/2 + (n-1)/4 for connected graphs is reachable inside the same subtraction-free exchange calculus, by flipping greedily along a spanning tree instead of appealing to spectral methods.

Every connected graph on n vertices with m edges has a cut S with 4*cut S >= 2*m + (n - 1).

Formalize a spanning-tree greedy in Bridges/MaxCutLocalSearch.lean, derive the bound from the exchange identity cut_flip, and check tightness on K3, C5 and Petersen by evaluation.

A verified Edwards bound strictly stronger than the averaging bound, obtained by finite means only.

A connected graph all of whose locally maximal cuts equal m/2 would show the gain needs global spectral information.
proof_strategy: Order the vertices along a spanning tree; place each vertex opposite its tree parent, gaining one full tree edge, and charge the remaining edges to the averaging identity; combine with the handshake identity 2*cut S = sum_v crossDeg S v.
title: Edwards-Type Local-Search Bound Above the Average

description:
The chamber complex of a min-plus aggregator has a complete dual graph and a binomial f-vector. We conjecture these two invariants characterize exactly the fans arising this way, namely normal fans of simplices. The approach is to reconstruct the weights from the fan using the rigidity theorem and then verify the resulting aggregator induces the fan.

A complete polyhedral fan in R^n / R.1 is the chamber complex of some min-plus aggregator iff it is the normal fan of a simplex, iff its dual graph is complete and its f-vector is (choose n (d+1)).

Formalize the fan of a min-plus aggregator as a Mathlib polyhedral object and prove both implications; test small cases (n = 2, 3) by enumerating complete fans with complete dual graph.

Gives a purely combinatorial recognition principle for tropical-linear social welfare functionals.

Exotic fans with complete dual graph exist, and the exchange law would need extra data (e.g. wall multiplicities) to pin the geometry down.
proof_strategy: Recover delta up to a constant from the walls via sub_const_of_decisiveSet_eq, build the candidate aggregator, and compare cell labels using closedCell_injOn.
title: Simplex-Normal-Fan Characterization of Min-Plus Chamber Complexes

description:
Additivity of the zeta-regularised residue under disjoint unions of graded G-sets is now a theorem. The conjecture is that the whole principal part is a ring-level invariant: the product grading of two graded G-sets is a Cauchy product of partition functions, so the Laurent moments of a product should be an explicit convolution of the moments of the factors. This would turn the residue into a homomorphism out of a Grothendieck ring rather than merely an additive invariant.

For eventually polynomial grade counts with polynomials P and Q, the product grading has grade counts eventually polynomial with polynomial R determined by the Cauchy product, and the Laurent moment vector of R is the convolution of the moment vectors of P and Q; in particular the residue of the product is a bilinear expression in the moments of the factors.

Formalise the product grading of graded G-sets, compute its transitivity counts, and compare circleIntegral_polyZeta_moment applied to the product with the conjectured convolution of laurentMoment vectors.

The map from graded G-sets to principal parts at q = 1 becomes a homomorphism of rings, giving a genuine K-theoretic invariant of graded actions.

The Cauchy product mixes the entire part into the principal part, showing that the residue is additive but not multiplicative and locating the obstruction in the tail correction.
proof_strategy: Multiply the two closed forms polyZeta P and polyZeta Q, expand in the (q-1)-adic Laurent basis using the proved moment formula, and match coefficients against the Newton expansion of the Cauchy product.
title: Residue Homomorphism on the Grothendieck Ring of Graded G-Sets

description:
The exact failure law uses only one property of the uniform codebook: an event that does not constrain a coordinate leaves that coordinate's collision probability equal to 1/M. Replacing uniformity by this axiom should extend the exact law to structured hash families.

Any hash family closed under re-randomisation of a single coordinate and 2-wise independent satisfies P[failure] = 1 - (1 - 1/M)^k exactly; t-wise independent families satisfy it up to an additive O(k^{t+1}/M^t).

Abstract ExactFailure.card_inter_collisionEvent_mul into a hypothesis on a general finite family of codebooks, and re-run the induction of card_noCollisionEvent_mul against it; test numerically on affine hash families over small fields.

Shannon's random-coding analysis becomes derandomisable with no loss, since small explicit families inherit the exact law.

The gap between structured and uniform families is quantified, isolating the exact cost of derandomisation.
proof_strategy: Replace the update-bijection by the closure axiom, keep the one-competitor-at-a-time induction, and control the error term by inclusion-exclusion truncated at depth t.
title: Conditional-Marginal Calculus for Non-Uniform Hash Families

description:
Quantization noise enters the decision certificate exactly like a fine-tune delta. Allocating bits inversely to the per-layer margin should therefore be optimal for preserving decisions at fixed total memory.

Under a fixed total bit budget, the allocation minimizing the number of flipped top-1 decisions satisfies bits_k = c - log2(margin_k) + O(1), so the near-tropical core can be quantized strictly harder than the diffuse tail.

Formalize the optimization with the perturbation-to-margin certificate; validate by quantizing a real stack layerwise and counting decision flips.

A principled, measurable rule for mixed-precision serving of transformer stacks.

Decision flips are dominated by error accumulation across layers rather than per-layer margins, pushing the analysis to the depth budget of C1.
proof_strategy: Model quantization as a sup-norm perturbation, apply strictTop_of_margin per layer, and solve the resulting convex allocation problem.
title: Margin-Proportional Quantization Budget

description:
Rigidity pins extremal shared-serving families as hubs, but does not evaluate a general family. Conjecture: the best simultaneous agreement of one shared model with a family equals 1 - nu/2, where nu is the fractional cover value of the pairwise-disagreement hypergraph. The approach is LP duality against the two nonnegative defects of the saturation identity.

For any family A_1..A_k, max over H of min over i of agr(H, A_i) equals 1 - nu/2 with nu the value of the fractional cover LP of the hypergraph whose hyperedges are the pairwise disagreement sets.

Formalise the LP and its dual, and check the equality on the hub family (where nu = 2/k) and on random families evaluated numerically.

Serving capacity of an arbitrary family becomes computable from a hypergraph statistic before any weights are shared.

Extremal geometry is richer than covering designs and the capacity needs a second parameter beyond nu.
proof_strategy: Use saturation_defect_identity to reduce to simultaneous vanishing of the Cauchy-Schwarz defect and the budget defect; recognise the feasibility condition as the covering LP and dualise.
title: Fractional-Cover Value of the Disagreement Hypergraph

description:
We realise nonzero-digit densities 0 and 1 over an arbitrary prefix. The conjecture is that the whole rational simplex of digit frequency vectors is realisable by irrational numbers sharing any prescribed finite prefix, so that the empirical frequency vector of a prefix constrains nothing at all.

For every x >= 0, every n, and every rational probability vector (p_0,...,p_9), there is an irrational y with the same first n decimal digits as x and digit-c frequency exactly p_c for each c.

Splice a periodic block pattern realising the frequencies onto Pyth.graft, perturb at the lacunary positions via Pyth.ofDigits_add, then prove frequencies by a block-counting argument.

Digit frequency measurement on any finite prefix is provably devoid of information about the number.

Some frequency vectors are unreachable under prefix constraints, revealing an unexpected arithmetic obstruction.
proof_strategy: Blocks of length L with prescribed digit multiplicities give frequencies exactly p_c; lacunary bumps break periodicity without moving frequencies since they occupy O(log M) positions.
title: Prescribed Digit Frequency Vectors Over Any Prefix

description:
The exact error identity |Q n − P n √2| = (√2−1)^n is now a theorem. We conjecture that the spine lists all best rational approximations to √2, with the side of approximation dictated by the parity of n, and that the constant 1/(2√2) is optimal.

For every rational a/b with 1 ≤ b < P (n+1) and (a,b) ≠ (Q n, P n), |√2 − a/b| > |√2 − Q n / P n|; moreover P n² · |√2 − Q n / P n| → 1/(2√2).

Formalise a pigeonhole argument on the lattice ℤ + ℤ√2 using pell_error_exact and the exact classification pell_unit_classification; test numerically for b ≤ 10^5.

A fully formal, continued-fraction-free proof that the Pell spine is the sequence of best approximations, transferable to every real quadratic unit.

A better approximation off the spine would contradict pell_unit_classification, so failure would expose a gap in the norm-one description of good approximations.
proof_strategy: If |√2 − a/b| is small then |a² − 2b²| < 1 forces a² − 2b² = ±1, so (a,b) lies on the spine by pell_unit_classification; monotonicity of the error then finishes.
title: Spine-Optimality of Diophantine Approximation

description:
Tasting at random with two-sided error should save at most a cubic factor over deterministic tasting. The approach is to average the deterministic covering argument that already proves D ≤ C0·C1 in this cycle. It quantifies how much a cook gains by guessing where to taste.

For every dish f, tasteCost f ≤ c · R_{1/3}(f)^3 for an absolute constant c.

Define randomised taste trees as PMFs over Taste n, prove the certificate-overlap lemma survives averaging, and check the bound numerically on the exhaustive n ≤ 3 census.

Randomness is essentially useless in the kitchen, matching the classical polynomial-equivalence phenomenon.

There is a recipe where random tasting is superpolynomially better, an unexpected culinary use of randomness.
proof_strategy: Yao's principle over the finite set of dishes plus the formalised restriction lemma restrict_isCertificate.
title: Cubic Randomised Tasting Bound

description:
The three links at an event have Minkowski lengths 4(c-b)^2, 4(a-b)^2, 4(c-a)^2. The multiset of link lengths at depth k is therefore an exactly computable invariant. The conjecture pins its minimum.

For every k the minimum of the link lengths over all events of depth k equals 4, and it is attained exactly at the events of the pure middle (Pell) spine and their A-children.

Compute the spectrum to depth 6, then prove the lower bound 4 by showing that each of |c-b|, |a-b|, |c-a| is a positive integer, and characterise equality by solving c-b = 1, a-b = ±1, c-a = 1 inside the tree.

A complete description of the shortest scales of the discrete geometry, the analogue of a lattice spacing, together with the exact locus where it is attained.

Some deeper branch achieves a smaller separation, which would contradict integrality, so the failure mode is a proof that the attaining locus is larger than the spine.
proof_strategy: Integrality gives length >= 4 immediately; equality analysis reduces to the twin-leg equation a-b = ±1 and to c-b = 1 (triples of the form (2m+1, 2m(m+1), 2m(m+1)+1)), both of which are classical families that can be characterised inside the tree by induction on depth.
title: Minimal Link Length Spectrum

description:
A mean-value step turns an anchor of quality delta into an enclosure of width Theta(delta^2), while continued-fraction convergents give delta ~ q^-2 at cost q^2. Conjecturally this yields certified enclosures of width epsilon at cost O(epsilon^{-1/2}) for any simple root of an entropy-type function whose sign at rationals is decidable by an integer comparison. It matters because it identifies Diophantine approximation, not brute-force arithmetic, as the resource that buys certified precision.

For f real-analytic with simple root p* and integer-decidable sign at rationals of denominator b at cost O(b^2), a certified enclosure of width epsilon is obtainable at cost O(epsilon^{-1/2}).

Instantiate the proved lemma BB84.newton_enclosure_step for a second threshold (six-state protocol) and measure achieved width against 4.9*(anchor error)^2.

Certified constants in information theory become cheap: 20+ decimals at the cost of today's 8.

Some obstruction (e.g. certificate size growth for non-binary entropies) limits the method to first-order gains.
proof_strategy: Abstract newton_enclosure_step over f and f', add a Diophantine input supplying convergents, and bound the derivative bracket by |f''| times the anchor error.
title: Quartic Certification Law for Entropy Thresholds

description:
The Pythagorean Hydra is flat (each head carries one natural number, its Berggren depth) and therefore lives at omega^omega. Iterating the address construction — heads that are Berggren words whose letters are themselves indexed by Berggren words — builds hydras of height n whose ordinal is a tower omega^omega^...^omega, with supremum epsilon_0. The conjecture is that the n-fold iterated Berggren hydra has exactly the strength of transfinite induction up to the n-th tower ordinal, so the family is unprovably terminating in PA in the limit.

For each n, the n-fold iterated Berggren hydra game terminates, provably in PA + TI(tower_n), and the union over all n has termination equivalent to TI(epsilon_0), hence unprovable in PA.

Formalize the level-2 game (heads = pairs (word, word)) with the lexicographic potential on Multiset (Multiset Nat); prove termination and exhibit plays of length exceeding every phi k d.

A genuine natural independence result whose objects are still Pythagorean triples, obtained by iterating the address map rather than by importing an abstract hydra.

The iteration collapses, showing that the freeness of the Berggren monoid caps the whole family at omega^omega — a strong structural rigidity statement.
proof_strategy: Replace the potential Phi by the Dershowitz-Manna order on nested multisets; upper bound via ordinal assignment, lower bound via the greedy strategy already used in exists_maximal_battle.
title: Iterated Berggren Hydras and the Epsilon-Nought Barrier

description:
Via the seed bijection, the tree zeta is a sum over primitive coprime pairs (m,n) with m+n odd of (m²+n²)^{-s}. Counting representations of an integer by such pairs should give an exact factorisation into ζ(s), L(s,χ₄) and ζ(2s), providing the meromorphic continuation the mission asked for and identifying the tree's zeros with classical ones.

For Re s > 1, Σ_w c(w)^{-s} = ¼ (ζ(s) L(s,χ₄)/ζ(2s) − 1); consequently the tree zeta continues meromorphically to ℂ with a simple pole at s = 1, and its zeros are those of L(s,χ₄) together with the poles of ζ(2s).

Prove a multiplicity formula for #{(m,n) : m²+n² = c, coprime, m+n odd, n<m} in terms of the divisor-counting function r₂, then compare Dirichlet series termwise using Mathlib's ζ and Dirichlet L-function API.

The Berggren tree zeta is an explicit product of classical L-functions, so 'RH for the Berggren tree' is exactly equivalent to RH for ζ and L(·,χ₄) — an exactly solvable dictionary rather than an independent problem.

The primitivity and parity constraints obstruct multiplicativity, isolating the tree zeta as a genuinely non-Eulerian Dirichlet series.
proof_strategy: Use Gaussian integers: primitive representations of c correspond to unit-times-associate factorisations of c in ℤ[i] with coprime factors; the parity condition removes the factor 2 and produces the ζ(2s) denominator by Möbius inversion over squares.
title: Exact Dirichlet Factorisation of the Berggren Tree Zeta

description:
Beyond the minimum, the second-smallest tropical monomial defines a refined complex whose cells are labelled by ordered pairs (winner, runner-up). We conjecture single-voter exchanges act on these labels as adjacent transpositions, making the dual graph a Cayley graph of the symmetric group.

The top cells of the (argmin, second-argmin) complex are labelled by ordered pairs of distinct voters, and two such cells are joined by a single-voter exchange iff their labels differ by an adjacent transposition of the induced score order.

Define secondAgg as tropAgg over S.erase (argmin), prove a master formula analogous to tropAgg_update, and identify the dual graph.

The full score order, not just the winner, is governed by a Coxeter-style exchange calculus, connecting the complex to the braid arrangement.

The refined complex has extra adjacencies, showing that runner-up dynamics are strictly richer than a Coxeter system.
proof_strategy: Iterate tropAgg_update on S.erase j, use decisiveSet_update_lower_subset for locality, and match the wall structure with the braid arrangement's.
title: Runner-Up Complex and Adjacent Transposition Generators

description:
The two-ordinate resolution criterion proved in this cycle should generalise: for m ordinates with minimum gap δ, a single inequality in g_{2s}(δ) should force the position profile to have exactly m local maxima. The approach exploits the two scale-doubling identities, which make the profile a polynomial in one variable per interfering pair. This turns a peak-finding heuristic into a theorem with an explicit constant.

There is an absolute constant C such that C·m·g_{2s}(δ)·max_i(1/4+t_i²) ≤ min_i(1/4+t_i²) implies posProfile S s has exactly m local maxima, one within o(s) of each t_i.

Formalise the m = 3 case first, using posProfile_pair_at/posProfile_pair_mid as the model; then run the numerical scan of ComputationalEvidence.md on random m-tuples to calibrate C before attempting the induction on Multiset.

The Gaussian-windowed detector provably counts zeros, not just detects them, giving a formally verified peak counter for critical-line ordinate families.

The failure will exhibit a configuration where three ordinates conspire to create a fourth peak, which would be the first rigorous 'phantom zero' construction for smooth windows and would bound how far any window-based counter can be trusted.
proof_strategy: Write posProfile as w_i-weighted sums of powers of u = g_{2s}(δ) via gaussWin_half_eq and gaussWin_eq_pow_four; bound the interference of the m-1 non-local terms by a geometric series; apply the derivative sign change argument on each interval between consecutive ordinates.
title: Multi-Ordinate Rayleigh Threshold for Gaussian Peak Counting

description:
Cycle 3 refuted the truncation explanation by computing the capped ceiling exactly, so the remaining structural freedom is non-nested (crossing) block structures. The conjecture is that the nested law acquires an explicit defect term governed by the crossing mass of the two set partitions. It matters because only crossing pairs can now produce a dial as low as 0.648 from two individually high-ceiling profiles.

For crossing block structures the squared Spearman coefficient equals the nested value minus a nonnegative defect determined by the meet of the two partitions in the partition lattice, and readings near 0.648 require crossing mass above 0.3.

Formalise the coefficient for an arbitrary pair of set partitions of the rank set, expand the covariance over meet blocks, and evaluate on small crossing examples exactly in Lean.

Every low dial reading with high individual ceilings certifies a crossing dependence between statistic and response.

The nested law extends verbatim and the partition lattice plays no role.
proof_strategy: Write both midrank vectors as conditional expectations with respect to the two partitions; the covariance is then controlled by their meet, and Cauchy-Schwarz gives the defect.
title: Crossing Statistic-Response Partition Defect

description:
The depth-graded silver zeta (1 − 3ε^{-2s})^{-1} is an Ihara-type zeta of a 3-regular tree with edge length 2 log(1+√2). Its pole set, now an exact theorem, should be the spectrum of a self-adjoint transfer operator attached to the Berggren substitution, giving a fully explicit Hilbert–Pólya model.

There is a self-adjoint operator T on L²(ℝ/(π/log(1+√2))ℤ) whose spectrum equals {Im s : 1 − 3ε^{-2s} = 0}, unitarily equivalent to the transfer operator of the substitution w ↦ {Lw, Mw, Rw} acting on ℤ[√2]-scaled functions.

Construct T explicitly as multiplication after Fourier transform, formalize the unitary equivalence, and prove the spectrum coincides with the pole set proved in silver_denom_eq_zero_iff.

The Berggren critical line becomes an operator spectrum, an exactly solvable Hilbert–Pólya model in which the mechanism is completely transparent.
