The arithmetic pole set of the silver zeta is not of spectral origin, delimiting how far the Hilbert–Pólya heuristic reaches for tree zetas.
proof_strategy: Compute the transfer operator of the free ternary substitution on the character group of ℝ/(π/log ε)ℤ; diagonalise it by Fourier inversion, and match eigenvalues 3ε^{-2s} with the zero condition of the denominator.
title: Transfer-Operator Realisation of the Silver Critical Line

description:
Coordinatewise addition and multiplication both fail to descend to the Moebius quotient. We conjecture a single cohomological explanation: the seam is a Z/2-torsor and the obstruction to descending an algebraic operation is a nonzero class in H^1(Z/2; -), nonzero precisely when the associated line bundle is nontrivial.

Let X be a topological ring and ~ the relation generated by a partial involution sigma on a subspace S with sigma acting by an orientation-reversing Z/2-torsor. Then a binary operation on X/~ lifting that of X exists iff the class of sigma in H^1(Z/2; X) vanishes; for the Moebius seam the class is nonzero.

Formalise the Moebius instance first (already done in no_induced_add / no_induced_mul), then define the cocycle for a general partial involution and prove the equivalence for finite group actions.

A single theorem subsuming all descent failures for quotients of number systems by twisted identifications.

Descent failure is a purely combinatorial fundamental-domain phenomenon with no cohomological content.
proof_strategy: Interpret a lift as a sigma-equivariant structure; the difference of two representatives defines a 1-cocycle; vanishing of its class is exactly well-definedness of the operation.
title: Cohomological Obstruction to Descent Along Twisted Seams

description:
Weights with pairwise gap at least gamma should make each open chamber contain a sup-ball of radius gamma/2 around any singleton-labelled profile, with gamma/2 optimal. For Pythagorean weights (a,b,c) the gap is min(b-a, c-b). This turns the exchange threshold into a quantitative robustness statement for the winner.

If |delta i - delta j| >= gamma > 0 for all i != j in S and decisiveSet x = {i}, then every y with sup |y - x| < gamma/2 also has decisiveSet y = {i}, and gamma/2 is the largest such radius.

Prove the inclusion from the 1-Lipschitz bound and the sharp threshold; exhibit an extremal profile attaining gamma/2.

A quantitative, noise-robust form of the exchange law, immediately applicable to numerically perturbed score profiles.

Robustness must depend on the profile and not only on the weight gaps, indicating a non-uniform geometry.
proof_strategy: Combine abs_tropAgg_sub_le with mem_decisiveSet_update_iff_le applied coordinatewise, then build the extremal profile from a wall point.
title: Spectral Gap Stability of Pythagorean Chambers

description:
With alpha computed exactly for clique sums, the gap between alpha and the Lovasz theta function becomes testable under gluing. We conjecture that the gap is additive up to the same minus-two defect, bridging the combinatorial trace calculus with semidefinite relaxations. Small cases with C5-like sides are finite computations.

For a clique sum along a clique of size k, theta(G) - alpha(G) <= (theta(G_1) - alpha(G_1)) + (theta(G_2) - alpha(G_2)) + min(k, 2).

Compute theta numerically for clique sums of two C5s glued along an edge and along a vertex, and compare with the exactly known alpha from the trace formula.

The trace calculus extends to spectral relaxations, giving gluing rules for Shannon capacity bounds.

A numerical violation would show the theta function is not controlled by separator traces, isolating a genuinely spectral obstruction.
proof_strategy: Build a block orthonormal representation from representations of the sides that agree on K, and bound the resulting theta value using the trace decomposition of alpha.
title: Clique-Sum Additivity of the Independence-Theta Gap

description:
The proved Theta(H) bounds leave a factor-100 gap to the experimentally observed density 0.1592 ~ 1/(2*pi). The Euclid bijection reduces the count to visible lattice points of opposite parity in a quarter disc, where a Moebius-weighted Gauss circle argument should produce the exact constant with a square-root error term. Settling it converts a qualitative Theta into a sharp asymptotic law for the Berggren tree.

#bergBox(H) = H/(2*pi) + O(sqrt(H) * log H); in particular #bergBox(H)/H tends to 1/(2*pi).

Formalize the Moebius sieve on the coprimality condition in BerggrenBoxCounting.pairBox, combine with a quarter-disc lattice point estimate, and check the constant numerically against the tables in ComputationalEvidence.md.

The Theta(H) theorem upgrades to an exact asymptotic with an effective error term, and the primitive-Pythagorean-triple counting function inherits the same sharp constant.

The visible-point heuristic fails for the opposite-parity subfamily, indicating a parity obstruction invisible to the sieve and forcing a different Euler factor.
proof_strategy: Write #pairBox(H) as a sum over g of mu(g) times the count of opposite-parity pairs in the disc of radius sqrt(H)/g, evaluate each inner count by the Gauss circle estimate, and sum the Moebius series to 1/zeta(2) times the parity factor.
title: Lehmer Constant for the Berggren Box

description:
The draw-weighted dial is the quadratic form p ↦ ½ pᵀ D p with D_ij = (x_i − x_j)(y_i − y_j). All regime dependence is spectral. Determining the inertia of D turns 'can an unbalanced draw flip the dial?' into an eigenvalue comparison.

For a comonotone population with pairwise distinct footprints, D has exactly one positive eigenvalue, and the flip threshold for the conditioning number satisfies κ_crit² = |λ_max| / |λ_min^-| up to a factor |ι|.

Formalize D as a Matrix ι ι ℝ, prove Hermitian, and relate ½ pᵀ D p to Catalog.UniformDial.wcov via wcov_eq_half_double_sum; then bound the Rayleigh quotient on the simplex.

The triage rule becomes computable from a single eigenvalue pair rather than from all pair masses.

The budget bound ε²C − M²Δ is the sharp regime-free criterion and no spectral shortcut exists.
proof_strategy: Write D = x yᵀ + y xᵀ − (x∘y) 1ᵀ − 1 (x∘y)ᵀ, a rank-≤4 perturbation of zero; compute inertia from the 4-dimensional Gram matrix of {x, y, x∘y, 1}.
title: Discordance Spectrum of the Pairwise Dial Form

description:
No matrix realizes a Markoff Vieta move, in contrast with the linear Berggren action. The conjecture is that degree two is optimal and that the obstruction is a rank computation on finitely many Markoff base points.

No polynomial map of degree less than two in any linear coordinate system realizes the Vieta involution on the Markoff surface, and the quadratic realization is unique modulo the surface equation.

Set up the general quadratic ansatz and solve the resulting linear system on a spanning set of Markoff triples.

A clean statement of why the Lorentz half of the Berggren machinery cannot transport, valid for all coordinate changes.

A hidden linearization exists, which would immediately import the Berggren hyperbolic geometry to the Markoff tree.
proof_strategy: Generalize the four-point obstruction of vieta_not_linear to a Vandermonde-type rank argument on more base points.
title: Optimal Nonlinearity Degree of the Vieta Involutions

description:
The silver abscissa failed for the full tree only because two of the three Berggren generators produce polynomially growing spines. Restricting to a subtree generated by hyperbolic words should restore the naive exponent log(branching)/log(spectral radius), turning the refuted conjecture into a true theorem with an explicit boundary.

For the subtree generated by two Berggren words that are hyperbolic as elements of SL₂(ℤ), the node zeta Σ c(w)^{-s} has abscissa exactly log 2 / log λ, with λ the smaller spectral radius, and the series diverges at the abscissa.

The sandwich version is already formalized for the MM/MR subtree (abscissa inside [0.196, 0.757]); the remaining test is to replace the crude per-block bounds by an invariant-cone argument giving matching exponential rates, and deduce a single abscissa.

The silver-abscissa conjecture is true after removing the parabolic directions, so the refutation is sharp and the boundary between silver and arithmetic behaviour is exactly the presence of parabolic generators.

Even purely hyperbolic subtrees inherit arithmetic abscissae, meaning the height grading is never controlled by spectral radii alone.
proof_strategy: Show the two generators preserve a common cone in which the norm grows by a factor in [λ, Λ] per letter; conclude c(w) ≍ (growth)^{|w|} with two-sided constants, then sum 2^d against those bounds.
title: Purely Hyperbolic Subtrees Restore the Silver Abscissa

description:
Cycle 9 identified the greatest fixed point of the diamond with the set of worlds reaching a cycle and refuted its identification with the recurrent set. The successor conjecture is that this gap is essential: recurrence is undefinable in the basic modal language but definable by the tangled return relation. This fixes an expressiveness threshold for probabilistic reachability.

No set of basic modal formulas defines the class of pointed finite support frames whose point is recurrent; the recurrent set is the greatest set X such that every w in X lies on a positive-length cycle inside X.

Collapse the absorbing two-state frame onto the one-state lazy frame by a surjective bounded morphism and apply Valid_of_boundedMorphism_surjective as in nonlazy_not_definable; for the positive half show the internally-cyclic sets form a complete lattice closed under unions.

Transience is provably invisible to the basic modal language while recurrence is definable one level up, in Cycle 1's tangled formalism.

A modal characterisation of recurrence exists, which would make the support of stationarity decidable by finitely many formulas.
proof_strategy: Undefinability by bounded-morphism transfer between absorbChain and the one-state loop; definability by closure of the internally-cyclic sets under arbitrary unions plus gfpDia_eq_reachesRecurrent.
title: Modal Invisibility of Transience

description:
No modal axiom set should define primitivity, nor bound the uniform primitivity exponent. Cycle 8 supplies, for each N, a frame whose exponent is exactly N, so the classes to be separated are now explicitly populated. This draws a sharp boundary around what correspondence theory expresses about mixing.

For every set Gamma of modal formulas and every natural N, Gamma defines neither the class of primitive support frames nor the class whose uniform primitivity exponent is at most N.

For each N take the nearest-neighbour chain on N+1 states, whose exponent is exactly N by nbrChain_exponent_eq, and collapse it by a surjective bounded morphism onto a lazy frame of smaller exponent; apply Valid_of_boundedMorphism_surjective.

Mixing is beyond modal axiomatisation, extending the limitative results from irreflexivity to quantitative dynamics.

A modal scheme forcing primitivity would be a positive correspondence result and a proof-theoretic certificate of mixing.
proof_strategy: Divisor lumpings of long cycles and the sharp nearest-neighbour family give, for every N, a pair of frames on opposite sides of the threshold but related by a surjective bounded morphism.
title: Modal Undefinability of Mixing Thresholds

description:
The wide-window limit recovers the catalog's harmonicSum; the conjecture is that the rate of convergence encodes the zero counting function, and that the whole scale space determines the zero family uniquely. The approach identifies gaussSpectral with a heat smoothing of the weighted counting measure and applies injectivity of the heat semigroup. It matters because it makes the smooth window a lossless, rather than merely convenient, reparametrisation of the data.

For a ConjSymm family with counting function N(T) ~ (T/2π)log(T/2πe), harmonicSum - gaussSpectral(S,s) ≍ (log s)/s² as s → ∞; moreover gaussSpectral(S,·) = gaussSpectral(S',·) on a nondegenerate interval implies S = S'.

Prove the injectivity half first for finite multisets by analytic continuation in 1/s², then test the asymptotic rate numerically against the first 10^4 ordinates before attempting the Mellin-transform argument.

The Gaussian scale space is a complete invariant of the zero family, so any statement about zeros can be restated as a statement about a single smooth function of one real variable.

There exist distinct zero families with the same scale space, which would exhibit an explicit kernel of the smoothing operator and bound what any window-based statistic can distinguish.
proof_strategy: Write gaussSpectral(S,s) = ∫ exp(-πt²/s²) dμ_S(t) for the weighted counting measure μ_S; substitute u = 1/s² to obtain a Laplace transform in u; use uniqueness of Laplace transforms for injectivity and a Mellin/Tauberian argument with the known counting asymptotics for the rate.
title: Tauberian Converse for the Wide-Window Limit

description:
Binary branching of the Markoff tree is caused by the degeneracy of the singular triples. Deforming the cubic surface should restore ternary branching and, for exactly one deformation parameter, allow a branching-compatible injection into the Berggren tree.

There exists k for which the Vieta tree of x^2+y^2+z^2-xyz = k is ternary, and exactly one such k admits a child-compatible injection into the Berggren tree.

Enumerate integral points for small k, count children per node, and formalize the ternary instance found.

The transfer conjectured in the mission statement becomes true after deformation, giving a Berggren model for a Markoff-like surface.

Ternary branching is impossible for the whole family, strengthening the branching obstruction proved here.
proof_strategy: Adapt the descent and unique-parent arguments of MarkoffFreeBinary to the deformed equation and recount children at nonsingular nodes.
title: Ternary Vieta Trees on Deformed Cubic Surfaces

description:
Tilting a window by x^k translates its threshold, so sweeping x over (0,∞) should sweep the unique maximiser over all degrees exactly when the log-graph is in strictly convex position. This is a Newton-polygon characterisation of strict log-concavity, proved here in one direction for binomial weights.

A positive window a on [0,n] is strictly log-concave iff for every d ≤ n there is x > 0 such that d is the unique maximiser of k ↦ a k * x ^ k.

Formalise the converse: if a k is not a vertex of the upper hull of (k, log a k), show no tilt makes k the strict maximiser; combine with binomialWeight_every_degree_is_unique_peak for the forward direction in general.

Provides a tilt-based, purely order-theoretic definition of strict log-concavity, convenient for tropical/Newton-polygon transfer.

Vertex sweep is strictly weaker than strict log-concavity, isolating a new intermediate class of sequences.
proof_strategy: Forward: choose the tilt with threshold d + 1/2. Backward: a non-vertex index is a strict convex combination, which no linear tilt can promote to a maximum.
title: Vertex Sweep Characterisation of Strict Log-Concavity

description:
The address bijection identifies the Berggren tree with the free monoid on three letters, an automatic structure whose first-order theory is decidable. Adding the hypotenuse as a function symbol imports the Pell recurrences of the B-spine, which are not recognisable by finite automata. The conjecture is that this addition is exactly the boundary between decidability and undecidability for the theory of the tree.

The first-order theory of (PPT, bergA, bergB, bergC) is decidable, while the theory of (PPT, bergA, bergB, bergC, c) with c the hypotenuse function interprets Presburger arithmetic with a multiplicative predicate and is undecidable.

Formalize the tree-automatic presentation via addr_bijective; for the negative half, define the B-spine hypotenuse sequence and encode squares as a definable predicate.

The Matiyasevich front of the original mission is answered exactly: undecidability appears not in the addressing, but in the arithmetic of hypotenuses.

The hypotenuse function stays automatic, and the entire Berggren structure is decidable — an unusually strong tameness statement for a Diophantine object.
proof_strategy: Use addr_injective to transport formulas to words; then interpret multiplication through the quadratic growth of the A-spine, in the style of the classical undecidability of (N, +, squares).
title: Automatic Structure of the Berggren Tree with Hypotenuse

description:
The proved finite binomial expansion makes every orbit invariant a polynomial of bounded degree in the iteration count, with weights that do not depend on the count. The conjecture is that this turns orbit membership for normalized series over a number field into a decidable question with an explicit bound on the witness. It would make the corrected-product dynamics algorithmically tractable level by level.

For normalized q-series f, g with coefficients in a fixed number field and f of depth k, the predicate 'exists n with g = f^{*n}' is decidable, and any witness n is bounded by an explicit function of k and the least level m at which f and g differ.

Formalize the decision procedure: at each level m solve the single polynomial equation sum_{d <= m/k} c_d * binom(n,d) = coeffAt m g supplied by PoleOrderTorsor.Norm.exists_binomial_coeffs, and prove termination using PoleOrderTorsor.Norm.deepSubgroup_succ_lt.

Corrected-product orbits become computationally comparable: orbit membership, orbit equality and the separating level all become effectively computable.

There are normalized series whose orbit invariants are identically degenerate at every level, which would contradict separatedness of the filtration and force a new invariant beyond the coefficient tower.
proof_strategy: Combine the n-independence of the binomial weights (coeff_pow_binomial_expansion) with the fact that a non-zero polynomial of degree at most m/k has at most m/k roots, and induct on the depth using strictness of the filtration.
title: Decidability of Corrected-Product Orbit Membership

description:
Define the spurious energy of a window as the sum of the scale-invariant sidelobe amplitudes of its Fourier transform. The conjecture is that this quantity is infinite exactly for windows with a boundary discontinuity and finite for Schwartz windows, making it a two-valued detector of smoothness. The approach is repeated integration by parts to convert the order of the boundary singularity into the polynomial order of the sidelobe envelope.

E(w) = Σ_n ξ_n·‖𝓕w(ξ_n)‖ over the non-principal local maxima of ‖𝓕w‖ diverges for every compactly supported w that is not C^∞, and converges for every Schwartz w.

Extend Algebra.SmoothWindows.Sidelobes from the indicator function to the family of B-spline windows (k-fold convolutions of rect), where the transfer function is sinc^k and the sidelobe amplitudes are explicit; check the divergence/convergence dichotomy against k.

Window quality becomes a single computable invariant, and 'peaks that are really sidelobes' get a sharp criterion independent of the data being analysed.

There is a compactly supported, non-smooth window with summable spurious energy, which would give a strictly better compactly supported detector than any Schwartz window — an outcome of independent practical interest.
proof_strategy: Integrate by parts k times against exp(-2πiξt); boundary terms of order k give ξ^{-k} decay; sum over the explicit sidelobe frequencies as in sidelobeFreq; compare with Real.not_summable_one_div_natCast and Real.summable_one_div_nat_pow.
title: Spurious Sidelobe Energy as a Smoothness Invariant

description:
The factor-B lower bound uses that a deterministic rule tells the adversary exactly which page to request next. A randomised rule breaks that coupling. The classical expectation is that the achievable ratio drops from B to logarithmic in B, which would identify randomisation, not signal quality, as the first real escape route.

There is a randomised eviction rule whose expected fault count on any stream over B+1 items is O(log B) times the offline optimum, while every deterministic rule is a factor B away.

Extend the Serves model with a probability measure over schedules and prove an expected-cost upper bound for the marking rule against the same offline bound offline_cost_bound.

Randomised eviction is provably outside the four-family bound and becomes the priority arm.

The gap is information-theoretic rather than adversarial, and only lookahead or larger budget can help.
proof_strategy: Phase decomposition of the stream, per-phase expected fault count for a marking rule, combined with the existing per-phase offline bound.
title: Randomisation Against the Adaptive Eviction Adversary

description:
For any continuous map into the carrier the nullity fibre is clopen, which is exactly the algebraic shadow of a branch that an attacker can observe. We conjecture that the guarded fragment coincides with the branch-free circuits, so that the guard is a constant-time discipline in disguise.

In a division-tolerant arithmetic circuit model, a circuit's value map is continuous into the transreal carrier iff no execution reaches an exceptional constructor on a boundary input; every unguarded circuit has an input pair separated by a single constructor observation.

Define a circuit model whose gates are the TExpr constructors, define an observation as the constructor tag of the output, and prove the separation statement using Transreal.isOpen_preimage_null.

The guarded transfer principle becomes a formal constant-time criterion for division-tolerant arithmetic.

Constructor observability is strictly coarser than continuity, and leakage needs a finer invariant than topology.
proof_strategy: Show the tag map Transreal → Fin 4 is continuous for the discrete topology on the three exceptional tags, so continuity forces the tag to be locally constant; then contrapose on the trichotomy.
title: Nullity Fibres as Side-Channel Observables

description:
For graphs of maximum degree at most three the non-backtracking trace sequence should determine the number of cycles of each length. The proved value at n = 3 (six times the number of triangles) is the first case, and the girth criterion pins the first nonzero index. This would make the Hashimoto trace a strictly finer invariant than the adjacency spectrum on this class.

If G and G' have maximum degree at most three and trace(B_G^n) = trace(B_{G'}^n) for all n, then G and G' have the same number of cycles of every length.

Compute the trace sequences of adjacency-cospectral subcubic pairs and compare cycle counts; formally, set up the triangular system relating trace(B^n) to cycle counts of length at most n and prove its unipotence by induction on n.

The non-backtracking trace sequence is a cycle-spectrum invariant, strictly refining the adjacency spectrum on subcubic graphs.

A cospectral subcubic pair with equal non-backtracking traces but different cycle counts exists, bounding how much combinatorial data the Hashimoto matrix retains.
proof_strategy: Induct on n: the contribution of length-n cyclic non-backtracking words splits into words spanning a single n-cycle (2n each, by the proved multiplicity bound) and words revisiting edges, which in a subcubic graph are controlled by shorter cycles already determined by the induction hypothesis; monotonicity under graph inclusion controls the error terms.
title: Cycle Spectrum Reconstruction for Subcubic Graphs

description: Ramsey's theorem states that any 2-coloring of the edges of K_6 contains a monochromatic K_3 (a triangle of one color). Applied to DNA: any sequence of 4^6 + 1 = 4097 nucleotides must contain a repeated 6-mer (by pigeonhole). But Ramsey theory for subsequences is more subtle: what is the minimum length L(k) of a DNA sequence over {A, C, G, T} such that every subsequence of length k contains a repeated 4-mer? Conjecture: L(k) = Theta(k * 4^4 * log(4^4)) = Theta(k * 256 * 8) = Theta(k * 2048). More precisely, by the Lovasz local lemma, L(k) >= 4^{4k/5} for sequences that avoid repeated k-mers in all subsequences. Conjecture: for real genomes, the actual L(k) is much smaller because real DNA has low complexity regions (microsatellites, Alu repeats) that create forced repeats. Specifically, the human genome has L(4) ~ 1000 (any 1000 consecutive bases contain a repeated 4-mer in some subsequence), while the random genome has L(4) ~ 4^4 * log(4^4) ~ 5000. Test: compute L(k) for real genomes vs random genomes and verify the factor-of-5 compression. Impact: DNA avoids subsequential repeats in a way that Ramsey theory predicts, but real genomes are 5x more 'forced' than random sequences.
proof_strategy: Define the subsequence Ramsey number L(k, s, alphabet) as the minimum length of a sequence over the given alphabet such that every subsequence of length k contains a repeated s-mer. For DNA: alphabet = {A, C, G, T}, s = 4 (4-mers). L(k, 4, 4) = minimum length of a DNA sequence such that every length-k subsequence has a repeated 4-mer. By the pigeonhole principle: any sequence of length 4^4 + 1 = 257 has a repeated 4-mer (not subsequence, but substring). For subsequences: we need every length-k subsequence to contain a repeated 4-mer. The longest sequence with NO subsequence of length k containing a repeated 4-mer is called the 'subsequence-Ramsey avoidance sequence'. Conjecture: this sequence has length O(k * 4^4 * log(4^4)). Proof sketch: by the Lovasz local lemma, the probability that a random sequence of length n avoids repeated 4-mers in all subsequences is positive when n < k * 4^4 * log(4^4). Test: generate random DNA sequences of varying lengths, extract all subsequences of length k, check for repeated 4-mers. Compare with real genomes (human chromosome 1, E. coli genome). Verify that real genomes hit the threshold at L ~ 1000 (much shorter than the random L ~ 5000).
title: The Ramsey Theory of DNA: Subsequence Avoidance in Genetic Codes

description:
The refinement potential increases by at most one per input symbol regardless of which symbol is chosen, suggesting adaptive experimenters gain nothing in symbol count over the fixed suite. We conjecture a matching Omega(|S|+|T|) lower bound for any adaptive strategy.

Every adaptive distinguishing strategy for machines with |S|, |T| states requires, in the worst case, at least |S| + |T| - 2 input symbols; adaptivity provides no asymptotic saving.

Formalise adaptive strategies as decision trees over inputs and outputs, and lower-bound their depth by the refinement potential of the extremal family.

The non-adaptive suite wordsUpTo (|S|+|T|-2) is optimal in symbol count, not merely sufficient.

There is an adaptive speed-up, which would give a genuinely new algorithmic primitive for conformance testing.
proof_strategy: Show that after k symbols the extremal tail/cycle pair is still in one refinement block; conclude the decision tree cannot separate them before depth |S|+|T|-2.
title: Adaptivity Gap for Machine Experiments

description:
Only 8 of the 84 order-4 unital magmas attaining the maximal associativity defect (n-1)^3 arise from the proved shift construction. We conjecture a forbidden-pattern characterisation of all maximisers and an explicit counting formula. This would turn a sharp inequality into a structure theorem.

A unital magma of order n >= 3 satisfies D = (n-1)^3 iff its product restricted to the non-units satisfies a finite forbidden-pattern condition generalising 'a*b = phi(b) with phi fixed-point-free'; the number of such labelled tables is 2 for n = 3 and 84 for n = 4, given in general by an explicit formula.

Exhaustively enumerate order-5 unital magmas attaining D = 64 (or sample if needed), extract the extremal tables, and formalise the resulting characterisation in Lean against ShiftMagma.defect_eq.

Extremal magmas are completely classified and the sharpness theorem upgrades to a bijective count.

The extremal family is wilder than pattern-defined, indicating that maximal incoherence is not finitely axiomatisable.
proof_strategy: Show that maximality forces, for each pair (a,b), the element a*b to avoid the fixed points of the right-translation structure; then reconstruct the table from that constraint and count.
title: Classification of Maximal-Defect Unital Magmas

description:
For a stationary specification the walk matrices are max-plus powers of a fixed matrix, so the value function should grow linearly with slope the max-plus eigenvalue, up to a bounded correction. The degenerate constant-weight case is already proved. Establishing the general case imports max-plus Perron-Frobenius into the formal DP framework.

For a stationary DP specification with transition matrix A on a finite state space, there is λ(A) and a bounded h with val n s − n • λ(A) − h(s) → 0, and optimal runs are eventually periodic with period dividing the cyclicity of the critical graph of A.

Formalise the max-plus eigenvalue as the maximum cycle mean, prove val_const_step's generalisation for irreducible A, and verify numerically on random 3x3 and 4x4 integer matrices.

Long-horizon DP values admit a closed asymptotic form, giving effective error bounds for truncated horizons.

Some finite state DP has genuinely non-linear value growth, contradicting max-plus Perron-Frobenius and indicating a hidden hypothesis.
proof_strategy: Use walk_chapman_kolmogorov to identify walks with max-plus powers, then subadditivity of the sequence sup_s,t walk 0 m s t plus Fekete's lemma to extract λ, and a cycle-decomposition argument for the bounded correction.
title: Max-Plus Spectral Asymptotics for Stationary DP

description:
Every Boolean readout of the splitting type gives a channel value; the conjecture is that the value 1 is attained only by the sign readout, and that the whole spectrum separates S3 from C3 and from degree-4 groups. This makes the one-bit verdict an extremal statement rather than a coincidence.

For an S3 cubic, max over Boolean readouts f of I(residue ; f(T)) = 1, attained uniquely at f = sign; for a cyclic cubic the maximum is log2 3 - 2/3 < 1.

Enumerate the 2^(c-1) two-block partitions of conjugacy classes, compute each channel value with the closed-form surprisal lemmas of S3TypeChannelLossy, and compare.

The one-bit law is an extremal characterisation of the index-2 subgroup A3 inside S3.

Some non-sign readout also reaches 1 bit, meaning the channel value does not pin down the quadratic resolvent.
proof_strategy: A Boolean readout has value 1 iff both its blocks carry mass one half and it is coupled deterministically to the residue; the first forces a normal subgroup of index 2, the second forces it to be the kernel of the sign character.
title: Boolean Readout Spectrum of a Cubic Field

description:
The median-of-medians selection algorithm is conjectured to have breakdown number exactly ceil(b/2)*ceil(s/2) on n = b*s points, asymptotically n/4. Since the universal equivariant ceiling is n/2, the algorithm pays a factor-two robustness tax intrinsic to its two-layer structure. The approach applies the proved single-layer robustness and sharpness results independently within blocks and then across blocks.

For n = b*s, the breakdown number of the median-of-block-medians estimator equals ceil(b/2) * ceil(s/2).

Define blockMedian in Lean over List (List Q), prove the lower bound by two nested applications of median_robust_quant_le and the upper bound by contaminating ceil(s/2) entries in each of ceil(b/2) blocks; sanity check with #eval on 16 = 4*4.

The first formal proof that a widely used selection algorithm is strictly less robust than the statistic it approximates.

Either the tax is smaller (some blocks can be shared) or larger (block interactions compound), and the failure pinpoints how corruption budgets combine across composition layers.
proof_strategy: Lower bound: a surviving inner median needs fewer than ceil(s/2) corruptions in its block, so fewer than ceil(b/2)*ceil(s/2) total corruptions leave more than half the blocks clean, and median_robust_interval applies at the outer layer. Upper bound: explicit contaminate applied blockwise plus countP_contaminate_le.
title: Block-Median Robustness Tax

description:
The exact identity 2*r*#edges + s*(r-s) = (r-1)*n^2 proved this cycle expresses the Turan number through the defect s*(r-s) with s = n mod r. The conjecture is that the same defect controls the extremal structure: almost-extremal K_{r+1}-free graphs are almost r-partite, with an explicit rather than o(n^2) error term.

Every K_{r+1}-free graph on n vertices with at least ex(n,K_{r+1}) - m edges becomes r-partite after deleting at most m + s*(r-s)/(2r) edges.

The convexity ingredient sum_i c_i^2 >= r*(n/r)^2 + (n mod r)*(2*(n/r)+1) is already proved (sum_sq_ge_balanced); derive the edge-deletion bound from it in Lean.

A verified Turan stability theorem with an explicit error term.

A near-extremal graph far from r-partite is a new extremal example.
proof_strategy: Express the edge count of an r-partite graph through the sum of squares of part sizes; minimize by convexity; compare with the exact extremal value already proved.
title: Defect Stability for Turan Graphs

description:
This cycle proved that a symmetry group is reconstructible from the interpretations it makes recoverable, provided interpretations may speak about configurations indexed by the whole carrier. The natural refinement bounds the arity: with only finitely many coordinates visible, one should recover the group only up to closure in the topology of pointwise convergence. This ties the definability boundary to the classical theory of closed permutation groups.

For a permutation group G on an arbitrary carrier, the group of permutations preserving every finite-arity G-recoverable interpretation equals the closure of G in the topology of pointwise convergence; in particular it equals G exactly when G is closed.

Formalise finite-arity configurations as maps from Fin n, define the induced symGroup, and compare with a pointwise-convergence closure predicate; test on the finitary symmetric group inside Sym(natural numbers), whose closure is the full symmetric group.

Recoverability determines the symmetry group exactly up to topological closure, giving a complete Galois theory of external interpretations.

Some non-closed group is already determined by its finite-arity theory, meaning structural truth sees more than pointwise approximation.
proof_strategy: One inclusion from continuity of preservation under pointwise limits; the other by adapting the membership interpretation memInterp to finite restrictions and extending partial agreements using the finite-arity kernel theorem.
title: Finitary Galois Closure of Interpretation Theories

description:
Phase-augmented worlds represent exactly the finite rooted directed preorders whose clusters have at most c elements, and this bound is sharp. We conjecture that the corresponding modal logic is S4.2 together with a single cluster-width axiom, so that the combinatorial parameter c is modally definable.

For each c, a modal formula is valid on every CWorldC (Fin n) (Fin m) c iff it is derivable in S4.2 extended by the axiom asserting that every final cluster has at most c points.

Write the cluster-width axiom in the catalog's MFormula syntax, prove frame correspondence against clusterSize_eq_min_phases, then filtrate the canonical model.

The phase count becomes a modally definable invariant, giving a graded family of complete logics interpolating between S4.2 and the theory of preorders.

Cluster size is combinatorially sharp but modally invisible, which would separate frame invariants from definable ones in this setting.
proof_strategy: Correspondence for the cluster-width axiom, then transfer validity along sat_bddMorphism using the proved representation and its converse.
title: Bounded-Cluster Modal Completeness

description:
The pole trichotomy is local; expressions are finite. We conjecture that continuity of transEval is equivalent to a finite conjunction of local sign conditions at the zeros of the denominator subexpressions, giving a decision procedure for continuity of the whole expression algebra.

For e : TExpr ℝ with continuous atoms, Continuous (transEval e) holds iff at every zero x₀ of every denominator subexpression the numerator is nonzero and both the numerator and the denominator have constant sign on a punctured neighbourhood of x₀.

Extend the induction in Transfer.lean with the three regimes of PoleTransfer.lean as the base cases, and test the resulting criterion against x/x, 1/x, 1/x², x/(x²) and (1/x) + (-1/x).

Guardedness can be replaced by a strictly weaker, decidable side condition, enlarging the conservative fragment.

Continuity of compound expressions depends on cancellation between infinities, and no purely local criterion exists.
proof_strategy: Structural induction; the new step is closure of the class of continuous transreal-valued maps under + and * away from the indeterminate forms, using the joint-discontinuity results of Boundary.lean to isolate the bad pairs.
title: Syntactic Decision Procedure for Transreal Continuity

description:
The proved upper bound trace(B^n) <= (#darts) q^n is matched, below the log_q N threshold, by a tree-covering lower bound. Combining the two should yield the Alon-Boppana inequality for the second adjacency eigenvalue of a connected (q+1)-regular graph.

For a connected (q+1)-regular graph on N vertices, lambda_2 >= 2 sqrt(q) - o(1) as N tends to infinity, derived from two-sided estimates on trace(B^n).

Prove the lower bound trace(B^n) >= N(q+1)q^{n-1}(1-o(1)) for n <= c log_q N by counting non-backtracking walks in the universal cover, then convert to eigenvalue estimates.

A formal Alon-Boppana theorem, hence a formal benchmark for Ramanujan graphs.

The non-backtracking trace loses too much information below the girth threshold, and spectral lower bounds need the adjacency matrix directly.
proof_strategy: Use the regular row-sum lemma to identify B with the q-ary branching walk, count walks that do not close early, and apply the power-sum characterisation of the spectral radius.
title: Alon-Boppana Bound from Non-Backtracking Trace Growth

description:
The pigeonhole converse bounds every encoder by M correct strings, while the exact law pins the random codebook's failure probability at 1-(1-1/M)^k. Comparing them turns the usual asymptotic rate statement into an exact threshold question about the least admissible codebook size.

For each epsilon in (0,1) the least M with 1-(1-1/M)^k <= epsilon equals ceil(k / ln(1/(1-epsilon))) + O(1), and no deterministic encoder achieves reliability 1-epsilon with fewer than (1-epsilon)|S| codewords.

Compute the least M by #eval for many (k, epsilon) pairs, fit the constant, then formalise the two-sided estimate from the exact law together with AlmostLossless.converse_card_good_le.

The price of randomisation in almost-lossless coding is an explicit constant, not merely a Theta(1/epsilon) factor.

The threshold has a genuinely non-logarithmic correction, indicating a second-order effect invisible to the exact law.
proof_strategy: Invert the exact law using log(1-1/M) expansions with explicit remainder, and pair with the converse counting bound.
title: Exact Randomisation Threshold Against the Pigeonhole Converse

description:
In l^2 every ball has Hausdorff dimension top, so topological largeness should force maximal dimension. The Fsigma case is already a theorem; the conjecture extends it to all sets with the Baire property and adds that non-meagre Borel sets must contain a Hilbert cube. This would show that dimension is invisible to Baire category except at the extreme value.

Every subset of l^2 with the Baire property is meagre or has dimH = top, and every non-meagre Borel subset contains a topological copy of the Hilbert cube.

Formalise Baire-property localisation to a ball and intersect with the flat cubes of le_dimH_ball; then build the cube copy by a Cantor scheme.

Hausdorff dimension collapses to a two-valued invariant on Baire-property sets in l^2.

There is a non-meagre set of finite Hausdorff dimension, an exotic object with no finite-dimensional analogue.
proof_strategy: Non-meagre plus Baire property gives comeagreness in some ball; a comeagre subset of a ball meets every flat cube in a comeagre subset, whose dimension is at least n for all n.
title: Category–Dimension Dichotomy Beyond the Borel Hierarchy

description:
The discrete bound by sums of Bhattacharyya angles is now proved. The remaining question is calibration: do those sums converge to the Fisher-Rao length as the partition mesh tends to zero? A positive answer identifies the Fisher-Rao length functional with the length structure of the spherical metric of the square-root embedding, and implies the geodesic lower bound.

For a C¹ curve of strictly positive probability vectors on [a,b], the sums ∑ₖ 2·arccos BC(p_{t_k}, p_{t_{k+1}}) over partitions converge to fisherRaoLength p v a b as the mesh tends to 0.

Establish the local expansion 2 arccos BC(p_s, p_t) = ∫_s^t speed + O((t−s)³) using the chord bound and the exact two-point evaluation, then sum over a partition and pass to the limit.

The Fisher-Rao length becomes the intrinsic length of the spherical metric, and the geodesic lower bound 2 arccos BC ≤ length follows immediately.

The integral functional would not be the induced length of the Bhattacharyya angle metric, indicating that the definition of fisherRaoLength needs a different normalisation.
proof_strategy: Local Taylor comparison of arccos BC with the Fisher-Rao speed, uniform continuity of the integrand on a compact interval, and Riemann-sum convergence.
title: Riemann Convergence of Bhattacharyya Angle Sums

description:
Real library design is constrained by budgets and architectures, not by cardinality alone. The conjecture is the matroid analogue of this cycle's results: greedy over any matroid of admissible libraries recovers at least 1/(1 + kappa) of the optimum for the Shtarkov price functional, degrading to 1/2 at maximal curvature and to exactness at kappa = 0.

For any matroid M on the pool Omega, the greedy library A produced by scanning models in order of marginal price satisfies shtarkov P A >= (1/(1 + curvature P Omega)) * shtarkov P B for every independent set B of M.

Formalise matroid exchange for Finset bases in Lean and combine it with curvature_marginal_ge exactly as the uniform case combines it with the covering inequality.

Curvature-aware library design extends to structured deployment constraints with a single scalar knob.

The uniform-matroid analysis of this cycle is special to cardinality constraints, isolating where the exchange property is essential.
proof_strategy: Pair up greedy and optimal elements by a matroid exchange bijection and charge each optimal element to its partner using the curvature inequality.
title: Matroid-Constrained Curved Library Design

description:
A security theorem quantified over output distributions whose collision probability is below the uniform value 2^{-ℓ} is vacuous. This thread found and repaired exactly such a defect in the catalog's privacy-amplification bound. The conjecture is that a single general satisfiability criterion decides vacuity for the whole family of Rényi-2 / min-entropy / guessing-probability hypotheses.

A hypothesis of the form ∑ p^2 ≤ f(ℓ,k) over normalized p on 2^ℓ points is satisfiable iff f(ℓ,k) ≥ 2^{-ℓ}, and every leftover-hash statement with f(ℓ,k) < 2^{-ℓ} is vacuous.

Prove the general iff in Lean (one direction is collision_ge_uniform, the other the uniform witness), then apply it mechanically to each collision-style hypothesis in the catalog.

A reusable audit lemma that certifies non-vacuity of cryptographic statements, protecting future formalizations from the same defect.

Some hypothesis shape admits satisfiability below the uniform collision value, which would contradict Cauchy–Schwarz and hence indicate a mis-statement of the normalization.
proof_strategy: Cauchy–Schwarz with the all-ones vector gives 1 = (∑p)^2 ≤ 2^ℓ·∑p^2; the converse is the explicit uniform witness.
title: Cauchy–Schwarz Vacuity Audit for Leftover-Hash Hypotheses

description:
The effective channel pool of the zero-fit dial ladder, measured by the reciprocal excess 1/rho^2 - 1, is fitted to within 0.027 by a quadratic law with a positive floor, but the residuals drift monotonically with bitlen. We conjecture a genuine change of growth exponent from 2 to 3 above some b0 between 96 and 160. Deciding this fixes the asymptotic shape of the erosion and hence every extrapolated band prediction.

There exists b0 in [96,160] such that e(b) = 1/rho^2(b) - 1 satisfies: e(b)/b^2 is strictly increasing for b > b0, and e(b) = Theta(b^3).

Run the uniform ladder at bitlens 96, 112, 128, 160 with the existing exp536 harness and three seeds each; fit e(b) = kappa*b^g + c and test g = 2 against g > 2 by likelihood ratio. Formalize the discriminating inequality in Lean as an exact rational comparison, as in quadratic_retrodiction.

The dial's usable range is bounded: the band floor is crossed permanently and the ladder cannot be rescued by larger samples, only by changing the statistic.

The quadratic-with-floor law extends, and the crossing bitlen of 84.4 is the permanent boundary; extrapolation to cryptographic bit widths becomes reliable.
proof_strategy: Work on the reciprocal scale where the model is additive (dilution_reciprocal_additive). Bound the residual of the quadratic fit at each new rung by an exact rational interval, then show no (kappa, c) pair can satisfy all rung constraints simultaneously, which is a finite linear feasibility problem in two unknowns and is decidable by linarith.
title: Cubic Pool Transition Above Bitlen 128

description:
Mode-convergence statements (binomial to Poisson, Poisson to normal) should be continuity statements for the map θ ↦ (⌈θ⌉₊ - 1, ⌊θ⌋₊). The conjecture is that brackets stabilise along any family of threshold windows whose thresholds converge to a non-integer, and genuinely oscillate when the limit is an integer.

For threshold windows with θ_j → θ: if θ ∉ ℕ then eventually firstArgmax = lastArgmax = ⌊θ⌋₊; if θ ∈ ℕ both ⌊θ⌋₊ - 1 and ⌊θ⌋₊ occur as brackets for infinitely many j in a suitable family.

Prove eventual constancy of Nat.floor and Nat.ceil near a non-integer, apply to θ_n = lam + lam/n, and construct an oscillating family for integral θ.

Explains uniformly why approximation theorems transfer modes, with explicit thresholds for 'eventually'.

Bracket transfer requires more than threshold convergence, e.g. uniform control of the criteria.
proof_strategy: Nat.floor is locally constant off ℤ; combine with ThresholdWindow.brackets_mono and brackets_step for the quantitative version.
title: Bracket Stabilisation Along Threshold Limits

description:
The finite deletion theorem proved this cycle reduces the classical factor-k/e improvement of the Erdos bound to a single elementary estimate on binomial coefficients. Feeding a Stirling-type bound into ramsey_deletion should give a fully verified asymptotic improvement of R(k,k) > 2^(k/2), with no probability theory at all.

R(k,k) > (1 - o(1)) * (k/e) * 2^(k/2), provable from ramsey_deletion together with C(n,k) <= (e*n/k)^k.

Prove C(n,k)*k^k <= (e*n)^k in Lean, instantiate ramsey_deletion at n = ceil((k/e)*2^(k/2)) and t = floor(2*C(n,k)/2^C(k,2)), and compare with the evaluated table for k <= 20.

First fully verified asymptotic improvement of the classical Ramsey lower bound.

The uniform Stirling estimate fails, isolating the analytic input the counting framework cannot absorb.
proof_strategy: Bound the averaged number of monochromatic k-sets by (e*n/k)^k * 2^(1 - k(k-1)/2); show it is at most n/2 at the stated n; apply the transversal deletion already formalized.
title: Asymptotic Deletion Gain for Diagonal Ramsey Numbers

description:
The Berggren tree carries two gradings, depth and hypotenuse height. The two-variable series Z(u,s) = Σ_w u^{|w|} c(w)^{-s} interpolates between the purely silver generating function (1-3u)^{-1} at s = 0 and the arithmetic tree zeta of abscissa 1 at u = 1. Understanding its abscissa curve s₀(u) explains exactly how the silver exponent degenerates into the arithmetic one.

For 0 < u < 1 the series Z(u,s) = Σ_w u^{|w|} c(w)^{-s} converges precisely for s > s₀(u), where s₀(u) = log(3u)/(2 log(1+√2)) for u ≥ 1/3 and s₀(u) < 0 for u < 1/3; s₀ is continuous, piecewise real-analytic, and non-smooth exactly at u = 1/3.

Formalize Z(u,s) as a summable family over List (Fin 3); prove convergence for s > s₀(u) using hyp_le_silver_pow and 3^d words per depth, and divergence at s₀(u) using the Mspine_silver_growth lower bound and depth_slice_lower.

The silver exponent and the arithmetic abscissa 1 become two points of one analytic curve, giving a precise sense in which the tree's spectral data controls its zeta function.

The two gradings are analytically independent, showing the silver spectral data has no influence whatever on the height-graded zeta.
proof_strategy: Upper bound: split the sum by depth, use c(w) ≥ 5 and c(w) ≤ 5(3+2√2)^d to compare with Σ_d (3u)^d 5^{-s}(3+2√2)^{-sd}. Lower bound: restrict to the middle spine and to the depth-d slice, where the counts are exactly 3^d.
title: Two-Variable Berggren Zeta and the Silver-to-Arithmetic Transition

description:
Classify all irreducible elements of ZM = Z[t]/(t^2-1) by their norm a^2 - b^2. The rational-integer case is now settled: n in Z is irreducible in ZM iff n = +-2. Prime norm suffices for irreducibility in general, and we conjecture that prime norm together with the single norm-4 family exhausts the irreducibles.

a + bt with a^2 - b^2 != 0 is irreducible in ZM iff |a^2 - b^2| is prime, or |a^2 - b^2| = 4 and a is odd (the associates of 2).

Formal Lean proof combining Moebius.ZM.irreducible_of_prime_natAbs, Moebius.ZM.irreducible_of_nrm_eq_four and Moebius.ZM.irreducible_mk_int_iff with a converse for b != 0: if |N| is composite and not 4 then exhibit a factorisation via the difference-of-squares parametrisation.

Complete arithmetic of the twist ring, giving explicit factorisation algorithms for 'Moebius integers'.

There exist sporadic irreducibles of composite norm, so the norm is not a faithful invariant on a non-domain.
proof_strategy: Write N = mn with m, n > 1 and both != 2; use the identity (a+bt) = ((m+n)/2 + (m-n)/2 t)(...) obtained from the hyperbolic parametrisation; treat the norm-zero locus separately via the zero-divisor description.
title: Norm-Form Classification of General Twist-Ring Irreducibles

description:
Witness B shows chi(G) = max(chi_1, chi_2) fails precisely when the edges of the glueing clique are split between the sides, so each side needs fewer than k colours. We conjecture the failure is controlled by a defect d measuring how far K is from being a clique on the worse side, giving a two-sided estimate for weak clique sums. This interpolates between the weak and genuine settings.

For a weak clique sum with defect d = |K| - max(omega_1(K), omega_2(K)), one has max(chi_1, chi_2) <= chi(G) <= max(chi_1, chi_2) + d.

Enumerate all weak clique sums on at most six vertices, record chi(G) - max(chi_1, chi_2) against d, then formalise the upper bound by extending the colour permutation to a partial matching on the split part.

A quantitative bridge covering both the proved chi = max theorem (d = 0) and the Witness B failure (d = 1).

The data would reveal a second parameter, presumably the interaction pattern of the split edges, needed to control colouring of weak sums.
proof_strategy: Colour the sides, permute colours to agree on the unsplit part of K, and spend at most d fresh colours on the split vertices.
title: Split-Clique Defect Bound for Weak Clique Sums

description:
For a random bounded poset on n points, we conjecture that the trivial upper bound n-1 on the switch number is asymptotically tight. The rank grading of a clock-and-switch world provides a potential function for a first-moment argument, and the proved cardinality bound is far too weak to explain the observed values.

For fixed p in (0,1), the random transitively closed bounded poset on n points has sw = (1 + o(1)) n with probability tending to 1.

Sample random bounded posets for n up to 8 and compute sw exhaustively; fit against n and against max(height, log2 n).

The worst-case bound card P - 1 proved here is also the typical case, so no better general construction exists.

There is a sublinear generic construction, presumably exploiting the cube's product structure more aggressively than a single climb.
proof_strategy: First moment over assignments of the cube: count monotone open maps and show the expected number is o(1) when m is sublinear.
title: Linear Switch Number for Random Bounded Posets

description:
The all-pairs stability bound ∑_{θ≠θ'} (1 − d_TV) ≤ #Θ(#Θ−1)·(#Θ − Cₛ) is proved in this cycle; the conjecture is that the sharp constant is 2(#Θ−1). The approach is a rearrangement argument on the sorted likelihood vector at each message. It would make rigidity of the maximal price quantitatively optimal.

For a finite source class, ∑_{θ≠θ'} (1 − d_TV(p_θ, p_θ')) ≤ 2(#Θ−1)·(#Θ − Cₛ), improving the proved constant #Θ(#Θ−1) by a factor #Θ.

Formalise in Lean by sorting the likelihood vector at each message and comparing ∑_{i<j} a_j with (k−1)·∑_{j≥2} a_j; test numerically on random rational classes first.

Rigidity of the upper endpoint becomes quantitative and dimension-free: the price of universality is controlled by the class's average statistical separation.

The overlap functional is genuinely one-dimensional and only extremal pairs matter, which would itself sharpen the picture.
proof_strategy: Fix a message, order the likelihoods, and charge each pair's minimum against the non-maximal part of the sum; sum over messages using the conservation law Cₛ + Ω = #Θ.
title: Sharp Constant in All-Pairs Affinity Stability

description:
The footprint weight is the exact first cumulant of the number of factor-base divisors of a sieve value. Conjecture: with the exact variance of D1, a concentration inequality forces the true relation yield to be monotone in the dial up to an explicit error term, converting the empirical regression into a proved inequality.

There is an explicit ε(B, window) such that if qrWeight N₁ B − qrWeight N₂ B > ε then the expected number of factor-base hits per location for N₁ exceeds that for N₂.

Prove the mean identity per window (already available) and add a Chebyshev bound from the variance law; check numerically on random N with B = 100.

The dial acquires a proof-backed operational meaning for sieve calibration, not just a regression score.

The mapping from footprint to smoothness probability is non-monotone, indicating higher cumulants dominate at practical window sizes.
proof_strategy: Mean-footprint identity plus a second-moment bound from the exact pattern law, then Chebyshev on the count of hits in a window.
title: Monotone Yield Ordering from the Footprint Cumulant

description:
Deciding whether a poset is an image of a given cube is a constraint satisfaction problem over the cube's cells. We conjecture NP-completeness in general and tractability for bounded width, matching the empirical running-time profile of the search used in this cycle.

Deciding sw(P) <= m is NP-complete, but solvable in polynomial time when the width of P is bounded.

Reduce 3-colourability or set cover to the cube-assignment problem; give a dynamic program along a chain decomposition for bounded width.

No closed-form formula for sw can be expected in general, which reframes Direction 1 as a bounded-width statement.

A polynomial algorithm for sw exists and would likely produce the exact formula of Direction 1 constructively.
proof_strategy: Encode variables as the values of the morphism on the atoms of the cube; openness constraints simulate covering conditions.
title: Complexity Dichotomy for Bounded-Morphism Search

description:
The proved identity N(zeta v) = -(a-b)^2 turns the leg defect of a Pythagorean triple into a norm condition in Z[sqrt 2]. Classifying triples with fixed defect k therefore becomes the classification of elements of norm -k^2 modulo units, a finite class-group computation for each k.

For each k >= 1 the set of primitive Pythagorean triples with |a - b| = k is a finite union of unit orbits in Z[sqrt 2], the number of orbits being determined by the factorization of k in Z[sqrt 2]; for k = 1 there is exactly one orbit, the B-spine.

Formalize the orbit correspondence and verify the predicted orbit counts for k = 1, 7, 17, 23 against an exhaustive tree search to depth 8.

Gives a complete arithmetic classification of near-isoceles Pythagorean triples in terms of ideal classes of Z[sqrt 2].

Some defects admit triples outside any unit orbit, showing that the silver coordinate loses information away from the light cone.
proof_strategy: Combine the norm identity with unique factorization in Z[sqrt 2] and the already proved unit criterion, then descend along the tree using the Adm invariant.
title: Almost-Isoceles Defect and Norm Forms of Z[sqrt 2]

description:
Ehrhart-style reciprocity at the single pole q = 1 is now a theorem: polyZeta P at q inverse is minus the generating function of the negative grades. The conjecture is that the law is equivariant for the root-of-unity twist, so that for a quasi-polynomial grade count the inversion q to q inverse permutes the poles by negating the Fourier index while reflecting each section polynomial.

For a grade count that is eventually quasi-polynomial mod m with sections P_j, the continued partition function satisfies Z(q inverse) = -q times the continued partition function of the grade count with sections given by the reflected polynomials P_j(-X-1) read in reversed Fourier order; in particular the principal part at the pole zeta^k is carried to the principal part at zeta^{-k}.

Combine polyZeta_inv_eq_comp with circleIntegral_twistPolyZeta: check that the twist q to w q commutes with inversion up to w to w inverse, then sum over the Fourier sections as in circleIntegral_multiPolyZeta.

The singularity divisor of a quasi-polynomial graded G-set carries an explicit involution, giving a duality between grade counts and their reflections that refines the residue calculus.

Inversion mixes the principal parts at different roots of unity, which would show that reciprocity is a phenomenon of the single pole at q = 1 and not of the divisor as a whole.
proof_strategy: Apply the proved reciprocity to each twisted section, use that the twist by w composed with inversion equals inversion composed with the twist by w inverse, and reassemble by discrete Fourier inversion.
title: Twisted Reciprocity at the Roots of Unity

description:
The conjectured greedy factor (1 - e^{-kappa})/kappa for the Shtarkov price functional is not implied by any single-step gap recursion. It should instead follow from a linear program in the vector of greedy gains, whose constraints are gain monotonicity, the submodular covering inequality at each step, and the curvature inequality for each already-chosen model. Establishing it would complete the curvature-dependent theory of universal decompressor library design.

For a pool Omega of curvature kappa and any target library B with |B| = n, every pool-restricted greedy run satisfies shtarkov P (A n) >= ((1 - exp (-kappa))/kappa) * shtarkov P B.

Formalise the n inequalities already available (greedyGain_antitone, gap_le_curvature_gain, curvature_marginal_ge) as a finite system and exhibit explicit nonnegative multipliers, verified in Lean by nlinarith or an induction on a weighted potential.

Universal compression inherits the sharp Conforti-Cornuejols guarantee, interpolating exactly between exact optimality at kappa = 0 and 1 - 1/e at kappa = 1.

The curvature product proved here is the true worst-case decay for the Shtarkov functional and the classical factor fails outside the abstract submodular setting; a separating instance would be a new extremal example.
proof_strategy: Guess the dual multipliers numerically on small n, then prove the resulting weighted-sum inequality by induction on the greedy step using the already-formalised generators.
title: LP-Certified Conforti–Cornuéjols Factor for Shtarkov Libraries

description:
The formalised rigidity gap bounds the whole singular tail of a 0/1 indicator matrix away from zero by (3-sqrt5)/2. Exhaustive computation suggests the much stronger statement that already the second singular value alone obeys this floor. Proving it would give a clean spectral dichotomy for combinatorial rectangles.

For every 0/1 matrix M of rank at least two, sigma_2(M)^2 >= (3 - sqrt 5)/2, with equality exactly when the non-trivial part of M is a copy of the 2x2 matrix [[1,0],[1,1]].

Formalise as a statement about Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) Bool; test exhaustively for m,n <= 5 by exact characteristic-polynomial computation over a splitting field, then attempt a local 2x2 certificate proof mirroring golden_core.

Gives a spectral certificate for rank-one-ness of 0/1 matrices with an absolute constant, strengthening productCoin_amplitude_sq_le_golden from a Frobenius-tail bound to a single-eigenvalue bound.

There are 0/1 matrices of rank >= 2 with arbitrarily small second singular value, meaning the golden constant is genuinely a tail phenomenon and cannot be localised in one eigendirection.
proof_strategy: Use the interlacing inequality for the 2x2 minor of determinant 1 supplied by a non-box witness: sigma_2(M) >= sigma_2 of the minor whenever the minor is chosen to be a principal submatrix in the right basis. The obstruction is that interlacing goes the wrong way for arbitrary submatrices, so one must instead build a two-dimensional test subspace from the L-shape witness.
title: Second-Eigenvalue Floor for Zero-One Matrices

description:
The top shape count of even closed walks of length 2k on k+1 vertices should equal catalan k times (k+1)!. This identifies the leading coefficient of the moment polynomial as the Catalan number and is the combinatorial core of Wigner's semicircle law. It is verified formally for k = 1, 2, 3.

For all k ≥ 1, EvenWalks.surjEvenWalkCount (k+1) (2*k) = catalan k * (k+1)!.

Formalize the bijection between even closed 2k-walks covering a spanning tree twice and pairs (labelling, Dyck path); check the identity by decide for k = 4 (needs an optimized decidable instance) and prove it by induction using the tree-contour recursion.

The leading coefficient of every even moment polynomial is catalan k, yielding all-order semicircle convergence in expectation.

Some non-tree shape survives at top degree, contradicting the vertex bound; the moment polynomial degree analysis would have to be revisited.
proof_strategy: Use two_mul_card_walkVertices_le to force exactly k edges of multiplicity two forming a spanning tree, then count contour traversals of doubled plane trees via the standard Dyck-path bijection, and multiply by (k+1)! for the labelling.
title: Catalan Law for Top Walk Shapes

description:
Rational star-powers of the corrected Monster product exist and are unique. Fixing a Laurent degree and varying the exponent r should produce a polynomial in r, whose degree and roots encode arithmetic of the 194 trace series.

For each k the function r -> (coefficient at degree k - 1 of the star-r-th power of a normalized f) is a polynomial in r of degree k with leading coefficient (f.coeff 0)^k / k!.

Prove the first three cases from the explicit expansions already formalized, then induct using the logarithm/exponential correspondence on 1-units.

Explicit closed forms for all rational star-powers, hence a complete coefficient calculus for the corrected moonshine group.

Non-polynomial dependence would reveal that ratPow is not compatible with coefficientwise limits.
proof_strategy: Show coefficient k of binomialSeries r is a degree-k polynomial in r (Ring.choose), then transport through substitution.
title: Rational Power Spectrum of the Monster Product

description:
The equality between the modal theory of clock-and-switch worlds and that of finite rooted directed posets is proved. We conjecture that this theory is exactly S4.2, giving a completeness theorem whose frames are products of a chain with a Boolean cube.

A modal formula is derivable in S4.2 iff it is valid on every CWorld (Fin n) (Fin m).

Formalise the finite model property for S4.2 (filtration of the canonical model) and compose it with valid_boundedPoset_iff_valid_cworld.

S4.2 gets a purely combinatorial frame class inside the catalog's Kripke semantics.

Cube frames validate a proper extension of S4.2, and identifying the extra axiom would characterise distributive-lattice-like frames modally.
proof_strategy: Canonical model plus filtration for S4.2, then transfer along the p-morphism lemma sat_bddMorphism.
title: Cube Frames and S4.2 Completeness

description:
The upper bound Psi(x,B) <= (log2 x + 1)^pi(B) proved here comes from an injection into exponent vectors. The same correspondence gives a lower bound by counting lattice points under the hyperplane sum e_i log p_i <= log x, yielding an unconditional two-sided estimate with no Dickman input at all.

Psi(x,B) equals, up to a factor bounded by a function of pi(B) alone, the number of nonnegative integer vectors (e_p)_{p <= B} with sum e_p log p <= log x, i.e. the volume of a simplex of dimension pi(B) with side log x / log p.

Formalise the bijection between B-smooth integers in [1,x] and lattice points of the simplex, then compare with exact Psi values (12, 34, 141, 733 computed here).

An unconditional, Dickman-free proof that the smooth pool is polylogarithmic at fixed B and grows subexponentially in the trade-off regime.

The lattice-point count must overcount by more than a pi(B)-dependent factor, exposing a genuinely arithmetic (non-combinatorial) input to smooth counting.
proof_strategy: The map n -> (v_p(n)) is a bijection onto the lattice points of the simplex; card of that lattice point set is bounded above and below by simplex volumes with Ehrhart-type corrections.
title: Two-Sided Exponent-Vector Sandwich for Smooth Counts

description:
Measure unbalancedness by majorization instead of ℓ¹ distance. For comonotone populations whose pair matrix is monotone in the key order, concentrating draw mass should decrease the dial monotonically, giving an order-theoretic form of the no-dilution claim.

If p ≺ q (q majorizes p) and the population is comonotone with D monotone in the key order, then wcov q x y ≤ wcov p x y, with equality iff p and q agree on the concordant support.

State via Mathlib's majorization/doubly stochastic API: q = p ∘ (doubly stochastic matrix) and prove the induced inequality for the quadratic form.

Uniform draws maximize the dial, which upgrades draw-invariance to an extremal principle.

Regime comparisons genuinely require metric, not order-theoretic, control.
proof_strategy: Birkhoff decomposition of the doubly stochastic map into transpositions plus a two-key exchange lemma for the quadratic form.
title: Majorization Monotonicity of the Yield Dial

description:
The L1 rounding energy of the mesh (1/q)Z equals the Mantel-Turan number floor(q^2/4). We conjecture the p-th moment gives a family of extremal numbers with an exact division-free identity for each p.

For every p >= 1 there are explicit polynomials P_p, R_p with 2^p (p+1) * sum_{j<q} min(j, q-j)^p = P_p(q) - R_p(q % 2).

Verify by decide for p <= 4 and q <= 40, then prove by the same lower/upper half splitting plus Faulhaber sums.

Every Lp quantization energy is an exact extremal-combinatorial quantity, linking loss exponents to Turan-type numbers.

Only p = 1 admits a clean closed form, isolating the Mantel bridge as special.
proof_strategy: Split the period at the midpoint, apply Faulhaber's formula on both halves, and match parities.
title: Higher-Moment Turan Numbers of the Mesh

description:
The continuous optimum of the mixed-precision cost is attained at a log-amplitude water-filling allocation. Real allocations must be integers, and the rounding of the allocation is itself a round-to-nearest problem, so the theory applies to itself.

Rounding the water-filling allocation to integers with total budget preserved costs at most a factor 2^{1/2} over the continuous optimum, and this factor is attained.

Formalize the integer-constrained minimum in Lean for small n and prove the factor bound; check attainment on explicit amplitude profiles.

A provably near-optimal integer mixed-precision schedule can be computed in one pass from weight statistics.

Integer allocation needs combinatorial search, and greedy rounding can be far from optimal.
proof_strategy: Bound each term by the rounding error of b_i, then apply the AM-GM optimum to the rounded allocation and compare.
title: Integrality Gap of Water-Filling Bit Allocation

description:
Keep the events (primitive triples) but replace the tree order by an arithmetic one, using the hypotenuse as a global time function and a divisibility or congruence condition as the causal relation. The aim is a locally finite poset on the same set whose interval cardinalities grow polynomially of degree at least two.

There is a relation R on primitive Pythagorean triples, refining c_u < c_v, which is a locally finite partial order whose intervals of cosmic-time extent T have cardinality asymptotically proportional to T^d for some d >= 2.

Define candidate relations (e.g. u R v iff c_u divides c_v, or iff v is reachable by a word whose Lorentz matrix is congruent to the identity mod N), count intervals computationally to depth 6, then formalise the winning candidate's poset axioms and interval bounds.

A Pythagorean causal set with a genuine Myrheim-Meyer dimension, separating 'the event set is fine' from 'the tree order is wrong'.

Evidence that the arithmetic of primitive triples supports only tree-like (dimension one) causal orders, which would be a structural theorem about the Berggren monoid.
proof_strategy: Local finiteness from the cosmic-time bound plus the finiteness of triples with bounded hypotenuse; interval growth by counting triples with hypotenuse in a window, which is governed by the classical count of representations as a sum of two squares.
title: Arithmetic Reordering of the Berggren Event Set

description:
Determine, for a finite abelian group G, how a rational prime p factors into irreducibles in the group ring Z[G], in terms of the character decomposition and a 2-adic defect. The Z/2 case is fully proved here: odd primes split as ((p+1)/2) ± ((p-1)/2)t while 2 remains irreducible because no element has norm ±2. The general case would give a factorisation theory for all 'twist rings'.

For finite abelian G and a rational prime p, the irreducible factorisation of p in Z[G] is determined by the splitting of p in each cyclotomic factor of Q[G] together with the congruence gluing conditions; in particular p is irreducible in Z[G] iff p divides |G| or p is inert in every character factor.

Formalise the norm map Z[G] -> Z given by the product of characters, prove multiplicativity, and reprove Moebius.ZM.irreducible_two and Moebius.ZM.odd_prime_splits as the G = Z/2 instance.

A uniform factorisation theory for group rings of orientation groups, with the Moebius case as the smallest example.

The Z/2 behaviour is an accident of the hyperbolic form a^2 - b^2 and orientation arithmetic does not generalise beyond order two.
proof_strategy: Multiplicative norm N(z) = prod_chi chi(z); reduce irreducibility to |N| prime plus a local obstruction at primes dividing |G|; handle the 2-adic defect by the parity congruence that cuts Z[G] out of the product of character rings.
title: Twisted Group-Ring Factorisation Spectrum

description:
Leakage of stacked reconciliation rounds is subadditive. We conjecture the exact deficiency is the dimension of the intersection of the two row spaces, making the inequality tight in general position. This would give an exact multi-round leakage formula rather than a bound.

For schemes S1, S2 on the same key length, rank(S1.stack S2) = rank S1 + rank S2 - dim(rowspace H1 ∩ rowspace H2).

Prove the row-space version of Scheme.ker_stack and apply Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq to row spaces; check numerically on random binary matrices.

Multi-round protocol leakage becomes exactly computable from pairwise round overlaps.

Some subtler interaction between rounds exists, indicating leakage is not a rank invariant.
proof_strategy: Identify range of the stacked map with the sum of ranges, dualise Scheme.ker_stack, and apply the modular law.
title: Rank-Intersection Deficiency of Composed Rounds

description:
For metric observations the behavioural distance is a supremum over all words. We conjecture the supremum is attained at depth at most |S|+|T|-2, so the distance is computable by the same finite suite that decides equivalence, bridging quantitative bisimulation with the combinatorial refinement bound.

For machines with observations in a metric space, sup over all words of the observation distance equals the maximum over words of length at most |S| + |T| - 2.

Replace the relation chain by the chain of epsilon-level sets and rerun the stabilisation argument uniformly in epsilon.

Quantitative behavioural distances become finitely computable with the same complexity as qualitative equivalence.

There is a genuinely metric phenomenon (slow convergence) with no finite-depth witness, separating quantitative from qualitative testing.
proof_strategy: For each epsilon, the sets {(s,t) : d_k(s,t) >= epsilon} form a decreasing chain of subsets of a finite set; stabilisation within |S|+|T|-2 steps follows from the same block count, then take a supremum over the finitely many attained values.
title: Bounded-Depth Realisation of Bisimulation Distance

description:
Functional rigidity proved here says a min-plus linear form with all monomials essential is determined by the function it defines. The natural generalization replaces linear monomials by arbitrary affine ones, and characterizes essentiality cell-theoretically.

For tropical polynomials p, q with affine monomials, p = q as functions iff their essential monomials (those labelling a top-dimensional cell) coincide; and every monomial of p labelling a top cell is essential.

Generalize tropAgg to monomials x -> <a i, x> + delta i, redo tropAgg_spike with directional spikes, and prove support and coefficient recovery.

A verified tropical Nullstellensatz for the min-plus semiring in the affine case, usable as infrastructure for tropical geometry in Lean.

Redundant monomials can be invisible yet label cells, meaning essentiality is not cell-detectable and the linear case is special.
proof_strategy: Replace the spike profile update x j c by a ray in the direction dual to a i, and run the same domination argument as in support_eq_of_tropAgg_eq.
title: Essential-Monomial Nullstellensatz for Tropical Polynomials

description:
The certified value r(a/b) equals (1/b) log of an explicit rational, i.e. a linear form in logarithms of integers. Baker-Wuestholz lower bounds for such forms, combined with the proved derivative bracket, should give an explicit c and mu with |p* - a/b| > c b^{-mu} for all rationals.

p* is transcendental and admits an effective irrationality measure mu < 10 with explicit constant.

Bound |2b log b - b log 2 - 2a log a - 2c log c| from below by a Baker-type estimate and divide by the certified derivative bracket [2.09045, 2.09047].

The first effective Diophantine statement about a cryptographic threshold constant.

The linear form degenerates for special (a,b), revealing unexpected algebraic relations among log 2, log a, log c.
proof_strategy: Formalize a usable special case of Baker's theorem for three logarithms, then apply newton_enclosure_step in reverse (distance from rate).
title: Effective Irrationality Measure for the BB84 Threshold

description:
Strong lumpability yields a bounded morphism and hence an inclusion of modal theories. The conjecture is that the converse holds for finite chains, making the modal theory a complete invariant up to lumping and giving a logical decision procedure for state aggregation.

For finite chains P and Q with nonnegative entries, Thm(markovSystem P) is contained in Thm(markovSystem Q) if and only if the support frames are connected by a zig-zag of surjective bounded morphisms.

Prove Hennessy-Milner for image-finite KFrames in Lean, construct the bisimulation quotient of suppFrame P, and verify the equivalence by enumeration on all chains with at most four states.

Modal theory becomes a complete finite invariant for state aggregation, decidable by comparing finitely many formulas.

There exist modally equivalent finite chains with no lumping relation, pinpointing the expressive gap of the basic modal language on supports.
proof_strategy: Forward direction is markovSystem_thm_of_lumpable; backward direction builds a characteristic formula per bisimulation class and reads the zig-zag off theory inclusion.
title: Lumpability Galois Correspondence for Finite Chains

description:
Ask when recoverability from structural truth coincides with definability in a finitary invariant language on an infinite model. The conjecture is that the coincidence holds exactly for omega-categorical structures, whose orbit partitions are finite in each arity, and that the parity example proved in this cycle is the minimal obstruction. This would locate the definability boundary precisely inside classical model theory.

For a countable structure M with automorphism group G, every orbit-constant interpretation is definable by a parameter-free first-order formula iff the orbit partition of each finite power of M is finite (Ryll-Nardzewski), and otherwise an explicit orbit-constant undefinable interpretation exists.

Formalise a finitary invariant language whose definable sets are finite unions of orbits with a fixed bound, prove the equivalence with finiteness of the orbit partition, and reuse parity_not_definable as the failure witness.

The boundary between recoverable and definable meaning is exactly the omega-categoricity line.

There is a structure with infinitely many orbits on which every orbit-constant interpretation is still finitarily definable, revealing a coarser criterion than orbit finiteness.
proof_strategy: Show a finitary language defines only finite unions of orbits and their complements; conversely, with finitely many orbits every invariant set is such a union by the Boolean-generation theorem of this cycle.
title: Finitary Definability Boundary for Omega-Categorical Models

description:
An excess is 'intrinsic to the family' if no feature that respects the family's symmetries can separate it. Formalising intrinsic-ness as invariance under the symmetry group turns the vague status into a decidable question about class functions.

If the split-ceiling excess is invariant under the full relabelling group of the root-position family, then every encoding built from group-equivariant features has population gain exactly 0; the excess is then intrinsic in a precise sense.

Identify the acting group, verify that candidate encodings are equivariant, and apply the invariance theorem Rsq_reindex to the induced action.
