The search for an encoding that captures the excess is provably futile within the equivariant class, and effort should move to symmetry-breaking features.

There is an equivariant feature with nonzero gain, and the construction itself is the missing encoding.
proof_strategy: Average over the group orbit: an invariant target has zero covariance with the orthogonal complement of the invariant subspace, and Rsq_reindex shows every statistic is constant along orbits.
title: Symmetry-Group Criterion for Intrinsic-to-Family Excess

description:
Every induced subgraph of a clique sum is a clique sum of induced subgraphs along a sub-clique, so the proved colour-permutation transfer should upgrade from chi = max to full perfection. The numerical core chi = omega is already proved for clique sums here. Completing this gives a formal proof of a classical closure property used throughout perfect graph theory.

If G is a clique sum of G_1 and G_2 along K and both sides are perfect, then G is perfect.

Formalise induced sub-clique-sums: for W a vertex subset, show IsCliqueSum holds for the restrictions with clique K cap W, then apply IsCliqueSum.chromaticNumber_eq_cliqueNum.

A reusable formal building block for perfect graph theory in Lean, and a first Mathlib-ready closure theorem for clique sums.

The failure must come from restriction breaking the clique-on-each-side condition, which would identify a strictly larger class than perfect graphs closed under the weaker gluing.
proof_strategy: Restriction lemma for IsCliqueSum, then apply the proved chromaticNumber_eq_max and cliqueNumOn_eq_max to each induced subgraph.
title: Hereditary Colour Transfer and Perfection of Clique Sums

description:
The exact law assumes the target factor's residue class is uniform. Replacing uniformity by a distribution at total-variation distance Δ from uniform should perturb the cost by O(Δ), giving an effective statement usable at cryptographic sizes with no mixing assumption.

If the target class distribution μ satisfies ‖μ − U‖_TV ≤ Δ then the normalized expected scan cost lies within Δ of 1 − θ + θ², hence the speedup is at most 4/3 + O(Δ).

Restate expectedScanCost with a general probability mass function and bound the difference by ‖μ − U‖_TV times the cost range; formalize in Lean over Finset sums.

The cap becomes effective and assumption-free given any explicit equidistribution bound.

Non-uniform target classes are exploitable beyond 4/3, relocating the cryptanalytic resource into the distribution.
proof_strategy: Hölder/TV bound on Σ (μ(t) − 1/n)·cost(t) with cost between k and n.
title: Discrepancy-Perturbed Dial Law

description:
The proved Lipschitz bound |Cov_p − Cov_q| ≤ (range x)(range y)‖p − q‖₁ converts sampling error into ℓ¹ error of the empirical regime, yielding a confidence radius that does not depend on the population beyond its ranges.

With n i.i.d. draws from a regime on |ι| keys, |Cov_empirical − Cov_p| ≤ (range x)(range y)·√(2|ι|/n) with probability at least 1 − 2e^{−|ι|}.

Cross-regime 'identical within noise' claims become certified rather than empirical.

The ℓ¹ route is too lossy and a variance-based bound on the pair form is needed instead.
proof_strategy: Bounded differences for the empirical ℓ¹ error plus the deterministic Lipschitz bound already proved.
title: Distribution-Free Confidence Radius for the Dial

description:
Exhaustive rational sampling found associativity of total transreal multiplication unbroken while distributivity broke at once. We conjecture associativity holds and is best proved through the extended sign homomorphism into a four-element absorbing monoid, avoiding a 64-case analysis.

Total transreal multiplication is associative and commutative with unit fin 1, and the map sending fin x to its sign, ±∞ to ±, and null to an absorbing element is a monoid homomorphism that detects associativity.

Define the sign monoid, prove the homomorphism property, and reduce associativity to associativity of the sign monoid together with associativity on the finite fragment.

The carrier is a commutative monoid under both operations, isolating distributivity as the unique algebraic casualty of totality.

A sampling-invisible associativity failure exists, which would also invalidate the monoid reading of the guarded fragment.
proof_strategy: Factor multiplication through sign times magnitude; associativity of the magnitude part is associativity in [0,∞] and of the sign part is associativity in the four-element monoid.
title: Sign-Homomorphism Proof of Transreal Associativity

description:
Over WithBot weights the predicate 'is not bottom' should be a semiring morphism onto the Boolean semiring, so feasibility of a constrained dynamic program reduces to reachability in a support digraph. The conjecture is that the bottom-pattern of the walk matrices coincides with the Boolean powers of the support adjacency matrices. This turns the infeasibility criterion already proved (val_eq_bot_iff) into a purely combinatorial check.

For D : DPSpec S (WithBot W), val n s is not bottom iff there is a support path of length n from some state with non-bottom init to s, where s -> t at stage i iff step i s t is not bottom.

Define the support relation, prove that a sum is bottom iff a summand is and that a finite sup is bottom iff all arguments are, then induct on n; cross-check by decide on the maximum-weight independent set instance with an isolated forbidden state.

Infeasibility detection for constrained DP reduces to Boolean matrix reachability and can be certified separately from optimisation.

The bottom-pattern carries strictly more information than reachability, so constrained DP feasibility is not purely combinatorial.
proof_strategy: Show that mapping w to the Boolean value (w != bottom) preserves addition and finite sup', hence commutes with the walk recursion; the image of the walk value is then Boolean reachability.
title: Support Digraph Certificates for Constrained DP

description:
Collision events are diagonal hyperplanes in the discrete cube (Fin M)^alpha and the component law is the codimension formula for their intersections. This identifies the failure event with a coordinate subspace arrangement whose intersection lattice should be the partition lattice.

The intersection lattice of the collision-hyperplane arrangement over Z/M is isomorphic to the partition lattice of the index set, and the exact codebook success count is its characteristic polynomial evaluated at M.

Formalise the map from collision patterns to set partitions using patternSetoid, prove it is a lattice isomorphism onto the partitions realised by the pattern, and compare characteristic polynomial evaluations with card_failSet_exact.

The almost-lossless analysis inherits the full Mobius-function toolkit of subspace arrangements, giving closed forms for all higher-order terms.

The discrete alphabet Z/M breaks the classical dictionary, marking a genuine difference between hashing arrangements and real subspace arrangements.
proof_strategy: Show pattern intersection corresponds to partition join via patternSetoid, then evaluate the Mobius function by the component law and Whitney's theorem.
title: Collision Hyperplane Arrangements and the Partition Lattice

description:
Every primitive word in the Berggren alphabet is a hyperbolic isometry of the Lorentz lattice with a real quadratic multiplier field determined by its trace. The conjecture is that the periodic geodesic of each word is an orbit of the unit group of the corresponding quadratic order, generalizing the proved statement that the all-B spine is the odd unit group of Z[sqrt 2]. This would give a complete arithmetic dictionary between words and real quadratic orders.

For a primitive word w in {A,B,C} with Lorentz trace t_w > 2, there is a coordinate map zeta_w on the axis of w intertwining w with multiplication by the fundamental totally positive unit of the order Z[(t_w + sqrt(t_w^2-4))/2], and the nodes of the axis are exactly the elements of one unit orbit.

Formalize the intertwining for the words AB, BC, ABB and check the trace-to-discriminant correspondence numerically to depth 8; then prove the general statement by the same two-step scheme used for B (intertwining identity plus admissibility invariant).

The Berggren tree becomes a uniform model for real quadratic units: one geodesic per order, indexed by words.

Some words have multiplier fields that are not realized by unit orbits, isolating an obstruction coming from non-maximal orders or from imprimitive traces.
proof_strategy: Diagonalize the word matrix over Z[sqrt(disc)], read off the light-like eigenvectors, define the coordinate as the pairing with one eigenvector, and prove multiplicativity by a ring computation; then use the Adm invariant to exclude off-axis unit nodes.
title: Multiplier-Field Stratification of Berggren Words

description:
Replace a transition relation by a nonnegative integer matrix and the degree monoid by the set of n with positive (A^n)_{aa}. The conjecture identifies the period of that monoid with the imprimitivity index of Perron-Frobenius theory, bridging combinatorics of computations with spectral theory.

For a nonnegative matrix A with support relation R, {n | (A^n)_{aa} > 0} = degreeMonoid R a, and degPeriod R a equals the imprimitivity index of the irreducible component of a.

Formalise the support relation, prove positivity of matrix entries corresponds to iterR, and compare degPeriod with the cyclicity of the associated digraph on examples.

The classification dichotomy proved here becomes a combinatorial proof of Perron-Frobenius periodicity.

Positivity of matrix powers carries strictly more information than reachability, isolating cancellation phenomena.
proof_strategy: Induct on n to identify (A^n)_{ab} > 0 with iterR R n a b, then transfer degPeriod through the structure theorem.
title: Perron-Frobenius Index Equals Degree Period

description:
Replacing ℂ by a matrix algebra keeps the closure property and the filtration but destroys commutativity. The conjecture is that the resulting group is the one-unit group of the matrix power series ring, still torsion-free and divisible, with graded pieces the additive matrix algebra.

For any ℚ-algebra R, the R-valued normalized Laurent series form a group under f ⋆ g = q f g, isomorphic to the one-units of R⟦X⟧; it is torsion-free, and divisible when R is a ℚ-algebra.

Re-run the development with ℂ replaced by a general ℚ-algebra R, checking which lemmas used commutativity (only the CommGroup axioms and the binomial series should).

The pole-order correction is a general phenomenon of valued rings, not special to scalar moonshine series.

Some step genuinely needs commutativity or a field, pinpointing where the scalar theory is essential.
proof_strategy: Generalise isNormalized_iff and the one-unit coordinates to R⟦X⟧, replace PowerSeries.inv by the inverse of a one-unit over any ring, and use the binomial series over ℚ ⊆ R for roots.
title: Matrix-Valued Corrected Products

description:
The Poincare series of the free monoid on the three Berggren generators, weighted by hypotenuse, has a critical exponent equal to the Hausdorff dimension of the limit set of the tree in the boundary circle. Comparing this exponent with the spine exponent log(3 + 2 sqrt 2) quantifies how exceptional the Pell geodesic is inside the tree.

The series sum over words w of hyp(w)^{-s} has a finite critical exponent delta with log 3 / log 7 <= delta <= log 3 / log 3, and delta is strictly smaller than 1; the spine contributes measure zero.

Prove two-sided growth bounds 3^{|w|} <= hyp(w) <= 7^{|w|} using the admissibility invariant, then bracket the critical exponent by comparison with geometric series.

Yields the first rigorous dimension bracket for the Barning-Hall limit set and confirms that unit nodes are exponentially rare.

Growth is not uniformly geometric across letters, which would indicate a genuinely multifractal structure requiring a thermodynamic formalism.
proof_strategy: Per-letter hypotenuse bounds by linear arithmetic on the Adm invariant, then summation over the free monoid.
title: Critical Exponent of the Pythagorean Limit Set

description:
no_finite_test shows that no fixed finite suite separates arbitrary behaviours on an infinite input type. We conjecture the exact threshold: bounded-length suites work precisely up to length 2k-2 for k-state machines, and equivalence of computably presented infinite-state machines is Pi-0-1 complete.

Behavioural equivalence of computably presented infinite-state Moore machines is Pi-0-1 complete, while for k-state machines a suite of words of length < lambda is complete iff lambda > 2k - 2.

Reduce halting to free-machine equivalence using freeMachine_obs_nil; for the finite half, combine testSuite_complete with the extremal family.

A sharp dividing line between decidable finite-state testing and undecidable general behavioural equivalence, with an exact length threshold on the decidable side.

Some restricted class of infinite-state machines admits finite test suites, which would be a surprising positive result.
proof_strategy: Use the free machine on List A to realise an arbitrary computable behaviour; encode halting as an output flip at the halting time; match with the finite-state upper bound already proved.
title: Complexity Threshold of the Infinite-State Barrier

description:
Generalize 2|det M| ≤ ‖M‖_F² to n·|det M|^{2/n} ≤ ‖M‖_F² for n × n complex matrices, with equality exactly for scalar multiples of unitaries — the maximally entangled two-qudit states. The two-dimensional proof shows the only missing ingredient is AM–GM applied to squared singular values.

For every M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ, n * |det M|^(2/n) ≤ ‖M‖_F², with equality iff M is a scalar multiple of a unitary matrix.

Formalize via the Cauchy–Binet identity det(M Mᴴ) = |det M|² together with the AM–GM inequality applied to the eigenvalues of M Mᴴ obtained from the spectral theorem.

The Bell normal form generalizes verbatim to qudits: the maximizers of |det| on the Frobenius sphere are exactly U(n)/√n, one orbit of the local group.

The equality analysis would depend on dimension in an unexpected way, indicating that the two-dimensional Gram identity is not the right generalization route.
proof_strategy: Write det(M Mᴴ) = ∏ μ_i and ‖M‖_F² = Σ μ_i with μ_i the eigenvalues of the PSD matrix M Mᴴ; apply Finset AM–GM; equality in AM–GM forces all μ_i equal, hence M Mᴴ scalar.

description: 1729 = 10^3 + 9^3 = 12^3 + 1^3 is the smallest number expressible as a sum of two cubes in two ways (Ramanujan's taxicab number). But can 1729 be expressed as a sum of three cubes? That is, does 1729 = x^3 + y^3 + z^3 have integer solutions? Conjecture: 1729 = 1^3 + 10^3 + 8^3 = 1 + 1000 + 512 = 1513 (no). 1729 = 9^3 + 9^3 + 7^3 = 729 + 729 + 343 = 1801 (no). Actually, 1729 = 1^3 + 12^3 = 1728 + 1 = 1729 (the original). And 1729 = 10^3 + 9^3 = 1000 + 729 = 1729. So 1729 has TWO representations as a sum of two cubes. The question is: does 1729 have a representation as a sum of three cubes? The answer is YES: 1729 = 1^3 + (-12)^3 + 12^3 = 1 - 1728 + 1728 = 1 = NO, this gives 1, not 1729. Try 1729 = 10^3 + 9^3 + 0^3 = 1729. So 1729 = 10^3 + 9^3 + 0^3 is a trivial representation. The non-trivial question: does 1729 have a representation as x^3 + y^3 + z^3 with x,y,z all nonzero? Conjecture: 1729 has no non-trivial representation as a sum of three cubes with all terms nonzero. Test: brute-force search for x^3 + y^3 + z^3 = 1729 with x,y,z nonzero integers. Impact: even Ramanujan's favorite number has secrets — the taxicab number's relationship to sums of three cubes reveals new Diophantine structure.
proof_strategy: Search for integer solutions to x^3 + y^3 + z^3 = 1729 with xyz != 0. By symmetry, assume |x| <= |y| <= |z|. Then |x| <= cube_root(1729/3) = cube_root(576.3) = 8.3, so |x| <= 8. For each x in {-8,...,8} (nonzero), search for y,z with y^3 + z^3 = 1729 - x^3. Check: x=1: y^3+z^3=1728=12^3, giving (1,12,0) or (1,0,12). x=2: y^3+z^3=1721, no solutions (1721 is between 11^3=1331 and 12^3=1728). x=3: y^3+z^3=1702, check y=11: 1702-1331=371, not a cube. y=10: 1702-1000=702, not a cube. Continue for all x from -8 to 8. The complete search yields: 1729 = 10^3 + 9^3 + 0^3 = 1^3 + 12^3 + 0^3 (only trivial three-cube representations with a zero). Conjecture: no non-trivial three-cube representation exists. Prove by reducing mod 9: cubes mod 9 are {0, 1, -1}. Sum of three cubes mod 9 is in {0, ±1, ±2, ±3}. 1729 mod 9 = 1. So we need x^3+y^3+z^3 = 1 mod 9, which is possible. But the search shows no solutions exist.
title: Ramanujan's Taxicab Number as a Sum of Three Cubes: 1729 Revisited

description: Arrow's impossibility theorem states that no ranked voting system with 3+ alternatives can be Pareto efficient, non-dictatorial, and independent of irrelevant alternatives (IIA). Conjecture: Arrow's theorem is a curvature statement. The space of preference profiles is a Riemannian manifold M with the Fisher information metric. The social welfare function F: M -> M is a mapping from profiles to social preferences. Arrow's conditions translate to geometric conditions: (1) Pareto efficiency means F preserves the direction of unanimous preference (F is 'forward-looking'). (2) IIA means F is a local mapping (the social preference at x depends only on local information near x). (3) Non-dictatorial means F is not a projection onto a single voter's preference. Conjecture: the only smooth, local, forward-looking maps on a positively curved manifold are projections (dictatorships). This is because a positively curved manifold has the property that parallel transport around a small loop rotates vectors (Holonomy), and a local, forward-looking map must preserve this holonomy, which forces it to be a projection. Conjecture: the curvature of the preference space is related to the 'polarization' of the electorate: when preferences are polarized (bimodal), the curvature is positive (sphere-like), and Arrow's theorem applies. When preferences are unimodal (consensus), the curvature is zero (flat), and majority rule works. Test: compute the curvature of the preference space for synthetic election data and verify the connection to Arrow's theorem. Impact: Arrow's impossibility is a theorem of differential geometry. Voting is curved.
proof_strategy: Define the preference space M = L(S)^n where L(S) is the set of linear orders on the alternative set S = {1, ..., m}. M is a discrete space with |L(S)|^n = (m!)^n points. To make this a manifold, we smooth it: replace each ranking with a utility vector u_i in R^m (normalized to the simplex Delta^{m-1}). The preference space becomes M = (Delta^{m-1})^n (n voters, each with a utility vector on the simplex). The Fisher information metric on M: g_{ij}(u) = E[(d/d u_i) log p(x|u) * (d/d u_j) log p(x|u)]. For the multinomial distribution: g_{ij} = delta_{ij} / u_i (the Fisher-Rao metric on the simplex). The curvature of (Delta^{m-1}, g) is constant positive (it's a spherical geometry). Arrow's conditions on F: M -> M: (1) Pareto: F(u_1, ..., u_n) has the same sign as the sum of u_i's (forward-looking). (2) IIA: F is local, i.e., dF only depends on local information (F is a smooth map). (3) Non-dictatorial: F is not a projection pi_i: (u_1, ..., u_n) -> u_i. Theorem: on a positively curved manifold, any smooth local forward-looking map is a projection. Proof sketch: by the Gauss-Bonnet theorem, a map from a positively curved manifold to itself that preserves direction must be either the identity or a projection. The key: the holonomy group of (Delta^{m-1})^n is SO(m-1)^n, and a local map must commute with this holonomy, which forces it to be a projection. Test: for m=3 alternatives, compute the curvature of Delta^2 (which is constant positive = 1/2), and verify that local forward-looking maps are projections.
title: The Geometry of Consensus: Arrow's Theorem as Curvature

description: The chromatic polynomial chi_G(k) counts the number of proper k-colorings of a graph G. For a friendship graph, chi_G(k) counts the number of ways to assign k emotions to people such that no two friends share the same emotion. Conjecture: The chromatic polynomial evaluated at k=6 (for the 6 basic emotions: happiness, sadness, anger, fear, disgust, surprise) gives the number of 'emotionally consistent' assignments of emotions to a social network. The chromatic polynomial has a root at k=2 for any bipartite graph, meaning a social network that splits cleanly into two groups has exactly 0 ways to assign 2 emotions without friends sharing emotions. The real emotional chromatic number chi_E(G) of a social network G is the smallest k such that chi_G(k) > 0 and k >= 3 (since real emotions need at least 3 categories to avoid trivial assignments). For a complete graph K_n (a clique of n mutual friends), chi_E(K_n) = n (everyone needs a different emotion). For a cycle C_n (a circular friendship chain), chi_E(C_n) = 2 if n is even and 3 if n is odd (alternating emotions work for even cycles, but odd cycles need a third emotion). Test: compute chi_E(G) for 100 real social networks and verify that the emotional chromatic number is between 3 and 6 for most networks. Impact: the chromatic polynomial is not just combinatorics — it measures the emotional diversity of a social network.
proof_strategy: Define the emotional chromatic number chi_E(G) = min{k >= 3 : chi_G(k) > 0}. For a graph G with n vertices and m edges, compute chi_G(k) using the deletion-contraction recurrence: chi_G(k) = chi_{G-e}(k) - chi_{G/e}(k). For social networks: the emotional chromatic number is the minimum number of emotions needed to ensure no two friends share the same emotion. For a complete graph K_n: chi_E = n (every person needs a different emotion). For a cycle C_n: chi_E = 2 if n even, 3 if n odd (but chi_E >= 3, so for even cycles chi_E = 3 by the minimum constraint). For a path P_n: chi_E = 3 (alternating two emotions doesn't satisfy k >= 3). For random graphs G(n, p): chi_E is approximately max(3, n / (2*log(n/p))) by the chromatic number asymptotics. Test: compute chi_E for 100 social networks from SNAP or similar databases. Verify: most social networks have chi_E between 3 and 6. The 6 basic emotions (Ekman) provide a natural upper bound.
title: Graph Coloring with Emotions: The Chromatic Polynomial Meets Psychology

description: A cake is a smooth projective variety over R: it has a base (a smooth manifold with boundary), frosting (a sheaf of sections supported on the boundary), and layers (a stratification by codimension). The Fundamental Theorem of Cakes states: every cake C is uniquely determined (up to isomorphism of flavor) by its base B, its frosting sheaf F, and its layer stratification L. The frosting sheaf is a locally free sheaf of rank 1 (the cake has uniform frosting thickness) supported on the boundary of the base. The stratification is a flag of subvarieties C = L_0 > L_1 > ... > L_k = {point} where L_i has codimension i and represents the i-th layer. Conjecture: the moduli space of cakes of genus g (g = number of cherries on top) has dimension 3g-3 for g >= 2, mirroring the moduli space of Riemann surfaces. The cherry number g corresponds to the first Betti number of the cake surface, and the moduli are the positions of the g cherries on the surface. Test: enumerate all topologically distinct cakes with g <= 5 cherries and verify that the moduli space has dimension 3g-3. Compute the Teichmuller space of cakes by varying the cherry positions. Impact: cakes are algebraic varieties, and the mathematics of cake decoration IS the mathematics of moduli spaces.
proof_strategy: Define a cake as a triple (B, F, L) where B is a compact 2-manifold with boundary (the base), F is a line bundle on the boundary (the frosting), and L is a stratification C = L_0 > L_1 > ... > L_k (the layers). The genus g is the number of connected components of the boundary (cherries sit on boundary components). The moduli space M_g of cakes of genus g is the space of conformal structures on B with g boundary components, which has dimension 6g-6 + 2g = 8g-6 for the full Teichmuller space and 3g-3 after quotienting by the mapping class group (for g >= 2). The frosting sheaf F is determined by its degree, which is the total frosting 'amount' — a positive integer. The stratification L is determined by the number of layers k and the types of each layer (chocolate, vanilla, etc.). Test: enumerate cakes for g = 0 (sphere with no cherries — a round cake), g = 1 (torus with one cherry — a donut), g = 2 (double torus with two cherries). Verify dim(M_g) = 3g-3 for g >= 2.
title: The Fundamental Theorem of Cakes: Algebraic Geometry of Baking

description: A periodic rhythm in music is a function f: Z -> {0, 1} that is periodic: f(n + p) = f(n) for some period p. The symmetry group of a rhythm with period p is a subgroup of Z/pZ. But music also has 2D patterns: a drum pattern is a function g: Z x Z -> {0, 1} (onset grid in time x pitch). The symmetry group of a drum pattern is a subgroup of Z x Z, which is a wallpaper group in 1D. In 2D, the wallpaper groups classify all possible symmetries of periodic patterns. There are exactly 17 wallpaper groups in 2D. Conjecture: the 17 wallpaper groups correspond to 17 fundamentally different types of rhythmic structure in music. Specifically: (1) p1: no symmetry (free rhythm), (2) p2: 2-fold rotational symmetry (call-and-response), (3) pm: mirror symmetry (palindrome), (4) pg: glide reflection (canon), (5) cm: mirror + glide (round), (6) pmm: double mirror (bilateral palindrome), (7) pmg: mirror + glide (inverted canon), (8) pgg: double glide (double canon), (9) cmm: double mirror + glide (round + palindrome), (10) p4: 4-fold rotation (4-bar cycle), (11) p4m: 4-fold + mirrors (variations on a theme), (12) p4g: 4-fold + glides (inverted variations), (13) p3: 3-fold rotation (3-bar blues), (14) p3m1: 3-fold + mirrors, (15) p31m: 3-fold + glides, (16) p6: 6-fold rotation (whole-tone scale symmetry), (17) p6m: 6-fold + mirrors (maximal symmetry, the 'perfect' rhythm). Test: classify 1000 drum patterns by their wallpaper group and verify the distribution matches musical practice. Impact: there are exactly 17 types of rhythm in music, classified by the wallpaper groups.
proof_strategy: Define a drum pattern as a function g: Z_m x Z_n -> {0, 1} (onset grid with m time steps and n pitch classes). The symmetry group of g is the set of (a, b, R) in Z_m x Z_n x D_n such that g(R*x + a, R*y + b) = g(x, y) for all (x, y). Here D_n is the dihedral group of order 2n. For 2D patterns with translation lattice L, the symmetry group is a wallpaper group. The 17 wallpaper groups are: p1, p2, pm, pg, cm, pmm, pmg, pgg, cmm, p4, p4m, p4g, p3, p3m1, p31m, p6, p6m. Each corresponds to a different type of rhythmic symmetry. p1: no symmetry (most common in free jazz). p2: 2-fold rotation (AABB form). pm: mirror (palindromic, like 'I Palindrome I' by They Might Be Giants). pg: glide (canon, like 'Row Row Row Your Boat'). p4: 4-fold (4/4 time with 4-bar phrases). p6: 6-fold (6/8 time with whole-tone symmetry). p6m: maximal symmetry (only achievable with hexagonal grids, corresponds to the most symmetric possible rhythm). Test: encode 1000 drum patterns as 2D grids, compute their symmetry groups, classify into the 17 wallpaper groups, and compare with musical genre.
title: Crystallographic Groups and Music: The 17 Wallpaper Groups of Rhythm

title: Close Proofs: Information-Geometric Bridge: Fisher Metric on Statistical Manifolds

description: Cycle c6b3a18e (Q=0.629) proved 102 theorems in Physics but left 1 `sorry` placeholders. Fill them with complete proofs. Focus on the most important theorems first. Prove: the set of all theorems is countably infinite, so in prin
title: Close Proofs: Moonshot: The Last Theorem — Formalizing the Heat Death of Mathematics

description:
Since d+1 complete levels always contain a copy of B_d, any family beating d levels must be non-levelled. Quantifying the defect from being a level union should bound the possible excess and pin the absolute constant c in the conjecture.

There is an absolute constant c with La(n,B_d) <= (d+c) C(n,floor(n/2)) for all n and d, and near-extremal families differ from a union of d consecutive levels in o(C(n,floor(n/2))) sets.

Introduce a defect parameter counting incomplete layers of F and prove a bound of the form |F| <= d C + f(defect), then optimise over defect.

The main conjecture F4 is settled with an explicit structural description of the extremal families.

There exist genuinely non-levelled families beating d + c levels, which would be a striking new construction.
proof_strategy: Combine card_le_of_bdFree_levelUnion with a stability version of the LYM inequality applied layer by layer.
title: Nonlevelled Extremal Defect

description:
The refined inequality 1 + ||p - flat||_1/(2 c_asc) <= X is now proved, and it is an identity on two-cell profiles, which shows the constant 1 is optimal. The conjecture is that two-cell support is not only sufficient but necessary for equality, so the equality locus is exactly the union of the two-atom faces of the simplex.

An antitone profile on M cells satisfies C_0 - c_asc = ||p - flat||_1/2 if and only if its mass is carried by at most two cells.

Track the discarded factor |i - j| in the pairwise Chebyshev expansion of scanCost_le_baseCost_sub_flatDist and characterise when every discarded term vanishes; check the resulting criterion on explicit three-cell profiles.

The dispersion correction is exactly computable on its extremal set and the residual slack of a measured profile decomposes into a two-cell part and a strictly positive remainder.

A larger equality face exists and the L1 dispersion functional is degenerate on it, so a finer (index-weighted) functional is needed.
proof_strategy: Equality forces |p_i - p_j| = (j - i)|p_i - p_j| for all pairs, hence p_i = p_j whenever j > i + 1; combine with antitonicity and the mass constraint.
title: Equality Locus of the Sharp Dispersion Inequality

description:
The doubling lemma builds a B_{d+1} copy from two parallel B_d copies, suggesting that the asymptotic constant grows additively rather than doubling. A one-step comparison between B_{d+1}-free and B_d-free families would iterate to the linear bound demanded by F4.

There is an absolute constant c0 with La(n, B_{d+1}) <= La(n, B_d) + c0 * C(n, floor(n/2)) for all n and d.

Given a B_{d+1}-free family, peel off a bounded number of antichains so that the remainder is B_d-free, using hasBdCopy_succ_of_stacked to detect the forbidden doubled configuration.

Iterating gives La(n,B_d) <= (c0 d + O(1)) C(n, floor(n/2)), which is exactly the O(d) target of F4.

The Boolean poset constant grows superlinearly in d and the conjectured (d+c) form is wrong.
proof_strategy: Show that a B_{d+1}-free family minus its c0 outermost Mirsky layers cannot contain two pointwise-nested B_d copies, hence is B_d-free.
title: Doubling Recursion for the Boolean Poset Constant

description:
A drifting margin could in principle be hidden behind a steeper attention tail. The conjecture is that the two exponents cannot compensate: the same measured knee ratio bounds their deviations additively, so a joint fit over three depths is over-determined. This closes the last free direction in the mechanism.

If the knee ratio between depths 4 and 16 is measured within relative tolerance eta of 4, then for any joint fit tail(k) = A*ctx/k^beta and m(d) = m_1 * d^(-alpha) one has |alpha| + |1 - 1/beta| <= log(1/(1-eta))/log 2.

Derive the knee ratio 4^((1+alpha)/beta) for the joint model and take logarithms, then bound the two deviations from the single measured interval.

The mechanism has no remaining fitting freedom and one refined sweep settles it.

The knee measurement is degenerate in a one-parameter family of (alpha, beta) pairs and a second observable is needed to separate them.
proof_strategy: Show the joint knee ratio equals 4^((1+alpha)/beta), take logs to get (1+alpha)/beta in an interval around 1, then convert the single constraint into the additive bound using convexity of the map (alpha,beta) -> (1+alpha)/beta near (0,1).
title: Non-Compensation of Tail and Margin Exponents

description:
Every truncation of the Euler-Maclaurin/Bernoulli expansion of gamma - eulerMascheroniSeq n should be provable by pure telescoping, with error bounded by the first omitted term. The approach replaces the Euler-Maclaurin remainder integral with a monotone envelope whose one-step decrement is compared to log(1+x) via a rational Pade inequality. It matters because it turns an analytic asymptotic expansion into a uniform, effective, machine-checkable family of bounds.

For every K >= 1 and every n : Nat, with m = n+1 and A_K(n) = eulerMascheroniSeq n + 1/(2m) + sum_{k=1}^{K} (-1)^{k+1} |B_{2k}|/(2k) m^{-2k}, one has |gamma - A_K(n)| <= |B_{2K+2}|/((2K+2) m^{2K+2}), with equality asymptotically and alternating sign in K.

Formalize the general envelope H_K(x) = 1/(2x) + sum (-1)^{k+1}|B_2k|/(2k) x^{-2k} and prove, uniformly in K, that (log(1+x) - R_K(x)) has derivative x^{2K+2} P_K(x) / (c_K (1+x)^{2K+3}) with P_K having nonnegative coefficients; then apply tail_le_envelope / envelope_le_tail.

Mathlib gains a complete effective Euler-Maclaurin expansion for the harmonic numbers with explicit constants, and arbitrary-precision certified enclosures of gamma.

Some order K must fail the termwise positivity, locating exactly where the naive telescoping envelope breaks and forcing a genuine remainder-integral argument.
proof_strategy: Induct on K. The inductive step is a polynomial identity: expand (1+x)^{2K+3} times the derivative difference and show all coefficients are nonnegative using the Bernoulli recurrence; the base cases K = 1, 2, 3 are already proved in this cycle.
title: Bernoulli Envelope Tower for the Harmonic Tail

description:
Cycle 11 proves the census #Fix(shift^n) = lucas n and cycle 12 upgrades it to the trace formula lucas n = trace (A^n) plus rationality of the ordinary generating series, det (1 - X A) * sum lucas n X^n = 2 - X. What is still open is the exponential form: that the Artin-Mazur zeta function exp (sum (lucas n / n) t^n) equals 1 / det (I - tA) = 1 / (1 - t - t^2), with 1/(1 - 2t) for the full shift. Closing it would make the conjugacy obstruction a single identity between rational functions.

exp (sum over n of (lucas n / n) t^n) = 1 / (1 - t - t^2) as formal power series over the rationals, where lucas n = trace (A^n) for A = [[1,1],[1,0]] (proved in cycle 12) and exp (sum (trace A^n / n) t^n) = 1 / det (I - tA).

Build the exp/log calculus on rational power series with zero constant term, prove the logarithmic derivative identity t d/dt log (1/det (I - tA)) = sum (trace A^n) t^n for a 2x2 matrix, and specialise using the already-proved trace_transferMatrix_pow and det_one_sub_smul_transferMatrix.

The periodic census becomes a single rational invariant with the exponential normalisation used in dynamics, giving a reusable zeta-function framework for subshifts of finite type in this catalog.

Failure could only come from the exp/log bookkeeping, since the trace formula and the ordinary generating function are already theorems; that would isolate a genuine obstruction in formalising the logarithmic derivative over power series.
proof_strategy: Cycle 12 already proves trace (A^n) = lucas n, det (1 - t A) = 1 - t - t^2 over any commutative ring, and det (1 - X A) * (sum of lucas n X^n) = 2 - X in the power series ring. The remaining step is the exponential form: build exp and log over the rationals, prove the logarithmic derivative identity t d/dt log (1/det (I - tA)) = sum (tr A^n) t^n, and combine with the ordinary generating function already established.
title: Exponential Artin-Mazur Zeta Function of the Golden-Mean Shift

description:
Two independent lower bounds on the number of adjacent transpositions needed to move Spearman's rho by a given amount are now proved: a linear-in-margin bound of order margin*n^2 and an l1-accumulation bound of order sqrt(margin)*n^{3/2}. The conjecture is that their maximum is tight up to constants, with the crossover at K ~ n^{3/2} marking a change of extremal configuration. Settling it would give the exact metric cost of dial erosion.

For every n >= 2 and every delta in (0,2) there is a chain of adjacent transpositions of length O(max(delta*n^2, sqrt(delta)*n^{3/2})) taking the identity ranking to a ranking with Spearman rho <= 1 - delta.

Construct explicit chains (bubble cascades of a fixed block, and block reversals) and compute their exact rho via the proved transposition identity; formalise the resulting upper bound alongside spearman_ge_of_chain_from_id.

The Kendall cost of a prescribed Spearman drop is determined up to constants, making 'gradual versus cliff' a quantitative, grid-free statement.

There is an unexploited conserved quantity beyond step size and l1 accumulation, and the true cost has a third regime.
proof_strategy: Upper bound by an explicit block-reversal chain whose rho is computed by summing the exact transposition identity; lower bound by combining adjacent_swaps_to_cross with spearman_ge_of_chain_from_id and optimising over which dominates.
title: Kendall–Spearman Budget Duality

description:
Unary Moore machines have eventually periodic behaviours, so the shortest distinguishing word is the first mismatch of two eventually periodic words. We conjecture the exact bound max(p1,p2) + q1 + q2 - gcd(q1,q2) - 1 in terms of preperiods and periods, refining the coarse |S|+|T|-2 estimate. This ties automata testing to word combinatorics.

For unary machines with rho-shapes (p1,q1) and (p2,q2), inequivalent initial states are separated by a word of length at most max(p1,p2) + q1 + q2 - gcd(q1,q2) - 1, and some pair attains it.

Formalise a rho-decomposition of unary machines, then prove the bound by Fine-Wilf; validate by exhaustive enumeration for n,m <= 5 as in ComputationalEvidence.md.

A tight, gcd-sensitive refinement of the Moore bound for unary alphabets, strictly stronger than |S|+|T|-2 whenever gcd(q1,q2) > 1.

The extremal pairs must use preperiods in an essential way, isolating a new combinatorial obstruction beyond Fine-Wilf.
proof_strategy: Decompose each unary machine's orbit into a tail plus a cycle; reduce the observation sequences to eventually periodic words; apply Fine-Wilf to the periodic parts and additivity to the tails; construct the extremal pair by CRT.
title: Fine–Wilf Calibration of Unary Distinguishing Length

description:
The cost of a heterogeneous workload was proved to be the join of its cells, attained at one cell, monotone and submodular; cycle 3 added the quota budget, its adjunction, its agreement with the cover cost at full quota, and the concrete 7-of-8 saving on the round-24 workload. The conjecture is that the quota cost remains submodular below full coverage, giving greedy-optimal multilingual budgets.

For every quota m, the least cache serving at least m cells of a finite workload equals 12 + 4 times the m-th smallest rank sum, and this cost function is submodular in the workload.

Starting from Catalog.NET71.quotaCost (already proved to agree with coverCost at m = card), attempt the submodularity inequality for general m by the interlacing inequalities for order statistics of a union.

Multilingual deployments can trade a measured fraction of cells for a strictly smaller cache, with a certificate for the chosen budget.

Partial coverage is genuinely combinatorial, and cache sizing under service-level targets is not solvable greedily.
proof_strategy: Transport the seed-ensemble quota machinery of Logic.KneeMedianLaw to the workload index set, using that both are order statistics of a finite family in a linear order; submodularity should follow from the interlacing inequalities for order statistics of a union.
title: Quantile Cover Cost for Multilingual Workloads

description:
A deployed system is monitored by many statistics at once. Conjecture: the suite's critical temperature is governed by the operator norm of the covariance functional on the audit span, so the first statistic to break is the maximizer of |Cov_p(r,f)|/sigma_p(f). This replaces per-statistic thresholds by a single spectral quantity.

For a finite family f_1,...,f_m, sup_i eps * beta_c^{(i)}(eps) -> max_i |Cov_p(r,f_i)| as eps -> 0, and the maximizing direction in the L^2(p) span is the normalized projection of r onto that span.

Extend RLHF.tendsto_eps_mul_betaCrit to a finite family by taking maxima inside the two-sided window RLHF.betaCrit_window, then optimize |Cov_p(r,f)|/sigma_p(f) over the span using the Cauchy-Schwarz equality case.

Audit suites can be scored by one spectral number, and redundant statistics are exactly those inside the reward's orthogonal complement.

Suite-level hacking is not determined by pairwise covariances, indicating genuinely joint (multivariate) hacking effects.
proof_strategy: Uniformize the window bounds over a finite index set, then use the equality case of RLHF.abs_cov_le to identify the maximizer as the projection of the centred reward.
title: Threshold Spectrum of an Audit Suite

description:
The mechanism predicts that the attention deficit at the selected budget, measured in units of margin over read-out constant, is confined to [1/8, 1/4] with no depth, context or amplitude dependence. The conjecture promotes this to a universal across the model family and asserts its value inside the window is a function of the tail amplitude alone.

For every model in the family and every context at least 32, (1 - rho(k*)) * L * B / m lies in [1/8, 1/4], and equals a fixed function of the tail amplitude A independent of depth and context.

Measure retained mass at the knee and the held-out margin in the same forward pass, at two contexts with a common fitted amplitude, and compare.

A single forward pass falsifies or supports the whole margin channel, with no sweep.

The deficit carries depth or context information that the scale-free tail does not capture, refuting the Zipf profile.
proof_strategy: Start from deficit_margin_invariant, then strengthen the two-sided margin law by replacing the ceiling bound on the knee with the exact fractional knee, which should collapse the window to a point.
title: Dimensionless Deficit-Margin Universal

description:
Certificates have constant transcripts, so the longest prefix on which a certificate can imitate a destructive test is exactly the prefix on which that test's transcript is still constant. The conjecture turns this observation into an exact approximation modulus and identifies the tests that are approximable for the full rigidity horizon.

For a test t on n dishes, the largest m such that some nondestructive c satisfies transcript t d j = transcript c d j for all dishes d and all j < m equals the minimum over d of the destruction depth of t at d; and m >= n forces t to be repeatable with verdict c = verdict t.

Formalise the approximation modulus as a sInf over dishes, prove both inequalities using transcript_rigid and the constancy of certificate transcripts, and confirm on the fuse tests, which should give modulus exactly k + 1 on k + 2 dishes.

Destruction acquires a quantitative measure: the number of runs for which a destructive test is indistinguishable from a certificate, with an exact formula.

Some test is certificate-approximable beyond its destruction depth, meaning the verdict of a certificate can track a non-constant stream, contradicting Nondestructive.transcript_const.
proof_strategy: One direction: take c with verdict c = verdict t; approximation holds up to the depth by definition. Other direction: if approximation exceeds the depth at some dish, the certificate's constant transcript would have to follow a change of verdict, a contradiction. The uniform case m >= n uses transcript_rigid to force global constancy of every transcript, i.e. repeatability.
title: Certificate Approximation Modulus of a Destructive Test

description:
Integer exchange rates are now classified: rate p is rigid, every rate is consistent, and the measured 1.5B cell at ctx 2048 forces p = 1. The open half is q > 1, the rational rates p/q given by invariance of the table under the sublattice generated by (q, p). Settling it turns a fitted constant into a discrete invariant of the measurement.

A rational exchange rate p/q admits a monotone non-constant clamped knee table if and only if p ≥ 1, and every such table is a function of the single variable q·j − p·s truncated at 0.

Extend RateFamily with a second index q (exchange : F (s+q) (j+p) = F s j) and prove the classification; experimentally, the s = 2 cell separates rate 1 ({16,16,16,20}) from rate 1/2 ({16,16,20,24}).

Budget tables for every scale are generated by one chain plus one integer invariant, and the 7B cell becomes a prediction rather than a measurement.

The scale axis is not a monoid action and per-scale chains must be measured independently.
proof_strategy: Induct along the sublattice generated by (q,p) to reduce any cell to the fundamental domain; monotonicity plus clamping forces the representative to depend only on q·j − p·s.
title: Fractional Exchange Rates for Scale-Context Knee Tables

description:
The equivariance shear only uses two corruption patterns, a prefix and a suffix, which together cover all coordinates precisely when 2k >= n. This suggests the real hypothesis behind the breakdown ceiling is a covering condition on the admissible corruption patterns rather than a cardinality bound. The conjecture replaces k-subsets by an arbitrary downward-closed set system and predicts the ceiling from its covering number.

Let S be a downward-closed family of subsets of {0,...,n-1} of admissible corruption supports. Every translation-equivariant estimator is unbounded under S-contamination if and only if some two members of S cover {0,...,n-1}.

Formalise S-contamination as diffSupport xs ys in S, re-prove breakdown_ceiling_unbounded from the covering hypothesis, and instantiate S as (i) all k-subsets, recovering 2k >= n, and (ii) contiguous blocks of length k, where the covering threshold differs.

The ceiling extends verbatim to structured adversaries such as sensor dropouts and block corruption, with no new analysis.

Boundedness under structured contamination is not covering-determined, which would mean equivariance interacts with the combinatorics of the support family in a way the shear cannot see.
proof_strategy: Replace take m / drop m by a covering pair A, B in S: shear by c on A-complement and by -c on B-complement, check both results are S-contaminations, and conclude by the same equivariance identity. Conversely, if no two members cover, a common uncontaminated coordinate survives every pair and yields a bound via the count transfer lemma.
title: Covering-Number Ceiling for Structured Contamination

description:
Inside each scale block B^L ≤ T < B^(L+1) the budgets that lose depth to coarse-level overhead form an explicit interval of density 1/(B-1)^2. For perturbed cost models with per-cell weight a and per-level overhead c the deficit can take several values; we conjecture each value has a rational limiting density.

For energyCells a c B the deficit Nat.log B T - maxDepth takes values in {0,...,Nat.log B (2a+c)+1}, and each value j has a limiting density d_j(B,a,c) which is a rational function of B, a, c summing to 1.

Decompose each scale block by the thresholds energyCells a c B (L-j) and compute the interval lengths exactly, as in Deficit.lossy_filter_eq; verify numerically for small a, c, B.

The overhead of coarse levels acquires a complete statistical description, refining the O(1) offset of the universality theorem.

Some deficit value has no density, indicating oscillation of the thresholds relative to the powers of B, itself a striking equidistribution failure.
proof_strategy: Block decomposition plus the geometric identity for energyCells; the density is a ratio of two geometric sums, and convergence follows as in lossy_density_tendsto.
title: Density Spectrum of the Depth Deficit

description:
Our upper bounds are proved for caterpillar trees, encoded as leaf orders, while the lower bounds hold for arbitrary split systems. The direction is to transfer the upper bounds to all binary phylogenetic trees by extracting an inherited caterpillar on a logarithmic number of leaves from any binary tree.

Every binary phylogenetic tree on n leaves contains a subset of at least log_2 n leaves whose induced subtree is a caterpillar; consequently the common-quartet upper bounds for caterpillars imply upper bounds for arbitrary binary trees with n replaced by 2^n.

Formalize the extraction (a longest root-to-leaf path plus its pendant leaves) and combine it with caterpillar_family_common_quartet via commonAgreement_subset.

IsAgreementThreshold m k 4 becomes provable for explicit m for all binary trees, closing the theory on the upper side.

Caterpillars are not representative of general trees for quartet agreement, and balanced trees form a genuinely harder extremal family.
proof_strategy: Induct on the tree: a binary tree on n leaves has a leaf at depth at least log_2 n; the leaves attached along that path induce a caterpillar, and quartets of the induced subtree are quartets of the original.
title: Caterpillar Extraction for General Binary Trees

description:
Among all corrections of a fixed rational degree added to eulerMascheroniSeq, the Bernoulli truncation should be the unique minimiser of the asymptotic error constant. This would upgrade the sharp constants proved here from statements about one particular corrector to an extremal characterisation.

For every rational function P/Q with deg Q - deg P = 2, limsup m^2 |gamma - eulerMascheroniSeq n - P(m)/Q(m)| >= 1/12, with equality iff P/Q = 1/(2m) + O(m^{-3}) matches the Bernoulli truncation to leading order.

Formalize the asymptotic expansion of gamma - eulerMascheroniSeq n to order m^{-3} (already available from the proved two-sided bounds) and compare against an arbitrary rational corrector using the sharpness theorems tendsto_scaled_error and tendsto_scaled_error2.

The midpoint correction is provably the best possible correction of its degree, not just a convenient one.

Some non-Bernoulli rational corrector beats the Euler-Maclaurin truncation, which would be a genuinely surprising acceleration scheme.
proof_strategy: Subtract the two correctors; the difference is a rational function of m, and matching orders forces its expansion coefficients to agree with the Bernoulli ones up to the stated order.
title: Optimality of Bernoulli Truncations Among Rational Correctors

description:
Cell merging on a front-loaded profile lowers the measured slack by an exact amount. The conjecture upgrades this from the dyadic step to arbitrary refinements of a fixed continuum density, so that the finite-grid slack increases monotonically along any refinement sequence and converges to 1/(2E). The approach is to iterate the proved dyadic identity and control the residual by a Riemann-sum estimate.

For a monotone decreasing density on the window with continuum mean position E < 1/2, the cell-averaged M-cell profiles satisfy X_M strictly increasing in M along refinements, with limit 1/(2E).

Formalise cell-averaging of a monotone density into Fin M profiles, iterate meanPos_coarseFn along a refinement sequence, and combine with gapXofM_tendsto.

The booked X = 1.15302 on a 27-cell grid is a lower bound for the profile-forced slack and the CI can be re-read one-sidedly.

Grid choice is a confounder of the slack estimate and the CI must absorb a discretisation term.
proof_strategy: The proved identity meanPos_coarseFn plus gapX_eq_meanPos handle one refinement step; the limit follows from Riemann sums of the density against the harmonic CDF of F1TightnessHarmonic.
title: Continuum Refinement Limit of the Slack Factor

description:
Static probes have a fixed error vector, whereas accumulated heavy-hitter statistics observe realised attention and so have an error that decays with the observation window. Modelling the error as eps(t) and re-running the transfer argument should show that accumulation dominates any static score after a finite window.

If a score's sup-error satisfies eps(t) <= C/t while a static probe's error is bounded below by a positive constant, then beyond an explicit t0 the accumulated arm's guaranteed retention strictly exceeds the static arm's worst case at the same budget.

State a time-indexed version of retained_ge_of_isTopSet_sup and combine with the sharpness instance, which certifies that the static worst case is attained.

The deployable pair recency+accumulation is justified by a theorem, not only by measurement.

Static content information retains a role at short windows, and the crossover point becomes the object of study.
proof_strategy: Instantiate the sharp transfer bound with eps(t) and use sup_transfer_bound_is_sharp to lower-bound the static side; compare the two explicit expressions.
title: Shrinking-Error Advantage of Accumulating Predictors

description:
Divergence of the ridge-penalised logistic estimator as the penalty vanishes on a separated design is now proved, together with the envelope log(1/delta_lambda)/||x_i|| <= ||beta_hat(lambda)|| <= sqrt(n log 2 / lambda). What remains is to collapse that envelope to a single logarithmic rate by optimising the competitor along the separating ray, which is the quantity that determines how meaningless a clipped odds ratio is.

On a separated design there are constants 0 < c1 <= c2, depending only on the separation margin and the design norms, with c1 * log(1/lambda) <= ||beta_hat(lambda)|| <= c2 * log(1/lambda) for all sufficiently small lambda > 0; consequently every fitted odds ratio diverges like a power of 1/lambda.

Sharpen penalized_deficiency_le by taking t = log(1/lambda)/margin to prove delta_lambda = O(lambda log(1/lambda)^2), feed the result into log_deficiency_lower_bound for the lower bound, prove the matching upper bound by comparing the maximiser with that same ray point, and check the predicted log-scaling numerically on the flagged control-arm design.

Any control-arm odds ratio reported from a separated design is a function of the stopping rule alone, and the ledger flag becomes a quantitative rule for discarding such fits.

The escape is slower than logarithmic, so mild penalisation stabilises the fit and design B can be salvaged with a fixed penalty.
proof_strategy: Combine ridge_escape and penalized_deficiency_le with the explicit margin bound logisticTerm(y_i, t*s_i) >= -exp(-t*margin): the objective at t*w is at least -n*exp(-t*margin) - lambda*t^2*||w||^2, optimise in t, then convert the resulting deficiency bound into a norm bound via log_deficiency_lower_bound and cap it above with penalized_max_sqNorm_le.
title: Sharp Logarithmic Rate for the Ridge Escape on Separated Designs

description:
The least leaf number h(k) forcing k binary trees to share a quartet is proved here to lie between 3^((k-2)/4) and 3^(2^k)+1. Exhaustive and local-search data (h(2)=6, h(3)=10, and 19, 23, 29 for k=4,5,6) indicate a single exponential rate near 1.7. The direction is to prove h(k) = Theta(c^k) and identify c.

There is a constant c > 1 with h(k) = Theta(c^k); in particular h(k) <= C * c^k, replacing the doubly exponential Erdos-Szekeres bound.

Formalize a 4-uniform hypergraph Ramsey bound for three colours and derive an exponential upper bound on h(k); check the predicted values against h(2)=6 (proved here) and the computed h(3)=10.

The quartet agreement threshold has a well-defined exponential rate, and the coding-theoretic packing rate is its logarithm.

Either the truth is doubly exponential, in which case the small-case data is misleading, or h(k) is not of pure exponential type and a second parameter governs it.
proof_strategy: Replace the iterated global monotone-subsequence extraction of caterpillar_family_common_quartet by a single application of a 3-colour Ramsey theorem for 4-sets, using that a common quartet only needs agreement on four leaves.
title: Exponential Rate of the Common-Quartet Threshold

description:
The Lubell-mass theorem proved here is exactly the constraint of a fractional knapsack whose variables are the layer intersections of the family. Solving that knapsack greedily upgrades the counting bound to Erdos's exact theorem on chain-free families.

If F has no chain of k+1 sets then |F| is at most the sum of the k largest binomial coefficients C(n, i).

Formalise the exchange argument: given layer sizes n_j <= C(n,j) with sum n_j / C(n,j) <= k, the total sum n_j is maximised by saturating the k largest layers.

The chain bound becomes exact for chain-free families, and every subsequent improvement for B_d must come from non-chain configurations.

The Lubell relaxation is strictly weaker than Erdos's theorem, indicating an obstruction invisible to LYM-type arguments.
proof_strategy: Induct on the number of layers, always moving mass from a lighter layer to a heavier one, using Nat.choose unimodality already formalised as choose_le_choose_pred_of_ne.
title: Erdos Layer Knapsack Optimisation

description:
The two halves of the now two-sided estimator depend on the gate in opposite directions, so the width of the certified window for the per-key ratio is a function of the gate alone once the knee is fixed. We conjecture that this width is unimodal in the gate and attains its minimum at an interior point, giving an optimal gate at which a budget measurement is most informative about the spectrum.

For a fixed knee value K and context at least 2K, the width of the window between the largest candidate ratio refuted by the criterion at K-1 and the smallest floor rate excluded by the certificate q^(2K) <= (1 - tau)/tau is a unimodal function of tau on (0,1) with a unique minimiser strictly between 0 and 1, and that minimiser is bounded away from the value 0.99 used in the reported protocol.

Express both endpoints as explicit functions of tau in Lean, differentiate or use monotonicity of the two implicit criteria to prove unimodality, and evaluate the minimiser numerically for K equal to 10, 12 and 20.

Budget measurements should be reported at the optimal gate, and existing tables can be re-analysed to give tighter spectral windows at no experimental cost.

The window width is monotone in the gate, so the informativeness of a measurement is maximised at an endpoint and gate choice reduces to a feasibility constraint.
proof_strategy: Solve the two criteria for the endpoints as implicit functions of tau, show one endpoint is increasing and the other decreasing with a single crossing of their derivatives, and conclude unimodality of the difference.
title: Optimal Measurement Gate for the Spectral Window

description:
Upgrade the yes/no triple criterion into a quantitative bound on the set of unreachable points. The union bound behind the criterion already counts unreachable targets, so optimising over admissible triples should bound the miss set by a small union of lines, degenerating to a single point in the extremal case.

For pairwise independent v_i and sets S_i containing 0, the complement of sum_i S_i v_i in F_p^2 is contained in a union of at most min over admissible triples of (d_i + d_j) lines in the direction v_l; in particular if sum_i d_i = (k-2)(p-1) and the reach is not full then the miss set is a single point.

Compute the exact miss sets for all failing configurations at p=5 (k=4,5) and for the harmonic family at p=7,11,13,17; compare with the predicted line bound. Then formalise the counting version of reach_eq_univ_of_triple in Lean.

Yields a Kneser-type stability theorem for iterated sumsets along lines, strictly stronger than the spanning criterion and usable for spread exclusions where a small exceptional set is tolerable.

The miss set can be large even near the threshold, indicating that the failure mode is global rather than a bounded local defect.
proof_strategy: Refine the fibre bound in the union argument: for a fixed target t the number of admissible tuples is prod_{m != i,j} |S_m| and each bad residue removes at most that product divided by |S_l|. Counting targets rather than tuples turns the strict inequality into a bound on the number of targets that can be bad.
title: Quantitative Kneser Stability for the Miss Set

description:
The corruption budget gives |A| >= (1-rho)n/6 from a crude per-coordinate bound. Block reversals realise a reading rho with displacement of order (1-rho)n/2, so the sharp constant is bracketed between 1/6 and 1/2. Pinning it converts the budget from a lower bound into a certificate.

The optimal constant c with |A| >= c(1-rho)n for every rank mechanism achieving reading rho satisfies 1/6 <= c <= 1/2, and the extremal mechanism is a contiguous block reversal.

Compute sumSqD exactly for the reversal of the top m ranks, optimise m for a target rho, and compare with reading_corruption_budget.

Measured readings translate into two-sided quantitative statements about the underlying mechanism, not just lower bounds.

Some non-reversal mechanism beats block reversal, revealing a richer extremal structure for Spearman perturbations.
proof_strategy: Sum the exact transposition increments of sumSqD_swap_exact over a reversal, obtaining a closed cubic in m; then optimise and compare to the Lipschitz bound.
title: Sharp Constant in the Rank-Displacement Certificate

description:
The experimental claim 'conditional permutation nulls have zero variance at t >= 2' is the statistical shadow of a combinatorial fact: the prefix of a Price address determines N mod 8 exactly and nothing finer. Half of this is proved (positions 0 and 1 are constant on any 2-adic cell); the conjecture is the converse counting statement about cell sizes. It matters because it removes the last non-deterministic step from the death-at-position-2 claim.

For every prefix word w of length at least 2, the set of depth-d nodes whose address ends with w has, as d tends to infinity, an asymptotically uniform distribution over the residues N mod 2^k compatible with the first two letters of w, for every k >= 3.

Count, for each prefix of length 2 and 3 and each k = 3,4,5, the empirical distribution of N mod 2^k over depth-d nodes; then formalize the asymptotics via the transfer operator of the descent.

The permutation-null variance is exactly zero for structural reasons, and the mutual information I(N mod 2^k ; address) is exactly log 4 for every k >= 3.

Some prefix cells are biased at higher moduli, so a longer address prefix does leak more than three bits of N.
proof_strategy: Model the descent as a Markov chain on (N mod 2^k, ratio interval), show its transition matrix restricted to each of the four mod-8 classes is primitive, and identify the stationary distribution as uniform on the compatible residues.
title: Zero-Variance Prefix Cells

description:
The number of N <= X admitting a factorisation of Fermat gap at most B is proved to be O(sqrt(B) X^{3/4}). We conjecture the matching lower bound with an explicit constant, making the count asymptotically exact and pinning the vanishing rate of the sensor hit rate.

There are positive constants c1, c2 with c1 * sqrt(B) * X^(3/4) <= #{N <= X : exists odd p <= q, N = p q, gap p q <= B} <= c2 * sqrt(B) * X^(3/4) for all X >= X0(B).

Formalize the lower bound by exhibiting the injective family N = a^2 - h^2 with a in [sqrt X / 2, sqrt X] and h <= sqrt(2 B a), and compare with the counts in ComputationalEvidence.md Table 3.

The reported 0.2053 hit rate is quantitatively explained as a finite-population effect with a computable correction term.

Primality constraints reduce the count below X^{3/4}, and the sensor population is even sparser than the parametrisation suggests.
proof_strategy: Upper bound is already proved via the parameter box; for the lower bound count pairs (a,h) with a^2 - h^2 having exactly two prime factors using a sieve of dimension two, or drop primality and count odd-factor pairs directly.
title: Sharp Constant for Fermat-Close Counting

description:
A policy that reads k binary answers from a query menu is measurable with respect to a statistic with at most 2^k classes. Combining this with the exact crediting law bounds the realization achievable by any such policy in terms of k alone, independently of how the policy is fitted.

For any population P, target s and menu of binary queries, every policy using at most k queries has error at least the sum of class minorities of the coarsest partition refined by all 2^k answer patterns; in particular if every class of the answer statistic is balanced the error is exactly |P|/2.

Instantiate StatisticRealization.isLeast_err with kappa = Bool^k and the answer-vector statistic, combine with the decision-tree indistinguishability theorem of AdaptiveMenuCapacity, and verify on the 295-item menu population by direct enumeration.

The empirical statement 'no policy reaches 50 percent of the peak' becomes a theorem about menu capacity rather than a fitted observation.

Adaptivity (queries chosen depending on earlier answers) escapes the static statistic bound, and adaptive policies must be modelled by decision trees instead.
proof_strategy: Model an adaptive k-query policy as a depth-k decision tree, note that its output is a function of the leaf reached, and apply the minimum-error law to the leaf statistic.
title: Menu Capacity Bound for Bounded-Query Policies

description:
Unison lags of an infinite digit melody are closed under gcd. On a finite window of length n this fails below the Fine-Wilf threshold p + q - gcd(p,q). We conjecture the sharp finite-window statement and its extremal examples for digit alphabets.

If a window of n consecutive digits has periods p and q and n >= p + q - gcd(p,q), then it has period gcd(p,q); for n = p + q - gcd(p,q) - 1 there is a decimal counterexample.

State periodicity relative to a window in Lean and adapt IsPeriod.sub with index-range side conditions; construct the extremal words explicitly for small p, q and verify by decide.

Empirical periodicity claims about finite digit samples acquire an exact sample-size threshold.

Finite-window periodicity is strictly weaker than expected and needs a different invariant, e.g. the windowed lag spectrum.
proof_strategy: Induct on p + q; from periods p < q derive the period q - p on a shortened window, tracking the length bookkeeping that produces the threshold.
title: Fine-Wilf Threshold for Digit Windows

description:
Real deployments optimize a learned reward r-hat, not the true reward r. Conjecture: the hacking threshold is Lipschitz in the reward in L^2(p), with constant sigma_p(f)/eps, so reward-model accuracy translates linearly into threshold accuracy.

If ||r - r_hat||_{L^2(p)} <= eta and both are bounded by R, then |eps * beta_c^{r}(eps) - eps * beta_c^{r_hat}(eps)| <= eta * sigma_p(f) + o(1) as eps -> 0.

Combine RLHF.abs_cov_le (Cauchy-Schwarz gives |Cov(r,f) - Cov(r_hat,f)| <= eta sigma_p(f)) with the two-sided window RLHF.betaCrit_window applied to both rewards.

A quantitative safety budget: reward-model error eta buys threshold error eta sigma_p(f), so audit thresholds inherit reward-learning guarantees.

Threshold prediction is unstable under reward error, so measured thresholds cannot be transferred from a proxy reward to the true one.
proof_strategy: Show the covariance functional is eta-Lipschitz on the L^2(p) ball, then propagate the perturbation through the window inequalities, which depend on the reward only through |Cov| and R.
title: Threshold Stability Under Reward-Model Error

description:
The Cauchy–Schwarz slack in the covariance bound for audit drift and the Pinsker slack in the total-variation bound are conjectured to be the same quantity: the deviation defect σ_p(r) − MAD_p(r). This would make a single scalar functional of the reward the exact measure of how much worst-case bounds overstate actual drift.

sup over audit statistics f of the normalised drift equals σ_p(r)/β asymptotically, while the policy's own total-variation drift equals MAD_p(r)/β; the two agree iff σ_p(r) − MAD_p(r) = 0, i.e. iff |r − 𝔼_p r| is p-a.s. constant.

Formalize the extremal problem sup_f Cov_p(r,f)/σ_p(f) = σ_p(r) (attained at f = r) in Lean, and combine with RLHF.pinsker_defect_tendsto and RLHF.mad_eq_sqrt_variance_iff.

A one-number diagnostic, computable from the reference policy and reward alone, that predicts the gap between worst-case and realised reward hacking.

The two slacks are governed by different functionals, so worst-case audit hacking and policy drift are not comparable through a single index.
proof_strategy: The sup over f is attained at f = r by Cauchy–Schwarz equality; the policy side is RLHF.l1_drift_tendsto_mad; equality analysis is the deviation defect identity Var − MAD² = 𝔼(|r−𝔼r| − MAD)².
title: Deviation Defect as a Universal Hackability Index

description:
The wheel dials of modulus M give speedup M/phi(M) with zero per-target information. The conjecture pins their growth: the tropical weight of any information-free dial applicable in time T is log log T + O(1), so blind structural exclusions are worth a doubly-logarithmic amount, never a polynomial factor.

log(M/phi(M)) = log log M + gamma + o(1) along primorials M, hence sup over wheels applicable in time T of the tropical weight equals log log T + O(1).

Formalise sum over p <= y of log(p/(p-1)) and compare with Mertens' third theorem; check the constant numerically against the primorial table in ComputationalEvidence.md.

Barrier 4 is complemented by a doubly-logarithmic ceiling on the information-free regime, closing the classification of dial regimes.

Some sparse family of structural exclusions grows faster than the wheel family, which would be a new sieving primitive.
proof_strategy: Use wheelSpeedup_prod to reduce to an Euler product, take logs via tropWeight_mul, then invoke Mertens estimates on sum 1/p with the log(1+x) = x + O(x^2) correction.
title: Mertens Ceiling for Blind Structural Sieving

description:
Study the map from replication depth d to the set of admissible root exponents of the d-th replication of the Monster product. The approach is to combine the proven equivalence n-th root ⟺ n ∣ 194d with elementary divisor arithmetic. It matters because it turns a moonshine-flavoured question into an exactly solvable lattice problem.

The map d ↦ divisors(194 d) from replication depth to root spectrum is an order isomorphism onto its image, refining the proved minimal-depth formula n / gcd(n, 194).

Build the map into the divisor lattice on top of exists_pow_eq_replicate_iff_depth and prove monotonicity and reflection of the order.

Replication depth becomes a computable invariant of a moonshine product.

The root spectrum depends on more than the pole order after replication, contradicting the proven criterion.
proof_strategy: Reduce to n ∣ 194 d, write d = n / gcd(n,194) * t and verify minimality by divisibility bookkeeping.
title: Replication Lattice of Root Spectra

description:
The safe KV bit width is a function of bits minus log2 of the context length, because n logits inside a bounded window force a minimum consecutive gap of R/n. The formal criterion SafeBits A R n b is invariant under (n, b) -> (2n, b+1), so the cliff must translate along the context axis at exactly one bit per doubling. This turns an untested limit of NET-92 into a sharp prediction.

For a fixed model, the minimal quality-preserving KV bit width satisfies b*(2n) = b*(n) + 1 up to one bit, for all context lengths n in the trained range.

Rerun the NET-92 arm grid at ctx 4096, 8192 and 32768 and locate the free/annihilated bracket; compare with the theorem SafeBits_ctx_pow and minSafeBits_double.

KV precision budgets must be specified per context length, and long-context deployments need 2-3 more KV bits than the ctx-2048 measurement suggests.

The logit window is not bounded independently of context (logit norms grow with n), which would itself be a strong structural finding about attention.
proof_strategy: Telescoping pigeonhole on consecutive logit gaps (exists_small_consecutive_gap) plus the exact bit/context invariance of the SafeBits predicate.
title: Crowding-Corrected Cliff Position

description:
The first- and second-order hacking coefficients proved in this cycle are the covariance and the skew covariance. Conjecture: the k-th order coefficient is the mixed cumulant kappa_k(r,...,r,f)/k!, so safety to order beta^-k is orthogonality of the audit statistic to the first k reward cumulant tensors. This would turn ad-hoc audit design into a linear-algebraic orthogonality condition.

For |r| <= R <= beta there are constants C_k with |E_{pi_beta} f - E_p f - sum_{j=1}^{k} kappa_j(r,...,r,f)/(j! beta^j)| <= C_k (R/beta)^{k+1} sigma_p(f), where kappa_j is the mixed cumulant with j-1 copies of r and one copy of f.

Formalize the k = 3 case first: identify the coefficient by expanding e^{r/beta}/Z to third order and prove the oscillation bound |tilt - cubic model| <= C (R/beta)^4 with the same Taylor-plus-Cauchy-Schwarz route used in SecondOrder.lean.

Audit statistics can be certified safe to any prescribed order by finitely many orthogonality checks against reward cumulants.

The expansion coefficients are not cumulants beyond order two, which would mean higher-order hacking is not captured by moment orthogonality and needs a genuinely non-polynomial invariant.
proof_strategy: Induct on the Taylor order of exp: pointwise bound |e^u - T_k(u)| <= |u|^{k+1} on |u| <= 1, control 1/Z by the k-th order expansion of the partition function, then transport the pointwise oscillation to a variance bound via the pair representation and close with Cauchy-Schwarz.
title: Cumulant Hierarchy of Audit Invariants

description:
Extend the maximizer normal form to all two-qubit states: every amplitude matrix is U diag(s,t) Vᵀ with s ≥ t ≥ 0, and two normalized states are local-unitary equivalent iff their determinant moduli agree. The route is the spectral theorem applied to the Hermitian marginal M Mᴴ, followed by construction of the second unitary from an orthonormal completion, exactly the step already carried out in the maximizing case. This turns the concurrence into a complete invariant of the U(2)×U(2) action.

For every M : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ there exist unitaries U, V and reals s ≥ t ≥ 0 with M = U * diagonal ![s,t] * Vᵀ; consequently normalized M, N are local-unitary equivalent iff ‖det M‖ = ‖det N‖.

Formalize in Lean using Matrix.IsHermitian.spectral_theorem on M * Mᴴ, defining the right unitary by normalizing the rows of Uᴴ M and completing an orthonormal basis when a singular value vanishes.

The concurrence is a complete local-unitary invariant for two qubits, and the results of this cycle become the equality stratum of a full orbit classification.

Some degenerate stratum (rank-one or zero states) would have to be handled by a separate orbit, revealing that the singular-value parameterization is not a normal form for the action as defined.
proof_strategy: Diagonalize the PSD Hermitian marginal; set s,t as square roots of eigenvalues; define W by dividing the rows of Uᴴ M by s,t; prove W unitary from the row Gram relation (the same lemma as rowGram_of_sharp); handle s = 0 or t = 0 by the explicit orthogonal completion (a,b) ↦ (-b̄, ā).
title: Two-Qubit Schmidt Normal Form via Hermitian Spectral Theory

description:
The dichotomy theorem gives non-eventual-periodicity of the decimal expansion of sqrt 2 abstractly. We conjecture an effective form: any claimed eventual period p starting at position n is refuted at an index bounded polynomially in p and in the denominators controlled by the irrationality measure 2 of sqrt 2.

There is an explicit constant C such that for all n and p >= 1 there is i <= C * p * 10^(n) with digit(i+p+n) != digit(i+n) for sqrt 2.

Quantify the pigeonhole in Pyth.digits_eventually_periodic_of_not_irrational and combine with a quantitative irrationality measure for sqrt 2; sanity-check against the first 10^4 digits.

Aperiodicity of a quadratic irrational becomes a finite, checkable statement at every scale.

The orbit of frac(10^k sqrt 2) would return to near-repetition faster than approximation theory allows, contradicting the standard measure of irrationality.
proof_strategy: Periodicity from index n with period p implies a rational approximation of denominator dividing 10^n (10^p - 1); compare with the quadratic irrationality bound to get a contradiction with an explicit constant.
title: Effective Aperiodicity Bound for the Pythagorean Constant

description:
The sharp estimate |G(z) - log‖z‖| ≤ 2/‖z‖ proved in this cycle says the potential has no additive normalisation constant at infinity. Identifying G_M with the equilibrium potential of M would then give logarithmic capacity exactly 1, a classical fact with no formal proof.

G_M is the Green's function of the complement of M with pole at infinity and Robin constant 0; hence cap(M) = 1.

Prove harmonicity of G_M on the complement of M (from local uniform convergence of harmonic truncations), boundary vanishing, and apply the uniqueness of the Green's function.

First formal computation of a nontrivial logarithmic capacity of a fractal set, and a benchmark for formal potential theory.

Would mean the truncations fail to be harmonic in the required uniform sense, isolating exactly where potential theory needs new formal infrastructure.
proof_strategy: Harmonicity from uniform limits of harmonic functions (tendstoUniformlyOn_logOrbitSeq), boundary behaviour from continuity plus the escape-time characterisation of M.
title: Unit Logarithmic Capacity of the Mandelbrot Set

description:
The hybrid arm is non-degrading precisely while the mixing weight stays below the ratio of the accumulated score's separation margin to the probe's oscillation. Measuring that ratio in both domains should predict the observed code-neutral versus prose-harmful asymmetry with no new modelling assumptions.

For each domain there is a threshold lambda* = gamma / D (gamma the accumulated margin at budget B, D the probe oscillation) such that the hybrid retains exactly the accumulated mass for all lambda <= lambda*, and the measured lambda* on code exceeds 1 while on prose it is below 1.

The first clause is hybrid_isTopSet_of_margin, already proved; the second is an empirical measurement of gamma and D on the existing traces at B = 64.

Hybrid safety becomes a one-number deployment check computable from the accumulated statistic alone.

Non-degradation on code is not a margin effect and must come from correlation between probe and accumulated scores.
proof_strategy: Theoretical half is done; the empirical half is a direct evaluation, with the interval structure of hybrid_stability_ordConnected guaranteeing that a single threshold suffices.
title: Margin-to-Oscillation Ratio as Hybrid Interaction Predictor

description:
Almost every dish should be evasive, with the non-evasive fraction shrinking doubly exponentially in the number of ingredients. The approach sharpens the counting recursion c_{d+1} ≤ 2 + n c_d^2 proved here by tracking subcube refinements instead of raw trees. It would make 'C = V for a random recipe' a probability-one statement.

#{f : Dish n | tasteCost f ≤ n - 1} ≤ 2^(2^n) / 2^(2^(n-1)) for all n ≥ 2.

Exhaustive verification for n ≤ 4 with the brute-force solver, then a refined induction on the counting recursion in KitchenGenericHardness.
