The kitchen is generically break-even; the interesting recipes are a measure-zero accident.

Non-evasive dishes are far more common than tree counting suggests, indicating strong structure among Boolean dishes.
proof_strategy: Replace the tree count by a count of distinct restrictions and use the fact that an optimal tree's subcube partition determines the dish.
title: Doubly Exponential Concentration of Evasiveness

description:
The classical bound ||S_N(alpha)|| <= 1/(2||alpha||) proved here is precisely the kernel estimate feeding the Erdos-Turan inequality. Formalizing that inequality would convert the file's qualitative Weyl cancellation into a quantitative discrepancy bound for the sequence {n alpha}.

For every alpha and every H >= 1, the discrepancy of {n alpha : n < N} satisfies D_N <= C(1/H + (1/N) sum_{h <= H} 1/(h ||h alpha||)) with an absolute constant C.

Formalize the Erdos-Turan inequality via Selberg polynomials built from the Fejer kernel, then substitute the proved bound norm_weylSum_le_intDist.

Explicit equidistribution rates for badly approximable alpha follow, e.g. D_N << (log N)^2/N for quadratic irrationals.

The constant structure of Erdos-Turan would need revision, which would be a major surprise.
proof_strategy: Selberg majorant/minorant construction from the proved approximate identity, Fourier expansion, and the kernel bound already proved.
title: Erdos-Turan Discrepancy From the Proved Weyl Bound

description:
A single scalar f, the variance inflation caused by overlap, damps every z-statistic of a pre-registration by 1/sqrt(f). Conjecture that the damping is uniform across primary and secondary cuts and across bootstrap schemes, so one audited number retracts or preserves a whole gate family.

If the honest variance of every reported statistic is f times the reported variance, then the honest z of each is its reported z divided by sqrt(f), and the family of gates at level c retracts simultaneously.

Prove zscore_scaled for a finite family of statistics sharing an inflation factor and derive the joint retraction threshold z_required = c*sqrt(f).

The seed-20260825 leg has an explicit pass mark computable before it is run.

Inflation is cut-dependent and each gate needs its own overlap accounting.
proof_strategy: Pure algebra of the map v -> f*v on the z functional, plus monotonicity of the tail probability in the threshold.
title: Uniform Root-Inflation Damping of Pre-Registered Gates

description:
Cap-riding is the integral form of an exponentially vanishing Fisher information. Quantifying the collapse turns the qualitative 'lower bound only' amendment into a sample-size requirement for pinning the steepness.

For the binned flat-plus-spike model with edge-bin width t, the Fisher information for the steepness b behaves as I(b) = Theta(rho^2 t^2 exp(-2 b t) / (p(1-p))); consequently a finite upper confidence limit at level alpha exists if and only if n is of order exp(2 B t) / (rho t)^2.

Differentiate the binned log-likelihood twice in b, bound the result above and below by constants times exp(-2 b t), and compare with the exp(-b t) envelope already proved in EdgeSpike.cap_gain_le.

Gives a closed-form sample size for identifying spike steepness; predicts that the audited n = 9594 cannot bound the steepness above regardless of cap.

Some other quantity (for example the mixture weight) would carry the information, and re-parameterisation rather than more data would fix identifiability.
proof_strategy: Write the edge probability as P - rho(1 - truncExpCDF), whose derivative in b is rho t exp(-b t)(1 + o(1)); insert into the two-cell information formula I(b) = (dp/db)^2 / (p (1-p)) and control the o(1) using the censoring bound.
title: Fisher-Information Collapse Rate for Censored Spikes

description:
The scale-k sieve examines exactly the residues in noncontracting k. The conjecture is that this is optimal: every non-contracting class really contains arbitrarily large non-descending inputs, so no smaller residue set is sound, and the true density is Theta(1/sqrt k) rather than the proved O(1/k).

For every k and every r with 2^k <= 3^(s_k(r)) there are arbitrarily large n with n mod 2^k = r and not (T^[k] n < n); moreover |noncontracting k| / 2^k = Theta(1/sqrt k).

Formalise the lower bound via the parity-word bijection and a local central limit estimate for the binomial count s_k; check k <= 12 by exhaustive computation.

The certification workload of any residue-based sieve is pinned down exactly, giving a sharp cost model for certified evidence.

A strictly smaller sound sieve exists, i.e. some non-contracting classes descend anyway, which would sharpen the descent theory itself.
proof_strategy: Use terras to produce explicit large non-descending representatives; replace Chebyshev by a de Moivre-Laplace estimate on onesCount.
title: Optimality of the Scale-k Residue Sieve

description:
The measured halving slope failed the -ln 2 test in the balanced stratum while the width-halving law is exact. The exact closed form halfIter k w = ceil(w / 2^k) makes the discrepancy a ceiling-phase artefact whose size is computable, predicting a shortfall that vanishes for large windows.

For w uniform on [W/2, W), the expectation of log(ceil(w / 2^k)) equals log w - k log 2 + Theta(2^k / W), so the fitted slope is -ln 2 (1 + Theta(2^k/W)); at the experiment's grid this yields a 10-20% shortfall for the balanced stratum and a negligible one for the unbalanced stratum.

Formalise the error term of halfIter_eq_ceilDiv, sum it over a dense grid of w with Finset.sum, and compare to the measured -0.5836 / -0.6589 slopes.

The A10 FAIL clause is an artefact of the discretisation, and the halving law can be reported as universally exact.

A genuine phase correlation between factor position and band entry exists, which would be a new structure in the distribution of min(p,q).
proof_strategy: Write ceil(w/2^k) = (w + r)/2^k with r = (-w) mod 2^k, expand log(1 + r/w) to first order, and bound the average of r over a residue-complete range by 2^(k-1).
title: Ceiling-Phase Correction to the Minus-Log-Two Slope

description:
Testing is 11.56% of per-factor work, so its batching is capped at a 1.131× end-to-end speedup, already nearly realised. We conjecture the exact composite ceiling when the finding phase is batched too, and that exceeding 1.5× requires the finding phase's per-candidate ratio to drop below 0.28.

With phase shares 1 − f and f and per-candidate batch/solo ratios c_f/s_f and c/s, the end-to-end speedup ceiling is 1/((1−f)c_f/s_f + f·c/s), which exceeds 3/2 iff (1−f)c_f/s_f + f·c/s < 2/3.

Generalise BatchCost.phase_residual to a finite family of phases and instantiate at two phases with the measured f = 1156/10000.

A quantitative roadmap: only the finding phase can deliver the next order of magnitude.

Phase costs interact non-additively (shared memory traffic), invalidating the additive Amdahl split used to report the +0.104.
proof_strategy: Additivity of costs plus a single division; equality analysis as in BatchCost.overall_saving_le_testing_share extended to Finset.sum over phases.
title: Multiplicative Amdahl Ceiling for Two-Phase Sieve Batching

description:
The cross-channel discrepancy of a population decouples into the oscillation of a single per-level functional over the window box, turning the sharp-constant question into a one-dimensional extremal problem. Cycle 4 solved it for the exponent pair (1, 1/2) via the Kantorovich inequality, obtaining log2((4+3*sqrt2)/8) and matching it to within 5% by an explicit two-point population. The conjecture extrapolates the exponent dependence found numerically.

For pointwise costs a*p^s and c*p^t on a window of spread 2^sigma, max |t*slope_s - s*slope_t| = (ln2/8)*s*t*|s-t|*sigma^2/Dk to leading order, attained by a two-atom population whose x^t-mean equals the harmonic mean of the window endpoints.

Extend the doubling-ray result (s = 2t, already proved with constant log2((1+2^t)^2/(4*2^t))) to a general power-mean version between exponents t < s, compute the oscillation of the per-level functional in closed form, and compare with the grid search (coefficient 0.0862 +- 0.0002 at sigma = 1 versus ln2/8 = 0.08664).

Every multi-channel benchmark gets an exact internal-consistency tolerance, and the (0.84, 0.52) refutation generalises to arbitrary cost exponents.

The oscillation is not governed by the two-atom endpoint configuration and the sharp constant depends on more than the window spread.
proof_strategy: Reduce to two-atom populations by an exchange argument, differentiate the per-level functional in the weight, and expand the resulting critical value in sigma.
title: Cubic Law for the Sharp Power-Mean Constant

description:
The dominant-block law bounds the Spearman ceiling by the largest tie class alone. We conjecture that the bound is attained exactly by the profile consisting of one block of size M and n-M singletons, making the inequality an equality case theorem over integer partitions.

For all n >= 2 and 1 <= M <= n, the minimum of rho^2 over tie profiles of n with maximal block M equals 1 - (M^3-M)/(n^3-n), attained uniquely at [M,1,...,1].

Exhaustive search over partitions for n <= 60, then a Lean exchange argument using superadditivity of m -> m^3 - m.

Gives the exact attainable dial range for every statistic, sharpening every exclusion result in the catalog.

Some intermediate profile beats the singleton completion, revealing a second-order term in the attenuation law.
proof_strategy: Splitting a non-maximal block into singletons decreases the tie correction (tieCorr_le_of_split), so any minimiser has all non-maximal blocks equal to 1.
title: Extremal Profiles for the Dominant-Block Bound

description:
The rank-perturbation Lipschitz law is symmetric in the two rank vectors, so corruption can be spent on either side. We conjecture that splitting the budget between the statistic and the response is exactly twice as efficient as spending it on one side.

The minimum number of transpositions needed to move rho by delta, when transpositions may act on either rank vector, is ceil(delta*n/12), half the one-sided cost ceil(delta*n/6).

Exhaustive optimisation over rank pairs for n <= 10, then a Lean proof of the matching bound.

Halves the empirical corruption estimate for the observed drop, to about n/300.

One-sided corruption is optimal, indicating an asymmetry in Spearman's response to rank noise.
proof_strategy: Optimise the exact increment -2(R_i-R_j)(S_i-S_j) over disjoint index pairs; the upper bound is a greedy pairing of extreme ranks.
title: Two-Sided Corruption Optimality

description:
For a single tail constraint the reachable slack interval is now exactly [(M+1)/(2M), (M+1)/(2Km+2)], with the upper endpoint attained by a two-atom profile. The conjecture extends this to the family of nested constraints in which the measured bulk exponent, spike weight and edge mass are actually booked, and predicts that two-atom profiles remain extremal.

For nested cuts K_1 < ... < K_r with required masses m_1, ..., m_r, the reachable mean positions form an interval whose endpoints are attained by profiles supported on at most two cells, and the maximal slack is (M+1)/(2*max_j K_j m_j + 2) whenever the constraints are consistent.

Formalise a finite family of edgeMass constraints, prove the analogue of meanPos_ge_of_edgeMass by summing the active constraints, and search for a three-constraint counterexample by exact rational enumeration on small M.

The measured tail statistics determine the admissible slack interval outright, making the booked CI a derived quantity.

Interactions between constraints matter and the polytope has vertices with three or more atoms, so the LP must be solved in full.
proof_strategy: Linear programming on the simplex: meanPos and each edgeMass are linear, so the optimum is at a vertex; bound the number of active constraints at a vertex by the dimension count.
title: Nested Tail Constraints on the Mean-Position Polytope

description:
cheap_signal_le_oracle bounds every cheap signal by the oracle but gives no size. The exchange kernel localises all lost value in the symmetric difference between the kept set and the oracle set, suggesting the gap equals a sum over score-versus-utility inversions crossing the budget boundary.

For any score s with kept set S and oracle set O at budget B, retained v O - retained v S = sum over the matched pairs of O\S and S\O of the utility differences, and this equals the total weight of boundary inversions of s against v.

State the matched-pair decomposition in Lean using a sorted pairing of O\S with S\O and prove equality, then evaluate the statistic on the measured retention tables.

The 5.7-point gap becomes a measurable inversion count, turning a policy comparison into a signal-quality statistic.

Gap size depends on more than pairwise inversions, so per-slot signal diagnostics cannot predict policy loss.
proof_strategy: Refine sum_le_sum_of_sdiff_dominated from a max/min bound to an order-isomorphic pairing of the two symmetric-difference halves.
title: Inversion Formula for the Oracle Gap

description:
Alignment pressure is measured by KL divergence, audit failure by the gap. Conjecture: the two are linked by a temperature-free exchange rate, so moving a statistic by eps costs at least eps^2 Var_p(r) / (2 Cov_p(r,f)^2) nats of KL divergence.

KL(pi_beta || p) >= (G(beta))^2 Var_p(r) / (2 Cov_p(r,f)^2) * (1 + o(1)) as beta -> infinity, with equality asymptotically for f proportional to the centred reward.

Rebuild the KL side (KL(pi_beta||p) = Var_p(r)/(2 beta^2) + O(beta^-3)) with the pair-representation technique of Core.lean and divide by the proved gap asymptotics.

A currency conversion between alignment budget and audit failure that is independent of temperature, giving deployable guarantees from a KL budget alone.

KL budgets do not control audit failure, so temperature must be monitored directly.
proof_strategy: Second-order expansion of the log-partition function gives the KL asymptotics; combine with beta G(beta) -> Cov and eliminate beta.
title: KL Exchange Rate for Audit Failure

description:
Nonnegativity, unit mass over one period and uniform-in-N concentration off the integers are all proved for the triangular kernel arising as ||S_N||^2. These are exactly the approximate-identity axioms, so Fejer summation of Fourier series should follow with no further harmonic analysis.

For every continuous 1-periodic f, the Fejer means (f * K_N)/N converge to f uniformly, where K_N(alpha) = 2 sum_{d<N} (N-d) cos(2 pi d alpha) - N.

Formalize the abstract approximate-identity convolution lemma and instantiate it with fejer_nonneg, fejer_kernel_mass and fejer_kernel_concentration.

A formal nonnegative approximate identity and Cesaro convergence of Fourier series become available on top of the proved identity.

The normalization or the concentration rate is off, which the proved Dirichlet formula would immediately localize.
proof_strategy: Split the convolution integral into a small neighbourhood of 0, controlled by uniform continuity and unit mass, and its complement, controlled by the 1/(4 delta^2) concentration bound.
title: Cesaro Convergence From the Triangular Kernel

description:
The retention deficit of a threshold is now known exactly as inversion mass minus concordance mass, but only when every retained target is sieved to the same depth. We conjecture that the same pairwise symmetrisation survives per-target sieve lengths, with each deferred/retained pair contributing a bilinear term, unifying the allocation and deferral theories in one identity.

For sieve lengths l and rates r with s split into retained K and deferred D, (sum over K of l) * (yield of s) - (sum over s of l) * (yield of K) = sum over D x K of (l i * r j - l j * r i).

Prove by the same double-sum manipulation as retention_deficit_eq with l-weighted cardinalities, then specialise l to a constant to recover the proved identity; check numerically on the clipped-floor allocation family.

Allocation policies and deferral policies are comparable inside a single bilinear inequality, so the clipped floor and the threshold can be optimised jointly.

Unequal depths introduce genuinely new cross terms and deferral must be analysed after, not with, allocation.
proof_strategy: Replace cardinalities by l-masses in the split-and-count argument of retention_deficit_eq; the cross terms are exactly the bilinear pair sum.
title: Work-Weighted Deficit Identity for Unequal Sieve Depths

description:
The square-hit bijection sends factorisations of s^2 to Pythagorean triples (k, s, u+k), and the Barning-Hall parent strictly decreases the hypotenuse. Conjecture that the descent also decreases the imbalance and terminates in logarithmically many steps, giving a canonical schedule through the tree of hits.

Transporting the Barning-Hall parent map through the square-hit bijection yields a factorisation of a strictly smaller square with strictly smaller imbalance k, reaching (3,4,5) in Theta(log(k+s)) steps.

Compute the transported map explicitly on the three inverse matrices, prove monotonicity of k, and bound the step count by a descent measure.

Fermat hits over square moduli inherit the full tree structure, so window walks become tree walks.

The imbalance is not monotone along the descent, isolating the branches where it grows.
proof_strategy: Combine square_hit_of_pythagorean with the catalog descent lemmas parent_hyp_lt and parent_hyp_pos, then bound the descent measure 3c - 2a - 2b.
title: Berggren Descent as a Factorisation Schedule

description:
Invisible vectors obey two independent extremal bounds: at least K+1 nodes, and total mass at least 2K. Their extremisers differ (binomial vectors versus PTE pairs), suggesting a quantitative trade-off between narrow support and small mass.

There is c > 0 such that every nonzero window-K invisible vector satisfies (number of nonzero nodes) * log(mass) >= c K^2; in particular minimal-support vectors have mass at least 2^{cK}.

Prove the special case: a window-K invisible vector supported on exactly K+1 nodes has mass at least 2^K, using the divided-difference rigidity already formalised in InvisibleWeightsRigidity.

The two extremal problems of the catalog are unified by a single inequality and the binomial basis becomes provably optimal in the narrow-support regime.

There exist narrow, light invisible vectors, which would immediately improve the growth base via the convolution engine.
proof_strategy: On a minimal support the vector is proportional to a divided-difference functional; bound its integrality denominators below by products of node differences and convert to a mass bound.
title: Mass-Support Uncertainty Principle

description:
If each taste destroys a portion and only b portions exist, decidability rather than efficiency becomes the issue. The approach formalises a budgeted, partly nonadaptive model on top of the existing checklist notion and classifies which dishes remain decidable. It captures the actual soufflé problem: cutting it open destroys the object being verified.

In the b-portion destructive model a dish is decidable iff it admits a nonadaptive checklist of size at most b; consequently the souffle is undecidable for every b < n, while anySpoiled is semi-decidable with a single portion.

Define the destructive model as a Taste tree whose probes must be chosen from a fixed budgeted checklist, and prove the equivalence using relevantSet_subset_of_checklist.

Destructive verification separates decidability from efficiency, giving a genuine culinary analogue of undecidability.

Adaptive reuse of partial portions recovers full power, meaning destruction costs nothing asymptotically.
proof_strategy: Show the destructive model collapses to nonadaptive tasting, then apply the formalised relevant-variable lower bound and the adaptivity gap example mux.
title: Destructive Tasting Classes

description:
The redundancy–capacity inequality I(w) ≤ log₂ Cₛ is conjectured to be tight exactly when the normalised maximum likelihood law is itself a mixture of the class. The approach uses the compensation identity to express the gap as a relative entropy against NML. This would identify the geometric obstruction separating average-case and worst-case universal coding.

For a strictly positive finite class, sup_w I(w) = log₂ Cₛ iff nml lies in the convex hull of {p_θ}, and the optimal prior equalises D(p_θ ‖ nml).

Formalise the equalisation condition in Lean on top of compensation_identity and mutualInfo_le_logb_shtarkovSum; check small classes numerically.

The two universality theories of the thread (worst-case and Bayes) are unified by a single convexity criterion.

A strictly positive capacity gap exists for representable classes, isolating a new invariant of source classes.
proof_strategy: Write log₂ Cₛ − I(w) as ∑_θ w_θ D(p_θ ‖ nml) plus a nonnegative remainder; apply Gibbs equality and a minimax/convex-hull separation argument on the simplex.
title: Capacity-Shtarkov Equality via Mixture Representability

description:
Extend the census objective to b-ary splitting and determine when the discrete optimum is a tie. For b = 2 the tie set has exactly two elements at dyadic widths; the conjecture is that for b >= 3 ties never occur at integer widths.

For b >= 3 and every integer W >= 2, the argmin of k + (W/b^k + 1)/2 over k in N is a singleton; for b = 2 it has two elements exactly when W is a power of two.

Prove the b-ary increment formula 1 - W(b-1)/(2 b^(k+1)), characterise equality as 2 b^(k+1) = W(b-1), and resolve that Diophantine condition.

Reporting 'the' optimal budget is unambiguous outside binary search, and the dyadic tie is a base-2 artefact.

Tie sets recur in other bases and every b-ary report must name a tie-breaking rule.
proof_strategy: Number-theoretic case analysis on 2 b^(k+1) = W(b-1) after the increment computation, mirroring census_tie_iff.
title: b-ary Census Tie Dichotomy

description:
Model the observed dial as a 2-adic statistic seen through a random rank-corruption channel of intensity theta. The p-adic ceiling law then predicts an effective base p(theta) that grows from 2 as theta increases, and the measured 6.97 fixes theta. This would convert the descriptive effective base into a generative mechanism.

There is a strictly increasing map p : [0,1) -> [2, infinity) with p(0) = 2 such that the expected Spearman coefficient of a 2-adic statistic under a Bernoulli(theta) transposition channel equals 3p(theta)/(p(theta)^2+p(theta)+1), and p(theta) = 2/(1-theta)^2 + O(theta^3).

Formalise the channel as a distribution over rank vectors, compute E[Sigma d^2] exactly using the transposition increment identity, and compare with the p-adic ceiling law.

The dial becomes a calibrated thermometer for corruption intensity, and the base-7 finding acquires a mechanism.

Rank corruption is the wrong channel and the attenuation must come from response noise correlated with the statistic.
proof_strategy: Linearity of expectation over independent transpositions plus the exact increment -2(R_i-R_j)(S_i-S_j) proved in ZeroFitDialPerturbation.
title: Bernoulli Corruption Channel for the Effective Base

description:
The tie-attenuation law is the top eigenvalue of the block-averaging projector acting on centred rank space. Extending the ssR/ssS decomposition to the full spectrum should give a ladder of canonical correlations, of which the recorded dial is only the first rung.

For a tie profile with blocks m_1,...,m_k the canonical correlations between the midrank vector and any refining response are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the block-averaging projector, whose multiset is determined by the profile alone.

Formalise the projector on the rank space of a profile, compute its spectrum for small profiles, and match against ssR/ssS.

Turns the single dial into a spectral fingerprint that identifies the tie profile, not just its ceiling.

The response enters beyond the projector, meaning the one-sided law hides response-dependent structure.
proof_strategy: Write ssR as a quadratic form of the projector, diagonalise blockwise, and identify eigenvalues with block sizes.
title: Spectral Ladder of the Tie-Attenuation Law

description:
For the action of G on G/H the rank should equal the number of (H,H)-double cosets, converting the second moment into a subgroup invariant. Combined with the proved rank splitting this would compute #(offDiag/G) as the number of nontrivial double cosets.

#((G/H × G/H)/G) = #(H \\ G / H) for every subgroup H of a finite group G.

Compose the proved suborbit bijection with a map from H-orbits on G/H to double cosets, sending the orbit of bH to H b H, and verify well-definedness and injectivity using Mathlib's Doset API.

Burnside moments compute double-coset counts, giving ∑_g |(G/H)^g|^2 = |H \\ G / H| · |G|.

The map fails to be injective, indicating a normality obstruction worth isolating.
proof_strategy: Apply orbits_prod_eq_orbits_stabilizer to reduce to H-orbits on G/H, then match those orbits with Doset.quotient.
title: Double-Coset Rank of Coset Actions

description:
The exact limit ||S_N(1/(2N))||/N -> 2/pi is proved, so the Jordan bound is asymptotically optimal at the lobe edge. What remains is that the edge is the actual minimizer over the whole main lobe, a monotonicity statement for the Dirichlet ratio. Together the two give a complete description of the Weyl sum on its main lobe.

For every N and every 0 <= a < b <= 1/(2N), |sin(pi N b)|/(N |sin(pi b)|) < |sin(pi N a)|/(N |sin(pi a)|); consequently min over |alpha| <= 1/(2N) of ||S_N(alpha)||/N equals ||S_N(1/(2N))||/N and tends to 2/pi.

Differentiate the logarithm of the ratio to get pi N cot(pi N alpha) - pi cot(pi alpha) and prove it is negative on the main lobe; then combine with norm_weylSum_endpoint_ratio_tendsto.

norm_weylSum_ge_jordan is optimal in the strongest sense: the constant 2/pi and the extremal frequency are both identified.

An interior critical point of the Dirichlet ratio exists inside the main lobe, which would be a genuinely new feature of the kernel.
proof_strategy: Log-derivative comparison for cot on (0, pi), reduced to the one-variable inequality N cot(N t) < cot t for 0 < t < pi/(2N).
title: Main-Lobe Edge as the Dirichlet Minimizer

description:
The proved sandwich |X|^k ≤ |G|·o_k ≤ |G|·|X|^k pins the exponential growth rate of the hierarchy at |X|. The conjecture sharpens this to an exact second-order expansion controlled by the second largest fixed-point count, making the hierarchy a spectral probe of the action.

|G|·o_k = |X|^k + m·r^k + O(s^k) where r is the largest fixed-point count among nonidentity elements, m the number of elements attaining it, and s < r.

Split the moment sum by the value of |X^g| and bound the tail; formalise as an inequality with explicit constants rather than an asymptotic statement.

Orbit counts on tuples determine the fixed-point spectrum of the action, an inverse-problem statement.

Cancellation among elements with equal fixed-point counts would have to be exhibited, contradicting positivity.
proof_strategy: Group the sum over g by the value a_g, use Finset.sum_le_sum on the tail with a_g ≤ s, and combine with the identity term.
title: Asymptotic Shape of Orbit Counts

description:
Generalise the entire chain of estimates from z²+c to z^d+c. Every step used only ‖z^d+c‖ ≥ ‖z‖^d - ‖c‖ and ‖c‖ ≤ ‖z‖, so the escape radius becomes max(2,‖c‖)^{1/(d-1)} and the potential satisfies G(f z) = d G(z). This yields compactness of all multibrot sets in one refactor.

For f(z) = z^d + c with d ≥ 2, an orbit escapes iff it ever exceeds R_d(c) = max(2^{1/(d-1)}, ‖c‖^{1/(d-1)}); the escape rate exists, satisfies G(f z) = d·G(z), and the degree-d multibrot set is compact.

Parametrise the five core lemmas (growth, invariance, distortion, summability, functional equation) by d and re-run the proofs; test sharpness numerically for d = 3,4,5.

One formal development covers the whole multibrot family, including the sharp radius, which is the standard but rarely formalised statement.

Would isolate a genuinely quadratic step (most likely the sharpness witness c = -2) that has no degree-d analogue.
proof_strategy: Replace the factor (‖z‖-1) by (‖z‖^{d-1}-1) and the constant 2 in the distortion estimate by d/(d-1); everything else is unchanged.
title: Degree-d Multibrot Escape Radius and Potential

description:
The floor law gives rho^2 > 1 - a^2 for modal mass fraction a, and a 15:1 profile violates the 0.53 floor. The two bounds bracket the cliff in the window 0.848 to 0.938 of modal mass. We conjecture the critical value is exactly sqrt(1 - 0.53^2), attained by two-block profiles.

sup over profiles with modal fraction a of spearmanSq equals 1 - a^2 + O(1/n), and inf equals 1 - a^2 - O(1/n); hence the 0.53 floor holds iff a <= sqrt(1 - 0.2809) = 0.848002...

Prove the two-block family [an, (1-a)n] has spearmanSq tending to 1 - a^2, and combine with mass_fraction_floor.

The robustness envelope acquires a sharp boundary expressible purely in modal mass, independent of bitlen and cap.

The floor depends on more than the modal block and the envelope needs a finer invariant.
proof_strategy: Evaluate spearmanSq on [m, n-m] in closed form via spearmanSq_eq, set m = an, expand in 1/n, and match against the mass_fraction_floor bound.
title: Exact Critical Modal Mass for the 0.53 Floor

description:
The ternary case admits exactly three trees because the density budget 1 = sum of 1/(a(a+b)) has three admissible solutions, one of which mixes Berggren and Price branches. For general arity k the same budget equation plus the power-of-two determinant constraint bounds the search space. Determining t(k), the number of k-ary trees, would show whether hybridisation is an accident of arity three or a general phenomenon.

For every k >= 2 the number t(k) of k-ary trees on the node set {1 <= n < m, gcd(m,n)=1, m+n odd} with root (2,1) is finite, with t(2) = 0, t(3) = 3 and t(k) >= 3 for k >= 3, and every branch of every such tree satisfies |det| <= 2.

Extend the finite search of evidence.py from triples to k-tuples of admissible matrices with |entries| <= 8, checking that the images partition the non-root nodes with first coordinate at most 200; then formalise the arity-k analogue of TernaryTree.no_branch_det_ge_three using the same root-child forcing argument.

The bound |det| <= 2 is a structural property of the node cone rather than of arity three, and the classification method generalises to a uniform theorem.

A k-ary branch with |det| = 4 exists, showing that the power-of-two spectrum is genuinely realised beyond 2 and that the ternary bound is a low-arity coincidence.
proof_strategy: Reuse preserves_iff to bound entries via root minimality, then run the root-child forcing argument (root_child_cases_*) for the k smallest uncovered nodes; the density budget forces the branch with maximal density to be bergA or priceP0 exactly as in exists_bergA_or_priceP0.
title: Hybridisation Threshold for k-ary Pythagorean Trees

description:
The three Berggren generators split into one parabolic and two hyperbolic directions, which makes the ternary tree exponentially unbalanced. The maximal depth reachable inside a hypotenuse box should be governed purely by the parabolic spine and hence grow like sqrt(H), while a typical node sits at logarithmic depth. This quantifies how far the tree is from a balanced ternary tree.

The maximal Berggren word length among triples with hypotenuse at most H satisfies D(H) = (1/2 + o(1)) * sqrt(H), while the average depth is Theta(log H).

Prove that a word containing k non-parabolic letters has hypotenuse at least 5^k, deduce k = O(log H), and combine with the closed form 4(j+1)^2+1 for parabolic runs; compare with the measured D(10^5) = 222.

The tree has a canonical thin spine, giving a seed-independent sqrt(H) lower bound for any single-orbit count and an explicit height function for enumeration algorithms.

Mixed words would have to beat pure parabolic runs, contradicting the multiplicative growth of the hyperbolic generators.
proof_strategy: Induct on word length splitting at each hyperbolic letter, apply the proved bound hyp_bB_gt (factor > 5 per hyperbolic step) and hyp_bC_iterate (quadratic parabolic growth), then optimise the resulting product-sum tradeoff.
title: Square-Root Depth Profile of the Berggren Tree

description:
Generalise the n = 5 enumeration to arbitrary sample size: compute the exact permutation-null size of a |ρ| ≥ t bar for every n, and prove monotonicity so that a threshold with a stated false-positive rate can be chosen in advance.

For each n the set of attainable Spearman values is the lattice {1 - 6D/(n(n²-1))} and the exact size of the |ρ| ≥ t test is a computable rational, decreasing in n for fixed t.

Prove the d² identity for general n from ∑ r = n(n+1)/2 and ∑ r² = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6, then formalise the size function and verify n = 4,5,6 by enumeration.

Every future round can pre-register a bar with a known false-positive rate instead of the conventional 0.7.

Non-monotone size in n would mean small-sample bars cannot be compared across rounds at all.
proof_strategy: Equiv.sum_comp for the rank moment identities; Finset.card computations for small n; a concentration bound on D for the asymptotic regime.
title: Exact Size Calculus for Rank-Correlation Bars

description:
Knee and decay rate are exact reciprocals, so the measured acceleration is a statement about how quickly attention de-peaks with context. The conjecture is that the asymptotic per-doubling rate ratio increases with parameter count and tends to 1, i.e. sufficiently large models have context-free budgets even after the transition.

There is rho(N) in (0,1] with lam_{j+1}/lam_j -> rho(N) for a model of N parameters, rho increasing in N and rho(N) -> 1 as N -> infinity; the 4.5B context-free threshold of the earlier cycle must be recomputed under the crossover family.

Fit lam_j = log(1/delta)/k*_j from the measured chains at 0.5B and 1.5B, extend by the 1.5B ctx = 4096 cell and a 7B quantized-offload cell, and check monotonicity of the fitted rho.

Large-model serving budgets are asymptotically context-free and the phase transition is a small-model phenomenon, which changes cache sizing for 7B and above.

The collapse is scale-invariant, so every model has the same post-corner slope in log-context and budget tables need the nonlinear term at every scale.
proof_strategy: Use knee_rate_reciprocal to convert measured chains into rate sequences; prove the model-free acceleration inequality (done, robustly to the grid gap) and then calibrate the crossover family lamCross per model, comparing base rates as in the cycle-1 scale calibration.
title: Scale-Dependent Rate-Collapse Exponent

description:
Fractal foams have non-integer effective branching. Extending the cost to a real base beta > 1 should preserve maximality (an order-theoretic fact) while making the depth a locally constant function of beta with an explicitly algebraic jump set.

For real beta > 1 the largest d with (beta^(d+1)-1)/(beta-1) <= T equals floor(log_beta((beta-1)T+1)) - 1, and as a function of beta it is left-continuous, non-increasing, with jumps exactly at the algebraic numbers solving (beta^(d+1)-1)/(beta-1) = T.

Restate Core with cost : natural -> real and reprove maximality; then derive the closed form with Real.logb and Nat.floor, and analyse the jump set by the intermediate value theorem.

The whole depth theory becomes available for fractal / non-integer branching geometries, with a rigidity statement about where depth can change.

Non-integer branching produces a genuinely different depth law, which would be evidence that integrality of B is physically essential.
proof_strategy: Order-theoretic maximality transfers unchanged; the closed form follows from strict monotonicity of beta^d and the floor characterisation of the real logarithm.
title: Real-Base Depth Function and Its Jump Set

description:
The three recorded seeds attain 86% of their Bhatia–Davis variance ceiling, so the dispersion is nearly two-point extremal. The conjecture is that under such near-extremal dispersion, adding seeds strictly dominates deepening seeds for any fixed compute budget, with the crossover independent of the unknown correlation structure.

If the seed-level variance is at least half of its Bhatia–Davis ceiling for the observed range, then for any fixed total number of draws the pooled estimator has smaller worst-case error with more seeds than with longer seeds.

Formalise the two-level variance decomposition in the rationals and compare the two designs under the Bhatia–Davis constraint.

The experiment protocol should be re-specified: more seeds, shorter runs, for the same compute.

Within-seed depth still buys accuracy, and the straddling CI can be closed by deeper runs.
proof_strategy: Bound the between-seed term by Bhatia–Davis and the within-seed term by the sub-sampling variance, then compare the two totals as functions of the split of a fixed budget.
title: Replication Design at a Bhatia–Davis Ceiling

description:
Windows of 2^s consecutive integers all carry the same trailing-zero tie profile, whatever their placement (proved in cycle 4). For a sample size L that is not a power of two the block counts become floor or ceiling of L/2^(k+1) depending on the window position, so the ceiling should wobble by Theta(1/L) in a way governed by the binary expansion of L.

For any A and L the k-th block of [A, A+L) has size floor(L/2^(k+1)) or that plus one, and the resulting ceiling equals 6/7 + f(L)/L + O(1/L^2) where f is a bounded nowhere-differentiable function of the binary expansion of L, with f identically zero exactly on powers of two.

Extend card_Ico_modEq with a floor correction term, evaluate the exact rational ceiling for all L up to 2^16 and all residues of A, and plot the normalised deviation L*(ceiling - 6/7).

Sample size, not just scale, becomes a tunable knob of the dial, and power-of-two sample sizes are exactly the stationary points.

The ceiling depends on L smoothly, and translation invariance extends to all sample sizes.
proof_strategy: Split [A, A+L) into full residue periods plus a remainder of length L mod 2^(k+1); count the remainder by a floor identity and feed the perturbed profile into spearmanSq_of_cubeSum.
title: Fractal Ceiling Wobble for Non-Dyadic Sample Sizes

description:
Localizing the transcendental BB84 threshold by integer certificates costs certificate bit-length proportional to (a+c)·log(a+c) per decimal digit of the QBER denominator. The conjecture is an exact yield law relating certificate size to certified digits, making certificate cost predictable rather than empirical.

Certifying d decimal digits of Q* requires certificates of bit-length Θ(10^d · d), and no scheme based on comparing (a+c)^(2(a+c)) with 2^(a+c)·a^(2a)·c^(2c) can do better.

Measure certificate bit-lengths at denominators 10^2, 10^3, 10^4 (already present in the catalog) and 10^5; fit, then prove the lower bound via the two Lipschitz bounds, which convert digit accuracy into an explicit two-sided rate margin.

Certificate cost for QKD parameter tables becomes predictable, and the four-decimal enclosure is provably near-optimal for its size.

A sub-exponential certification scheme exists, which would be a significant improvement in machine-checked transcendental localization.
proof_strategy: Express the certificate margin as (a+c)·r(Q) and sandwich it using binEntropy_lipschitz_upper and binEntropy_lipschitz_lower, then bound the integer sizes needed to detect a margin of that order.
title: Digit Yield of Integer Threshold Certificates

description:
The bit depth at which quantised cache keys destroy attention decisions should be predictable from the top-1 margin distribution alone. The formal bound flips_le_small_margin_count says the number of broken decisions is at most the number of positions whose margin is below twice the quantiser step; the conjecture is that this bound is tight up to a constant on real models. If so, the cliff location is a measurable statistic of a single forward pass, not an empirical property of each quantiser.

For a fixed model, the fraction of flipped top-1 attention decisions under b-bit key quantisation equals F(2^{1-b}) + o(1), where F is the empirical CDF of the top-1 score margin.

Histogram top-1 margins per layer on the held-out slice; compare F(2^{1-b}) with the measured flip rate at b = 8, 6, 5, 4; formalise the matching lower bound as a companion to flips_le_small_margin_count.

Key bit-depth selection becomes a calculation, not a sweep, and the weight/key asymmetry is explained by margin statistics.

Flip rate is driven by correlated, not marginal, perturbations, and a joint (multi-position) theory of decision stability is needed.
proof_strategy: Upper bound is flips_le_small_margin_count. For the lower bound, build an adversarial-free model: for a quantiser with independent uniform round-off, a margin below the step size flips with probability bounded below by a constant, giving a matching count up to that constant.
title: Margin-CDF Law for the Attention-Key Precision Cliff

description:
Monotone degradation was derived purely from the single-crossing property of linear families. A combiner that violates single crossing should be able to improve on both pure arms, so the negative NET-61 result is about the additive parametrisation rather than about content signals as such.

There exist a, p, v and a combiner f monotone in each argument such that the top-B set of f(a,p) strictly beats the top-B set of a + lambda*p for every lambda >= 0.

Search small instances for such an f; then formalise one witness in Lean with a forced-kept-set argument like topSet_eq_initial_of_strictAnti.

The refutation of P1 is a statement about additive scoring, and nonlinear gating becomes the natural next experimental arm.

Any monotone combiner is trapped on the same trade-off path, strengthening the law to all monotone score combinations.
proof_strategy: Construct an instance where the optimal kept set is not top-B for any linear functional of (a,p) — i.e. lies strictly inside the convex hull of the sweep path — and exhibit a monotone f selecting it.
title: Single-Crossing Barrier for Nonlinear Combiners

description:
A coverage claim of the form 'four feature classes were tested and all failed' should be a single theorem about the concatenated design, since the union can explain strictly more than the sum of the parts when the blocks are non-orthogonal. Restating the ceiling over an arbitrary finite index type makes the union a sum type and the coverage claim a corollary.

For blocks B1..Bm with correlation ceilings rho_b and a joint frame bound lambda, the incremental R-squared of the union is at most the sum over b of (card B_b) rho_b squared times (1 - R0) divided by lambda, and this is attained when the blocks are mutually orthogonal.

Generalise blockClass and FrameLower from Fin k to an arbitrary Fintype and derive the union bound for a Sum type index.

Multi-class negative results become single certificates instead of collections of separate experiments.

Cross-block interaction can exceed the sum of individual ceilings, and coverage claims must be re-run jointly.
proof_strategy: Reindex the block by a sum type, transport the frame bound, and apply the existing Cauchy-Schwarz plus AM-GM core unchanged.
title: Coverage Algebra for Unions of Covariate Blocks

description:
The multiplicative monoid generated by normalized q-series should be isomorphic to the product of the additive monoid of pole orders with the group of 1-units, giving a universal target for pole-order-additive invariants.

The submonoid of the Laurent series field generated by all normalized series is isomorphic as a monoid to Multiplicative N times OneUnit, the N-component being the pole order.

Define the submonoid in Lean, build the homomorphism from the pair (pole order, 1-unit), and prove bijectivity using the order valuation.

A clean universal property for pole-order invariants, extending the unit-group splitting to the non-invertible graded setting.

The monoid contains unexpected elements, indicating that products of normalized series generate more than the graded model.
proof_strategy: Mirror the proof of unitEquiv: existence from the factorization q^{-m} times a 1-unit, injectivity from additivity of the valuation.
title: Graded Monoid Classification of Pole Data

description:
The first nonzero term of the trace sequence sits exactly at the girth, and computations on the pentagon, hexagon and Petersen graph show its value is 2*girth times the number of shortest cycles. The lower bound of this equality is proved; the upper bound needs a uniqueness statement for non-backtracking walks in 2-regular graphs.

If G contains a cycle then trace(B^{girth}) = 2 * girth * (number of cycles of length girth).

Show that a closed non-backtracking walk of length equal to the girth spans exactly a shortest cycle, and that a non-backtracking walk in a 2-regular graph is determined by its first dart; then count fibres.

The Hashimoto trace sequence determines the girth and the number of shortest cycles.

Some graph admits a cyclic non-backtracking word of girth length that is not a rotation or reversal of a shortest cycle, which would be a new combinatorial phenomenon.
proof_strategy: Combine the proved edge-counting bound (a closed non-backtracking walk of length n forces a cycle of length at most n inside its own edge set) with 2-regular determinism to sandwich the fibre size at exactly 2 * girth.
title: Exact Girth Multiplicity of the Non-Backtracking Trace

description:
Replace the integer-dimensional coordinate cells of the aleph-one surface by products of self-similar Cantor factors, producing surfaces whose achievable Hausdorff-dimension spectrum is an arbitrary sup-closed subset of [0,∞]. The current arithmetic surfaces are the integer shadow of this family. This would show that the arithmetic-to-geometry dictionary extends from subsets of ℕ to closed subsets of the half-line.

For every sup-closed D ⊆ [0,∞] with 0 ∈ D there is A ⊆ ℓ² with {dimH B : B ⊆ A closed} = D.

Formalise dimH of a product of n middle-α Cantor sets, then rerun the surfaceOf union argument with those cells.

Hausdorff-dimension spectra of Hilbert-cube subsets are completely classified by sup-closure.

Some sup-closed set is unattainable, revealing an extra constraint on countable unions in ℓ².
proof_strategy: Lower bounds via Lipschitz projections onto the Cantor factors, upper bounds via Lipschitz sections; then dimH_iUnion turns the family into a supremum.
title: Fractional Cell Spectrum of Arithmetic Surfaces

description:
The only position-declining carrier of the Fermat sieve is the set of positions j dividing the base value v(0). Its exact density is 1/j, so its counting function is the divisor-counting function of v(0) restricted to the sieve range. We conjecture the classical Dirichlet asymptotics transfer verbatim, giving the exact functional form of the small-j profile that exp 578 asked for.

For base values v(0) uniform in a window, the expected number of positions j <= J with j | v(0) is log J + 2*gamma - 1 + o(1), and the block excess of [1,K] over (K,2K] tends to log 2.

Extend FermatPosition.divisor_positions_small_j_excess from a strict block inequality to an asymptotic; verify numerically with the sieve code in evidence/ over many base values.

The functional form of the only genuine positional carrier is known exactly, and its total mass can be subtracted from any observed profile.

The self-divisor carrier interacts with the sieve polynomial beyond the uniform model, which would itself be a new positional mechanism.
proof_strategy: Sum the exact per-scale density 1/j (card_filter_dvd) over j <= J and apply Dirichlet's hyperbola method to control the error term.
title: Divisor-Counting Profile of Self-Divisor Sieve Positions

description:
Prime hypotenuses of the tree are exactly the primes ≡ 1 mod 4, each at a unique node. The tree-specific question is therefore not how many primes there are below H, but how they are distributed across depths, where the silver poles at Re s = σ₀ predict an oscillation of frequency π/log(1+√2).

π_tree(H) = ½ Li(H) + O(H exp(−c√log H)), and the number of prime nodes of depth at most d is ≍ (3+2√2)^d/d with a secondary oscillatory term of frequency π/log(1+√2).

Derive the first statement from prime_hyp_iff plus the prime number theorem in arithmetic progressions; test the second numerically by counting prime hypotenuses per depth slice up to depth 12 and fitting the oscillation.

The tree has a prime number theorem whose error term is genuinely controlled by its own silver poles — the analogue of zero-controlled error terms in the classical theory.

The depth distribution of prime nodes is governed by the arithmetic of m²+n² alone and carries no trace of the silver spectrum.
proof_strategy: Combine prime_hyp_iff with Dirichlet/PNT in progressions for the height count; for the depth count use the seed bijection to translate depth into a continued-fraction-type statistic of (m,n) and apply a transfer-operator equidistribution argument.
title: Silver-Oscillatory Prime Hypotenuse Counting

description:
Stratify the orbit-counting language by the size of the orbits whose indicators are available. The conjecture is that each level is strictly more expressive than the previous one on suitable finite models, with the union being the full orbit language. This would turn the qualitative 'counting modalities are necessary' result into a quantitative definability rank.

For each k there is a finite model with a group action such that some interpretation is definable using orbit predicates of orbits of size ≤ k+1 but not using only those of size ≤ k; the union of all levels is the orbit language.

Define the languages L_k inductively in Lean, prove soundness and a separation example at each level (e.g. cyclic actions with orbits of prescribed sizes).

Definability of external meaning acquires a well-defined rank, refining the finite collapse theorem.

Bounded counting collapses at some finite level, meaning a single bounded modality suffices for all finite models.
proof_strategy: Generalise countGen_of_invariantSet to a size-indexed induction; build separations from disjoint unions of cyclic actions with distinct orbit sizes.
title: Strict Hierarchy of Bounded Counting Modalities

description:
For eventually periodic grade counts the residue spectrum at the m-th roots of unity is now proved to be a complete invariant of the grade germ. The conjecture extends this to quasi-polynomial grade counts, where each singularity carries a whole principal part instead of a single residue, and the section polynomials should be recoverable from those principal parts.

Two grade counts that are eventually quasi-polynomial mod m agree in all sufficiently large grades if and only if their partition functions have the same principal part at every m-th root of unity.

Transport the laurentMoment computation along the twist q -> w q to obtain the moments at each pole, then invert the discrete Fourier transform coefficientwise as in eventuallyEq_of_residueSpectrum_eq.

The singularity divisor with principal parts becomes a complete classifying invariant of quasi-polynomial graded G-sets up to finitely many grades.

Some nonzero quasi-polynomial grade count has vanishing principal parts everywhere on the unit circle, which would produce an entire partition function with quasi-polynomial coefficients.
proof_strategy: Difference the two continuations, remove all singularities using the proved principal parts, apply the identity theorem on the preconnected complement of the finite pole set, and read off the coefficients at 0.
title: Complete Singularity Divisor for Quasi-Polynomial Germs

description:
Differencing floors of scaled prefix sums gives a candidate multi-client Bresenham counter that is realisable for k = 2 but can decrease for k >= 3. The conjecture is that realisability is governed by a simultaneous-jump condition on neighbouring Beatty sequences, hence by gcd conditions relating each prefix sum to the period.

nestCnt r k is realisable by a schedule iff for every i < k the Beatty sequences of slopes pre_i/R and pre_{i+1}/R never increment at the same time step.

Formalise the simultaneous-jump condition in Lean and prove both directions; validate against the census of k = 3 profiles with rates <= 4, where exactly 18 of 64 fail.

A complete arithmetic classification of when prefix-sum floors define a schedule, generalising the k = 2 Bresenham theorem.

The obstruction is not purely pairwise, indicating a genuinely higher-order interaction between three or more prefix slopes.
proof_strategy: Monotonicity of a counter is equivalent to no simultaneous jump of the two neighbouring floors; translate simultaneous jumps to solvability of t*pre_i = -s mod R via the three-distance theorem.
title: Arithmetic Criterion for Nested-Floor Schedulability

description:
Turn the formal escape-time test into a machine-checked renderer: each dyadic box whose N-th iterate is certified outside the disk of radius 2 by interval arithmetic is provably disjoint from M, and such boxes exhaust the complement. Soundness is already a theorem; exhaustion follows from the nested intersection representation of M.

M = ⋂_N (complement of the union of dyadic boxes certified escaping at time N), and each certified box is disjoint from M.

Implement complex interval arithmetic in Lean, prove the enclosure lemma for z ↦ z²+c, and combine with Mandelbrot_eq_iInter and tendsto_atTop_of_exists_escape.

Produces the first fully verified Mandelbrot renderer whose 'outside' pixels are theorems, and a certified exhaustion of the complement.

Failure could only come from the exhaustion half, indicating boxes touching the boundary need a different (measure-theoretic) treatment.
proof_strategy: Interval enclosure by monotonicity of the modulus, plus isClosed_testSet and testSet_antitone for the limiting statement.
title: Certified Escape-Time Rendering of the Mandelbrot Complement

description:
Second-differencing a histogram of bin averages is exactly convolution of the second derivative with a Bartlett kernel. This turns the fitted-vertex significance test into a parameter-free curvature-sign readout with an analytic error term, eliminating the degenerate-fit failure mode observed at nb = 33. It gives the named follow-up (binning-independent shape test) a concrete estimator.

For f in C^2 and bin width w, binVal f o w (i+1) - 2 binVal f o w i + binVal f o w (i-1) = w * (f'' convolved with the triangular kernel of half-width w) evaluated at binCenter o w i.

Formalise in Lean by twice applying intervalIntegral.integral_comp_add_right to slidingAvg and integrating by parts; verify numerically against the exp-581 regenerated positions.

The 30-cell grid collapses to a single sign vector with analytic standard errors; hump significance becomes testable without any fit.

Curvature readout is bin-width dependent and the shape test must be replaced by a bandwidth-selection procedure.
proof_strategy: Write binVal as slidingAvg (proved), express the second difference as an integral of f over a triangular weight by telescoping two box kernels, then integrate by parts twice.
title: Curvature-Sign Certificates for Box-Averaged Windows

description: An argumentation framework AF = (A, R) consists of a set of arguments A and an attack relation R subset A x A. The preferred extensions of AF are the maximal admissible sets (subsets S of A that defend themselves against all attacks and are maximal with this property). Conjecture: the preferred extensions of AF form a simplicial complex K(AF) on the vertex set A. The homology groups H_n(K(AF)) measure the 'holes' in the argumentation structure. H_0 measures the number of connected components (independent debate threads). H_1 measures circular arguments (cycles where each argument attacks the next, and the last attacks the first). H_2 measures 'spheres' of arguments (3D cycles where arguments form a spherical shell). Conjecture: for any argumentation framework, the Euler characteristic chi(K(AF)) = |A| - |R| + sum_{n>=2} (-1)^n * dim(H_n) equals |preferred extensions| - |grounded extension size|. This connects the topology of the argument to its semantics. Test: construct K(AF) for 100 argumentation frameworks from debate transcripts, compute homology groups, and verify the Euler characteristic formula. Impact: arguments have topology. Circular arguments are 1-holes, and 3D argument spheres are 2-holes. The shape of a debate is a topological invariant.
proof_strategy: Define the argumentation complex K(AF): vertices = arguments in A, simplices = independent sets (subsets S of A such that no two arguments in S attack each other). The independent sets form a simplicial complex because if S is independent, so is any subset of S. This is the 'clique complex' of the complement of the attack graph. Properties: (1) preferred extensions are maximal simplices of K(AF). (2) stable extensions are maximal simplices that are also 'dominating' (every argument not in S is attacked by some argument in S). (3) The grounded extension is the intersection of all preferred extensions, which is the 'core' of K(AF). The homology H_n(K(AF)) measures: H_0 = number of connected debate threads (components of the complement of R). H_1 = circular arguments (cycles in the attack graph where a1 attacks a2, a2 attacks a3, ..., a_k attacks a1). H_2 = 3D argument spheres (sets of arguments that form a spherical shell of attacks). The Euler characteristic: chi(K(AF)) = sum_{n>=0} (-1)^n * dim(H_n) = sum_{n>=0} (-1)^n * f_n where f_n is the number of n-simplices. Conjecture: chi(K(AF)) = |preferred extensions| - |grounded extension|. Test: construct AFs from debate data, compute K(AF), calculate homology and Euler characteristic, verify the formula.
title: The Topology of Argumentation: Why Debates Have Holes

description:
This thread proves that eventually quasi-polynomial grade counts give partition functions with finitely many, completely described singularities on the unit circle. The conjecture is the converse dichotomy: any other orbit-counting sequence of polynomial growth produces a function for which the unit circle is a natural boundary, so there is no intermediate behaviour.

For a grade count of polynomial growth, the generating function continues analytically past some arc of the unit circle if and only if the grade count is eventually quasi-polynomial.

Formalise a lacunary family (for example grade counts supported on powers of two) and prove non-continuability by an Ostrowski-Hadamard gap argument; combine with the proved quasi-polynomial direction.

Analytic continuability becomes an exact characterisation of quasi-polynomial orbit growth, upgrading the residue calculus of this thread into a classification theorem.

There is an orbit-counting sequence that is not quasi-polynomial yet has a meromorphic continuation, which would reveal a new class of graded G-sets with computable residues.
proof_strategy: One direction is proved here; for the other, combine a gap theorem with the Fourier sectioning to reduce an arbitrary sequence to a quasi-polynomial part plus a lacunary remainder.
title: Natural-Boundary Dichotomy for Orbit-Counting Series

description:
The characterisation isDPRun ↔ endpoint-optimal has the shape of an adequacy theorem for a deduction system whose judgements are score bounds. The conjecture is that a finitely axiomatised system derives exactly the valid bounds, with normal derivations in bijection with DP runs and cut elimination corresponding to Bellman's optimality principle. This makes DP optimality certificates first-class proof objects.

There is a finitely axiomatised sequent system with judgements (n, s, w) such that ⊢ (n, s, w) iff w ≤ val n s, cut-free derivations correspond bijectively to DP runs ending at s, and cut elimination is exactly isDPRun_of_score_eq_val.

Define the deduction system inductively in Lean, prove soundness against score_le_val and completeness against exists_dpRun_ending, and prove a cut-elimination theorem.

DP optimality becomes certifiable by small checkable proof terms rather than by recomputation.

No finitely axiomatised system captures the bounds, indicating that DP optimality is not finitely presentable as a logic.
proof_strategy: Take axioms for init and a cut rule composing a bound at stage n with a transition; soundness is score_le_val, completeness is the backtrace construction, and cut elimination follows from prefix optimality.
title: Bellman Cut Elimination

description:
High-precision computation shows the leading term L(u) = exp(-u(ln u + ln ln u - 1)) overshoots the Dickman function by a factor that grows with u (12.5 at u=2, 31 at u=14.75, 602 at u=40), so the leading term is only ever accurate in the exponent. The conjecture pins down the growth of that ratio.

L(u)/rho(u) = (1+o(1)) * sqrt(2*pi*u) * exp(u*(ln ln u - 1)/ln u) * C(u) with C(u) slowly varying and bounded between 1 and 4 for 10 <= u <= 100.

Extend the interval power-series computation of rho to u = 200 at 200-digit precision and fit ln(L/rho) - ln(sqrt(2 pi u)) - u(ln ln u - 1)/ln u; formalise the proved base case rho(u) = 1 - ln u on (1,2].

Gives a usable finite-u correction factor for smoothness estimates in sieve parameter selection, replacing the leading term.

The ratio has a genuinely different shape, indicating the saddle-point expansion of rho needs a further term at reachable u.
proof_strategy: Saddle-point analysis of the Laplace transform of rho, matched against the exact closed form on (1,2] and the delay differential equation u rho'(u) = -rho(u-1) which is formalised here.
title: Second-Order Ratio Law for the Dickman Leading Term

description:
A one-parameter additive score family visits few distinct top-B sets. Each unordered pair of slots crosses at most once as the weight grows, and only kept/evicted pairs can change the set, so the sweep should visit at most B(n-B)+1 distinct kept sets. This bounds the number of genuinely distinct policies any lambda-grid can test.

For scores a + lambda*p on n slots with budget B, the number of distinct sets S admitting IsTopSet (hybrid a p lambda) B S for some lambda >= 0 is at most B*(n-B)+1.

Formalise the breakpoint set {(a i - a j)/(p j - p i)} and show the kept set is constant between consecutive breakpoints, then count boundary pairs; test numerically by dense sweeps for n <= 9.

Any lambda-grid finer than B(n-B) points is provably redundant, bounding the cost of every future sweep experiment.

Additive families are richer than the crossing picture suggests, and grid design must be instance-dependent.
proof_strategy: Use probe_dominance_of_lambda_lt to show each pair swaps at most once, biject set changes with pair swaps across the kept/evicted boundary, and sum.
title: Boundary-Pair Bound for Additive Sweep Complexity

description:
The refuted conjecture becomes true once the class of theories is enlarged from the common refinement of capC and valSys to all finite transitive tag-indexed frames with a valuation. The approach is to place each tag's accessibility image at a prescribed rung of a single 'type ladder' built from a chain of worlds, a valuation cut, and per-tag activity windows. It matters because it would show that the height vector and the reflection-depth vector are genuinely independent coordinates of GL theories, with the only constraint being the pointwise inequality r i <= min N (d i).

For every N and all d r : Nat -> Nat with r i <= min N (d i) there is a consistent GL theory S with Provable S (box_i^k bot) iff min N (d i) < k, and DepthReflection r' i S iff r' <= r i, for every tag i.

Formalize a parametric frame family in Lean (worlds 0..M, per-tag window [b i, H i], valuation blockVal w) and prove the two spectra via provable_frameSys_box_iff for the upper bound and satF_congr_of_approx for the lower bound; test candidate parameter formulas first by exhaustive Boolean-algebra enumeration as in ComputationalEvidence.md.

The mission conjecture is correct after replacing the refinement class by all GL frames, and the height and reflection-depth vectors are free independent invariants.

There is a second, frame-independent inequality tying the two vectors, strictly stronger than the pointwise bound and the image-monotonicity principle; finding it would be a new structural theorem about GL.
proof_strategy: Fix M = 2N and the valuation cut w = N. Give the tag of class (h, rho) an interval image whose top exceeds w by exactly rho and whose length forces height h, using a three-parameter relation (source band and target cut) that is transitive by construction. Upper bound: the probe box_i^rho (atom 0) is true on the image and false at the world just above it. Lower bound: a bounded bisimulation E k identifying worlds with equal min(m, w + k) and equal window membership, fed into satF_congr_of_approx.
title: Full GL Realizability of Height-Depth Profiles

description:
The proved minimum-error law gives the exact error of any statistic-measurable policy. We conjecture that it also controls the mutual information between the statistic and the target, turning the campaign's bit-valued reports and its percentage-credited reports into two readings of one functional.

For a finite population P, statistic T and Boolean target s, the mutual information I(T; s) is at most H(s) - H(irredError P T s / |P|), with equality iff every class of T is pure or balanced.

Formalize empirical entropy on a Finset, prove the inequality from the class decomposition already used in err_eq_sum, and check it numerically on the populations of ComputationalEvidence.md Table 4.

Bits realized and percentage credited become formally interchangeable, and the 0 percent strict verdict becomes a zero-information theorem.

Error-based and information-based crediting are genuinely different functionals and the campaign must report both.
proof_strategy: Decompose the empirical joint distribution over T-classes, apply concavity of entropy per class, and bound the conditional entropy of s given T from below by the binary entropy of the class minority fraction.
title: Fano-Type Crediting Inequality

description:
The thresholds of BB84, the six-state protocol and their higher-dimensional analogues are zeros of Q-linear combinations of logarithms of rationals. The conjecture is that all are transcendental with unbounded continued-fraction partial quotients, and that each textbook percentage is a low-order convergent, as is verified here for 11/100 and p*.

Every QKD one-way threshold of the form 1 - a H_2(Q) - b H(f(Q)) = 0 with rational a,b is transcendental, and its convergents include the conventional percentage quoted in the literature.

Formalize the six-state rate function, run the certificate scheme at denominators 100 and 10000, and compare the convergents of the resulting enclosure with 12.6 percent.

A uniform explanation of why textbook QKD percentages are so short: they are convergents, hence optimal rational summaries.

Some protocol has a badly approximable threshold, which would itself be a striking arithmetic phenomenon.
proof_strategy: Baker's theorem for transcendence; the certificate equivalence plus newton_enclosure_step for the convergent computation.
title: Diophantine Genericity of QKD Threshold Spectra

description:
The forced displacement of the dial is now proved to equal 3/28 - 31/(10b) under the fitted law, hence to saturate at 10.7 percent and to cross the floor budget 3/40 exactly at bitlen 97. What remains open is whether the actual mechanism attains this lower bound up to a constant, which would make the observed dial a near-extremal rank perturbation.

The displaced fraction |A|/n of the recorded exp-538 rank vectors is bounded above by C times reqFrac (rhoModel b) for an absolute constant C and every measured bitlen b.

Instrument the exp-538 script to emit rank vectors, compute the displaced set exactly, and compare |A|/n against reqFrac rho for bitlens 44 to 92.

The erosion mechanism is near-extremal: it moves few observations very far, a checkable fingerprint that identifies the mechanism class.

The mechanism is diffuse and the crude per-coordinate bound is far from tight, so a second-moment refinement of the budget is needed.
proof_strategy: Combine reading_corruption_budget with an upper construction from block reversals, using the exact transposition increment of sumSqD_swap_exact.
title: Attainability of the Saturated Displacement Budget

description:
The proved equivalence markoff_uniqueness_iff_min_determined shows the middle entry is always forced by the outer pair. Hence the open uniqueness conjecture is a statement about the minimum alone, a strictly one-variable problem.

Uniqueness of the ordered Markoff triple given its maximum is equivalent to uniqueness of the minimum, and holds unconditionally for all maxima in the classified x = 1 and x = 2 fibres.

Prove uniqueness for maxima lying in the silver branch using markoff_min_two_classification, then attempt congruence obstructions for general maxima.

A new, strictly smaller formulation of the Markoff uniqueness conjecture, with two infinite families settled.

A counterexample to the reduction would be a counterexample to uniqueness itself, hence a famous result.
proof_strategy: Combine markoff_middle_unique with the pairwise coprimality invariant MReach.isCoprime and quadratic residue conditions on the maximum.
title: One-Variable Reduction of Markoff Uniqueness

description:
Chaining r dials into one integer is injective precisely under a mixed-radix condition on the frame vector. Failure at any level collapses the label set by a computable factor, so a linear pass over the frames certifies or refutes an entire pipeline. This generalises the two-dial width criterion already proved.

The map (a_1,...,a_r) |-> sum_i a_i * M_i with a_i < B_i and M_1 = 1 is injective on the product of alphabets if and only if M_{i+1} >= B_i * M_i for all i; when the condition first fails at level i the image cardinality drops by the factor prod(B_j) / (M_{i+1}(B_i - 1)/M_i + B_i)-style expression inherited from the two-dial count.

Induct on r, reducing to ChainedLabelWidth.chain_inj_of_lt at each level; formalise the count by iterating chain_image_eq_range.

Whole-pipeline width certification becomes a single linear-time check with a Lean proof behind it.

Injectivity would depend on the alphabet contents and not only on their sizes, which would make static width checking impossible and force run-time collision detection.
proof_strategy: Induction on the number of dials with the division-based injectivity argument as the inductive step; counterexample construction at the first violated level.
title: Mixed-Radix Width Calculus for Multi-Dial Chaining

description:
Strict submultiplicativity of the memoryless Shtarkov sum was proved here from a single deficient pair of constant strings. The conjecture upgrades it to a uniform constant factor, which would give a quantitative Fekete rate rather than mere convergence. The route is per-type accounting using the Bernoulli machinery already formalised.

For a binary alphabet and n₁, n₂ ≥ 1, Cₛ(n₁+n₂) ≤ (3/4)·Cₛ(n₁)·Cₛ(n₂); hence log₂ Cₛ(n)/n → 0.

Extend maxLik_tied_const_le_quarter from constant strings to all pairs of strings with distinct empirical types, then sum the deficits over the type decomposition.

A quantitative Fekete rate for universal compression of memoryless sources, with explicit constants.

The deficit is concentrated on few string pairs, indicating that the tied-product view is too coarse for rates.
proof_strategy: Type decomposition: bound the tied envelope on each pair of type classes by the product of envelopes times an explicit factor determined by the two empirical distributions.
title: Uniform Multiplicative Deficit for the Memoryless Price

description:
The proof that well-ordered chains of Hausdorff dimensions are countable used only order-density of the rationals in the codomain. Abstracting it yields a ceiling theorem for every monotone invariant valued in a linear order with a countable order-dense subset: box, packing, Assouad and conformal dimension included.

If L is a linear order with a countable order-dense subset, every well-founded subset of L is countable; hence no uncountable strictly increasing well-ordered chain of such invariants exists.

Refactor countable_of_isWF to the abstract setting and instantiate at ℝ≥0∞ and at any future Mathlib dimension invariant.

No fractal invariant of this type can index an ℵ₁-hierarchy — the aleph-one slogan is impossible for structural, not accidental, reasons.

Some invariant has a codomain without countable order-density, opening the door to genuinely transfinite dimension scales.
proof_strategy: For each non-maximal element of a well-founded set take its immediate successor and insert a member of the countable dense set into the gap; distinct elements get distinct members.
title: Cardinal Ceiling for General Fractal Invariants

description:
The least number of switches sw(P) needed to represent a finite bounded poset P as a bounded morphic image of a Boolean cube is not determined by cardinality and height. We conjecture an exact formula in terms of a cover-branching profile counting the points that must be entered by a dedicated switch. This would turn the proved upper bound |P|-1 and the two lower bounds into a single exact invariant.

sw(P) equals the maximum over maximal chains C of (|C| - 1) plus the number of points that must be entered from C by a single extra switch; in particular sw is not a function of (|P|, height P).

Exhaustively compute sw for all bounded posets on at most 7 points with the openness-pruned assignment search, and compare with the candidate formula; formalise the resulting upper bound as a refinement of representable_card_sub_one.

The greedy climb is optimal for every finite bounded poset and sw becomes a computable order invariant.

The gap between the cardinality and height bounds hides a genuinely new obstruction, most likely of width type.
proof_strategy: Upper bound by running the greedy climb along a chain-adapted linear extension using only the branching switches; lower bound by lifting a chain plus a counting argument on the rank grading.
title: Switch Number as an Order Invariant

description:
The sensitivity lower bound on tasting time proved in this cycle is conjectured to be polynomially tight: deterministic query complexity of a dish is at most the fourth power of its maximal pivotal-set size. The approach chains the formalised bound s(f) ≤ D(f) with a block-sensitivity layer and the already proved product bound D ≤ C0·C1. It would make 'find one pivotal ingredient' a complete design principle for tasting protocols.

For every dish f : Pantry n → Bool, tasteCost f ≤ (max over x of (pivotalSet f x).card) ^ 4.

Formalise block sensitivity bs(f), prove C(f) ≤ s(f)·bs(f) and bs(f) ≤ s(f)^2, then combine with the existing tasteCost_le_cert_mul.

Kitchen verification time is controlled by a purely local quantity, computable from single-ingredient swaps.

There is a dish with tiny local sensitivity but expensive global tasting, i.e. a genuinely non-local recipe.
