title: Sensitivity–Tasting Polynomial Equivalence

description:
Ask when a single structural invariant generates all recoverable interpretations of a finite graph. The conjecture is that the degree interpretation is complete exactly for graphs whose automorphism orbits coincide with degree classes. This connects the definability boundary to graph reconstruction questions.

For a finite graph Γ, every recoverable interpretation factors through the degree map iff any two vertices of equal degree lie in the same Aut(Γ)-orbit.

Formalise the two partitions (degree classes and orbits) as Setoids and prove the factorisation equivalence; test on the 3-path (positive) and on a vertex-transitive-looking but asymmetric regular graph (negative).

Degree becomes a certified complete invariant for a precisely delimited class of graphs.

There are graphs where degree classes equal orbits yet some recoverable interpretation is not a function of degree, contradicting the orbit factorisation and forcing a re-examination of the orbit quotient.
proof_strategy: Use recoverable_factors_uniquely to reduce to comparing the orbit partition with the degree partition; build counterexamples from regular graphs with small automorphism groups.
title: Degree Completeness for Graph Interpretations

description:
For (q+1)-regular graphs the matrices counting non-backtracking walks of length m between vertices should satisfy a three-term recursion A_{m+1} = A A_m - q A_{m-1}, making them Chebyshev-like polynomials in the adjacency matrix. This turns the dart-indexed Hashimoto matrix into a vertex-indexed polynomial calculus. It would give closed formulas for trace(B^n) in terms of the adjacency spectrum.

For a (q+1)-regular graph, A_1 = A, A_2 = A^2 - (q+1)I and A_{m+1} = A A_m - q A_{m-1}, where A_m counts non-backtracking walks of length m between vertices.

Formalise A_m as a counting matrix using the vertex characterisation already proved, then prove the recursion by splitting a walk of length m+1 at its last step and correcting the single forbidden backtracking pattern.

trace(B^n) becomes computable from the adjacency spectrum alone for regular graphs, and Ramanujan bounds follow from Chebyshev estimates.

The correction term is not local, meaning non-backtracking counts genuinely need the dart-level matrix even in the regular case.
proof_strategy: Induct on m using the vertex form of the trace theorem; the inclusion-exclusion for the forbidden pattern u_{i+2} = u_i contributes exactly the -q A_{m-1} term via the constant row sum q.
title: Chebyshev Recursion for Non-Backtracking Walk Matrices

description:
Aggregation rules on the simplex become maps of the positive orthant of a sphere under the square-root embedding. Combining the spherical contraction lemma of the Arrow–Curvature file with the length functional proved here should show that Fisher-Lipschitz unanimous aggregators are strictly L¹-contractive unless dictatorial.

Every continuous unanimous aggregation rule that does not increase Fisher–Rao length is L¹-contractive on pairs of distinct profiles, with contraction constant strictly below 1 unless the rule is a coordinate projection.

Formalize Fisher-Lipschitz aggregation on the open simplex, apply l1_le_fisherRao_length to the image of a geodesic, and use cos_midpoint_ge_avg for the strict contraction.

Provides a metric, curvature-driven version of Arrow-type impossibility inside the catalog.

Positive curvature alone would not obstruct fair aggregation, isolating the combinatorial content of Arrow's theorem.
proof_strategy: Transport curves through the aggregator, bound the image length by the source length, then apply the strict spherical midpoint contraction.
title: Curvature Obstruction for Fisher-Lipschitz Aggregation

description:
Uncompensated RTN attains an l1 defect of n*Delta/2 exactly on coherent-sign configurations. Error feedback re-injects the signed residual, which should destroy coherence and reduce the worst case to O(sqrt(n)*Delta).

For the error-feedback quantizer with unit mesh, the accumulated defect over n coordinates is bounded by Delta/2 uniformly in n, and the resulting loss defect is O(sqrt(n)) rather than O(n).

Formalize the error-feedback recursion in Lean and prove the running-residual invariant; validate numerically against per-channel RTN on the same tensors.

Compensation dominates scale choice below the empirical cliff, with a proof rather than an experiment.

The coherent worst case survives compensation, and only outlier handling helps.
proof_strategy: Show the feedback residual stays in [-Delta/2, Delta/2] by induction, then telescope the partial sums.
title: Square-Root Law for Error-Feedback Quantization

description:
Two-client Bresenham service times realise the classical two-gap (Sturmian) structure. Composing Bresenham splittings along a tree of depth d should yield a gap spectrum of bounded size, quantifying how much regularity survives recursion.

For a splitting tree of depth d, the set of gaps between consecutive services of any fixed client has at most 2^d + 1 elements; for d = 1 it is exactly {floor(R/r), ceil(R/r)}.

Prove the d = 1 case in Lean from the existing waiting-window theorems, then induct on the tree using schedCnt_node_left/right; test the general bound by enumeration for d = 2, 3.

Recursive Bresenham schedules are quasi-Sturmian, giving strong burstiness guarantees on top of the discrepancy bound.

The gap spectrum blows up, showing that low discrepancy does not imply bounded gap complexity.
proof_strategy: Express a depth-d service time as a composition of depth-1 Beatty maps and apply the three-distance theorem level by level, tracking how many gap values each composition can create.
title: Gap Spectrum of Recursive Bresenham Words

description:
The exponent ℓ(M) = |M| − #orbits measures how much external meaning structural truth destroys; this cycle proved it additive over disjoint unions and equal to the sum over orbits of (orbit size − 1). The remaining question is the behaviour under the diagonal action on a product, where orbit counts can exceed the product of the factor counts. A clean superadditivity law would complete the calculus of meaning loss for composite systems.

For nonempty finite G-models M and N with the diagonal action on M × N, ℓ(M × N) ≥ ℓ(M) + ℓ(N), with equality precisely when one factor is rigid or the point stabilisers of the two factors are mutually cofinal.

Formalise the product action's orbit count via stabiliser intersections and compare with meaningLoss_eq_sum_orbits; test small cyclic and symmetric actions exhaustively by #eval before proving.

Meaning loss becomes a computable superadditive invariant of group actions, composable across systems.

Composite systems can lose less meaning than their parts, indicating destructive interference between symmetry groups.
proof_strategy: Decompose both sides by meaningLoss_eq_sum_orbits and bound the orbit sizes of the diagonal action below by the maximum of the factor orbit sizes using the orbit-stabiliser theorem.
title: Superadditivity of Meaning Loss Under Product Actions

description:
The minimal coefficient-l1 norm of a nonzero integer polynomial divisible by (X-1)^K is conjectured to be exactly 2K for every K. The lower bound 2K is now a theorem via Newton's identities, and equality is equivalent to the existence of an ideal Prouhet-Tarry-Escott configuration of size K. Settling it would determine the exact cost of invisibility to a power-sum window of any length.

For every K >= 1, minMass K = 2K; equivalently an ideal PTE pair of size K exists for every K.

Extend the certified witness table beyond K = 12 inside Catalog/Applications/PTEIdealWitnesses.lean, or prove a nonexistence obstruction that contradicts minMass K = 2K for some K.

The mass invariant is linear, the exponential upper bound 24^(K/12) is vacuous asymptotically, and the classical PTE existence problem is resolved affirmatively.

Some window has minMass K >= 2K + 2, giving the first proven nonlinear jump in the invariant and the first proven nonexistence of an ideal PTE configuration.
proof_strategy: Work in the polynomial model minMass K = min l1 over nonzero P with (X-1)^K | P; build P as a sparse product with controlled cancellation, or derive an obstruction from valuations of coefficients at small primes.
title: Polynomial Mass Growth for Truncated Power-Sum Windows

description:
The finite LLL proved in this thread already carries the lopsided one-sided hypothesis, so it applies beyond product spaces. The open problem is to certify the lopsided bound for the uniform distribution on permutations by an explicit injection, unlocking Latin-square avoidance theorems with no measure theory.

For the uniform measure on Equiv.Perm (Fin n), pattern events A_(i,j) satisfy P(A_(i,j) and avoid S) <= P(A_(i,j)) * P(avoid S) whenever S avoids the row/column dependency set, hence Latin squares avoiding a sparse forbidden set exist when e*p*(d+1) <= 1.

Build the uniform FinProbSpace on permutations, prove the lopsided bound by an explicit injection, and instantiate lovasz_local_lemma_symmetric.

First verified non-product application of the local lemma, covering Latin squares.

The failing injection exhibits a dependency pattern with positive correlation, of independent interest.
proof_strategy: Represent avoid S as a set of permutations; construct an injection from the permutations in A_(i,j) intersect avoid S into pairs (permutation in avoid S, choice of image), and count.
title: Lopsided Dependency Certificates for Permutation Problems

description:
Every normalised spectral moment of the symmetric Rademacher ensemble should converge to the corresponding semicircle moment. Polynomiality reduces this to a single leading coefficient, and the odd orders are already exact at finite N.

For every m, expect (normalizedMoment (W ·) m) tends to WignerSemicircle.semicircleMoment m as N tends to infinity.

Combine EvenWalks.evenClosedWalkCount_eq_sum_choose with the conjectured top shape count and take limits of the explicit rational function of N.

The moment method for the semicircle law is complete at all orders for this ensemble, with exact finite-N formulas at every order.

Either the shape counts grow faster than the degree bound allows or the semicircle moments are not the limits, contradicting the verified orders 2, 4 and 6.
proof_strategy: Write the moment as a finite sum of binomials over shape counts, divide by N^(k+1), and use that C(N,r)/N^(k+1) tends to 0 for r < k+1 and to 1/(k+1)! for r = k+1.
title: All-Order Semicircle Convergence in Expectation

description:
Witness A shows that alpha_1 + alpha_2 - 1 fails for k >= 2, with a loss of exactly one further vertex. We conjecture the loss disappears in the fractional relaxation: the fractional independence number satisfies the minus-one bound for every k. This would identify the minus-two defect as an integrality gap phenomenon rather than a structural one.

For every clique sum, alpha_f(G) >= alpha_f(G_1) + alpha_f(G_2) - 1, where alpha_f is the fractional independence number (LP relaxation over cliques).

Compute alpha_f on Witness A and on all enumerated k = 2 and k = 3 shapes; then formalise using the fractional transversal machinery already in the catalog.

The minus-two loss is an integrality gap of exactly one, quantifying the LP-IP gap for clique sums.

A fractional counterexample would show the loss is structural and would sharpen the trace calculus to fractional traces.
proof_strategy: Take optimal fractional independent sets on each side, average their K-restrictions, and use that a fractional independent set puts total weight at most 1 on a clique.
title: Purely Integral Nature of the Minus-Two Defect

description:
Strict loss under merging means that any collision leaves a measurable trace in the label entropy of a full-support population. Comparing the measured label entropy against the declared alphabet product then detects collisions from a single run, with no cross-check needed.

If a population has full support on A x B and the measured label entropy is strictly below the entropy of the pair variable, then the encoding is non-injective; quantitatively the shortfall is at least 1/(A*B) bits per merged pair.

Combine LabelEntropy.D_pos_of_two_positive with H_sub_H_push to derive the shortfall bound, then instantiate on the audited 4 x 9 population as in narrow_frame_strictly_loses.

Every past run in the ledger can be re-audited from its stored entropy value alone.

Some collisions are entropy-neutral, which can only happen off full support, and the audit would need support certification first.
proof_strategy: Per-fiber strict deficit plus the fiber decomposition of the entropy loss, with the explicit two-atom lower bound already used for the 1/18 gap.
title: Single-Run Collision Detection by Entropy Shortfall

description:
The zero-sum indicator on the k-fold product of a finite abelian group should be orthogonal to every predictor that is a sum of functions each omitting at least one coordinate. We proved the k = 2 and k = 3 cases; the general case follows the same conditional-mean argument. It matters because it tells an encoding search, in advance, exactly which degrees cannot possibly help.

For a finite abelian group G, k >= 2, y(x) = [x_1 + ... + x_k = 0] on G^k, and any family of functions h_S depending only on coordinates in S with |S| < k, cov(y, sum_S h_S) = 0 exactly; moreover the degree-1..(k-1) ceiling of y is 0 and the degree-k encoding attains R^2 = 1.

Formalise by induction on the omitted coordinate: for fixed values of the coordinates in S, the conditional mean of y over the omitted coordinate is 1/|G|; conclude cov = 0 as in cov_triAlign_pairwise_eq_zero.

Any joint-alignment excess of order k is provably invisible below degree k, so encoding rounds can be pruned to the single relevant degree.

Some sub-degree encoding correlates with zero-sum alignment, which would expose an asymmetry between the group structure and the product measure worth isolating.
proof_strategy: Marginalise over the omitted coordinate using the group inverse (a unique solution of the zero-sum equation), exactly as in sum_triAlign_mul_snd_thd; then apply msse_ge_varr_of_cov_eq_zero.
title: Degree-k Blindness for k-Fold Zero-Sum Alignment

description:
Replace the layer count in serveCost by the covering number of the family of fine-tune tails at the margin scale. Models whose tails lie within eps of a common center can share the tail as well, giving the amortized law n*r + min(D,n).

Serving n fine-tunes with guaranteed decision agreement costs s + N(eps) * (L - s) memory, where N(eps) is the eps-covering number of the tail family in the coordinatewise sup metric, and this is optimal.

Formalize the covering argument on top of shared_core_agreement_bound; measure N(eps) empirically for a family of fine-tunes of one base model.

Multi-fine-tune serving cost is governed by the diversity of tails, not their number.

Tails are essentially in general position and per-model tail storage is unavoidable.

title: Covering-Number Serving Law

description:
Because the second-order term can oppose the first, the audit gap need not be monotone in temperature. Conjecture: there are explicit finite models whose hacked set {beta : |G(beta)| >= eps} is disconnected, so a system can be safe at one temperature and hacked both below and above it.

There exist a three-point model and eps > 0 for which {beta >= R : |G(beta)| >= eps} is not an interval.

Search inside the biased two-point family of SharpOrder.lean extended by a third response, then certify the two crossings and the intermediate safe temperature by interval arithmetic in Lean.

Monitoring at a single temperature is unsound; the supremum definition of beta_c used here is the only robust one.

The audit gap is unimodal in beta, which would upgrade the sharp threshold to a genuine phase transition with a single crossing.

title: Non-Interval Hacked Sets from Sign-Changing Skew Covariance

description:
The associative-triple count is multiplicative under products of magmas. This turns the associativity density into a multiplicative invariant and suggests a Dirichlet generating function whose coefficients are powers of A(M), linking coherence defects to analytic bookkeeping.

A(M^k) = A(M)^k for all k, hence 1 - d(M^k) = (1 - d(M))^k, and the generating function Z_M(s) = sum_k A(M)^k k^{-s} determines A(M); every non-associative magma is asymptotically totally non-associative under powering while its codiscrete bicategory stays coherent.

Iterate assocCount_prod in Lean to get A(M^k) = A(M)^k by induction and derive the density limit; check numerically for the order-3 maximiser.

Coherence defects admit an Euler-product bookkeeping, connecting magma combinatorics to Dirichlet-series methods.

Multiplicativity fails to extend beyond binary products, isolating a genuine obstruction in iterated products.
proof_strategy: Induct on k using the proved binary multiplicativity, then take logs of densities.
title: Euler Product for Associativity Density

description:
Quantify how far an arbitrary interpretation is from being recoverable. The conjecture is that the minimal number of reassignments equals the sum over orbits of the orbit size minus the largest value multiplicity, achieved by majority vote within each orbit. This yields an approximate version of the classification theorem.

For finite M and I : M → V, min over recoverable J of |{x : I x ≠ J x}| equals Σ_{orbits O} (|O| − max_v |{x ∈ O : I x = v}|).

Formalise the repair distance as a Finset.card minimum over the recoverable subtype and prove matching upper and lower bounds orbit by orbit.

The definability boundary becomes robust: near-recoverable interpretations are quantitatively characterised.

Global correlations between orbits would allow cheaper repairs than the orbit-local bound, revealing hidden structure in the orbit quotient.

title: Orbit-Wise Majority Repair Distance

description:
Measured joint capacities sit far below their CRT ceilings. We conjecture the shortfall is governed by the occupancy of a random table: with N samples and M joint cells, the attained alphabet is concentrated around M(1-(1-1/M)^N), and the capacity is within o(1) of log2 of that quantity. This turns the observed gap into a predictable law rather than an artefact.

For a battery whose joint reading is uniform on M cells and a sample of N i.i.d. individuals, the empirical capacity satisfies log2(M(1-(1-1/M)^N)) - o(1) <= I <= min(log2 N, log2 M) with probability tending to 1.

Formalise the occupancy expectation and a Chernoff bound for the number of occupied cells, then combine with TraceBattery.H_le_log_card_img and a matching lower bound on H for near-uniform distributions.

The measured values 7.9455 / 10.4462 / 12.1080 become predictions of N alone, giving an independent estimate of the population size.

The shortfall encodes structure of the trace statistics (non-uniformity of dial readings), which would be a stronger and more interesting finding.

title: Sparse-Table Capacity Law for Dial Batteries

description:
Curvature equal to 1 certifies that some model in the pool adds nothing on top of the others, and duplicated models force curvature 1. The conjecture is a quantitative converse making curvature a statistical test for model copying in a deployed pool, with sample complexity governed by the proved bound kappa >= 1 - (|Omega| - 1) delta.

There are constants such that any pool whose curvature is at most 1 - epsilon contains no pair of sources at total-variation distance below epsilon/(|Omega| - 1), and epsilon-accurate curvature estimation from samples requires O(|X| / epsilon^2) samples per model.

The exact two-source law curvature_pair (kappa = 1 - delta) already gives the pairwise statement; add an empirical-Shtarkov concentration bound to turn it into a sample-complexity claim.

Curvature becomes an auditable statistic for detecting duplicated or distilled models in a pool.

Curvature conflates duplication with other degeneracies, and a finer invariant separating them is needed.

title: Curvature as a Model-Duplication Detector

description:
The Pell recursion of the spine has reciprocal characteristic polynomial 1 - 6X + X^2, which factors through the Satake-like parameters 3 +- 2 sqrt 2. Since these have product 1 rather than the residue norm 2, the resulting Dirichlet series is an L-function of a unit, not of an automorphic form; its analytic behaviour should be governed entirely by log(3 + 2 sqrt 2).

The Dirichlet series sum over n of c_n^{-s}, where c_n is the n-th spine hypotenuse, converges for Re(s) > 0, extends meromorphically, and its rightmost singularity is at s = 0 with the exponential scale log(3 + 2 sqrt 2) controlling the local expansion.

Use the proved Binet formula to compare the series with the geometric series in (3+2 sqrt 2)^{-s} and formalize the resulting convergence and comparison estimates.

Gives an explicit non-automorphic L-function attached to the tree, sharply separating unit L-factors from Hilbert modular ones.

The comparison fails because of the correction term in Binet's formula, revealing arithmetic content beyond the leading eigenvalue.

#{Berggren nodes with hypotenuse <= X and quality > 1} >> X^{theta} for some theta > 0.

description:
The residue modulus that realises the coupling bit should be exactly the conductor of the quadratic resolvent, i.e. |disc| stripped of square factors and adjusted at 2. Here it is verified for -243, -108 (modulus 3) and -23 (modulus 23).

description:
The sufficient-statistic bound Cₛ ≤ #σ is saturated exactly when every fibre of the statistic carries a full unit of maximum-likelihood mass. For memoryless sources this would require a parameter making the law uniform on a whole type class, which product laws cannot do for several types at once. Proving non-saturation would show the (n+1)^{#A} bound is never tight.

The method-of-types upper bound is never attained, so the true constant in the Rissanen rate is strictly smaller.

title: Non-Saturation of the Method-of-Types Bound

description:
The exact grouping gain identity says the repaired damage bound is half the total amplitude deficit. Hence the fraction of damage repaired by group-g quantization should equal one minus the ratio of mean group amplitude to global amplitude, a checkpoint statistic.

For a fixed tensor, the ratio (grouped worst-case bound)/(per-channel worst-case bound) equals mean_g(A_g)/max(A), and the measured cross-entropy repair tracks this ratio monotonically.

Compute mean/max amplitude ratios per group size on a released checkpoint and compare with measured delta-CE repair across group sizes 32/64/128/256.

Group size can be chosen analytically from weight statistics, with no evaluation sweep.

Damage is dominated by outlier channels rather than aggregate dispersion, favouring outlier-aware schemes.

title: Amplitude-Dispersion Law for Group-Wise Repair

description:
The exchange distance from a chamber to a cell is |T \\ {i}|, a quantity in which the weights do not appear. We conjecture that the exchange metric therefore remembers only the support, in sharp contrast with the aggregator (which remembers everything) and the labelling (which remembers the weights modulo a constant).

For any two weight systems delta, delta' on the same support S, the exchange metrics of the two complexes are isometric via the identity on labels; and bounded-size exchange metrics already recover delta modulo a constant.

Prove the first half from exchange_distance; for the second half, restrict to moves of size at most one voter with a prescribed budget and compute which walls are reachable.

Completes a three-level hierarchy of invariants: metric < labelling < function, with exactly identified loss at each level.

The exchange metric secretly encodes numerical data, which would be surprising given its combinatorial formula.

title: Weight-Blindness of the Exchange Metric

description:
Cycle 4 proves the analytic order of vanishing of the completed function Lambda_E at the central point agrees with the central multiplicity m_+ modulo 2. Conjecture that the two are equal on the nose, because the substitution T = exp(-sL) is a local biholomorphism.

For a duality eigensystem over the complex numbers with Q not equal to 1 and exp L = Q, analyticOrderAt (completedL E L) 1 = m_+.

Transport the algebraic factorisation P(T) = (1 - QT)^{m_+} G(T), G(Q^{-1}) nonzero, through T = exp(-sL) and compute analyticOrderAt of the resulting product.

description:
Construct the Böttcher conjugacy on the escaping region of the quadratic family as the complex refinement of the escape rate already formalised. The modulus of the Böttcher map is exp of the Green's function, so the convergence proof reuses the telescoping estimate log_distortion verbatim on complex logarithms. description:
The equal-volume peeling has maximal thickness exactly R N^{-1/d}, attained at the innermost shell. The conjecture is that this is optimal among equal-volume peelings and quantifies the loss relative to the equally spaced peeling.

min over equal-volume peelings of max_k (r_k - r_{k+1}) equals R N^{-1/d}, while min over all peelings equals R/N; the ratio is N^{1-1/d}.

Formalise the two optimisation problems for finite N and small d; the equal-volume constraint fixes the radii, so the first claim is a uniqueness statement.

Equal-volume peelings are the canonical worst case for thickness, justifying their use as a benchmark.

Some non-uniform volume allocation beats the ratio N^{1-1/d}, giving a better peeling ladder.

description:
Completeness of the invariant reduces the question of which finite gap sets are realisable by machines to the arithmetic classification of numerical semigroups by genus, an actively studied counting problem.

A finite set G ⊆ ℕ is the gap set of some machine iff G is the gap set of a numerical semigroup; consequently the number of machines with exactly g gaps, up to bisimulation, is the number of numerical semigroups of genus g.

Enumerate numerical semigroups of small genus and match with gap sets computed from chain machines.

Machine-realisability of gap patterns is exactly the genus classification, importing its asymptotics into computation theory.

Machines realise gap patterns not coming from numerical semigroups, so the invariant sees more than arithmetic.

title: Prescribed Gap Sets of Machines

description:
Every primitive Pythagorean triple has a unique address word over the three Berggren letters. Reading that word in a larger alphabet at each stage is a Goodstein-style base bump, and subtracting one letter is the Goodstein decrement. The conjecture is that the resulting sequence of triples always reaches (3,4,5), with termination equivalent to transfinite induction below omega^omega.

For every primitive Pythagorean triple t, the Pythagorean Goodstein sequence starting at t reaches (3,4,5) in finitely many steps, and this statement is equivalent over PRA to TI(omega^omega).

Define the base-bump on List BStep, prove termination by the ordinal assignment sum k^{position}, and compute the sequence for the first several triples in Lean by #eval.

A Goodstein theorem whose objects are Pythagorean triples, with an exactly calibrated proof-theoretic strength.

Some sequence cycles or diverges, which would contradict addr_injective and hence expose a hidden non-freeness of the tree.
proof_strategy: Assign to a word the ordinal in Cantor normal form given by its letters; base bumping preserves the ordinal, decrementing lowers it; conclude by well-foundedness of omega^omega.
title: Pythagorean Goodstein Sequences via Address Base-Bumping

description:
Hauptmoduln of genus-zero groups sit inside the corrected-product group, but the group operation should destroy modularity immediately. The conjecture asks that each complex one-parameter subgroup meets the modular locus in finitely many points, quantifying how far McKay-Thompson series are from being closed under the operation.

For a McKay-Thompson series T, the set {r : ℂ | T^{⋆r} is the q-expansion of a hauptmodul} is finite (in fact {0,1}).

Combine the coefficient scaling law coeffAt_cpow with the integrality and Hecke-type recursions satisfied by hauptmodul coefficients; contradiction for r outside a finite set.

The corrected product is a strictly non-modular operation: moonshine data generate free directions inside the group.

There is a hidden one-parameter family of modular functions, which would be a striking new structure.
proof_strategy: Use the replication formulae for McKay-Thompson coefficients as polynomial constraints, and the linear scaling of the depth invariant to show at most finitely many r satisfy them.
title: Transversality of the Modular Locus

description:
For any Galois extension with group G, the Chebotarev channel from residue class to Frobenius class should carry exactly log2 of the index of the commutator subgroup. This unifies the S3 one-bit law with the cyclic-cubic log2 3 law already proved. It turns an information-theoretic constant into a group-theoretic invariant.

I(residue mod conductor ; Frobenius class) = log2 [G : G'] for every finite Galois group G with the Chebotarev joint law.

Instantiate S3General.Imut_eq_logb_card_of_coupling with D = G/G', B = conjugacy classes weighted by class size, and verify the balance hypotheses by decide for all transitive groups of degree at most 5.

The channel value becomes a computable invariant of the Galois group, and 1.0000 is exactly the signature of an index-2 commutator quotient.

There exist groups where the residue class sees more than the abelianisation, contradicting class field theory; the coupling model would need conductor-dependent corrections.
proof_strategy: Show the joint table factors as n(a,c) = [chi(a) = pi(c)] * m(c) with pi : classes -> G/G' well defined (abelianisation is constant on conjugacy classes), then apply the coupling-quotient law; balance follows from the equidistribution of G/G' fibres.
title: Abelianised Frobenius Capacity Law

description:
The greedy largest-lag rule appears to keep every client within one service unit of its ideal share for every rate profile and client count. The lead half of this is already proved; the lag half requires controlling cancellation among the other clients' leads. Establishing it would give a fully online, formally verified schedule matching the optimal Tijdeman-type discrepancy.

For all k, all positive rate profiles r with R = sum r_i, all i < k and all t: |R * count_i(t) - r_i * t| < R for the greedy largest-lag schedule.

Extend Catalog/Novelty/FairScheduleGreedy.lean: strengthen glag_upper from (k-1)(R-1) to R-1 by an induction on t with a potential function on the sorted lag vector; falsify by an exhaustive search over profiles with k <= 6 and rates <= 12.

An explicit, online, formally verified unit-fair schedule for arbitrary positive rates, strictly better than the log-depth tree bound.

A concrete profile where greedy fails, isolating the exact cancellation mechanism that Tijdeman-style constructions must repair.
proof_strategy: Use sum_glag (lags sum to zero) plus one_le_obj_greedy; order the lags and show the greedy step is a contraction of the largest-lag potential, so the maximum lag can never cross R.
title: Unit-Fair Greedy Scheduling

description:
The unconditional bound q > 2/3 is proved for every Berggren node. The conjecture is that 2/3 is exactly the infimum, approached along the near-isoceles Pell branch. The approach is to produce infinitely many nodes whose abc-product is squarefree, or has radical (abc)^{1-o(1)}.

inf over Berggren tree nodes of q = 2/3, and the infimum is not attained; along the B-spine, q_n = 2/3 + O(1/log c_n) for infinitely many n.

Formalize a squarefree-values result for the quadratic forms giving the near-isoceles legs, then combine with BerggrenABC.two_thirds_lt_quality and the growth law bHyp_bounds.

The lower edge of the abc quality spectrum is exactly computed for an infinite family, the first such result.

Radicals of near-isoceles Pythagorean legs are systematically deficient, itself a striking arithmetic phenomenon.
proof_strategy: Squarefree sieve for c = m^2+n^2 and legs along the Pell recursion; upper-bound the powerful part by a standard x^{1/2} count and compare with the exponential growth of c_n.
title: Sharp Lower Edge of the Pythagorean Quality Spectrum

description:
Our converse shows any correct protocol needs V(n,t) distinguishable transcripts in the worst case. The conjecture upgrades this to an expected-length bound over a noise distribution, showing interaction (Cascade-style) saves at most O(1) bits. Approach: freeze one party's input to reduce interaction to a one-way code, then apply Kraft's inequality to the induced prefix-free encoding.

For every correct two-way reconciliation protocol on n-bit keys with correction radius t, the expected transcript length under errors uniform on the radius-t sphere is at least log2 V(n,t) - c for an absolute constant c.

Formalise expected transcript length for a Protocol with a finite binary-string alphabet, and combine Protocol.transcript_injOn_ball with the Kraft inequality already in Computation.KraftConverse.

Adaptive reconciliation protocols carry no asymptotic leakage advantage over syndrome coding.

There is a genuinely interactive protocol with sub-sphere-packing average leakage, which would be a new primitive for QKD post-processing.
proof_strategy: Freeze Bob's input at 0; injectivity on the ball gives a uniquely decodable code on the ball; Kraft plus Jensen yields the expected-length bound.
title: Interactive Advantage Collapse for Two-Way Reconciliation

description:
The path-shaped completeness theorem should generalise to rooted finite trees, with the Chapman-Kolmogorov identity replaced by an interchange law between the sup over children and addition across siblings. The proof should reuse sup'_add and add_sup' unchanged, inducting on tree depth. This unifies Viterbi decoding with belief propagation on trees.

For a DP specification on a finite rooted tree assigning weights to parent-child state pairs, every labelling of the tree is dominated by a run of the bottom-up DP, and the bottom-up value is the greatest achievable score with a given root state.

Define an inductive rooted tree with a finite state space, define bottom-up val, and re-prove score_le_val, exists_dpRun_ending and dp_complete by structural induction.

A single formal framework covers path and tree DP, and the tree-decomposition case becomes a corollary.

The interchange law fails without extra hypotheses, revealing that path DP completeness is genuinely one-dimensional.
proof_strategy: Structural induction on the tree; at a node, use add_sup' once per child and Finset.sup'_comm to reorder, exactly as in walk_chapman_kolmogorov.
title: Tree-Shaped Dynamic Programming Completeness

description:
After reconciliation the key is uniform on a coset of the code. We conjecture a leftover-hash statement relative to that coset: hashing to ℓ bits leaves guessing probability at most 2^(ℓ-(n-m)) for perfect schemes. This makes the reconciliation-then-amplification pipeline end-to-end verifiable.

For a perfect separating scheme and a 2-universal linear hash family G to ℓ bits, max over strategies of the probability of guessing G(a) from (transcript, hash description) is at most 2^(ℓ-(n-m)) + ε with ε the usual smoothing term.

Instantiate exists_large_fiber_pair with the hash as second component and count collisions within a single coset using Scheme.card_consistent_transcript.

Gives a fully formal secret-key-rate theorem n - m - O(log 1/ε) for syndrome reconciliation.

Coset structure interacts badly with universal hashing, forcing extra entropy loss in QKD post-processing.
proof_strategy: Reduce to a collision-count on a coset, which is a translate of a subspace, and apply the standard second-moment bound.
title: Coset Leftover Hashing After Reconciliation

description: In homotopy type theory (HoTT), equal things can be equal in different ways — there can be multiple paths between two points. Apply this to cooking: two recipes can produce the same dish, but the paths (methods) may differ. The type of a dish is its flavor profile (a point in taste space R^n where n is the number of flavor dimensions). Two recipes are 'equal' if they produce the same flavor profile, but the path between them (the transformation from one recipe to another) may not be unique. Conjecture: The space of all recipes that produce a given flavor profile has the homotopy type of a CW-complex whose cells correspond to the possible ingredient substitutions. For example, the space of recipes that produce 'chocolate chip cookies' has the homotopy type of S^0 (two points: with nuts and without nuts), because the only binary choice is nuts/no-nuts. More complex dishes have higher homotopy groups: the space of recipes for 'curry' has pi_1 = Z (generated by the loop 'add more spice -> simmer -> add more coconut milk -> simmer -> add more spice'), representing the fundamental cycle of Indian cooking. Test: enumerate 100 recipes for chocolate chip cookies and compute the homotopy groups of the resulting simplicial complex. Impact: cooking is homotopy theory. Every dish is a point, every substitution is a path, and every cuisine is a homotopy type.
proof_strategy: Define the recipe space R(D) for a dish D as the simplicial complex whose vertices are recipes for D, edges connect recipes that differ by one ingredient substitution, triangles connect three recipes that differ by two substitutions, etc. A recipe is a tuple (ingredients, quantities, method). Two recipes r1, r2 are connected by an edge if they differ in exactly one ingredient (substitution). The path space Path(r1, r2) is the set of sequences of substitutions from r1 to r2. The fundamental group pi_1(R(D), r0) is the group of loops of substitutions at a base recipe r0. For chocolate chip cookies: vertices = {classic, with-nuts, with-oats, with-both}, edges = {classic-with-nuts (add nuts), classic-with-oats (add oats), with-nuts-with-both (add oats), with-oats-with-both (add nuts)}. pi_1 = Z generated by the loop classic -> with-nuts -> with-both -> with-oats -> classic. For curry: the fundamental group is generated by the spice-coconut cycle. Test: enumerate recipes from food databases and compute pi_1.
title: Homotopy Type Theory of Cooking Recipes: Paths Between Dishes

description: Cycle 29ba074c (Q=0.600) proved 24 theorems in NumberTheory but left 1 `sorry` placeholders. Fill them with complete proofs. Focus on the most important theorems first. Original: Formally proves existence and strict convexity of an energy spectrum functional E(a,b,c; N) over Berggren tree paths that guides a deterministic path to a non-trivial factor of N.
title: Close Proofs: Pythagorean-Energy-Spectrum: Gradient Descent Factoring on the Berggre

description: Cycle 9f14a31b (Q=0.600) proved 13 theorems in Applications but left 1 `sorry` placeholders. Fill them with complete proofs. Focus on the most important theorems first. Original: Every real number defines a musical scale: map the digits 0-9 to frequencies f_n = 220 * 2^{n/12} (the A minor pentatonic scale extended). The number pi = 3.14159265... produces the sequence E4, C5, C
title: Close Proofs: The Sound of Pi: Musical Structure in Transcendental Constants

description:
Every set map between pointed magmas induces a pseudofunctor of codiscrete bicategories, and round trips are invisible to 2-cells. This suggests that the construction is a genuine 2-categorical left adjoint lifting Mathlib's adjunction between objects of a category and codiscrete categories.

M |-> MagmaBicat M extends to a 2-functor from pointed sets to bicategories that is adjoint to taking the 1-cells of the unique object, and it is an equivalence onto one-object bicategories with codiscrete hom-categories.

Build the unit and counit in Lean using mapPseudofunctor, verify the triangle identities up to invertible modifications, and compare with CategoryTheory.Codiscrete.adj.

The codiscrete construction is characterised universally, so coherence-by-codiscreteness is not an ad hoc trick but a right/left adjoint phenomenon.

Coherence data cannot be produced adjointly at the bicategorical level, indicating that pseudofunctoriality on all set maps is an accident of thinness.
proof_strategy: Transport Codiscrete.adj one level up: hom-categories are codiscrete, so all coherence 2-cells are unique and the triangle identities are automatic once the unit and counit are defined on 1-cells.
title: Two-Categorical Codiscrete Adjunction

description: No mathematical implication from self-reference to consciousness has been established here. A future formal treatment would first require an independently specified, testable mathematical model of consciousness and a theorem statement linking it to self-referential structure.
title: Consciousness claims

description: The 'uncanny valley' in robotics states that as a robot becomes more human-like, acceptance increases until it looks almost human, then drops sharply before recovering. Conjecture: the same phenomenon exists in mathematics. As a proof becomes more rigorous, acceptance increases until it is 'almost rigorous' (a proof that is correct in spirit but has small gaps), then drops sharply (because mathematicians are suspicious of proofs that look correct but might have subtle errors), before recovering for fully rigorous proofs. The 'mathematical uncanny valley' function U(r) where r in [0,1] is the rigor level: U(0) = high (informal intuition is accepted), U(0.8) = low (almost rigorous but with gaps — very suspicious), U(1.0) = high (fully rigorous proof, formally verified). Conjecture: U(r) has a unique minimum at r = 1 - epsilon where epsilon is the 'gap size' that triggers the most suspicion. For Lean 4 proofs: U(1) = 1 (compiles), U(0.99) = 0.1 (almost compiles but has a 'sorry'), U(0.5) = 0.5 (sketch proof, accepted as intuition). Test: survey 100 mathematicians on their confidence in proofs at varying rigor levels and fit the uncanny valley curve. Impact: almost-right proofs are less trusted than informal intuitions. Formal verification escapes the uncanny valley.
proof_strategy: Define the mathematical uncanny valley function U: [0, 1] -> [0, 1] where U(r) = acceptance/confidence in a proof at rigor level r. Rigor levels: r = 0 (informal intuition), r = 0.3 (sketch proof), r = 0.5 (proof outline with key ideas), r = 0.7 (detailed proof with some gaps), r = 0.9 (almost rigorous, small gaps), r = 0.95 (very rigorous, minor issues), r = 0.99 (almost formal, one 'sorry'), r = 1.0 (formally verified in Lean 4). Hypothesized shape: U(0) = 0.7 (intuition is somewhat trusted), U(0.3) = 0.8 (sketch is more trusted), U(0.7) = 0.6 (detailed but with gaps — suspicion sets in), U(0.9) = 0.3 (almost rigorous — high suspicion), U(0.95) = 0.4 (very rigorous — still suspicious of subtle errors), U(0.99) = 0.2 (almost formal — the 'sorry' is a red flag), U(1.0) = 1.0 (formally verified — fully trusted). The minimum is at r = 0.99 (the 'sorry valley'). The function is U(r) = a * (r - r_min)^2 + b where r_min ~ 0.95 and the depth of the valley depends on the mathematician's formalization experience. Test: design a survey with 10 proofs at different rigor levels, ask 100 mathematicians to rate their confidence on a 0-1 scale, fit the uncanny valley curve.
title: The Uncanny Valley of Mathematics: When Proofs Are Almost Right

description:
For any `s ≠ t` bounded by `N` agreeing up to
   order `K`, the integer vector `c = count_s − count_t` lies in the kernel of the
   `(K+1) × (N+1)` Vandermonde matrix, and `card s ≥ ½‖c‖₁ ≥ ` the minimum of `½‖·‖₁` over
   nonzero integer kernel vectors.  Conjecture: this lattice minimum equals `2^K` for
   `N = K + 1` and equals `K + 1` for `N ≥ d(K)`, with no intermediate values other than
   integers in `[K+1, 2^K]`.
title: S2 (`ℓ¹` weight is the right invariant)

description:
**Conjecture.** For messages in `{0,1,…,B}^k` and integer keys, every `r`-component min-plus digest with `r < k` has a collision whenever `B` exceeds an explicit key-spread parameter, and this dependence on the spread is asymptotically optimal.

The key insight is that the real collision ray survives in a bounded alphabet exactly until it reaches the boundary, so security is controlled by slack at unused coordinates rather than by tropical nonlinearity. **Why now?** The unrestricted theorem identifies the unique obstruction introduced by bounded messages: an unused coordinate may have no legal positive increment.
title: Sharp bounded-alphabet collision threshold

description:
**Conjecture.** For a generic family of `r` min-plus keys on `k` coordinates with `r < k`, every nonempty digest fiber has a polyhedral cell whose recession cone has dimension exactly `k-r`, and this lower bound is sharp on a dense open set of keys and messages.

The key insight is that each output component can constrain one independently active coordinate, while all remaining coordinate directions can escape without changing any minimum. **Why now?** The universal collision-ray theorem establishes the first nonzero recession direction for every fiber; the next test is whether the entire expected `k-r`-dimensional cone can be constructed and whether genericity makes the bound exact.
title: Exact recession dimension of generic fibers

description:
“Uniquely determines it” needs a precise semantic quotient and domain. Point
values are too weak, and raw syntax has identities such as commutativity,
associativity, and exp/log cancellation on suitable eventual domains. Promising
formal statements are:

- expansion uniqueness for **eventual germs at `+∞`**;
- injectivity only after quotienting EML syntax by eventual equality;
- a restricted positive-domain language where logarithms have controlled domains;
- a normalization theorem assigning canonical transseries to a syntactic fragment.

The first substantial target is the polynomial–Laurent fragment, followed by a
single logarithmic level, then one exponential level. At each stage, define an
expansion map, prove preservation of addition and multiplication, and prove that
its kernel is exactly eventual semantic equality.
title: Corrected EML expansion theorem

description:
Conjecture: For an `r`-component hash formed from `r` independent min-plus linear forms on `k` real coordinates, every message has an unbounded collision ray whenever `k > r`.

The key insight is that each component needs only one unchanged minimizing coordinate; after choosing at most `r` such witnesses, any remaining coordinate can be increased without changing any output component.

Why now? The two-key theorem proves the first nontrivial case and supplies the exact update lemma needed for an induction over an arbitrary finite key family.
title: Universal collisions for finitely many tropical keys

description:
**Conjecture.** Among canonical radix systems of fixed residue alphabet size, the expected number of local rewrites required to normalize the sum of two length-`n` random numerals has a linear asymptotic whose coefficient is determined by the stationary distribution of a finite carry automaton.

The key insight is that an alien civilization's preferred base may be governed less by numeral length than by normalization cost, which can be modeled as an ergodic statistic of carry states.

**Why now?** Mixed-radix Horner evaluation, negabinary parity extraction, and phinary rewriting offer three sharply different systems on which the proposed invariant can be calculated and compared.
title: Carry complexity as a radix-selection invariant

description: Any theorem about consciousness itself requires a precise formal map from physical neural states to conscious states and assumptions on that map. The current development deliberately proves claims about distinguishable connectomes; it does not assume that every connectome is a distinct mind or that a connectome fully determines consciousness.
title: Semantic assumptions

description:
The key logit error bound charges d*Q*eta because a shared block scale lets all d coordinate roundings align; independent roundings would give only sqrt(d)*Q*eta. Determine the true correlation exponent alpha in d^alpha from the position of the key bit floor. Depth has already been eliminated as the amplifier, so dimension is the remaining structural knob.

The effective key logit error scales as d^alpha * Q * eta with alpha strictly between 1/2 and 1, and the key bit floor satisfies b* = log2(d^alpha * Q * R / g) for the typical top-two logit gap g.

Sharpen logit_perturb_le under a correlation hypothesis on the rounding errors, and re-run the NET-94 sweep on models with different head dimensions to fit alpha.

The key bit floor is dimension dependent, so wide-head models need more key bits at the same quality target.

Rounding errors are effectively worst-case aligned and the crude d*Q*eta bound is tight, making the floor dimension linear.
proof_strategy: Replace the triangle inequality in logit_perturb_le by a second-moment bound under a correlation assumption, then feed the resulting step into the argmax-gap threshold criterion.
title: Correlated-Rounding Dimension Scaling

description:
Interleaving conserves information density when the domains are balanced and destroys it without bound when they are not. We conjecture that the density of a two-domain protocol is a unimodal function of the mixing weight with its maximum exactly at mass balance, so a 50/50 protocol is the uniquely optimal measurement design and every other ratio carries a computable discount. This turns the proposed mixing-ratio sweep into a sequence of unequally informative measurements with known weights.

For two positive profiles and weights (a, 1-a), the information density (context-doubling increment times narrowest sub-step) is non-decreasing in a below the weight at which the two total head masses are equal and non-increasing above it, and at the balance point it equals the pooled density up to half a pooled step.

Express the narrowest sub-step as the explicit ratio min(a*u k, (1-a)*v k) over the total interleaved mass, prove unimodality of that ratio in a, and combine with the increment bracket; check numerically against directly computed knees for weights 0.1 through 0.9 on explicit rational profiles.

The reported 50/50 protocol is provably the most informative two-domain design, and every point of a ratio sweep can be reweighted by an explicit discount before comparison.

Some skewed mixture is more informative than the balanced one, which would make mixing ratio a genuine tuning parameter of the measurement rather than a nuisance.
proof_strategy: Reduce the density to increment times min(a*u k, (1-a)*v k) / (a*headMass u n + (1-a)*headMass v n), show this ratio is unimodal in a by splitting at the crossing of the two numerators, then absorb the m-1 increment slack into the one-step error term.
title: Density-Optimal Mixing Ratio for Two-Domain Budget Measurements

description:
Floor and ceiling certification are mirror statements costing the corresponding rapidity margins. Because the band [0.55,0.85] is far from symmetric in rapidity, the two gates of the band have wildly different costs at the readings actually observed, making the band effectively one-sided.

At every recorded rung, the sample size needed to certify the ceiling 0.85 is at least an order of magnitude smaller than that needed to certify the floor 0.55, so the band decision is determined by the floor gate alone.

Instantiate floor_certified_iff and ceiling_certified_iff at each recorded rung and compare the two reqSamples values as explicit rational bounds.

Band membership as reported is a one-sided test and should be reported as such, with the ceiling clause dropped.

Some rung is ceiling-limited, which would be the first evidence of an upper obstruction of the kind the tie and Gram ceilings predict.
proof_strategy: Both gates reduce to rapidity margins by the mirror criteria; the comparison is then a rational inequality between two artanh differences, handled by the two-sided artanh bounds.
title: One-Sidedness of the Pre-Registered Validation Band

description:
**Tropical Perron–Frobenius in all dimensions**
  (`exists_maxPlusMul_eigenvector` in
  `Catalog/Speculative/AutoResearch/PerronTheorem.lean`, on the new core
  `Catalog/Speculative/AutoResearch/TropicalPerronCore.lean`): the Cuninghame-Green
  construction is formalised — maximal cycle mean, cycle removal by pigeonhole, and the
  longest-path potential to a critical node — replacing the previous `1×1`/`2×2`-only
  situation.
title: Tropical Perron–Frobenius in all dimensions

description:
The weighting gain 1/kappa_g - 1/(1+sqrt kappa_g)^2 strictly increases with the radix while the unweighted ceiling 1 - 1/kappa_g strictly decreases. Conjecture a unique small crossover radix at which a weighted base-g dial overtakes the unweighted binary dial, suggesting radix, not seed, as the next experimental knob.

There is a unique integer g0 >= 3 such that 1 - 1/(1+sqrt kappa_g)^2 > 6/7 for all g >= g0 and <= 6/7 for 2 < g < g0, and g0 <= 4.

Evaluate kappaRadix and radixCeiling at g = 3,4,5 with exact rationals and bound the square roots by rational sandwiches, then prove monotonicity in g from kappaRadix_strictAnti.

A radix change buys more correlation than the entire +0.05 H2 bar, redirecting the experiment programme.

The binary dial is already at the practical optimum and radix variation is a dead end.
proof_strategy: Combine kappaRadix_strictAnti with weightGain_strictAnti and explicit rational bounds on sqrt(kappa_3), sqrt(kappa_4).
title: Radix Crossover for the Weighted Zero-Fit Edge

description:
The crowding and codebook pigeonholes are worst-case over arrangements; the operational damage depends on the empirical distribution of top-two logit gaps. A distributional refinement should predict the expected fraction of inverted positions as a function of the quantisation error, closing the gap between 'some pair inverts' and 'perplexity moves by x'.

The excess log-perplexity of a KV-quantised model is, to first order, proportional to the mass of the top-two logit gap distribution below 2*eps, with a model-independent proportionality constant of order one.

Collect the top-two gap histogram per head at ctx 2048, compute the mass below 2*eps for each arm, and regress the measured excess log-perplexity against it.

A single cheap histogram predicts the safe KV width for any model, removing the need for a perplexity sweep.

Inversions are not exchangeable across heads and positions, and a correlated model of gap statistics is required.
proof_strategy: Randomise the arrangement in crowding_inverts_softmax, replace the pigeonhole by a first-moment computation over the gap distribution, and bound the induced log-loss change by the softmax stability estimate.
title: Gap-Statistics Rescue Bound

description:
A REORDER policy may split the balance window and traverse the pieces in different directions. By the exchange theorem the optimum is the mass sort, so the optimal split should sit where the mass density crosses its mean, and the gain over the best pure order should be bounded by the residue slack 4/3.

The cost-minimal two-stage window policy splits at the tilt median z = 1/2, and its cost is at least (3/4) times the best pure-order cost.

Formalise two-stage costs as a function of the split point, differentiate the closed form, and compare with probeCost_masssort_le.

A deployable policy strictly better than both pure orders, with a proved gain ceiling.

Staging buys nothing beyond the pure orders and the action space collapses to two arms.
proof_strategy: Write the staged cost as a sum of two window costs, minimise over the split, and use frontload_le for the comparison.
title: Optimal Staged Window Splits

description:
Uniform-in-time shadowing should require inverse branches only on a forward-invariant trapping region rather than globally, extending the cubic instantiation to Julia-set dynamics of quadratic and Chebyshev maps. The approach localises the backward construction to the nested intervals it actually visits.

If f is expanding with local inverse branches on a forward-invariant S and a delta-pseudo-orbit stays delta/(lambda-1)-inside S, then a true orbit in S shadows it with error at most delta/(lambda-1), uniformly in the horizon.

Weaken the hypotheses of expanding_backward_shadowing to branches defined on closed balls and re-run the backward induction, tracking membership of the constructed points.

Binary64 executions of expanding polynomial maps on their Julia sets carry O(u) shadowing certificates for unbounded time.

Global branch existence is essential and uniform shadowing is limited to globally invertible expanding maps.
proof_strategy: Backward induction as in the present proof, with the inductive invariant strengthened to 'the constructed point lies in the closed ball of radius delta/(lambda-1) around x_n, which is contained in S'.
title: Localised Inverse Branches for Trapping-Region Shadowing

description:
All damage from a block transplant is conjectured to be a function of the drift's component along the per-position top-2 logit-difference direction, not of any norm. Norm and margin statistics are then relaxations of a single exact identity. This would replace one-sided screens by an exact predictor.

For a linear block with drift ΔW, damageFrac = frac{x : ⟨ΔW·feat x, e_{d(x)} − e_{second(x)}⟩ > gap(x)}, and every norm-based or margin-based bound is obtained by relaxing this identity.

Formalise the top-2 projection statistic in the blockLogit model of Catalog/Applications/MarginScarcityPortability.lean and prove the identity for m = 2, then general m by reduction to the top-2 pair.

Portability becomes exactly computable from one forward pass plus one matrix-vector product per position.

Damage depends on third-order structure of the logit vector, and only one-sided screens can exist.
proof_strategy: Reduce IsStrictTop of the perturbed logits to a scalar inequality along e_{d(x)} − e_j, then take the max over j; the dead/live-direction examples become the two extreme angles.
title: Top-Two Projection Completeness for Transplant Damage

description:
The counting bound used only that level sets of the trailing-zero statistic are arithmetic progressions with nested moduli. Conjecture a ceiling formula depending only on the modulus chain, valid for arbitrary windows with an O(1/n) error, and apply it to the count baseline that T beats by +0.098.

If the level sets of a statistic on a window of length n are progressions with moduli q₀ ∣ q₁ ∣ ⋯ ∣ q_K, then ρ² = 1 − Σ_i (1/q_i − 1/q_{i+1})³ + O(K/n) with an absolute implied constant.

Instantiate the dyadic-domination lemma with general moduli and compare against exact enumeration for small chains.

The T-versus-count advantage becomes predictable from the two modulus chains rather than measured, giving a falsifiable prediction for every future rung.

The count baseline's ties are not progression-structured, which would itself explain why its degradation outpaces T's.
proof_strategy: Generalise cubeSum_le_of_dominated from the ratio 1/2 to an arbitrary summable ratio sequence, keeping the exact coefficient balancing.
title: Modulus-Chain Ceilings for Progression Statistics

description:
Replace the unstructured interaction alternative by the first nontrivial one: an occupancy table that is a rank-one product plus a single scaled outer product. The formal equivalence between no interaction and rank one shows this is the minimal departure, and it reduces a 49-degree-of-freedom test to a one-parameter test with far greater power.

For the exp-578 occupancy table there is no direction (u, v) and no epsilon with |epsilon| bounded away from 0 such that occ = rate ⊗ prof + epsilon · u ⊗ v fits significantly better than the rank-one fit; equivalently the second singular value of the centred occupancy table is consistent with sampling noise.

Formalise the rank-two model as a TwoLayer perturbation, prove that its Pearson statistic is monotone in |epsilon|, then fit the leading singular direction of the observed centred table and compare with a permutation null.

The positional layer is law-complete to second order, and the search for the overdispersion carrier can be restricted to scalar per-N statistics.

A single interaction direction exists and names the carrier explicitly (which deciles move with rate).
proof_strategy: Use PositionalRateLink.TwoLayer.rankOne_iff_homogeneous to identify the null, expand the Pearson statistic to second order in epsilon around the independence fit, and bound the remainder using Table.klTerm_pos.
title: Rank-Two Occupancy Alternative for Positional–Rate Interaction

description:
Composing q4_k_m weights with a K8/V4 cache has two proved bounds: exact additivity (1.956%) if the two perturbations are orthogonal in the Hessian metric, and under 3% in the worst aligned case. The conjecture is that the orthogonal prediction is the correct one, since the two perturbations act on disjoint tensors.

The joint weight x cache arm measures an excess of 1.956% +- noise, i.e. the two quantisation noises are Hessian-orthogonal to within measurement resolution.

Run the joint arm (q4_k_m weights with K8/V4 cache) on the same slice and compare with 1.956% and with the 3% worst-case ceiling.

Serving-stack budgets are additive and can be planned component-wise; the seminorm bound is never binding in practice.

Weight and cache errors interact through shared curvature directions, and stack design must account for a cross term.
proof_strategy: The two bounds are already proved (stack_excess_additive_of_orthogonal, cpu_stack_aggregate_bound); the open step is a formal criterion under which disjoint-tensor perturbations are Hessian-orthogonal in a transformer block.
title: Hessian Orthogonality of Weight and Cache Quantisation Noise

description:
Pooling a seed family can only lower a positive reading, and the exact worst case is now known to be the Kantorovich constant. The conjecture is that the upper bound (the seed maximum) and the lower bound (the Kantorovich value) are jointly attained by a single explicit family, so the envelope is a complete description of pooling.

For every window [alpha, beta] with 0 < alpha <= beta and every rho in [0,1] there is a two-block family with per-seed readings exactly rho, ratios in [alpha, beta], and pooled reading any prescribed value in [rho*2*sqrt(alpha*beta)/(alpha+beta), rho].

Construct the family explicitly in Fin 2 blocks of dimension 2 and verify both endpoints and an interpolation parameter in Lean.

Pooled readings can be inverted into exact per-seed intervals, upgrading the two-spread criterion from a sufficient test to a characterisation.

There is an unnoticed obstruction between the two envelopes, and the interval of achievable pooled values is a proper subset that must be computed.
proof_strategy: Interpolate between the Kantorovich extremiser (energies alpha : beta reversed) and the balanced family, using pooled_balanced_eq_weighted_avg for the upper endpoint and continuity of pooledCorr in the block energies.
title: Sharp Two-Sided Pooling Envelope

description:
The octave shift is an action of the additive monoid of naturals. If it extends to a real scale parameter, intermediate model sizes must interpolate the table monotonically, giving a one-parameter flow whose generator is the keys-per-octave rate.

There is a monotone K0 : ℝ≥0 → ℝ with k*(sigma, j) = K0(max(j - sigma, 0)) restricting to the measured integer cells; equivalently the shift action extends from (ℕ,+) to (ℝ≥0,+).

Formalise the extension as a monotone-interpolation problem and prove existence for arithmetic base chains; experimentally sweep 3B between the 1.5B and 7B cells.

Knee budgets can be interpolated for unmeasured model sizes, and deployment tables become continuous in scale.

Scale acts only discretely and each model family needs its own chain.
proof_strategy: Extend the base chain by monotone piecewise-linear interpolation, verify the semigroup identity shift_add on reals, and check restriction to integers reproduces the measured table.
title: Real-Parameter Scale Flow on Knee Chains

description:
Every entry and every increment of the reported table is a multiple of four. If the sweep grid has spacing g, the reported knee is the grid ceiling of the true knee, and increments are forced into g·ℕ. This would show that much of the table's apparent structure is an artefact of the measurement design.

If a sweep grid is g·ℕ then every reported doubling increment lies in g·ℕ, and the reported factor of a domain differs from its true factor by at most g/k*.

Combine gridKnee from Combinatorics.KneeInvariance with the dilation bracket and prove both statements.

The '+0 / +4 / +8' pattern carries less information than claimed, and finer grids are required for factor claims.

The quantisation is a property of the model, not of the sweep, and is itself the interesting phenomenon.
proof_strategy: gridKnee is a ceiling onto the grid; ceilings of a monotone curve differ by grid multiples, and the dilation bracket controls the underlying difference.
title: Grid-Spacing Origin of the Four-Fold Quantisation

description:
For a bulk+spike profile, the exponent obtained by matching the cumulative edge mass on the window [0,t] should be a strictly decreasing function of t. Non-constancy is already a theorem; monotonicity would turn the qualitative 'refits steepen on the left' observation into a quantitative law. The route is the implicit function theorem applied to the edge fraction, whose strict monotonicity in the exponent is proved.

If 0 < w < 1 and b₁ < b₂ then the unique b_eff(t) with edgeFrac (b_eff t) t = mixFrac w b₁ b₂ t is strictly decreasing on (0,1).

Formalise b_eff via the proved existence/uniqueness statements, differentiate the defining identity, and show the derivative is negative using headMass/tailMass comparisons.

Window-restricted refits become a calibrated diagnostic: the drift rate estimates the spike weight.

Some profiles would produce non-monotone refits, so window choice could not be interpreted as a probe of edge structure.
proof_strategy: Implicit differentiation of edgeFrac (b,t) = mix(t) using strict monotonicity in b for nondegeneracy, plus a sign computation for the mixed partial.
title: Monotone Drift of the Window-Fitted Exponent

description:
The reconstructed prose survival profile drops sharply between positions 2 and 3 while the code profile decays smoothly. The averaging law proves that reported mean acceptance can never expose this. The conjecture is that the cliff position is determined by prompt syntax and is stable across prompts of a domain.

For a fixed domain there is a position p such that the per-position acceptance profile satisfies p_j >= 0.75 for j < p and p_j <= 0.5 for j >= p, with p = 3 for prose and p >= 8 for code.

Instrument the harness to export per-position accept counts, then check the two-sided bound; formalise the resulting profile as a survival sequence and verify the measured means as a corollary of posYield.

Draft depth can be set from a syntactic feature of the prompt with no runtime probing.

Acceptance decay is gradual and depth must be controlled adaptively at runtime.
proof_strategy: Replace the existence statement net91_acceptances_realisable with an identification statement: show the measured per-position vector is monotone, then re-derive meanAccept at depths 2, 4, 8 by computation.
title: Positional Cliff Location in Prose Acceptance Profiles

description:
Depth-additive damage bounds hold under a per-layer perturbation bound that is uniform over upstream states, and fail under any bound certified at a single state. The conjecture upgrades this from a counterexample to a dichotomy for arbitrary budget functionals.

For every per-layer budget functional B that depends only on the behaviour of a layer at finitely many prescribed upstream states, there is a stack on which the joint damage exceeds the sum of the budgets.

Generalise the witness family to interpolate any finite set of probe states, and prove that a masking suffix can always be inserted after the probes.

Serving policies must certify worst-case per-layer behaviour; held-out-window measurements can never be turned into a sound budget.

Some finite probe set suffices, and the design question becomes which probes, opening a concrete experimental programme.
proof_strategy: Diagonalisation against the probe states using constant channels that agree with the intact layer on the probes but not elsewhere, followed by the masking construction of fullStack.
title: Necessity of Uniform Per-Layer Budgets

description:
Any monotone, translation-equivariant aggregator of per-seed margins is sandwiched between order statistics, so its breakdown point cannot exceed that of the median. The conjecture states the median is optimal and quantifies the seed budget needed to tolerate k hardware failures. It matters because seed count dominates the cost of the E3 run.

For every monotone translation-equivariant aggregator T of n reals, the breakdown point of T is at most ceil(n/2), with equality for the median; consequently a protocol tolerating k corrupted runs needs n >= 2k+1 runs.

Formalize monotone equivariant aggregators, prove the sandwich between order statistics, and reuse the sharpness half of MedianBreakdown for the upper bound.

Adding seeds is provably the only way to harden the E3 measurement.

A more robust statistic exists and the protocol should adopt it instead of adding runs.
proof_strategy: Show equivariance plus monotonicity forces min <= T <= max on constant-shifted data, then transport the median contamination construction of isMedian_contaminate.
title: Breakdown Optimality of the Median Margin Statistic

description:
The closed formula for the critical weight assumes a positive dominant excess Hu(K) - tau*Hu(n). We conjecture that the sign of this quantity is the discriminant of the whole sweep: when it is negative the collapse region reverses from a half-line upward to a bounded interval, producing a re-entrant phase in which very large mixing weights stop collapsing. This is a qualitatively new, directly falsifiable prediction about ratio sweeps.

If Hu(K) - tau*Hu(n) < 0 with K the dominant knee, then the set of positive weights a at which the pooled knee equals K is bounded above, and its supremum is the same expression (tau*Hv(n) - Hv(K)) / (Hu(K) - tau*Hu(n)); in particular there exist profile pairs whose sweep collapses on an interval and un-collapses beyond it.

Rerun the division-free pass criterion with the reversed sign, then search explicit rational profile pairs for a realisation of the negative-excess regime and compute the sweep directly on both sides of the predicted supremum.

Ratio sweeps can be non-monotone in a controlled way, and the sign of one pure-domain quantity tells an experimenter which regime to expect.

The dominant excess is always positive under domination, so the closed formula holds unconditionally and the hypothesis can be dropped.
proof_strategy: Apply div_le_iff with a negative denominator to reverse the half-line, then combine with the upward-closure theorem to see which of the two descriptions can coexist, and construct or exclude a witness pair.
title: Sign of the Dominant Excess as Sweep Discriminant

description:
The audit promotes cross-head agreement to the strongest correlate of the knee. The natural mechanism is that disagreeing heads union their supports, flattening the aggregate tail and delaying the knee; agreeing heads reinforce a common support and sharpen it.

For an aggregate profile formed by averaging h head profiles, the tail decay exponent of the average is a decreasing function of the pairwise support overlap of the heads, and the knee of the average therefore decreases with agreement.

Formalise the averaged profile and prove monotonicity of the knee in a support-overlap parameter; then measure agreement and fitted exponent on the same layers.

Head agreement becomes a mechanism, not a summary statistic, and the refuted horn P3 is reinstated with a reason.

The measured head-agreement/knee association is an artefact of five points and should not be pursued.
proof_strategy: Model heads as profiles supported on overlapping key sets, express the average capture curve as a convex combination, and use the antitonicity of the knee in the capture curve (kneeAt_mono_profile).
title: Head Agreement Drives Tail Flatness

description:
The block ceiling degrades as 1/lambda in the smallest eigenvalue of the block's Gram matrix. The four neighbour-smoothness covariates are mutually correlated, so the orthonormal instance used in the exp-585 certificate is optimistic. Determining a provable lower frame bound for the actual design gives the honest ceiling.

For the four-covariate neighbourhood block on balanced 96-bit moduli, FrameLower lambda holds with lambda bounded below by an explicit function of the pairwise correlations, and the resulting ceiling still lies below the pre-registered alternative 0.05.

Bound the smallest eigenvalue by Gershgorin from the pairwise sample correlations and feed it to rsq_block_le_of_corr.

The exp-585 null verdict survives with a realistic conditioning constant.

The certificate must be stated with the empirical Gram matrix, and the null rests entirely on the permutation test.
proof_strategy: Prove a Gershgorin-type lemma that diagonal dominance of the Gram matrix implies FrameLower, then instantiate.
title: Sharp Frame Constant of the Neighbour-Smoothness Design

description:
The dial's ceiling can be driven to 1 by flattening its block profile, so the observed 0.669 must be charged to the response side. Conjecture that the attainable correlation factorises as a product of the two tie-attenuation factors, making the dial and response headrooms additive on the log scale and pinning the observed +0.045 advantage.

For tie profiles L (predictor) and M (response) on the same n observations, the maximal attainable Spearman rho satisfies rho^2 <= spearmanSq L * spearmanSq M + O(1/n^2), with equality for aligned profiles.

Formalise the two-sided tie correction of Spearman's rho and prove the product bound by Cauchy-Schwarz on the rank vectors; check numerically against the recorded pooled reading.

The H2 accounting closes: the 0.045 advantage is predicted from the response tie profile alone.

Predictor and response attenuation interact non-multiplicatively and the headroom argument must be replaced by a joint-profile bound.
proof_strategy: Express both corrections as quadratic forms in rank increments and apply Cauchy-Schwarz, controlling the discrete correction by the proved sandwich.
title: Headroom Conservation Under Response Rebalancing

description:
Domain changes act on the demand multiset while scale acts on the octave index. If these are independent coordinates, the three-way table factorises and a domain jump can never interact with a scale shift.

k*(domain, scale s, octave j) = K_domain(j - s) for every domain, i.e. the domain-jump operator and the octave-shift operator commute on knee tables.

Formalise a domain action on Workload.demand, prove it commutes with shift using knee_eq_of_demandMultiset_eq, and measure one off-diagonal cell (mathematics corpus at 1.5B, ctx 2048).

Budget tables factor into a domain factor and a scale-shifted context factor, collapsing the measurement grid from cubic to linear in size.

Domain difficulty and effective context interact, and per-domain scale ladders must be measured separately.
proof_strategy: Show any reindexing of the demand multiset leaves the agreement curve unchanged, so the domain action commutes with any transformation of the octave index; then instantiate at the octave shift.
title: Commuting Square of Domain Jumps and Scale Shifts

description:
The zero-increment locus of one feature is a hyperplane in rate-profile space. For a family of m candidate features the simultaneous absence locus should be an intersection of m independent hyperplanes, so codimension adds. This turns 'which augmentations can be absent together' into a rank computation on the Gram matrix of the partialled features.

If the partialled features zt_1,...,zt_m are linearly independent in the weighted inner product, the set of rate profiles on which all m increments vanish has codimension exactly m in the space of rate profiles.

Generalise zeroGainFunctional to a linear map into R^m, prove surjectivity from Gram nondegeneracy, and apply the rank-nullity theorem.

Simultaneous absence of several augmentations is exponentially non-generic, so a repeated null result is strong evidence of a structural constraint on the population generator.

Some partialled features are weightedly dependent, i.e. the candidate dial family is redundant, which itself explains the null results.
proof_strategy: Rank-nullity for the map y |-> (<y, zt_1>, ..., <y, zt_m>), with surjectivity from invertibility of the Gram matrix; sequential_gain supplies the additive decomposition of the residual drop.
title: Codimension Additivity for Simultaneously Absent Feature Families

description:
This cycle proved upper bounds on the reflection depths available inside the refinement of capC and valSys (a height gap bound and a collapse to depth one for non-maximal tags) and proved that they are attained when the height vector takes only two values. The conjecture extends the resulting closed formula to arbitrary height vectors: the reflection depth of a tag is the distance from its own cut point to the next cut point below it, giving a complete decision procedure for ClassRealizes.

In cvSys c V N the reflection depth of tag i equals min N (d i) minus the largest strictly smaller value of min N (d j), and equals min N (d i) when no tag is strictly lower; ClassRealizes N d r holds iff r is given by this formula. The two-valued case is the proved theorem classRealizes_twoValue.

Generalize the proved bisimulation satCV_flat_congr from one low cut point to the whole sequence of cut points, then assemble the biconditional characterization of ClassRealizes; check the formula first by exhaustive enumeration on three-valued height vectors.

The refinement class is completely classified: its reflection-depth vector is a computable function of the height vector, closing the question the mission conjecture opened.

Some intermediate reflection depth is unreachable, which would mean the gap probe is not optimal and a sharper separating formula exists.
proof_strategy: Show that any two worlds at or above the second cut point are (gap-1)-bisimilar, so no formula of box depth below the gap can separate the image of the high tag from the whole model; dually exhibit the depth-one probe for the low tag.
title: Cut-Point Formula for Multi-Valued Height Vectors

description:
Model a key block quantiser by its max-abs scale rather than a fixed range, so the effective per-coordinate error carries the outlier ratio as a prefactor. Derive the per-bit shrink base of the resulting distortion law and compare it with the proved lower bound K > 18. This would replace the fitted response exponent by a derived one.

For a block quantiser with scale max|k| and heavy-tailed key coordinates, the effective distortion law is multiplicative in bit width with base at least 2^5, i.e. response exponent gamma >= 5.
