Formalise a max-abs block quantiser in Lean over Fin d, prove an error bound of the form (max/typ) * 2^(-b), and instantiate net94_forces_superbinary_shrink with it; empirically, measure the outlier ratio of key rows per bit width.

The NET-94 cliff has a derived mechanism, and key-cache schemes can be ranked a priori by their outlier ratio.

The cliff is not outlier driven and some other nonlinearity (rounding correlation, block-size interaction) carries the exponent.
proof_strategy: Bound the quantisation error of a max-abs block quantiser, feed it into logit_perturb_le as the per-coordinate budget, then apply key_bit_shrink_base_lower_bound to the resulting law.
title: Outlier-Scaled Block Quantisation Exponent

description:
The celestial map sending an event to (a/c, b/c) is injective into the rational points of the unit circle, and the Pell spine converges to the irrational direction sqrt(2)/2. The conjecture is that the closure of the image is the whole open first-quadrant arc, so the conformal boundary of the causal set is all of null infinity in that sector.

The set { (a/c, b/c) : (a,b,c) a primitive Pythagorean triple with a,b,c > 0 } is dense in the open arc { (x,y) : x,y > 0, x^2+y^2 = 1 }.

Formalise Berggren's completeness theorem (every primitive triple is a node of the tree, via descent using the parent map already formalised), then derive density from the Euclid parametrisation and density of the rationals.

The boundary of the Berggren causal set is exactly the celestial arc: a fully formalised discrete model of null infinity for the 2+1 null cone.

The image omits an arc, which would contradict the classical Euclid parametrisation and hence indicate an error in the descent, so the informative outcome is the completeness theorem itself.
proof_strategy: Descent: the parent map decreases the hypotenuse (parent_hyp_lt in the catalog) and preserves primitivity, so every primitive triple reaches (3,4,5); then Euclid seeds (m,n) with n/m dense in (0,1) give directions dense in the arc.
title: Celestial Density of the Berggren Boundary

description:
Extend the exact equational transfer to an order transfer. With the natural partial order in which nullity is incomparable, guarded expressions should preserve and reflect inequalities and have connected image, yielding an intermediate value theorem whose only failure mode is a jump through nullity.

For guarded e₁ e₂, (∀x, transEval e₁ x ≤ transEval e₂ x) ↔ (∀x, realEval e₁ x ≤ realEval e₂ x); moreover the image of a connected domain under a guarded expression is connected, and the image of an unguarded expression is disconnected exactly when it meets null.

Define the partial order on Transreal, prove the finite fragment is an order embedding, and derive the connectivity statements from the clopen nullity fibre.

Genuinely analytic theorems, not only identities, transfer through the finite fragment.

The transfer principle is intrinsically equational and the exceptional constructors obstruct order-theoretic reasoning.
proof_strategy: Order embedding of fin plus injectivity gives the biconditional; connectivity follows from the openness and closedness of the nullity fibre together with the connectedness of the finite fragment.
title: Order Transfer and the Transreal Intermediate Value Theorem

description:
The reported +4 shift is compatible with any true tax in the open interval (0,8). The conjecture is that some language realises a true tax that is not a multiple of the grid step, invisible at step 4 and visible at step 2. This separates the horn P1 (full step) from P2 (intermediate) at the level of the unquantised knees rather than the reported ones.

There is a corpus whose unquantised knee at ctx 512 differs from English by a value in (0,4) union (4,8), while its step-4 reading differs by exactly 4.

Re-run the English and candidate sweeps on a step-2 grid; formally, instantiate Catalog.NET71.true_knee_bracket at step 2 and check whether the two bracketing intervals still overlap.

Grid-quantised knee claims must always be reported as intervals, and the 'one full step' language of rounds 21-24 is a resolution artefact.

Domain shifts are genuinely quantised at 4 keys, which is strong evidence for a discrete mechanism (positions per idea) rather than a continuous density effect.
proof_strategy: Generalise gridUp_le_iff and true_knee_bracket to arbitrary step s, derive the interval (s*(j-1), s*j], and show the step-2 and step-4 brackets of the same corpus intersect in at most one point unless the true shift is a multiple of 4.
title: Sub-Step Tokenizer Tax Below the Grid Resolution

description:
With both ceilings known, define a statistic's efficiency as reading^2 divided by its tie ceiling. At bitlen 52 the dial has efficiency 0.58 and the count baseline 0.41. Conjecture that this efficiency gap lower-bounds the extra mutual information the 2-adic valuation carries about the response, via a Fano-type inequality for rank correlations.

For any response Y and statistics T, C on the same sample, eff(T) - eff(C) <= c * (I(T;Y) - I(C;Y)) for an absolute constant c, where eff denotes squared Spearman reading divided by tie ceiling.

Formalise efficiency in the existing tie-profile framework, prove the data-processing direction first (C a function of T implies eff(C) <= eff(T)), and calibrate c on the recorded bitlen-52 pair.

The dial's advantage becomes a certified information statement rather than a correlational one, and the validation band acquires an information-theoretic meaning.

Rank efficiency and mutual information are not comparable, so dial advantages must be reported strictly as rank statistics.
proof_strategy: Data-processing for refinements (already available as the nested-profile refinement bound) plus a Fano inequality applied blockwise to the coarser statistic.
title: Efficiency Gap as an Information Lower Bound

description:
Retention loss of a score-driven evictor should be controlled by the true-importance mass lying within the score's error of the budget cut-off, not by the global R^2. The approach refines the transfer theorem by splitting keys into a safe core (margin exceeds twice the error) and a boundary band. It matters because it replaces a domain-universal statistic that provably cannot explain the measurements by one that can.

Measured band mass (total importance of keys within 2*eps of the budget cut-off) at B = 64 differs between code and prose even though the probe R^2 values agree to within 0.011, and the band mass upper-bounds the observed arm gap in both domains.

The inequality is now proved as retention_gap_le_band_mass; what remains is to measure band mass on the NET-69 code and prose traces at B = 64 and check that it tracks the measured 11.91-point gap and separates the two domains.

The probe deficit becomes predictable from the tie structure of the key population, and the code/prose difference should show up in band mass rather than in R^2.

Retention loss depends on global rather than local structure, and the search for a sufficient statistic must move to rank correlations.
proof_strategy: Apply the exchange inequality on S \ T and T \ S; keys outside the band cannot be exchanged by isTopSet_eq_oracle_of_margin, so only band keys contribute, and each contributes at most its own mass.
title: Band Mass as the Domain-Discriminating Retention Statistic

description:
With the blocked knee now exact for every block size, the block-size sweep becomes a deterministic arithmetic object. We conjecture it is a sawtooth: the knee is the doubled pooled knee corrected by the block-local offset of that knee, so the entire sweep is predicted by one pooled measurement plus the residues of the knee modulo each block size.

For a fixed profile pair, gate and context, the blocked knee at block size b lies in the window from 2Q - (Q mod b) to 2Q + b - (Q mod b), where Q is the pooled knee, and its exact position inside the window is determined by the two component head masses at the block boundary; in particular the sweep jumps exactly at the divisors of Q.

Combine the exact intra-block knee theorems with the sharpened aligned bound, then evaluate the predicted sweep against a direct computation on explicit rational profiles for all block sizes up to the context length.

Block-size sweeps require no new measurement and any observed deviation isolates tokenisation or positional effects outside the model.

Blocking carries information beyond the pooled knee and its residues, so block size is a genuine physical parameter rather than a gauge.
proof_strategy: Case analysis on the half-block containing the crossing, using the two master identities, then arithmetic of Q mod b and Q / b to assemble the envelope.
title: Block-Size Sawtooth for Interleaved Key Budgets

description:
Swapping uniform for balanced draws moves the tie ceiling by less than 0.07 in rho. We conjecture a general budget: two draw laws whose modal fractions differ by delta have ceilings within delta of each other, which turns every law-swap experiment into a falsifiable prediction with an explicit tie budget.

For tie profiles L, L' with modal fractions a, a' one has |sqrt(spearmanSq L) - sqrt(spearmanSq L')| <= |a - a'| + O(1/n), and the bound is attained by two-block profiles.

Prove the Lipschitz bound from the mass-fraction floor and the dominant-block upper law, then check sharpness on two-block families.

Any recorded law-to-law dial movement above the modal-fraction gap is provably a response effect.

Ceilings can move more than modal fractions and law-swap comparisons need the full profile.
proof_strategy: Sandwich each ceiling between 1 - a^2 and the half-mass style cap, then use the mean value bound for the square root on the resulting interval.
title: Universal Law-Change Capacity in Modal Fraction

description:
Refine the binary mirror/non-mirror distinction into a rank filtration counting how finely a probe splits each magnitude cell. Conjecture that every window-local realized probe has rank 1 (a mirror) while the factor-derived positional bit has rank at least 2, so no realized probe of intermediate rank exists. This would explain why every measured channel collapsed to an exact null while the oracle bound survived.

For probes computed from a poly(log N) read of the isqrt-anchored window, the mirror rank is 1; for 1{d<=B} it is at least 2 on any family containing two same-magnitude instances with different smallest factor.

Define mirrorRank as the maximum over magnitude cells of the number of distinct probe values on the cell; prove rank 1 for signVector and its post-processings using signVector_const, and rank >= 2 via oracle_informative_within_magnitude_cell.

The realized probe class is provably sealed as a class, not instance by instance.

There exists a window-local probe separating same-magnitude instances, i.e. a genuinely new channel.
proof_strategy: Cell-wise fibre counting on top of MirrorsMagnitude; the rank-1 direction is mirror_tuple plus mirror_comp, the rank-2 direction is an explicit two-instance witness.
title: Mirror-Rank Dichotomy for Deterministic Probes

description:
The reward range, standard deviation and mean absolute deviation are the q = ∞, 2, 1 members of one family of centred L^q norms, indexed by the order of the divergence used to measure drift. The conjecture asserts D_α(π_β‖p) = α·Var/(2β²) + O(β⁻³) and an L^q drift law with constant ‖r − 𝔼r‖_{L^q(p)}. It would unify the three competing constants in the catalogue into a single theorem.

For every q ∈ [1,∞], β·‖(π_β − p)/p‖_{L^q(p)} → ‖r − 𝔼_p r‖_{L^q(p)}, and for every Rényi order α > 0, β²·D_α(π_β‖p) → α·Var_p(r)/2.

Formalize the L^q statement for q = 1, 2, ∞ first (q = 1 is RLHF.l1_drift_tendsto_mad, q = ∞ is a sup' computation), then the general q by the same centred-tilt expansion; check numerically on rare-spike and 3-point families.

A single drift theorem specialising to all constants in the RLHF drift thread, with the divergence order as the only parameter.

Some divergence order has a drift constant that is not a centred moment, which would mean the tilt expansion is not uniform in the order.
proof_strategy: Write π_β = p e^{s}/W with s = (r − 𝔼r)/β, expand e^{s} − W = s + O(s²) termwise as in RLHF.abs_l1_numerator_sub_mad, and take L^q(p) norms instead of L^1(p); the remainder is bounded by ‖s‖²_{L^{2q}} which is O(β⁻²).
title: Rényi-Order Interpolation of Alignment Drift Constants

description:
The spacing variances 0 (rigid), 3 pi / 8 - 1 (GUE) and 1 (Poisson) are already proved to be strictly ordered. Extend this to the full moment sequence and conjecture that the second moment alone classifies the regime of a finite spectrum up to fluctuations of order n^{-1/2}.

The k-th moments of the Wigner surmise and of the exponential law agree only at k = 0 and k = 1, and the second moment separates all three regimes with an explicit gap.

Iterate the antiderivative recursion used for the second and fourth Gaussian moments to get all even moments in closed form, then compare with k factorial.

A single computable statistic classifies finite spectra, with a proved separation constant.

Some higher moment coincidence exists, indicating an unexpected relation between the Wigner surmise and the exponential law.
proof_strategy: Induction on k using integration by parts on (0, infinity), with the Gaussian half-integral as base case.
title: Moment Fingerprint Classification

description:
The edge-decile mass is now proved to be a strictly increasing bijection from the window ratios (1, infinity) onto (1/10, 1), so each tercile identifies one ratio. To convert the exp-580 non-rejection into a positive equivalence claim, the inverse map needs an explicit modulus of continuity on the observed range of masses.

On any compact subinterval [m0, m1] of (1/10, 1) the inverse of m -> decileMass r 0 is Lipschitz with an explicit constant C(m0, m1), and applying it to the measured masses 0.229 / 0.245 / 0.230 yields window-ratio intervals that overlap pairwise.

Bound the derivative of r -> harmCDF r (1/10) from below on the relevant ratio range, invoke the inverse function bound, and propagate bootstrap intervals for the three tercile masses through the resulting Lipschitz constant.

Positional universality is upgraded from a failure to reject into a quantified equivalence claim about one identified parameter.

The inverse is too steep at the observed masses to certify equivalence, so a larger sample or a second shape parameter is required.
proof_strategy: Use harmCDF_hasDerivAt_ratio and harmCDF_deriv_ratio_pos to bound the derivative below on a compact ratio interval, then combine with harmCDF_ratio_bijOn and edge_decile_lt_iff_ratio_lt to transfer the bound to the inverse.
title: Lipschitz Inversion of the Edge-Decile Map into a Ratio Equivalence Test

description:
The interior-argmax certificate is currently qualitative: an interior peak proves the weight is not matched. The conjecture upgrades it to a quantitative lower bound on the angle between the weight and the matched direction, in terms of the observed drop from the peak to the edge window.

If R2(w,m) + delta <= R2(w,t) for some t < m, then the cosine between w and the matched filter in the s-weighted inner product is at most 1 - c*delta, with c depending only on R2(w,t).

Prove the equality case of Cauchy-Schwarz for the weighted sums used in R2_le_matched, then combine with peak_margin_eq to produce the explicit constant.

The observed peak height becomes a calibrated measurement of weight suboptimality, usable to rank candidate weights without refitting.

Peak height carries no metric information about the weight and only the binary certificate survives.
proof_strategy: Use the Lagrange identity to express the Cauchy-Schwarz defect as a sum of pairwise cross terms, bound it below by the angle, and feed the peak-margin identity into that bound.
title: Quantitative Mismatch Angle from Peak Height

description:
Rounded execution of a straight-line polynomial program is claimed to be exactly an execution of the same parameterised family at a detuned parameter precisely when each parameter occurs once in the expression DAG. The approach lifts the three-rounding computation of the logistic product form to arbitrary DAGs. It matters because it turns backward-error analysis into a syntactic property of programs.

A straight-line program computing p_θ admits family-structural backward error with constant γ_k(u), k the depth, iff each parameter node has out-degree one in the evaluation DAG.

Formalise DAG evaluation with a RoundingModel; prove the positive direction by induction on the DAG, and refute the multi-occurrence case by exhibiting rounding errors that force distinct effective parameters in the two monomials of r*x - r*x^2.

Backward-error certificates can be generated by a compiler pass from program syntax alone.

Structural backward error is genuinely semantic and must be re-proved per program.
proof_strategy: Induction over the DAG with the composition lemma gamma_mul_bound; for the converse, choose rounding signs making the two monomial factors differ and show no single parameter reproduces the value for all x.
title: Syntactic Criterion for Structural Backward Error

description:
Pooling constrains the alternative but also the null; only the latter is unbounded. The conjecture lower-bounds the null misspecification gap by a divergence between stratum nulls, implying pooled AICc can be inflated arbitrarily by refining strata while every stratum stays sub-bar. It matters because it turns an apparent paradox into a quantitative diagnostic.

For nested fits over B strata, pooled dAICc - sum of stratum dAICc >= G - 2(B-1), and G is at least the sum of chi-square divergences between each stratum null and the pooled null.

Formalise the divergence lower bound for exponential-family nulls and instantiate it on simulated two-band Poisson data.

Pooled dAICc alone can never certify a component; matched strata become mandatory.

Pooled evidence carries stratum-level information after all, and the retraction of the persistence reading would need revisiting.
proof_strategy: Second-order expansion of the log-likelihood around the pooled null maximiser plus the already-proved sup-of-sum vs sum-of-sups inequality.
title: Null-Heterogeneity Dominance in Pooled Model Selection

description:
The parameter map predicts a realizable speed-up of 1/Lambda = 1.306 while the proven bound is 1.506, and the dispersion refinement lowers the threshold further. Formalising the predicted value as a two-sided interval turns the planned simulation into a genuine test rather than a consistency check.

Any window-ascending policy on the measured profile has speed-up in [1/Lambda - eps, 1/Lambda + eps] with eps determined by the profile CI, and never exceeds bound/(1 + ||p - flat||_1/(2 c_asc)).

Prove a stability bound for S_asc in the L1 distance on profiles (the analogue of gapX_stability) and instantiate it at the measured CI endpoints together with speedup_mul_le_bound_dispersion.

An observation above the refined threshold refutes the mapping; an observation inside the window confirms it, with no free parameters.

The speed-up is not determined by the shape layer alone and a rate-layer coupling must be admitted.
proof_strategy: Combine policy_speedup_le_Sasc with a Lipschitz estimate for revCost/scanCost in the profile and the proved dispersion refinement.
title: Falsification Window for the Scan-Simulation Closer

description:
The success count of an oblivious inspection schedule depends only on its size; the conjecture extends this to adaptive decision trees, up to a factor 1+o(1), unless the test predicates are pairwise correlated. This would make the guidance null a theorem about all heuristics, not just the ones measured.

For every adaptive decision tree of depth s over the sample space (Fin t -> ZMod N) whose queries are gcd tests, the number of accepted streams is at most s * r * N^(t-1), where r is the number of revealing residues.

Define depth-s adaptive decision trees over samples and prove the union bound by induction on depth; compare against hitSet_card_eq_scaled.

Every 'smart traversal' claim for gcd dives is refuted at the level of the model, so no experiment is needed to reject it.

A correlated predicate family exists where adaptivity provably helps, which is the interesting design case.
proof_strategy: Induct on decision-tree depth, applying the single-query union bound at each node and summing over branches.
title: Schedule-Independence Law for Oblivious Search

description:
For weight-w b-bit keys the modal trailing-zero class carries exactly a w/b fraction of the keys. The floor law then gives rho^2 > 1 - (w/b)^2 for every weight. We conjecture a matching upper bound, so that the balanced dial degrades smoothly in w and crosses the 0.53 floor at w/b about 0.848.

spearmanSq (weightBlocks b w) = 1 - (w/b)^2 + O(1/C(b,w)) uniformly in w, hence the balanced dial clears 0.53 exactly when w/b <= 0.848 asymptotically.

Formalise the sum of cubes of the binomial profile via Vandermonde-type identities and compare with (w/b)^2 C(b,w)^3.

The balanced-key envelope gets an exact boundary in the single parameter w/b, testable by a weight sweep.

Higher blocks of the binomial profile contribute at leading order and the modal fraction is not the right invariant for balanced draws.
proof_strategy: Write sum over k of C(b-1-k, w-1)^3 as a hypergeometric sum, bound it by the modal term times a geometric factor (w/b)^2, and combine with the dominant-block upper law.
title: Weight Cliff for Balanced Keys

description:
Mirrors contribute nothing and each Boolean oracle bit contributes at most a factor two. Conjecture that any battery of mirrors plus L factor-derived bits leaves at least |Omega|/2^L indistinguishable instances, and that this is tight for well-chosen thresholds.

For any finite family of magnitude mirrors together with L Boolean factor-derived probes, the largest class of instances agreeing on all readings has cardinality at least |Omega| / 2^L, with equality achievable.

Combine mirror_conditional_zeroInfo (mirrors are constant on cells) with multi_oracle_pigeonhole, then construct a tight family from dyadic factor thresholds.

The surviving positional channel is quantitatively capped: no amplification beyond one bit per threshold read.

Some interleaving of mirrors and oracle bits amplifies, which would be the first realized amplification in the round-70 programme.
proof_strategy: Fibre the instance set by magnitude cell, apply the pigeonhole inside each cell, and sum; tightness by an explicit dyadic construction.
title: No-Amplification Threshold for Mixed Probe Batteries

description:
The proved two-sided law brackets the break-even block size between C²ln(1/ε)/(44δ²) and C²ln(1/ε)/(9δ²) with δ = Q*−Q. Both constants are lossy because each replaces the entropy derivative log((1−Q*)/Q*) by a rational bound valid on a whole interval. Evaluating the derivative at the certified enclosure of Q* should collapse the ratio to 1 + O(10⁻⁴), upgrading the Θ-bracket to a certified asymptotic constant.

For Q in [1/10, Q*), n*(Q) = C²ln(1/ε)/(K²δ²)·(1 + O(δ)) with K = 2log₂((1−Q*)/Q*) rational to four decimals, and the certified upper and lower constants differ by less than 1 %.

Re-run breakeven_ge_of_gap and breakeven_le_of_gap with the Lipschitz constants instantiated on [Q, Q*] using the enclosure Q* ∈ (0.1100, 0.1101) rather than on [1/10, 1/5]; check numerically against the direct computation n* ≈ 1.25·10¹¹ at Q = 11 %.

A closed-form deployment rule with a certified constant, not merely a scaling law.

The remaining slack is intrinsic to the √n accounting rather than to the entropy estimate, which would localize the loss in the AEP correction term.
proof_strategy: Apply the two Lipschitz bounds on the short interval [Q, Q*], where the derivative varies by O(δ), and propagate the resulting rate sandwich through finiteKeyBits_neg_iff and finiteKeyBits_pos_of.
title: Unit Constant Ratio for the Break-Even Law

description:
The Hamming-weight tie ceiling equals 1 - (F(b) - 2^b)/(8^b - 2^b) with F the Franel numbers. Using the P-recursive relation (n+1)^2 F(n+1) = (7n^2+7n+2) F(n) + 8 n^2 F(n-1), derive the exact asymptotic ceiling 1 - c/b + O(b^-2). This upgrades the proved sandwich [0.9747, 0.9996] at bitlen 52 to an exact constant.

For the binomial tie profile on 2^b points, rho^2_count = 1 - (sqrt(3)/(2*pi))/b + O(b^-2), and the exact value is 1 - (F(b)-2^b)/(8^b-2^b).

Formalise the Franel recursion in Lean, prove the exact identity via the tie-attenuation law, then bound F(b)/8^b between explicit rational sequences derived from the recursion.

The count baseline's ceiling becomes a closed-form benchmark at every bitlen, making dial-versus-count comparisons exact rather than sandwiched.

The Franel normalisation is not asymptotically smooth, which would indicate an arithmetic obstruction in the cube sum and force ceiling comparisons to stay interval-valued.
proof_strategy: Attenuation law plus a discrete Gronwall/telescoping estimate on the ratio F(n+1)/(8 F(n)) obtained from the three-term recursion.
title: Franel Exact Ceiling Law for the Count Baseline

description:
The proved rate is 0 ≤ RΛ - d·thickness ≤ RΛ²/(d+Λ). Numerics indicate the true gap is RΛ²/(2d) + O(1/d²), so the constant can be halved. Establishing the exact second-order term would make the bound asymptotically optimal at both orders.

d·(R - shellRadius R d N 1) = RΛ - RΛ²/(2d) + O(1/d²) with Λ = log(N/(N-1)).

Replace 1+u ≤ e^u by 1+u+u²/2 ≤ e^u (valid for u ≤ 0) in neg_log_sub_mul_one_sub_rpow_inv_le and track the cubic remainder.

A complete asymptotic expansion of equal-volume peelings, with both the leading constant and the first correction proved optimal.

The correction term is not Λ²/2, indicating that the rescaling by d is not the natural one at second order.
proof_strategy: Taylor bounds for exp on (-∞,0] from Real.exp_bound, then the same squeeze as in the first-order proof.
title: Second-Order Expansion of the Rescaled Shell Thickness

description:
The complementation bijection is witness-preserving, so it should transport not only solvability but every modular counting class. The conjecture is that P to its complement is a parsimonious self-reduction, making the mod-2 assembly count a complementation invariant while the exact count stays #P-hard.

For every framed puzzle P, the assembly counts of P and of its complement are equal, and the map P to compPuzzle P is a polynomial-time parsimonious self-reduction of the assembly counting problem.

Combine assemblyEquiv with the piece-count encoding of the catalog reduction and formalise a counting-reduction predicate; check the mod-2 invariance on enumerated small instances.

Modular counting for jigsaw assembly inherits all hardness of modular SAT counting, with complementation as a free symmetry of the instance space.

The encoding, not the mathematics, breaks parsimony, indicating that piece multiplicities carry counting information.
proof_strategy: Lift assemblyEquiv along toFormula, use toFormula_compPuzzle for compatibility, then argue polynomial size of compPuzzle.
title: Parity-Preserving Self-Reduction for Assembly Counting

description:
The pin overcharge is proved to lie in [1/2, 5/4). Its running average over widths 2..N oscillates rather than converging: 0.87985 at N = 10^3, 0.93621 at N = 10^5, and 0.87497 at N = 2^18. The conjecture is that this is exact log-periodicity, with mean value 7/8 along dyadic N.

The average of census W (kPin W) - min_k census W k over 2 <= W <= N converges to 7/8 along N = 2^m, and in general converges to a nonconstant continuous log-periodic function of log2 N.

Use the closed form 2 - 3W/2^(k+3) on the gap-2 locus and 1/2 on the dyadic locus to evaluate the block sums exactly, then take the Cesàro limit along and between powers of two.

Amortised audit corrections for pin-based budgets are computable in closed form and depend only on the mantissa of the width.

The mean converges, and a single amortised correction constant suffices.
proof_strategy: Block decomposition over dyadic ranges, exact summation of the closed form within each block, then a renewal/log-periodicity argument.
title: Log-Periodic Mean of the Pin Overcharge

description:
Saturation at B* = 400 was measured under the harmonic weight; this cycle proves that no uniform window bound survives the passage to alpha = 1/2. The positive counterpart is a rescaling law expressing the saturation scale at exponent alpha in terms of the one at exponent 1.

If the harmonic dial saturates at B*, then the alpha-dial saturates at B*_alpha = Theta(B*^(1/(2-2alpha))) for 0 <= alpha < 1, and does not saturate for alpha <= 1/2 in the strong (uniform) sense.

Compute R^2(alpha) as a function of the window edge B on the stored counts for B in {50, 100, 200, 400, 800} at alpha in {0.5, 1}, and compare the fitted saturation points against the predicted exponent.

Every recorded saturation constant in the lab can be transported to the sqrt-weight by an explicit formula.

Saturation is data-driven rather than mass-driven, and each weight requires its own measurement.
proof_strategy: Use the proved envelope for T_alpha(B) to bound the marginal explanatory contribution of the window [B, 4B), then sum dyadically.
title: Rescaling Law for Window Saturation Scales

description:
The argmax-gap threshold mechanism of the existing KV-cache files and the dilation budget of this cycle describe the same cache. The conjecture is that the top-two logit gap distribution dilates with context by the same character, so the quantisation cliff and the key-count tax move together by one factor.

If the critical gap band scales as chi(lam) under a language shift, then the bit-width at which the argmax inverts and the key budget required to clear a retention bar shift by the same multiplicative factor.

State the coupling as an inequality between the critical band of softmaxW_rank_inversion and chi lam, and instantiate the dilation budget with the gap-based budget.

One experiment predicts both the quantisation cliff and the retention cliff for a new language.

Bit-width fragility and key-count fragility are independent axes and must both be measured.
proof_strategy: combine softmaxW_rank_inversion with the dilation law; show the induced budget satisfies the DilationBudget axioms with the same character.
title: Gap-Threshold and Key-Budget Coupling

description:
For a two-parameter fade fit, optimality is certified by three residual alternations. A new rung is informative exactly when it destroys the alternation pattern of the previous optimum. The conjecture turns this into a stopping rule for the bitlen sweep: measure until the alternation pattern is stable, then stop.

Appending the recorded U116 rung to the U96..U112 ladder strictly increases the minimal noise, while appending U120 does not change the optimal ratio by more than the identifiability window.

Compute the Chebyshev optimum of the five- and six-rung windows exactly in Lean and compare optimal (L, lambda, eta) triples with the proved four-window optimum.

Ladder experiments admit a principled stopping criterion that does not depend on a pre-registered band.

Minimal noise is not monotone in the data window, and the alternation certificate has no predictive content.
proof_strategy: Monotonicity of a Chebyshev optimum under adding constraints is immediate; the content is the exact new optimum, obtained by solving the two-parameter linear program on the enlarged node set.
title: Alternation Count as the Ladder Stopping Rule

description:
Recast the fade in the correlation-angle coordinate arccos, where the measured ladder's 116 rebound is compatible with a concavity hypothesis that raw-correlation antitonicity fails. Conjecture that angular deceleration forces convergence of the angle and forbids re-entry into the 0.55 spherical cap. This replaces a falsified monotone model by a testable curvature model.

If theta_n = arccos(rho_n) satisfies theta_{n+2} - 2 theta_{n+1} + theta_n <= 0 for n >= 3 then theta_n converges and lim theta_n >= arccos(0.488), so rho_n < 0.55 for all n >= 3.

Formalise angular deceleration and apply the plateau localisation theorem to theta; numerically check the derived rebound bound against the measured 112/116/120 rungs.

Band loss at U108 is permanent for the angular model class and the rebound is quantitatively bounded.

The fade has no monotone description in either natural coordinate, so the plateau reading is unsupported.
proof_strategy: Use corr_angle_triangle to justify the angle metric, then run plateau_of_geometric_deceleration on theta with a ratio derived from the second difference.
title: Angular Curvature Obstruction to Band Re-entry

description:
Paper 178's practical floor should be characterised as an approximate fixed point of the per-notch descent map rather than as a threshold. Writing the retention r(b) = s(b+1)/s(b), the floor is the bitlen where r(b) approaches 1 from below while s(b) is still positive, producing a long flat tail rather than an edge.

If r is monotone increasing to 1 and s(b+1) = r(b)*s(b), then for any eta > 0 the set of bitlens with |s(b) - lim s| < eta is an infinite terminal segment, and the crossing of any level tau > lim s has overshoot at most (1 - r(b*))*tau.

Extend crossing_no_jump and crossing_relative_overshoot to a variable retention sequence and prove convergence of the induced product.

The floor is a limit, not a threshold, and 'bitlen 54' is only the first bitlen inside a chosen band.

There is a genuine terminal bitlen after which the dial is exactly flat, which would be a new structural phenomenon.
proof_strategy: Telescoping product bounds plus monotone convergence over the rationals, with the overshoot bound inherited from crossing_no_jump.
title: Fixed-Point Characterisation of the Practical Floor

description:
A property determined by finitely many digits should be unable to separate any asymptotic behaviour. We conjecture that every prefix-measurable property containing a point contains rationals, non-normal irrationals, and continuum many of each, so that asymptotic digit laws are never prefix-measurable.

If P is a set of reals such that every x in P has an n with the whole n-digit cylinder of x contained in P, then P contains a rational, an irrational with nonzero-digit density 0, an irrational with nonzero-digit density 1, and uncountably many elements.

Instantiate Pyth.prefix_determines_no_digit_law and Pyth.not_countable_prefix_class at the cylinder witnessing membership.

A clean impossibility theorem: no experiment reading finitely many digits can decide any asymptotic digit law.

The cylinder topology would carry more arithmetic information than expected, contradicting the graft construction.
proof_strategy: Direct: the cylinder given by prefix-measurability already contains all grafted witnesses.
title: Collapse of Prefix-Measurable Properties

description:
Turns the parity threshold into a prediction about where the count advantage must vanish. Under decorrelation the advantage obeys alpha >= rho - sqrt(1-rho^2), which is positive exactly when rho > 1/sqrt(2), so the advantage cannot disappear before the dial crosses that value.

For every bitlen b with dial rho(b) > sqrt(2)/2 and decorrelated baselines, the count advantage satisfies alpha(b) >= rho(b) - sqrt(1 - rho(b)^2) > 0; interpolating the recorded readings places the crossing near bitlen 56.

Prove the inequality from corr_lower_bound with c <= 0, then instantiate at the recorded readings for bitlens 44, 52, 64, 72 and check the sign pattern of alpha.

The reported decay of the advantage from +0.07 to below +0.05 is forced, not incidental, and pins the crossing bitlen.

The two statistics are measurably correlated, which is itself a new arithmetic fact about the 2-adic valuation versus popcount.
proof_strategy: Substitute b = rho - alpha into the Gram inequality with c <= 0 and solve the resulting quadratic in alpha.
title: Crossing Bitlen of the Count Advantage

description:
The raw and excess readings of a dispersion reduction differ by the exact factor (D-1)/D, so both published columns encode one number. Conjecture that the residual dispersion left after the harmonic dial is itself explained by a single conditional parameter, testable by refitting on the conditioned population.

There is a constant c such that the conditional dispersion after removing the harmonic dial equals 1 + c uniformly across the population strata used in exp 577.

Refit the dispersion model stratum by stratum, converting all reported reductions through reading_ratio before comparison.

The residual structure is one parameter, not a new arithmetic phenomenon.

The residual is stratum-dependent and a further arithmetic covariate exists.
proof_strategy: Use the exact reading algebra to normalise the readings, then compare implied dispersions as in readings_consistent.
title: Single-Parameter Residual Dispersion After Harmonic Weighting

description:
The complementarity law asc + desc = L + 2 is a conservation law over the window. The conjecture is the matching minimax statement: no deterministic scan order can be uniformly better than the better of the two endpoint orders, up to a 1+o(1) factor, because an adversary can place the divisor where the order looks last.

For every deterministic order sigma of a window of length L there is a pool on which sigma's mean cost is at least (L+2)/2 - o(L), whereas the better endpoint order costs min(zbar, 1-zbar)*L + 1.

Formalise a scan order as a bijection Fin (L+1) -> window and the cost as the position of the divisor; the adversary picks the divisor in the top half of sigma's schedule.

The two orders studied here are not an arbitrary pair but the extreme points of the whole reorder class.

Some interleaved order dominates both endpoints, which would reopen the reorder-class question with a genuinely new candidate.
proof_strategy: Pigeonhole on the schedule: half the window is scanned in the second half of the schedule; aggregate with the per-key aggregation lemmas already proved.
title: Minimax Optimality of Endpoint Scan Orders

description:
The per-candidate cost of batching a stream is A/k + c + q·k^(μ−1) where μ is the big-integer multiplication exponent. We conjecture a unique minimiser k* = (A/((μ−1)q))^(1/μ), degenerating to 'bigger is always better' as μ → 1. This explains the measured word-model reversal as a property of schoolbook arithmetic rather than of batching.

For A, q > 0 and 1 < μ ≤ 2, the function k ↦ A/k + c + q·k^(μ−1) on (0,∞) attains its infimum at exactly one point k* = (A/((μ−1)q))^(1/μ), and the infimum is c − q + μ(μ−1)^{(1−μ)/μ}A^{(μ−1)/μ}q^{1/μ}.

Formalise with Real.rpow; differentiate or apply weighted AM-GM. The μ = 2 case is already proved as BatchYield.blockCost_eq_opt_iff.

Crossover thresholds for batch smoothness testing scale as a root of the setup/penalty ratio, so GMP-level constant factors relocate but never remove the optimum.

The optimum is not unique or not of root type, indicating additional structure (e.g. cache effects) in the cost model.
proof_strategy: Weighted AM-GM on the two nonconstant terms, with equality analysis via strict convexity of x ↦ x^(μ−1) plus Real.rpow_natCast bridging.
title: Square-Root Law for Optimal Batch Size under Sub-Quadratic Multiplication

description:
The collision-mass criterion 4·eps² separates certifiable from uncertifiable positions. The conjecture is that this is a genuine threshold: above the critical entropy nothing is certifiable, below it almost everything is. The upper half is already proved.

With H*(eps) = 2·log(1/(2·eps)), positions with Renyi-2 entropy above H* are never margin-certified, and for score vectors with collision mass bounded away from 4·eps² a positive fraction is certified.

Prove the converse of diffuse_not_certified under an anti-concentration hypothesis on the score vector, in Catalog/Applications/MarginScarcityEntropy.lean.

Portability screening reduces to a single entropy histogram per block.

Collision mass is too coarse and a higher Renyi order is needed.
proof_strategy: Lower-bound the top-1 gap by the top coordinate minus the second, and control the second coordinate by the collision mass of the tail of the sorted vector.
title: Renyi-2 Threshold Law for Certifiable Portability

description:
The finite-size correction to the p-adic ceiling decays like p^{-2b}, uniformly in the base. Hence every valuation-type dial saturates well before the bitlens used in the FACT rounds, and any residual bitlen dependence is diagnostic of a non-tie mechanism.

For all p >= 2 and b >= 40, rho^2(p,b) - 3p/(p^2+p+1) < 10^{-24}.

Strengthen padic_ceiling_close to a uniform numeric statement and instantiate at b = 40.

Provides a one-line falsification test for every future bitlen sweep in the programme.

Some base has anomalously slow saturation, contradicting the closed form.
proof_strategy: From the exact formula the excess is L(p)/(p^b(p^b+1)) <= 1/4^b; monotonicity in b then gives the uniform bound.
title: Uniform Bitlen Saturation for Valuation Statistics

description:
For rational rates with unit-numerator minority the context-doubling increment is multiplied by the interleaving period, i.e. the reciprocal of the rarest rate. We conjecture the general law for arbitrary rate vectors, where the pattern is quasi-periodic rather than periodic: the multiplier becomes the return time of the rarest domain. This would make the increment a function of the mixing rates alone, independent of the number of domains.

For a Beatty-type interleaving in which domain j occupies a fraction p_j of the keys, the context-doubling increment of the mixture equals the ceiling of 1 / min_j p_j times the pooled increment, up to an additive error of one return time.

Replace the periodic index decomposition of the s:1 reduction by a Beatty pattern, prove the head-mass identity at return times of the rarest domain, and check numerically on 70/30, 80/20 and 80/10/10 mixtures against directly computed knees.

Mixture increments are predicted from the rates alone, and a measured increment identifies the rarest rate of the corpus mixture.

Quasi-periodicity interacts with the profile shapes and only exactly periodic mixtures admit a clean multiplier.
proof_strategy: Bound the number of rare-domain keys in any window by the Beatty three-distance property, transfer the aligned head-mass identity with one key of slack, then rerun the knee bracket argument.
title: Beatty Interleaving and the Return-Time Multiplier

description:
The proved estimate franel(2m+1)*(3m+1) <= 8^(2m+1) is off by a factor of about 2.7 from the true asymptotics franel(n) ~ 2*sqrt(3)*8^n/(3*pi*n). Sharpening it would make the inversion threshold provable uniformly in parity with no finite case check.

For all n >= 1, 2*franel(n)*n <= 8^n, with the constant 2 asymptotically optimal up to sqrt(3)/pi.

Induction on n using the Franel recurrence (n+1)^2 F(n+1) = (7n^2+7n+2) F(n) + 8 n^2 F(n-1), verified numerically for n <= 40 by exact evaluation.

One clean estimate replaces both parity cases and the small-bitlen checks in the threshold theorem.

The crude max-times-total bound is essentially the only elementary route, and thresholds must stay case-split.
proof_strategy: Feed the three-term Franel recurrence into a strengthened induction hypothesis of the shape 2 n F(n) <= 8^n (1 - c/n).
title: Sharp Constant for Odd Franel Cube Sums

description:
In the narrow-spike limit the profile depends on the spike exponent only through an exponentially small remainder, while the spike weight survives in the limit. This explains why a fitted spike exponent can be boundary-censored while the associated mass fraction is stable.

sup over windows of |mixFrac w b₁ b₂ t − (w + (1-w) edgeFrac b₁ t)| = O(2^{-b₂}) as b₂ → ∞, while w is recovered exactly as the limit of the excess over the bulk prediction.

Upgrade the proved pointwise limit to a uniform bound using the closed form for edgeFrac and elementary estimates on (1+t)^{1-b}.

Reported spike exponents should be quoted as lower bounds only; spike mass is the identifiable parameter.

The spike exponent would be identifiable and boundary-censored fits would indicate a modelling error rather than flat likelihood.
proof_strategy: Explicit estimate of ((1+t)^{1-b}-1)/(2^{1-b}-1) − 1 in terms of 2^{1-b}, uniform for t in a compact subinterval.
title: Censored Spike Exponent versus Identifiable Spike Weight

description:
Pooling across seeds never inflates a correlation, so a pooled ladder converging to a positive floor forces, at every rung, a seed whose reading is at least the pooled one. The conjecture upgrades this rung-wise statement to a single seed family whose own ladder has liminf at least the pooled floor, making a pooled floor a genuine per-seed phenomenon rather than a concatenation artefact.

If the pooled readings rho_k converge to L > 0 and the number of seeds is fixed and finite, then there is a seed index k0 with liminf of the per-seed readings for that seed at least L.

Combine exists_seed_corr_gt_of_pooled_gt with a pigeonhole over the finitely many seed indices and a liminf argument along the resulting subsequence.

A pooled floor certifies a per-seed floor, so the dial signal is intrinsic and the QR-lottery construction retains structure at all bitlens.

Pooled floors can arise from a rotating set of seeds with no individual floor, and the pooled protocol must be replaced by per-seed reporting.
proof_strategy: Finitely many seeds plus a rung-wise witness gives an infinitely repeated index by pigeonhole; pass to that subsequence and take liminf.
title: Upward Inheritance of Floors Through Seed Pooling

description:
A transfer slope strictly below one is forced by noise in the measured footprint, and the slope identifies the noise-to-signal ratio. Correcting for it should reconcile the base dial readings across populations and isolate the disagreement in a single moment coordinate.

With slope s = Var x/(Var x + Var u), the corrected base variance shares of the five populations agree to within the proved ell-1 stability bound, and the residual disagreement is confined to the sigma_zy coordinate.

Instantiate slope_attenuation and slope_band with the recorded slope 0.898 to pin rho = 1/s - 1, then compare corrected base R-squared values against the wcov_stability_tv bound.

The base dial is fully transferable once attenuation is corrected, sharpening the contrast with the non-transferable increment.

The base dial is population-specific too, which would demote the footprint dial itself and force a redesign of the per-N dial.
proof_strategy: Algebraic identification of rho from the slope, then the total-variation stability bound applied coordinatewise.
title: Attenuation-Corrected Footprint Transfer

description:
The two extreme spines of the tree are the centred-square spine A^n (hypotenuse 2n^2+6n+5) and the Pell/NSW spine B^n (hypotenuse 1,5,29,169,985,...). They should bracket the depth of every node: logarithmic below, square-root above. This converts the sharp hydra bound (k+1)^(depth+1) into an explicit bound in the hypotenuse.

For every primitive triple with odd first leg, log_{3+2sqrt2}(c) - 1 <= bergDepth (a,b,c) <= (sqrt(2c)-1)/2, with both bounds attained on the B- and A-spines respectively.

Prove c_parent >= (c-1)/6 and c_parent <= c - 2*sqrt(2c) + O(1) from the parent formula, then induct along the descent.

An effective, closed-form bound on the length of any Pythagorean battle in terms of the triple itself.

There are triples whose descent is anomalously long or short, revealing a new arithmetic invariant of the tree beyond the hypotenuse.
proof_strategy: Bound 3c-2a-2b using a^2+b^2=c^2 and the extremal configurations a=b (giving the A-spine) and b minimal (giving the B-spine); nlinarith on each side, then a Nat induction on the descent.
title: Depth-Hypotenuse Bracket for the Berggren Tree

description:
Cycle 2 proved that a finite ladder cannot distinguish a positive floor from finite extinction: two explicit continuations match all seven recorded rungs, one floored at 0.218 and one reaching zero at bitlen 160. Identifiability must therefore come from a rate hypothesis. The conjecture is that the recorded ladder admits no uniform contraction factor, so the Aitken floor estimate in the catalog is not licensed by the data.

The unconditional half is proved: any q bounding the six recorded step ratios satisfies q >= 2, while every q-contractive ladder with q < 1 has the explicit floor rho_n - |d_n|/(1-q). The open half is that the least noise level making the ladder 1/2-contractive exceeds the model-free noise floor 0.0101 derived from step-ratio mismatch.

Formalise a noise-subtracted contraction hypothesis over the rationals, minimise the admissible eta on the six recorded steps, and compare with the recorded noise floor.

The plateau and extinction readings of the thread are formally unresolved by all data recorded so far, and the next experiment must be designed to bound the contraction factor rather than to add another rung.

A uniform contraction factor exists, the floor is identifiable, and the extinction forecasts are excluded.
proof_strategy: limit_not_identifiable gives the negative half; for the conditional half, iterate the contraction bound to a geometric tail estimate and compare with the Aitken identity aitken_eq_floor of the catalog.
title: Rate-Bounded Identifiability of a Dial Floor

description:
Budget monotonicity is proved; the missing quantitative law is concavity, i.e. that oracle retention gains are the sorted utilities and hence diminishing. This converts a fixed policy gap into an equivalent multiplicative budget, making 'x points below oracle' comparable across budgets.

With nonnegative utilities the oracle retention f(B) satisfies f(B+1) - f(B) >= f(B+2) - f(B+1) for all B < n, and f(B+1) - f(B) equals the (B+1)-st largest utility.

Prove that oracle value at budget B equals the sum of the B largest utilities by iterating the exchange kernel, then read off increments; test against the measured 32/64/128 retention rows.

The policy gap can be quoted as an equivalent budget multiplier, a scale-free way to compare cheap policies.

Retention gains are not governed by the utility order statistics, so per-budget measurement cannot be extrapolated.
proof_strategy: Show any top set by v of size B+1 contains a top set of size B, then induct; concavity follows from monotonicity of the order statistics.
title: Concavity of Oracle Retention in the Budget

description:
The window of a 2k-bit modulus contains residues from about k+1 bits up to about 2k+3 bits, and the exact band populations are square-root differences. We conjecture the occupied bands are contiguous and the histogram is unimodal with mode at the top band.

For N with bitlen N = 2k, the set of occupied bands is an interval of integers containing k+1 and 2k+3 as approximate endpoints, and b -> #{j : bitlen v(j) = b} is unimodal.

Apply card_band_formula for all b, use resid_left_end_le for the bottom endpoint and j = 3s for the top, and prove monotonicity of b -> floor(sqrt(N + 2^b - 1)).

Band-stratified models need no fitted band weights and no support assumptions.

Some band is empty between two occupied bands, contradicting monotonicity of the residue.
proof_strategy: Telescoping of card_lowBand over thresholds plus endpoint estimates.
title: Lowest Occupied Band and Histogram Unimodality

description:
A floor value is meaningless without the resolution 2 eta / |1 - lambda| at which it is identified. This cycle determined eta and lambda exactly for the U112 record, so the window becomes a theorem rather than a fit. The conjecture is that all floor estimates recorded in the thread lie in a single such window.

The Aitken floor 2299719/4850000 of the U116 record, the three-rung mean 14348/30000 and the optimal floor 725197/1780000 proved here all lie within the identifiability window of radius 2 eta* / (1 - lambda*) around the optimal floor.

Evaluate the three constants against the window bound; each comparison is a rational inequality closable by norm_num.

The thread's competing floor estimates are statistically indistinguishable, and the apparent disagreement is a resolution artefact.

At least two estimators are inconsistent at the record's own resolution, which refutes the single-lambda model class outright.
proof_strategy: Combine floor_identifiability_threshold with the exact eta*, lambda* of this cycle; all steps are exact rational arithmetic.
title: Resolution-Relative Floor Windows

description:
Cycle 4 proved that any quadratic-pool law matching the 44- and 88-rungs must carry a strictly positive constant c. We conjecture c is a property of the rank-correlation estimator at a given sample size, not of the sampled population, and that it scales as 1/N. This would identify the floor as finite-sample attenuation and remove it from the structural model.

For ladders on uniform integers, Pythagorean even legs, and Pell spines run with the same sample size N and tie handling, the fitted floors agree within their confidence intervals, and c(N) * N is constant in N.

Refit c on each ladder family; rerun one rung at N/4 and 4N and compare c*N. In Lean, state the invariance as a two-sided rational bound on the ratio of fitted floors and discharge it by norm_num once the numbers are recorded.

The structural model becomes the floorless quadratic pool, and the odds-law falsification at the 84-rung must be revisited as an artefact of sample size.

The floor is population-dependent and encodes a genuine non-channel source of correlation, which is a new object to characterise.
proof_strategy: Use the product law rho^2 = rho^2_tie * dilution to separate estimator effects from channel effects: the tie factor is exactly computable from the 2-adic profile, so any residual constant must live in the dilution factor. Then compare the fitted floor against the exact finite-sample attenuation of Spearman's statistic on the same profile.
title: Estimator-Side Universality of the Forced Noise Floor

description:
The quantity varr(addPart f)/varr f is an exact, computable property of a target that upper-bounds what any degree-1 encoding can ever achieve. Sorting a catalogue of number-theoretic targets by this statistic predicts, before any model is fitted, which ones a phase dial can move at all.

Across a catalogue of root-position targets, the measured out-of-sample degree-1 R^2 never exceeds the computed ceiling, and targets with ceiling below 0.05 never show a reproducible positive gain.

Compute rowMean/colMean/addPart for each target on the population grid and compare the ceiling with the measured cross-window R^2.

Encoding rounds can be scheduled by a cheap deterministic statistic instead of by search.

Measured gains above the computed ceiling would indicate that the fitted family is not degree-1 after all, localising a specification error.
proof_strategy: Rsq_additive_le_ceiling gives the inequality; the empirical half is a direct computation on the grid.
title: Degree-1 Ceiling as a Pre-Fit Target Sorter

description:
Additive elementary rules act as multiplication by a Laurent polynomial, so their stationary loci are kernels of circulant matrices over F2. The conjecture computes the dimension as the degree of gcd(p_r(x), x^n - 1), turning the observed mod-3 and mod-2 dichotomies into a single cyclotomic statement.

For each additive elementary rule r with stationarity polynomial p_r over F2, dim V(f_r, n) = deg gcd(p_r(x), x^n - 1); in particular dim V(90, n) = 2 if 3 divides n and 0 otherwise, and dim V(150, n) = 2 if n is even and 1 if n is odd.

Formalise the circulant kernel of p_r acting on F2[x]/(x^n - 1) and derive rule90_fixedSet_eq_zero_of_not_three_dvd and rule150_fixedSet_of_odd as corollaries.

The fixed-point dimension of every additive rule becomes a cyclotomic invariant of n, definitively divorcing it from Wolfram classes.

The discrepancy must sit in the constant sector corresponding to the root x = 1 in characteristic two, which then needs separate treatment.
proof_strategy: Identify configurations with F2[x]/(x^n - 1), rewrite stationarity as multiplication by p_r, and compute the kernel via gcd with x^n - 1.
title: Circulant Kernel Dictionary for Additive Rules

description:
Conditioning on our own existence forces one coordinate but leaves the others independent, by the cylinder factorisation. We conjecture that the conditional expected number of other civilizations is still at most N p, so observing our own existence cannot rescue a small Drake expectation.

E[#civilizations − 1 | site i civilized] = (N−1) p ≤ N p in the finite product model.

Exact conditional computations by enumeration for N ≤ 4; formalise conditioning as a ratio of Prb values and reuse prb_cylinder for the independence step.

Anthropic self-selection provides no evidential boost for cosmic neighbours within this model class.

The model's independence assumption is doing hidden anthropic work and must be replaced.
proof_strategy: Marginalise coordinate i via prb_cylinder, then apply drake_expected_count to the remaining N−1 coordinates.
title: No-Self-Selection Bound for Posterior Neighbour Counts

description:
The bitlen × cap ceiling table of the zero-fit dial factorises exactly into a row function and a column function. We conjecture this is not an accident of the dyadic profile but the signature of two knobs acting on disjoint parts of the tie profile: truncation of the tail versus rescaling of the whole space. A converse would make rank deficiency a diagnostic for knob independence.

If a two-parameter family of tie profiles is obtained by applying a tail-truncation operation indexed by u and a self-similar scaling indexed by b, then spearmanSq is a product f(u)·g(b); conversely, a nonvanishing 2x2 determinant in the ceiling table implies the two operations do not commute on the profile.

Formalise truncation and scaling as operations on List N, prove the product form in general, and exhibit a non-commuting pair whose ceiling table has rank two.

Every dial in the programme can be certified interaction-free by checking two one-parameter families instead of a full grid.

Rank-one is specific to the 2-adic profile and grid sweeps remain necessary.
proof_strategy: Compute the Kendall correction of truncated scaled profiles by the geometric-series argument of tieCorr_capBlocks, then divide by n^3 - n and observe the separation; for the converse, differentiate the determinant with respect to a perturbation of one block.
title: Rank-One Ceiling Tables for Composed Tie Statistics

description:
The k-th orbit count on tuples should be the Stirling transform of the orbit counts on injective tuples, generalising the proved rank splitting o_2 = o_1 + #(offDiag/G). This exhibits the moment hierarchy as the moment sequence whose factorial moments are the injective-tuple counts.

For every finite G-set X and every k, #((X^k)/G) = ∑_{j≤k} S(k,j) · #(Inj(Fin j, X)/G), where S(k,j) are Stirling numbers of the second kind.

Decompose Fin k → X over the kernel setoid, prove that each kernel class is G-equivariantly isomorphic to the injective tuples on the quotient, and count.

Gives exact formulas for o_k from finitely many invariants d_1,…,d_k, and recovers rank splitting as the case k = 2.

Some kernel classes fail to be G-stable, which would reveal an error in the equivariant decomposition of tuple space.
proof_strategy: Partition Fin k → X by Setoid.ker, use the SubMulAction of injective tuples, apply Burnside levelwise and sum.
title: Stirling Transform of the Orbit Hierarchy

description:
The original motivation for the assigned conjecture was to exclude the p=5 spread profile (8,2,2,2,2,2) via a k-auxiliary-class argument. That route is dead as stated, since the conjecture is false exactly at (k-2)(p-1). The conjecture here is that the profile is still excluded, using the proved triple criterion together with the profile dichotomy.

Every configuration of six auxiliary classes at p=5 realising the profile (8,2,2,2,2,2) has a triple of indices with deficiency sum less than 5, hence spans F_5^2 and is excluded.

Enumerate all deficiency profiles compatible with (8,2,2,2,2,2) at p=5 and check the triple criterion against each; for the profiles where the criterion is silent, run the exhaustive failing-configuration search of Direction 1.

Restores the intended exclusion with a formally proved criterion, and shows the exclusion never needed the false (k-2)(p-1) bound.

The profile survives, and a genuinely new invariant beyond deficiency sums is required to exclude it.
proof_strategy: Translate the class sizes into deficiencies, apply KneserLines.reach_eq_univ_of_triple to the three classes of smallest deficiency, and for the residual profiles invoke reach_eq_univ_of_exists_full or a direct finite check formalised by decide.
title: Auxiliary-Class Spread Exclusion at p = 5

description:
Repeated keys and a nonuniform prior are two independent discounts on the factorial sorting baseline. We conjecture that they compose exactly: state counts multiply, entropies add, and the optimal expected comparison count of a prior-sensitive multiset sorter sits within one comparison of H(q).

For a prior q on the n!/prod m_i! distinguishable rearrangements, the optimal expected comparison count lies in [H(q), H(q)+1), and H(q) <= log2(n!/prod m_i!) with equality iff q is uniform.

Instantiate the general finite-ensemble entropy sandwich of Novelty.PriorSensitiveSorting at the ensemble Input w of this cycle.

A single two-parameter ledger (repetition, prior) governs all comparison-sorting erasure, unifying two previously separate refinements of log2(n!).

Repetition and prior interact, so the multinomial floor is not the uniform-prior specialisation of the entropy floor and a joint analysis is required.
proof_strategy: Transport the Kraft/prefix-free entropy sandwich along the equivalence between the sorter transcript space and the rearrangement ensemble, then apply the uniform-prior equality case.
title: Orthogonality of Repetition and Prior Refinements

description:
Quantify when the calibrated pair-statistic test can see the proved -4/q^2 deficit. Combining the exact covariance at every lag with the exact finite-sample validity of the permutation p-value should give an explicit sample-size threshold above which the test has power above any prescribed level, while every marginal test remains exactly at its nominal level. Flatness of the lag spectrum means averaging over lags accumulates signal at a known rate.

There is an absolute constant c such that for n >= c q^4 / rate^2 the max-calibrated lag-averaged pair test detects the deficit at level 0.01 with power at least 0.8, whereas every marginal test has power exactly equal to its level.

Derive a Chebyshev or Bernstein bound for the pair-count statistic using cov_lag_eq, and combine with perm_pval_valid; validate by simulation at q = 5, 7, 11.

The pre-registered consecutive-v study gets a concrete sample-size design rather than an exploratory scan.

The deficit is undetectable at feasible sample sizes, which would retire the consecutive-v route as decisively as the j-marginal route.
proof_strategy: Second-moment bound on the pair-count using the exact lag covariance, then invert the resulting tail bound against the calibrated critical value.
title: Power Threshold for the Lag-Averaged Pair Statistic

description:
Exact identifiability shows one rung plus a ratio bound leaves an interval of length d0 r/(1-r) of admissible plateaus. Conjecture that each additional measured rung contracts this interval by exactly the factor r, giving a closed formula for the number of extra rungs needed to identify the plateau to within the U108 CI half-width. This converts 'measure more rungs' into a costed experimental plan.

After m further rungs the admissible plateau interval has length d0 r^{m+1}/(1-r), so identification to within 0.0445 needs ceil(log(0.0445 (1-r)/(d0 r))/log r) rungs, i.e. three at r = 1/2 and d0 = 0.0259.

Generalise plateau_set_exact to a prefix of m measured rungs and compute the resulting interval length in Lean.

The programme has an explicit stopping rule for the bitlen ladder.

Plateau identification is either cheaper or impossible, and the ladder design must change.
proof_strategy: Induct on the number of prescribed initial steps, applying plateau_attainable to the shifted sequence at each stage.
title: Rung Budget for Plateau Identification

description:
Every domain measured so far pays 4 extra keys per context doubling. The conjecture is that a long-range-structured corpus breaks this, and that the failure is observable as a crossover of budget laws rather than as a small deviation, at which point the mixed-workload envelope leaves the class of budget laws entirely.

There is a corpus whose increment differs from 4; for any such corpus no exchange law relates it to the ladder, and the envelope of it with German prose is not a budget law.

Measure one long-range corpus (LaTeX with cross-references) at ctx 512, 1024 and 2048; formally, check the hypotheses of Catalog.NET71.exchange_fails_of_inc_ne and of NET68's envelope_not_a_law against the fitted increments.

Deployment tables become genuinely two-dimensional: no single base-plus-increment law can size a mixed workload, and the crossover context must be computed per pair of domains.

The universal increment survives its sharpest test, promoting it from a fitted regularity to a candidate scale law of the architecture.
proof_strategy: Fit each corpus law from two contexts by ext_of_two_points, compare increments, and apply crossover_of_inc_lt to locate the context at which the sign of the shift changes; the envelope failure then follows from NET-68's envelope_not_a_law.
title: Increment Anomaly and the Breakdown of the Envelope Law

description:
The trailing-zero tie profile of the even legs 2mn of the Euclid family with odd generator m is literally the dyadic profile, proved in pythLeg_profile_eq_dyadic. Since the product law factorises the dial into a tie factor and a channel factor, the two ladders can differ only in the channel factor. We conjecture they coincide rung by rung within seed noise, including the first band miss at bitlen 88.

For every odd generator m and every recorded bitlen b, the Pythagorean even-leg ladder value rho_pyth(b) satisfies |rho_pyth(b) - rho_unif(b)| < 0.03, and rho_pyth(88) < 0.55 < rho_pyth(84).

Substitute the sampler n -> 2mn into the exp536 harness for m = 3, 5, 2^k+1 and rerun all ten rungs with the same seeds. Formalize the transfer of the tie factor in Lean (already done) and the band-miss consequence as an exact inequality on the recorded values.

The erosion is arithmetic-free: it depends only on bit width, so the dial can be calibrated once and reused across arithmetic families.

The channel factor is sensitive to arithmetic structure, isolating a Pythagorean-specific channel that the uniform ladder cannot see, and giving a new invariant of the Euclid family.
proof_strategy: Use pythLeg_profile_eq_dyadic to transfer the tie factor exactly, then apply product_law_factorised to reduce the comparison to the channel factors alone; bound their difference by the alphabet-universal dilution law, which is insensitive to the generator m.
title: Pythagorean Even-Leg Ladder Coincidence

description:
The proved sign-flip criterion compares expected costs. Under a quantile criterion the two window policies should flip at a different band width, opening an interval of delta on which mean-optimal and median-optimal orders disagree. The closed-form band law makes the cost distribution explicit.

There is a nonempty interval (delta_1, delta_2) containing 80 - 56*sqrt 2 on which the mean-optimal and the median-optimal window policies differ.

Compute the c.d.f. of u = 1/sqrt r for r ~ U[1,1+delta], formalise both medians in Lean and compare with crossoverWidth.

Deployment guidance must declare its risk criterion; the barrier map gains a second threshold.

Mean-optimality is criterion-robust and one threshold suffices.
proof_strategy: Invert the explicit c.d.f. of u on [1/sqrt(1+delta),1], solve the median equations, compare with the proved mean crossover.
title: Quantile Sign-Flip Band of Indeterminacy

description:
The straddle window of a dial eroding by at least d per rung has width below 2w/d. Conjecture that acceleration shortens it quadratically: if the rung steps increase by at least a per rung, the window has width at most 2 once a ≥ w/d². The recorded 96/100 straddle pair and the resolved bitlen-104 interval are the first confirmation.

For f with f(k+1) ≤ f(k) − d − a·k and half-width w, the set {k : |f(k) − B| < w} has at most 2 elements whenever a·d ≥ w.

Formalise as a statement about quadratic sequences and check against the recorded rungs 96–112.

Envelope certification reduces to a two-reading computation, cutting the experimental cost of each round.

Ambiguity windows can persist under acceleration, so band decisions need more rungs than currently budgeted.
proof_strategy: Sum the quadratic descent bound between the extreme straddling indices and compare with 2w, as in straddle_indices_close but with the arithmetic-progression step.
title: Two-Rung Ambiguity Window under Accelerating Fade

description:
Tie resolution can buy at most 0.0598 of Spearman advantage for the capped dial over bare parity, yet the experiment records 0.10 to 0.15. The excess must be response coupling, not granularity. We conjecture the excess is exactly the part of the response explained by the event v2 >= 2 conditionally on parity.

For the recorded response, Spearman(T, rate) - Spearman(parity, rate) = tie term (< 0.06) + coupling term, and the coupling term equals the Spearman correlation of rate with the indicator of v2 >= 2 restricted to even keys, up to O(1/sqrt(N)).

Re-run exp 523 with the response decomposed by parity and compare the measured coupling term with the residual 0.10 - 0.06.

The dial's advantage gets a mechanistic explanation and a predictive formula for other statistics.

The advantage is a sampling artefact and the recorded gap band should shrink under larger N.
proof_strategy: Decompose the rank covariance over the parity partition, apply the midrank collapse identity to each part, and bound the cross term by the tie ceiling of the conditional profile.
title: Slack Budget for the T-versus-Count Advantage

description:
The increment depends on signed second moments, while R-squared readings are sign-blind. A single explicit pair of populations already defeats any predictor built from the three marginal variance shares; the conjecture upgrades this from one pair to a robust family.

There is no function F with Delta-R-squared = F(R2(x,y), R2(z,y), R2(x,z)) valid on all finite populations, and the set of population pairs witnessing the failure contains an open set in moment space.

Perturb the constructed pair (rateSB, rateSC) within the moment parametrisation and show the increment gap stays bounded away from zero on a neighbourhood, using pgain_moment_formula.

Reporting protocols must record signed covariances; sign-blind dashboards cannot certify or refute an augmentation.

Some extra invariant pins the sign down, which would be a genuinely new constraint on admissible populations.
proof_strategy: Explicit counterexample (already proved) plus continuity of the rational moment formula to open up the witness set.
title: Inadmissibility of Sign-Blind Dial Reporting

description:
The finite-key machinery here is parametric in the rational rate rho and in the threshold zero Q*, so a certified positive rate for two-way post-processing above 11 % QBER would immediately extend the whole parameter table and the two-sided break-even law. The conjecture is that the same integer-certificate technique certifies positivity of the advantage-distillation rate up to roughly 20 % QBER.

For the two-way advantage-distillation rate r₂(Q), there are integer certificates proving r₂(Q) > 0 for every rational Q ≤ 0.19, and the corresponding break-even block sizes obey the same Θ((Q₂*−Q)^{-2}) law.

Define r₂ in Lean, derive its rational form analogous to secureKeyRate_ratio_eq, and search for the optimal pair (m, num/den) of the hybrid certificate at Q = 0.15, 0.18, 0.19.

The certified QKD parameter table extends past the one-way threshold, and the deployment moral (finite-key corrections dominate) is shown to be threshold-independent.

Two-way protocols have a genuinely different finite-key structure, isolating where the O(√n) accounting of this thread stops applying.
proof_strategy: Reuse finiteKey_extraction and breakeven_two_sided_law verbatim with the new rho and the new threshold zero; the only new work is a rational-form identity and integer certificates for r₂.
title: Advantage Distillation Above the One-Way Threshold

description:
Since the population gain of singleton phases is exactly zero, any measured same-window gain is finite-sample noise. The conjecture pins its size: expected apparent R^2 gain equals the number of dialled features divided by the sample size, up to lower-order terms. This converts an anomaly into a calibration check.

For a target with zero population correlation with a d-dimensional feature block, the expected same-window R^2 gain of ordinary least squares is d/n + o(d/n), and the cross-window gain has expectation 0.

Re-run the exp 483 pipeline with d in {5,10,20,40} and n varied by subsampling; fit the measured gain against d/n and check the slope is 1 and the intercept 0.

The +0.0215 is fully accounted for as an estimator artefact and the residual excess must be sought at higher degree.

Something beyond ordinary overfitting is inflating the same-window gain, e.g. leakage between the window splits.
proof_strategy: Population orthogonality (proved here) plus the standard chi-squared distribution of the residual projection; the population half is already formal via cov_graphInd_additive_eq_zero.
title: Overfit Scaling Law for a Provably Null Dial

description:
Pitch-class reduction modulo twelve is injective on decimal digits, so octave equivalence is vacuous there, but it fails from base thirteen on. We conjecture a sharp threshold with quantitative divergence of the interval-class and interval histograms.

Pitch-class reduction is injective on base-b digits iff b <= 12; for b >= 13 there are melodies whose interval-class and interval histograms differ in total variation by at least (b - 12)/b.

Generalize pitchClass_inj_of_lt to arbitrary bases, then construct explicit melodies in base b >= 13 whose folded histogram collapses two distinct interval values.

Mod-12 analyses of digit melodies are provably content-free precisely in the bases used by decimal studies.

Octave folding carries information even below base thirteen, which would change how interval classes should be reported.
proof_strategy: Injectivity is Nat.mod_eq_of_lt; failure uses the pair (0, 12); the total-variation bound counts the digit pairs whose distance exceeds eleven.
title: Base Threshold for Octave-Equivalence Faithfulness

description:
The Laurent coefficients of the 194-fold product in degrees 2k-194 are the elementary symmetric functions of the head table. Newton's inequalities for real-rooted polynomials predict log-concavity of these coefficients, giving a new structural constraint on any candidate head table.

For the Monster head table t, e_{k-1}(t) e_{k+1}(t) <= e_k(t)^2 for all 1 <= k <= 193, and e_k(t) != 0 for all k <= 194.

Formalize Newton's inequality for the polynomial prod (X + t_i) over R and combine with coeff_headProduct_esymm; evaluate on candidate tables.

The moonshine product has a unimodal coefficient profile, constraining admissible head tables.

The first failing index k exposes a sign pattern in the character values chi_196883(g).
proof_strategy: Prove Maclaurin/Newton inequalities for real-rooted integer polynomials by induction on derivatives, then transport along MoonshineHeadRigidity.coeff_headProduct_esymm.
title: Newton Log-Concavity of the Moonshine Product Spectrum

description:
The signed carrier attaches to each modulus a whole vector of character alignments, so the scalar ANOVA ceiling must be upgraded to a trace inequality on the between-cell covariance before the follow-up experiment can quote a bound. Conjecture that the scalar ceiling holds verbatim along every probe direction, with the same constant, which the scalar equality case shows is unimprovable.

For a vector-valued response Y with cell means M_c and grand mean M, and any unit probe u with directional ceiling rho_u, one has (sum_c w_c <u, M_c - M>)^2 <= rho_u * tr(TSS) * sum_c w_c^2 / n_c, with equality attainable for every number of cells.

Formalise the vector statement by applying multicell_contrast_le_of_rsq to the scalar response i -> <u, Y i> and taking a supremum over u; verify the equality case transfers from multicell_ceiling_sharp; then instantiate on simulated alignment vectors.

The signed follow-up experiment inherits a pre-proved, sharp ceiling, so a null there is quotable as a theorem rather than a p-value.

Vector-valued carriers have genuinely more separating power than any single probe direction, and multivariate criteria must be searched directly.
proof_strategy: Reduce along probe directions: for fixed u the response is scalar, so the proved contrast ceiling applies; control the supremum over u by the trace of the between-cell covariance and transfer the equality case from the rank-one configuration used in multicell_contrast_eq_of_measurable.
title: Multivariate Contrast Ceiling for Vector-Valued Carriers

description:
Over a fixed smallest coordinate x the Markoff Vieta dynamics is linear, given by an SL2(Z) matrix of trace 3x. For x = 1 and x = 2 these are the golden and silver dynamics, and the x = 2 branch coincides exactly with the Berggren silver spine. The conjecture is that every Markoff fibre is realized by a Berggren-type Pythagorean spine.

For every x that is the smallest entry of some Markoff triple, the trace-3x element of SL2(Z) governing the fibre is realized by a product of Berggren generators acting on a Pythagorean spine.

Formalize orbits of markoffFiberMat x and compare with evalPair products; begin with x = 5 (trace 15).

The failed global transfer is replaced by a complete fibrewise dictionary between Pythagorean spines and Markoff branches.

The x = 1, 2 coincidences are sporadic, isolating exactly which quadratic units are shared by the two trees.
proof_strategy: Classify each fibre by descent as in markoff_min_two_classification, then match the resulting SL2(Z) conjugacy class against products of the catalog Berggren matrices.
title: Fibrewise Berggren Realization of Markoff Branches

description:
Allowing n regrown heads at move n (the Kirby-Paris convention) keeps termination — proved here via Dershowitz-Manna — but destroys the elementary bound. The conjecture is that the greedy strategy then takes ackermannian time, placing the game exactly at level F_omega of the fast-growing hierarchy: not primitive recursive, yet still provably terminating in PA.

The greedy stage-dependent Berggren battle from a single head of depth d has length at least A(d), the diagonal Ackermann function, and at most F_omega(c) for an explicit c.

Define the stage-indexed game StepsToStage and prove length >= A(d) by induction on d, matching the known analysis of flat hydras.
