A precise placement of a Pythagorean game at the Ackermann barrier: the first non-primitive-recursive phenomenon on the Berggren tree.

The stage dependence is absorbed by the potential, showing the game remains elementary and that branching alone can never leave the elementary class.
proof_strategy: Transfer the standard Hardy-hierarchy analysis of omega^omega to the multiset potential Phi, using exists_maximal_battle for the strategy and phi_le_pow for the upper bound.
title: Ackermannian Lower Bound for the Stage-Dependent Pythagorean Hydra

description:
The coarse binary ceiling is attained exactly by top-segment responses, and the tip-blind ceiling is attained by an explicit nesting. The bottom-blind ceiling is currently only an upper bound. If it too is attained, the recorded dial value pins the response's resolution into a two-sided interval rather than merely excluding deep blindness, which strengthens every exclusion result of this cycle into a characterisation.

For every b > t there exists a response constant on the bottom 1 − 2^{-t} of the T-order and strictly increasing above it whose squared Spearman correlation equals the value given by bottom_merged_ceiling_gen.

Construct the response as the midrank map of bottomMergedProfile, as done for the tip in tip_blind_response_admissible, and verify covNest_eq_ssR saturates the Cauchy–Schwarz step in nested_spearmanSq.

The recorded dial determines the resolution depth exactly: t = 2 is not merely allowed but realisable.

There is a further loss factor between coarsening and attainability, and the ladder overestimates every rung.
proof_strategy: Follow aligned_response_attains_ceiling and tip_blind_response_admissible: exhibit the nesting, compute covNest and ssR of the coarse profile, and check the ratio equals the closed form.
title: Attainment of the Blindness Ceiling

description:
Upgrade the classification into a stability theorem: a normalized state whose concurrence deficit is ε lies within distance O(√ε) of the Bell orbit. The marginal-level estimate is already proved here as frobSq_marginal_eq (distance squared exactly (1 - C^2)/2), so only the passage from a nearly maximally mixed marginal to proximity to the orbit is missing.

There is an absolute constant c such that for every normalized M with 1 - concurrence M = ε, there are unitaries U, V with ‖M - localAct U V bell‖_F ≤ c√ε.

Formalize by tracking the two inequalities used in row_sq_of_sharp with an explicit ε, then constructing U from Gram–Schmidt on the (nearly orthonormal) rows and bounding the correction.

Maximal entanglement becomes robust: certification of near-maximal concurrence certifies proximity to a Bell state, which is what experiments actually measure.

There would be near-maximizers far from the orbit, meaning the maximizing locus is not isolated in the quotient and concurrence is a poor witness of Bell-state proximity.
proof_strategy: From gram_identity get normSq(rowInner) ≤ ε/2 and (row0Sq - row1Sq)² ≤ 2ε; apply Gram–Schmidt to the rows with quantitative error control; assemble U and estimate ‖√2 M - U‖.
title: Quantitative Stability of the Maximally Entangled Orbit

description:
The only universal lower bound currently proved uses the first slot alone and is tight for the uniform profile. A pigeonhole argument over a full period should force strictly more accumulated error whenever no rate divides the period, closing part of the gap to the greedy upper bound.

Every schedule satisfies max_i sup_t |R*count_i(t) - r_i*t| >= R - max_i r_i + c(k) with c(k) unbounded, so the one-slot bound is not tight for k >= 3.

Search exhaustively over all schedules of one period for small k and R to compute the true optimum, then formalise the resulting pigeonhole argument in Lean.

The optimal fairness constant is strictly larger than the trivial bound, and round robin's optimality is special to the uniform profile.

The one-slot bound is already tight in general, and the greedy or tree upper bounds are correspondingly loose.
proof_strategy: Within one period each client must receive exactly r_i services; count the sign changes of the lag vector and use pigeonhole to force a client whose lag exceeds the claimed bound.
title: Period-Wide Lower Bounds for Fair Schedules

description:
The sign structure of G(x) = sin x (2 - cos x) - x is proved: a single crossing xc in [2.1, 2.2) separates unresolved from resolved two-tone responses. Certifying further digits is now purely a matter of rigorous evaluation of G at rational points, since uniqueness of the crossing is already a theorem. This would give the rectangular-window resolution limit as an explicit certified constant.

The unique root of sin x (2 - cos x) = x in (0, pi) satisfies 2.1391821737 < x* < 2.1391821738, hence the critical time-bandwidth product satisfies 4.2783643474 < (Delta T)_crit < 4.2783643476.

Combine exists_rayleigh_critical_scale with Taylor-remainder bounds for sin and cos at rational arguments to evaluate G at 2.1391821737 and 2.1391821738 with certified error.

The Rayleigh criterion for a rectangular aperture acquires an explicit certified constant, refining rayleigh_threshold_exact.

The numeric value quoted in the optics literature is wrong, which would be a surprising failure of a textbook constant.
proof_strategy: Interval arithmetic on truncated Taylor series for sin and cos, plus the proved strict monotonicity of G on [0, pi/2] and strict antitonicity on [pi/2, pi].
title: Certified Digits for the Rayleigh Resolution Constant

description:
The lab-wide rule that replication legs must vary the master seed is conjecturally equivalent to pairwise disjointness of consumed index sets, which is exactly the proved equality case for inverse-variance pooling. Formalising the certificate turns a procedural rule into a checkable proposition.

An inverse-variance pool of legs from one stream reports its true variance if and only if the legs' consumed index sets are pairwise disjoint.

Generalise Design.trueVar_eq_naiveVar_iff_disjoint from two legs to a finite family with interior weights.

Published joint intervals are honest exactly when a disjointness certificate accompanies them.

Some non-disjoint families still pool honestly, and the certificate must be weakened to a cancellation condition on signed overlaps.
proof_strategy: Expand the pooled variance as a quadratic form in the weights; the off-diagonal entries are nonnegative multiples of intersection cardinalities, so the sum vanishes iff each does.
title: Disjointness Certificates for Replication Legs

description:
Beyond qualitative concavity, the midpoint defect of sigma should be pinned between two constant multiples of (s-t)^2 (1+s+t)^{-5/3}. The exponent 5/3 is dictated by the second derivative sigma'' = -6 (27t-1)^{-5/3} up to constants, so the conjecture asserts that the naive scaling is the true one uniformly on the physical range.

There exist 0 < c1 <= c2 such that for all s,t >= 1/27, c1 (s-t)^2 (1+s+t)^{-5/3} <= sigma((s+t)/2) - (sigma s + sigma t)/2 <= c2 (s-t)^2 (1+s+t)^{-5/3}.

Differentiate lagrangeExponent twice using HasDerivAt.rpow_const on top of lagrangeExponent_hasDerivAt, then apply the Taylor remainder bound on the segment [s,t] and check the endpoint scaling numerically on a grid first.

Concavity upgrades to a quantitative modulus, which is what any application (rate-of-convergence for averaging schemes) actually needs.

The defect degenerates near the threshold t = 1/27 where sigma'' blows up, so no uniform two-sided modulus exists and the estimate must be stated on [1/27 + delta, infinity).
proof_strategy: Compute sigma'' explicitly, prove it is negative and comparable to (27t-1)^{-5/3} on the range, and integrate the second-order Taylor formula twice over the midpoint stencil.
title: Five-Thirds Modulus of Strong Concavity

description:
Gram positivity for three vectors is equivalent to the ellipse inequality (c-ab)^2 <= (1-a^2)(1-b^2), which this cycle showed is strictly stronger than its AM-GM relaxation. The conjecture is that a record of k statistics against one response is governed by a nested chain of ellipsoid certificates given by the leading principal minors of the Gram matrix, with the innermost one pinning the matrix completely.

For k statistics with readings a_1,...,a_k against a unit response, the achievable set of pairwise correlations is exactly the set cut out by the nonnegativity of all leading principal minors of the bordered Gram matrix, and the k-th minor is tight precisely for the equidistant extremisers of the capacity sheet.

Formalise the k = 3 case (a four-by-four bordered Gram determinant) and compare its projection to the pairwise ellipse certificates already proved.

Multi-statistic records get exact feasibility tests, replacing the current per-pair certificates.

The projections of the higher minors are strictly larger than the pairwise intersections, and the pairwise certificates are the best practical tool.
proof_strategy: Use the Cholesky/Schur-complement factorisation of a positive semidefinite Gram matrix to express each minor as a residual norm, exactly as gram_det_nonneg does for k = 2.
title: Determinantal Hierarchy of Ellipse Certificates

description:
The dilution law is characterised by additivity of the reciprocal excess, proved in dilution_unique. The additivity defect of a recorded ladder is therefore a parameter-free residual: zero for every independent-channel model, and measurable directly from existing rungs. We conjecture it is strictly positive with bilinear growth and separates competing laws more sharply than any fitted goodness-of-fit statistic.

Delta(b,b') = e(b+b'-1) - e(b) - e(b') + e(1) is strictly positive for all recorded rung pairs and satisfies Delta(b,b') = Theta(b*b').

Compute all 45 defect pairs from the ten recorded rungs; bootstrap CIs from the three seeds. Formalize positivity of a representative set of defects in Lean as exact rational inequalities, in the style of quadratic_retrodiction.

Model selection for correlation ladders can be done without fitting, by testing a functional equation, which removes fit degrees of freedom from every band decision.

The channel picture is inadequate and the erosion must be modelled by a mechanism with interaction terms, contradicting the exact factorisation proved in product_law_factorised.
proof_strategy: Derive the defect identity from dilution_reciprocal_additive, then show that a pool of size p(b) yields Delta = p(b+b'-1) - p(b) - p(b') + p(1), which is identically zero exactly when p is affine and equals 2*kappa*b*b' when p is quadratic. Compare with the recorded values by exact rational arithmetic.
title: Additivity Defect as a Parameter-Free Model Selector

description:
Extends the decorrelated capacity law k·rho^2 <= 1 to families with pairwise correlation at most gamma, giving rho^2 <= (1 + (k-1)gamma)/k. The approach diagonalises the equicorrelated Gram matrix (1-gamma)I + gamma J and applies the same residual-norm argument used for Bessel's inequality. It matters because real baselines are never exactly decorrelated, so the usable budget is the gamma-version.

If k statistics have pairwise correlations at most gamma >= 0 and each correlates at least rho >= 0 with a shared response, then k*rho^2 <= 1 + (k-1)*gamma*rho^2, i.e. rho^2 <= (1+(k-1)gamma)/k.

Formalise the eigenvalue decomposition of (1-gamma)I + gamma J over Fin k and repeat the residual expansion of bessel_ineq with a non-orthonormal Gram matrix; check sharpness with the equicorrelated explicit family generalising parity_capacity_realizable.

Every recorded multi-baseline dial reading becomes a measurable lower bound on the mutual correlation of the baselines.

The Gram budget is not the binding constraint for correlated families and the parity phenomenon is specific to exact decorrelation.
proof_strategy: Write the Gram matrix as (1-gamma)I + gamma J, bound its inverse quadratic form from below by (1-gamma)^{-1}, then apply the projection inequality 0 <= ||w - P w||^2 exactly as in bessel_ineq.
title: Parity Capacity Staircase for Rank Dials

description:
Measured Spearman correlation of a tied statistic factorises into a tie-ceiling factor, now known in closed form, and a response factor. Since the ceiling is flat to O(4^-b) across bitlens, the entire recorded bitlen decline must sit in the response factor. Formalising a truncated-response model makes that factor computable and refutable.

If the response resolves only the first t tie blocks of a profile L then rho^2 = 1 - 12*sum_{j>t}(m_j^3-m_j)/(n^3-n); for the dyadic profile at bitlen b this equals 1 - (8^{b-t}-1)/(7*(8^b-1)) approximately, and matching the recorded values 0.78/0.72/0.65/0.61 forces t to be constant in b.

Formalise partial-resolution profiles in Lean over the existing spearmanSq framework and evaluate the closed form at b = 44, 48, 52, 64, 76 against the recorded dial values.

The dial's bitlen dependence is fully explained by a fixed-resolution response, and the dial becomes predictable at any bitlen.

The response is bitlen-dependent, and the dial measures an interaction rather than a property of the statistic.
proof_strategy: Split the tie correction as a sum over resolved and unresolved blocks, reuse ssS_eq_ssR_add for the resolved part, and evaluate the geometric tail exactly.
title: Response-Side Attenuation Factorisation of the Zero-Fit Dial

description:
The dial's effective base — the base p whose p-adic tie ceiling matches the observed rho-squared — drifted from 7 at bitlen 76 to 8 at bitlen 92. The conjecture is that this drift decelerates and saturates strictly between 22 and 23, the value forced by the hyperbolic erosion law's asymptote 5/14. This turns a soft decay statement into a bounded, sharply falsifiable one.

There is p_infty in (22,23) such that the effective base p(b) of the uniform dial satisfies p(b) -> p_infty, and p(b) <= 23 for every bitlen b >= 1.

Define effBaseOf as the least p with rho^2 <= padicLimit p, prove it antitone in rho, and prove effBaseOf (rhoModel b) <= 23 for all b together with convergence.

The dial degrades to a fixed finite-resolution valuation dial rather than to noise, so the measurement remains informative at every bitlen.

The effective base grows without bound, the reading tends to 0, and the hyperbolic fit must be replaced by a faster-decaying law.
proof_strategy: Invert padicLimit p = 3p/(p^2+p+1) asymptotically (p ~ 3/rho^2), compose with rhoModel, and use padicLimit_strict_anti plus effective_base_antitone to transfer monotonicity.
title: Effective-Base Linearity Law

description:
Only the sign-flip involution and the identity x^2 = 1 were used to prove the ensemble dichotomy. Replacing the second by a general even moment sequence should turn the indicator of an even walk into a product of moments over edge multiplicities.

For independent symmetric entries with moments mu_j, E[tr W^L] = sum over closed L-walks of the product over edges of mu_(multiplicity).

Refactor prod_entry_flipEdge_family and prod_entry_eq_one_of_even to carry a weight, then re-derive the counting theorems with the weight specialised to mu_j = 1.

All the counting results of this cycle apply verbatim to arbitrary symmetric sign-invariant ensembles, giving universality of the moment formulas.

The Rademacher case is special and the involution argument does not survive weighting, isolating exactly where independence is needed.
proof_strategy: Replace the configuration space by a product of symmetric measures, keep the edgewise sign flip as the involution, and evaluate the surviving monomials edge by edge using the even moments.
title: Weighted Dichotomy for General Symmetric Ensembles

description:
Subadditivity gives an upper budget but no explanation of why a 0.04-bit dial can add two bits to a joint reading. A chain rule, with conditional entropies defined fibrewise, would give matching lower bounds and quantify the redundancy between dials.

H(joint over insert a S) = H(joint over S) + sum over fibres of the conditional entropy of dial a, and consequently H(joint) >= max_i H(dial i) with equality iff every other dial is a function of dial i.

Define conditional entropy by the fibrewise sum already isolated in H_split_fiberwise and prove the identity by rearranging that sum; derive the equality case from the equality case of data processing.

Per-dial spread stops being paradoxical: joint gains are conditional, not marginal, informations.

The fibrewise decomposition is not additive, which would indicate an error in the empirical-measure model of capacity.
proof_strategy: Expand both sides through H_split_fiberwise; the difference telescopes to a sum of per-fibre entropies with weights equal to fibre probabilities.
title: Chain Rule Lower Bound for Heterogeneous Dial Batteries

description:
The catalog now realises the heights 1, 2 and 3 by explicit orders 231, 105 and 385, each generating an infinite odd-radical class. The conjecture is that every positive integer occurs as the height of some cyclotomic frame, so the height function from squarefree odd radicals to positive integers is onto.

For every positive integer h there is a squarefree odd n with max_k |coeff k (cyclotomic n ℤ)| = h.

Search ternary and quaternary radicals for the smallest witness of each h up to h = 10; formalise each witness with the explicit-polynomial and Möbius-cancellation method used for Φ₁₀₅, Φ₂₃₁ and Φ₃₈₅.

The height is a complete surjective invariant onto the positive integers, and the odd-radical classes stratify the orders into infinitely many nonempty height classes.

Some integer is skipped, which would be a surprising rigidity in the coefficient spectrum and a sharp constraint on any formula for A(n).
proof_strategy: Use Bang's bound A(Φ_{pqr}) ≤ p-1 as a ceiling and an explicit family attaining it; interpolate between consecutive heights by varying r modulo pq, controlling the coefficient by the numerical-semigroup indicator formula.
title: Surjectivity of the Frame Height Function

description:
All capacity results so far assume an exactly known retention gate. If the gate is known only to lie in an interval, the knee becomes an interval too and the sweep must serve its whole length. The conjecture is that gate uncertainty enters the design theory through the same scalar as tolerance.

With gate uncertainty [tau-, tau+] inducing a knee spread factor kappa >= 1, the exact s-point capacity is geoSum (a*b/kappa) s, so gate uncertainty and tolerance are interchangeable currencies.

Define kneeInterval A tau- tau+, prove monotonicity of the knee in the gate, and rerun the cycle-6 peeling induction with the interval-serving condition.

The whole deployment cost model collapses to one scalar combining tolerance and gate uncertainty.

Gate uncertainty is a genuinely second dimension of experiment design and must be reported alongside the sweep grid.
proof_strategy: Monotonicity of knee in the gate gives the interval; the serving condition becomes an inclusion of intervals, which is the cycle-6 condition with rescaled tolerances.
title: Capacity of Gate-Uncertain Sweeps

description:
The entropy destroyed by a narrow chained frame is the mass-weighted average of log of fiber size, and for pj = a*M+b the fiber profile is an explicit arithmetic object. Computing it yields an exact worst-case loss for each frame triple (A,B,M), replacing the crude log2(max fiber) ceiling. This makes pre-registration of an encoding's information budget possible.

For M <= B and A >= 1 the fiber of the label n under (a,b) |-> M*a+b has size #{a < A : 0 <= n - M*a < B}, and the uniform-population entropy loss equals log2(A*B) - H of the induced label distribution, a rational-weight expression in A, B, M with maximum value log2(ceil(B/M)) attained at the central labels.

Formalise the fiber-size formula in Lean on top of ChainedLabelWidth.chain_image_eq_range, then combine with LabelCollapseCeiling.D_le_mass_mul_logb_card and D_uniform_fiber to prove the exact loss identity; validate numerically over a grid of (A,B,M).

Every chained frame gets an a-priori information budget, so audits become a table lookup rather than a re-run.

The loss depends on more than the fiber profile, which would indicate an error in the deficit decomposition and force a re-examination of H_sub_H_push.
proof_strategy: Interval identification of the image (already proved), count of representations n = M*a + b by a division argument, then the per-fiber deficit identity for uniform weights.
title: Closed-Form Collapse Loss for Arithmetic Frames

description:
The dial capacity threshold for a triple is (3 rho^2 - 1)/2, which is negative exactly below rho = 1/sqrt(3). Below that horizon a third statistic fits with no correlation at all, so the capacity constraint stops binding. The conjecture identifies the bitlen at which the count-parity verdict degrades into a failure verdict with the bitlen at which the pooled reading crosses the horizon.

The count-parity-to-failure crossing bitlen b* is the bitlen at which rho(b) crosses 1/sqrt(3) = 0.5774; the recorded declines rho(44)=0.78, rho(64)=0.641, rho(72)=0.605 place b* between 80 and 100.

Run the uniform dial cell at bitlens 80, 88 and 96, record the pooled reading, and check whether the verdict changes exactly as rho crosses 0.5774.

The advantage bar can be replaced by a scale-free reading horizon, and the dial law acquires a predicted endpoint.

Capacity does not govern the verdict transition and the decline of rho is not the operative mechanism.
proof_strategy: The closed form dialThreshold rho 3 = (3 rho^2 - 1)/2 is already a theorem; the empirical half is an extrapolation of the recorded rho(b) curve against that horizon.
title: Capacity-Two Horizon at Reading One Over Root Three

description:
The proved sandwich accelerated n < gamma < accelerated2 n has width exactly 1/(12(n+1)^2) and endpoints that are rational numbers plus a single logarithm. Combining it with certified interval bounds for log(n+1) yields a machine-checked decimal expansion of gamma, and the sixth-order version reduces the cost per digit cubically.

For every d there is an explicit n = O(10^{d/6}) such that the accelerated3-based enclosure determines gamma to d decimal digits, and the enclosure is verifiable in Lean with only rational arithmetic plus one certified logarithm bound.

Instantiate the enclosure at n = 0 (already gives gamma < 7/12), then at n = 1, 3, 7 using Real.log_two-style bounds, and measure the digits gained.

Mathlib's bounds 1/2 < gamma < 2/3 can be replaced by an arbitrary-precision certified enclosure produced by a uniform lemma.

The bottleneck is certified logarithm evaluation rather than the acceleration, redirecting effort to interval arithmetic for log.
proof_strategy: Use accelerated_lt_accelerated2_sandwich together with rational bounds for log(n+1) obtained from the same Pade inequalities proved in this cycle, which bound log(1+x) between explicit rational functions.
title: Certified Decimal Enclosure of Euler's Constant

description:
Only states reachable from the initial states can ever participate in an experiment, so the block-counting potential should be bounded by the reachable counts. We conjecture the bound r_S + r_T - 2 with r the reachable-state counts, which is strictly better for machines with dead states.

If r_S and r_T are the numbers of states reachable from s and t, then inequivalent s,t are separated by a word of length at most r_S + r_T - 2.

Instantiate the abstract stabilisation theorem exists_stable_index on the subtype of reachable states of the disjoint union.

The bound becomes invariant under adding unreachable states, hence a genuine invariant of the behaviour rather than the presentation.

Reachability interacts with the refinement chain in an unexpected way, indicating the potential function must count unreachable blocks too.
proof_strategy: Define the reachable submachine, show obs is unchanged, and apply the existing partition-refinement engine to the smaller finite type.
title: Reachability-Relativised Moore Bound

description:
The Berggren maps act linearly on log c but arithmetically on log rad, exhibiting quality dynamics as a skew product over a hyperbolic map with silver-ratio expansion. The conjecture is that the depth-n quality distribution converges weakly to an explicit measure.

As n -> infinity the empirical distribution of q over the 3^n nodes at depth n converges weakly to a limit law supported in [2/3, 1], with mean determined by the silver ratio 3 + 2 sqrt 2.

Formalize the transfer operator on pairs (log c, log rad) using bHyp_bounds and quality_mul_log_rad, and compute the invariant measure of the linear part.

An exactly solvable statistical model of abc quality, with a predicted quality histogram at each depth.

Radical fluctuations dominate the linear expansion, showing that abc quality has no self-averaging behaviour even in the most structured family.
proof_strategy: Prove that log c is asymptotically n log(silver) plus a bounded cocycle, then model log rad by an additive arithmetic function and apply an Erdos-Kac-type argument.
title: Skew-Product Descent Operator for abc Quality

description:
Label merges can manufacture apparent conditional independence but can never hide a genuine dependence. Extending the data-processing inequality to conditional mutual information would show that all collision artifacts in routing tables are false negatives, never false positives, fixing the sign of every possible error in the reported tables.

For any labelling f and any joint weight on X x Y x Z, I(f(X);Y|Z) <= I(X;Y|Z), with equality for injective f; consequently a reported conditional independence may be an artifact while a reported dependence never is.

Slice the conditional mutual information over z and apply the existing per-slice machinery (H_joint_sub and D_superadditive) uniformly in z.

All per-dial routing tables inherit a proven one-sided error guarantee.

Conditional readings would need independent verification, and the claim that the single-dial tables are unaffected by chaining bugs would require a separate argument.
proof_strategy: Reduce to the unconditional statement fibrewise in z, then sum the slice-wise deficits using concavity of entropy exactly as in MI_pushFst_le.
title: One-Sidedness of Conditional-Independence Artifacts

description:
Quantify how far a population is from comonotone by the least ℓ¹ perturbation of the rates that removes all discordant pairs, and relate it two-sidedly to the discordance mass that governs the triage rule.

If δ is the least ℓ¹ perturbation of y making (x, y + δ) comonotone, then δ² ≤ Δ ≤ 2·δ·range(x).

Formalize the repair distance as an infimum over rearrangement-compatible perturbations and prove both inequalities against Catalog.UniformDial.discordanceMass.

The QS triage rule can be stated with a single interpretable population parameter.

Discordance mass carries information not visible to any ℓ¹ repair, and pairwise data is irreducible.
proof_strategy: Upper bound by explicitly repairing with the monotone rearrangement of y; lower bound by summing the discordant pair deficits along an inversion-minimizing chain.
title: Comonotone Repair Distance

description:
The proved converse says the conclusion of the mission conjecture holds exactly when the number of -Q fixed points is even. Conjecture that the invisible part of the eigenvalue data is generated by moves that add or delete a pair of -Q fixed points, giving a complete classification of eigensystems up to the sign invariant.

Two duality eigensystems of the same degree and weight have equal sign if and only if they differ by twists, permutations, and finitely many insertions or deletions of a pair of -Q fixed points.

Formalise the move relation as an inductive relation on eigensystems and prove sign invariance plus completeness in degrees at most 4 by exhaustive case analysis.

A complete normal form for duality eigensystems modulo the sign, i.e. a classification of what the functional equation can and cannot see.

There are sign-equivalent systems not related by the moves, hence a finer invariant beyond the fixed-point parity.
proof_strategy: Sign invariance is immediate from prod_alpha_eq_sign_mul_pow; completeness proceeds by induction on the number of duality 2-cycles, normalising each pair by a twist.
title: Kernel of the Sign Invariant and Double-Minus Moves

description:
The thick shells form a terminal block, so the volume they carry is exactly (thickCount)/N times the volume of the ball. The conjecture converts the count bound into a volume statement and locates the regime where the thick block is negligible.

sup over N >= (R/delta)^d / 2 of thickCount R d N delta / N tends to 0 exponentially in d, while the supremum over all N equals 1.

Combine thickCount_le with all_thin_iff_card; the exponential decay follows from N >= (R/delta)^d/2 and thickCount <= 1 + R/(d delta).

Boundary concentration is quantified at the level of volume, not just of radii.

There is an intermediate range of N where thick shells carry a constant volume fraction, contradicting the counting bound.
proof_strategy: Divide the proved count bound by N and substitute the threshold value of N.
title: Volume Fraction of the Thick Block

description:
The Markoff binary tree embeds depth-preservingly in the Berggren ternary tree, but the arithmetic sizes grow at different exponential rates, silver versus golden. The conjecture quantifies the resulting distortion by the ratio of the two logarithmic growth rates.

The embedding is an isometry for the word metric and has arithmetic distortion exactly log(3+2*sqrt 2)/log((3+sqrt 5)/2).

Formalize the limits log(bHyp n)/n and log(markoffSpine n)/n and compute their ratio.

A precise metric dictionary between the two trees, replacing the false isometric transfer.

Growth along generic branches differs from growth along spines, revealing branch-dependent exponents.
proof_strategy: Solve both linear recursions via their proved characteristic polynomials and take logarithms.
title: Distortion Constant of the Markoff-in-Berggren Embedding

description:
Scalar sections of the Moebius bundle must vanish in every unit window (now proved). We conjecture the sharp rank threshold: for R^d-valued antiperiodic maps, nowhere-vanishing continuous sections exist exactly when d >= 2, with the circle map as universal witness. This separates the d = 1 obstruction from its higher-rank vanishing.

A continuous f : R -> R^d with f(x+1) = -f(x) and f(x) != 0 for all x exists if and only if d >= 2; for d = 1 the zero set meets every interval of length one.

Formalise the witness x -> (cos(pi x), sin(pi x), 0, ..., 0) for d >= 2 and derive the d = 1 impossibility from MoebiusSections.antiperiodic_has_zero_window.

Non-orientability of the Moebius bundle is a strictly rank-one phenomenon, quantifying when orientation data can be evaded.

Some higher-rank twisted bundle over the circle still forces a zero, indicating an obstruction beyond the first Stiefel-Whitney class.
proof_strategy: Existence: explicit trigonometric witness. Non-existence for d = 1: intermediate value theorem on each unit window, as already proved.
title: Rank Threshold for Nowhere-Vanishing Twisted Sections

description:
The four-constructor carrier was topologised by fiat as EReal ⊔ {Φ}. We conjecture that this is forced: any compact Hausdorff topology making the finite fragment an open copy of the line and nullity isolated is that one. The approach is an ends argument for the real line inside a two-point remainder compactification.

If t is a compact Hausdorff topology on Transreal such that fin is an open embedding and {null} is open, then t equals the topology induced by the bijection Transreal ≃ EReal ⊕ Unit.

Formalise the end compactification of ℝ, show any compactification with two-point remainder of a two-ended locally compact space is the end compactification, then apply it to the complement of {null}.

All sharpness theorems about the division boundary become topology-canonical rather than model-dependent.

There is an exotic compact Hausdorff transreal topology; the guard's necessity would have to be re-examined in it.
proof_strategy: Complement of {null} is compact Hausdorff, contains range fin open with two-point complement; show each remainder point has a neighbourhood basis meeting exactly one end using local compactness and connectedness of the line.
title: Uniqueness of the Two-Point Transreal Compactification

description:
The upper bracketing degree of the binomial weights is ⌊(n+1)α⌋ with α = p/(p+q), a Beatty sequence. The conjecture is that the increment word of the argmax staircase is the Sturmian word of slope α, so the combinatorics of binomial peaks is the combinatorics of a circle rotation.

The word w n = lastArgmax (n+1) - lastArgmax n ∈ {0,1} is the Sturmian/Beatty word of slope p/(p+q); in particular it is balanced and has exactly n+1 factors of length n when α is irrational.

Identify lastArgmax with ⌊(n+1)α⌋ (already proved) and connect to mathlib's Beatty sequence API; verify balance numerically for several α.

Transfers the full Sturmian toolkit (continued fractions, three-distance theorem) to statements about binomial peaks.

The staircase carries extra arithmetic from the +1 shift and is not literally Sturmian, which itself is a precise structural statement.
proof_strategy: Rewrite ⌊(n+1)α⌋ - ⌊nα⌋ and apply the standard characterisation of balanced words.
title: Sturmian Structure of the Argmax Staircase

description:
The invariant minMass is submultiplicative but not multiplicative (strict at (2,2)). We conjecture that the multiplicativity defect is always positive beyond the trivial windows and that the invariant is log-concave in the window length.

minMass(K)^2 >= minMass(K-1) * minMass(K+1) for all K >= 2, and minMass K1 * minMass K2 > minMass (K1+K2) for all K1, K2 >= 2.

Check against the certified values 2,4,6,...,20,?,24 and against any new witness; formalise the general inequality by an interpolation argument on seeds.

minMass has a Fekete limit computed by its small values, giving the exact growth base as an infimum over certified windows.

Some window is anomalously expensive, which would localise the failure of the linear law to a specific K.
proof_strategy: Combine PTERigid.minMass_submul with a splitting construction that turns a window-(K+1) witness into a window-(K-1) and a window-2 witness of controlled mass.
title: Log-Concavity of the Minimal Mass Invariant

description:
Each added regressor improves the weighted fit by ⟨r,z⟩²/‖z‖². Summing these gains over arbitrary footprint-derived regressors should saturate at a population invariant determined by the concordant and discordant pair masses, explaining why augmented R² is stable across regimes.

For rank-encoded dials, sup over finite regressor families of the augmented R² equals 1 − Δ/(C + Δ).

Define the family of monotone re-encodings of the footprint, use augment_gain_eq iteratively, and bound the total gain with wcov_budget.

The augmented R² ceiling is a regime-free population statistic, fully explaining the uniform-vs-balanced agreement.

Augmented R² depends on the regressor list in an essential way and cross-regime comparisons need the list fixed.
proof_strategy: Gram–Schmidt in the p-weighted inner product; upper bound by Cauchy–Schwarz plus the concordance budget, lower bound by an explicit rank-encoding family.
title: Augmentation Saturation Plateau

description:
The truncation scaling of the head dial is now pinned for every pure power law with exponent at most one. The conjecture is that for a bulk times edge mixture the same scaling is governed by the bulk exponent alone, so the ratio of dials at two truncations estimates the bulk exponent and is blind to the edge. Combined with the window law, which sees the edge and not the bulk, this separates the two parameters.

For a mixture with weights w in (0,1) and exponents a < 1 < b, the mixture head mass times n^{1-a} tends to (1-a) times the mixture head sum at window m, with no dependence on b.

Split the mixture head sum by the mediant identity of HarmonicBulkSteeperEdge, apply headSum_sandwich_lower and headSum_sandwich_upper to the shallow component and boundedness to the steep one, then squeeze.

Recorded dials at two truncations yield the bulk exponent directly, and the window statistics then yield the edge parameters.

The truncation scaling mixes both exponents, and dial levels at different truncations cannot be compared without knowing the edge.
proof_strategy: Bound the steep component by a convergent series and the shallow one by the proved sandwich; the ratio of the two contributions is O(n^{a-1}).
title: Bulk-Exponent Readout from Two Truncations

description:
The tree discrepancy theorem charges exactly one unit per splitting level, so minimising discrepancy over splitting trees is a weighted-path-length problem. Huffman trees should therefore beat balanced trees on skewed profiles, replacing the log2(k) bound by an entropy bound.

For every positive rate profile there is a splitting tree whose recursive Bresenham schedule has normalised discrepancy at most 1 + H(r)/log 2, where H is the entropy of the normalised rates.

Define Huffman trees over STree in Lean, prove the weighted-path-length identity, and combine it with STree.tree_disc; compare numerically against bal_isFair on skewed profiles such as (1,1,1,100).

Scheduling discrepancy is bounded by an information-theoretic quantity, bridging source coding and fair queueing.

Per-client discrepancy is not governed by average depth, so the level-charging bound of tree_disc must be non-uniform across clients.
proof_strategy: Refine tree_disc to a per-client bound involving the depth of that client's leaf, then apply the Huffman optimality theorem for weighted external path length.
title: Huffman-Shaped Splitting Trees

description:
Shtarkov sums tensorise under independent repetition of the experiment. The conjecture is that the curvature of the k-fold product pool tends to zero exponentially in k at a rate given by the Chernoff separation of the sources, so greedy library design becomes asymptotically optimal for long blocks even for pools where it is not optimal per symbol.

If the sources of Omega are pairwise distinct then curvature of the k-fold product pool is at most C * exp(-c k) for constants depending only on the pool, hence the greedy gap is at most (|Omega| - 1) * C * exp(-c k) times the optimum.

Combine the catalog tensorisation lemmas for Shtarkov sums with greedy_low_curvature_gap; verify the predicted rate numerically for two-source pools before formalising.

Greedy universal decompressor libraries are asymptotically optimal in the block length, a strong practical guarantee.

Curvature is not tensor-stable, which would identify a genuinely single-letter obstruction to greedy library design.
proof_strategy: Show the marginal ratio of a product pool factorises up to error terms controlled by the total-variation product bound, then apply the Chernoff estimate.
title: Curvature Decay for Tensor-Power Pools

description:
The bounded search is now
   formalized as the computable function `fermatSearch : ℕ → Option (ℕ × ℕ)`, together
   with its soundness (`fermatSearch_sound`) and completeness (`fermatSearch_complete`)
   theorems, upgrading the *existence* criterion to a *correct algorithm* theorem.
   Remaining refinements: extract the returned `t` as an explicit `Nat.sqrt`-based
   witness, and show `fermatSearch` returns `none` exactly on primes and prime powers'
   trivial-only cases.
title: Deterministic termination of the scan. — Done

description:
The Fermat scan cost of an odd integer equals the minimum over its divisor pairs of the midpoint excess over the integer square root. We conjecture that this minimum is governed by the number of distinct prime factors, so that highly composite integers are strictly easier to navigate than semiprimes of the same size. This turns the 'navigation sensor' of the campaign into a multiplicative-structure statistic.

For odd N with omega(N) distinct prime factors, min over d | N, 1 < d < N of ((d + N/d)/2 - isqrt N) is at most C * N^(1/2) * 2^(-omega(N)) for an absolute constant C, and this is sharp up to constants.

Instantiate scanHit_iff_exists_divisor and compute the minimum over Nat.divisors N for all odd N below 10^6, stratified by omega(N); then attempt the upper bound by a pigeonhole over the 2^omega(N) divisor pairs inside [1, sqrt N].

The navigation sensor is a multiplicative statistic and its hardness is concentrated exactly on semiprimes, sharpening barrier 6 to a statement about the divisor lattice.

The scan cost is dominated by the extreme divisor pair, and the sensor carries no more information than the least prime factor.
proof_strategy: Use the proved bijection between nontrivial divisor pairs and nontrivial Fermat representations; distribute the divisors of N in [1, sqrt N] and bound the smallest midpoint excess by the largest gap between consecutive divisors near sqrt N.
title: Divisor-Lattice Navigation Spectrum

description:
The value-guided search wins because it sweeps values upward, and its first hit is provably min(p,q). The worst case is settled: SearchOrder.enumeration_defeated shows every N-independent enumeration is defeated by large semiprimes. The open part is the average case, where a single composite probe can batch many primes at once.

For every search order determined by candidate values alone, the expected number of expansions before the first a with gcd(a,N) > 1 is at least min(p,q)^(1-o(1)) for a uniformly random semiprime N = pq, even allowing composite probes that batch many prime tests into one gcd.

Formalize the averaged adversary argument over value-only orderings using the linear ticket bound TreeSieve.lottery_union_bound to cap how many primes a bounded prefix can cover, and check it against randomized simulations of batching heuristics.

Value-guided tree search cannot beat exponent 1/2, closing the multi-target route in the strong sense.

There is a value-only ordering below trial division, which would be a genuinely new factoring heuristic.
proof_strategy: Fix the order, then average over semiprimes: for any prefix of the order shorter than min(p,q), the set of moduli hit by that prefix has density controlled by the total bit-length of its elements, as in TreeSieve.lottery_union_bound; the worst-case step is already SearchOrder.enumeration_defeated.
title: Optimality of Ascending Order for Relaxed Multi-Target Search

description: For a specified finite neural-state transition graph, assign each readout channel a topology generated by its distinguishable state subsets. Test whether adding a readout node strictly coarsens consensus exactly when that node excludes an open set shared by all previous readouts. A measured transition graph and readout table make this directly falsifiable by finite computation.
title: Empirical encoding conjecture

description:
Neither acceleration proved here is specific to 3n+1: drop-below soundness needs only well-founded descent, and the scale-k sieve needs only sparsity of non-descending residues, which follows from an affine transport formula on Z/m^k. The conjecture is that certified sublinear verification transfers to every such map below the critical exponent.

For an integer map that is affine on residue classes mod m^k with transport slope q^s / m^k, the drop-below plus residue sieve certifies [1,B] with examined-input density tending to zero precisely when log q / log m < 1.

Instantiate sieve_scale for the 5n+1 and 3n+1-analogue maps, compute non-descending densities at k <= 10, and check the predicted phase transition at log q / log m = 1.

A single certified verification engine covers a whole family of dynamical conjectures, with a proved cost model.

Some sub-critical map resists sieving, isolating an arithmetic obstruction invisible to the density heuristic.
proof_strategy: Abstract terras to a general transport lemma; re-run the Chebyshev counting with log q / log m in place of log 3 / log 2; reuse sieve_scale verbatim.
title: Transport Sieves for General qn+r Dynamics

description:
The formalised bound says n runs of a test decide whether two dishes are observationally equivalent, but exhaustive enumeration for n <= 4 and a 5-dish Fine-Wilf extremal witness both indicate that n-1 runs suffice. The conjecture is that n-1 is the exact threshold. It matters because it converts a linear bound into an exact query complexity for repeated destructive testing.

For every finite dish type D with n = card D >= 2, every test t : D -> Bool x D and all dishes d, e: if transcript t d j = transcript t e j for all j < n - 1, then transcript t d m = transcript t e m for all m; and there exist D, t, d, e realising first disagreement at index n - 2.

Starting from the formalised orbit dichotomy and the proved threshold n, tighten the window estimate by one, e.g. by showing that when both transients are nonempty the two orbits cannot both saturate the dish space; verify the extremal side by extending clockTest to coprime cycle pairs p + q = n.

Observational equivalence under destructive testing has exact query complexity n - 1, matching the destruction-depth bound and making the two sharp constants of the theory equal.

There is a family of tests whose dishes stay indistinguishable for at least n - 1 runs; such a family would be a new extremal object interpolating between rho shapes and coprime cycle pairs.
proof_strategy: Reuse the proved dichotomy (orbit_period_eq_of_meet and card_add_card_le_of_disjoint) and the engine transcript_agree_of_window, then improve the window estimate by one unit: in the disjoint case the gcd is at most the smaller period, and in the merging case the shared cycle is counted once in the union of the orbits.
title: Sharp Distinguishing Threshold for Destructive Tests

description:
Prefix-sum dominance implies cost dominance but is only partial, whereas cost is total. The induced structure should be a lattice whose minimal elements are exactly the mass-sorted enumerations, so distance-to-optimal becomes a structural rather than scalar quantity.

On a fixed mass vector the front-loading preorder on enumerations is a lattice whose minima are the mass-sorted orders, and the cost gap is monotone in the lattice distance.

Formalise the dominance order on permutations, prove minimality via the exchange theorem, and check lattice axioms on small cases by decide.

Audits can report a structural distance-to-optimal instead of a single speedup.

Only scalar cost comparison is available and partial audits stay incomparable.
proof_strategy: Abel identity cost_eq_tail_sums plus Hardy-Littlewood-Polya majorization; minimality from probeCost_masssort_le.
title: Majorization Lattice of REORDER Policies

description:
The B₂ orbit was shown to be the Pell ladder, so its discrete logarithm modulo p should be the discrete logarithm in the norm-one torus of 𝔽_p(√2). Establishing the isomorphism would give the exact period of the B₂ spine (p∓1 depending on the quadratic character of 2) and replace pigeonhole period bounds by sharp ones.

For odd prime p the cyclic group generated by B₂ in GL₃(ℤ/p) is isomorphic to the norm-one subgroup of 𝔽_p(√2)^×, of order p−1 if 2 is a square mod p and p+1 otherwise.

Construct the explicit ring map ℤ[√2] → Mat₃ sending 1+√2 to a square root of B₂ on the Pell plane, then compute orders for a range of primes and compare with p∓1.

The 'discrete-logarithm-like problem for B₂' becomes a torus discrete logarithm with known index-calculus behaviour, giving a concrete hardness assumption.

The B₂ spine has a smaller period than the torus predicts, giving an unexpected shortcut attack on the seed-recovery problem.
proof_strategy: Diagonalise B₂ over 𝔽_p(√2) using the proved factorisation (B₂+I)(B₂²−6B₂+I)=0; identify the two-dimensional block with multiplication by 3+2√2; compute the order of that unit.
title: Norm-One Torus Model of the B2 Discrete Logarithm

description:
The dial regression converges to a single-bit tropical regression as alpha grows. Quantifying the rate identifies the exponent beyond which the grid carries no information, giving a principled right endpoint for future alpha grids.

With M the smallest and M' the second smallest active prime, |R^2(alpha) - R^2(tropical)| = O((M/M')^alpha) as alpha -> infinity.

The pointwise estimate |normDial - tropDial| <= |supp| * (M/M')^alpha is already formalized; propagate it through the covariance quotient and check numerically on the exp-577 supports.

The alpha grid can be truncated rigorously, cutting compute per dial fit.

The collapse is slower than geometric, implying long-range interference between primes in the window.
proof_strategy: Bound each term (M/ell)^alpha by (M/M')^alpha for ell > M, then use Lipschitz continuity of the covariance quotient on a neighbourhood of the non-degenerate limit.
title: Exponential Rate of Tropical Collapse

description:
The spectrum k^2 unfolds to an exact arithmetic progression and is maximally rigid, but the fractional parts of k^2 alpha are expected to have Poisson pair correlation for generic alpha. Conjecture a sharp dichotomy between rational and Diophantine alpha, formalized with the same pair-correlation counting machinery.

For alpha rational the unfolded pair correlation of the sequence of fractional parts of k^2 alpha is the staircase 2 floor(t), while for alpha of finite Diophantine type less than 2 it converges to the Poisson value 2t.

Reuse pairCorrCount on the sequence of fractional parts and prove the rational case exactly by periodicity; attack the Diophantine case via exponential sums.

A fully formal instance of the Rudnick-Sarnak pair correlation phenomenon, bridging number theory and spectral statistics.

The dichotomy has a third regime, which would refine the current arithmetic picture.
proof_strategy: Rational case: periodicity reduces to a finite count identical to the biUnion decomposition already used. Diophantine case: Weyl differencing plus a second moment bound on the pair-correlation counting function.
title: Quadratic Spectra Modulo One

description:
Three interaction axioms relate the provability box to the temporal box. One is sound on the catalog frame class; the other two are proved non-derivable here by explicit two-world and one-world separating frames. We conjecture the separation is structural: adding either of the other two collapses the provability modality entirely.

Adding ◼A ⟹ ◻A or ◻A ⟹ ◼A to TGL yields a system deriving ◻⊥, hence unsound on every frame with non-empty accessibility.

Extend the Derivable inductive with each candidate axiom and attempt to derive ◻⊥ using reflexivity of T together with converse well-foundedness of R; check soundness against rigidTimeFrame.

The catalog's choice of the persistence axiom ◻A ⟹ ◼◻A is canonically forced, not a modelling convention, and the frame class is rigid.

There is a second consistent bimodal Löb logic over the same frame skeleton, worth axiomatising and comparing.
proof_strategy: From reflexivity of T and the candidate axiom derive a diagonal instance of compat forcing R to be reflexive somewhere, then contradict irreflexivity implied by converse well-foundedness.
title: Interaction-Axiom Trichotomy for Bimodal Löb Systems

description:
The proved invariance of the knee under modifications of the capture curve below tolerance is a monoid action on profiles. Classify the invariants of that action to determine exactly which head statistics can appear in any knee law.

Every function of an attention profile that is invariant under all tolerance-preserving head modifications factors through the residual curve beyond the head budget; in particular no function of the top-r mass alone is invariant unless it is constant.

Define the monoid of admissible head modifications in Lean, prove the knee is invariant, and prove the factorisation for the induced quotient.

Head statistics are ruled out a priori as knee predictors, replacing correlational refutation with a structural one.

Some head statistic survives the action and becomes the natural candidate predictor.
proof_strategy: Build the action from staged reparametrisations, use knee_depends_only_on_tail as the invariance lemma, and quotient by the orbit equivalence to obtain the factorisation.
title: Gauge Freedom of the Head and Knee Invariants

description:
Preserving the frame condition T w w' → R w' v → R w v under filtration required adding a box-persistence clause to the filtered temporal relation. We conjecture this is an instance of a general recipe covering every Sahlqvist interaction axiom of that shape, yielding filtration and finite model theorems for a whole family of bimodal logics at once.

For any bimodal frame condition of the form T w w' → R w' v → R w v, the filtration of T strengthened by persistence of R-boxed closure formulas preserves the condition, and the resulting truth lemma holds verbatim.

Parameterise filtR and filtT over abstract modal constructors and a condition witness, re-derive filtT_filtR_compat, filtR_measure_lt and the truth lemma, then instantiate at the temporal case and check that all existing theorems still typecheck.

A reusable filtration library covering the catalog's provability-logic and poset-theory directories, with finite model properties obtained by instantiation rather than by re-proof.

The temporal case exploits reflexivity of T in a way not shared by general interaction conditions, isolating exactly which conditions are filtration-stable.
proof_strategy: Observe that filtT_filtR_compat uses only the R-persistence clause and no property of the temporal modality; abstract the two clauses into a typeclass and re-run the three-line argument.
title: Uniform Filtration Recipe for Sahlqvist Interaction Conditions

description:
The Berggren monoid is free over ℤ, so all relations modulo m come from reduction. Empirically the number of distinct length-k states jumps from 3^k to a constant with no intermediate polynomial regime; the conjecture asserts this cutoff is sharp and that all relations are long.

For m coprime to 6 the image of the Berggren monoid in GL₃(ℤ/m) admits only relations of length ≥ c·log m, and #{states of length k} = min(3^k, |image|)(1+o(1)) with a sharp cutoff.

Enumerate states of each length for m up to a few hundred and fit the transition width; formalise the lower bound on relation length via the hypotenuse growth estimate 5^{t+1} ≤ c_t.

The Berggren congruence monoid behaves like a random expander quotient of the free monoid, an attractive source of hash-like constructions.

Short relations exist, giving explicit collisions and hence a structural attack on any Berggren-based commitment.
proof_strategy: Use applyWord_injective for freeness over ℤ and pellC_lower_bound-style growth to show any relation forces a large integer state, hence a large modulus.
title: Sharp Cutoff for the Berggren Congruence Monoid

description:
This cycle proves one quadrant outright: the trinomial simplex has exponentially decaying Hellinger affinity together with curvature +1/4. The conjecture is that sensitivity and curvature are completely decoupled, all four sign/decay combinations being realised by finite-support models. It matters because the folklore inference 'exponential sensitivity, therefore hyperbolic' would then be wrong in every direction, not just one.

There exist finite-support models realising each of the four combinations of {Hellinger affinity rho^n decaying exponentially, decaying only polynomially along some parameter curve} with {curvature strictly positive on the whole parameter set, curvature strictly negative on the whole parameter set}.

Reuse FisherIdentifiability.rho and hellinger_affinity_prod on the tied two-group model restricted to the region where its curvature is negative, and construct a degenerating family whose affinity tends to 1 at the boundary; formalise each of the four witnesses as a separate theorem.

Statistical distinguishability and information-geometric curvature carry strictly independent information, so neither can be substituted for the other in identifiability arguments.

A genuine implication between decay rate and curvature sign exists on finite supports, which would be a new and useful structural theorem.
proof_strategy: Use the product formula for Hellinger affinity to reduce decay to a single-observation quantity rho < 1; control rho by the chordal distance on the sphere of radius 2; then choose models whose second fundamental form prescribes the curvature sign independently of that distance.
title: Four-Quadrant Independence of Hellinger Decay and Curvature Sign

description:
The pointwise blindness theorem is now proved for every form x^2 + D y^2 (NormFormBlindness.normForm_gcd_eq_one), the D = 1 and D = 2 blind sets are proved incomparable, and each blind set of composite moduli is proved infinite (SearchOrder.infinite_blindOne_semiprimes, SearchOrder.infinite_blindTwo_semiprimes). The open part is quantitative: the blind semiprimes for a fixed D should have density 1/4, and a search allowed to switch between k forms should still miss a positive-density set of moduli.

For each fixed D the set of primes inert for x^2 + D y^2 has natural density 1/2, so the semiprimes N = pq that a D-form search provably cannot split have density 1/4; for any finite set of forms D_1,...,D_k the jointly blind semiprimes still have density bounded below by a positive constant depending only on k.

Count inert primes and blind semiprimes up to 10^7 for D = 1, 2, 3, 5 and for pairs of forms; formalize the fixed-D case from Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions, using the already-proved congruence characterisations inert_one_iff and inert_two_iff.

No finite menu of norm forms escapes the obstruction: every algebraic-tree factoring proposal of this shape misses a positive-density family of moduli.

Some finite family of forms is jointly surjective onto prime classes, and a form-switching tree search would have no blind moduli.
proof_strategy: The pointwise step is done (primitive representation forces -D to be a quadratic residue modulo each prime divisor). For density, translate inertness into congruence conditions modulo 4D as in inert_one_iff / inert_two_iff, apply Dirichlet, and finish with inclusion-exclusion over the k forms.
title: Norm-Form Blindness Classes for Algebraic Search Trees

description:
For fixed p and k, decide exactly which deficiency profiles (d_1,...,d_k) admit a pairwise independent configuration whose reach misses a point. The proved triple criterion shows that the three smallest deficiencies must sum to at least p; enumeration shows this is not sufficient. The conjecture asks for the exact list of exceptions, which appears to be governed by a projective (cross-ratio) obstruction rather than a numerical one.

A profile d_1 <= ... <= d_k admits a failing configuration iff d_1+d_2+d_3 >= p and the profile is not in an explicitly describable exceptional list (at p=5,k=4 the exceptions are (0,2,3,3),(1,2,2,2),(2,2,2,2); at p=7,k=4 one exception is (1,3,3,4)).

Exhaustive enumeration over normalised direction tuples and sets of prescribed cardinality for p=5,7,11 and k=4,5; then formalise the resulting characterisation as a decidable predicate and prove both directions in Lean against KneserLines.reach_eq_univ_of_triple.

Gives a complete, checkable criterion for when sum_i S_i v_i = F_p^2, superseding all deficiency-sum bounds and yielding the k-auxiliary-class spread exclusion directly.

The set of failing profiles is not determined by the profile alone in a simple way, which would indicate a genuine dependence on the projective configuration of the directions and redirect effort to Direction 2.
proof_strategy: Necessity is the contrapositive of reach_eq_univ_of_triple. For sufficiency, build failing configurations profile-by-profile from the harmonic quadruple by enlarging the two co-singleton sets and shrinking the two short sets; handle the exceptional profiles by the full-set Cauchy-Davenport theorem reach_eq_univ_of_exists_full and by a refined union bound.
title: Profile Dichotomy for Planar Spanning Sumsets

description:
Strict majorization says a non-flat descending weight beats the baseline strictly, but says nothing about how much. The Chebyshev double sum is a quadratic form, suggesting the defect is bounded below by a squared distance to flatness.

For antitone normalised w on positions M, C_0 - EC >= c * M * (sum_i |w_i - 1/M|)^2 for an absolute constant c > 0.

Formalise via the double-sum identity, comparing the pairwise sum with the L1 distance by Cauchy-Schwarz; test the constant numerically over random antitone weights.

The master chain gains a quantitative, distribution-free margin, upgrading strict inequalities into usable gaps.

The defect degenerates for weights concentrated at the extremes, and only a weighted (position-dependent) distance can control it.
proof_strategy: Write the defect as a positive combination of (i-j)(w_i-w_j) terms and bound the pairwise sum below by the squared L1 distance using rearrangement.
title: Quadratic Stability of the Majorization Defect

description:
The log-convexity defect separates a flat-plus-spike mixture from every single truncated-exponential law by a margin independent of the spike steepness. The per-index k-bin version is already proved in this cycle (defect_mixK_ge, single_law_separationK); what remains is the summed invariant, uniformity for r near 1, and sharpness of the constant.

For k equal bins the summed second log-differences of the flat-bulk plus edge-spike mixture satisfy sum_j (p_j p_{j+2} - p_{j+1}^2) >= c * rho (1 - rho) / k with c absolute and no restriction on r in (0,1), and the proved per-index constant 1/(8k) is sharp up to a factor 2, attained at r = 1/2.

Sum the closed form of EdgeSpikeDefect.defect_mixK_eq over j, bound the resulting geometric sum below uniformly in r, and exhibit the extremal configuration at r = 1/2 to test sharpness.

Model selection for edge kernels becomes a distance computation with explicit constants, valid at every optimiser cap and independent of the unidentified steepness.

The margin must degrade with the number of bins, which would mean fine binning genuinely destroys the evidence for a second component and would explain cross-pipeline disagreement.
proof_strategy: The single-law bin vector is geometric, so all second differences vanish by the identity r^{j-1} r^{j+1} = (r^j)^2. For the mixture, expand: the cross term is (1-rho)/k * rho * (p_{j-1} + p_{j+1} - 2 p_j) and geometric convexity makes each bracket positive; sum the resulting telescoping series.
title: Defect-Margin Identifiability Principle

description:
Over a window of K rungs, the number of sign changes of the step sequence is 0 for any multiplicative or positively-contracting affine fade, and K-1 for a negatively-contracting one. Any intermediate count forces noise bounded below by the smallest step that breaks the pattern. This makes a purely combinatorial statistic of the ladder into a quantitative noise certificate.

If a ladder is a noisy affine fade with ratio lambda and noise eta over rungs 0..K, and the step sequence has s sign changes with 0 < s < K-1, then eta >= (1/2) * min over pattern-breaking indices of |step|.

Define signChanges of a finite step sequence in Lean, prove the two extreme cases from affineFade_alternates_of_neg and multiplicative_fade_no_rebound, then the intermediate bound by localising at a pattern-breaking index.

A single integer statistic of the recorded ladder yields a lower bound on experimental noise without any model fit.

Sign patterns are compatible with arbitrarily small noise, and only magnitudes constrain the model.
proof_strategy: Localise: at a pattern-breaking index apply positive_step_above_floor_forces_noise, or its mirror image below the floor, and take the minimum over such indices.
title: Sign-Change Count as a Fade-Law Discriminator

description:
Every deterministic channel on residues is fully pinned (gap 0), as proved in general here. The open half is the extremal one: how large can the output entropy be, and which groups achieve it.

For any modulus m and any sign-stable type map T on (ZMod m)^x, I(X;T) = H(T) and H(T) <= log2 (number of divisors of the exponent of (ZMod m)^x/{±1}), with equality iff the quotient is elementary abelian.

The equality I = H is already formalised (mutualInfo_eq_entropyOut). For the bound, enumerate moduli m <= 200 in Lean, compute H(T) via entropyOut, and compare with log2 of the divisor count.

The ladder has a universal ceiling depending only on the exponent, so entropy growth along the ladder is governed by divisor counts.

Some rung exceeds the divisor-count ceiling, indicating that the type map is not the order map for that conductor.
proof_strategy: Determinism gives H(X,T) = H(X) (already proved). For the ceiling, note the support of T is contained in the divisors of the exponent, and Shannon entropy on a support of size k is at most log2 k, with equality iff uniform; then classify abelian groups with uniform order profile.
title: Universal Pinning Bound for Deterministic Residue Channels

description:
Extend the window-score calculus from exactly orthogonal columns to columns whose Gram matrix is diagonally dominant. The conjecture is that dilution, matched-filter dominance and the peak-margin identity survive with a multiplicative 1 + O(eps) loss. This matters because real indicator columns are only approximately orthogonal.

If the Gram matrix G of the window columns satisfies ||G - D|| <= eps * lambda_min(D) with D the diagonal part, then for every weight w and window B one has R2(w,B) <= (1+C*eps) * R2(matched,B), and appending a column orthogonal to the response decreases R2 by at least (1-C*eps) times the orthogonal-model amount.

Formalise a Gram-perturbation version of Model in Lean, with the orthogonality field replaced by a bound on off-diagonal inner products, and re-derive R2_le_matched and noise_dilutes with explicit constants.

All conclusions of the orthogonal theory transfer to realistic column families, so an observed interior argmax remains a certificate of weight mismatch.

Interior maxima can be produced by column correlation alone, and no conclusion about the weight can be drawn from the shape of the window curve.
proof_strategy: Write the quadratic form of the window statistic as diagonal plus perturbation, bound the perturbed denominator two-sidedly by lambda_min/lambda_max, and propagate the bounds through the existing division inequalities.
title: Near-Orthogonal Window Calculus

description:
The density of ECM stage-1 orders firing in the last tau-fraction of the prime schedule should equal log(1/(1-tau))/log B1 asymptotically. The trace law turns the positional question into a Mertens sum over primes in ((1-tau)B1, B1]. It replaces the pre-registered constant-tail hypothesis by a decaying law.

For fixed tau in (0,1), the density of n <= M with pi(maxPF n) > (1-tau) pi(B1) and maxPF n <= B1 equals (log(1/(1-tau))/log B1)(1+o(1)) as B1 -> infinity.

Formalize Mertens' second theorem with explicit error, combine with lateCount_le_primeContribution and a matching Bonferroni lower bound; check against the sieve table for N = 10^3..10^7.

The late tail of any stage-1 trace is predictable from B1 alone, giving a parameter-free null for future ECM accounting audits.

The union bound is lossy at the top of the schedule, indicating correlations between large-prime divisibility events that themselves need explanation.
proof_strategy: Union bound (already formal) for the upper bound; inclusion-exclusion to second order for the lower bound; Mertens with error term to evaluate the reciprocal sum over the window.
title: Mertens Firing-Tail Law

description:
The reciprocal certified value is a Bernoulli agreement probability, and composing strata is strictly submultiplicative. The conjecture identifies the exact submultiplicativity slack as an information-theoretic quantity rather than a mere algebraic remainder.

The slack D(mu1*mu2, P1*P2) - D(mu1,P1)*D(mu2,P2) equals the probability that the two AND-products agree while some coordinate pair disagrees, and this quantity is monotone in the mutual information between the two filter indicators.

The identity half is already proved (coupling_slack_identity); formalise the monotonicity half against a mutual-information functional and test numerically.

Composed guarantees can be reported with a quantified conservatism, not just an inequality.

The slack is not an information functional, and composition must be handled locus by locus.
proof_strategy: Interpret both sides as probabilities over four independent Bernoulli variables and compare the two events; then relate the difference to a KL divergence.
title: Information Defect of Stratum Composition

description:
A finite sweep determines only the interval between the last failing and first passing grid budgets. Bounding the demand density bounds the agreement curve's slope, which should convert grid mesh into a quantitative bracket width and expose the point past which refining the grid is useless.

For a workload whose demand multiset has at most rho*n windows at any single demand value, a sweep of mesh m determines the knee to width at most min(m, ceil(slack/rho)), and this is sharp.

Extend GridRazorBracket with a density hypothesis on Workload.demand, prove the width bound, and exhibit a matching extremal profile.

The sub-20 addendum at ctx 2048 is provably decisive or provably futile before it is run.

Bracket width is not controlled by density alone and additional structure of the demand tail is needed.
proof_strategy: Bound agreeCount differences by the density hypothesis to get a Lipschitz constant for the agreement curve, then apply the Galois adjunction knee_le_iff to transfer the bound to the knee.
title: Density-Limited Grid Resolution of the Knee Bracket

description:
Lift the sharp stage-1 threshold theory to the difference stage. Stage 2 kills orders that are B1-powersmooth after removing a single prime factor in (B1, B2], so the criterion should become a two-parameter threshold and the firing count an exact product formula. The stage-2 arms of the audited experiment never executed, so a theorem is the only available validation.

A point of order n is killed by the (B1,B2) difference stage iff n = s*r with maxPrimePow s <= B1 and r = 1 or r prime in (B1,B2]; the firing count in Z/m is gcd(m,lcm(1..B1)) times (1 + #{r prime in (B1,B2] : r divides m / gcd(m,lcm(1..B1)))}).

Formalize the criterion by the same factorization argument as dvd_stage1Scalar_iff, then count the firing set as a disjoint union over the admissible prime r.

Exact stage-2 success rates replace the usual heuristic, and the B2/B1 scaling law of the pre-registered H1 hypothesis becomes computable in closed form.

The difference stage kills strictly more orders than the criterion allows, indicating that intermediate differences contribute extra collisions.
proof_strategy: Write the stage-2 scalar as k(B1)*r for each admissible prime r, apply the stage-1 divisibility criterion to each factor, and take the union over r with inclusion-exclusion (the events are disjoint because r is uniquely determined by n).
title: Stage-Two Difference-Stage Firing Criterion

description:
Cycles 5, 6 and 7 all consume the same lemma: any two admissible words glue through one buffer letter. The conjecture is that the least buffer length g of a subshift of finite type simultaneously characterises Devaney chaos, the shift in the supermultiplicativity inequality, and the minimax mistake rate, so that a single combinatorial constant has a topological, a combinatorial and a learning-theoretic reading.

For a subshift of finite type X on {0,1} with specification constant g, (i) the shift on X is Devaney chaotic iff g is finite, (ii) #L(n) · #L(m) ≤ #L(n+m+g) with g least such, and (iii) the minimax mistake rate is 1 - 1/(g+1); the three characterisations of g agree.

Abstract admissible_glue to a hypothesis `glue : ∀ v w ∈ L, ∃ u, |u| = g ∧ v ++ u ++ w ∈ L`, then re-run goldenMean_transitive, card_goldenWords_mul_le and exists_adversary_stream against that hypothesis and check each proof survives verbatim.

A reusable Lean framework in which one combinatorial constant delivers chaos, entropy subadditivity and a learning bound for any subshift of finite type.

Any of the three implications failing pinpoints an extra property of the golden-mean case that the current proofs use silently, which is exactly the kind of hidden hypothesis this abstraction is designed to expose.
proof_strategy: Replace the literal buffer `[false]` by an abstract gluing word of length g throughout; transitivity and supermultiplicativity are immediate reparameterisations, while the mistake bound needs the block induction of cycle 7 with block length g+1 instead of 2.
title: Specification Constant as a Trivalent Invariant of Constrained Truth Streams

description:
The reading 'D = 1 + betweenVar/mean' is valid only if the within-cell law is Poisson-calibrated. The conjecture is that the residual within-cell dispersion at bitlen 96 is itself strictly above 1, i.e. the excess is not purely latent-rate heterogeneity but includes within-N clustering of gcd-chain hits.

For the exp-576 ensemble, withinVar > avg after conditioning on every recorded dial, with the gap growing in the number of j-samples per N.

Measure D_within at two j-sample budgets and compare with Logic.QRDial.poisson_mixture_disp, whose hypothesis withinVar = avg is exactly the calibration being audited.

The mixed-Poisson framing must be replaced by a self-exciting model, changing every published dispersion reading in the line.

Heterogeneity is confirmed as the sole source, and the carrier is a per-N latent rate — a purely arithmetic object.
proof_strategy: Use the exact ANOVA identity to isolate withinVar, then compare against the mean; the identity is proved in var_decomposition and needs no distributional input.
title: Within-Cell Poisson Calibration Audit

description:
The booked envelope over (m, M, P) is sharp but wide. Adding the within-cell shape booking Theta should collapse it to an identity up to a second-order term. The conjecture quantifies how much shape information a single scalar booking carries.

For every weight honouring bookings (m, M, P) with within-cell factors Theta_R, Theta_C, the expected scan cost equals P*Theta_R*centre(R) + (1-P)*Theta_C*centre(C), and constraining Theta_R, Theta_C to an interval [1-e, 1+e] shrinks the admissible cost interval to width O(e*M).

Formalise the width bound as a corollary of booked_law_theta_form plus explicit bounds on centre(R), centre(C); test numerically on random weights with controlled Theta.

Bookings with Theta become a complete reporting convention: a two-sided guarantee, not just a point estimate.

Some other shape statistic (e.g. the second moment) is the minimal sufficient booking, and Theta alone is not enough.
proof_strategy: Start from the exact Theta-form law, bound centre(R) and centre(C) by the stratum endpoints, and optimise over the admissible Theta interval.
title: Theta-Refined Booked Envelope

description:
The strict window law is now proved for every finite positive combination of power laws with two distinct exponents. The conjecture extends it to a continuous mixing measure over exponents, whose kernel-to-power-law ratio is a Laplace transform in the logarithmic variable and hence convex.

For any finite nonnegative measure mu on exponents that is not a point mass, and any c, the ratio k -> (integral k^{-x} dmu(x)) / k^{-c} is strictly convex in log k, and the induced window-implied exponent is strictly antitone in the window width.

Replace the finite-sum convexity lemma genRatio_strict_log_convex by its integral analogue and re-run genHeadMass_strict_single_crossing with the integral kernel.

Antitone window curves are a universal signature of exponent heterogeneity, never of a single law.

Some heterogeneous kernel produces an increasing window curve, which would be a genuinely new phenomenon worth isolating.
proof_strategy: Convexity of Laplace transforms (Cauchy-Schwarz in the mixing variable) replaces the finite-sum strict convexity; the prefix-sum and no-return arguments are unchanged.
title: Continuous Mixing Measures and the Window Law

description:
The positional layer is deterministic, so the only stochastic ingredient is the smoothness of a residue of known bit length. A residue of half size is smooth with probability rho(alpha/2) rather than rho(alpha), which should quantitatively reproduce the observed roughly equal split between the inclusion artifact and the residual edge component.

The inclusion-channel share of the left-edge weight equals the ratio of Dickman-weighted band masses computed from card_band_formula, and for 96-bit moduli it lies in [0.45, 0.55].

Evaluate the band populations exactly for a sample of 96-bit moduli, weight them by a Dickman table, and compare the predicted share with the reported edge-weight drop.

The observed split needs no positional kernel at all beyond the deterministic band geometry.

A genuine positional kernel independent of residue size survives, which would be new structure in the window.
proof_strategy: Exact band counting plus standard smoothness heuristics; falsifiable by a single computed number.
title: Dickman Smoothness Boost as the Source of the Fifty-Fifty Split

description:
It is proved that log a(n)/n → 0, in contrast with the exponential growth of unrestricted polyomino counts. This places square-core stacks in the Hardy–Ramanujan class of one-dimensional interface models and suggests the constrained ensemble has the classical partition limit shape after √n scaling.

The rescaled column-height profile of a uniformly random square-core stack of area n converges, after dividing both coordinates by √n, to the Vershik curve e^{-cx} + e^{-cy} = 1 with c = π/√6, symmetrized about the core.

Combine the proved layer decomposition with known limit-shape results for partitions with bounded parts, conditioned on the two slopes having parts ≤ k-1 with k ≈ 0.5404√n.

The square-core constraint is asymptotically invisible at the level of the limit shape, confirming universality of the Vershik curve for constrained interfaces.

The core imposes a macroscopic plateau, producing a genuinely new limit shape with a flat segment of length proportional to √n.
proof_strategy: Transfer the two-sided conditioned partition ensemble supplied by the layer decomposition to the classical grand-canonical partition measure, then apply concentration for independent geometric multiplicities.
title: Zero Entropy Density and Limit Shape of Constrained Interfaces

description:
Lift the proved lag spectrum from a prime modulus to a prime power. The obstruction argument uses only invertibility of k and 2, which survives in the local ring, while the two-root count becomes Hensel's lemma. Summing over prime powers would give the adjacent covariance of the full smoothness indicator rather than only its squarefree part.

Over ZMod (q^e) with q an odd prime and N a unit square, the divisibility set has exactly two elements, the lag-k double-hit set is empty unless 4N = k^2 in ZMod (q^e), and the non-exceptional lag covariance is exactly -4/q^(2e).
