Redo four_mul_eq_sq_of_lag with units in ZMod (q^e), obtain the two-root count from Hensel lifting, and recompute cov_lag_eq; cross-check by decide at q^e = 9, 25, 27.

The deficit law extends to full smoothness, so the factor-base sum becomes a sum over prime powers with a geometrically convergent tail.

Higher prime powers interact with the polynomial structure, revealing a genuinely new local obstruction beyond the field case.
proof_strategy: Replace field nonzero-divisor steps by unit hypotheses; use ZMod.isUnit_iff_coprime for invertibility of k and 2, and Hensel lifting for the root count.
title: Prime-Power Lag Spectrum via Hensel Lifting

description:
Cycle 1 shows that beating 4/3 requires soundness strictly above retention. This direction quantifies the price in bits: the soundness excess should be controlled by the square root of the mutual information between the target and the dial's kept set, making the cap an information inequality rather than an accounting identity.

For a uniform prior on the candidate pool and a kept set K(N) determined by N, s - theta <= sqrt(I(N; K)/2); consequently any dial with speedup above 4/3 has I(N; K) >= 2 (1-2theta)^4 / (16 (1-theta)^2).

Prove the total-variation form of the excess, then apply a formalised Pinsker inequality to the finite mutual information of Tropical.OrbitDialInformation.

Barrier 4 upgrades from a cost statement to an information-theoretic obstruction, applying to every dial family at once.

There exist low-information, high-soundness dials on uniform priors, which would be a genuine new factoring primitive.
proof_strategy: Write s - theta as the difference of the kept-mass under the conditional and the marginal law, bound it by total variation, and apply Pinsker to the finite joint distribution.
title: Pinsker Price of Super-Exchangeability

description:
The sign word of a measured ladder's grid second differences is a model-free invariant that excludes whole shape classes before any parameter fit. Convex laws (hyperbolic, geometric, exponential-to-floor) realise only all-nonnegative words; concave laws only all-nonpositive ones. The recorded T-dial ladder realises neither, which is a structural, not statistical, refutation.

Proved: for every law A + C*g(b) with g convex and C >= 0 the 4-bit grid second differences are nonnegative, so a ladder with both a strictly positive and a strictly negative grid second difference is unfittable by any signed-curvature law. The open refinement is quantitative: the number of sign changes in a ladder's curvature word certifies a lower bound on the differential order of any law that can fit it.

The sign law and the categorical exclusion are formalised as signedLaw_second_difference and no_signed_curvature_law; the refinement needs a Lean notion of k-fold monotone laws and a bound on the sign changes each order admits.

Model selection for dial ladders reduces to a finite combinatorial check, and every published fade law in the thread is refuted in one line.

Some convex family produces sign-alternating grid second differences, which would identify the extra degree of freedom the current fits are missing.
proof_strategy: The midpoint convexity inequality gives the sign law directly; the refinement should iterate it on higher-order differences, each order contributing one admissible sign change.
title: Curvature-Sign Spectroscopy of Fading Dials

description:
Every McKay-Thompson head coefficient should be derivable, like the 1A entry proved here, from an eta-quotient q-expansion checked by the Lean kernel. The pipeline uses only unit-ness of eta products in Z[[X]], never modularity. Completing it would convert the 194-entry head table from quoted data into verified data.

For each of the 194 conjugacy classes g of the Monster there is an integral exponent vector r with (prod_d eta(d tau)^{r_d}) + const having q-coefficient c_g(1), and the truncation identity mod q^8 is kernel-decidable.

Define etaQuotient for an arbitrary exponent vector, reprove unit-ness and truncation stability by the existing AgreeBelow calculus, and discharge class 2A end to end before looping over all classes.

The head conjecture becomes a single decide over 194 verified integers via head_check_iff.

The classes without eta-quotient hauptmoduln isolate where genuinely modular input is unavoidable.
proof_strategy: Generalize MoonshineJ.deltaPart to arbitrary exponent vectors; reuse isUnit_deltaPart, deltaPart_stable and j_coefficients_unique verbatim; discharge each class by decide on truncated list arithmetic.
title: Eta-Quotient Certificates for the Full Monster Head Table

description:
The exact predictor identity shows the analytic speedup is (1-z)/z up to O(1/L). Enumeration at bit length 12 gives 0.5441 against the analytic 0.55529, a gap consistent with a single half-step rounding term. The conjecture makes that correction explicit and equidistribution-driven.

For same-bit-length pools at bit length b, Sum(desc)/Sum(asc) = (1-zbar)/zbar + c/sqrt(N) + O(1/N) with c determined by the equidistribution of the fractional parts of sqrt(N/2) and sqrt(N).

Enumerate bit lengths 12 through 18, fit the residual against 1/sqrt(N), and formalise the leading term using descCost_lt_ascCost_of_real_margin together with an equidistribution input.

The finite-size gap between theory and simulation is fully explained, closing the last modelling caveat.

A second-order effect (prime correlations inside the window) contributes at order 1/sqrt(N), which would be of independent interest.
proof_strategy: Write asc and desc costs as real quantities plus explicit ceiling/floor defects; average the defects using Weyl equidistribution of sqrt of integers.
title: Lattice Correction to the Tilt-Only Predictor

description:
The root component reveals exactly two residue triples mod 4 and small explicit sets mod 3,5,7,8,16. The conjecture is that these are precisely the congruence-admissible triples: the tree reveals everything the local conditions allow, so the orbit dial can never contain more than the ordinary residue dials do.

For every modulus m the revealed set of the Berggren root component equals the set of (a,b,c) mod m with a^2+b^2 = c^2, a odd, 4 | b, 3 | ab, modulo the tree's symmetry group.

For each small m, enumerate both sets by decide and compare; then prove transitivity of the Berggren action on the primitive conic mod m for m coprime to 6.

Barrier 5 extends to all mod-N orbit projections with a uniform proof, closing the triplet-tree campaign structurally.

Some modulus exhibits an under-sampled orbit, reopening the question of orbit-specific residue content.
proof_strategy: Show the three Berggren moves generate the stabiliser action on the conic mod m via a Cayley-graph connectivity check, then lift with Hensel/CRT to all m.
title: Congruence Closure of the Berggren Revealed Spectrum

description:
Stacking dials adds log-speedups and hedging takes minima, so dials live in Tropical R. The conjecture is that the exchangeable dials form the unique maximal bounded sub-semiring, so that barrier 4 is an algebraic property of the dial semiring rather than a feature of one cost model.

The set of achievable tropical weights is a sub-semiring of Tropical R; the weights of exchangeable dials form its unique maximal bounded sub-semiring, equal to the window [0, log(4/3)], and every soundness-preserving endomorphism acts by a positive scalar on weights.

Define the dial semiring on top of tropWeight, verify closure under stack and hedge, and characterise bounded sub-semirings by an extremality argument.

The two regimes (information-bearing and structural) are algebraically separated, giving a coordinate-free formulation of barrier 4.

There are exotic dial compositions outside the semiring, meaning the accounting is not compositional and each dial family needs separate treatment.
proof_strategy: Use tropWeight_mul for closure under stacking and trop addition for hedging; boundedness of the exchangeable window is exchangeable_cap, unboundedness of the structural part is wheel_speedup_unbounded.
title: Tropical Dial Semiring and Cap-Preserving Morphisms

description:
Cycle 3 shows the slack orbit of a geometric demand ladder is dense exactly when log_2 alpha is irrational. The effective question is how long one must wait for a slack within epsilon of the ceiling 2, and the answer should be governed by the continuants of log_2 alpha via the three-distance theorem.

The least n with slack(alpha^n) > 2 - epsilon satisfies q_k <= n <= q_{k+1} where q_k are the continued-fraction denominators of log_2 alpha and k is minimal with 1/q_k < c*epsilon.

Formalise the three-distance theorem for the orbit fract(-n theta) and derive two-sided hitting-time bounds; test numerically against alpha = 3 and alpha = golden ratio squared.

Turns the qualitative sharpness result into a schedule-length guarantee: one can certify how many rounds an exchange needs before it demonstrably nears the worst case.

Density would be non-effective for some alpha, pointing to Liouville-type growth ratios as pathological scheduler inputs.
proof_strategy: Three-distance theorem plus best-approximation properties of continuants; the qualitative density already proved supplies the existence half.
title: Continued-Fraction Hitting Times for Starvation Slack

description:
The stage-1 schedule weights a prime p by floor(log_p B1) bits of work, so the step-normalized and work-normalized firing traces differ exactly on orders divisible by higher prime powers. This predicts a second, independent observable for the next experiment.

For B1 >= 10^3 the expected gap between the work-normalized and step-normalized firing index is Theta(sqrt(B1) log B1 / (B1 / log B1)) and is dominated by the O(sqrt(B1)) schedule primes with exponent at least 2.

Prove matching upper and lower bounds for log2 stageProd B1 y against pi(y) log2 B1 and theta(y), then measure both traces in the next ECM run.

Recording both traces yields a direct read-out of the prime-power structure of the group order, a new factor-local invariant.

The two normalizations agree to leading order, so trace bookkeeping can safely ignore prime powers.
proof_strategy: Split log stageProd into theta(y) plus the higher-prime-power correction, bound the correction by Chebyshev-type estimates, and compare with the pi-weighted step count.
title: Work-Trace versus Step-Trace Separation on Prime Powers

description:
Ramanujan-type congruences for tau modulo 691, 23, 7, 5, 3, 2 are congruences between q-expansions, hence finite statements in (Z/l)[[X]]/(X^N) for each window N. A mod-l analogue of the AgreeBelow calculus would make each window a kernel decision, giving reusable certificates for modular-form congruences.

For each classical Ramanujan congruence modulo l, the truncated congruence holds for every window N and is decidable in time polynomial in N.

Define AgreeBelowMod l N, reprove the product/power/cancellation lemmas, and verify l = 691, 23, 7 at N = 20 by decide.

A reusable, kernel-checkable certificate scheme for congruences between modular forms.

The first failing window exposes a normalization error in the classical statement.
proof_strategy: Reduce the integral eta-product computation modulo l via the ring hom Z -> Z/l, transport AgreeBelow through map_ringHom, and discharge windows by decide on lists over ZMod l.
title: Modular Congruence Certificates in Truncated Power Series

description:
The two-component parameter space carries an exact involution exchanging the components and complementing the weight. Off the diagonal the action is free, so critical points of any observable-based criterion come in pairs, which is exactly the role-swapped optimum reported in the ledger.

For a two-component mixture of truncated exponentials the involution (rho, b1, b2) -> (1 - rho, b2, b1) acts freely off the diagonal b1 = b2, and every non-diagonal critical point of a criterion computed from the bin probabilities occurs in an orbit of size two joined by a ridge along which the criterion varies by a bounded amount.

Formalise the involution as a group action on the parameter space minus the diagonal, prove freeness, and analyse the criterion on the quotient via a Morse-theoretic count for a fixed synthetic data set.

Explains role-swapped optima as a structural feature; optimisers should be run on the quotient (for example by imposing b1 <= b2) rather than being restarted.

The observed role swap is data specific and would indicate a genuine second mode rather than a symmetry artefact.
proof_strategy: Freeness is the statement that (rho, b1, b2) = (1 - rho, b2, b1) forces b1 = b2. Invariance of all observables is EdgeSpikeDefect.twoComp_role_swap; transfer criticality through the quotient map and count orbits.
title: Role-Swap Quotient Geometry

description:
Count how many integers in the Hasse window of p have largest prime power at most B = p^theta. The catalog now gives an exact firing criterion (maxPrimePow n <= B), so ECM stage-1 success over random curves reduces to this counting problem. A uniform Dickman-type asymptotic would replace the folklore smoothness heuristic by a theorem.

For B = p^theta with 0 < theta <= 1, the proportion of integers n in [p+1-2 sqrt p, p+1+2 sqrt p] with maxPrimePow n <= B equals rho(1/theta) + O(p^{-delta}) uniformly in theta, where rho is the Dickman function.

Formalize the lower bound for theta close to 1 by counting window integers divisible by a prime power above B (inclusion-exclusion over primes in (B, p+1+2 sqrt p]); verify numerically for p up to 10^7 before formalizing.

ECM stage-1 success rates become theorems rather than heuristics, and the transition to certainty at theta = 1 is provably continuous, killing any wall-shaped claim.

The window distribution deviates from Dickman, which itself would be a significant statement about prime powers in short intervals.
proof_strategy: Upper bound: union bound over prime powers q^e in (B, window top]; each contributes at most window length / q^e + 1 multiples. Lower bound: Bonferroni truncation plus Mertens-type sums.
title: Powersmooth-Order Density Threshold for Hasse Windows

description:
A B_{d+1}-free family cannot contain two pointwise-nested chains of length 2^d, a strictly stronger restriction than the absence of a single chain of length 2^{d+1}. Averaging this deficiency over random full chains should give the first constant-factor improvement over the chain bound. The formal criterion is already available.

Every B_3-free family F of subsets of [n] satisfies the Lubell bound sum_{A in F} 1/C(n,|A|) <= 6 + o(1), hence La(n,B_3) <= (6+o(1)) C(n, floor(n/2)).

Formalise a random-full-chain averaging in the existing Lubell framework and show that chains meeting F in 7 sets force a forbidden parallel-chain configuration in a positive proportion of neighbouring chains.

The chain factor 2^d - 1 is not optimal already at d = 3, giving the first step towards La(n,B_d) <= (d+c)C(n,floor(n/2)).

Long chains are the true obstruction and the extremal families for B_3 must contain 7-chains, reshaping the conjecture.
proof_strategy: Combine hasBdCopy_succ_of_parallel_chains with a weighted count over maximal chains, discarding families whose Lubell mass concentrates on 7-chains.
title: Parallel-Chain Deficiency Bound

description:
Because the firing threshold equals the largest prime factor, the median normalized firing index is pi(B1^rho)/pi(B1) with rho the Golomb-Dickman constant. This explains the measured medians 0.09-0.10 as a Dickman phenomenon rather than an elliptic-curve one.

median_{n <= B1} pi(maxPF n)/pi(B1) = Theta(B1^(rho-1) log B1) with rho = 0.6243299885...

Prove the two-sided smooth-number bounds needed for the median of log maxPF n / log n, then apply Chebyshev bounds on pi; validate against the sieve table (medians 0.083, 0.034, 0.020, 0.005 for N = 10^3..10^6).

Early firing is universal across all stage-1 implementations and carries no curve-specific information, closing the trace channel as a factorization side channel.

Some arithmetic of elliptic-curve orders biases the largest prime factor away from Dickman, which would be a genuinely new statement about #E(F_p).
proof_strategy: Dickman rho as the limit distribution of log maxPF n / log n, plus Chebyshev-type upper and lower bounds for pi to convert an exponent statement into a counting statement.
title: Dickman Median of the Normalized Firing Index

description:
The permutation p-value is exactly super-uniform in finite samples, whereas the chi-square approximation to the interaction likelihood-ratio statistic relies on asymptotics that fail on sparse occupancy tables. The conjecture is that on tables of the exp-578 sparsity the chi-square p-value is anti-conservative by a quantifiable amount.

For occupancy tables with expected cell counts below a fixed threshold, the chi-square p-value of the interaction statistic has null rejection probability strictly exceeding the nominal level, while the permutation p-value does not.

Simulate null tables at the observed sparsity, compare empirical rejection rates of both rules against the proved bound permPValue_valid, and formalise the union of both decisions with the Bonferroni theorem.

All round-80 family-B decisions should be re-expressed in permutation terms, strengthening the null result.

The chi-square calibration is adequate at this sparsity and the two analyses can be reported interchangeably.
proof_strategy: Use permPValue_valid for the exact side, and bound the chi-square error by comparing the exact multinomial log-likelihood ratio with its quadratic expansion via Table.klTerm_pos.
title: Exact Calibration Dominance of Permutation over Asymptotic Chi-Square

description:
The catalog's TempProv structure axiomatises provability indexed by a discovery time but is so far witnessed only by the degenerate model that proves nothing. We conjecture that TGL is complete for TempProv models, and that the finite canonical worlds constructed here provide the missing non-degenerate witnesses, bypassing Solovay-style fixed points.

A formula A is TGL-derivable iff every TempProv model validates its translation under every interpretation of the atoms.

Build a translation from CanWorld (subformulas A) to TempProv, verify persist, K, sigma1 and loeb against the canonical relations, and check that the resulting model refutes exactly the non-derivable formulas.

The semantic and algebraic layers of the catalog's temporal Gödel–Löb development are reconciled, and godel_second_at_time becomes a corollary of a single completeness theorem.

The TempProv axioms are strictly stronger than TGL, and the surplus identifies precisely which arithmetical facts are not modally expressible.
proof_strategy: Read prov t A off membership of A in the stage-t canonical world; persistence follows from the box-clause of filtT, sigma1 from derivable_four, and loeb from exists_box_succ.
title: Arithmetical Completeness of Time-Stamped Provability

description:
Invert the robustness bound: a mixture with relative composition drift δ can shrink a relative excess by at most the factor (1-δ)/(1+δ), so absorbing amplitude A requires δ ≥ A/(2+A). This turns a single-geometry verdict into a scale-free necessary condition on any future mixture model. It is a two-line consequence of mixPred_drift_bounds but has not been stated as a design rule.

Any cell mixture absorbing a relative excess A must exhibit maximal per-cell composition drift δ ≥ A/(2+A); for A = 0.1774 this is δ ≥ 0.0815, thirty times the measured 0.00269.

Formalize as a theorem in Shared.MixtureRateDialBaseline: from the two-sided drift bounds derive the contrapositive of H0_excess_survives_measured with δ as a variable.

Every future mixture baseline can be rejected or accepted from its measured drift alone, before fitting.

The two-sided drift bound is not tight and some non-uniform drift pattern absorbs more than (1-δ)/(1+δ) allows.
proof_strategy: Take the excess_ratio_lower_bound_div inequality, solve for δ at equality, and check tightness with a two-cell example where one cell drifts by +δ and the other by -δ.
title: Drift Budget Lower Bound for Mixture Absorption

description:
The ANOVA degree-one ceiling and the contingency enrichment ratio agree in the extreme case already proved. The conjecture is that they are two readings of the same orthogonal decomposition, so the maximal marginal enrichment is an explicit function of the variance of the additive part of the hit indicator.

For any hit indicator f on a product space, the supremum over marginal cells of the enrichment ratio is a monotone function of varr (addPart f) / varr f, equal to 1 exactly when addPart f is constant.

Express the cell enrichment as an affine functional of f, project onto the additive subspace using addPart, and compare with Rsq_additive_le_ceiling.

One invariant governs both the regression and the contingency view, so a single diagnostic number certifies that no marginal analysis can succeed.

The two views are genuinely inequivalent and a sweep could be flat in one and informative in the other, which would itself be a useful methodological warning.
proof_strategy: Write the cell mean of f as an inner product with a cell indicator, decompose the indicator into additive and interaction parts, and use the orthogonality already proved in PhaseRouteANOVA.
title: Shared Degree-One Invariant for Enrichment and R-Squared

description:
The proved lower bound spends one tree per 3^{1/4} leaves because it is a union bound over all ordered quadruples. Since the agreement probability is exactly 3^{-(k-1)} by the ternary balance theorem and quartets sharing at most two leaves are nearly independent, the Lovasz Local Lemma should improve the exponential base.

There are avoiding families of k random caterpillars on n leaves whenever k >= 3 log_3 n + O(1), improving the constant 4 in exponential_lower_bound, hence h(k) >= 3^{k/3 - O(1)}.

Formalize the symmetric Lovasz Local Lemma for the events 'all k trees agree on quartet Q', with dependency degree O(n^3) and probability 3^{-(k-1)}, and re-derive the avoidance statement in the Lean framework of exists_quartet_avoiding_family.

The exponential lower bound base rises from 3^{1/4} = 1.316 toward the empirically observed 1.7, narrowing the gap with the upper bound.

The quartet agreement events are more strongly dependent than their pairwise leaf overlap suggests, indicating a hidden global constraint in tree space.
proof_strategy: Use three_mul_qclass_card for the exact per-quartet probability, bound the dependency degree by counting quadruples sharing a leaf, and apply the symmetric LLL condition e * p * (d+1) <= 1.
title: Local-Lemma Sharpening of the Avoidance Rate

description:
The side of the window centre on which a chord-gap vertex falls is decided by the convexity of the profile's derivative. Convex derivative gives a left vertex, linear derivative gives the exact centre, concave derivative gives a right vertex. This converts a measured vertex position into a structural constraint on the underlying profile.

Let f be differentiable and strictly concave on [a,b]. If f' is convex then the maximiser of gap f a b is < (a+b)/2; if f' is affine it equals (a+b)/2; if f' is concave it is > (a+b)/2.

Prove the Hermite-Hadamard comparison between the mean of f' over [a,b] and f'((a+b)/2), then transport through the StrictAntiOn characterisation of the vertex already in HumpWindowGeometry.

A measured vertex at 0.5901 is a direct measurement of a concave slope profile, which j^2 - N does not have; the elimination of H0 becomes a positive identification criterion.

Vertex position carries no curvature information beyond the profile itself, and the location must be attacked through the reference parametrisation instead.
proof_strategy: Hermite-Hadamard for convex f' on [a,b]; the vertex satisfies f'(xi) = mean slope, and StrictAntiOn f' converts the inequality mean >= f'(midpoint) into xi <= midpoint.
title: Curvature Dichotomy for Chord-Referenced Vertices

description:
The accessibility relation of every canonical temporal GL model is a strict order graded by the number of realised boxed subformulas. We conjecture that the minimal countermodel size is exactly one more than the longest chain in this graded poset, making it an order-theoretic rather than a logical quantity. This bridges modal completeness theory with finite poset combinatorics.

The minimal number of worlds in a TempFrame countermodel of a non-derivable A equals 1 + d(A), where d(A) is the longest strictly boxCount-increasing chain in the boxed subformulas of A.

Define minCountermodelSize by Nat.find over finite_model_property_sharp, compute both sides on the six sample formulas of ComputationalEvidence.md, then attempt induction on d(A).

Countermodel size becomes computable from the box skeleton alone, independently of propositional content, giving an exact complexity measure for TGL refutation.

Propositional content genuinely contributes to countermodel size, and the extra contribution isolates the non-order-theoretic part of Löb refutation.
proof_strategy: Lower bound: exhibit a chain of worlds forced by iterated exists_box_succ. Upper bound: show the selective canonical model of Direction 1 is exactly a maximal chain, using filtR_measure_lt to prevent branching from increasing height.
title: Löb Depth as an Exact Complexity Invariant

description:
Everything in this cycle is controlled by the dimensionless product of steepness and edge-bin width. Turning that into a design rule fixes the edge bin before any fit and forbids reporting point estimates above a computable ceiling.

At sample size n, tolerance level alpha and edge-bin width t, the largest steepness admitting a finite upper confidence limit is b* = (1/t) log(sqrt(n) rho t / z_alpha) up to absolute constants; choosing the edge bin so that b t is approximately 1 maximises the identifiable range.

Combine the Fisher-information conjecture with the ray theorem EdgeSpike.identified_ray, then check the resulting formula against bootstrap cap-hit fractions on synthetic data at several n.

Yields a pre-registration rule: report steepness as a lower bound whenever the fitted value exceeds b*, and choose bins so that b t is of order one.

The censoring threshold depends on more than the product b t, so bin geometry cannot be optimised in advance.
proof_strategy: Invert the exponential envelope of cap_gain_le at the noise scale 1/sqrt(n), and match with the ray threshold B0 of identified_ray, which is exactly the b at which 2 rho exp(-b t) drops below the tolerance.
title: Censoring Threshold as a Pre-Registration Design Rule

description:
For a semiprime N = pq with B below p, hits at q cannot come from order completion; the exact rate there is 1/m per point. We conjecture the total stage-1 success rate decomposes as the order-completion rate plus an additive error bounded by c B / q, making the collision floor a rigorously controlled term rather than a heuristic.

There is an absolute constant c such that for all semiprimes N = pq with B < p < q, |success rate - order-completion rate| <= c B / q.

Formalize the two-modulus firing event as a product count over Z/m_p x Z/m_q and bound the q-side contribution using firing_count_eq_one_of_all_prime_factors_gt.

The collision model is retired as an explanatory mechanism at low B1, with an explicit error bar.

There is a regime where collisions contribute at the same order as order completion, and the mechanism attribution must be made scale-dependent.
proof_strategy: Split the CRT product group, apply the exact firing count on each factor, and bound the cross terms by the q-side rate 1/m together with a union bound over the schedule.
title: Additive Bound on the Collision Floor

description:
The primes at which consecutive sieve positions are positively rather than negatively correlated are exactly the prime divisors of 4N-1, which is already proved. Counting them bounds the positive contribution to the total adjacent covariance and would show that the aggregate sign is negative for every N.

The number of exceptional primes is omega(4N-1) = O(log N / log log N), and the sum of 1/q over them is strictly smaller than the sum of 4/q^2 over the factor base, so the total adjacent covariance is negative for every N.

Formalise the omega bound for 4N-1 and compare the two finite sums for the standard quadratic-sieve factor bases; the comparison is a finite computation for any concrete N.

The sign of the consecutive-position effect is universal, giving a one-sided pre-registered hypothesis.

For some N the exceptional primes dominate, making the effect sign N-dependent and requiring a two-sided test.
proof_strategy: Use the proved divisor characterisation four_mul_eq_one_iff_dvd, then a standard bound on the number of distinct prime factors, then compare the two explicit sums.
title: Divisor-Count Bound for the Exceptional Locus

description:
Explains the empirical residue-class confinement of the mod-N orbit as an exact conservation law: the orbit is exactly the joint level set of the Lorentz form and the determinant character. Proving the inclusion is immediate; the content is the reverse inclusion.

For N coprime to 6, the mod-N Berggren orbit of (3,4,5) equals the set of primitive points of the null cone of the Lorentz form lying in a fixed coset of the image of the Berggren monoid in PGL_3(Z/N); the number of reachable nz-histogram classes is bounded independently of N.

Compute orbit sizes against joint level-set sizes for small N; formalise the easy inclusion, then attempt transitivity on the null cone over Z/p.

Sharp reachable-state counts replace empirical percentages and improve the ambiguity bounds of Hardness.lean.

A third independent invariant exists, which is new structure in the Berggren monoid.
proof_strategy: CRT reduction to prime powers, then a Witt-type transitivity argument for the orthogonal group acting on isotropic vectors.
title: Joint Invariant Confinement of the Modular Berggren Orbit

description:
Construct the Markov measure on the golden-mean subshift with transition weights 1/φ and 1/φ² and prove it is shift invariant with entropy log φ, matching the covering-number growth already established. The construction uses the clopen cylinder algebra and Carathéodory extension on the compact space proved compact in cycle 1. Cycle 6's Fekete inequalities supply the subadditivity that makes the entropy limit exist independently of the Fibonacci formula.

There is a shift-invariant Borel probability measure μ on GoldenMean with μ(cylinder w) = φ^{-|w|} up to boundary weights, and its measure-theoretic entropy equals log φ, which is the topological entropy computed by card_goldenWords.

Formalise the Markov measure via Carathéodory extension on the clopen cylinder algebra isClopen_cylinder, then compute the entropy of the 2x2 Perron-Frobenius eigenvector and compare with tendsto_log_coveringNumber.

The variational principle for this subshift is fully formalised, and the box dimension result upgrades to a measure-theoretic dimension statement.

The failure would have to come from non-additivity on the cylinder algebra, indicating that the recursive definition of goldenWords does not match the Markov structure, which would be a surprising defect in the combinatorial model.
proof_strategy: Cylinders are clopen and form a semiring of sets; additivity reduces to fib(n+2) = fib(n+1) + fib(n) with the φ-weights, i.e. to 1/φ + 1/φ² = 1. Extend by Carathéodory, then use compactness for regularity.
title: Parry Measure of Maximal Entropy for the Golden-Mean Subshift

description:
Nested Reed–Solomon codes RS(k₁) ⊆ RS(k₂) with the computed dual dimensions give a CSS construction whose quantum parameters follow from the classical minimum distances proved here. Conjecture the resulting [[n, k₂-k₁, min(n-k₂+1, k₁+1)]] parameters and formalize the CSS bookkeeping over a finite field.

For 1 ≤ k₁ ≤ k₂ ≤ n, the CSS pair (RS(k₂), RS(k₁)⊥) yields a quantum code with n - (k₂ - k₁) stabilizer generators and distance at least min(n - k₂ + 1, k₁ + 1).

Prove the nesting RS(k₁) ⊆ RS(k₂) as a Submodule inclusion, combine with finrank_dualCode_code, and state the CSS distance bound as a weight statement about the quotient of the two codes.

A fully verified family of quantum error-correcting codes derived from the classical results in this file.

The distance bound degrades on the quotient, pinpointing where classical minimum distance fails to control quantum distance.
proof_strategy: Submodule inclusion from degreeLT monotonicity; dual dimension from finrank_add_finrank_dualCode; weight bounds transported to coset representatives.
title: CSS Quantum Codes from Nested Reed–Solomon Pairs

description:
Numerically a(n) ≤ p(n) for all n ≤ 200. The Durfee square identity expresses p(n) as the same layered sum as a(n) but with Euler products truncated one step later, giving coefficientwise domination. Formalizing this would also produce a Lean proof of the Durfee square identity itself.

For every n, a(n) ≤ p(n); more precisely p(n) = Σ_{k²≤n} Σ_{i+j=n-k²} p_{≤k}(i) p_{≤k}(j), and a(n) is the same sum with p_{≤k-1} in place of p_{≤k}.

Formalize the Durfee square bijection between partitions of n and triples (k, λ, μ) with λ, μ partitions with parts ≤ k and |λ|+|μ| = n-k², then compare layer by layer using the already proved pb b m ≤ pb (b+1) m.

Square-core stacks embed quantitatively inside partitions, and every upper bound for p(n) transfers to a(n).

Some layer of the stack decomposition overshoots its Durfee counterpart, which would reveal an unexpected overcounting in the stack model.
proof_strategy: Conjugation plus the Durfee square extraction, formalized in the style of the existing bijection card_squareCoreStacks; then Finset.sum_le_sum over the common index set of core sizes.
title: Durfee-Square Domination by the Partition Function

description:
The energy dynamics is a
   piecewise-Möbius interval map conjugated by `log`. Studying the invariant
   measure of the induced map on `(0,∞)` (or on `r ∈ (1,∞)`) would quantify how
   the "energy spectrum" of level-`k` nodes distributes as `k → ∞`, connecting
   the tree to Gauss-map / continued-fraction ergodic theory: the inverse
   branches `r ↦ 1/(2−r)`, `1/(r−2)`, `r−2` are exactly continued-fraction-type
   maps.
title: Iterated dynamics and equidistribution

description:
On the trinomial simplex the alpha-connection curvature is proved here to be exactly (1 - alpha^2)/4, a quadratic in alpha with vanishing linear term. The conjecture is that the vanishing of the linear term is universal, forced by the skew-symmetry of the Amari skewness tensor, so that every finite-support model satisfies K_alpha = A - B alpha^2 and in particular the two dually flat connections have equal curvature.

For every finite-support model, the Gauss curvature of Amari's alpha-connection satisfies K_alpha = K_0 - B alpha^2 for a function B depending only on the metric and the skewness tensor C; in particular K_{+1} = K_{-1}.

Expand the Riemann tensor of Gamma - (alpha/2) C in powers of alpha; prove the coefficient of alpha^1 vanishes using the total symmetry of C and metric compatibility; verify numerically on the tied two-group and independence models before formalising.

The alpha-family curvature of any finite-support model is determined by two numbers, and the e- and m-connections are curvature-indistinguishable, sharpening the duality theory.

There is a finite-support model whose alpha-curvature has a genuine linear term, breaking the symmetry alpha ↦ -alpha and giving a new invariant separating the two dual connections.
proof_strategy: Write R^{(alpha)} = R + alpha X + alpha^2 Y with X linear in the covariant derivative of C; contract with the metric and use the total symmetry C_{ijk} = C_{(ijk)} together with dg = -C to kill the alpha^1 contraction.
title: Universal Quadratic Law for Alpha-Connection Curvature

description:
Margin scarcity is conjectured to increase monotonically with layer depth in the last blocks of a transformer, making the tail structurally the least portable region. Combined with the two-scalar bound this yields a monotone, transplant-free damage profile.

For the last k blocks, the mean top-1 gap mu_l is non-increasing in l, hence the certified damage bound (G − mu_l)/(G − 2·eps) is non-decreasing in l.

Measure mu_l and G per layer with a logit lens and compare the predicted bound against measured transplant damage per layer.

Layer selection for model surgery can be made analytically, top-down.

Some late layers are more portable than earlier ones and depth is not the right ordering variable.
proof_strategy: Express mu_l as a telescoping sum of per-layer logit increments and bound the late increments by the residual-stream norm growth.
title: Depth Monotonicity of Margin Scarcity

description:
The tropical model of the same ablation programme assigns a net an epistasis order via transversals of near-optimal paths; the probabilistic model assigns a stack a contraction profile. The conjecture is that these two invariants coincide, bridging combinatorial and probabilistic accounts of the same measurements.

For a stack whose suffix contraction coefficients are c_1 >= ... >= c_n, the epistasis order of the associated prunable net equals the number of indices with c_i < 1.

Build the map sending a Dist/Kern stack to a prunable net, compute both invariants on the affine family and on the tail-pair model, and prove the equality in the deterministic case first.

A single invariant governs both the tropical cost table and the probabilistic ablation profile, unifying two independent formalisations of the programme.

The two models measure genuinely different aspects of epistasis, and tropical cost tables cannot be read as contraction data.
proof_strategy: Deterministic stacks give permutation and constant channels only, whose contraction coefficients are 1 and 0; match these against surviving paths in the prunable net and extend by convexity using the affine family as the interpolating case.
title: Epistasis Order Equals Contracting Suffix Length

description:
Replace v = j^2 - N by v = f(j) - N for a sieve polynomial f of degree d. Mean preservation of the root count is pure fibre counting and still holds, so a mixture excess persists; what changes is the distribution of the root count, which is governed by the factorisation type of f mod q and hence by the Galois group of f.

For a separable f of degree d and odd prime q, the variance of the root count over targets N mod q equals the number of non-identity elements of the Galois group of f fixing a root, up to O(1/q); consequently the mixture excess for the multiplicative proxy is p*c + V_f*(c-1)^2/2 + O((c-1)^3) with V_f a Galois invariant.

Formalise rootCountM for the fibres of a general polynomial map on ZMod q, enumerate cubics and quartics with decide for q up to a few hundred, and compare the measured variance with the orbit count predicted by Frobenius cycle types.

The divisibility-mixture baseline extends to number field sieve style polynomials, where the predicted hump amplitude becomes a Galois-theoretic quantity.

The excess depends on more than the Galois data, indicating that the quadratic case is special and the mechanism is tied to the two-point structure of quadratic residues.
proof_strategy: Fibre counting gives the mean; for the variance count pairs (x,y) with f(x) = f(y), i.e. points of the fibre product curve, and evaluate that count by Chebotarev / Lang-Weil for the splitting field of f(X) - f(Y).
title: Mixture Spectrum of Higher-Degree Sieve Polynomials

description:
Because the lag spectrum is flat, the variance of the number of factor-base hits in a window of L consecutive positions is the independence value minus a correction that is L times one explicit constant, up to a bounded remainder from the two exceptional lags. This turns the proved covariance into a directly usable statement about sieve yield variance.

For a window of L consecutive positions the hit-count variance equals L p (1-p) - 4 L sum_i 1/q_i^2 plus a remainder bounded by a constant times L / q_min^3, so the independence model always overstates the variance.

Expand the variance of a window sum into single-position variances and pairwise lag covariances, substitute lag_spectrum_flat and card_exceptionalLags, and bound the exceptional terms; check numerically for small q and L.

Sieve yield estimates based on independence are conservatively biased by a computable amount, which can be corrected in practice.

Cross-prime or long-range effects not captured by the pairwise lag covariance dominate, indicating higher-order dependencies worth their own study.
proof_strategy: Bilinearity of the empirical covariance over the window sum, then the flat-spectrum substitution, then a counting bound on how often an exceptional lag occurs among the L(L-1)/2 pairs.
title: Window-Variance Correction for Sieve Yield Estimates

description:
The 4/3 residue cap was shown to be the maximum of the fire-or-silent law along its uninformative diagonal P = mu. This suggests every constant cap in the barrier map is the extremum of a slice of the same two-parameter cost surface, cut out by an informational budget curve. Proving this would replace a list of separate caps by one variational principle.

For every budget curve P = g(mu) with g(mu) >= mu and g concave on [0,1], sup_mu 1/(1 - (1-mu) g(mu)) is attained at the unique mu with g'(mu) = (1-g(mu))/(1-mu), and equals 4/3 exactly when g = id.

Formalise the slice function in Lean over the existing costFireOrSilent, prove the first-order condition by differentiating, and check the g = id case against residue_cap_isGreatest.

All barrier-map caps become extrema of one surface; new caps can be read off from new budget curves.

The 4/3 cap is an accident of the diagonal and each cap needs its own derivation.
proof_strategy: Reduce to maximising a rational function of one variable; use strict concavity of g and positivity of the denominator to get uniqueness, then specialise.
title: Diagonal Extremality of the Residue Cap

description:
The exact grouped mean-square formula reduces the GPTQ group-correlation penalty to the number of same-group ordered pairs in the selected key set. The conjecture identifies this count as a Schur-convex function of the group occupancy profile, so balanced selections are optimal and single-group selections worst. This converts a kernel-design question into an extremal set-system statement.

Among group occupancy profiles with sum_t m_t = k and m_t <= g, the same-group pair count sum_t m_t(m_t-1) is minimised exactly at the balanced profiles, with minimum r*q*(q+1) + (N-r)*q*(q-1) for k = qN + r; the counting identity and the maximum k(k-1) are already proved.

Iterate the proved one-step smoothing inequality pairs_smoothing by induction on the imbalance of the profile, using samePartners_sum_eq_profile to transfer back to selections.

A provable scheduling rule: interleave top-k selection across quantization groups.

Some skewed allocation would beat the balanced one, indicating a non-convex interaction landscape.
proof_strategy: Partition S by group, count ordered pairs per block, and use convexity of x -> x(x-1) with a smoothing/majorization exchange argument.
title: Schur-Convexity of the Group-Aligned Interaction Penalty

description:
All node sets used here are arithmetic. The interpolation isomorphisms isolate the only property actually used, namely invertibility of the evaluation system at the node set, suggesting the theory transfers to geometric grids and Laurent charts.

For q of infinite multiplicative order in a domain R, the geometric node set {q^k : |k| ≤ d} certifies identities between Laurent expressions with exponent window [-d,d], in every commutative ring where the relevant elements are invertible.

Parametrise stdGrid by an abstract node set with a nonvanishing Vandermonde determinant hypothesis and check that degree_exact, exists_unique_interpolant, exists_unique_downset_interpolant and finrank_boundedDegree re-elaborate.

The chart calculus extends from polynomial to Laurent charts, covering identities on tori and q-analogues with the same finite-check methodology.

Vandermonde invertibility is not the only ingredient, and the arithmetic of the grid {0,…,d} plays a hidden role that must be isolated.
proof_strategy: Replace X^k by X^k with k ∈ ℤ via a localisation, transport the exactness proof through the ring map ℤ[x, x⁻¹] → R, and use the geometric Vandermonde determinant ∏_{i<j}(q^i - q^j) ≠ 0.
title: Geometric Node Systems for Laurent Charts

description:
An oracle answering the sensor 1{gap <= B} at every threshold B reconstructs the factorisation. We conjecture that a single fixed threshold suffices, because multiplying N by small squares rescales the gap predictably, so binary search can be simulated by rescaling instead of by varying B.

For every fixed B >= 1 there is a polynomial-time algorithm that factors odd semiprimes using only queries of the form 'is gap(M) <= B' for integers M derived from N by multiplication by squares of small integers.

Formalize the rescaling identity relating gap(N) and gap(t^2 N) for small t, then build the search in Lean on top of least_accepting_eq_gap.

Barrier 6 becomes a completeness theorem: one bit of the navigation sensor is as hard as factoring.

The sensor family is strictly stronger than any single threshold, and the crediting framework must be indexed by B.
proof_strategy: Control gap(t^2 N) via the midpoint identity mid(tp, tq) = t * mid(p,q) and the interlacing of isqrt(t^2 N) = t * isqrt(N) + error, then use the monotone family of rescalings as a substitute for varying the threshold.
title: Single-Threshold Factoring Completeness of Sensor Oracles

description:
Determinism has been proved for the Brahmagupta pair: the subtractive gcd is exactly q and the additive one exactly p. The conjecture is that for an arbitrary pair of essentially distinct representations the extracted prime is read off the class bits, so no gcd computation is needed to know which factor appears.

For essentially distinct representations (a,b), (c,d) of N = pq, gcd(ad - bc, N) = q iff the two representations share their p-bit, and equals p iff they share their q-bit.

Check all eligible N < 10^6 by brute force, then formalise using the Z[i] factorisation supplied by gaussianInt_split.

Euler's method becomes fully deterministic and gcd-free in its combination step.

Some pair's extraction is not predicted by the bits, contradicting unique factorisation in Z[i] - a sharp falsifiability test.
proof_strategy: Write z1 = pi_p * pi_q and z2 = pi_p' * pi_q' with each pi a Gaussian prime; Im(z1 conj(z2)) has norm-gcd equal to the norm of the shared factor, which is the prime whose bit agrees.
title: Bit-Predicted Extraction for Arbitrary Representation Pairs

description:
The unconditional clause L7-e is equivalent to a sublinear-time factoring separation. The relativized version, where the enumeration may query residues of N, is within reach because promotion counts are key-independent at every modulus.

No enumeration computable from residue queries alone beats the mass-sort optimum on an MLR population; equivalently every residue-oracle policy has speedup 1 against a flat prior.

Formalise a residue-oracle machine model over Finset.range (M*m) and derive the no-gain corollary from keyed_promotion_factor_blind and flat_prior_cost.

The barrier-4 residue stratum closes unconditionally in the relativized model; only prior shape remains.

Some oracle policy gains, and the factor-blind law needs an exception clause.
proof_strategy: Key-independence of promotion counts plus flat-prior invariance of enumeration cost.
title: Oracle-Relative Factor Blindness of Residue Enumerations

description:
The balanced (fixed-weight) draw law approaches the universal Spearman tie ceiling 6/7 from below at rate Theta(1/v). We conjecture the exact rate constant is 9/343 = 9/7^3, arising as (1/8)(3/2)(1/7 - 1/343) where the gain 1/7 is the Catalan first-step anomaly and the loss 1/343 is the summed Weierstrass defect of all deeper steps. This identifies a closed-form asymptotic for the deployment-envelope margin of the zero-fit dial.

lim_{v -> infinity} v * (6/7 - spearmanSq (centralProfile v)) = 9/343.

Squeeze the deficit between two explicit rational bounds of the form 9/343 +- C/v^2 by refining loss_invariant into a two-sided invariant, then conclude with a Filter.Tendsto argument; numerically the exact-rational sweep to v = 1200 already agrees to five digits.

The bitlen-60 margin (0.856238... versus 6/7) becomes a closed-form quantity, and every future envelope check at a new bitlen reduces to evaluating 6/7 - 9/(343 v).

Either the Weierstrass loss series is not summable termwise at second order or the profile has a hidden third-order correction, which would invalidate the geometric heuristics used throughout the catalog's ceiling bounds.
proof_strategy: Refine the deficit invariant of loss_invariant to carry both a lower and an upper accumulated deficit with quadratic-in-depth coefficients, sum the resulting geometric series in closed form (x^3/(1-x)^3 at x = 1/8 gives 1/343), and pass to the limit.
title: Catalan Deficit Constant Nine Over Three Hundred Forty-Three

description:
For balanced semiprimes N, define the capture spectrum C(X) = Σ_{ℓ ≤ X} r_ℓ², where r_ℓ is the sample correlation between the per-N log hit rate and the product-form Legendre indicator at prime ℓ. The conjecture is that C(X) stays below the pre-registered 0.30 bar for every X up to 10⁶ at bitlen 96, so the overdispersion carrier is not a small-prime residue effect at any window. The family capture bound turns this into a finite scalar computation with a proved stopping rule.

For bitlen-96 balanced semiprimes, sup_{X ≤ 10⁶} Σ_{ℓ ≤ X} r_ℓ² < 0.30, hence no affine recalibration of the ℓ ≤ X product-form dial family attains a 30% dispersion reduction.

Compute the 78k per-prime correlations and partial sums; compare against Logic.QRDial.family_bar_missed, whose hypothesis is exactly Σ_j corrSq y (s j) < 3/10.

The papers-136/139 dial line does not extend to bitlen 96 at any prime window; the carrier of u ≈ 10 clustering is a genuinely new N-structure.

Papers 136/139, 220 and 226 unify under a scale-dependent dial bound, with the crossing point of C(X) giving the calibration scale.
proof_strategy: Independent characters make distinct primes orthogonal, so Logic.QRDial.family_capture_bound applies verbatim; the only inputs are the per-prime shares, and monotonicity of partial sums gives the sup.
title: Prime-Window Capture Spectrum for Quadratic-Residue Dials

description:
The law of total variance shows the unexplained dispersion lives entirely in the variance of the per-modulus rate. Conjecture that this variance is generated by an arithmetic mixing variable, namely the small-prime divisor structure of the sieve polynomial values, and not by anything positional.

There is a scalar arithmetic statistic s(N), computable from the factorisation of the sieve base value v(0) = b^2 - N over the factor base, such that conditioning on s(N) reduces the residual dispersion index of the hit counts to 1 + o(1).

Compute s(N) for the exp-578 family, regress the hit counts on s(N), and check whether the conditional dispersion index drops to 1; formalise the reduction as an instance of law_total_variance with the conditional variances equal to the conditional means.

The overdispersion is fully explained arithmetically, closing the round-80 open problem.

The carrier is not divisor-structural and must be sought in the geometry of the scan window.
proof_strategy: Combine PositionalRateLink.law_total_variance with the exact 1/d window density of Catalog.NumberTheory.FermatPositionDensity to compute the conditional mean rate given s(N).
title: Divisor-Mixture Carrier of Between-Modulus Rate Variance

description:
Cut-offs below 0.1123 are provably degenerate for all 96-bit moduli and 0.2072 is provably not. We conjecture the exact supremum of universally degenerate cut-offs is the infimum of the crossing curve, (sqrt 6 - 2)/4, approached as N tends to 2^96 from below.

sup {c : for all 96-bit N and all j with u(j) <= c one has j^2 - N < 2^95} = (sqrt 6 - 2)/4, and the supremum is not attained.

Sharpen sharp_degeneracy from the rational 2246/20000 to arbitrary c < (sqrt 6 - 2)/4, and construct for each epsilon a modulus below 2^96 with a full-size residue at position (sqrt 6 - 2)/4 + epsilon.

The degeneracy phenomenon is characterised by a single quadratic irrationality.

The discrete threshold is strictly below the continuum infimum, which would mean lattice effects survive at 96 bits and contradict fraction_bridge.
proof_strategy: Monotonicity of crossingPos plus the discrete-continuum bridge, with an explicit family of moduli approaching 2^96.
title: Exact Universal Degeneracy Constant (sqrt 6 - 2)/4

description:
Extend the exact two-point root-count mixture from primes to prime powers. For odd p and k >= 1 the number of solutions of x^2 = a mod p^k depends on the p-adic valuation of a, and the induced variance controls how much of a smoothness hump a prime power can carry. This fixes the size of the effect for composite moduli, where the current work proves strict positivity but not the exact amplitude.

For odd p and k >= 1, the exact identity sum over a mod p^k of c^{X(a)} equals p^k*c + E_{p,k}(c) where E_{p,k} is an explicit polynomial vanishing to second order at c = 1, and the variance sum over a of (X(a)-1)^2 equals an explicit function of p and k asymptotic to p^k(1-1/p).

Formalise rootCountM for m = p^k, enumerate 3^5, 5^3, 7^3 with decide to fix the pattern, then prove by stratifying a by v_p(a) and Hensel lifting each stratum.

The divisibility-mixture baseline becomes fully explicit for every smooth modulus, so the predicted hump amplitude of a sieve is computable from the factor base alone.

Prime powers carry a different share than primes, separating the m|v conditioning strata and identifying a new covariate family.
proof_strategy: Stratify by v_p(a); for v_p(a)=0 lift the prime-case roots by Hensel (exactly two lifts); for 0 < v_p(a) < k substitute x = p^ceil(i/2) y; sum the strata geometrically.
title: Mixture Spectrum for Prime Powers

description:
B_2-freeness is equivalent to the local statement that every open interval (A,D) spanned by two members of the family contains at most one further member. This converts a four-element search into a counting condition on intervals, which is the natural input for entropy or flag-algebra methods.

La(n, B_2) <= (2 + o(1)) C(n, floor(n/2)), proved via the interval-local characterisation.

Formalise the equivalence from HasBdCopy 2 and then bound the Lubell mass of families satisfying the interval condition.

The long-standing diamond conjecture is resolved, and the doubling lemma lifts the result towards general d.

The interval condition is too weak to detect the extremal structure, isolating precisely which global information is needed.
proof_strategy: Unfold HasBdCopy for d = 2, then run a two-step Lubell split conditioned on the interval structure of the family.
title: Interval-Local Characterisation of Diamond-Freeness

description:
Because Fisher-z pooling is Einstein velocity composition, rapidity is the unique coordinate in which correlation pooling is a group operation. Conjecture that the bitlen fade is exponential in rapidity with a finite plateau rapidity and that the seed ensemble is a translation family in that coordinate. This makes the plateau a constant of the generator rather than of the sampling grid.

There exist kappa > 0 and z_inf with artanh(rho_L) = z_inf + (artanh(rho_96) - z_inf) exp(-kappa (L - 96)) for the seven measured rungs within CI width, and the per-seed rapidities differ by bitlen-independent offsets.

Fit the three-parameter rapidity model to the seven rungs and to the per-seed triples; compare residuals with the affine-in-rho fit.

The band floor becomes a rapidity threshold and the plateau is a generator constant.

The fade is not a noise-accumulation process and the plateau is an artefact of the bitlen grid.
proof_strategy: Use tanh_artanh_add and fisherAdd_assoc to show that accumulating independent noise acts by rapidity translation, then derive the exponential law from a one-parameter semigroup argument.
title: Rapidity-Additive Fade Law

description:
Interpolate the proved geometric and Pareto knee bounds by a single power-law family: if the residual after r+j keys decays like R·j^(-α), the knee should satisfy k* - r ≍ (R/(1-τ))^(1/α). This turns per-domain tail-shape analysis into a law with one measurable exponent.

For every attention profile whose residual satisfies R/(j+1)^α ≤ 1 - cum(r+j) ≤ R'/(j+1)^α with α ≥ 1, the knee obeys c₁(R/(1-τ))^(1/α) ≤ k* - r ≤ c₂(R'/(1-τ))^(1/α) with absolute constants c₁, c₂.

Formalise the α-indexed staged profile in Lean and prove both inequalities; check the α → ∞ limit reduces to the existing geometric bound.

The knee becomes predictable from a single fitted exponent per domain, replacing the current correlational reporting.

The knee depends on more than the leading tail exponent, and any per-domain summary must retain at least two tail parameters.
proof_strategy: Lower bound by evaluating the residual at the knee as in heavy_tail_knee_lower_bound; upper bound by choosing j with R'/(j+1)^α ≤ 1-τ and applying kneeAt_le; sharpness by an explicit staged profile with power-law steps.
title: Tail-Exponent Law for the Attention Knee

description:
Because the x-coordinate detector is invariant under the elliptic involution, the detected orders are the divisors of the sumset J+J together with the difference set J-J of the visited multiple set J. Conjecture: the sequential run is far from optimal and a Sidon-complement construction detects many more orders at equal cost.

The advantage already proved at k = 4 (the set {1,2,4,8} detects orders 9, 10 and 12 that {1,2,3,4} misses) persists and grows: the ratio of detected-order counts between the best J of size k and the sequential set tends to infinity with k.

Exhaustive or randomized search over J for small k, then a Lean certificate for the winning set using the divisibility characterization xEq_iff_dvd.

A cheap redesign of stage one improves the constant of every lite-style method.

The sequential run is combinatorially optimal for involution detectors, a satisfying rigidity statement.
proof_strategy: Reduce detection to divisibility of sumset and difference-set elements, then optimize the divisor mass of the resulting multiset.
title: Involution-Optimal Visiting Sets

description:
Every reading converts into a forced rank-displacement fraction (1-rho)/6, turning model selection into a statement about how much of the sample a mechanism must touch. The hyperbolic law saturates at 3/28 and can never demand more; any extinction law demands unboundedly more, with the crossing at bitlen 120. The budget is therefore a combinatorial falsification test that needs no curve fitting at all.

Any rank-level mechanism reproducing the recorded ladder must displace a fraction of the sample that exceeds 3/28 at some bitlen at most 128; equivalently, no bounded-displacement mechanism explains the thread.

Instantiate reading_corruption_budget at each recorded rung and compare with 3/28; formalise the resulting monotone budget ladder in Lean.

The hyperbolic shape class is refuted a second time, by a purely combinatorial argument independent of any fit.

The budget stalls below 3/28, which would be strong evidence for a genuine floor and against extinction.
proof_strategy: Combine reqFrac monotonicity with the recorded rungs, then use floor_is_the_seven_point_five_percent_budget for the converse direction to pin the mechanism from both sides.
title: Corruption-Budget Saturation Test

description:
Each coordinate face of the Berggren tree is supported on prime classes fixed by a quadratic character. The hypotenuse face is exactly the 1 mod 4 primes; the leg faces should have their own, different, congruence supports. Classifying them tells any tree-based sieve in advance which moduli it can never split.

For a primitive Pythagorean triple (a,b,c) with b even, every odd prime divisor of c is 1 mod 4, every prime divisor of b is unrestricted, and every odd prime divisor of a is 1 mod 4 or 3 mod 4 according to the parity of the parametrizing pair (m,n) modulo 4.

Formalize the leg analogue of TreeSieveHyp.prime_dvd_hyp_one_mod_four via the (m,n) parametrization and verify exhaustively for tree depth <= 8.

Every face-restricted tree sieve carries a provable blindness class, extending TreeSieveHyp.hypotenuse_face_blind_semiprime.

The blindness obstruction is confined to the hypotenuse and leg-based sieves remain generic lotteries.
proof_strategy: Use the primitive parametrization a = m^2 - n^2, b = 2mn, c = m^2 + n^2; reduce divisibility of each coordinate to solvability of x^2 = -1 or x^2 = 1 in ZMod p, then apply ZMod.exists_sq_eq_neg_one_iff.
title: Quadratic-Residue Face Selection for Tree Sieves

description:
Exact scale invariance holds only for the untruncated attention profile. On [1, C] the additive unit of mass breaks homogeneity and produces a crossover context length, a candidate mechanism for the reported onset near two thousand tokens. The conjecture makes the onset a theorem about a squeeze between two explicit budgets.

For the profile x^(-s) on [1,C] with s<1 the exact budget is (τ C^(1-s) + (1-τ))^(1/(1-s)), it exceeds the scale-invariant budget τ^(1/(1-s)) C, and the relative gap is decreasing in C.

Compute the truncated mass integral with integral_rpow, derive the gate, and prove both inequalities in Lean.

The phase-transition onset is a boundary-layer artefact of finite context, with a computable crossover.

The onset needs a genuinely different mechanism, e.g. head specialisation rather than mass truncation.
proof_strategy: integral_rpow on [1,C]; monotonicity of x ↦ (τ x + (1-τ))^(1/(1-s)) / x^(1/(1-s)); rpow inequalities.
title: Truncated-Zipf Crossover Scale

description:
Spreading the 0.1578 of squared correlation that the extension window 400 < ℓ ≤ 10⁶ would have to supply over at most 78498 primes forces some single Legendre-symbol dial to reach r² ≥ 2·10⁻⁶. The conjecture is that no symbol in that window reaches the floor at bitlen 96, so the scale-shift hypothesis fails and the carrier lies outside the QR dial family. The test is a single pass over 78k per-prime correlations with a proved threshold.

For bitlen-96 balanced semiprimes, max_{400 < ℓ ≤ 10⁶} r_ℓ² < 2·10⁻⁶ for the per-N log hit rate, hence Σ_{400 < ℓ ≤ 10⁶} r_ℓ² < 0.1578 and the ℓ ≤ 10⁶ family misses the 0.30 bar.

Compute the per-prime squared correlations over the extension window and compare with the hypotheses of Logic.QRDial.exp576_window_extension_target; a single symbol above the floor is required for the scale-shift reading to survive.

The QR dial family is exhausted at bitlen 96 and the u ≈ 10 carrier is structure outside every recorded mechanism.

The informative window has genuinely moved past 400, and the crossing prime calibrates a scale-dependent dial bound unifying papers 136/139 and 220.
proof_strategy: Bessel budget for orthogonal dials plus a pigeonhole over the extension window, both already formalized; the empirical input is only the list of per-prime shares.
title: Per-Symbol Detection Floor for Extended Prime Windows

description:
The hump calculus uses the exact first Dickman branch rho(u) = 1 - log u on [1,2], where convexity is elementary. The measured regime is u about 2.5, on the second branch, so the calibration needs convexity of rho on all of [1, infinity), which follows from the delay equation but is absent from Mathlib.

The Dickman function rho is convex on [1, infinity), and the two-point mixture excess (rho(u) + rho(u-delta))/2 - rho(u - delta/2) is positive and strictly increasing in delta for all u > delta > 0.

Define rho by the delay equation with rho = 1 on [0,1], prove positivity and monotone decrease by branch induction, then derive that rho'(u) = -rho(u-1)/u is increasing.

The amplitude-to-spread inversion applies at the measured u about 2.5, making the calibration directly usable on sieve data.

Convexity fails on a later branch, so a mixture can lower the smoothness rate there - a qualitatively new and testable prediction.
proof_strategy: Branch induction with the integral form rho(u) = rho(n) - integral of rho(t-1)/t; monotonicity of rho gives monotonicity of rho', hence convexity.
title: Dickman Convexity Beyond the First Branch

description:
The set of Pythagorean states reachable modulo m from (3,4,5) appears to have exactly ½m²∏(1−p⁻²) elements, i.e. half of the punctured null cone modulo a prime. Proving it would replace the crude 2p² upper bound used in the current hardness theorems by the exact (p²−1)/2 and make every ambiguity bound tight. The approach is to identify the Berggren monoid image with an index-two subgroup of the modular orthogonal group of a²+b²−c².

For all m ≥ 3 the Berggren orbit of (3,4,5) in (ℤ/m)³ has cardinality ½ m² ∏_{p|m} (1 − p⁻²); for prime p this is (p²−1)/2, exactly half the punctured null cone.

Formalise the count of zeros of the ternary form a²+b²−c² over 𝔽_p via the substitution (x,y,z)=(c−a,c+a,b) reducing to xy=z², then show the orbit is one of the two cosets of the index-two subgroup generated by the three moves.

All ambiguity and impossibility thresholds sharpen from 2p² to (p²−1)/2, and the observation space of the adversary is completely determined.

The orbit is a proper subset of the half-cone, revealing an additional arithmetic invariant beyond the Lorentz form and primitivity.
proof_strategy: Prove #{v ∈ 𝔽_p³ : v₁²+v₂²=v₃²} = p² by the xy=z² count; prove the Berggren generators lie in SO(Q) and generate an index-two subgroup; transitivity on the coset by lifting the integer classifier.
title: Half-Cone Orbit Count for Berggren Moves mod m

description:
Transfer the multiplicative pole-order theorem to q-expansions of modular functions at the cusp. The approach is to identify orderTop with the cusp valuation and deduce that a product of m ≥ 2 Hauptmodul-shaped functions cannot itself be a Hauptmodul. It matters because it converts an algebraic valuation statement into a statement about modular curves.

No product of m ≥ 2 normalized q-expansions of weight-zero modular functions is again a Hauptmodul for the same group.

Match orderTop with the cusp order in Mathlib's modular forms API and apply prod_isNormalized_iff.

The pole-order obstruction gives a purely formal proof of a genus-zero rigidity statement.

The cusp valuation differs from the formal Laurent order in the relevant normalization, indicating a definitional mismatch to repair.
proof_strategy: Define the q-expansion map into ℂ⸨X⸩, prove it is a ring homomorphism preserving order, and pull back prod_isNormalized_iff.
title: Cusp-Order Obstruction to Modular Invariance

description:
The geometric fragment is now known to be closed under Cauchy products and its germs are totally ordered by the lexicographic order on coefficients. Adding multiplicative inverses for series with nonzero leading coefficient should make the germs an ordered field, that is a Hardy field. This would complete a formal-to-analytic dictionary for asymptotic expansions.

For a GeoSeries c with nonzero leading coefficient there is a GeoSeries c' and a rate r such that eval c * eval c' equals 1 eventually; consequently the germs of the geometric fragment modulo eventual equality form an ordered field.

Construct the inverse by normalizing the leading coefficient, writing c as leading times (1 - u) with u of positive rank, and inverting by the geometric series in u; verify convergence with GeoSeries.tail_bound and multiplicativity with GeoSeries.evalT_mulG.

A fully formalized Hardy field arising from a Hahn-type coefficient algebra, with order given by eval_lt_iff_lexLt.

Inversion leaks out of every geometric rate, and the correct object is a localization rather than a field of germs.
proof_strategy: Neumann series in u with geometric rate control, then transfer the field axioms through the injective interpretation.
title: Hardy Field Structure on Geometric Fragment Germs

description:
The Gödel-universe conjecture is not asserted here: a closed
   timelike curve is geometric, whereas self-consistency requires an additional dynamical law.
   A faithful future treatment should first formalize a Lorentzian spacetime, timelike curves,
   Gödel's metric, and a matter evolution relation. It should then state consistency relative to
   that evolution law rather than infer it from geometric closure alone.
title: Lorentzian geometry boundary

description:
The proved non-asymptotic law has remainders 2·Var/β² (upper) and 3·Var/β² (lower). The conjecture is that both optimal constants are 1, because the Taylor remainder and the normalisation shift partially cancel rather than adding. Random search shows the current bounds are never violated but are not far from tight.

For β ≥ range r, |‖π_β − p‖₁ − MAD_p(r)/β| ≤ Var_p(r)/β².

Re-run the proof of RLHF.abs_l1_numerator_sub_mad keeping the sign of (W_β − 1) instead of taking absolute values, and test the resulting constant numerically over random instances with β/range near 1.

A clean, memorable non-asymptotic drift law with all constants equal to 1.

There is a genuine instance forcing a constant above 1, which would identify the extremal reward shape for finite temperature.
proof_strategy: Split 𝔼_p|e^s − W| into the parts where e^s ≥ W and e^s < W; on each part the W-shift has a fixed sign, so it cancels against the corresponding part of 𝔼_p|s| rather than adding.
title: Optimal Second-Order Constants in the Mean-Deviation Drift Law

description:
The per-curve success probability of ECM-lite is a divisor-mass average over the Hasse interval rather than a birthday probability. We conjecture the average density of points of order at most B is asymptotically (sum over d<=B of phi(d)/d)/p, i.e. about 0.61B/p.

As p tends to infinity with B fixed, the average over random curves E/F_p of #{P in E : ord(P) <= B}/|E| equals (1/p)·sum_{d<=B} phi(d)/d · (1 + O(p^{-1/2})).

Compare against the measured medians in ComputationalEvidence.md; formalize the fixed-group exact count (done: card_lowOrder_eq_sum_totient) and combine with an equidistribution input for |E| in the Hasse interval.

The ECM-lite budget constant is pinned to 1/(0.61B), completing the quantitative model of the lite arm.

Group orders in the Hasse interval are biased in their small divisors in a way that matters for stage one.
proof_strategy: Exact totient count per cyclic group, then average d | N over N in the Hasse interval using the Deuring/Birch equidistribution heuristic made effective.
title: Hasse-Interval Divisor Mass for Low-Order Points

description:
For E(F_p) isomorphic to Z/n1 x Z/n2 the stage-1 firing count is the product of the two smooth parts, which is at least the cyclic count. We conjecture the average multiplicative gain is exactly the torsion Euler factor over the primes dividing gcd(n1,n2).

Averaged over curves with point group Z/n1 x Z/n2 of fixed order m, the gain gcd(n1,k)gcd(n2,k)/gcd(m,k) tends to the product over primes q dividing gcd(n1,n2) of (1 + 1/q).

Compute the gain exactly for all factorizations m = n1 n2 with n1 dividing n2, weighted by the number of curves realizing each group; compare with the conjectured Euler product.

Curve selection favouring small-prime torsion has a quantified, provable stage-1 advantage.

The rank-two advantage is not captured by torsion primes alone and depends on finer curve statistics.
proof_strategy: Use card_firingSet_prod to reduce the gain to a product over primes of q^(min(v_q n1,e)+min(v_q n2,e)-min(v_q m,e)), then average over the divisor structure.
title: Torsion Gain of Rank-Two Point Groups

description:
The proved two-sided bounds 2*m*j <= k^2 + 2*m and k^2 <= 2(u+k)*j pin the Fermat frontier offset at Theta(k^2/sqrt N). Promote this to an exponent law in terms of k = N^alpha, making the stipulated oracle cost laws into theorems.

For N = u(u+2k) with k = N^alpha, the anchored ascent offset satisfies j = Theta(N^(2*alpha - 1/2)) for 1/4 < alpha < 1/2, and j = O(1) for alpha <= 1/4.

Wrap the two proved inequalities with Nat.sqrt asymptotics and instantiate at k = N^alpha; verify numerically on semiprime families with prescribed imbalance.

Fermat-window cost becomes a theorem-level baseline against which any claimed channel must be measured.

One of the two inequalities is not tight, revealing extra structure in the anchor correction N - m^2.
proof_strategy: Divide the two proved bounds by 2m and 2(u+k) respectively and control m = floor(sqrt N) between sqrt N - 1 and sqrt N.
title: Frontier-Cost Exponent Law for Balanced Semiprimes

description:
The mixing-ratio response of the top-k attention budget is Schur-concave in the key-count vector, not merely maximised at the balanced point; cycle 4 proves the non-strict ordering and the open part is strictness. The approach is to quantify the mass moved by one Robin Hood transposition and compare it with the spacing of the knee grid. It matters because it would reduce the whole ratio sweep to a single scalar imbalance parameter.

For a strictly antitone profile and m + l = m' + l' with (m, l) majorising (m', l'), the mixed knee satisfies k*(m, l) <= k*(m', l') (proved in cycle 4 as mixKnee_majorise), and the inequality is strict whenever the profile's tail ratio exceeds a threshold depending on the gate.

Quantify the mass moved by one Robin Hood step using headMass_majorise and mixHead_majorise, compare it with the spacing of the retained-fraction grid, and test numerically on power-law profiles where the grid is fine.

Mixed-corpus budget tables can be indexed by imbalance alone.

Knee curves can have interior local minima, so the reported premium is not a robust design parameter.
proof_strategy: Start from mixKnee_majorise (mirroring plus transposition concavity of head mass), then bound below the increase in the retained fraction produced by one transposition and show it exceeds the gap to the next grid point whenever the profile decays slowly enough.
title: Strict Schur-Concavity of the Mixed Attention Budget

description:
Combining `PCPBridge.lean` with the simulator of
   `ThreeColoringZK.lean` should yield a *zero-knowledge PCP*: the verifier's local view of
   the randomized proof string is simulable. The counting lemma `perm3_pair_count`
   generalizes to `k` queries as long as the queried vertices carry pairwise distinct
   colours, which fails in general — quantifying the resulting leakage is an interesting
   combinatorial question.
title: Zero knowledge for the PCP verifier

description:
Reading a knee on a coarse grid returns a bracket, not a value. The NET-78 grid leaves the true knee anywhere in [33,40], and both endpoints are realised by explicit profiles matching the whole table. Probe design is therefore threshold search on a monotone predicate, with a matching information-theoretic lower bound.

Three further probes suffice to determine the knee inside a bracket of width 8, and no adaptive strategy using two probes can, because a monotone predicate on 8 candidate thresholds has 8 distinguishable outcomes.

Formalise adaptive probe strategies as decision trees over monotone predicates and prove a depth lower bound of ceil(log2 (b-a+1)) together with a binary-search strategy attaining it; empirically, probe k = 34, 36, 38.

Every reported knee acquires a certified resolution, and grid design becomes a theorem-backed part of the protocol rather than a convention.

Some structural property of retention curves (e.g. concavity of the tail) lets fewer probes suffice, which would itself be a strong statement about attention profiles.
proof_strategy: Model a probe as evaluating a monotone Boolean predicate; count reachable leaves by induction on tree depth; realise the upper bound by explicit binary search, reusing the sharpness witnesses pLow and pHigh for the adversary argument.
title: Optimal Probe Design for Knee Brackets

description:
Prefix R-squared curves were shown not to be unimodal even for sorted signals of equal mass. The natural next question is how bad it can get: how many strict local maxima can such a curve have, as a function of the number of columns.

For m columns of equal mass with nonincreasing nonnegative signals, the curve k -> A_k^2/k has at most floor(log2 m) + 1 strict local maxima, and a geometric signal profile attains this bound.

Decide small cases m <= 8 by exhaustive rational search in Lean, and formalise the geometric lower-bound family; attack the upper bound by induction on blocks between consecutive maxima.

Bootstrap argmax distributions may legitimately have several modes, and their number is bounded, which calibrates how many modes are worth reporting.

A single window curve can have arbitrarily many modes, so grid-based argmax reporting is unstable in principle and should be replaced by matched-weight scoring.
proof_strategy: Show that between consecutive strict local maxima the running numerator must at least double, using the exact step law, and conclude by comparing with the total signal.
title: Local Maximum Count for Prefix R-Squared Curves

description:
The correlation ratio of the partition of moduli into L-mass cells is an exact ceiling on every criterion measurable in the L-mass, and on every contrast such a criterion can form; the constant in that ceiling is now known to be unimprovable at every cell count. Conjecture that the ceiling is uniformly small: the deviation field has almost all of its energy within L-mass cells, at every threshold scale.

For every x and every partition of squarefree moduli m in [3, M] into level sets of the L-mass P(m) rounded to precision eps, the within-cell energy of log D(m) is at least (1 - o(1)) times its total energy as M tends to infinity.

Compute withinSS/TSS directly over the discriminant cells for increasing M and decreasing eps; check for a floor. In Lean, instantiate lmass_nonlinear_floor and betweenSS_le_of_rsq with the measured theta.

No function of the L-mass, however nonlinear, can serve as an MA-1 criterion; the negative result becomes unconditional in the nonlinear class.

A nonlinear criterion exists that the registered log-log fit could not see, and the sweep's linear protocol was underpowered.
proof_strategy: Pair moduli with nearly equal L-mass but widely different phi(m) using the multiplicativity of the L-mass over the discriminant divisors; show the deviation gap between such pairs is bounded below by the size effect quantified in rsq_affine_ge_of_noise.
title: Between-Cell Energy Floor for Discriminant Partitions

description:
The named gap L4 asks for a stratum measure Delta(pi, R) for scan orders. With the positional law now a single scalar function of the block measure, Delta can be defined as the integrated excess of costCert under the order pi over the identity order, making L4 and the L7 extremality claim precise.

Delta(pi, R) >= 0 for every order pi with equality iff pi is measure preserving on the corner window, and Delta is maximised among N-computable orders by the sqrt-descending order, with extremal value 1/2 - o(1).
