Define Delta as a finite sum over window cells in Lean, prove nonnegativity by convexity of costCert in mu, and evaluate the sqrt-descending order on small N.

L4 is closed and L7 becomes a concrete extremal problem over computable orders.

Order effects are not captured by the block measure alone and the positional law needs a genuinely order-dependent refinement.
proof_strategy: Nonnegativity from Jensen applied to the affine-in-P, convex-in-mu structure of costCert; extremality by an exchange argument on inversions.
title: Stratum Measure as a Tropical Corner Defect

description:
Every L-estimator (weighted average of order statistics) should have breakdown number equal to the tent profile min(j+1, n-j) evaluated at the extreme support points of its weight vector. The approach lifts the two count-based sandwich lemmas from single order statistics to finite convex combinations. It matters because it would compute the breakdown numbers of the trimmed mean, Winsorised mean and trimean as instances of one theorem.

For weights w on {0,...,n-1} with nonnegative entries summing to 1, the breakdown number of xs \mapsto \sum_j w_j \cdot orderStat j xs equals min(jmin+1, n-jmax) where jmin and jmax are the smallest and largest indices with w_j > 0.

Formalise trimmedMean alpha as an L-estimator in Lean and prove IsLeast {k | not EstBounded ...} = min(jmin+1, n-jmax); first check the alpha-trimmed mean on ratios16 for alpha = 1/8, 1/4, 3/8 by #eval on the profile formula.

A single theorem yields the breakdown numbers of the whole classical L-estimator family, and shows no L-estimator beats the median.

There is an L-estimator whose interior weights create extra robustness, which would contradict the support-functional picture and force a genuinely new mechanism.
proof_strategy: Robustness: apply orderStat_le_of_countP / le_orderStat_of_countP to each charged index, then bound the weighted sum by the extreme bounds. Sharpness: contaminate the jmin+1 lowest (resp. n-jmax highest) coordinates and use countP_contaminate_le to drive the charged extreme order statistic to minus infinity, dominating the fixed weight.
title: Concave Breakdown Profiles for L-Estimators

description:
Scalar stability for the Kantorovich inequality is now proved: slack eps forces the ratio profile within weighted L1 distance eps/(2*alpha*beta*(beta-alpha)) of the window endpoints. The conjecture transfers this to the geometric dial, where the per-seed readings also vary, so the observed excess of the pooled reading over the sharp bound mixes reading spread with ratio spread. The claim is that the two contributions separate with an explicit constant.

For a block family with per-seed readings in [rho, rho+delta] and ratios in [alpha, beta], pooledCorr - rho*2*sqrt(alpha*beta)/(alpha+beta) is bounded below by c1(alpha,beta) times the weighted L1 distance of the ratio profile to the window endpoints, minus c2*delta.

Instrument the proof of pooled_kantorovich_bound to carry the slack term rather than discarding it, then combine with kantorovich_stability and the reading spread bound from seed_reading_window; check numerically on two-block families with prescribed reading and ratio spreads.

A measured pooled excess becomes a two-sided measurement of the seed energy profile, upgrading the inverse pooling law from a window to a quantitative reconstruction.

Reading spread and ratio spread cannot be disentangled from a single pooled number, and per-seed instrumentation is mandatory for any structural conclusion about seeds.
proof_strategy: Track the Cauchy-Schwarz defect in blockDot alongside the Kantorovich defect, express both against the same weighted measure given by the block energies, and apply kantorovich_stability to the ratio half while bounding the reading half by delta times the total energy.
title: Stability Transfer to the Geometric Pooled Dial

description:
This cycle produced a finite-support model with negative Fisher curvature at one point and positive curvature at another, but no model with constant negative curvature. The conjecture is that constancy is the real obstruction: on a finite support the Gauss equation for the isometric embedding p ↦ 2√p into the sphere of radius 2 forces the intrinsic curvature to be 1/4 plus the determinant of a second fundamental form, and prescribing that determinant to be a negative constant is a Codazzi obstruction. It matters because it turns 'exponential sensitivity implies hyperbolic geometry' from a slogan into a provably false statement with an explicit boundary.

There is no two-parameter statistical model with finite support and strictly positive probabilities whose Fisher-Rao Gauss curvature equals a constant c < 0 on a nonempty open subset of the parameter space.

Formalise the Gauss equation for surfaces in the round sphere of radius 2 in Lean on top of FisherIdentifiability.pullback_eq_fisher, then show det(II) = c - 1/4 with c < 0 is incompatible with the Codazzi equations for an immersion whose components are algebraic in the probabilities; test computationally first on all four- and five-outcome models with polynomial coordinates of degree at most 3.

Constant negative Fisher curvature is a purely infinite-support (or non-algebraic) phenomenon, and every claim of 'hyperbolic statistical geometry' on a finite alphabet is false as stated.

An explicit finite-support hyperbolic model exists, which would give a finite combinatorial model of the hyperbolic plane with a statistical interpretation.
proof_strategy: Embed via p ↦ 2√p; apply the Gauss equation K = 1/4 + det(II); differentiate the Codazzi equations; use that the coordinates are algebraic to bound degrees and derive a contradiction from a leading-coefficient comparison.
title: Nonexistence of Constant-Negative Fisher Curvature on Finite Supports

description:
Type entropy is a shape invariant, not a size invariant, so along conductors f the value should oscillate rather than increase with degree. We conjecture unbounded oscillation with liminf zero.

The sequence f -> orderEntropy(Gal(Q(zeta_f)+/Q)) has liminf 0 and limsup +infinity, and is non-monotone in the degree phi(f)/2.

Compute orderEntropy for the Galois groups of Q(zeta_f)+ for f up to a few hundred using the closed form for products of cyclic groups; exhibit explicit conductor pairs with larger degree but smaller entropy.

Entropy cannot be used as a proxy for degree; it must be interpreted as a structural fingerprint.

Entropy is a monotone function of the degree, which would make the ladder's measurements redundant.
proof_strategy: Use the closed form H(prod C_{n_i}) as a rational combination of log2 p; take f = 2p with p prime (cyclic rungs, entropy ~ log2 of divisor count of p-1) versus f = product of many small primes (elementary abelian rungs) to force oscillation.
title: Non-Monotone Type Entropy Along the Real Cyclotomic Ladder

description:
The quartic barrier says two distinct representations cannot both be shallow. With r representations the r large parts are r distinct integers below sqrt(N), which should sharpen the barrier quadratically in r. This would show that Euler-style methods get worse, not better, as the input acquires more eligible prime factors.

If N has r pairwise essentially distinct two-square representations, then the depth t at which an ascending scan has collected all of them satisfies t^4 > 2 (r-1)^2 N.

The case r = 3 is already proved (quartic_barrier_three: 8N < a3^4); formalise general r by induction on the sorted list of large parts and check the constant numerically for n = 1105 and n = 32045.

Euler's route degrades as omega(n) grows; the cost barrier compounds.

Many representations make the search shallow, cracking the cost barrier.
proof_strategy: Sort the r large parts; the smallest is at most sqrt(N) - (r-1); apply the same step as quartic_barrier to the extreme pair.
title: Representation-Count-Weighted Depth Barrier

description:
The firing position equals pi(largest prime factor of the powersmooth part). We conjecture that the expected normalized position decays like 1/u where u = log p / log B, so early fire survives arbitrarily large smoothness deficits. This is the named open question of the experimental chain.

For orders m in the Hasse interval of p with nontrivial B-powersmooth part, the mean of pi(lpf(gcd(m,k(B))))/pi(B) is O(1/u) with u = log p / log B.

Census the exact position functional over Hasse intervals for growing p at fixed u (the definitions of ECMStage1FiringRate are computable), then formalize the upper bound conditional on a Dickman-type input for the largest part of a smooth number.

Low-B1 ECM success is early-firing at every scale, justifying schedule truncation as a practical stage-1 optimization.

Early fire is a small-u artefact and truncation loses success probability at cryptographic scales.
proof_strategy: Isolate the arithmetic functional lpf of the smooth part, use the exact position theorem firingCutoff_isLeast, and import a largest-prime-factor distribution bound for smooth numbers; pi is nearly linear in log by Chebyshev.
title: Early-Fire Persistence at Large Smoothness Deficit

description:
Replace the sign-blind magnitude readout by the signed pairing of the AP-deviation field with each real character mod m, and regress it on the signed L-value profile. The magnitude sweep is provably blind to this component, so the null it recorded transfers no information to the signed question. A criterion, if one exists, must live in the signed pairing.

For a suitable normalisation, the signed alignment A(m, chi) = sum_a (pi(x;m,a) - E) chi(a) satisfies a nontrivial linear relation with log(1/L(1,chi)) whose R^2 exceeds 0.5 on squarefree moduli, whereas the magnitude readout has R^2 below 0.1 on the same sample.

Compute A(m, chi) for all real characters of moduli up to 1500 at x = 2^28; regress on log(1/L(1,chi)) at cell level; compare with the magnitude carrier on the identical sample. The invariance obstruction is already formalised (exp566_signed_route_unconstrained) and certifies that the two carriers are genuinely different instruments.

MA-1 effectivity acquires a computable per-character criterion, and the barrier item is downgraded from axiomatic to conditional.

The L-value route is closed in both magnitude and sign, and MA-1 effectivity must be sought in a non-character invariant.
proof_strategy: Expand pi(x;m,a) - E in the character basis; the signed pairing is a single character sum, so the explicit formula relates it to zeros of L(s,chi); bound the contribution of low-lying zeros by the size of L(1,chi) via Deuring-Heilbronn repulsion.
title: Signed Character Alignment as the MA-1 Effectivity Carrier

description:
The image principle proved here says reflection depth only depends on, and is monotone in, the accessibility image of a tag. The conjecture upgrades this to an exact formula: the reflection depth is the least modal depth at which the image fails to realize all types of the model, turning a proof-theoretic invariant into a model-theoretic one and explaining every bound obtained so far.

For a finite frame theory frameSys R V N, the reflection depth of tag i equals the least k such that some world of the model has a depth-k modal type not realized in the image Im_i; moreover any monotone assignment of depths to the inclusion poset of images, bounded by the heights, is realizable by a suitable valuation.

Define depth-k types in Lean as the truth-set classes of the finitely many formulas of box depth <= k, prove that each type of a finite model is definable by a formula of that depth, and derive the equality; then attempt the realizability half on small posets by explicit construction.

All bounds on reflection depth become corollaries of a single counting principle, and the invariant is manifestly bisimulation-invariant.

Definability of types fails at some depth, revealing a genuinely proof-theoretic residue in DepthReflection that is not captured by the semantics.
proof_strategy: Finite model plus finitely many formulas per depth gives a finite type space; the characteristic formula of a type is the conjunction of a finite set of separating formulas, whose box depth is bounded by k. Monotonicity is then subset-realizes-fewer-types.
title: Reflection Depth as Type-Realization Index

description:
Equality of two Monster-sized Laurent products is decidable through multiset comparison, bypassing the series entirely. Quantifying the gap between the multiset route and any coefficient-based route would formalize the value of the rigidity theorem as a proof-complexity statement.

Deciding equality of two integral head products takes O(n log n) steps via sorting, while any certificate that only reads Laurent coefficients needs Omega(n^2) arithmetic operations.

Implement both procedures over Fin n -> Z in Lean, prove equivalence via head_rigidity, and bound their step counts in a simple cost model.

A template for replacing algebraic identity checks by combinatorial certificates in formalized mathematics.

Coefficient-based certificates carry information the multiset route does not, contradicting rigidity.
proof_strategy: Formalize a cost-annotated evaluator, prove the sorting-based algorithm correct from head_rigidity, and derive the lower bound from the number of independent symmetric functions needed to separate multisets.
title: Certificate Complexity of the Moonshine Product Equation

description:
The firing-position CDF of ECM stage 1 is the gcd staircase, a step function with at most omega(m) jumps, while the uniform comparison on the prime schedule has pi(B) steps. We conjecture an explicit sup-distance floor forced purely by the jump budget. This converts the experimental KS rejections into an unconditional inequality.

For m nonzero and B with pi(B) > omega(m), sup_L |gcd(m,k(B,L))/gcd(m,k(B,B)) - pi(L)/pi(B)| >= (pi(B) - omega(m)) / (2 pi(B) (omega(m)+1)).

Upgrade ECMStage1.exists_flat_run from a flat fibre to a flat interval of the schedule, bound the sup-distance on that interval from below by half its uniform increment, and verify sharpness numerically on orders with evenly spread prime divisors.

KS rejection of uniformity for stage-1 firing positions becomes a theorem rather than a statistical finding, for every order and every bound.

There exist orders whose gcd staircase tracks the uniform schedule closely, and the observed non-uniformity is a property of the smooth-order distribution rather than of the staircase mechanism.
proof_strategy: Gap pigeonhole on the jump set, then a two-point evaluation of |F - U| at the endpoints of the longest flat block, using that a constant function differs from an increasing one by at least half its increment somewhere on the block.
title: Kolmogorov–Smirnov Floor for GCD Staircases

description:
Winner shares are realisable arbitrarily by choice of sampler, so they carry no algorithm-intrinsic information. Conjecture that the pointwise dominance order on cost vectors is the complete invariant: two portfolios induce the same set of achievable share-and-ranking profiles across all samplers iff their cost matrices have the same dominance order.

Two finite cost matrices are sampler-equivalent (same achievable pairs of winner-share vector and static ranking over all weightings) if and only if they induce the same pointwise dominance preorder on members.

Formalise sampler-equivalence in the framework of Probability.PortfolioShareRealizability and verify the equivalence by exhaustive search over small matrices before attempting the general proof.

Benchmark claims must be re-stated relative to a named sampler or to the dominance order, sharpening the scope caveat recorded in the ledger.

Some sampler-invariant statistic beyond dominance exists, and identifying it would give a genuinely algorithm-intrinsic benchmark.
proof_strategy: One direction follows from share_realizability by exhibiting extreme-point samplers; the converse requires separating hyperplanes on the simplex of weightings.
title: Sampler-Invariant Content of a Factoring Portfolio

description:
Replace the smooth Lipschitz response by a threshold response driven by the top-two logit gap: attention is intact while key noise stays below half the gap and its ranking is destroyed above it. Because noise halves per bit, the resulting transition window is at most one bit, matching the observed sharpness that the smooth law cannot produce.

The key bit floor equals ceil(log2(d*Q*R / g_typ)) where g_typ is the typical top-two logit gap, so it is predictable from a single forward pass without any perplexity sweep.

Measure the top-two logit gap distribution per head, compute the predicted floor, and compare with the bracketed floor in (5,8]; the Lean side (rank inversion, order-1 damage, one-bit critical band) is already proved in Algebra.KVCacheArgmaxThreshold.

The key floor is a gap statistic of the model, predictable without a perplexity sweep.

Degradation is diffuse rather than argmax driven, and the exponent picture of cycle 2 is the correct one.
proof_strategy: Compare exponentials directly for a two-point softmax, derive the ranking inversion from g < 2*eps, then bound the resulting output jump below by a sigmoid difference.
title: Argmax-Gap Threshold Law for Key Noise

description:
Generalise budget_neutral_split_better from a single reallocation step to the full optimisation over all allocations with a fixed total width, for a key term obeying the squaring law and a value term obeying the doubling law. The objective is a sum of a doubly exponential and a geometric term, so the optimum should be a corner allocation rather than a balanced one.

For fixed bK + bV = 2B and any positive constants, the minimiser of keyDist c bK + valDist R bV is attained at the largest feasible bK, i.e. the allocation is always maximally asymmetric until the value term saturates.

Formalise the discrete optimisation over the finite ladder of allocations in Lean and prove the corner solution by a monotone exchange argument.

The serving default generalises: always spend bits on keys first, down to the value floor.

There is an interior optimum, and a genuinely mixed schedule beats both q8/q4 and q6/q6 at some budget.
proof_strategy: Exchange argument: show that any allocation with bK < bV strictly improves under a one-bit shift using bit_shift_to_keys_improves, then conclude by finite descent.
title: Optimal Bit Ladder for Mixed-Precision Caches

description:
Linear pricing for fixed comparison hints, geometric pricing for adaptive ones, r^k for r-ary oracles, and multiplicative pricing for coprime residues are all instances of one counting bound. The conjecture makes the equality case a characterisation of the channels in which adaptivity buys nothing at all.

For a hint channel given by a family Q of question maps into a finite alphabet A, the number of candidates separable by k queries is at most |A|^k, with equality attainable non-adaptively if and only if Q contains k questions whose joint answer map is injective on the window; in that case adaptivity yields no improvement for any k.

Generalise card_image_transcriptG_le to an arbitrary question family, prove the two directions of the equivalence, and test on the comparison channel (fails, premium 2^k/(k+1)), the bit-test channel (holds, premium 1) and the residue channel (holds).

A single conservation law replaces the ad hoc hint taxonomy, and adaptivity premia become computable from channel structure alone.

Adaptivity can outperform every non-adaptive selection even in channels with injective joint answer maps, implying genuine conditioning gains beyond counting.
proof_strategy: Forward direction by transcript counting; converse by simulating any adaptive strategy with the injective non-adaptive battery and post-processing the answer vector.
title: Transcript Conservation and the Worthlessness of Adaptivity

description:
Depth measures how far an observer looks, multiplicity how wide. The conjecture asserts these coordinates never interact: parametric witness families exist for every prescribed depth and degree defect, and the invariant lattice they generate has exactly two limit points.

For all k and d there are pointed models that are depth-k equivalent and bisimilar yet whose root out-degrees differ by exactly d; and the lattice of invariants generated by the depth-k and degree-j observations has exactly the two limit points BisimInv and IsoInv.

Generalize multR to a family with d duplicated successors, prove bisimilarity by the same class-kernel argument, and compute out-degrees by decide; then prove the lattice statement from the separation witnesses.

The observational lattice is a product of two independent chains, so any observational language is classified by a pair of numbers.

Depth-bounded counting is strictly more expressive than the two coordinates separately, revealing a genuinely two-dimensional observational logic.
proof_strategy: Duplicate the successor of the multiplicity witness d times, reuse isBisim_multCls with an extended class map, and combine with Hierarchy.multiplicity_gap_beyond_every_depth for the depth coordinate.
title: Orthogonality of Depth and Multiplicity Observations

description:
The exact two-primary law Ipair(2^k) = (4/3)(1 - 4^{-k}) proved in this cycle is conjectured to be the q = 2 case of a uniform geometric law Ipair(q^k) = Ipair(q)(1 - q^{-2k})/(1 - q^{-2}) for every prime q. The approach is to close the class-wise fibre sandwich for odd q by showing the product residue covers exactly one coset of q^{v+1} Z on each type class. This would upgrade the current one-sided envelope into an equality and make the whole channel explicitly computable from its prime values.

For every prime q and every k >= 1, Ipair (q^k) = Ipair q * (1 - q^{-2k}) / (1 - q^{-2}).

Formalise the counting lemma card {s < q^k : s = r mod q^{v+1}} generalised to unions of q-1 progressions, then reuse Ipair_ge_Wsum and Wsum_prime_pow_closed exactly as in Catalog/Tropical/OneBitCapTwoPower.lean. Numerically pre-check for q in {3,5,7}, k <= 4 against brute force.

Ipair becomes a completely explicit multiplicative invariant, immediately giving the Euler product of Direction 3 and the sharp odd threshold of Direction 2.

The fibre sandwich is genuinely lossy for odd q, and the true odd law must involve a second-order correction depending on the residue structure of the units modulo q^k.
proof_strategy: Fix a type class A x B of box (q^k) with v = min(v_q(a), v_q(b)). Show prodRes maps the class onto the full coset r + q^{v+1} Z inside range (q^k), of size q^{k-v-1}(q-1) or q^{k-v-1}; combine uEnt_le_logb_card_of_mapsTo with uEnt_class_ge to force equality, then integrate with the existing recursion Wsum_succ.
title: Geometric Self-Similarity of Primary Type-Pair Towers

description:
Mixture weights are binning-dependent, which is why two pipelines report 8.6 percent and 48 percent edge mass for the same profile. The total log-convexity defect, suitably normalised, should converge to a functional of the underlying profile and therefore agree across pipelines.

For flat-plus-spike profiles the limit of k times the sum of the k-bin second log-differences exists as k tends to infinity, depends only on the profile (not on the grid), and vanishes exactly on single-law profiles.

Compute the normalised defect for the truncated exponential and for the mixture at k = 3, 6, 12, 28 in Lean using exact rational or Float arithmetic, then prove convergence via a Riemann-sum estimate for the second derivative of log density.

Provides a pipeline-independent scalar for reporting edge kernels, removing the mass-fraction ambiguity flagged in the audit.

Edge-kernel strength is intrinsically grid-relative and any cross-paper comparison must fix the grid first.
proof_strategy: Second log-differences of a smooth log density approximate (log f)'' times the squared bin width; the mixture's log density has a curvature spike near the edge whose integral is grid independent. Formalise as a limit of Riemann sums with a uniform remainder bound.
title: Binning-Invariant Spike Functional

description:
The proved bounds give log a(n) ≍ √n with constants 0.34 and 30. The data and a saddle-point computation both predict the exact asymptotic log a(n) ~ π√(2n/3), the same constant as for the unrestricted partition function. Establishing it would identify the universality class of the model exactly.

log a(n) / √n → π √(2/3) as n → ∞, where a(n) is the number of stack polyominoes of area n with square core.

Strengthen the two-regime estimate of Σ_{i=1}^b -log(1-x^i) in StackSquareCoreSharp.lean to the integral bound π²/(6t) at x = e^{-t}, then optimize t = π/√(6n); for the lower bound, restrict the layer sum to k ≈ 0.5404√n and bound below by a single Euler-product term.

a(n) is asymptotically as large as p(n) on the exponential scale, so the square-core constraint costs only a subexponential factor.

The core constraint changes the free energy, and the constant would identify a new universality class for shape-constrained interfaces.
proof_strategy: Rankin bound (already formalized) plus a sharp comparison of Σ_i -log(1-e^{-it}) with (1/t)∫_0^∞ -log(1-e^{-s})ds = π²/(6t); matching lower bound from the single layer k = ⌊0.5404√n⌋ using the two-pow lower bound machinery.
title: Hardy–Ramanujan Constant for Square-Core Stacks

description:
The 2x2 independence model is proved here to be Fisher-flat, and the tied two-group model - which is the same model with the tie t ↦ t² breaking the product structure - is proved to be curved. The conjecture is that this is an equivalence: among finite-support two-parameter models with diagonal Fisher metric, vanishing curvature characterises local statistical independence. It would give curvature the status of an exact obstruction to factorisation.

Let a finite-support two-parameter model have Fisher metric diag(a(u,v), b(u,v)) with a, b > 0 and smooth. Then the Gauss curvature vanishes identically if and only if there is a local reparametrisation in which the model is a product of two one-parameter models.

Formalise the two-dimensional diagonal-metric curvature formula, prove K = 0 forces the mixed second derivatives of log a and log b to vanish, and integrate. The forward direction is already available as IndependenceModel.indepCurvature_eq_zero; the converse is a Frobenius integrability argument.

Gauss curvature becomes a computable certificate of statistical dependence, testable from the metric alone without touching the joint distribution.

There is a flat but genuinely non-product finite-support model, which would be a new source of exotic dually flat structures.
proof_strategy: Write K for a diagonal metric explicitly; set it to zero; obtain a linear PDE system in log a and log b; apply Frobenius to construct the separating coordinates.
title: Flatness-Independence Equivalence for Diagonal Fisher Metrics

description:
A non-constant monotone dish invariant under a transitive group of ingredient permutations should be evasive, so that symmetric recipes force a full cook before any verdict. The approach adds a group-action layer to the pantry and applies a fixed-point/Euler-characteristic argument. This turns the intuition 'in a symmetric stew you must check everything' into a theorem.

If f is monotone, non-constant and invariant under a transitive subgroup of the symmetric group acting on the n ingredients, then tasteCost f = n.

Formalise monotone dishes and group invariance over Pantry n, verify the claim exhaustively for n ≤ 4 by the brute-force solver, then formalise the Rivest–Vuillemin argument for prime-power n.

A large, natural family of recipes is provably break-even (C = V), strengthening the inversion result of this cycle.

Some symmetric monotone recipe admits a shortcut, which would be a genuinely surprising culinary and combinatorial object.
proof_strategy: Simplicial-complex model of monotone dishes plus a group-action Euler characteristic computation; the existing pivotalSet machinery supplies the lower-bound interface.
title: Evasiveness of Symmetric Monotone Dishes

description:
Every curvature computation in this cycle is a fixed finite sequence of rational operations applied to polynomial probability coordinates, so the degree of the resulting curvature is determined by the input degree. The conjecture makes that explicit and deduces a degree bound for the sign-change locus. It matters because it converts 'does this model change curvature sign?' into a finite algebraic question with an a priori bound.

If a finite-support two-parameter model has probability coordinates that are polynomials of total degree at most d, then the Gauss curvature is a rational function whose numerator has total degree at most P(d) for an explicit polynomial P, and the locus {K = 0} is an algebraic curve of degree at most P(d).

Track degrees symbolically through fisher, dg, the inverse metric, chr, dchr and riemann for symbolic d; verify the resulting P against the tied model (d = 3) and the independence model (d = 2); then formalise the propagation lemmas in Lean.

Sign changes of Fisher curvature can be decided by a bounded-degree real quantifier elimination, making 'is this model somewhere negatively curved?' effectively decidable.

Curvature degree can blow up beyond the naive count, indicating unexpected cancellation or growth in the Christoffel symbols worth isolating.
proof_strategy: Induct over the fixed operation sequence, bounding numerator and denominator degrees at each step, with the determinant of the metric as the only denominator; then apply Bezout to the numerator.
title: Degree Propagation Bound for Curvature of Algebraic Statistical Surfaces

description:
The proved capacity bound k <= (1-c)/(rho^2-c) comes from comparing the squared length of the sum of the dials with its projection on the rate. Conjecture that equality characterises a regular-simplex configuration around the rate direction, and determine exactly for which (k, rho, c) such a configuration exists. This says whether a four-dial ensemble at the band floor is constructible or merely not excluded.

Equality in k <= (1-c)/(rho^2-c) holds iff all pairwise inner products equal c, all inner products with the rate equal rho, and the sum of the dials is parallel to the rate; such a family exists in R^k iff c = (k rho^2 - 1)/(k - 1) and c >= -1/(k-1).

Formalise the equality case of the Cauchy-Schwarz step and construct the candidate simplex family as an explicit Gram matrix, checking positive semidefiniteness.

Ensembling strategies have an exactly known optimum and the four-dial bound at the floor is achieved.

The capacity bound is not tight and a strictly better packing bound exists for weak dial families.
proof_strategy: Track the equality conditions through the Gram expansion, then diagonalise the candidate Gram matrix (a rank-one perturbation of the identity) to decide semidefiniteness.
title: Extremal Configurations for the Dial Capacity Bound

description:
Everything is proved for groupoids.  Transporting across
   the fundamental-groupoid functor to genuine aspherical spaces requires the equivalence
   between homotopy classes of maps of aspherical spaces and of their fundamental
   groupoids, which is not in Mathlib and remains the main missing ingredient for a
   statement such as "degree classifies self-maps of the topological circle".
title: Topological realisation

description:
The inverse theorem realizes any prescribed interval histogram at a single lag. The next question is joint control at two lags. We conjecture free joint realizability for coprime lags and a tropical obstruction otherwise.

For coprime k, l >= 1 and admissible histograms N_k, N_l of equal mass there is a decimal melody realizing both simultaneously; for l = 2k the support of N_l is forced into [0, 2 max supp N_k].

Extend the interleave construction to a Chinese-remainder indexing of positions and prove the counting lemma for the product window; derive the obstruction from maxInterval_add_le.

No pair of lag statistics can certify structure in a digit expansion, closing the methodological question raised by lag-12 claims.

There is a genuine multi-lag invariant of digit melodies, which would be the first real statistic in this family.
proof_strategy: Use CRT to split positions into independent threads for coprime lags; for dependent lags use the tropical triangle inequality on the lag monoid to bound the joint support.
title: Joint Realizability at Coprime Lags

description:
For the unrestricted class the version space after any finite sample has cardinality continuum; for the period-T class T samples identify the hypothesis and T-1 do not. The conjecture interpolates: for a class closed under a shift structure with T orbits, T samples collapse the version space to a point and T-1 never do.

If H is closed under a finitely generated shift monoid acting on the positive integers with exactly T orbits, then the version space of any target after sampling one point per orbit is a singleton, and there is a sample of size T-1 leaving at least two hypotheses.

Formalise for cyclic groups first (already done for periodicity), then for products of shifts; falsify by exhibiting a shift-closed class needing more than T samples.

Sample complexity for structured Boolean classes is a purely orbit-counting quantity, computable from the symmetry rather than from VC arguments.

Orbit count is not the right invariant, and the correct one would be a new combinatorial parameter for exact identification.
proof_strategy: Generalise periodic_ext by strong induction along the orbit order; construct the (T-1)-sample counterexample by flipping one orbit representative.
title: Orbit-Count Threshold for Version-Space Collapse

description:
Differentiating the monomial x^{-n} lowers the rank by one and multiplies by -n, so termwise differentiation of a geometrically bounded series should again be geometrically bounded after an arbitrarily small inflation of the rate. The conjecture is that the germ interpretation is a differential ring map. This would make the fragment a differential subring of germs, the standard setting for Hardy fields.

For every GeoSeries c and every r greater than c.ratio there is a GeoSeries c' of rate r with coefficients c'.coeff n = -(n-1) * c.coeff (n-1), and eval c is differentiable on a neighbourhood of infinity with derivative eventually equal to eval c'.

Formalize termwise differentiation of the tsum using Mathlib's theorems on differentiation of uniformly convergent series, and control the extra factor n by GeoSeries.succ_le_const_mul_pow.

The geometric fragment is a differential ring and the germ interpretation is a differential embedding, enabling formalized asymptotic ODE arguments.

Differentiation genuinely escapes the fragment, isolating a new obstruction invisible at the level of coefficients.
proof_strategy: Locally uniform convergence of the differentiated series on x > r, plus the already proved linear-growth absorption lemma.
title: Differential Closure of the Geometric Fragment

description:
Since an exact conditional null characterises mirrors, define a transfer functional as the supremum of residual dependence over conditioning partitions and conjecture that it vanishes exactly on mirrors. This replaces z-scores against row-shuffle nulls with a single well-defined quantity.

For a feature Phi and magnitude M, T(Phi) := sup over partitions refining M of the residual joint-fibre discrepancy is zero if and only if Phi is a deterministic function of M; moreover the supremum is attained at the finest partition.

Formalise partitions as Finset-valued quotients, prove monotonicity of residual discrepancy under refinement, and combine with mirror_iff_conditional_zeroInfo.

Experiments can report one number whose vanishing is a proof of determinism.

There are features with vanishing coarse-partition residual but nonzero fine-partition residual, i.e. genuinely partition-dependent channels.
proof_strategy: Lattice induction over partition refinement plus the counting identity behind zeroInfo_of_conditional_homogeneous.
title: Conditional-Null Completeness of Magnitude Stratification

description:
The threshold 1/27 is the AM-GM maximum of the product of a three-point probability vector, so the concavity boundary coincides with the entropy maximiser. The conjecture is that this is a general phenomenon: on the k-simplex, the functional p -> sigma_k(prod p) is strictly Schur-concave, so its level sets are majorisation classes and the uniform distribution is its unique maximiser.

For p in the k-simplex, sigma_k(prod_i p_i) <= 1/k with equality iff p is uniform, and p majorises q implies sigma_k(prod p) <= sigma_k(prod q).

Formalise the k = 3 Schur-concavity first (a two-variable transfer/Robin Hood step with the third coordinate fixed), then use Finset induction and Mathlib's weighted AM-GM for the general bound.

The concavity guard 1/27 is revealed as an entropy-theoretic quantity, bridging convex analysis and majorisation theory, and gives a monotone growth-rate functional on the simplex.

Schur-concavity fails near the boundary where the product vanishes and sigma is in its convex regime, which would localise the bridge to the interior of the simplex.
proof_strategy: Fix all but two coordinates; the product is then a concave quadratic in the transferred pair, and sigma is increasing, so a single Robin Hood transfer increases the value. Combine with the already-proved equality case three_mass_prod_eq_inv27_iff.
title: Schur-Concavity of the Product-Mass Exponent on the Simplex

description:
The measured four-domain table collapses to one affine function of (domain rank + context doublings). The conjecture is that the depth axis supplies a third rung of the same kind, so the budget is affine in a three-term sum. The approach is to adjoin a second exchange law to the rigidity theorem already proved and test it at one new cell.

There is a constant step s and a rung function on layer counts such that budget(domain, doublings, layers) = 12 + s*(rank(domain) + doublings + layerRung(layers)) for every measured cell.

Prove the three-variable form of Catalog.NET71.diagonal_rigidity from two exchange laws plus one constant increment, then measure the German cell at half depth and ctx 512 and compare with the predicted value.

Cache sizing for any (domain, context, depth) configuration reduces to reading one integer, and deployment tables become one-dimensional in all three knobs.

The exchange law is axis-specific, so the domain/scale collapse is a coincidence of two axes and the table must be stored, not computed.
proof_strategy: Iterate the induction of diagonal_rigidity: fix one axis, obtain affinity along the other by the constant-increment hypothesis, then transport along each exchange law; independence of the axioms is inherited from exchange_without_affine and increment_without_exchange.
title: Three-Axis Rank-Sum Collapse for Attention Budgets

description:
Relation rate and resolution depth independently cap the dial, so the admissible region for a measured value is the intersection of the rate parabola and the blindness ladder. The conjecture is that this intersection is nonempty exactly for measured ρ below an explicit piecewise-algebraic envelope, and that the recorded point (p, ρ) = (1/8, 0.7195) lies inside it only for responses with at least three distinct output levels.

Any response at relation rate 1/8 achieving ρ ≥ 0.7192 at exact bitlen 48 must take at least three distinct values and must separate the 2-adic classes v₂ ≤ 2.

Combine relation_response_not_binary (rules out two levels) with resolution_threshold_at_bitlen48 (rules out depth ≥ 3 blindness) into a single Lean statement about the number of level sets.

The measurement itself certifies a lower bound on the arity of any explanatory statistic.

Some two-level or bulk-blind response evades both caps, meaning one of the two ceilings is not tight enough to combine.
proof_strategy: Show a response with two level sets is the binary case, apply the rate parabola; show a response blind on the bottom bulk is dominated by bottomMergedProfile via ssR_coarse_le; conclude by contradiction with the recorded value.
title: Rate-Resolution Trade-off Surface

description:
For every position t >= 2 the set of odd legs carrying a same-odd-leg pair of nodes that agree below t and split at t is now proved infinite, via a quadratic family. The conjecture upgrades infinitude to positive density: the number of such odd legs below X is at least c_t * X / log X, and among same-odd-leg pairs the splitting fraction tends to a positive constant. It matters because it separates 'sealed by a sparse conspiracy' from 'sealed generically'.

For every t >= 2 there is c_t > 0 such that the number of odd N <= X admitting two valid Price nodes of odd leg N that agree at all positions below t and split at t is at least c_t * X / log X for all large X.

Count sealed odd legs below X for X up to 10^7 by factoring each odd N into coprime pairs and reading v2 of (b-a)/2, and fit the growth; then formalize a lower bound by restricting to N with a prescribed divisor of controlled 2-adic type.

Sealing is a generic property of odd legs, so no probabilistic classifier reading N can guess position t with advantage bounded away from zero.

Sealed odd legs are sparse, and a classifier correct on almost all N may exist despite the proved infinitude of counterexamples.
proof_strategy: Parametrize same-odd-leg nodes by coprime factorisations N = a*b, express the position-t letter via the valuation of (b-a)/2, and produce for each residue class a positive proportion of N with two factorisations of the required valuations using a sieve on N = (2^(t+1) k + 1) * odd.
title: Positive Density of Sealed Odd Legs

description:
Generalises the 1 mod 4 law for Pythagorean hypotenuses to arbitrary integral ternary forms of signature (2,1): the primes dividing a linear functional on a primitive orbit are confined to the classes where the restricted binary form is isotropic. This explains, structurally, why a tree dive under-samples factor-revealing residues. It converts an experimental null into an unconditional obstruction.

For an integral ternary quadratic form Q of signature (2,1), a primitive Q-orbit O and a linear functional l whose kernel carries a definite binary form of discriminant D, every prime p dividing l(v) for some v in O satisfies (D | p) = 1; in particular such primes have density at most 1/2.

Formalise the binary case Q|ker l = a x^2 + b y^2 and derive p ∣ l(v) ⟹ (-ab/p) = 1 using ZMod legendre symbols; instantiate at Q = x^2+y^2-z^2, l = z to recover prime_dvd_hyp_mod_four.

Every hyperbolic-tree factoring proposal inherits a provable blind spot of density at least 1/2, closing barrier 2 unconditionally.

Some functional has unrestricted divisor primes, giving the first candidate for a non-null tree dive.
proof_strategy: Reduce mod p, use primitivity to produce a nonzero isotropic vector in ker l over F_p, contradict anisotropy of the restricted form.
title: Anisotropy Obstruction for Orbit Divisor Primes

description:
The class bit has been proved equal to divisibility by a chosen Gaussian prime above p. The remaining step is to identify that choice with a Frobenius/Artin symbol, turning the elementary counting theorem into a hand-computed instance of class field theory over Q(i).

The class map of the counting theorem is the restriction of the Artin map Cl(Z[i]/N) -> Gal(Q(i)/Q)^k to elements of norm N.

Prove that conjugating the representation of p flips the bit (immediate from gaussianInt_dvd_exactly_one) and match the involution with complex conjugation; compare with Mathlib's GaussianInt prime factorisation.

The counting theorem is a shadow of class field theory, with a purely computational handle on the Artin symbol.

The bit is strictly finer than the Frobenius symbol, which would be surprising and worth isolating.
proof_strategy: gaussianInt_dvd_iff_cross identifies the bit with membership in the prime ideal (e + f i); the two ideals above p are exchanged by conjugation, which is the nontrivial element of Gal(Q(i)/Q).
title: Artin-Symbol Identification of the Representation Bits

description:
Cycle 7 proved that every channel's slope deficit is the same functional of one population: s - slope_s = log2(M_s(16)/M_s(24))/Dk for the shape moments M_s(k) = mean (p_k/2^k)^s. The reported slopes are therefore two samples of a single drift function D(s), at s = 1 (trial division) and s = 1/2 (Pollard rho). A pure rescaling of the shape would make D linear, so the shape of D reads off how the sampler's normalised dispersion moves with k.

For the round-41 balanced-semiprime sampler the drift function D(s) = log2(M_s(16)/M_s(24))/8 is strictly convex with a zero in (1/2, 1); equivalently D(s)/s is strictly increasing on (0, 1], so D is not linear and the normalised log-dispersion Var(log u_k) increases with k.

Compute M_s(k) for s on a grid in (0, 2] from the seed-20260920 draws, form D(s), and check convexity and the sign change; formally, prove in Lean that D is linear if and only if the normalised populations are proportional, starting from the proved identity shape_drift_identity.

The trial and rho deficits are explained by a single dispersion drift of the sampler, and the across-k table must report the whole drift curve rather than one slope per channel.

The two deficits cannot come from one population under pointwise power costs, so at least one reported slope is a fitting artefact rather than a measurement.
proof_strategy: Apply the proved identity at each exponent, express D as a difference of cumulant generating functions of log u_k, and use Holder and strict convexity of the cumulant generating function to reduce non-linearity of D to non-proportionality of the two normalised populations.
title: Drift Spectrum of the Shape Moments

description:
Existence of a determinant-maximizing inscribed ellipsoid is now formalized for arbitrary closed bounded sets. The conjecture is that for convex bodies the maximizer is unique, which would complete John's theorem on the existence-and-uniqueness level. The route is strict concavity of log det combined with convexity of the constraint set in the matrix variable.

For a convex body K with nonempty interior in R^n, there is exactly one positive definite A maximizing det A subject to E A contained in K.

Formalize that inscribedGens K is convex when K is convex, prove strict concavity of log det on positive definite matrices, and derive uniqueness by contradiction from the midpoint of two maximizers; test numerically by running a determinant maximization from several random starting points for polytopes in dimensions 2 and 3.

Yields the John ellipsoid as a well-defined function of the body, unlocking John position, distance estimates and Banach-Mazur bounds in formalized form.

Non-uniqueness for a convex body would contradict strict concavity of log det and would point to an error in the identification of the constraint set as convex.
proof_strategy: Show that E((A+B)/2) is contained in the convex hull of E A and E B, hence in K; use the strict concavity inequality det((A+B)/2) > sqrt(det A det B) for distinct positive definite A, B (a consequence of the AM-GM inequality applied to the eigenvalues of A^{-1/2} B A^{-1/2}); conclude that two distinct maximizers are impossible.
title: Uniqueness of the John Ellipsoid

description:
The abstract threshold theorem shows that a monotone schedule is optimal as soon as the conditional cost matrix has decreasing differences in (smoothness quantile, member). Conjecture that the five-member factoring portfolio does satisfy this over powersmoothness quantiles, so the optimal paid-probe schedule is an interval rule in one scalar.

For the portfolio (rho, p-1 at cap 256, PM1 at cap 1024, Fermat, trial division) ordered by probe cap, and instances binned by the largest prime power of p-1, the matrix of conditional expected costs has decreasing differences; hence the optimal dial is monotone in the quantile.

Bin the per-N CSVs by powersmoothness quantile, form the conditional cost matrix and check decreasing differences directly; then instantiate exists_monotone_optimal_dial on the resulting rational matrix.

The paid-probe schedule collapses to a threshold search in one number, with each member played on an interval of quantiles.

Some pair of members crosses twice, so the winner is not monotone in powersmoothness and the organising axis of the cell is not order-faithful.
proof_strategy: Check the finitely many inequalities of DecreasingDifferences on the binned matrix, then apply leastArgmin_monotone and dial_fibers_ordConnected.
title: Powersmoothness Single-Crossing Certificate

description:
log(j^2 - N) splits into a fast factor log(j - sqrt N), near-singular at the inner window edge, and a slow factor log(j + sqrt N). Every geometric statement proved in this cycle is carried by the fast factor. A degree-d sieve polynomial with d roots near the window would have d fast factors, and its vertex would be set by their interlacing.

For a polynomial P with real roots r_1 < ... < r_d and a window [a,b] disjoint from the roots, the chord-gap vertex of log|P| on [a,b] lies strictly left of (a+b)/2 whenever all roots lie left of a, and strictly right whenever all roots lie right of b; mixed configurations interpolate.

Generalise strictConcaveOn_logSize to sums of log|x - r_i| and rerun the vertex_lt_midpoint argument with the sum of reciprocals as the derivative.

The hump is a general polynomial-sieve phenomenon with a root-configuration invariant, and a right-of-centre vertex identifies roots to the right of the window.

The j^2 - N case is special and the two-factor split is not the operative structure.
proof_strategy: Additivity of chord gaps over the factor logs, plus the fact that a sum of strictly decreasing convex reciprocals is strictly decreasing and convex; then the same midpoint comparison, applied factorwise.
title: Two-Factor Concavity Decomposition of Polynomial Sieve Windows

description:
The Theta(H) count proved here traces back to the fact that Euclid's parametrisation of Pythagorean triples uses two integer parameters of size sqrt(H). The same template should give Theta(H^{k/2}) for any Diophantine family with a k-parameter homogeneous quadratic parametrisation, in particular Theta(H^2) for primitive Pythagorean quadruples. This turns a counting theorem into a general exponent principle.

For a primitive family parametrised bijectively by k coprime integer parameters via forms of degree 2, the number of members inside the box [1,H]^d is Theta(H^{k/2}); for Pythagorean quadruples k = 4 and the count is Theta(H^2).

Formalize the quadruple parametrisation (a,b,c,d) from four parameters, redo the injection into a parameter box, and instantiate the CoprimePairDensity argument in four variables.

A single reusable counting template covers triples, quadruples and higher Lorentz trees, and the vanishing-density statement generalises to all dimensions.

Coprimality or parity conditions in dimension four are not of product type, so the parameter box is not filled with positive density and the exponent drops.
proof_strategy: Copy the two-step scheme of BerggrenBoxCounting: an injection of the family into a k-dimensional parameter box of side sqrt(H) for the upper bound, and a density lower bound for admissible parameter tuples via a gcd sieve.
title: Dimension-Parameter Exponent Law for Pythagorean Boxes

description:
The footprint dial depends only on N modulo the factor base and is provably blind to primality and to semiprimality; the neighbourhood layer is provably free of the dial. Both proofs run through a CRT prescription plus a shift by a large multiple of the modulus. This direction conjectures a single theorem covering every feature invariant under a congruence subgroup.

If a feature F of the integers satisfies F(N) = F(N') whenever N is congruent to N' modulo a fixed positive integer Q, then for every value of F attained at an argument coprime to Q, and every prescribed finite pattern of prime divisors of the neighbours N plus or minus one, there are arbitrarily large N realising both.

Generalise exists_large_congr_omega from the primorial of the factor base to an arbitrary modulus Q and from two neighbours to a finite family of shifts.

All residue-dial features are simultaneously null for every neighbourhood-type covariate, closing the class-level question in one step.

Some congruence-invariant feature does constrain neighbourhood structure, which would itself be a positive finding.
proof_strategy: Chinese remainder over the coprime pair (Q, product of prescribed large primes), then a shift by a multiple of the joint modulus to push the solution past any bound.
title: Congruence-Invariant Features Are Multiplicatively Blind

description:
Because Ipair is additive over coprime factorisations, n -> 2^{Ipair n} is multiplicative, so its Dirichlet series should factor as an Euler product whose local factors are explicit once the primary law is known. The q = 2 factor is already fully determined by the closed form proved in this cycle. This bridges an information-theoretic invariant with analytic number theory.

D(s) = sum_{n>=1} 2^{Ipair n} n^{-s} equals prod_q ( sum_{k>=0} 2^{Ipair(q^k)} q^{-ks} ) for Re s > 1, with a simple pole at s = 1.

Formalise multiplicativity of n -> 2^{Ipair n} from Ipair_mul_of_coprime, then apply the Mathlib machinery for Euler products of multiplicative arithmetic functions; bound the local factor at q = 2 using Ipair_two_pow_lt_four_thirds.

The distribution of cap-breaking orders becomes accessible to Tauberian methods, giving Direction 4 for free.

The series diverges at s = 1 faster than a simple pole, which would mean the average of 2^{Ipair n} grows and the cap is broken on a set of positive logarithmic weight.
proof_strategy: Show 2^{Ipair n} is multiplicative and uniformly bounded on prime powers (by 2^{4/3} at q = 2 and 2^{39/40} at odd q), so the Euler product converges absolutely for Re s > 1; identify the residue at s = 1 by comparison with zeta.
title: Euler Product for the Exponentiated Type-Pair Channel

description:
The proved chord bound says the Euclidean chord of the square-root embedding is at most half the Fisher–Rao length. The conjecture upgrades chord to arc: twice the Bhattacharyya angle is at most the length. This would identify the Fisher–Rao distance on the simplex with the spherical distance of the square-root embedding, completing the classical picture inside a formal library.

For every C¹ curve of strictly positive probability vectors on [a,b], 2·arccos(∑ᵢ √(p_a i · p_b i)) ≤ fisherRaoLength p v a b.

Formalize by partitioning [a,b], applying sqrt_chord_le_half_fisherRao_length on each piece, converting chords to angles via 2·arcsin(chord/2), and passing to the limit with additivity (fisherRaoLength_add).

The Fisher–Rao geodesic distance formula becomes available formally, and every divergence bounded by the angle inherits a length bound.

Some curve would beat the spherical geodesic, contradicting the isometry of the square-root embedding; a failure would have to come from a defect in the length functional's definition.
proof_strategy: Chord-to-arc comparison on a partition plus a Riemann-sum limit; the angular test function arccos⟨x₀,x_t⟩ is differentiable away from the initial point, which the partition argument avoids.
title: Spherical Geodesic Lower Bound for Fisher–Rao Length

description:
The knee curve is a complete invariant of the attention capture curve (proved in NET73MajorizationDuality). Conjecture that the same information is carried by the Rényi entropy spectrum of the attention mass vector, so that knee dominance between domains is equivalent to domination of all Rényi entropies. This would upgrade the one-sided collision bound to an exact characterisation.

For sorted attention mass vectors p, q with total mass 1, the knee curves satisfy k*_p(tau) <= k*_q(tau) for all tau in (0,1) if and only if H_alpha(p) <= H_alpha(q) for all alpha >= 1.

Formalise Renyi entropies over the MassVector structure and prove both implications; the forward direction follows from Schur concavity, the converse from a majorization-recovery argument on capture curves.

The knee is exactly an entropy functional, giving a closed-form predictor of KV budget from attention statistics.

There exist domains with identical Renyi spectra but different knees, showing the knee sees strictly more than entropy.
proof_strategy: Use kneeDominates_iff_majorizes to reduce to majorization, then apply Schur-concavity of Renyi entropies and the Hardy-Littlewood-Polya characterisation of majorization by doubly stochastic maps.
title: Rényi Spectrum Determination of the Knee Curve

description:
Combines the tie-attenuation ceiling of the dyadic profile with the parity threshold: two decorrelated tied statistics should obey a threshold equal to the geometric mean of their tie ceilings times 1/sqrt(2). This is the first bound in the thread that the recorded 0.605 would come close to.

For decorrelated statistics with tie profiles L1, L2 and shared response, the common reading satisfies rho^2 <= (spearmanSq L1 + spearmanSq L2)/2; for the dyadic dial this gives rho <= sqrt(6/7)*sqrt(2)/2 ≈ 0.655.

Compose the midrank collapse identity sp_eq_ssR with bessel_corr, then evaluate at dyadicBlocks 72 and the binomial profile of the count baseline.

The recorded 0.605 sits within 8% of a proved ceiling, making the dial a near-extremal configuration.

Tie attenuation and Gram attenuation interact non-multiplicatively and a genuinely two-dimensional analysis is required.
proof_strategy: Realise each tied statistic's centred midrank vector as an orthogonal projection of the response ranking; apply Bessel to the two projections and bound each projected norm by its tie ceiling.
title: Tie-Gram Interference Threshold

description:
The optimal constant log(N/(N-1))/d for the outer shell of an equal-volume peeling should depend only on the dimension and the number of shells, not on the body, as long as the peeling is by dilates. For peelings by parallel bodies the constant should strictly increase unless the body is a ball, giving a new rigidity characterisation of the ball.

For a convex body K with 0 in its interior, the dilate peeling has outer gauge-thickness exactly 1-(1-1/N)^{1/d}; among all peelings by parallel bodies the ball uniquely minimises the outer thickness at fixed volume fractions.

Prove the dilate case from Measure.addHaar_smul, then attempt the rigidity case for K + εB using Brunn-Minkowski.

The concentration bound proved here is a statement about homogeneity alone, and the ball is characterised by extremal peeling geometry.

Some non-ball body peels more efficiently, exposing a new extremal problem in convex geometry.
proof_strategy: Homogeneity gives the dilate case verbatim; for rigidity, express the parallel-body volume as a Steiner polynomial and compare its first derivative with the isoperimetric ratio.
title: Gauge-Invariance of the Optimal Peeling Constant for Convex Bodies

description:
Every bound proved this cycle carries one unknown, the intra-modulus correlation rho of the drift-power readout. Conjecture that rho is positive and decays like C/u across the u = 9-14 band if the candidate-side deficit is a real weak scale effect, and is zero within error if the readout is pure randomness. It is estimable from the already recorded per-cluster counts.

The intra-modulus correlation of the band-9 drift-power readout satisfies rho(u) = C/u + o(1/u) with C > 0, and rho = 0 exactly under the randomness null.

Estimate rho as the between-modulus variance component of the persisted per-cluster rates of exp569b, then substitute into var_grandMean and cov_legMean to price the retracted joints.

The cluster ceiling and the population covariance become numbers, and the mechanism note acquires a quantitative handle opposite in sign to the paper-136 sieve advantage.

The clustered bounds collapse to the i.i.d. case and the randomness line is strengthened rather than merely extended.
proof_strategy: Formalise the variance-component decomposition of a clustered sample and prove that the between-cluster mean square is an unbiased estimator of sigma^2(1 + (m-1)rho), giving rho by inversion.
title: Intra-Modulus Correlation Law at the Smoothness Frontier

description:
Cycle 6 proved that the exact s-point capacity of a sweep with tolerance a below and b above is geoSum (a*b) s, so only the product matters. Deployment ratios are rarely integers, so the question is whether the product law survives rational tolerances, where the peeling step acquires a floor.

For rational a, b >= 1 the exact s-point capacity is the integer part of the geometric sum in the single variable a*b, with extremal grid given by the same offset recursion rounded down; in particular capacity is still a function of the product alone.

Restate AsymLocalises over the rationals, redo the peeling induction with Nat.floor, and either prove the floor-geometric formula or exhibit an accumulating-rounding counterexample at a = b = 3/2.

The one-dimensional cost model for sweeps extends to realistic (non-integer) memory-headroom ratios.

Rounding accumulates across sweep points and the capacity depends on a and b separately, making asymmetric designs strictly preferable.
proof_strategy: Track the single floor in the peeling step; bound the accumulated rounding loss by a telescoping estimate, or search small rational cases for a gap.
title: Product Law Beyond Integer Tolerances

description:
The attainable dial depends on a tie profile only through the scalar ratio ssR/((n^3-n)/12), so asking which response shape is hardest to fit becomes an extremal problem for one functional over compositions of n. The geometric family is now solved in closed form, which fixes one axis of the problem; the conjecture is that the extremes are the equal-block and maximally-skewed profiles.

Among all tie profiles of n items with exactly k blocks, ssR is maximised by the profile with k equal blocks and minimised by the maximally skewed profile (one block of size n-k+1 and k-1 singletons); consequently the relation-rate ceiling is smallest for the equal-block profile.

Formalise an exchange argument: moving one unit of mass from a smaller to a larger block changes ssR by an explicit sign-definite amount, computed with ssR_append and ssR_shift_parallel.

The recorded dyadic regime can be located exactly inside the order of all tie spectra, not just the geometric ones.

The dial ceiling is not monotone under mass transfer between blocks, so no single scalar summary of a tie profile controls it.
proof_strategy: Write ssR for a two-block perturbation using the parallel-axis identity, show the difference factors as (mass moved)x(gap between block centres), and iterate to the extremal shapes.
title: Extremal Tie Spectra for the Dial Ceiling

description:
Count parity forces a dispersion floor on the seedwise advantage record, and the capacity law forces a threshold on the mutual correlation of a statistic family. Both are values of the same constrained quadratic optimisation, read once on the seed index and once on the statistic index. The conjecture is that the two numbers coincide at the recorded cell.

For a count-parity record of r seeds with l below the bar, the minimal pooled advantage energy r*mu^2 + r*l/(r-l)*(mu-tau)^2 equals the maximal energy compatible with a family of size K(rho, gamma) at mutual correlation exactly dialThreshold rho (K+1).

Evaluate both sides at the recorded cell (r=6, l=3, mu=0.059, tau=0.05, rho=0.641) and, if they agree, formalise the common variational problem in Lean.

The order-statistic layer and the correlation-geometry layer are the same theorem in two indexings, collapsing the thread to a single principle.

The two layers remain genuinely independent and the bridge theorem is the strongest available coupling.
proof_strategy: Write both quantities as the value of minimising a quadratic form subject to one linear equality and one one-sided box constraint, and compare the Lagrange conditions.
title: Dispersion-Capacity Duality

description:
Viewing the maximal depth as an entropy budget, its discrete derivative in log-scale is a susceptibility that is almost always 1. We conjecture a fluctuation law: the exceptional scales where the susceptibility jumps have density controlled by the same 1/(B-1)^2 constant.

For every cost in the geometric universality class, maxDepth cost (B*T) - maxDepth cost T is 1 for all T outside a set of density 0 in each scale block, and the exceptional set is exactly the lossy set of Deficit.

Formalise the susceptibility as a function of T, express it through the block decomposition, and bound the exceptional set by the lossy interval.

The depth behaves like a thermodynamic potential with computable fluctuations, connecting the arithmetic of repunits to extensivity of holographic entropy.

The susceptibility fluctuates at positive density, showing that depth is not asymptotically linear in log T even in an averaged sense.
proof_strategy: Use monotonicity (maxDepth_mono_threshold) plus the sandwich to force the increment into {0,1,2}, then identify the increments via the interval endpoints of the block decomposition.
title: Depth Susceptibility and Fluctuation Law

description:
Sequential composition of tests multiplies verdict functions with a twist by the residue map, which is precisely a semidirect-product cocycle. The conjecture is that the verification monoid is isomorphic to the Boolean verdict monoid extended by the opposite transformation monoid, which would explain the commutation of certificates and yield the counting theorems as corollaries.

For every type D there is a monoid isomorphism between (Test D, seq, one) and the semidirect product of (D -> Bool, pointwise and) by the opposite of End D acting by precomposition; under it the nondestructive tests correspond to the first factor and the reversible tests to the preimage of Perm D.

Define the semidirect-product monoid structure on (D -> Bool) x (End D)^op in Lean, construct the map t |-> (verdict t, residue t), prove multiplicativity from seq's definition, and derive card_nondestructive and card_reversible as corollaries.

The taxonomy becomes an algebraic classification: certificates are a submonoid isomorphic to a Boolean lattice, reversible tests are the preimage of the unit group, and non-commutation is a cocycle phenomenon.

The twist fails to satisfy the semidirect-product axioms for some D, which would mean the verdict-residue pairing carries strictly more structure than the state transition suggests.
proof_strategy: Check the cocycle identity verdict (seq t1 t2) = verdict t1 and verdict t2 composed with residue t1 directly from the definition, then assemble a MulEquiv whose inverse sends (f, s) to fun d => (f d, s d); transport the existing counting equivalences through it.
title: Semidirect Product Structure of the Verification Monoid

description:
C3 fails on the odd side, but only barely: the supremum of the odd primary contributions is about 1.0655, and its partial sums over increasing odd primes first exceed 1 at the eighth odd prime q = 23. The conjecture is that this is sharp, so an odd cyclic order can break the one-bit cap only if it has at least eight distinct prime factors. This converts the failed dichotomy into a precise combinatorial threshold.

If n is odd and Ipair n > 1 then omega(n) >= 8; and there exists an odd n with omega(n) = 8 and Ipair n > 1.

Strengthen Ipair_odd_le_omega to a weighted bound sum over p in primeFactors n of G(p), prove G is decreasing, verify the eight smallest odd primes numerically inside Lean with explicit logarithm bounds, and bound the tail sum for q > 23 by a Mertens-type estimate.

The even/odd dichotomy is replaced by a clean quantitative statement: evenness OR at least eight odd primary components.

Either an odd cap breaker with omega <= 7 exists (contradicting the numerics), or the supremum G(q) is not attained in the limit k -> infinity, indicating the primary law is not geometric.
proof_strategy: Use Ipair_eq_sum_prime_powers, bound each summand by G(p) = Ipair(p) p^2/(p^2-1) via the primary law, then bound the sum of the eight smallest G values below 1 and control the tail by sum over q > Q of log2 q / q^2.
title: Eighth-Prime Threshold for Odd Cap Breakers

description:
The present formalization
   proves the chain-complex dimension theorem over any field.  Realizing every
   binary CSS chain complex by a *simplicial complex with its standard incidence
   maps* is a substantially stronger representability claim and should not be
   conflated with merely viewing matrices as abstract differentials.  Determine
   necessary and sufficient representability conditions, or produce a minimal
   counterexample.
title: Separate simplicial, cellular, and graph models

description:
Mathlib currently notes that a canonical embedding of all real numbers into surreals remains to be constructed (`SetTheory/Surreal/Dyadic.lean`). Once an ordered embedding `ι : ℝ → No` is available and its topological embedding property is proved, one should show that each real open set is the inverse image along `ι` of a surreal-open set. A natural candidate for an interval union is
   `⋃ (a,b) with Ioo a b ⊆ U, Ioo (ι a) (ι b)`.
title: Real open-set extension

description:
(Sub-conjecture 3 of the previous cycle, "bridges
   versus finite sides", is now *proved*: see `bridge_dichotomy`.)  The natural next step is
   the size-3 analogue: if a cubic graph has a finite vertex set `S` with
   `(cutEdges G S).ncard = 3` and `S.card > 1`, is `S` contractible without affecting
   Berge–Fulkerson?  In the finite theory this reduction to cyclically 4-edge-connected graphs
   is standard; `cutEdges_finite_and_handshake` supplies the parity bookkeeping, and the only
   genuinely infinite ingredient is that contraction of a finite side preserves local
   finiteness and cubicity.
title: Higher odd cuts with a finite side

description:
Extend the cycle-2 count from
   `A/B` to a general `F ∈ ℚ[X, Y]`: the number of semiprimes `pq ≤ X` with
   `F(pq, p) = 0` should be at most `deg_X F · π(√X)`, provided no fibre
   `F(·, p)` vanishes identically — and the exceptional fibres should
   themselves be at most `deg_Y F` in number.  This would upgrade
   `FactoringLab.algebraic_barrier` from a qualitative to a quantitative
   statement, matching what cycle 2 achieved for the polynomial and rational
   barriers.
title: Counting barrier for algebraic relations

description:
(`predCount`,
   `predCount_le_bayes`, `predCount_asym_le_best_constant`,
   `predCount_sym_singleton_le_constant`,
   `sym_singleton_positive_information_zero_advantage`,
   `predCount_sym_beats_constants_of_card_three`,
   `units_positive_information_zero_advantage`, in
   `Catalog/Tropical/SmoothSelfHintPredictionAdvantage.lean`): scoring a
   residue-reading predictor `f : G → Bool` by the number of ordered pairs it classifies
   correctly, **no** predictor beats the better constant predictor for the asymmetric
   event (any target, any group), and — the new phenomenon — none beats the constant
   predictor for the *symmetric* event with the arithmetic target `A = {1}` as soon as
   `4 ≤ |G|`, even though the mutual information there is strictly positive.  The
   hypothesis is sharp: in a group of order `3` the Bayes predictor scores `6` against
   `5` and `4` for the two constants.  Arithmetically (`l ≥ 5` prime): the symmetric
   divisibility event leaks bits about `N mod l` that no algorithm can convert into a
   better-than-trivial guess.  So the visible half of the dichotomy is visible only in
   the information-theoretic sense — operationally the whole dichotomy is invisible.
title: Positive information, zero prediction advantage

description:
Φ₂₃₁ is flat while Φ₁₀₅ has height two. The conjecture is that flatness of Φ_{pqr} is governed by an explicit congruence condition on r modulo pq, expressible through the inverse residues that appear in the semigroup description of the binary case.

For odd primes p<q<r, Φ_{pqr} is flat iff r ≡ ±1 (mod p*q) or an explicit linear condition on (q⁻¹ mod p, r⁻¹ mod p) holds.

Enumerate ternary radicals below 10^5, tabulate flat ones, and fit the residue pattern; then formalise the resulting criterion against the verified examples Φ₁₀₅ and Φ₂₃₁.

Flatness of ternary cyclotomic polynomials becomes decidable by a residue computation.

The counterexample sharpens the search for the true criterion and bounds its complexity.
proof_strategy: Lift PMFrameSemigroup.coeff_pmFrame_family_indicator to three generators, express coefficients as differences of numerical-semigroup indicators for ⟨p,q,r⟩, and characterise when consecutive indicator differences never exceed one.
title: Residue Criterion for Flat Ternary Frames

description:
Refinement of a response is not monotone for the attainable dial: a balanced binary response reaches 7/8 while the fully refining dyadic response is capped near 6/7. The conjecture identifies the exact algebraic locus in the (rate, depth) plane where coarsening starts to help, turning an isolated inequality into a curve.

The set of (p,t) with (7/2)p(1−p) > (7/2)(2^t−1)2^t·8^{-t} + 8^{-t} is exactly the region bounded by an explicit conic, and it contains (1/2, 3) but not (1/8, 2).

Compare the two closed forms dyadic_binary_ceiling and bottom_merged_ceiling_gen symbolically in Lean and decide membership for the dyadic grid p = 2^{-s}, t ≤ 6.

Coarser statistics are provably preferable in a computable region, giving a design rule for dial construction.

The inversion at p = 1/2 is an isolated artefact of the balanced case and refinement is essentially monotone elsewhere.
proof_strategy: Clear denominators in both closed forms, reduce to a polynomial inequality in 2^t and p, and discharge with nlinarith plus the two-power bounds already in the catalog.
title: Coarsening Inversion Locus

description:
Every monotone convex budget law equals the max-plus polynomial of its own tangents, so its phase transitions are exactly the corners of a tropical curve. The conjecture is that the number of corners counts attention regimes, giving a geometric invariant of a model's context behaviour.

A knee law with r phase transitions is a max-plus polynomial with exactly r+1 non-redundant monomials, and r is bounded by the number of distinct attention regimes of the model; for the 0.5B model r = 1 up to ctx = 4096.

Measure ctx = 8192 and 16384 for the 0.5B model; fit the tangent envelope and count non-redundant monomials, comparing with kneeRamp_two_monomials which proves the current count is 2.

Budget tables acquire a geometric normal form: a small list of slopes and corners, one per attention regime, replacing per-context tables.

Convexity fails at some octave (increments decrease), which would refute the convex-fit family used for all current lower bounds and force a non-convex model.
proof_strategy: Discrete Legendre biconjugation (proved) reduces the count to redundancy of tangents; redundancy is decidable octave by octave, so the count is a finite check against the measured chain.
title: Tropical Corner Count for Multi-Regime Attention

description:
The cost law uses only the mean accepted-run length, but realized throughput is a ratio of random variables. Using the tail-sum bridge, both the mean and the variance of the run length are determined by the survival curve. Conjecture: the flatness of measured throughput near the argmax is explained by a second-order term proportional to the run-length variance, and this term can shift the argmax by at most one when the survival curve is antitone.

With X the accepted-run length at depth d (tail probabilities s), E[X] = Σ_{i<d} s_i and Var(X) = Σ_{i<d} (2i+1) s_i - (Σ_{i<d} s_i)², and the variance-corrected objective E[X]/(1+cd) - κ Var(X)/(1+cd)² has an argmax within distance 1 of the mean-only argmax for small κ.

Derive the variance tail-sum identity by the same Abel summation used in accept_eq_tailsum, then bound the perturbation with argmax_stable.

Latency-tail-aware serving gets a closed-form depth rule from the same survival measurement.

Variance effects can move the optimum arbitrarily far, so mean-throughput tuning is unsafe under tail-latency SLOs.
proof_strategy: Abel summation gives E[X²] = Σ (2i+1) s_i; then treat the variance term as a bounded perturbation of the gain and apply the existing stability theorem.
title: Second-Order Cost Law from Run-Length Variance

description:
SET-class actions compose multiplicatively on measures while COST-class actions compose additively on queries, which are exactly the two operations of the min-plus semiring underlying the whole barrier thread. The conjecture is that a single graded cost algebra has the T1 law as its degree-zero part and the T2 curve as its degree-k part, so that T2 is generated by iterated T1 rather than being an independent stratum.

There is a graded cost algebra whose SET grade composes multiplicatively and whose COST grade composes additively, with the T1 law as degree 0 and the T2 curve W/2^(k+1) + k as degree k, and on which speedup is a homomorphism; the degree-k identity itself is already proved (halvingCost_eq_netCost).

Extend the proved halving identity to mixed pipelines that interleave certified fixed-window stages and residue filters, and check that the residue cap and the bits cap are the extrema of the two grades.

T1 and T2 collapse into one algebraic object and the barrier map has a single generating law.

Adaptivity contributes structure not expressible by composing fixed-window oracles, and the two strata must stay separate.
proof_strategy: Induct on the number of halving stages using costCert_half_block_const (each certified half-window stage costs exactly 1/2 regardless of P) plus the additive query charge from marginal_net_identity.
title: Min-Plus Cost Algebra Unifying SET and COST Actions

description:
The unique nontrivial square position of a semiprime sieve is the terminal Fermat position 2(b+j0) = p+q, and it satisfies 2*b*j0 <= d^2 with d the half-difference of the factors. This makes the position of the square value an exact read-out of factor imbalance and suggests an early-abort criterion for Fermat-type search.

If d <= N^(1/4) then the terminal position is the first position at which the square part of v(j) exceeds v(j)/b, so scanning square parts detects the terminal position before reaching it.

Sieve balanced and mildly unbalanced semiprimes, record the largest square divisor of each v(j), and check whether the terminal position is the first to satisfy the criterion.

A cheap early-abort test for Fermat/QS style searches on unbalanced moduli, with a proved positional bound behind it.

Square parts of sieve values are noisier than the terminal bound suggests, quantifying how much of the square-part signal is background.
proof_strategy: Combine square_position_unique and terminal_position_bound with a bound on the expected square part of a random value of the same size.
title: Terminal Position Read-Out for Unbalanced Semiprimes

description:
The proved converse to slope identifiability shows two exponents differing by 2*sigma/Dk admit admissible populations with identical two-point slopes. It applies only to two-level designs; with m levels inside the same span an adversary must satisfy more constraints with the same window slack.
