Quantifying the gain turns experiment design into an optimisation problem.

For a least-squares slope fit over m equally spaced levels in a window of spread 2^sigma, exponents alpha1 < alpha2 are indistinguishable iff alpha2 - alpha1 <= c_m * sigma/Dk with c_m decreasing to 0; no finite m removes within-k confounding (Dk < 1), but m = 5 at Dk = 8 separates 0.84 from 1.

Generalise slope_band_attained to m endpoint-saturating levels, compute the least-squares slope of the adversarial curve in closed form, and extract c_m.

Round-42 can be designed to a stated resolution by choosing m and Dk, instead of reporting confounded within-k fits.

Extra levels inside a fixed span buy nothing, and only widening the bit range can resolve exponents.
proof_strategy: Write the least-squares functional on the log-log data, note the adversary maximises a linear functional over the window box, and evaluate that linear program at its vertices.
title: Multi-Level Estimators Past the Two-Point Confounding Threshold

description:
The dyadic dial is the p = 2 case of a p-adic family whose ceiling tends to 3p/(p^2+p+1). The count baseline generalises to the p-ary multinomial row. The inversion threshold b >= 3 proved for p = 2 should become a threshold B(p) growing like log p.

For every prime p there is B(p) = Theta(log p) such that the p-ary count profile has strictly larger tie ceiling than padicBlocks p b exactly when b >= B(p), and B(2) = 3.

Prove a multinomial analogue of the Franel bound and rerun the cube-sum comparison; check small p and b by exact rational evaluation.

The dial's tie disadvantage against counting baselines is a universal arithmetic phenomenon, not a binary accident.

Some prime inverts the ordering, isolating p = 2 as structurally special.
proof_strategy: Cube sums: geometric sum (p^{3b}-1)/(p^3-1) against sum of cubes of multinomial coefficients, bounded by max times square-sum with a p-ary central-multinomial estimate.
title: p-Adic Inversion Threshold Function

description:
The proved inequality r² ≤ η² quantifies how much a dial loses by being fitted affinely. The conjecture is that the deficit η² − r² is bounded below by a universal constant fraction for monotone-but-convex dials such as the product-form Legendre count, so all previously published R² legs understate dial strength by a predictable factor.

For the product-form dial at bitlen 96, η² ≥ 1.5·r², and this ratio is stable across prime cuts.

Recompute the recorded dials cellwise (level sets) and compare with their linear fits, using disp_reduction_eq_eta_sq to express both legs in the same units.

All prior R²-based dial verdicts should be re-read cellwise; some may cross their bars.

The dial is effectively linear in the log-rate, and the R² leg is a faithful summary — simplifying the whole comparison line.
proof_strategy: corr_sq_le_eta_sq gives the inequality; the quantitative factor should follow from a convexity/Jensen estimate on the conditional-mean curve.
title: Linear-Fit Deficit of Recorded Dials

description:
All ceiling bounds in the catalog compare cube sums of tie profiles with equal totals. We conjecture the ceiling is Schur-concave in the profile, so that majorization between profiles orders their ceilings, and the balanced profile is extremal in its weight class. This would replace a family of block-by-block estimates with one order-theoretic principle.

If profiles L and L' have the same total n and L majorizes L', then spearmanSq L <= spearmanSq L'; in particular the ceiling is minimized by the majorization-maximal profile at fixed n.

Since spearmanSq L = 1 - (sum of m^3 - n)/(n^3 - n), the claim reduces to Schur convexity of the power sum of cubes, provable by the Hardy-Littlewood-Polya transfer argument; the single transfer step is already formalized for lists of naturals (spearmanSq_transfer), so what remains is the chain decomposition of a majorization relation.

cubeSum_balanced_le, weight_ceiling_ge and loss_invariant all become corollaries, and any new draw law can be placed in the envelope by a majorization comparison alone.

The ceiling depends on more than the multiset order of the profile, meaning the envelope must be certified law by law and no universal comparison principle exists.
proof_strategy: Use the proved single-transfer inequality (cubeSum_transfer / spearmanSq_transfer) as the base step and iterate it along the majorization chain, then transport the conclusion through the proved antitonicity of the ceiling in the cube sum at fixed total.
title: Schur Convexity of the Spearman Tie Ceiling

description:
Curvature saturates at 1 as soon as the pool has more models than the alphabet has messages, so nontrivial curvature lives only below the capacity threshold |Omega| <= |X|. The conjecture is a matching construction: for every kappa in [0,1] and every pool size below the threshold there is a pool of probability mass functions realising exactly that curvature.

For all n <= |X| and all kappa in [0,1] there exists a pool Omega of n probability mass functions on X with curvature exactly kappa, and no such pool exists when n > |X|.

The impossibility half is the proved theorem curvature_eq_one_of_card_lt and the case n = 2 of the realisation half is the proved theorem exists_pool_curvature_eq; formalise the remaining sizes by an explicit family interpolating between disjointly supported models (kappa = 0) and duplicated models (kappa = 1).

Curvature becomes a complete invariant of pool geometry below the capacity threshold, and low-curvature library design is exactly a coding problem.

Some curvature values are unreachable, revealing a hidden quantisation of the achievable marginal ratios.
proof_strategy: Interpolate between a partition-supported pool and a duplicated pool and show the curvature moves continuously by computing the marginal ratios in closed form.
title: Pigeonhole Curvature-Capacity Threshold

description:
For the trailing-zero statistic, a draw law is summarised by the mass alpha of the odd class and the geometric tail it induces. Conjecture a closed one-parameter ceiling formula in alpha that is strictly decreasing, so that uniform draws (alpha = 1/2) are the worst case and every less odd-heavy law sits above the 6/7 ceiling: the deployment envelope is one-sided.

For the alpha-geometric 2-adic profile, rho^2(alpha) = 1 - alpha^3/(1 - (1-alpha)^3) exactly, this is strictly decreasing on (0,1), and rho^2(1/2) = 6/7.

Generalise dyadicBlocks to alpha-geometric profiles with rational alpha, evaluate the tie correction as a geometric series, and differentiate the closed form.

The bitlen-52 envelope claim extends from a 1 percent total-variation ball to the entire half-space alpha <= 1/2 of draw laws.

Some non-uniform draw law is more tie-attenuated than the uniform one, which would identify a concrete adversarial sampling regime for the dial.
proof_strategy: Geometric-series evaluation of the cube sum, as in the p-adic ceiling law, followed by a monotonicity computation on the resulting rational function of alpha.
title: One-Sided Envelope for Odd-Class Mass

description:
A sweep sees a curve only through the ceiling of its knee in the grid. This direction upgrades that pointwise factorisation to a statement about equivalence relations: the poset of grids under refinement should embed isomorphically into the poset of indistinguishability relations on retention curves.

For grids G subset H, the relation 'same H-reading at every gate' refines 'same G-reading at every gate', strictly whenever H\G contains a realisable knee; the map G -> (~_G) is an order isomorphism onto its image.

Define ~_G in Lean, prove monotonicity and strictness using the step-curve witnesses of grid_reading_underdetermines_knee.

Experiment design becomes a lattice problem with a canonical minimal experiment for each distinguishability requirement.

Distinct grids can be experimentally equivalent, which itself sharpens the design question.
proof_strategy: Factorisation theorem gives the forward inclusion; step curves with knees in H\G give strictness; antisymmetry from realisability of every knee.
title: Grid Refinement Lattice of Distinguishable Sweeps

description:
The cyclic which-factor wall proved this cycle shows that a transitive shift fixing the public data forces exactly zero leakage. For a product of k primes with distinct splitting types the labelling should be a free S_k-torsor on the generic stratum, so the swap-invariant public data leaks nothing and every decoder succeeds with probability 1/k!.

On the stratum where all k splitting types are distinct, I(labelling ; (type multiset, N mod f)) = 0 and every decoder is correct on exactly a 1/k! fraction.

Instantiate mutInfo_eq_zero_of_shift with the generators of a free S_k action on k-tuples of exponents, or generalize its hypotheses from one shift to a finite group acting freely.

A sharp, dimension-free statement about factor-identification leakage for multi-prime RSA moduli.

Some stratum admits partial identification, an exploitable structural leak worth quantifying.
proof_strategy: Replace transitivity of a single permutation pi by transitivity of a group of permutations of the value space; balance of fibres then follows from orbit-stabiliser exactly as in card_fiber_const.
title: Symmetric-Group Which-Factor Walls for k-Almost-Primes

description:
The capacity curve (1 + sqrt(1 + 4k(k-1)beta))/(2k) is now proved to be the exact extremal serving value, attained only by hub families. Conjecture: measured multi-adapter degradation tracks it, and the gap to the curve measures the family's distance from hub geometry.

For a family of k fine-tunes with pairwise agreement beta, the best achievable mean agreement is at most (1 + sqrt(1 + 4k(k-1)beta))/(2k), tends to sqrt(beta) as k grows, and at beta = 0.8327 no family of twelve fine-tunes attains it.

Measure pairwise agreement of a family of adapters, then measure the best shared model's mean agreement as k grows, and compare with meanAgree_le_capacityCurve, capacityCurve_tendsto_sqrt and net54_no_saturating_family_of_twelve.

Serving capacity is a measurable, certified quantity with a design rule for how many fine-tunes to co-locate.

Real families sit far inside the extremal curve, and the gap itself becomes the object of study.
proof_strategy: Upper bound proved from the multiplicity count via the quadratic root; attainment by the hub construction; non-attainment at generic budgets from quantisation.
title: Serving-Capacity Curve in the Wild

description:
Numerically the entanglement profile of an MDS code state is the tent min(|S|, n-|S|, k) log q rather than the classical staircase. Proving the tent formula would make the code state a discrete Ryu-Takayanagi geometry whose minimal surface is the smaller side of the cut.

For an MDS code with 2 ≤ q, entanglementEntropy (codeState C S) = min(|S|, n - |S|, k) * log q for every cut S.

Compute the reduced density matrix in the regime d ≤ |S| ≤ n - 1 and show it is maximally mixed on q^min(|S|,|Sᶜ|) levels; verify small cases with exact rational linear algebra.

MDS code states are exactly the discrete holographic states with a two-sided RT formula, strengthening the tensor-network / quantum-error-correction dictionary.

Some MDS code state has a non-flat spectrum across a middle cut, which would give a new invariant separating MDS codes of equal parameters.
proof_strategy: Apply the proved case to the complementary cut and combine with schmidtRank_codeState_le_pow_compl plus the purity identity of Direction 3.
title: Holographic Tent Profile for MDS Code States

description:
Comparing tie ceilings at fixed mass is comparing cube sums in reverse order, and cube sum is Schur-convex. Inversion should therefore follow from a majorisation statement: the geometric profile majorises the binomial profile once both have at least four blocks.

For every b >= 3 the dyadic profile majorises the binomial profile of the same mass 2^b in the dominance order, and consequently every Schur-convex functional, not just the cube sum, separates the two dials.

Verify dominance by partial sums of sorted profiles for b <= 20 exactly, then prove the general partial-sum inequality by induction on the number of leading blocks.

A single order-theoretic fact replaces all analytic estimates and extends automatically to every Schur-convex tie functional.

Cube sums separate the profiles for a reason special to the exponent three, which itself demands explanation.
proof_strategy: Compare the partial sums 2^{b-1}+...+2^{b-j} with the j largest binomial coefficients using the standard central-binomial tail bound.
title: Majorisation Criterion for Tie Ceilings

description:
The scan-order contest factors through the single functional E[z(r)] of the generator's ratio law. For the one-parameter family of densities proportional to r^{-theta} on the balance band, the mean tilt should be strictly decreasing in theta with a unique crossing of 1/2. This would classify all power-law generators by one number.

For mu_theta with density proportional to r^{-theta} on [1,2], the map theta -> E_{mu_theta}[zOfRatio] is strictly decreasing and crosses 1/2 at a unique theta*, computable in closed form in terms of sqrt(2).

Evaluate the closed-form rpow integrals for E[z] under mu_theta using the same antiderivative technique as tiltAntideriv, then prove strict monotonicity in theta by differentiating under the integral sign.

Any power-law generator can be certified adversarial or favourable to window-ascending by a single scalar comparison.

The mean tilt is non-monotone in the concentration parameter, so the scope boundary is not a threshold phenomenon and per-generator analysis is unavoidable.
proof_strategy: Reuse integral_tilt_combo with exponent -theta-1/2 in place of -5/2; monotonicity from a covariance (Chebyshev association) inequality between the decreasing z and the tilting weight.
title: Tilt Spectrum of Power-Law Ratio Generators

description:
The firing count saturates at m exactly when m is B-powersmooth, and the exact jump formula makes the whole staircase explicit. We conjecture that reaching half the maximum requires only a square-root-sized bound for almost all orders, quantifying the diminishing return of raising B1.

For all but O(x / log x) of the m <= x, the least B with 2 gcd(m,k(B)) >= m satisfies B <= sqrt(max prime power divisor of m).

Compute the half-saturation bound directly from the exponent vector using gcd_stage1_jump for all m up to a few million, and measure the exceptional set.

Stage-1 bounds well below the powersmoothness threshold already capture half the achievable success, a concrete cost-model statement.

Half-saturation is governed by the top prime power itself and there is no cheap partial regime.
proof_strategy: Reduce half-saturation to a knapsack inequality on the exponent vector via the exact jump formula, then use standard estimates for the density of orders with a dominant top prime power.
title: Half-Saturation Threshold of the Smoothness Bound

description:
Our harmonic theorem computes the informed player's value at the uniform prior. We conjecture that the uniform prior is the exact minimiser of that value over all priors on arrangements, so maximal uncertainty is the adversary's optimum. The value functional is a sum of expected posterior maxima and should be Schur-convex.

For every prior P on the u! arrangements, the optimal feedback value V(P) under unit scoring satisfies V(P) >= V(uniform) = H_u, with equality iff P is uniform; and V is Schur-convex in P.

Compute V(P) by dynamic programming over posteriors for u <= 5 on a grid of priors, including all priors supported on two arrangements, and test the majorization order.

The 'no edge from uncertainty' slogan upgrades to a variational principle: uniform shuffling is the unique worst case for any predictor.

Some structured prior is harder to predict than the uniform one, which would identify a new class of adversarial shuffles.
proof_strategy: Write V(P) as a supremum of linear functionals of P (one per deterministic strategy tree), hence convex; then use permutation symmetry plus convexity to conclude Schur-convexity and minimality at the flat point.
title: Schur-Convexity of the Informed Player's Value

description:
*[settled in cycle 4: the abelian half is proved, the identification with the one-parameter subgroup is false — see below]*  The centralizer of a
   non-identity element of `ScalingMap` is abelian, and equals the image of the
   one-parameter subgroup through it precisely when its exponent is not `1`;
   for exponent `1` (pure dilations `y ↦ c y`) it is the full dilation
   subgroup.  *The key insight is* that the infinitesimal statement proved in
   cycle 3 (centralizer of a field is the line it spans) should integrate to the
   group level, the exceptional case being the one where the flow has no fixed
   point in `(0, ∞)`.  *Why now?*  `EMLScalingGroupDuality` already has the
   group law, the trivial-centre theorem and the classification of involutions,
   so the computation is a finite case analysis on `(coeff, expo)`.
title: (NC5 — global centralizer in the group picture.)

description:
A finite
   -dimensional real Lie algebra `L` admits a surjection onto `EMLGen` if and
   only if `L` is not perfect and its derived algebra contains an
   `ad`-eigenvector of nonzero eigenvalue.  *The key insight is* that
   `scaleChar` is the universal map to an abelian algebra (cycle 2) and
   `isNilpotent_of_lie_eq_self` (cycle 3) says the eigenvector is nilpotent in
   every representation, so the obstruction is intrinsic and not
   representation-dependent.  *Why now?*  Both halves are already formalized as
   standalone theorems; only the assembly into an iff remains.
title: (NC6 — the trace obstruction is the only obstruction.)

description:
The both-parents-collapse floor is a computable functional of a layer transplant. Conjecture: for tail swaps it rises with the number of swapped layers and saturates at two layers, while for bulk swaps it stays negative (vacuous) at every width. This separates entanglement depth from perturbation magnitude.

For k-layer swaps at the tail boundary the floor beta - min(agr(H,A), agr(H,B)) is nondecreasing in k and within 10% of its k=2 value already at k=2, whereas for bulk swaps it remains negative for all k below the boundary.

Run one-, two- and three-layer swaps in both directions and evaluate the floor with Catalog.Probability.TailTransplantGeometry.novelFrac_ge_baseline_sub_agree.

The sharing boundary is a sharp two-layer interface, and serving systems can share all but two layers with a certificate.

Entanglement is graded, and the boundary must be chosen per model rather than fixed at two layers.
proof_strategy: Monotonicity of the floor under composition of swaps, via the Hamming triangle inequality applied to the chain of intermediate hybrids.
title: Dose-Response Curve of the Novelty Floor

description:
True ECM replaces the window [1,B] by the divisor-closed set of B-smooth integers, whose density is governed by Dickman's rho. We conjecture that the two arms have equal curve budget exactly when B is of order log^2 p, and that below that threshold the lite arm is exponentially worse.

There are absolute constants c1 < c2 with: for B <= c1 log^2 p the true-ECM budget is smaller than the lite budget by a factor tending to infinity, and for B >= c2 log^2 p the two agree up to constants.

Run the still-deferred lcm-based arm on the same population and fit both budgets; formally, compare the truncated totient count with the count of smooth divisors of the group order.

The deferred ECM arm of paper 154 gets a sharp quantitative statement rather than a measured slope.

Smooth-order density in the Hasse interval behaves unlike the Dickman heuristic at these sizes, itself a notable finding.
proof_strategy: Contrast card_lowOrder_eq_sum_totient with the smooth-divisor count of |E|, then insert Dickman-type density bounds.
title: Crossover Bound Between Lite and lcm-Based ECM

description:
Complementation has fixed points at two levels: flat edges in the alphabet, and the empty assembly at zero variables. The conjecture is that a geometric realisation functor identifies the first with the boundary cells of the assembled figure and forces a congruence between its Euler characteristic and the combined assembly count mod 2.

For a geometric realisation of a framed puzzle with flat frame, the number of boundary cells equals the number of complementation-fixed edges, and the Euler characteristic is congruent mod 2 to the combined assembly count.

Define a realisation from pieces to a CW structure, compute both invariants for small grid puzzles, and formalise the congruence.

Solution-count parity acquires a topological reading as a boundary invariant.

The two fixed-point phenomena are unrelated, and parity is purely a cube symmetry.
proof_strategy: Build the CW realisation, use comp_fixed_iff_flat for the local identification, and compare with the gauge decomposition of the assembly space.
title: Two-Level Fixed-Point Correspondence for Framed Boundaries

description:
Saturation of the weighted dial is exactly the smallness of the tail mass of the squared amplitude profile. Conjecture that for the arithmetic profile the tail decays like 1/B, so that the window needed for a given accuracy is inversely proportional to the tolerance and independent of the population size.

For the arithmetic amplitude profile a_l comparable to 1/l on primes, 1 - weightedR2 over a window of cutoff B is Theta(1/log B), matching the Theta(1/n) law already proved for the index model.

Transfer the proved model bounds (harmonic_weightedR2_ge and harmonic_weightedR2_le) to the prime-indexed profile using Mertens' theorem for the tail of sum 1/l^2 over primes.

Window size is a tolerance parameter, not a scale parameter: B* is universal.

Saturation depends on the population and the B*=400 location is population-specific.
proof_strategy: Telescoping upper bound (already proved) plus an integral comparison lower bound for the tail.
title: Spectral Tail Law for Dial Saturation

description:
The consecutive gap ratio r is invariant under affine rescaling and needs no unfolding, so its mean is a genuine universality constant. Compute the Poisson value 2 log 2 - 1 and the Wigner-surmise value exactly, and show both are strictly below the rigid value 1 attained in the limit by the quadratic spectrum.

The double integral of min(s,t)/max(s,t) against exp(-s-t) over the positive quadrant equals 2 log 2 - 1, and the analogous Wigner-surmise average is strictly larger and strictly less than 1.

Formalize the two-dimensional integrals by symmetry reduction to s < t and a change of variables u = s/t, reusing the Gaussian moment lemmas of SpectralPoissonVsGUE.

An unfolding-free numerical fingerprint separates all three regimes, usable directly on finite experimental spectra.

The r-statistic fails to separate the classes and unfolding is unavoidable after all.
proof_strategy: Reduce to a one-dimensional integral in u = s/t via Fubini and the substitution t -> t, then integrate u/(1+u)^2 type expressions in closed form.
title: Gap-Ratio Universality Constants

description:
Exact bin averaging is an L-infinity contraction, so it cannot create a hump; sample counting is not, so all artefact risk lives in the sampling step. Quantifying the count at which a spurious hump becomes likely separates a harmless convention amendment from a load-bearing one.

No curve with sup f < 1 + delta admits a grid whose exact bin averages exceed 1 + delta; for counted histograms with n cells the least N making a spurious 1 + delta hump probable satisfies N = Theta(n log n / delta^2).

The first half is already proved (hump_certifies_peak); formalise the counting half via the Gumbel ceiling of Direction 3 and check by simulation at delta = 0.02.

Audit ledgers can be split mechanically into binning amendments (harmless) and sampling amendments (load-bearing).

Binning conventions can also inject bias and every convention change must be re-registered.
proof_strategy: L-infinity contraction of the averaging operator for the first half; for the second, invert the Chernoff bound of Direction 3 to solve for N.
title: Contraction Separation between Averaging and Counting

description:
The MDS property alone pins down the number of codewords of each weight. Conjecture the closed formula A_w = C(n,w) Σ_j (-1)^j C(w,j)(q^{w-d+1-j} - 1) for an [n,k,n-k+1] code over a field with q elements. The proof route is inclusion–exclusion over coordinate subsets, using that every k-subset is an information set.

For every [n,k,n-k+1] linear code over F_q and every w ≥ d = n-k+1, the number of codewords of Hamming weight w equals C(n,w) Σ_{j=0}^{w-d} (-1)^j C(w,j) (q^{w-d+1-j} - 1).

Formalize the count of codewords vanishing outside a subset S as q^{max(0, k - (n - #S))} using restrict_bijective_of_mds, then apply Möbius inversion on the subset lattice.

The complete weight distribution of Reed–Solomon codes becomes a corollary, with no field-specific input.

Some MDS code has a weight distribution not determined by its parameters, contradicting the information-set count and revealing an error in the subset-counting step.
proof_strategy: Count codewords supported in a fixed subset via the information-set isomorphism, then invert over the Boolean lattice with Finset inclusion–exclusion.
title: Forced Weight Enumerator of MDS Codes

description:
The power-law recall model and the Zipf attention model are conjectured to be the same object in different coordinates, with the recall exponent determined by the attention decay exponent. Matching the two retention curves on a window would let a KV-cache budget measurement read off the attention decay directly.

If the Zipf retention curve (k/C)^(1-s) and the power-law retention 1 - A k^(-a) agree on an interval of budgets, then the amplification exponents coincide: b/a = 1 and a = 1 - s is forced on that window.

Equate the two retention functions at three budgets and derive the parameter relations with Real.rpow algebra in Lean.

The measured a ~ 0.81 is a spectral measurement of attention decay, not a fitting constant.

The two model classes are genuinely inequivalent and the exponent must be measured per corpus.
proof_strategy: Take logarithms of both curves, differentiate the identity through finite differences at three points, solve the resulting rpow system.
title: Recall-Decay Exponent Identity

description:
All proofs in these cycles use the rank group Z only through its order and the comparison x^r = o(x^s) for r < s. Replacing Z by an arbitrary ordered abelian group embedded in the reals, with Hahn-type supports, should reproduce the entire theory with the lexicographic order replaced by the Hahn order.

For an ordered abelian group Gamma with an order embedding into the reals, and Hahn series over Gamma with reverse well-ordered support and geometrically bounded coefficients, the germ interpretation is injective, order preserving for the Hahn order, multiplicative for the Hahn product, and its expansion fibres are cosets of the flat germs.

Generalize monoZ to monoGamma, restate tail_bound as a sum over an initial segment of the support, and re-run the cycle 1 to 6 proofs against Mathlib's HahnSeries API.

A general bridge between Hahn series algebra and asymptotic analysis, subsuming Puiseux, transseries and Laurent scales in one formalized theorem set.

The embedding of the rank group into the reals is essential, isolating archimedean-ness as the true hypothesis behind the germ interpretation.
proof_strategy: Replace the geometric tail by a sum over a reverse well-ordered support, using that an order embedding into the reals makes every such support order isomorphic to a subset of the naturals below any bound.
title: Rank Scales over Ordered Abelian Groups

description:
The Shannon ceiling is strict for every mixed multiset. We conjecture the deficit is exactly the Gaussian normalisation of the multinomial distribution, growing like ((r-1)/2) log2 n, which is the finite-size thermodynamic signature of key repetition.

n*H(p) - log2(n!/prod m_i!) = ((r-1)/2)*log2 n + O(1) for multiplicity profiles with all m_i = Theta(n), where r is the number of occurring keys.

Combine Stirling bounds for each factorial with the proved strict inequality; verify numerically for r = 2,3 and n up to a few hundred by kernel-checked rational bounds.

Physical sorters of repeated-key streams dissipate kT log 2 * H(p) per item with an explicit logarithmic finite-size correction.

The deficit has a different order, indicating that the empirical distribution is not the correct thermodynamic ensemble for finite multiset streams.
proof_strategy: Apply Stirling with explicit error terms to n! and each m_i!, subtract, and control the remainder using the strictness result already proved.
title: Logarithmic Finite-Size Deficit of the Shannon Ceiling

description:
Extend the binary lattice-point model to ternary orders: the coefficient of X^n in the frame geometry of (p,q,r) counts lattice points of a box on the plane ip+jq+kr=n. The conjecture is that the resulting count deviates from its mean by at most p-1, which is Bang's theorem. This turns a classical polynomial statement into a counting problem already half-formalised in the catalog.

For odd primes p < q < r and all k, |coeff k (cyclotomic (p*q*r) ℤ)| ≤ p - 1.

Formalise the ternary frame geometry as the product of three truncated geometric series, prove a box-uniqueness lemma modulo p, and bound the alternating differences; test numerically on all p*q*r ≤ 10^4 first.

Bang's theorem enters the catalog and globalises to all orders with three odd prime divisors via height reduction.

A concrete counterexample triple would contradict a classical theorem, indicating a modelling error to be localised.
proof_strategy: Generalise PMFrame.repPair_unique from a line in a 2-box to a plane section of a 3-box; control the count by equidistribution of jq+kr modulo p; conclude by telescoping the coefficient recursion.
title: Bang Bound via Plane Lattice Sections

description:
Extend the single-block duality eigensystem to a graded family H^0..H^{2n} in which duality pairs degree i with degree 2n-i. Conjecture that the global zeta functional equation has exponent the Euler characteristic and sign carried entirely by the middle block. This would explain why root numbers of varieties are middle-cohomology invariants.

For a graded duality system, Z(1/(q^n T)) = ± q^{n·chi/2} T^chi Z(T) with chi = sum (-1)^i b_i, and the sign equals (-1)^{m_+ of the middle block}.

Formalise a GradedDualSystem structure (blocks plus pairing between i and 2n-i), prove block-wise telescoping using rootSign_directSum, and derive the global equation.

The root sign of a variety is a middle-cohomology invariant, provable in the eigenvalue model without any geometry.

Off-middle blocks contribute signs, which would identify a new invariant beyond the fixed-point count.
proof_strategy: Pair blocks i and 2n-i into fixed-point-free duality eigensystems; apply the cycle-1 pairing lemma to each pair (no fixed points, hence sign +1) and the cycle-1 sign law to the middle block.
title: Graded Poincaré Duality and the Global Zeta Sign

description:
The French knee is only bounded below (k* > 32). Using the majorization duality, a censored knee constrains the capture curve to a half-space. Conjecture that French is uniformly dominated by German prose in capture, i.e. the ordering is not a late crossing but a global one.

The French capture curve lies pointwise below the German one, so k*(fr, tau) >= k*(de, tau) for every tolerance tau in (0,1), not only at the measured tolerance.

Measure the knee at two further tolerances; formally, verify KneeDominates de fr and derive CaptureMajorizes de fr via kneeDominates_iff_majorizes.

Domain hardness is a total order on these five domains, and one tolerance suffices to rank them.

Capture curves cross, so the domain ranking is tolerance-dependent and no single knee number characterises a domain.
proof_strategy: Instantiate majorizes_of_kneeDominates with the measured pairs and use monotonicity of the capture curve to interpolate between measured tolerances.
title: Censored-Knee Dichotomy for French Prose

description:
The tie-attenuation functional is built from the power sum p_3 of a partition, which is Schur-convex, so the dial should be strictly order-reversing for the dominance order on partitions. This bridges rank-correlation attenuation with symmetric-function theory.

If lambda dominates mu as partitions of n then rho^2(lambda) <= rho^2(mu), with equality iff the partitions have equal third power sum; the refinement order case is already proved.

Prove Schur-convexity of Sum lambda_i^3 and combine with the closed form of spearmanSq_eq; check all partitions of n <= 9 by exact enumeration in Lean.

Tie profiles are totally ordered by a classical combinatorial invariant, giving sharp best and worst case dials for any fixed number of classes.

Dominance is too coarse and the dial requires the full multiset of block sizes.
proof_strategy: Schur convexity via the Muirhead-type transfer (Robin Hood) operation, each step increasing Sum lambda_i^3.
title: Dominance Order Monotonicity of Tie Attenuation

description:
The breakdown threshold of the median was shown to coincide with the unique-decoding radius of the two-point translation code. The conjecture is that this is an instance of a general duality: for any group acting coordinatewise, the equivariant breakdown ceiling is half the minimum Hamming distance of the orbit. This bridges robust statistics and coding theory at the level of definitions, not analogy.

For a group G acting coordinatewise on Q^n and a G-equivariant estimator T, the breakdown number of T at xs is at most ceil(d_G(xs)/2) where d_G(xs) is the minimum Hamming distance from xs to a distinct orbit point.

Instantiate G as the scaling group acting on a positive sample and formalise the resulting ceiling for the MAD; compare against the known MAD breakdown point 1/2 and against a deliberately sparse orbit where the bound should bite earlier.

Breakdown points of all equivariant estimators become computable from an orbit geometry, and dispersion estimators get their first formal ceilings.

The translation case is special, which would isolate exactly which property of translations (full-support displacement) drives the ceiling.
proof_strategy: Generalise the shear: split xs at m = n - k, act by g on one part only, and show the two hybrids are within k of xs whenever 2k >= dist_H(xs, g.xs). Then equivariance forces T on the two hybrids to differ by an unbounded amount as g ranges over the orbit.
title: Minimum-Distance Duality for Group-Equivariant Estimators

description:
The proved limit sup_k Ipair(2^k) = 4/3 identifies four thirds of a bit as the exact two-adic saturation level of the type-pair channel. The conjecture is that Ipair is the tropicalisation of a multiplicative height on the lattice of cyclic quotients, with local weights q^{-2} coming from the fibre geometry of the sum map on a product of type classes, so the maximum over orders with at most m primary parts has an explicit closed form.

sup { Ipair n : omega(n) <= m } = 4/3 + sum over the first m-1 odd primes q of Ipair(q) q^2/(q^2-1), attained only in the limit along towers.

Prove the supremum statement for m = 1 and m = 2 from the primary law of Direction 1 plus CRT additivity, then verify the value numerically for m <= 5 by brute force over highly composite n.

Ipair is a genuine tropical height and its extremal values are computable, giving a canonical ordering of cyclic orders by information content.

The supremum is not additive across primary parts, indicating a hidden interaction term between primary components that CRT additivity does not see.
proof_strategy: Combine Ipair_eq_sum_prime_powers with the monotone convergence Ipair_two_pow_tendsto and its odd analogues; extremality follows because each summand is increasing in its exponent and bounded by its own supremum.
title: Four-Thirds Saturation as a Local Tropical Height

description:
The geometric coupling bound 1 - (1 - d_TV)^n is provably valid but never tight for 0 < d_TV < 1. Replacing total variation by the Hellinger affinity, which is exactly multiplicative over products, should give matching upper and lower amplification laws. This turns n-sample indistinguishability from an inequality into an asymptotically exact rate.

For finite laws p, q with affinity rho = sum_x sqrt(p x * q x), one has 1 - rho^n <= d_TV(p^{otimes n}, q^{otimes n}) <= sqrt(1 - rho^{2n}), and both are strictly sharper than 1 - (1 - d_TV)^n when 0 < d_TV < 1.

Define hellingerAffinity in the TotalVariation namespace, prove multiplicativity by the same Fintype.prod_sum route used for sum_diag_powCoupling, then prove the Le Cam sandwich 1 - rho <= d_TV <= sqrt(1 - rho^2) pointwise and tensorize.

Sample-complexity bounds in the catalog become tight up to constants and the vacuous linear hybrid bound can be retired everywhere.

Some pair violates the lower sandwich, which would identify a new obstruction to multiplicative amplification and force a per-coordinate correction term.
proof_strategy: Cauchy-Schwarz for the upper bound, the elementary inequality min(a,b) >= a*b/max(a,b) for the lower bound, and exact multiplicativity of rho over product laws.
title: Exact Hellinger Amplification Law

description:
The trailing A-run of a Price address equals the 2-adic valuation of the smaller Euclid parameter, so run statistics are valuation statistics. The conjecture pins the limiting distribution of runs over triples ordered by hypotenuse.

The proportion of primitive triples with hypotenuse at most X whose Price address ends in exactly r letters A tends to 2^{-(r+1)} as X tends to infinity.

Count runs for all primitive triples with c <= 10^7 and compare with the geometric law; formalise the finite-range version as an explicit inequality.

Terminal-run statistics of Pythagorean trees become an exactly solvable model, transferable to other valuation-driven trees.

Ordering by hypotenuse biases the valuation, revealing a correlation between the archimedean size and the 2-adic depth.
proof_strategy: Use trailingA_eq_padicValNat to convert the count into a count of pairs (m,n) with v2(n) = r and m^2+n^2 <= X, then a lattice point estimate.
title: Valuation Spectrum of Terminal Runs

description:
After reindexing from the centre, shell thickness is the discrete derivative of j^{1/d} scaled by R N^{-1/d}. Counting shells thicker than a budget therefore becomes counting lattice points under a power curve. The conjecture is an exact closed form for the count, refining the Theta(R/(d delta)) bounds proved in this cycle.

thickCount R d N delta = max{m <= N : R N^{-1/d} (m^{1/d} - (m-1)^{1/d}) > delta}, and for d >= 2 this equals min(N, floor((R/(d delta))^{d/(d-1)} N^{-1/(d-1)}) + O(1)).

The two-sided bounds peeling_thick_decay and peeling_thick_lower already pin the count to two consecutive integers (thickCount_pinned); test the exact value numerically at the boundary j^{d-1} N = (R/(d delta))^d and formalise the tie-break.

The uniform bound 1 + R/(d delta) becomes an exact asymptotic, and the peak location N* = Theta(R/(2 d delta)) is explained.

The discrete derivative must fail to be squeezed by its endpoints, indicating a genuinely arithmetic obstruction at small m.
proof_strategy: Monotone thickness gives a single boundary inequality; apply the mean value theorem to x^{1/d} on [m-1,m] and invert.
title: Lattice-Point Formula for the Thick-Shell Count

description:
The proved sandwich 2bj <= v(j) <= 2bj + j^2 + 2b pins log v(j) to log(2bj) with an explicit error, so the magnitude-only prediction for the hit density at position j is the Dickman value rho(log v(j)/log B) with bounded uncertainty. The conjecture is that the entire observed within-N profile is inside this band.

For balanced semiprimes and j <= b, the empirical hit density at position j lies within sampling error of rho(log(2bj)/log B), with no residual positional term.

Formalise an interval bound for the Dickman function in Lean, combine with sieveVal_sandwich, and compare against the decile data recorded in ComputationalEvidence.md.

The residual overdispersion thread loses its positional carrier candidate and must be sought in per-N (rate) rather than within-N (position) structure.

The gap between the observed profile and the Dickman band is a quantitative, reproducible carrier with a known size.
proof_strategy: Combine the sandwich with a rigorous rho enclosure via its delay differential equation; propagate the log-magnitude interval through rho's monotonicity.
title: Dickman Calibration of Sieve Hit Profiles

description:
The bound capacity <= log2 of the product of moduli is sharp only for pairwise coprime moduli. For general batteries the joint alphabet of residue dials on a cyclic population is the lcm, not the product. We conjecture the exact ceiling is log2 lcm and that it is attained on the population Z/lcm.

For dials reading n mod m_i on a population contained in Z/L, the joint capacity is at most log2 lcm(m_1,...,m_k), with equality when the population is all of Z/lcm.

Refine TraceBattery.capacity_le_logb_prod by replacing the piFinset bound with the image of the CRT map, and instantiate capacity_eq_logb_pop_of_injective on ZMod (lcm).

The reported ceilings 713 / 6417 / 51336 are correct exactly because 31, 23, 9, 8 are pairwise coprime; any future battery with repeated prime factors must use the lcm ceiling.

Some population would exceed the lcm ceiling, contradicting the pigeonhole structure of residue dials.
proof_strategy: Show the joint residue map factors through ZMod (lcm) via ZMod.castHom, bound the image, then transfer through the alphabet ceiling.
title: Exact CRT Ceiling via Least Common Multiple

description:
Flat ternary orders exist (231, 399) and each one lifts, by height reduction, to an infinite family 2^a p^b q^c r^d. The conjecture is that flat ternary radicals are not sporadic but have positive density among all ternary radicals.

The set { p*q*r : p<q<r odd primes, Φ_{pqr} flat } has positive relative density among ternary squarefree odd numbers.

Count flat ternary radicals up to 10^6 and estimate the ratio; verify the lifting step formally with PMFrame231.flatFrame_of_oddRad_231 applied to further verified flat radicals.

The flat class is much larger than the ω_odd ≤ 2 class, and the classification proved here is only a first approximation.

Flat ternary orders are sporadic and the ω_odd ≤ 2 classification is essentially optimal.
proof_strategy: Combine the residue criterion of direction 3 with a sieve over admissible residues of r modulo pq, then lift by height reduction.
title: Positive Density of Flat Ternary Radicals

description:
The deterministic replication law says eps-close curves with margins above eps have equal knees, and the sharpness theorem shows no bound holds without margins. The probabilistic version should give the agreement probability in terms of the ratio of measured margin to sweep noise.

For sub-Gaussian per-budget noise of scale sigma around a common curve with gate margins at least m, the two knees agree with probability at least 1 - 2 exp(-m^2/(2 sigma^2)).

Formalise sub-Gaussian noise on the retention curve and combine a union bound over the two critical budgets with the deterministic replication law.

Replication experiments can be powered in advance: the measured margins decide whether an agreement is informative.

Knee agreement is dominated by correlated rather than independent noise, and joint models are needed.
proof_strategy: Condition on the two critical budgets; apply the deterministic law with eps = m and bound the failure probability by concentration.
title: Probabilistic Replication Bound at Measured Margins

description:
Turn the newly formalized maximality of the John ellipsoid into the classical algebraic identity carried by the contact points. When the maximal inscribed ellipsoid of K is the unit ball, the contact points should admit positive weights resolving the identity matrix. This bridges convex optimization (first-order conditions for log det) with linear algebra (resolutions of the identity).

If K is a convex body whose maximal-volume inscribed ellipsoid is the unit ball, then there are unit vectors u_1, ..., u_N in the boundary of K and weights c_i > 0 with sum c_i u_i u_i^T = I and sum c_i u_i = 0, and N can be taken at most n(n+3)/2.

Formalize the first-order condition: for every symmetric H with positive trace, the perturbed generator I + tH fails to be inscribed for small t > 0; dualize this to a separation statement in the space of symmetric matrices; verify numerically for the cube, the simplex and random polytopes in dimensions 2 and 3.

Provides the algebraic engine behind John position, and hence formalized routes to the John inclusion K contained in n times the ball and to reverse isoperimetric estimates.

Failure would mean that maximality of the determinant is not detected by first-order perturbations, which would indicate that the constraint set has a degenerate boundary at the maximizer and would demand a nonsmooth analysis.
proof_strategy: Differentiate log det at the maximizer to obtain the trace functional; show that the cone generated by the matrices u u^T over contact points u must span all symmetric matrices, else a strictly determinant-increasing perturbation stays inscribed; extract the weights from a separating hyperplane and Caratheodory's theorem for the dimension bound.
title: Contact-Point Decomposition in John Position

description:
The uniform-divisor null model and the uniform-integer null model give opposite predictions for the late-firing tail (63/64 versus < 0.08 at B1 = 100). Quantify how fast a batch of m recorded hits separates them.

The log-likelihood ratio between the integer and divisor models on m independent empty-tail observations grows at least like c(tau) m log log B1, with the divisor model rejected at m = O(1) for every B1 >= 100.

Compute both tail probabilities in closed form (already formal for the divisor side) and bound the ratio; replay against the 55 recorded hits of exp 570.

The trace observable is a cheap, decisive discriminator between accounting models for guarded-affine ECM, usable as a routine audit.

The two models are statistically close on realistic batch sizes and the empty tail is uninformative, which would weaken the paper 218 conclusion.
proof_strategy: Exact divisor-count factorization for the divisor model, the log-decay bound for the integer model, then a Chernoff/binomial comparison.
title: Divisor-Model Separation Exponent

description:
The elementary half of the MDS conjecture bounds the length of a nontrivial MDS code by the field size. Conjecture that any [n,k,n-k+1] code with 2 ≤ k ≤ n-2 over a field with q elements satisfies n ≤ q + k - 1. The route is that the dual information-set property makes parity-check columns pairwise non-proportional points of a projective space.

If C ≤ F_q^n is MDS with 2 ≤ k ≤ n - 2, then n ≤ q + k - 1.

Extract from dual_weight_lower_bound that every n-k columns of a parity-check matrix are independent, normalize to a systematic form, and count admissible columns over F_q.

Reed–Solomon codes are length-optimal over their field, and no MDS code can beat them asymptotically for fixed q.

A longer MDS code exists, which would be a counterexample to a long-standing expectation and would have to be exhibited explicitly.
proof_strategy: Systematic parity-check matrix; general position of columns; pigeonhole on the q+k-1 possible normalized columns.
title: Length Barrier for MDS Codes over Small Fields

description:
Quantify how badly the prime surface fails to be triangulable by counting the minimal number of Lipschitz d-cells needed to cover its truncation at level d. The upper bound is already constructive; the conjecture is that it is sharp, so the covering number equals the prime counting function.

For finite S, the minimal number of Lipschitz d-cells covering surfaceOf S equals #S; for S the primes and d → ∞ this is asymptotically d / log d.

Prove the lower bound cell-count ≥ #S in Lean using dimH monotonicity per cell, then instantiate with Mathlib's prime counting estimates.

Non-triangulability acquires a quantitative, number-theoretic modulus.

Cells can be reused across dimensions, meaning Lipschitz cells are strictly more efficient than simplicial ones.
proof_strategy: Each covering cell has dimH ≤ d; a cell of dimension n > d cannot be covered by fewer than one cell per dimension level, giving an injection from S into the cell index set.
title: Prime-Gap Modulus of Non-Triangulability

description:
All features of the per-N yield dial factor through the residue vector of N modulo the factor-base primorial. The supremum of R² over all functions of that vector is therefore a single well-defined quantity. Conjecture: the linear span of the per-prime indicators already attains it.

sup over all f of R²(f(N mod P)) equals the R² of the best linear combination of the indicators 1_{QR mod p}, p ≤ B.

Formalise conditional expectation over the finite pattern space using card_qr_pattern; compare best linear fit with best arbitrary fit on the 2^{|base|} pattern classes for small B.

Feature engineering on residue statistics is closed: nothing beyond the per-prime indicators can help.

There exist interaction features (pairs of primes) with strictly greater explanatory power, which would be a concrete new dial.
proof_strategy: Use the exact pattern law to write the conditional expectation as a function on the Boolean cube, then compare its Fourier expansion with the degree-one part.
title: Residue Sigma-Algebra Ceiling for Yield Prediction

description:
The Berggren tree is 3-regular and 3 = q+1 for q = 2, the residue cardinality at the ramified prime above 2 in Z[sqrt 2]. The conjecture is that the boundary Cantor set is equivariantly homeomorphic to P^1 of a local field with residue field of size 2, with the proved relations TU = 3 and (UT)^2 = 3(UT) becoming the Iwahori-Hecke relations of that tree.

There is a PGL(2)-equivariant homeomorphism from the boundary of the Berggren tree onto P^1(Q_2) carrying the transfer operator to the spherical Hecke operator at the prime 2.

Construct the Bruhat-Tits tree of PGL(2, Q_2) in Lean, build the address map from vertices to words, and verify that the constructed Hecke operator satisfies the already-proved relations.

The degenerate {0,3} spectrum is explained structurally as an Iwahori degeneration rather than as an accident of the transfer operator.

The Berggren boundary carries extra structure not visible on the Bruhat-Tits boundary, pinpointing where the analogy with p-adic groups breaks.
proof_strategy: Use the Euclid-parameter (spin) representation to map words to GL(2,Z) matrices, reduce mod powers of 2, and identify address prefixes with lattice classes.
title: Bruhat-Tits Realization of the Ternary Pythagorean Boundary

description:
The formalized coprime-pair lower bound uses the crude tail estimate sum_{g>=2} 1/g^2 <= 25/36, costing a factor of about 2.7 against the truth 6/pi^2. Replacing the tail by an explicit finite sum plus 1/G yields any constant below 2/pi^2 with a purely rational, kernel-checkable computation. This directly improves the box-counting lower bound.

For every epsilon > 0 there is an explicit finite computation proving #copOpp(X) >= (2/pi^2 - epsilon) X^2, and hence #bergBox(H) >= H/8 for H large.

Replace CoprimePairDensity.sum_inv_sq_le by a decidable finite sum bound with parameter G, re-run bergBox_card_ge, and check the resulting constant.

A fully elementary proof of a near-optimal lower bound for the number of primitive Pythagorean triples in a box, with no analytic input.

The sieve-by-gcd step, not the tail bound, is the true bottleneck, meaning the loss is structural and an inclusion-exclusion of higher order is required.
proof_strategy: Bound the tail sum_{g>G} 1/g^2 by 1/G via telescoping, evaluate sum_{g=2}^{G} 1/g^2 as an exact rational by decide/norm_num, and propagate through the existing card_cop_ge chain.
title: Elementary Sieve Constant Refinement

description:
The Hensel step proved for odd primes breaks at p = 2, where the derivative 2x is not invertible. For odd N the congruence x² ≡ N mod 2^k is solvable only when N ≡ 1 mod 8, and then has four roots for every k ≥ 3. Conjecture: the even prime therefore contributes a footprint 4/2^k, twice the odd density, and the yield dial needs a separate N mod 8 term.

For odd N and k ≥ 3, hitCount N (2^k) = 4 if N ≡ 1 (mod 8) (the vanishing case N ≢ 1 mod 8 is already proved as hitCount_two_pow_eq_zero); consequently the mean footprint of the even part of the factor base is 4·Σ_{3≤k} 2^{-k} on the residue class 1 mod 8 and 0 elsewhere.

Adapt the lifting bijection of hitCount_pow_succ, replacing the unique-lift step by the two-lift step forced by the non-invertible derivative; check the counts by decide for 2^3, 2^4, 2^5 and N = 1, 9, 17, 3.

The dial gains an exactly computed, arithmetically distinct N mod 8 feature, a candidate explanation for a further slice of the residual.

The even prime's contribution is not a pure residue-class effect, which would make the 2-part of the sieve genuinely different from its odd part.
proof_strategy: Reuse dvd_sq_sub_congr and cast_sub_mod; replace the linear congruence 2at ≡ −m mod p by the 2-adic analysis of x² − N mod 2^{k+1}, where each root mod 2^k lifts to zero or two roots.
title: Four-Root Two-Adic Footprint of the Even Prime

description:
This cycle proved that typeEntropy q is rational exactly at the prime q = 2. Combined with CRT additivity and the prime-power saturation law, the natural completion is that the type entropy of degree m is rational precisely when m is a power of two, the dyadic tower being the unique source of rational values.

For every m >= 1, typeEntropy m is rational if and only if m is a power of 2 (in which case it equals 2 - 2^{1-e} for m = 2^e).

Write typeEntropy m through typeEntropy_mul_of_coprime and typeEntropy_prime_pow_eq as a rational combination of log2 p and log2 (p-1) over p | m, then apply irrational_log_combination after proving that no cancellation between distinct primes can occur.

A complete rationality classification of the cyclic splitting-type entropy, with the dyadic tower isolated as the only rational family.

There is a multiplicative coincidence between the numbers p and p-1 for distinct primes, itself a strong Diophantine statement.
proof_strategy: Reduce to a linear relation with rational coefficients among the logarithms of the integers p and p-1 for p | m, and rule it out by unique factorisation applied prime by prime.
title: Dyadic Rationality Threshold for the Type Entropy

description:
The divisibility law proved for d interlock depths used only that translation acts freely on the cube. Replacing the cyclic group by an arbitrary finite group acting freely on the alphabet should give divisibility of the combined assembly count by the group order, with the failure case characterised by alphabet fixed points.

If a finite group G acts on the interlock alphabet with no non-identity element fixing a letter, then for n at least 1 the combined assembly count of the G-orbit of a framed puzzle is divisible by the order of G.

Generalise stable_card_eq_mul_gauge to a free G-action on the assembly cube and instantiate with a non-abelian G acting freely on its own underlying set.

Tab-blank parity is one instance of a general representation-theoretic constraint on puzzle solution counts.

Commutativity is essential, and the gauge section has no non-abelian analogue.
proof_strategy: Replace the depth gauge by a set of orbit representatives via a choice of transversal, and prove the bijection with representatives times G by orbit-stabiliser.
title: Free Group Actions on Interlock Alphabets

description:
In every finite-dimensional real representation `ρ` of `EMLGen` of dimension
   `n`, the image `ρ (shiftIdeal)` is simultaneously strictly triangularizable,
   and `ρ D` is conjugate to a matrix whose diagonal blocks are those of a
   semisimple operator with integer eigenvalue *differences*; equivalently
   `V = ⨁_{j} V_j` with `ρ T : V_j → V_{j+1}`.
   *The key insight is* that cycle 3 gives nilpotency of `ρ T` for free, and
   nilpotency plus the eigenvector relation `⁅ρ D, ρ T⁆ = ρ T` is exactly the
   hypothesis of the weight decomposition for the generalized eigenspaces of
   `ad (ρ D)`.  *Why now?*  The missing analytic input (nilpotency) is a
   theorem, and Mathlib has generalized eigenspace decompositions for
   endomorphisms of finite-dimensional spaces.
title: (NC4 — the whole representation is nilpotent-by-abelian, quantitatively.)

description:
(`reprCount`,
   `autocorrelation_eq_reprCount`, `charSum_sq_eq_reprCount_sum`,
   `reprCount_const_iff_trivial`, `miF_symJointG_eq_zero_iff_trivial`,
   `abelian_dichotomy`, `miF_symJointG_pos_units_of_nontrivial`, in
   `Catalog/Tropical/SmoothSelfHintInvisibleTargets.lean`): in a finite **abelian**
   group the representation count `r_A(n) = #{(a,b) ∈ A² : ab = n}` is constant *only*
   for `A = ∅` and `A = G`, hence the symmetric leak vanishes iff the target is trivial
   and is strictly positive for every other target.  The proof is Fourier analysis on
   `Additive G`: `r̂_A = (1̂_A)²`, so constancy kills every nontrivial character sum and
   `1_A` must be constant.  This **closes the previous cycle's Conjecture B in the
   abelian case**, which is the case relevant to `(ZMod l)ˣ` and hence to the
   divisibility events `l ∣ p - 1`.
title: Invisible targets classified for abelian groups

description:
Upgrade the proved continuity of G_M on {‖c‖ > 2} to a Lipschitz estimate with an explicit constant on each region {‖c‖ ≥ R}, R > 2. The uniform 2^{-n} truncation bound reduces this to differentiating the finite polynomial c ↦ z_{n+2}(c). The result would be the first quantitative formal control of the exterior geometry of the Mandelbrot set.

For every R > 2 there is K_R with |G_M(c) - G_M(c')| ≤ K_R ‖c - c'‖ for all ‖c‖,‖c'‖ ≥ R, and |G_M(c) - log‖c‖| ≤ C/‖c‖.

Combine abs_potentialSeq_sub_le (error 2^{-n}) with a derivative bound for the polynomial c ↦ critOrbit c (n+2) on the region, then optimise n ≈ log₂(1/‖c-c'‖).

Yields effective bounds on the harmonic measure and a certified numerical algorithm for G_M with rigorous error bars.

Would reveal that the doubly exponential growth of derivatives defeats the truncation trade-off, pointing to Hölder rather than Lipschitz behaviour.
proof_strategy: Bound ∂_c z_{n+2}(c) by ∏ 2‖z_k‖ ≤ exp(2^{n+3} G_M), balance against the 2^{-n} truncation error, choose n optimally.
title: Explicit Lipschitz Modulus for the Douady–Hubbard Potential

description:
For the ball the exact thin-shell threshold is (R/delta)^d, which is the volume ratio between the body and a delta-ball. The conjecture is that this is the correct general statement for arbitrary convex bodies, up to Banach-Mazur distortion.

For a convex body K and budget delta, the least N whose equal-volume peeling of K has all shells of thickness at most delta equals vol(K)/vol(delta B) up to a factor depending only on the Banach-Mazur distance from K to the ball.

Numerically peel cubes and simplices in dimensions 2-5 and compare the observed threshold to the volume ratio; then formalise the ball case as a lower bound for general K.

The thin-shell threshold is a volumetric invariant, not a spherical accident.

Anisotropy changes the exponent, and the threshold sees the isotropic constant of K rather than its volume alone.
proof_strategy: Sandwich K between inscribed and circumscribed balls and transfer the exact ball threshold through the two inclusions.
title: Volume-Ratio Threshold for General Convex Bodies

description:
For profiles with a spectral gap the mixing premium should be independent of the context length, while gapless profiles should show a premium growing linearly in the context. The approach transports the existing decay dichotomy through the sup-convolution. It decides whether mixed budget tables need re-measurement per context level.

Geometric decay implies k*_balanced(2N) - k*_pure(2N) is constant in N; a positive uniform weight floor implies it grows linearly in N.

Instantiate the sup-convolution with the uniform profile and compute both knees in closed form; contrast with the geometric instance already proved uniformly in N.

One mixed measurement extrapolates across contexts for gap-possessing models.

Mixed budget tables must be re-measured at every context level.
proof_strategy: Combine kstar_uniformly_bounded_of_geometric_decay and kstar_ge_of_bounded_ratio with the two-sided mixed bounds, using kstar_mono_context to compare across context lengths.
title: Context-Scaling of the Mixing Premium

description:
The Heisenberg group formalised here should sit as a normal subgroup inside a semidirect product with SL₂(ℝ) acting on chirped Gaussian windows. The approach is to add the chirp generator to the two existing generators (translation and modulation) and check the Weyl cocycle extends. This bridges the algebra of the window with the symplectic geometry of phase space.

The assignment s ↦ gaussC s extends to an SL₂(ℝ)-equivariant family of chirped Gaussians exp(-π(α+iβ)t²) intertwining the linear symplectic action on (a,b) with the Gabor transform, and Heis is normal in the resulting semidirect product.

Define the chirp operator in Lean, verify the cocycle condition against the existing Heis group instance, and check that the Fourier transform corresponds to the rotation by π/2 using fourier_gaussC and fourier_transOp/fourier_modOp.

gaussSpectral becomes one coordinate of an equivariant family, and monotonicity in the width is revealed as the action of the diagonal one-parameter subgroup — a structural explanation, not a computation.

The obstruction will be a genuine cocycle class, which would show that the discrete (multiset-supported) Gabor transform has a metaplectic anomaly absent in the continuous theory.
proof_strategy: Extend heisRep by the chirp multiplication operator; verify the three Bruhat relations; use fourier_gaussC to compute the action of the Weyl element on the Gaussian ray; conclude normality of Heis from the commutator formula modOp_transOp.
title: Metaplectic Extension of the Gabor Window Action

description:
Batteries so far are read all at once. An adaptive scheduler interleaves dial readings and scanning. We conjecture adaptivity buys nothing, because the achievable cost is determined by the induced partition of the class space, which adaptivity cannot refine beyond the non-adaptive product partition.

For every adaptive dial-aware strategy over a battery there is a non-adaptive strategy with the same expected cost; the adaptive caps are therefore still 4/3 (single pass) and < 2 (expected position).

Model an adaptive strategy as a decision tree over dial answers, formalize the induced partition, and extend schedule_sum_lower_bound from two branches to 2^d branches.

The converse extends to all scan-order algorithms with congruence oracles, adaptive or not.

Adaptive scheduling is a genuine resource and the converse must be restricted to oblivious scans.
proof_strategy: Induction on tree depth, applying the triangular-sum lower bound leafwise and recombining.
title: Adaptive Battery Non-Advantage

description:
Doubling the context should not double the knee if attention capture is concave in the number of retained keys. Formalise concave capture curves and prove a Karamata-style comparison bounding the knee at doubled context by twice the knee at base context, with equality exactly for uniform attention.

If cum is concave with cum 0 = 0, then k*(tau) at context 2n is at most twice k*(tau) at context n, with equality iff the attention mass is uniform on its support.

Add a concavity field to AttentionProfile, prove the doubling bound by induction on increments, and check the equality case against the uniform profile.

KV budgets scale sublinearly with context, so long-context serving costs grow slower than context length.

Concavity is not the right regularity for attention capture, and the 512 -> 1024 knee data must be explained by a shape change instead.
proof_strategy: Decreasing increments give cum(2k) <= 2 cum(k); apply this at k = k*(tau) and use kneeAt_le.
title: Sublinear Knee Growth under Context Doubling

description:
Both the class-group residue dial and the weighted product dial collapse the PP and NN factorisation types. Conjecture a single obstruction theorem: any readout that factors through a group homomorphism from the multiplicative monoid of integers to a finite abelian group is blind to that distinction. This would close a family of proposed factoring covariates at once.

If f is a monoid homomorphism from integers coprime to m into a finite abelian group G, and f(p) = f(q) = g while f(p') = f(q') = g^{-1}, then f(pq) = f(p'q').

State and prove the homomorphism version in Lean, then derive both the Jacobi dial and the class-group dial collapses as instances.

A whole class of proposed dials is provably factor-blind, independent of window size.

Some non-multiplicative readout escapes the collapse, which would be the first genuinely new covariate.
proof_strategy: Direct computation in G, then instantiate with the Jacobi symbol homomorphism and with the class-group composition law.
title: Abstract Factor-Blindness Obstruction for Multiplicative Readouts

description:
The infinitesimal bound ∑|vᵢ| ≤ √(∑vᵢ²/pᵢ) discards a variance term. Quantifying that defect converts the length inequality into an identity plus an explicit nonnegative functional, giving a quantitative rigidity statement for L¹-efficient curves.

There is an absolute c > 0 with fisherRaoSpeed p v − ∑ᵢ|vᵢ| ≥ c · Var_p(|v|/p) for every strictly positive probability vector p and tangent vector v.

Prove the squared version by expanding the Cauchy–Schwarz defect ∑ᵢ pᵢ(|vᵢ|/pᵢ − ∑ⱼ|vⱼ|)² and comparing with the difference of square roots; calibrate c against arcsin r − r in the two-point family.

L¹-efficient curves are exactly those with velocity proportional to the distribution, a rigidity theorem for information geometry.

The deficiency must degenerate near the simplex boundary, indicating a weighted rather than absolute constant.
proof_strategy: Expand the Cauchy–Schwarz defect, use √A − B ≥ (A − B²)/(√A + B), and bound the denominator by the ℓ¹ norm.
title: Cauchy–Schwarz Deficiency for Information Speed

description:
The universal cap is 4/3 for single-pass scans and r for full reveals with r symbols. We conjecture a monotone one-parameter family of caps indexed by the fraction s of rejected classes the algorithm may skip for free, interpolating the two. This would say precisely how much of a sieve's advantage comes from skipping rather than from filtering.

For skip fraction s ∈ [0,1] the maximal speedup of an r-block dial is C(r,s) = 1 / min_θ Σ_i θ_i (θ_i + (1-s)(θ_1 + … + θ_{i-1})), which is continuous and increasing in s, with C(r,0) = 2r/(r+1) and C(r,1) = r.

Define the s-cost in Lean as a Finset sum, prove the closed form by the same doubling identity used for prefixCost, and minimize by Cauchy–Schwarz; verify exhaustively on rational density grids for r = 2,3,4 and s ∈ {0, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, 1}.

Any claimed congruence speedup can be classified by its skip budget, and the 4/3-versus-2-versus-r confusion disappears.

Skipping interacts with density in a non-monotone way, which would itself be a new phenomenon worth isolating.
proof_strategy: Doubling identity 2Σθ_iS_i = (Σθ)² + Σθ² generalizes to a weighted version; minimize the resulting quadratic form under Σθ = 1.
title: Skip-Budget Interpolation of the Dial Cap

description:
The kink in a model's top-k retention knee curve occurs where the knee crosses a model-independent critical key budget, rather than at a model-independent context length. For the 0.5B model the crossing index of 24 keys is exactly the measured corner at ctx=2048. The two readings predict different 1.5B behaviour at ctx=4096 and are already separated formally.

For every model f in the programme, the index of the corner of f equals crossIdx f 24; in particular the 1.5B curve does not kink until ctx = 16384 and its knee at ctx = 4096 is 20, not 28.

Run the 1.5B cell at ctx = 4096 on the same held-out windows and gate; compare with kneeLargeBUD 3 = 20 and kneeLargeCTX 3 = 28, which are proved to differ by exactly 8.

Budget tables become a single scale-free curve in the key budget, with context entering only through the crossing index; deployment tables can be generated per model from its pre-corner slope.

The transition is a property of the context window itself, so every model inherits the same ~2048-token cliff and per-model tables must each carry a nonlinear term past it.
proof_strategy: Formalise crossIdx for each fitted law, prove the two transfer laws convex, monotone and feasible, and show they agree below the corner and separate at j = 3; then discharge the measurement against the separated values.
title: Budget-Threshold Universality of the Attention Corner

description:
Orbit purity holds for translation actions in any finite group, abelian or not. The conjecture is that the full orbit-length spectrum, indexed by conjugacy classes, identifies the group among groups of the same order for small orders.

For finite groups G, H with |G| = |H| <= 32, equality of the multisets {(order of g, number of translation orbits) : g in G} together with the conjugacy class sizes implies G ≅ H.

Formalise the orbit machinery for non-abelian G (the current proof of card_orbits_mul_addOrderOf only uses that orbits are cosets), then verify by decide on S3, D4, Q8, A4 and their order-mates.

The ladder extends past abelian Galois groups with an invariant that is still computable from splitting data alone.

Two non-isomorphic groups share the spectrum, so non-abelian rungs need genuinely representation-theoretic invariants (character tables).
proof_strategy: Generalise transOrbit to left cosets of the cyclic subgroup generated by g; purity is immediate. Then the spectrum encodes the order statistics plus class sizes; compare with known results that order statistics alone do not determine a group (Thompson) and test whether the class refinement repairs it in the small range.
title: Frobenius Orbit Spectra as Non-Abelian Rung Invariant

description:
The certified value of minMass 11 is either 22 or 24, and it is 22 exactly when an ideal Prouhet-Tarry-Escott pair of size 11 exists. We conjecture the value is 24, i.e. no such pair exists. This would be the first proven gap in the ideal PTE sequence.

minMass 11 = 24, equivalently no two disjoint multisets of 11 naturals share their power sums p_0,...,p_10.

Either exhibit a size-11 ideal pair and discharge PTEIdeal.minMass_eleven_eq_22_iff, or prove a congruence obstruction for integer polynomials of l1 norm 22 divisible by (X-1)^11.

PTEIdeal.minMass_ge_two_mul_add_two becomes unconditional at K = 11, exhibiting the first nonlinear value of the invariant.

The linear law minMass K = 2K extends through K = 12 without exception, strengthening the case for direction 1.
proof_strategy: Combine the parity lemma, the disjointness rigidity theorem (both sides must have 11 distinct nodes), and 2-adic or 3-adic constraints on the coefficient vector of a degree-bounded polynomial with an 11-fold root at 1.
title: Ideal Size-Eleven Configuration

description:
Since the average hit count of any sieve map is pinned to |domain|/|targets|, no single-prime measurement can separate the x^2-N pool from a random pool. Any real deviation must live in the joint law of admissibility and hit patterns across two or more primes at fixed N. This turns a vague randomness question into a sharp two-prime independence statement.

For fixed N and distinct odd primes p, q not dividing N, the events 'p divides x^2-N' and 'q divides x^2-N' are exactly independent for x uniform mod pq, and hence the smooth-density model factorises exactly over the factor base.

Prove the CRT product formula for the joint hit count mod pq, then measure higher-order (three-prime, prime-power) correlations empirically against the proved two-prime baseline.

The Dickman-style independence heuristic for the sieve is exact at the level of the factor base, and the only remaining error is the finite-x correction.

A measurable cross-prime correlation exists, which is the first genuine non-randomness of the relation pool and would change sieve yield predictions.
proof_strategy: Chinese remainder theorem gives Z/pq = Z/p x Z/q as rings; the hit sets are products, so counts multiply. Formalise via ZMod.chineseRemainder and the fiber-counting lemma sum_fiber_card.
title: Cross-Prime Correlation as the Sole Non-Random Degree of Freedom

description:
The unique corrected square root of the moonshine Hauptmodul J has integral Laurent coefficients as far as computed, while its cube root does not. We conjecture integrality holds at the prime 2 for all coefficients, and that this encodes 2-adic congruences for the coefficients of J. Proving it would connect the star-root construction with replication identities.

Let g be the unique normalized Laurent series with q g^2 = J. Then every Laurent coefficient of g lies in Z; equivalently the binomial series (1+X)^{1/2} substituted with q J - 1 has 2-integral coefficients.

Formalize the star-root over Z_2 rather than C, using PowerSeries.binomialSeries with r = 1/2 over the binomial ring Z_2, and prove that substitution preserves 2-integrality; verify numerically to degree 50 first.

A new family of 2-adic congruences for the j-function coefficients, obtained purely from the group structure of normalized q-series.

The first denominator identifies a precise obstruction, isolating the 2-adic valuation of the coefficients of J where the pattern breaks.
proof_strategy: Work in the 1-units of Z_2[[X]]; show squaring is bijective on 1 + 2X Z_2[[X]] and locate J's power-series part inside a subgroup on which the square root is integral, using the binomialSeries machinery already used for divisibility.
title: Dyadic Integrality of Hauptmodul Star-Roots

description:
No `EMLExpr` denotes `Real.sin` on
   all of `ℝ` (and likewise for `Real.cos`).  A proof route is to formalize the
   one-variable consequence of o-minimality of the real exponential field:
   the zero set of an exp-log term is a finite union of points and intervals,
   whereas the zeros of sine form an infinite discrete set.  A single explicit
   expression whose evaluation equals sine everywhere would falsify this.
title: Trigonometric non-representability

description:
In every
   finite-dimensional real representation `ρ` of `EMLGen` of dimension `n`,
   `(ρ T)^n = 0` — established here for `n = 2`
   (`rep_dim_two_shift_isNilpotent`, via Cayley–Hamilton) and conjectured in
   general; the shift
   ideal acts by nilpotent operators, so the only irreducible finite-dimensional
   representations are the one-dimensional characters `g ↦ c · g.scale`.
   *The key insight is* that `rep_shift_trace_pow_eq_zero` already gives every
   power sum `p_k = tr(B^k) = 0`, and in characteristic zero Newton's identities
   convert vanishing power sums into `charpoly B = X^n`, which is nilpotency.
   *Why now?*  The power sums are formal; the missing ingredient is the Newton
   identity bridge between `Matrix.trace (B ^ k)` and
   `Matrix.charpoly`, for which Mathlib has both the symmetric-function API and
   `LinearMap.isNilpotent_iff_charpoly`.
title: (NC1 — from trace to nilpotency; dimension two already proved.)

description:
The centralizer of
   `emlField g` inside the `C¹` vector fields on `(0, ∞)` is one-dimensional
   when `g.scale ≠ 0` and infinite-dimensional when `g.scale = 0`.
   *The key insight is* that the centralizer equation is the same singular first
   order ODE treated in cycle 2, but with eigenvalue `0` instead of `-1`, so the
   glueing lemma `const_of_deriv_eq_zero_punctured` applies verbatim and the
   dichotomy is exactly the presence or absence of the singular point.
   *Why now?*  Both halves reduce to lemmas already proved here; only the
   dimension count of the solution space remains.
title: (NC3 — centralizer dichotomy, restated from SC2.)

description:
Introduce Hamming weight on
   finite binary cochains and define primal and dual logical distances as minima
   over nonzero homology and cohomology classes.  Prove the standard
   `min(systole, cosystole)` theorem under explicit finiteness and nondegeneracy
   assumptions.  This will prevent the primal girth from being mistaken for the
   complete quantum distance.
title: Formalize CSS distance, not only graph girth

description:
Characterise the attention-profile families whose retention knee grows as a*log2(ctx)+b. The trichotomy theorem shows Zipf tails give an almost linear knee and fixed geometric tails a constant knee, so the measured law forces a geometric tail whose rate drifts with the context. The conjecture pins the class exactly, up to uniform constants.

A profile family on n keys has knee a*log2 n + b at gate tau for all n iff its tail mass beyond k is within a uniform constant factor of (1-tau)*2^{-(k-b)/a}.

Define driftGeomCurve in Lean, prove its knee equals a*Nat.log 2 n + b, then prove the converse bound on tail mass for any family with that knee law.

The deployment table becomes a two-parameter mechanistic model (slope = tail rate, intercept = tokenisation) rather than a lookup table.

Knee laws are not determined by tail mass alone and a finer invariant (e.g. block structure of the profile) is required.
proof_strategy: Dyadic block induction as in harm_two_pow_lower/upper, applied to the drifting-rate family; then a squeeze between two geometric families bracketing the measured curve.
title: Drifting-Geometric Tail Class for Logarithmic Knee Laws

description:
The formal end-to-end result here needs only |A|+1 smooth relations, where A is the set of admissible primes. Combining it with an effective density statement for quadratic residues among the primes up to B would convert the folklore factor-2 saving of the quadratic sieve into a theorem with an explicit error term.

For every non-square N and every B >= B0(N), |A(N,B)| = pi(B)/2 + O(sqrt(B) log(B|N|) / log B), hence pi(B)/2 + O(...) + 1 smooth relations provably suffice to produce a congruence of squares.

Formalise the character-sum count of primes p <= B with (N|p) = 1 under GRH or via Chebotarev with an effective error, then plug into qs_congruence_of_squares.

A fully proved relation-count bound for the quadratic sieve, halving the classical unconditional requirement.

The admissible set is not equidistributed for some N, which would itself be a striking arithmetic phenomenon.
proof_strategy: Quadratic reciprocity turns admissibility into a congruence condition on p; apply an effective prime-counting theorem in arithmetic progressions, then combine with the formalised F2 dimension argument.
title: Effective Admissible-Half Relation Bound

description:
Extremal serving values are exactly the quantised pairs: beta = c(c-1)/(k(k-1)) and M = c/k for an integer c, necessary by saturation_quantised and sufficient by the complete c-design of quantised_values_are_exactly_realised.
