Conjecture: the bound degrades continuously in the distance delta from beta to that finite set, giving a strictly better bound than the capacity curve for generic budgets such as the measured 0.8327.

If dist(beta, {c(c-1)/(k(k-1)) : c <= k}) = delta > 0 then every shared model satisfies M <= capacityCurve k beta - f(delta, k) with f(delta,k) of order delta/(k(1-beta)).

Relax the constancy of matchCount in saturation_quantised to a near-constancy estimate and track the resulting Cauchy-Schwarz defect quantitatively.

Generic families obey a strictly sharper serving bound, and the sharpening is computable from beta alone.

The curve is asymptotically attained even at non-quantised budgets, and quantisation is a measure-zero phenomenon.
proof_strategy: Integrality of the matched count forces a minimal Cauchy-Schwarz defect once the optimum is non-integral; insert that defect into saturation_defect_identity and re-solve the quadratic.
title: Quantisation Gap Below the Capacity Curve

description:
Asks for genuinely arithmetic witnesses of the capacity law: families of statistics on b-bit integers (2-adic valuation, popcount residues, digit sums modulo distinct primes) that are asymptotically pairwise decorrelated. Combined with the capacity law they cap any dial built from k such statistics at 1/sqrt(k).

For every k there is a family of k arithmetic statistics on {0,...,2^b-1} whose pairwise Spearman correlations tend to 0 as b -> infinity; consequently their common reading against any response is at most 1/sqrt(k) + o(1).

Compute the pairwise rank correlations of the 2-adic valuation and popcount profiles exactly at small b, and formalise the limit via equidistribution of digits modulo independent moduli.

Dial engineering has an information-theoretic ceiling: adding decorrelated baselines strictly lowers the attainable common reading.

Arithmetic statistics on binary expansions are inherently correlated, which would itself explain the persistent count advantage.
proof_strategy: Express each statistic as a sum of digit functions, compute covariances by independence of digits under the uniform law, and bound the rank-vs-value discrepancy by the tie profile.
title: Orthogonal Arithmetic Statistic Families

description:
Existence of a square sub-product follows from an 𝔽₂ pigeonhole. We conjecture the exact count: r relations over a factor base of size d give 2^(r − rank) − 1 nonempty square sub-products, so the observed zero splits at exp 561 are fully explained by r ≤ d with no arithmetic obstruction.

Let M ∈ 𝔽₂^(r×d) be the parity matrix of r smooth relations. The number of nonempty subsets with square product is 2^(r − rank M) − 1; in particular it is positive iff rank M < r, and rank M ≤ d always.

Formalise the parity map as a linear map (Fin r → ZMod 2) →ₗ (κ → ZMod 2) and count its kernel with Module.finrank and Fintype.card of a subspace over ZMod 2.

Sieve yield analysis reduces entirely to rank statistics of random 𝔽₂ matrices, decoupled from N.

Some square sub-products are missed by the parity map, meaning the exponent-vector encoding loses information — a definitional problem.
proof_strategy: Rank-nullity over ZMod 2 plus Fintype.card_eq_two_pow_finrank; subtract the empty subset.
title: Parity-Rank Kernel Count for Sieve Relations

description:
Complete enumeration shows every value 0..27 occurs as the defect of an order-4 unital magma, while at order 3 the value 1 is impossible. We conjecture that this is the only gap in the entire family.

For n >= 4 every d with 0 <= d <= (n-1)^3 is the defect of some unital magma of order n; for n = 3 the attainable set is exactly {0,2,3,4,5,6,7,8}.

Formalise the order-3 statement by decidable enumeration over the 81 tables, and prove the n >= 4 case by an explicit interpolating family of tables.

The defect is an unconstrained combinatorial statistic above order 3, so no hidden congruence obstructions exist beyond commutative parity.

There are further congruence obstructions on defect values, refining the parity theorem.
proof_strategy: Start from a monoid table and change one product entry at a time, controlling the change in the number of broken triples, to realise every intermediate value.
title: Defect Spectrum Gap at Order Three

description:
Prove that the number of equivalence relations on Fin n satisfies the Bell recurrence, hence equals Mathlib's Nat.bell n. The approach decomposes a partition of Fin (n+1) by the block containing the last element, matching the recurrence's binomial sum. This closes an explicit TODO in Mathlib and upgrades all Bell-number results here to statements about Nat.bell.

Nat.card (Setoid (Fin n)) = Nat.bell n for all n.

Formalise the bijection Setoid (Fin (n+1)) ≃ Σ (s : Finset (Fin n)), Setoid ((Fin n) \ s) and compare cardinalities with Nat.bell_succ.

partitionCount_log_convex becomes log-convexity of Nat.bell, and sum_fixedPoints_perm_pow becomes the classical Poisson moment theorem in Mathlib's own vocabulary.

Mathlib's Nat.bell would not count partitions, indicating an indexing mismatch in its definition that must be documented.
proof_strategy: Induct on n; classify a partition of Fin (n+1) by the block containing the top element; sum over the size of that block using Finset.sum_pow_mul_eq_max_pow-style counting and Nat.bell_succ.
title: Bell Recurrence via Orbit Surgery

description: Let `p₁, …, pₖ` be distinct primes and `M = ∏ pᵢ`. Among candidates `0 ≤ n < M`, the checks `pᵢ ∣ n` isolate `0`. Conjecture: in a standard PA sequent calculus, a balanced conjunction of these checks yields a backward certificate of size `O(k log M)`, while any certificate restricted to testing candidates one by one has size `Ω(M)`. The claim is falsifiable by explicit proof-size upper and lower bounds in the selected calculus.
title: Arithmetic residue certificates

description:
Prime inflation and the reflection X ↦ -X preserve the multiset of absolute coefficient values, and together they collapse every order onto its odd radical. The conjecture is the converse: two orders with the same coefficient multiset must share an odd radical, making the odd radical a complete invariant.

If for all B, (∀k |coeff k Φ_m| ≤ B) ↔ (∀k |coeff k Φ_n| ≤ B) holds together with equality of coefficient multisets, then oddRad m = oddRad n.

Search for coincidences among coefficient multisets of Φ_n for n ≤ 10^4 with distinct odd radicals; formalise the negative result as a uniqueness theorem via degrees φ(n) and the semigroup formula.

The odd radical is a complete invariant of the coefficient multiset of a cyclotomic polynomial.

An accidental coincidence would be a new arithmetic identity between distinct cyclotomic families.
proof_strategy: Use φ(n) to pin the degree, then reconstruct the odd radical from the pattern of sign changes given by the numerical-semigroup indicators.
title: Completeness of Inflation and Reflection

description:
For X uniform on the unit ball of R^d, the rescaled boundary distance d(1-|X|) should converge in distribution to Exp(1) with an explicit O(1/d) Kolmogorov rate. All tail probabilities are already computed as (1-u/d)^d; what remains is to phrase them as a statement about the pushforward measure and to make the error uniform in u. This turns a geometric concentration fact into a probabilistic limit theorem.

If X_d ~ Uniform(B(0,1) in R^d) then d(1-‖X_d‖) converges in distribution to Exp(1), and sup_u |P(d(1-‖X_d‖) > u) - e^{-u}| = O(1/d).

Formalise the pushforward of volume under x ↦ d(1-‖x‖) and compare its CDF to 1-e^{-u} using peel_volume_fraction_tendsto plus a uniform version of shell_thickness_rate.

Equal-volume peelings of balls become a source of exponential random variables, linking the peeling programme to concentration of measure.

The convergence fails to be uniform, isolating a boundary regime u ≍ d where the profile is not exponential.
proof_strategy: Measure.addHaar_ball gives the CDF exactly; bound e^{-u} - (1-u/d)^d by u^2/(2d) using the log-convexity estimates already proved, then apply the portmanteau/CDF criterion.
title: Exponential Radial Law for Uniform Points in High-Dimensional Balls

description:
On the geometric family the knee is exactly characterised by r^k <= 1 - tau, so one fitted decay rate per domain predicts the whole knee curve. Conjecture that fitting r to attention logs recovers the predictive power that tokens-per-word failed to provide.

Fitting a geometric capture curve per domain yields knee predictions with rank correlation at least 0.9 against the measured knees, in contrast to the -0.40 obtained from tokens-per-word.

Estimate r per domain from attention mass logs, compute predicted knees via kneeAt_geometric_le_iff, and re-run the Spearman and R-squared statistics formalised in NET73TokenizationDensity.

The domain shift has a one-parameter explanation on the decay axis, replacing the refuted tokenization hypothesis.

Attention capture is not geometric, and the knee requires the full capture curve rather than any one-parameter summary.
proof_strategy: Use kneeAt_geometric_le_iff to convert fitted rates into predicted knees, then reuse the spearman and rsq definitions to state and check the new correlation claim.
title: Decay-Rate Regression as the Replacement Predictor

description:
New in this cycle:
   `WignerBridge.frac_large_eigenvalues_le` is a deterministic Markov inequality for
   the ESD of any real symmetric matrix, and
   `RademacherWigner.expect_frac_large_eigenvalues_le` turns the uniform moment bound
   into `E[#{i : |λᵢ|/√N ≥ t}/N] ≤ (k+1)^(2k)/t^(2k)`, independent of `N`. Hence
   `RademacherWigner.esd_tight`: for every `ε > 0` there is a threshold `t` (one may
   take `t = 2/√ε`) with expected mass at most `ε` outside `[−t, t]` **in every
   dimension**. This is precisely the compactness hypothesis of Conjecture 4.
title: Tightness of the empirical spectral distribution

description:
Conjecture that every tie ceiling is governed by a single functional of the limiting block-mass profile, namely rho^2 -> 1 - ||alpha||_3^3. The dyadic profile gives 1/7 and the binomial profile gives 0, recovering both laws proved this cycle. Extremising the functional under a resolution constraint should reproduce the resolution law and the dominant-block laws as the two endpoints.

If the block-mass profile m_j/n converges to alpha in l^3, then the tie ceiling converges to 1 - sum_j alpha_j^3; moreover min ||alpha||_3^3 = 1/K^2 over K-block profiles and max = alpha_max^3 + o(1).

Formalise the l^3 limit statement for profiles given by a summable weight sequence, then verify it against the dyadic (geometric) and binomial profiles already in the catalog.

One theorem subsumes the resolution law, the dominant-block laws and the p-adic ceiling law, with sharp constants.

Ceilings depend on more than the third moment of the mass profile, indicating that finite-n corrections are not uniformly controlled.
proof_strategy: Rewrite the attenuation law as 1 - sum (m_j/n)^3 + sum (m_j/n)/n^2, then prove l^3 continuity of the cube functional and control the remainder by the resolution bound.
title: Cubic Shape Functional for Rank-Tie Ceilings

description:
The pooled inverse-bitlen law crosses the exact 2-adic tie ceiling at bitlen 31, proved as a sharp threshold in inverse_law_respects_tie_ceiling. We conjecture this crossing is a physical regime boundary of the dial: ceiling-limited and flat below it, dilution-limited and decaying above it, with a non-analytic kink at the crossing.

In the infinite-sample limit, rho^2(b) = min(spearmanSq(dyadicBlocks b), C/b), so rho^2 is constant to within 10^-26 for b <= 30, strictly decreasing for b >= 31, and non-differentiable at the crossing.

Run the ladder at bitlens 16, 24, 28, 32, 36 with large N; test flatness below 31 and slope -C/b^2 above it, and test for a kink by fitting one-sided slopes. In Lean, the two exact curves and their unique crossing are already available, so the statement to formalize is the min-form identity at each tested rung.

The dial has an exactly located operating window, and every ladder below bitlen 31 measures the tie ceiling rather than the statistic of interest.

The two limiting mechanisms blend smoothly, implying an interaction term that product_law_factorised excludes for the finite-sample model, and hence a genuinely new effect.
proof_strategy: Both curves are exactly known: the ceiling is (6/7)(1 + 1/(2^b(2^b+1))) from dyadic_spearmanSq, the dilution law is C/b. Prove the crossing is unique and transversal by strict monotonicity of both sides (dyadic_ceiling_strict_anti and the strict antitonicity of C/b), which forces non-differentiability of the pointwise minimum.
title: Tie-Ceiling Crossover Kink at Bitlen 31

description:
The rational identity sum 1/(a_i(a_i+b_i)) = 1 proved for every ternary tree is the algebraic shadow of an equidistribution statement: each branch image occupies an exact area fraction of the node cone. Upgrading it to a counting theorem with an error term would make the conservation law analytic rather than formal.

For each branch M = (a,b;c,d) of a ternary Pythagorean tree, the number of nodes whose image under M has first coordinate at most B equals (3/pi^2) B^2/(a(a+b)) + O(B log B), and the three counts sum to the number of non-root nodes with first coordinate at most B.

Compute the three counts numerically for B up to 10^5 and fit the error; formally, count coprime opposite-parity lattice points in the triangle {0 < y < x, a x + b y <= B} using Moebius inversion over the density 3/pi^2 of the node set.

The tree condition becomes an exact equidistribution partition of the coprime cone, giving a soft proof that no fourth tree exists via a density obstruction.

The branch images are not equidistributed, so the density identity is a coincidence of the three solutions rather than a structural constraint.
proof_strategy: Write the count as a Moebius sum over d | gcd of triangle lattice counts, apply the standard Gauss bound to each triangle, and sum the tail; the parity condition contributes a factor handled by splitting the sublattice modulo two.
title: Lattice-Point Form of the Branch Density Conservation Law

description: Fix a sequent calculus for the bounded arithmetic fragment containing formulas `n < N`, divisibility, conjunction, and equality. For every `N ≥ 8`, compare the shortest derivation of `n = 6` from `n < N` with the shortest derivation from `n < N`, `2 ∣ n`, and `3 ∣ n`. Conjecture: for at least 90% of `N ≤ 10^4`, the consequence-guided derivation has at most half as many inference nodes. A proof enumerator can decide this finite claim once the calculus and node-count convention are fixed.
title: Bounded-arithmetic compression benchmark

description: Conjecture: there exists an infinite family of PA propositions and verified consequence lists for which the formal candidate search space shrinks by an unbounded factor, but the shortest proof length decreases by at most an additive constant. This would show that semantic search compression and syntactic proof compression are independent measurements. Test by exhaustive shortest-proof enumeration in successively larger bounded fragments.
title: Strict filtering without proof shortening

description:
We prove that the Euclid-parameter
   substitutions preserve `0 < n < m`, coprimality and opposite parity. Adding
   the classical converse — that `IsCoprime m n` plus opposite parity implies
   the triple `(m²−n², 2mn, m²+n²)` is primitive, and that every primitive
   triple arises this way — would upgrade `energy_step` into a statement about
   *all* primitive triples, and give a bijection between the tree and the free
   ternary monoid.
title: Full primitivity certificate

description:
Determinism forces a gapless degree monoid, so simulating a nondeterministic machine deterministically must distort the invariant. Using the time-rescaling law, define the determinisation cost of a submonoid M as the least k such that the colon monoid (M : k) is a full arithmetic progression. The conjecture pins this cost for two-loop machines.

For coprime p, q > 1 the least k with {n | k*n ∈ ⟨p,q⟩} = dℕ for some d equals p*q - p - q + 1.

Formalise the colon monoid via mem_degreeMonoid_pow and compute {n | k*n ∈ ⟨p,q⟩} for small coprime pairs; then prove the general bound by the residue criterion.

Gives a quantitative price of determinism expressed purely in numerical-semigroup data.

The determinisation cost is not controlled by the Frobenius number, indicating a finer invariant than the gap set is needed.
proof_strategy: Use mem_degreeMonoid_pow to reduce to arithmetic of the colon monoid, then apply mem_iff_residue_le to characterise when the colon monoid is gapless.
title: Deterministic-Simulation Cost of a Numerical Semigroup

description:
Restricting to integer coefficients gives a subgroup of the corrected-product group which should remain torsion-free but lose divisibility. Measuring the failure computes the divisible hull of integral normalized series inside the full group.

The integral normalized series form a subgroup Norm(ℤ) that is torsion-free and not divisible; for the class 1A moonshine series J, J^{⋆(1/n)} has integral coefficients only for n = 1.

Formalize Norm(ℤ) as the preimage of integral one-units and compute coeffAt (1/n)-powers level by level using coeffAt_cpow and the binomial coefficients Ring.choose (1/n) j.

The corrected product has an arithmetic refinement, with a computable denominators obstruction at each filtration level.

Integral one-units are already divisible, which would be a surprising arithmetic rigidity statement.
proof_strategy: Show closure of integrality under ⋆ and inverse via the integrality of coefficients of u⁻¹ for u ≡ 1 mod X, then exhibit an explicit denominator in the binomial expansion of J^{⋆(1/n)}.
title: Integral Sublattice and Failure of Divisibility

description:
The proved sign law shows epsilon depends only on the fixed-point data of the duality involution, which is the hallmark of a Lefschetz-type invariant. Conjecture that epsilon factors through the Burnside ring of the acting group, making it a mod-2 Euler characteristic of the fixed-point set.

For a finite group G acting on the index set through duality-compatible permutations, E -> epsilon(E) is additive on direct sums, invariant under twists, and factors through the augmentation A(G) -> Z/2 given by the mod-2 Euler characteristic of fixed-point sets.

Formalise G-equivariant duality eigensystems, verify additivity and twist invariance (already proved for the trivial group), and construct the map to Z/2.

Root signs become equivariant-topological invariants, opening a transfer of Lefschetz machinery into functional-equation signs.

The sign carries strictly more information than the fixed-point set of the group action, isolating a genuinely arithmetic residue.
proof_strategy: Use rootSign_directSum and rootSign_twist as the two Burnside axioms; compute epsilon on transitive G-sets and check the induction formula.
title: Burnside-Ring Factorisation of the Root Sign

description:
The Price tree exposes exactly two address letters to 2-adic residues of the odd leg, while the Berggren tree exposes none to 3-adic residues. The conjecture is that the number of visible clicks equals the number of valuation levels of the halved coordinate that survive the quadratic reconstruction of the odd leg, giving a single formula covering both trees. It matters because it turns two isolated 'residue dial' phenomena into one structural invariant of ternary triple trees.

For a triple tree whose moves halve one of two linear forms L1, L2 with the odd leg N a fixed quadratic expression in them, the maximal k such that the first k letters are functions of N mod p^m for some m equals the number of steps for which the p-adic valuation of the halved form is determined by N; for the Price tree at p = 2 this number is 2, and for the Berggren tree at p = 3 it is 0.

Formalize the invariant for the Price and Berggren move sets and verify it reproduces the proved values 2 and 0; then test it numerically on the Barning-Hall and Price variants before attempting the general proof.

A single theorem subsumes both trees' sealing results and predicts the visible prefix length of any new triple tree without measurement.

The visible prefix length is tree-specific, and the two-tree adic map is a coincidence of the particular move matrices rather than a structural law.
proof_strategy: Express each move as its action on (U, V) = (p+q, q-p), track v_p of each coordinate along a descent, and show the odd leg N = (V^2 - U^2)/const determines the valuation only up to the cap observed in the run laws; conclude with the twin-family construction to show the cap is sharp.
title: Two-Sided Adic Budget for Pythagorean Triple Trees

description:
The Welch–Berlekamp linear system produces the transmitted polynomial whenever at most (n-k)/2 errors occurred. Conjecture that solvability plus the polynomial identity N = E·p can be proved purely inside the degreeLT packaging already used for the encoder, giving a verified decoder matching the proved unique-decoding radius.

For t ≤ (n-k)/2 and any received word y at distance ≤ t from a codeword enc(p), every nonzero solution (E, N) with deg E ≤ t, deg N < t + k of the system E(α_i) y_i = N(α_i) satisfies N = E * p.

Set up the system as a linear map between degreeLT spaces, show the kernel is nontrivial by dimension count, and prove N - E*p has more roots than its degree.

A machine-checked decoder correctness proof at the exact radius already established as optimal for unique decoding.

The dimension count fails for some parameter range, marking the precise boundary where the linear-algebraic decoder must be replaced.
proof_strategy: Rank-nullity on the Welch–Berlekamp map; root counting for N - E*p at the n evaluation points.
title: Berlekamp–Welch Correctness at the Unique-Decoding Radius

description:
For any strictly monotone real cubic p, the inverse branch should be concave exactly above the image of p's inflection point. Since that image is a polynomial expression in the coefficients, the curvature threshold becomes an algebraic invariant of the cubic, computable without any analysis. This turns a question about convex geometry into one about coefficient loci.

Let p y = y^3 + a y^2 + b y + c be strictly monotone on R and y* = -a/3. Then ConcaveOn R (Ici t0) (p^{-1}) iff t0 >= p(y*), where p(y*) = c - a b/3 + 2 a^3/27.

State it in Lean for p given by its coefficients with hypothesis 3b >= a^2 (monotonicity), reduce to the depressed cubic by the Tschirnhaus shift, and reuse the transport argument of lagrangeExponent_concaveOn.

The constant 1/27 of this cycle is exhibited as p(y*) for the normalisation a = -1, b = 1/3, c = 0, and every catalog cubic acquires a computable concavity threshold.

Monotonicity of a cubic does not suffice to make its inverse curvature-monotone, forcing an extra nondegeneracy hypothesis such as a perfect-square derivative.
proof_strategy: Shift y -> y + y* to kill the quadratic term, factor p through a pure cube plus a linear term, and analyse the sign of the second derivative of the inverse via (p^{-1})'' = -p''/(p')^3, whose sign changes exactly at y*.
title: Inflection-Image Threshold for General Real Cubics

description:
Summing the per-prime shares over all odd primes up to B turns the mixture amplitude into an explicit function of the smoothness bound. Mertens-type estimates should give a log-log law, which is directly falsifiable by measuring the hump at several bounds B.

For fixed weight c with X = (c-1)^2/(2c), the total amplitude A(B) = sum over odd primes q <= B of log(1 + (1 - 1/q)X) satisfies A(B) = X * log log B + C(X) + o(1) as B tends to infinity, with C explicit.

Combine the sandwich bounds on each share with Mertens' second theorem for sum of 1/q, then compare the prediction with amplitudes measured at several smoothness bounds.

The hump amplitude becomes a predicted function of the sieve parameters, converting the mechanism into a quantitative forecast rather than a post hoc explanation.

The measured amplitude scales differently in B, which would show the carrier set is not the full factor base but a bounded subset of small primes.
proof_strategy: Write log(1 + (1-1/q)X) = X/q-free main term plus O(1/q^2) corrections via the sandwich, sum with Mertens, and control the tail by comparison with a convergent series.
title: Factor-Base Amplitude Law in the Smoothness Bound

description:
The corrected-product group should be isomorphic to the additive group X*ℂ[[X]] via a formal logarithm, which would linearise the whole theory and upgrade the complex power operation into a genuine ℂ-module structure on normalized series.

There is a group isomorphism Norm ≃* Multiplicative (X·ℂ⟦X⟧) given by f ↦ log (q·f), with inverse w ↦ q⁻¹ · exp w.

Define log as substitution of (u-1) into Σ (-1)^{m+1} X^m / m and prove exp (log u) = u for one-units, using PowerSeries.exp and the substitution API.

Torsion-freeness, unique divisibility and the filtration all become statements about a ℚ-vector space; cpow becomes a scalar action.

Formal exp/log fail to be mutually inverse in this setting, isolating a genuine multiplicative phenomenon not visible additively.
proof_strategy: Build formal log by substitution, prove log (u*v) = log u + log v via the derivative characterisation, then invert with exp using the substitution composition lemmas.
title: Logarithmic Linearisation of the Corrected Product

description:
For imaginary quadratic `K` with `t` prime discriminant divisors, prove
   `Nat.card (Cl ⧸ Cl²) = 2^{t-1}` and identify the corresponding class field as the genus
   field. Combined with the present count, when `Cl(𝒪_K)` is elementary abelian of rank `r` the
   genus field is the whole Hilbert class field and `r = t - 1`. Falsifiable at `K = ℚ(√-15)`,
   where the prediction is degree `2`.
title: Genus theory

description:
Finite machines realise every submonoid of ℕ, but with how many states? The gap count of ⟨p,q⟩ should force a linear lower bound on the state space of any realising machine, matched by the chain construction.

Every machine with degree monoid ⟨p,q⟩ (p, q coprime, both > 1) has at least p + q - 1 states, and the chain machine attains this bound.

Exhaustively enumerate relations on Fin k for k < p + q - 1 and small coprime p, q, checking the degree monoid; then prove the bound via bisimulation invariance.

Turns the Sylvester genus into a state-complexity measure for nondeterministic machines.

A cleverer machine encodes ⟨p,q⟩ compactly, revealing that the gap set is not the right complexity proxy.
proof_strategy: Show a machine with few states yields few loop lengths through the base state, hence a small generating set, contradicting the count (p-1)(q-1)/2 of gaps.
title: State-Complexity Lower Bound from Sylvester Genus

description:
The Maslov gap and the top-1 margin bound each other two-sidedly. Conjecture that for random score vectors the gap concentrates, producing a sharp threshold at margin ~ log n separating tropical (max-like) from diffuse (soft) layers.

For x with i.i.d. sub-Gaussian coordinates and top-1 margin m, the Maslov gap concentrates around log(1 + (n-1) E e^{-m}) with fluctuations O(1/sqrt n), so the tropical/diffuse boundary is a sharp threshold in m at log n.

Prove concentration for the Gaussian case in Lean using the two-sided bounds maslovGap_le_of_margin and margin_le_of_maslovGap, then check numerically against measured per-layer gap medians.

Crystallization is a property of the margin distribution, not of the trained weights, and can be predicted before training.

The tail's large Maslov gap reflects weight structure and must be explained by the learned attention geometry.
proof_strategy: Sandwich lse between max and max + log n, then apply sub-Gaussian tail bounds to the runner-up gap.
title: Tropical Crystallization Threshold

description:
The bridge says the branch parameters `(σ,ε)` live in a
   two-dimensional space and take only three values. A quantitative separation
   result — e.g. a margin bound showing the three branch outputs are separated
   by at least `min(log 2 − E, …)` — would turn the range-partition theorem into
   a robustness statement for a trained neuron reading noisy energies.
title: Learnability

description:
`no_binaryProduct_of_disjoint` shows products fail precisely when setups share no
reading. Conjecture: the failure is classified by a `Čech`-style obstruction — the
category of setups over a fixed universe has all limits iff the nerve of the covering
family is connected, and the number of connected components of that nerve equals the
number of distinct "incompatible interpretive frames" of the joke.

**The key insight is** that the existence of a limit is a *connectivity* statement
about the intersection pattern of the setups, so limit-failure is a combinatorial
invariant (a nerve) rather than a categorical accident.
**Why now?** The nonexistence proof given here already runs through
`prod.fst`/`prod.snd` and disjointness; upgrading disjointness to nerve-connectivity is
a finite combinatorial induction.
title: Colimit Obstruction Class for Setup Categories

description:
**Conjecture.** For a depth-$L$ transformer the epistasis order at a fixed
tolerance grows like the width of the *deepest* co-adapted block, and this block
is an interval of layers: there is a partition of $\{0,\dots,L-1\}$ into intervals
such that the near-optimal path hypergraph is the union of the "all-of-a-block"
hyperedges of the partition.

The key insight is that a co-adapted unit is not a statistical cluster but a
*minimal transversal* of the near-optimal path family, and the block-realization
theorem shows minimal transversals of any size are tropically realizable — the
empirical question is only whether the realized ones are contiguous.

**Why now?** The hitting-set characterization turns a costly ablation sweep into a
hypergraph-covering question that can be tested with $O(L^2)$ pair ablations plus
a single fit, instead of $2^L$ subsets.
title: Transversal-number depth law

description:
**Conjecture.** A layer-wise pruning budget is safe (per-layer accounting is
valid) **iff** the induced path system satisfies the merge axiom up to an additive
slack $\delta$, and the total super-additivity of a network is bounded by
(number of layers) $\cdot\ \delta$.

The key insight is that the per-layer budgeting bound upgrades a *local* two-path
exchange property into a *global* bound on every subset at once, so a finite
certificate implies a statement over the whole Boolean lattice.

**Why now?** The $\delta$-relaxed merge axiom is checkable from pairwise data
already collected, and would give the first certificate of safe per-layer
budgeting rather than a heuristic.
title: Merge-axiom certification of prunability

description:
**Conjecture.** For a sorted attention profile that is asymptotically Zipf with exponent $s > 1$,
the knee at gate $\tau$ satisfies $k^*(n) = \Theta\big((1-\tau)^{-1/(s-1)}\big)$ uniformly in $n$,
so that two knee measurements at different gates determine $s$ up to $o(1)$.

*The key insight is* that the tail criterion converts the gate slack $1 - \tau$ into a tail-mass
budget, and for a power-law tail the inverse of the tail function is again a power law with
exponent $1/(s-1)$.

*Why now?* The tail criterion is already established and gate-general; the missing ingredient is a
matching lower bound via integral comparison.

**Test.** Establish matching upper and lower bounds for the Zipf knee and check numerically that
the measured grid ($0.9318$ / $0.9532$ / $0.9660$ / $0.9759$) pins $s \in [2.2, 2.3]$.

**If true:** a knee sweep measures a spectral exponent of the model's attention, turning the knee
into a model-internal observable. **If false:** the knee depends on more than the tail exponent,
and the profile must be described by at least two parameters.
title: Spectral-exponent read-off (the knee as a spectrometer)

description:
**Conjecture.** Restricting `horocycle_preserving_iff_translation` to `SL(2,ℤ)` yields:
a matrix in `SL(2,ℤ)` preserves every horocycle at `∞` iff it is `± transMat n` with
`n ∈ ℤ`, and the failure set — parabolics with a different fixed point, e.g.
`!![1,0;1,1]` — is in explicit bijection with `ℚ ∪ {∞}` via the continued-fraction
expansion of the fixed point.

**The key insight is** that the counterexample `parabolic_not_horocycle_preserving`
is not an anomaly but the generic member of a `ℚ`-indexed family: the fixed point of a
parabolic is the obstruction, and over `ℤ` fixed points are exactly cusps.

**Why now?** `parabolic_fixed_point` and `parabolic_conjugate_to_translation` are
already proved for real matrices; the integral statement needs only a denominator
argument, and it links this file to the catalog's continued-fraction modules.

description:
**Conjecture.** Among graphs formed from `n` triangles by identifying vertices while keeping a connected triangle-intersection pattern, the windmill graph extremizes the ratio between the number of six-emotion assignments and the number of minimum-palette assignments; characterize all equality cases.

The key insight is that the windmill’s independent outer pairs produce the exact ratio `2 · 10^n`, suggesting that overlap geometry controls a multiplicative entropy loss.

**Why now?** Closed formulas are available at both the minimum palette and the six-emotion palette, providing a calibrated baseline against which more complicated triangle gluing patterns can be tested.
