description:
**Conjecture.** In a temporal corpus filtration with bounded document size, an abrupt increase followed by decay in persistent second homology detects a sustained failure of local conformality more reliably than raw triangle or tetrahedron counts.

The key insight is that pairwise projection can fill a spurious triangle even when no triple witness exists, whereas persistence across the genuine hypergraph filtration records whether the resulting cavity survives subsequent documents.

**Why now?** Monotonicity of the corpus complex provides a valid filtration, and the explicit strict-loss example supplies the elementary mechanism from which a statistical change-point theory can be built.
title: Persistent detection of localized structural change

description:
The completed Lean development establishes the finite minimum-information-partition
semantics, existence of a minimizing partition, nonnegativity, the exact bridge
`Φ > 0 ↔ CutConnected` for nonnegative weighted directed networks, and transfer of
pointwise multiplicative cut approximations to `Φ`. These results are structural;
they do not assert an NP-hardness classification or a runtime bound for a concrete
algorithm. The items below identify the additional definitions and proofs required
for those claims.
title: Current formal boundary

description:
`Catalog/Bridges/GraphTheory/RipsLinkGuardedInterval.lean`

Global Betti numbers cannot separate manifolds from singular homology mimics; the mission's
Directions 4 and 5 therefore ask for *local* link data and for an interval-valued detector
with stable endpoints.  This file supplies the quantitative skeleton of both, again as a
chain in which each result uses the previous ones.

1. `ripsBall` / `linkDeg` — the closed vertex star of a sample point and its cardinality.
   `mem_ripsBall_iff_isRipsSimplex` identifies the ball with the set of vertices spanning
   an edge with `v`, so the link degree is an invariant of the Rips complex.
2. `ripsBall_mono`, `linkDeg_mono` — link degrees are monotone in the scale.
3. `IsDeltaMatching`, `dist_map_le`, `le_dist_map` — a `δ`-matching distorts distances by at
   most `2δ`: the local shadow of the distortion bound of cycle 1.
4. `Separated`, `map_injOn` — on an `η`-separated sample with `2δ < η`, a `δ`-matching is
   injective, so it cannot collapse links.  (Randomised search shows the hypothesis is not
   removable: collapsing matchings do destroy link degrees.)
5. `ripsBall_image_subset`, `linkDeg_le_of_matching` — hence
   `linkDeg S ε v ≤ linkDeg T (ε + 2δ) (f v)`.
6. `GuardedAt`, `GuardedAt_mono`, `GuardedAt_perturb`, `GuardedAt_perturb_ray` — the local
   guard "every vertex link has at least `k` vertices" is an up-set in the scale, is
   transported by a `δ`-matching with a `2δ` shift, and then holds on the whole ray.
7. `exists_diam_bound`, `guardedAt_diam`, `guardSet_nonempty`, `guardSet_bddBelow` — the
   guarded interval `guardSet S k` is a nonempty up-set bounded below by `0`, so its left
   endpoint `guardThreshold S k` exists and is nonnegative.
8. `guardThreshold_stability`, `guardThreshold_stability_abs` — **the endpoint of the
   guarded interval is stable**: under a `δ`-matching of an `η`-separated sample with
   `2δ < η`, `|guardThreshold T k − guardThreshold S k| ≤ 2δ`.  This is the Lipschitz
   endpoint stability asked for in Direction 5, for the link-degree guard.
9. `guardSet_pair`, `guardThreshold_pair` — the guarded interval of `{0, r} ⊆ ℝ` at `k = 2`
   is exactly `[r, ∞)`: the guard is not vacuous and the endpoint is computed exactly.
10. `linkDeg_shift_sharp` — the `2δ` shift of step 5 is optimal: for any `η < ε + 2δ` there
    is a `δ`-matching with `linkDeg S ε 0 = 2` but `linkDeg T η (f 0) = 1`.
title: Cycle 2 — Directions 4 and 5: link certificates and the guarded interval

description:
*Status of the previous C3 (now settled).* The former C3 asked for a five-party
entropy vector satisfying subadditivity, strong subadditivity, weak monotonicity
and monogamy while violating the cyclic inequality. Such a vector now exists in
machine-checked form: `EmergentGeometry.Sw` in
`Catalog/Novelty/CyclicIndependence.lean`, with
`cyclic5_independent_of_SA_SSA_WM_MMI` verifying all four families over the full
`32^3` space of disjoint mask triples and
`no_bulk_geometry_realises_Sw` showing no bulk graph can produce it. The
successor conjecture below asks how *tight* that obstruction is.

**Conjecture.** The cyclic inequality is a *facet* of the five-party holographic
entropy cone: there are `30` linearly independent entropy vectors, each realised
by an explicit finite bulk graph in the sense of `HoloModel`, that saturate
`entropy_cyclic5` with equality. Equivalently, the inequality cannot be written
as a positive combination of other valid holographic inequalities.

*The key insight is* that the contraction rule
`cyc c₀ c₁ c₂ c₃ c₄ = c₄ ∧ ¬c₂ ∧ (c₀ ∨ (c₁ ∧ ¬c₃))` is *bijective* on the
patterns it does not annihilate, and bijectivity of a contraction map is exactly
the condition for the associated inequality to be saturated on a full-dimensional
family of graph states.

*Why now?* The violating side is settled (`Sw_violates_cyclic5` gives a gap of
exactly one unit, and the four validity families are exhaustively checked), so
what remains is the saturating side: a rank computation over explicitly
constructed graphs, each of which is already expressible with the `HoloModel`,
`cutWeight` and `entropy` machinery in this project.

---
title: C3. Facet conjecture for the cyclic inequality

description:
**Conjecture.** For the group `Γ(t,a) ≤ SL(2,ℝ)` generated by `transMat t` and the
elliptic rotation `rotMat a` (the Cayley conjugate of `spbMat a`), there is an explicit
real-algebraic threshold `T(a)` such that `Γ(t,a)` is discrete and free of rank 2
exactly when `|t| ≥ T(a)`, and `T(a)` is the root of a polynomial whose coefficients
are the entries of `cayleyMat * rotMat a * cayleyMat⁻¹`.

**The key insight is** that after the Cayley transform both generators act on the unit
disc, where `discHoro` supplies a *single* scalar Lyapunov function: horocycle height
is exactly invariant under the parabolic and strictly monotone under the elliptic away
from the fixed point, so the classical ping-pong sets can be defined by inequalities
on `discHoro` rather than by ad-hoc fundamental domains.

**Why now?** `discHoro_cayleyC`, `discPar_preserves_discHoro` and
`normSq_cayleyC_lt_one` are already formalised with zero sorries, which is precisely
the analytic input a ping-pong argument needs; the remaining work is combinatorial
bookkeeping rather than new analysis.

---
title: Ping-pong discreteness for the parabolic–elliptic pair

description:
**Conjecture.** If the edges of a random graph carry *independent* complex phases
(each present edge `(i,j)` weighted by an independent unit-modulus random variable,
with `w_{ji} = \overline{w_{ij}}` relaxed to genuine independence), then the empirical
spectral distribution of the normalized adjacency matrix converges, as `n → ∞`, to a
rotationally invariant law supported on a full two-dimensional disk — in sharp
contrast to the line-locked fixed-amplitude model.

The key insight is that line-locking is caused entirely by the scalar–Hermitian
factorization `z·B`: all randomness sits inside a single Hermitian matrix, and one
complex scalar can only rotate and dilate a real spectrum. Breaking the shared phase
is therefore both necessary and, conjecturally, sufficient to recover circular-law
behaviour.

Why now? The exact obstruction has been isolated in closed form, so the search for a
circular law can be aimed precisely at the models that violate the factorization,
rather than at the undirected fixed-amplitude model where no such law can exist.
title: Two-dimensional spectra require broken phase symmetry

description:
**Conjecture.** For computable uniformly hyperbolic maps with rational cone certificates, the maximum certifiable shadowing horizon at fixed tolerance grows at least polynomially in the reciprocal local defect when all certificate arithmetic is performed at logarithmic precision.

The key insight is that dynamical existence, numerical conditioning, and computational complexity must be controlled simultaneously; none alone establishes a feasible shadowing algorithm.

**Why now?** The current geometric bound exposes an exponential obstruction for continuity-only arguments, making quantitative hyperbolicity the natural candidate mechanism for a polynomial complexity law.
title: Polynomial shadowing horizons from quantitative hyperbolicity

description:
**Conjecture.** On every compact subset of the half-plane `Re(s) > 1`, finite
prime occupation products converge uniformly to the Riemann zeta function when
the prime cutoff and occupation ceiling tend jointly to infinity.  The error
admits a uniform split into an omitted-prime contribution and the additive
occupation-tail contribution established by the finite model.

The key insight is that the occupation error is already controlled independently
of the omitted modes, so the two limits can be scheduled using separate majorants.

**Why now?** The finite geometric defect has an exact factorization and an
additive upper bound; only a compact-uniform prime-tail estimate remains to join
it to the classical Euler product.
title: Locally uniform joint removal of prime and occupation cutoffs

description:
**Conjecture.** A positive integral occupation sector can realize the gamma
factor of the completed zeta function, and its coupling to the prime sectors can
be chosen so that Mellin duality acts as the reflection `s ↦ 1-s`.

The key insight is that nonarchimedean truncation errors are now isolated and
controlled, leaving the local factor at infinity as a separate construction
rather than an unexplained correction.

**Why now?** The finite prime model supplies a stable multiplicative core and a
precise error budget against which an archimedean sector can be tested.
title: Archimedean completion as a distinguished boundary mode

description:
**Conjecture.** In every connected graph satisfying Baker–Norine Riemann–Roch, the involution `D ↦ K-D` preserves the set of divisor classes of degree `g-1` and rank at least `r`, and its fixed classes govern the sharp threshold for half-canonical existence.

The key insight is that at degree `g-1`, Riemann–Roch forces equality of the ranks of a divisor and its residual, producing a genuine duality on candidate witnesses. **Why now?** The residual-rank identity is available without any probabilistic assumptions and suggests reducing the search to paired or fixed divisor classes.
title: Residual pairing of extremal witnesses

description:
**Conjecture.** For finite frameworks whose attack graph is a directed cactus and has no self-attacks, the first Betti number of the preferred-generated complex equals the number of induced directed cycles satisfying an explicit parity-and-defence condition.

The key insight is that an attack cycle alone is insufficient: admissible defence determines whether its combinatorial trace survives filling by higher-dimensional preferred faces. **Why now?** The failure of the naive cycle interpretation shows that a restricted graph class and a defence-sensitive criterion are necessary and directly testable.
title: Exact characterization of attack cycles detected by first homology

description:
**Conjecture.** For a finite atom set, consistent signed states and single-atom revisions form an oriented cubical graph whose strongly connected components are classified by the set of atoms that have been assigned a sign.

The key insight is that a consistent state chooses at most one of two complementary vertices over each atom, while revision changes one coordinate without disturbing the others.

**Why now?** The exact equivalence between consistency and conflict-freedom supplies a combinatorial complex, and the revision invariant supplies a well-defined dynamics on its faces.
title: Revision paths and cubical state geometry

description:
Partition derivable statements by proof-theoretic complexity and define the entropy dimension of each stratum from its cumulative growth rate. Conjecture that natural calculi exhibit a nontrivial multifractal spectrum and that the union dimension is the supremum of the stratum dimensions, while intersections obey a strict dimension drop under an independence condition.

The key insight is that a single provable/unprovable ratio discards internal geometry, whereas a spectrum can distinguish several mechanisms of derivability with the same zero ambient density.

Why now? Positive ambient entropy coexisting with zero derivability density supplies the first robust separation needed to define and compare lower-dimensional strata.
title: Dimension spectrum of theorem families

description:
**Conjecture.** For a uniformly chosen endpoint extension among currently legal coordinate flips, the probability that a greedy snake in `Q_n` survives for `2^(α n)` steps has a sharp threshold at a constant `α` strictly greater than one half.

The key insight is that each accepted vertex excludes a radius-one neighborhood from future nonconsecutive use, so the extension process resembles random sequential adsorption with highly structured overlaps in the Hamming cube.

**Why now?** The census supplies long trajectories and many inequivalent optima, while the coding interpretation identifies the correct exclusion geometry. Together they make survival probabilities and overlap corrections measurable and mathematically testable.
title: Random extension threshold for long snakes

description: `FiniteStateIdentity.lean` proves decidability by reducing trace equivalence to a search over finite Boolean relations. A stronger development would implement the standard greatest-fixed-point refinement algorithm on `Finset (S × T)`, prove that it terminates, prove it computes the greatest bisimulation, and establish a polynomial running-time bound. This would turn the existence-level decision procedure into executable verified code.
title: Extract an explicit partition-refinement algorithm

description:
The current formalization identifies weighted integrated information exactly with a
finite minimum-cut functional. A faithful NP-hardness theorem for a richer IIT model
requires first fixing an input encoding, a decision problem, and a polynomial-time
reduction notion. Future work should define Boolean transition systems and probability
distributions with bit-size-aware encodings, then reduce a standard NP-hard partition
problem to the resulting normalized information partition problem. No complexity claim
is made without that infrastructure.
title: Complexity layer

description:
**Conjecture.** An algorithm that, given `N` and a hint interval of width `W`,
returns the true trace using `poly(log N)` filter evaluations exists **iff**
there is a `poly(log N)` algorithm that, given `N` and `t`, decides whether
`t² − 4N` is a perfect square for `Ω(W)` many `t` simultaneously (a "batch
square-detection oracle").

*The key insight is* the exact Fermat equivalence
`exists_factorisation_iff_isSquare_int`: the trace scan and the difference-of-
squares scan are the *same* predicate, so amplification of the hint is
equivalent to batching square detection over the window.

*Why now?* The equivalence is now a theorem over `ℤ` with no side conditions,
so the reduction can be stated as a clean formal statement about predicate
families rather than an informal analogy.
title: C3. Hint amplification is equivalent to a square-root oracle

description:
**Conjecture.** If an encoder may toss true coins and is only required to
decode correctly with probability `1 - δ` over its own randomness *and* a
uniform input, then some input still needs `≥ n - log₂(1/δ) - 1` bits.

*The key insight is* that a randomized scheme is a distribution over
deterministic schemes, and an averaging (first-moment) argument selects one
deterministic scheme with the same error, which our counting bound already
kills.
*Why now?* `prng_assisted_no_gain` already handles "best of `2^m` deterministic
schemes"; the missing step is a Markov-type averaging lemma over `Finset`
distributions, which Mathlib's `Finset.sum` API supports directly.
title: C2. Randomized compressors: a `δ`-error scheme still needs `n - log(1/δ)` bits

description:
**Conjecture.** Replace pairs of rationals by finite lexicographic towers `ℚ^(k+1)`. Successively projecting away the last coordinate yields a filtration of observations, and an event first becomes visible precisely at the earliest coordinate where its mass is nonzero. Every normalized nonnegative finite measure therefore determines a hierarchy of real-valued shadow measures.

The key insight is that the first-coordinate standard part proved here is the first stage of a general valuation-like filtration, not an isolated construction.

**Why now?** The two-coordinate model already exhibits exact normalization, finite additivity, and collapse to a Dirac measure; finite towers provide a concrete setting in which higher-order infinitesimal visibility can be tested.
title: Dirac collapse for finite lexicographic probability towers

description:
**Conjecture.** Any invariant that distinguishes all finite groups of order at most `N` must encode asymptotically more information than the prime-factor ledger and any bounded list of scalar invariants; an extension-action encoding can achieve this lower bound up to a polynomial factor in description length.

The key insight is that the enormous number of groups at prime-power orders arises from extension choices invisible to composition factors, so classification can be viewed as a compression problem constrained by group cohomology.

**Why now?** The smallest collision already proves that scalar chemistry is lossy. A census up to 2000 can compare concrete encoding lengths and expose which structural descriptors scale with the true diversity of groups.
title: Information-theoretic optimality of periodic-table invariants

description:
Conjecture: If messages are restricted by a sparse system of integer difference constraints and the output must equal a prescribed value, tropical preimage existence exhibits a dichotomy governed by the constraint graph: it is polynomial-time decidable on bounded-treewidth graphs and NP-complete on unrestricted graphs.

The key insight is that the unconstrained fiber has a complete coordinatewise certificate, so any genuine hardness must arise from coupling the coordinates rather than from the tropical minimum itself.

Why now? The exact fiber characterization isolates the inequalities and active equality that a constraint system must interact with, making both dynamic programming and hardness reductions sharply testable.
title: Complexity transition under coupled message constraints

description:
**Conjecture.** In a finite-time stochastic implementation of irreversible sorting, any
nonconstant work distribution on the support forces expected work strictly above
`kT log(n!)`, with a quantitative excess controlled by a divergence between forward and
reverse sorting trajectories.

The key insight is that logical entropy supplies only the quasistatic baseline; strict
convexity should convert work fluctuations into a positive surcharge. **Why now?** The exact
factorial baseline is available, so simulations can test candidate divergence bounds
without ambiguity about the equilibrium term.
title: Fluctuation penalty above the sorting Landauer bound

description:
**Conjecture.** For fixed `k ≥ 5`, the proportion of effective divisors of degree `g-1` having rank at least `k-1` tends to one as `n→∞`, uniformly over simple connected `k`-regular graphs.

The key insight is that high degree may make low-rank divisor classes sparse even in graphs with highly non-generic geometry. **Why now?** A uniform counting statement would simultaneously prove existence and explain why the eventual theorem should be insensitive to the detailed structure of the regular graph.
title: Uniform probabilistic witness principle

description:
**Conjecture.** For finite probabilistic transition systems, an ε-approximate structural analogy transports every modal formula of depth `d` with truth-probability error at most `dε`, and this linear bound is sharp.

The key insight is that the modal induction used for exact invariance should accumulate local correspondence defects once per nested transition observation.

**Why now?** Exact transport identifies the proof architecture and the modal box as the sole error-propagating case, making both the bound and candidate extremal examples concrete.
title: Quantitative Copycat stability

description:
**Conjecture.** A Markovian causal return operator that is contractive in Wasserstein distance on a complete space of probability laws has a unique invariant law, and every initial boundary distribution converges to it at a geometric rate. Deterministic fixed points appear as the Dirac-measure special case.

The key insight is that a self-consistent history can be generalized from a single state to a stationary distribution when microscopic causal response is noisy. **Why now?** Deterministic contraction already yields existence, uniqueness, and attraction; transport contraction is the natural probabilistic extension of precisely those three conclusions.
title: Stochastic Novikov consistency

description:
**Conjecture.** If research-community labels are defined independently of the citation complex, then no uniformly stable rule can recover them from first homology alone; recovery becomes possible only after adding vertex metadata or a generative assortativity assumption.

The key insight is that a cycle is an incidence pattern rather than a semantic object, so identical complexes can support incompatible assignments of mathematical schools.

**Why now?** Structural topology can now be cleanly separated from interpretation. This makes it possible to state identifiability assumptions explicitly and test whether metadata genuinely contributes information beyond graph connectivity.
title: Stability of semantic labels under topological perturbation

description:
**Conjecture.** Let a periodic Born-probability sequence have period `k`. For every observation length `N`, its Cesàro mean differs from its one-period mean by at most `2k/N` in total variation distance, and the optimal universal constant can be characterized from the extremal mass profile within one period.

The key insight is that division of `N` by `k` separates exact complete blocks from a single bounded remainder.

**Why now?** The complete-block identity isolates the only possible source of error, making a sharp finite-time mixing estimate the natural next step.
title: Sharp remainder bounds for arbitrary observation windows

description:
**Conjecture.** In the random graph process, with probability tending to one,
the first graph whose minimum degree reaches two is simultaneously the first
graph whose edges admit a two-regular cover of size `⌈Δ/2⌉`.

The key insight is that the incidence-capacity obstruction is already sharp
vertex by vertex, so the only remaining question is global: whether the process
has supplied enough connectivity to extend every controlled forest system at
once. Once minimum degree two removes the last local obstruction, the parity
defect that a completion must absorb is uniformly zero or one, leaving no room
for a second bottleneck.

**Why now?** The parity law isolates the incidence defect as exactly `Δ mod 2`,
reducing a delicate hitting-time statement to a single structured global
completion problem with a known local budget.
title: Optimal-cover hitting time in the random graph process

description:
**Conjecture.** For a finite atom set `A`, the strongly connected component of the revision
graph indexed by an assigned set `S ⊆ A` is isomorphic (as a graph with self-loops removed)
to the `|S|`-dimensional hypercube graph `Q_{|S|}`, so it has `2^{|S|}` vertices and
diameter `|S|`; the whole revision graph is the disjoint union of these cubes together with
the strictly monotone edges that enlarge `S`, and its condensation is order-isomorphic to
the Boolean lattice `2^A`.

*Falsifiable content.* Exhibit a component that is not a cube, or a pair of states in one
component whose revision distance exceeds `|S|`. `mutually_reachable_iff` fixes the vertex
sets of the components; the metric statement is untouched so far.
title: Component geometry: cube structure, diameter, and orientation

description:
`rom_union_bound` shows that an adversary precommitting to `Q` pairs `(a i, z i)` succeeds
with probability at most `Q/q` over the oracle answer vector.  Conjecture: in a cyclic group
of prime order `q`, equality holds **iff** the commitments `a i` are pairwise distinct (and
`Q ≤ q`); if two indices share a commitment, the success probability drops by at least
`1/q²`.  Falsifiable: exhibit a family with repeated commitments attaining `Q/q`.
title: C1. The `Q/q` random-oracle bound is tight, and `Q/q` is attained only by distinct commitments

description:
`penrose_stability` bounds the *unweighted* accumulated defect `∫ p` in terms of `δ`, at
the price of the constant `1/(1 - δU)²` that blows up as `δ → 1/|θ_model(t₀)|`.
The upper half of this conjecture is now **proved**: `penrose_weighted_stability` and its
congruence form `weighted_defect_le_of_almost_saturated` give
`∫₀^{t₀} p/θ² ≤ δ·U²` with no smallness hypothesis on `δ` at all.  What remains open is the
*matching lower bound*: that for every `δ ≥ 0` there is an admissible subsolution attaining
`∫₀^{t₀} p/θ² = δ·U²` (equivalently, that the extremal profile concentrates the whole
defect at the endpoint `t₀`), which would make the constant `U²` sharp and turn the
estimate into an equality characterisation.

**The key insight is** that `1/θ - t/m` is monotone with margin exactly `p/θ²`, so the
weighted defect — and not the defect itself — is the quantity the comparison controls; the
unweighted statement is a corollary that costs precisely the range of `θ`.

**Why now?** The upper bound is in place, so the remaining work is purely constructive:
the `riccatiSol` / `tanSol` building blocks already formalized supply the candidate
extremal profiles, and the numerics of `ComputationalEvidence.md §6` (second table) show
the ratio approaching `1` as the defect is concentrated near `t₀`.

**Falsifiable by:** a uniform gap — a constant `c < 1` such that every admissible
subsolution satisfies `∫ p/θ² ≤ c·δU²` — which would refute sharpness.  (The reverse
inequality `∫ p/θ² > δU²` is now excluded by theorem.)

---
title: Conjecture D′ (Stability with the defect measured in the affine, not weighted, norm)

description:
*Any algorithm that factors `N = pq` using only pairwise gcds of iterates of a
degree-`d` polynomial map mod `N` must perform `Ω(√p)` gcd operations, and the
`p + 1` pigeonhole bound of `exists_collision_mod_p` is tight up to the birthday
square root.*

**The key insight is** that the collision structure proved in
`Round7RhoNoiseFloor` is purely a statement about the reduced walk on `ℤ/pℤ`;
the birthday bound should therefore be provable as a counting statement about
functional graphs, independently of any randomness assumption.
**Why now?** The correlation lemma (`rhoZ_iterate_modEq`) and the extraction
lemma (`gcd_extract_of_dvd_sub`) are both formal, so the remaining step is a
purely combinatorial estimate on the rho-shaped functional graph.
title: Conjecture C (aggregation lower bound for correlated samplers)

description:
**Conjecture.** For every finite bulk geometry and boundary region `A`,
`entropy M A` equals the maximum value of a flow from `A` to the complementary
boundary subject to the capacity constraints given by the weights — and the
holographic inequalities proved here all follow from flow superposition.

*The key insight is* that the recombination arguments used for monogamy are
"cut-side" proofs; the corresponding "flow-side" proofs would replace 64-case
Boolean checks by explicit convex combinations of flows, which generalise to
inequalities with fractional coefficients.

*Why now?* The cut side is fully formalised (`cutWeight`, `entropy`,
`entropy_le_of_contraction`), so max-flow/min-cut can be attacked as a statement
about objects that already exist in the project rather than as new theory.

---
title: C4. Bit threads: min cut equals max flow in the emergent geometry

description:
**The key insight is** that replacing the fixed exponential base by a schedule that itself
depends on the level, `V (k+1) = A_k (V k) · V k` with `A_k` the `k`-th Ackermann level, should
push the representation length from `log*` down to `α`, the inverse Ackermann function, and the
characterization theorem predicts exactly when. **Why now?** The characterization
`bigO_logStar_iff_tower_le` is stated purely in terms of the weight sequence, so the same proof
skeleton transfers verbatim once `α` and its inverse-pair with the Ackermann hierarchy are
formalised.
title: Inverse-Ackermann analogue: two-parameter schedules

description:
**Conjecture.** The map (primitive Pythagorean triple) `↦` (short-leg knee at gate `τ`)
is, for each `τ`, a surjection onto an interval of integers `[1, K(τ)]` with
`K(τ) = ⌈log(1-τ) / log 0.708⌉`, and every fibre is a union of similarity classes closed
under scaling.

The key insight is that the knee factors through `legRatio`, which is a similarity
invariant, so the fibres of the knee are exactly unions of Euclid-parametrised families
`(m² - n², 2mn, m² + n²)` with `arctan` in a fixed window. **Why now?** The universal
budget `12` at gate `0.98` is proved and sharp; the remaining question is how the
budget partitions the triple family, which is a purely arithmetic question about density
of `(m²-n²)/(m²+n²)` in `(0, 1/√2]` and connects the attention-budget theory to the
Berggren-tree machinery already in the catalog.
title: Similarity-Class Spectrometry for Pythagorean Profiles

description:
**Conjecture.** For max-affine expressions with affine leaves in general position in dimension `n`, the codimension-two singular strata of the decision complex are bounded by the number of intersecting `(n+1)`-subsets of active leaves, rather than by a product of pair counts across network layers.

The key insight is that singularities arise from simultaneous affine ties in the realized upper envelope, not merely from pairs of neurons in an architecture. **Why now?** The width-one obstruction rules out the unguarded layerwise pair-product formula and points to active-set incidence as the correct combinatorial invariant.
title: Arrangement-sensitive singularity bound

description:
**Conjecture.** For every `n ≥ 2`, rooted spanning trees of `K_n`, recurrent chip configurations, and sink-reduced divisor classes admit mutually inverse bijections, all counted by `n^(n-2)`.

The key insight is that the burning algorithm should simultaneously certify reducedness and orient each nonsink vertex toward its first burning predecessor, producing a tree rather than merely a counting identity.

**Why now?** Reduced representatives are the proposed engine for Riemann–Roch, while the same representatives are classically enumerated by trees; a direct bijection would unify the rank theory with Cayley enumeration.
title: Spanning trees, parking functions, and divisor classes

description:
**Conjecture.** There is no universal affine formula depending only on the numbers of arguments, attacks, preferred extensions, and grounded arguments that equals the Euler characteristic of the preferred-generated complex; however, on finite acyclic frameworks the Euler characteristic is determined by the intersection poset of preferred extensions through inclusion–exclusion.

The key insight is that Euler characteristic depends on overlaps among maximal faces, information erased by the four proposed scalar counts. **Why now?** The two-isolated-argument obstruction rules out the original formula, while the antichain structure points to the intersection poset as the minimal richer invariant.
title: A corrected Euler–semantics identity

description:
**Conjecture.** For every fixed uniformity `r ≥ 3`, there are infinitely many pairs `(n,k)` for which the clique-incidence hypergraph has exactly `C(n,k)` distinct edges and its chromatic obstruction is asymptotically sharp at the first-moment threshold `2^(C(k,r)-1)`.

The key insight is that diagonal Ramsey avoidance is exactly Property B for a highly structured incidence hypergraph, so improvements should exploit collisions and codegrees among incidence edges rather than treating bad cliques independently. **Why now?** The exact bridge isolates the only place where the general sparse-hypergraph estimate loses information: the geometry of overlaps between families of `r`-subsets.
title: Exact Property-B incidence threshold

description:
**Conjecture.** For a growing random co-citation corpus, there is a sharp threshold at which every clique in the pairwise co-citation graph acquires a common document witness, and hence the higher-order corpus complex becomes equal to its flag completion.

The key insight is that equality of the two complexes is governed by one exact obstruction: pairwise compatibility without a global witness.

**Why now?** The three-theorem boundary example isolates the smallest obstruction, while the conformality criterion turns the disappearance of all such obstructions into a precise event whose threshold can be studied probabilistically.
title: Conformality thresholds in temporal co-citation hypergraphs

description:
**Conjecture.** The sharp frontier `reversible_history_iff` (history capacity `m ≥ maxFiber f`
is necessary and sufficient for a reversible implementation) has an *amortised* form: for
every `ε > 0` there is `n` and a reversible implementation of `f^{×n}` whose history register
has capacity `2^{n(condEntropyW f p + ε)}` when the inputs are i.i.d. `p`, and none with
capacity `2^{n(condEntropyW f p − ε)}`.

*The key insight is that* `condEntropy_prodMap` shows the expected history capacity is exactly
extensive while `log₂ maxFiber` is extensive but strictly larger (`strict_refinement_example`
tensored with itself), so the block-coding gap between the two is precisely the
`ℓ^∞ → ℓ^1` collapse of the asymptotic equipartition property.

*Why now?* Extensivity of all three quantities is now proved, so the only missing ingredient
is a typicality argument for the fiber-size distribution; the exact single-shot endpoints are
already pinned by `reversible_history_iff` and `condEntropyW_le_logb_maxFiber`.
title: B″. A conditional-entropy frontier for reversible implementations

description:
Define `D(n)` to be the least depth at which the spoke of index `n` appears, i.e. the least
length of an address `g` with `applyGens g root = eu m n` for some `m`.  Proved here:
`log₃(n/2) < D(n)`, and `D(n) ≤ n − 1` via the `mA` branch.  The conjecture is that the
lower bound is the truth for *every* `n`:

  `D(n) = Θ(log n)`,  i.e.  `D(n) ≤ K · log n` for an absolute constant `K`.

*The key insight is* that the coprime-pair tree of `mA_eu`/`mB_eu`/`mC_eu` is a disguised
Stern–Brocot tree, so the depth of the pair `(m, n)` is a sum of partial quotients of the
continued fraction of `m/n`, and `D(n)` is the minimum of that sum over the admissible
partners `m`.  A uniform `O(log n)` bound is therefore a Zaremba-type statement: it holds
as soon as every `n` admits a partner `m` whose continued fraction has bounded partial
quotients.  Conversely a failure of `D(n) = O(log n)` would produce an explicit family of
integers with no bounded-quotient partner.

*Why now?* The lower bound is proved (`spoke_index_depth_lower_bound`), both extremal
families are proved (`mA_iterate_root_eu` for the slow one, `mB_iterate_root_eu` together
with `pell_ge_two_pow` for the fast one — the Pell branch has all partial quotients equal
to `2`), and the intertwining reduces the general case to a purely continued-fraction
statement about the classical Stern–Brocot tree.  This also turns a question about a
*picture* into a question about Diophantine approximation, which is the kind of bridge the
rest of this development is built on.

---
title: Conjecture D (Sharp depth function of a spoke)

description:
**Statement.** For a finite `2`-dimensional nerve (regions, overlaps, triple
overlaps), `dim H¹ = |E| − |V| + 1 − rank(δ¹)`, where `δ¹` is the plaquette
coboundary; equivalently `dim H¹ = dim ker δ¹ − (|V| − 1)`.

**Evidence.** Verified in the two extreme cases proved here: the loop
(`rank δ¹ = 0`, `dim H¹ = 1`) and the discrete torus, where the `(m+1)(n+1)`
plaquette relations have rank `|V| − 1` and cut `dim H¹` from `|V| + 1` down to
exactly `2` (`finrank_torusH1`).

**The key insight is** that the drop from the graph Betti number to the true
Čech `H¹` is precisely the rank of the plaquette relation matrix, so counting
adversarial obstructions of a real cover is a rank computation, not a homotopy
computation.

**Why now?** `NerveBetti.finrank_nerveH1` already gives the `1`-dimensional case
by rank–nullity, and the same rank–nullity argument applies verbatim once `δ¹`
is defined; the torus file supplies the nontrivial test case.

**First Lean target.** Define `delta1 : (Edge → ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] (Plaq → ℝ)` and prove
`finrank (ker δ¹ ⧸ range δ⁰) + (|V| − 1) = finrank (ker δ¹)`.

---
title: C1. Plaquette rank conjecture (dimension of `H¹` for `2`-dimensional nerves)

description:
**Conjecture.** Within the Hopf-invariant family `T r` the area functional
`4π² r √(1 − r²)` has no interior minimizer, but the *Willmore-type* functional
`W(r) = ∫ (1 + H²)` restricted to this family is uniquely minimized at
`r = √2/2`; more generally, the Clifford torus minimizes area among Hopf-invariant
tori that are additionally **minimal surfaces**, and that constraint singles out
`r = √2/2` as the unique critical point of the area functional.

*The key insight is* that in the symmetry-reduced picture the area becomes the
single function `4π² r √(1−r²)`, whose unique interior critical point is a
maximum, so any correct extremality statement must be constrained; criticality,
not minimality, is what the Clifford parameter satisfies.

*Why now?* `area_eq` gives the reduced functional in closed form,
`clifford_unique_maximizer` fixes its shape completely, and
`clifford_unique_critical_point` shows `r = √2/2` is its only critical point, so testing any candidate
constrained functional is now a one-variable calculus exercise that can be
formalized directly.
title: Constrained extremality replacing the false Clifford minimality claim

description:
**Conjecture.** For every `r ≥ 2`, the `r`-fold self-similar refinement (each position
split into `r` positions of weight `p_i/r`) leaves the top-mass functional invariant:
`T_{rk}(split_r p) = T_k(p)`; and the invariance characterises self-similarity, i.e. a
profile family whose gaps are invariant under refinement at *two* coprime ratios is
asymptotically self-similar.

*The key insight is* that the dyadic proof (`SelectionExchange.topMass_split_le`) needs
only one combinatorial fact — a set of `2m` positions contains `m` positions carrying half
the mass — whose `r`-fold analogue is an equipartition statement: a set of `rm` positions
splits into `r` blocks of `m`, one of which carries at least `1/r` of the mass.

*Why now?* The dyadic case is proved with no positivity, ordering or normalisation
hypotheses, which is exactly the regime in which the equipartition argument generalises;
and the `r = 4` case is what the programme's `4×` context jumps actually measure.
title: C5. Refinement invariance beyond the dyadic case

description:
**Conjecture.** For every odd positive integer `n`, the angular spectrum selected by the `T(2,n)` Alexander polynomial is the disjoint union of primitive `2d`-th root strata over all divisors `d > 1` of `n`. The multiplicity-free channel count is therefore the sum of `φ(2d)` over those divisors.

The key insight is that the alternating Alexander polynomial satisfies `(X+1)A_n(X)=X^n+1`, whose cyclotomic factors are indexed by the divisors of `n`.

**Why now?** The prime case has been reduced exactly to coprimality modulo `2p`; composite parameters are the next falsifiable test of whether spectral splitting tracks arithmetic factorization.
title: Composite torus knots split into cyclotomic spectral strata

description:
**Conjecture.** For every finite graph and every positive `k`, quotienting cop configurations by permutations of the `k` cops preserves every bounded-horizon winning region and the stabilized winning region, while reducing the configuration factor from `|V|^k` to the number of multisets of size `k` drawn from `V`.

The key insight is that capture, simultaneous cop movement, and the cops-first forcing condition are invariant under relabeling indistinguishable cops. **Why now?** The iteration invariant isolates exactly the semantic facts that a quotient implementation must preserve, making a correctness proof and an empirical complexity comparison sharply testable.
title: Symmetry-reduced backward search

description:
**Conjecture.** The weighted determinant `det(z·B) = zⁿ·det(B)` vanishes for a fixed
nonzero `z` if and only if the underlying graph has no perfect matching of a certain
signed type; consequently, for random `G(n, p)` the probability that the weighted
matrix is singular exhibits the same threshold as the appearance of an isolated
vertex, independent of `z`.

The key insight is that the complex amplitude is a global unit that cannot create or
destroy singularity — singularity is a purely combinatorial property of the indicator
matrix `B`, so all `z`-dependence factors out through `zⁿ`.

Why now? The clean determinant factorization makes the `z`-independence of singularity
explicit, reducing a question about complex-weighted matrices to a classical question
about zero-one matrices with known threshold behaviour.
title: Determinant zeros track the underlying combinatorics

description:
**Conjecture.** Among the twists `E^d` with `d` a squarefree sum of two squares, the
sign of the functional equation (the root number) takes each value `±1` on a set of
positive density, and the density of `d` with root number `-1` is bounded away from
both `0` and `1`.

*The key insight is* that the sum-of-two-squares condition is a union of arithmetic
progressions cut out by splitting behaviour at the primes `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)`, and the
local root numbers of `E^d` are themselves governed by congruence conditions on `d`;
the two systems of congruences are independent enough that neither can force the
global sign.

*Why now?* The multiplicative closure and infinitude of the parameter set are now on
firm footing, so the density questions can be phrased entirely in terms of the
monoid of sum-of-two-squares integers rather than the geometry of the surface.
title: Root-number stratification of the sum-of-two-squares family

description:
**Statement.**  There is a function `f(ε)` such that if `H` is a poset whose
comparability graph admits an `ε`-uniform equipartition into `t` parts with all
pair densities in `(δ, 1-δ)`, then `H` contains every poset on
`f(ε)·log |H|` points as an induced subposet.

**The key insight is** that regularity converts the *global* counting statement
into a *local* embedding statement: a dense regular pair behaves like a random
bipartite graph, and a random bipartite graph on `2^{n/2}` vertices contains all
bipartite posets on `n` points with high probability.

**Why now?**  `comparability_regularity` puts Mathlib's Szemerédi Regularity
Lemma in exactly the poset-theoretic form required, and
`isBipartiteUniversalGraph_of_isBipartiteUniversal` shows that the passage
between posets and graphs is lossless for the height-`≤ 2` class, which is the
extremal class.

---
title: C4.  Regularity certifies universality

description:
**Conjecture.** For `m > 0` fixed, the gap function `t ↦ m·d(t,ℤⁿ)²` restricted
to shifts with denominator dividing `q` attains its minimum *exactly* at shifts
with a coordinate of exact denominator `q`, with value `m/q²`
(`Cycle2.gap_rational_shift` is the inequality); and for irrational `t` the
sequence of best rational approximations `p_k/q_k` of a coordinate produces gaps
`≍ m/q_k²`, so that `liminf q² · gap` over the convergents is positive iff the
coordinate is badly approximable.

*The key insight is* that `distZ_rat_ge` is the Diophantine statement
`‖a/q‖_ℤ ≥ 1/q` in disguise, so the spectral gap of a shifted lattice form is a
*continued-fraction invariant* of the shift, not merely a metric quantity.

*Why now?* Mathlib has continued fractions and the Hurwitz/Dirichlet
approximation theorems; combining them with `distZ_rat_ge` turns the qualitative
"off-lattice ⇒ positive gap" theorem into a quantitative badly-approximable
dichotomy with no new lattice theory required.
title: C3. Rational shifts are extremal: a Diophantine dichotomy for the gap

description:
**Conjecture.** For every family of exact filters `S_m ⊆ ℤ/m` computable from
`N mod m` in `poly(log m)` time, and every hint window of width `W`, the number
of surviving candidates is at least `W / ∏_{m ∈ 𝕄} m` whenever `∏_{m ∈ 𝕄} m ≤ W`.
Consequently, isolating a `k`-bit hint requires moduli whose product is `2^{Ω(k)}`,
hence total sieve work `2^{Ω(k / log k)}`.

*The key insight is* that exactness forces `S_m ⊇ T_m` (proved:
`traceSet_subset_of_exact`), and CRT makes the survivor count exactly
multiplicative (proved: `card_survivors_zmod`), so the only remaining freedom is
how large the modulus product is allowed to be.

*Why now?* The coupled case — filters that correlate the primes arbitrarily — is
already closed here (`coupled_exact_filter_card_ge`); what remains is the
complexity-theoretic bookkeeping of the sieve cost, which is a finite, formalisable
accounting exercise rather than a new mathematical idea.
title: C2. Free filters cannot beat the primorial, even with an oracle for `ω(N)`

description:
*For every prime `p ≠ q`, any graph invariant of the zero-divisor graph of
`ℤ/pqℤ` that is computable in time `polylog N` from `N` alone is a function of
`N` alone; equivalently, every invariant that separates two semiprimes of equal
size requires `Ω(min(p,q))` vertex queries.*

**The key insight is** that `Round7ZDG.vertex_gives_factor` shows a *single*
vertex already yields a factor, so an invariant is either blind (a function of
`N`) or its evaluation embeds trial division — there is no middle regime.
**Why now?** The graph is now a formal `SimpleGraph` with a proven bipartite
adjacency and degree sequence, so query-complexity statements about it can be
formalised directly on top of `Round7ZDGDegrees`.
title: Conjecture A (structural-witness dichotomy)

description:
**Conjecture.** For every node `(m,n)` the Berggren depth equals
`d_B(m,n) = Σ_i a_i − (number of "reflect" steps)`, where `a_i` are the partial
quotients of the *subtractive* expansion of `m/n` generated by the three parent rules
(`m < 2n`: reflect; `2n < m < 3n`: reflect-and-shift; `m > 3n`: subtract `2n`).
In particular `d_B(m,1) = (m−2)/2` exactly, and `d_B` is a function of the ratio `m/n`
alone in the sense that `d_B(m,n) = d_B(m',n')` whenever `m/n = m'/n'` (which for
coprime pairs is a tautology, so the content is the closed formula, not the invariance).

*The key insight is* that `berg_ratio_bound` (`m ≤ (2d+3)n`) is the crude shadow of an
exact identity: the Berggren descent **is** the slow (subtractive) Euclidean algorithm on
`(m,n)`, so its depth must be the sum of partial quotients, not their number.
*Why now?* The parent rule is already formalised (`berg_parent`) and the ratio bound is
proved; only the accounting of the three branch types against the continued-fraction
digits remains, and it is a finite induction over the same three cases.
title: C1. Exact Berggren depth = odd-continued-fraction length

description:
**Conjecture (barrier).** There is no predicate `P(N, w)` computable in time
`poly(log N, |w|)` such that, for every odd semiprime `N`, `P(N, w)` holds exactly for
the prefixes `w` of the Berggren (or Price) address of the `N`-node. Equivalently, the
address string is incompressible relative to `N`.

*The key insight is* that a prefix predicate would let one binary-search the address and
so factor in polynomial time, while the trade-off theorem
`m ≤ 2·s·(2d+3)²` shows the address *length itself* already encodes the size of Fermat's
scan — so the predicate would have to decide Fermat's cost from `N` alone.
*Why now?* The trade-off inequality gives the first formal handle: it converts "no
pruning rule" from folklore into a statement about a proved numerical coupling.
title: C3. No polynomial-size branch predicate for the `N`-node

description:
For fixed `N` and non-torsion `P`, the number of distinct primes dividing
`den x(P), …, den x(nP)` grows like `c·n²/log n` (up to constants), and all but `O(1)` of them
are primes of good reduction.

*The key insight is* that `log den x(nP) ~ 2ĥ(P)n²` by the theory of canonical heights, so the
total prime mass grows quadratically while the bad primes contribute `O(log n)`; the good
primes must therefore dominate asymptotically.

*Why now?*  The exact `2`-adic growth theorem in the catalog already gives the quadratic lower
bound along `2^k`-orbits, so a first, unconditional weak form ("infinitely many distinct good
denominator primes for a fixed curve") looks reachable without the full height machinery.
title: Conjecture C5 (density of good denominator primes)

description:
**Conjecture.**  For a family `W₁,…,W_m` of proper subspaces of an `n`-dimensional `𝔽_p`-space,
the failure probability at width `k` is exactly
`∑_{∅ ≠ S ⊆ [m]} (-1)^{|S|+1} p^{-k·codim(⋂_{j∈S} W_j)}`,
and in particular the curve `k ↦ P(cure)` is *strictly* increasing whenever `m ≥ 1`, closing the
gap between `failProb_antitone` (proved) and strict monotonicity (proved here only for `m = 1`).

*The key insight is* that inclusion–exclusion over the lattice generated by the obstructions
turns the failure count into a signed sum of exact subspace counts, each of which is already a
`p`-power — so the whole curve is a finite Dirichlet polynomial in `p^{-k}`, whose leading term
forces strict decrease of the failure mass.

*Why now?*  The exact single-subspace count (`card_tuples_mem`) and the union bound
(`failCount_le_sum`) are already formalised; only the alternating-sum bookkeeping over
`Finset (Fin m)` remains, and `Catalog/NumberTheory/SubspaceCounting.lean` supplies the
Gaussian-binomial machinery for the intersections' codimensions.
title: C1. Exact multi-obstruction curve via subspace Möbius inversion

description:
**Conjecture.**  Let the `k` exclusive directions be drawn from *any* exchangeable distribution
on `V^k` whose one-dimensional marginal has full support.  Then the reliability curve is still
monotone and still satisfies `P(cure at k) < 1` for every `k` — i.e. `IsMonotoneRamp` is
robust to the uniformity assumption, and no distributional assumption can create a cliff.

*The key insight is* that the prefix-fibration argument of `failCount_succ_le` never uses
uniformity, only that the failure event is closed under deleting a coordinate; positivity comes
from the atom at `0`, which any full-support marginal charges.

*Why now?*  The combinatorial core (`failCount_succ_le`) is proved; generalising it means
replacing counting measure with an arbitrary product/exchangeable measure, for which Mathlib's
`MeasureTheory` product API suffices.
title: C5. Cliffs are impossible for any exchangeable draw model

description:
**Conjecture.** Let `h(t) = 1/log(1/t)` be a gauge function.  Then the generalised
Hausdorff measure `H^h(P)` is finite and positive iff the primes have positive
"logarithmic density" in the sense of Chebyshev; and `H^h(T) > 0` for the twin
subfractal `T` iff the twin prime conjecture holds with the Hardy–Littlewood
density.

*The key insight is* that dimension is the wrong functional: the prime fractal has
`dim_H = 0` and `dim_B = 1`, so all power gauges `t^s` are degenerate on it, whereas a
logarithmic gauge is exactly calibrated to `d(p, next p) ≍ 1/(p (log p)^2)`.

*Why now?* `twin_dist_le` and `zero_mem_closure_iff_infinite` show the twin primes
enter the metric picture only through the single accumulation point `0`;
`primeFractal_isolated` shows that no power-law dust exists anywhere else.  A gauge
measure is the first functional that can distinguish the twin subfractal from a
random sparse subfamily.
title: C3. Twin primes are invisible to *every* dimension, but visible to gauge functions

description: Define representations of inputs and outputs, effective initial conditions, admissible real constants, observation precision, and time bounds. Without these restrictions, a continuous system may hide a noncomputable set in an initial condition or parameter rather than compute it. A meaningful conjecture should distinguish oracle information from dynamics.
title: Super-Turing hypothesis as a precise separation

description:
**Conjecture.** Up to permutation, the only nonzero integral solutions of
\(x^3+y^3+z^3=1729\) with \(\max(|x|,|y|,|z|)\le 207\) are
\((13,-7,-5)\); at height 215 a second orbit appears, represented by
\((-215,98,208)\).

The key insight is that the minimal orbit is isolated by a large height gap, so
the geometry of the cubic surface may impose stronger sparsity than congruence
conditions alone suggest. **Why now?** The sharp classification through height
13 provides a certified base case, while the next candidate orbit gives a
precise falsifiable boundary for an expanded search and descent argument.
title: Complete the integral-point census at moderate height

description:
**Conjecture.** If a permutation satisfies `σ(n)/n → 1`, then `p_{σ(n)}/p_n → 1`; conversely, prime-ratio convergence to one forces `σ(n)/n → 1`.

The key insight is that the asymptotic equivalence `p_n ∼ n log n` should transport relative index displacement exactly to relative prime displacement, including along nonmonotone permutations.

**Why now?** This would identify the full well-behaved class by a purely combinatorial condition and clarify why adjacent swaps work while random macroscopic rearrangements do not.
title: Local-displacement characterization under prime asymptotics

description:
**Conjecture.** For every positive `η` there is a positive `δ` such that every weakly `D₆`-free family of subsets of `[n]` with size within `δ` middle layers of the optimum differs, on at most `η` middle layers, from a four-layer family governed by a closure operator of bounded local complexity.

The key insight is that six distinct intermediate sets between bottom and top nearly saturate the proper part of a three-dimensional Boolean interval, so near-extremality should force a coherent local closure rule.

Why now? The interval obstruction identifies the local configuration that must be suppressed, making a local-to-global stability program testable.
title: Stability for large weakly `D₆`-free families

description:
**Conjecture.** For each `m ≥ 2` there is a finite "collision signature" `σ_m(a) ∈ ℤ^m`,
computable from the counts `#{(x,y) : x^m + a x = y^m + a y}`, such that the curve
`y² = x³ + a x + b` is supersingular for all `b` iff `σ₃(a)` takes one of two explicit
values, generalising `cube_bijective_iff_char_neg_three`.

**The key insight is** that supersingularity of a whole *line* in the family is equivalent
to the vanishing of one vertical second moment, and that this moment is a linear function
of a collision count — a combinatorial quantity that never mentions the curve.

**Why now?** The equivalence "cubing bijective ⟺ `χ(-3) = -1`", proved here from a
collision count alone, is the `m = 3` case, and it already produced supplementary quadratic
reciprocity for `-3` as a corollary; the same argument shape should run for `x^m`.
title: C4. A purely combinatorial criterion for supersingularity in every residue class

description:
> **Conjecture.** For a semiprime `N = pq`, every function `g : ℤ/Nℤ → ℂ`
> computable from `N` alone by a bounded-depth arithmetic circuit has
> exponentially small correlation with the indicator of the coset structure
> `{x : gcd(x, N) > 1}`; consequently no bounded-depth arithmetic algorithm can
> produce a congruence of squares.

*The key insight is* that `congruence_of_squares` makes the *exploitation* step
free, so any lower bound must attack the *production* step; and the production
step is precisely a correlation-with-a-hidden-subgroup question, which is a
rank/Fourier-analytic statement rather than a number-theoretic one.

*Why now?* This cycle isolated the exploitation step as a proved, unconditional
reduction, so the remaining difficulty is now localised to one clean statement.
The correlation formulation also matches the DFT machinery (`ZMod.dft`) already
imported here.

**Falsifier.** A bounded-depth arithmetic circuit family over `ℤ/Nℤ` with
inverse-polynomial correlation with `gcd(x,N) > 1`.

---
title: C4. Structural orthogonality as a rank condition (`OrthogonalityRank`)

description:
`mutualInfo_eq_entropy_sub_condEntropy` proves the identity `I(X;Y) = H(Y) − E_k[H(Y | X = k)]`
in general, and `pinned_iff_commutator_invariant` / `mutualInfo_eq_zero_iff_indep` identify the
two extreme values of the pinned fraction.  The extremal half is a theorem too: for a *balanced*
observable (an index-two congruence condition, e.g. the Jacobi sign) and a fork of density
`d ≤ 1/2`,

```
I(X ; Y) ≤ binEntropy d − binEntropy (2d) / 2 = C(d) ,
```

with equality exactly for the forks supported inside a single coset
(`mutualInfo_le_singleCoset`, `mutualInfo_singleCoset_eq`, restated as `mutualInfo_le_cosetProfile`).
The analytic engine is sub-additivity of the binary entropy (`binEntropy_add_le`).
title: C1 — pinned fraction and extremal forks *(closed)

description:
Let `Oracle(N, P, n) = den x(nP)`.  For odd squarefree `N`, every value returned for `n`
coprime to `N` is a `N`-unit, and the multiset of prime valuations of the oracle outputs is
determined by `(N, P)` alone.  Hence no algorithm making `poly` oracle queries with
`gcd(n, N) = 1` can output a nontrivial factor of `N` with non-negligible probability.

*The key insight is* that C1 turns the "no factor appears" theorem into an information-theoretic
independence statement: the oracle factors through data that is invariant under all
factorisations of `N`, so it is simulable without knowing `p` and `q`.

*Why now?*  The invariance half is already a theorem (`factorisation_barrier`), and the
`N`-unit half is proved for `n = 2^k` this cycle; C1 supplies the missing indices, after which
the barrier statement is a formal consequence rather than a heuristic.
title: Conjecture C4 (a quantitative barrier: denominator oracles are factoring-useless)

description:
**Conjecture.** Define the *logarithmic dimension defect*
`δ(P) = lim_{m→∞} (1 − log N(m)/log m) · log m / log log m`.
Then `δ(P) = 1` for the prime fractal, `δ = 0` for every self-similar set of
dimension `1`, and `δ(A) = 1` for `A = {1/log n : n ∈ ℕ}` as well.

*The key insight is* that `log N/log m = 1 − log log m/log m + o(1/log m)` whenever
`N(m) ≍ m/log m`, so the *rate* at which the box dimension approaches `1` — invisible
to the dimension itself — is a sharp invariant separating "arithmetically thin"
dimension-1 sets from geometric ones.

*Why now?* This is exactly the quantity the mission's numerical test would have
measured (0.84 at `10^7`, 0.88 at `10^12`); `eventually_boxCount_le` and
`eventually_boxCount_ge` already pin `1 − log N/log m` between
`log log m/log m` and `4 log log m/log m` up to constants.
title: C2. The logarithmic defect is a genuine second-order invariant

renormalisation steps with block-growth law `r`, so the threshold says that a coarse-graining
scheme reaches system size `n` in `O(log* n)` steps exactly when its block growth is at least

description:
**Conjecture.** With `p = c·log n/n` and `c > 1`,
`Prob p {s | (graphOf s).Connected} - Prob p {s | ∀ v, ∃ u, (graphOf s).Adj v u} → 0`;
i.e. above the threshold, *the only* obstruction to connectivity is an isolated vertex.

This strengthens the pair (`prob_exists_isolated_tendsto_zero`,
`prob_connected_log_tendsto_one`): the current proofs bound both quantities separately,
whereas the conjecture asserts the events differ with vanishing probability.  It is
falsified by exhibiting `c > 1` and a positive `ε` with a subsequence on which the gap
exceeds `ε`.  A proof should follow by refining `prob_disconnected_le` to cuts of size
`2 ≤ k ≤ n/2` only, whose total contribution is `O(n^{-δ})` for `δ = δ(c) > 0`.
title: C2. Sharp threshold for minimum degree ≥ 1 versus connectivity coincide

description:
**Conjecture.** `max_{a,b} a(a,b)²` over `F_p` is attained at some pair with `b² = a³`
(equivalently `j = 0` or `j = 1728` up to twist) for infinitely many `p`, and never
exceeds `4p - 3`.

**The key insight is** that `exists_frobTrace_sq_ge` gives the lower bound `q - 1` for the
maximum, while the curves with extra automorphisms are exactly the ones whose traces are
constrained by the twist involution `frobTrace_twist` to lie in a thin set — so extremal
behaviour and extra symmetry should coincide.

**Why now?** Both endpoints are now formal: the existence of a large trace is proved from
the second moment, and twisting is proved to negate the trace, so the conjecture is a
statement about the interaction of two theorems already in the library, testable by
exhaustive kernel computation for `p ≤ 40`.
title: C5. Extremal traces are attained on the diagonal `b = a`

description:
**Conjecture.** `sup_n I_pair(n) = 4/3 + Σ_{p odd prime} p²/(p²−1) · I_pair(p) ≈ 2.41738`,
the supremum is never attained, and the restriction to odd `n` has supremum
`≈ 1.08405`.  In particular there is **no** `n` with `I_pair(n) ≥ 2.42`, while
the cap `1` is exceeded by infinitely many `n`.

*Status.* Numerical (summation over primes below `2·10⁶`; the tail is `O(log X / X log 2)`).
The lower half of the statement is partly formal: additivity plus
`one_lt_Ipair_odd_order` gives infinitely many above-cap orders.

*The key insight is* that additivity turns `sup I_pair` into a **sum over all
prime powers of a convergent series**, because the prime-order channel decays like
`I_pair(p) = (log₂p + 2/ln 2)/p² + O(log p / p³)`: an information channel that
grows without bound in the number of states can still have bounded mutual
information, and here the bound is a prime-zeta-type constant.

*Why now?* Conjecture C1 supplies the prime-power values, `Ipair_prime` the prime
values and `Ipair_prime_le_envelope` an already-formal `O(1/p)` envelope; upgrading
that envelope to the true `O(log p / p²)` order is a one-variable calculus estimate
and immediately yields summability, hence boundedness.
title: C2. `I_pair` is globally bounded, with an explicit irrational supremum

description:
**Conjecture.** For a fixed graph `H` with `m(H) = max_{H' ⊆ H, v(H')>0} e(H')/v(H')`
and `p_n = ω(n) · n^{-1/m(H)}` with `ω → ∞`, the number of copies of `H` in `G(n,p_n)`
is positive with probability `→ 1`, while for `ω → 0` it is `0` a.a.s.

The `→ 0` half is already implied by `first_moment_threshold`; the `→ 1` half needs the
second-moment estimate `Var X = O((E X)^2 / Φ)` with `Φ = min_{H'} E[X_{H'}]`, which can
be assembled from `ErdosRenyi.secondMoment_subgraphCount` (exact overlap sum) plus
`subgraph_count_pos_whp`.  Falsifiable by a single `H` for which the claimed exponent
`1/m(H)` is wrong (e.g. by simulation for `H = K_4` with a pendant edge).
title: C3. Threshold for a fixed subgraph `H` at `n^{-1/m(H)}`

description:
**Conjecture.** For every `ε > 0` the set of primes `p ≡ 1 (mod 4)` with
`W(p)² > (1-ε)·4p` has positive relative density; equivalently, the odd leg `a` of
`p = a² + b²` satisfies `b = O(p^{ε})` for a positive-density set of primes.

*The key insight is* that near-attainment means `p = a² + b²` with `b` tiny, i.e. `p`
lies just above a square — so the conjecture is a statement about primes of the form
`a² + b²` with `b` bounded, closely tied to Landau–Ramanujan and to primes represented by
thin quadratic families.

*Why now?* `weil_floor_near_attained` proves attainment at 97.7 % for `p = 173`;
`jacobsthal_identity` converts the analytic question into a purely Diophantine one about
the two-square decomposition, where sieve technology applies.

---
title: C4. Weil-floor attainment has positive density

description:
**Conjecture.** `covTop e → (2 log 2 − 1)/4 ≈ 0.09657` as `e → ∞`.  Rescaling `p = 2^{k-1}x`,
`q = 2^{k-1}y` sends the balanced support to `S = {(x,y) ∈ [1,2]² : x ≤ y}` (area `1/2`), the event
`p_{k-2} = 1` to `A = S ∩ {x ≥ 3/2}` (area `1/8`, so `P(A) = 1/4`) and the carry-out event to
`B = S ∩ {xy ≥ 2}` (area `1 − log 2`, so `P(B) = 2(1 − log 2)`); since `A ⊆ B`, the limiting
covariance is `P(A)(1 − P(B)) = (2 log 2 − 1)/4`.

*The key insight is* that `hiSet ⊆ topSet` is a *scale-invariant* condition once `p = 2^{k-1}x`,
`q = 2^{k-1}y`, so the covariance is a Riemann sum for a fixed planar area functional and must
converge, with the observed decreasing sequence `0.222, 0.180, 0.138, 0.118, 0.107` as its
approximants.

*Why now?* `covTop_pos` already proves positivity for all `e` by a purely combinatorial argument;
the limit statement needs only a lattice-point-counting error term, well inside reach.

title: C3. Sharp constant for the top-bit covariance

description:
**Conjecture.** Let `N` be odd and squarefree and let `k` be coprime to `λ(N)`,
so that `x ↦ x^k` permutes `Z/NZ`.  Then

`N − #cycles(x ↦ x^k)` is odd  ⟺  `k ≡ 3 (mod 4)` and `#{p ∣ N : p ≡ 1 (mod 4)}`
is odd.

In particular the sign of every power permutation is computable in polynomial
time from `N` and `k` *given the factorisation-free data alone*, so the power
family — the natural non-affine enlargement of the attack surface — leaks
nothing either.

*The key insight is* that a CRT product of permutations of odd-cardinality
factors has sign equal to the product of the signs
(`sign(σ₁ × σ₂) = sign(σ₁)^{|X₂|}·sign(σ₂)^{|X₁|}` with both exponents odd), so
the composite sign is the product of the prime signs, and the prime sign is
already a theorem here (`power_readout_sign_law`): it is nontrivial exactly for
`p ≡ 1 (mod 4)` and `k ≡ 3 (mod 4)`.

*Why now?* The prime case and the whole orbit-count transport theory are proved
(`cycleCountOf_pow_prime`, `numOrbits_permCongr`, `numOrbits_optionCongr`); only
the CRT step is missing.  Exploratory enumeration of all odd squarefree `N < 200`
and all `k < 30` for which `x ↦ x^k` is a permutation found no violation (this is
exploratory computation, not a verified check).  A single counterexample pair
`(N, k)` would refute it.
title: C1. The power readout stays factorisation-free at composite moduli

description:
**Conjecture.** For every prime `p` and every `k ≥ 1`,

  `I_pair(p^k) = (1 − p^(−2k)) · p²/(p²−1) · I_pair(p)`,

equivalently `I_pair(2^k) = (4/3)(1 − 4^(−k)) = (4^k − 1)/(3·4^(k−1))`.

*Status.* **Proved on both evaluated ladders, open in general.**  The exact values
`I_pair(2) = 1`, `I_pair(4) = 5/4`, `I_pair(8) = 21/16`, `I_pair(16) = 85/64`,
`I_pair(32) = 341/256` and `I_pair(3) = log₂3 − 10/9`,
`I_pair(9) = (10/9)log₂3 − 100/81`, `I_pair(27) = (91/81)log₂3 − 910/729` are all
`sorry`-free Lean theorems (`Ipair_val_2/4/8/16/32`, `Ipair_val_3/9/27`; the two
new ones, at `32 = 2^5` and `27 = 3^3`, are in
`Catalog/Shared/CyclicTypeChannelPrimePower.lean`).  Against them the closed form
is a theorem on the evaluated range: `Ipair_two_pow_closed_form` gives
`I_pair(2^k) = (4^k − 1)/(3·4^(k−1))` for `1 ≤ k ≤ 5`, and
`Ipair_three_pow_closed_form` gives `I_pair(3^k) = (1 − 9^(−k))·(9/8)·I_pair(3)`
for `1 ≤ k ≤ 3`.  Beyond that it is verified numerically to `10⁻⁹` for
`p = 2, k ≤ 7` and `p = 3, 5, 7, k ≤ 3`, and open for general `p, k`.

*The key insight is* that the `p^k`-box splits along the valuation filtration
`v(a) = 0, 1, …, k`: the type of `a` is `p^(k−v(a))`, the residue `a + b` has
valuation `min(v(a), v(b))` off the diagonal, and the entire conditional law is a
`p`-adically self-similar copy of the `p^(k−1)` law — the geometric factor
`1 − p^(−2k)` is exactly the sum of that self-similarity.

*Why now?* The prime case is already a theorem in complete generality
(`Ipair_prime`), and its proof is organised by the fibres of the residue map; the
prime-power case needs only the valuation refinement of the same fibre
decomposition, with the induction step supplied by the self-similarity above.
title: C1. The prime-power closed form

description:
**Conjecture.** Sorting independent blocks has additive minimum logical-erasure work, while
any reversible implementation requires a history space whose cardinality is the product of
the block factorials; equality should characterize protocols with no cross-block garbage.

The key insight is that entropy adds while reversible state counts multiply, suggesting a
sharp bridge between product decision trees and tensorized thermodynamic resources. **Why
now?** Existing composition and history-space results provide the one-block ingredients,
while the equality case remains open and falsifiable on small block systems.
title: A thermodynamic direct-sum theorem for independent sorting tasks

description:
For essentially small categories whose sets of isomorphism classes carry probability measures, conjecture a measurable chain rule for functors with countable or standard Borel fibers. Infinite information loss should occur exactly when the conditional fiber entropy diverges on a set of positive output measure, rather than merely when one infinite fiber exists.

The key insight is that infinity is a property of a weighted conditional expectation, not a consequence of cardinality alone.

Why now? Finite uniform fibers exhibit the logarithmic law exactly, while the failure of unweighted counting on large categories pinpoints the measure-theoretic hypotheses needed for an infinite extension.
title: Measured entropy for infinite categories

description:
**Conjecture.**  For every prime `p ≥ 11` and every `N ∈ 𝔽_p^×`,
`{x + y + z : xyz = N} = 𝔽_p`; and `p = 3, 5, 7` are the only exceptions.

*Status.* Verified for `p ≤ 19`; formally verified at `p = 11`
(`tripleSumSet_full_eleven`) with the exception at `p = 5` also formal
(`tripleSumSet_not_full_five`).

*The key insight is* that `s` is a three-factor sum iff the quartic
`w² = z²(s-z)² - 4Nz` has a point with `z ≠ 0`; this is a genus-1 curve, so the
Hasse–Weil bound gives `p + O(√p)` points and forces solvability once
`p ≥ 11`.

*Why now?*  It isolates exactly *why* the trace is special: the two-factor
constraint is a conic (one quadratic condition, one bit), the three-factor
constraint is an elliptic curve (no condition at all beyond small `p`).  Formalising
it would need a Hasse-type bound for a specific quartic family — a realistic
target, since the family is completely explicit.
title: C2.  The arity-3 collapse has threshold exactly 11

description:
**Conjecture.** With `L_p := p²/(p²−1) · I_pair(p)`,

  `{n : I_pair(n) > 1} = { n : Σ_{p^k ‖ n} L_p (1 − p^(−2k)) > 1 }`,

and the smallest **odd** member of this set is `3³ · 5² · 7 · 11 · 13 · 17 · 19 · 23 = 5 019 589 575`
(value `≈ 1.00540`), while the smallest member overall is `4`.

*Status.* The description is a theorem *given* C1 (additivity is proved); the
extremal claim is a knapsack computation over prime-power multisets, currently
numerical.  The proved odd witness `300 840 735 195` is `≈ 60×` larger than the
conjectured minimum.

*The key insight is* that above-cap-ness is a **subset-sum condition on the prime
factorisation**, with weights that decay like `log₂p / p²`; the optimisation is a
knapsack whose "value per unit `log n`" ranking is `L_p / log p`, decreasing in `p`,
so the extremal orders are products of an initial segment of primes with small
exponent corrections at `3` and `5`.

*Why now?* Deciding membership for any *specific* `n` is already mechanical
(additivity plus `Ipair_prime`), as the odd witness demonstrates; only the
minimality claim needs the prime-power values, i.e. C1.
title: C3. Exact description of the above-cap set

description:
**Conjecture.** For `k ≥ 2`, the set `P_k = {(1/log p, 1/log(p+2), …) : p, p+2, … prime}`
⊆ `ℝ^k` has Hausdorff dimension `0` and box-counting dimension `1` if and only if the
Hardy–Littlewood `k`-tuple conjecture holds for that tuple; otherwise the box
dimension drops below `1`.

*The key insight is* that in the diagonal-collapsing coordinates the `k`-tuple set is
a graph over a subfamily of primes, so its box count is exactly the counting function
of the tuple — turning a dimension statement into an equivalent of a counting
conjecture, in the same way as `twin_conjecture_iff_zero_mem_closure` does for `k = 2`
at the level of a single point.

*Why now?* The `k = 1` machinery (`boxCountSet`, the separation lemma
`boxIndex_lt`, the Chebyshev lower bound) is formalised and generalises verbatim to
product boxes; only the counting input changes.
title: C5. Higher-dimensional prime fractals and the `k`-tuple conjecture

description:
Conjecture: For tropical circuits whose acceptance region is defined by output thresholds, mining difficulty is controlled by the recession cone of the corresponding polyhedral complex; finite expected search requires the nonce trajectory to avoid every nontrivial recession direction.

The key insight is that the proven coordinate update is a recession direction of a hash fiber, so unrestricted nonce motion can produce entire rays of equivalent candidates rather than pseudorandom trials.

Why now? The collision construction supplies an explicit recession direction, while the concavity bridge links tropical evaluation to the geometry needed to classify threshold regions.
title: Mining thresholds and recession cones

description:
**Conjecture.** Under any regenerative random-permutation model with finite mean cycle-block length, the prime ratio converges almost surely to one; under heavy-tailed block laws of infinite mean, convergence exhibits a sharp tail-index transition.

The key insight is that finite cycles cause only local index displacement, while heavy-tailed blocks can create infinitely many macroscopic jumps.

**Why now?** The million-prime experiment disproves naive finite-uniform typicality and shows that a meaningful density question must begin by specifying a coherent infinite probability model.
title: Probability laws for explicit random infinite permutations

description:
For the directed centered model, conjecture a high-probability lower bound on the least singular value of `A-wI`, uniform for `w` outside a slightly enlarged circular-law disk, with constants depending explicitly on `p` and `|z|`.

The key insight is that eigenvalue plots alone cannot distinguish genuine circular behavior from nonnormal pseudospectral instability; least-singular-value control supplies the missing robust criterion.

Why now? The undirected model is exactly normal, so replacing it by a directed model introduces nonnormality as a new phenomenon that must be quantified rather than inferred visually.
title: Quantitative pseudospectral separation

description:
Construct datasets whose overlap nerve is not flag and quantify the failure of pairwise consistency to detect incompatible triple overlaps. Conjecture that the minimal order of compatibility checks needed for exact recovery equals one plus the largest dimension of a minimal nonface of the nerve.

**The key insight is...** pairwise overlap information reconstructs every higher face precisely in the flag case, making minimal nonfaces the natural certificates of undetected incompatibility.

**Why now?** The flag-nerve bridge supplies an exact boundary between graph-based consistency methods and genuinely higher-order methods.
title: Higher-order compatibility beyond pairwise overlaps

description:
For composable functors between finite skeletal categories, define object loss from the uniform distribution on source objects and conditional loss relative to the intermediate image. Conjecturally, the loss of the composite is the first loss plus the expected loss of the second stage precisely when the intermediate fibers satisfy a conditional-uniformity law.

The key insight is that the proved finite chain rule should admit a relative version analogous to conditional entropy, but composition requires weighting each intermediate object by its actual pushforward probability.

Why now? The separation of output entropy from expected logarithmic fiber size isolates the two terms that a compositional theorem must track and reveals exactly where naive additivity can fail.
title: A chain rule for composable finite functors

description:
Find a family of finite graph-zeta factors whose normalized zero measures converge to a zeta-like spectral measure, and determine whether their rational reciprocal harmonics converge to a canonical regularized reciprocal-zero sum.

The key insight is that finite graph spectra provide exact algebraic identities and critical-circle theorems, while a limiting process may retain enough structure to illuminate infinite zeta spectra.

Why now? Exact local factorization and harmonic identities are available at every finite stage, making convergence and loss of rationality concrete falsifiable questions.
title: Graph-to-Riemann limiting bridge

description:
**Conjecture.** For every well-founded dependency network, the least ordinal rank strictly decreasing along edges is invariant under edge subdivision and nonincreasing under semantics-preserving quotient maps; moreover, it exactly measures the minimum hierarchy height required to eliminate all apparent cycles.

The key insight is that untangling may be quantified by ordinal height rather than treated as a binary property, linking dependency analysis to termination complexity.

**Why now?** Natural-valued ranks already prohibit every finite cycle, and the next testable step is to determine whether least ordinal ranks behave functorially under standard transformations of dependency networks.
title: Ordinal Height Measures the Cost of Untangling

description:
**Conjecture.** A partial-recursive oracle-machine model admits a concrete jump operator whose iterates form a strict order embedding of the natural numbers into the Turing degrees.

The key insight is that diagonal complementation supplies the combinatorial obstruction, while a universal relativized machine supplies the effective coding needed to turn that obstruction into reducibility statements.

**Why now?** The sequence-level diagonal theorem and the existing abstract strict jump hierarchy delimit exactly what must be added: a universal machine, relativized simulation, and the halting reduction.
title: A concrete relativized jump and strict degree hierarchy

description:
**Conjecture.** Call a holographic model *bulk-minimal* if no hidden cell can be
deleted or merged into a boundary cell without changing some entropy. Then two
bulk-minimal models with identical boundary entropy functions are isomorphic as
weighted graphs; equivalently, `weight_eq_half_mutualInfo` extends from
`NoBulk` models to bulk-minimal ones.

*Progress this cycle.* The hidden-cell-free case is now completely settled:
`entropy_eq_iff_mutualInfo_eq` and `spacetime_from_entanglement` in
`Catalog/Novelty/EmergentGeometryReconstruction.lean` show that for `NoBulk`
models the two-point mutual informations determine every region entropy *and*
the whole bridge relation, and `weight_diag_is_gauge` shows this is sharp (the
self-loop weights are pure gauge). What remains open is exactly the extension to
bulk-minimal models below.
