state whose four amplitudes lie in `ℚ(i)` is maximally entangled (`C = 1`) iff
its amplitude quadruple, cleared of denominators, is a primitive integral
solution of `x² + y² + z² + w² = 2N` with the two Hopf vectors forming an
antipodal pair of the associated Pythagorean quadruple; the achievable
`(p, q, C)` triples over `ℚ(i)` are exactly the rational points of a conic.

*The key insight is* that `maximally_entangled_iff_antipodal` turns a quantum
extremality condition into a Diophantine antipodality condition on Pythagorean
quadruples.

*Why now?* Both halves are already formal: the quadruple identity and the
antipodality characterisation. The missing step is a rational-parametrisation
argument of the sort the Pythagorean catalogue is built for.

**Falsification test:** a maximally entangled state over `ℚ(i)` whose Hopf
vectors are not antipodal (would contradict the proved theorem), or a rational
`(p,q,C)` triple off the conic.
title: Conjecture E (Pythagorean arithmetic of maximal entanglement)

description:
A Berggren seed `(m,n)` lies within hyperbolic distance `D` of the line of radial value `a/b` iff
the continued fraction of `n/m` is eventually periodic with the period dictated by `a/b`; for the
integral lines this reads `[0; k, k, k, …] = 1/λ_k`, and the "thickness" of a drawn line is
`2 arcsinh(1/(2 λ_k))`.

**The key insight is** that `pellOrbit_ratio_error` shows the conic points are exactly the
convergents of `[0;k,k,k,…]`, and hyperbolic distance from a geodesic with quadratic-irrational
endpoint is, up to bounded error, `-log` of the approximation quality `|x - p/q| q²`.

**Why now?**  Both sides are formalized: the distance-to-geodesic formula
(`isLeast_dist_vline_of_linear`) and the quantitative slope convergence
(`pellOrbit_ratio_tendsto`); cycle 8 identifies the alignment classes whose endpoints are the
quadratic irrationals in question.
title: Sub-conjecture A (Continued-fraction dictionary for the visible lines)

description:
**Conjecture.** For the propositional pigeonhole formulas `PHP_n`, every irreversible verifier
constrained to `n^{O(1)}` bits of retained state dissipates at least `2^{Ω(n)} · k_B T ln 2`
of heat: the hypothesis `2^n ≤ proofSize n` of `heat_superpolynomial` can be *proved* rather
than assumed for a fixed proof system.

*The key insight is that* the bridge theorem shows the physics is determined entirely by the
register-size gap `S − M`, so the whole difficulty transfers to formalising one exponential
resolution lower bound.

*Why now?* The thermodynamic half is finished and unconditional, and `erasedBits_prodMap`
now shows the heat is extensive over independent instances, so an amplified family is
immediately available once a single-instance bound exists.
title: D′. Unconditional heat bounds for pigeonhole formulas

description:
**Conjecture.** Among all simple `k`-regular graphs, `K_{k+1}` maximises the rank at
the half-canonical degree `g − 1`, the maximum being `((k+1)² − 9)/8` for even `k`
(where `K_{k+1}` has an odd number of vertices and a constant theta characteristic).
In particular the half-canonical rank of a `k`-regular graph is `O(k²)` and the
`Θ(k²)` scale is achieved.

*The key insight is* that rank at a fixed degree measures how *short* the Laplacian
lattice's covering vectors are, and the complete graph has the densest possible
Laplacian lattice for its degree — its lattice is a scaled copy of the root lattice
`A_{n−1}`, whose covering radius is the smallest among all `n`-vertex graph
Laplacians.

*Why now.*  `four_mul_rank_gt_genus_K_odd` proves `4r > g` on `K_{2m+3}`, i.e. the
half-canonical rank there is a *positive proportion of the genus*, while the
Brill–Noether heuristic predicts `r ≈ √g` and the previous cycle's universal theorem
only gives `k − 1`.  The gap between `k − 1` and `k²/8` is now a proved fact rather
than a numerical observation, and the conjecture asserts the upper end of that range
is the truth.
title: Complete graphs maximise the half-canonical rank

description:
**Statement.** Parallel transport around the boundary of a hyperbolic triangle
rotates the tangent plane by exactly `π - (α+β+γ) = κ · area`, and this
rotation angle is invariant under the Möbius action.

*The key insight is* that in the conformal model the connection form is
`-d(log y)` twisted by the rotation generator, so the holonomy integral splits
into a sum of boundary terms along geodesics (each contributing `0`) plus the
exterior-angle jumps at the vertices; the ideal case is then the degenerate
statement that a `0`-angle vertex contributes a full `π`.

*Why now?* Conjecture B gives invariance of the area, and the present files give
the exterior-angle bookkeeping at ideal vertices; the remaining step is the
one-dimensional transport ODE along a geodesic, which is an ordinary
differential-equation computation rather than a new geometric idea.

**Falsifiable form.** Numerically transport a unit tangent vector around the
truncated ideal triangle of `truncatedIdealTriangleArea` and compare the total
rotation with `κ · area`.
title: Conjecture E — holonomy reading of the angular defect

description:
softmax transformer blocks

**Conjecture.** The uniform closure on compacta of finite compositions of *softmax* attention
layers with residual connections and coordinatewise multiplicative gating contains
`attentionAlgebra`, with an explicit inverse-temperature schedule `β(ε) = O(log(1/ε))`.

*The key insight is* that `softmaxHeadRead_zero_scores` already realizes a linear readout as a
zero-score softmax head, and the exponential concentration bound of `SoftmaxLookup.lean`
(`sum_weight_erase_le`) controls the deviation of a finite-`β` head from a hard selection, so
products of readouts should be reachable by stacking two layers with logarithmically scaled
scores.

*Why now?* Both ingredients are already formalized in this catalog; the missing step is a single
composition estimate, so the conjecture can be attacked directly and refuted by an explicit
two-token counterexample if the residual structure is insufficient.
title: C2. Softmax realizability: every element of the attention algebra is a limit of genuine

description:
**Conjecture.** On the `N`-quantized cube of sequences, the minimal number of heads of an exact
symmetric model interpolating an invariant target grows like `Θ(N^{|ι|·|κ|}/|Γ|)`, while the
number needed for `ε`-approximation of a Lipschitz target grows like `Θ((L/ε)^{|ι||κ|}/|Γ|)`;
in particular exact interpolation and uniform approximation have the *same* exponent but differ
by the symmetry factor `|Γ|`.

*The key insight is* that the group-averaging step divides the effective domain by the orbit
size, so both counting problems descend to the orbit space, where the finite lookup theorem of
`TransformerArchitecture.lean` and the separation lower bound of `FiniteLookupSeparation.lean`
apply verbatim.

*Why now?* The orbit-space picture only became available with `SaturatedUnder` and the averaging
argument proved this cycle; the statement is a finite counting claim, hence decidable at small
parameters.
title: C4. Quantized-domain phase transition between exact and approximate universality

description:
**Old conjecture C1 (Zolotarev–Frobenius for the full stratified readout) is now
a theorem**, and in fact the classification has been completed for *all* moduli:

* `index_prime_pow_parity` — `i_{p^k} ≡ i_p (mod 2)` for odd `p`: the order can
  only grow by a power of `p` when the modulus is raised
  (`orderOf_prime_pow_dvd`), so `i_{p^k} = p^{k−1−j}·i_p` with an odd cofactor.
* `sum_idx_divisors` — `∑_{e ∣ N} i_e ≡ 1 + ∑_{p ∈ primeFactorsList N} i_p
  (mod 2)` for odd `N`: every divisor with two coprime factors `> 2` is
  parity-dead.
* `zolotarev_general` — for **every** odd `N` and every `a` coprime to `N`,
  `J(a | N) = 1 ⟺ N − #cycles` is even.
* `parity_readout_even` — at an even modulus `N = 2^s·m` the sign sees only the
  stratum `4`: the permutation is always even when `N ≡ 2 (mod 4)`, and is odd
  exactly when `4 ∣ N` and `a ≡ 3 (mod 4)`.  The odd part of `N` is invisible.
* `permutation_sign_law` — the two halves combined: a single sign law valid for
  every modulus, whose value is computable in polynomial time from `a` and `N`
  alone.

The affine extension was opened and has now been **completely closed**
(`Catalog/Physics/PermutationReadout{Affine,Sign,AffineClass}.lean`):

* `cycleCountOf` — a cycle count for *arbitrary* self-maps of `ZMod N`, shown
  compatible with the multiplicative one (`cycleCountOf_mul`), together with its
  conjugation invariance (`cycleCountOf_conj`).
* `cycleCountOf_affine` — whenever `1 − a` is invertible mod `N`, the shift is a
  conjugating translation, so `#cycles(x ↦ a·x + b) = #cycles(x ↦ a·x)` for
  every `b`.
* `cycleCountOf_add` — the complementary extreme `a = 1`: the translation
  `x ↦ x + b` has exactly `gcd(N, b)` cycles, i.e. the free gcd probe.
title: Resolved in earlier cycles

description:
**Conjecture.** For the radially projected boundary complex of the `4`-cube after
`k` subdivisions, the smallest nonzero eigenvalue of the normalized graph
Laplacian converges to the first eigenvalue `3` of the Laplace–Beltrami operator
on the unit three-sphere, with error `O(4^{-k})`.

*The key insight is* that the exact sign-vector distance data of the tesseract
gives explicit control of edge lengths at every scale, so the discrete Dirichlet
form can be compared term by term with the smooth one.

*Why now?* The exact tesseract diameter results already in the catalog supply the
coarsest-scale constants, and the eigenvalue `3` on `S³` is available in closed
form, so the comparison is quantitative from the start.
title: Discrete-to-smooth spectral comparison on `S³`

description:
**Conjecture.** No experiment on a fixed-step grid, at any number of seeds, can certify
the Zipf amplitude to better than `s/2^i` at rung `i`; in particular the seed-1 window
cannot be narrowed below `(15.5, 16]` before `ctx = 8192`, and any claimed "exact product
law" at `ctx ≤ 4096` is an artefact of the grid.

*The key insight is* that identification is geometric and no faster: there is always an
amplitude differing from the fitted one by `16/2^N` that reproduces every reported knee
through rung `N` (`KneeResolution.exists_indistinguishable_amplitude`), matching the
upper bound `32/2^N` to a factor `2`. Exactness claims are therefore statements about the
sweep, not the model — made precise by `KneeResolution.isKnee_iff_rounding`, which
identifies the measured knee as a rounding of a real number.

*Why now?* The matched bounds are proved; the open part is the *multi-seed* version — does
averaging `m` seeds beat `s/2^i`, or is the barrier information-theoretic in the seeds
too? A concentration argument over the seed ensemble would settle it.

---
title: C4. The resolution-barrier conjecture

description:
**Statement.** Let the bubble be any (not necessarily spherical) region whose shape function
equals `1` on a body of inradius `R` and `0` outside a shell of thickness `Δ`.  Then the
total Eulerian energy satisfies `E ≤ -(v²/12)(R²/Δ)(1 + o(1))` as `Δ → 0`, with the constant
`1/12` unimprovable.

**Status after this cycle.** Proved for spherically symmetric walls, and *sharply*:
`warp_energy_floor_is_sharp` shows the minimum of the radial energy integral over all
admissible profiles is exactly `ab/(b-a)`, attained by `f'(r) ∝ -1/r²`; the piecewise-linear
wall exceeds it by exactly `Δ/3` (`linear_wall_excess`).  The open part is the removal of
spherical symmetry.

**The key insight is** that the energy functional is a weighted `L²` norm of `∇f` subject to
a single linear normalisation, so the floor is a Cauchy–Schwarz dual norm — and the dual
norm of a *shape* constraint is a purely geometric (capacity-like) quantity, which should
identify the true minimum with the electrostatic capacity of the shell.

**Why now?** The Cauchy–Schwarz argument is already formalized in one dimension; lifting it
to three dimensions only requires Mathlib's `MeasureTheory` Hölder inequality plus a
capacity estimate, both within reach.

---
title: C1. Universal exotic-energy floor: `|E| ≥ v² R² /(12 Δ)` for *every* superluminal bubble geometry

description:
**Conjecture.** If a branch in one appreciably normalized finite state has infinitesimal amplitude, then every product branch containing it has zero observed probability after tensoring with any finite state whose squared norm is finite and appreciable. Conversely, tensoring two appreciable branches preserves positive observed weight whenever both standard-part weights are positive.

The key insight is that product amplitudes multiply and standard part is multiplicative on finite hyperreals, so invisibility should form a tensor ideal among branches.

**Why now?** Single-state invisibility is known, but compositional stability is essential before the model can represent composite systems or independent experiments.
title: Tensor-product stability of infinitesimal invisibility

description:
**Conjecture.** For finite groups, every property determined solely by the multiset of composition factors and invariant under replacing each solvable factor by another cyclic factor of the same prime order factors through the dichotomy “all factors are cyclic of prime order” versus “at least one factor is nonabelian simple.”

The key insight is that solvability genuinely belongs to composition-factor chemistry, whereas commutativity, nilpotency, derived length, and automorphism-group order depend on extension data.

**Why now?** The present obstruction cleanly separates factor data from multiplication data, allowing the boundary of composition-determined properties to be formulated rather than inferred from isolated examples.
title: Solvability is the maximal robust composition-factor property

description:
**Conjecture.** For elliptic curves over the rationals, a computable bound depending polynomially on conductor data determines how many Taylor coefficients at the central point must be examined before the first nonzero coefficient appears.

The key insight is that uniqueness of the first nonzero coefficient is elementary once its existence below a known bound is guaranteed; the substantive arithmetic problem is to produce that bound uniformly.

**Why now?** Separating finite jet search from the nonvanishing bound turns an informal “compute the order of vanishing” proposal into a falsifiable quantitative conjecture.
title: Effective analytic-rank bounds from arithmetic complexity

description:
**Conjecture.** The surface \(x^3+y^3+z^3=1729\) contains infinitely many
primitive integral points, not merely infinitely many rational points.

The key insight is that the small primitive point and the much larger candidate
point may lie in an arithmetic orbit generated by rational self-maps of the
cubic surface, with integrality recurring along a subsequence. **Why now?** Two
widely separated primitive-looking orbits motivate searching for a geometric
composition law rather than treating solutions as isolated accidents.
title: Unbounded primitive points on the 1729 surface

description:
**Conjecture.** For certificate protocols over a multivariate polynomial ring with bounded generator degree, there is an explicit primitive-recursive bound on the first common stabilization stage of the certificate cost, key ideal, and leading-term ideal.

The key insight is that a single maximum synchronizes independently obtained stabilization stages, while Gröbner-theoretic degree control may make the ideal-theoretic stage quantitative.

**Why now?** Qualitative synchronized stabilization is established. Adding degree and generator bounds turns its nonconstructive ideal component into a falsifiable numerical claim with direct families of extremal examples.
title: Noetherian multigraded stabilization bounds

description:
**Conjecture.** Under multiplication of two prime torus-knot phase filters with moduli `2p` and `2q`, the resulting angular channels are governed by the image of `(ℤ/2pℤ)ˣ × (ℤ/2qℤ)ˣ` under the Chinese remainder correspondence, with degeneracies determined by `gcd(p,q)`.

The key insight is that each prime torus spectrum is not merely a set of roots but a torsor for a modular unit group, while optical phase multiplication adds angular indices.

**Why now?** Exact coprimality selection and charge additivity are both available, making their interaction a concrete algebraic prediction rather than a qualitative analogy.
title: Optical products realize convolution in modular unit groups

description:
**Conjecture.** Within the family `T(2,p)` for odd primes, the number of distinct Alexander-selected angular channels and their modular addition table uniquely determine `p`, and hence determine the Alexander polynomial and knot determinant.

The key insight is that the channel set is the full unit group modulo `2p`, has cardinality `p−1`, and is a single cyclotomic Galois orbit.

**Why now?** The exact residue classification turns an inverse optical problem into a finite reconstruction problem with an immediately testable uniqueness criterion.
title: Spectral measurements recover torus-knot parameters

description:
**Conjecture.** If two nonstationary branching profiles differ on a set of levels of asymptotic density zero and their branching numbers are uniformly bounded above and below away from the unary degeneration, then their limiting relative entropy dimensions agree whenever either limit exists.

The key insight is that sparse changes contribute sublinear error to both logarithmic volumes. **Why now?** Repetition invariance and weighted composition already establish the finite-block algebra needed to quantify the effect of exceptional blocks.
title: Stability under sparse adversarial perturbations

description:
**Conjecture.** For every fixed `k ≥ 3`, deciding whether the emotional chromatic number of a finite network is at most `k` remains computationally equivalent, under polynomial reductions, to deciding whether its chromatic counting function is positive at `k`; this equivalence persists for succinctly represented networks and preserves natural approximation gaps.

The key insight is that the semantic threshold and the algebraic positivity test are exactly the same decision boundary above the emotional floor.

**Why now?** The threshold equivalence identifies a precise bridge on which reductions, parameterized algorithms, and counting-versus-decision separations can be compared without changing the underlying instances.
title: Complexity of emotional-threshold detection

description:
Fix an ensemble in which a uniformly chosen set of cells receives independently uniform symbols, conditioned only on clue consistency within each visible row, column, and block. Conjecture that, as the block size tends to infinity, resolution refutations of unsatisfiable instances have their largest median width in a narrow density window, and that this window is separated from the density maximizing satisfiability variance.

The key insight is that satisfiability and proof complexity are different observables and need not share a critical point. **Why now?** The structural antitonicity result identifies a natural monotone coupling, while the coloring correspondence supplies standard graph and proof-complexity encodings.
title: Proof-complexity peak for independently assigned clues

description:
For a fixed deterministic variable-ordering and value-ordering rule, conjecture the existence of an explicit family of order-`n` Sudoku instances requiring `exp(Ω(n²))` search-tree nodes, while admitting polynomial-size certificates of unsatisfiability in a stronger proof system.

The key insight is that a meaningful exponential claim must quantify over an explicit algorithm or proof system rather than over “backtracking” as an undifferentiated class. **Why now?** The CSP–coloring equivalence permits transfer of adversarial constructions and lower-bound methods from graph-coloring search trees.
title: Exponential lower bounds for a specified backtracking rule

description:
**Conjecture.** For every geodesic avoiding a fixed Euclidean neighborhood of the
origin, every normal Jacobi field with zero initial value grows at least
exponentially after reparametrization by a curvature-dependent affine scale.

The key insight is that strict negativity alone is not uniform near the origin,
but exclusion of a neighborhood may provide a usable negative upper bound along
controlled geodesic regions. **Why now?** The exact curvature formula permits
explicit bounds, while the intrinsic identification makes those bounds applicable
to Jacobi fields independently of coordinates.
title: Quantitative divergence controlled by integrated curvature

description:
**Conjecture.** Every noninjective one-dimensional cellular automaton over a finite alphabet is noninjective on some finite periodic ring, with the detecting circumference bounded effectively in terms of alphabet size and radius.

The key insight is that collisions of bi-infinite configurations should be compressible into cycles in a finite de Bruijn product graph. **Why now?** The observed accidental finite-ring bijections show that one must quantify the detecting circumference; a graph-theoretic bound would turn finite experiments into a complete decision procedure.
title: Residual detection of nonreversibility

description:
**Conjecture.** There is no polynomial bound, uniform over alphabet size, relating the radius of a reversible cellular automaton to the minimum radius of its inverse.

The key insight is that bijectivity guarantees a local inverse but need not preserve locality at a comparable scale; information can be routed over long distances before being decoded. **Why now?** Separating global group structure from fixed-radius strata makes inverse-radius distortion a precise quantitative invariant of reversible computation.
title: Quantitative inverse-radius bounds

description:
**Conjecture.** Among prime powers, the field size maximizing the asymptotic gain of the four-layer construction is characterized uniquely by a balance equation between the corank-two probabilities below the middle layer and the full-rank deficit above it.

The key insight is that the gain is a signed combination of limiting random-matrix rank probabilities, and its optimizer should arise where the marginal entropy cost of the two exceptional coranks balances.

Why now? The gain has an explicit positive rational factor multiplied by the convergent product `Δ_q`, so the conjecture can be tested numerically and attacked by monotonicity estimates for Euler products.
title: An entropy characterization of the optimal field size

description:
**Conjecture.** A canonical signed path construction can be chosen so that connected sum of knot diagrams corresponds to concatenation or Cartesian product of their path ensembles, with additive area and multiplicative sign.

The key insight is that product state spaces produce Cauchy products of signed generating functions, exactly matching multiplicativity of the Alexander polynomial under connected sum.

**Why now?** The algebraic product law already holds for arbitrary signed state families. What remains is to enforce geometric locality strongly enough that the product operation agrees with an explicit gluing of knot diagrams.
title: Connected sum as concatenation of path ensembles

description:
**Conjecture.** For complex inverse temperature in any closed half-strip
`Re(s) ≥ 1 + δ`, the finite occupation defect satisfies a modulus bound with the
same geometric decay rate obtained by replacing each local weight by its
absolute value.

The key insight is that the algebraic defect identity remains valid over the
complex numbers, while absolute values reduce its quantitative control to the
nonnegative real estimate.

**Why now?** The real-weight theorem identifies the exact inequality that must be
transported through the complex norm, providing a direct route to locally
uniform analytic convergence.
title: Complex-temperature occupation bounds

description:
**Conjecture.** Every divisor class on the complete graph `K_n` has a unique reduced representative relative to a chosen sink, and the rank of a divisor can be read from the minimum defect of its associated parking function. Complementation by the canonical divisor reverses this defect and proves the full Riemann–Roch identity.

The key insight is that Dhar reduction turns an infinite chip-firing equivalence problem into a finite inequality system on sorted integer vectors.

**Why now?** The canonical coefficient, canonical degree, genus, zero rank, and canonical-rank consequence have been isolated, so the missing step is precisely the reduced-divisor rank duality rather than any numerical graph calculation.
title: Parking-function proof of complete-graph Riemann–Roch

description:
**Conjecture.** For fixed `r ≥ 3`, a dependency-sensitive colouring argument applied to the clique-incidence hypergraph yields diagonal Ramsey lower bounds exponentially stronger than the raw Property-B edge-count criterion for an infinite range of `k`.

The key insight is that two bad-clique events are independent unless their candidate vertex sets overlap in at least `r` vertices, giving an explicit and unusually rigid dependency graph. **Why now?** The incidence formulation makes both edge sizes and pairwise intersections binomial quantities, providing the data needed for a quantitative local-lemma analysis.
title: Local-lemma improvement from clique codegrees

description:
**Conjecture.** For a nonuniform distribution on finite network histories and any randomized observation channel whose expected Hamming distortion is at most \(D\), the mutual information between the history and the record is bounded below by source entropy minus the logarithm of the largest admissible distortion ball, with a correction determined by the decoder's excess-distortion probability.

The key insight is that the deterministic fibre-covering argument should become an entropy decomposition: conditioning on a record confines likely histories to a distortion neighborhood, while atypical reconstruction failures contribute a controlled correction.

**Why now?** The exact finite covering converse identifies the correct combinatorial volume term, so the remaining work is to replace worst-case fibre cardinality by conditional entropy without changing the geometric core.
title: Entropy-sensitive dynamic converse

description:
**Conjecture.** For every finite connected two-dimensional cell complex and every additive coefficient group, a discrete increment field is developable if and only if its cellular curvature vanishes and its period vanishes on a generating family of one-cycles.

The key insight is that the torus calculation separates the local obstruction, represented by the cellular coboundary, from the global obstruction, represented by first cohomology. **Why now?** The complete periodic-grid classification and its gauge invariance identify exactly which ingredients must be replaced by cellular boundary maps and cycle generators.
title: Cellular classification beyond the torus

description:
**Conjecture.** Let a triangulated non-orientable manifold carry increments twisted by its orientation local system. A flat twisted field is developable precisely when all periods vanish on the orientation double cover and satisfy the deck-transformation anti-invariance condition.

The key insight is that non-orientability should enter through twisted coefficients rather than through an undefined assertion that the manifold contains a particular optical illusion. **Why now?** The untwisted torus theorem isolates the integration argument, making the orientation local system the single new structural component to test.
title: Orientation covers and signed holonomy

description:
**Conjecture.** In a directed reflexive-transitive multiverse of relational set universes, the modal persistence profile of anti-Extensionality is determined by whether forcing maps preserve the kernel of the membership-observation map; kernel-preserving extensions validate necessity of anti-Extensionality, while kernel-separating extensions make it merely possible.

The key insight is that the observation kernel converts a foundational anti-axiom into algebraic data whose behavior under world extension can be tracked by modal frame semantics.

**Why now?** Membership codes already admit a direct representation as Boolean worlds, providing a concrete bridge between relational set semantics and modal forcing frames.
title: Modal persistence of anti-axiom witnesses

description:
**Conjecture.** For every finite group `G`, there is a representation-ring-valued negative Euler characteristic whose stabilization by a real `G`-representation `V` is multiplication by the determinant character of `V`; the antipodal suspension law is the `G = ℤ/2` sign-representation case.

The key insight is that ordinary parity is the determinant character of a one-dimensional sign representation, suggesting that integer dimension should be replaced by the real representation ring.

**Why now?** The established bridge between parity-character pro-towers and exact antipodal suspension identifies both sides of the proposed equivariant generalization in the first nontrivial group.
title: Equivariant stabilization and Euler parity for finite group actions

description:
**Conjecture.** The ideal completion of the poset of finite signed states is homeomorphic, under a natural Scott topology, to the space of arbitrary signed states; consistent ideals correspond exactly to globally consistent states.

The key insight is that arbitrary states are directed unions of finite fragments even though the finite fragments themselves are not closed under arbitrary unions.

**Why now?** The arbitrary-union obstruction identifies the missing operation, while finite-union closure suggests ideal completion as the canonical repair rather than an ad hoc enlargement.
title: Compact completion of finitary dream states

description:
**Conjecture.** On finite transitive converse-well-founded frames, modal fixed-point alternation depth is bounded above by reflective proof depth plus frame height, and this bound is asymptotically sharp.

The key insight is that transitivity collapses repeated boxes while fixed-point alternation consumes ordinal rank. **Why now?** The frame boundary for iterated provability and the exact grammar translation make both complexity measures simultaneously available.
title: Alternation depth versus reflection depth

description:
**Conjecture.** In a physical complexity model closed under composition,
complementation, and polynomially bounded oracle access, an efficiently realizable
complete process for any fixed level of the polynomial hierarchy collapses every
higher physically realizable level to that level.

The key insight is that the extended Church–Turing inclusion should interact with
hierarchy stability through closure under oracle simulation, not through an
unqualified assertion about all physical processes. **Why now?** The present
complexity transfer identifies the first-level collapse mechanism; the next test is
whether it persists under alternating oracle structure.
title: Physical Polynomial-Hierarchy Collapse Criterion

description:
For prefix-free proof descriptions, conjecture a sharp lower bound on expected thermodynamic cost in terms of the Shannon entropy of the induced theorem distribution, with equality characterized by complete prefix codes.

The key insight is that Kraft’s inequality should replace the coarse binary scarcity axiom and convert counting incompressibility into an entropy-sensitive coding theorem.

Why now? The current half-incompressibility theorem proves the coarse uniform case; a prefix-free refinement would connect proof complexity, coding theory, and thermodynamic entropy without changing the linear Landauer cost law.
title: Prefix-free ensemble refinement

description:
**Conjecture.** Every interpretation between essentially algebraic theories whose model functor is accessible and preserves finite limits factors, up to natural isomorphism, as a reflective localization, followed by the free functor of a finitary monad, followed by a Morita equivalence.

The key insight is that the three factors isolate distinct semantic changes: discarding models, freely closing models under new operations, and changing presentation without changing model theory.

**Why now?** The compositional calculus of mutations and reflective quotients identifies the endpoint adjunction of any proposed factorization, making uniqueness and obstruction questions precise.
title: Localization–Monad–Morita Factorization

description:
**Conjecture.** Every finitary propositional context induces an endofunctor on a suitable category of valuations and semantic entailments, and substitution by semantically equivalent formulas is a natural isomorphism between the induced operators.

The key insight is that congruence of implication is the binary base case of a general compositionality theorem indexed by formula contexts.

**Why now?** Semantic replacement has been verified for implication in both arguments, providing the inductive seed for arbitrary contexts and, subsequently, algebraic signatures with binding.
title: Logical Contexts as Natural Semantic Operators

description:
**Conjecture.** The jump of a finite oracle join is Turing-equivalent to the join of the individual jumps, uniformly in the oracle indices.

The key insight is that the cut principle and least-upper-bound characterization should turn a coding theorem for paired oracle queries into an algebraic preservation law.

**Why now?** Binary joins and their universal property are already established, making this a focused test of whether the abstract hierarchy interacts correctly with degree-theoretic lattice structure.
title: Finite joins commute with the jump up to Turing degree

description:
**Conjecture.** At successor stages take the relativized jump and at effective limit stages take a uniform join; every resulting level below the Church–Kleene ordinal is strictly above all earlier levels and the construction is invariant, up to Turing degree, under equivalent ordinal notations.

The key insight is to combine successor diagonalization with the join universal property at limits, while treating invariance under notation as the central coherence condition.

**Why now?** The finite successor mechanism and finite join mechanism have been separated and proved structurally, exposing exactly the two ingredients that a transfinite recursion must generalize.
title: Transfinite effective iteration extends the hierarchy through computable ordinals

description:
**Conjecture.** A finite-dimensional translation-invariant quantum walk is periodic if and only if all ratios of eigenvalues are roots of unity; when its transition amplitudes lie in a fixed number field, its least period admits an explicit bound in terms of the field degree and state-space dimension.

The key insight is that global phase is invisible to Born probabilities, so probability-periodicity is governed by eigenvalue ratios rather than individual eigenvalues.

**Why now?** The averaging results assume finite order; a cyclotomic criterion would turn that dynamical hypothesis into an arithmetic condition that can be checked from the spectrum.
title: Period bounds from cyclotomic spectra

description:
Suppose an inverse system of coefficient rings admits compatible Bernoulli-type exponential series at every stage. Under suitable completeness hypotheses, the stagewise series should assemble uniquely into a series over the inverse-limit ring, and coefficient extraction should commute with every projection.

The key insight is that an all-index numerical identity and an inverse-limit universal property can interact only through continuity of coefficientwise operations.

Why now? The present results establish both packages separately and identify the precise missing bridge: compatible coefficient rings and a topology supporting infinite series.
title: Naturality of all-index generating packages

description:
Construct explicit formal, graphical, and contrapuntal syntax categories whose morphisms encode substitution, visual completion, and reversible musical transformation. Conjecture that a nontrivial full subcategory of each admits equivalences preserving a common self-application operation, and that the resulting diagonal witnesses agree under those equivalences.

The key insight is that preservation of a binary evaluation table, rather than a bare bijection of artifacts, is exactly what makes fixed points transport.

Why now? The conditional transport theorem isolates the complete interface that concrete domain models must implement, while the failed bare-bijection conjecture identifies the principal obstruction.
title: A syntactic GEB equivalence preserving substitution

description: `LifeboxInformationIdentity.lean` proves the algebraic no-cloning theorem for a two-dimensional state space. No-cloning does not imply undecidability. A valid undecidability theorem would require a precise model of quantum programs, an equivalence predicate, and a reduction from a known undecidable problem. Future work should formalize such a programming-language semantics rather than infer computability consequences from a physical non-copying theorem.
title: Separate quantum no-cloning from undecidability

description:
**Conjecture.** For every symmetrizable generalized Cartan matrix, the dominant labels occurring in the decomposition admit a finite collection of weighted-degree inequalities on the oriented multiple-bond Dynkin graph, generalizing the simply-laced criterion `degree(i) + degree_D(i) ≥ 2`.

The key insight is that coroot pairings turn root sums into weighted in-degrees, so non-simply-laced dominance should remain local after edge multiplicities and symmetrizers are incorporated. **Why now?** A complete simply-laced criterion is available as an anchor, and the weighted formulation can be tested immediately on rank-two finite and affine matrices.
title: Dominance graph criterion beyond simply-laced type

description:
**Conjecture.** After localization away from the metaplectic denominator, the twisted Chinta–Gunnells averaging operator is an idempotent in a completed unequal-parameter Hecke algebra, and its image is exactly the space appearing in the decomposition theorem.

The key insight is that finite Reynolds projection and twisted Weyl averaging share the same projection geometry, while the cocycle should deform the group algebra into a Hecke-type completion. **Why now?** The finite idempotence theorem identifies the algebraic identity that the localized cocycle must satisfy and separates it from all convergence questions.
title: Hecke-idempotent interpretation of twisted averaging

description:
**Conjecture.** There is a terminating, confluent finite-state rewrite system that converts every Zeckendorf representation into a finite base-`φ` expansion with digits `0` and `1`, no adjacent ones, and bounded negative support; its output is canonical among expansions satisfying a fixed endpoint convention.

The key insight is that both systems normalize by the same local relation, `011 ↔ 100`, but Zeckendorf indices and phinary exponents impose different boundary conditions.

**Why now?** Uniqueness of nonconsecutive Fibonacci sums and the golden-ratio carry law are established independently, making confluence and endpoint control the remaining testable bridge.
title: A transducer between Zeckendorf and phinary normal forms

description:
**Conjecture.** There is a smallest combination of dependent products, self-typing universes, and extensionality principles sufficient to derive contradiction, and removing any one component yields a model with normalization.

The key insight is that “Type in Type” packages several closure principles; isolating the minimal contradictory fragment would distinguish genuine hierarchy collapse from harmless recursive syntax.

**Why now?** The current separation between well-founded levels, reversible lifting, and universal semantic representation supplies three independently variable axes for a sharp minimality analysis.
title: A Minimal Girard Boundary

description:
1. Package `hallMul` and componentwise addition as a concrete quasifield structure that includes the division and unique-solvability laws absent from the current lightweight `RightQuasifield` class.
2. Define incidence for `CoordPoint` and `CoordLine`, prove all projective-plane axioms, and formalize Desargues configurations.  This would permit an incidence-level theorem deriving failure of Desargues directly from the proved associativity defect.
3. Replace the numerical collineation-order formulas by actual finite collineation groups and projective general linear groups, construct the relevant action or embedding, and derive the strict cardinality comparison group-theoretically.
4. Generalize the explicit order-nine Hall construction to quadratic extensions over the finite fields for which the Hall construction applies.  The original informal assertion at every prime-power order must not be used: prime-order planes are Desarguesian, and non-Desarguesian constructions require additional hypotheses on the order.
5. Determine the exact left, middle, right, and full nuclei of the concrete Hall multiplication, then connect their sizes to incidence-geometric invariants.
6. For the separate Fibonacci development, an unbounded Carmichael theorem would require a genuine proof of the large-index primitive-part estimate.  Until that analytic/number-theoretic argument is formalized, the certified theorem should retain the upper bound `n ≤ 10000`.
title: Remaining mathematical extensions

description:
**Conjecture.** The divisor-lattice Möbius inversion and the Boolean-lattice
binomial inversion combine into a natural two-parameter convolution whose
spectral decomposition simultaneously encodes reciprocal-power moments and
arithmetic divisor sums.

The key insight is that both inversion laws recover primitive data from
cumulative data, but on different incidence algebras. **Why now?** Their verified
coexistence in the cutoff theory suggests a concrete tensor-product incidence
algebra rather than a merely metaphorical analogy.
title: Divisor-incidence and binomial-incidence compatibility

description:
**Conjecture.** For every fixed pair `l ≥ k ≥ 3`, every sufficiently large outerplanar `C_{k,l}`-free graph whose spectral radius is within `o(n^{-1/2})` of the optimum can be transformed into the corresponding extremal universal-vertex construction by changing `o(n)` edges.

The key insight is that near equality in the adjacency-matrix energy estimate should force the Perron vector to concentrate around a bounded dominating core, while outerplanarity constrains the remaining vertices to path-like pieces.

**Why now?** The edge-to-spectrum bridge isolates the analytic loss precisely, making it possible to separate quantitative eigenvector stability from the forbidden-cycle decomposition.
title: Stability of the universal-vertex outerplanar construction

description:
**Conjecture.** For fixed `l ≥ k ≥ 3`, every sufficiently large planar `C_{k,l}`-free spectral extremizer has a dominating core of size at most two, and deletion of that core leaves a graph of uniformly bounded maximum degree whose nontrivial components belong to a finite family determined by `k` and `l`.

The key insight is that the two-vertex core in the classical planar join construction is not merely an example: concentration of spectral mass and exclusion of two cycles sharing a vertex should make every larger high-weight core combinatorially unstable.

**Why now?** A bounded-core formulation converts an asymptotic spectral problem into a finite structural classification and directly suggests the finite list of local replacements needed for a proof.
title: A bounded-core theorem for planar forbidden-cycle extremizers

description:
**Conjecture:** the two-sided maximisers (equivalences) between carriers form a
groupoid under composition, whose isotropy at a single carrier is its
automorphism group; in the self-finite case this recovers the symmetric group,
and the one-sided maximisers form its associated monoid of split idempotents.

*The key insight is* that composition preserves perfection and Copycat is a
two-sided unit, so maximisers are already closed under the operations that define
a groupoid — only invertibility of each two-sided maximiser remains, which is
exactly the extracted equivalence. *Why now?* The unit laws and composition
closure are proved, so the algebraic structure is one invertibility lemma away.
title: Maximisers form a groupoid, and self-maximisers a group

description:
**Conjecture.** For a monotone but not necessarily continuous self-observation
operator, the least fixed point is reached by continuing the finite stages into
the transfinite: iterate along ordinals, take suprema at limits, and the least
fixed point appears at a stage bounded by the cofinality of the underlying
lattice; the least ordinal at which it appears (the *emergence rank*) is an
order invariant of the operator.

The key insight is that the strict gap between the finite-stage supremum and the
least fixed point is not a defect but a *measure*: the discontinuity witnessed on
two stacked limit levels has emergence rank exactly two, and stacking `k` limit
levels produces rank exactly `k`.

Why now? The finite-stage approximation theorem and its discontinuous witness
isolate the precise place where finite emergence fails, giving a concrete first
rung of a transfinite ladder that can now be defined and calibrated.
title: A transfinite emergence hierarchy for discontinuous observers

description:
Replace the integer growth group by a divisible ordered abelian group, initially
`ℚ ×ₗ (ℚ ×ₗ ℚ)`. The parity obstruction then disappears. A faithful
real-closedness theorem should be developed for Hahn series over a real closed
coefficient field and a divisible value group. This requires formalizing the
relevant Hahn-field real-closure theorem rather than asserting a typeclass for
this integer-ranked model.

A later model should support arbitrarily many iterated exponential and logarithmic
levels. Candidate exponent structures include finitely supported maps from a
well-ordered level type into `ℚ`, with a reverse lexicographic order chosen to
match asymptotic dominance.
title: Corrected real-closedness program

description:
A tempting strengthening of the finite-group averaging theorem is:

> **Unconditional averaging conjecture.** Every degree-one cocycle of a finite
> group acting linearly on a field-vector space is a coboundary, even when the
> group order is zero in the coefficient field.

This conjecture is **disproved uniformly in every prime characteristic** in
`Catalog/Pythagorean/GreenbergMuZeroSharpness.lean`.

For a prime `p`, let

- `G = Multiplicative (ZMod p)`, the additive cyclic group of order `p` written
  multiplicatively;
- `V = ZMod p`;
- every element of `G` act trivially on `V`; and
- `c(g)` be the underlying additive coordinate of `g`.

Then `c(gh) = c(g) + g · c(h)`, so `c` is a degree-one cocycle. Every coboundary
for the trivial action is identically zero, whereas `c(1) = 1 ≠ 0`. Thus `c` is
not a coboundary. Moreover, the cardinality of `G`, cast into `ZMod p`, is zero.
This proves that the invertibility hypothesis in finite averaging marks a real
boundary, rather than an artifact of the usual proof.
title: Contrarian conjecture tested

description:
Conjecture: for a fixed public key `pub ≠ 1` in a group of prime order `q`, the following are
equivalent for the predicate `Accepts g pub`: (i) any two accepting transcripts with a common
commitment and distinct challenges determine a unique extracted exponent; (ii) for every
`(a, z)` the accepting-challenge set has cardinality exactly one.  We proved (ii) ⇒ tight
soundness error; the converse direction, stated as an abstract property of an arbitrary
acceptance predicate `P : G → ZMod q → ZMod q → Prop`, is open in the formalization and is
the natural definition of a "generic Σ-protocol with knowledge error `1/q`".
title: C3. Special soundness is equivalent to the `1/q` soundness error in this model

description:
**Conjecture.** For every `n` the maximum of the Baker–Norine rank over all divisor
classes of degree `d` on `Kₙ` is attained at the *concentrated* divisor `d·q`, and
equals `a(a+1)/2 + min(b, a)` where `d = a(n−1) + b`, `0 ≤ b ≤ n−2`.  At `d = g−1`
this makes the sequence of maxima `0, 0, 2, 2, 5, 5, 9, 9, 14, 14, …` (A000096 with
each term doubled), so `Kₙ` attains `k − 1 = n − 2` **only** for `n = 7`.

*The key insight is* that the deficiency `d(D) = min_s (∑_v ⌈(s − D v)/n⌉ − s)`
supplied by `linEquiv_effective_iff_K` is a *concave-like* functional of the
multiset of values of `D`: spreading chips out can only create more distinct
residues mod `n`, and each distinct residue costs one unit of ceiling, so the
extremal configuration is the maximally concentrated one.

*Why now.*  With the effectivity criterion proved, the conjecture is no longer a
statement about chip-firing sequences but about an explicit ceiling sum, testable in
`O(n)` per class.  The exhaustive data (all `262144` classes on `K₈`, §1 of
`ComputationalEvidence.md`) agree, and both endpoints of the conjecture are now
theorems for the uniform family (`rankBN_const_K` gives the value at `a`-flat
divisors).  A proof would turn `N₀(5) > 6` and `N₀(7) > 8` into theorems and hence
show that the hypothesis "`k ≥ 6`, `k ≠ 7`" of the uniform half-canonical theorem is
*necessary*.
title: The maximum rank at the half-canonical degree on `Kₙ`

description:
Let `G` be a finite connected graph with `V` vertices and `E` edges, all stalks
equal to a fixed `d`-dimensional space over a field `K`, and let each oriented
edge carry an invertible restriction map, so that the sheaf is a
`GL_d(K)`-local system.  Then

```
dim H¹(G; 𝓕)  =  d·(E - V) + dim (K^d)^{hol(𝓕)},
```

where `hol(𝓕) ≤ GL_d(K)` is the holonomy group generated by transporting around
a basis of cycles at a base point, and `(K^d)^{hol}` is its fixed subspace.
Equivalently: `dim H⁰ = dim (K^d)^{hol}` and the Euler characteristic
`euler_characteristic` does the rest.

*The key insight is* that for invertible restriction maps the entire cohomology
of a connected nerve is controlled by a single group-theoretic invariant — the
fixed space of the holonomy representation — with the combinatorics entering
only through the cycle rank `E - V + 1`.  The proved cases
`cyclic_holonomy_criterion` (`d = 1`, `G` a cycle: fixed space is `K` iff
`∏ aᵢ = 1`) and `finrank_H1_disjointLoops` (a disconnected instance) are the two
extreme corners of this formula.

*Why now?*  The two proved corners already exhibit both terms of the right-hand
side separately, and the abstract ledger `euler_characteristic` /
`finrank_H1_add_finrank_range` is in place, so only the identification
`H⁰ = (K^d)^{hol}` remains.  Falsifiable by enumerating `2 × 2` matrices over
`𝔽₃` on the theta graph.
title: Conjecture A (Monodromy rank law for graph data sheaves)

description:
For every infinite address `α : ℕ → Gen` the plotted points of the nodes
`applyGens (take k α) root` converge to a boundary point `ξ(α)`, and

  `ξ(α)` is rational  ⟺  `α` contains only finitely many `B`'s.

Moreover the approach is polynomial (`Θ(k^{-2})`) in the rational case and exponential
in the other.

*The key insight is* that the two parabolic letters conserve a linear functional whose
zero locus is a *rational* null direction, while `B` is hyperbolic with an irrational
axis; so rationality of the limit should be exactly the assertion that the address is
eventually parabolic.

*Why now?* `branch_growth_sandwich` already separates the two growth regimes by the count
of `B`'s, `charge_invariant_under_C` shows the charge is frozen by `C`'s, and
`no_triple_direction_at_pi_div_four` handles the model irrational point.  What remains is
(i) existence of `ξ(α)` — a nested-interval argument for the Stern–Brocot-like ordering of
the coprime-pair tree — and (ii) a Lyapunov estimate for products of the three matrices.

---
title: Conjecture B (Arithmetic ⇔ dynamics along an infinite address)

description:
The rational half of this conjecture is now a theorem: every primitive rational ideal
point is approached by infinitely many pairwise distinct curves of the plot, one for each
charge `2n²` (`star_multiplicity_at_every_primitive_ideal_point`), and by
`tree_spoke_charge_spectrum` those are the only charges that occur.  What remains is the
contrasting statement:

  every irrational boundary point is approached by **at most one** curve of the plot; more
  precisely, for irrational `ξ` and any `d > 0` there are only finitely many nodes `v` of
  the tree with `c_v·‖dir v − ξ‖² ≤ d`.

*The key insight is* that `chord_times_hyp_eq` turns "lying on a curve into `ξ`" into the
Diophantine condition `|a/c − ξ| ≪ 1/c`, i.e. into an approximation of quality `1/c`
rather than the generic `1/c²`; at a rational point the horocycle supplies infinitely many
such approximations, while at an irrational point their existence would force `ξ` to be
extremely well approximable by the very sparse set of triple directions.

*Why now?* Both inputs exist: `chord_sq_ratio` and `chord_times_hyp_eq` reduce the
multiplicity count to counting integer solutions of `⟨v,p⟩ = −d`, and
`no_triple_direction_at_pi_div_four` shows the technique is already able to certify
irrational boundary points.

---
title: Conjecture C (Multiplicity at an *irrational* boundary point)

description:
**Conjecture.** For block sorting, define the *garbage index* of a reversible protocol as
`|Aux| / (m!·n!)`.  Then the minimal number of elementary uncomputation steps needed to
bring a protocol to the garbage-free case is `Θ(log (garbage index))`, and the class of
protocols with garbage index `1` is exactly the class characterised by
`block_history_equality_iff_no_garbage` — i.e. bijectivity of the history map is not only
necessary and sufficient but *quantitatively stable*: a protocol within a factor `1 + ε` of
the minimum has history map surjective on a `(1 − ε)`-fraction of `Aux`.

The key insight is that our equality theorem is an all-or-nothing pigeonhole statement, while
`block_history_strict_of_garbage` shows the failure mode is a cardinality defect that should
carry a metric, not just a boolean. **Why now?** Both endpoints (equality iff bijective, and
strictness under non-surjectivity) are proved, so the interpolating stability statement is
the only missing piece and is falsifiable on `(m, n) = (3, 2)` by exhaustive search.
title: Uncomputation quantifies the equality case of the direct-sum theorem

description:
**Specification (to be formalised, then tested).**  Site: the category whose objects
are the arcs `[i, i+ℓ]` of the cyclic lattice `ZMod n` and whose morphisms are
inclusions, with the Grothendieck topology generated by finite covers by overlapping
arcs.  Presheaf: `F(U) = { partial configurations on U that satisfy the update
equation at every site whose full neighbourhood lies in U }`, with restriction the
obvious truncation.

**Conjecture.**  `F` is a sheaf, and `Γ(ZMod n, F) ≅ V(g,n)`; moreover `F` is flasque
if and only if `g` is right-transitive in the sense of
`CAShiftsPolynomialsOrbits.RightTransitive`, so the `16` census rules are exactly the
ones with vanishing higher cohomology on the cyclic site.

*The key insight is* that gluing partial fixed configurations across overlapping arcs
is exactly the propagation argument used in
`fixedPoints_eq_singleton_zero_of_right_transitive`, so the obstruction to gluing is
the failure of that local criterion.

*Why now?*  The propagation lemma is already isolated and proved; the sheaf language
would turn it from an ad-hoc induction into a cohomological statement, and gives a
concrete falsifiable prediction (flasqueness ⇔ right transitivity) rather than a vague
analogy.
title: C5. A sheaf on the lattice site, specified before use

description:
**Conjecture.**  There is a point-free tropical ideal — for instance the
vanishing ideal of two distinct points, or the tropicalization of a curve — whose
degree-`d` truncation has a matroid that is *not* uniform for `d` large enough,
in contrast with `truncation_isCircuit_iff` for a single point.  Concretely, the
number of circuits of the degree-`d` truncation grows strictly slower than
`binom(N_d, 2)`, where `N_d` is the number of monomials of degree at most `d`.

*The key insight is* that a single point imposes exactly one linear condition per
degree, giving corank one and hence a uniform matroid, whereas several conditions
force dependencies among monomials and thus non-trivial circuits.

*Why now?*  The uniform case is now a theorem, so any deviation is measurable
against a proved baseline, and the truncation formalism
(`truncation_eq_tropVanishing`) transfers the question to explicit finite
matroids.
title: C3. Degreewise matroids of tropical ideals are non-uniform in general

description:
**Statement.** There is a polynomial-time reduction from factoring semiprimes to
the problem: given the multiset `jointLaw N` (as an explicit list) and `N`,
output a nontrivial factor of `N`. Conversely, given the factorisation the law
is computable in polynomial time.

**The key insight is** that the law's `+1`-fibre determines the multiset of
`lcm` values of pairs of divisors of `(p−1)/2` and `(q−1)/2`, which is a
"divisor-lattice tomography" problem whose difficulty can be pinned to the
hardness of recovering `p−1` from `φ(N)`-type data.

**Why now?** Item 4 shows the law alone is insufficient, so the only remaining
question is the *relative* hardness — precisely the shape of statement a
reduction can settle.
title: C3 (Hardness of the inverse problem). Reconstructing `N` from its joint law is as hard as factoring.

description:
**Conjecture.** For the `k`-bit prime semiprime support, the number of parities with nonzero
Walsh coefficient for `f_j` is at least `2^{Ω(k)}` for every information-bearing `j` — i.e. the
lower bound in `card_support_ge_of_flat` is essentially attained, so the factoring bit is not just
flat but *maximally spread*, behaving like a random function of its input.

*The key insight is* that flatness alone (`|corr| ≤ ε` everywhere) forces support size `≥ ε^{-2}`,
and the measured `ε ≈ 10^{-2}` at `k = 14` already forces `≥ 10^4` nonzero coefficients; pushing
`ε` down to the noise floor `2^{-n/2}` would force exponentially many.

*Why now?* Both halves of the needed inequality are now formal: `exists_corr_sq_ge` gives the floor
and `card_support_ge_of_flat` converts a flatness bound into a support lower bound. Only the
support-restricted analogue of Parseval remains.
title: C5. Spectral spreading is achieved by the factoring function

description:
**Conjecture.** For a pinned fork with cyclic quotient of order `m` and conductor
`f`, the function `m' ↦ I(p mod m' ; F)` is `0` for every `m'` with `f ∤ m'`, and
equals `H(1/m)` for every multiple of `f`: the information profile is a
*characteristic function of the divisibility relation*, so the conductor is
recoverable from entropy measurements without any algebraic input.

*The key insight is* that a non-multiple of the conductor intersects every fibre
of the ray-class group in equal proportion, which is exactly the "flat" branch of
the trichotomy — the mod-3 blindness proved in `mod_three_flat` is the smallest
instance.
*Why now?* `info_of_flat` and `info_of_pinned` are proved, and `mod_three_flat`
shows the CRT mechanism at the conductor's own prime; the general statement is a
finite computation in `(ℤ/lcm)ˣ`.
title: C5. Minimal conductor is detected by information alone

description:
**Conjecture.** Let `X` be any congruence observable whose image has `m` equiprobable values
(a conductor of index `m`) and let `Y` be a fork of density `d ≤ 1/m`.  Then
```
I(X ; Y) ≤ binEntropy d − binEntropy (m d)/m = : C_m(d) ,
```
with equality exactly for the single-fibre forks, `C_m(1/m) = log m`, `C_m` strictly increasing on
`[0, 1/m]`, and `C_m(d)/d → log m` as `d → 0⁺`; consequently the pinned fraction of a rare fork
tends to `0` for *every* conductor, at the universal rate `log m / log(1/d)`.

**The key insight is** that the index-two proof never used two-ness: the balanced case rests on
sub-additivity of the binary entropy applied to the fibre-conditional densities, and the same
argument applied to `m` equal fibres gives an `m`-term sub-additivity with the same equality case,
so the whole profile theory of C9 is a one-parameter family whose parameter is the *index of the
conductor*, not the field.
**Why now?** All three ingredients exist: `binEntropy_add_le` (which already generalises to
`m` summands by induction), `mutualInfo_balanced_eq` (whose proof is fibrewise), and the Taylor
estimate that produced the `d log 2` asymptotic.  Falsifiable by a single fork over a
three-fibre conductor with `I > C₃(d)`.
title: C14. A universal density–information inequality for arbitrary conductors

description:
**Conjecture.** For lens spaces the two halves of the conjectured coupled
obstruction are independent: the linking-form half is exactly "`n` is a perfect
square" (proved), while the intersection-pairing half is a genuinely finer
congruence condition on the second lens parameter.  Concretely: there exist
`q` coprime to `m²` for which `L(m², q)` passes the metabolicity test but admits
no compatible pair of unimodular integral forms, so metabolicity alone is not
sufficient for embedding.

*The key insight is* that `exists_metabolizer_iff_isSquare` is uniform in `q`,
i.e. the linking form is blind to the second lens parameter, while embeddability
demonstrably is not; the residual information must therefore live entirely in the
intersection pairings of the complementary pieces.

*Why now?* The linking half is now a theorem with all subgroups quantified over,
so the search for the missing condition has a precise target: an obstruction that
distinguishes different `q` with the same `n = m²`.
title: Beyond the linking form: the intersection-pairing half of the obstruction

description:
**Conjecture.** For a finite abelian group `A` with nondegenerate symmetric
linking form `λ`, the existence of a metabolizer forces `|A|` to be a perfect
square, and conversely every `λ` on `A ⊕ A` of hyperbolic type is metabolic; the
cyclic case proved here is the extremal one in the sense that `A` cyclic admits a
metabolizer for at most one subgroup.

*The key insight is* that the annihilator computation `H_d^⊥ = H_{n/d}` is a
duality statement `|H| · |H^⊥| = |A|`, which holds for every nondegenerate form,
so the square-order conclusion should be a formal consequence of nondegeneracy
alone.

*Why now?* The cyclic proof isolates exactly which step uses cyclicity
(classification of subgroups by divisors), so replacing it by Pontryagin duality
for finite abelian groups is a self-contained formalization target.
title: Metabolicity for non-cyclic linking forms

description:
**Conjecture.** A linear inequality `Σⱼ cⱼ S(Bⱼ) ≤ Σᵢ dᵢ S(Aᵢ)` with nonnegative
integer coefficients holds for the min-cut entropies of *every* finite bulk
geometry if and only if it is witnessed by a `ContractionMap` in the sense of
`Catalog/Novelty/HolographicContractionCalculus.lean` (after replacing each
region by `dᵢ`, resp. `cⱼ`, parallel copies).

*The key insight is* that the min-cut entropy of a graph is a minimum of linear
functionals of Boolean patterns, so any valid inequality must survive the
"worst-case pattern" test, and that test is exactly Hamming contraction.

*Why now?* Both new inequalities proved here (monogamy, five-party cyclic) were
obtained by finding a contraction map by computer search over `2^k` patterns,
and the search space is small enough that completeness can be tested
exhaustively for `k ≤ 5` before attempting a proof.

---
title: C1. The contraction calculus is complete for graph models

description:
**Conjecture.** Every knee-level statistic that is invariant under the Galois adjunction
`kneeInf c ⊣ c` — i.e. every functional of the passing up-set rather than of the curve —
is reproducible across seeds, and every non-reproducible statistic (margins, effective
support, top-`k` mass) is not. In particular the *sign* of every inter-seed knee
difference is predicted by curve domination alone, while no magnitude is.

*The key insight is* that the knee functional is a left adjoint
(`KneeResolution.knee_galoisConnection`), so it factors through the up-set of passing
budgets and forgets everything else about the curve; the domination theorems
(`KneeDrift.drop_direction_forced` versus `KneeDrift.domination_does_not_force_drop`) are
the first two instances of the resulting dichotomy.

*Why now?* The adjunction is proved and the two boundary instances are proved. The
conjecture predicts, before any further run, exactly which of the round's reported
quantities will replicate at a third seed — a pre-registered, cheap, falsifiable test of a
structural claim.
title: C5. The adjoint-invariance conjecture

description:
| result | Lean name |
|---|---|
| parity-free zigzag on `C_m □ C_k` for commuting generators | `isHamiltonian_of_abelian_directProduct` |
| generalized dihedral pair | `isHamiltonian_of_dihedral_pair` |
| index-two alternating word | `isHamiltonian_of_index_two_pair` |
| **twisted direction-sequence criterion (metacyclic `⟨a⟩ ⋊ ⟨b⟩`)** | `isHamiltonian_of_twisted_directions` |
| the twist alone closes the cycle when `gcd(e−1, |a|) = 1` | `isHamiltonian_of_metacyclic_coprime_twist` |
| **nonabelian metacyclic groups with `|a|` prime** | `isHamiltonian_of_metacyclic_prime_normal` |
| two connection elements in one coset of a normal subgroup of prime order | `isHamiltonian_of_same_coset_pair`, `isHamiltonian_of_same_coset_pair'` |
| two connection elements in mutually inverse cosets | `isHamiltonian_of_inverse_coset_pair` |
| **general coset-pair criterion, voltage form (no parity hypothesis)** | `isHamiltonian_of_coset_pair_of_voltage` |
| **general coset-pair criterion: `x` of odd order `k`, `y = A·xᵐ`** | `isHamiltonian_of_coset_pair` |
| the case `m = 2` of the criterion | `isHamiltonian_of_square_coset_pair` |
title: Coset-by-coset criteria

description:
**Conjecture.** The budget needed to retain `98 %` of the attention *mass* grows like
`N_eff(ctx) ∝ ctx^{0.86}`, while the budget needed to retain `98 %` of the *accuracy*
grows like `ctx` (the product law). The two curves therefore cross, and beyond the
crossing context the knee is strictly **above** the mass-retention budget: attention mass
stops being the mechanism of the knee.

*The key insight is* `SelectionDilution.budget_ge_of_retained_mass`: concentration alone
forces `k ≥ β²·N_eff`, a bound with a *different exponent* from the product law, so the
two cannot both be exact laws for all context.

*Why now?* At `ctx = 2048` the two budgets are `≈ 505` (mass) and `256` (accuracy) — they
have already crossed, and `SelectionDilution.net45_mass_retention_at_knee_bound` proves
the knee budget cannot retain the mass. Measuring the retained *mass* at the knee in the
next run is a one-line addition to the harness and directly tests the conjecture.
title: C3. Mass retention and accuracy retention diverge

description:
**Conjecture.** The Zipf amplitude `A` of `Probability.AttentionCostLaw` is identifiable
only to width `s/2^{D(η)}`, where `D(η)` is the certified depth of the chain at the
harness noise `η` — not to width `s/2^n` for the number `n` of rungs actually run. At
`η = 0.006` this gives width `8`, not the width `2` window `(14, 16]` claimed from four
rungs.

*The key insight is* that `Logic.KneeResolutionLimits` computes the resolution of a rung
*assuming its reading is correct*, while `KneeMarginChain.net45_chain_collapse` shows only
the first two readings are certified at the measured spread; identifiability must be
computed on the certified prefix.

*Why now?* Both halves are already formal — the resolution theory in
`KneeResolutionLimits` and the depth theory here — so the conjecture is a Lean
development away, and it decides whether the programme's headline amplitude window is
real.
title: C4. The certified-depth bound on amplitude identifiability

description:
**Statement.** The number of mirror nodes of height at most `N` in dimension three is
asymptotically `C · N log N` for an explicit constant `C`, and more precisely the counting
function is a Dirichlet convolution of `τ(a²)` with the constraint `a + p + q ≤ N`,
`pq = a²`.

*The key insight is* that the divisor law `mirror_pairs_card` turns a geometric count (lattice
points on the mirror hyperplanes of the reflection group) into a purely multiplicative one, so
the asymptotics is a divisor-sum problem rather than a lattice-point problem.

*Why now?* The bijection with factorisations `a² = pq` is now a theorem, and `τ(a²)` summatory
asymptotics are classical; the only missing step is controlling the height constraint
`a + p + q ≤ N`.
title: Conjecture D (arithmetic of mirror loci: a Dirichlet law)

description:
**Statement.** For `n ≥ 4` no finite set of integral Lorentz matrices acts transitively on the
primitive null vectors with non-negative coordinates via height-decreasing moves; equivalently,
the descent process based on all-ones-type reflections fails to be finitely generated.

*The key insight is* that the all-ones reflection leaves the lattice exactly when `n ≤ 3`
(catalog `refl_not_integral_of_four_le`), so any higher-dimensional generating set must use
reflections in vectors of norm dividing `2`, and the descent complex bound `#S ≤ n − 2` shows
these cannot lower the height uniformly.

*Why now?* The obstruction is already isolated in two theorems (integrality failure in the
catalog, dimension bound here), so the remaining work is a classification of the admissible
reflection vectors.
title: Conjecture E (no integral reflection group beyond dimension three)

description:
**Conjecture.** A program implementing a differentiable map on a compact invariant set, together with machine-checkable stable/unstable cone bounds and a uniform local rounding certificate, admits a computable horizon-independent shadowing radius. The radius should be extractable from the cone expansion, contraction, angle separation, and rounding constants.

The key insight is that a raw Lipschitz estimate records only worst-case expansion, whereas hyperbolic cone data records the directional cancellation that makes classical shadowing possible.

**Why now?** The finite-horizon geometric estimate isolates exactly the step that loses uniformity, so the missing directional structure and the constants it must replace are explicit and testable.
title: Certified shadowing from cone-field data

description: Determine conditions under which a closure invariant `J` and evaluation point `z` satisfy `log |J_{K₁#K₂}(z)| = log |J_{K₁}(z)| + log |J_{K₂}(z)|`, and test whether departures from additivity track interaction between experimentally defined process segments. **The key insight is...** multiplicativity of the Eisenstein norm already yields an exact power law, suggesting that logarithmic information is structurally justified only when the underlying topological invariant has a compatible product theorem. **Why now?** The algebraic iteration law supplies a rigorous null model against which interaction effects can be measured.
title: Additive information under independent braid composition

description:
There exist two computable traversal policies on the same successful-prefix tree with identical positive dimension for which one has polynomial expected discovery time and the other has exponential expected discovery time.

The key insight is that fractal geometry describes abundance but not visitation order. **Why now?** Arbitrary terminal length already shows that geometry alone cannot determine proof length; the next test is to separate policies while holding the entire successful-path set fixed.
title: Policy separation at fixed dimension

description:
**Conjecture.** There is a congruence-and-factorization descent proving that any
nonzero solution of \(x^3+y^3+z^3=1729\) below height 13 is impossible without
exhaustive enumeration.

The key insight is that the factorization of sums of cubes, combined across
carefully chosen pairings and moduli, may force one coordinate into the boundary
case \(|x|=13\). **Why now?** Exhaustive arithmetic has established the exact
answer, making it possible to design and test a conceptual certificate against
a known sharp target.
title: A descent certificate for minimum-height signed decompositions

description:
**Conjecture.** In the pointwise topology on the infinite symmetric group, the set of permutations for which `p_{σ(n)}/p_n` converges is dense but meagre, while the subset with limit one is also dense and meagre.

The key insight is that finite-support permutations give density, whereas infinitely many independently prescribed index expansions and contractions should force oscillation on a residual set.

**Why now?** The finite-extension theorem settles the dense half and identifies the exact cylinder structure needed for a diagonal category argument.
title: Baire-category classification of convergent prime rearrangements

description:
Let each ordered off-diagonal edge be present independently with probability `p`, give every present edge amplitude `z`, subtract the mean matrix, and normalize by `|z|√(np(1-p))`. Conjecture: for fixed `0 < p < 1` and nonzero `z`, the empirical spectral distribution converges to the uniform measure on the unit disk.

The key insight is that directing the edges removes the transpose correlation that forces undirected spectra onto a line, while centering removes the rank-one mean outlier.

Why now? The exact phase-locking obstruction identifies both modifications—direction and centering—that the original model lacked, making this a sharply specified replacement rather than a cosmetic variant.
title: Directed fixed-amplitude circular law

description:
**Conjecture.** For every finite alphabet with at least two symbols, the group of reversible one-dimensional cellular automata contains finitely generated subgroups of exponential growth that strictly extend the shift--symbol-permutation subgroup.

The key insight is that fixed-radius strata are not groups, but bounded-radius generators can create increasingly large interaction ranges under composition. **Why now?** The infinite shift--complement subgroup identifies the first algebraic layer; controlled marker constructions offer a route to noncommuting reversible generators beyond it.
title: Growth of the reversible automorphism group

description:
**Conjecture.** If each query has at most `q` outcomes, every sorter requires depth at least
`⌈log_q(n!)⌉`; under a physical model charging `kT log q` per fully erased query register,
the ideal total work remains `kT log(n!)`, independent of `q`.

The key insight is that changing query radix trades depth against information per query but
should not alter the reversible information balance. **Why now?** The binary theorem exposes
the exact structural argument, and small multiway trees can immediately test sharpness and
equality conditions.
title: Multiway comparisons and optimal radix

description:
**Conjecture.** A stepping-up construction can be expressed as an entropy-preserving transformation between avoidance colourings whose loss is controlled by the incidence codegree profile, yielding a double-exponential lower bound for diagonal 3-uniform Ramsey numbers.

The key insight is that stepping-up and Property B both transform colourings into constraints on families of subsets, suggesting that the binary-string construction can be measured by entropy rather than only by cardinality. **Why now?** The exact incidence bridge supplies a common language in which lower-bound colourings and stepping-up transformations can be compared without conflating the graph and hypergraph levels.
title: Entropy-compressed stepping-up

description: Conjecture that a finite flag complex with sphere homology, quantitatively controlled vertex links, and a suitable discrete curvature or expansion condition admits a certified manifold core whose geometric realization is a homology sphere; in dimension three, add a verifiable simple-connectivity certificate to obtain a topological three-sphere. **The key insight is...** global Betti numbers must be supplemented by local link data to distinguish manifolds from singular homology mimics. **Why now?** The full-simplex boundary demonstrates that global simplex counts rapidly lose topology, while links remain sensitive to local dimension and singularities.
title: Local-link certification of spherical manifold structure

description:
**Conjecture.** No Hausdorff topology simultaneously extends the Euclidean topology on the finite fragment, makes total addition and multiplication jointly continuous everywhere, and makes both signed infinities non-isolated.

The key insight is that limits approaching opposite infinities force their sum toward nullity, while nearby finite cancellations remain finite, creating incompatible separation requirements. **Why now?** The algebraic table identifies the precise exceptional fibers whose topological neighborhoods must be compared.
title: Topological impossibility at nullity

description:
**Conjecture.** A winning position whose defender has uniformly finite legal branching cannot have a game value of countable cofinality greater than `ω`, and stronger uniform branching constraints impose corresponding restrictions on its Cantor normal form.

The key insight is that limit values arise from suprema of defender choices, so geometric bounds on legal branching should translate into ordinal cofinality bounds.

**Why now?** The explicit `ω^n` and `ω^ω` constructions use countable branching at precisely the limit-forming nodes, making branching the natural structural invariant to test.
title: Cofinality Bound from Finite Branching

description:
**Conjecture.** For each fixed `k` and treewidth bound `t`, the stabilized `k`-copwin computation admits a representation whose size is linear in the number of vertices, with constants depending only on `k` and `t`.

The key insight is that the one-round forcing operator only observes local adjacency and membership information, suggesting a finite interface state over each tree-decomposition bag. **Why now?** The semantic operator is independent of any concrete table layout, enabling alternative compressed implementations to be compared against the same correctness specification.
title: Structural compression on bounded-width graphs

description:
Construct a proof-quality zero-counting certificate showing that the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function have no ordinates in `[-3,3]`. This would settle the support question behind the proposed octave and fifth cutoffs: under the stated reciprocal-sum definition, both harmonics would be zero rather than arithmetically distinct.

The key insight is that arithmetic classification must follow, not precede, certified knowledge of which zeros lie in the window.

Why now? Rigorous interval methods and explicit argument-principle computations make a finite low-height certification sharply testable.
title: Certified low-height window theorem

description: “Random true statement of length `n`” is not determined until one fixes a language, semantics, proof calculus, and probability distribution on the true formulas.
