The canonical fixed-width model formalized here has linear mean code length and therefore disproves any model-independent exponential claim. Future work should study explicitly specified ensembles—for example, uniformly sampled provable formulas in a bounded syntax—and distinguish statement length, shortest-proof length, and shortest-program length.
title: Proof systems and truth distributions

description:
Let theorem lengths be generated by a scale mixture of geometric distributions whose entropy parameter has density proportional to a power near zero. Conjecture that the mixed length distribution has a regularly varying tail, with exponent determined by the small-entropy mixing law, and prove a converse under a Tauberian regularity condition.

The key insight is that a fixed entropy produces geometric decay, so a genuine power law must arise from heterogeneity across proof regimes rather than from one homogeneous proof space.

Why now? The exact constant successive-ratio law rules out the naive power-law prediction and points directly to scale mixtures as a falsifiable replacement.
title: Power laws from mixtures of geometric proof regimes

description:
**Conjecture.** Every normalized, translation-equivariant, coordinatewise-minimum-preserving map from a finite tropical projective space to the tropical line is a finite minimum of coordinate projections. Moreover, the irredundant set of coordinates occurring in this representation is unique.

The key insight is that preservation of tropical addition should convert the aggregator into a semimodule homomorphism, while projective normalization removes the common additive ambiguity.

**Why now?** The binary minimum example proves that weak tropical axioms extend strictly beyond dictatorship, and a complete representation theorem would identify the entire surviving class rather than one isolated counterexample.
title: Classification of finite min-plus aggregators

description:
Every lattice point in the `t`-fold affine dilation about the all-ones vector is a sum,
after the corresponding translation, of `t` lattice points from the original
parking-function polytope. This predicts the integer-decomposition property uniformly
for all positive generalized parking profiles.

The key insight is that affine dilation preserves the full sorted inequality system,
so a decomposition theorem can be sought rank by rank rather than in ambient
coordinates.

Why now? Affine transport has been established at the level of parking vectors and
profiles; the remaining testable step is a constructive decomposition of integral
points in the convex hull.
title: Integer decomposition compatible with affine dilation

description:
**Conjecture.** After a uniform power-of-`q` renormalization, every coefficient in the dominant-weight decomposition of the rational-function-field multiple Dirichlet series is a polynomial in `q` with nonnegative integer coefficients, and its value at `q = 1` is a weight multiplicity in the highest-weight module determined by the twisting parameter.

The key insight is that dominant labels already come from a highest-weight module, suggesting that arithmetic coefficients refine crystal multiplicities rather than merely being indexed by them. **Why now?** The decomposition theorem supplies canonical coefficients, so positivity can be tested in low-rank finite and affine examples without ambiguity about normalization or basis choice.
title: Function-field coefficient positivity and crystal multiplicities

description:
**Conjecture.** Classify all quadratic algebraic integers `β` of norm two for which the digit set `{0,1}` gives unique finite expansions of every element of the ambient imaginary quadratic integer ring. The classification should be expressible through the geometry of a finite exceptional region for norm descent.

The key insight is that the proved base `i − 1` theorem reduces the infinite lattice to parity extraction, strict norm decrease, and five exceptional points; the same three-part mechanism should distinguish the successful quadratic radices.

**Why now?** Complete negabinary and Gaussian base theorems provide one-dimensional and two-dimensional models, making a uniform classification both concrete and falsifiable.
title: Canonical binary expansions in imaginary quadratic rings

description:
**Conjecture.** For binary statements of length `n`, any family of predictors that realizes every Boolean semantics exactly requires at least `2^n` bits of worst-case advice; under a 95-percent Hamming-accuracy requirement, the optimal advice length is governed asymptotically by the volume of radius-0.05 Hamming balls in the Boolean cube.

The key insight is that finite computability does not remove information-theoretic storage barriers, and approximate prediction converts truth tables into a covering-code problem.

**Why now?** The exact table theorem identifies the ambient Boolean cube, while the adversarial theorem shows that semantics-free guarantees need additional information.
title: Quantitative advice lower bounds for bounded semantics

description:
For a fixed global field and bounded ramification, form a bipartite graph of rank-two
automorphic and Galois representations using independently established local-global
compatibilities.  After normalization by admissible local types, conjecture that the
largest-component density becomes nonzero above a universal critical mean degree, and that
this boundary is unchanged by every continuous monotone zero-reflecting observable applied
to the density.

**The key insight is...** graph formation and measurement should be separated: compatibility
determines whether a giant component exists, while the observable controls only how its size
is reported.

**Why now?** The cyclotomic rank-one model now admits an exact separation between arithmetic
threshold and response law, supplying a null model for testing the same separation in
higher-rank datasets.
title: Higher-rank compatibility percolation with a deformation-invariant boundary

description:
Across number-field families ordered by discriminant, conjecture that coherence observables
fall into finitely many universality classes characterized by a local homogeneity identity:
tree-like compatibility networks have exponent `1`, symmetry-breaking character models have
exponent `1/2`, and multicritical families realize a discrete sequence of higher rational
exponents.

**The key insight is...** an exponent should be inferred from rescaling around the boundary,
not from the arithmetic name of the underlying objects.

**Why now?** Exact power-response rescaling shows that boundary location and exponent can be
varied independently, making it possible to distinguish genuine geometric universality from
a chosen measurement law.
title: Arithmetic universality from exact local homogeneity

description:
Replace carriers by finite categories and the maps by functors `F : A ⥤ B`,
`G : B ⥤ A`, scoring the analogy by how close `G ∘ F` is to the identity functor
(number of objects fixed up to isomorphism, or the isomorphism defect of the
counit). **Conjecture:** one-sided maximisers are exactly the functors admitting
a retraction (categorical split monomorphisms), and two-sided maximisers are
exactly the equivalences of categories.

*The key insight is* that the fixed-point count of the discrete round trip is the
object-level shadow of the counit `G ∘ F ⇒ id`, so "fixed concept" becomes
"object where the counit is an isomorphism," and split-mono/equivalence survives
verbatim. *Why now?* The discrete base case has been pinned down exactly, so the
only new ingredient is bookkeeping of natural isomorphisms — the extremal
combinatorics is already understood.
title: Categorical lift preserves the maximiser dichotomy

description:
**Conjecture.** For a strictly convex, twice-differentiable radiator law with
`f(0) ≤ 0`, the cost reduction from splitting a collector of area `a` into `k`
equal independent radiators is bounded below by an explicit expression in the
modulus of strict convexity of `f` on `[0, a]`, and this bound is asymptotically
sharp as `k → ∞`.

The key insight is that the splitting law is currently qualitative (strict
decrease), but the size of the decrease is governed by how strongly `f` curves;
a modulus-of-convexity estimate converts the sign statement into a rate.

**Why now?** The qualitative splitting law is proved and its exact hypothesis
(`f(0) ≤ 0`) identified, so the remaining question is purely quantitative and can
be tested against closed-form curvature bounds for standard cost laws.
title: Quantitative splitting gain

description:
**Conjecture.** For any positive-definite binary quadratic form `Q(u, v)` of
discriminant `-4`, the family of twists `E^{Q(u,v)}` realizes rank one infinitely
often, and the resulting surface `Q(u,v) y² = f(x)` is birational to
`(1 + t²) y² = f(x)` over the field generated by the form's automorphisms.

*The key insight is* that every form of discriminant `-4` is `\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})`-equivalent
to `u² + v²`, so the norm form `1 + t²` is not special — it is the canonical
representative of an entire equivalence class of quadratic-form twists.

*Why now?* With the `1 + t²` case reduced to the sum-of-two-squares monoid, the
equivalence of forms gives an immediate, testable generalization whose only new
ingredient is the class-number-one structure of discriminant `-4`.
title: Quadratic-form twists beyond `1 + t²`

description:
For all `ℤ`-modules `G`, `H` and all `n`, the two left-derived functors of the tensor product
agree: `Tor(ModuleCat ℤ) n ≅ Tor'(ModuleCat ℤ) n`, and in particular
`Tor₁(G, H) ≅ Tor₁(H, G)`.

*Status.* Mathlib defines both `Tor` (derived in the second variable) and `Tor'` (derived in the
first) but does not prove them isomorphic. Our computation gives strong evidence in the cyclic
case: `Tor₁(G, ℤ/k) ≅ G[k]` (`torOneZModIso`), which for `G = ℤ/m` has order `gcd(k, m)`,
symmetric in `k` and `m`; and `Torₙ₊₂(G, ℤ/k) = 0` (`isZero_Tor_two_le_zmod`) matches the
vanishing of `Tor'ₙ₊₂` predicted by the same resolution used in the other variable. Falsified by
a pair `G`, `H` and a degree `n` with `Torₙ(G, H) ≇ Tor'ₙ(G, H)`.
title: C4. Balancing of `Tor`

description:
The files work with degrees `0,1,2` (plus the generators in degree `3`, which is all that
is needed to know that `MH_{2,2}` is the cycle group).  The first substantial extension is
to define `MC_{k,ℓ}` for all `k` (tuples indexed by `Fin (k+1)`, or lists), the alternating
sum differential, and to prove `∂² = 0`.  The only genuinely fiddly part is the simplicial
identity for the "length-preserving deletion" faces; the key auxiliary fact is that if
deleting `x_i` preserves the total length then `x_{i-1} ≠ x_{i+1}`, which is already
proved here in the `k = 2` case inside `delta2gen`.
title: A. The full magnitude chain complex in all degrees

description:
**Conjecture.** The map sending a history `ls` to its action `B ↦ reviseSeq B ls` is a
monoid homomorphism from `List (Literal Atom)` (concatenation) onto the monoid of partial
sign assignments `Atom →₀ Option Bool` under *right-biased overwrite*, and its kernel
congruence is generated by exactly the two local rules `revise_comm_of_ne_atom` and
`revise_revise_of_eq_atom`.

*Falsifiable content.* Produce two histories with the same action that cannot be connected
by a finite chain of the two local rewrites. `reviseSeq_ext_iff` already shows that the
action is determined by `lastSign`, so the open half is completeness of the rewrite system;
`normalForm_unique` supplies the confluence target.
title: The revision monoid is the free "last-write-wins" monoid

description:
**Conjecture.** The certificate theory of `GridCertificates.lean` survives
non-commutativity: every non-developable `G`-valued field on the `m × n` grid has a
certificate that is either a single tile boundary or one of the two fundamental loops,
of combinatorial length at most `max m n`.  Note that the cycle-space argument used in
the additive case (`grid_cycle_span`, a statement about the ℤ-module of one-chains) is
unavailable here: the analogue must be proved with free-group relations, using the
fundamental group of the torus rather than its first homology.  Whether the abelian
bound `max m n` is preserved, or must be replaced by a word-length bound in
`π₁`, is exactly the testable point.
title: Non-abelian certificates on the grid

description:
Add to `TropIIA + TropPareto + TropDiagIdem` either (i) homogeneity under all rational
scalings, `f (q ⊙ x) = q ⊙ f x` for `q ∈ ℚ`, or (ii) continuity of `f` in the order
topology.  Then `f` is a coalition rule.

Evidence: the refutation `not_oligarchy_of_tropIIA_tropDiagIdem` uses the distortion
`φ(r) = 2r` for `r ≥ 0` and `r/2` for `r < 0`, which is continuous but only
*doubling*-homogeneous; conversely, `isTropLinear_of_tropIIA_constScale` shows that full
scalar homogeneity forces linearity, and then `oligarchy_iff` applies.

Falsifiable: a continuous (respectively rationally homogeneous) additive unanimous
diagonally idempotent rule differing from every `tropCoalition s`.  Version (ii) would fall
to a continuous variant of `φ` that is doubling-homogeneous yet non-linear; version (i)
requires a `φ` homogeneous for every rational scalar but not additive.
title: Conjecture B (Continuity, or rational homogeneity, restores the oligarchy theorem)

description:
For a nontrivial commutative semiring `S` the following are equivalent: (a) `S` has no zero
divisors; (b) for every `n`, the additive, multiplicative, unanimous maps `Sⁿ → S` are
exactly the `n` projections.

Evidence: (a) ⟹ (b) is proved (`semiring_arrow_iff`), and (b) fails for the product
semirings `R × R'` (`exists_nondictatorial_of_zero_divisors`), which are exactly the
"decomposable" zero-divisor examples.  The open content is that *every* semiring with a
zero divisor `st = 0`, `s,t ≠ 0`, admits a non-dictatorial rule — the natural candidate
being `x ↦ s ⊙ x₀ ⊕ t ⊙ x₁` after normalising `s ⊕ t = 1`.

Falsifiable: a commutative semiring containing a zero divisor for which every additive,
multiplicative, unanimous `f : S² → S` is a projection (e.g. `ℤ/4ℤ`, where `2·2 = 0` but
`2` cannot be completed to a unanimous pair, is the first place to look).
title: Conjecture C (Zero divisors characterise the dictatorship theorem)

description:
The orbit-Bernoulli model is the natural biased model, but is it the *only*
extremal one?  Conjecture: among all probability distributions `P` on
`GroupInvariantPattern G α` whose expected number of "on" orbits is `m θ`, the
entropy `entropyBits P` is maximized precisely by `orbitBernoulli θ`, with value
`m · H₂(θ)`.  *Refutation:* a group action, a `θ` and a distribution with the
same expected onset density and strictly larger entropy.  Together with the
proved deficit law this would make `m · (1 - H₂(θ))` the exact information cost
of a stylistic onset density, rather than merely the cost of one particular
model.
title: N5. Maximum entropy at fixed onset density

description:
**Conjecture.** If `G̃ → G` is a finite regular cover of `(q+1)`-regular graphs with covering
group `Γ`, then the chord spectrum of `G̃` is the disjoint union of the chord spectrum of `G` and
the chord spectra of the twisted (Artin–Ihara) factors, and it is rational iff every twisted
factor has rational trace and determinant.  Cycle 1 proves the analogous statement for Cartesian
products (`chord_cartesian_add`: chord spectra add as a sumset) and shows the total chord value is
always `0` (`total_chord_eq_zero`), so any invariant must be built from the multiset, not its sum.

*The key insight is* that chord value = adjacency eigenvalue (`localFactor_chord`), so operations
on graphs act on chord spectra exactly as they act on adjacency spectra; covers are the first case
where the action is by *induction of representations* rather than by a sumset.

*Why now?* The Cartesian-product case is now a theorem with an explicit eigenvector `v ⊗ w`; the
same explicit-eigenvector technique applies verbatim to the regular representation of a cyclic
cover.
title: Chord spectra of graph covers: a new-factor criterion

description:
For a bipartite pure state in `ℂ^m ⊗ ℂ^n` the Hopf construction gives two
circles in `S^{2N−1}`, `N = mn`. **Conjecture:** for `N ≥ 3` the two circles are
always *unlinked* (all Gauss linking numbers vanish, since circles unknot in
codimension ≥ 3), while the correct invariant is the rank of the coefficient
matrix; equivalently entanglement is the failure of the state to lie on the
Segre variety, detected by the Plücker relations rather than by any linking
number.

*The key insight is* that the equivalence "entanglement = linking" is not a
general principle but a coincidence of the two-qubit case, where the fibre
complement in `S³` is a solid torus with `H₁ ≅ ℤ`.

*Why now?* Our definition of linking is completely explicit
(`HopfLink.windingNumber` of the linear functional `det(u,·)`), so the
higher-dimensional statement can be tested by the same machinery: `det(u,·)` is
replaced by an `(N−1)`-form and the winding integral by a degree computation.

**Falsification test:** produce, for some `m·n ≥ 6`, two Hopf fibres in
`S^{2mn−1}` with a nonzero Gauss linking number.
title: Conjecture B (linking is a low-dimensional accident; rank is the invariant)

description:
The additive correction in `myers_bound_with_shortfall` is not optimal: the sharp bound is
`L ≤ π√(m/ε) + f(D/ε)` with `f(x) < x` for `x > 0`, `f(x)/x → 1` as `x → 0⁺`, and `f`
determined by the extremal profile that places the whole shortfall where the Prüfer phase
moves slowest (i.e. where `|θ|` is largest).

**The key insight is** that the shortfall is charged at the *worst-case* weight
`a/(a² + θ²) ≤ 1/a` in the phase estimate, whereas an actual profile pays the true weight;
the deficit between the two is exactly the gap seen numerically in
`ComputationalEvidence.md §7`, where the proved bound over-estimates the blow-up time by a
factor of about two.

**Why now?** The weighted form of the estimate is already isolated inside
`arctan_expansion_decay_with_defect`, and `myers_phase_stability` shows how to keep the
weight `a/(a² + θ²)` rather than discarding it — the same bookkeeping applied to the
shortfall gives a variational problem in one function.

**Falsifiable by:** a curvature profile with shortfall `D` whose blow-up time exceeds
`π√(m/ε) + f(D/ε)` for the candidate `f`.

title: Conjecture B′ (Sharp constant for the shortfall correction)

description:
The structures `GeodesicCongruence`, `TrappedSurface` and `JacobiField` formalized here
are exactly the data induced by a smooth Lorentzian manifold satisfying the null energy
condition along a null generator of a trapped surface; consequently every bound, every
rigidity statement *and every stability estimate* proved here upgrades, with no new
analysis, to genuine null geodesic incompleteness — and to the classical rigidity
conclusion "the extremal spacetime is the constant-curvature model" — once the index-form
machinery is available.

**The key insight is** that all of the analytic content of the Penrose–Hawking theorems is
the one-dimensional comparison theory established in this project; the differential
geometry only supplies the Raychaudhuri equation as an *instance* of the structures.

**Why now?** Mathlib has semi-Riemannian metrics and geodesics but no Raychaudhuri
equation; the missing step is a single lemma deriving the equation for the second
fundamental form of a null hypersurface, after which every theorem here applies verbatim.

**Falsifiable by:** discovering that the induced expansion of a null congruence fails one
of the structure's hypotheses (e.g. differentiability of `θ` on a half-open affine
interval) in a physically relevant example.
title: Conjecture E (From congruences to spacetimes)

description:
**Conjecture.** On any graph of minimum degree `k`, a divisor with `m ≥ 1` chips at
every vertex has rank at least `min(m(m+3)/2, m + k)`, and this is sharp: complete
graphs attain the first term and `k`-regular graphs of large girth the second.

*The key insight is* that the complete-graph proof fires the nested chain of
threshold sets `S_t = {v : E v ≥ t}` *simultaneously*, as one Laplacian vector
`f = u − 1` with `u_v = ⌈(E v − (m − t))/n⌉`; on a general graph the same vector is
still available, and the only thing that changes is that `outdeg(S_t, v)` replaces
the constant `n − |S_t|`, which the minimum-degree hypothesis controls from below.

*Why now.*  The target value is no longer a guess: `rankBN_const_K` proves it is
attained, and `rank_const_K_gt_threshold_bound` proves the previously available
one-shot bound `2m + ⌊m²/4⌋` is strictly smaller for every `m ≥ 3`.  So the
conjecture is exactly the statement that the complete-graph mechanism is universal,
and its first open case, `m = 3` (`9` versus the proved `8`), is a finite check on
small `k`-regular graphs.
title: Iterated firing: the true one-shot ceiling for general graphs

description:
**Conjecture.**  For the separable box update `boxStep lo hi η` on `d` coordinates with
`s := #{i : lo i < hi i}` nondegenerate coordinates, the total ReLU width required to
implement one simultaneous step (as a map `ℝᵈ → ℝᵈ` built from scalar units with
arbitrary affine skips) is exactly `2d + 2s`.

*The key insight is* that separability makes the curvature test coordinatewise
(`sep_minimizes_iff_coordinatewise` is the loss-side shadow of the same phenomenon), so
the widths add: each degenerate coordinate contributes the point-case width `2` and
each nondegenerate coordinate the segment-case width `4`.

*Why now?*  `box_minimizes_iff_mem_box` and `box_descent_reaches_minimizer` show the
`d`-dimensional dynamics factor exactly through the `d` scalar ones, and the scalar
widths `2` and `4` are now theorems, so the only missing ingredient is a
`d`-dimensional counting argument.

---
title: Tropical width spectrum of `d`-dimensional box descent

description:
**Conjecture.** A weight-graded dg-algebra `A` is pure if and only if the inclusion of the
diagonal cocycle subalgebra `diagAlg ⊆ A` (already constructed, with zero differential) induces
a *surjection* on cohomology in every degree **and** the off-diagonal part of `A` is exact as a
complex in each fixed weight. In particular purity is equivalent to a statement about a single
strict subalgebra, with no reference to truncations.

*The key insight is* that `diagAlg → H(A)` is always multiplicative and its surjectivity is the
only place where purity was used in `diagonal_strict_section`; the converse direction should
recover weight-wise acyclicity from surjectivity plus a dimension/graded-Nakayama argument.

*Why now?* `diagSubalg_surjective_on_cohomology` supplies one direction verbatim; the converse
is a finite bookkeeping statement about the same objects. Falsifiable by an example where
`diagAlg` surjects on cohomology but some off-diagonal weight-complex has cohomology.
title: C2. Purity is detected by the diagonal subalgebra alone

description:
**Statement.** For `T` a real Möbius map of positive determinant and `S` a
measurable subset of the upper half-plane,
`∫_{T(S)} dx dy/y² = ∫_S dx dy/y²`.

*The key insight is* that `mobius_conformal_factor` already contains the
proof: the real Jacobian of `T` viewed as a map `ℝ² → ℝ²` is `‖T'(z)‖²`, and
`Im T(z) = ‖T'(z)‖ · Im z` is exactly the statement proved, so the density
`1/y²` transforms with the reciprocal of the Jacobian.  What remains is
Mathlib's change-of-variables theorem, not geometry.

*Why now?* Mathlib has `MeasureTheory.integral_image_eq_integral_abs_det_fderiv_smul`;
the missing input was precisely the pointwise identity now proved.

**Falsifiable form.** Apply `z ↦ -1/z` to the ideal triangle `(0,1,∞)`, whose
image is the ideal triangle `(∞,-1,0)`; the conjecture predicts both have area
`π`.  Any numerically different value refutes it.
title: Conjecture B — area is a Möbius invariant, hence a genuine isometry invariant

description:
**Statement.** Let `P` be an ideal `n`-gon (vertices any `n` distinct boundary
points).  Every geodesic triangulation of `P` by non-crossing diagonals uses
exactly `n - 2` ideal triangles, and consequently `area(P) = (n-2)π/κ` for
*every* such triangulation.

*The key insight is* that the vertical-strip decomposition proved in
`idealPolygonArea_eq` is one particular triangulation, so triangulation
invariance is equivalent to the purely combinatorial statement that all
triangulations of a convex `n`-gon have `n - 2` cells — an Euler-characteristic
argument that is cross-domain (combinatorics feeding a measure-theoretic
identity) and independent of the analysis already done.

*Why now?* The analytic half is finished and sharp; only the combinatorial half
remains, and it is finite and inductive.

**Falsifiable form.** Exhibit a triangulation of an ideal pentagon whose cells'
areas sum to something other than `3π`.
title: Conjecture C — ideal polygons are rigid *and* triangulation-independent

description:
**Conjecture.** Let `A(n, q)` be the set of transcript maps realisable by *adaptive
comparison* algorithms, where the `k`-th query is a function of the previous answers and is
one of the `q`-outcome order queries on `n` items.  Then `A(n, q)` is strictly smaller than
the set of injective maps `Perm (Fin n) → Fin d → Fin q` for every `q ≥ 3` and every
`d < ⌈log_q (n!)⌉ + c` with an absolute constant `c ≥ 1`, and the exact minimal adaptive
depth exceeds the counting bound `⌈log_q (n!)⌉` for infinitely many `(n, q)`.

The key insight is that our proved lower bound `Sorter.clog_le_depth` uses only injectivity,
whereas realisable transcripts must additionally be *consistent*: the fibre of any prefix of
a transcript is an order ideal cut out by the queries asked so far, and multiway order
queries cannot split a permutation class into `q` arbitrary pieces. **Why now?** The counting
bound is proved and its achievability (`exists_sorter_clog_depth`) is proved to hold in the
*abstract* transcript model, so the gap between the two models is now a sharply posed,
finitely testable question for small `(n, q)`.
title: Semantic realisability of transcript profiles (the comparison-availability gap)

description:
**Statement.** Over the definitions `shuf` (shuffle) and `deconc`
(deconcatenation coproduct) of `Catalog/Novelty/`, for every nonempty word `w`
and every field `K ⊇ ℚ`,
`Σ_{(u,v) ∈ deconc w} (-1)^{|u|} · (count z (shuf (reverse u) v)) = 0` for all
`z`, i.e. `S(w) = (-1)^{|w|} · reverse w` is the antipode of the graded Hopf
algebra `(K⟨X⟩, ⧢, Δ_deconc)`.

*The key insight is* that the already-proved bialgebra axiom
`deconc_bind_shuf` upgrades to a Hopf structure precisely because the
deconcatenation coproduct is connected and graded, so the antipode is forced by
Takeuchi's recursion — and the closed form must then be a *signed multiset
identity between shuffles of reversals*, which is a purely combinatorial claim
amenable to the counting machinery (`count_shuf_eq_count_unsh`,
`count_deconc`) already developed here.

*Why now?* All of the counting infrastructure for `shuf`, `unsh` and `deconc`
now exists and is verified; the antipode is the last missing structure map, and
it is exactly the input needed to state Sweedler duality intrinsically.

---
title: C1. The antipode of the shuffle Hopf algebra is the signed reversal

description:
**Conjecture.**  For the vanishing ideal of a point and a test set `U` consisting
of all polynomials supported on a finite monomial set `E`, the Buchberger
completion of `∅` returns, up to tropical scaling, exactly a set of polynomials
whose supports are the circuits of the degree-`E` matroid — i.e. Buchberger
completion is a circuit enumeration algorithm in the tropical world.

*The key insight is* that leading-monomial reducibility, the driving relation of
the completion step, is monotone in the support order, so unresolved obstructions
must have minimal support.

*Why now?*  Both halves exist formally and are already connected:
`exists_buchberger_completion_vanishing` runs the algorithm on this ideal, and
`truncation_isCircuit_iff` identifies the target set.
title: C4. Buchberger completion computes circuits

description:
For a positive-definite `Q` on `ℤⁿ` the covering radius² is the maximum, over the Delaunay cells
`D` of the lattice, of the circumradius² of `D`, and this maximum is a rational function of the
Gram matrix with denominator a power of `det Q`.  In rank two the formula is `covRad`, whose
denominator is `4 det Q`; the conjecture is that in rank `n` the denominator divides
`(2 det Q)^{n-1}`.

*The key insight is* that cycle 11 proves the rank-two case by two entirely separate mechanisms —
an *integral* inequality `a p(p−1) + c q(q−1) + b p q ≥ 0` for the lower bound, and the *Lagrange
barycentric identity* plus concavity for the upper bound — and neither mechanism refers to the
rank: the barycentric identity holds in any rank, and the integral inequality is the statement
that the recentred paraboloid `Q(x) − ℓ(x)` is nonnegative on the lattice, where `ℓ` is the linear
form dual to the deep hole.

*Why now?* `covering_data_of_basis` shows the whole argument is stable under `GL_n(ℤ)`, so only a
*combinatorial* input is missing — a nonnegative-weight decomposition of the fundamental cell into
simplices with lattice vertices, i.e. an obtuse superbasis, which exists in rank `≤ 3`.  Rank
three is therefore an immediate, finite target.

---
title: Conjecture F (Delaunay formula for the covering radius in every rank)

description:
`W(Q) = {4μ(v/2)}` is a complete invariant in rank two (cycle 10), so the first isospectral pair
with equal `W` occurs in rank `≥ 3`.  Conjecture: the pair `(μ(Q), λ₁(Q), det Q)` is a complete
invariant of a binary lattice, and in rank three there exist non-isometric lattices with the same
theta series **and** the same covering radius but different `W`.

*The key insight is* that `covRad λ₁ b c` together with `λ₁` and `det = (4λ₁c − b²)/4` determines
`(λ₁, b, c)` — three rational equations in the two unknowns `b, c` with a positivity constraint —
so in rank two the covering radius is already a *second* complete invariant, independent of the
enumerator; if this collapses in rank three, the failure is exactly the phenomenon that separates
covering from packing.

*Why now?* All three quantities are already formalised (`IsMinEnergy`, `covRad`,
`rank_two_covering_radius`), so the rank-two half is an algebraic elimination, and the rank-three
half needs only the diagonal case, which cycle 9 computes.

---
title: Conjecture G (The covering radius separates what the theta series cannot)

description:
**Conjecture.** For any finite abelian group `G` and any `g ∈ G` acting on a
`G`-set built functorially from `ℤ/N`, the orbit count is a `ℤ`-linear functional
of the fixed-point sequence `k ↦ #Fix(g^k)`, and every such functional is
computable from `(N, ord_N b)` alone precisely when the local orders coincide.

*The key insight is* `Round11.card_fix_eq_fpr` together with
`Round11.groupoid_balanced_no_leak`: the topological invariant is an average of
the fingerprint, and in the balanced case the average collapses to `(d + N − 1)/d`,
a function of `N` and `ord_N b` only. *Why now?* Both ingredients are proved; the
general form needs only Burnside plus the CRT decomposition already formalised.
title: C3 (Burnside seal, general form).

description:
**Statement.** The number of `N ≤ X` that are products of two distinct odd
primes and admit a coprime semiprime `N' ≤ X^{1+o(1)}` with
`jointLaw N = jointLaw N'` is `(1 − o(1))` times the number of semiprimes up
to `X`.

**The key insight is** that the joint law only remembers the pair
(abelian group `Z_{p−1} × Z_{q−1}`, quadratic character), and the number of such
isomorphism classes with `φ(N) ≤ Y` grows far more slowly than the number of
semiprimes — a pigeonhole in a quotient category, not in the integers.

**Why now?** Item 5 above makes the transport mechanism a theorem, so the
conjecture reduces to counting isomorphism classes of pairs (group, character),
which is a tractable multiplicative-number-theory problem (Erdős–Pomerance-style
counts of `φ`-fibres).
title: C1 (Collision density). Almost every semiprime has a joint-law twin.

description:
*(Superseding the earlier C5, whose congruence-transporting form is now proved
as `transport_coprime_iff` and whose unrestricted form is refuted by
`polynomial_hypothesis_necessary`.)*

**Statement.** There are infinitely many semiprimes `N = p·q` with
`p < q` for which `gcd(N, 2^N - 1) = p`; equivalently, infinitely many prime
pairs with `ord_p(2) = q` and `q ∣ p - 1`. Moreover the counting function of
such `N` up to `X` is `X^{1/2+o(1)}`, so the exponential leak has density `0`
among all semiprimes and does **not** threaten randomly generated RSA moduli.

**The key insight is** that `prime_dvd_mersenne_iff` reduces the leak to an
order condition, `ord_p(2) ∣ N`, and for a semiprime this forces
`ord_p(2) ∈ {1, q}`; so the leaking moduli are exactly those built from a prime
`p` whose order of `2` is the *other* prime factor — a condition of
Artin/Wieferich type, verified here at `p = 23`, `q = 11`, `N = 253`.

**Why now?** The order criterion and one explicit witness are already
formalised; what is missing is an infinitude argument (a Zsygmondy-style
primitive-divisor input: for each prime `q`, a primitive prime divisor `p` of
`2^q - 1` has `ord_p(2) = q`, and one needs `p ≡ 1 mod q` together with
`N = pq` in the required range). Falsifiable in either direction: a proof that
only finitely many such pairs exist would be equally interesting, and a density
above `X^{1/2+ε}` would make the exponential modulus a genuine cryptanalytic
concern.
title: C5 (Order-sieve frontier: which semiprimes does the exponential modulus factor?).

description:
**Conjecture.** Any candidate filter that is `M`-periodic accepts exactly `|S|`
of every `M` consecutive candidates (proved here as `card_window_filter`);
therefore *no* periodic test can convert an interval hint into positional
information.  The conjecture is that the converse holds too: a filter that
amplifies an interval hint must be aperiodic, hence must depend on the *size* of
the candidate — and every size-dependent exact test known (Fermat, Lehman,
Hart) already costs `Ω(N^{1/3})`.

*The key insight is* that "residue information" and "positional information" are
orthogonal: CRT independence makes the survivor set a union of full residue
classes, which is translation-invariant by construction.

*Why now?* `card_window_filter` isolates the periodicity hypothesis in one line
of Lean, so the converse can be attacked as a statement about the aperiodicity
of the accepted set rather than about factoring itself.
title: C5. Positional blindness is the real obstruction (a general no-go)

description:
**Conjecture.** The MODPAR primitive has query complexity exactly
`Θ(m / log m)` for recovering `{p mod m, q mod m}`: the adversary bound of
`ModPar.transcript_eq_of_avoids` (a query set avoiding ≤ 6 marked classes is
uninformative) is tight up to the `log` factor achieved by a randomized
group-testing strategy over the residues.

*The key insight is* that the parity pattern is a *sparse* Boolean vector (3 ones
out of `m`, `ModPar.card_support`), and sparse recovery from parity queries is
exactly group testing — so the true complexity should be sub-linear, contradicting
the folklore `Ω(m)` reading of the closure.

*Why now?* The support and its size are both proved exactly, so the two sides of
the bound can be compared without any further structure theory.
title: C4. A decision-tree lower bound with a matching upper bound

description:
*(The exponential case is now closed: `geometric_scaling_law` proves
`b(m+1)/2 ≤ noiseFloor ≤ b(m+1) + b/(1-r)` at the natural cut
`r^{m+1} ≤ b ≤ r^m`, i.e. `noiseFloor ≍ b·log(1/b)/log(1/r)`.  What remains is
the power-law case, where the counting function is polynomial rather than
logarithmic.)*

For the power-law spectrum `aᵢ = (i+1)^{-β}` with `β > 1`, truncated at any
`n ≥ b^{-1/β}`, there are constants `0 < c_β ≤ C_β` with

```
c_β · b^{1 - 1/β}  ≤  noiseFloor(a, b)  ≤  C_β · b^{1 - 1/β}.
```

**The key insight is** that the head/tail sandwich of Part IV converts the
analytic scaling law into pure counting: `#{i : aᵢ ≥ b}` plus a tail energy, so
the exponent `1 - 1/β` is a statement about the *counting function of the
spectrum*, not about any optimisation.

**Why now?** `half_minSum_le_noiseFloor` and `minSum_head_tail` reduce the
problem to two elementary sums, both of which have closed forms (geometric) or
standard integral comparisons (power law); this would give the first fully
formal derivation of a neural-scaling-law exponent from a variational principle.

**Falsifier:** a `β` for which the two-sided bound fails for arbitrarily small
`b`.

---
title: Conjecture D3 (Power-law scaling law)

description:
**Conjecture.**  The class of "residue-dial observables" is closed under
products (proved: `ResidueDial.prod`), under composition with any function of
the readout, and under *conditioning on a polynomial-time computable predicate
of `N`* — and it is exactly the class of observables invariant under the action
of `(ℤ/|D|)ˣ`-preserving bijections of the semiprime family.  In particular no
finite or `poly(log N)`-sized family of extrinsic discriminants gives a
factoring advantage.

*The key insight is* that the tensor closure proved in cycle 3 turns a family of
individually weak observables into a single weak observable, so amplification
arguments (majority vote over many `D`) cannot work: the amplified statistic is
still a dial.

*Why now?*  `ResidueDial.prod` is already formalised; the remaining step is a
"dial ⇒ no advantage" theorem stated over a probability space of semiprimes,
for which Mathlib's `PMF`/`Finset` machinery suffices.

**Lean shape.**
`theorem no_advantage (d : ResidueDial m ι) (A : ι → Bool) : ∀ N M, sameResidue N M → A (readout N) = A (readout M)` and its amplified version over `Finset` families.

---
title: C3. Dial Algebra: the closure of factor-blind observables

description:
**Conjecture.**  For a class group `G` and semiprimes `N = pq` drawn with
classes `([𝔭], [𝔮])` uniform in `G × G`, the observation `[𝔭][𝔮]` has exactly
`log₂|G|` bits of Shannon information about the pair, while the pair carries
`2 log₂|G|` bits: the dial destroys exactly half of the class information, and
none of the destroyed half is recoverable from `N mod |D|`.

*The key insight is* the fibre count `product_fiber_card`: every observed class
is compatible with exactly `|G|` ordered pairs, uniformly — so the loss is not
merely typical but exact and distribution-independent.

*Why now?*  `product_fiber_card` is proved here; converting an exact fibre count
into an entropy statement is a finite computation with Mathlib's
`Finset`-based entropy or a direct counting argument.

**Lean shape.**
`theorem dial_entropy_loss (G) [Group G] [Fintype G] : H(pair | product) = Real.logb 2 (Fintype.card G)`.

---
title: C4. Quantitative collapse: how many bits does a dial destroy?

description:
**Conjecture.** Shor's period-finding applied to `k ↦ a^k mod N` recovers
`ord_N(a)` in polynomial time but *provably cannot* recover any individual
`ord_p(a)`: the reduced-modulus data `{ord_{N/d}(a)}` is accessible to a quantum
sampler only through states supported on the strata `S_d`, whose total weight is
`(p+q−1)/N = O(N^{-1/2})` for balanced semiprimes. Formally: preparing a
uniform superposition over a non-unit stratum requires a factor of `N`.

*The key insight is* that the asymmetry proved here lives entirely on a set of
measure `O(N^{-1/2})`, so the quantum advantage in period finding does not
transfer to the asymmetric readout without a state-preparation oracle that is
itself as hard as factoring.

*Why now?* The density statements are proved (`informative_density`,
`informative_density_sqrt`), and the stratum decomposition is available as a
Lean-level partition (`sum_stratum_card`), which is exactly the decomposition a
quantum register would need.
title: C5. The quantum channel is exactly the missing enumeration

description:
**Conjecture.** For a fixed `G`, the set of achievable pairs
`(rate, information)` over *all* conjugation-stable forks and *all* moduli is the
finite set `{(|S|/|G|, H(pq) − p·H(q)) : S a union of G^ab-fibres thinned by a
G-orbit}` — in particular it is contained in the curve family
`I = H(pq) − p·H(q)` with `p ∈ (1/[G:G'])·ℤ` and `q ∈ (1/|G'|)·ℤ`.

*The key insight is* that every fork factors as (pinned part) ∘ (flat thinning),
because the commutator subgroup acts transitively on the ambiguity: the leakage
law is not one example but a normal form.
*Why now?* `info_leak`, `info_leak_strict` and `abelian_hom_eq_one_on_V4` give
the two extremes; the missing step is a decomposition lemma "every fork is a
`q`-thinning of its `G^ab`-saturation", which is a finite-group statement.
title: C2. Universal leakage spectrum of a Galois group

description:
**Conjecture.** For `N = p₁ ⋯ p_k` with independent uniform classes in a finite group `G` of order
`n`, the accessible dial satisfies
```
I(class N ; [some pᵢ splits]) ≤ k² / n²   for all k ≥ 2, n ≥ 2,
```
and, for fixed `n`, `I` is strictly decreasing in `k` with at least geometric rate: extra factors
*destroy* the dial rather than accumulate it (the measured ratios `I(k+1)/I(k)` are `≈ 1/7` at
`n = 3` and `≈ 1/16` at `n = 4`).

**The key insight is** that the product map `Gᵏ → G` is a homomorphism with uniform fibres, so the
conditional law of the split pattern given `class N` depends on the observable only through the
event `class N = 1`; inclusion–exclusion over the `k` factors then makes the fibre discrepancy
`O(k (n−1)^{k−1} / n^k)`, and squaring it inside the `χ²` bound is what produces the rapid decay
in `k`.
**Why now?** The wall half is proved for all `k` (`kfactor_wall`), the `k = 2` dial is exact with a
sharp constant (C6), and the `χ²` bound `mutualInfo_le_chi2` converts a fibre count directly into
an information bound; the missing ingredient is purely combinatorial.  Falsifiable by one
`(n, k)` with a measured dial above `k²/n²`; the measured table (`ComputationalEvidence.md`,
cycle 2) is consistent and suggests the bound is far from tight.
title: C13. `k`-factor products: the dial decays like `k²/n²` (and in fact much faster)

description:
**Conjecture.**  Let `S` be a finite candidate set and `h` a hint.  Define the
invariance group `Γ_h = { σ ∈ Sym(S) : h ∘ σ = h }`.  Then the number of
readings satisfies `#readings = |S| / |Γ_h|` **iff** `Γ_h` acts freely and
transitively on every class; and in general `#readings · min_orbit ≤ |S|`, with
equality exactly when all orbits are of equal size.  Cycle III proves the
inequality (`card_image_mul_le`); the conjecture is the equality case and its
characterisation.

*The key insight is* that a hint is not a function but a partition, and a
partition with a group of symmetries can only be as fine as the coarsest orbit
decomposition — so the "wasted bits" of every hint family in the taxonomy are a
single group-theoretic invariant, not four separate accidents.

*Why now?*  Cycles I–III already give the two extreme cases in Lean (trivial
group: exact `2^t`; Klein four-group: exact `2^{t-3}`), so the general statement
can be attacked with the existing `cost_ge_of_family` / `card_image_mul_le`
machinery plus Mathlib's `MulAction` orbit-counting API.
title: C1. Deficit = order of the invariance group, exactly (not merely `≥`)

description:
**Conjecture.** `TS` is real closed. By `EMLTS.isRealClosed_iff_exists_root_odd_monic`
(proved this cycle) this is now *equivalent* to the single clause: every **monic**
odd-degree `P ∈ TS[X]` has a root in `TS`. The proposed route is: (i) the `orderTop`
valuation on `TS` has divisible value group `Rank` and residue field `ℝ`, and `ℝ` is
real closed (`Real.instIsRealClosed`, proved this cycle from the IVT); (ii) a
Newton-polygon induction reduces an odd-degree `P` to an odd-degree polynomial over the
residue field, which has a root; (iii) Hensel lifts it — the lifting step is already
formalised as `EMLTS.exists_root_of_residue_simple_root`.

**The key insight is** that the induction cannot be `ω`-indexed. Our experiments show two
independent obstructions, both now documented as negative evidence rather than guesses:
a family `c_n t^n` with infinitesimal `c_n` need not be summable in a Hahn field of rank
`≥ 2` (explicit counterexample `c_n = single (1, -n) 1`), and the Newton iterates
`2^k · δ` never leave one archimedean class of a rank-`4` lexicographic group. So the
correct statement of the induction is transfinite: the approximation sequence must be
indexed by the order type of the support, and the summability condition must be
`Set.IsPWO` of the union of supports, not convergence in a metric sense.

**Progress this cycle.** The scaling step is done unconditionally
(`EMLTS.exists_newtonScale_normalized`), so the conjecture may now be restated in its
sharpest form: *every normalised monic odd-degree `P ∈ TS[X]` has a root*, where
normalised means `|P.coeff i| ≤ 1` for all `i` and `|P.coeff i| = 1` for some `i < n`.
The only remaining input is the *residue* step: pass to the monic real polynomial
`p̄ ≠ X^n` of degree `n`, take one of its real roots `a`, and either lift it (if simple,
which is `EMLTS.exists_root_of_residue_simple_root`) or substitute `X ↦ a + Y` and
re-scale — the latter being the transfinite recursion described below.

**Why now?** Every ingredient except that induction is in place and machine-checked:
henselianity of `ℝ⟦X⟧` (`PowerSeriesHensel.instIsAdicCompleteSpanX`), the lifting
theorem in `TS`, divisibility of `Rank`, real closedness of the residue field, and the
reduction of the whole problem to one clause. A falsifiable milestone on the way: the
deformation theorem `EMLTS.exists_root_perturbed_real_polynomial` should generalise from
one infinitesimal parameter to any finite tuple of infinitesimals; if it does not, the
summability obstruction above is essential and the transfinite formulation is forced.
title: C2. Real closedness via a transfinite Newton polygon over a divisible rank group

description:
**(A) Coset-by-coset traversal.**  A hamiltonian cycle in `Cay(G, S)` is produced by choosing a
cyclic subgroup `N = ⟨a⟩` with cyclic "quotient direction" `b`, traversing each coset of `N`
completely, and choosing a direction for each traversal so that the accumulated column shift is
`0` in `N`.  For `N` central the closing condition is the arithmetic congruence
`m ∣ ∑_{j<k} d j` (`isHamiltonian_of_directions`); with a twist `b a b⁻¹ = a^e` it becomes the
*geometric* congruence `m ∣ ∑_{j<k} d j eʲ` (`isHamiltonian_of_twisted_directions`).  The
geometric sum explains *why* the twisted case is easier rather than harder:
`(e − 1) ∑_{j<k} eʲ = eᵏ − 1 ≡ 0 (mod m)` holds automatically, so a nontrivial twist supplies
its own closing certificate.

**(B) Voltage.**  More generally (`isHamiltonian_of_factorGroup`), any `k`-periodic walk whose
prefix products meet each coset of `⟨z⟩` exactly once, where `z` is the *voltage* of one turn,
closes into a hamiltonian cycle after `|z|` turns.  This is the factor group lemma, formalized
here without ever forming a quotient group: the distinctness hypothesis is stated as
`P i' * (P i)⁻¹ ∈ ⟨z⟩ → i = i'`.  Principle (A) is the special case where the walk is
`a, …, a, b, a, …, a, b, …`.

**(C) The coset-pair criterion closes the transversal case.**  The gap left by the previous
cycle — a connection set that misses the normal subgroup `N = ⟨a⟩` and meets each nontrivial
coset at most once — is now a theorem.  The decisive observation is that one should *not* look
for a positive word: with `x̄ = 1` and `ȳ = m` in the quotient, the only `±`-free words whose
steps sum to `0` are `x^k` and `y^k`, both of voltage `1`.  The word that works is the
`k`-periodic **`x`-then-`x⁻¹` word**

```
x, x, …, x  (t times),  y,  x⁻¹, x⁻¹, …, x⁻¹  (t − 1 times),  y        with t = k − m,
```

whose prefix products run through the cosets `N, Nx, …, Nx^{k−1}` exactly once and whose
voltage is `B · (x B x⁻¹)` for a conjugate `B` of `A`.  That voltage is *never* trivial: it is
trivial only if `x B x⁻¹ = B⁻¹`, and conjugation by `x` has odd order `k` on the cyclic group
`⟨a⟩` of odd prime order `q`, while inversion has order `2` — so `B = 1`, a contradiction.  No
arithmetic side condition on the twist survives, which is why the criterion
(`isHamiltonian_of_coset_pair`) is uniform in `m` and applies equally to abelian and nonabelian
groups.  Combined with the dichotomy `pq_isHamiltonian_or_transversal` and the small-prime
cases `p = 2, 3`, this yields the complete order-`pq` theorem.

---
title: Organizing principles

description: For arbitrary dense point clouds, explicitly producing all pairwise filtration values requires `Ω(N²)` output operations; an `O(N log N)` exact algorithm can therefore exist only under an implicit, sparse, bounded-dimensional, or output-sensitive representation. A precise lower bound should be proved in a comparison or algebraic decision-tree model.
title: Complexity claim requires a sparse model

description:
For linear restriction maps with Gaussian local noise and a Gaussian prior on global sections, test whether least-squares minimization of the coboundary norm equals the posterior mean, and characterize when its excess risk is controlled by the nonzero spectrum of the first sheaf Laplacian. The conjecture is that cohomology accounts for the irreducible component of risk while small positive eigenvalues account for instability.

**The key insight is...** maximum-likelihood claims become valid only after specifying a probability model, and the cochain complex naturally supplies the relevant quadratic form.

**Why now?** The exact patchability criterion cleanly identifies the nullspace that any statistical risk decomposition must isolate.
title: Statistical optimality under an explicit Gaussian sheaf model

description:
**Conjecture.** Once finite conductor fibres and an effective equality test are established for a specified natural subclass, there exists a canonical enumeration ordered first by conductor, then degree, then a normalized lexicographic arithmetic code.

The key insight is that “the first hundred” is meaningful only after proving finite fibres, eliminating duplicate codes, and fixing a canonical tie-breaker.

**Why now?** The logical prerequisites for a defensible enumeration are now explicit, turning an informal listing problem into a sequence of falsifiable classification and effectiveness questions.
title: Canonical conductor-ordered enumeration

description:
Let orbitals `(n,l)` have unperturbed Coulomb energy depending only on `n`, and perturb them by a term that is strictly increasing in `n+l`, with ties broken by `n`. Conjecture that there is a quantitative open region of perturbation parameters for which the first 118 orbital occupations follow the Madelung order.

The key insight is that the false Coulomb closures `2,10,28,60,110` arise from exact degeneracy in `l`; lifting that degeneracy in a controlled order can convert a hydrogenic spectrum into the observed block structure.

Why now? The cumulative Coulomb theorem isolates the degeneracy that must be broken and supplies exact gap sizes for perturbative inequalities.
title: Madelung ordering as a spectral perturbation theorem

description:
**Conjecture.** For a commitment-based certificate protocol whose transcript semantics is compositional over proof trees, every permitted refinement preserves completeness, special soundness, and honest-verifier zero knowledge, while weakly reducing verifier work.

The key insight is that conclusion preservation alone is insufficient for cryptography; refinement must commute with transcript extraction and simulation as well as with logical interpretation.

**Why now?** The syntactic refinement layer and the cryptographic state layer are already cleanly separated. This makes it possible to state preservation obligations as local laws for each rewrite constructor and then lift them to arbitrary refinement sequences.
title: Cryptographic soundness preserved by proof normalization

description:
**Conjecture.** Within a proof grammar containing divisibility, parity, coprimality, and contradiction rules, all standard elementary certificates of the irrationality of the square root of two reduce to one of finitely many normal-form skeletons, and these skeletons have equal minimal audited cost.

The key insight is that the current four-stage audit trail simplifies only structural redundancy; enriching the grammar with arithmetic inference can test whether mathematically distinct arguments share a common irreducible core.

**Why now?** A concrete normal certificate and an exact cost trail are available as a baseline. The conjecture can be attacked incrementally by adding arithmetic rewrites and checking confluence and lower bounds at each extension.
title: Arithmetic normal forms for irrationality certificates

description:
**Conjecture.** In each sufficiently large subject area, the minimum number of incomparable statements forced by bounded dependency depth grows superlinearly in the logarithm of corpus size.

The key insight is that topological depth controls antichain width through rank collisions, so domain growth can be studied without assuming a power law. **Why now?** A rigorous finite width–depth mechanism is available, and domain-level rank histograms provide a direct empirical test.
title: Width–depth growth across mathematical domains

description:
**Conjecture.** If a heavy-tailed reuse law exists, its exponent depends systematically on topological rank: early foundational layers have a heavier out-degree tail than late layers.

The key insight is that a single global exponent discards the hierarchy that every finite acyclic dependency network necessarily possesses. **Why now?** Canonical ancestor ranks provide a principled stratification for testing whether the apparent tail is structural or a mixture of heterogeneous layers.
title: Rank-conditioned heavy tails

description:
**Conjecture.** In controlled experiments where successive revisions preserve a proof's stated conclusion while reducing independently measured structural complexity, confidence recovery is governed more strongly by removal of unresolved dependencies than by raw length reduction.

The key insight is that semantic content and structural complexity are distinct coordinates; refinement can hold the first fixed while changing the second.

**Why now?** A precise complexity-decreasing refinement model makes it possible to design paired stimuli that isolate dependency structure from conclusion and topic.
title: Semantic invariance and confidence recovery

description:
**Conjecture.** The inclusion matrix between `r`-sets and `k`-sets has a spectral certificate that distinguishes Ramsey-forcing incidence hypergraphs from arbitrary non-two-colourable uniform hypergraphs and improves the known counting obstruction by a factor exponential in `k`.

The key insight is that the auxiliary hypergraph is governed by the Johnson association scheme, whose eigenspaces encode intersection statistics invisible to first-moment counting. **Why now?** The Property-B equivalence provides a direct target for importing algebraic information from inclusion matrices into two-colourability.
title: Spectral obstruction for Ramsey incidence hypergraphs

description:
**Conjecture.** Every countable ordinal is the game value of a winning position on an infinite board using only finitely many pieces.

The key insight is that delaying gadgets can encode countable suprema, while forced corridors encode successor and ordinal addition. The central difficulty is realizing arbitrary countable limit constructions without introducing infinitely many pieces.

**Why now?** Explicit game trees already realize the hierarchy through `ω^ω`, isolating the exact operations that a geometric construction must simulate.
title: Countable-Ordinal Realization by Finite Material

description:
**Conjecture.** For coherent theories, two reflective axiom additions over the same base theory are equivalent over the base if and only if their induced idempotent monads are isomorphic as monads.

The key insight is that an idempotent monad should retain the closure operation imposed by the new axioms while forgetting accidental syntax.

**Why now?** Reflective mutations already compose and canonically induce monads, so the conjecture reduces classification of semantic changes to a comparison internal to one model category.
title: Mutation Monads Classify Conservative Axiom Addition

description:
Define the multiplicity-sensitive, conjugate-symmetric sum
`H(T) = Σ_{|Im ρ|≤T} 1/ρ` and determine an explicit renormalization under which `H(T)`
converges, with a quantitative error term derived from the Riemann–von Mangoldt formula.
This is falsifiable by comparing the predicted error against certified zero tables.
**The key insight is** that conjugate pairing converts a conditionally organized complex sum
into a real spectral statistic while zero counting controls its tail.
**Why now?** The finite separation and conjugation principles isolate exactly which analytic
estimates must be added to obtain a global theorem.
title: Renormalized zeta harmonic convergence

description:
**Conjecture.** For every symmetrizable Kac–Moody root datum and twisting weight, the shifted Chinta–Gunnells averages form a topological Schauder basis of the invariant holomorphic functions on every Weyl-stable compact subset of the interior of the complexified Tits cone, when coefficients are ordered by dominance.

The key insight is that the finite orbit-indicator decomposition should persist as a locally finite triangular expansion once orbit support is replaced by dominance-controlled analytic support. **Why now?** The finite theorem isolates uniqueness from analytic continuation, making the exact convergence statement that remains to be established both visible and testable.
title: Locally finite orbit-triangular decomposition on the Tits cone

description:
**Conjecture.** If nonnegative weights `a_n` satisfy `∑ a_n/n² < ∞`, then the
associated infinite geometric mixture is completely monotone:
`(-1)^r Δ^r C_k ≥ 0` for all `r,k`, and every completely monotone sequence whose
representing measure is supported on `{1-n⁻² : n ≥ 1}` arises uniquely this way.

The key insight is that each forward difference multiplies a geometric mode by
`-n⁻²`, turning all orders of finite differences into reciprocal moments.
**Why now?** The first-difference identity and positivity result identify the
correct representation theorem and its exact support.
title: Complete finite-difference hierarchy for positive measures

description:
**Conjecture.** Any increasing integer sequence whose successor differs from the globally greedy admissible choice by a uniformly bounded amount has a chronological additive hypergraph with zero upper edge density.

The key insight is that approximate greediness may preserve enough separation from the restricted sumset to suppress additive triples statistically even when exact sum-freeness is lost. **Why now?** The exact repaired rule produces an empty chronological hypergraph, providing the extremal endpoint from which a quantitative stability theory can be developed.
title: Hypergraph sparsity under bounded perturbations

description:
**Conjecture.** For each fixed `l ≥ k ≥ 3`, there are positive constants `a_{k,l}` and `b_{k,l}` such that every sufficiently large planar graph with spectral radius exceeding the `C_{k,l}`-free optimum by `ε n^{-1/2}` contains at least `a_{k,l} ε n - b_{k,l}` copies of `C_{k,l}`.

The key insight is that excess Rayleigh mass should be convertible into many local augmentations around high-weight vertices, and each augmentation either improves the candidate extremizer or creates an intersecting pair of cycles.

**Why now?** The baseline square-root estimate identifies the natural normalization for spectral excess, while recent structural extremal results indicate which local configurations should witness supersaturation.
title: Spectral supersaturation for intersecting cycles

description:
**Conjecture.** The negation/liar operator that obstructs complete self-knowledge
is exactly the order-reversing map with no monotone approximation, whereas every
*monotone* self-reference operator admits an emergent fixed point computed as the
limit of finite self-observation stages; consequently the consistent fragments of
a self-referential system are precisely its monotone sub-operators.

The key insight is that the diagonal obstruction and the emergent construction
are two faces of one dichotomy: order-reversal kills fixed points, order-
preservation guarantees an emergent one, and the finite-stage supremum makes the
latter constructive.

Why now? With the emergent fixed point pinned down as a concrete limit of finite
stages, the long-standing contrast between paradoxical (order-reversing) and
benign (monotone) self-reference can be made quantitative rather than merely
qualitative.
title: Emergent fixed points of self-reference operators

description:
**Conjecture.** For the fixed-amplitude Erdős–Rényi model `G(n, p)` with weight `z`,
there is a sharp threshold `p*(n)` such that above it the largest-modulus eigenvalue
is asymptotically `p·(n-1)·|z|` (the mean-direction outlier), while the bulk stays
within radius `2√{np(1-p)}·|z|`; the outlier separates from the bulk exactly when
`p·(n-1) > 2√{np(1-p)}`.

The key insight is that the deterministic complete-graph computation `(n-1)z` is the
`p → 1` endpoint of a family of expected row sums `p·(n-1)`, and the outlier/bulk
separation is governed by comparing this expected row sum with the semicircle radius
of the centered indicator matrix.

Why now? Both endpoints are already understood — the deterministic outlier for the
complete graph and the row-sum disk bound scaled by `|z|` — so the remaining task is
to interpolate them across `p`, a concrete and falsifiable analytic problem.
title: A phase-transition threshold for the mean-direction outlier

description:
Let `C` be a chain complex of free `ℤ`-modules and `G` an abelian group. Then for every `n` there
is a short exact sequence
`0 → Hₙ(C) ⊗ G → Hₙ(C ⊗ G) → Tor₁(Hₙ₋₁(C), G) → 0`,
natural in `C` and `G`, and split (non-naturally).

*Status.* We proved the theorem for the two-term free complex `C = (ℤ --(·k)--> ℤ)` in both
degrees: `H₀(G ⊗ C) ≅ G ⊗ H₀(C)` (`uctHomologyZeroIso`, no correction term since `H₋₁ = 0`) and
`H₁(G ⊗ C) ≅ Tor₁(G, H₀(C))` (`uctHomologyOneIso`, pure correction term since `H₁(C) = 0`,
`isZero_resComplex_homology_one`); the correction term is genuinely nonzero
(`not_isZero_uct_tor_term`, `torOneZMod_self_ne_zero`). We also proved the flat-coefficient case
`Hₙ(C ⊗ G) ≅ Hₙ(C) ⊗ G` for arbitrary complexes over any commutative ring
(`homologyTensorFlatIso`). Proving the general statement needs freeness of submodules of free
`ℤ`-modules (cf. C2) and the splitting `C ≅ Z ⊕ B[-1]`. Falsified by a free complex `C`, a group
`G` and a degree `n` where the displayed sequence is not exact.
title: C5. Universal coefficient theorem with the `Tor` correction term

description:
Cycle 1 established a sharp dichotomy: the Möbius identification
`(n,+1) ~ (−n,−1)` on `ℤ × {±1}` is a **free `ℤ/2`-cover of the point set**
(`Mobius.MInt.fiber_card`, `Mobius.MInt.deck_action_free`) that is
**multiplicatively trivialisable** (`Mobius.MInt.polarEquiv`,
`Mobius.MInt.orientationSplitting`) and **additively non-liftable**
(`Mobius.MInt.no_separable_lift_of_add`), while the ring itself is just `ℤ`
(`Mobius.MInt.equivZ`).  Every conjecture of the original mission is decided by
this dichotomy: class number one ✔, prime double cover ✔ *on elements* /
✘ *on the spectrum*, distinct factorisations of `6` ✔ *as oriented tuples* /
✘ *as a UFD failure*, non-Ore ✘, off-critical-line zeros ✔ *only trivial ones*
and equivalent to ¬RH otherwise.
title: Part I — status of the cycle-1 conjectures

description:
**Conjecture.** Every completely additive `f : ℕ_{>0} → ℝ` determined by prime values
`f(p) = φ(1/p)` for a fixed continuous `φ` fails to be injective; more precisely, injectivity of a
completely additive `f` forces the values `{f(p)}` to be linearly independent over `ℚ`, which is
impossible for any rational-valued rule such as `f(p) = 1/p`.  Cycle 1 proves the failure for the
prime chord (`primeChord_not_injective`, primitive collision `4 ↔ 27`, family `(4k, 27k)`).

*The key insight is* that a prime-indexed harmonic statistic is a monoid homomorphism from a free
commutative monoid of infinite rank into a one-dimensional group; faithfulness is therefore a
`ℚ`-linear independence statement about the prime values, not an analytic accident.

*Why now?* The exact collision family found computationally and proved in `PrimeChords.lean`
pinpoints the obstruction, and the `ℚ`-linear-independence reformulation is a finite-dimensional
statement that Lean's `LinearIndependent` API can express directly.
title: No completely additive prime-indexed encoding is faithful

description:
Cycle 2 proved the qualitative half of the original Conjecture D
(`integral_H1_torsion`, `torsion_obstruction_invisible_to_field_coefficients`).
The sharpened form now conjectures the exact module, and extends it off the
disjoint-loop nerve.  For stalks `ℤ` and restriction scalars `aᵢ ∈ ℤ`:

```
H¹(disjoint loops)  ≅  ⨁ᵢ ℤ/(aᵢ - 1)ℤ,
H¹(the n-cycle)     ≅  ℤ/(∏ᵢ aᵢ - 1)ℤ.
```

So on a connected cyclic nerve the *entire* integral obstruction is the cyclic
group cut out by the holonomy minus one, and the field-valued monodromy
criterion `cyclic_holonomy_criterion` is its reduction modulo the statement
"is this group infinite?".

*The key insight is* that the exponent of the integral obstruction is a
holonomy invariant, not a rank invariant: `∏ᵢ aᵢ - 1` refines the field-valued
dichotomy `∏ᵢ aᵢ = 1` vs `≠ 1` into an infinite arithmetic hierarchy, so two
datasets that look identical to every rational computation can be separated by
a single congruence.

Cycle 3 already proves the *exponent* half of this (the determinant of the
cyclic coboundary is `±(∏ᵢaᵢ - 1)`, and `det_smul_H1Zmat_eq_zero` then kills the
module); what remains is that the module is *cyclic*, i.e. the Smith normal form
has a single nontrivial invariant factor.

*Why now?*  `ker_transport` and `mem_range_loopDZ` already supply both halves of
the argument — transport identifies the cocycle condition and the divisibility
description identifies the coboundary image — so the cyclic case is a Smith
normal form computation on an explicitly triangular matrix.  Falsifiable by
computing `H¹` of the `ℤ`-sheaf on the `2`-cycle with `a = (2,2)`: the
conjecture predicts `ℤ/3`.
title: Conjecture D (Arithmetic transport law over `ℤ`) — sharpened after cycle 2

description:
The exact-relation half is now proved.  With a node of hypotenuse `c` drawn at radius
`r = 1 − 1/c`, `drawn_curve_equation` gives the closed relation
`‖dir v − dir p‖² = 2 d (1 − r)/c_p` between the angular and the radial coordinate along
the spoke of charge `d`, and `draw_tendsto_dir` shows the drawn curve really does run into
the boundary star centre.  The remaining, geometric half is:

  the drawn image of a spoke is, up to a bi-Lipschitz reparametrisation, a genuine
  Euclidean horocycle of the Poincaré disc with curvature a function of `d/c_p` alone, and
  no drawn spoke is an arc of a circle orthogonal to the boundary (no spoke is a geodesic).

*The key insight is* that the proved relation `‖dir v − dir p‖² = 2 d (1 − r)/c_p` is
*exactly* the equation of a Euclidean circle internally tangent to the unit circle at
`dir p`, once the drawn radius `r` is converted to the Poincaré radial coordinate; so the
conjecture is the statement that this coordinate change is bi-Lipschitz on `r ∈ [0,1)`,
which is a one-variable estimate on `1 − 1/c` versus `tanh`.

*Why now?* All the arithmetic input is proved: `drawn_curve_equation` supplies the exact
algebraic relation, `contact_order_two_lower` / `contact_order_two_upper` pin the contact
order at two, which already rules out first-order-contact radii, and `chord_sq_ratio`
separates spokes of different charge quantitatively.

---
title: Conjecture E (The drawn picture: from the exact relation to the drawn shape)

description:
**Conjecture.** For every complex square matrix `A`, `det (exp A) = exp (tr A)`;
consequently a Hermitian `H` satisfies `exp (i H) ∈ SU(n)` if and only if
`tr H ∈ 2π ℤ`, which is the exact trace congruence class asked for in
direction 5.

*The key insight is* that the missing ingredient is not the determinant
identity itself but a **norm-independence lemma for the exponential on a
finite-dimensional algebra**: the matrix exponential is usually developed
against the `L^∞` operator norm, while the C⋆-structure — and hence the
continuous functional calculus used for exponential surjectivity — lives on the
`L^2` operator norm. The two exponentials are the same function but are not the
same object as written. Establishing that the exponential depends only on the
topological ring structure unlocks both frameworks simultaneously.

*Why now?* This cycle produced the first statement that mixes the two worlds —
the matrix corollary of exponential surjectivity is stated in the `L²` setting —
so the mismatch is now an explicit, isolated, provable lemma rather than a
diffuse inconvenience.
title: C1. The determinant–trace bridge: `det (exp A) = exp (tr A)`

description:
**Conjecture.** Allow the `k`-th query to have its own radix `q_k`.  Then the minimal
"mixed-radix depth vector" for sorting `n` items satisfies `∏_k q_k ≥ n!`, the ideal work
`kT ∑_k log q_k` is minimised exactly when `∏_k q_k` is the smallest product of the allowed
radices exceeding `n!`, and the resulting minimum work exceeds `kT log (n!)` by strictly less
than `kT log (max_k q_k)` — a strict improvement over the fixed-radix sandwich
`optimal_radix_work_sandwich` whenever `n!` is not a power of a single allowed radix.

The key insight is that the fixed-radix sandwich loses up to one full query register because
`⌈log_q n!⌉` overshoots; mixing radices makes the overshoot a number-theoretic approximation
problem for `n!` by products from a fixed multiplicative set. **Why now?** The fixed-radix
theorem gives the exact baseline and the exact loss term, so the mixed-radix optimum is a
well-posed integer-programming question that can be solved exactly for `n ≤ 8`.
title: Radix-mixing and the optimal query alphabet

description:
**Conjecture.** For a spectrally sandwiched form with `m > 0`,
`lim_{s→∞} −(1/s)·log Θ(s) = μ(Q, t)`, and moreover
`Θ(s)·exp(s·μ(Q,t)) → r(μ)`, the number of integer points attaining the minimum
(finite by `card_solutions_le`).

*The key insight is* that `theta_decay` proves one inequality
(`≥ m·d(t,ℤⁿ)²` for the rate) purely from the term bound, while the matching
upper bound must come from isolating the minimising terms and dominating the rest
by the counting estimate `N(R) ≤ (2√(R/m)+1)ⁿ` — i.e. the *counting* theorem and
the *decay* theorem are two halves of one Laplace-type asymptotic.

*Why now?* Both halves are already formalised; the missing step is a dominated
tail estimate `∑_{Q(x−t) ≥ μ+δ} exp(−sQ) ≤ C·exp(−s(μ+δ))`, which follows from
polynomial coefficient growth by a summation-by-parts argument on `ℤⁿ` — a
finite-combinatorial lemma, not new analysis.
title: C2. Gap–theta duality: the decay rate of `Θ` *equals* the inhomogeneous minimum

description:
**Conjecture.** `FreeWitness.not_revealsFactor_of_congruenceDetermined`
generalises from "determined by `N mod m`" to "determined by the value of a
fixed polynomial-size arithmetic circuit on the digits of `N`": no such
invariant names a nontrivial factor of every large semiprime, unless factoring
is in P.

*The key insight is* that the Dirichlet argument only used one property of the
class `{N : N ≡ a mod m}` — that it contains two *coprime* semiprimes.  Any
invariant whose level sets contain two coprime semiprimes is blind in exactly
the same way, and level sets of small circuits are large.

*Why now?* The meta-theorem is already stated abstractly over an arbitrary
`I : ℕ → ℕ`; only the "level sets are rich" input has to be replaced, turning a
number-theoretic lemma into a combinatorial one.

*Round-4 progress.* The *list* version of C2 is now proved:
`CandidateLists.no_bounded_candidate_list` shows that a congruence-determined
function returning a whole set of candidate divisors, of size bounded by any
fixed `k`, still fails on some large semiprime — the witness being a family of
`k+1` pairwise-coprime semiprimes in one residue class
(`CandidateLists.exists_coprime_semiprime_family`).  What remains open in C2 is
replacing "congruence-determined" by "circuit-determined".
title: C2. Beyond congruences: polynomial-time-determined invariants

description:
**Conjecture.** The obstruction `not_dvd_hypot` (no node has `N ∣ m²+n²` when
`N` has a prime factor `≡ 3 mod 4`) is sharp: for `N` all of whose prime factors are
`≡ 1 (mod 4)`, the nodes with `N ∣ m²+n²` form exactly `2^{ω(N)}` congruence classes of
`(m : n) mod N`, one for each factorisation of `N` into Gaussian primes up to units and
conjugation, and each class contains a node at Price depth `O(log N)`.

*The key insight is* that `m² + n² = |m + in|²`, so hypotenuse divisibility is a
statement about Gaussian ideals, and the tree structure should intertwine with the
Gaussian class group action rather than with the rational ratio `m/n`.
*Why now?* The mod-4 obstruction is proved, so the complementary case is precisely
delimited; Mathlib's `ZMod`, `legendreSym` and Gaussian-integer API make the counting
statement formalisable.
title: C5. A hypotenuse-side tree over the Gaussian integers

description:
**Conjecture.**  For every non-idoneal `D`, computing a single entry `r_Q(N)` of
the representation vector for a semiprime `N` is as hard as factoring `N`:
there is a randomised poly-time reduction `FACTOR ≤ r_Q`.

*The key insight is* that for non-idoneal `D` the entry `r_Q(N)` distinguishes
the ideal classes `[𝔭][𝔮]` from `[𝔭][𝔮̄]`, and the difference between those two
is precisely the choice of a prime above `p` — a choice that, for `N = pq`,
encodes the splitting of `N` in a non-abelian extension.

*Why now?*  Cycle 1 shows the *only* discriminants for which the vector is
cheap are exactly the ones for which it is useless; C2 asserts that the trade is
exact, upgrading "REFUTED for these `D`" to "REFUTED for all `D`", and closing
the extrinsic corner unconditionally.

**Lean shape.**  A formal reduction is out of reach, but the algebraic core is
not: `theorem class_of_prime_not_residue_determined (D : ℤ) (h : ¬ OneClassPerGenus D) : ∃ p q : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ q.Prime ∧ (p : ZMod |D|.toNat) = q ∧ classOf p ≠ classOf q`.

---
title: C2. The Hardness Dial (converse of the refutation)

description:
For a fixed bound `B`, define the "CM stage-1 success set" `S_B` of primes `p`
with `#E(𝔽_p) ∣ lcm(1..B)`. Then `S_B` restricted to the inert half equals the
Williams `p + 1` success set exactly (`cm_smooth_iff_plusOne_smooth`), while on
the split half `S_B` is disjoint from the `p+1` set infinitely often, yet the
symmetric difference is invisible from any residue of `N`.

**The key insight is** that `split_breaks_plusOne_channel` (`p = 5`: `3 ∣ p+1`
but `3 ∤ #E`) is the first member of an infinite family, and that the
distinguishing data — the Hecke eigenvalue `a_p` — is a `GL₂` invariant with no
abelian residue shadow, so any factoring gain must come from the *smoothness*
side, which is size-driven and residue-free.

**Why now?** The exact split/inert partition is now a theorem, so the two
success sets can be compared unconditionally rather than statistically.

---



# Three concrete next-cycle sub-conjectures
title: Conjecture E (twist-orbit equidistribution is *not* a factoring channel)

description:
**Conjecture.** For a cyclic order `n` with at least three splitting types, *every*
binary read-out `h ∘ T` satisfies `H(h ∘ T) < H(T) − δ(n)` with an explicit
`δ(n) > 0` depending only on the `φ`-rates; in particular no binary read-out of a
multi-state type channel can reach the type entropy.

*Status.* The non-strict inequality is a theorem for all read-outs (`uEnt_comp_le`);
strictness is proved only for the two natural read-outs at `n = 4, 6`
(`rootCount_lossy_4/6`, `Isplit_lt_Ipair_4/6`).

*The key insight is* that the entropy defect of a coarsening equals the average
entropy *inside* the merged fibres, which for a binary partition of a `k`-state
`φ`-law is bounded below by the smallest two rates.

*Why now?* The proof of `uEnt_comp_le` is already term-wise; converting one
inequality in that proof into a strict one on a single fibre gives the result.
title: C4. Strict data processing for multi-state read-outs

description:
**Conjecture.**  If some good prime `ℓ ≥ 5` divides `den x(2P)` for an integral point `P` of
`E_N`, then `P` has infinite order and the `ℓ`-adic valuations `v_ℓ(den x(2^k P))` grow
linearly in `k`, with slope `1` in the sense `v_ℓ(den x(2^k P)) = v_ℓ(den x(2P)) + 2(k-1)` for
all `k ≥ 1` when `ℓ` is odd.

*The key insight is* that the formal group at `ℓ` gives `v_ℓ(x(2Q)) = 4 v_ℓ(x(Q))/2`-type
doubling behaviour, and the catalog already proves the qualitative persistence statement
(`kernel_stable_two_pow`) and the infinitude of the orbit; what is missing is the exact
arithmetic progression of valuations.

*Why now?*  The valuation lemmas (`pow_dvd_den_double_iff`) in `Shared.MordellDenominatorValuations`
give the base case, and the induction is purely `2`-adic bookkeeping.

---
title: C4. Denominator growth forces rank

description:
**Conjecture.**  The counting statements above are statements about residue classes; upgrading
them to statements about actual denominators requires an integral point of `E_N` in the given
class.  Conjecture: for every prime `ℓ ≥ 5` and every residue `c` mod `ℓ` there are infinitely
many `N ≡ c (mod ℓ)` such that `E_N(ℤ)` contains a point in every active class of `ℓ`.

*The key insight is* that the constructions used here (`N = ℓ² - 1`, `P = (1, ℓ)` and
`N = 1 - ℓ³`, `P = (ℓ, 1)`) are one-parameter families producing a point in a *prescribed* class,
and the general statement is a question about representing residues by the two-variable form
`y² - x³`.

*Why now?*  The two explicit families are already proved in the catalog, so the induction is on
the number of classes rather than on new elliptic-curve theory; and this is precisely the gap
between the density theorems of cycle 2 and unconditional statements about denominators.
title: D3. Realisability requires a rational point (the missing arithmetic input)

description:
**Conjecture.** For fixed `N` and `P` of infinite order, the set of primes `ℓ` for which the
apparition index is even has natural density `1/2` inside the primes; equivalently the parity of
`ord(P mod ℓ)` equidistributes.

*The key insight is* that the parity of the order of a reduction is governed by the splitting of
the `2`-division field of `E_N` — a Chebotarev condition — so the density is the proportion of
Frobenius classes acting without fixed vector on `E[2]`.

*Why now?* Cycle 7's density theorem gives the counting framework, and Mathlib's Galois and
Chebotarev-adjacent machinery has grown enough that the `2`-division field of a Mordell curve
(a pure cubic extension) can be handled explicitly rather than abstractly.
title: C3. Density of primes whose apparition index is *even* is exactly `1/2`

description:
