**Conjecture.** For a uniformly random `x ∈ {0,1}^n`, the probability that
*some* generator describable in `m` bits outputs `x` is at most `2^{m+1-n}`; so
the expected payoff of searching a library of generators grows only linearly in
the library's description size while the search cost grows exponentially.

*The key insight is* that a library is itself data: describing which generator
to use costs exactly the bits it saves, which is the content of
`family_hard_strings_are_abundant`.
*Why now?* The counting half is proved; turning it into a probability statement
requires only `PMF.uniformOfFintype` and the existing `Finset.card` bound.
title: C5. Kolmogorov-structure view: "seed hunting" is a measure-zero strategy

description:
**Conjecture.** Let `Rank_k` be the `k`-fold iterated-exponential rank group
(`Rank_2` is the group formalised here, with coordinates for `exp exp x, exp x, x, log x`)
and `TS_k = Lex (HahnSeries Rank_k ℝ)`. Then for every `k` the natural inclusion
`TS_k ↪ TS_{k+1}` is a strict, order-preserving, non-cofinal embedding, and the direct
limit `TS_∞ = colim_k TS_k` satisfies the asymptotic comparison theorem *and* has no
nonzero element flat with respect to any `TS_k`. Concretely and falsifiably: there is an
element of `TS_3` (namely `exp(−exp(exp x))`) that is dominated by every transmonomial of
`TS_2`, so `EMLTS.eq_zero_of_abs_lt_all_transmonomials` becomes **false** if the ambient
field is enlarged while the test family is not.

**The key insight is** that the asymptotic comparison theorem is not a statement about
transseries at all, but about the *cofinality of the transmonomial family inside the
positive cone*: the proof `EMLTS.exists_mono_lt_of_pos` only uses that every nonzero Hahn
series has an `order` and that the rank group has no maximum — so the theorem transfers
verbatim to any scale, and fails exactly across scales.

**Why now?** The whole infrastructure is already parametric in the rank group: `Rank` is
used through `rk`/`rd/ra/rb/rc` and `exists_rank_nsmul` only, so replacing `ℝ ×ₗ …` by a
colimit of lexicographic powers is a mechanical refactor, and the comparison proof would
survive unchanged. This makes the conjecture cheap to test and its failure mode explicit.
title: C1. The scale-completion conjecture (flatness is a depth phenomenon)

description:
**Conjecture.** For every cell of the (depth × context) grid there is a number
`m(cell) = bar − c(k*⁻)` (the deficit at the grid point below the knee) such that the
knee is seed-stable exactly when `m(cell) > η`, where `η` is the inter-seed spread of the
retained curve at that cell. Quantitatively: across cells, the empirical probability that
the knee moves by one grid step should be a monotone function of `η / m` alone, with a
sharp transition at `η/m = 1`.

*The key insight is* that `KneeFluctuation.robustKnee_iff` makes stability an exact
inequality between two independently measurable quantities — the margin and the spread —
so "knee fluctuation" is not noise to be averaged away but a deterministic consequence of
a measured collar around the bar.

*Why now?* Both quantities are already recorded by the existing harness (NET-44 reports
`0.003` and `0.010` at the broken cell, and `0.012 > 0.010` at the protected one); no new
instrumentation is needed, only reading the margins the sweeps already produce.

---
title: C1. The margin–fluctuation law: a knee moves *iff* its margin is under the spread

description:
**Conjecture.** For every cell, `d·ctx/32 = max over seeds of k*`, up to one grid step —
the fitted constant `1/32` is a *worst-seed* constant, not an average-seed constant.
Testable prediction: at every cell where a third seed is run, the knee is `≤` the law's
value, and the fraction of seeds attaining it stays bounded away from `1`.

*The key insight is* `KneeEnsemble.ensemble_max_is_safe`, `ensemble_max_is_least_safe`
and `KneeLattice.knee_worstCase`: the only budget a sweep can certify is the maximum of
the measured knees — which is literally the knee of the pointwise-infimum (worst-case)
curve — so any "safe" law is by construction an upper envelope, and its apparent
exactness at a single seed is the statement that that seed happened to be the worst one.

*Why now?* Two seeds already exist at every cell of the grid after NET-44; a single third
seed per cell turns the conjecture into a decisive measurement, and
`KneeEnsemble.certified_budget_mono` says the certified budget can only move one way.

---
title: C3. The product law is exactly a `sup` over seeds, not a mean

description:
**Conjecture.** Along a doubling ladder on which the product law `k* = A·d·ctx/δ` is exact
at every rung, the margin at rung `i` satisfies `m_i ≤ M·ρ^i` with `ρ < 1`; consequently
the certified depth of an exact chain grows only like `log(1/η)`, and **no exact chain of
more than `O(log(1/η))` rungs can ever be certified at noise `η`**.

*The key insight is* that exactness is a quantisation coincidence: rung `i` reports the
grid point immediately above a continuous knee whose fractional position in the last grid
cell is essentially equidistributed, and the margin is the retained-accuracy increment
across that fraction of a cell — an increment which shrinks as the retained curve
flattens with context. The NET-45 ladder `0.007, 0.010, 0.003, 0.006, 0.0013` is
consistent with `ρ ≈ 0.6` on the odd subsequence and is already at the resolution limit
of the harness.

*Why now?* `KneeMarginChain.CertDepth` and `certDepth_antitone` give the exact
book-keeping, and five rungs of margins are recorded. A sixth rung (`ctx = 4096`) with a
margin below `0.0008` would confirm the geometric law and would also prove that the
programme can never certify the chain it is measuring.
title: C1. The margin law: margins decay geometrically along an exact chain

description:
**Statement.** There are no indices `a < b < c < d` with
`antiFib b - antiFib a = antiFib c - antiFib b = antiFib d - antiFib c`.

**The key insight is** that `8·antiFib n = (2n-1)² + 7`, so a four-term progression of
anti-Fibonacci numbers is *exactly* a four-term progression of odd squares — and by
Fermat's right-triangle theorem no four distinct squares are in arithmetic progression.
The proved bridge `antiFib_AP_iff_pythagoreanTriple` already reduces the three-term case
to Pythagorean triples; the four-term case should reduce to `x⁴ - y⁴ = z²`.

**Why now?** Mathlib already contains the descent infrastructure for the quartic Fermat
equation (`not_fermat_42`, the `Fermat42.Minimal` machinery) and the full classification
of Pythagorean triples, so the missing step is the passage from `a⁴ + b⁴ ≠ c²` to
`a⁴ - b⁴ ≠ c²`, a single extra descent that is now within formalisation reach.

**Falsifiable:** a brute-force scan over `a < b < c < d ≤ 10⁵` either produces a
counterexample or supports the conjecture; the scan is cheap because of the proved
`O(1)` membership test `isAntiFibValue`.

---
title: C1. No four anti-Fibonacci numbers are in arithmetic progression

description:
The repetition theorem here increases
   the number of queries. Dinur-style gap amplification keeps the query complexity constant
   at the price of a larger alphabet; formalizing even the graph-powering step (with
   expander mixing, which Mathlib now partially supports) would be a substantial next
   target on the road to `NP ⊆ PCP(log n, O(1))`.
title: Genuine gap amplification for the PCP theorem

description:
Under any standard representation
   of computable real functions that includes sine, the claim that every
   computable real function has an exact finite EML expression is false.  This
   follows from Conjecture 1; conversely, either a finite EML expression for
   sine or a chosen computability model excluding sine would falsify the stated
   formulation.
title: Computability thesis counterexample

description:
**Conjecture.** Every positive integer with two distinct representations as a
sum of two positive cubes admits a primitive representation as a sum of three
nonzero signed cubes.

The key insight is that allowing cancellation moves the problem from the
positive cone to an affine cubic surface, where nearby larger cubes can create
primitive points invisible to positive searches. **Why now?** The identity
\(1729=13^3-7^3-5^3\) supplies the first concrete bridge between taxicab
multiplicity and primitive signed three-cube representability.
title: Primitive points versus taxicab decompositions

description:
**Conjecture.** For a knotted optical field whose transfer polynomial is the Alexander polynomial, the total radial Lyapunov growth equals the logarithmic Mahler measure of that polynomial. Cyclotomic torus knots have zero growth, while the figure-eight knot has positive growth `2 log φ`.

The key insight is that Mahler measure sums the logarithmic moduli of roots outside the unit circle, exactly the data discarded by a root-of-unity-only spectrum.

**Why now?** The established cyclotomic/off-circle dichotomy supplies explicit zero-growth and positive-growth test cases with reciprocal root geometry.
title: Mahler measure bounds spectral radial instability

description:
Conjecture: there are parsimonious jigsaw gadgets for which the cubical complex generated by single-variable flips deformation-retracts onto the corresponding SAT solution complex.

The key insight is that preserving witnesses alone captures vertices, whereas controlled local reconfiguration can preserve adjacency, connected components, and ultimately homotopy type.

Why now? A canonical vertex bijection is available; the next falsifiable step is to characterize exactly when one-variable changes correspond to bounded local rearrangements of pieces.
title: Topology of the solution complex

description:
**Conjecture.** For a stationary ergodic sequence of ambient and successful branching pairs `(Bₙ,Sₙ)` satisfying `1 ≤ Sₙ ≤ Bₙ` and suitable logarithmic integrability, the almost-sure proof-search dimension is

`E[log S₀] / E[log B₀]`.

The key insight is that logarithmic path volumes are additive cocycles, so their ratio should converge by ergodic averaging. **Why now?** The deterministic profile theorem supplies the exact finite-block identity whose random-block limit this conjecture predicts.
title: Ergodic branching and almost-sure dimension

description:
**Conjecture.** For a comparator network implemented by reversible gates with a designated
reset protocol, the minimum dissipated work is governed by the conditional entropy of the
comparison transcript given the sorted output, rather than by the transcript length.

The key insight is that repeated comparisons can be logically correlated, so only the
unrecoverable part of their joint transcript should incur a Landauer cost. **Why now?** The
factorial lower bound and the redundant-padding counterexample isolate precisely the missing
ingredient: an explicit account of which transcript registers are reset.
title: Physical comparison gates with explicit reset registers

description:
**Conjecture.** If two finite argumentation frameworks are strongly equivalent under preferred semantics, then the downward-closed complexes generated by their preferred extensions are simple-homotopy equivalent after deleting vertices that occur in no preferred extension.

The key insight is that strong semantic equivalence should control not only the maximal faces but also the collapses among all their subfaces. **Why now?** The antichain theorem identifies maximal faces as the semantic data, while the generated-complex construction supplies the canonical topological object on which elementary collapses can be tested.
title: Semantic equivalence and simple-homotopy type

description: Define the guarded Poincare interval as the set of scales at which the Rips complex simultaneously has sphere homology, manifold-like links, and a prescribed connectivity certificate. Conjecture that its endpoints are Lipschitz-stable, away from critical-value collisions, under matched perturbations of the sample. **The key insight is...** a robust detector should be an interval-valued invariant rather than the smallest scale satisfying a nonmonotone homological predicate. **Why now?** Rips inclusion is monotone, but sphere homology need not be; endpoint stability must therefore exploit persistence gaps rather than monotonicity of the predicate itself.
title: Stability of a guarded Poincare interval

description:
**Conjecture.** For every consistent Boolean signature formed from Extensionality, acyclicity, existence of an empty code, and existence of a universal code, there is a finite relational universe of at most four set-codes realizing that signature; the optimal carrier size is computable from the signature.

The key insight is that small relational universes behave like finite constraint-satisfaction instances, while the axioms impose graph-theoretic separation, cycle, source, and sink conditions.

**Why now?** Two one-point and two two-point witnesses already realize every combination of Extensionality and acyclicity, suggesting a broader finite-basis phenomenon.
title: Classification of minimal models for anti-axiom signatures

description:
**Conjecture.** Up to bounded morphism, every finite pointed model satisfying `□P ∧ ¬□□P` contains the pointed two-edge chain as a generated quotient; in particular, three worlds are minimal when seriality is imposed at the distinguished world and its successor.

The key insight is that failure of axiom 4 must expose a composable pair of accessibility edges whose composite edge is absent. **Why now?** An explicit minimal witness and the universal transitivity obstruction provide the two extremal cases needed for a structural classification.
title: Minimal-frame classification of uniterated provability

description:
For every finite proof verifier, conjecture that there is a reversible implementation whose dissipated heat can be made arbitrarily small at the cost of retaining a history register, and that the minimum required history capacity is controlled by the largest verification fiber.

The key insight is that fiber multiplicity simultaneously measures logical information loss and the ancillary memory required to distinguish merged computational histories.

Why now? The one-bit entropy bridge identifies the physical unit of proof cost, while the finite ensemble results provide complexity-sensitive workloads on which a quantitative memory–dissipation frontier can be tested.
title: Reversible verification space–heat frontier

description:
Define a hierarchy in which an evaluation table represents only predicates of bounded syntactic, geometric, or musical complexity. Conjecture that diagonal fixed points persist exactly when the represented class is closed under composition with the chosen semantic endomorphism and under diagonal evaluation. Determine the minimal closure axioms and exhibit sharp finite counterexamples when either closure condition is removed.

The key insight is that full surjectivity is stronger than the diagonal proof uses; only representability of a particular composite is essential.

Why now? Boolean universality is impossible, so a graded theory of representable fragments offers a testable route to concrete finite models without weakening the fixed-point mechanism into metaphor.
title: A graded Lawvere theorem for partial universality

description:
**Conjecture.** Every countable dependency relation that is well-founded and has finite predecessor sets admits a rank into the natural numbers that strictly decreases along dependency edges; without finite branching, ordinal-valued ranks are necessary and sufficient.

The key insight is that absence of cycles is weaker than the existence of a numerical level assignment, while finite branching may bridge that gap by bounding the height below each node.

**Why now?** The finite-cycle obstruction isolates rank descent as the mechanism behind untangled hierarchies, making the precise boundary between natural and transfinite ranks directly testable.
title: Rankability Characterizes Predicative Dependency

description:
**Conjecture.** If `E^{d₁}` and `E^{d₂}` both have rank one with generators of
controlled height, then for a positive proportion of pairs `(d₁, d₂)` the composite
twist `E^{d₁ d₂}` again has rank one, exhibiting the rank-one locus as "almost closed"
under the Brahmagupta–Fibonacci product of parameters.

*The key insight is* that the sum-of-two-squares parameters form a monoid under the
Brahmagupta–Fibonacci identity, and the twist coefficients compose as
`(a d₁² , b d₁³)` then `(·) d₂` = `(a (d₁d₂)², b (d₁d₂)³)`, so the arithmetic of the
parameters and the geometry of the twists are compatible semigroup actions.

*Why now?* Both the parameter monoid and the coefficient composition law are now
explicit and verified, turning a vague "twists compose" slogan into a precise
statement about a semigroup action whose orbits can be sampled.
title: A closed multiplicative structure on rank-one twists

description:
**Established.** A fundamental discriminant is squarefree if and only if it lies in the
`D ≡ 1 (mod 4)` branch: the even branch always carries a factor of `4`, so the prime `2`
ramifies wildly there, while the odd branch is squarefree and hence tamely ramified at every
odd prime divisor.

**Conjecture (remaining refinement).** This branch dichotomy upgrades to a prime-by-prime
statement: for every fundamental discriminant, the primes that ramify tamely (dividing `D`
exactly once) are precisely the odd prime divisors, with the prime `2` the unique wildly
ramifying prime, occurring exactly in the `D = 4m` branch.

*The key insight is* that the factor of `4` in the even branch is the sole obstruction to
squarefreeness, so squarefreeness is a clean binary invariant separating the two branches.

*Why now?* The local color dictionary already detects ramification (color `0`) uniformly; the
tame/wild distinction is the missing refinement that upgrades "ramified" to a prime-by-prime
statement, and the odd branch has just been shown to be squarefree.
title: Tame ramification characterises the odd branch

description:
**Conjecture.** For every `n` there exists a positive integer expressible as a
sum of two positive cubes in at least `n` distinct ways.

The key insight is that the affine Fermat cubic `x³ + y³ = N` is an elliptic
curve, and a single rational point of infinite order generates infinitely many
rational representations; clearing denominators by a common cube collapses `n`
of them onto a single integer that inherits `n` integer representations.

Why now? The cycle established the exact provable boundary: the elementary
scaling map multiplies a fixed representation set by a cube but never *creates*
new representations, so genuine growth in the count must come from the group law
on the cubic. Isolating this obstruction pinpoints precisely the arithmetic
input — a non-torsion rational point — that any full proof must supply.
title: Unbounded representation counts (existence of Taxicab(n) for all n)

description:
Under a *non-unitary* local operation `A ⊗ B` with `‖A‖, ‖B‖ ≤ 1` (a local
filtering), the concurrence satisfies `C(A⊗B ψ) ≤ ‖det A‖·‖det B‖·C(ψ)`, with
equality iff `A` and `B` are proportional to unitaries. **Conjecture:** the
linking number is therefore *never* increased by local operations, and the
resulting monotone is exactly the degree of the map induced on fibre
complements.

*The key insight is* that `entanglementDet_localAct` already gives the exact
transformation law `det ↦ det A · det B · det`, so monotonicity is a statement
about `|det A| ≤ 1` for contractions — the analytic input, not the algebraic one.

*Why now?* The transformation law is proved; the remaining step is Hadamard's
inequality for `2×2` contractions, which Mathlib can support.

**Falsification test:** a contraction `A` with `‖A‖ ≤ 1` and `|det A| > 1`
(impossible), or a filtering that raises the concurrence of some state.
title: Conjecture D (entanglement monotonicity as a topological degree bound)

description:
Fix a field `K` and a feature count `N`.  Call a functional `Φ` a *marginal
predictor* if `Φ` depends only on the per-feature observation marginals and the
overlap incidence.  Conjecture: for every marginal predictor `Φ` there is a
distribution over data sheaves on `N` features, with all restriction maps
invertible, such that

```
E |dim H¹ - Φ|  ≥  N/4.
```

*The key insight is* that `missing_rate_does_not_determine_H1` gives a
*uniform* family realising all of `0 … N` on a single nerve with a single
missingness profile, so any predictor blind to the restriction maps must pay the
full spread of that family — the minimax error is linear in `N`, not `o(N)`.

*Why now?*  The realisability theorem is proved and constructive (the witness is
`aᵢ = 1` on a chosen subset, `2` off it), so the remaining step is a
one-line averaging argument over a uniformly random subset.  Falsifiable by
exhibiting a marginal predictor with sublinear expected error.
title: Conjecture C (Obstruction dimension is not a marginal statistic — quantitative form)

description:
**Statement.**  For `2 × 2 × n` tensors the generic Kronecker orbit is open and dense, and its
density rate is `ε^{d}` with `d` the degree of the corresponding Kronecker discriminant; the
five-node argument used here generalizes to a `(d + 1)`-node finite difference, giving the
constant `d! / 2^{d} \binom{2d}{d}`-type bound.

**The key insight is** that nothing in this cycle used `n = 2` beyond the fact that the invariant
restricted to a line through the "diagonal" direction is a *monic* polynomial of known degree;
monicity is exactly the statement that the diagonal tensor has invariant `1`.

**Why now?**  Cycle 3 conjectured the `2 × 2 × n` classification; this cycle shows that its
topological half needs only monicity, so the quantitative statement may well be easier than the
classification itself.
title: C3. The same quantitative picture for `2 × 2 × n`

description:
**Conjecture.** If `A` and `B` are weight-graded dg-algebras that are `wt`-pure, then the graded
tensor product `A ⊗ B` (bigraded by the sum of bidegrees) is `wt`-pure, hence formal; and purity
passes to filtered colimits of weight-graded dg-algebras with weight-preserving transition maps.
Consequently formality for spaces satisfying weight-monodromy is stable under products and under
passage to limits of admissible covers.

*The key insight is* that purity is a *pointwise* condition on bidegrees and the diagonal
`w = wt n` is a subgroup of `ℤ²`, so it is preserved by every operation that adds bidegrees.

*Why now?* The definitions in this development are already stated bidegree-wise, and the
Künneth-type step needed is exactly the statement that the diagonal is closed under addition,
which is used (and proved) in `sPiece_mul_le`. Falsifiable: a pure `A` and pure `B` whose
tensor product has cohomology off the diagonal.
title: C5. Formality descends along filtered colimits and tensor products of pure algebras

description:
**Conjecture.**  For every rule `g` and every `n ≥ 1` the quotient
`MvPolynomial (ZMod n) (ZMod 2) / fixedIdeal g n` is a finite-dimensional
`GF(2)`-algebra — hence of Krull dimension `0` — and its `GF(2)`-dimension equals
`#V(g,n)`.  Thus Krull dimension is a *useless* invariant here, while the length of
the coordinate ring recovers exactly the point count.

*The key insight is* that the Boolean relations `X i ^ 2 - X i` force the quotient to
be a product of copies of `GF(2)`, one per `GF(2)`-point, so all the information sits
in length, not dimension — which explains why the "dimension tracks complexity"
heuristic of cycle 0 had to fail.

*Why now?*  `fixedIdeal` and `mem_zeroLocus_iff_isFixed` are in place; what is missing
is the Chinese-remainder decomposition of a Boolean quotient ring, a self-contained
piece of commutative algebra.
title: C4. The fixed-point coordinate ring is `0`-dimensional but its length separates rules

description:
**Conjecture.** For every `ε > 0` the number of bases `a` modulo a prime `p`
with `ord_p(a) ≤ p^{1-ε}` is `O(p^{1-ε})`, hence a `1 - o(1)` fraction of bases
have order `> p^{1-ε}`; the classical Fourier-sample requirement is therefore
`N^{1-o(1)}`, not merely `√N`.

**The key insight is** that the covering bound `#{ord ≤ B} ≤ B²` used in
`card_small_order_le` is wasteful: in a cyclic group `#{ord ≤ B}` is exactly
`∑_{d ∣ n, d ≤ B} φ(d) ≤ B·(number of divisors)`, which is `B^{1+o(1)}`.

**Why now?** `card_small_order_le` is formalised and its only ingredient is
`IsCyclic.card_pow_eq_one_le`; upgrading `∑_{d ≤ B} d` to
`∑_{d ∣ n, d ≤ B} φ(d)` is a purely combinatorial refinement that immediately
sharpens `classical_sampling_barrier`.

*Status after cycle 3:* the divisor-indexed form
`#{ord ≤ B} ≤ B · #{d ∣ |G| : d ≤ B}` is now **proved** in
`Catalog/Computation/QuantumClassicalBoundary/OrderStatistics.lean`
(`card_small_order_le_divisors`, `exists_base_large_order_divisor`). What remains
open is the analytic input `τ(n) = n^{o(1)}` needed to convert it into the clean
`p^{1-ε}` statement.

---
title: C4. Order statistics: from `> √p` to `> p^{1-ε}`

description:
**Conjecture.** For every `r` there is an explicit polynomial criterion in the
residues `vᵢ = aⁱ mod N`, with coefficients in the real subfield of the `r`-th
cyclotomic field, deciding whether the fundamental bin `k = 1` is the largest
non-DC bin of the value signal; and for `r ≥ 5` the set of `(N, a)` failing the
criterion has positive density.

**The key insight is** that at `r = 4` the two competing bins have the closed
forms `√((v₀-v₂)²+(v₁-v₃)²)` and `|v₀-v₁+v₂-v₃|`
(`norm_dft_order_four_one`, `norm_dft_order_four_two`), i.e. the comparison is a
rational inequality; for general `r` the analogous comparison is an inequality
between norms of cyclotomic integers, still decidable instance by instance.

**Why now?** The `r = 4` criterion is proved and instance-checked in
`Catalog/Computation/QuantumClassicalBoundary/HarmonicCriterion.lean`; extending
it needs cyclotomic norm computations rather than any new conceptual input.
title: C6. A closed-form hiding criterion for every period, not just `r = 4`

description:
**Conjecture.** If `d_p ≠ d_q` then the orbit count `C(b)`, together with `N` and
`n`, determines `{p, q}` in polynomial time; consequently an `N`-computable
orbit-count oracle is *equivalent* to factoring, not merely implied by it.

*The key insight is* that `Round11.groupoid_affine_hint` already expresses the
orbit count as the affine observation `(n/d_p - 1)p + (n/d_q - 1)q = known`, and
`Round11.weighted_sum_prod_inversion` already shows that such an observation,
together with `pq = N`, leaves at most two candidates. *Why now?* Both halves are
proved here; what remains is only the bookkeeping that the two coefficients do
not both vanish outside the balanced case, plus a model of "polynomial time" in
which to state the equivalence.
title: C4 (Unbalanced orbit counts are a factoring oracle).

description:
**Statement.** Let `T` be a statistic of `p` computable in time `poly(log N)` from `N` and
`p mod m` alone. Then `T` is hint-computable, hence information-free on the candidate set.
Equivalently: any dial with a genuine `Ω(N^{1/4})`-scale conductor that is *evaluable* from
public data yields a factoring algorithm.

**The key insight is** that the no-self-amplification theorem already kills every statistic of
the form `g(N, p mod m)`; the open part is the converse — that a non-hint-computable but
efficiently evaluable statistic must leak `p` itself.

**Why now?** The formal notion of hint-computability is exactly the hypothesis a reduction
would need, and the pinning-window bound supplies the quantitative target
`lcm(m, M*) ≥ N^{1/2}`.
title: Conjecture B (Aperiodic dials are the only escape, and they are as hard as factoring)

description:
**Conjecture.** `lim_{M→∞} (1 − λ₁(2^M − 1, M)) (M+1) = c*` exists, `c* = 2π²/3 · κ` for an
explicit `κ`, and for all `r ≤ 2^M` and `k ≢ 0`, `(1 − λ_k)(M+1) ≥ 2` with the supremum of
the *minimal-gap-over-large-r* profile attained along Mersenne cycles.

*The key insight is* that for `r = 2^M − 1` the dyadic orbit `{2^t}` is exactly the set of
binary place values, so the deficiency is a geometric series `Σ 4^t/r²` truncated at the
top — a self-similar quantity, which is why the numerics converge to five digits by
`M = 12`.

*Why now?* `dyadicEigen_mersenne_ge` already gives the `Θ(1/M)` shape with constant 106;
closing the gap between 106 and 3.3946 needs only sharper cosine control at the few top
frequencies (`t ≥ M − 3`), where the quadratic bound is wasteful.
title: C2. The Mersenne family is the extremal gap family, with constant `c* ≈ 3.3946`

description:
The original conjecture — that the completeness threshold is `Θ(N)` rather than `Θ(√N)` — is now a
theorem: the least positive exponent with `R_k(N) = φ(N)` is exactly
`lcm(p-1, q-1) = φ(N)/gcd(p-1, q-1)`, and this extends to every squarefree modulus, where the
threshold is the Carmichael exponent `lcm_{r | N}(r-1)`.

A later cycle went further: `R_k(N) = ∏_{p | N} gcd(φ(p^{v_p(N)}), k)` for *every* odd `N`, which
identifies the aggregation depth of an arbitrary odd modulus as its Carmichael exponent
`λ(N) = lcm_{p | N} φ(p^{v_p(N)})`.

**Successor conjecture (the 2-adic case).** For `N = 2^e · M` with `M` odd and `e ≥ 3`,
`R_k(N) = gcd(2, k) · gcd(2^{e-2}, k) · ∏_{p | M} gcd(φ(p^{v_p}), k)`, and the least complete
exponent is `lcm(2^{e-2}, λ(M))` — strictly smaller than `φ(N)`, so the even part *shortens* the
aggregation depth by a factor of two without ever making it polynomial.

*The key insight is* that the proof for odd moduli needed only multiplicativity of the witness over
coprime factors plus cyclicity of each local unit group, and cyclicity fails exactly at `2^e`,
`e ≥ 3`, where the local group is `Z/2 × Z/2^{e-2}`; the missing ingredient is a root count in a
product of two cyclic groups, which the multiplicativity of root counts over direct products already
supplies.

*Why now?* Multiplicativity of the witness over coprime factors and the product root count are both
established, and the `Z/2 × Z/2^{e-2}` structure of the unit group modulo `2^e` is standard, so only
the transport step is missing.
title: C1 (resolved, now generalised). The Carmichael threshold

description:
**Conjecture.** For `N = pq` and `a` ranging over all primitive multipliers, the
map `a ↦ #cycles(σ_a)` is *constant*, equal to `gcd(p−1, q−1) + 3`; for general
`a`, `#cycles(σ_a)` is determined by `(ord_p(a), ord_q(a), N)` alone, and by
`cycleCount_excess` the only datum it adds to the free lcm is
`gcd(ord_p a, ord_q a)`.  Conjecturally, an oracle returning
`gcd(ord_p a, ord_q a)` for chosen `a` does **not** give a polynomial-time
factoring algorithm — the pair `(lcm, gcd)` does not determine the unordered
pair `{ord_p a, ord_q a}` (e.g. `{1,6}` and `{2,3}` share `lcm = 6`,
`gcd = 1`).

*The key insight is* the collapse proved here as `cycleCount_primitive`
(`φ(N)/lcm(p−1,q−1) = gcd(p−1,q−1)`) together with
`cycleCount_eq_prod_iff_coprime_orders`: the readout's surplus is a single
divisor-theoretic invariant, not a two-dimensional readout.

*Why now?* `cycleCount_primitive`, `cycleCount_semiprime` and
`cycleCount_excess` are proved; the open half is the *hardness* claim, which can
be formalised as a reduction: "factoring with a `gcd(ord_p a, ord_q a)` oracle"
is the right next formal target.
title: C3. Cycle-count spectroscopy determines `gcd(p−1, q−1)` and nothing more

description:
Let `f` be any function of the residue `N mod M` (`M` fixed) and let
`p < q` be inert primes with `N = pq`. Then `f(N mod M)` cannot agree with the
least-factor bit `[ℓ ∣ #E(𝔽_p)]` on all such semiprimes: for every `M` there is a
collision `pq ≡ p'q' (mod M)` with opposite bits.

**The key insight is** that `which_factor_bit_invisible` is the case `M = 12`,
`ℓ = 3` of a general symmetry: multiplication of residues is commutative, so any
`M`-residue statistic is invariant under swapping the two factors, while the
least-factor bit is not — the obstruction is group-theoretic (a `ℤ/2` orbit
argument on `(ℤ/M)*×(ℤ/M)*`), not analytic.

**Why now?** Making the barrier a theorem (rather than one collision) converts a
statistical "null" into a proof, and needs only Dirichlet's theorem on primes in
arithmetic progressions to produce the second pair.

---
title: Conjecture C (a congruence-closure barrier theorem)

description:
**Conjecture.** Let `L/ℚ` be Galois with group `G`, let `N ⊴ G` with `G/N` cyclic
of order `m`, and let `F = [Frob ∈ N]`.  Then `F` is pinned by the character of
conductor `f(G/N)` and `I(p mod f ; F) = H(1/m)` exactly; conversely, if a fork
of rate `1/m` attains `I = H(1/m)` for some modulus, its defining set is a union
of fibres of a cyclic quotient of order `m`.

*The key insight is* that the entropy value `H(1/m)` is not a coincidence of the
cubic case: it is the entropy of the uniform distribution on the fibres of
`G ↠ G^ab ↠ C_m`, and the trichotomy theorem already forces saturation to be
equivalent to determinism, so only the *rate* survives as an invariant.
*Why now?* Both halves are now formal objects: `info_eq_top_iff` supplies the
converse direction abstractly, and `factorsThroughAb_iff` supplies the group
side; only the Artin/Chebotarev bridge remains to be axiomatised or imported.
title: C1. The conductor–order dictionary: `I = H(1/m)` iff the fork is a fibre of an order-`m` quotient

description:
**Conjecture.**  Let `r_n(N, ℓ)` be the number of residue classes `x mod ℓ` that produce `ℓ` in
`den x(nP)`.  Then `∑_{N mod ℓ} r_n(N, ℓ) = c_n · ℓ + O(1)` with `c_n = deg ψ_n / (n-1)`, and
for fixed `N` the density of primes with `r_n(N, ℓ) = k` is given by the Chebotarev density of
the corresponding conjugacy class in `Gal(ℚ(E_N[n])/ℚ)`.

*The key insight is* that the layer-2 count (`1` at supersingular, `0` or `3` at ordinary
primes) is exactly the splitting type of `ℓ` in `ℚ(∛N, ζ₃)`, and layer 3 adds the trivial class
`x ≡ 0` plus the splitting type of `T³ + 4N`; both are Kummer extensions, so the general
statement is a Chebotarev computation for the `n`-division field.

*Why now?*  The exact averages (`∑ = ℓ`) are already proved here by a bijection, and Mathlib
has the Frobenius/Chebotarev machinery for abelian extensions; the Kummer case `n = 2, 3` is
within reach without the full `n`-division field.

---
title: C2. Exact class counts and a Chebotarev law

description:
**Conjecture.**  Fix a semiprime `N = pq`.  The probability, over integral points `P` of `E_N`
and over `n ≤ T`, that a prime dividing `den x(nP)` lies in `{p, q}` tends to `0` as `T → ∞`;
in fact the expected number of such occurrences is `O(log log T)` while the total number of
denominator primes is `≫ T`.

*The key insight is* that `p` divides `den x(nP)` only when the reduced point is `O` in
`E_N(𝔽_p)`, an event of probability `≈ 1/#E(𝔽_p) ≈ 1/p`, whereas good primes `ℓ` contribute at
rate `1/ℓ` each and there are `≫ T` of them below the height of `nP`.

*Why now?*  This cycle proves the exact per-prime densities (`1/ℓ` on average) that the
heuristic needs; converting them into a statement about a single orbit requires only a height
bound, and the catalog's `MordellInfiniteOrbit` supplies the necessary non-torsion input.

**Falsifiable form.**  Find a semiprime `N` and a point `P` whose orbit exhibits `p` or `q` in
the denominators with frequency bounded below.

# Cycle 2 addendum: three next-cycle sub-conjectures

Cycle 2 turned the class counting around and computed, for a fixed prime `ℓ`, how many residues
`N mod ℓ` are denominator-active
(`Catalog/Combinatorics/MordellDenominatorDensity.lean`): exactly `(ℓ+2)/3` at ordinary primes,
all `ℓ` at supersingular primes, all `ℓ` at layer 3 for every prime, with layer totals `ℓ`
(doubling) and `2ℓ - 1` (tripling).  This sharpens C2 and suggests the following.
title: C5. A "good prime" is never a factor oracle

description:
**Conjecture.**  For `ℓ ≡ 1 (mod 3)` the set of layer-2 blind residues is exactly
`{c ≠ 0 : -c is not a cube mod ℓ}`, of size `2(ℓ-1)/3`, and every such `c` becomes active at
layer 3 through the free root `x ≡ 0`; consequently, for every `N` and every prime `ℓ ≥ 5` there
is an `n ≤ 3` making `ℓ` a potential denominator prime.

*The key insight is* that "blindness" is a purely Kummer-theoretic condition — the cubic residue
character of `-N` mod `ℓ` — and the free root of `ψ₃` is a *character-free* mechanism, so the
union of two layers is unconditionally surjective on residues.

*Status after cycle 2.*  The cardinality half is now a theorem
(`three_mul_card_blindResidues2_of_one_mod_three`: exactly `2(ℓ-1)/3` blind residues) and the
characterisation of blindness as "`-N` is not a cube mod `ℓ`" is `mem_blindResidues2_iff`; what
remains open is the *uniform in `N`* statement that a single `n ≤ 3` always suffices once an
integral point in the free class `x ≡ 0 (mod ℓ)` is available — which is exactly D3.

*Why now?*  Both halves are already formalised separately here (the `0 ∨ 3` dichotomy and
`V3_nonempty`), so only the arithmetic realisability input is missing.
title: D2. Blind residues are exactly the non-cubes, and they vanish at level 3

description:
**Conjecture.** For `E_55`, `P = (9,28)` and the set `S_x` of good primes `ℓ ≤ x`, the joint
modulus `M(S_x) = lcm{m_ℓ : ℓ ≤ x}` satisfies `log M(S_x) ≫ x^{1−ε}`; in particular the density
`1/M(S_x)` of simultaneous violations decays super-polynomially in `x`.

*The key insight is* that the apparition indices `m_ℓ` are orders of a fixed point in the groups
`E(F_ℓ)`, whose sizes are `ℓ + O(√ℓ)` and whose factorisations are essentially independent, so
their lcm inherits nearly the full product of the largest prime factors.

*Why now?* The joint modulus is now a theorem-level object (`joint_apparition_finset` produces
it with the bound `∏ 4ℓ`), so the conjecture is a statement about a defined quantity and can be
tested directly against the apparition table already computed.
title: D2. Simultaneous apparition moduli grow like the product

description:
**Conjecture.** For every polynomial-time generator family `G_n : {0,1}^{s(n)} → {0,1}^n`
and every polynomial-time decoder, the number of `n`-bit strings compressible
below `n - d` bits is at most `2^{n-d+1}`, and moreover the *time-bounded*
complexity `KC^t` satisfies `KC^t(x) ≥ KC(x)` with the counting bound holding
uniformly in `t`; hence no complexity assumption (P ≠ NP, one-way functions)
can ever be used to beat pigeonhole.

*The key insight is* that the counting argument never inspects the decoder, so
it survives verbatim under any resource bound — bounding resources can only
*remove* decodable strings, never add them.
*Why now?* Our `KC` and `exists_shortest_code` are stated for an arbitrary
`D : List Bool → Bits n`; specializing `D` to a step-indexed interpreter is a
purely definitional extension of the existing files.
title: C1. Resource-bounded seeds do not restore the trick — with an *exponential* loss

description:
**Conjecture.**  If the delta cost obeys the triangle inequality, then the optimal cost of
serving a set `S` of domains from one pretrained decoder is, up to a factor of 2, the
minimum weight of a spanning structure on `S` in the delta metric — so a *library* of
patches costs the metric entropy of the domain space, not `|S|` independent patches.

*The key insight is* `minPlusComp_eq_self_iff_triangle` and `optCost_minPlusComp`: under
the triangle inequality, multi-hop patches never help *within* a stream, which is exactly
the condition making a spanning-tree/Steiner argument tight *across* domains.

*Why now?*  The triangle-inequality machinery and the superadditivity lemma
(`optCost_append_ge`) are in place; what remains is to connect them to a combinatorial
optimum over the domain set, which is a finite, decidable target.
title: C4. Delta reuse across domains: a metric-entropy law for patch libraries

description:
| previous conjecture | status | theorem |
|---|---|---|
| C1 (margin law `1 − ρ(k*) = Θ(m/(L·B))`) | **proved**, with explicit constants `1/8`, `1/4` | `margin_law_theta` (`margin_law_upper`, `margin_law_lower`), plus `marginKnee_antitone`, `marginKnee_inverse_scaling`, and the numeric prediction `netB_margin_channel_lower_bound` |
| C2 (depth drift of `N_eff` is Zipf-amplitude drift) | **refuted in its conjectured form**, and replaced | `amplitude_forced_by_depth_linear_knee`, `amplitude_times_depth_not_constant`; the surviving statement is the depth-independent ceiling `effSupport_ceiling_depth_independent` with the numeric corollary `netA_budget_lower_bound` |
| C3 (`ctx = 1024` mass bound) | **proved** | `mass_at_law_budget_le`, `ctx1024_mass_prediction`, non-vacuity by `uniform_row_realises_ctx1024_hypotheses` |
| C4 (random-`k` control law) | **proved** | `sum_powersetCard_mass`, `random_mass_average`, `selection_gain_le`, `netB_selection_gain_le` |
| C5 (nonexpansiveness is load-bearing) | **proved, both branches** | `depth_leg_linear_of_near_isometry` (survives `Λ ≤ 1 + c/d`), `expansive_knee_not_linear` (fails for fixed `Λ > 1`) |

What C1 now says precisely: at the budget the margin channel selects, the
attention *deficit* satisfies `m/(8LB) ≤ 1 − ρ(k*) ≤ m/(4LB)`, so the knee is
governed by the held-out logit margin and the read-out constant alone; at the
measured long-context cell the certified mass ceiling `ρ ≤ 0.65` turns this into
the falsifiable numeric prediction `m > 1.4·L·B`.  What C2 now says: a
*depth-linear* knee forces the tail amplitude to be exactly `δ/32` at **every**
depth, so `A(d)·d` grows linearly rather than staying constant — the `13 %`
drift of `N_eff` across `d = 4, 8, 16` cannot be tail drift.  What survives is a
cap that the tail does impose on the concentration statistic,
`N_eff ≤ 8·A·ctx + 4`, i.e. `δ ≥ 4·(N_eff − 4)/ctx ≥ 1.52` at the deepest cell.
C3–C5 are as stated in the second cycle: a context-independent mass ceiling
`sqrt(d/(32α))`, an exact control mean `k/ctx` with selection gain capped at
`5.2`, and the near-isometry dichotomy `x ∼ c/d` versus `x ∼ const`.
title: Closed since the first cycle (now theorems, no longer conjectures)

description:
**D1 — the `exp c` factor is measurable, and `c ≈ ‖J‖`-drift is `O(1)`.**  For
the trained stacks, the per-layer Jacobian norms should satisfy `Λ_i ≤ 1 + c/d`
with `c ≤ 1` at every measured depth, so `depth_leg_linear_of_near_isometry`
gives an end-to-end constant `exp c ≤ e`; a measured `c` above `log 2` would
predict a visible upward bend of `k*(d)` between `d = 16` and `d = 32`.  *The
key insight is* that the two branches of C5 are separated by exactly the scaling
`x ∼ c/d` versus `x ∼ const`, so the single spectral number `d·(Λ−1)` decides
which regime a checkpoint is in — before any sweep is run.  *Why now?*
`expansive_knee_not_linear` makes the failure mode quantitative, and Jacobian
norms are a static, cheap measurement on checkpoints already trained.

**D2 — the selection gain saturates its certified ceiling.**  The measured ratio
(top-`k` mass)/(random-`k` mass) at the knee should equal `κ·ctx/sqrt(k·N_eff)`
with `κ ∈ [0.7, 1]` at every grid cell; `κ ≤ 0.3` would mean the mass channel is
not what top-`k` selection exploits.  *The key insight is* that
`selection_gain_le` relates two *independently measurable* quantities, so its
slack is an observable rather than a modelling choice.  *Why now?*
`netB_selection_gain_le` certifies the ceiling `5.2` at the measured cell and
the control already logs both sides.

**D3 — `N_eff` grows like `ctx^0.85`, and the mass ceiling drifts up slowly.**
The measured supports at `d = 4` (`46.6` at `ctx = 128`, `152.11` at `ctx = 512`)
fit `N_eff ≈ 0.75·ctx^0.85`, predicting `N_eff(1024) ≈ 275 ± 15` and hence a
retained-mass ceiling `sqrt(128/275) ≈ 0.68` at the law's budget; a measured
`N_eff(1024) ≥ 512` would instead put the cell in the linear regime where
`mass_at_law_budget_le` caps the mass at the context-independent `0.354`.  *The
key insight is* that the ceiling depends on `d` and on the growth exponent of
`N_eff` **only** — the context length cancels exactly when the growth is linear.
*Why now?*  Both regimes are pre-registered as theorems and `N_eff` is already
logged by the concentration stage.
title: Still open from the second cycle

description:
**Statement.** Let `W : Fin 22 → Fin 11 → ℝ` with zero bias be such that `x ↦ relu(Wx)` is
injective. Then there is a permutation `π` of the 22 units, positive scalars `cᵢ > 0` and an
invertible `A ∈ GL₁₁(ℝ)` such that the rows satisfy `w_{π(i)} = cᵢ · (A e_i)` for `i < 11` and
`w_{π(i)} = −c_i · (A e_{i−11})` for `i ≥ 11` — i.e. every optimal architecture is a
reparametrised positive/negative split.

**The key insight is** that `balanced_activation_at_optimum` already forces the 22 rows to
split into two blocks of 11 that are *mutually antipodal in sign pattern* across every
transverse direction, and a set of vectors whose sign patterns are exactly complementary on
all of `ℝ¹¹` must be an antipodal pair of bases.

**Why now?** The balanced-activation theorem proved in this cycle supplies precisely the
combinatorial input (two disjoint spanning blocks of size exactly `11`) that was missing; the
remaining step is a sign-pattern classification, which is finite-dimensional linear algebra.

**Falsifier.** A single injective bias-free `22 × 11` layer whose rows are not of this form.
