title: Conjecture A — the bias-free optimum is *unique up to symmetry

description:
Demand that `e⁻¹` send the class of an
   unramified prime `𝔭` to `arithFrobAt 𝔭`, and prove that `𝔭` splits completely in `H` iff
   `[𝔭] = 1`. In the elementary abelian case this refines the counting above into a splitting
   law: the primes splitting completely in the degree-`p^k` class field of a subspace `W` are
   exactly those whose class lies in `W`.
title: Frobenius compatibility of the Artin datum

description: Hara–Slade lace-expansion results concern sufficiently high-dimensional lattices and mean-field asymptotics, not an exact square-lattice constant. A faithful development should first formalize convolution, the two-point function, susceptibility, the lace coefficients, and the bootstrap estimates, then derive the applicable high-dimensional asymptotics.
title: Hara–Slade program

description: Lean cannot place a literal proper class inside its ordinary type theory. Mathlib’s `Surreal.{u}` is a universe-relative type of numeric pre-games modulo equivalence. The key boundedness theorem applies to families whose index type is small relative to that universe. The connector theorem is therefore a precise theorem about each such universe-relative surreal line. A class-topological treatment of Conway’s full `No` would require an explicit theory of large/class-indexed topologies and should not silently be identified with ordinary set-based topology.
title: Proper-class caveat

description:
For each `c` strictly between zero and one, the normalized two-qubit states of concurrence `c`, modulo global phase, have a uniform diffeomorphism type, with topology changing only at the product and maximally entangled strata.

**The key insight is...** although concurrence itself cannot be an integer linking number, its critical level sets may still carry meaningful and computable topology.

**Why now?** Explicit interior values and the two boundary values are available, making the conjecture falsifiable through a combination of singular-value coordinates and level-set analysis.
title: Topological stratification of fixed-concurrence level sets

description:
**Conjecture.** For every spectral gap parameter `ε>0`, there is a constant `C(ε)` such that every connected `k`-regular graph with normalized spectral gap at least `ε` and `n ≥ C(ε)k` has a degree-`g-1` divisor of rank at least `k-1`.

The key insight is that expansion should make chip-firing mass redistribution sufficiently uniform to replace a quadratic counting threshold by a linear one. **Why now?** The numerical obstruction is already absent at quadratic scale, leaving expansion as a specific additional mechanism that can plausibly control reduced divisors.
title: Expansion-driven linear threshold

description:
**Conjecture.** For every position from which the attacker forces mate, the accessibility rank of its legal-play relation equals its minimax ordinal game value after the standard winner/loser normalization.

The key insight is that accessibility recursion and ordinal minimax recursion are two presentations of the same well-founded strategy tree, but alternating choices require a carefully polarized rank transformation.

**Why now?** The present escape theorem identifies the complementary non-well-founded case by an explicit infinite chain, while the abstract hierarchy supplies nontrivial well-founded test cases.
title: Strategy-Tree Rank Correspondence

description:
**Conjecture.** On an `m × n` periodic grid, every non-developable increment field has a certificate consisting either of one tile with nonzero curvature or of a simple noncontractible cycle of length at most `m + n` with nonzero period.

The key insight is that local curvature and two fundamental holonomies form a complete obstruction triple, so a compact witness should be extractable without inspecting every closed walk. **Why now?** The classification gives completeness; the remaining testable problem is to obtain sharp bounds and an explicit certificate-extraction algorithm.
title: Minimal certificates of periodic impossibility

description: The factor `T * log 2` is presently a stipulated mathematical scaling law with Boltzmann’s constant normalized to one. A physical treatment should distinguish logical erasure from proof verification, model reversible proof checking, include Boltzmann’s constant and units, and prove lower bounds from explicit irreversible state transitions. Raw proof length alone cannot do this: the padding counterexample shows that semantically irrelevant storage can increase length without changing modeled information cost.
title: Physical calibration

description:
**Conjecture.** The discrepancy `F⁺(N) − F⁻(N)` is bounded in absolute value by a slowly
growing function (conjecturally `O(√N)`), so the two signs stay nearly balanced; at `N = 1000`
the discrepancy is only `2`.

*The key insight is* that the sign of a fundamental discriminant is decoupled from its
squarefree class structure except through the single congruence that distinguishes
`D ≡ 1 (mod 4)` from `D = 4m`, making a large systematic imbalance impossible.

*Why now?* With both signed counts certified, the discrepancy can be tabulated exactly and its
growth rate probed empirically before a proof is attempted.
title: Sign symmetry is a lower-order phenomenon

description:
Every nondegenerate Lucas sequence that is a strong divisibility sequence should satisfy a finite gcd transport theorem, with primitive prime divisors inducing exact synchronization laws outside an explicitly classifiable exceptional set.

The key insight is that induction over finite insertion uses only the binary strong-divisibility identity, while the apparition argument uses only primality and minimality.

Why now? The Fibonacci proof identifies precisely which components are sequence-independent and which require Lucas-specific arithmetic.
title: Lucas-sequence finite-meet transport

description:
The isomorphism `Ext¹(ℤ/k, Y) ≅ Y/kY` is natural in `Y`: for every morphism `f : Y ⟶ Y'` of
`ℤ`-modules the induced square, with vertical maps the isomorphisms and horizontal maps
`Ext¹(ℤ/k, f)` and the map induced by `f` on the quotients, commutes.

*Status.* The isomorphism itself is a theorem: `extOneZModEquiv` gives `Y ⧸ kY ≃+ Ext¹(ℤ/k, Y)`
for every `k ≠ 0`, built from the explicit surjection `y ↦ extClass ∘ (1 ↦ y)`
(`extOneHom_surjective`) whose kernel is exactly `kY` (`ker_extOneHom`). What is not formalised is
functoriality of this description in `Y`. Falsified by a morphism `f` for which the square fails
to commute.
title: C1. Naturality of the isomorphism `Ext¹(ℤ/k, Y) ≅ Y/kY`

description:
For a `ℤ`-module `G`: `G` is flat if and only if `Tor₁(G, ℤ/p) = 0` for every **prime** `p`.

*Status.* The version quantified over all `k ≠ 0` is now a theorem:
`flat_iff_isZero_torOne_zmod` proves `Flat ℤ G ↔ ∀ k ≠ 0, Tor₁(G, ℤ/k) = 0`, via
`flat_iff_torsionFree` (flat = torsion-free over a Bezout domain),
`isZero_kernel_mulBy_iff` (`ker(k·) = 0` iff `k` acts injectively) and the computation
`torOneZModIso : Tor₁(G, ℤ/k) ≅ G[k]`; the strengthening
`flat_iff_isZero_tor_succ` shows flatness is equivalent to the vanishing of *all* `Torₙ₊₁(G, −)`.
The conjecture asks whether the test family can be shrunk to the primes, i.e. whether
`G[p] = 0` for all primes `p` forces `G[k] = 0` for all `k ≥ 1`. Falsified by a group `G` with
`G[p] = 0` for every prime `p` but `Tor₁(G, ℤ/k) ≠ 0` for some `k`.
title: C3. `Tor₁` against the prime cyclic groups already detects flatness

description:
Original conjecture: `∀ a, psi a < Om`. This is **false** for the unrestricted hull:
`Bridges.OrdinalCollapsing.not_forall_psi_lt_Om`. For `a < b` the ordinal `psi a` *is* a
generator at stage `b`, whereas `psi b ∉ Gen (gens b)`; so `psi a ≠ psi b`, and with
`psi_mono` this upgrades to `psi_strictMono`, hence `a ≤ psi a` (`self_le_psi`) and
`Om ≤ psi Om`. The exact form of the failure is now known: `psi c < Ω` *does* hold for
every countable `c` (`psi_lt_Om`), and the first value at or above `Ω` is
`psi Ω = ε_{Ω+1}`.

> **C1′.** Let `psi'` be the *restricted* Madore collapse, defined by
> `gens' a = {0, Ω} ∪ {psi' c | c < a ∧ c ∈ Gen (gens' a)}`. Then `psi' a < Ω` for every
> `a`, `psi'` is non-decreasing, and `psi' (ε_{Ω+1})` is the Bachmann–Howard ordinal.
> Falsifiable by exhibiting `a` with `psi' a ≥ Ω`. Formalising `psi'` requires a
> simultaneous recursion between the hull and the function, which is the main technical
> obstacle; the results proved here for `psi` (`psi_zero`, monotonicity, the bridge
> theorems) should transfer, since the two functions agree at `0` and the chain
> `ε₀ = psi 0 < psi (Ω^ω)` uses only generators of the form `psi c` with `c` explicitly
> in the hull.
title: C1. The collapse stays countable: `psi a < Ω` — REFUTED (formally)*

description:
> **C6.** *(Collapsing is exactly the loss of one epsilon number.)* For the unrestricted
> hull, `range psi = ε '' {a | a ≠ Ω}` is now a theorem (`range_psi`). Conjecture: for
> the restricted collapse of C1′, `range psi' = {ε_a | a < Ω} ∪ {ψ'-values below Ω}` is
> instead a set of order type `Ω` cofinal in `Ω`, and `psi'` is *not* injective.
> Falsifiable by proving `psi'` injective, or by exhibiting a value of `psi'` at or
> above `Ω`.

> **C7.** *(Notation systems.)* The term system `OTerm` modulo `Step` (equivalently, its
> normal forms) with the induced order is order-isomorphic to a *proper initial segment*
> of `Iio (psi (ε_{Ω+1}))`, not to all of it: the missing ordinals are exactly those
> whose `Ω`-CNF needs a value `psi a` with `a` not itself denoted by a term. Falsifiable
> by producing a surjection of term values onto `Iio (psi (ε_{Ω+1}))`.

> **C8.** *(Sharpness of the PA bridge.)* The `ψ`-free fragment of the term system and
> the `PA` notation system have the same values:
> `{t.val | t : OTerm, t.Simple} = {o.repr | o : ONote, o.NF}`, and `ofONote` maps every
> `NF` notation to a `Simple` term. Value preservation and order reflection are already
> proved (`val_ofONote`, `ofONote_val_lt_iff`, `strictMono_ofONote`), and the left-hand
> side is `Iio ε₀` (`simple_val_range`), so the conjecture is equivalent to: every
> ordinal below `ε₀` is `o.repr` for some `NF` notation `o`. Falsifiable by an ordinal
> `< ε₀` outside the image of `ONote.repr`, or by an `NF` notation whose `ofONote`
> translation is not `Simple`.
title: New conjectures suggested by the closed form

description:
The reciprocity conjectured by Koizumi–Liu and proved in the paper for central
arrangements is a relation between the ranks of `MH_{k,ℓ}` of an arrangement and of its
"complement" data, ultimately Alexander duality for the associated simplicial complex.
This needs A, C and a formalization of Alexander duality for simplicial complexes,
which is not currently in Mathlib; it is the most distant of these targets.
title: F. Homological reciprocity

description:
**Statement.**  `U(n+1) ≤ 2·U(n) + 1`.  Together with the proved strict
monotonicity this would give `U(n) ≤ 2^{n-3}·5` from `U(3) = 5`, and, more
importantly, any single improved value `U(n₀) < 2^{c·n₀}` would propagate to
`U(n) ≤ 2^{cn + O(1)}` for all `n`.  The known values `1, 3, 5, ≤ 8` satisfy it
with room to spare (`8 ≤ 2·5 + 1`).

**The key insight is** that a host for `n+1` points should be assembled from two
copies of a host for `n` points — the points below and the points not below a
distinguished element — plus one connecting point, mirroring the recursive
structure of the Boolean lattice; the difficulty is that the distinguished
element of the embedded poset is not known in advance, so the two copies must be
glued in a way that keeps *both* possible readings induced.

**Why now?**  The deletion argument of `isUniversalPosetOfSize_pred` shows that
the "remove one point" direction of this recursion behaves perfectly (it loses
exactly one point); the conjecture asks whether the reverse direction loses only
a factor of two, and the machinery for building and transporting hosts
(`isUniversalPosetOfSize_of_host`, `IsUniversalHost.congr`) is already in place.
title: C5.  A doubling recursion: `U(n+1) ≤ 2·U(n) + 1`

description:
**Statement.** Every solution of `C(n,k) = C(n-1,k+1)` with `1 ≤ k ≤ n-2` is a member
of the Fibonacci family, i.e. `n = F(2i+4) F(2i+5)` and `k = F(2i+2) F(2i+5)` for
some `i ≥ 0`.  Equivalently: with `m = n - k`, the integer `(5m-1)(m-1)` is a perfect
square iff `m = F(2i+3) F(2i+5)` (or `m ∈ {1,2}`).

**Status here.** `Singmaster.choose_cross` proves the combinatorics-to-arithmetic
direction and `Singmaster.fib_cross` proves that the Fibonacci pairs are solutions.
The converse (completeness) is open in this development.

**The key insight is** that `5m^2 - 6m + 1 = \square` is, after the substitution
`x = 10m - 6`, the Pell equation `x^2 - 5y^2 = 16`, whose solution semigroup is
generated by the fundamental unit `(9 + 4\sqrt5)` of `ℤ[\sqrt5]`; Fibonacci numbers
enter exactly because that unit is `φ^6`.

**Why now?** This is a genuine algebra/combinatorics bridge: it converts a statement
about binomial coefficients into a statement about the unit group of a real quadratic
order, and Mathlib already has `Zsqrtd`, Pell equations and the Fibonacci API used in
`cassini_odd`.

---
title: cross-row equation

description:
**Conjecture.** There is an explicit finite-dimensional bigraded dg-algebra over `Q` — of
Poincaré type of a surface, with `dim H^1 = 2`, `dim H^2 = 2` — carrying a triple Massey product
that is nonzero for *every* choice of primitives. By `not_weightPure_of_massey` such an algebra
admits no pure weight grading, giving a fully formal, self-contained counterpart of the
non-formal smooth proper rigid-analytic surfaces.

*The key insight is* that non-formality can be certified purely by a finite linear-algebra
computation (the Massey representative is not in the image of `d` restricted to one graded
piece), so the certificate is decidable once the multiplication table is fixed.

*Why now?* The obstruction theorem is proved; only the construction of one concrete bigraded
algebra instance (a `GradedAlgebra` structure on a finite-dimensional model) is missing, and
Mathlib's `AddMonoidAlgebra.gradeBy` machinery — used already in
`Catalog/Novelty/WeightMonodromyExamples.lean` — gives a template. Falsifiable: a proof that
every finite-dimensional bigraded model of a surface with these Betti numbers is formal.
title: C3. Non-formality of rigid-analytic surfaces has an explicit finite-dimensional witness

description:
**Conjecture.** For every `U ∈ GLₙ(ℤ)`, the transformed form `Q_U(y) = Q(Uy)`
with shift `U⁻¹t` has the *same* inhomogeneous minimum `μ(Q_U, U⁻¹t) = μ(Q, t)`
and the same solution counting function, but its spectral bounds `m_U, M_U` can
differ arbitrarily; consequently the LLL-reduced representative minimises the
ratio `M_U·n/4 : m_U·d(U⁻¹t,ℤⁿ)²` and the sandwich `inhomMin_sandwich` becomes
asymptotically tight after reduction.

*The key insight is* that `inhomMin` is a `GLₙ(ℤ)`-invariant of the pair
`(form, shift)`, whereas both ends of the proved sandwich are not — so lattice
reduction is precisely the act of choosing coordinates in which the two
*non-invariant* bounds pinch the *invariant* quantity.

*Why now?* The invariance half is a short bijection argument on `ℤⁿ` (the map
`x ↦ U⁻¹x` is a `Finset`-preserving equivalence), so the conjecture can be split
immediately into a provable invariance lemma and a genuinely open optimisation
statement about reduced bases.
title: C4. Reduction stability: the gap is invariant, the covering bound is not

description:
**Conjecture.** If for some shift `t` with all coordinates irrational the theta
series of `A` factorises as a product of `n` one-dimensional shifted Gaussian
sums for all `s > 0`, then `A` is diagonal.  Equivalently: the failure of
multiplicativity of `Θ` is a faithful invariant detecting off-diagonal mass.

*The key insight is* that `Cycle2.theta_diagonal` proves factorisation from
diagonality by Fubini on `ℤⁿ`, and the reverse direction should follow by
comparing the `s → ∞` expansions: the first two exponents of `Θ` recover the two
smallest values of `Q(x − t)`, and matching all of them across the product
forces the Gram matrix to split.

*Why now?* The proved ingredients (`tsum_pi_prod`, `summable_theta`, and the
counting bound that makes coefficientwise comparison legitimate) already give
uniqueness of Dirichlet-type expansions in this setting; the remaining work is
combinatorial bookkeeping of exponents, not new convergence theory.
title: C5. Theta factorisation obstructs off-diagonality (a converse to `theta_diagonal`)

description:
**Conjecture.**  For coefficient vectors `c₁, c₂` on a finite ground set `E`, the
*stable* intersection `H(c₁) ∩_st H(c₂)`, defined as the set of limits
`lim_{t → 0} (H(c₁) ∩ H(c₂ + t·v))` along a generic perturbation direction `v`,
satisfies the vector elimination axiom, even though the set-theoretic
intersection does not (`intersection_not_satisfiesElimination`).

*The key insight is* that the failure exhibited in this cycle is caused by a
non-transverse coincidence of two tropical minima, and perturbing one hyperplane
destroys precisely that coincidence while leaving the elimination witnesses
constructed in `tropVanishing_elimination` intact.

*Why now?*  The formal framework (`IsTropicalLinearSpace`, the explicit witness
construction, and a verified counterexample delimiting the truth) is in place, so
the conjecture is a statement about one extra limit operation rather than about
an untested definition.
title: C1. Stable intersection repairs elimination

description:
Extend `nondetExtIter : ℕ → SurvivalGame → SurvivalGame` to a tower indexed by ordinals: at
successors refine by `ω`, at limits take the dependent lexicographic sum used to build
`limitGame`. Conjecturally the value at level `δ` is `ω ^ δ` for every `δ` below the first
fixed point of `δ ↦ ω ^ δ`, and the tower's own limit is exactly `ε₀`:

```lean
theorem towerValue (δ : Ordinal) : (tower δ finiteGame).value = ω ^ (δ + 1)
theorem tower_limit_value : (towerLimit finiteGame).value = ε₀
```

**The key insight is** that the level-`k` bound already proved here comes entirely from the key
function `limitKey ⟨k, a⟩ = ω ^ k + typein a`, and that key is definable uniformly in the level:
replacing `k : ℕ` by `δ : Ordinal` turns the finite Cantor-normal-form argument into the general
one, so no new combinatorics is needed — only a type-level transfinite recursion.

**Why now?** The `Σₗ`-based limit construction is verified, including its well-foundedness
(the actual obstacle: Mathlib has no `IsWellOrder` instance for lexicographic sigma types, and
the key function supplies one). Moreover `ImmortalitySigmaLimit.sigmaGame_value_eq` already
proves the *general* limit step — any chain of lives cofinal in an additively principal ordinal
attains it — so only the transfinite type-level recursion remains to be built.

---
title: Conjecture A — The transfinite refinement tower reaches `ε₀` exactly at level `ε₀`

description:
**Statement.** Let `H` be an external hint distribution on `[0, N)` and let
`ε = Pr[gcd(N, H) ∉ {1, N}]`. Then any gcd-based factoring procedure using one
sample from `H` succeeds with probability exactly `ε`, and amplification to
constant success requires `Θ(1/ε)` independent samples — with no speed-up from
combining the hint with any polynomial derived modulus.

**The key insight is** that `useful_hint_count` pins `ε = (p+q-1)/pq` for the
uniform hint, and `derived_hints_useless` shows the derived data adds a
deterministic function of `N`, hence zero information; so the whole gain must
come from the hint's own structure.

**Why now?** Both halves are already formal here; what is missing is the
sampling lemma (a Chernoff/independence argument over `Finset`), which Mathlib's
probability library supports. Falsifiable: exhibit a hint distribution with
`ε` small where a derived modulus provably improves success probability.
title: C3 (Quantitative hint-amplification threshold).

description:
**Conjecture.** For every `d` and every GF(2) polynomial `P` of degree `≤ d` in the bits of `N`,
the fraction of *odd* pairs `(p,q)` mod `2^t` on which `P(N) = p_j` is exactly `1/2` for all
`1 ≤ j < t` — and this remains true when `P` is allowed to read, in addition, any `o(t)` of the
high bits of the true integer product `pq` (not merely `pq mod 2^t`).

*The key insight is* that the proved theorem already handles *arbitrary* functions of the low
block, so the only extension needed is to let the predictor see a bounded amount of magnitude
information; the group-theoretic proof (`group_zero_block`) should survive as long as the extra
information is a function of a coset of a subgroup of bounded index.

*Why now?* `group_zero_block` isolates the mechanism as the regular representation, which makes the
"low block + bounded magnitude" hybrid a statement about a subgroup filtration rather than about
primes.

---
title: C4. No low-degree GF(2) approximator, unconditionally, via the low block

description:
**Conjecture.** For every `k ≤ min(p,q)` and every `N = pq`, the *weight
enumerator* of the evaluation code `C_k(N)` — not merely its minimum distance —
is the Hadamard product of the two Reed–Solomon weight enumerators, and every
one of its "gaps" (weights not attained) determines `max(p,q)`.  Consequently a
`poly(log N)`-time algorithm for *any* single nonzero coefficient of the weight
enumerator yields a factoring algorithm.

*The key insight is* that `RSMind.card_zeroSet_le` is really a statement about
the product structure of the zero set (`RSMind.card_zeroSet_le_mul`): the whole
weight spectrum, not just its minimum, is a product of prime-level spectra, so
every spectral feature is a free witness.

*Why now?* The minimum-distance case is fully proved (`min_distance_general`,
exact for all `k ≤ p`); the general spectrum needs only a counting refinement of
the same CRT injection, with no new machinery.
title: C1. The CRT-splitting dichotomy for evaluation codes

description:
**Conjecture.** For `N` a product of `k` unramified primes of the `A₄`-field,
the mutual information between `N mod 9` and the full split-vector satisfies
`I_k = Θ(k·3^{-k})` for the "all split" fork and `I_k → H(Bin-class)` for the
count fork; in particular the *per-factor* information tends to `0`
geometrically, quantifying "factor-useless".

*The key insight is* that thinning by `3^{-(k-1)}` sends the leakage law into the
regime `H(pq) − pH(q) ≈ pq·log₂(1/p)`, which is linear in `q`; the proved limit
`info_all_split_tendsto_zero` is the qualitative shadow of that asymptotic.
*Why now?* The exact `k`-dependent closed form `H(3^{-(k+1)}) − (1/3)H(3^{-k})`
is already formal, so the conjecture is now a pure asymptotic analysis exercise
about `H` near `0`.
title: C4. Collapse rate of the multiplicative channel

description:
**Conjecture.** The sequence `n ↦ n² I(n)` is strictly decreasing for `n ≥ 2` and
`n² I(n) > 1 − log 2` for every `n`, with the sharp two-sided expansion
```
n² I(n) = (1 − log 2) + 1/(4n) + O(1/n²) .
```
(The tabulated differences `n·(n²I(n) − (1 − log 2))` are `0.253` at `n = 100` and `0.250` at
`n = 1000`, so the first-order coefficient is `1/4`, not the `9/4` of the polynomial part alone:
the cubic Taylor terms contribute `−2` to it.)

**The key insight is** that the `1/n` coefficient is a *cancellation residue* — the `9/4` produced
by the quadratic Taylor part is cut down to `1/4` by the cubic parts of the three logarithms — so
monotonicity of the dial is equivalent to positivity of a single explicit
rational-plus-logarithmic function of `n`, with no group theory left in it.
**Why now?** The exact identity `n_sq_semiprimeDial_eq` reduces everything to a one-variable
inequality, and the Taylor machinery (`abs_log_one_sub_taylor_le`) is already in place; only a
derivative sign is missing.
Falsifiable by a single pair `n < m` with `n² I(n) < m² I(m)`; the tabulated values
`0.8630, 0.4540, 0.3979, 0.3352, 0.3094, …` are consistent with the claim.
title: C12. `n² I(n)` is strictly decreasing, and `1 − log 2` is approached from above

description:
**Conjecture.**  For an odd prime `q` and `N ∈ 𝔽_q^×`, the *difference* invariant
`D_q(N) = {x - y : xy = N}` satisfies `|D_q(N)| = (q + χ_q(-N))/2`, and the pair
`(S_q(N), D_q(N))` determines the unordered factor pair modulo `q` but never the
ordered one — so no symmetric residue observable can break the `p ↔ q` symmetry.

*Status.* Open; the size claim follows the same discriminant computation
(`x - y` has `(x-y)² = s² - 4N` replaced by `(x+y)² = d² + 4N`), so it should be
provable by the method of `card_traceSet_prime`.

*The key insight is* that the swap `x ↔ y` acts on every factorisation datum, and
the trace and the difference generate the whole invariant ring of that action; a
congruence attack therefore lives on the quotient, where `p` and `q` are
indistinguishable by construction.

*Why now?*  `card_traceSet_prime` already contains all the machinery (the involution
`x ↦ N/x`, the degenerate-fibre count), so C5 is a short extension that closes the
"never isolate `p` or `q`" clause of the verdict at the same level of rigour as the
rest.
title: C5.  Higher symmetric functions of a semiprime are congruence-free

description:
**Conjecture.** For every prime `f` and every `ε > 0` there is `X₀` such that the
empirical joint law of `(T(p), T(q), N mod f)` over semiprimes `N = pq ≤ X ≥ X₀` is
within `ε` of the uniform exponent model used here; consequently the measured
Monte-Carlo channel converges to the exact `I_pair(f−1)` computed in this
development.

*Status.* Supported numerically (`1.2452` vs `5/4`, `1.4711` vs `log₂3 − 1/9`), and
the *algebraic* half is a theorem here (`exists_generator_ordType`: the exponent
model is a faithful description of `(ℤ/f)ˣ`).  The analytic half is Chebotarev plus
a semiprime equidistribution input.

*The key insight is* that only the *uniformity of `p mod f`* is needed, not the full
Chebotarev machine: the channel value is a continuous function of the joint residue
law, so an effective equidistribution estimate transfers directly to an error bound
on `I_pair`.

*Why now?* The channel is now an explicit finite formula in the residue law, so any
equidistribution input can be plugged in as a perturbation bound — the Lipschitz
constant of `I_pair` in the joint law is the only missing lemma.

---
title: C5. Chebotarev realisability of the exponent model

description:
**Statement.** Let `N ∈ ℤ`, let `ℓ` be an odd prime and let `P₁, P₂` be rational points of
`E_N` lying in the denominator kernel at `ℓ`, with `v_ℓ(den x(P₁)) ≠ v_ℓ(den x(P₂))`. If
`P₁ + P₂` is affine with `x`-coordinate `x₃`, then
`v_ℓ(den x₃) = min(v_ℓ(den x(P₁)), v_ℓ(den x(P₂)))`; and if the two valuations agree, then
`v_ℓ(den x₃) ≥ v_ℓ(den x(P₁))`, with equality unless `ℓ ∣` an explicit resultant.

**The key insight is** that `kernel_stable_add` already produces the chord `x`-coordinate as an
explicit ratio `A/B` of integers in the coprime parametrisation `x = a/e²`, `y = b/e³`, so the
`min` law is a statement about the `ℓ`-adic sizes of the three summands of `A` — no formal-group
machinery is needed, only a term-by-term valuation count.

**Why now?** The closure statement is proved, so the qualitative half of the ultrametric picture
is settled; what remains is exactly the quantitative refinement, and the integer identity that
carries it is already in the file as `chord_den_not_dvd_of_kernel`.
title: C1. Ultrametric valuation law for the chord

description:
**Conjecture.**  For every `k`, `t` and every pair of position sets
`A, B ⊆ {0,…,k−1}` with `|A| = |B|`, and every candidate set `S` that is a
union of residue classes mod `2^k`, the two bit-leak hints have identical class
size *multisets*, not merely identical sizes on the full cube.  Consequently a
Coppersmith-style advantage of contiguous top-half leakage is invisible to any
counting argument and must be charged entirely to lattice reduction.

*The key insight is* that "position" is an algorithmic resource, not an
informational one; the Coppersmith condition `t ≥ k/2` cannot be recovered from
any cardinality bound, which is why every attempt to beat it by re-arranging
the leaked bits has failed.

*Why now?*  `card_fiber_coordRestrict_congr` proves the full-cube case in three
lines; the general case is the statement that the two coordinate subgroups are
conjugate under a permutation of the cube, which is within reach of Mathlib's
`Equiv.Perm` API.
title: C3. No hint family is position-sensitive at the counting level

description:
**Conjecture.**  Let `h(p)` be any hint computable from `(N, p mod m)` alone.
Then on the set `S_N` of candidates consistent with `N`, `h` cannot cut the
search below the "trace-set floor" `|S_N| / m`; in particular no `N`-checkable
hint of unbounded length beats a `log₂ m`-bit external hint.  Cycle I proves the
degenerate case (hint depending on `N` only: zero information,
`worstCost_of_public`).

*The key insight is* that checkability against public data is exactly
factorisation through a public quotient, and factorisation through a quotient is
the same phenomenon that makes public hints worthless — the floor is a fibre
count, not a cryptographic assumption.

*Why now?*  `worstCost_of_public` gives the mechanism; the general version needs
only the product-of-quotients bound already used in `worstCost_pair_ge`.
title: C5. A trace-set floor for `N`-checkable hints

description:
For every non-torsion integral point `P` of `E_N` with `N` squarefree there is `n₀` such that
for all `n ≥ n₀` the denominator `den x(nP)` has a prime divisor `ℓ` with `ℓ ∤ den x(mP)` for
all `1 ≤ m < n`, and every such primitive `ℓ` is a prime of good reduction for `n` large.

*The key insight is* that primitivity plus the singular-locus law forces the new prime to be
good: bad primes are confined to the finitely many indices divisible by a factor of `N`, so
almost all primitive divisors are good, which quantifies "the conjecture fails infinitely
often" into "it fails at almost every index".

*Why now?*  The catalog already has the apparition-index subgroup `denKernel` and the exact
`2`-adic growth law; combining them gives a lower bound on `den x(nP)` and an upper bound on
the contribution of old primes, which is the standard shape of a Zsygmondy argument.
title: Conjecture C3 (primitive divisors: a Zsygmondy law for Mordell denominators)

description:
**Conjecture.**  For every integer `q ≥ 2` (not necessarily prime) define the ramp series
`R_q(s) = ∑_k q^{-ks}`.  Then `∏_{q ≥ 2} R_q(s)` diverges for all `s`, while the product
restricted to the characteristics realisable by the model (`q` a prime power) equals
`ζ(s)·∏_{p} ∏_{r ≥ 2} (1 - p^{-rs})^{-1}`, i.e. the reliability model over all *finite fields*
computes `∏_{r≥1} ζ(rs)`.

*The key insight is* that allowing `𝔽_{p^r}` as the coefficient field replaces each Euler factor
`(1-p^{-s})^{-1}` by the full `r`-tower, and the resulting product telescopes into a product of
shifted zeta values — so "which reliability curves are realisable" is an arithmetic question.

*Why now?*  `EOSRampZetaBridge.tprod_rampSeries_eq_riemannZeta` establishes the `r = 1` layer
using Mathlib's `riemannZeta_eulerProduct_tprod`; the model itself already works over any finite
field, only the `ZMod p` specialisation is hard-coded.
title: C4. Zeta-side refinement: the ramp series detects primality

description:
**Conjecture.** For every `m`, there is a family `F` of `2^m` decompressors and
a string `x` such that `min_i KC(F_i, x) = n - m` exactly, i.e. the additive
loss `m` in `exists_hard_for_whole_family` cannot be improved to `m - 1`, while
simultaneously *no* family achieves `min_i KC(F_i, x) ≤ n - m - 1` for all `x`.

*The key insight is* that the family decoder `familyDecoder F` is an optimal
prefix-selection machine, so the `m` index bits are simultaneously sufficient
(upper bound, already proved) and necessary (matching lower bound, open).
*Why now?* `exists_code_of_small_set` gives the tightness technology on the
constructive side; the lower bound needs only a partition-counting argument
over `2^m` decoders.
title: C4. Descriptive-complexity form of the family bound: the `log`-loss is optimal

description:
**Statement.** For every `m ≥ 22` there is an injective ReLU layer `ℝ¹¹ → ℝᵐ` whose frame
constants satisfy `α ≥ 1/2 + c·(m − 22)/m` for an absolute `c > 0`, and no injective layer of
width `m` has lower frame constant `α > 1/2 + C·(m − 22)/m`. In particular the optimal
condition number `√2` at `m = 22` improves *continuously*, not discontinuously, with width.

**The key insight is** that the lower frame constant is controlled by the worst antipodal
pair, and the proof of `double_frame_lower` localises the loss of a factor `2` to coordinates
whose sign flips; adding redundant detectors in generic directions reduces the number of
coordinates that can flip simultaneously without being seen.

**Why now?** The sharp constants `1/2` and `1` are now proved for the optimum, so a
width/conditioning trade-off curve has two anchored endpoints to interpolate between.

**Falsifier.** A width-`23` layer with frame constant `1/2` that is provably optimal, or a
width-`m` layer beating the claimed upper envelope.

---
title: Conjecture B — the width law is stable: `2n(1+ε)` units buy conditioning `1/(1+ε)`

description:
**Conjecture.** A flat, period-free periodic increment field admits a piecewise-linear developable realization in three-space with prescribed edge lengths if and only if each fundamental tile satisfies its polygon inequalities and the induced rotational holonomy is trivial.

The key insight is that additive height integrability is necessary but does not control metric compatibility or rotational holonomy. **Why now?** The additive classification cleanly identifies the residual geometric data, allowing counterexamples and positive constructions to target metric and rotational constraints separately.
title: Developable realizations with metric constraints

description:
Conjecture: There exist bounded-depth tropical circuits with coordinate mixing and a discrete message alphabet for which finding collisions is average-case hard under a standard combinatorial assumption, whereas every fixed number of uncoupled min-plus linear forms remains collision-rich.

The key insight is that adding independent linear keys does not create diffusion: security requires nonlinear reuse and coupling of coordinates, not merely more coordinatewise minima.

Why now? The universal two-key collision theorem gives a rigorous obstruction that candidate constructions must escape and suggests a precise design test: every input coordinate must influence active witnesses through multiple coupled layers.
title: Collision resistance from nonlinear tropical circuits

description:
For a radial Woods–Saxon potential with a standard spin–orbit term and parameter intervals calibrated to medium and heavy nuclei, conjecture that certified eigenvalue enclosures preserve the ordering needed for closures at `28`, `50`, and `82` throughout nontrivial parameter boxes.

The key insight is that a useful comparison with experiment requires robust eigenvalue inequalities over parameter ranges, not a single floating-point diagonalization.

Why now? The exact combinatorial shell counts identify the required multiplicities, while modern interval eigensolvers can test whether realistic potentials realize them stably.
title: Woods–Saxon spectral certification with interval bounds

description:
**Conjecture.** Tropical preimage search is polynomial-time for nonce families described by difference constraints, but becomes NP-complete when the nonce language permits arbitrary binary linear constraints, even for a fixed number of digest components.

The key insight is that each tropical output condition is a union of linear regions indexed by active coordinates; tractability depends on whether the nonce language preserves shortest-path structure or can encode disjunctive choices. **Why now?** Unrestricted inversion and collision construction are explicit, so any computational hardness must arise from the geometry of the admissible nonce family rather than from the min-plus hash itself.
title: Complexity transition for nonce-restricted tropical mining

description:
**Conjecture.** If every preferred extension of a finite framework contains its grounded extension and every argument outside the grounded extension has a unique defender inside it, then the preferred-generated complex collapses onto the simplex spanned by the grounded extension.

The key insight is that unique semantic defence may define dominated vertices, translating grounded semantics into a sequence of topological elementary collapses. **Why now?** The attack-free boundary case exhibits complete collapse to a simplex, and the generated construction makes the proposed domination mechanism precise.
title: Grounded-core collapse criterion

description:
**Conjecture.** For a finite network of interacting polynomial causal loops, a weighted product metric yields unique global consistency whenever the nonnegative matrix of componentwise Lipschitz influences has spectral radius below one. Conversely, linear networks with spectral radius at least one admit parameters exhibiting either nonuniqueness or instability.

The key insight is that network consistency should be governed by spectral gain around all feedback cycles, not by the largest local coupling in isolation. **Why now?** The one-loop theorem supplies the scalar base case, and causal networks provide a falsifiable bridge between fixed-point theory, matrix analysis, and polynomial dynamics.
title: Coupled spacetime loops and spectral contraction

description:
For a concrete arithmetized theory with a fixed prefix-free syntax, conjecture explicit upper and lower bounds on the shortest fixed-point sentence in terms of the description length of its provability predicate. Test whether bounded recodings preserve these bounds up to additive constants.

The key insight is that semantic incompleteness yields existence but no numerical threshold; quantitative diagonalization must account for the cost of quotation, substitution, and the provability predicate.

Why now? The abstract boundary is clear: counting laws and fixed-point laws are presently separate, so coding-cost estimates are the necessary bridge between them.
title: Gödel fixed points with quantitative coding bounds

description:
**Conjecture.** The map sending a fundamental discriminant `D` to the quadratic field
`ℚ(√D)` is a bijection onto the set of quadratic fields; hence the count `608` equals the
number of quadratic fields `ℚ(√d)` whose discriminant has absolute value at most `1000`.

*The key insight is* that a quadratic field is determined by its discriminant, and every
fundamental discriminant arises from exactly one field, so counting discriminants counts
fields with no double-counting.

*Why now?* The discriminant side of this bijection is now enumerated and certified; only the
field-theoretic uniqueness statement remains, making the correspondence a concrete finite
target rather than an asymptotic one.
title: The census determines the field census bijectively

description:
The case `k = 2` is now proved: `rk MH_{2,2}(Q_n) = 2ⁿ·C(n+1,2)`.  The general statement
suggested by `ComputationalEvidence.md` is `rk MH_{k,k}(Q_n) = 2ⁿ·C(k+n-1, n-1)`, i.e.
`2ⁿ` times the Hilbert function of the polynomial ring on the `n` hyperplanes — the
Stanley–Reisner ring of the full simplex, which is the complex attached to each tope of
the Boolean arrangement.  With A and B in place, the same Euler-characteristic argument
used in `finrank_ker_delta2_add` (a surjection onto a free module splits, so ranks add)
computes every `rk MH_{k,k}` from the chain counts; the combinatorial input is then the
alternating-sum identity `Σ_j (-1)^j · #MC_{k-j,k} = 2ⁿ·C(k+n-1,n-1)`.
title: C. Rank of `MH_{k,k}` as a Hilbert function

description:
The step from the Boolean arrangement to an arbitrary real arrangement is the step from
`Finset (Fin n)` to the set of topes of an oriented matroid (covectors of maximal
support).  A reasonable formalization target is: define topes abstractly as a set of sign
vectors closed under the tope axioms, prove `dist T T' = |Sep(T,T')|` for the tope graph
(the partial-cube property), and re-derive stages 3–9 in that generality.  `topeGraph_dist`
here is the special case where all `2ⁿ` sign vectors are topes.  Note that stages 7, 8, 10
are already proved for arbitrary (finite, connected) graphs, so only the counts of stage 9
have to be redone.
title: D. General real arrangements and oriented matroids

description:
Let `f = tropForm a` be unanimous with `a k = 1` and let
`c = min { untrop (a j) : j ≠ k, a j ≠ 0 }` be the smallest finite handicap among the other
voters (finite exactly when `f` is not a dictatorship).  Then the classical-IIA violation
can be realised with cost perturbations of size `Θ(c)`: two profiles agreeing in all
individual rankings, differing in a single voter's reported costs by at most `c + ε`, whose
social rankings disagree — and no perturbation of size below `c` suffices.

Evidence: `nondictatorial_violates_classical_IIA` constructs a violation with a
perturbation of size `100 + c`, hence `O(c)`; the lower bound is the open part and would
say that the handicap `c` measures exactly how much cardinal information the rule consumes.

Falsifiable: a unanimous non-dictatorial tropical linear rule whose ordinal violations all
require perturbations `ω(c)`, or one admitting a violation with perturbation `< c`.
title: Conjecture E (Quantitative ordinal price)

description:
For a data nerve `N` and its `1`-skeleton `N¹`, define the *flag defect*
`fd(N,𝓕) = dim H¹(N¹;𝓕) - dim H¹(N;𝓕) ≥ 0` (nonnegativity is
`finrank_H1full_le_finrank_H1`).  Conjecture: `fd(N,𝓕)` equals the rank of the
`δ¹` matrix restricted to the pairwise cocycle space, and in particular
`fd(N,𝓕) = 0` for **every** sheaf on `N` if and only if every `2`-cell of `N`
has a restriction map whose triple-overlap alternating sum is already implied by
its pairwise faces.

*The key insight is* that the flag/pairwise reduction is not a property of the
nerve's combinatorics at all — the triangle counterexample has the most
symmetric possible combinatorics — but a rank condition on `δ¹`, so the correct
"flag" hypothesis is homological, not simplicial.

*Why now?*  `flag_reduction_fails` shows the simplicial formulation is dead, and
`finrank_H1full_add_finrank_range` already expresses both dimensions in terms of
`rank δ⁰` and `dim ker δ¹`, reducing the conjecture to a statement about
`rank δ¹`.  Falsifiable on any synthetic nerve with two `2`-cells.
title: Conjecture B (Sheaf-theoretic redundancy of the flag hypothesis)

description:
**Conjecture.** For every `a, b` with `disc a b ≠ 0`, `a(a,b)² ≤ 4q`, and this is provable
from (i) the exact second moment, (ii) `frobTrace_twist`, and (iii) the multiplicativity of
the count under base change `F → F_{q^n}` — with no Riemann–Roch and no Jacobian.

**The key insight is** that `a(a,b)² ≤ 4q` is equivalent to the positivity of the quadratic
form `n ↦ q^n + 1 - a_n` on all extensions, and `a_n` satisfies the Newton recursion
`a_{n+1} = a₁a_n - q a_{n-1}` that can be *derived* from moment identities over each
`F_{q^n}` rather than from the Frobenius eigenvalue picture.

**Why now?** `EllipticPointCount.lean` is stated for an arbitrary finite field, not just a
prime field, so the base-change tower is already expressible; and `hasse_F5 … hasse_F13`
show the bound holds exhaustively in the accessible range, so a counterexample search is
already closed off for small `q`.
title: C2. Hasse's bound follows from the moments plus twist symmetry

description:
**Conjecture.** For every `Γ`-invariant `g ∈ C(K, ℝ)` and `ε > 0`, there is a `Γ`-invariant
element of `attentionAlgebra` that `ε`-approximates `g` and is a sum of at most
`poly(dim, 1/ε)` products of readouts — in particular independent of `|Γ| = n!`, which is what
the averaging proof of `group_uniform_universal` currently spends.

*The key insight is* that averaging over `Γ` is a *projection*, not a construction: the invariant
subalgebra is already generated by the multisymmetric power sums `x ↦ ∑_i ∏_a (x_i a)^{e_a}`,
each of which is a **single** product of readouts, so the group sum can be eliminated in favour
of a generating set of size polynomial in the feature dimension and the degree.

*Why now?* The stability lemma `attentionAlgebra_compPerm_mem` plus the sharp barrier give both
halves needed to measure such a bound: any candidate generating set can be tested against the
`1/2` barrier of `symmetry_barrier_position_read`, so the conjecture is falsifiable by an
explicit finite computation at small `|ι|`.
title: C1. Head-count law: the symmetric approximant needs only orbit-many heads, not `|Γ|`-many

description:
**Conjecture.**  For `n ≥ 1`, rule 110 has a configuration of minimal period `> 1` on
`ZMod n` if and only if `4 ∣ n`.  The "if" direction is proved
(`rule110_exists_minimalPeriod_two`); the "only if" direction is verified for
`n ≤ 8` computationally.

*The key insight is* that the smallest rule-110 glider has spatial period `4`, so all
short orbits should be pullbacks along `ZMod n → ZMod 4`, and the conjecture says that
the entire short-orbit structure of the universal rule on a torus is generated by a
single four-cell pattern.

*Why now?*  The simulation-embedding theorem `minimalPeriod_pull` gives one direction
for free, and it also says what a proof of the converse must produce: a retraction of
the periodic part of the dynamics onto the four-site lattice.
title: C3. Rule 110 has a non-fixed periodic configuration exactly when `4 ∣ n`

description:
**Statement.** The map sending a linear representation `(λ, μ, γ)` to the series
`w ↦ λ μ(w) γ` induces a bijection between the finite-dimensional comodule
structures on `K⟨X⟩` (for `Δ_conc`) and the space of representative functions,
and it is an algebra isomorphism for both the Hadamard and the shuffle products.

*The key insight is* that `representative_tfae` already identifies "finite
dimensional space of left translates" with "has a linear representation"; adding
the shuffle multiplicativity `isRepresentative_shuffleSeries` upgrades this
bijection from a linear isomorphism to a bialgebra isomorphism — the Sweedler
dual statement of the paper.

*Why now?* Both halves (Kleene–Schützenberger and shuffle closure) are now
formalized and sorry-free; only the naturality of the correspondence remains.
title: C5. Sweedler duality is an isomorphism onto the representative functions

description:
**Conjecture.** The optimal constant in `ρ_k ≤ C·r^k` is
`r = exp(−D(θ‖½))` with `θ = log 2 / log 3` and
`D(θ‖½) = θ log 2θ + (1−θ) log 2(1−θ) ≈ 0.0347`, i.e. `r ≈ 0.9659`; moreover
`ρ_k ≍ k^{-1/2} r^k`.

**The key insight is** that the Chernoff step proved here used the *convenient*
tilt `x = 2`, chosen because it keeps every inequality inside `ℕ` (the rate then
comes out as `(243/256)^{1/5} ≈ 0.98963`); the *optimal* tilt is
`x* = θ/(1−θ) ≈ 1.71`, and it can only be exploited once real exponents
(`Real.rpow`) are allowed into the argument.

**Why now?** The exact generating function `∑_{n<2^k} x^{s_k(n)} = (1+x)^k` is
already a theorem for every `x` in every commutative semiring, in particular for
real `x`; only the optimisation `min_x (1+x)/x^θ` remains, which is a
one-variable calculus problem well inside Mathlib's reach.

---
title: C1′. The sharp large-deviation rate

description:
**Conjecture.**  For fixed `N`, the set of theories `{valSys V N : V}` ordered by
inclusion is a complete lattice, with the meet of `valSys V N` and `valSys V' N` given
by the pointwise disjunction of the valuations restricted to the worlds where they
agree, and with the chain of §2's rigidity as its skeleton.  Moreover the depth-graded
reflection conditions are *not* monotone along this order: there are `V, V'` with
`valSys V' N ⊆ valSys V N` and strictly larger reflection depth on the smaller theory.

**The key insight is** that inclusion between valuated theories was reduced this cycle
to a *pointwise* condition on the valuations (`spectrumSys_inclusion_iff`: agreement at
every world of the smaller model), and pointwise conditions on `Bool`-valued functions
are exactly what produces lattice structure — whereas reflection depth is a
*non-local* functional of the valuation, hence has no reason to be monotone.

**Why now?**  The inclusion criterion is proved for the one-parameter block family; the
general statement is the same argument with `blockVal w` replaced by an arbitrary `V`,
using `satV_blockVal_congr` in its general form.

*Falsified by* two valuated theories with no greatest lower bound in the family, or by
a proof that reflection depth is monotone.
title: The inclusion order of valuated theories is a lattice

description:
> **Conjecture.** Define the *arity* of a cost profile `f` as the least `k` such
> that `f x ≤ k · exp(c · x^{1/k})` for some `c > 0` and all large `x`. Then the
> arity classes are strictly nested: for every `k` there is a cost profile of
> arity `k+1` that is not `O` of any arity-`k` profile, and a profile is
> polynomially bounded iff it has no finite arity.

*The key insight is* that the AM–GM proof of `tradeoff_lower_bound` shows the
exponent `1/k` is not a design parameter of any algorithm but the balance point
of a multiplicative constraint — so "improving the exponent" is literally the
same problem as "adding a stage", and polynomial time is the `k → ∞` limit.

*Why now?* `tradeoff_lower_bound`, `tradeoff_attained` and
`tradeoff_unbounded_arity_is_poly` are proved, so both endpoints of the ladder
are formalised; only the strictness of the intermediate steps is open, and it
reduces to a `Superpoly`-style limit computation of the kind already automated
in `AsymptoticLadder.lean`.

**Falsifier.** Exhibit `c, c'` and `k` with
`(k+1)·exp(c·x^{1/(k+1)}) = O(k·exp(c'·x^{1/k}))`; this would collapse the
ladder and invalidate the classification's non-degeneracy.

---
title: C1. The trade-off arity conjecture (`AritySeparation`)

description:
**Conjecture.** Let `n = m·r` and let `v : Fin n → ℂ` be nonzero with
`#supp v · #supp (DFT v) = n` (equality in `dft_support_uncertainty`). Then
`supp v` is a coset of a subgroup of `ℤ/n` and `v` is constant in modulus on its
support; i.e. `v` is a phase-modulated comb. Consequently the state Shor's
circuit prepares is, up to phases and translation, the *only* extremal input.

**The key insight is** that the two inequalities used in the Donoho–Stark proof
(triangle inequality for `DFT`, and again for the inverse) are simultaneously
tight exactly when all contributing phases align, which forces the support to be
an arithmetic progression closed under translation — a subgroup coset.

**Why now?** `dft_support_uncertainty` and `comb_saturates_uncertainty` are
already formalised in `Catalog/Computation/QuantumClassicalBoundary/Boundary.lean`;
the equality analysis is a finite-dimensional rigidity argument that needs no new
analytic input. A counterexample would be equally interesting: it would exhibit a
non-comb state as sharp as the comb.

---
title: C1. Uncertainty-extremality characterises the Shor input state

description:
The sterility theorem closes the greatest-common-divisor channel for multiplicative walks. Whether
*any* efficiently samplable classical stochastic process on `Z/N` can have provably useful randomness
beyond the birthday floor of its orbit remains open; all known candidates reduce either to smoothness
(subexponential, governed by the Dickman–de Bruijn density) or to order finding (currently quantum).
title: C4. Beyond gcd channels for random walks

description:
Formally: for every `M ≥ 1` there are primes `p ≡ q (mod M)`, both `≡ 1 (mod 3)`,
with `2` a cube mod `p` and not mod `q`.  We proved this for every `M ∣ 720720`;
the general case is stated but not settled.

**The key insight is** that `2` is a cube mod `p` exactly when `p = x² + 27y²`,
a *splitting* condition in the non-abelian field `ℚ(∛2, ω)`, and a congruence
condition would force the splitting set of a degree-3 non-normal field to be a
union of ray classes — contradicting the non-abelian Galois group `S₃`.

**Why now?** Mathlib now has Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic
progressions and a usable class-field-theoretic vocabulary; the remaining gap is
a Chebotarev-free argument: it suffices to exhibit, for each `M`, a *pair* of
primes in one class with different splitting behaviour, and the `x² + 27y²`
parametrisation makes such pairs constructible rather than merely dense.
title: Conjecture A (unbounded escape). *For every modulus `M`, cubic residuacity of `2` is not `M`-periodic on primes.

description:
**Conjecture.**  For every `n ≥ 2`, every integral point `P = (x, y)` of `E_N` with
`ψ_n(x, y) ≠ 0`, and every prime `ℓ ≥ 5` with `ℓ ∤ N`:
`ℓ ∣ den x(nP) ↔ ℓ ∣ ψ_n(x, y)`, where `ψ_n` is the `n`-th division polynomial of
`y² = x³ + N`; moreover the exceptional evaluation of the numerator `φ_n` on the locus
`ψ_n = 0` is always of the form `c_n · N^{k}` with `c_n` composed of the primes `2` and `3`
only.

*The key insight is* that the two evaluations computed here at layer 3, `φ₃ ≡ 64N³` on
`x ≡ 0` and `φ₃ ≡ -1728N³` on `x³ ≡ -4N`, are the discriminant/`j`-invariant constants
`2⁶` and `2⁶3³` of the Mordell family — the same constants that force the hypothesis `ℓ ≥ 5`,
and they should recur at every layer because `φ_n` and `ψ_n²` are coprime up to the
discriminant.

*Why now?*  Layers 2 and 3 are proved in this catalog from Mathlib's affine group law with no
extra theory, and Mathlib now carries enough of the `WeierstrassCurve` API that `ψ_n` can be
introduced by the standard recursion; the induction step is the addition formula already used
here for `2P + P`.

**Falsifiable form.**  Compute `ψ₄, φ₄` for `y² = x³ + N` and check whether the exceptional
value of `φ₄` on `ψ₄ = 0` involves a prime `≥ 5`.

---
title: C1. The division-polynomial tower (layer `n`)

description:
**Conjecture.** For every bound `B` there are semiprimes `N = pq` and `N' = p'q'` with
`p, q, p', q' > B` such that the sets of primes `ℓ ≤ B` appearing in the first `B` denominators
of some orbit coincide; more strongly, the whole "denominator support function" mod `B!` depends
only on `N mod B!`.

*The key insight is* that the local law at a good prime `ℓ` depends only on `N mod ℓ`, so any
finite amount of denominator data is a function of a residue of `N`, which by Dirichlet is shared
by semiprimes with arbitrarily large factors.

*Why now?* Cycle 6 shows every good prime appears, so the *support* is essentially all primes;
the only remaining information is the apparition indices, and these are now known to be bounded
functions of `N mod ℓ` — making the barrier statement fully quantitative and provable.
title: C4. The denominator support does not determine the factorisation of `N` — quantitatively

description:
**Conjecture.** Fix `B`. There is `L = L(B)` such that if `N ≡ N′ (mod L)` and the chosen points
have the same reduction data at all primes `ℓ ≤ B`, then the sets of primes `ℓ ≤ B` occurring in
the first `B` denominators of the two orbits coincide.

*The key insight is* that the whole apparition computation at `ℓ` takes place in `E(F_ℓ)`, which
depends on `N` only through `N mod ℓ`, so the joint behaviour below `B` depends on `N` only
through `N mod ∏_{ℓ ≤ B} ℓ`.

*Why now?* Cycle 9 shows the support is *all* good primes, so the remaining information is the
finite set of indices; those are exactly what the mod-`L` reduction controls, which turns the
"barrier" heuristic into a finite, checkable statement.
title: D3. The denominator support is a function of `N mod L` for a computable `L`

description:
Let `N` be odd and squarefree, `P` an integral point of `E_N`, and `n ≥ 1` with
`gcd(n, N) = 1`.  Then `gcd(den x(nP), N) = 1`; conversely, for each prime `p ∣ N` there are
points `P` for which `p ∣ den x(pP)`.

*The key insight is* that at a bad prime `p ∣ N` the reduced curve `y² = x³` has cuspidal
non-singular locus `E_ns(𝔽_p) ≅ (𝔽_p, +)`, on which multiplication by `n` is injective exactly
when `p ∤ n`; the case `n = 2^k` proved this cycle
(`integral_point_orbit_no_factor`) is the special case where injectivity is automatic for odd `p`.

*Why now?*  The whole proof reduces to one formal statement — that `t = x/y` is additive modulo
`p` on the cuspidal locus — and the coprime parametrisation `x = a/e², y = b/e³` already in the
catalog turns that into a polynomial congruence identity, which is within reach of `linear_combination`.
The observed `n = 5` appearance of the bad prime `5` on `E_55` (see `ComputationalEvidence.md`)
is exactly the predicted converse.
title: Conjecture C1 (the `n`-coprime anti-factoring law)

description:
**Conjecture.** For every `n ≥ 2` the residual entropy of the cycle type given the sign is
`H(T | sign) = H(T) - 1`, and `H(T)` equals the entropy of the partition distribution
`p(λ) = 1 / z_λ` with `z_λ = ∏ i^{m_i} m_i!`; consequently
`H(T) = log₂ n! - (1/n!) ∑_{λ ⊢ n} (n!/z_λ) log₂ (n!/z_λ)` and
`H(T) - 1 → ∞` at rate `Θ(log n)`.

*The key insight is* that `1/z_λ` is a probability distribution on partitions independent of the
sign conditioning, so the entire non-abelian residual is the entropy of the Cauchy/Ewens measure at
parameter `1`.

*Why now?* `mutInfo_cycleType_sign_eq_one` already gives `H(T | sign) = H(T) - 1` for all `n`
(`condEnt_eq_uEnt_sub_one`); what remains is the closed form of `H(T)` itself, for which Mathlib
has `Equiv.Perm.card_cycleType_eq` style counting available.
title: C2. The exact residual for `Sₙ`: `H(T) - 1` in closed form

description:
**Conjecture.** For appreciably normalized finite states, equality of all standard-part Born probabilities defines an equivalence relation compatible with relabelling and with tensoring by an appreciably normalized ancillary state. The quotient admits a canonical map to the simplex of real probability distributions.

The key insight is that infinitesimal perturbations of amplitudes can change exact hyperreal weights without changing any observed probability, suggesting that observation is naturally a quotient rather than an injective representation.

**Why now?** The equal-amplitude and infinitesimal-amplitude results isolate both sides of this equivalence: ket labels alone do not alter probabilities, whereas infinitesimal changes can disappear under observation.
title: Observational equivalence as a quotient of non-Archimedean state space

description:
Fix a sound, computably axiomatized theory capable of elementary arithmetic and a prefix-free universal description language. Conjecture that no computable function uniformly bounds the shortest-proof complexity of all theorems of statement length at most `n`.

The key insight is that the finite counting argument should become a Chaitin-style diagonal obstruction once statement syntax, soundness, and prefix-free descriptions are coupled.

Why now? The finite ensemble theorem isolates the exact scarcity axiom required for incompressibility, while the unbounded-cost theorem identifies the remaining task: prove unboundedness relative to a concrete proof system and then strengthen it to domination.
title: Computable-bound escape for shortest proofs

description:
There exists a family of finite proof systems for which reversible verification using subexponential auxiliary space necessarily incurs superlinear recomputation time, while irreversible linear-time verification destroys a linear number of transcript bits.

The key insight is that preserving a verifier transcript avoids erasure but forces a pebbling tradeoff between retained checkpoints and recomputation. **Why now?** The adversarial coverage theorem isolates the information that a verifier must distinguish; adding reversible pebble games can turn this static obstruction into a time-space-energy tradeoff.
title: Bennett tradeoff for theorem verification

description:
Assign weights to verified implications among automorphic, Galois, and arithmetic-geometric
objects, and define susceptibility as the expected increase in the largest coherent component
after one additional verified compatibility.  Conjecture that a canonical normalization
produces a unique susceptibility maximum, stable under zero-reflecting deformations of the
component-density observable.

**The key insight is...** a scientifically meaningful threshold should be recoverable from a
peak response in the connection data and should not move when the reporting scale changes.

**Why now?** The exact deformation-invariance theorem isolates observable choice as a
non-source of boundary movement, so empirical threshold variation can be attributed to graph
construction or weighting instead.
title: Susceptibility-derived cyclotomic thresholds

description:
For all `ℤ`-modules `X`, `Y` and all `n : ℕ`, `Extⁿ⁺²(X, Y) = 0`.

*Status.* Now proved in three cases. (i) `Extⁿ⁺²(X, ℤ) = 0` for all `X` (`ext_int_eq_zero`;
injective dimension of `ℤ` is `≤ 1`, and the bundled `intInjectiveResolution` gives `Rⁿ⁺²F(ℤ) = 0`
for every additive `F`). (ii) `Extⁿ⁺²(ℤ/k, Y) = 0` for all `Y` (`ext_zmod_eq_zero`). (iii) More
generally `Extⁿ⁺²(X, Y) = 0` for every **finitely generated** `X` and every `Y`
(`ext_fg_eq_zero`), obtained from the free presentation `0 → ker f → ℤᵐ → X → 0` whose kernel is
again free (`free_ker_of_fin`) via the abstract criterion
`ext_eq_zero_of_projective_presentation`. The remaining case is `X` of infinite rank; it needs the
statement — not currently in Mathlib — that *every* submodule of a free `ℤ`-module is free.
Falsified by a single pair `X`, `Y` with `Ext²(X, Y) ≠ 0`.
title: C2. Hereditarity of `ℤ`: all `Extⁿ` vanish for `n ≥ 2`

description:
**Statement.**  There is a computable function `ρ(M, δ)` such that: given a tensor `a` over
`ℚ(i)` with entries of modulus `≤ M` and `‖hyperdet a‖ ≥ δ`, every tensor within `ρ(M, δ)` of `a`
is GHZ-equivalent, *and* an explicit invertible triple `(A, B, C)` realizing the equivalence can
be computed with coefficients bounded by an explicit function of `M` and `δ`.

**The key insight is** that `slocc_ghz_of_close` already supplies `ρ(M, δ) = δ / (128 M³)`; what
remains is to track the size of the matrices produced by the normal-form pipeline
(`exists_diagonalizing_A`, `exists_rank_one_factor`), each step of which is a single division by a
quantity bounded below in terms of `δ`.

**Why now?**  The stability radius is the missing analytic ingredient for turning the
classification into a *numerically robust* algorithm; with `hyperdet_lipschitz` in hand the rest
is bookkeeping on the constructive proofs already formalized.
title: C2. An effective decision procedure with certified radius

description:
**Conjecture.** For the splitting field of a quintic with `Gal = A₅` and *any*
modulus `m`, *every* splitting fork satisfies `I(p mod m ; F) = 0`, i.e. the
factorisation type of `p` is statistically independent of every congruence class.

*The key insight is* that `A₅` is perfect, so the only abelian data attached to
`Frob` is trivial — already proved here as `A5_absolutely_unpinnable`; what
remains is to convert "no abelian character sees it" into "zero mutual
information", i.e. equidistribution of Frobenius within each ray class.
*Why now?* `A5_fork_factors_iff_constant` shows the group side is closed; the
analytic side is exactly Chebotarev for the compositum with `ℚ(ζ_m)`.
title: C3. `A₅` gives an unconditional information wall

description:
**Statement.** Fix `N = 55` and `P = (9,28)`. For every prime `ℓ ∉ {2,3,5,11}` there is `k ≥ 1`
with `ℓ ∣ den x(kP)`, and the apparition index `m(ℓ)` of `den_apparition_index` equals the order
of the reduction `P̄` in the finite group `E_55(𝔽_ℓ)`; in particular `m(ℓ) ∣ #E_55(𝔽_ℓ)` and
`m(ℓ) ≤ ℓ + 1 + 2√ℓ`.

**The key insight is** that `ℓ ∣ den x(kP)` says exactly that `kP` reduces to the point at
infinity mod `ℓ`, so the index produced abstractly by the subgroup argument must coincide with
the order of the reduced point — turning an existence statement into a computable quantity
bounded by Hasse.

**Why now?** The index `m(ℓ)` now exists as a theorem rather than a heuristic, and two of its
values are pinned down (`m(7) = 2`, `m(13) = 3`); identifying it with the order of `P̄` is the
single missing bridge between the elementary denominator theory here and reduction mod `ℓ`.
title: C2. Every good prime appears in the orbit of one non-torsion point

description:
**Conjecture.** Let an ordered non-Archimedean real-closed field carry a standard-part map on its finite elements, and let its quadratic extension play the role of complex scalars. Every self-adjoint matrix whose entries and eigenvalues are finite admits an orthogonal spectral decomposition, and taking standard parts intertwines this decomposition with the ordinary real or complex spectral decomposition whenever distinct eigenvalue clusters remain appreciably separated.

The key insight is that appreciable spectral gaps should prevent infinitesimal perturbations from merging eigenspaces under standard part.

**Why now?** Finite Born normalization and infinitesimal branch collapse isolate exactly the algebraic and boundedness hypotheses needed to test this claim first for two-by-two matrices, before introducing infinite-dimensional completeness.
title: Finite-dimensional non-Archimedean spectral calculus

description:
**Conjecture.** Under a pairwise log-linear likelihood model for voting histories, the posterior over role assignments is an Ising model conditioned on fixed total wolf number; Bayesian role complementation acts as spin flip, while vote correlations become couplings whose sign predicts coalition polarization.

The key insight is that the centered one-player posterior already transforms exactly as an Ising spin, and pairwise log likelihoods naturally become quadratic spin interactions. **Why now?** The one-site symmetry bridge is established, so the next falsifiable step is to derive and test the full constrained Gibbs representation.
title: Spin-system representation of correlated suspicion

description:
**Conjecture.** In a precisely specified choiceless set theory with dependent choice and a strong regularity principle, universal Lebesgue measurability is equivalent to a determinacy-style statement for a definable class of infinite games, but it is independent of the bare negation of Choice.

The key insight is that measurability arises from regularity or determinacy structure, not from the logical negation of a selection principle by itself. The correct bridge should therefore factor through games rather than proceed directly from anti-Choice.

**Why now?** Separating relation-level anti-axioms from extra semantic structure prevents the common invalid inference from “Choice fails” to “every set is measurable” and gives a falsifiable route to a guarded replacement.
title: Choice failure versus universal measurability under explicit regularity hypotheses

description:
For uniformly sampled true statements of length `n` in a decidable finite theory, conjecture that shortest-description cost has linear mean growth, while exhaustive proof-search work can have exponential mean growth for natural proof enumerations.

The key insight is that description length and search time obey different counting laws: incompressibility makes a constant fraction of objects require nearly `n` bits, whereas locating those descriptions may require exploring exponentially many candidates.

Why now? The present bounds rule out exponential mean growth from a cost functional linear in description complexity under the uniform binary model, sharply locating exponential behavior in search dynamics or sampling bias instead.
title: Linear mean cost versus exponential proof-search cost

description:
**Conjecture.** For each fixed dimension `k` in a calibrated sparse temporal hypergraph model, the expected Betti number has a piecewise-polynomial scaling law whose exponent is strictly below `k + 1` outside a narrow critical window.

The key insight is that the universal binomial chain ceiling permits polynomial growth only as an upper bound, while boundary ranks and face dependencies determine the smaller effective exponent.

Why now? The dimension-uniform power law is obstructed by finite-dimensional vanishing, focusing attention on fixed-dimensional regimes where asymptotic scaling is mathematically coherent.
title: Fixed-dimensional Betti scaling

description:
**Conjecture.** For an electorate of size `n`, every anonymous normalized tropical aggregator whose irredundant support has size `k` must violate strong coalition independence on at least a proportion `1 - 1 / binomial(n,k)` of the orbit of its minimal dependence set; this bound is sharp for the minimum over all `k`-subsets averaged in tropical projective space.

The key insight is that anonymity spreads any minimal decisive support across its full permutation orbit, whereas an ultrafilter can select only one principal generator.

**Why now?** The qualitative incompatibility between anonymity and singleton dictatorship suggests a measurable defect theory, and finite permutation orbits provide an explicit arena in which sharp bounds can be sought.
title: Quantitative anonymity–independence tradeoff

description:
**Conjecture.** Let `𝒢` be a proper minor-closed graph class and let `F` be a fixed connected graph with a cut vertex lying on two cycles. If the `F`-free spectral extremizers in `𝒢` have unbounded order, then after deleting a bounded dominating set their component types converge to a finite periodic family under path concatenation.

The key insight is that separator structure in minor-closed classes should interact with Perron-vector localization to reduce global optimization to a finite-state transfer problem along bounded-width pieces.

**Why now?** Intersecting-cycle exclusions provide the simplest nontrivial test case where separator topology, spectral concentration, and finite-state path structure all appear simultaneously.
title: A minor-closed spectral compactness principle
Alternative topologies

description:
**Conjecture.** There is a deterministic family of auxiliary arithmetic objects attached to a composite integer `n` for which a polynomial number of exact local-factor queries yields, through an explicitly checkable decoder, a proper divisor of `n`.

The key insight is that an evaluator contributes to factoring only when a proved decoder converts its outputs into divisibility certificates; evaluation speed alone has no arithmetic content.

**Why now?** The reduction framework identifies the exact target: construct the query family and prove the decoder certificate, rather than assuming that an elliptic curve over a non-field automatically reveals a factor.
title: Certified factor extraction from bad local Euler data

description:
**Conjecture.** Let each tropical hash component have a set of active minimizing coordinates at a message. The fiber contains a coordinate cone of dimension at least `d` if and only if the union of these active sets admits a transversal whose complement has cardinality at least `d`.

The key insight is that collision directions are governed not merely by the number of outputs, but by the combinatorics of which coordinates can certify their minima. **Why now?** Selecting one minimizer per component proved one escaping direction; replacing this selection by a system-of-distinct-representatives analysis should expose the full local fiber geometry.
title: Hall-type criterion for multidirectional collision cones

description:
**Conjecture.** For a graph with `n` vertices and fixed `k`, the standard monotone elimination operator on robber–cop configurations stabilizes in at most `n^(k+1)` changing rounds, and every rejected configuration admits a replayable certificate of depth at most that bound.

The key insight is that the abstract cardinality bound becomes an explicit complexity theorem once configurations are encoded as one robber position and `k` cop positions; the deletion history should simultaneously serve as a correctness certificate.

**Why now?** A representation-independent round bound is available, so the remaining issue is a faithful configuration encoding and a proof that the paper's local update is contracting and monotone.
title: Polynomial certificate bound for explicit k-cop state spaces

description:
**Conjecture.** For each finite level, arithmetic augmented by a truth predicate for the previous level has exactly the same computable sets as the corresponding finite Turing-jump iterate, under a uniform translation preserving provability of arithmetical sentences.

The key insight is to compare theories through representability and effective interpretation rather than identifying deductive strength with reducibility by analogy.

**Why now?** The computational hierarchy is structurally complete, and the present critique identifies the missing bridge precisely: a syntax-and-semantics interpretation theorem linking oracle answers to arithmetical proofs.
title: Oracle theories and Turing jumps coincide under an explicit interpretation

description:
**Conjecture.** Among corpora on `n` theorems whose documents have size at most `d`, the maximum possible `k`-th Betti number is attained by a highly symmetric design and has order `n^(k+1)` only for fixed `k < d`, with constants depending essentially on both `d` and the coefficient field.

The key insight is that polynomial growth can be plausible in fixed dimension even though it is impossible uniformly across dimensions; document-size bounds determine which chain groups can exist at all.

**Why now?** The binomial ceiling supplies the correct ambient scale, while dimension vanishing rules out overgeneralization. The remaining extremal problem is concrete, finite, and testable on designs, multipartite constructions, and random bounded hypergraphs.
title: Extremal Betti profiles under document-size constraints

description:
**Conjecture.** Under any computably samplable sequence of full-support distributions on arithmetic sentences whose lengths tend to infinity, no computable predictor is uniformly 95-percent accurate unless the distributions concentrate on a computably decidable semantic fragment.

The key insight is that meaningful average-case accuracy depends jointly on semantic hardness and on how probability mass moves through increasingly expressive fragments.

**Why now?** Pointwise exactness on finite domains has ruled out bare fixed-length impossibility, leaving distributional uniformity as the natural testable replacement.
title: Distribution-sensitive limits for bounded truth prediction

description:
**Conjecture.** Let `F⁺(N)` and `F⁻(N)` count fundamental discriminants in `(0, N]` and
`[-N, 0)` respectively. Then both `F⁺(N)/N` and `F⁻(N)/N` converge to `6/π²`, and the exact
value at `N = 1000` (`303` and `305`) already sits within the expected error band.

*The key insight is* that fundamental discriminants are governed by a squarefree sieve on a
fixed union of residue classes modulo `16`, so their density is the squarefree density `6/π²`
distributed evenly across the admissible classes.

*Why now?* The predicate is now decidable and its finite counts are certified, so the density
claim can be tested against exact data at successively larger bounds and then attacked with a
squarefree-density argument rather than assumed.
title: The counting function is asymptotically `6/π² · N` per sign

description:
**Conjecture.** For every `c ∈ ℝ`,
`Prob ((log n + c)/n) {s | (graphOf s).Connected} → exp(-exp(-c))`.

Falsifiable: a proof must in particular reproduce the value `e^{-1} ≈ 0.3679` at
`c = 0`, and any numerical simulation deviating from `e^{-e^{-c}}` refutes it.
The missing ingredient is a Poisson limit theorem (method of moments or Stein–Chen)
for the isolated-vertex count `I_n`, whose factorial moments in the present model are
exactly computable by the same block-avoidance technique as `expect_avoidCount_sq`:
`E[(I_n)_r] = n(n-1)⋯(n-r+1)·(1-p)^{r(n-1) - C(r,2)}`.  The case `r = 2` is now proved
(`expect_isolated_count_factorial_two`:
`E[I_n(I_n-1)] = n(n-1)(1-p)^{2n-3}`), so the remaining milestone is:

> **C1'.** The `r`-th factorial moment formula above for all `r`, whose combinatorial
> core is `|star(v_1) ∪ ⋯ ∪ star(v_r)| = r(n-1) - C(r,2)` for distinct vertices — a
> direct generalisation of `card_incident_union`.
title: C1. Poisson window at `p = (log n + c)/n`

description:
**Conjecture.** Direction A of the previous cycles (a *single* family escaping *every*
computable bound) is **false** in the following sharp sense: for every family
`c : ℕ → Code` of `haltVerifier`-provable statements with *decidable* range and computable
inverse on that range, the function `s ↦ proofCost s` restricted to the range is computable,
so the computable bound `B := proofCost ∘ c ∘ index` dominates on the whole family.
Consequently escape (`escape_set_infinite`) is optimal: uniform domination can only be
recovered by allowing the escaping family to depend on the candidate bound, or by dropping
decidability of the range.

*The key insight is that* `proofCost` is *semi*-computable — unbounded search terminates on
provable statements — so non-computability lives entirely in deciding provability, not in
measuring it; a family whose members are known to be provable therefore carries no
Chaitin-style obstruction, and the diagonal must be relocated to the membership test.

*Why now?* `ShortestProofEscape` already contains the collapse `Provable s ↔ V s (B s)` for
cumulative verifiers and the finite-exception absorption, which is exactly the machinery a
refutation needs; and stating the conjecture as a refutation makes the previously open
direction A decidable in one cycle instead of open indefinitely.
title: A″. Shortest-proof cost of a computably enumerated theorem family is computable — hence domination fails
