**Conjecture.** For a model `p` in `attentionAlgebra ι κ`, the subgroup
`{σ : p ∘ permAct σ = p}` is determined by the values of `p` on the orbit of a single generic
sequence, and equals the stabilizer of the positional encoding in the sense of
`PositionalSymmetry.posStab`.

*The key insight is* that `orbit_barrier_lower` converts symmetry detection into an
approximation-error measurement: a non-symmetry of `p` shows up as a nonzero orbit oscillation,
which is exactly the quantity the sharp barrier measures.

*Why now?* The barrier is now known to be an equality, not just an inequality, so orbit
oscillation is a *complete* invariant rather than a one-sided test.
title: C3. Symmetry-group determination: the invariance group of a trained architecture is

description:
**Conjecture.** `group_uniform_universal` remains true when the finite group `Γ` is replaced by a
compact group acting continuously on the position space (e.g. rotations of a circular position
encoding), with Haar averaging in place of the finite sum, and the barrier becomes half the
oscillation over the (now compact) orbit.

*The key insight is* that the only property of `Γ` used in the proof is that averaging is a
bounded projection onto the invariants that preserves the subalgebra — a property Haar measure
supplies for compact groups.

*Why now?* The proof of `symmetrize_error` isolates exactly this projection property, so
replacing `∑_{g ∈ Γ} / |Γ|` by `∫ dμ` is a localized change; a counterexample would have to come
from failure of subalgebra stability, which is testable on the rotation group of a 4-token ring.
title: C5. Beyond finite groups: compact symmetry groups and continuous positional encodings

description:
changing the rational locus

**Statement.** For a parameter `q : K`, define the `q`-shuffle on words by the
recursion `au ⧢_q bv = a(u ⧢_q bv) + b(au ⧢_q v) + q · [a=b] · ⟨ab⟩(u ⧢_q v)`.
Conjecture: for every `q`, `(K⟨X⟩, ⧢_q)` is associative and commutative, and
the set of representative functions is closed under `⧢_q` for every `q`, i.e.
the rational locus is a *deformation invariant*.

*The key insight is* that the proof of `isRepresentative_shuffleSeries` uses
only the bialgebra axiom `unsh_append` for the dual coproduct, never the precise
combinatorics of the shuffle; so any deformation whose dual coproduct is still
multiplicative for concatenation must preserve rationality.

*Why now?* The proof in `ShuffleOfSeries.lean` is already written in exactly this
"axiom-only" style, so the deformed case should require only a new
`unsh_q_append` lemma and nothing else.

description:
**Conjecture.**  Every tropical linear space `V ⊆ T^E` on a finite ground set is
obtained from a finite family of tropical hyperplanes by *stable* intersection
followed by deletion; equivalently, the operations proved to preserve tropical
linear spaces in this cycle (`isTropicalLinearSpace_scaleSet`,
`isTropicalLinearSpace_deletion`) together with stable intersection generate the
whole class from hyperplanes.

*The key insight is* that the circuits of `V` (now available as a formal object,
with circuit elimination proved) each cut out a hyperplane containing `V`, and
the circuit elimination axiom is exactly the compatibility needed to reassemble
`V` from those hyperplanes.

*Why now?*  `circuit_elimination` and `exists_isCircuit_subset` supply the
combinatorial skeleton; what remains is a purely constructive reassembly step.
title: C2. Every tropical linear space is a hyperplane intersection minor

description:
**Conjecture.**  A subsemimodule `I` of the tropical polynomial semiring that
satisfies the degreewise elimination axiom and whose degree-`d` matroid is
uniform of corank one for all `d` is precisely the vanishing ideal of a single
point of `ℚ^σ`.

*The key insight is* that corank one in each degree pins down one linear
functional per degree, and the multiplicativity proved in
`vanishesAt_mul_left` forces those functionals to be compatible across degrees,
hence to come from a single evaluation.

*Why now?*  The forward direction is fully proved in this cycle
(`truncation_isCircuit_iff` plus `vanishingIdeal`), so only the converse — a
rigidity statement about compatible corank-one systems — remains.
title: C5. A Nullstellensatz for tropical ideals with elimination

description:
**Conjecture.** Let `S(N)` be any statistic of the form `∑_{(x,y) ∈ C(N)} w(x, y)` with
`w` a product of Jacobi-type characters and `C(N)` a conic mod `N`.  Then `S` is
multiplicative in the modulus, `|S(N)| = O(N^{1/2+o(1)})`, and `S(N)` is computable from
`N` alone in time `N^{1+o(1)}` but from `(p,q)` in time `polylog(N)` — so the
"free-witness" gap is exactly the Weil floor.

*The key insight is* that the CRT proof of `circleWeightZ_mul` never used the specific
weight: multiplicativity plus a per-prime Weil bound is automatic for any character
weight on any conic, which is why CIRC, BQF, GSP and JACSIGN all die the same death.

*Why now?* `circleWeightZ_mul` is proved for an arbitrary modulus and the per-prime bound
is proved by an elementary second moment; generalising both to arbitrary conics and
character products is a mechanical extension of the existing Lean development.
title: C5. No polynomial-time-computable circle statistic beats the floor

description:
**Conjecture.** `I_pair(n) ≤ H(T_n) − H(T_n | pair)` is not tight, but the sharper law
`I_pair(n) < log₂(number of divisors of n)` holds for all `n`, with the maximum of
`I_pair` over `n ≤ N` attained at the `n ≤ N` maximising `τ(n)` weighted by `2`-adic depth
(e.g. `n = 12` and `n = 24` dominate their neighbourhoods).

*Status:* consistent with all enumerated data (`n ≤ 40`); no proof.

**The key insight is** that the number of type states equals `τ(n)`, so the pair alphabet
has `τ(n)(τ(n)+1)/2` letters and the whole channel is a quotient of the divisor lattice of
`n` — the capacity should therefore be governed by lattice invariants, not by `n` itself.

**Why now?** `HT_divisor_formula` already expresses the marginal entropy purely in terms
of the divisor lattice; the same technique applied to the *pair* law reduces the
conjecture to an inequality between two divisor sums.
title: C4. Divisor-lattice control of the capacity

description:
For a prime `ℓ ≥ 5` with `ℓ ∤ N` and `m ≥ 1`, the set
`E_m(ℓ) = {O} ∪ {P : ℓ^{2m} ∣ den x(P)}` is a subgroup of `E_N(ℚ)`, and
`v(P + Q) ≥ min(v(P), v(Q))` for `v(P) = ½·v_ℓ(den x(P))`.  Consequently
`d(P, Q) = ℓ^{-v(P−Q)}` is an ultrametric on `E_N(ℚ)` making it a non-archimedean topological
group.

*The key insight is* that the intersection identity `x₁x₂x₃ = ν² − N` for the chord
`y = λx + ν` converts the subgroup property into a valuation computation on `ν`, avoiding the
full formal-group machinery: the level-1 case is already proved (`kernel_stable_add`) and the
level-`m` case is the same computation with `a₁ = a₂` cancellation tracked.

*Why now?*  It would give the first genuinely topological statement in this thread — an
ultrametric group structure on `E_N(ℚ)` built purely from denominators — and it upgrades every
"divides" statement in the catalog to a metric one.
title: Conjecture C2 (the filtration is a group filtration)

description:
**Conjecture.**  For any decoder given by a conditional probability model, the
arithmetic-coding residual lengths satisfy the hypotheses of `optCost_replicate_eq` up to
an additive `2` bits per message, so all the sharp results here transfer verbatim to real
LLM-as-decompressor pipelines with an `O(1)` per-message slack.

*The key insight is* that `CompressionDelta.SharedCodec` plus
`decodeStream_encodeStream` already isolate the only property the theory needs from a
decoder: exact round-tripping on a domain of at most `2^s` messages.

*Why now?*  It converts the abstract cost model into a falsifiable engineering claim
(measure `r`, `D`, and the coherence length `L` on a real corpus and check
`r + min(2D,L)/(2L)` against measured bits-per-message), while keeping the losslessness
gate formally verified.
title: C5. A losslessness-preserving compiler from probabilistic models to min-plus costs

description:
**Conjecture.** For every resource hierarchy closed under composition with a specified family of overhead functions, mutual simulations from that family induce an order isomorphism between the quotient hierarchies of language classes.

The key insight is that substrate independence should be governed by an algebra of admissible rescalings rather than by a single privileged cost measure.

**Why now?** Levelwise equality has been isolated as the exact case, so the next step is to replace equality by cofinal equivalence and determine the minimal closure axioms.
title: Universal hierarchy invariance under admissible resource rescaling

description: Formalize a clocked transition system whose reversible simulation retains a history tape. The computational phase should be represented by an injection and therefore incur zero logical loss in the finite model; only discarding the history should contribute. The main quantitative question is whether a polynomial-time machine admits a reversible transition system with polynomially bounded clock and history state.
title: Reversible simulation followed by a localized reset

description:
**Conjecture.** For a fixed base curve `E`, a positive proportion of the
sum-of-two-squares twists `E^d` with root number `-1` have analytic rank exactly `1`
(hence algebraic rank `1` by the theorem of Gross–Zagier–Kolyvagin).

*The key insight is* that the first moment of the derivative `L'(E^d, 1)` over the
sum-of-two-squares family is strictly positive while the second moment is bounded,
so a Cauchy–Schwarz argument forces a positive proportion of nonvanishing
derivatives — precisely the lower-derivative contribution omitted in earlier work.

*Why now?* The twist–standard-model isomorphism makes it possible to transport point
constructions on `(1+t²)y² = f(x)` directly to the Weierstrass model, giving explicit
candidate generators whose heights can be estimated against the derivative moments.
title: Positive proportion of rank exactly one

description:
Conjecture 5 of the inherited list, sharpened so that it is decidable by a
finite computation.  For the disjoint-loop generative model with restriction
scalars `a` and Gaussian noise of variance `σ²`, the minimiser of the weighted
coboundary residual `‖δf - g‖²` has expected held-out squared error strictly
below that of mean imputation **iff** `#{i : aᵢ = 1} > 0`, for every `σ > 0`.

*The key insight is* that `finrank_H1_disjointLoops` makes the stratification
variable — `dim H¹` — an explicit, exactly computable function of the generative
parameters rather than an estimated quantity, so the "preregistered parameter
regime" demanded by the original conjecture can be written down in closed form
instead of being searched for.

*Why now?*  With `dim H¹` available in closed form, the comparison reduces to
comparing two explicit quadratic forms, which is a finite algebraic
computation; no simulation is needed to settle it.


---
title: Conjecture E (Cohomological regularisation beats mean imputation exactly on the positive-`H¹` stratum)

description:
> **Conjecture.** `ClassifiedResourceHypothesis` is not provable in the abstract
> cost-profile model: there is a model of the `ClassicalAlgorithm` signature in
> which some algorithm is polynomially bounded and limited by no classified
> barrier, and another in which every algorithm is limited by one. Hence the
> capstone conditional is optimal — no strengthening to an unconditional lower
> bound is possible at this level of abstraction.

*The key insight is* that `schema_nonvacuous` already exhibits both a
classified-and-slow algorithm and a fast-and-unclassified one within the *same*
model; upgrading this to a genuine independence statement would prove that the
honest scope of the framework is forced, not a matter of taste.

*Why now?* The model is small (a cost function plus a lower bound on it), so
independence is a finite-combinatorial matter about `Filter.atTop` statements,
and both witnesses are already constructed and verified.

**Falsifier.** A proof of `ClassifiedResourceHypothesis` from the axioms of the
model — which, by `no_poly_under_CRH`, would immediately yield an unconditional
super-polynomial lower bound for classical factoring in this model and would
therefore be a major result in its own right.
title: C5. Classification completeness is independent (`CRHIndependence`)

description:
**Conjecture.** The constructions of this project extend verbatim from `dz²` on the torus to a
unit-area holomorphic quadratic differential on a closed surface of genus `g ≥ 2`: the extremal
map is affine in the flat structure of the differential, its dilatation defines the Teichmüller
metric, the associated stretch line is a unit-speed geodesic (the analogue of
`teichDist_stretchLine`), the mapping class group acts properly discontinuously with finite
stabilizers (the analogue of `finite_smul_dist_le`), the systole is continuous and its
superlevel sets are cocompact (the analogue of `mahler_compactness`), and the resulting space
has dimension `6g − 6`.

*The key insight is* that the torus computation never uses global uniformization: it uses only
that the extremal map is affine in the flat structure determined by a quadratic differential,
that the "denominator" quadratic form on the relevant lattice of periods is proper, and that the
systole is a `1`-Lipschitz-in-log function of the marked point — the three ingredients isolated
in `LinearQC.lean`, `ProperAction.lean` and `MahlerCompactness.lean`.
*Why now?* The genus-one case is closed end-to-end, including the three facts (properness,
attainment, compactness of the thick part) that in the classical literature are quoted from
Teichmüller's and Mahler's theorems; the higher-genus statement can therefore be attacked by
replacing "affine map of `ℂ` respecting a lattice" with "affine map of the flat structure of a
quadratic differential", keeping the whole algebra of `LinearQC.lean` unchanged.
title: E5. Higher genus: quadratic differentials, `6g−6`, and Mahler compactness

description:
**Conjecture.** The Lipschitz bound `entropy_lipschitz` is invertible on
`NoBulk` models: if two such models have entropy functions differing by at most
`ε` on every boundary region, their geometries differ by at most `Cε` in total
area, with an absolute constant `C` (conjecturally `C = 2`, from
`weight_eq_half_mutualInfo`).

*The key insight is* that reconstruction `w(u,v) = I(u:v)/2` is not merely
pointwise but Lipschitz, so entanglement data determines geometry *stably*,
which is what "spacetime emerges from entanglement" should mean physically.

*Why now?* The exact (`ε = 0`) case is now a theorem
(`spacetime_from_entanglement`), and one direction of the Lipschitz equivalence
is already available as `entropy_lipschitz`;
the converse is a finite computation with the same three entropies per edge, and
its failure for models with hidden cells is already visible in the star/triangle
example.
title: C5. Continuity forces geometry: an inverse stability theorem

description:
For any `M ∈ ℂ^{m×n}`,
`(Tr M Mᴴ)² − Tr((M Mᴴ)²) = 2 Σ_{i<j, k<l} |M_{ik}M_{jl} − M_{il}M_{jk}|²`.
**Conjecture:** this identity, once formalised, subsumes every quantitative
result of this cycle: the `2×2` case is `hopf_dot_identity`, the trace form is
`purity_eq`, and the right-hand side is the squared generalised concurrence of a
qudit pair.

*The key insight is* that the "Bloch gap" `pq − ⟨h(u),h(v)⟩` is nothing but the
Cauchy–Binet expansion of a `2×2` Gram determinant, so the whole geometric
picture is a shadow of exterior algebra.

*Why now?* We proved the `2×2` instance twice (algebraically and geometrically),
the reduced-density-matrix instance, and — in `QubitQudit.lagrange_complex` —
the full `2 × ι` instance for arbitrary finite `ι`. Only the `m × n` case with
both dimensions large remains, and it needs just `Finset` sums over pairs.

**Falsification test:** any single numerical instance where the two sides differ.
title: Conjecture C (Cauchy–Binet is the general Bloch-gap identity)

description:
**Conjecture.** There are integers `c₃, c₂` (depending only on `χ(-3)` and `χ(-1)`) with

`∑_{a,b ∈ F} a(a,b)⁴ = 2q⁵ - 3q⁴ + c₃ q³ + c₂ q²`.

**The key insight is** that the fourth moment reduces, exactly as the second moment did in
`sum_char_shift_pair`, to the `b`-sum `∑_b χ((b+u₁)(b+u₂)(b+u₃)(b+u₄))`, and that this sum
is *elementary* whenever the `uᵢ` collide in pairs — the genuinely quartic case is the only
Weil-type input, and it is governed by a single hyperelliptic curve of genus 1 whose own
count is again in the family.  So the fourth moment should be self-referential and
computable by the same collision bookkeeping as `collisions_formula`.

**Why now?** The second-moment proof in `EllipticSecondMoment.lean` already contains the
entire machinery (`sum_char_quadratic`, collision counts by inclusion–exclusion); only the
degree-4 shift sum is missing, and the numerical table for `q = 5, 7, 11, 13` can pin the
constants `c₃, c₂` before a line of Lean is written. A verified fourth moment would give
`#{(a,b) : |a| ≥ λ√q} = O(q²/λ⁴)`, a genuine improvement on
`card_large_frobTrace_le`.
title: C1. The fourth moment is exactly `2q⁵ - 3q⁴ + O(q³)` with an explicit closed form
Stronger algebraic-topological consequences

description:
**Conjecture.**  Replace the tropical `L¹` loss by the pinball loss
`Lτ(θ) = Σᵢ ρ_τ(θ − xᵢ)` with `ρ_τ(z) = max (τ z) ((τ − 1) z)` for `τ ∈ (0,1)`.  Then
the minimizer set is the closed interval of `τ`-quantiles of the sample, and the
associated clipped update reaches it in `⌈dist/η⌉` steps, with ReLU width `2` when the
quantile is unique and `4` when it is an interval.

*The key insight is* that all proofs in this cycle used only two facts about the loss:
a *block-counting* identity (`l1Loss_growth_right/left`) and the piecewise-linear
structure of the update; both survive verbatim with the block sizes weighted by `τ`
and `1 − τ`, which merely changes the growth slopes from `1` and `2` to `τ` and
`min τ (1−τ)`-type constants.

*Why now?*  The counting mechanism has been isolated into two reusable lemmas that
already take the split index `j` as a parameter, so the quantile case is a
re-instantiation rather than a new proof.

---
title: Quantile flows: the same theory for asymmetric tropical losses

description:
**Statement.** For every `m ≥ 4`, the number of *ordered* quadruples of positive indices
`(a, b, c, d)` with `antiFib a + antiFib b + antiFib c + antiFib d = m` equals `σ(2m - 7)`,
the sum of the divisors of `2m - 7`.

**The key insight is** the reduction proved this cycle: such quadruples correspond exactly
to representations of `8m - 28 ≡ 4 (mod 8)` by four *odd* squares, and Jacobi's four-square
theorem counts those: for `N ≡ 4 (mod 8)` the number of signed representations is
`16 σ(N/4)`, and the `2⁴` sign choices divide out, leaving `σ((8m-28)/4) = σ(2m-7)`.  The
formula therefore turns an additive-basis statement into an exact multiplicative identity,
and in particular re-proves `sum_four_iff` because `σ(2m-7) > 0`.

**Why now?** The reduction to four odd squares is already formalised
(`Catalog/Computation/AntiFibonacciLagrange.lean`, `four_odd_squares` and `sum_four_iff`),
so the only missing ingredient is Jacobi's four-square theorem, whose modern proof needs
just the Hurwitz quaternion order — a self-contained piece of algebra that Mathlib's
existing quaternion and Euclidean-domain API can support.

**Falsifiable:** the identity is checked in Lean for `4 ≤ m ≤ 13`
(`reprCount m = σ(2m-7)`, see the Evidence section of the same file); a single larger `m`
with `reprCount m ≠ σ(2m-7)` refutes it outright.
title: C7. A Jacobi formula for anti-Fibonacci representations

description:
Fix `s ≥ 3` and `L ≥ 2s+2`. Conjecture that there are constants `δ>0`, `n₀`, and `C` such that every `n`-vertex graph of circumference at most `L` with at least `(1-δ)N(C_{2s+1},H(n,L))` copies of `C_{2s+1}` differs from some copy of `H(n,L)` in at most `Cn` edge edits, for all `n ≥ n₀`.

The key insight is that near equality in the peripheral-to-core injection should force almost every long odd cycle to saturate the charging map, producing a common small core shared by most cycles.

Why now? The exact local equality conditions are visible in the charging proof and provide a concrete route from cycle counts to global structural stability.
title: Stability from near-maximal odd-cycle count

description:
**Conjecture.** Let `A` be a weight-graded dg-algebra which is `wt`-pure with `wt 1 = α > 0`.
Then for every `n ≥ 3` and every defining system for an `n`-fold Massey product of diagonal
cocycles `x_1, …, x_n`, the resulting representative is a coboundary; more precisely, every
entry `a_{i,j}` of a bihomogeneous defining system has weight excess
`w − deg = α · (j − i)`, and the final representative has excess `α (n − 2) > 0`.

*The key insight is* that the weight excess is an additive "defect counter": products add it and
each primitive raises it by exactly `α`, so the excess of a Massey representative counts the
number of primitives used and can never return to `0`.

*Why now?* The `n = 3` case is fully formalised (`massey_zero_of_weightPure`,
`massey_zero_of_pureFor`) and its proof is exactly this excess count; what remains is the
combinatorics of defining systems and Koszul signs, which is now the only missing ingredient.
Falsifiable: exhibit a pure weight-graded dg-algebra with a nonzero 4-fold Massey product.
title: C1. Higher Massey products are killed by purity, with an exact excess formula

description:
For the Gaussian curve define `V(p) = (#E(𝔽_p) mod ℓ)`.  Conjecture: the
`σ`-algebra generated by `{V(p)}` intersected with the `σ`-algebra of congruence
conditions on `p` is generated by the single condition `p mod 4ℓ`, i.e.
`cm_shadow_is_congruence` is sharp: for every `M` not divisible by `4ℓ` there are
inert primes `p ≡ q (mod M)` with `ℓ ∣ #E(𝔽_p)` and `ℓ ∤ #E(𝔽_q)`.  **The key
insight is** that on the inert half `#E = p + 1` exactly, so sharpness is a
statement about arithmetic progressions, not about elliptic curves.  **Why now?**
One direction is already a theorem; the converse needs only Dirichlet.
title: G (the `12`-periodic CM shadow is *exactly* the abelian part)

description:
The present state space is an abstract
   complete metric space. A next step is to build `evolve` from actual geodesic
   propagation on a compact Lorentzian manifold with closed timelike curves, and to
   identify explicit geometric conditions (curvature / focusing bounds along the
   loop) that make the round-trip map contracting.
title: Genuine pseudo-Riemannian geometry

description:
**Conjecture.** For semiprimes `N = pq` the pair `(W(N), A_ν(N))` is equidistributed on
the "Weil circle" `u² + v² ≤ 16N` in the sense that, for any fixed `ε > 0`, the map
`N ↦ W(N)/(4√N)` has limiting distribution the (Sato–Tate-type) pushforward of the
product of two arcsine laws — hence carries `O(1)` bits about `p` versus `q`.

*The key insight is* that `jacobsthal_identity` forces `W(p)` and its nonresidue twin to
trade off with `4p` conserved: any large signal in one leg is compensated in the other,
so a witness reading only one leg sees a conserved-quantity projection, never the split.

*Why now?* The identity is now a theorem, so the statement is unconditional in its
algebraic half; only the equidistribution half is open, and the `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)`
vanishing already proves a density-1/2 zero-information family.

---
title: C2. The two-leg trade-off is a hard obstruction to factor leakage

description:
**Conjecture.** Let `t ≥ 2`, `1 ≤ j < t`. Over the support of *ordered* odd pairs `p < q` mod `2^t`
the correlation of `p_j` with any statistic of the low block `N mod 2^t` is nonzero, but every such
correlation is bounded by `C · 2^{-t/2}`, and the entire defect is carried by the event
`p < q` — formally, the correlation equals `Cov(1[p<q], g(N)) · (something depending only on j)`
up to `O(2^{-t})`.

*The key insight is* that `lowblock_corr_zero` fails on the ordered support for exactly one reason:
the sign-reversing involution `p ↦ p XOR 2^j` used in `sum_bitSign_oddRes` does not preserve
`p < q`, so the defect must be a functional of the order statistic alone, i.e. a magnitude
statistic — the same family as the top-bit law.

*Why now?* The proof of the exact theorem isolates the involution as the single point of failure,
and the computations in `ComputationalEvidence.md` already show the defect shrinking as
`2/15, 2/31, 1/21` while the maximising parity migrates from `∅` to a *high* bit `{6}`.

---
title: C1. The ordering defect is exactly a top-bit statistic

description:
**Conjecture.** For `Gal = (ℤ/f)ˣ` non-cyclic (composite `f`), the splitting type
`T(p) = ord_f(p)` still gives `I(p mod f ; T) = H(T)` exactly, but the pair capacity is
*strictly smaller* than the cyclic value of the same order: `I_pair(G) < I_pair(C_{|G|})`
whenever `G` is abelian non-cyclic.

*Status:* untested here — the present development covers the cyclic case only.

**The key insight is** that in a non-cyclic group many elements share the same order, so
the type map has larger fibres and the pair channel loses the discriminating power that
the cyclic order-lattice provides.

**Why now?** The Lean development is stated for an arbitrary finite index set of
occupation numbers (`Hlist`, `Ipair_eval`), so switching the underlying group from `ℤ/n`
to `ℤ/a × ℤ/b` requires only a new enumeration, not new theory.
title: C5. Non-cyclic Galois groups: the abelian type channel

description:
**Conjecture.** The image of `EMLTS.emlGermHom` is a Hardy field, and it is *maximal*
among Hardy fields whose elements have transseries expansions of exponential depth `≤ 2`:
any germ that is comparable to every EML germ and is closed under differentiation already
lies in the image. Falsifiable form: exhibit a germ (say a solution of
`y' = y² − x` on `(1,∞)`) that is comparable to all EML germs, has depth-`≤2` asymptotics,
and is not an EML germ.

**The key insight is** that the two Hardy-field axioms are now theorems rather than
hypotheses — `EMLTS.eventually_strictMono_or_strictAnti_or_const` (no oscillation) and
`EMLTS.tendsto_EMLFun_limit` (limits exist) — so maximality becomes a purely
model-theoretic saturation question about the value group `Rank`, not an analytic one.

**Why now?** The germ embedding `EMLTS.emlGermHom_injective` and the compatibility of the
formal and analytic derivatives (`EMLTS.hasDerivAt_EMLFun`) make the image a *differential*
subring of the germ ring; verifying the field axiom needs only
`EMLTS.eventually_ne_zero`, which is proved. So the statement "the EML germs form a
Hardy field" is within one short file, and maximality is the first genuinely open step.
title: C4. `EMLTS.EMLFun` germs generate a maximal Hardy field of exp-log germs

description:
**Conjecture.** Given a finite infinitesimal probability model and a tropical penalty vector, there is a sharp oscillation threshold for observables below which ordinary standard-part expectation and tropical maximization select the same exposed face of the outcome simplex. Beyond that threshold, every disagreement pattern compatible with the supports can occur.

The key insight is that the inequality `f(i) + M_i ≤ f(r)` is not merely sufficient: its boundary should form the normal fan separating stable support agreement from visible-outcome escape.

**Why now?** The finite reservoir bridge supplies one complete cone of this fan and shows explicitly why unconditional agreement is false.
title: Quantitative stability threshold for tropical and additive observations

description:
For `A = (1/N) XᵀX` with `X` an `N × n` matrix of i.i.d. standard Gaussians and
`n/N → γ ∈ (0,1)`,

```
(1/n) · tr (A (A + b•1)⁻¹)  →  1 - b · m_γ(-b),
```

where `m_γ` is the Stieltjes transform of the Marchenko–Pastur law; consequently
the noise floor per parameter converges to `b (1 - b m_γ(-b))`.

**The key insight is** that the trace lemma turns the noise floor into a linear
spectral statistic of the sample covariance, precisely the class of quantities
controlled by the Stieltjes transform — so a random-matrix limit theorem
transfers verbatim to a learning-theoretic constant.

**Why now?** The catalog already contains a Wigner semicircle development
(`Catalog/MachineLearning/WignerSemicircle/`), and Round 6 supplies the exact
identity `tr(A(A+b)⁻¹) = Σ μᵢ/(μᵢ+b)` needed to phrase the limit as convergence
of an empirical spectral integral; joining the two files is the shortest path to
a formally verified "double descent"-style curve.

**Falsifier:** a mismatch between the finite-`n` numerics of
`tr(A(A+b)⁻¹)/n` and `1 - b m_γ(-b)` beyond `O(n^{-1/2})`.

---
title: Conjecture D5 (Noise floor of a random covariance: Marchenko–Pastur regime)

description:
**Conjecture.**  For a tropical affine model with *shared* parameters across
coordinates, the `L¹` empirical risk is a tropical polynomial in the parameters and its
minimizer set is a bounded tropical polytope (a finite union of alcoved polyhedra);
clipped subgradient descent with a fixed step reaches this set in finitely many steps
for every positive step size, again with a projection-invariance conservation law.

*The key insight is* that `projIcc`-invariance (`intervalStep_proj`) is what made
finite termination possible in the separable case: the projection onto the minimizer set
is a conserved quantity of the flow, and the same conservation should hold for the
metric projection onto any polyhedral minimizer set of a piecewise-linear convex risk.

*Why now?*  This cycle establishes the conservation law and finite termination for
points, segments and boxes — exactly the alcoved polytopes of dimension `0` and `1` and
their products — so the general polyhedral statement is the first genuinely new case.

---
title: Non-separable tropical models: descent onto a tropical polytope

description:
On the A-spine the quality bound q < 2 - eps is equivalent to a lower bound on rad(n) rad(n+1) rad(2n^2+2n+1). Proving such a bound for all n would give the first uniform abc-type gap for an infinite Pythagorean family.

There is delta > 0 with rad(n) rad(n+1) rad(2n^2+2n+1) >= n^{1+delta} for all n >= 2; consequently q <= 2 - eps(delta) on the whole A-spine.

Formalize the reduction (already available through BerggrenABC.spine_hit_criterion and one_lt_quality_iff) and attack the radical inequality for n in fixed congruence classes.

A uniform quality ceiling below 2 for an infinite abc family, unconditionally.

There are spine parameters with triply deficient radicals, producing abc triples of quality approaching 2 - a sensational counterexample-hunting target.
proof_strategy: Split n into powerful and squarefree parts; use the classical bound on the number of powerful numbers up to x plus the coprimality of n, n+1, 2n^2+2n+1.
title: Spine Radical Inequality as a Uniform Quality Gap

description:
The seeded convolution engine converts any certified invisible seed into a global growth bound. We conjecture the existence of seeds whose mass is subexponential in the window, built as products of sparse binomials X^a - 1 with tuned exponents, driving the growth base to 1.

For every K there is a nonzero P in Z[X] with (X-1)^K dividing P and coefficient l1 norm at most exp(C sqrt(K log K)).

Search exponent sequences (a_1,...,a_K) minimising the l1 norm of the product, certify the best families in Lean, and feed them to PTEBase.exists_invisible_pow_of_seed.

Every exponential upper bound in the catalog collapses to subexponential, and the minimal-mass problem becomes a question of polynomial versus subexponential growth.

There is a genuine exponential barrier for products of sparse binomials, isolating cancellation, rather than divisibility, as the obstruction.
proof_strategy: Adapt Atkinson-style constructions for products of (1 - x^{a_i}) with exponents in an arithmetic-progression-free pattern, and bound the l1 norm by iterated convolution estimates already formalised as l1_kconv_le.
title: Subexponential Seeds via Sparse Binomial Products

description:
Observing a product of k primes only through the unordered multiset of splitting types should still leak exactly one bit, for every k. The k=1 and k=2 cases are proved here with different type profiles, suggesting a convolution-stable mass balance.

For every k >= 1, I(residue class of n = p_1...p_k ; multiset of splitting types) = 1 exactly.

Define the k-fold multiset alphabet with multiplicities given by the multinomial expansion of the profile 1:3:2, prove the sign-product factors through the multiset, and apply the character channel law.

Factorisation-type data never leaks more than one bit about a squarefree integer's quadratic character, at any number of factors.

There is a k at which the multiset readout becomes correlated beyond the sign, which would be a genuinely new arithmetic correlation.
proof_strategy: Induction on k: the multiplicity profile of the k-fold multiset is the k-fold convolution of 1:3:2, and the sign-balanced halves stay balanced because the generating function evaluated at -1 vanishes for k >= 1.
title: k-Fold Semiprime Channel Saturation

description:
Height reduction proves that the coefficient height of a cyclotomic polynomial depends only on the odd radical, and the values 1, 2, 3 are now realised formally by 231, 105, 385. The open half asks how the height grows along squarefree odd radicals with three prime factors, and whether it is unbounded there.

The height function is constant on fibres of the odd radical, and sup { A(Φ_{pqr}) : p<q<r odd primes } = ∞.

Compute A(Φ_{pqr}) for all ternary radicals below 10^5 and fit growth; formally, iterate the explicit-polynomial method already used for Φ₁₀₅ and Φ₃₈₅ on families such as 5·7·r.

Heights are a genuine odd-radical invariant with unbounded range on ternary orders.

Ternary heights would be uniformly bounded, contradicting the reduction or known growth results.
proof_strategy: Constancy is PMFrameHeight.frameBoundedBy_iff_oddRad; unboundedness needs an explicit family with growing coefficients, constructed from the semigroup formula plus a pigeonhole on residues.
title: Odd-Radical Height Spectrum

description:
The exact variance of the dial, Σ_{p ≤ B} (p²−1)/p⁴, converges as B → ∞ while its mean Σ (p+1)/p² diverges. The centred dial is therefore a sum of independent bounded terms with summable variances and must converge in law to a nondegenerate limit: an infinite Bernoulli convolution with weights 2/p and success probabilities (p+1)/(2p). Identifying that limit law turns the empirical spread of the feature into an arithmetic constant.

The centred dials qrWeight(·,B) − Σ_{p≤B}(p+1)/p² converge in distribution as B → ∞ to a nondegenerate law of variance Σ_{p odd prime} (p²−1)/p⁴, and that law is absolutely continuous.

Formalise the finite-B distributions from card_qr_pattern, prove tightness from the uniform bound qrWeight_variance_lt_half, and compare the resulting characteristic function ∏_p (1 − a_p + a_p·e^{2it/p}) with an empirical histogram over one period for B = 5, 7, 11, 13.

The dial has a universal limiting fluctuation profile, so calibration constants measured at one factor-base bound transfer to any other.

The limit is singular or degenerate, meaning the dial's fluctuation is dominated by finitely many small primes and the feature is effectively low-dimensional.
proof_strategy: Kolmogorov two-series theorem applied to the independent indicator terms (independence supplied by card_qr_pattern, variances by sum_sq_dev_qrWeight), then Erdős-style analysis of the infinite Bernoulli convolution for absolute continuity.
title: Bernoulli-Convolution Limit Law of the Centred QR Dial

description:
The dial-blindness theorem is an instance of a general symmetry principle: features invariant along arithmetic progressions cannot separate primes from semiprimes. Conjecture: every feature computed from finitely many residues of N modulo primes ≤ B has AUC exactly 1/2 for that task.

For any F : (ZMod P) → ℝ and any n, there are primes q > n and semiprimes m > n with F(q mod P) = F(m mod P); consequently the induced ranking has AUC 1/2 on matched families.

Generalise qrWeight_blind_semiprime from qrWeight to an arbitrary function of the residue vector, then combine with the catalog AUC lemma auc_eq_half_of_blind.

A clean frontier: residue-only features are provably useless for factor detection, and any positive result must use non-residue information.

Some residue statistic would detect factor structure, contradicting Dirichlet-type equidistribution — a major surprise.
proof_strategy: Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions supplies both primes and products of two primes in each unit class mod P; blindness is then function-composition.
title: No-Free-Lunch Frontier for Modular-Reduction Features

description:
Reading a dial is free in the current law. Charging c per reading converts the cap into a profitability criterion: the absolute saving of a density-θ dial on an n-class scan is n(θ − θ²), maximized at n/4. Superconstant-cost congruence tests are then provably unprofitable.

With reading cost c and baseline n, a dial of density θ is profitable iff c < n(θ − θ²); in particular no dial with c ≥ n/4 is ever profitable.

Add the cost term to expectedScanCost in Lean, maximize θ − θ² = 1/4 by completing the square, and compare against simulated trial division with explicit residue tests.

Residual gap (2) — superconstant-cost tests — closes inside the scan-order framing.

Some expensive local test pays for itself, locating a resource outside the classified set.
proof_strategy: Elementary completion of the square; the saving n(θ − θ²) ≤ n/4 with equality at θ = 1/2.
title: Zero-Profit Threshold for Cost-Charged Filters

description:
Binary dials have caps 4/3 (single pass) and 2 (expected position); r-ary single-pass dials have cap 2r/(r+1); r-ary full reveals have cap r. We conjecture a single two-parameter surface C(r, accounting) with these four corners, settling which constant any given cryptanalytic claim is about.

Under expected-position accounting an r-block dial has supremum speedup exactly r, approached but not attained, so C(r, position) = r and C(r, phase) = 2r/(r+1); the surface is jointly monotone.

Generalize the triangular-sum optimality lemma to r blocks and compute the optimum of Σ_i θ_i (S_{i-1} + (θ_i n + 1)/2); verify numerically for r ≤ 6 and n ≤ 10^4.

A complete dictionary between accounting conventions and barrier constants.

The two refinements interact, revealing a genuinely new obstruction beyond the density-only law.
proof_strategy: Leafwise triangular-sum bound plus the doubling identity, then optimization under Σθ = 1.
title: Two-Parameter Cap Surface for r-ary Dials

description:
The prime-power saturation law turns the type entropy of a squarefree degree into a pure sum over primes. For the primorial degree P(x) that sum is governed by two classical Mertens estimates, predicting H = log2 x + log2 log x + c + o(1) with c approximately -1.9254.

H(T_{P(x)}) - log2 x - log2 log x converges to an absolute constant c, where P(x) is the product of the primes up to x.

Formalize H(T_{P(x)}) = sum over p <= x of (log2 p - ((p-1)/p) log2 (p-1)) from typeEntropy_prime_pow_eq and typeEntropy_mul_of_coprime, then bound the two prime sums.

The information content of the splitting type is doubly logarithmic in the conductor, so pinning stays bounded while the degree explodes.

Either the reduction to a prime sum fails, or the Mertens cancellation is not uniform, pointing to an arithmetic obstruction in the channel.
proof_strategy: Apply the saturation law termwise, split the summand as log2(p/(p-1)) + log2(p-1)/p, and use Mertens' theorems for sum 1/p and sum log p / p.
title: Mertens Growth Law for the Primorial Type Channel

description:
The prime-degree splitting-type channel is the two-point vector (1/q, (q-1)/q), whose Renyi entropy of every real order is now in closed form, and the orders 0, 1, 2 are strictly ordered with integer certificates. The conjecture upgrades those finitely many comparisons to strict monotonicity in the order parameter, with infimum log2(q/(q-1)).

For every prime q >= 3 the map a -> H_a(T_q) is strictly decreasing on (0, infinity) and tends to log2(q/(q-1)) as a tends to infinity.

Differentiate the closed form typeRenyi_prime_formula in a and identify the derivative with minus a Kullback-Leibler divergence between the escort distribution of order a and the original two-point vector; then prove strict positivity of that divergence for a non-uniform pair.

The whole Renyi spectrum of a cyclic prime-degree channel is pinned between one bit and log2(q/(q-1)), an effective two-sided bound uniform in the conductor.

The order profile is non-monotone somewhere, which for a two-point distribution would contradict the escort-divergence identity and reveal an error in the closed form.
proof_strategy: Write H_a = (1-a)^{-1} log2 S(a) with S(a) = p1^a + p2^a, compute d/da of the quotient, and reduce the sign to Jensen strictness for the escort weights; the discrete cases already proved supply sanity checks at a = 0, 1, 2.
title: Continuous Renyi Monotonicity at Prime Degree

description:
Pinning is exact on unramified classes because the type is a deterministic function of the residue. Enlarging the sample space by the single ramified prime p = f should degrade the identity by a computable amount of order (log f)/f, and by nothing else.

With the ramified class adjoined, H(T) - I(p mod f ; T) = Theta((log f)/f), and the difference is 0 exactly when the ramified class is removed.

Compute the enlarged-channel entropies exactly with uEnt_eq_shannon for f = 7, 13, 19, 31 and fit the constant; then prove two-sided bounds.

Full pinning becomes a theorem with an explicit error term, valid uniformly in the conductor.

Ramification interacts with the type distribution non-perturbatively, a genuinely new phenomenon.
proof_strategy: Treat the enlarged space as a one-point perturbation, expand uEnt_eq_shannon in 1/f, and control the log terms with the logb bounds already proved.
title: Ramification as the Unique Obstruction to Pinning

description:
For n = pq with coprime factors, ZMod n splits as a product, so an encoding at modulus n is a two-block encoding. The conjecture is that the degree-1 ceiling of a target factors through this splitting in a computable way. This turns 'which modulus to dial' into arithmetic rather than search.

If y on ZMod n x ZMod n is transported along the CRT equivalence to (ZMod p x ZMod q)^2, then varr(addPart y) is unchanged, and for alignment targets the ceiling is 0 for every divisor structure of n.

Combine Rsq_reindex with varr_split; instantiate the CRT equivalence ZMod (p*q) ~ ZMod p x ZMod q from Mathlib and compute both sides for n = 15, 21, 91.

Composite-modulus encodings inherit their ceilings from the prime factors, so the 3..97 scan already covers the composite range.

Composite moduli carry structure absent at prime moduli, which would be a genuinely new dial for the next round.
proof_strategy: Relabelling invariance of avg/cov/varr (proved) plus the uniqueness of the additive/interaction split under a product-preserving equivalence.
title: CRT Ceiling Arithmetic for Composite Moduli

description:
Using the exact identity residual entropy = n - rank H, the Shannon-limit statement for reconciliation becomes a question about achievable ranks of parity-check matrices with large minimum distance. We conjecture the Gilbert-Varshamov style family attains residual rate 1 - h(p) and that nothing beats it.

For every p in (0,1/2) there are schemes with m/n → h(p), t/n → p, separating, and residual min-entropy rate → 1 - h(p); and no separating family with t/n → p has residual rate above 1 - h(p).

Prove a Gilbert-Varshamov existence lemma for binary matrices with prescribed kernel distance, then combine with Scheme.residual_min_entropy and Scheme.sphere_packing_leakage for the converse.

A Shannon coding theorem stated entirely in transcript-leakage terms, fully formalised.

The transcript formulation is strictly weaker than the channel-coding formulation, isolating where the gap arises.
proof_strategy: Counting/greedy construction for achievability; the already-proved sphere-packing bound plus entropy estimates of binomial sums for the converse.
title: Exact Rate-Leakage Curve for Bit-Flip Channels

description:
The knee of a mixed corpus is sandwiched between its component knees. Conjecture the stronger statement that it is monotone in the mixing weight, so the knee budget of a corpus is a monotone interpolation between its ingredients and can be tuned continuously.

For fixed profiles P and Q and fixed tolerance, the map lam |-> k*(mix lam P Q)(tau) is monotone in lam.

Prove monotonicity of the mixture capture curve in lam when one profile majorizes the other, and exhibit a counterexample when the curves cross.

Corpus KV budget can be interpolated from component budgets, giving a design rule for data mixtures.

Mixing is genuinely non-monotone, so corpus composition must be tested empirically rather than interpolated.
proof_strategy: Differentiate the mixture capture curve in lam: it is affine, so monotone in lam pointwise iff P.cum - Q.cum has constant sign; combine with kneeAt_mono_profile and produce a crossing counterexample otherwise.
title: Monotone Mixture Calculus for Corpus Design

description:
The hybrid dyadic–Padé certificate log(N/D) ≥ m·log 2 + 2(y−1)/(y+1) with y = N/(2^m·D) is now proved, with residual error cubic in y−1. Iterating the Padé step on successive square roots, using log y = 2^k·log(y^{1/2^k}), should shrink the residual like 4^{-k} at a certificate cost linear in 2^k. This would give the tightest rational key-rate certificates obtainable from a fixed integer budget.

For every rational QBER a/(a+c) and every k, the k-fold iterated root certificate lower-bounds the key rate with relative error O(4^{-k}), each step being a single integer comparison between N^{2^k} and a dyadic multiple of D^{2^k}.

Formalize log(N/D) = 2^k·log((N/D)^{1/2^k}) and apply log_pade_lower at each level on top of secureKeyRate_ge_of_cert_hybrid; instantiate at Q = 10 % and 11 % for k = 1, 2, 3 and compare with the exact values 0.0620088 and 1.68084e-4 bits.

A uniform, arbitrarily sharp certificate calculus for all rational QBERs, superseding both parent schemes.

The Padé residual does not compose across roots, isolating an obstruction to iterated rational certification of transcendental rates.
proof_strategy: Induct on k: write y_k = y^{1/2^k}, use log y = 2 log √y and the cubic error term of the [1/1] Padé approximant to control the residual, with the integer comparison obtained by squaring the certificate 2^k times.
title: Geometric Convergence of Iterated Root Certificates

description:
Under a mass-preserving r-fold token split the knee scales multiplicatively, so in log-context coordinates the slope of the knee law should be invariant and only the intercept should shift by log2 r. This makes any new domain a one-parameter falsifiable test.

For a geometric-tail family, knee(tokenSplit r p, tau) = knee(p, tau) + Nat.log 2 r + O(1), hence the log-law slope is domain-invariant and the intercept shifts by log2 of the tokens-per-word ratio.

Prove the shift identity for the drifting-geometric family and compare against a code/math corpus sweep at three contexts.

Deployment tables for new domains are predicted from a single tokenisation statistic.

Domain shifts alter the tail shape itself, and slope must be re-measured per domain.
proof_strategy: Compose the dilution sandwich with the drifting-geometric knee formula and take logarithms; control the O(1) by the sandwich endpoints.
title: Tokenisation Intercept Shift with Invariant Log-Slope

description:
We proved that agreement of m normalized factors up to degree N-1 forces agreement of their product up to degree N-m. We conjecture the shift m is optimal and that the truncation map is surjective onto the expected affine space, so exactly m coefficients of information are lost and no more.

For each m and N the map from m-tuples of truncated normalized series to truncated products is surjective onto the fibre determined by the leading coefficient, and there exist tuples agreeing to degree N-1 whose products differ at degree N-m+1.

Construct explicit witnesses with single-coefficient perturbations and formalize the surjectivity by an inductive lifting argument on truncations.

A sharp information-theoretic bound for reconstructing factors from a moonshine-type product.

Additional hidden constraints link the coefficients of products of normalized series.
proof_strategy: Induct on the truncation level; at each level the obstruction is a single linear equation in the new coefficients, solvable since the leading coefficient is a unit.
title: Optimal Determinacy Radius for Pole-Order-m Products

description:
Classify which pairs (k*@n, k*@2n) are reachable from a base pair by the composite operation dilate p ∘ contract q. Dilation multiplies the doubling increment while merging quantises it, so the reachable set is a nontrivial arithmetic region rather than a ray. The result would replace per-domain grid sweeps by a decision procedure on two measured numbers.

A pair (a, b) is reachable from (16, 20) by dilate p ∘ contract q iff there exist p, q ≥ 1 with p·(⌈16/q⌉−1) < a ≤ p·⌈16/q⌉ and p·(⌈20/q⌉−1) < b ≤ p·⌈20/q⌉; in particular b = a forces q ≥ 5.

Formalise the reachable set as a predicate in Lean and prove both inclusions; the forward inclusion follows from ratDilate_bracket, the converse needs explicit profiles.

Any new domain is characterised by two integers, and the reported per-domain factor tables become derivable rather than measured.

The reachable set is strictly smaller, so some measured pairs need a mechanism outside dilation and merging.
proof_strategy: Forward: ratDilate_bracket. Converse: build geometric profiles with prescribed knees and verify by rational arithmetic, as in kstar_dilate_lt_mul_example.
title: Mixed Dilation-Merging Classification of Budget Curves

description:
Cycle 5 gives an explicit stabilisation locus for a geometrically decaying profile in terms of the gate slack of the limit knee. The conjecture is that the closed-form uniform budget geometricBudget r tau, computed from the decay ratio and the gate alone, is always itself such a locus. On the dyadic witness the two numbers coincide exactly at 21, and that value is tight.

For a positive profile with w(i+1) <= r*w(i), 0 < r < 1 and 0 < tau < 1, one has kstar w m tau = kinf w tau for every m >= max (geometricBudget r tau) 1.

Compare the geometric tail at geometricBudget r tau with the slack tau * tsum w - headMass w (kinf w tau - 1) and feed the comparison into stabilisation_locus_explicit; falsify by constructing a profile whose limit knee has slack smaller than the tail at the budget.

A domain's entire budget curve, including where it freezes and what it freezes at, is computable from (r, tau) before any sweep is run.

Stabilisation can be arbitrarily late relative to the uniform budget, so the locus genuinely depends on the profile and not only on its decay ratio.
proof_strategy: Bound the tail at the budget by (1 - tau) * w 0 using kstar_le_geometricBudget's inequality, then compare with the slack, which is positive by minimality of kinf; the refutation direction tunes a geometric profile so that headMass (kinf - 1) is just below tau * tsum w.
title: Uniform Budget as Stabilisation Context

description:
Upgrade the window-consistency statements for the German (20, 24) and code (12, 12) rows to explicit profiles. Each realiser would prove that the anomaly is a ceiling artefact of the mechanism rather than evidence against it.

There is a geometric profile w and a gate τ with kstar w 512 τ = 16, kstar w 1024 τ = 20, and kstar (ratDilate 5 4 w) 640 τ = 20, kstar (ratDilate 5 4 w) 1280 τ = 24.

Search (r, τ) computationally, then verify the four knee values in Lean by rational arithmetic.

The German row is fully explained by rational rescaling and the sharpened verdict becomes a four-of-five statement.

The window is not attained, so the mechanism over-predicts and needs an additional constraint.
proof_strategy: Use closed-form geometric partial sums to compute retained mass exactly, then bracket each knee with a pass/fail pair as in net65_razor_bracket.
title: Explicit Realisers for the Anomalous Domain Rows

description:
Because the gap between the matched-context and token-matched readings is exactly c times the base increment, a domain is determined by the pair (factor, increment) rather than by a factor alone. The conjecture is that these two integers predict every further context column, making a third measurement a genuine falsification test.

For a c-fold dilation of a base curve with increment D per doubling, the measured knee at the m-th doubling satisfies c·(K + (m−1)·D) − c < k*_dilated ≤ c·(K + (m−1)·D), for every m ≥ 1.

Iterate token_matched_window along a doubling chain and prove the resulting bracket by induction on m.

Two integers per domain replace an entire grid sweep, and a ctx = 2048 column is predicted in advance.

The increment itself drifts with context, so no finite descriptor of a domain exists and per-context sweeps are unavoidable.
proof_strategy: Induction on the number of doublings, using token_matched_window at each step and the additivity of the base increment along the chain.
title: Two-Number Domain Descriptor: Factor and Increment

description:
The monotonicity of the rescaled shell thickness in the dimension was deduced from the fact that the Cesaro averages of the geometric sequence y^i decrease. The conjecture is that this is the whole story: any peel profile with antitone gaps has monotone rescaled deficit, and conversely.

For antitone nonnegative a : N → R the averages (1/n)∑_{i<n} a i are antitone in n, and a PeelProfile has monotone rescaled deficit iff its gap sequence has antitone Cesaro averages.

Generalise sum_geom_avg_antitone from y^i to an arbitrary antitone sequence, then quantify over the catalog's PeelProfile structure.

The abstract PeelProfile API inherits all the concentration results proved here for balls.

A counterexample profile separates geometric peelings from abstract ones and explains why the ball case is special.
proof_strategy: Split the range into head and tail as in sum_geom_avg_antitone; the converse direction should follow by choosing a i = 1 - r_i and inverting the substitution y = t^{1/(ab)}.
title: Cesaro Antitonicity as the Engine of Dimension Monotonicity

description:
A key cache cannot exceed the context it summarises. This single constraint refutes the geometric continuation of the NET-78 chain without any new measurement, and suggests that all admissible knee laws are polynomial in the number of doublings, with vanishing retained fraction.

Any budget law whose increments grow geometrically violates f j <= 512 * 2^j for all large j; conversely every feasible law that is convex and monotone is bounded by a polynomial in j, so its keepFraction tends to 0.

Prove the converse direction in Lean: from feasibility plus convexity derive a polynomial bound on f, and combine with the proved squeeze ratio_vanishes_of_poly.

The space of admissible continuations collapses to polynomial fits, reducing the ctx = 8192 experiment to a two-way test between 56 and 80 keys.

Some feasible law grows faster than any polynomial while staying under the exponential ceiling, and the ctx = 8192 prediction interval must stay open.
proof_strategy: Use discrete convexity to bound increments by their terminal value; contrast geometric growth with the exponential ceiling via 2^m <= 4^m; for the converse, bound f by its tangent envelope and control the envelope degree.
title: Feasibility Ceiling as a Selection Principle

description:
The Spearman tie ceiling is an affine function of the cube sum of the tie profile, and the cube sum is strictly convex. Hence the ceiling should be strictly concave along mass-preserving mixtures of profiles: a dial run on a mixture of two draw laws resolves strictly better than the average of the two pure dials. This upgrades the existing total-variation Lipschitz envelope to a shape statement.

For profiles L, L' of equal length and equal mass and t in (0,1), spearmanSq (tL + (1-t)L') > t spearmanSq L + (1-t) spearmanSq L'.

Prove coordinatewise strict convexity of cubeSum and transport through spearmanSq_eq; verify numerically on dyadicBlocks 8 against binomBlocks 8.

Mixed deployment envelopes are automatically safer than their worst pure component, removing the constant from the envelope bounds.

Mixtures can under-resolve, and envelope claims must continue to carry the explicit Lipschitz constant.
proof_strategy: Write spearmanSq = 1 - (cubeSum - n)/(n^3 - n) at fixed mass n, then use strict convexity of x -> x^3 coordinatewise and equality analysis for the strictness.
title: Strict Concavity of the Tie Ceiling Along Mixtures

description:
The chord distance sqrt(2-2rho) is a metric on normalised statistics. The conjecture is that the trailing-zero statistic moves Lipschitz-continuously in 1/bitlen and that the recorded dial decline is the image of that curve. This is the one direction of the original set that remains fully open.

There is L > 0 with corrDist(T_b, T_b') <= L * |1/b - 1/b'| for all bitlens b, b', and the recorded readings 0.78, 0.641, 0.605 at bitlens 44, 64, 72 satisfy the induced triangle inequalities.

Check the three recorded chords against corrDist_triangle in Lean; then formalise the two-adic block comparison between T_b and T_b'.

The dial law extrapolates to untested bitlens with a certified error bar, which also pins down the horizon of the capacity conjecture.

The dial decline is not a continuous deformation of one statistic but a change of statistic, and cross-bitlen pooling is invalid.
proof_strategy: Express T_b and T_b' on a common sample space via the two-adic valuation profile, bound the centred inner product by the overlap of the dyadic blocks, and convert to chord distance.
title: Chord-Metric Lipschitz Continuity of the Bitlen Dial

description:
Every subset of the Boolean cube is realised as an assembly space by a framed puzzle with 2^n - |S| clause pieces, which is far from minimal. The conjecture is that the minimum equals the CNF clause complexity of the indicator, and that for complement-stable S a minimal realisation can be chosen complement-stable. This turns the free involution into a symmetrisation operator on the space of realisations.

For complement-stable S there is a minimum-size framed puzzle P with assemblySet P = S such that compPuzzle P is a permutation of P.

Formalise clause complexity of the indicator and prove a symmetrisation lemma; verify by enumeration for n = 2, 3 that minimal realisations of stable sets can be paired up under complementation.

Complementation becomes a normalisation procedure for puzzle descriptions, giving canonical forms for self-dual instances.

There are stable spaces whose economical realisations are all asymmetric, exhibiting a symmetry-versus-size tradeoff.
proof_strategy: Take a minimal realisation P, form the multiset union with compPuzzle P, and show redundancy elimination via the gauge decomposition does not increase size.
title: Minimal Clause Realisations of Complement-Stable Assembly Spaces

description:
Price letters are readable mod 4 and mod 8 and unreadable deeper; Berggren letters are provably unreadable 2-adically at any depth. The conjecture is the exact mirror statement at the prime 3, making the two trees complementary seals.

The last Berggren letter is a function of the triple's residues modulo 3 and modulo 9, and for every k there exist two Berggren children of different letters whose triples agree modulo 2^k (already proved) while no such pair exists modulo 3.

Formalise a Berggren letterOf on actGen and prove the mod-3 classification; reuse the counterexample construction of Price2Adic.berg_twoAdic_blind for the negative half.

A clean placement theorem: each ternary Pythagorean tree is sealed at exactly one adic place.

The Berggren alphabet is not a residue dial at all, and the placement claim must be weakened to Price only.
proof_strategy: Compute the Berggren children's triples modulo 9 in terms of the parent's parameters, as in berg_children_diff, and check that the three residue patterns are pairwise distinct.
title: Adic Complementarity of Ternary Pythagorean Trees

description:
Gauss-sum magnitudes are constant across residue classes and hence buy a speedup of exactly one. The open question is whether the argument (phase) of the Gauss sum, which does vary, can approach the universal 4/3 scan cap.

For every quantisation of the argument of the quadratic Gauss sum into t bits, the induced residue dial has density bounded away from 1/2 uniformly in t, so the speedup it buys is bounded strictly below 4/3.

Compute the argument distribution of twisted Gauss sums over ZMod p for many primes; formalise the density bound and feed it to ResidueDial.speedup_strictMonoOn.

Character-sum cryptanalysis provably cannot reach the scan cap, extending the zero-bit magnitude theorem to the full complex value.

There is a phase-based dial at the cap, and the magnitude/phase split becomes the sharp boundary of the barrier.
proof_strategy: Use gaussSum_mulShift to reduce the phase to the quadratic character value times a fixed phase, then bound the density of a quadratic-residue-defined class set.
title: Argument-Phase Gauss Dial Below the Four-Thirds Cap

description:
All theories here are truncations of the frame at a level N. The conjecture removes the truncation: arbitrary unbounded height vectors together with reflection depths bounded by them should be realized on an infinite frame, with the truncated theories forming a chain whose colimit is the limit theory and whose reflection depths stabilize.

For arbitrary d r : Nat -> Nat with r i <= d i and d unbounded there is a consistent GL theory on an infinite transitive tag frame with Provable S (box_i^k bot) iff d i < k and DepthReflection r' i S iff r' <= r i, unique up to bisimulation once the tag images are fixed.

Define the untruncated frame theory (validity at all worlds) in Lean, prove consistency and the GL axioms without the truncation, and transfer the height and depth computations using that a formula of box depth k inspects only k levels.

The height and reflection-depth invariants are genuinely infinitary invariants of GL theories, not artefacts of finite truncation.

Some profile is realizable at every finite truncation but not in the limit, exhibiting a compactness failure for the depth-restricted reflection rules.
proof_strategy: Take the union of the truncated frames; validity at all worlds is the intersection of the truncated theories. Heights are computed pointwise by the same probe formulas; for the depths use that box depth k truth at a world is determined by the k worlds below it, so the truncated bisimulations glue.
title: Limit Profiles Over Infinite Frames

description:
Depth-augmented sealing is now a theorem at every position: the word family A^(t-1) B A^t versus C A^(t-3) C A^(t+1) gives, for each t >= 2, two Price nodes of equal odd leg and equal depth that split at position t. That family is rigid, producing exactly one pair per position, while at t = 2 a second family C A^j C A^2 versus B A^(j+3) gives infinitely many. The conjecture is that infinitude holds at every position, indeed with a positive proportion of odd legs carrying such a pair.

For every t >= 3 the set of odd legs N admitting two valid Price nodes of odd leg N, of equal address length, agreeing at all positions below t and splitting at t, is infinite (it is proved infinite for t = 2); quantitatively its counting function below X is at least c_t * X / log X.

Search for a two-parameter word family: pairs of Price words of equal length whose leaves have equal odd legs, using the closed forms eval(A^i B A^t) = (2^(i+1) + 2^t + 1, 2^t) and eval(C A^j C A^(t+1)); then formalize the resulting family as in Probability.PriceTwoAdicDepthSealing. Numerically, count equal-depth splitting pairs below X with scripts/price_two_adic_depth_family_check.py.

No classifier reading the pair (odd leg, depth) is even eventually correct at any position t >= 2, upgrading no_eventual_oddLeg_classifier to its depth-augmented form.

Equal-depth coincidences are sparse, and a (N, depth) classifier correct for all large N could exist despite the proved counterexample family.
proof_strategy: Parametrize both nodes by words of equal length, reduce the equal-odd-leg condition to the Diophantine identity a1(a1 + 2^(t+1) n1) = a2(a2 + 2^(t+1) n2) in the Euclid data of the two base nodes, and produce solutions with a free parameter by choosing a2 with v2(a2^2 - 1) = t + 1; then control the depths by expressing both nodes as explicit words.
title: Infinitude of Equal-Depth Splitting Pairs

description:
With a fixed number of budget evaluations per cell, which sweep minimises the worst-case implied margin band? The conjecture is that geometric grids are optimal and the achievable half-width is the N-th root of the budget range. This converts the observed dyadic obstruction into a concrete experimental design.

Among all sweeps with N evaluations in [k_min, k_max], the minimal worst-case implied margin ratio band is [(k_max/k_min)^(-1/N), (k_max/k_min)^(1/N)], attained exactly by the geometric grid.

Formalize a sweep as a finite set of budgets, define its worst-case band via GridReport, and prove the min-max over sweeps.

The number of forward passes needed to test E3 at plus/minus 10 percent is determined exactly.

Non-geometric adaptive sweeps beat geometric ones, and a bisection protocol should replace the fixed grid.
proof_strategy: Reduce to minimising the maximal consecutive ratio of a partition of a ratio interval; use the AM-GM style argument on the product of consecutive ratios, which telescopes to k_max/k_min.
title: Optimal Geometric Sweeps for Knee Estimation

description:
A disordered refinement cascade with level-dependent branching r(k) has a maximal supported depth trapped between two logarithms. We conjecture that the true depth is governed by the Birkhoff average of log r, not by the endpoints of the quench window. This would make the depth of a random foam a genuinely ergodic-theoretic quantity.

If (1/k)·∑_{j<k} log r j → m > 0 then maxDepth (schedCells r) T = (log T)/m + O(1) uniformly in T.

Formalise schedWeight r k = exp(∑_{j<k} log r j), replace the constant base in Universality.maxDepth_sandwich by schedWeight, and prove matching upper/lower bounds from the Birkhoff average; test numerically on periodic and Sturmian schedules.

The logarithmic depth law becomes a statement about ergodic averages, unifying homogeneous, periodic and random foams.

Depth is sensitive to the fluctuation, not just the mean, of the branching schedule, which would identify a new disorder-driven correction term.
proof_strategy: Generalise the sandwich argument: lower bound via schedWeight d ≥ exp((m-ε)d) for large d, upper bound via schedCells d ≤ 2·schedWeight d; convert both to logarithms of T.
title: Ergodic Depth Law for Quenched Branching Schedules

description:
A ternary word indexed by 4-subsets is realizable by a binary tree only if every 5-leaf window is realizable. We enumerated 210 valid two-premise five-leaf rules and formalized three of them. The conjecture is that these local rules are complete: local consistency on all 5-windows implies global realizability.

A word w in (Fin 3)^{C(n,4)} is the quartet signature of a binary phylogenetic tree if and only if the restriction of w to every 5-element leaf subset is the signature of a tree on those five leaves.

Formalize the window restriction using the restrict predicate of Combinatorics.Core, then prove the reconstruction direction by building splits from the 0-letters; verify by exhaustive enumeration at n = 6, 7 that no locally consistent non-realizable word exists.

The quartet code is a genuine low-density parity-check code with constant window size, so its rate can be estimated by standard LDPC counting.

Global quartet consistency needs windows of unbounded size, and the coding analogy is only an upper-bound heuristic.
proof_strategy: From a locally consistent word, define a binary relation 'a,b form a cherry relative to c,d' and show the five-leaf rules make it a compatible split system, then invoke the splits-equivalence theorem for trees.
title: Local Axiomatization of Quartet Consistency

description:
Extend the exact Blaschke-Santalo equality for a single ellipsoid to bodies generated by finitely many ellipsoids. Polarity exchanges hulls with intersections, so the single-ellipsoid identity together with the polar calculus of this thread should give explicit two-sided bounds for the volume product of such bodies, producing calibration examples for the reverse Santalo inequality.

For invertible A and B, vol(conv(E A ∪ E B)) * vol((conv(E A ∪ E B))°) <= vol(B_n)^2, with equality if and only if E A = E B.

Prove that a set and its convex hull have the same polar, combine with polarSet_union and polarSet_ellipsoid to get (conv(E A ∪ E B))° = E((A^T)^{-1}) ∩ E((B^T)^{-1}), then bound the volume of that intersection; test numerically for diagonal A, B in dimensions 2 and 3.

Yields an explicit, fully formalized family attaining or nearly attaining the Santalo bound, useful as a calibration class.

A hull of two ellipsoids would beat the ball, contradicting Blaschke-Santalo; a genuine counterexample would be a major discovery, so failure most likely localizes an error in the polarity step.
proof_strategy: Prove polarSet (convexHull s) = polarSet s from linearity of the inner product, combine with polarSet_union, polarSet_ellipsoid and volume_ellipsoid, then use monotonicity of volume under inclusion together with volume_mul_volume_polarSet_le.
title: Volume Products of Multi-Ellipsoid Bodies

description:
Fiberwise dominance of conditional means is now proved to preserve both the optimal dial value and the best static value. The open half is the distributional one: conditional stochastic dominance on every fiber is weaker per fiber, and it is unclear whether it still licenses deletion or whether the variance tail defeats it as it defeats global mean comparison.

If member b stochastically dominates member a conditionally on every fiber of obs, then deleting b changes neither dialValue nor bestConstant; and unconditional stochastic dominance does not suffice.

Formalise conditional stochastic dominance in the finite rational framework, derive fiberwise mean inequalities from ev_le_of_stochDom, feed them into dialValueOn_erase_of_fiberwise_dominates, and search small cost matrices for the separating counterexample in the unconditional case.

Portfolio pruning gains a distribution-level certificate strictly weaker per fiber than the mean test now proved safe.

Only fiber-mean comparisons are safe, and distributional eliminations in the literature need re-auditing.
proof_strategy: Apply ev_le_of_stochDom fiber by fiber to obtain the hypothesis of the proved fiberwise elimination theorems; build the counterexample from the two-instance portfolio of mean_elimination_unsafe.
title: Conditional Distributional Dominance as an Elimination Certificate

description:
The recorded dial fades monotonically with bitlen once the U116 rebound is removed. Pooling and seed imbalance have both been eliminated as explanations, so the fade should come from tie geometry: the trailing-zero statistic has a fixed dyadic tie profile while the response's tie profile coarsens with bitlen. The conjecture makes the fade a product of two computable tie corrections.

There are tie-correction factors T_stat and T_resp(L), depending only on the tie profiles, with rho(L) = T_stat * T_resp(L) and T_resp(L+1)/T_resp(L) bounded above by a constant q < 1 for all large L.

Formalise the two-sided tie-corrected Spearman ceiling for a pair of tie profiles, specialise the statistic side to the dyadic profile of Novelty.ZeroFitDialU64, and check the resulting ratio against the de-noised ladder ratios 0.9472, 0.9207, 0.9750, 0.9469, 0.9444.

The fade becomes a theorem about tie profiles rather than an empirical law, and the no-floor theorem of this cycle applies unconditionally.

The fade is driven by the response distribution itself, and the dial must be re-instrumented with a tie-free response before further ladder rungs are meaningful.
proof_strategy: Extend the tie-attenuation identity rho^2 = 1 - 12*sum(m^3-m)/(n^3-n) to a two-profile version by applying it separately to each ranking and combining through the Gram inequality of ZeroFitDialU72Parity; then estimate the dyadic profile sums geometrically.
title: Bitlen-Indexed Tie Attenuation for the Zero-Count Dial

description:
The de-noised ladder obeys a per-rung ratio bound 0.98. Combined with the geometric envelope theorem this yields an exact, falsifiable prediction five rungs ahead, already proved in Lean. The conjecture is that the law persists and the prediction holds.

Continuing the bitlen sweep at the recorded cadence, the pooled Spearman reading five rungs after U120 is below 0.40.

Run the sweep to five further bitlens and compare with the proved bound rho(5) < 0.40 under the hypothesis rho(k+1) <= 0.98*rho(k); a reading above 0.40 refutes the ratio bound at some rung.

The no-positive-floor theorem applies to the measured ladder and the floor hypothesis is dead.

Some rung violates the 0.98 ratio, locating a bitlen at which the fade mechanism changes, which is itself the most informative possible outcome.
proof_strategy: Already proved as u120_predicts_below_forty; the open part is experimental, namely whether the hypothesis holds at the next five rungs.
title: Five-Rung Refutation Test for the Persistent Fade Law

description:
For multi-objective RLHF with a vector reward the KL drift should still be governed by the covariance matrix (trace/2), but the total-variation drift should be the mean Euclidean norm of the centred reward vector, which is not a function of the covariance matrix. This predicts a genuine multi-objective phenomenon invisible to KL-based analysis.

For r : Ω → ℝ^k and temperature β, β·‖π_β − p‖₁ → 𝔼_p‖r − 𝔼_p r‖ and β²·KL(π_β‖p) → tr(Cov_p(r))/2; the first limit is not determined by Cov_p(r).

Formalize the scalar proof with s_y = ⟨θ, r y − 𝔼r⟩/β replaced by a vector inner product; exhibit two vector rewards with equal covariance matrices but different 𝔼‖r − 𝔼r‖ and compute both drifts numerically.

Multi-objective alignment needs a norm-based, not covariance-based, drift budget.

The vector L¹ law collapses to a covariance functional, meaning the L¹/L² distinction is an artifact of dimension one.
proof_strategy: Termwise Taylor bound |e^x − 1 − x| ≤ x² applied to x = ⟨direction, centred reward⟩/β, then the same triangle-inequality transfer as RLHF.abs_l1_numerator_sub_mad, with 𝔼_p‖·‖ replacing 𝔼_p|·|.
title: Vector-Reward Drift and the Failure of Covariance Sufficiency

description:
The argmax of the cost law is decided by the sup-norm accuracy of the cumulative mean acceptance, and the stability theorem already converts accuracy into a margin condition. Conjecture: for a measured margin g between the best and second-best depth over a sweep of horizon D, n = O(D^2 log(D/delta) / g^2) prompts per cell suffice for the sweep argmax to equal the population argmax with probability at least 1 - delta. This replaces per-position instrumentation by a sample-size prescription on aggregates only.

Let m_hat(d) be the empirical mean acceptance over n i.i.d. prompts with per-prompt accepted counts in [0, D]. If min over d != d0 of (gain(d0) - gain(d)) > 2 D epsilon and n >= D^2 log(2 D / delta) / (2 epsilon^2), then with probability at least 1 - delta the empirical argmax over {1..D} equals the population argmax.

Combine a Hoeffding bound for each of the D cells with a union bound, then feed the resulting sup-norm accuracy into argmax_stable; instantiate with the measured prose margin 0.0764 and code margin 0.1468.

The NET-96 conclusion can be certified at a stated confidence from aggregate throughput alone, with an explicit prompt budget.

Aggregate concentration is too weak at realistic n, which would make direct per-position logging mandatory for any certified claim.
proof_strategy: Per-cell Hoeffding gives |m_hat(d) - m(d)| <= epsilon with probability 1 - delta/D; a union bound over d <= D gives a uniform event on which argmax_stable applies verbatim.
title: Sample-Size Law for a Certified Speculation Optimum

description:
The equilibrium law says the optimal depth is where per-position survival crosses c times throughput. Reading it backwards, each observed optimum under a different overhead c pins the survival curve between two consecutive values. Conjecture: a sweep over k distinct overheads determines the survival curve to within an explicit interval at k positions, with no per-position logging at all.

For antitone s and overheads c₁ < … < c_k with optima d₁ ≥ … ≥ d_k, one has s_{d_j} < c_j·gain(c_j, s, d_j) ≤ s_{d_j - 1} for each j, and these intervals are nonempty and shrink as k grows.

Formalize the two-sided sandwich from marginal_neg_iff_survival_below_throughput plus optimal_depth_antitone_in_cost, then instantiate on a synthetic geometric curve and check interval widths.

Per-position acceptance becomes measurable from throughput alone, sidestepping the (2i+1)δ amplification entirely.

Some survival curves are indistinguishable by any overhead sweep, which itself would be a clean identifiability obstruction.
proof_strategy: Combine the equilibrium iff at the optimum with the nonnegativity of the marginal one step earlier; monotonicity of optima in c comes from marginal_antitone_in_cost.
title: Overhead-Sweep Identifiability of the Survival Curve

description:
Real traffic mixes registers. Since the cost law is linear in the survival curve, the mixture λ sᴬ + (1-λ) sᴮ has gain equal to the same convex combination of the two gains. Conjecture: the optimal depth of the mixture always lies between the two register optima and is monotone in λ, so mixed-traffic tuning needs no new measurement.

If d_A and d_B are global optima for antitone sᴬ, sᴮ with d_A ≤ d_B, then every global optimum of λ sᴬ + (1-λ) sᴮ lies in [d_A, d_B], and the least optimum is monotone nondecreasing in λ for the curve with the deeper optimum.

Prove gain c (λ s + (1-λ) t) d = λ gain c s d + (1-λ) gain c t d, then bound the marginal of the mixture; instantiate on proseSurv and codeSurv at λ = 1/2.

A single interpolation formula tunes deployment depth for arbitrary traffic mixes from two per-register sweeps.

Mixtures can have optima outside the hull, meaning register detection (not interpolation) is required at serve time.
proof_strategy: Linearity of accept in s gives linearity of gain; the marginal of the mixture is the mixture of marginals, so sign changes are trapped between the two crossing points.
title: Mixture Interpolation of Register Optima

description:
For geometric survival the optimal depth is bracketed between log((1-r)/c)/log(1/r) and the first d with rᵈ(1+cd) < c, both Θ(log 1/c). Conjecture: the bracket collapses, i.e. d*(c)·log(1/r) - log(1/c) stays bounded as c → 0, so the slope of measured d* against log(1/c) estimates 1/log(1/r).
