There is a constant K depending only on r such that |d*(c)·log(1/r) - log(1/c)| ≤ K for all sufficiently small c > 0, where d*(c) is any global optimum for geomSurv r.

Sharpen geom_depth_upper_bound by absorbing the (1+cd) factor via a log-log estimate, then combine with geom_depth_log_lower_bound.

The acceptance rate r is measurable purely from how the optimal depth responds to thread count or quantization.

The (1+cd) verification term contributes a genuinely unbounded correction, so depth-versus-overhead plots cannot be read as acceptance-rate measurements.
proof_strategy: Show rᵈ(1+cd) < c holds as soon as d ≥ (log(1/c) + log log(1/c) + C)/log(1/r), using d ≤ 2^{d log(1/r)/2} to dominate the linear factor.
title: Logarithmic Depth Exponent Recovers the Acceptance Rate

description:
The proved ceiling Var >= rho*sigma^2/k says precision at the u>=9-14 frontier is limited by the number of semiprime moduli, not by samples per modulus. Conjecture that the observed 3-5% deficit cannot be resolved at k=128 for any m, and quantify the k needed.

For intra-modulus correlation rho > 0, no run with k moduli can certify a deviation smaller than z*sqrt(rho)*sigma/sqrt(k), independently of the number of samples per modulus.

Combine ClusterModel.var_grandMean_ge_cluster_floor with the z-threshold to derive a minimal-k theorem, then evaluate at the observed deficit.

The frontier is pushed only by enlarging the modulus population; wall-clock spent on longer runs is provably misallocated.

Intra-modulus correlation is zero to within measurement, and sample-count scaling is restored.
proof_strategy: Chain the cluster floor with the gate inequality and solve for k; sharpness follows from the attained limit as m tends to infinity.
title: Cluster-Count Barrier at the Scale-Smoothness Frontier

description:
The master bound Var >= sigma^2/|U| over all weightings gives the smallest deviation an entire lineage of runs could ever certify, computable from the union of consumed draws before any new compute is spent.

A lineage that has consumed |U| distinct draws cannot certify a relative deviation below c*sigma/sqrt(|U|) at level c, whatever analysis is applied afterwards.

Combine Design.var_combo_ge_distinct_draws with the z-threshold; instantiate at the union of exp567, exp569 and exp569b draws.

Every future leg comes with a computable minimum size for the effect it can decide, ending post-hoc reweighting disputes.

Some estimator outside the linear-in-draws class beats the floor, which would itself be a significant methodological finding.
proof_strategy: Chebyshev's sum inequality on the coefficient vector of the pooled linear form, with equality exactly at the uniform weighting.
title: Distinct-Draw Floor as a Pre-Registration Requirement

description:
If an orthogonal family of m dials misses the H1 bar, then every member has squared correlation below 0.30/m. Read contrapositively, explaining a dispersion index of 7.27 requires at least one mechanism of strength r² ≥ (D−1)/(m·D). The conjecture is that the true carrier is concentrated: a single mechanism with r² ≥ 0.25, not a diffuse sum of weak ones.

Any orthogonal explanatory family for the exp-576 log-rates that meets Σ_j r_j² ≥ 0.30 contains a member with r_j² ≥ 0.25.

Orthogonalize the recorded dials plus candidate structural covariates (p−q gap, class-number proxies, smoothness of p±1) and inspect the largest individual share against Logic.QRDial.family_capture_bound.

The search for the carrier can be restricted to single strong covariates, drastically shrinking the mechanism space.

The carrier is diffuse, and only high-dimensional joint models can reach the bar — which itself constrains the mechanism.
proof_strategy: Pigeonhole on the exact additive ceiling Σ_j cov²/var, combined with the dispersion floor certified in exp576_residual_dispersion.
title: Carrier-Strength Pigeonhole for Overdispersed Hit Counts

description:
Paper 225's clause 'book at stored P̂ only if raw P̂ was stored' is a special case of a quantitative criterion: booking at a point value is admissible exactly when the inversion cell diameter 2δ/m is below the booking precision. The conjecture is that this criterion reclassifies a positive fraction of ledger anchors, while leaving every feasibility margin intact.

For every anchor in the ledger with storage precision δ and local slope bound m, the booking is point-admissible iff 2δ/m < 10⁻⁴; under this rule all recorded feasibility inequalities S_raw ≤ S_A survive.

Instantiate Logic.AnchorResolution.cell_diam_le and cell_mem_of_close with the recorded (δ, m, L) per anchor, and check the feasibility conclusion with p225_four_margins_hold.

The ledger gains a uniform, checkable admissibility rule replacing case-by-case clauses.

Some anchors are resolution-limited beyond their recorded margins, and those loci need re-derivation rather than rebooking.
proof_strategy: Two-sided bracketing of the resolution cell (expansive lower bound, Lipschitz upper bound) plus the margin-stability lemma.
title: Uniform Resolution-Limit Admissibility Criterion for Booked Anchors

description:
The 2^k branch of the master inequality uses pigeonhole, which is tight only for balanced filters. Replacing the bucket count by an entropy of the bucket-size distribution should give a strictly stronger bound for unbalanced filters, with equality exactly at the uniform filter.

For a filter assigning M slots to buckets with size distribution p, the worst-case speedup satisfies S <= 2^{H_infinity(p)}/(Lambda*Theta), where H_infinity is the min-entropy, and this refines the 2^k bound since H_infinity(p) <= k.

Prove the min-entropy version in Lean as a replacement for exists_large_bucket, then check that master_inequality_of_filter still composes.

The master chain becomes sensitive to filter quality, giving nontrivial bounds for skewed hash functions.

Worst-case bucket size, not entropy, is the right complexity measure, and the pigeonhole bound is already optimal.
proof_strategy: Replace the counting argument by a max-vs-average comparison; the largest fiber has size M*2^{-H_infinity} by definition of min-entropy.
title: Entropy Refinement of the k-Bits Branch

description:
Generalise the query price from a constant c_q to a schedule (c_j) and ask when the census and economics objectives still differ by a constant. The conjecture is that additive rigidity characterises affine schedules exactly. If it fails for convex schedules, the choice between k_opt^cost and k_opt^econ becomes a real modelling decision rather than a bookkeeping convention.

For a price schedule (c_j) the difference (sum_{j<k} c_j + (T0-1)/2^k) - census (2(T0-1)) k is constant in k if and only if c_j is constant; for strictly increasing c_j the two argmin sets differ by an amount that is unbounded as T0 grows.

Formalise the schedule objective in Lean, telescope the increments to get the bracket c_k >= W/2^(k+2), and instantiate with c_j = 1 + eps*j to compare brackets against census_argmin_iff.

The k-taxonomy needs a fourth entry (schedule-optimal budget) whenever query prices are not flat.

Additive rigidity is robust and the three-way taxonomy is complete for all pricing models.
proof_strategy: Increment analysis plus the existing discrete-convexity principle min_of_local_min, which applies verbatim once increments are shown monotone.
title: Convex Price Schedules and Taxonomy Separation

description:
Price the residual scan as (W/2^k)^alpha for 0 < alpha <= 1, modelling cheaper-than-linear residual work. The conjecture is that the continuous optimum offset from log2 W depends only on alpha, giving a one-parameter deformation of the recorded -1.5288 offset.

The continuous minimiser of x + (W 2^(-x))^alpha / 2 sits at log2 W - (1/alpha) log2 (2 / (alpha ln 2)), reducing to log2 W - 1.5288... at alpha = 1.

Differentiate in Lean via the certificate exp(-alpha u) >= 1 - alpha u, the direct generalisation of the proof of econC_min_at_kOptEcon.

A single formula covers all residual-scan cost models, so offsets are comparable across experiments with different scan costs.

Offsets are model-specific and cross-experiment offset comparisons are meaningless.
proof_strategy: Substitute u = (x - x*) alpha ln 2, reuse the convexity certificate, then transfer to the discrete argmin via monotone increments.
title: Sublinear Residual Exponent Family

description:
The flatness factorisation shows that a window's explained variance is the amplitude profile's Rayleigh quotient against the covariate. Conjecture that among all arithmetically computable weight profiles the harmonic profile is optimal up to a bounded factor. Testing this settles whether 1/l is canonical or merely convenient.

For every weight profile w supported on primes below B, the explained variance R2(w) is at most C times R2(1/l) with an absolute constant C, whenever the signal amplitudes satisfy a_l = Theta(1/l).

Formalise R2 for arbitrary weights in the orthonormal model (already available as R2_of_orthonormal) and prove the comparison by Cauchy-Schwarz plus a two-sided amplitude hypothesis; verify numerically on the exp 577 population.

The 1/l dial is canonical: no reweighting can improve it beyond a constant.

There is a strictly better computable dial, and the covariate upgrade is not finished.
proof_strategy: Write R2(w) as an inner-product ratio, apply Cauchy-Schwarz in the amplitude-weighted inner product, and bound the resulting ratio by the two-sided amplitude comparison.
title: Rayleigh-Optimal Weight Profiles for Residue Dials

description:
The flipped dial is the clean dial multiplied by the twist character chi4(l)chi4(N). Conjecture that the covariance of the flipped dial with any fixed target is bounded by a Polya-Vinogradov-type character sum, hence negligible relative to the clean dial's covariance. This would upgrade the erratum from empirical to provable.

For a window P of odd primes and a target bounded by 1, the covariance of the flipped dial with the target is O(sqrt(N) log N) uniformly, while the clean dial's covariance is of order |P|.

Express the covariance as a sum of chi4-twisted Jacobi symbols over the window using jacobi_eq_twist_mul, then apply a character-sum bound.

The paper-226 secondary weakness is provably a form artifact, not arithmetic.

The flipped form carries genuine signal and the erratum must be narrowed.
proof_strategy: Split the window by l mod 4 using dial_forms_agree_on_one_mod_four, then bound the 3 mod 4 part by a multiplicative character sum estimate.
title: Character-Sum Cancellation for the Reciprocity Twist

description:
The unfolded quadratic spectrum has two-level density exactly 2 floor(t), a staircase with plateaus, while Poisson and GUE densities are continuous. Conjecture that a plateau in the limiting two-level density is an absolute obstruction to being the limit of a determinantal or Poisson process.

If the limiting normalized two-level density of a sequence of finite spectra is constant on some interval of positive length, then that sequence is not the empirical spectrum of any determinantal or Poisson point process with continuous correlation kernel.

Prove that determinantal and Poisson two-level densities are strictly increasing, then combine with picket_pairCorr_density_tendsto.

Gives a one-line certificate of non-randomness for deterministic spectra.

Some determinantal process has a plateau, which would be a new and surprising kernel degeneracy.
proof_strategy: Strict monotonicity of t -> integral of the two-point function over |x-y| <= t for a positive continuous kernel, versus the locally constant staircase.
title: Staircase Obstruction to Random-Matrix Statistics

description:
A verifier holding several destructive tests may schedule them adaptively, choosing the next test after seeing the current verdict. The conjecture is that this adaptivity buys nothing beyond reachability in the induced deterministic automaton, so the number of distinct achievable verdict streams stays polynomially bounded in the number of dishes.

For a finite dish type D with n dishes and any battery t_1, ..., t_k of tests, the set of verdict streams obtainable by adaptive schedules has cardinality at most n times the number of dishes reachable from the start, hence at most n^2, with equality only when the residue maps generate a transitive submonoid of End D.

Model schedules as words over the battery alphabet, define the reachable-state automaton, and bound the number of distinct stream functions by the number of reachable Myhill-Nerode classes; check small cases by enumeration for n <= 4 and k <= 3.

Destructive multi-test verification has the same coarse information content as single-test verification, giving a clean composition law for verification batteries.

Adaptive scheduling extracts strictly more information than reachability allows, which would identify a genuinely new resource in destructive verification.
proof_strategy: Show that the stream produced by a schedule depends only on the current state, then apply the Myhill-Nerode collapse for the k-letter automaton on n states, using the single-letter case (transcript_characterization) as the base case.
title: Adaptive Battery Reachability Bound

description:
The Euclid map (m,n) -> (m^2-n^2, 2mn, m^2+n^2) is proved here to be a bijection from nodes to primitive Pythagorean triples with even second leg. Trees built from 3x3 integer matrices acting directly on triples are the classical Barning-Hall picture; the conjecture is that every such tree is the pushforward of one of the three trees on parameter space.

Every ternary tree structure on primitive Pythagorean triples generated by 3x3 integer matrices acting on (x,y,z) is the pushforward along the Euclid map of one of the three trees on the node set; in particular there are exactly three, and no branch matrix has determinant of odd prime absolute value.

Formalise the pushforward of an IntMap to a 3x3 matrix and verify the Barning-Hall matrices are the pushforwards of the Berggren branches; then search 3x3 integer matrices with small entries preserving the primitive-triple set and compare with the three predicted families.

The classification of Pythagorean trees is intrinsic to the triples and independent of the Euclid parametrisation, and the mixed tree yields a previously unlisted 3x3 generating triple.

There is a triple-space tree not induced by any parameter-space tree, so the Euclid parametrisation loses tree structure and the two classification problems genuinely differ.
proof_strategy: Use toTriple_inj and exists_node_of_isPPT to transport covering and injectivity across the bijection; the only new content is that a linear map on triples pulls back to a linear map on parameters, which follows from comparing quadratic forms coefficientwise.
title: Transport of the Classification to Triple-Space Linear Maps

description:
Global separation of the mixture family from the single-law family is proved. The conjecture localises it: any two distinct windows already suffice to exclude every single power law, so a two-number summary is a complete falsification test.

For 0 < w < 1, b₁ ≠ b₂ and any t₁ ≠ t₂ in (0,1) there is no b with edgeFrac b t₁ = mixFrac w b₁ b₂ t₁ and edgeFrac b t₂ = mixFrac w b₁ b₂ t₂.

Compare the single-law curve b ↦ (edgeFrac b t₁, edgeFrac b t₂) with the mixture point using the head/tail comparison lemmas.

Two decile measurements constitute a complete falsification test for the pure power-law form.

There are windows on which a mixture is exactly mimicked, so window selection must be justified.
proof_strategy: Show the single-law curve is the graph of a strictly convex function of the first coordinate and that mixtures lie strictly below it, via strict log-convexity.
title: Two-Window Separation of Bulk-Plus-Spike Profiles

description:
The continuum obstruction proved here should transfer to the discrete counting problem for positions j where j² − N satisfies a fixed arithmetic condition, giving a genuinely arithmetic falsifiable statement rather than a statement about a fitted curve.

Any weak-* limit of the normalised empirical position measures with log-convex density is not a pure power law, and finite-N fitted exponents inherit the window drift up to O(N^{-1/2}).

Formalise the empirical measures, prove tightness, and combine Portmanteau with the log-convexity obstruction.

The bulk+spike description becomes an arithmetic statement about quadratic residues, not merely a curve-fitting summary.

The continuum model would be an artefact of normalisation and the discrete profile could be a genuine power law.
proof_strategy: Uniform density bounds on the counting measure, weak-* compactness, and closedness of multiplicative convexity under limits.
title: Discrete-to-Continuum Transfer for Quadratic Hit Profiles

description:
The mixture weight is now provably identifiable from a single head window, and the window-implied exponent curve is strictly antitone. The conjecture is that the remaining coordinate, the edge exponent b, is recovered by a second window, making the full mixture identifiable. This turns the recorded edge statistics into parameter estimates rather than a paradox.

For fixed a and n, the map (w, b) -> (impliedExp(m1), impliedExp(m2)) is injective on (0,1) x (a, infinity) for any 1 <= m1 < m2 < n.

Building on mixHeadMass_strictMono_weight, determine the sign of the head mass derivative in b and apply a two-dimensional monotone-map injectivity criterion.

Edge fraction plus first decile determine the edge component; the recorded triple becomes an over-determined consistency check.

Distinct edge components are observationally equivalent on two windows, and a third statistic is mandatory.
proof_strategy: Strict monotonicity in w follows from headMass_lt_of_exponent_lt via the mediant identity; monotonicity in b is delicate, since raising b steepens the edge but lowers the mass it carries, so the Jacobian sign must be computed rather than guessed.
title: Edge-Exponent Recovery from Two Head Windows

description:
The window-implied exponent of a bulk x edge mixture is now known to be strictly decreasing in the window width, but with no modulus. The conjecture supplies one, converting a qualitative diagnostic into a test with power: it states how far apart two recorded window exponents must lie before a second component is certified.

There is kappa(w, b-a) > 0 with c(m1) - c(m2) >= kappa(w, b-a) * log(m2/m1) / log n for all 1 <= m1 < m2 < n.

Replace the strict convexity input by its quantitative form (the exp-convexity defect on an interval of length L is at least a constant times L^2) and propagate the defect through the prefix-sum argument.

Recorded window exponents can be converted into a lower bound on the mixture weight and on the edge-bulk exponent gap.

The gap degenerates for extreme weights, and window statistics detect a second component only qualitatively.
proof_strategy: Bound the convexity defect of t -> A e^{alpha t} + B e^{gamma t} from below on the log-window, then track the resulting strict surplus in the discrepancy prefix sums.
title: Quantitative Gap for the Strict Window Law

description:
A finitely supported perturbation of the head of a pure power law also inflates narrow-window exponents. The conjecture is that the two mechanisms are separated by the eventual shape of the implied-exponent curve: eventually constant for a contamination, strictly decreasing at every width for a mixture.

If the kernel is a pure power law outside a finite head set, the window-implied exponent is eventually constant in m; for a genuine two-component mixture it is strictly decreasing for all m.

Formalise the contamination claim for the discrete kernel family (finite support of the discrepancy makes prefix sums stabilise) and combine it with implied_exponent_strictAnti.

The recorded edge statistics can be classified as mixture-like or contamination-like without any new experiment.

Head statistics cannot separate the two mechanisms and a tail-side statistic is required.
proof_strategy: For contamination, the discrepancy sequence has finite support, so prefix sums stabilise; for mixtures, the strict single-crossing law forbids stabilisation.
title: Mixture Versus Head Contamination Discriminator

description:
NET-95 compared a toy RTN quantiser at small scale with k-quants at 7B scale, confounding quantiser quality with model scale. block_scaling_is_a_bit_shift shows the quality half is exactly log2(R / rms r) bits, computable from the weight tensors alone. The conjecture is that at fixed scale the two ladders are rigid translates of each other by that many bits.

At fixed model and slice, the excess-perplexity curves of a globally scaled RTN quantiser and a per-block k-quant satisfy E_kquant(b) = E_RTN(b - log2(R / rms r)) up to the measurement noise floor, with log2(R / rms r) at most (1/2) log2 B.

Quantise the same 7B model with RTN and with k-quants at 8, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 bpw; compute R and rms r from the weight tensors; check whether the two curves superpose after the predicted horizontal shift.

The floor is fully attributable to quantiser quality, closing the documented confound and making floor location a tensor statistic.

Scale contributes independently of range profile, implying calibration exploits structure beyond dynamic range (e.g. Hessian anisotropy).
proof_strategy: Combine block_scaling_is_a_bit_shift with quantizer_quality_is_a_bit_shift: both reduce a change in error constant to a translation in bit width, provided the curvature model's error constant is the only channel through which the quantiser acts.
title: Fixed-Scale Separation of Round-to-Nearest and k-Quant Ladders

description:
A per-bit multiplier bounded by 3 keeps excess perplexity finite at every bit width, but perplexity is bounded above by the unigram-entropy ceiling of the corpus. The two facts are incompatible below some bit width, so the geometric band must break; the conjecture pins where.

There is a bit width b* in (1, 2.6) at which the measured per-bit multiplier first exceeds 3, and beyond which excess perplexity saturates rather than grows geometrically; b* is determined by the point at which quantised weights retain less than one bit of information per parameter.

Extend the ladder with iq2_xxs, iq2_s and iq1_s arms on the same rig; compute per-bit multipliers with the exact-rational band test of weight_ladder_geometric_band.

The floor exists after all, but as a saturation ceiling rather than a cliff, and its location is an information-theoretic constant of the architecture.

Geometry persists to sub-1-bit widths, which would contradict any capacity argument and force a revision of the curvature model.
proof_strategy: Formalise the entropy ceiling as an upper bound on perplexity, then show that a geometric lower bound on excess with ratio > 1 must eventually exceed it, yielding existence of a breakdown point by a discrete intermediate-value argument.
title: Breakdown Point of the Geometric Bit-Width Band

description:
Strict convexity of excess perplexity in bit width was proved for the measured k-quant ladder over all ten triples. The conjecture is that convexity is a necessary condition for a Pareto-efficient quantiser family: a concave kink identifies a rung that is dominated by interpolating its neighbours.

For any quantiser family whose rungs are Pareto-optimal in the (bits, quality) plane, the excess-perplexity curve is convex in the bit width; conversely, a concave triple exhibits a rung strictly improvable by mixed-precision interpolation between its neighbours.

Run the convexity check of weight_ladder_convex on additional families (iq3_xxs, iq4_nl, awq, gptq); for any concave triple, build the interpolating mixed-precision model and verify it dominates.

Convexity becomes a cheap automated audit for new quantisation formats, and any violation is an actionable design bug.

Some genuinely Pareto-optimal families are concave, meaning bit width is the wrong x-axis and the correct cost coordinate is something else (e.g. effective bits after entropy coding).
proof_strategy: Formalise mixed-precision interpolation as a convex combination of rungs in the (bits, excess) plane and show that a concave triple yields an interpolant with strictly lower excess at equal average bit width; the converse direction is the audit statement.
title: Convexity Audit for Quantiser Families

description:
The hump vertex is an invariant of the pair (profile, grid parametrisation), not of the profile alone. Reparametrising the window before fitting transports the vertex by an explicit amount, and an equal-u grid is exactly such a reparametrisation. This is the only registered channel not already excluded by the left-of-centre obstruction.

For a strictly increasing smooth phi : [0,1] -> [a,b], the vertex of gap (f . phi) 0 1 is phi^{-1} of a point strictly right of the vertex of gap f a b whenever phi' is increasing; for the equal-u grid on j^2 - N the shift is large enough to carry a left-edge vertex past the window centre.

Define reparametrised gap in Lean, prove the transported vertex equation f'(phi(y)) phi'(y) = chord slope, and evaluate for phi induced by equal steps in u = log v / log B.

The measured 0.5901 is a property of the u-grid, not of the arithmetic; the hump question is answered and closes the 228-229-231 thread.

The vertex is grid-robust as well as sign-robust, and the carrier lies outside the window-geometry channel entirely.
proof_strategy: Chain rule on the vertex equation plus the existing StrictAntiOn/MVT machinery; monotonicity of the transported slope in phi'.
title: Reference Reparametrisation as the Vertex Carrier

description:
R = T/M compares a bin average of a smoothness density with that density at a bin summary value, so log R is a Jensen gap proportional to the within-bin variance of log v times the curvature of the density. On j^2 - N that variance is an explicit function of window position with an interior maximum, giving a hump that owes nothing to a chord reference.

log R(x) = (1/2) (d^2/du^2 log rho)(u(x)) * Var_bin(log v) + O(third moment), and for the window value profile x(x+2c) the bin variance of log v, at fixed bin width, has an interior maximum whose location depends on c.

Formalise the second-order Jensen expansion for a log-convex density and compute Var_bin(log v) for logSize c on equal-width bins; compare the predicted amplitude scaling in bin width against the bin-width permutation probe already formalised.

A hump with an interior, tunable vertex arises with no chord reference, escaping vertex_lt_midpoint and supplying a genuine carrier.

The Jensen route predicts the wrong amplitude scaling in bin width and is eliminated by the same permutation probe, leaving no registered geometric carrier at all.
proof_strategy: Taylor expansion with explicit remainder for a C^2 log-density; explicit computation of the second moment of logSize c over a bin using the concavity bounds proved here.
title: Jensen Gap of the Smoothness Density across a Bin

description:
The proved bound 2^(2n) on countermodel size for the temporal Gödel–Löb calculus is exponential, but the filtration measure shows all depth is linear in the number of boxed subformulas. We conjecture that a selective canonical model, generated only from the worlds actually demanded by the existence lemmas, has polynomially many worlds. This would turn a decision procedure that is currently doubly exponential in the search space into a tractable one.

For every non-derivable A there is a TempFrame countermodel with at most p(subformulaCount A) worlds for a fixed polynomial p; and at most subformulaCount A + 1 worlds when A has no implication nested under a box.

Replace CanW by the closure of the refuting world under exists_box_succ and exists_glob_succ, bound its cardinality by the recursion depth, and compare with the verified minimal countermodels of size 1 and 2 recorded in ComputationalEvidence.md.

finite_model_property_sharp upgrades from an exponential to a polynomial bound, and bounded model search for TGL becomes practical.

An explicit formula family with exponentially large minimal countermodels exists, proving the 2^n bound essentially tight and closing the tightness question.
proof_strategy: Induct on the filtration measure boxCount: each application of exists_box_succ strictly increases it, so the generated subframe is a tree of depth at most the number of boxed subformulas; bound the branching by the number of boxed subformulas not yet realised.
title: Polynomial Width Collapse for Temporal Löb Countermodels

description:
The scale-free bound 100 (j^2 - N) < 45 N for first-decile points is proved for N >= 2^16 and fails at N = 36482. We conjecture 36483 is the exact threshold, making the size hypothesis optimal.

For every N >= 36483 and every j with s < j and 5(j - s) < s + 5 one has 100 (j^2 - N) < 45 N, and N = 36482 admits a first-decile j violating it.

Prove the inequality for N >= 36931 by the existing 192 sqrt N + 64 < N route and close [36483, 36930] by an explicit decidable enumeration over s = floor(sqrt N).

The degeneracy mechanism is optimal and fully characterised at every scale.

A second exceptional modulus above 36482 exists, revealing an extra rounding phenomenon in the decile definition.
proof_strategy: Split into an asymptotic range handled by existing arithmetic and a finite range handled by enumeration.
title: Sharp Threshold 36483 for the Scale-Free 0.44 Constant

description:
Recovery of a length-k Berggren control word from one state in (ℤ/m)³ is possible for very large m and impossible for small m; this cycle brackets the transition between 3^{k/3} and 5·7^k. The conjecture is that the true transition is at m ≍ 7^{αk} with α = log 3 / log 7. The route is an average-case growth estimate for the hypotenuse along a random branch.

There is α = log 3 / log 7 such that modular seed recovery of length-k words is possible for m ≥ 7^{(α+ε)k} and impossible for m ≤ 7^{(α−ε)k}, for every ε > 0 and all large k.

Compute the distribution of log c after k random moves (a random walk with three explicit multiplicative steps) and compare the resulting typical modulus with the counting obstruction 3^k.

The security parameter of any Berggren-based construction is pinned exactly: modulus size must be sub-7^{αk} to be safe.

The transition is governed by the worst-case rather than the typical branch, meaning rare heavy branches dominate the recoverability question.
proof_strategy: Upgrade hyp_applyWord_le to a per-branch estimate; use a large-deviation bound for the sum of the three log-factors; combine with mod_ambiguity_lower_bound on the other side.
title: Silver-Ratio Phase Transition for Modular Seed Recovery

description:
The fitted exponent alpha-hat = 1/2 is conjectured to be exact, not a grid artifact: for QR indicators over primes in a window, the R^2-optimal weight exponent converges to 1/2 as the window grows. The approach is to combine the existence theorem for a maximizer with the exact window-mass order B^(1-alpha).

For the QR product dial with window [3, B] and any fixed bit length, the maximizer alpha*(B) of R^2 satisfies alpha*(B) -> 1/2 as B -> infinity.

Refine the alpha grid to step 0.05 on the same exp-577 counts, and repeat at windows B = 100, 200, 400, 800; formalize the limit statement using OptimalExponent.exists_interior_max_R2 as the existence input.

The canonical covariate acquires a derivation rather than a fit, and all downstream dial computations inherit an exact parameter.

The optimum is window-dependent and every saturation and cut-off constant must be re-measured per window.
proof_strategy: Write R^2(alpha) as a ratio of finite sums, use log-convexity of S_alpha to control the numerator, and match the window-mass envelope 3*4^(-alpha) B^(1-alpha) <= T_alpha(B) <= 3 B^(1-alpha) against the variance of the response.
title: Square-Root Optimality of the Product-Dial Weight

description:
At the optimum the derivative of R^2 vanishes; differentiating the finite sums turns this into a balance between the weighted covariance of log(ell) with the response and the weighted variance of log(ell). This converts exponent fitting from a grid search into solving one scalar equation.

alpha* solves cov(y, d/dalpha S_alpha) * var(S_alpha) = cov(y, S_alpha) * cov(S_alpha, d/dalpha S_alpha), where d/dalpha S_alpha = -sum_ell log(ell) ell^(-alpha).

Formalize differentiability of alpha |-> S_alpha (finite sum of const^alpha) and derive the first-order condition; check numerically that the solution lies in [0.45, 0.55] on the exp-577 data.

The exponent can be estimated at full precision from the same data, removing the +/-0.25 grid limitation.

R^2 is not differentiable-in-practice at the optimum, indicating a non-smooth or multi-modal landscape.
proof_strategy: Differentiate under the finite sum, apply the quotient rule to cov^2/(var*var), and use strict log-convexity to rule out degenerate stationary points.
title: Stationarity Equation for the Fitted Exponent

description:
Log-rate regression on Poisson counts attenuates R^2 but is claimed to leave the argmax intact. Strict log-convexity of the weight family provides the identifiability needed to make this a theorem rather than a heuristic.

If counts are Poisson with log-mean affine in S_{alpha_true}, then the population argmax of the log-rate R^2 equals alpha_true, and the sample argmax converges to it as the number of data points grows.

Simulate Poisson counts from a known alpha_true on the recorded supports and check recovery; formalize the population statement using the strict Cauchy-Schwarz inequality proved here.

Bootstrap confidence intervals for alpha-hat gain a theoretical justification.

The reported CI [0.5, 0.5] measures grid rigidity rather than statistical precision.
proof_strategy: Show the population R^2 is uniquely maximized at alpha_true using strict non-proportionality of distinct exponent covariates, then apply a uniform law of large numbers over a compact exponent interval.
title: Argmax Consistency Under Poisson Attenuation

description:
Realisability of a single interior argmax was proved this cycle (interior_argmax_realizable). The successor conjecture asks for control of the entire argmax landscape: any admissible pattern of local maxima should be realisable by a suitable response, which would mean that multi-modal bootstrap argmax distributions carry no structural information at all.

For orthogonal columns of equal mass and any subset T of {1,...,m} containing no two consecutive integers, there is a response whose unit-weight window curve has exactly T as its set of strict local maxima.

Concatenate the formalised dip witness a = (3,1,1) into blocks, one per element of T, and verify the resulting curve pattern in Lean by the exact step law.

The shape of an observed window curve constrains only the response, so no number of modes should be read as structure of the column family.

Some patterns of local maxima are impossible, and the observed pattern does constrain the underlying signal profile.
proof_strategy: Induct on blocks: after each block the running numerator and mass are known, and the step law decides the sign of each increment; choose block sizes so that each new block overtakes the running mean exactly once.
title: Prescribed Local-Maximum Sets for Window Curves

description:
Saturation locations are read off a factor-two grid. The conjecture makes precise what such a grid can resolve: the continuous argmax is pinned only to within one grid cell, and any two locations inside a cell are indistinguishable from grid values.

Given the values of a signal-then-noise window curve at the grid points B_0 < 2B_0 < 4B_0 < ..., for any two candidate continuous argmax locations lying in the same cell there exist two models reproducing all grid values exactly and having those two argmax locations.

Formalise a continuous-window version of the model (mass measure on the index axis) and construct the two matching models explicitly, verifying equality of grid values by the peak-margin identity.

Reported saturation locations must always be quoted as cells, and refinement claims below one factor-two step are unsupported by the data.

Grid values do constrain the location beyond the cell, and a finer estimator can be extracted from the same measurements.
proof_strategy: Use the peak-margin identity to express grid values as functions of the accumulated mass at the grid points only, then redistribute mass inside a cell while keeping the endpoint masses fixed.
title: Grid Resolution Limits for Saturation Locations

description:
Generators that draw the two primes from different bit lengths push the ratio past 2, so the small factor exits the canonical window. The conjecture is that this is total rather than gradual: with a skew of k bits the in-window fraction is exactly zero and no admissible window multiplier below 2^k restores it.

If 2^(b-1) <= p < 2^b and 2^(b+k-1) <= q < 2^(b+k) with k >= 1, then p*q >= 2*p*p, so the small factor is never in the canonical window; and the R-window contains it only if R >= 2^k.

Formalise directly from window_iff_balanced (an inequality on naturals), then generalise the R-window membership criterion to q < R*p and instantiate.

The in_win column is a pure function of bit-length skew, and the ascending order is undefined (not merely slower) for skewed generators.

Some skewed pairs remain in-window, so window membership depends on finer arithmetic than bit lengths.
proof_strategy: Nat inequalities: q >= 2^(b+k-1) >= 2*2^(b-1) > p gives q >= 2p directly; the R-window case is window_iff_balanced with 2 replaced by R.
title: Bit-Length Skew and Window Extinction

description:
Descent certificates form a complete proof system for statements of the form forall n >= 1, p n, while finite checking alone is unsound. Defining the certificate complexity as the least admissible window N, the conjecture is that it is finite for every true statement but not computable, relocating open conjectures from unbounded verification to the search for one reduction function.

The function taking a decidable predicate p with forall n >= 1, p n to the least N admitting a descent certificate is total but not computable; for the Collatz predicate it is finite iff the Collatz conjecture holds.

Formalise the totality from descentCertificate_nonempty_iff and derive non-computability by reduction from the halting problem for fuelled checkers.

Bounded verification effort can be reported as a lower bound on certificate complexity, giving a principled stopping rule for certified search.

Certificate complexity would be computable, yielding a decision procedure for a large family of universal arithmetic statements.
proof_strategy: Totality: the trivial certificate of descentCertificate_nonempty_iff. Non-computability: encode halting into the base window using truncate.
title: Certificate Complexity of Universal Statements

description:
For a geometric local density the relative edge weight of a band of 2m cells is exactly tanh(m log(1/r)/2). The conjecture extends this to regularly varying densities with local log-slope alpha, predicting exponential decay of the apparent edge component away from a truncation boundary. It matters because it predicts the observed sub-bar/absent pattern quantitatively rather than qualitatively.

For a density with local log-slope alpha at the truncation point, the relative edge weight of the adjacent band of width 2m satisfies w = tanh(alpha m / 2) (1 + o(1)), hence decays like exp(-alpha m).

Sandwich the density between geometric majorants and minorants with slopes alpha +- epsilon and formalise the two-sided bound.

A closed-form null prediction for edge weights at any truncation, removing the need for post-hoc fits.

The boundary effect is not slope-local, and edge weights must be modelled globally.
proof_strategy: Monotone comparison of sums, using the exact geometric identity and the linear envelope already proved.
title: Tanh Scaling of Truncation-Boundary Edge Weight

description:
The higher-order convexity guess of the previous cycle is refuted: the third core layer conv 2 is an exact quasi-polynomial of degree 3 and period 2, whose third difference equals -(t+2) at 2t and +(t+3) at 2t+1, and a itself fails 3-convexity at n = 7. The data instead show a rigid parity law for the sign of the third difference of a, which is the natural replacement conjecture.

For every odd n ≥ 7, a(n+3) + 3a(n+1) < 3a(n+2) + a(n), and for every even n ≥ 8 the reverse strict inequality holds; equivalently sign(Δ³a(n)) = (-1)^n for n ≥ 7.

Extend the exact quasi-polynomial computation from conv 2 to conv b via the b-step peeling recurrence generalizing conv_two_step, isolate the period-2 component of each layer, and bound the contribution of layers with k ≥ C n^{1/2} by the uniform Rankin estimate; check the pattern numerically far beyond the 32-term table.

The counting function has an exactly periodic third-difference sign law, a strong rigidity statement for a sequence with no product formula.

The first n where the parity law fails marks the point where a layer of period > 2 overtakes the period-2 component, quantifying the arithmetic depth of the model.
proof_strategy: Layer-by-layer quasi-polynomial expansion (proved for k = 3 in StackSquareCoreLayerThree), plus tail control from log p_{≤b}(m) ≤ 8√m + 12 for the layers of large core size.
title: Parity-Alternating Third Differences of Square-Core Counts

description:
The layer decomposition makes the core size k a random variable under the uniform measure on square-core stacks of area n. Saddle-point analysis predicts concentration at k ≈ (log 2)√(6n)/π with fluctuations of order n^{1/4}, matching the observed maximizing layers at n = 100 and 200.

Under the uniform measure on square-core stacks of area n, k/√n → (log 2)√6/π ≈ 0.5404 in probability, and (k - c√n)/n^{1/4} converges to a centered Gaussian.

Prove exponentially small tail bounds for layers with k ≥ C√n and k ≤ ε√n using the uniform bound log p_{≤b}(m) ≤ 8√m + 12, then a local expansion of the layer free energy.

The square core behaves as a sharply concentrated order parameter, giving a genuine limit theorem for a shape-constrained polyomino ensemble.

The measure spreads over many core sizes, which would signal a degenerate or first-order transition instead of the predicted smooth saddle.
proof_strategy: Uniform Rankin bounds for the tails plus a two-term expansion of log L_k(n) around the saddle; the concavity of u ↦ -u² + 2G(u) supplies the required strict maximum.
title: Core-Size Concentration and Its Fluctuation Scale

description:
Guaranteed stage-1 success over the whole Hasse window requires the scalar to be divisible by every prime in the window, hence to have bit length of order p / log p. The conjecture asserts this is optimal over all schedules, so the wall region is exponential-cost certainty rather than failure.

Any scalar k such that every integer in [p+1-2 sqrt p, p+1+2 sqrt p] divides k satisfies log2 k >= (1+o(1)) p / log p.

Formalize: such a k is divisible by every prime in the window; then bound the product of those primes from below using a Chebyshev-type estimate for primes in a short interval.

The recorded wall is definitively reinterpreted as a cost law; no algorithmic exploitation of the certainty regime is possible.

There exists a sub-exponential certificate schedule, which would be a genuine algorithmic advance for ECM.
proof_strategy: Primes in the window divide k; product of primes in an interval of length 4 sqrt p around p is exp((1+o(1)) * 4 sqrt p) by PNT in short intervals, and adding all window integers forces divisibility by lcm of the window, whose log is asymptotically p / log p by Chebyshev.
title: Cost-Certainty Tradeoff Law for lcm Schedules

description:
Generalize the four-outcome ledger to moduli with k prime factors: each trial reveals the subset S of primes whose order completed. The conjecture is that these subsets behave as independent Bernoulli coordinates with the exact rates gcd(m_i, k(B))/m_i, giving closed-form multi-prime ECM success probabilities.

For N = p_1...p_k and a uniformly random point, the events {order completes mod p_i} are independent with probabilities gcd(m_i, lcm(1..B))/m_i, so P(reveal a proper factor) = 1 - prod(1-r_i) - prod(r_i).

Formalize independence for the CRT product of cyclic groups (a direct product argument extending card_firingSet_prod), then verify the resulting formula numerically for k = 3.

Exact multi-prime ECM success formulas replace the single-prime heuristic, and the dead outcome gets an exact probability.

Correlations between group orders at distinct primes exist, which is itself a statement about curve-order distributions.
proof_strategy: CRT decomposition of the point group, product formula for firing sets (card_firingSet_prod), inclusion-exclusion for the reveal event.
title: Outcome Algebra of CRT-Guarded Inversions

description:
The candidate values j^2 - N meet each odd prime p on 1 + chi_p(N) residues, so the per-modulus smoothness bias is a product of factors 2 or 0. Conjecture: stratifying the modulus population by its quadratic-character profile removes essentially all of the observed sub-1 drift and shrinks the cluster-bootstrap spread by the predicted factor. This turns a null result into a structural explanation.

For a population of moduli stratified by S(N) = sum over p <= 100 of chi_p(N), the within-stratum smoothness ratio of x^2 - N against size-matched controls tends to 1 with variance O(1/m), while the unstratified estimator has variance bounded below by (2^k - 1)/m.

Re-run the 128-cluster design with strata. The structural half is already formalized: U9Drift.classCount_stratification_is_exact shows the class-count strata carry zero within-stratum dispersion of the multiplicative bias, so what remains is to persist per-cluster counts keyed by the class count and evaluate the stratified point estimate.

The band-9 drift is fully explained as a quadratic-class sampling fluctuation; no new smoothness phenomenon at u ~ 9.

A residual deviation survives conditioning, which would be a genuine arithmetic effect beyond the local densities.
proof_strategy: Multiplicativity of the local densities over distinct primes, then the sign-product moment computation of U9Drift.mean_signProd applied stratum-wise.
title: Quadratic-Class Stratification of the Smoothness Ratio

description:
Any true deviation of the smooth density from the Dickman model should carry the finite-size signature log log v / log v rather than a constant factor. Conjecture: the band-indexed ratio r(u) satisfies r(u) - 1 = c * log log v / log v + o(...), so a slope estimate across bands is better powered than a single-band ratio.

There is c such that across bands the measured ratio satisfies |r(u) - 1 - c * loglog v / log v| < epsilon uniformly on 6 <= u <= 14.

Estimate the slope across bands 6-14 at fixed per-band precision; formalize the monotonicity and window bounds of the correction and the induced ordering of band ratios.

The drift question is answered by a one-parameter fit with far more power than any single band.

Deviations are band-idiosyncratic, pointing to a modulus-population artifact rather than an analytic correction.
proof_strategy: Combine the antitone finite-size correction with the exact local densities to bound the band-to-band ratio difference.
title: Logarithmic Slope Test for the Dickman Approach Zone

description:
Because the per-modulus bias has variance exponential in the number of small primes, the estimator's spread is governed by the number of distinct moduli and not by the number of candidate/control pairs. Conjecture: beyond a modest pairs-per-modulus threshold, the cluster-bootstrap half width is independent of the pair count.

The half width of the cluster-bootstrap interval is c/sqrt(m) + O(1/(m*sqrt(n_per))) with c determined by the between-modulus variance; in particular doubling n_per at fixed m cannot reduce the half width by more than the second-order term.

Two runs at equal m and 1x/4x pairs per modulus. The structural half is now closed: U9Drift.cluster_bootVar_eq proves the cluster-bootstrap variance is exactly betweenVar/m, with no within-cluster term, so what remains is to measure betweenVar from persisted per-cluster counts.

Future runs should buy moduli, not samples; the 10-30x ask becomes a 10-30x cluster ask.

Within-cluster noise still dominates at these rates, meaning the rare-event regime is not yet in the asymptotic zone.
proof_strategy: Law-of-total-variance decomposition for the clustered ratio estimator, with the between term computed by the sign-product second moment.
title: Cluster-Count Power Law for Smoothness Ratio Studies

description:
For indicator outcomes the gain from pairing is exactly twice the excess joint smooth rate over independence. Conjecture: in the band-9 design this excess is negligible, so the paired matching contributes no variance reduction and the design can be simplified without loss.

The empirical covariance of the candidate and control smoothness indicators satisfies |Cov| < 0.05 * sqrt(Var_cand * Var_ctrl) at band 9.

Persist joint counts in the patched writer and evaluate Cov = r - p q directly; the Lean identities evar_sub_indicator and paired_design_gain_iff turn the counts into a decision.

Pairing is decorative at these rates; control integrity must be argued from the identical code path alone.

Pairing is load-bearing and any unpaired re-analysis of past rounds is anti-conservative.
proof_strategy: Empirical variance decomposition plus Cauchy-Schwarz, already formalized as U9Drift.evar_sub and U9Drift.ecov_sq_le.
title: Measurable Value of Paired Control Matching

description:
Banking a direction-stable observation is a sign test whose null probability is 2^(1-k) for k split-halves. Conjecture: adopting k >= 6 as a pre-registration gate removes essentially all historical banked-tension entries that later failed to replicate, at no additional compute cost.

For every banked direction-stable tension recorded with k <= 5 split-halves, the associated null probability exceeds 0.05; and a k >= 6 gate is achievable by re-partitioning existing samples.

Recompute split-half depth for each banked entry and apply split_halves_needed_for_significance; formalize the multiple-comparison correction across the ledger.

A cheap, purely statistical gate that prevents future over-banking.

Some banked entries had genuine depth and their tensions deserve full-power follow-up.
proof_strategy: Exact enumeration of constant sign patterns (card_allSame) plus a union bound over the ledger.
title: Depth-Six Gate for Direction-Stable Observations

description:
Charge each dial its own evaluation cost kappa per candidate and re-derive the filter accounting. The conjecture is that the exchangeable cap degrades to 1/(kappa + 3/4) and that a critical overhead kappa* = 1/4 makes even the deterministic parity dial net-negative. This explains, deterministically, why every NET-loaded arm of the experiment read below 1.

For loadedSpeedup s theta kappa = (kappa + 1 - s + s*theta)^{-1}, one has loadedSpeedup theta theta kappa <= 1/(kappa + 3/4) for all theta, and loadedSpeedup 1 (1/2) kappa < 1 iff kappa > 1/2.

Extend OrbitDialCap.dialCost with an additive overhead term and rerun the completed-square argument; verify the critical constants by norm_num.

The barrier-4 scope note becomes quantitative: structural shaves pay for themselves only below an explicit overhead threshold.

The unloaded cost model is not the right idealisation and the NET-loaded readings need a separate mechanism.
proof_strategy: cost(s,theta) + kappa is still affine in s, so the same completed square (theta - 1/2)^2 bounds it; the threshold follows by solving a linear inequality.
title: Loaded Cap Law with Dial Overhead

description:
The repaired additive control is strictly informative, with p-value exactly one half, on the amplitude window below 2|B|/A determined by the overlap B of the deviation field with the perturbation direction and the direction energy A. The width of that window is a Rayleigh quotient in the direction, so the control designer's choice of direction has a closed-form optimum which points back at the signed deviation field.

The width 2|<c - E, w>| / ||w||^2 of the informative window is maximised, over all nonzero directions w, exactly at w proportional to c - E, with maximal width 2 / ||c - E||, and the maximum is attained only there.

Prove the Rayleigh-quotient optimisation from Cauchy-Schwarz and its equality case, formalised alongside chiSq_twoPoint_pvalue_eq_half; then evaluate the resulting optimal direction on the exp-566 count fields and compare its empirical rejection rate with random directions.

The protocol gains a canonical, computable control direction, and its optimum coincides with the signed carrier, unifying the control design with the signed follow-up.

Window width is not the right power functional and the control must be calibrated against the full amplitude distribution instead.
proof_strategy: Write the window width as 2|<v, w>| / ||w||^2 with v = c - E; scale invariance reduces to unit w, where Cauchy-Schwarz gives |<v, w>| <= ||v|| with equality iff w is parallel to v; combine with the exact quadratic amplitude profile chiSq_perturb.
title: Optimal Perturbation Direction for the Additive Control

description:
Quantisation fails in two independent ways: resolution, which block scaling shifts by exactly log2(1/rho) bits, and distinctness, which no affine rescaling can restore because 16 codes cannot separate 32 block entries. The conjecture is that at 4 bits the binding constraint is distinctness, so block-scaled variants will not rescue the NET-92 cell.

q4_1 and iq4_nl KV caches at block length 32 recover less than half of the q4_0 excess log-perplexity, while an 8-bit cache with the same block scaling recovers essentially all of it.

Run the NET-92 grid with --cache-type-k/v in {q4_1, iq4_nl, q5_0, q8_0} and compare excess log-perplexities against the bit-shift prediction of block_scaling_is_bit_shift.

No 4-bit KV format at block length 32 is viable; the fix must increase the number of codes, not the number of scales.

Resolution was binding after all, and rescue_requires_16x_concentration bounds the dynamic-range concentration that the block format achieves.
proof_strategy: Pigeonhole on codebook cardinality against block length (block_collision), plus invariance of collisions under affine rescaling and the exact softmax tie of collided keys.
title: Resolution Versus Distinctness Thresholds

description:
An observer monitoring k of T epochs detects at least one civilization with probability 1 − (1 − pk/T)^N up to quadratic corrections. We conjecture that this depends on the monitored set only through k, so no allocation of search effort beats uniform coverage.

For every S ⊆ Fin T with |S| = k, Prb{f | ∃ i, f i ∈ some '' S} lies between N p k/T − (N p k/T)²/2 and N p k/T.

Formalise the event for general S, apply prb_cylinder and one_sub_pow_le, and verify exactly by enumeration for T ≤ 5.

SETI-style search strategy is effort-limited, not strategy-limited, inside this model.

Non-uniform epoch marginals exist and targeted search has provable advantage.
proof_strategy: Exchangeability of epochs gives the marginal p·k/T per site; then the same Bernoulli/Bonferroni sandwich as in prb_exists_civ_le / prb_exists_civ_ge applies verbatim.
title: Linearity of Detection Probability in Search Effort

description:
On dyadic windows the pinned cost exceeds the optimum by exactly one half query, and the general bracket log2 W +- 1/2 is now proved. The exact defect between the closed form and the optimised curve should be an explicit sawtooth on each dyadic period, which would pin the recorded cost-offset bracket to a formula.

For W = 2^m t with t in [1,2), (log2 W + 1/2) - min_k netCost W k = 1/2 - min(t/2 - log2 t, t/4 + 1 - log2 t), a sawtooth attaining 1/2 exactly on dyadic W.

Prove in Lean that the min over k is attained at one of the two scales floor(log2 W) and floor(log2 W) - 1, then compute the two branches.

The cost-offset bracket becomes a closed form and the three competing k conventions get a single reconciling formula.

The optimum wanders over more than two scales and the offset is not periodic in log2 W.
proof_strategy: Show netCost W k is unimodal in k via the net marginal identity (its sign flips once), so the argmin is the largest k with W/2^(k+2) >= 1; then evaluate.
title: Half-Query Pin Defect for Non-Dyadic Windows

description:
Upgrades the injection used for the rho bound to a bijection, giving the exact count of collision-free streams modulo N = pq, and then the sharp threshold constant sqrt(2 ln 2 p). This makes the birthday heuristic a formal theorem over composite moduli.

The number of streams in (range (p*q))^t with pairwise distinct residues mod p equals descFactorial p t * q^t, and the least t with success probability at least 1/2 is ceil(sqrt(2 log 2 * p)) + O(1).

Replace card_injMod_le by a Finset.card_bij' equality, then estimate the product of (1 - i/p) with Mathlib's Real.log machinery.

A reusable formal birthday theorem for composite moduli, applicable to all collision-based cryptanalysis in the catalog.

The fibration x -> (x mod p, x div p) fails to be measure preserving and the rho heuristic needs another justification.
proof_strategy: Bijection via CRT-free fibration plus Fintype.card_embedding_eq, then real-analytic estimates on the falling factorial.
title: Exact Birthday Constant over Composite Moduli

description:
Attaches an explicit bit-cost model to the multiplication-free Berggren expansion and shows that the cheaper node cost does not change the hit density, so trial division wins by a constant factor at every budget. This turns the measured constant-factor deficit into a theorem-shaped claim.

With per-node cost Theta(log N) for the Berggren expansion and per-trial cost Theta(log N) for trial division, the cost to reach success probability 1/2 satisfies cost_dive >= 4 * cost_TD for all semiprimes with p_min >= 5.

Define a bit-cost function on control words using the growth bound hyp_applyWord_le, and compare with the p_min/4 lower bound of trial_division_scaling.

The campaign headline 'TD-class with worse constants' becomes fully formal and cost-model explicit.

There is a cost model where the dive wins, which would be a genuine algorithmic finding.
proof_strategy: Combine the exponential growth bound on hypotenuses with the exact hit density (p+q-2)/pq and the union bound.
title: Cost-Normalised Dominance of Trial Division

description:
Unimodality plus the monotone stopping rule imply that hill-climbing draft depth is globally optimal for any monotone acceptance profile. A runtime controller comparing next-position survival with c times the current speedup should therefore dominate every static depth setting.

For every monotone survival profile and every c > 0, the depth returned by the marginal-survival controller attains the global maximum of genSpeedup, and its throughput exceeds that of the best single static depth chosen across both domains by at least 20 percent on the NET-91 workload.

The first half is already proved (profile_greedy_depth_optimal); the second half is an experiment comparing the controller against the best fixed depth over a mixed prose/code workload.

Domain-adaptive depth becomes a two-line change with a proof of optimality behind it.

Estimation noise in the survival probability dominates the theoretical gain, and depth should be set per-domain offline.
proof_strategy: Formalise a noisy-estimate variant: if the estimated survival is within epsilon of the true one, the controller's depth is within one step of optimal, with a throughput loss bounded by the curvature of genSpeedup.
title: Exactness of the Marginal-Survival Depth Controller

description:
In the yield/cost separation, KV-cache quantisation should act only on the cost side, and only on the term that grows with the number of verified positions. This predicts its entire effect from the already-fitted curve, with no change to the acceptance profiles.

Quantising the target KV cache to q8_0 replaces the cost curve b + k d + m d^2 by b + k d + (lambda m) d^2 with lambda < 1, leaving both reconstructed survival profiles within measurement error.

Re-run the twelve cells with a quantised KV cache, re-fit, and check that only m moves; in Lean, prove that a pure contraction of m strictly increases the optimal depth.

KV quantisation and draft depth compose predictably; the ladder can be planned rather than swept.

Quantisation perturbs acceptance as well, coupling the two sides and invalidating the separation.
proof_strategy: Prove monotonicity of the greedy stopping depth in the curvature coefficient using the same cross-multiplication used for deepenPays_mono_acceptance, then instantiate numerically.
title: KV-Quantisation as a Pure Curvature Contraction

description:
Prove that the Hausdorff dimension of the golden-mean subshift in the first-disagreement ultrametric equals its box dimension log φ / log 2. The upper bound follows from the exact covering already proved; the lower bound uses the mass distribution principle applied to the uniform cylinder measure. This is a genuine strengthening, since Hausdorff ≤ box always but equality can fail.

dimH GoldenMean = Real.log Real.goldenRatio / Real.log 2 in the cantorDist metric.

Formalise with Mathlib's Metric.dimH, using goldenMean_cover for the upper bound and a Frostman/mass-distribution lemma with the uniform measure on the fib(n+2) cylinders for the lower bound.

The golden-mean subshift becomes a fully quantified fractal in Lean, with matching Hausdorff, box and entropy dimensions.

A strict inequality would signal that the cylinder measure is far from uniform at some scales, contradicting the sharp two-sided bound φ^n ≤ fib(n+2) ≤ φ^{n+1}.
proof_strategy: Upper bound: the fib(n+2) cylinders of diameter 2^{-n} give a Hausdorff sum φ^{n+1} 2^{-ns} which tends to 0 for s > log φ / log 2. Lower bound: the uniform measure gives μ(B(x,2^{-n})) ≤ φ^{-n}, so the mass distribution principle applies.
title: Hausdorff-Box Dimension Coincidence for Golden-Mean Streams

description:
Cycle 7 proves the golden-mean subshift has minimax online mistake rate exactly 1/2 while its entropy is log φ ≈ 0.694 log 2, so the two quantities disagree. The conjecture is that the minimax rate of a constrained binary source is 1 - 1/k, where k is the longest run the constraint can force, and is therefore independent of topological entropy. This would show that counting complexity and online-prediction complexity are genuinely different resources.

For the k-constrained subshift on {0,1} forbidding k consecutive `true`s, the minimax number of mistakes in n rounds is (1 - 1/k) n + O(1), while the topological entropy is log of the largest root of x^k = x^{k-1} + ... + 1; the two are not functions of one another.

Parameterise advMove of cycle 7 from `last letter is true` to `last k-1 letters are true`, re-prove the `no k consecutive correct rounds` lemma, and pair it with the generalised density bound k · #{trues} ≤ (k-1)(n+1) for the upper bound.

A clean separation theorem: entropy does not control online learnability for constrained sources, and the correct invariant is the forced-run length.

If the rate does track entropy, the adversary construction must be improvable, which would itself yield a new entropy-based online algorithm for constrained sources.
proof_strategy: Upper bound: the always-false predictor errs exactly on the `true`s, bounded by the generalised density bound. Lower bound: the adversary contradicts the prediction whenever free, and is forced at most one round in every k, giving at least (1-1/k) n mistakes by an induction in blocks of k.
title: Forced-Run Law for Minimax Online Prediction Rates

description:
Every floor statement proved in this cycle compares candidate floors at one common fade ratio. If the ratio is estimated from the same rungs, the set of pairs (floor, ratio) consistent with the data at noise eta should be a curve rather than a point. The conjecture is that this curve sweeps an interval of floors much wider than the pre-registered window, so a floor reported without an independent handle on the ratio is not a measurement.

For the recorded rungs and any eta at least the U116 rebound size, the set of pairs (L, lambda) with |lambda| < 1 for which the rungs form a noisy affine fade with floor L, ratio lambda and noise eta contains a continuous curve whose floor-projection is an interval of length at least 0.1.

For each lambda solve the one-step consistency inequalities for L, exhibit the resulting interval-valued map in Lean, and evaluate its projection at the recorded rungs.

Floor reports must be accompanied by an independent ratio estimate; the U116 floor window is a statement about the fit, not about the dial.

The rungs pin the pair jointly, and the reported floor window is a genuine measurement of the dial.
proof_strategy: Solve the per-rung constraints for L as a function of lambda, then show the resulting family of intervals is nonempty on an open set of ratios and compute the union.
title: Consistency Curve of Floor and Ratio for a Fixed Ladder

description:
Cycle five pinned the minimax floor error at eta/2 when the residuals are only assumed bounded with a known alternating pattern. The open successor couples the residuals to the dynamics: the readings must satisfy the noisy affine fade recursion with an unknown ratio lambda, which both restricts the adversary and hides the floor behind a second unknown. The conjecture is that the resulting minimax error is governed by the distance of lambda from 1 and, crucially, still does not improve with the number of rungs.

For the class of noisy affine fades with noise eta and unknown ratio lambda in [-1+delta, 1-delta], the minimax floor error from any number of rungs is between eta/2 and 2*eta/delta, and is bounded below by a constant multiple of eta/delta; in particular it does not tend to zero as the number of rungs grows.

Combine floor_identifiability_threshold, which makes two floors confusable exactly when |1-lambda| |L1-L2| <= 2 eta, with a two-point construction at the worst admissible lambda, and compare against the midrange and the Aitken estimator on the recorded rungs.

Reporting a floor without an independent handle on the ratio is bounded away from the truth by eta/delta however long the sweep is run, so longer sweeps are the wrong experimental investment.

Some estimator exploits the recursion to beat the static barrier, and longer sweeps do buy floor accuracy.
proof_strategy: Upper bound by the identifiability threshold applied to the midrange window; lower bound by exhibiting two fades with different floors, ratios inside the admissible range, and identical readings.
title: Minimax Floor Estimation Under an Unknown Fade Ratio

description:
The measured smoothness advantage of tree values should be fully explained by the halving of the effective factor base to primes 1 mod 4. A Mertens estimate restricted to that progression predicts a bounded, computable boost factor rather than the naive 44x.

For B-smoothness with B in the experimental range, the ratio of smooth-density among Berggren hypotenuses to smooth-density among random integers of the same size is bounded by a constant independent of B, and equals the Mertens ratio for the progression 1 mod 4 up to lower-order terms.

Compute smooth-density ratios for tree values versus random values at several B and sizes; compare with the Mertens prediction for primes 1 mod 4.

The boost is a constant factor and, by DixonCollapse.exponent_dominance, cannot change any cost exponent.

Tree values carry smoothness structure beyond the character constraint, and the naive 44x prediction needs a new explanation.
proof_strategy: Combine TreeSieveHyp.berg_hyp_primeFactors_subset with an effective Mertens theorem for arithmetic progressions and a Dickman-style smoothness estimate over restricted factor bases.
title: Character-Density Accounting of the 7.31x Smoothness Boost

description:
Random nontrivial square roots of 1 mod pq split N with probability 1/2, but the explicit Bezout root z = 1 - 2up always splits, returning exactly p. Quantifying this shows all the cost of Dixon-type methods sits in producing relations, none in exploiting them.

For distinct odd primes p, q and any Bezout pair (u,v) with up + vq = 1, gcd(1 - 2up - 1, pq) = p; consequently the yield of structured roots is 1 while the yield of uniformly random square roots of 1 is exactly 1/2.

The first half is proved (DixonCollapse.gcd_pair_recovers_factorization, which also gives gcd(z+1,pq) = q); formalize the second half by counting the four square roots of 1 modulo pq via the CRT isomorphism ZMod (pq) = ZMod p x ZMod q.

Dixon-class cost accounting reduces entirely to relation generation, sharpening barrier 8.

Structured roots sometimes fail, indicating a hidden dependence on the Bezout representative.
proof_strategy: Use ZMod.chineseRemainder to enumerate the square roots of 1, then apply the already-formalized gcd computation to each of the four lifts.
title: Unit Yield of Bezout-Structured Square Roots

description:
Conjecture that no search policy under end-verification-only semantics can achieve an exponential cost rate below min(b, 1/alpha), so the DFS/restart envelope proved in cycle 3 is optimal, not merely best-of-two. The approach is to model a policy as a distribution over descent sequences and bound the expected number of visits before a correct leaf is verified. It matters because it converts an engineering comparison into a lower-bound theorem.

For every policy P that only learns success at leaves, limsup (log E_P(h))/h >= log (min b (1/alpha)) whenever the oracle accuracy is alpha and the branching factor is b >= 2.

Formalise policies as functions from visit histories to next nodes; prove the bound by a counting argument over the alpha^h-probability correct root-leaf path, and check numerically against random hybrid schedules.

The exponent law becomes a complexity statement: accuracy alpha buys exactly a base 1/alpha and nothing better.

There exists a schedule with an intermediate base, which would be a genuinely new search strategy.
proof_strategy: Yao-style averaging over the uniformly random correct path, plus the observation that a policy visiting fewer than (min b (1/alpha))^h nodes misses the correct leaf with probability tending to one.
title: Information-Theoretic Floor for End-Verification Ascent

description:
Restart-with-cutoff descends d levels under oracle guidance and sweeps the remaining h - d exhaustively. Its cost is the product of the two laws already formalised. The conjecture is that the resulting exponent is a maximum of the two endpoint rates weighted by the depth split, hence never strictly between them at the optimum.

For cutoff fraction t = d/h in [0,1] the exponent is t*log(1/alpha) + (1-t)*log b, and the minimiser over t is always t = 1 or t = 0 according to whether alpha b > 1.

Define cutoffCost b w alpha t h in Lean, compute its log-rate limit, and minimise the resulting affine function of t.

The phase transition at alpha = 1/b is first-order in the schedule parameter: the optimum jumps between endpoints.

A genuinely mixed schedule beats both pure ones, contradicting the envelope picture.
proof_strategy: The cost factorises as h * alpha^(-th) * b^((1-t)h) up to polynomial factors; take logs and minimise an affine function on [0,1].
title: Cutoff-Restart Interpolation Without Intermediate Bases

description:
If the oracle accuracy varies with depth as alpha_1, ..., alpha_h, the restart law becomes h divided by the product of the alpha_j. The conjecture is that the exponent depends on the accuracy profile only through its geometric mean, so that a channel that is accurate at shallow depths and blind deep down is worth exactly its geometric mean.

The restart exponent for a profile (alpha_j) equals the limit of -(1/h) * sum_j log alpha_j, i.e. log of the reciprocal geometric mean, and the crossover with DFS is at geometric mean 1/b.

Generalise restartCost to a product of per-level accuracies, prove the log-rate identity, and specialise to geometrically decaying profiles alpha_j = alpha * rho^j.

Empirical per-level accuracy measurements can be aggregated to a single number before any economics is done.

The profile shape matters, and shallow accuracy is worth more than deep accuracy (or vice versa), which changes how channels should be measured.
proof_strategy: Cesaro convergence of (1/h) sum log alpha_j, plus the geometric-trial expectation already proved for a constant accuracy.
title: Geometric-Mean Reduction for Depth-Dependent Oracles

description:
Interpolate between end-verification-only and step-verification by letting a verifier of cost v fire every k levels. The conjecture is that the optimal spacing k* scales like log_b(1/v) and that the exponent degrades continuously from 1 (cheap verification) to min(b, 1/alpha) (no verification), giving a quantitative price for verification.

With verification cost v per firing and spacing k, the exponent is (1/k) * log(min(b^k, alpha^(-k)) + v * b^k) and its minimiser satisfies k* = Theta(log_b(1/v)).

Define the k-spaced schedule cost recursively, prove its closed form as in cycle 1, and analyse the resulting one-parameter minimisation.

A per-step feature costing v is worth building precisely when v is below an explicit threshold, closing the barrier probe quantitatively.

Verification cost enters only the prefactor, and end-verification semantics is not the bottleneck it appears to be.
proof_strategy: Same telescoping sum as the DFS law with wrong-subtree size b^k instead of b^j, then optimise the exponent over k by calculus on the closed form.
title: Partial Verification as a Third Resource

description:
The critical accuracy ((1+c)h/F)^(1/h) is increasing in c (proved) and, for fixed budget F, eventually increasing in h. The conjecture is that its supremum over h is attained at an explicit h_max and that beyond that depth no accuracy strictly below 1 can win, giving a hard depth ceiling for oracle-guided ascent against an exact solver.

For fixed c, F the function h -> ((1+c)h/F)^(1/h) is unimodal with a unique maximiser, tends to 1 as h -> infinity, and the win region {(alpha,h) : alpha > alpha*(c,F,h)} is bounded in h for every alpha < 1.

Differentiate the log of the critical accuracy, (1/h)(log((1+c)h) - log F), in h and locate its critical point; formalise the resulting unimodality and the depth ceiling for fixed alpha < 1.

There is a computable maximal depth at which any given oracle accuracy can still beat a given exact solver.

Deep instances remain winnable at fixed accuracy, contradicting the observed unwinnable deep tail.
proof_strategy: Calculus on g(h) = (log((1+c)h) - log F)/h, whose derivative vanishes at log((1+c)h/F) = 1; combine with breakeven_iff to transfer the analysis to the win region.
title: Breakeven Surface and the Maximal Winnable Depth

description:
A memoryless backoff arbiter pays the worst-case factor rho. Allowing a deficit counter to carry unused window between rounds should lower the long-run average slack to the geometric mean sqrt(rho) while leaving the per-round worst case at rho. The approach models the arbiter as a measure-preserving skew product over the rotation identified in cycle 3.

For every grid ratio rho > 1 there is a state-dependent arbiter whose long-run average slack equals sqrt(rho), and no arbiter with per-round windows in rho^Z achieves long-run average slack below sqrt(rho).

Formalise a deficit-counter arbiter as a sequence recursion over demands, prove the Cesaro limit of its log-slack equals 1/2 using the ergodic average already computed in jitter_mean_log_slack, and prove the matching lower bound by convexity.

Separates worst-case from amortised scheduling guarantees: the factor 2 is a per-round artefact, not an amortised cost.

The dyadic overshoot is intrinsically per-round and memory cannot help, strengthening ptx_two_optimal_ceiling_iff to amortised schedules.
proof_strategy: Model the arbiter state as a point of the circle R/log rho Z; identify the induced map as a rotation; apply Birkhoff to the already-computed invariant density; lower bound by Jensen applied to the log-slack.
title: Deficit-Carrying Arbiters and the Geometric-Mean Barrier

description:
Cycle 2 proves that uniform phase jitter gives geometric-mean slack exactly sqrt(rho) for every request. The conjecture is that no phase distribution does better in the worst case over requests, so log-uniform jitter is the unique minimax-optimal randomisation of a grid arbiter. The approach averages the log-slack over the request as well as the phase and applies Fubini.

For every probability measure mu on the phase circle, sup over x of the mu-averaged log-slack is at least 1/2, with equality only for the uniform measure; consequently the minimax geometric-mean slack of any randomised grid arbiter is sqrt(rho).

Formalise the double average of fract(theta - t) over theta and t, prove it equals 1/2 by Fubini, and deduce the sup bound; test uniqueness by perturbing mu with a point mass.

Fixes log-uniform backoff jitter as the provably optimal randomisation, giving designers a canonical choice.

Some skewed jitter distribution beats uniform, which would be a concrete improvement to exponential-backoff practice.
proof_strategy: Fubini on the product of the phase measure and the uniform measure over one period, then a strict-inequality argument for non-uniform mu using the density of rotations.
title: Minimax Optimality of Log-Uniform Jitter

description:
The aggregate bound sums the per-class factor 2. For n classes with rationally independent log-demands the per-class slacks equidistribute independently, so the aggregate slack should concentrate at the mean 1/log 2 with fluctuations of order 1/sqrt(n), and the worst case 2 should require an aligned instance.

For demands whose base-2 logarithms are rationally independent, the aggregate slack (sum of services)/(sum of ideals) tends to (rho-1)/log rho as the number of classes grows, and instances with aggregate slack above 2 - epsilon form a set of vanishing measure.

Formalise Weyl equidistribution for several independent exponents, combine with the proved per-class density, and derive a law of large numbers for the aggregate ratio.

Channel-level provisioning can use 1.443x rather than 2x headroom, a 28 percent capacity saving with rigorous justification.

Aggregate alignment is common, and the per-class worst case really is the design constraint at channel level.
proof_strategy: Multi-dimensional Weyl criterion, then a Birkhoff average of the slack function against the product Haar measure; the Finset bounds ptx_aggregate_floor and ptx_aggregate_lt_two provide the deterministic envelope.
title: Aggregate Slack Concentration for Many Transport Classes

description:
Exact service occurs precisely when the ideal share is a power of two. For rational parameters and occupancy p = 1/n this asks whether gamma*d/(beta*log n + M + gamma - r) can be a power of two, a linear-forms-in-logarithms question. The conjecture is that exactness fails for all n that are not powers of two.
