If beta, gamma, M, r, d are rational with beta nonzero and p = 1/n with n a positive integer that is not a power of two, then the ideal share is never an integer power of two, so slack > 1 strictly.

Extend the argument of irrational_logb_two_three from log_2 3 to log_2 n for non-powers of two, then clear denominators to reduce the exactness equation to an irrationality statement.

Exact service is arithmetically impossible for essentially all physical occupancies: the floor is never attained in practice, only approached.

There are tuned occupancies with zero quantisation loss, which would be valuable design points for real arbiters.
proof_strategy: Unique factorisation to prove log_2 n irrational for n not a power of two, then a rationality contradiction after clearing denominators in the exactness equation.
title: Arithmetic Obstruction to Exact Service

description:
Every retention bound proved so far is dial-agnostic. We conjecture that the retention loss of a dial at fixed work fraction is controlled exactly by the symmetric difference between its keep-set and the true top-k set, not by any rank correlation. This would replace a correlation-based deployment criterion by a set-based one that is both computable and tight.

For nonnegative rates r on a finite set s with |K_d| = |K_r*| = k, the retention deficit satisfies (sum over K_r* of r) - (sum over K_d of r) <= (max r) * |K_d symmetric-difference K_r*| / 2, and this is attained.

Formalise as a strengthening of sum_le_of_bounded_exceptions with the exceptional set taken to be the symmetric difference; test tightness on random rate vectors and on factor bases with periodRate.

Deployment should tune dials to top-k set agreement rather than to Spearman correlation.

Rank correlation retains a role no set-overlap statistic captures, and the discordance budget is the right currency.
proof_strategy: Pair each element of K_d \ K_r* with one of K_r* \ K_d and bound each pair's contribution by max r; attainment by a two-value rate profile.
title: Symmetric-Difference Optimality of Threshold Dials

description:
The headroom of an admissible factor base is now reduced to the scalar p_min times the harmonic sum of its primes. Since admissibility is a density-one-half condition, that harmonic sum should grow like half of log log B, making the headroom predictable from B alone rather than measured per target.

For the admissible primes A of a factor base bounded by B, p_min * (sum over A of 1/p) = Theta(log log B), hence the oracle-to-mean rate ratio is Theta(|A| / log log B) rather than Theta(|A|).

Combine headroom_ratio_eq with a Mertens-type estimate restricted to the admissible primes; check numerically for B up to a few thousand against the exact ratio computed from periodRate.

Adaptive headroom is predictable from the factor-base bound alone and does not require per-target measurement.

The fine structure of the admissible set, not its density, controls the headroom.
proof_strategy: Express the harmonic sum over admissible primes as half the full prime harmonic sum plus a Chebotarev error term, then apply Mertens' second theorem.
title: Mertens Ceiling on Adaptive Headroom

description:
Threshold deferral is now proved exactly minimal when the dial is injective, and the failure mode for general dials is quantified as the tie multiplicity at the threshold. We conjecture that a strict threshold together with a deterministic tie-break attains the minimum-work schedule for every rate profile, so no subset search is ever needed.

For any finite s, rates r and attainable quota Q, there are a threshold theta and a prefix P of the tie class at theta such that (strict keepSet) union P is quota-feasible and of minimum cardinality among all quota-feasible subsets of s.

Construct the policy from keepSet_card_eq_add_tie_slack by truncating the tie class, and verify it against exhaustive subset search on small random instances, including the tied lab instance (3,3,1).

The one-parameter deferral policy is exactly optimal in full generality, injective dial or not.

Ties are a genuine degree of freedom and threshold parametrisation loses work that a subset search would recover.
proof_strategy: Split keepSet into the strict part and the tie class; the strict part is forced, and among quota-feasible completions inside the tie class all elements are interchangeable since their rates are equal, so any prefix of the right size works.
title: Deterministic Tie-Breaking for Strict Threshold Deferral

description:
The deployed dial counts admissible primes below a bound, while the proved yield-relevant quantity is twice the harmonic sum of those primes. We conjecture that the disagreement between the two rankings is controlled by the smallest admissible prime of each target, so the measured Spearman deficit is an arithmetic, bounded effect rather than noise.

For targets N1, N2 with admissible sets A1, A2 below B, if min A1 = min A2 then the counting dial and the aggregate rate 2 * H_A order N1 and N2 identically up to a discrepancy bounded by 2 * |count difference| / min A; hence the inversion set of the counting dial is contained in the set of pairs with distinct smallest admissible primes.

Compute factorBaseRate and the QR count for all N in a range and all B up to a few hundred, and compare the inversion set with the predicted containment; formalise the containment as a statement about discordantPairs.

The QR count can be replaced by a weighted count with a provable, not empirical, calibration.

The counting dial's predictive power comes from window truncation effects the per-period idealisation cannot see.
proof_strategy: Bound the harmonic sum above and below by count / max A and count / min A, then compare the two ratios pairwise.
title: Weighted-Count Calibration of the QR Dial

description:
The sharp decorrelation bound proved this cycle is a spherical triangle inequality, suggesting that the natural coordinate for the bitlen ladder is the correlation angle arccos(rho) rather than rho itself. In angle coordinates the recorded steps rescale and the U112 re-acceleration is reduced. The conjecture is that the ladder is an affine fade in angle with a single ratio and strictly smaller minimal noise than in correlation coordinates.

There exist A, mu with |mu| < 1 such that the angles theta_k = arccos(rho_k) of the recorded ladder satisfy a noisy affine fade with minimal noise strictly below the correlation-coordinate optimum 73943/7340000.

Recompute the Chebyshev optimum of the four residuals theta_{k+1} - (Theta + mu (theta_k - Theta)) and compare with the proved optimum in correlation coordinates; formalise using the same alternation certificate.

The fade is a rotation phenomenon and the band floor should be re-registered as an angle threshold.

Correlation is the intrinsic coordinate and the re-acceleration is a genuine change of regime, not a coordinate artefact.
proof_strategy: Transfer the equioscillation machinery (affine_of_param_diff, alternation_forces_noise) to the transformed data; monotonicity of arccos preserves the strictly declining hypothesis needed by the sign argument.
title: Angle-Coordinate Affinity of the Dial Ladder

description:
The small-prime QR dial has variance exactly 1/2 and hence constant information content, independent of the bit length of N. Since the measured ladder does fade, the fade must be located in the coupling between the dial and the downstream rate. The conjecture makes this quantitative by bounding the fade by a coupling-side quantity only.

For every bit length, the Spearman correlation between the QR dial and any downstream statistic is bounded by the correlation between the rate and the CRT-measurable sigma-algebra generated by the small primes, and this bound is bit-length free.

Formalise the conditional-expectation projection onto the CRT factors and prove the projection bound; compare with the recorded ladder values 0.5739 .. 0.4621.

The fade is a property of the rate model, and dial engineering cannot recover the band.

There is a bit-length dependent loss on the dial side, contradicting the exact equidistribution proved here.
proof_strategy: Use card_filter_crt to identify the CRT factor decomposition, then a Cauchy-Schwarz projection bound in the Gram geometry of Algebra.ZeroFitDialU72Parity.
title: Information-Coupling Separation for Residue Dials

description:
CRT independence extends the two-prime binomial law to r small primes, giving an exact Binomial(r, 1/2) law for the dial. Rank correlations against a fixed downstream statistic must then degrade with r because the dial concentrates. The conjecture predicts the fade rate from r alone.

For r small primes the maximal Spearman correlation attainable between the r-prime QR dial and any bounded response decays like c / sqrt(r), with an explicit constant independent of the bit length of N.

Prove the exact Binomial(r, 1/2) level-set counts by induction using card_filter_crt, then bound rank correlation by the ratio of dial standard deviation to its range.

Dial ladders can be redesigned with r tuned to the target band, decoupling the fade from bit length.

Correlation loss is not concentration driven, and the multi-prime dial retains resolution the binomial law forbids.
proof_strategy: Induct on the number of primes with the CRT counting lemma; the concentration bound follows from an exact variance computation as in two_mul_dial_variance.
title: Binomial Concentration Limit of Multi-Prime Dials

description:
Formalize 'position dial' as failure of translation invariance of window composition and prove that finite-valued classifiers of j with bounded drift are exactly the almost periodic ones. This upgrades the negative result of paper 242 from 'residue classes fail' to a structural criterion on any candidate carrier. It gives future experiments a decidable pre-screen.

For a finite-valued f : ℤ → α, the window counts count f a L c are independent of a for all L in a fixed multiple class iff f is periodic; and drift of order Θ(1) in L forces the Fourier–Bohr spectrum of the indicator functions of f to contain a non-rational frequency.

Extend Catalog/Shared/MixtureRateDialResidueCarriers.lean: prove the converse of count_const_of_period_dvd (constancy of window counts at all lengths implies periodicity), then formalize the almost periodic version.

Any candidate carrier can be screened by a translation-invariance test before any statistics are run.

There exist aperiodic classifiers with exactly flat composition, so flatness is strictly weaker than periodicity and the screen must be refined.
proof_strategy: One direction is count_succ_of_period. For the converse, take L = 1: constancy of one-point counts is literally periodicity; for the almost periodic case, use the mean of indicator functions and Weyl equidistribution.
title: Aperiodicity Criterion for Positional Carriers

description:
With every residue classifier excluded, the remaining j-local data is the size of v = j^2 - N and its large-prime structure. Conjecture that the u* = 0.65 excess is carried by the boundary of the smoothness test rather than by any arithmetic class of v. The test is a positional split of hits by the largest prime factor of v.

Conditioned on window position t, the distribution of log P⁺(v)/log v (P⁺ = largest prime factor) is not t-independent, and its t-dependence reproduces a peak at t ≈ 0.65 to within the measured amplitude.

Define the u-statistic as a Lean function of v and formalize the monotone relation between the Dickman weight and the largest-prime-factor threshold; empirically, bin hits by P⁺ and refit.

The non-divisibility positional mechanism is a size/boundary effect, not an arithmetic one, and the map entry gets a mechanism.

The carrier is neither residue-type nor size-type, forcing a genuinely new class of statistics (e.g. correlations between consecutive j).
proof_strategy: Combine the Dickman bounds already in Catalog (NumberTheory.ProfileFormResidualPeak, Shared.DickmanFiniteCorrection) with the ray-collapse theorem: the shape B is the only carrier of position, so identify B with a P⁺-conditioned Dickman weight.
title: Smoothness-Size Carrier for the Mid-Window Excess

description:
The minimal enrichment of the refuted model lets cells depend on the window index as well as on j, e.g. (divisibility cell, parity of the bin). Its mixture family has dimension two, so it is not a ray and the invariance theorem does not apply. Characterize exactly how much positional freedom each extra grid dimension buys.

For a classifier of the form (f j, g b) with f m-periodic and g arbitrary, the achievable prediction family is the linear span of {S_g · B} and has dimension equal to the number of distinct values of g; the maximal absorbable amplitude grows linearly in that dimension.

Generalize FlatComposition to a rank condition on the matrix S_{c,b} and prove that the achievable set is the column span; instantiate with the product grid.

There is a precise dimension/absorption trade-off, and the 0% removal is explained as a rank-1 phenomenon.

Rank alone does not control absorption and positional freedom is a finer invariant than dimension.
proof_strategy: Replace the scalar K by a coefficient vector; mixPred_eq_smul becomes a matrix-vector identity and mixture_family_eq_ray becomes 'achievable set = column span of S'.
title: Two-Dimensional Cell Grids with Window-Index Dependence

description:
For odd N the bit 2 | j^2 - N is exactly the parity of j, and for odd p the p-bit rate is 0, 1/p or 2/p according to the Legendre symbol of N. Assemble these into an exact CRT formula for the 16 cell populations of a 210-window and prove the resulting rate spread bound. This makes the measured kappa/g spread 0.645-1.406 a computable prediction rather than a fit.

The population of the cell with pattern S ⊆ {2,3,5,7} in any 210-window equals the product over p ∈ S of r_p(N) and over p ∉ S of (p - r_p(N)), where r_p(N) = 1 + χ_p(N) for p ∤ N and 1 for p | N; hence the rate spread is bounded by the product of the (1 + χ_p) factors.

Prove multiplicativity of windowCount over the CRT decomposition 210 = 2·3·5·7 in Lean, with sqCount_three/five/seven as the per-prime inputs.

The measured per-cell rate spread becomes an exact arithmetic prediction depending only on N mod 210.

Some cell populations depend on more than N mod 210, contradicting the periodicity theorem — which would be an inconsistency, so falsity would indicate an error in the measurement pipeline.
proof_strategy: CRT bijection ZMod 210 ≃ ZMod 2 × ZMod 3 × ZMod 5 × ZMod 7, then count square roots of N in each factor by decide.
title: Parity Merging and the Quadratic Residue Rate Table

description:
The exact identity gram_gap_eq expresses the loss of the advantage certificate relative to the Gram certificate as half the squared difference of residual lengths. Conjecture that this defect is asymptotically delta^4 / (8 (1 - rho^2)), so the two certificates agree to fourth order in the advantage. This decides whether measuring the dial/baseline correlation directly is experimentally worthwhile.

For a = rho + delta/2 and b = rho - delta/2 with |rho| < 1, (1 - delta^2/2) - (a b + sqrt((1-a^2)(1-b^2))) = delta^4/(8(1-rho^2)) + O(delta^6).

Expand the closed form of gram_gap_eq in Lean with an explicit remainder bound and evaluate at each measured rung.

Advantage-only readings are provably within O(delta^4) of optimal; no new experiment is needed.

Direct measurement of corr(T, count) carries first-order information and should be scheduled.
proof_strategy: Write sqrt(1-a^2) - sqrt(1-b^2) as (b^2-a^2)/(sqrt(1-a^2)+sqrt(1-b^2)) and bound the denominator between explicit constants.
title: Quartic Defect Law for Decorrelation Certificates

description:
Generalise the two-domain sup-convolution to d domains and determine the exact multi-domain budget. Cycle 6 settles the equal-size case on the geometric profile: the d-fold knee at gate 0.98 is exactly ceil(143 d / 25), so the per-domain cost is 5.72 keys and the d-times-pure ceiling is attained only for d <= 3. What remains is the barycentric (unequal domain sizes) case, which decides whether balanced mixing still maximises the budget over the whole simplex.

For d domains of comparable mass the d-fold knee is maximised at the barycentre of the mixing simplex, and at the barycentre it equals ceil(rho * d) for a profile- and gate-dependent rate rho strictly below the pure budget; for the profile (1/2)^i at gate 0.98 the rate is 143/25 (proved in cycle 6 as mixNKnee_geomHalf), so d times the pure budget is only an upper bound and fails to be exact from d = 4 on.

Replace the single per-domain size m in mixNHead by a vector of sizes, re-derive the tangent upper bound and the block-allocation lower bound, and check numerically whether an unbalanced size vector can beat the barycentre at fixed total context.

Multi-domain agentic workloads are cheaper than pairwise extrapolation predicts, by the factor 143/150 per domain already at d = 4.

The maximum of the simplex sits at an unbalanced corner and mixed budget tables must be indexed by the full domain-size vector.
proof_strategy: Keep the two bounds of cycle 6 (tangent inequality for the upper bound, an explicit allocation using only the two block sizes adjacent to the tangency point for the lower bound) and make the per-domain sizes a vector, using the concavity argument of NET90BalancedPeak to compare barycentre with corners.
title: Multi-Domain Bump Simplex

description:
The a-posteriori recursion E(n+1) = δ + |4-8x_n| E(n) should grow with rate exp(n ln 2) for almost every initial condition, halving the exponent of the global-Lipschitz bound and doubling the certified simulation horizon. The approach couples the nonautonomous shadowing recursion with the Birkhoff ergodic theorem for the arcsine invariant measure.

For Lebesgue-a.e. x_0 in [0,1], (1/n) log E(n) tends to ln 2 where E is the errBound recursion driven by L n = |4 - 8 x_n|.

Formalise the arcsine invariant density for the r=4 logistic map, apply Birkhoff's theorem to log|f'|, and combine with errBound monotonicity.

Certified shadowing horizons for binary64 chaotic simulation roughly double, matching observed numerics.

The observed 2^n growth is not ergodic-generic and shadowing horizons must be certified per orbit.
proof_strategy: Conjugate to the tent map by x = sin^2(pi t / 2), transport Lebesgue measure, evaluate the Birkhoff average of log|f'| exactly, then sandwich errBound between products of local factors.
title: Lyapunov-Exact Shadowing Horizon for the Logistic Map

description:
Genuine IEEE executions of the logistic map are conjectured to realise the sharp exponential shadowing bound, because rounding near the critical point x = 1/2 has a systematic sign. The approach analyses the sign of the rounding error of 4*x*(1-x) as a function of the binary expansion of x.

There is x_0 in [0,1] and c > 0 such that for all n the binary64 execution satisfies |x_n - y_n| >= c u 2^n for every exact orbit y with y_0 = x_0.

Search over binary64 initial values for orbits whose per-step defects share a sign, then formalise the resulting lower bound by an induction mirroring finite_shadowing_sharp.

Floating-point chaotic simulations provably fail to be pointwise-accurate orbits, making the pseudo-orbit reading mandatory rather than convenient.

Rounding defects decorrelate and typical executions are far better shadowed than the worst case, suggesting a probabilistic refinement of the defect certificate.
proof_strategy: Exhibit an initial value whose orbit visits a neighbourhood of 1/2 with controlled binary expansion; prove one-signed defects there by exact rational computation, then propagate with the reverse triangle inequality.
title: Coherent Rounding Bias at the Critical Point

description:
The analytic certificate gamma_{2n}(u) times the magnitude functional should agree, within a factor two, with the width returned by one interval-arithmetic step on the same Horner program, yielding an executable certified pipeline from program to shadowing theorem. The approach compares both recursions term by term.

For every coefficient list and every x, the width of the interval-Horner evaluation lies between gamma_{2n}(u) hornerAbs as x and 2 gamma_{2n}(u) hornerAbs as x.

Define outward-rounded interval Horner in Lean, prove both inequalities by the same induction that proves hornerFl_forward_defect.

Shadowing certificates can be produced at runtime by interval arithmetic with no analytic bookkeeping.

Interval widths overestimate the true defect superlinearly, motivating affine-arithmetic certificates instead.
proof_strategy: Induct on the coefficient list; the interval recursion satisfies w(n+1) = |x| w(n) + u(|a| + |x| m(n)) which is the same recursion driving gamma, up to the factor-two slack from outward rounding.
title: Interval Arithmetic Equals the Analytic Defect Certificate

description:
The effective p-adic base of a reading is Theta(rho^{-2}), proved here by the bracket 1/rho^2 - 1 < p <= 3/rho^2. Combining that with a linear late-epoch fade predicts that the effective base grows quadratically in the bitlen, so the dial degenerates through the primes at an accelerating rate rather than settling at base 23 as the hyperbolic law predicted.

Under any fade with rho(b) asymptotically c*(B - b) on a finite window, the effective base satisfies p(b) = Theta((B-b)^{-2}); in particular the recorded bases 6, 8, 10, 14 at bitlens 76, 92, 104, 120 lie on a quadratic in b, not a linear one.

Prove the bracket and monotonicity in Lean, compute the effective base of every recorded rung, and fit linear against quadratic on the four data points.

Base drift becomes the natural coordinate for the thread: fade laws should be fitted in base space, where they may be linear even when they are not in rho space.

The bases grow linearly, which would force rho(b)^{-2} to be linear, i.e. an inverse-square-root fade -- a shape class not yet tested.
proof_strategy: effective_base_bracket plus strict antitonicity of padicLimit gives uniqueness and monotonicity; the quadratic claim then follows by substituting the linear fade into the bracket and comparing integer parts.
title: Quadratic Effective-Base Drift

description:
The T-over-count advantage was flat (0.070, 0.073) through bitlen 76, spiked to 0.126 at bitlen 104, then collapsed to 0.047 by bitlen 112. The catalog knows both tie ceilings in closed form: 6/7 for the dyadic profile and 1 - 4/(3b+2) for the binomial one. The conjecture is that the spike marks the bitlen at which the count baseline's realised correlation crosses a fixed fraction of its own ceiling, i.e. the count statistic stops resolving before the dial does.

The bitlen maximising the T-over-count advantage is the bitlen at which the count baseline's ceiling utilisation rho_count^2 / (1 - 4/(3b+2)) first falls below the dial's utilisation rho_T^2 / (6/7).

Compute both utilisations at every recorded rung from the closed-form ceilings in the catalog, and check whether the crossing bitlen coincides with the advantage maximum at 104.

The advantage becomes a derived quantity, predictable from tie geometry alone, and the count baseline's death bitlen is computable in advance.

The advantage spike is a response-side effect, which localises the mechanism of the fade in the response rather than in either statistic.
proof_strategy: Use ceiling_utilisation_collapsed and count_ceiling_ge to express both utilisations in closed form, differentiate the difference with respect to b, and locate the sign change.
title: Advantage Spike as a Tie-Ceiling Crossing

description:
Reading a measured ladder as monotone, or as a contracting plateau, costs a definite per-rung measurement-error budget. For the recorded T-dial ladder those prices are exactly 0.0113 and at least 0.012823, and they lie strictly between the per-seed half-spread 0.008 and the pooled CI half-width 0.0445. The gap converts a modelling dispute into a variance-reduction experiment.

The monotone price of a finite ladder is half its largest pairwise excursion max over k <= l of (r l - r k), realised by the suffix-maximum flattening; this is now proved, and the local variant using only consecutive increases is refuted. The open half is experimental: any rerun of the T-dial ladder whose per-rung dispersion is at most 0.008 either removes the bitlen-116 rebound or refutes the 1/2-contractive plateau reading.

The price identity is formalised as ladder_mono_price with the counterexample consecutive_price_insufficient; the remaining test is to rerun exp 541 at increased seed count and compare the realised dispersion with the two prices.

Model selection between plateau and extinction becomes an experiment-design question with a computable target variance, rather than a curve-fitting dispute.

The rebound survives variance reduction, which would make the non-contractive step a property of the mechanism rather than of the instrument and would settle the plateau dispute against the plateau.
proof_strategy: Necessity is the two-sided error bar across an arbitrary increasing pair; sufficiency is the suffix-maximum flattening, whose deviation at every rung is bounded by the largest pairwise excursion. The experimental half then follows from noise_price_verdict.
title: Noise-Price Separation of Dispersion Scales

description:
The Pell analogue of Wall–Sun–Sun primes is non-empty: 13 and 31 both satisfy p² ∣ P(rank p), verified in Lean. We conjecture the set is infinite with log-log density, twice the Fibonacci heuristic because the discriminant 8 is ramified at 2. Certifying more members turns a folklore heuristic into measurable data.

The set {p prime : p² ∣ pellP (pellRank p)} is infinite and its counting function is asymptotically c·log log x with c ≥ 1.

Extend the certified search past 10^6 using the formalised rank law dvd_pellP_iff_pellRank_dvd, verifying each candidate with a decide-checked divisibility; compare the observed count with log log x.

The Pell spine gives the first family of explicitly known Wall–Sun–Sun-type primes, and Fibonacci's emptiness becomes a small-sample artefact.

A finite exceptional set would signal an unknown obstruction attached to the ramified prime 2 in ℤ[√2].
proof_strategy: Combine pellRank_mul_of_coprime with a p-adic expansion of the silver unit: p² ∣ P(rank p) iff the Fermat quotient of the fundamental unit vanishes mod p; model that quotient as equidistributed.
title: Silver-Ratio Wall–Sun–Sun Density

description:
The Pell case is now a theorem (pellQ_dvd_iff, pellQ_gcd_law): the half-companion sequence is divisibility-graded by parity of the index quotient, and its gcd is either Q(gcd) or 1. We conjecture that the same parity grading holds for the companion sequence of every Lucas pair (a, -1), with an extra factor 2 exactly when a is odd. This would isolate strong divisibility as a norm-form phenomenon and the parity grading as a property of the unit index lattice.

Let V 0 = 2, V 1 = a, V (n+2) = a V (n+1) + V n and g = gcd m n. Then gcd (V m) (V n) = V g when m/g and n/g are both odd, and gcd (V m) (V n) divides 2 otherwise, with value 2 attained exactly when a is odd.

Parameterise the Pell development by a: reprove V m ∣ U (2m), strong divisibility of U, gcd (U m) (V m) ∣ 2 and the congruence V (b + 2m) ≡ c · V b mod V m, then rerun the proof of pellQ_gcd_law verbatim; test numerically on a = 1 (Lucas, where gcd (L 3) (L 6) = 2) and a = 3.

Every real quadratic order gets a complete companion gcd calculus, and the Pell theorem becomes the a even, 2-torsion-free instance.

Some Lucas pair produces a gcd value exceeding 2, meaning the index lattice grading is not by ℤ/2 alone and an extra ramification invariant is needed.
proof_strategy: Work in the order ℤ[u] with u^2 = a u + 1: V n = u^n + ū^n, V m ∣ U (2m) and the two-step congruence give coprimality at even multiples; combine with strong divisibility of U and the coprime factorisation U(2g) = 2 U g V g.
title: Parity-Graded Divisibility for Companion Spines

description:
The Legendre refinement of the Fermat law was closed in this cycle (pellRank p divides p-1 exactly for p congruent to plus or minus 1 mod 8). The successor question is how the rank grows on prime powers: geometrically with ratio p, except at Pell-Wall-Sun-Sun primes where the growth is delayed by exactly one step.

With e(p) the largest exponent such that p^e divides pellP (pellRank p), for every k >= 1 one has pellRank (p^k) = p^(max (k - e p) 0) * pellRank p.

Compute pellRank (p^k) for all primes p < 10^4 and k <= 4 using the certified law dvd_pellP_iff_pellRank_dvd, and check the formula, paying attention to p = 13 and p = 31.

Combined with pellRank_mul_of_coprime this determines pellRank on every modulus from its values at primes, completing the divisibility theory of the spine.

A prime power where the rank jumps by a non-p factor would break the p-adic filtration of the unit group of Z[sqrt 2] and indicate a wild ramification effect.
proof_strategy: Lifting the exponent for the silver unit: u^(rank) = 1 + p^e w with w a unit, then binomial expansion of (1 + p^e w)^p controls the valuation at each step.
title: Prime-Power Rank Growth off the Wall–Sun–Sun Locus

description:
Pythagorean triples with consecutive legs are exactly the odd Pell spine points, and their hypotenuses are 1 mod 4. We conjecture the sharper local law: every prime factor of such a hypotenuse is ±1 mod 8. This is a geometric statement whose proof is purely local-arithmetic.

If a² + (a+1)² = c² then every prime factor q of c satisfies q ≡ ±1 (mod 8); in particular 3, 5, 11, 13 never divide c except through the square 169 = 13².

From 2c² = (2a+1)² + 1 deduce that -1 and 2 are both squares mod q using ZMod.exists_sq_eq_neg_one_iff and the classification nearIsosceles_iff; verify on the first twenty spine terms.

A congruence atlas for a classical geometric family, and an explanation of why 169 is the unique composite hypotenuse in the visible range.

A hypotenuse with a prime factor ≡ 3 (mod 8) would break the norm-form description of the spine, forcing a wider class of quadratic orders.
proof_strategy: Local analysis of x² + 1 = 2y² at each odd prime q ∣ y: it forces (−2/q) = 1, then quadratic reciprocity gives q ≡ ±1 (mod 8).
title: Congruence Atlas of Near-Isosceles Hypotenuses

description:
After the dichotomy theorem, all information in a 0/1 scan lies in the rate curve p. Conjecture that p, assumed Hölder-smooth of order β on the scan axis, is recoverable from a single scan of length n at the one-dimensional nonparametric rate n^{-β/(2β+1)}, and that no estimator does better. The approach is to combine the exact moment calculus of the product model with a two-point (Le Cam) argument between two curves whose scans are hard to tell apart.

For the product Bernoulli scan model with rate curve p in a Hölder-β ball, the minimax L2 risk of estimating p from one scan of length n is of order n^{-2β/(2β+1)}.

Formalise the upper bound for a binned estimator using the exact variance identity bernExp_centeredPairSum_sq specialised to k = 0, and the lower bound by a two-point argument with an explicit bump perturbation of the rate curve.

Positional-excess modelling becomes a solved estimation problem with an explicit optimal bin width; all future gains are quantified.

Some scan-specific structure (dependence, or non-Hölder curvature) is present after all, reopening the closed thread.
proof_strategy: Upper bound: bias-variance split with the proved variance identity. Lower bound: Le Cam two-point with a single bump, using the product structure to bound the chi-square distance between the two product laws.
title: Minimax Recovery of the Positional Density Curve

description:
The Chebyshev floor 1/(16 m t^2) proved here is polynomial; the true floor should be exponential. Conjecture that the detrended lag-k statistic satisfies a Bernstein bound exp(-c m t^2) under pure density. The route is the same multilinear expansion that gave the variance, pushed to the fourth moment and then to a bounded-difference argument.

P(|centeredPairSum| >= t m) <= 2 exp(-c m t^2) for an absolute constant c > 0, under any rate curve with values in [0,1].

Prove the fourth-moment identity by classifying overlaps of two index pairs, then apply a fourth-moment or bounded-difference inequality inside the finite product model.

The pre-registered 0.05 bar corresponds to an astronomically small null probability, upgrading the exclusion from 'rare' to 'impossible at this scale'.

Heavy-tailed behaviour of the statistic would mean the bar must scale with the window, changing the pre-registration rule.
proof_strategy: Expand E[(sum of terms)^4] into centred products over index multisets; all terms with a singleton index vanish by bernExp_centered_prod_eq_zero; the survivors are O(m^2), giving a fourth moment bound and hence a Bernstein-type tail.
title: Fourth-Moment Law and Exponential Noise Floor

description:
The alternation count and the lag-1 cross-product see the same dependence parameter but different heterogeneity confounds: second order in delta for runs at c = 1/2, second order for the lag statistic as well but with a different constant and opposite sign behaviour. Conjecture that a fixed linear combination of the two statistics has zero first-order and zero second-order heterogeneity bias while retaining first-order sensitivity to lambda.

There are constants (alpha, beta), independent of the rate curve, such that alpha * (alternation deficit) + beta * (lag-1 statistic) has heterogeneity bias O(delta^3) and Markov signal Theta(lambda).

Compute both expectations exactly (already available: bernExp_altCount and bernExp_centeredPairSum) as polynomials in the residuals e_i and match coefficients.

A confound-free single-number test for sequence structure, strictly more powerful than either channel alone.

The two confounds are collinear, and no combination improves on the better single channel.
proof_strategy: Both expectations are explicit quadratics in e; equate the quadratic forms and solve the resulting 2x2 linear system for (alpha, beta), then verify the Markov signal is nonzero.
title: Joint Runs-and-Lag Channel with Orthogonal Confounds

description:
A record whose mean-centred cyclic autocorrelation is the same at every nonzero lag must sit at the level -1/(n-1). Conjecture that among 0/1 records the constant-profile ones are exactly the indicator vectors of cyclic difference sets and their complements, so the extremal flat profile is a design-theoretic object.

Refined after this cycle: the equivalence 'constant nonzero-lag autocorrelation iff constant difference multiplicity' is now proved (constant_profile_iff_constant_diffMult); the open part is the fluctuation law, namely that for a uniformly random support of size k the maximal deviation max_{k != 0} |d_S(k) - |S|^2/n| is of order sqrt(|S| log n).

Use the proved identity cAutocov_indic to turn the fluctuation statement into a concentration bound for the difference-multiplicity function, and verify the constant-profile classification exhaustively for n <= 31 by decidable computation.

The 'maximally flat, slightly negative' profile observed in the data is the signature of a design, giving a sharp null shape to compare against.

There are non-design constant-profile records, and the extremal set is larger than expected.
proof_strategy: Expand the autocorrelation of an indicator vector as the difference-multiplicity function minus k^2/n; constancy of the former is the difference-set condition by definition.
title: Constant-Profile Records and Cyclic Difference Sets

description:
The order-1 coincidence scan is now fully solved: its lag-1 correlation is c(1-b)/(1-ab) in the three latent rates, maximised over a rate window [l,u] by u(1-l)/(1-ul) and attained by the alternating curve, with supremum 1 over all curves, while every lag at least 2 is exactly zero. Conjecture that the order-r scan Y_i = X_i * ... * X_{i+r} has an analogous closed form: profile supported exactly on lags 1..r, each value a rational function of the 2r+1 latent rates in which the common product factor cancels, and each attaining supremum 1 as the rate window opens.

For the order-r coincidence scan of a product Bernoulli scan with rates in (0,1), Cov(Y_i, Y_{i+k}) = 0 for all k > r, and for 1 <= k <= r the lag-k correlation equals (prod_{j=r+1}^{r+k} p_{i+j}) * (1 - prod_{j=k}^{r} p_{i+j}) / (1 - prod_{j=0}^{r} p_{i+j}) times a factor free of the shared rates; its supremum over rate curves with values in (0,1) is 1 for every k <= r.

Extend bernExp_hit_prod3 / bernExp_hit_prod4 to products over arbitrary finite index sets, then compute the order-r covariance by the same cancellation used in maCorrProfile_lag_one_eq; verify the closed forms by exact rational evaluation for r = 2, 3 before formalising.

Mechanism selection becomes a support-length readout: the largest lag with a nonzero profile value is exactly the coincidence order, independent of all amplitudes.

Higher-order coincidence scans leak into far lags, and finite dependence range is not detectable from the profile support alone.
proof_strategy: Independence gives the joint moment as a product of rates over the union of the two index blocks; subtracting the product of marginals leaves the overlap factor, which factors as a shared product times a complementary difference, exactly as in the r = 1 case. Sharpness follows by the alternating-curve construction generalised to period r+1.
title: Finite-Range Coincidence Scans of Order r

description:
Extend the halving recursion of this cycle to arbitrary base p, proving that uniform draws from {0,…,n−1} have p-adic tie ceiling 3p/(p²+p+1) + O(1/n) for every n, not only for n = p^b. The defect Σ mⱼ³ − ((p−1)³/(p³−1))n³ is invariant under n ↦ pn, exactly as in the dyadic case. This makes the effective-base inversion of round 65 independent of the sampler.

For every prime p ≥ 2 and every n ≥ 2, the Spearman tie ceiling of the p-adic valuation statistic on {0,…,n−1} satisfies |ρ²(n) − 3p/(p²+p+1)| ≤ C_p/n with C_p ≤ 3.

Define padicRangeBlocks p n = (n − ⌈n/p⌉) :: padicRangeBlocks p ⌈n/p⌉ and mirror devE_even / devE_le / devE_ge for base p; then reuse spearmanSq_eq.

The p-adic ceiling law becomes sampler-independent and the effective-base-seven inversion is structural rather than an artefact of power-of-p sample sizes.

Some base p has range-dependent ceilings, and every effective-base inference in the catalogue must be re-derived with the actual sample size.
proof_strategy: Strong induction on n through n ↦ ⌈n/p⌉, with the geometric fixed point (p−1)³/(p³−1) cancelling the cubic term; bound the residual by 3n² uniformly in p.
title: General-Base Range Law for p-adic Tie Ceilings

description:
The defect devE is constant along doublings and contracts by 1/4 at each odd step, the signature of a Takagi-type self-similar function. Conjecture that devE(n)/n² converges, along n with prescribed binary tails, to an explicit nowhere-differentiable profile with infimum −3/7 and supremum 0.

There is a continuous nowhere-differentiable T : [0,1) → [−3/7, 0] with devE(n)/n² − T(frac(log₂ n)) → 0 along every sequence whose odd part tends to infinity.

Compute devE(n)/n² for all n < 2^20, bucket by frac(log₂ n), and check convergence of the empirical profile; then formalise the contraction estimate.

Deployment envelopes acquire a proved ceiling band rather than a single ceiling number.

The defect has genuinely non-self-similar behaviour, contradicting the doubling invariance already proved, so the failure would have to come from the odd step.
proof_strategy: Interpret the odd step as an iterated function system with contraction ratio 1/4 and apply a Banach fixed-point argument in the space of bounded functions of frac(log₂ n).
title: Takagi Profile of the Dyadic Ceiling Defect

description:
With sampler geometry excluded, the erosion must live in the response. Model the measured dial as ρ_max(b)/√(1+η(b)) and conjecture η linear in the bitlen across 56 ≤ b ≤ 116. This predicts the recorded concave acceleration while any sampler mechanism is bounded by O(2^−b).

There are α, β > 0 with |measured(b) − √(6/7)/√(1 + α + βb)| ≤ 0.01 for every recorded rung b ∈ {56, 64, 76, 92, 96, 100, 104, 108, 112}.

Fit α, β to two rungs and check the remaining seven; formalise the resulting inequalities as exact rational bounds in Lean.

The dial's fade is a single-parameter noise-accumulation law, and extrapolation to any bitlen becomes a proved bound.

Noise power is super-linear, pointing at a multiplicative rather than additive degradation of the response.
proof_strategy: Combine the exact tie ceiling with the attenuation identity for independent additive noise, then verify the nine rational inequalities by norm_num.
title: Linear Noise-Power Model for the Response Channel

description:
Whether an erosion is a cliff currently depends on the spacing of the bitlen grid. We propose an intrinsic criterion: a rung is cliff-like when its step exceeds the rho-motion attainable by o(n^2) adjacent transpositions. The conjecture is that under this criterion no rung of the recorded T-dial ladder is cliff-like.

For every consecutive pair of recorded rungs of the T-dial ladder at sample size n = 4096, the observed step is smaller than the maximal rho-motion of any chain of at most n^{3/2} adjacent transpositions.

Instantiate spearman_ge_of_chain_from_id at n = 4096 and compare with each recorded step (0.05 at U76->U84 being the largest).

The whole ladder is certified gradual in a grid-free sense, and the 'crossing test' language can be replaced by a budget statement.

At least one rung is a genuine rank-geometric cliff, which localises the mechanism to that bitlen.
proof_strategy: Evaluate the quadratic budget at K = n^{3/2} to get a maximal motion of order 24*n^3/(n(n^2-1)) ~ 24, then sharpen with the linear budget to obtain a usable threshold and compare rung by rung.
title: Intrinsic Cliff Criterion for Rank Dials

description:
The crossing dichotomy shows that eventual crossing is equivalent to the model floor L lying below the band floor, and two exhibited fades straddle it while fitting the record within the margin. The conjecture is that the ladder identifies only the product a(1-lambda) and never L itself at the recorded resolution, so no finite prefix of the ladder decides crossing.

For every finite set of recorded rungs with sup-residual tolerance eta >= 0.008 there exist contractive fades with floors on opposite sides of 0.55 fitting all of them.

Generalise crossing_undecidable_at_margin_resolution from three rungs to an arbitrary finite family by solving the two-sided interpolation constraints explicitly in the rationals.

The crossing test is unfalsifiable at the current resolution and must be replaced by an estimate of the local slope.

A specific rung count suffices to decide the crossing, giving a concrete stopping rule for the experiment.
proof_strategy: Given rungs with tolerance eta, pick L just below the floor and choose lambda close enough to 1 that the fade is within eta of a constant on the observed window; the constant model exists precisely when the window spread is at most 2*eta.
title: Floor Identifiability Under Rebound

description:
The dead-direction counterexample is conjectured to be typical rather than exceptional: for rotation-invariant random drifts the correlation between weight distance and damage vanishes as the feature dimension grows, while margin scarcity stays informative. This would explain why norm-based portability heuristics fail in practice.

For a uniformly random drift direction in dimension k, corr(weight distance, damage) = O(1/sqrt k) while corr(margin scarcity, damage) is bounded below by a positive constant.

Formalise the spherical concentration estimate for the projection onto a fixed top-2 direction and combine with margin_predicts_norm_does_not.

Norm-based portability heuristics are provably useless at scale.

Norm distance retains predictive power for structured (non-isotropic) drifts, and the relevant question becomes drift anisotropy.
proof_strategy: Concentration of the projection of a uniform sphere point onto a fixed unit vector, then transfer to the damage indicator via the top-2 identity of direction 1.
title: Genericity of Norm Anti-Prediction in High Dimension

description:
As a monotone rank dial approaches a pre-registered floor, its rapidity margin decays linearly in the bitlen while the required sample size grows as the inverse square of the margin. This predicts a last decidable rung b_max(N) for any experiment of size N, growing only logarithmically in N. The barrier, not the dial, then governs what the ladder can report.

If artanh rho(b) = z0 - s*b with s > 0 and the floor has rapidity zf, then the smallest sample size that certifies rung b is 3 + (z/(z0 - s*b - zf))^2, so b_max(N) = (z0 - zf)/s - (z/s)/sqrt(N-3) and no experiment of size N can classify any rung beyond it.

Formalise b_max as a definition over the recorded ladder and prove the two-sided bound using reqSamples_scaling and the artanh bounds of the U80 files; then evaluate at the recorded rungs 44..120.

Every reported band decision beyond b_max is uninformative, and the thread's crossing tests must be re-budgeted rather than re-run.

Either the fade is not linear in rapidity (curvature, see direction 2) or the intervals are not Fisher intervals, both of which are checkable against the recorded CIs.
proof_strategy: Combine floor_certification_criterion with the linear rapidity model; monotonicity of reqSamples in the margin (reqSamples_strict_anti) turns the certification set into an interval of bitlens, whose right endpoint is b_max.
title: Quadratic Identifiability Barrier for Fading Rank Dials

description:
Rapidity is the canonical coordinate on correlations, so the bitlen ladder is a curve in a one-dimensional hyperbolic metric. Linear fade is the geodesic case; the recorded rebounds and decelerations are curvature. Curvature is coordinate-free and can be compared with the seed-spread noise floor.

The second difference of artanh rho over equally spaced bitlens is bounded in absolute value by the rapidity image of the seed spread; i.e. every recorded non-linearity in the ladder is noise-compatible.

Compute second differences of artanh rho on the recorded rungs and compare with artanh of the seed spread, formalised as a finite inequality over explicit rationals in the style of u80_crossing_before_84.

The single-parameter linear-rapidity model is sufficient for the whole thread, and all rung-to-rung commentary about acceleration is unsupported.

There is a genuine mechanism switching on at a specific bitlen, and its location is pinned by the curvature maximum.
proof_strategy: Express second differences as logarithms of rational cross-ratios via two_artanh_eq_log, reducing each comparison to a rational power inequality closable by norm_num.
title: Hyperbolic Curvature of the Bitlen Ladder

description:
A measured advantage delta of a statistic over a baseline yields a Gram decorrelation certificate of strength growing in delta, and a resolution cost growing as delta^-2. The informativeness of a parity measurement is therefore a product of an increasing and a decreasing factor and should have an interior optimum.

The quantity (delta^2/2) * (number of draws affordable at a fixed budget with margin delta) is maximised at a unique delta*, and the recorded advantages of the T-dial thread pass through delta* between bitlen 44 and bitlen 80.

Define the informativeness functional over the rapidity advantage, prove unimodality by a derivative argument, and evaluate at the recorded advantages 0.07 and 0.053.

There is an optimal bitlen for measuring count parity, and the thread has passed it; further parity measurements are cheaper to obtain at lower bitlen.

Either the Gram certificate or the resolution cost is not the binding constraint, isolating which of the two governs parity claims.
proof_strategy: Differentiate the product of the Gram bound and the inverse resolution cost in the rapidity variable; use the strict monotonicity results (reqSamples_strict_anti, rapidity_advantage_ge) to localise the stationary point.
title: Stationary Advantage for Parity Certificates

description:
Hard top-k and dense attention are endpoints of a softmax temperature family, and the transmitted quantization variance was proved to be exactly the weight energy sum of squares. The conjecture upgrades the two endpoint values to a continuous strictly monotone curve, turning the interaction penalty into a tunable dial.

For softmax weights w(tau) on fixed non-constant scores, tau -> sum_i w_i(tau)^2 is strictly antitone on (0, infinity) with limits 1 and 1/n, and the mean-square interaction equals sigma^2 (sum_i w_i(tau)^2 - 1/n).

Formalise softmax weights, differentiate the collision probability in tau, and compose with meansquare_wRead, which already allows arbitrary weights.

Continuous, predictable budget tables parameterised by attention temperature.

Intermediate temperatures could be worse than both endpoints, a stronger deployment warning.
proof_strategy: Express the weight energy as a Renyi-2 collision probability and show its tau-derivative is a negative variance-type quantity via Cauchy-Schwarz.
title: Softmax-Temperature Interpolation of Quantization Interaction

description:
Selection stability is gated by the proved 2*eps score margin and the threshold is sharp. Adding a distribution on the top-k boundary gap converts the gate into an expected cost, and separates the two NET-83 mechanisms by their order in the quantization scale.

If the top-k boundary gap has density bounded by C near 0, the expected flip contribution to the interaction is at most 2*C*eps*diam(values); flips dominate for small eps (linear) and noise dominates for large eps (quadratic).

Formalise a finite gap ensemble, bound the flip probability by the contrapositive of selection_stable_of_margin, and bound the loss on the flip event by the value diameter.

A quantitative safety rule for 4-bit quantization at a given attention budget.

Flip costs are superlinear, implying heavy-tailed sensitivity of sparse attention to quantization.
proof_strategy: Union bound over boundary pairs times a Lipschitz bound on the sparse read.
title: Gap-Density Law for Top-k Selection Flips

description:
With the interaction term now in closed form, choosing bits and keys under a memory constraint is a convex program rather than a heuristic. The conjecture is that the 1/k interaction term strictly excludes the extreme corner of the budget simplex, so optimal deployments are interior.

For A convex decreasing in k and sigma(b)^2 = c*4^(-b), the minimiser of A(k) + Q(b) + sigma(b)^2 (1/k - 1/n) under a linear memory constraint is interior, with optimal k scaling like sigma(b)^(2/3).

Formalise the objective over the reals, use convexity of k -> 1/k, and derive first-order conditions in Lean.

A closed-form deployment rule replacing the additive budget tables that NET-83 refutes.

Corner solutions are sometimes optimal, licensing aggressive combined compression.
proof_strategy: Strict convexity plus a boundary-derivative blow-up at k -> 0 coming from the interaction term.
title: Interior Optimum for Joint Bit-Width and Key-Budget Allocation

description:
Recentering the quantization error on the selected key set was proved to remove the first-order interaction, but the corrector must know the realised selection. If quantization itself flips the selection, the corrector centres on the wrong set and a residual penalty proportional to the symmetric difference returns.

With recentering on the pre-quantization top-k set S and realised set S', the residual interaction is at most 2*eps*|S symmetric-difference S'|/k, and vanishes exactly on the stable regime characterised by the 2*eps margin condition.

Combine recentering_kills_interaction with selection_stable_of_margin, bounding the sparse error mean on the symmetric difference.

A cheap corrector with a certified residual, restoring additive budget tables in the stable regime.

Correctors must be selection-adaptive at runtime, raising their cost.
proof_strategy: Split the sparse error mean over S cap S' and the symmetric difference; the first part vanishes by construction, the second is sup-norm bounded.
title: Residual Interaction of Selection-Aware Recentering under Flips

description:
The split-count projection of the semiprime splitting-type pair carries a strictly positive but rapidly vanishing amount of information about the residue of the semiprime. We conjecture strict positivity for all cyclic orders and a log n / n decay rate. This would separate the split-count read-out from a true information wall.

For every n >= 2, Isplit n > 0, and Isplit n = O(log n / n) as n grows through orders with a bounded number of divisors.

Formalise the general fibre profile of sProj over the residue classes of prodRes (the n = 12 case is splitProfile_rigid_12), then bound the resulting entropy difference; check numerically for n up to 200.

The split count is a leaky but asymptotically negligible channel, and the only genuine wall in the model is the which-factor wall.

Some cyclic order has an exactly closed split-count channel, giving a second, arithmetic wall to classify.
proof_strategy: Show the residue-0 fibre has split-count profile (1, n-1) while all other fibres share a common profile; expand the entropy difference and estimate with the mean value theorem for log.
title: Positivity and Decay of the Split-Count Channel

description:
The which-factor wall proved here rests only on a fixed-point-free involution of each read-out fibre. We conjecture the full converse: a functional of the ordered exponent pair leaks order information exactly when it takes a swap-fixed value on a positive-measure set.

For a finite set s with an involution sigma and a read-out k with k o sigma = k on s, and any w with w o sigma = tau o w for a fixed-point-free involution tau of the alphabet, mutInfo s w k = 0; conversely if w has a sigma-invariant value on a nonempty subset then some symmetric k has positive mutual information with w.

Generalise mutInfo_eq_zero_of_flip from Bool to an arbitrary alphabet with a fixed-point-free involution, and construct the converse witness by conditioning on the sigma-fixed part.

The wall is a purely group-theoretic phenomenon, transferable to every symmetric fork in the catalog.

The Boolean case is special and the arithmetic of ordType does enter, which would be a surprise.
proof_strategy: Replace the two-element fibre count by an orbit-counting argument: each fibre is a union of free tau-orbits, so the conditional distribution of w is uniform on each orbit.
title: Orbit-Theoretic Which-Factor Wall

description:
The proved law H(Pi) = 2H(T) - #asym(n)/n^2 turns the semiprime pair entropy into an arithmetic quantity: the collision probability of two independent phi-distributed splitting types. Since sum over d | n of phi(d)^2 is multiplicative, the defect should factor over prime powers, giving a closed form for every n from a prime-power table.

S(n) = sum_{d | n} phi(d)^2 is multiplicative, hence 2 H(T) - H(Pi) = 1 - prod_{p^k || n} S(p^k)/p^{2k}.

Prove multiplicativity of S via Nat.ArithmeticFunction.IsMultiplicative and combine with card_asym_eq and pairEntropy_symmetrization_law.

The semiprime pair channel of every cyclic order is computable from the prime-power case, eliminating all remaining per-order enumeration.

The defect carries genuinely non-multiplicative arithmetic, which would contradict the independence heuristic behind the model.
proof_strategy: phi is multiplicative and d -> phi(d)^2 is the pointwise square of a multiplicative function; Dirichlet convolution with the constant function 1 preserves multiplicativity.
title: Multiplicative Factorisation of the Symmetrization Defect

description:
Degree 12 beats every other computed cyclic order in pair-channel capacity despite not being the largest. The symmetrization law splits the capacity into a divisor-richness term and a defect bounded by one bit, suggesting that the ranking is governed by the divisor function alone.

Among cyclic orders n with n + 1 prime and n <= 100, I_pair(n) / log2 n is maximised at n = 12, and in general I_pair(n) = 2H(T)(n) - conditional term with the leading behaviour controlled by d(n).

Combine typeEntropy_formula with pairEntropy_symmetrization_law to reduce the comparison to explicit divisor sums, then verify the finite range by a decidable computation.

Divisor richness, not group size, is the design parameter for maximal type-pair capacity.

A large smooth order overtakes 12, and the richness heuristic needs a correction term.
proof_strategy: Bound the conditional entropy term uniformly by one bit using the sandwich theorems, then compare 2H(T) across the finite candidate set.
title: Divisor-Richness Optimality of Degree Twelve

description:
Refining the residue of a single prime beyond the modulus f gives no extra information about its splitting type. We conjecture the semiprime analogue: refining N mod f to N mod f^k changes neither the which-factor wall nor the pair channel, because every such refinement is still symmetric in the two primes.

For every k >= 1 the which-factor mutual information against the read-out (typePair, N mod f^k) is 0, and the pair channel I({T(p),T(q)} ; N mod f^k) equals I_pair.

Instantiate whichFactor_wall with the thickened symmetric read-out; for the second half, exhibit the thickened residue as a symmetric refinement and compare conditional entropies.

No p-adic thickening of the modulus can break the semiprime wall, isolating asymmetry as the only useful side information.

Thickening leaks, and the exponent model of the semiprime channel is not faithful beyond the first level.
proof_strategy: The thickened read-out factors through a swap-invariant function of the exponent pair, so the involution hypothesis of mutInfo_eq_zero_of_flip is unchanged; for the channel equality use the data-processing order between the two read-outs in both directions.
title: Thickening Invariance of the Semiprime Pair Channel

description:
Generalize the pole-order classification of power classes from the value group Z to an arbitrary linearly ordered abelian group. The approach is to split the valuation sequence of the Hahn field and use unique divisibility of series with leading coefficient one. It matters because it would identify the root-extraction obstruction of any Hahn field with a single quotient of its value group.

For a Hahn field C[[q^G]] over a linearly ordered abelian group G, the units modulo n-th powers are isomorphic to G/nG via the order map.

Restate unitsModPowEquiv with Z replaced by a general G, reusing the order homomorphism and the binomial root construction for the unit part.

Every root-extraction question over a Hahn field reduces to arithmetic in G/nG, subsuming the Z, (1/N)Z and Q results of this thread.

Some value group carries an obstruction beyond its order quotient, which would be a genuinely new phenomenon.
proof_strategy: Split the exact sequence 1 -> units of the valuation ring -> units -> G -> 0, show the first term is n-divisible, and compute the quotient.
title: Kummer Theory of Hahn Fields over General Value Groups

description:
The pole filtration of ℂ⸨q⸩ is multiplicative and its graded pieces are one-dimensional. The approach is to build the associated graded algebra and identify it with the polynomial ring ℂ[t] graded by pole order. It matters because it would make pole order literally a degree, unifying the multiplicative and linear faces of the obstruction.

The associated graded algebra of the filtration (poleSpace m) is isomorphic as a graded ℂ-algebra to ℂ[t] with t of degree 1, the class of x of pole order m mapping to leadingCoeff(x)·t^m.

Starting from the proved multiplicativity poleSpace_mul_mem, define the graded multiplication on the pieces of finrank_gradedPiece and construct the algebra map to ℂ[t].

Pole order becomes a degree function and the m-fold product theorem becomes the statement deg(∏) = Σ deg.

The filtration fails to be multiplicative in the required strict sense, isolating a genuine obstruction to grading.
proof_strategy: Use leadingCoeff multiplicativity to define the product on graded pieces, then check the algebra axioms degree by degree using finrank_gradedPiece.
title: Associated Graded Algebra of the Pole Filtration

description:
Extend pole-order additivity from finite to infinite families. The approach is to use additivity in WithTop ℤ and show that partial products leave every bounded region of the value group. It matters because it shows the obstruction is absolute rather than quantitative for infinite moonshine-type products.

No nonzero Laurent series is a limit of partial products of an infinite family of normalized series; equivalently, the orders of the partial products diverge to -∞.

Formalize the sequence of partial products, apply orderTop_prod, and prove divergence of the order sequence.

Infinite Monster-type products only exist after a pole-cancelling renormalization such as multiplication by q^m.

Some summability condition permits convergence, which would give a genuinely new normalization for infinite products.
proof_strategy: Induct on the partial product index using orderTop_prod_normalized, then argue divergence in WithTop ℤ.
title: Divergence of Infinite Normalized Products

description:
Degree-graded exactness is the corner case d < #S of a quantitative statement about how often two distinct bounded-degree expressions can agree on a grid. Proving the density version turns the deterministic certificate into a randomised one and supplies a missing classical lemma. The reflection layer reduces the problem to a single statement over the integers.

For a domain R, finite S ⊆ R and distinct polynomials p ≠ q of total degree ≤ d, #{x ∈ Sⁿ : p(x) = q(x)} ≤ d · (#S)^(n-1).

Prove the bound by induction on n through MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv and the univariate root count, then re-derive ChartCalculus.NExpr.toZ_eq_of_grid as the special case d < #S.

The chart calculus gains a probabilistic identity test with explicit failure probability d/#S, and the deterministic theorems become the zero-error endpoint of a family.

Agreement loci of bounded-degree polynomials would exhibit unexpected concentration, contradicting the univariate root bound in some coordinate — pointing to an error in the degree bookkeeping rather than to new mathematics.
proof_strategy: Write p - q as a polynomial in the last variable with coefficients of lower total degree; split the grid according to whether the leading coefficient vanishes, apply the induction hypothesis on one part and the univariate root bound on the other.
title: Schwartz-Zippel Density for Chart Certificates

description:
Unisolvence at lattice nodes is now known to hold exactly while the exponents stay below the characteristic, both for total degree and for arbitrary downsets. The open question is quantitative: once the threshold is crossed, how many nodes are needed, and is the excess governed by collisions of the reduction map on the downset?

Over a field of prime characteristic p and a finite downset D whose coordinates reach p, the minimum cardinality of a uniqueness set for the D-supported polynomials is still #D, but no natural-number lattice node set attains it; the minimal integral node set exceeds #D by exactly the number of collisions of ℕ → 𝔽_p on D, a function of base-p digits.

For p = 2, 3 and boxes b = p, p+1 in two variables, enumerate node sets of (ZMod p)² of size #D, decide unisolvence by the rank of the evaluation matrix, and compare the minimum attained size with #D and with the digit prediction.

The cost of identity certificates in characteristic p is quantified exactly, extending the optimal node theory beyond the proved threshold.

Either the dimension bound is not tight in positive characteristic, or some non-lattice node set attains it, showing that minimal certificates are not governed by the arithmetic of the node coordinates.
proof_strategy: Lower bound: downset_uniqueness_set_card_ge already applies over any field. Upper bound: weaken the cast-injectivity hypothesis of downset_unisolvent_of_castInj to a multiset statement and count collisions of the reduction map via base-p digits.
title: Minimal Node Sets Past the Characteristic Threshold

description:
The free ring ℤ[x] detects every chart-calculus identity, and ℤ itself is a test ring. With parameters adjoined this can fail, and the conjecture is that the failure is measured by explicit torsion data computable from the syntax tree via the optimal certificate.

For the parametrised calculus, validity over ℤ implies validity over every commutative ring iff the integer N obtained as the gcd of the coefficients of toZ e₁ - toZ e₂ is 0 or 1; otherwise ZMod N is a counterexample ring.

Extend NExpr with parameter constructors, re-prove universal_iff_toZ_eq over ℤ[params], and verify the ZMod N counterexample construction on identities such as 2xy = 0.

A complete arithmetic classification of which rings detect which polynomial identities, with a decision procedure computing N from a support-adapted number of evaluations.

Some identity fails over a ring of characteristic not dividing N, which would mean the free-ring factorisation eval_X_eq_toZ does not extend to parameters as stated.
proof_strategy: Factor evaluation through ℤ[params][x] and analyse the cokernel of the coefficient map; torsion in the cokernel is exactly the obstruction.
title: Torsion Obstruction to Integer Test Rings

description:
Solo ablation costs should be exactly the point costs damped by the contraction coefficient of the downstream suffix. The upper bound is proved and is now known to be attained; the conjecture asks for a matching lower bound under a Doeblin minorisation, which would make the solo profile a computable function of the contraction spectrum and the point profile.

For a finite-state stack in which every layer satisfies a Doeblin minorisation, solo_j is bounded below by c_j' * point_j with c_j' an ergodic coefficient of the suffix after j; in particular a flat solo profile forces c_j * point_j to be constant in j.

Formalise the ergodic coefficient of a composed suffix in the Dist/Kern framework and prove a lower bound for tv (chain S mu) (chain S nu) in terms of it; instantiate on the affine family of NET59GeometricSharpness.

The solo profile becomes an invertible measurement once the contraction spectrum is known, so per-layer budgets can be recovered from ablation data plus a contraction probe.

Solo ablation data is not invertible even with contraction information, and per-layer budgeting must be abandoned in favour of set-level criteria.
proof_strategy: Hahn decomposition plus a minorisation coupling: split each kernel as eps*nu0 + (1-eps)*residual and track the residual mass through the suffix, mirroring the proof of tv_push_le_dobrushin.
title: Doeblin Lower Bound for Solo Ablation Profiles

description:
Because the measured cost of an arity-(k+1) experiment is exactly a geometric sequence in k, the ratio of consecutive measurements is the contraction coefficient itself. This turns a sweep over arities into a direct measurement of a structural quantity, with no model fitting and no assumption of layer importance.

For any finite-state stack, the ratio between the arity-(k+2) and arity-(k+1) ablation costs of a fixed layer converges to the contraction coefficient of the ablated downstream layer, with deviation from a geometric sequence bounded by the spread of the downstream coefficients.

Prove the exact geometric law for uniform spectra (already available as probe_cost), then bound the deviation for a two-valued spectrum and compare with exact rational evaluations.

A short arity sweep measures the contraction spectrum of a served model directly, giving a cheap structural diagnostic.

Ablation curves conflate contraction with point damage, and the spectrum must be probed by other means.
proof_strategy: Write the measured cost as a product over surviving layers (D2), then estimate ratios of consecutive products by the extreme coefficients of the spectrum.
title: Inversion of the Ablation Arity Curve

description:
hasExpansion_iff_flat_sub identifies each fibre of the expansion map with a coset of the flat germs. The conjecture is that this coset is as large as possible, so coefficient extensionality fails maximally rather than marginally. Flat.bigO_mul already shows the flat germs absorb multiplication by bounded germs.

The set of germs at +infinity with identically zero asymptotic expansion has cardinality 2^(2^aleph_0), and the same holds for every nonempty fibre of the expansion map.

Formalize an injection from bounded functions modulo eventual equality into flat germs via g mapsto g(x) * exp(-x), and prove distinct arguments give germs that are not eventually equal.

The failure of the analytic claim is not a boundary phenomenon: almost all functions sharing an expansion are pairwise distinct germs.

Flat germs would be small, suggesting a canonical summation operator selecting a representative in each fibre.
proof_strategy: Use Flat.bigO_mul with bounded g, then separate germs along sparse sequences where the chosen bounded functions differ by a definite amount.
title: Maximal Cardinality of the Flat Defect

description:
The convergent fragments realize exactly the geometrically bounded coefficient sequences. Divergent sequences of factorial growth admit no convergent realization, yet a Borel-type construction should give a smooth one. The fibre description hasExpansion_iff_flat_sub is already proved for arbitrary coefficient sequences, so only existence is missing.

For every a : nat -> real there is f : real -> real with HasExpansion f a, while for a of factorial growth no GeoSeries c satisfies c.coeff = a.

Formalize a cutoff construction f(x) = sum_n a_n x^{-n} chi(lambda_n / x) with rapidly chosen scales lambda_n, and verify HasExpansion by the truncation estimate used in eval_hasExpansion.

The expansion map is surjective, so the whole formal coefficient space is analytically realized and the flat kernel is its exact defect.

Some coefficient sequences are analytically unrealizable, giving a growth obstruction invisible to the formal Hahn-series picture.
proof_strategy: Cutoff construction with a summable choice of scales, each tail controlled by the already formalized geometric estimate.
title: Borel Realization Beyond the Convergent Fragment

description:
Over a q-letter alphabet the universal tie-attenuation constant of the zero-fit dial is 3q/(q^2+q+1), now proved exactly. We conjecture that a composition-constrained draw law (uniform on words of length b with exactly z zeros) exceeds that constant precisely when z/b > 1/q, so the critical surface is the uniform composition itself. The binary half-weight line is the case q = 2 of this statement.

For q >= 2, b >= 2 and 1 <= z <= b-1, the trailing-zero ceiling of the fixed-zero-count law satisfies rho^2 > 3q/(q^2+q+1) if and only if z/b > 1/q; on the line z/b = 1/q the ceiling is at most the constant, with equality only at (q,b,z) = (2,4,2).

Generalize geom_cube_bound to the q-ary composition profile (a hockey-stick slice weighted by powers of q-1), then repeat the two-sided argument of ZeroFitDialSparseWindow60; an exact-rational sweep over 2 <= q <= 6, 2 <= b <= 22 and all z already shows 0 mismatches.

Deploying the dial on any alphabet reduces to one inequality on the zero-letter frequency, and the whole binary theory (phase boundary, rates, validation band) transports with q as a parameter.

The critical composition drifts with the alphabet size, meaning the geometric profile picture is binary-specific and each alphabet needs its own phase analysis.
proof_strategy: Show the block ratio of the composition profile is monotone in the trailing-zero index, dominate the cube sum by the corresponding geometric series, and compare with the exact head-to-total ratio; the resulting polynomial inequality should degenerate at z/b = 1/q exactly as 3c^2+3c+1 = 7 does at c = 1 in the binary case.
title: Uniform-Composition Criticality for Radix-q Dials

description:
Under a pure fixed-weight law the popcount baseline is constant and its ceiling is exactly 0, while under uniform draws it has more tie headroom than the trailing-zero statistic. We conjecture the count ceiling increases monotonically in the mixing width of the weight distribution, so the measured advantage of T over count can never be explained by tie granularity anywhere between the two extremes.

For a mixture of fixed-weight laws with weight fractions supported in [1/2, 3/5], the popcount Spearman ceiling is bounded away from 1 by an absolute constant while the trailing-zero ceiling stays above 0.73; both bounds are monotone in the support width.

Model the mixture profile as a convex combination of binomial blocks, bound its cube sum below by the pure-weight case, and compare with binomBlocks; verify numerically on mixtures at bitlen 60.

The +0.151 advantage recorded at bitlen 60 is provably not a headroom artefact for any realistic draw law, closing the last confound in the dial's validation.

There exists a mixture width at which the count baseline gains enough headroom to explain the advantage, which would require re-running the round-51 comparison under that draw law.
proof_strategy: Write the mixture tie profile as a sum of fixed-weight profiles, apply the collapse result at width zero and the inversion result at full width, and interpolate with a convexity estimate on the cube-sum functional.
title: Monotone Advantage Under Weight Mixing

description:
The erased information of a multiset sorting task is a function on the refinement lattice of key partitions. We proved it is monotone; we conjecture it is a polymatroid rank function, hence submodular, with a characterised strictness locus.

For partitions P, Q of the n slots, E(P) = log2(n!/prod_B |B|!) satisfies E(P join Q) + E(P meet Q) <= E(P) + E(Q), and E is strictly monotone except across splits of singleton blocks.

Reduce to an inequality among products of factorials via the division-free identity, then verify by exhaustive decide for n <= 7 before attempting the general proof.

Multiset erasure is a polymatroid rank, importing the whole submodular optimisation toolkit into reversible-sorting thermodynamics.

Erasure is monotone but not submodular, so no matroidal structure organises key coarsening and greedy key-merging schedules can be suboptimal.
proof_strategy: Express both sides through Nat.multinomial_spec and the merge identity, reduce to a factorial inequality for the block intersection matrix, and prove it by induction on the number of blocks.
title: Coarsening Lattice of Erasure Values

description:
Column scaling by a vector of nonzero multipliers is a weight-preserving linear isomorphism of F^n. Conjecture that the entire package proved for RS codes (dimension k, distance n-k+1, information sets, dual distance k+1) transports to generalized Reed–Solomon codes, and that the class of GRS codes is closed under duality. This upgrades a single family to the standard workhorse family of coding theory.

For distinct α : Fin n → F and v : Fin n → Fˣ, the code GRS(α,v) = {(v_i p(α_i))_i : deg p < k} has finrank k, minimum distance n-k+1, and its dual is GRS(α,w) for an explicit w.

Define the scaling automorphism as a LinearEquiv of Fin n → F, prove hammingNorm invariance, and push ReedSolomonMDS.minDist_code and minDist_dualCode_code through it; identify the dual multiplier via Lagrange interpolation of ∏_{j≠i}(α_i-α_j).

All MDS results in the catalog apply to the full GRS family, including the dual, giving a duality-closed class.

The failure must occur in the dual multiplier identification, isolating a genuine obstruction in the pairing rather than in the weight theory.
proof_strategy: Weight invariance under coordinatewise units; transport of finrank along a LinearEquiv; explicit computation of the dual multiplier from the derivative of ∏(X-α_j).
title: Generalized Reed–Solomon Transport of MDS Equality

description:
The order-profile (type) entropy of a finite abelian group is conjectured to be a complete isomorphism invariant for orders up to 100. This cycle proved the first non-trivial instance, separating C12 from C6xC2 at degree 12. If true, a single measured real number identifies the Galois group of an abelian rung.

For finite abelian A, B with |A| = |B| = n <= 100, orderEntropy A = orderEntropy B implies A ≅ B.

Enumerate all abelian groups of each order n <= 100 in Lean as products of ZMod p^k, compute orderEntropy in closed form as a rational combination of log2 p, and prove distinctness by rational linear independence of the log2 p.

The measured entropy of a rung determines its Galois group, making the ladder's single scalar a complete classifier.

There is a collision pair of abelian groups sharing an order profile; the entropy must then be refined by a second statistic (e.g. the pair-channel spectrum).
proof_strategy: Write H(A) = sum over divisors d of (n_d/n) log2 (n/n_d) with n_d = #elements of order d; reduce equality of two such expressions to equality of the vectors (n_d) using Q-linear independence of {log2 p}; then invoke the fact that the order profile of an abelian group determines its type decomposition for small orders.
title: Entropy Injectivity for Abelian Galois Rungs

description:
The spreading law gives at least R/epsilon active notches. For a dial whose notch sizes themselves decay geometrically with ratio q, the number of notches needed to accumulate a decline R should grow like log(1/(1-q)) faster than the linear count. The conjecture quantifies how much more gradual a geometric dial is than the worst case.

If the notch sizes satisfy d_{k+1} <= q*d_k with 0 < q < 1 and the total decline is R with max notch epsilon, then the number of positive notches is at least log(1 - R*(1-q)/epsilon)/log q.

Prove the geometric-sum inequality in Lean over the rationals and instantiate with the exact cap notch (3/4)*8^{-u} of ceiling_colStep_exact.

Any geometrically decaying dial is provably cliff-free with a bound depending only on q, no data needed.

Gradualness is genuinely a data property and cannot be inferred from the notch decay alone.
proof_strategy: Sum the geometric majorant of the notches and invert the resulting inequality; formalise with induction plus a monotone log bound over the rationals.
title: Logarithmic Spreading Exponent for Geometric Dials

description:
A one-key convention move changes the Spearman ceiling of a balanced profile by less than 4/N. Iterating along a path of single-key edits should show that any convention affecting t keys changes the ceiling by less than 4t/N, making all sublinear conventions invisible at recorded bit lengths.

For a balanced profile of N keys, any two tie profiles differing by a transport of t keys satisfy |rho^2 - rho'^2| < 4t/N, provided every intermediate profile stays balanced.

Iterate convention_move_bound along an explicit edit path and control the balance condition at each step.

Convention-freedom of the dial is established once and for all, for every convention of sublinear support.

There exist balanced-to-balanced edit paths whose cumulative effect is superlinear, which would locate a real convention sensitivity.
