proof_strategy: Induction on t with the triangle inequality, plus a lemma that balance is preserved along the canonical edit path.
title: Tensorised Convention Invisibility

description:
The prime-power indicator is a sparse 0/1 feature on the key range {1,...,N}. The proved ceiling gain <= B^2 * density converts sparsity into a hard bound on the augmented dial. Combining it with an elementary sieve bound on the density of prime powers yields an asymptotic no-signal theorem for the prime-power dial.

For every N, every draw regime p on {1,...,N} and every residual with sup-norm at most B, the prime-power augmentation gain is at most B^2 * delta_N where delta_N is the regime mass of the prime powers; and for the uniform regime delta_N -> 0, so the gain tends to 0 uniformly over bounded residuals.

Formalise #{n <= N : IsPrimePow n} <= N/3 + O(log N) via the mod-6 sieve (all prime powers above 3 are congruent to +-1 mod 6, plus at most log_2 N + log_3 N powers of 2 and 3), then instantiate gain_le_sup_sq_density and gain_lt_of_density_small.

The prime-power feature is asymptotically worthless as a per-N dial for bounded residuals, closing the EXTENDED-DIAL question in the negative for large key ranges.

The residual must be unbounded in sup norm, which would relocate the effect to heavy-tailed yield profiles and change the experimental design.
proof_strategy: Sieve bound on the counting function of prime powers, then the already-proved sparse-feature ceiling; the limit statement is a direct epsilon/B^2 comparison.
title: Prime-Power Density Ceiling for Integer Key Populations

description:
Cycle 2 showed that bisimulation plus out-degree matching still fails to determine isomorphism, the obstruction being sharing. The conjecture is that a single integer, the sharing index (reachable worlds minus unravelling nodes), is a complete invariant for graded-bisimilar finite pointed models. This would turn the residual gap into a computable number and identify the unravelling as the canonical representative.

For finite pointed models M, N that are bisimilar with equal out-degrees at every related pair, M and N are isomorphic if and only if their sharing indices coincide; the unravelling is the unique representative of sharing index 0.

Define the unravelling of a tag-indexed frame inside the satF semantics, prove it bisimilar and multiplicity-matched to the original, and verify the criterion on the shareR/treeR witnesses of BisimulationBeyondMultiplicity.lean before attempting the general finite case.

The bisimulation/isomorphism gap becomes fully quantified: modal observation plus counting plus one integer determines the model up to isomorphism.

A second, non-numeric obstruction to isomorphism exists beyond folding, and the resolution hierarchy has at least four strictly distinct levels.
proof_strategy: Construct the unravelling by finite paths, prove a bisimulation with degree matching, then build an isomorphism by induction on height between two models with equal sharing index using the pigeonhole argument of isEmpty_pointedIso_share_tree run in reverse.
title: Sharing Index as the Exact Residue of Graded Bisimulation

description:
Cycle 5 proved that depth-k observation determines the modal theory of worlds of height at most k. The algorithmic counterpart is that partition refinement decides bisimilarity on a truncation in exactly that many rounds, with the chain frame as the worst case. This would turn a semantic criterion into a verified decision procedure with a matching lower bound.

Partition refinement decides bisimilarity of the worlds 0..N of any tag-indexed frame in at most N rounds, the bound being attained on the chain frame, and the number of bisimulation classes below N is at most N+1 with equality exactly for the chain.

Implement the refinement as a Lean function on Finset partitions, prove its fixed point equals Bisim.Bisimilar restricted to the truncation using Collapse.depthEq_iff_modEq_of_le, and measure rounds on chainR, multR, shareR by evaluation.

Every bisimulation-invariant statement about truncated catalog frames becomes machine-checkable by computation with a proved optimal round bound.

Refinement rounds and modal depth are not the same resource, revealing a gap between logical and algorithmic measures of behaviour.
proof_strategy: Show the k-th refinement equals depth-k equivalence by induction on k, then apply the collapse theorem to conclude at k = N; sharpness reuses not_depthEq_succ_chain.
title: Partition Refinement with Tight Round Complexity

description:
Adding the graded modality 'at least j successors satisfy a' to the language should characterize exactly the invariance class strictly between bisimulation and isomorphism that cycles 1 and 2 bracketed. The conjecture is a Hennessy-Milner theorem for that language, with graded bisimulation on the semantic side.

On tag-indexed frames, two pointed models satisfy the same graded modal formulas if and only if they are related by a graded bisimulation, and the induced invariance class strictly contains BisimInv and is strictly contained in IsoInv.

Define the graded language and its semantics by counting successors with succList, prove transport along graded bisimulations, and prove the converse by conjoining the finitely many separating formulas exactly as in modEq_forth; strictness reuses multR and the shareR/treeR pair.

The observational ladder gains a proved middle rung, and multiplicity-sensitive invariants get an intrinsic logical characterization.

Counting observations are not compositional in this setting, which would make out-degree an invariant with no modal definition at all.
proof_strategy: Mirror the Hennessy-Milner proof of BisimulationResolution.lean, replacing the existential successor matching by a Finset.card_bij argument between successor sets satisfying each characteristic formula.
title: Graded Hennessy-Milner Theorem for the Multiplicity Layer

description:
Since truncated GL theories and their reflection-depth spectra are bisimulation invariants, unravelling a realizing frame cannot change the spectrum. The conjecture is that every realizable spectrum is realizable on a sharing-free frame with linearly many worlds.

Every reflection-depth spectrum realized by some tag-indexed frame truncated at N is realized by a tree frame, and the minimal world count of such a tree frame grows linearly in the length of the spectrum.

Apply TheoryTransfer.depthReflection_congr_of_bisim to the unravelling of the frames used in TagReflectionDepthRigidity and count worlds.

All catalog realizability results acquire a canonical sharing-free normal form, simplifying every downstream rigidity argument.

Sharing is proof-theoretically economical: some spectra need exponentially fewer worlds when folding is allowed, which is itself a strong complexity statement.
proof_strategy: Combine the bisimulation invariance of provability with an explicit unravelling and a count of the paths below the truncation level.
title: Tree Normal Form for Reflection-Depth Spectra

description:
**Conjecture.**  Let `f : ℝ → ℝ` be continuous and piecewise linear with exactly `r`
kinks.  Then the minimal `k` for which there exist `a b c : Fin k → ℝ` and `p q : ℝ`
with `reluNet a b c p q = f` is exactly `r`.

*The key insight is* that `reluNet_kink_witness` already converts a nonvanishing
discrete second difference into a *distinct* unit whenever the test windows are
disjoint, so the lower bound `r ≤ k` needs no convexity, no differentiability, and no
sign pattern — only separation of the kinks; the matching upper bound is the telescoping
construction used in `intervalStep_eq_four_relu`.

*Why now?*  This cycle proved the two smallest instances (`r = 2` for the scalar
clipped update, `r = 4` for the interval update) with the same mechanism, and
`descent_step_relu_width_dichotomy` shows the width is a genuine invariant of the
tropical minimizer geometry rather than an artifact of the formula.

---
title: Width equals the number of curvature sites (general PL width theorem)

description:
Model the round-trip as a completely positive
   trace-preserving map (Deutsch's D-CTC prescription) on density matrices and prove
   existence of self-consistent mixed states via the Brouwer/Schauder fixed-point
   theorem on the compact convex state space, connecting to the catalog's existing
   quantum-information developments.
title: Quantum Novikov principle

description:
mixing weight `a ∈ (0,1)` the supremum of the convexity defect
of `f ∘ gridRound δ` over convex `L`-Lipschitz `f` and all weight pairs equals
`2·L·r = L·δ` and is **never attained**; moreover the set of attained defects is
dense in `[0, L·δ]`, with gap structure governed by the three-distance theorem for
the continued fraction of `a`.  Consequently the *expected* defect of a stochastic
interpolation schedule is strictly smaller for an irrational mixing weight than for
any rational weight of comparable granularity.
title: mixing weight `a ∈ (0,1)` the supremum of the convexity defect

description:
Equivalently: for every `R ≤ 1/2` and every placement of the points, all connected
components are finite.  The upper bound `Rmin ≤ 1/2` is proved (the line configuration
`lineConfig`); the formalised lower bound is only `Rmin ≥ 1/3`.  Evidence: an exhaustive
convex optimisation over all periodic drifting paths of period `≤ 4`, and a random
search for periods `5 … 8`, never produced a longest edge below `1/2`
(`ComputationalEvidence.md`).  *Falsifiable*: a periodic path of some period `T` with
nonzero drift and all edges `< 1/2` would refute it.
title:
Equivalently: for every `R ≤ 1/2` and every placement of the points, all connected
components are finite.

description:
Define `D_k(n) = Π_k(n) − M_k(n) ≥ 0`.  Cycle 3 proves `D_k(n) = 0` iff `n` is squarefree, and
computes the *local* deficiency exactly:
`Π_k(p^e) − M_k(p^e) = (p−1) ∑_{i<e} p^{ik} (L^{e−1−i} − p^{e−1−i})` with `L = p^k+p−1`
(`gcdMoment_prime_pow_deficiency`).  The conjecture is the global counterpart: for `k ≥ 3` the
pair `(n, D_k(n))` determines the full exponent pattern of `n`, and `D_k(n)/Π_k(n)` is, up to
`O(p_min^{-k})`, the fraction of the divisor lattice of `n` that is not squarefree.
**The key insight is** that the local deficiency is a difference of two geometric series whose
ratios are `p^k` and `p`, so `log_p (D_k(p^e))` is `(e−1)k + O(1)`: each repeated prime
contributes a *quantised* amount to the deficiency, and the quantisation levels for distinct
primes are incommensurable once `k ≥ 3`.
**Why now?** Both inputs are formalised — the exact local deficiency and the multiplicativity of
`M_k` and `Π_k` — and cycle 4 identifies `D_k(n) = 0` with the unique maximiser of the
refinement order, so the global statement is a bookkeeping problem about products of explicitly
known local terms, exactly the shape that Conjecture 2 also needs.
title: Define `D_k(n) = Π_k(n) − M_k(n) ≥ 0`.

description:
Composition of radius-`r` and
   radius-`s` cellular automata has radius at most `r + s`; maps of exactly one
   fixed radius are generally not closed under composition.  Define the full
   reversible finite-radius group together with its radius filtration, and
   prove the composition and inverse-radius bounds that are available.
title: Radius filtration under composition

description: The current register is uniform, so cardinality and Shannon entropy agree. For nonuniform input distributions, define the logical loss through pushforward entropy and prove a work bound proportional to `H(p) - H(f_*p)`. This would distinguish a many-to-one map whose unused fibers have zero probability from one that actually destroys likely distinctions.
title: Nonuniform inputs and fiber-weighted reset cost

description:
**Zero-energy escape (the `E = 0` half of old Conjecture 4).** `strictly_convex_escape`
  (a general convexity lemma) plus positivity of the potential gives
  `nonneg_energy_escape`: at `E ≥ 0` the moment of inertia tends to `+∞` in forward or in
  backward time, and hence `bounded_motion_energy_neg`: every eternally bounded three-body
  motion has **strictly negative** energy.
title: Zero-energy escape (the `E = 0` half of old Conjecture 4).

description:
**Spectral form of the entropy.** For every finite dead-end-free graph carrying a Perron datum (a
  strictly positive eigenvector of the transfer matrix), the entropy equals the logarithm of the
  eigenvalue. This was Conjecture 1 of the previous cycle, now proved in Perron form: the analytic
  invariant is computed by linear algebra. The proof pinches the number of length-$n$ paths between two
  constant multiples of $\lambda^n$ using only the minimum and maximum of the eigenvector.
title: Spectral form of the entropy.

description:
**The analogy distance is an attained metric** (`Catalog/Probability/AnalogyMetric.lean`).
  `analogyDist M N` — the least defect of an approximate structural analogy — is
  realized as a minimum over the finitely many atom-preserving renamings
  (`optimalAnalogy`), so `∃ ApproxAnalogy M N ε ↔ analogyDist M N ≤ ε`
  (`analogyDist_le_iff`).  It satisfies the metric axioms (`analogyDist_self`,
  `analogyDist_comm`, `analogyDist_triangle`, all read off from the groupoid
  operations), lies in `[0,1]` (`analogyDist_mem_Icc`), and its zero set is exactly
  isomorphism (`analogyDist_eq_zero_iff`), so it is a genuine metric on isomorphism
  classes.  Depth-`d` truth probabilities are `1 − (1 − d(M,N))^d`-continuous with
  the optimal renaming (`optimal_transport_le`), and the constant is exact:
  `Sharp.dist_eq` computes `d(exactSys, leakySys ε) = ε` for the extremal family,
  which attains the modulus.  This closes Conjecture 3 of the previous cycle.
title: The analogy distance is an attained metric

description:
the **Helly number `d + 1` for tropically convex subsets of `ℝ^d`**
  (`tropConvex_helly`) and its sharpness (`tropConvex_helly_number_sharp`),
  which **settles the previous cycle's conjecture**: it is true for every
  `d ≥ 1` (`tropicalHellyConjecture_holds`) with a strictly better constant than
  the conjectured `2 * d`, and false for `d = 0`
  (`tropicalHellyConjecture_zero`);
title: the Helly number `d + 1` for tropically convex subsets of `ℝ^d`

description:
**Multi-prime cap (new this cycle; Conjecture 1 of the previous cycle, cap half).**
  `ORDial.multiInfo_le_orCap`: for every profile, every finite abelian class group and
  every number `k ≥ 2` of prime factors, the `k`-prime OR channel also obeys `Φ_k ≤ g(2)`.
  The proof runs through the multi-prime mean law `avg f_k = μ^k` (`ORDial.avg_forkPow`),
  the window law `f_k ≤ μ^{k-1}` (`ORDial.forkPow_le_pow`), and the new two-variable
  analytic core `H(μx) − μH(x) ≤ orCap` for `x ≤ μ²` (`ORDial.prodEnt_le_orCap`).
title: Multi-prime cap (new this cycle; Conjecture 1 of the previous cycle, cap half).

description: Replace configuration-description length by a transition cost, such as the number of state changes or a weighted dissipation functional. Prove upper and lower asymptotic bounds under explicit architecture assumptions. This would separate the proved combinatorial comparison from claims about actual silicon or neural tissue.
title: Physical energy model

description:
Let `Λ ⊆ ℝ^d` be a full-rank lattice with basis matrix `B`. The data
`|t(P + v) ∩ Λ|` for all real `t > 0` and all `v ∈ Λ` determines `1_P` almost everywhere, with
constants depending only on `λ_1(Λ)` and `λ_d(Λ)`; moreover, the sparse-grid probe reconstructs
`1_P` using `O(1)` counting queries per probe point. Consequently, a "lattice-count oracle" for a
secret body `P` (as arises in lattice-based counting/`CVP`-style side channels) leaks `P` up to
null sets, with query complexity polynomial in the desired accuracy and in `λ_d/λ_1`.
title: Let `Λ ⊆ ℝ^d` be a full-rank lattice with basis matrix `B`. The data

description:
**C1 (functoriality of the classification).**  `inducedHom_id` shows the identity functor
  induces the identity homomorphism, `inducedHom_comp_conj` shows the homomorphism induced by
  a composite is conjugate to the composite of the induced homomorphisms, and
  `toConjClass_comp` upgrades this to an exact identity of conjugacy classes.  So the
  classification bijection is compatible with composition; what remains open is the full
  2-categorical (bicategorical) statement, recorded as N1 below.
title: C1 (functoriality of the classification).

description:
Also resolved: the `Tor`-theoretic half of the old Conjecture 4.  Mathlib derives `Tor`
in the *second* variable and does not relate it to flatness; using the δ-functor
structure in the *first* variable, `Catalog.Bridges.flat_iff_isZero_Tor_one` now proves
both directions of `Module.Flat R N ↔ ∀ M, IsZero (Tor 1 M N)`, together with
`isZero_Tor_succ_of_flat_left` (flat modules are `Tor`-acyclic in the underived
variable).
title: Also resolved: the `Tor`-theoretic half of the old Conjecture 4.

description:
**QVandermonde.lean** *(settles the replacement sub-conjecture (C3) of the previous cycle)* —
  the **q-Vandermonde (Chu–Vandermonde) convolution**
  `[m+n choose k]_q = ∑_{a+b=k} q^{(m-a)b} · [m choose a]_q · [n choose b]_q`
  (`poincare_add`) over an arbitrary commutative semiring and with no restriction on `k, m, n`,
  proved by induction from `q`-Pascal with a term-by-term exponent identity
  (`qvandermonde_exponent`); its `m ↔ n` symmetry (`poincare_add_symm`), which is invisible
  term by term; the recovery of `q`-Pascal as the case `n = 1` (`poincare_succ_of_add`); the
  classical Vandermonde convolution at `q = 1` (`choose_add_convolution`); and the geometric
  form `#Gr(k, V) = ∑_{a+b=k} q^{(m-a)b} · #Gr(a, 𝔽_q^m) · #Gr(b, 𝔽_q^n)` for `dim V = m + n`
  (`card_grassmannian_add`), the point count of the stratification of `Gr(k, U ⊕ W)` by
  `dim (X ∩ U)`.
title: QVandermonde.lean

description:
**Conjecture D2, settled for abelian `G`** (`SolomonZetaPadicGroupRing.lean`).  For a finite
  commutative group `G` of exponent dividing `pᵉ`, the group ring `ℤ_p[G]` is local
  (`isLocalRing_padicMonoidAlgebra`) with maximal ideal the preimage of `pℤ_p` under the
  augmentation and residue field `𝔽_p` (`residueFieldPadicMonoidAlgebraEquiv`).  Consequently
  the local Solomon formula applies verbatim to free `ℤ_p[G]`-lattices:
  `#Aut(X)·#{N ≤ Λⁿ : Λⁿ/N ≅ X} = (∏_{i<d}(pⁿ − p^i))·#(𝔪X)ⁿ`
  (`autCard_mul_quotIsoCount_padicMonoidAlgebra_free`), in particular for `Λ = ℤ_p[ℤ/pℤ]`
  (`autCard_mul_quotIsoCount_padicCyclic_free`).  The bridge is the coefficientwise reduction
  `ℤ_p[G] → 𝔽_p[G]`, whose kernel lies in `p·ℤ_p[G]`.
title: Conjecture D2, settled for abelian `G`

description:
**Conjecture D5, settled in corrected form** (`SolomonZetaFreenessCriterion.lean`).  For `R`
  noetherian local with finite residue field and all `R/𝔪ʲ` finite, a finitely generated
  `R`-module `M` is free of rank `n` **iff** `Σ_{Y ≤ X} μ(Y,X)·#Hom(M,Y) = (∏_{i<d}(qⁿ − q^i))·#(𝔪X)ⁿ`
  for every finite quotient type `X` (`nonempty_linearEquiv_free_iff_mobiusWeight_eq`, and
  `..._padic` over `ℤ_p`).  The engine is a *counting rigidity*
  (`ker_le_ker_of_card_surj_eq`): composition with a surjection `π : Rⁿ ↠ M` embeds surjections
  `M ↠ X` into surjections `Rⁿ ↠ X`, so equality of counts forces every surjection `Rⁿ ↠ X` to
  kill `ker π`; taking `X = Rⁿ/𝔪ʲRⁿ` and Krull's intersection theorem gives `ker π = 0`.
  Two by-products: free lattices *maximise* the weights (`mobiusWeight_le_freeMobiusWeight`),
  and the conjecture's claim that one test space of residual dimension `n+1` suffices is
title: Conjecture D5, settled in corrected form

description:
- **Uniqueness of $3003$.** Is $3003$ the only integer of multiplicity exactly eight? A
  competitor would have to be simultaneously triangular and an adjacent repetition; by the
  classification, the next adjacent repetition already has $29$ digits.
- **Non-adjacent infinite families.** Are there infinitely many $t$ with $N(t) \ge 6$ coming
  from non-adjacent column coincidences such as $120 = \binom{16}{2} = \binom{10}{3}$? Each
  fixed pair of columns $(j,k)$ gives a curve $\binom{n}{j} = \binom{m}{k}$ with, typically,
  finitely many integral points, so any infinite family must use unbounded columns.
- **Sharpening the counting bound.** Restricting the admissible box by the smoothness theorem —
  the value must itself be $\sqrt{2X}$-smooth — should lower the logarithmic factor in
  $\#\{t \le X : N(t) \ge 3\} \le (\sqrt{2X}+2)(\log_2 X+1)$.
- **Improving the universal bound.** The row pigeonhole $4^b \le (2b+1)\binom{2b}{b}$ is nearly
  sharp; the remaining loss in $N(t) \le \log_2 t + \log_2(2\log_2 t + 1) + 1$ is the crude
  "at most two occurrences per folded column index".
title: Uniqueness of $3003$.

description: For every irreducible crystallographic root system `Φ`, a Mathlib definition of Au's normalized Witten zeta function extends meromorphically to a neighborhood of `2 / h`, has no pole of order greater than one there, and its complex residue equals `RootInvariants.universalLeadingResidue` for the invariant data of `Φ`.
title: Full analytic leading-pole theorem

description:
**C1 (the uncertainty principle is not about `𝓕`) — now a theorem.**
  `abstract_uncertainty` proves: if `T` is the transform with kernel
  `k : G → H → ℂ`, all entries of modulus `≤ μ`, and `f` can be reconstructed
  from `T f` by a kernel `l : H → G → ℂ` with entries of modulus `≤ ν`, then
  every non-zero `f` satisfies `1 ≤ μ · ν · |supp f| · |supp (T f)|`.  Three
  instantiations are proved: `donoho_stark_of_abstract` (Fourier, `μ = 1`,
  `ν = |G|⁻¹`, recovering the Donoho–Stark constant `|G|`),
  `matrix_uncertainty` (the Elad–Bruckstein coherence bound `1 ≤ μ² ·
  |supp f| · |supp (Uᵀ f)|` for any matrix with orthonormal rows) and
  `unbiased_uncertainty` (the normalised complex-Hadamard / mutually-unbiased
  form `n ≤ |supp f| · |supp (Uᵀ f)|`), with `hadamard2_uncertainty` as an
  explicit non-Fourier witness.  Sharpness is also formalised:
  `support_kernelTransform_delta` and `flat_kernel_card_bound` show that for a
  flat kernel Dirac masses attain the bound, so the constant `(μν)⁻¹` is
  optimal.  The unexpected structural conclusion is that the relevant invariant
  is the **coherence `μν`**, not the group order: `|G|` only ever enters through
  the normalisation of the inversion kernel.
title: C1 (the uncertainty principle is not about `𝓕`) — now a theorem.

description:
**C7 (the ceiling periodic constant is optimal) — PROVED.**  In `AsaiPeriodicOptimal.lean`
  the extremal `q`-periodic family `resFamily q D` (one form per residue class, eigenvalue
  `√D` on its own class) has Gram matrix exactly `D · 1_{m ≡ n (q)}` (`gram_resFamily`), and
  `isLeast_periodic_constant` proves that `D · ⌈N/q⌉` is the **least** admissible large sieve
  constant for it: the upper bound is `largeSieve_of_periodic_gram_ceil`, the matching lower
  bound `le_of_largeSieve_resFamily` comes from testing the inequality against the indicator
  of the residue class of `0`, whose size is at least `⌈N/q⌉`
  (`ceilDiv_le_card_residue_zero`).  `periodic_saving` records the resulting gain over the
  trivial constant `D · N`.
title: C7 (the ceiling periodic constant is optimal) — PROVED.

description:
**sufficiency, proved** (`exists_tropEigenBot_of_stronglyConnected`): if the support
  digraph `Supp A = {(i,j) : A i j ≠ ⊥}` is strongly connected then `A` has an eigenvalue
  with a finite eigenvector, and that eigenvalue lies between the smallest and largest
  finite entry.  The proof is a *penalty perturbation*: replace each `⊥` by
  `−(n·(max − min) − min + 1)`, apply the finite-entry theorem `exists_tropEigen`, normalise
  the eigenvector to have maximum `0`, and use short support walks
  (`exists_short_supp_walk`) to confine its entries to `[−n·(max − min), 0]` *independently
  of the penalty*; a row optimum at a `⊥` position would then have to be within that box,
  which the penalty excludes.
title: sufficiency, proved

description:
**QFactorialRatio.lean** — the **ratio formula**
  `[n choose k]_q · [k]_q ! · [n-k]_q ! = [n]_q !` over an arbitrary commutative semiring
  (`poincare_mul_qFact`), proved by induction from `q`-Pascal, together with its geometric
  form `#Gr(k,V) · #Fl(𝔽_q^k) · #Fl(𝔽_q^{n-k}) = #Fl(V)`
  (`card_grassmannian_mul_card_flags`), the point-count shadow of the fibration
  `Fl(V) → Gr(k,V)` with fibre `Fl(W) × Fl(V/W)`.
title: QFactorialRatio.lean

description:
> **Resolved since the previous cycles.**
> * "AND universally beats OR" is a theorem: `Ior_le_Iand`, `Ior_lt_Iand`,
>   from the general mirror principle `binI_mirror`.
> * "`Is n · n / log₂ n → 1`" and "`Is n ≥ c/n`" are **false**, refuted formally
>   by `not_tendsto_one_of_scaled` and `not_exists_linear_lower_bound`: the true
>   order is `log₂ n / n²`.
> * The former Conjecture 4, "`n² · Is n · log 2 − log n → 2`", is now the
>   theorem `Is_exact_constant`, with the explicit rate `2/n`
>   (`Is_const_bound`); the sharper second-order statement
>   `n(L(n) − 2) → −1/2` is the theorem `Is_second_order`.  Conjecture 3 below
>   is the arity-`r` generalisation that survives.
> * The first half of Conjecture 3 — `n^r · Is_r(n) · log 2 − log n → r` — is
>   now the theorem `IsR_arity_constant`, for **every** arity `r ≥ 2`, with the
>   explicit rate `2r/(n−1) + 6·2^r/n` (`IsR_arity_constant_bound`).  The
>   mechanism conjectured there is exactly what the proof shows: the column with
>   `m = 0` non-splitting factors contributes `n log n`, the column `m = 1`
>   contributes `r`, and every column `m ≥ 2` contributes `O(1)` because its two
>   cells cancel to first order.  What remains open is only the second-order
>   coefficient `r(r−3)/4` for `r ≥ 3`.  Conjecture 6 below is the corresponding
>   statement about how loose the χ² bound is.
> * The single-fork half of Conjecture 4 is now a theorem **in quantitative
>   form**: the arity-`r` channel exists as a formal object (`IsR`), obeys the
>   one-bit cap at every arity (`IsR_le_one`), and satisfies the exact χ² law
>   `chiSquare_forkJointR` giving `IsR r n ≤ (n−1)^{1−r}/log 2`
>   (`IsR_le_geometric`) — so extra factors *strictly dilute* rather than
>   amplify, with `IsR r n → 0` as `r → ∞` for every `n ≥ 3`
>   (`IsR_tendsto_zero_arity`), while `IsR r 2 = 1` for every `r`
>   (`IsR_two_eq_one`).  What remains open in Conjecture 4 is only the *many
>   independent forks* version.
> * The prior-theoretic half of the former Conjecture 5 is now the theorem
>   `balanced_prior_of_mutualInfo_eq_one`, with the corollary `Is_eq_one_iff`
>   (`Is n = 1 ↔ n = 2`).  Conjecture 5 below is what remains open: the cap over
>   arbitrary 0/1 profiles, where the class alphabet is no longer binary.
title: > Resolved since the previous cycles.

description:
(`SemigroupGaps.lean`): `Δ_{a,b} = 1 − (1−X)·G` where `G` is the gap
   generating polynomial of `⟨a,b⟩`; `coeff_n Δ = [n ∈ ⟨a,b⟩] − [n−1 ∈ ⟨a,b⟩]`; all
   coefficients are `0, ±1`; **`⟨a,b⟩` is a symmetric semigroup**, proved *from* the
   palindromicity of the knot invariant; and `2·#gaps = (a−1)(b−1)` (Sylvester's genus).
title: Semigroup gaps

description:
For `k ≥ 1` write `L_k(t) = t^k + t − 1`.  Then the moment `∏_i L_k(a_i)` over a factorisation
`N = ∏_i a_i` is *strictly Schur-convex in the multiset of `log a_i`*, and the boundary case is
exactly `k = 2`: `log L_k(e^u)` is strictly convex in `u` for `k ≥ 3`, affine to first order for
`k = 2` on the locus `a+b+c+d = N−1`, and degenerate for `k = 1`.
**The key insight is** that `pairMoment_eq_euler` turns every identifiability statement in this
project into a statement about one univariate function `L_k`, so the `k = 2` exception is not an
accident of the algebra but the vanishing of a single convexity defect.
**Why now?** The two-factor case is fully proved in both directions (strict for `k ≥ 3` via
`pairMoment_spread_strict_unconditional`, with an explicit two-parameter family of collisions for
`k = 2`), so the convexity statement can be tested against a complete data set rather than a
heuristic one.
title: For `k ≥ 1` write `L_k(t) = t^k + t − 1`.

description: Define the honeycomb graph explicitly, define its SAW counts, and state the Duminil-Copin–Smirnov theorem as an honest theorem target equating its connective constant with `√(2 + √2)`. The algebraic facts proved here can then serve as downstream lemmas; they are not a substitute for the parafermionic-observable proof.
title: Hexagonal lattice model

description: Compute the Levi-Civita connection, Riemann and Ricci tensors, scalar curvature, and Einstein tensor. Then define `T = G/(8π)` and prove the Einstein field equation by construction. This is the precise interpretation of “solution”: the metric generally is not a vacuum solution, but determines a stress-energy tensor.
title: Curvature and Einstein tensor

description:
Can the exponent-depth lower bound be promoted from "algorithms restricted to free witnesses" to
"algorithms with black-box access to arithmetic modulo `N`"? A generic-group-model result of this
shape would be the strongest available formal evidence that factoring is classically hard, and it is
the precise open problem the framework isolates.
title: C3. An unconditional lower bound

description:
Because descent is `O(1)`, the depth of a node is the
   number of energy iterations needed to return to `log 2`. Bounding this by
   `O(log c)` (via the growth `r ↦ r+2` and `r ↦ 2 ± 1/r`) would give a formal
   `O(log c)`-time membership/indexing algorithm for the Berggren tree derived
   purely from the neuron.
title: Depth from energy

description: Specify a concrete infinite- or transfinite-dimensional manifold category (Hilbert manifolds, Fréchet manifolds, or ordinal-indexed local models). The present work does not call `ℓ²` a two-dimensional surface or formalize manifold charts, because those claims would not follow from infinite Hausdorff dimension alone.
title: Manifold notions

description: The robust inequality does not require a globally split state space. It can therefore be applied locally to nontrivial finite coverings. A complementary topological development should construct an explicit connected two-sheeted cover and prove that it has local sheet swaps but no continuous global fibrewise choice of the opposite sheet.
title: Nontrivial coverings

description:
A ReLU network computes a
   tropical rational function; the `b`-smoothed network computes a
   log-sum-exp expression. Quantifying the uniform distance between a smoothed
   network of depth `d` and its tropical limit (an `O(d · log(width)/b)` bound)
   would extend the bridge theorem from one neuron to a whole architecture.
title: Tropical polynomials from neural networks

description: For the bandwidth-scaled kernel in Conjecture 2, retaining the largest `⌈C√N⌉` normalized weights yields total discarded mass at most `ε` with probability at least `1-N^{-2}`, for a bandwidth `β(d,N,ε)` specified in advance. A counterexample consists of a sampled configuration whose normalized tail mass exceeds `ε`.
title: Top-k approximation error

description: Prove that every finite `K₅`-minor-free graph can be reduced, using clique-sums, to planar graphs and the Wagner graph, and derive `FourColorTheorem → HadwigerFive`. Together with `wagner_forward`, this yields the substantive Wagner equivalence rather than only the logical contrapositive formulation proved here.
title: Wagner structural bridge

description:
Replace abstract finite PMFs with
   executable samplers and prove each public-key and challenge-ciphertext game
   hop from a formally stated decisional Ring-LWE assumption.  The current
   `indCPA_of_decisional_ringLWE` theorem is the final reduction step and does
   not claim an unconditional proof that Ring-LWE is hard.
title: Distribution-level Ring-LWE games

description: Any topological derivation must construct a non-discrete space from ranked profiles (for example, via a geometric realization of an order complex), prove that the Arrow axioms induce the required continuous/equivariant map, and identify precisely which antipodal equality contradicts which social-choice axiom.
title: Build a genuine topological bridge

description:
State universality on a compact permutation-invariant domain with
   a precise architecture class, topology, activation assumptions, and approximation norm.
   The current equivariance theorem supplies the symmetry-preservation component, but density
   requires a separate constructive approximation argument.
title: Approximation theory

description: Prove that every projectively consistent exchangeable family of finite-dimensional quantum states is represented by a probability measure on one-site density matrices. This requires finite-dimensional convexity, compactness of the density-operator space, and a measure representation or moment-determinacy argument.
title: The converse representation theorem

description:
The `⟸` direction is a short argument from the first-order condition;
the `⟹` direction is constructive on the line: `f` is obtained by integrating the monotone
multifunction `T⁻¹ − I`, and `firm_iff_monoLip` already supplies exactly the monotonicity
needed for that integral to exist.  `proj_unique_argmin` is the special case `f = indicator
of [a,b]`, already proved.
title: The `⟸` direction is a short argument from the first-order condition;

description:
The current dimension theorem treats activity as the range of a linear map from
behavioral coordinates. A nonlinear version should formalize a smooth map from
a `d`-dimensional behavioral manifold into neural state space and prove that an
immersed image has dimension at most `d`. Rank bounds on the derivative are a
natural first bridge.
title: Nonlinear neural manifolds

description:
Combine sparse layers with Hamming-distance constraints. The resulting question
is the maximum cardinality of a constant-weight binary code with prescribed
minimum distance. Formal targets include Johnson-type and sphere-packing bounds,
and explicit constructions showing when sparse representations remain robust to
neuron flips.
title: Noise robustness versus metabolic energy

description: Construct the canonical quotient homomorphism from the idèle class group of `K` onto `Cl(𝒪_K)`, identify its kernel with the subgroup generated by archimedean components and local unit groups, and prove that pullback identifies ideal-class characters exactly with idèle-class characters trivial on that kernel.
title: Idèlic realization of the unramified correspondence

description:
**The splitting distinguisher.** The attack recovers the secret by testing
  whether the constructed abelian surface splits as a product of elliptic
  curves. `kani_ker_inter_left` and `kani_ker_inter_right` are the local
  statements behind this test; the global criterion needs the theory of
  principal polarizations and the Weil pairing on `E₁ × E₄`.
title: The splitting distinguisher.

description:
The existing population result models the variance law algebraically. A deeper
formalization would define independent random neural responses, prove the
variance of their average, and derive concentration or confidence-interval
bounds. Extensions could cover heterogeneous variances, correlated neurons,
and optimal weighted decoding.
title: Population precision from probability theory

description: The current theorem excludes distance-expanding, hence isometric and bi-Lipschitz, embeddings into finite-dimensional spaces. A purely topological non-embedding theorem would require covering-dimension or cohomological-dimension machinery and is strictly stronger than the metric result proved here.
title: Stronger embedding obstruction

description:
Endow `ℝ` with the
   `b`-deformed operations `(⊕_b, +)` as a genuine `Semiring` instance
   transported along `x ↦ e^{bx}` from `ℝ_{>0}`, and formalize the statement
   that these semirings converge (in the sense of Gromov–Hausdorff or of
   pointwise convergence of structure maps) to `Tropical ℝ`.
title: Tropical semiring structure as a Lean instance

description:
Construct a proper Boolean algebra extending the finite--cofinite
   algebra on `[0,1]` and extend `probability` to it while preserving normalization, positivity,
   finite additivity, and singleton mass `epsilon`; alternatively, prove that a specified candidate
   algebra admits no such extension.
title: Larger event algebra

description: **Circuit-elimination closure conjecture.** For a finite matroid, imposing `MinAttainedTwice` only on a circuit generating family closed under circuit elimination cuts out the full `BergmanFan`. A generating family and a weight satisfying its constraints but violating another circuit constraint would refute it.
title: Circuit-elimination closure conjecture.

description:
Relate the normalized finite-family hull
   `TropicalConvexity.tropicalConvexHull` to
   `TropicalHelly.tropConvHull`, whose weights currently have no normalization
   condition. This should make the convexity theorem and Carathéodory theorem
   directly reusable through one interface.
title: Unify the two hull interfaces

description:
For every field of characteristic different from two and every nonsingular curve
   \(E_A : y^2=x^3+Ax^2+x\), the rational map
   \((x,y)\mapsto(x+x^{-1},\,y(1-x^{-2}))\) extends uniquely to a degree-two separable isogeny of smooth projective curves whose kernel is exactly \(\{\mathcal O,(0,0)\}\).
title: Projective extension and exact kernel

description: **Direct-sum product conjecture.** The Bergman fan of a finite direct sum of matroids is naturally homeomorphic to the product of their Bergman fans, compatibly with circuit components and lineality spaces. Any finite pair for which the canonical restriction map fails to be a homeomorphism would refute it.
title: Direct-sum product conjecture.

description: For every type `X`, every `N : Fin n → TopologicalSpace X`, and every extension `N' : Fin (n+1) → TopologicalSpace X` whose first `n` channels agree with `N`, prove `consensus N' ≤ consensus N`. This is falsified by any explicit extension violating the topology-lattice inequality.
title: Finite observer-complexity monotonicity

description: Study the counting function for theorems having a proof of length at most `n`. Upper bounds follow from finite alphabets; meaningful lower bounds require explicit proof families. This would replace the idealized `min N n / n` observable with one induced by an actual proof-search strategy.
title: Complexity-sensitive scarcity

description:
Package the diagonal
   coefficients into Mathlib's smooth-manifold/Riemannian framework and prove
   that the intrinsic curvature definition reduces to the closed formula used
   here. This would connect the existing coordinate calculation to the fully
   intrinsic curvature tensor.
title: Derive curvature directly from a metric tensor

description: For every finitely generated tropical ideal over `Tropical (WithTop ℚ)` and every monomial order, there is a finite test set `U` such that `IsGroebnerBasisOn m I U G` is equivalent to divisibility of the leading monomial of every nonzero member of `I` by a leading monomial from `G`.
title: Finite universal obstruction set

description:
Lift `balanced_minimizes_energy` to a genuine
   `argmin` statement over the finite candidate set of valid abscissae using
   Mathlib's `IsMinOn` / `StrictConvexOn.lt_of_ne`, making the "gradient descent on a
   convex spectrum" reading a literal Lean theorem about the minimizer.
title: Real-analytic optimization view

description: An arbitrary bijection can rearrange a countable set and radically alter natural density. Formalize robust alternatives based on string length, proof length, prefix-free description complexity, or upper Banach density, and state exactly which zero-density claims survive re-enumeration.
title: Enumeration-independent density notions

description:
Make `compCount`, `IsK2UnionK1Free` and `freeParam`
   decidable for `Fin n`-indexed graphs so that the finite checks in §2 of
   `ComputationalEvidence.md` — and the scans behind Conjectures 4 and 5 — can be replayed
   inside Lean by `decide` rather than by external enumeration.
title: Decidable regression harness

description:
Cycle 3 upgraded sharpness from "the maximum is attained" to "every
lattice value is attained", and cycle 4 turned the maximum into an identification
theorem; the outstanding step is a *closure* description of `defectSet`, which is a
finite convex-geometry computation for each `q` and is falsifiable by one
exhaustive rational scan.
title: Cycle 3 upgraded sharpness from "the maximum is attained" to "every

description:
**C6′ (a ramification principle).** Formulate and prove: for a CM elliptic
  curve with CM field `K`, the trace `a_p` modulo `λ^k` is a function of `p`
  modulo a small modulus precisely when `λ` ramifies in `K`. The two curves
  treated here are the class-number-one cases; higher class-number CM curves
  over number fields would test the principle properly.
title: C6′ (a ramification principle).

description:
Let `S` be any statistic computable from `N` and a bounded-length window. **Conjecture.**
`S` is invariant under the swap `p ↔ q` of the two prime factors, hence cannot output
"the smaller factor" without solving factoring; formally, there is a family of moduli on
which every such `S` is constant while the factorisations differ.
title: Let `S` be any statistic computable from `N` and a bounded-length window.

description:
Prove distinct fundamental
   discriminants yield distinct primitive quadratic Dirichlet characters, and conversely
   classify primitive quadratic characters by fundamental discriminants. This is the precise
   finite-order degree-one correspondence relevant to quadratic fields.
title: Injectivity and surjectivity in the quadratic case

description: Connect discrete firings to stochastic or deterministic mass-action semantics. Exact trajectory simulation will require a carefully stated encoding and observation theorem; ordinary differential-equation trajectories should not be conflated with discrete reaction traces.
title: Mass-action kinetics

description: Define a finite topological simplicial complex, its realization, and a triangulation homeomorphism. Prove that each realized simplex has finite Hausdorff dimension under a Lipschitz-compatible metric, then derive the no-triangulation theorem from `no_finite_finiteDim_cover`.
title: Abstract triangulations

description: The proved universal property can be lifted from the concrete category of monoids to a statement about coequalizers or regular epimorphisms in categories of algebraic structures. This would make “forgetting is quotienting” functorial and allow compatibility results for products and further quotients.
title: Categorical packaging

description:
Two-sided bounds
   on the Fermat offset (`fermatOffset_lower/upper`), degree-one homogeneity
   (`fermatOffset_scale`), and the mechanism theorem: above scale `112·W`, a
   window hit *forces* the middle band (`hit_implies_middle_band`), hence pins
   the Berggren letter (`window_hit_determines_berggren_letter`).  The constant
   is sharp to two units (`threshold_sharp`, witness at scale `110·W`).
title: The window is a ratio sensor with a sharp threshold

description: Import or define a concrete Turing-machine model, encode configurations in one fixed wetware state family, and prove a commuting simulation diagram for each transition. A useful final theorem would preserve halting and output, with an explicit neuron and time overhead.
title: Uniform Turing-machine simulation

description: For finite free coordinate modules, transpose defines a functor from the opposite matrix category. The composition law is proved explicitly. The file also proves the corresponding composition-reversal theorem for Mathlib's actual circle-valued `PontryaginDual.map`.
title: Contravariant character duality

description: Separate logical irreversibility from physical dissipation by defining an implementation semantics and explicitly assuming a thermodynamic realization theorem. This would clarify exactly where the physical Landauer principle enters beyond the formal accounting functional.
title: Physical assumptions

description:
Neither direction relating `β_p` to the
   smallest eigenvalue `λ_min` of the rotated Laplacian is formalized here (the
   eigenvalue itself is not yet defined in these files; see item 5).  The easy
   direction `λ_min ≤ β_p` is immediate once `λ_min` is introduced as an infimum
   of Rayleigh quotients, since phase vectors are particular test vectors; the
   substantial content of the paper is a Trevisan-style bound `β_p ≤ C √λ_min`
   obtained by rounding.
   Formalizing the rounding argument (a random threshold on the phase of the
   eigenvector) is the natural next target, and needs a Lean development of the
   `p`-phase sweep cut.
title: The Cheeger-type inequalities

description:
(Exclusivity is automatic when the target has maximum degree at most one —
   `isExclusive_of_deg_le_one` — and all optimal splits computed in this project are exclusive.)
   For every finite graph `G`, the minimum number of splits producing a cograph equals the
   minimum number of *exclusive* splits producing a cograph.
   Falsifiable by a graph whose exclusive cograph splitting number is strictly larger than its
   unrestricted one.
title: No exclusivity gap for cograph splitting

description:
For a random `F ∈ ℤ[X]` of degree `d` with
   coefficients bounded by `H`, the specialized polynomial `Ψ_F(·, N)` is
   nonconstant with probability `1 − O(H^{-1})`; so "almost every" polynomial
   invariant is on the *recovery* side of the dichotomy, and the `N`-only side
   is a measure-zero coincidence — the structural reason so few of the 284
   tested invariants were informative is that the informative ones are exactly
   the circular ones.
title: Reduction-slope statistics

description: Specify a verified Markov partition and transition graph for a precise Lorenz map or template. Only after that step, compare its inverse limit and Čech cohomology with the abstract finite-graph construction; the present results do not assert that comparison.
title: Build a Lorenz-specific comparison

description:
For every finite `G`, `split_IsChordal(G) ≤ |E| − |V| + c(G)`, where `c(G)` is the number of
   connected components; i.e. one split per independent cycle suffices.  The case of a single
   cycle is proved for `C₄` (`chordal_split_cycleC4_exact`), where unfolding the cycle at one
   vertex produces the path `P₅` (`isSplit_pathP5_cycleC4`).  Falsifiable by a graph needing more
   splits than its cyclomatic number.
title: A cyclomatic bound for chordal targets

description: The probability measure on `(0,1)` with density `1 / (π * sqrt (x * (1-x)))` is invariant under the full-strength logistic map. Equivalently, integrating an integrable test function after `logistic` against this density gives the same integral as before composition.
title: Arcsine invariance

description:
`r(D) − r(K − D) = deg D + 1 − g`.  With
   `Reduced.lean`, `ReducedUnique.lean` and `Dhar.lean` the reduced-divisor calculus
   is complete, so the missing ingredient is the combinatorics of acyclic
   orientations with a unique source: the non-special divisors of degree `g − 1` are
   exactly the classes `ν_σ`, and reversing `σ` realises `D ↦ K − D`.  This is what
   makes the half-canonical degree self-dual and hence the natural place to test the
   Brill–Noether conjecture: at `deg D = g − 1` Riemann's inequality gives nothing.
title: Baker–Norine Riemann–Roch

description:
Under a second-moment hypothesis on
   the hidden units, `√m (m τ_m − |c|/E[a g])` converges in distribution to a
   centred Gaussian with variance `|c|² Var(a g) / E[a g]⁴`, i.e. the grokking
   delay of a random wide network satisfies a central limit theorem.
   *The key insight is* that `unitDelay_width_law` writes the delay as the
   smooth function `x ↦ |c|/x` of the empirical mean, so the delta method turns
   Mathlib's CLT into a CLT for the delay.
   *Why now?* The almost-sure law (`iid_width_law_ae`) is proved with exactly
   the i.i.d. hypotheses Mathlib's CLT machinery uses, so only the delta method
   has to be supplied.
title: (P3) Fluctuations of the width law

description: The `d + 1` support bound for normalized max-plus tropical convex hulls yields a separation certificate of size at most `d + 1` for a point outside a finitely generated tropical convex set, and this certificate implies the general tropical Helly bound in Conjecture 1.
title: Carathéodory–Helly duality

description:
Formalize the quadratic extension `ℚ(√D)`, identify
   its Galois group with a two-element group, and prove the Frobenius splitting criterion at
   every unramified prime. This would turn the local Legendre-symbol classification into an
   explicit shape-to-color statement.
title: Quadratic fields and Frobenius

description: Generalize `TwoLevelTangle` to a directed graph or category whose vertices are formal systems and whose edges are interpretations. Characterize which cycles preserve truth, reflect proof, or transport independence, and prove a cycle theorem for arbitrary finite hierarchies.
title: Graph-shaped tangled hierarchies

description: Construct a polynomial-size gap-amplified proof oracle for finite graph 3-colourability whose verifier makes a fixed constant number of queries and rejects every false instance with probability at least `1/100`, independent of the number of vertices and edges.
title: Constant-gap PCP for graph 3-colouring

description: Replace diagonal probability vectors by arbitrary positive trace-one matrices and define tensor powers through Mathlib's tensor-product API. Prove that finite convex mixtures of `ρ ^⊗ n` are invariant under the unitary representation of every site permutation.
title: General finite-dimensional density operators

description:
The current results assume `rate < 1`. Physical
   time machines can be non-expansive but not strictly contracting (`rate = 1`).
   Extend to firmly non-expansive maps / averaged iterations (Krasnoselskii–Mann),
   where the fixed-point set may be a nontrivial *manifold of consistent histories*
   rather than a single point — a formal model of the "multiplicity of consistent
   solutions" discussed by Echeverria–Klinkhammer–Thorne for the billiard example.
title: Beyond the contracting regime

description:
Prove
   `gaussBinom q (n+1) (k+1) = gaussBinom q n k + q^{k+1} * gaussBinom q n (k+1)` directly in ℕ,
   and deduce `gaussBinom_symm` for arbitrary `q > 1` (not only for prime `q`, where the present
   proof goes through the `(ZMod q)^n` model). Falsifiable at `q = 4, n = 2, k = 1`.
title: The `q`-Pascal recursion

description: For finite candidate spaces with deterministic Boolean checks, define information gain as `log₂(|C| / |S|)`, where `C` is the initial space and `S` its nonempty survivor set. Conjecture: under uniform exhaustive enumeration, the median number of candidates inspected after filtering decreases by a factor between `2^(I-1)` and `2^(I+1)`, where `I` is the information gain. Exhaustive tests over all check families on spaces of size at most 16 can confirm or refute the finite instances.
title: Information gain predicts finite search reduction

description:
Given a continuous functor between
   subcanonical sites, prove that the induced pullback on sheaves carries represented sheaves to
   the represented sheaves of the image objects exactly when the functor preserves covering
   families and the relevant finite limits.
title: Sheaf Yoneda compatibility with change of site

description:
With `cantorDist_le_iff_agreeTo` in hand, a minimal cover of the
   golden-mean set at scale `2⁻ⁿ` uses exactly `fib (n+2)` balls. Convert the exact Fibonacci
   counts into a logarithmic limit `log (fib (n+2)) / (n log 2) → log φ / log 2` and feed it into
   Mathlib's covering-number / box-dimension definitions to prove upper and lower box dimensions
   coincide with `truthDimension`.
title: Box dimension as a limit

description:
Replace `(ℤ/p)^r` by an arbitrary finite abelian
   group `A`. The number of intermediate fields is the number of subgroups of `A`, which is
   multiplicative over the primary components; prove
   `Nat.card (Subgroup A) = ∏_p Nat.card (Subgroup A_p)` and, for `A_p = ⊕ ℤ/p^{λ_i}`, the
   Birkhoff–Hall count. Falsifiable already at `A = ℤ/4`, where the answer is `3`, versus
   `A = (ℤ/2)²`, where it is `5`.
title: General finite abelian class group

description: Replace the idealized measurement table with qubit states over a two-dimensional complex Hilbert space, density operators, projective measurements, and completely positive trace-preserving maps. Derive the finite measurement probabilities from the Born rule.
title: Hilbert-space protocol semantics

description: Before formalization, specify whether the cutoff is `< ω²` and what closure operation is intended. Also, there is no smallest positive surreal infinitesimal: if `x > 0` is infinitesimal, then `x/2` is a smaller positive infinitesimal once field arithmetic is available. Thus the phrase “the smallest positive infinitesimal” must be replaced, for example by the particular monomial `ω⁻¹`; even then equality with `ℝ(ω⁻¹)` requires substantial correction because bounded-birthday classes and generated rational-function fields are different constructions.
title: Reassess the proposed `No_{ω²} = ℝ(x)` claim

description:
`SplitChain.of_isSplit` produces an *exclusive* chain (each `singleSplit` step has
   `A ∩ B = ∅`) from the hypothesis `IsProjExclusive H f`, which is strictly stronger than
   `IsExclusive H f`.  Conjecture: there are finite `G, H, f` with `IsSplit G H f` and
   `IsExclusive H f` for which **no** chain `SplitChain True G H f` exists — i.e. the ordering
   of splits genuinely matters for exclusivity, and `IsProjExclusive` is the right invariant.
   Falsifiable by proving `IsExclusive H f → SplitChain True G H f` in general.
title: Exclusive splittings need not decompose into exclusive single splits

description:
The failure set of *any* width-`m`
   two-layer ReLU network probed along a ray has at most `⌈m/2⌉ + 1` connected
   components, and the comb network of `WidthLawsAndRelapses.lean` is extremal.
   *The key insight is* that the ramped output is piecewise linear with at most
   `m` breakpoints, so the number of sign changes is bounded by the number of
   slope reversals; the comb realizes one reversal per three units, and the
   conjecture is that no configuration does better than one per two.
   *Why now?* The lower bound is proved for every `k`, so only a counting
   argument on breakpoints — entirely finite and combinatorial — is missing.
title: (P1) The `⌈m/2⌉` relapse bound

description:
(`SupportLaw.lean`, Cycle 12 — *this closes former Conjecture 1*).
    `coeff_n Δ = [n ∈ S] − [n−1 ∈ S]` turns the support into a boundary count of the
    semigroup: with `upJumps` (entering `S`) and `downJumps` (leaving `S`),
    `#upJumps = #downJumps` by the telescoping identity `∑_{n≥1} coeff_n Δ = Δ(1) − 1 = 0`,
    `supp Δ_{a,b} = {0} ∪ upJumps ∪ downJumps`, and hence
    **`#supp Δ_{a,b} = 2·β(a,b) + 1`** with `β = #downJumps` the number of maximal gap runs.
    For the catalog pencil, `β(2,N) = (N−1)/2`, i.e. `#supp A_N = N`.
title: The support law

description: Both coordinatewise multiplication and coordinatewise addition fail the representative-independence test. For multiplication, applying the twist to both representatives reverses the fiber sign twice, while the quotient gluing reverses it only once. Thus there is no induced operation of the stated kind, so the advertised zero-divisor calculation does not establish a ring or a failure of integral-domain structure.
title: Coordinatewise operations induce a ring on the Möbius quotient

description:
(`Staircase.lean`, Cycle 15 — *new*). For the neighbouring
    parameters `b = a+1` the semigroup has a closed membership test,
    `n ∈ ⟨a, a+1⟩ ↔ n % a ≤ n / a` (`isRep_succ_iff`): writing `n = a·q + r` with `r < a`,
    membership means "the quotient pays for the remainder". The gap runs are then explicit —
    their starting points are exactly the `a−1` numbers `q·(a+1) + 1`, `0 ≤ q < a−1`
    (`downJumps_succ`) — so `β(a, a+1) = a−1` and
    **`#supp Δ_{a,a+1} = 2a − 1`** (`torusAlexander_staircase_support`). This settles the
    `β(a,a+1)` half of Conjecture 1 below, and it shows the Cycle 13 bound is *strict* here:
    for `a ≥ 3` one has `2a − 1 > a + 1 = max(a, a+1)`
    (`torusAlexander_staircase_support_gt`). Both families with an exactly known support —
    the pencil `T(2,N)` and the staircase `T(a,a+1)` — realise the common value `a + b − 2`
    (`torusAlexander_staircase_support_eq_add_sub_two`).
title: The staircase family

description:
The renaming equivariance
   `strictLocalMax_of_renaming` should extend to a groupoid action whose orbits
   are exactly the fitness level sets; if so, the migration graph descends to a
   finite quotient on which "distinct strict local maxima" is decidable.
title: Fitness-preserving refactoring is a groupoid

description: Extend the simplified QAP protocol with a formally modelled random oracle and prove that replacing the verifier's random evaluation point by a hash-derived challenge preserves the existing degree-over-field-size soundness bound up to an explicit oracle-query loss.
title: Fiat–Shamir soundness in a random-oracle model

description: In any fixed finitely branching proof calculus, count both the derivation of each consequence and the backward certificate. Conjecture: there is no universal constant `c < 1` such that every consequence-stable proposition has total certified cost at most `c` times its shortest direct proof. A counterexample family would consist of propositions whose shortest backward certificates asymptotically reproduce their shortest direct proofs.
title: Certificate-cost threshold

description:
`(x_c - x)^m·κ_m(x) → (m-1)!·x_c^m` for every
   `m ≥ 1`: the pole order of the `m`-th cumulant is exactly `m`.  The cases `m = 1, 2, 3` are
   now proved (`meanArea_pole_residue`, `areaVariance_pole_residue`,
   `areaThirdCumulant_pole_residue`); the uniform statement would identify the full singular
   structure of the horizon free energy as `log Z(x) = -log(x_c - x) + O(1)`, i.e. an exactly
   logarithmic free energy at the transition.  The key insight is that all three residues come
   from a single simple pole of `Z` at `x_c`: `(x d/dx)^m log Z` differentiates only the factor
   `-log(x_c - x)` to leading order, and that factor is now available in closed form.
title: All cumulants at the Hagedorn point

description:
`card_comp_set_cyc` proves
   `|(E ∘ C)[n]| = n!` analytically.  The bijection `S ≅ E ∘ C` itself (a permutation is
   the set of its cycles) is the natural next target; `blockSigmaEquiv` (a partition
   decomposes the underlying set) is the tool for transporting the cyclic structures.
   The same remark applies to `D ≅ E ∘ C₂`, proved here only at the level of counts.
title: The cycle decomposition as a species isomorphism

description: Over every finite field, if a received vector at `n ≥ d + 2e + 1` distinct locations differs from some degree-at-most-`d` polynomial in at most `e` positions, then a Berlekamp–Welch linear system has a solution `(E,Q)` with `E ≠ 0`, `degree E ≤ e`, `degree Q ≤ d+e`, and `Q(xᵢ)=received(xᵢ)E(xᵢ)` at every location; polynomial division recovers the unique polynomial from `ShamirErrorCorrection.unique_reconstruction_with_errors`.
title: Berlekamp–Welch existence

description:
For every `C¹` vector field with
   a nondegenerate saddle node at `μ = 0`, the passage time between two fixed
   levels satisfies `|μ|^{1/2} · T(μ) → π / √(f_xx f_μ / 2)`; the normal form
   value `π` of `bottleneck_sharp_constant` is therefore an invariant of the
   bifurcation, not of the model.
   *The key insight is* that `bottleneck_sharp_constant` shows the limit does
   not depend on the observation level `A`, which is exactly the scale
   invariance one needs for a normal-form reduction to transport the constant.
   *Why now?* The constant is proved for the normal form and the perturbation
   theorems `perturbed_two_equilibria` / `perturbed_no_equilibrium` already
   control the diagram under uniform perturbations of the field.
title: (P2) Universality of the constant `π`

description:
Because `IsEvenWalk` is decidable, the counts of
   `ComputationalEvidence.md` are now checked *inside the Lean kernel*
   (`WignerEvenWalkCount.lean`): `18` even closed `4`-walks on `3` vertices, `60` on
   `4` vertices, `2` even closed `6`-walks on `2` vertices and `66` on `3` vertices,
   and `0` at odd lengths `3, 5`. Via `expect_trace_pow_eq_card` these are exact
   moments: `E[tr W⁴] = 18` (`N = 3`), `= 60` (`N = 4`), `E[tr W⁶] = 2` (`N = 2`),
   `= 66` (`N = 3`), `E[tr W⁵] = 0` (`N = 3`) — the last an independent check of the
   odd-order vanishing theorem, the sixth-moment values a kernel confirmation of
   Conjecture 1 at `N = 2, 3`.
title: Kernel-verified enumeration

description:
**Symplectic Ruelle bound (old Conjecture 5).** `SymplecticRuelleData` carries the
  Hamiltonian pairing; `two_mul_card_pos_le` shows at most half of the exponents are
  positive, giving `2 h_KS ≤ d λ_max`, i.e. `λ_max ≥ 2h_KS/d`. For the Lagrange spectrum
  this improves `λ_max ≥ h_KS/4` to `λ_max ≥ h_KS/2`.
title: Symplectic Ruelle bound (old Conjecture 5).

description:
The exact identity and the sharp constant 16 are theorems
(`weil_deficiency`, `W_sq_le_four_p_sub_sixteen`, `improved_floor_sharp`); only the
infinitude of primes `a² + 4` (an Euler-type problem) is open, and partial sieve results
(almost-primes of that shape) can already be formalised as a weakened version.
title: The exact identity and the sharp constant 16 are theorems

description:
Fix a recursively
   axiomatized increasing sequence of PA fragments `(PA_t)` and interpret `□_t A` as
   `Prov_{PA_t}(⌜A⌝)`. Conjecture: after specifying a recursively enumerable modal
   calculus for these indexed operators, its theorems are exactly the formulas valid
   under every arithmetical substitution. A single modal formula separating the two
   sets refutes this conjecture for that clock and calculus.
title: Arithmetical completeness requires a precise clock

description:
The naive guess "for
   nonzero `λ_1, …, λ_k ∈ F_p` with `k ≥ 2p-3`, every `τ ∈ F_p` is the sum of a
   subset of size `≤ p-2`" — which would lower the heavy-class threshold from
   `2p-2` to `2p-3` — is **false**, and the counterexample is machine-checked
   (`Heis.short_constant_sums_ne`): for `p = 5` and `λ_1 = … = λ_7 = 1` no subset
   of size `≤ 3` sums to `4`.  The corrected conjecture is: *if the `λ_i` are not
   all equal and `k ≥ 2p-3`, then every `τ ∈ F_p` is a subset sum of size
   `≤ p-2`; if they are all equal to `λ`, the only exception is
   `τ = (p-1)λ`.*  Proving it would exclude the surviving profiles
   `(7,7,1,1,1,1)` and `(7,3,2,2,2,2)`, lowering `20` further.
title: Cardinality-constrained subset sums (corrected)

description:
The sum-integral loss is quantifiable:
   `∑_{j≥k}(j+1)^(−α) ≥ k^(1−α)/(α−1) − α·k^(−α)/2`, so the ceiling of
   `power_tail_knee_bound` is tight to first order in `1/k`.  (Cycle-5 evidence: at
   `α = 3/2, k = 256` the true tail is `0.0365` against the bound `0.125`, so the *constant*
   is far from tight for small `α` — the conjecture is that the loss is entirely due to the
   crude majorant `c·(i+1)^(−α)`, not to the summation step.)
title: Sharp constant in the power-tail bound

description:
If the clocks at all finite refinement depths are combined by an ordinal sum or an equivalent dependent lexicographic construction, the resulting survival value is exactly
   ```lean
   ω ^ ω
   ```
   and it strictly exceeds every finite refinement value.
title: The finite-refinement limit is `ω^ω`

description:
**colour-critical subgraphs have large minimum degree**
  (`exists_subset_minDegree_of_not_colorable`): every finite graph that is not
  `k`-colourable contains a vertex subset in which *every* vertex has at least
  `k` neighbours — proved by a greedy re-colouring of a minimal
  non-`k`-colourable subset;
title: colour-critical subgraphs have large minimum degree

description:
For
   `K = ZMod 2` and `V = Fin 3 → ZMod 2`, every
   `B : Fin 3 → Basis (Fin 3) K V` admits `G` satisfying
   `IsRotaArrangement B G`. This is a finite decidable specialization and can
   be refuted by one explicit triple of bases or proved by exhaustive reduction.
title: Finite-field exhaustive rank-three case

description: Add a blinding polynomial that is a random multiple of the target polynomial and prove both that QAP validity is preserved and that the verifier's opened value distribution is independent of the witness whenever the blinding coefficient is uniform over the field.
title: QAP zero knowledge by polynomial blinding

description:
On an
   `n`-cycle, cyclic shift and pointwise complement commute, shift has order
   `n`, and complement has order two.  Prove the resulting presentation and
   identify the faithful permutation group, handling the degeneracy at
   `n = 1` separately.
title: The group generated by the six elementary reversible maps

description:
Define concatenation followed by an output projection and prove
   equivariance of the full block. A correct rank theorem should use explicit independence
   hypotheses: additional heads do not increase rank automatically (duplicate heads are a
   counterexample), while concatenation with a head whose column space contributes a direct
   summand increases rank additively.
title: Multi-head attention

description:
Clarify which quantum group is intended at the unit-modulus parameter
   `q = exp(2πiγ₁)`. Establish its star structure, unitary representations, and
   the precise Casimir eigenvalue formula; the undeformed labels `n(n+1)` cannot
   simply be assumed for a generic deformation.
title:
Clarify which quantum group is intended at the unit-modulus parameter
   `q = exp(2πiγ₁)`.

description: The operational spectrum of undetectable non-stabilizer errors is proved extensionally equal to the spectrum of non-boundary cellular cycles. Their infima are therefore equal. If first homology is nonzero, the minimum is attained and strictly positive.
title: Distance equals the combinatorial one-systole

description:
For every formalized Grothendieck topos, construct the
   double-negation sheaf subtopos and prove that its subobject frames are Boolean algebras, while
   the inclusion into the original topos is universal among geometric morphisms from Boolean
   toposes.
title: Booleanization by double negation

description: A claim such as `π₁ = ℤ` requires a specified space with a cycle. Build a finite cyclic substitution graph for a curry model, define edge-path reduction, and prove that reduced loops have an integer winding number classifying homotopy classes.
title: A genuine circle model

description:
Use stochastic matrices or Markov kernels. A fixed point is
   then a stationary distribution rather than an unchanged event. Finite-state existence could
   be proved algebraically; uniqueness would require irreducibility or contraction hypotheses.
title: Probabilistic causal loops

description:
Conjecture: derivability in the
   specified calculus is decidable by searching the bound in Conjecture 2 with an
   executable finite-frame model checker. Termination plus verified soundness and
   completeness of this algorithm would prove the claim.
title: Decidability via bounded countermodel search

description:
The current theorem formalizes the easy map
   from integral points to local points. A useful next layer would distinguish
   integral, rational, real, and all-prime local solvability, so failures or
   limitations of converses cannot be conflated.
title: Hasse-principle interface

description: **Connected projectivized fan conjecture.** For every finite circuit-connected matroid of positive rank, the quotient of `BergmanFan M` by constant translations is path connected. A finite connected matroid with a disconnected projectivized Bergman fan would refute it.
title: Connected projectivized fan conjecture.

description: Define a concrete finite proof calculus, proof semantics, and minimum derivation length. Construct theorem families for which a formal lower bound on shortest proof length can be proved, rather than identifying candidates with proofs by definition.
title: Shortest-proof complexity

description: Define search-LWE and decisional-LWE as explicit distribution ensembles indexed by a security parameter. Formalize polynomial-time reductions and negligible functions so that the existing coordinate and affine-rerandomization lemmas can be assembled into a complexity-theoretic reduction theorem.
title: Define search-LWE and decisional-LWE as explicit distribution ensembles indexed by a security parameter.

description: The present development proves the algebraic obstruction at the setoid level. A later development could use Mathlib quotient-topology APIs to establish topological properties, after first correcting the proposed subset and its accumulation point.
title: Formalize the actual quotient topology

description: Over a field, prove the Künneth description of `H*(M_N)` as the graded tensor product of the cohomology rings of its sphere factors. The finite-stage Poincaré polynomial should be `∏_{n < N} (1 + t^n)` after handling the `S⁰` component convention carefully.
title: Finite-stage cohomology

description:
Pythagorean quadruples and the Cayley
   quaternion trees have similar matrix generators; identifying the correct
   scalar energy (if one exists) is the natural next test of how far a
   single-neuron encoding of a Diophantine tree can reach.
title: Higher-dimensional analogues

description: **Nested fan convexity conjecture.** If a finite matroid is nested, then its Bergman fan modulo constant translations is an ordinary convex polyhedral cone. A nested matroid with two projective Bergman weights whose midpoint is not a Bergman weight would refute it.
title: Nested fan convexity conjecture.

description: Define graph cochains for the finite approximants, calculate the maps induced by truncation, and form the corresponding direct limit. Relate this construction explicitly to the proved dyadic group `ℤ[1/2]` where the bonding system is doubling.
title: Compute cohomological transition maps

description:
Prove that
   `(x,y) ↦ x ⊕_b y` is convex but not strictly convex, being affine along the
   diagonal `x = y` (`lse_self` already gives the diagonal restriction exactly);
   the tropical limit `max` is convex and affine on each of two half-planes.
title: Strict convexity as a function of two variables

description: The current Mathlib surreal development supplies addition but not a full ring structure on `Surreal`; consequently the proved equivalence is a plain equivalence induced by an injective additive map. Once surreal multiplication and its laws are available, prove that `dyadicMap` is multiplicative and package its range as an ordered subring isomorphic to `ℤ[1/2]`.
title: Upgrade the image equivalence algebraically

description: For every finite set of places carrying GL(2) Satake pairs, the product of the local tensor-square Euler denominators is conjectured to factor as the product of all symmetric-square denominators times the product of all determinant denominators. This is falsifiable by specifying a finite family over a commutative ring and finding unequal resulting polynomials.
title: Finite Euler-product transfer

description:
Define exponential probability measures
   by densities and derive the closed form from the measure-theoretic relative
   entropy integral. This would connect the present algebraic interface directly
   to Mathlib probability distributions.
title: Measure-theoretic KL derivation

description:
**Conjecture.** In a finite social-deduction game whose information states form a belief-state Markov process, maximum-posterior elimination is globally optimal whenever the village continuation value is adaptively submodular in the set of eliminated wolves and exchangeable under permutations of surviving identities.

The key insight is that the proved affine continuation theorem is the one-step, modular boundary case of a broader diminishing-returns principle. **Why now?** The exact boundary between local classification optimality and sequential optimality has been isolated, making exchangeability and diminishing returns separately testable.
title: Adaptive-submodularity criterion for greedy posterior voting

description: Construct connected homotopy 2-types with isomorphic fundamental groups but inequivalent second homotopy groups (as modules over `π₁`), and prove they are not equivalent. A first test case is the trivial `π₁` with `π₂ = ℤ` versus `π₂ = 0`.
title: Failure beyond 1-types via explicit 2-type data

description:
For finite-state Markov pruning with transition probabilities bounded away from zero, a path-sampling estimator recovers the successful-set dimension with exponentially decaying error probability, uniformly over model size after an explicit mixing-time correction.

The key insight is that successful-prefix growth becomes an additive functional of a finite-state chain. **Why now?** Exact periodic benchmarks expose bias directly and provide calibration cases before moving to large theorem corpora.
title: Statistically consistent dimension estimation

description:
**Conjecture.** For bounded independent survey responses whose population mean has minimum margin `δ` over `m` tested rigor levels, empirical averaging identifies the true minimum with probability at least `1-η` once the sample size is on the order of `δ⁻² log(m/η)`, and this dependence is optimal up to constants.

The key insight is that deterministic stability below error `δ/2` converts any uniform concentration inequality directly into a sample-complexity theorem.

**Why now?** The sharp deterministic boundary is known, so the remaining question is an experimentally testable concentration problem with explicit parameters.
title: Statistical recovery at the half-margin threshold

description:
**Conjecture.** Among profiles with fixed endpoints and fixed minimum value, strictly single-valley profiles uniquely minimize total variation; every additional reversal incurs a variation penalty equal to twice the total height of the added excursions.

The key insight is that the exact descent-plus-recovery identity turns visual “wiggles” into an additive combinatorial penalty.

**Why now?** The single-valley variation law provides the baseline needed to define and test an excess-variation statistic on survey data.
title: Variation as an empirical valley-strength statistic

description:
**Conjecture.** For finite-memory demons obeying a Crooks-type fluctuation relation,
the probability of observing total work below the Landauer threshold decays
exponentially in the number of independently erased bits, uniformly over every
polynomial-time control strategy.

The key insight is that rare negative-work trajectories need not contradict the
second law; the physically testable obstruction is an exponential concentration
bound on repeated erasure. **Why now?** The expectation-level Jarzynski argument
already supplies the correct threshold, while repeated finite systems provide a
concrete setting in which to seek sharp tail estimates.
title: Fluctuation-Robust Demon Impossibility

description: To approach a two-resource hierarchy, define cyclic implementations whose work registers and memory size are bounded as functions of input length. Seek explicit families with polynomial runtime and superlogarithmic entropy export, and separately families with long runtime implemented by nearly reversible transitions. Any impossibility theorem must state the reset, cyclicity, and bounded-memory assumptions explicitly.
title: Cyclic bounded-memory implementations

description:
**Conjecture.** On a chordal interference graph with nonnegative vertex spill costs
and a fixed register budget `k`, a minimum-cost spill set can be computed by a
dynamic program over any clique tree, with per-node state space bounded by a
function of the maximum clique size.

The key insight is that the clique spill lower bound is already tight on a single
clique, so the only remaining difficulty is bookkeeping how adjacent cliques share
vertices — exactly the overlap information a clique tree records. **Why now?** With
the local constraint proved exactly tight, the open problem is purely the global
assembly, and a clique tree turns that assembly into a bounded-width recursion.
title: Clique-tree dynamic programming for exact weighted spilling

description:
**Conjecture.** The clique spill lower bound `ω - k` is globally tight exactly on the
chordal graphs: for every non-chordal graph there is a register budget forcing
strictly more than `ω - k` spills, and for every chordal graph the bound is
achievable for all budgets.

The key insight is that an induced chordless cycle raises the chromatic demand above
the clique number, creating spill obstructions that no single clique can witness —
the `C_5` case already separates the two quantities. **Why now?** The lower bound is
now a theorem for all graphs, so the live question is precisely characterizing when
it is *achievable*, and chordality is the natural candidate boundary.
title: A sharp defect threshold for the clique lower bound

description:
**Conjecture.** Given two swarms of equal total area whose area vectors are
comparable in the majorization order, the more spread-out (more majorizing) swarm
has the larger total cost for *every* convex radiator law, and strictly larger for
every strictly convex law unless the two allocations are permutations of each
other.

The key insight is that the equal-area optimum is the bottom element of the
majorization order, so the scalar optimality theorem should lift to a full order
isomorphism between allocation spread and cost, unifying every convex law at once.

**Why now?** The equal-area minimum is the extreme case of exactly this order;
proving the general monotone comparison would subsume the current result and
connect swarm design to the classical theory of Schur-convex functions.
title: Majorization dominance of allocations

description:
For pairwise coprime moduli whose ranks of apparition exist, the rank of their product should equal the least common multiple of their individual ranks, subject to explicit local conditions at primes dividing the discriminant.

The key insight is that the proved gcd synchronization is the meet-side shadow of a dual join law on divisibility loci.

Why now? Exact prime-index apparition gives a clean family of test cases in which the proposed lcm law predicts simultaneous Fibonacci divisibility without additional recurrence calculations.
title: Finite lcm law for ranks of apparition

description:
**Conjecture.** Let a finitely supported state have finite hyperreal amplitudes and appreciable nonzero squared norm. Then taking the standard part of every normalized Born weight produces a nonnegative real probability distribution of total mass one. Its support is exactly the set of branches whose normalized weights are appreciable and have positive standard part.

The key insight is that standard part should commute with finite sums once all summands are finite, while appreciability of the norm prevents normalization from magnifying an infinitesimal numerator into a visible weight.

**Why now?** Normalization and the disappearance of one infinitesimal branch have been established separately; the finite-support theorem would unify them into a complete measurement law.
