title: Standard-part Born measures on arbitrary finite supports

description:
**Conjecture.** For fixed wolf density below one half, there is a critical signal-to-noise ratio in an exchangeable voting-channel model above which Bayesian villagers have win probability bounded away from zero uniformly in population size, while below it their win probability converges to the information-free baseline.

The key insight is that posterior concentration, rather than posterior ranking alone, should control whether information overcomes the wolves' elimination rate. **Why now?** The exact information-free recurrence supplies a null model, and likelihood channels can be compared against it through posterior concentration inequalities.
title: Value-of-information phase transition

description:
For each explicitly specified rounding rule and each word size \(p\), determine the
entire cycle-length spectrum of the resulting finite logistic map and test whether its
maximum cycle is exponentially large while its median cycle remains substantially
smaller.

The key insight is that state-space cardinality supplies only an upper bound on first
repetition; arithmetic rounding determines the actual functional graph.

Why now? The universal lower-bound conjecture is ruled out by short exceptional orbits,
so the meaningful replacement is a rounding-sensitive distributional classification.
title: Precision-specific period spectrum

description:
In the ensemble obtained by retaining each entry of a uniformly sampled completed grid independently with probability `p`, conjecture a sharp threshold for uniqueness of completion, despite existence having probability one for every `p`. Determine whether the uniqueness threshold is governed by the smallest nontrivial trade (a finite set of entries that can be exchanged between two completions).

The key insight is that solution-generated clues eliminate the existence transition but preserve a nontrivial transition in the number of completions. **Why now?** The exact solvability-at-every-density theorem redirects the phase-transition question toward a monotone observable that can genuinely change in this ensemble.
title: A sharp threshold for uniqueness rather than existence

description:
**Conjecture.** Every oriented knot diagram with `n` crossings admits a canonically defined forbidden region and a local sign attached to each surviving path from `(0,0)` to `(n,n)` such that the resulting signed area generating function is its normalized Alexander polynomial. The construction should intertwine Reidemeister moves with explicit sign-preserving, weight-preserving cancellations or bijections.

The key insight is that positivity is the only universal obstruction detected by coefficient counting; the Alexander state sum already supplies exactly the missing cancellation data.

**Why now?** The unsigned formulation is ruled out even under arbitrary path deletion, while finite signed state sums are universal. The remaining test is therefore structural rather than existential: signs and paths must be extracted locally and naturally from a diagram.
title: Diagram-local signed path model

description:
**Conjecture.** For a Fisher metric with Lipschitz covariant derivative, one Euler natural-gradient step differs from the corresponding exponential-map step by a cubic local-model error, and this error accumulates to a sharp global convergence penalty proportional to the integrated metric variation along the orbit.

The key insight is that natural gradient selects the correct tangent vector, but a retraction determines whether that vector is transported along the manifold with controlled geometric error.

**Why now?** A concrete variable-metric example already separates the Euler endpoint from the geodesic midpoint, making the size and accumulation of that discrepancy the next measurable quantity.
title: Retraction error as the boundary between local and geodesic descent

description:
**Conjecture.** Every finite simplicial complex is homotopy equivalent to the downward closure generated by the preferred extensions of some finite argumentation framework, with the number of added arguments bounded linearly by the number of minimal nonfaces.

The key insight is that attacks and defenders can act as gadgets enforcing precisely a prescribed antichain of facets. **Why now?** Preferred families are necessarily antichains, exactly as facet families are, so the corrected construction turns realizability into a concrete synthesis problem rather than a mismatch of definitions.
title: Realizability of simplicial complexes by argumentation semantics

description:
**Conjecture.** Let each respondent's confidence profile be strictly convex on a common ordered grid, with minimum position lying within distance `d` of a central level. If the discrete second differences have a common positive lower bound, then the aggregate profile has a unique minimum within distance `d` of that level.

The key insight is that curvature may replace the unrealistic requirement that every respondent have exactly the same minimum.

**Why now?** Common-location aggregation and margin stability identify precisely which parts of the argument survive summation; discrete curvature is the next quantitative invariant capable of controlling displaced minima.
title: Localization under heterogeneous valley positions

description:
For fixed `s` and forbidden path order `P`, determine the exact maximum number of copies of `C_{2s+1}` and characterize every extremizer. Conjecture that an endpoint version of the core–periphery charging map yields a finite family of extremal templates, with parity corrections analogous to the exceptional edge in the bounded-circumference construction.

The key insight is that a path has two boundary positions, so successor charging should lose control only at controlled endpoints rather than at an exceptional cyclic transition.

Why now? The cyclic argument cleanly separates the injective combinatorial mechanism from the graph-specific construction, making its linear-order analogue precise and testable.
title: Path-forbidden analogue through endpoint charging

description:
For finite metric carriers, replace the fixed-point count by the maximal
displacement `max_a d(bwd(fwd(a)), a)` of the round trip. **Conjecture:** a
minimiser exists over any finite family of candidate analogies, the minimal
displacement is zero exactly for the perfect analogies of the discrete model, and
displacements compose subadditively: the round-trip displacement of `ψ ∘ φ` is
bounded by a Lipschitz-weighted sum of the individual displacements.

*The key insight is* that the discrete perfect analogies are the zero-displacement
core, so the metric theory is a continuous relaxation whose minimum recovers the
combinatorial optimum. *Why now?* Finiteness gives existence of minimisers for
free, and the composition law for perfect analogies is the exact `displacement =
0` case of the conjectured inequality.
title: Metric fidelity admits minimisers with a quantitative composition bound

description:
**Conjecture.** `R = (∑ᵢ dᵢ) − D` (single drops minus block drop) separates arms
far better than any single intervention: `|R| ≤ 0.004` for every
self-sufficient arm and `R ≤ −0.2` for every dependent one, at every width,
with no intermediate values.

*The key insight is* that `R` has a curvature meaning — `R ≥ 0` for convex,
`R = 0` for affine, `R ≤ 0` for concave read-outs — so an empirical bimodality
of `R` is a claim about the *shape* of the boundary read-out, not about
accuracy, and one gap-free measurement of `R` would upgrade "saturates at k = 2"
to "the read-out is affine below the knee and saturated above it".

*Why now?* `R` is computable from data already collected in NET-27/29/30 (it
needs only ctl, all zero1 and zeroAll), so the first test is a re-analysis, not
a new round.
title: C2 — The redundancy defect is the round's real observable

description:
Connect any spectral statement to the analytic continuation and functional
   equation of the zeta function. Without a theorem linking the operator's
   characteristic or spectral determinant to zeta, self-adjointness alone does
   not imply the Riemann hypothesis.
title:
Connect any spectral statement to the analytic continuation and functional
   equation of the zeta function.

description:
**Conjecture.** For reciprocal Alexander polynomials with no unit-circle roots, each reciprocal pair `r, r⁻¹` controls a pair of exponentially growing and decaying radial modes, not real angular OAM residues. For the figure-eight knot, the rates are the logarithms of `(3 ± √5)/2`.

The key insight is that angular propagation detects root argument, whereas radial growth detects root modulus; reducing a real root modulo one confuses these two observables.

**Why now?** The figure-eight polynomial has been proved to vanish nowhere on every angular grid, sharply isolating the alternative physical interpretation that must be tested.
title: Off-circle Alexander roots predict evanescent rather than OAM channels

description:
Conjecture: there is a geometric gadget family for which the number of rectangular assemblies equals the number of satisfying assignments, up to a formula-independent symmetry factor computable in polynomial time.

The key insight is that witness preservation is stronger than equisatisfiability and naturally targets counting reductions; rigid framing should quotient out translations, rotations, and interchangeable copies.

Why now? The abstract construction already gives a canonical bijection of witness spaces, so every discrepancy in a geometric implementation can be localized to gadget automorphisms.
title: Parsimonious counting hardness

description:
**Conjecture.** If a function on the positive real axis and its Mellin transform are each concentrated on uniformly porous sets in logarithmic coordinates, their joint concentration decays exponentially with the number of resolved scales.

The key insight is that the Mellin transform becomes a Fourier transform after the logarithmic change of variables, while geometric progression becomes translation across logarithmic scales. **Why now?** The strip identity principle establishes qualitative rigidity, and multiscale porosity supplies a falsifiable route to a quantitative exponent.
title: Mellin uncertainty for multiplicatively porous sets

description:
Conjecture that two locally permutation-invariant clue ensembles can have asymptotically distinct satisfiability thresholds even when they have the same expected clue density and the same one-cell marginals. A concrete comparison should use independently assigned locally consistent clues versus clues generated by perturbing a random completed grid.

The key insight is that density forgets correlations, whereas Sudoku constraints are dominated by correlated row, column, and block collisions. **Why now?** Restrictions of completed grids are solvable at every density, providing an exact endpoint against which genuinely random-value models can be compared.
title: Ensemble non-universality of the satisfiability threshold

description:
**Conjecture.** A layerwise region recurrence becomes valid after replacing raw width `w_i` by the rank of the affine hyperplane arrangement induced on each incoming region; the resulting bound is the product of arrangement growth functions and is strictly sharper than `2^L ∏ w_i` whenever bottlenecks occur.

The key insight is that width counts available gates, whereas arrangement rank counts gates capable of cutting a specific inherited region. **Why now?** The exponential-product expression has been separated from its unproved geometric recurrence, making the missing local cutting hypothesis explicit and experimentally testable.
title: Realized-region recurrence with activation rank

description:
**Conjecture.** For every reduced alternating knot diagram, the coefficientwise absolute value of its normalized Alexander polynomial is the area generating function of paths avoiding a diagrammatically defined Ferrers-type region, after an explicit grading shift.

The key insight is that alternating Alexander polynomials have a controlled sign pattern, suggesting that cancellation can be factored into a global alternating character while the remaining magnitudes are honest counts.

**Why now?** The torus family shows precisely how an alternating sign pattern obstructs unsigned counting while leaving positive magnitudes. A geometric model for those magnitudes would recover a substantial and sharply delimited part of the original proposal.
title: Alternating knots and unsigned absolute coefficients

description:
**Conjecture.** On a geodesically complete statistical manifold with sectional curvature in a fixed interval, positive injectivity radius, and a geodesically strongly convex, geodesically smooth loss, exponential-map natural-gradient descent with a constant admissible step has a linear rate whose constants depend on intrinsic curvature and convexity but not on the coordinate condition number of the Fisher matrix.

The key insight is that coordinate conditioning should disappear only after both the update and the regularity assumptions are expressed intrinsically; curvature distortion then replaces matrix conditioning as the relevant obstruction.

**Why now?** The exact constant-metric cancellation identifies the flat base case, while the Euler-midpoint counterexample isolates the missing geometric ingredient: the exponential map.
title: Curvature-controlled exponential-map descent

description:
**Conjecture.** For a geodesically strongly convex loss and update size `a/(t+b)`, the objective gap has a polynomial exponent determined sharply by the product of intrinsic strong convexity and `a`; exponential decay is impossible unless the effective step sizes have a divergent linear-scale average.

The key insight is that strong convexity alone does not create an exponential iteration rate when the step sizes vanish harmonically; the cumulative step length, not dimension, determines the exponent.

**Why now?** The matched quadratic admits an exact inverse-square objective law, providing a calibration case against which the general intrinsic theorem can be tested.
title: Sharp classification of harmonic schedules

description:
For an alphabet of size `q`, determine the largest word length for which one can avoid two disjoint, order-isomorphic occurrences of the same scattered word of length `m`. The conjecture is that the extremal function has an exponential main term in `m`, but with a base strictly smaller than the naive `q^m` once arbitrary scattered occurrences, rather than aligned blocks, are counted.

The key insight is that aligned-block coding supplies a universal benchmark while overlap constraints among scattered words should create additional entropy loss. **Why now?** The collision and disjointness bounds isolate the exact structural point where ordinary pigeonhole counting stops, making the missing overlap estimate sharply testable.
title: Sharp extremal law for repeated scattered words

description:
For a stationary ergodic source of entropy rate `h < log q`, conjecture that the typical waiting time for a repeated length-`m` block scales as `exp(hm/2)` up to subexponential factors, and that low-complexity mixtures exhibit a detectable downward deviation governed by their lowest-entropy component.

The key insight is that cardinality `q^m` should be replaced probabilistically by the effective typical-set size `exp(hm)`, after which birthday-type collision behavior predicts a square-root threshold. **Why now?** The worst-case coding theorem clarifies which part of the claimed genomic compression is universal and which part must be attributed to source entropy.
title: Entropy-sensitive compression in stationary genomic models

description: Let a compact smooth submanifold have reach at least `τ`, and let a finite sample have Hausdorff distance at most `δ` from it. Conjecture that there is an explicit nonempty interval of Rips scales, with endpoints depending only on `δ` and `τ`, on which the Rips complex is homotopy equivalent to the manifold. For a simply connected closed three-manifold whose recovered homology is that of the three-sphere, determine additional computable local conditions sufficient for sphere recognition. **The key insight is...** perturbation stability must be combined with geometric regularity; homology alone cannot supply the missing local manifold structure. **Why now?** The exact `2δ` scale translation isolates the noise contribution, making a sharp reach-dependent interval a concrete target.
title: Quantitative homotopy recovery under reach and density

description:
**Conjecture.** If two machine substrates simulate one another with polynomially bounded overhead and polynomially related encodings of input size, then their polynomial-time and polynomial-witness language classes coincide, even when the simulations are not resource-exact.

The key insight is that exact simulations are stronger than complexity theory normally requires: polynomial classes should absorb polynomial distortion while still preserving the deterministic-versus-witness question.

**Why now?** The exact-overhead theory identifies every point where costs enter the transport argument, making the polynomial closure conditions explicit and testable.
title: Polynomial-overhead invariance of asymptotic classes

description:
**Conjecture.** For a family of finite decision processes with bounded error, any
implementation whose expected running time is polynomial but whose workspace is
reused across instances must dissipate at least a constant times the conditional
entropy of the discarded computation history. A matching reversible construction
should attain the bound up to polylogarithmic overhead.

The key insight is that time complexity and dissipation become coupled only after
one specifies which intermediate information is irreversibly discarded, rather
than merely classifying the final decision problem. **Why now?** The finite
pushforward entropy inequality and the positive one-bit work bound isolate exactly
the local information-loss quantity that a family-level theorem must aggregate.
title: Quantitative Complexity–Dissipation Tradeoff

description:
**Conjecture.** Let a finite hypergraph index subfamilies of phylogenetic trees, with each hyperedge carrying a common induced subtree on the same leaf set. If the intersection graph of the hyperedges is connected, then the union of all indexed trees has that common induced subtree. Conversely, disconnectedness is the only obstruction valid for arbitrary split systems.

The key insight is that equality of restriction witnesses propagates along overlaps exactly as a locally constant function propagates on a connected space.

**Why now?** Chain gluing establishes the path case. Recasting the result for arbitrary connected overlap graphs would create a reusable local-to-global principle and clarify its relation to sheaf-style consistency.
title: Connected-family gluing beyond chains

description:
For every nonexceptional composite index, the primitive part of the corresponding Fibonacci number should contain a prime whose divisibility locus is exactly the multiples of that index. This would extend finite-family synchronization from prime indices to the full range of Carmichael’s theorem.

The key insight is that finite gcd transport already converts an exact apparition law for one prime into synchronization over every finite family, so only primitive-prime existence remains quantitative.

Why now? The finite-meet mechanism has been isolated from the growth argument, allowing cyclotomic estimates to be developed independently and attached at a single interface.
title: Composite-index synchronization through cyclotomic primitive parts

description:
`FSAccepts` hashes `(pub, a, m)`.  Conjecture: if the message is dropped from the hash input
(oracle of the form `H : G × G → ZMod q`), then there is an explicit adversary that, given a
single valid signature on `m₀`, produces a valid signature on every message `m`, i.e.
universal forgery with probability `1`; whereas with the message included, the `Q/q` bound of
`rom_union_bound` continues to hold.  This is a concrete, checkable separation between the
two hashing conventions inside the present formalization.
title: C5. Fiat–Shamir with commitment-only hashing is insecure for multi-message signing

description:
**Conjecture.** For a fixed finite-outcome protocol `S` obeying Jarzynski at cost `ΔF`,

```
lim_{n→∞} -(1/n) log P( ∑ W_i ≤ n·w )  =  I_S(w)  ≥  β (ΔF - w),
```

where `I_S` is the Legendre transform of `Λ_S(λ) = log ⟨e^{λ W}⟩`, and equality
`I_S(w) = β(ΔF - w)` holds **iff** the sub-threshold mass of `S` sits at the single work
value `w` (the "all-or-nothing" protocol).

*Status.* `FluctDemon.single_deficit_bound` gives `≥` at `n = 1`, and the new
`FluctDemon.crooks_deficit_le_rev` identifies the exact one-shot slack: the bound is
`e^{-β(ΔF-w)}·m_rev(w)` with `m_rev(w)` the reverse mass of the time-reversed deficit
event, and this is attained with equality for `coinDemon` at `w = ΔF - log(3/2)/β`.  So the
sharpened one-shot statement is tight; the open content is now purely the `n → ∞`
tensorisation of the factor `m_rev(w)`, which we conjecture contributes the missing
`I_S(w) - β(ΔF - w)`.

*Falsifiable:* a two- or three-outcome protocol with `I_S(w) = β(ΔF-w)` whose sub-threshold
mass is spread over two distinct work values; equivalently, one whose reverse mass
`m_rev(w)^n` fails to capture the `n`-fold slack.
title: Exact large-deviation rate and the equality case

description:
**Conjecture.** Define, for an injective description scheme on `2^N` statements, the
*search profile* `s(x) =` number of candidates examined before `x`'s description is found.
Conjecture that `s` obeys a tiling law dual to `complete_code_tiles`: the descriptions
enumerated before position `t` occupy disjoint cylinders of total measure `t · 2^{-N}`, and
that `mean_searchWork_ge` follows from this measure identity together with
`card_compressible_le`, unifying the two counting laws the thread has kept separate.

*The key insight is that* `kraft_inequality` and `card_compressible_le` are one counting fact
seen through `2^{-|w|}` and through `#{|w| ≤ m}`; completeness turns the first into an exact
partition (`complete_code_tiles`), so the search order should inherit an exact measure
identity rather than only an inequality.

*Why now?* The tiling statement proved in the previous cycle is precisely the missing
exactness; the earlier formulation of this conjecture (a bound on `∑ 2^{-searchWork}`) was not
stable under re-enumeration, and the measure-theoretic form removes that defect while
remaining cheap to falsify by machine at `N = 4`.
title: E′. A tiling law for search cost

description:
**Statement.**  For a two-qubit density matrix `ρ` of rank `≤ 2` the convex-roof concurrence is
`max(0, λ₁ − λ₂)` with `λ₁ ≥ λ₂` the square roots of the eigenvalues of `ρ ρ̃`; `(λ₁ − λ₂)²` is a
discriminant of exactly the shape `pencilB² − 4 d₀ d₁`.

**The key insight is** that the spectrum of `ρ ρ̃` for a rank-two state is the spectrum of a `2 × 2`
pencil built from the two pure states in the decomposition, so `hyperdet_eq_discriminant` and
`exists_diagonalizing_A` apply verbatim.

**Why now?**  This is still the one missing ingredient for the exact CKW identity
`τ_{A|BC} − C_AB² − C_AC² = 4|Det ψ|`, and it is the only conjecture of the previous cycles that
has not yet been reduced to routine work.
title: C5. Wootters' formula for rank-two two-qubit states, via the Alice pencil (carried over)

description:
**Conjecture.** The bound of `CandidateLists.no_bounded_candidate_list` is
quantitatively sharp in the following sense: for a modulus `m` and a threshold
`B = N`, any congruence-determined candidate list that succeeds on all
semiprimes below `N` must have size `Ω(π(√N) / m)`, i.e. essentially the trial
division list, and the residue class contributes only a constant-factor saving.

*The key insight is* that the coprime family constructed above can be taken
inside a single class of *any* modulus, so the class structure removes no
candidates at all beyond those excluded by congruence obstructions on the
factors themselves.

*Why now?* The qualitative statement is proved unconditionally; the quantitative
version needs only a counting version of the same Dirichlet input (prime
counting in progressions), which is available in effective form.
title: C6. Quantitative candidate-list growth

description:
**Statement.** A prime `p > 2` divides some anti-Fibonacci number iff `-7` is a quadratic
residue modulo `p`, i.e. iff `p = 7` or `p ≡ 1, 2, 4 (mod 7)`; and the set of such primes
has density `1/2`.

*Status update (this cycle).* The congruence criterion is now **proved** in
`Catalog/Computation/AntiFibonacciPrimeDivisors.lean` (`prime_dvd_antiFib_iff`, uniform in
`p` including `p = 2`), together with the two infinitude statements
`infinite_divisor_primes` and `infinite_nondivisor_primes` (Dirichlet).  What remains open
is only the *quantitative* half: that the divisor primes have natural density exactly
`1/2`, i.e. `#{p ≤ x : p ∣ some antiFib n} ~ x / (2 log x)`, which needs the prime number
theorem in arithmetic progressions rather than mere infinitude.

**The key insight is** the proved spectrum criterion `m ∈ range(antiFib mod p) ↔ 8m - 7 is
a square`: taking `m = 0` this says `p ∣ antiFib n` for some `n` iff `-7` is a square mod
`p`, which by quadratic reciprocity is a congruence condition modulo `7`.

**Why now?** Mathlib has full quadratic reciprocity (`legendreSym.quadratic_reciprocity`)
and the residue-spectrum theorem is already formalised, so only the reciprocity
computation for the discriminant `-7` remains; the density statement then follows from
Dirichlet's theorem, also available.

**Falsifiable:** list the primes dividing some `antiFib n` for `p < 1000` and compare with
the residues `1, 2, 4 (mod 7)`; a single mismatch refutes it.

---
title: C6. The omitted residues determine the sequence's prime divisors

description:
**The key insight is** that a knee reading converts directly into a lower bound on the
heaviest key's mass, so $\mathrm{base}(\text{domain})$ should be exactly the reciprocal of
the domain's asymptotic top-key mass — a *shape* invariant that can be measured without any
downstream task.

**Why now?** The attention-profile calculus already supports the inequality in one
direction, and the uniform profile shows it is tight; what is missing is a matching upper
bound for realistic, heavy-tailed profiles.
title: D2. The base is a concentration invariant

description:
The key insight is that the bound `knee ≥ tau²/C` needs no tokenizer, no domain
label and no notion of "word": it is computed from the attention weights alone,
and it is sharp on the flat profile, so it cannot be improved as a function of
the collision mass. Why now? Attention maps are already logged in the existing
sweeps, so the collision mass costs one extra reduction per head; the immediate
test is whether French exhibits a smaller collision mass than English at the
same context length, and whether the ratio of collision masses tracks the ratio
of knees across all five domains. If it does, budget provisioning becomes a
measurement on the model rather than a per-language calibration campaign.
title: Collision mass as a domain-free knee predictor

description:
**Conjecture.** If a finite graph contains a complete graph on `t` vertices as a minor, then its chromatic counting function vanishes at every nonnegative palette size below `t`. Conversely, determine natural minor-closed graph classes on which this vanishing pattern forces a complete `t`-minor.

The key insight is that Hadwiger-type structure can be phrased as an interval of forced zeros rather than only as a lower bound on a chromatic number.

**Why now?** The exact minimal-positive-value characterization isolates the zero interval that must be controlled, while deletion–contraction offers a natural mechanism for tracking it through graph reductions.
title: Clique minors as chromatic vanishing certificates

description:
**Conjecture.** The exponential map based at the origin is a global
diffeomorphism from its tangent plane onto the split-metric plane.

The key insight is that a complete simply connected surface with nonpositive
sectional curvature should have no conjugate points and no competing geodesic
segments. **Why now?** The frame-independent sectional curvature is globally
nonpositive and vanishes only at the base point; completeness is the principal
remaining geometric hypothesis to test.
title: Global injectivity of the exponential map

description:
**Conjecture.** For every distribution on permutations, there is a comparison sorter whose
expected comparison count is within an additive constant times `n` of the Shannon entropy,
and whose reversible history can be compressed to the same scale.

The key insight is that factorial entropy is merely the uniform-prior case; biased input
orders should admit both shorter decision paths and smaller retained histories. **Why now?**
The present synthesis separates worst-case tree capacity from erased information, making a
prior-sensitive formulation both natural and experimentally testable.
title: Tight entropy-sensitive sorting under nonuniform priors

description:
**Conjecture.** One may take `N₀(k) ≤ 2k²` in uniform half-canonical existence.

The key insight is that `2k²` already guarantees non-negativity of the relevant Brill–Noether number with one unit of arithmetic slack. **Why now?** This is the first explicit scale singled out by the exact regular-graph calculation, so it is a falsifiable target for exhaustive tests and structural estimates.
title: Quadratic universal threshold

description:
Define `U_g(m,r)` as the least window length such that every window in a finite genome `g` contains some length-`m` word with at least `r` disjoint occurrences. Conjecture that, after controlling for local GC content and assembly gaps, human chromosomes have `U_g(4,2)` separated by a constant factor from matched first-order Markov surrogates.

The key insight is that a window-uniform statistic turns the informal phrase “any consecutive bases” into a reproducible extremal observable, while disjointness prevents a homopolymer overlap from being counted ambiguously. **Why now?** A universal upper benchmark is available, so empirical comparisons can report both absolute values and normalized compression ratios.
title: Window-uniform repetition statistic for real genomes

description:
**Conjecture.** On a graph with `n` vertices and `k` cops, backward search stabilizes after at most `n^(k+1)` strict updates; moreover, there are families for which the necessary number of updates grows polynomially in the number of game states.

The key insight is that the winning tables form an increasing chain in a finite state space, so every non-stable update must add a state. **Why now?** The established monotonicity and fixed-point characterization reduce termination to a quantitative chain-length problem, and implementations can record the exact stabilization depth across graph families.
title: Certified finite stabilization bound

description:
For each `r ≥ 0`, classify and enumerate cyclic binary words in which at most `r` peripheral symbols are followed by peripheral symbols, with weights recording core and peripheral vertex choices. Conjecture that, for fixed word length, the resulting weighted enumerator is the trace of a `2(r+1) × 2(r+1)` transfer matrix and satisfies a linear recurrence whose characteristic polynomial factors according to the allowed defect states.

The key insight is that deleting at most `r` exceptional peripheral positions restores an injective rotation map, while a finite-state automaton records where those deletions occur.

Why now? The one-defect circumference theorem supplies the base case `r=1`, and the finite-state formulation can simultaneously control circumference and exact cycle counts.
title: A weighted transfer-matrix theorem for bounded exceptional transitions

description:
There should be an explicit bound, polynomial in the logarithmic height of the defining recurrence data, beyond which every index admits a synchronizing primitive prime for all finite index families.

The key insight is that synchronization itself has no quantitative cost once a primitive divisor exists; every effective bound can therefore focus entirely on the growth of the primitive part.

Why now? The structural theorem turns a potentially many-family assertion into one primitive-divisor estimate, making uniform quantitative bounds testable.
title: Effective exceptional-set bounds from finite synchronization

description:
`Catalog/Combinatorics/B3FreeWeakStrongGap.lean` settles the weak-versus-strong question
in the negative, and much earlier than predicted: the first counterexample has `|P| = 2`,
not `|P| = 4`.  For the two-element **antichain** `A₂` we prove

* `La(n, A₂) = 1` (`La_antiPoset_two`; more generally `La(n, Aₘ₊₁) = m`, `La_antiPoset`),
* `La*(n, A₂) = n + 1` (`LaStar_antiPoset_two`),

hence `La*(n, A₂) − La(n, A₂) = n` (`LaStar_sub_La_antiPoset_two`) and
`La* = (n+1)·La`.  So no bound `La* ≤ c·La` holds with `c` independent of `n`, and the
catalog inequality `La_le_LaStar` is never an equality in general.  The mechanism is
identified exactly: a *weak* copy of an antichain is merely an injection
(`weakFree_antiPoset_iff`), whereas a *strong* copy must be an **induced** — i.e.
incomparable — pair, so strong `A₂`-freeness is literally the statement that the family is
a chain (`strongFree_antiPoset_two_iff`).
title: Cycle update: Conjecture 5 is refuted, and its replacement

description:
**Conjecture.** For the exact `k`-bit prime semiprime support, for every fixed degree `d` there is
`k_0(d)` such that for all `k ≥ k_0(d)` and all `1 ≤ j ≤ k - 7`, every parity of degree `≤ d` of
the bits of `N` correlates with `p_j` by at most `C_d · π(2^k)^{-1/2} · polylog`, while for
`j > k - 7` the maximum degree-1 correlation stays bounded away from `0`.

*The key insight is* that the two proved theorems bracket the truth from both sides — exactly zero
below (`lowblock_corr_zero`, on the odd support) and strictly positive above (`covTop_pos`) — so the
only open content is the *transition window*, whose width the experiment measures as ~6 bits.

*Why now?* `highDegree_mass_ge` converts any such correlation bound into a statement about where
the Fourier mass lives, so a single quantitative equidistribution input (primes in short
arithmetic progressions mod `2^t`) would upgrade the empirical claim to a theorem.

---
title: C2. A degree hierarchy over the prime-restricted support

description:
**Conjecture.** For every `0 < ε ≤ 2/√3` the `ε`-thick part of the moduli space is compact,
connected and nonempty, and its complement — the `ε`-thin part — is connected; hence the moduli
space has exactly one end, and the systolic functional `sys` is an exhaustion whose level sets
`{sys = ε}` are connected for all small `ε`.  Quantitatively, the thin part is homeomorphic to a
punctured disc, with `−log sys` as the radial coordinate.

*The key insight is* that compactness of the thick part is now a theorem (`isCompact_fdThick`,
`mahler_compactness`), and that the collar lemma `collar_lemma` shows the thin part is
parametrized by the unique short vector (`shortest_unique_of_sys_lt_one`) — that uniqueness *is*
the statement that the thin part has one component per cusp, and the torus has one cusp.
*Why now?* Both ingredients were missing before this cycle: without continuity of `sys` the
thick part was not known to be closed, and without uniqueness of the shortest vector the thin
part could a priori have several components.  Only the connectivity of `𝒟 ∩ {Im ≤ 1/ε}` — a
convexity statement in coordinates — remains.
title: E4. The moduli space of tori has exactly one end

description:
**Statement.** For each `n` the set of branching numbers realised by nodes with positive
coordinates is exactly `{2ⁿ − k : k ranges over the possible sizes of the "non-child" family}`,
and this family is always a simplicial complex whose face numbers are governed by the harmonic
inequalities `xᵢ·(Σ_{j≠i} xⱼ − xᵢ) ≤ …`.  For `n = 3` this gives `{6,7}`; the conjecture is that
for `n = 4` it is exactly `{11, 12, 13, 14, 15}`.

*The key insight is* that non-children are precisely the faces of the *weak* descent complex,
so the branching number equals `2ⁿ` minus the number of faces, and the exact spectrum is a
statement about which downward-closed families are realisable by null vectors.

*Why now?* The realisability question is already reduced to explicit inequalities by
`DescendsOn.mono` and `DescendsOn.card_le`, and dimension three is completely solved
(`quad_children_card`), providing a template.
title: Conjecture B (the exact branching spectrum in dimension `n`)

description:
1. **(S1)** `minimal_card_on_nodes`: for `A = {0, c, 2c, …, Nc}` the minimal near-miss
   cardinality is again `2^{N-1}` — dilation invariance of the extremal problem.
2. **(S2)** `support_gap_two`: there is *no* near miss at level `N ≥ 2` with
   `#supp s + #supp t = N + 1` and `lam ≥ 2` whose two sides have equal support size unless
   `N` is odd — a parity obstruction visible in the tables of `ComputationalEvidence.md`.
3. **(S3)** `fwdDiff_kernel_dimension`: the space of `ℤ`-valued functionals on `{0,…,N}`
   annihilated by every near miss at level `N` has rank exactly `N`, spanned by
   `x ↦ x^k`, `k < N`; equivalently the near-miss functional is a *cyclic* vector for the
   shift operator on that space.
title: Three concrete next-cycle sub-conjectures (recursive abduction)

description:
For each finite semantic set `B`, classify the largest family of endomorphisms `F ⊆ (B → B)` for which a single presentation can represent every diagonal composite associated with `F`. Conjecture that maximal families are controlled by the directed graph of fixed points of the transformation monoid generated by `F`.

The key insight is that Boolean negation fails because it is fixed-point-free, suggesting that obstruction is governed by transformation-monoid structure rather than cardinality alone.

Why now? The universal Boolean impossibility theorem supplies the first sharp negative case, and finite transformation monoids make exhaustive testing and structural classification feasible.
title: Obstruction spectra for finite semantic domains

description:
**Conjecture.** For fixed `a ≠ 0` the normalised traces `a(a,b)/√q`, `b ∈ F`, have
*third* vertical moment `∑_b a(a,b)³ = q · T(a)` where `T(a)` is again an elliptic
point count — explicitly, `T(a) = -(#E_a(F) - q - 1)` for `E_a : y² = x³ + a x`.

**The key insight is** that the cube of the character sum sums over triples `(x,y,z)` and
the `b`-sum of `χ((b+u)(b+v)(b+w))` is exactly the count of an elliptic curve, so the odd
moments of the family close up on the family itself: the vertical moment hierarchy is a
*fixed point*, not an expansion.

**Why now?** `vertical_second_moment` gives the even case in closed form and shows the
answer depends only on `χ(-3)` and `χ(-a/3)`; the odd case is the first place where the
elementary method must produce an elliptic count rather than a constant, which makes the
conjecture sharply falsifiable by a single `#eval` over `F_13`.
title: C3. The vertical distribution of `χ(-a/3)` forces an exact "vertical Sato–Tate defect"

description:
*Let `D` be any distribution on `[1, N)` whose density is computable from `N` in
`polylog N` time and is `ε`-close to uniform in total variation. Then a single
sample from `D` reveals a nontrivial factor with probability at most
`2/min(p,q) + ε`.*

**The key insight is** that `Round7ZDG.atomic_uniform_success_le` already proves
the uniform case with the exact constant `2/p`, and the perturbation term is
forced by the total-variation bound; the content is that `polylog`-computability
prevents any density from concentrating on the `p + q - 2` zero divisors.
**Why now?** The uniform bound is formalised and the vertex set is exactly
characterised, so only the TV-perturbation layer remains.
title: Conjecture B (atomic-uniform noise floor as a theorem, not a principle)

description:
**Conjecture.**  The lower bound of `prob_indep_and_cure_ge`,
`f(k) = 1 - m p^{-k} - (p^k-1)/((p-1)p^n)`, is maximised at
`k* = ⌊(n + log_p(m(p-1)))/2⌋ + O(1)`, i.e. the best exclusive width is roughly `n/2`, and the
maximum value is `1 - Θ(p^{-n/2})`.

*The key insight is* that the reliability error decays like `p^{-k}` while the genericity error
grows like `p^{k-n}`, so the sum is a convex Laurent polynomial in `p^k` whose minimum is at the
geometric mean of the two scales — the "boundary token" problem is an AM–GM balance, not a
capacity constraint.

*Why now?*  Both error terms are already proved in Lean; only a one-variable convexity argument
over `x = p^k` is missing.
title: C3. Ramp/anti-ramp trade-off has an interior optimum

description:
**Conjecture (metatheoretic, then empirical).** For any fixed sweep precision `η > 0`
there is no `n` such that an `n`-seed ensemble certifies an exact knee law at a cell whose
reference margin is below `η`; empirically, the width of the two-sided knee bracket at a
cell should *not* shrink as seeds accumulate, but converge to a strictly positive width
determined by `η` and the local slope of the retained curve.

*The key insight is* `KneeEnsemble.ensemble_underdetermines_knee`: a single grid point
whose deficit is within the spread already yields an admissible curve with a smaller
knee, and that construction is independent of how many seeds have been run — extra seeds
add data but no resolution.

*Why now?* NET-44 closed the last single-seed cell, so the next natural move is "more
seeds"; this conjecture predicts that the move buys nothing unless the *precision* of the
sweep (grid step and evaluation noise) improves first, which is a cheap thing to test by
re-running two existing cells at four seeds.
title: C5. No finite seed budget certifies an exact knee law at fixed precision

description:
**Conjecture.** If $\mathcal F$ is weak $B_d$-free and $\mathcal G$ is weak $B_e$-free, then
$\mathcal F \cup \mathcal G$ is weak $B_{d+e}$-free; likewise for strong freeness.

*Status.* The case $e = 1$ is the Antichain Union Theorem proved this cycle (a weak $B_1$-free
family is exactly an antichain). Exhaustively verified with no counterexample for $n = 3$ and
$(d,e) \in \{(1,1),(1,2),(2,1)\}$, and for $n = 4$ with $d = e = 1$. Equivalently, in poset
form: for every subset $A \subseteq B_{d+e}$ containing no weak copy of $B_e$, there is an
order embedding $B_d \hookrightarrow B_{d+e}$ whose image avoids $A$.
title: F1. Subadditivity of the free dimension

description:
**Conjecture.** $\mathrm{La}(n,B_{d+1}) - \mathrm{La}(n,B_d) \ge \binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$
for all $n \ge d+1$.

*Status.* Open. The pigeonhole bound above gives $2^n/(n+1)$, short by a factor of order
$\sqrt n$ exactly in the regime where the extremal number is already a constant times the
central binomial coefficient. For the level-restricted problem the quantitative form is a
theorem: the level optima for consecutive $d$ differ by exactly one central binomial
coefficient. *Falsifiable* by one pair $(n,d)$ with a smaller gain.
title: F2. A full central binomial coefficient of gain

description:
**Conjecture.** As `β → ∞` with `ΔF = k_B T log 2` fixed at the Landauer value, the exponent
`β(ΔF - w)` tends to `-βw`, so the bound is vacuous for every fixed `w > 0` and informative
only for `w ≤ 0`.  Consequently an apparent zero-work erasing demon obtained in the `T → 0`
limit must have diverging resources: with `w = 0`, `FluctDemon.stopping_reliability_bound`
gives `m ≤ log(1/δ)/log 2`, a *`β`-independent constant* on the number of erasures the
demon can complete at fixed success probability — and by `FluctDemon.stopping_wald` the
expected work still grows like `ΔF·E[N]`, so the only escape is `E[N] → ∞`.

This turns the "Zero-Temperature Boundary Classification" conjecture of the original
direction into a quantitative dichotomy: at `T → 0` the loophole closes as a divergence of
the *resource* `E[N]`, not of the exponent.

*Falsifiable:* a family of finite stopping strategies, parameterised by `β`, with `w = 0`,
`ΔF = k_B T log 2`, deficit probability bounded below, bounded `E[N]`, and outcome-space
size `O(poly)`.
title: Zero-temperature degeneration of the exponent

description:
**Conjecture.** `N₀(5) > 6` and `N₀(7) > 8` — no `5`-regular graph on `6` vertices
and no `7`-regular graph on `8` vertices carries a divisor of degree `g − 1` of rank
`k − 1` — while both thresholds are finite and at most `2k + 7`.

*The key insight is* that the two residual degrees are exactly those where
`m = ⌊(k−2)/2⌋ ∈ {1, 2}`, i.e. where the now-proved exact value `m(m+3)/2 ∈ {2, 5}`
of the uniform witness is *below* `k − 1`; for every larger `m` the quadratic growth
of `m(m+3)/2` overtakes the linear `k − 1`, which is precisely why `k ≥ 6, k ≠ 7`
was provable and these two were not.

*Why now.*  `rank_thetaChar_K_odd_ge_regularity` makes the crossover explicit:
`m(m+3)/2 ≥ 2m + 1 = k − 1` exactly when `m ≥ 2`, with equality at `m = 2` (`k = 6`,
`K₇`) — so `K₇` is the unique tight case, and `K₆`, `K₈` fail by exactly the amount
the formula predicts (`2 < 4` and `5 < 6`).  Combined with Conjecture 1 this becomes
a theorem, and the remaining content is the *existence* of the finite thresholds,
for which the `bnNumber_regular_pos_iff` criterion already gives the linear scale.
title: The residual degrees `k = 5` and `k = 7`

description:
For real positive semidefinite `A ≼ B` (Loewner order) and `b > 0`,

```
tr (A (A + b•1)⁻¹)  ≤  tr (B (B + b•1)⁻¹).
```

**The key insight is** that `x ↦ x/(x+b) = 1 - b/(x+b)` is operator monotone, so
the statement reduces to the antitonicity of the matrix inverse on the positive
cone, `A ≼ B ⟹ (B+b·1)⁻¹ ≼ (A+b·1)⁻¹`, followed by taking traces — turning an
analytic inequality into a congruence-transformation argument with
`PosSemidef.sqrt`.

**Why now?** Round 6 already provides the exact resolvent diagonalisation
(`resolvent_eq`) and the identification of the trace with `effDim`, so the only
missing ingredient is the operator-inverse antitonicity, which is a
self-contained matrix lemma; with D1 the entire Part I–VI theory upgrades from
"fixed spectrum" to "monotone in the data covariance", i.e. *more data in the
Loewner sense never lowers the effective dimension.*

**Falsifier:** a pair `A ≼ B` of `2×2` PSD matrices with
`tr(A(A+b)⁻¹) > tr(B(B+b)⁻¹)`.

---
title: Conjecture D1 (Loewner monotonicity of the noise floor)

description:
**Conjecture.**  Let `M` be squarefree odd and coprime to `N`.  Then the trace set
`S_M(N)` is determined by, and determines, the tuple of Legendre symbols
`(χ_p(N))_{p ∣ M}` *together with* `N mod M`; and the *size* `|S_M(N)|` is
determined by the Jacobi symbol data alone:
`2^{ω(M)} |S_M(N)| = ∏_{p ∣ M} (p + χ_p(N))`.

*Status.* The size formula follows from `card_traceSet_prime` plus
`traceNat_primorial` (both proved); the "no more" half — that no function of
`S_M(N)` beyond the character tuple is computable in polynomial time from `N` — is
open.

*The key insight is* that every bit the trace exposes to a congruence battery is a
value of a quadratic character of the *public* modulus, hence computable by
reciprocity in polynomial time from `N` alone; a leak would have to come from the
*joint* distribution across primes, which the CRT factorisation of the trace set
rules out.

*Why now?*  This is the exact information-theoretic form of Barrier 2, and it is
now within reach: multiplicativity and the prime-level formula are theorems, so
only the "no residual information" half remains.
title: C3.  The visible bits are exactly the Jacobi symbols — no more

description:
**Conjecture.**  For a semiprime `N = pq` and a squarefree odd `M` coprime to `N`,
the number of `t ∈ [1, N]` with `t mod M ∈ S_M(N)` is
`(1 + o(1)) · N · 2^{-ω(M)} · ∏_{p ∣ M}(1 + χ_p(N)/p)`,
and in particular a congruence battery must use `ω(M) ≥ log₂ N - O(1)` primes before
a single candidate trace remains.

*Status.* The lower bound `≥ (∏(p-1)/2^{ω}) (N/M - 1)` is proved
(`trace_pinning_barrier`); the matching upper bound and the `o(1)` are open.

*The key insight is* that the surviving set is a union of `|S_M|` full residue
classes, so its density is *exactly* `|S_M|/M` up to boundary terms — the only
question is the boundary, which is `O(|S_M|)` and hence negligible when `M ≪ N`.

*Why now?*  With the lower bound formal, the upper bound is elementary counting;
together they would give the first fully formal statement of the shape "residue
information about the trace is worth `ω` bits and the search space is `log₂ N`
bits", i.e. a proved (not measured) version of the paper's verdict.
title: C4.  Quantitative pinning threshold

description:
**Statement.** For semiprime `N = pq`, the multiset of primes dividing `den x(kP)` for
`k ≤ K` is, for every fixed `K`, computable from `N` alone in time polynomial in `log N` *given
oracle access to the points* — and contains no subsequence that isolates `p` or `q` more often
than the trivial guess. Concretely: there is no function of `{den x(kP) : k ≤ K}` that outputs a
nontrivial factor of `N` for a positive proportion of semiprimes.

**The key insight is** that the apparition index law makes the appearance of *every* prime — good
or bad — governed by the same mechanism (the order of the reduced point), so the primes dividing
`N` enjoy no structural distinction inside the denominators; the survey data (`p` present 54.5%,
`q` present 0%) is exactly what this predicts.

**Why now?** With closure, the index law and the infinite-orbit theorem in place, the barrier can
be stated as a theorem about the index function `ℓ ↦ m(ℓ)` rather than as a collection of
counterexamples; the missing step is a uniform bound showing `m(p)` and `m(q)` are not
distinguishable from `m(ℓ)` for good `ℓ`.
title: C5. Denominator data cannot recover the factorisation of `N`

description:
**Conjecture.** For every divisor `D` on `Kₙ` and every `r`, if `r(D) < r` then the
failure is witnessed by a *monotone staircase*: there is an effective divisor `E` of
degree `r` whose value multiset is `{c, c−1, …}` in the sorted order of `D` (at most
`n` such `E` up to relabelling) with `D − E` not equivalent to an effective divisor.
Consequently the rank of a divisor on `Kₙ` is computable in `O(n log n)`.

*The key insight is* that the deficiency `d` is monotone under the dominance order
on sorted value vectors, so among all test divisors of a fixed degree the ones
maximising `d(D − E)` are the extreme points of the dominance order — exactly the
staircases, which is why the single explicit divisor `stairE` already realises the
upper bound `m(m+3)/2`.

*Why now.*  `stairE`/`isReduced_stairF` show a staircase realises the obstruction for
uniform `D`, and the `K₈` computation of §1 found that a filter using only the `22`
monotone staircase test divisors of degree `6` already eliminated all but `28` of
the `262144` classes — no non-staircase witness was ever needed.  Proving this would
give the first polynomial-time *certified* rank algorithm for a nontrivial family.
title: Staircases are the only obstructions

description:
**Statement.**  There are explicit constants such that for normalized `ψ`,
`τ_{A|BC} − τ_ABC ≥ c · ‖hyperdet ψ‖^{1/2}`, and consequently the monogamy inequality of Cycle 1
is strict with a quantitative gap on the whole GHZ class.

**The key insight is** that the residual tangle differs from the one-tangle by `4|Det ψ|` up to
the convex-roof correction, so the effective genericity proved here converts "the GHZ class is
dense" into "the monogamy gap is bounded below on a dense open set", with the same `ε⁴` rate
transported through the square root.

**Why now?**  The exact identity is still open (it needs Wootters' formula), but the *inequality*
direction only needs the bounds proved in this cycle plus `residualTangle_le_oneTangleA` from
Cycle 1.
title: C4. Monogamy defect is controlled by the hyperdeterminant, effectively

description:
`La*(n, Aₘ) = Σ_{i<m−1} (n + 1 − 2i)` for `m − 1 ≤ ⌈(n+1)/2⌉`: a strong `Aₘ`-free family
is, by Dilworth's theorem, a union of `m − 1` chains, and the maximum union of `k` chains
in `2^[n]` should be the total length of the `k` longest chains of a symmetric chain
decomposition.  The cases `m = 2` (`LaStar_antiPoset_two`, value `n + 1`) and `m = 3`
(`LaStar_antiPoset_three`, value `2n`) are now **proved**, the latter in
`Catalog/Combinatorics/B3FreeAntichainThree.lean` and *without* Dilworth or
Greene–Kleitman: the upper bound is a pure layer count (a strong `Aₘ`-free family meets
every layer in fewer than `m` sets, `card_filter_card_lt_of_strongFree`, giving the general
bound `La*(n, Aₘ) ≤ Σ_i min(m − 1, C(n,i))`, `LaStar_antiPoset_le_sum_min`), and the lower
bound is an explicit union of two disjoint chains.
*The key insight is* that for small `m` the naive layer bound `Σ_i min(m − 1, C(n,i))`
already coincides with the Greene–Kleitman value, because near the ends of the cube the
binomial coefficients are smaller than `m − 1`; the first `m` where the two quantities
diverge is `m = 4` at `n = 4`, which is therefore the decisive test case.
*Why now?*  With `m = 2, 3` closed exactly and the general layer bound proved, the
conjecture reduces to a single finite comparison per `(m, n)` plus a chain construction.
title: Sub-conjecture (Greene–Kleitman in this language)

description:
**Conjecture.**  Let `T g : Matrix (Cell × Cell) (Cell × Cell) ℕ` have entry
`T[(a,b),(b',c)] = 1` iff `b = b'` and `g a b c = b`, and `0` otherwise.  Then for all
`n ≥ 1`,
`#V(g,n) = trace (T g ^ n)`.
Consequently `n ↦ #V(g,n)` satisfies a linear recurrence of order at most `4` with
integer coefficients, and is a sum of `n`-th powers of the eigenvalues of a `4×4`
`0/1`-matrix.  In particular the sequences `1,1,4,1,1,4,…` (rule 90), `2,4,2,4,…`
(rule 150) and `1,3,1,3,…` (rule 30), each now proved individually, would become
instances of one eigenvalue phenomenon rather than three separate arguments.

*The key insight is* that a fixed configuration on `ZMod n` is precisely a closed walk
of length `n` in the fixed-edge de Bruijn graph, so counting is a trace, and the
arithmetic periodicity observed for rules 90, 150 and 30 comes from roots of unity in
the spectrum.

*Why now?*  The descent theorem `ncard_fixed_eq_of_periodic` already proves the
special case where the graph is a disjoint union of cycles; the general case only
needs the "matrix power counts walks" lemma, which is the missing infrastructure.
title: C2. Transfer-matrix trace formula for every rule and every size

description:
**Conjecture.** For `N = pq` with both primes `≡ 1 (mod 4)`, `v₂(W(N)) = 2` exactly, and
more generally `v₂(W(N)) = #{primes p | N with p ≡ 1 mod 4}`; consequently the 2-adic
valuation of the statistic counts the number of `1 mod 4` prime factors — a genuine but
*already publicly computable* invariant (it is determined by `N mod 4` for semiprimes),
so it leaks nothing new.

*The key insight is* that `W_mod_four` gives `v₂ = 1` at each `1 mod 4` prime and
multiplicativity adds valuations, so the 2-adic content of the statistic is exactly the
count of such factors and nothing more.

*Why now?* `W_mod_four` and `WZ_mul` are proved; the conjecture is a short corollary for
semiprimes and an induction for general `N`, and its "leaks nothing new" half is a
precise, falsifiable information claim.

---
title: C3. `v₂(W(N))` is a complete obstruction to a "dial + parity" witness

description:
**Conjecture.** Let a source be supported on a set `A ⊆ {0,1}^n` and let `G` be
a generator with `s`-bit seeds. The optimal expected code length using `G` is
`H_0(A ∩ range G) + Pr[A ∖ range G]·n ± 1`; in particular the PRNG's dividend
equals exactly `Pr[x ∈ range G]·(n - s)` bits and vanishes for any source whose
support is not correlated with `range G`.

*The key insight is* that `prng_dichotomy` splits every source into a
"generated" part (compressible to `s` bits, by `exists_code_of_small_set`) and a
"free" part (incompressible, by `exists_KC_ge`); the conjecture says these two
regimes are the whole story with no interaction term.
*Why now?* Both halves of the split are already theorems; what remains is the
expectation bookkeeping over a `Finset`-supported distribution.
title: C3. Structured sources: a sharp "PRNG dividend" theorem

description:
**Conjecture.** `lim_{m→∞} N(m) log m / m = 1`, where `N(m) = boxCount m` is the number
of boxes of size `1/m` meeting the prime fractal.  Equivalently
`N(m) = (1 + o(1)) m / log m`.

*The key insight is* that the occupied boxes split into a "dense tail" (indices
`k ≤ m/log X` are all occupied because every interval `(e^{m/(k+1)}, e^{m/k}]` contains
a prime once `m/(k(k+1))` is large) and a "sparse head" (one box per prime `p ≤ X`),
and optimising the split at `X = m` makes the tail `m/log m` and the head `o(m/log m)`;
the constant `1` then comes from the tail alone, not from `π`.

*Why now?* The two-sided bracket `m/(16 (log m)^4) ≤ N(m) ≤ 5 m/log m` is already
formalised, and the numerical band (`N log m / m ∈ [1.26, 1.75]`, decreasing) is in
`ComputationalEvidence.md`.  Closing the gap needs only prime existence in the
intervals `(e^{m/(k+1)}, e^{m/k}]` — Bertrand's postulate (in Mathlib) already handles
`k ≲ √m`, and any Chebyshev-type short-interval result upgrades this to the full range.
title: C1. Exact Minkowski constant: `N(m) · log m / m → 1`

description:
Replace `evolve : α → α` by a set-valued
   round-trip map and prove existence of consistent histories via Nadler's
   contraction principle for multifunctions, capturing scenarios where the outcome
   of a loop traversal is not deterministic.
title: Set-valued / multivalued evolution

description:
**Conjecture.** For `p = (1-ε)/n` with `0 < ε < 1` there is `A = A(ε)` such that
`Prob p {s | largestComponent s ≤ A · log n} → 1`, and the explicit choice
`A = 3/(ε - log(1+ε))` works.

The natural Lean route avoids branching processes entirely: a first-moment bound on the
number of *connected* vertex sets of size `k` — `C(n,k) k^{k-2} p^{k-1}` for trees —
combined with the cut machinery of `ErdosRenyiConnectivityUpper` (`cutEdges`,
`sum_over_small_sets`).  Falsifiable numerically: simulate `G(n,(1-ε)/n)` and check
whether the largest component exceeds `A log n` with non-vanishing frequency.
title: C4. Giant component: quantitative subcritical bound

description:
**Conjecture.** If `r = n mod 2^k` satisfies `3^{s_k(r)} < 2^k` then
`T^[k] n < n` already for every `n ≥ 2^k` (equivalently: `T^[k] r ≤ r + 2` for
every contracting `r < 2^k`).

**The key insight is** that the crude growth bound `T^[k] r ≤ 2^k r`, which
produced the `2^k·4^k` threshold, is exponentially lossy: the exact solution of
the affine recursion gives `2^k · T^[k] r = 3^{s} r + c(w)` with an intercept
`c(w) = ∑_i 3^{s−i} 2^{j_i}` that is *itself* controlled by the contraction
condition `3^s < 2^k`.

**Why now?** The exact affine formula `T^[k](r + 2^k m) = T^[k] r + 3^{s} m` is
already proved (`terras`); the missing piece is the closed form for the
intercept `c(w)`, provable by the same single induction. Exhaustive search
(`ComputationalEvidence.md` §5, §7) finds `T^[k] r − r ≤ 2` for every contracting
`r < 2^k` with `k ≤ 13`, and no descent failure other than `n ∈ {0,1}`.

---
title: C2. The descent threshold is `O(1)`, not `8^k`

description:
**Conjecture.** For every infinite set `S ⊆ ℕ` of exponents with `#(S ∩ [1, X]) = O(X^{1-ε})` and
every prime `q`, there are still two distinct primes `p ≠ p'` with `R_k(pq) = R_k(p'q)` for all
`k ∈ S ∩ [1, N]`.

*The key insight is* that the Dirichlet argument used for finite `S` only needs the primes to be
`≡ 1` modulo `lcm(S ∩ [1, X])`, and for sparse `S` that lcm is still small enough for a prime of the
right size to exist under standard prime-gap heuristics — so sparsity, not finiteness, is the
operative hypothesis.
title: C2. Joint closure survives unbounded but sparse exponent sets

description:
**Conjecture.**  For every odd prime `p` and all `N, N' ∈ 𝔽_p^×`,
`S_p(N) = S_p(N')` implies `N = N'`.

*Status.* Verified for `p ≤ 41` computationally; formally verified at `p = 13`
(`traceSet_injective_thirteen`).

*The key insight is* that `S_p(N) = {s : χ(s² - 4N) ≠ -1}` is the "non-residue
locus" of the quadratic pencil `s² - 4N`, and two such loci coincide only if the
pencils agree: the overlap `|S_p(N) ∩ S_p(N')|` is a two-variable character sum
equal to `p/4 + O(√p)` for `N ≠ N'`, whereas equality would force `p/2 + O(1)`.

*Why now?*  The Legendre-symbol identification proved in this cycle
(`two_mul_card_traceSet_eq_add_legendreSym`) shows the *size* of `S_p(N)` sees only
`χ_p(N)`; C1 says the *set* sees everything.  That gap is precisely the information
that a residue attack fails to convert into factors, and pinning it down turns the
qualitative verdict "the trace is the least hidden invariant" into a theorem about
how much is hidden.
title: C1.  The trace set is a complete invariant of the modulus

description:
**Conjecture.**  For every `n ≥ 2` and every prime `ℓ ≥ 5` not dividing `n`,
`∑_{c mod ℓ} #{x mod ℓ : ℓ ∣ den x(nP) for x ≡ c}` equals `(n² - 1)·ℓ/ (something explicit) + O_n(1)`;
concretely, `deg ψ_n = (n² - 1)/2` or `(n² - 4)/2` and the total should be
`deg ψ_n · ℓ / (deg ψ_n) = ℓ` per irreducible factor, giving `#{factors}·ℓ + O(1)`.  The proved
values are `ℓ` for `n = 2` and `2ℓ - 1` for `n = 3`.

*The key insight is* that each factor of `ψ_n` over `ℚ(N)` is, like `T³ + N` and `T³ + 4N`, a
Kummer-type polynomial in `x` whose root count averages exactly `1` over `N mod ℓ`, so the total
counts the *number of irreducible factors*, not their degrees.

*Why now?*  The two proved cases are exactly the two smallest instances of this factor count
(`ψ₂ = T³ + N`: one factor; `ψ₃ = 3T(T³ + 4N)`: two factors), and the averaging bijection used
here (`x ↦ -x³`) generalises verbatim to any factor of the shape `T^k + cN^j`.

**Falsifiable form.**  Compute `∑_c #V₄(c)` for `ℓ = 7, 13, 19`; the conjecture predicts a value
of the form `k·ℓ + O(1)` with `k` = number of `ℚ(N)`-irreducible factors of `ψ₄`.
title: D1. The layer-`n` total is `(n² - 1)·ℓ + O(1)`

description:
Fix a prefix length in advance and compare centered decimal-digit autocorrelations at lags 1–12 against the exact permutation distribution, with family-wise error controlled across constants and lags. The conjecture is that none of the three advertised preferred lags remains significant after correction at prefix lengths 10³, 10⁴, and 10⁵.

The key insight is that an exact finite-sample null distribution separates reproducible digit evidence from interpretations based only on irrationality. Why now? The deterministic energy identity identifies the precise statistic to test and exposes every convention that must be fixed before significance has a meaning.
title: Certified finite-prefix null tests for π, e, and √2

description:
For a finite self-adjoint Hamiltonian decomposed into irreducible angular-momentum sectors, conjecture that sufficiently small perturbations commuting with the symmetry action preserve cumulative shell multiplicities whenever adjacent spectral clusters have a positive gap.

The key insight is that periodic structure depends on spectral projections and their ranks, not on exact numerical eigenvalues; ranks should remain constant until a gap closes.

Why now? The diagonal shell model gives explicit eigenvectors and multiplicities, making it possible to formulate a quantitative gap condition and then broaden from diagonal matrices to general Hermitian operators.
title: Stability of closed-shell counts under symmetry-preserving perturbations

description:
For any fixed positive scale `E₀`, conjecture that nuclear binding energies across all stable isotopes cannot satisfy `round(E/E₀)=Z` consistently, even after choosing one representative isotope per element.

The key insight is that binding energy is controlled primarily by mass number and saturation, whereas atomic number is a charge count; a universal scalar rounding rule discards the independent neutron degree of freedom.

Why now? The shell-spectrum results clarify the valid role of multiplicity while separating it from the stronger and falsifiable claim that energy values themselves encode atomic numbers by uniform rounding.
title: No universal energy-rounding scale recovers atomic number

description:
**Conjecture.** For a fixed, versioned mathematical corpus, the tail exponent of theorem reuse remains within a narrow interval when dependencies are measured under three distinct policies: direct constant references, transitive references, and references after collapsing definitional expansions.

The key insight is that a scale-free claim is scientifically meaningful only if it is stable under reasonable choices of graph extraction. **Why now?** The structural results separate universal consequences of acyclicity from corpus-dependent statistics, making extraction sensitivity the first falsifiable obstacle.
title: Stable exponents under dependency extraction

description:
**Conjecture.** In a sparse random corpus with bounded expected document size and theorem degrees converging to a nondegenerate distribution, each fixed-dimensional normalized Betti number has a deterministic limit, while the unnormalized Betti number is bounded above by the corresponding binomial face count and is typically of strictly smaller order.

The key insight is that the universal binomial ceiling controls the available chain generators, but boundary ranks—not simplex counts alone—determine the surviving topology.

**Why now?** The structural ceiling and dimension-vanishing theorem identify exactly which asymptotic claims are possible; specifying a random incidence model is the missing ingredient needed to replace an unsupported power law by a falsifiable limit theorem.
title: A null model for higher-dimensional citation topology

description:
**Conjecture.** For every $d \ge 2$ there is $n_0$ with
$\mathrm{La}(n,B_d) < \mathrm{La}^*(n,B_d)$ for all $n \ge n_0$: the proved inequality
$\mathrm{La} \le \mathrm{La}^*$ is eventually strict, even though the layer invariants coincide.

*Status.* Open; the first cases go the other way. Equality is proved for $n = d$, for
$n = d+1$, for all $n$ when $d = 1$, and on level families for all $n$ and $d$. So any such
$n_0$ must exceed $d+1$, and the separating families cannot be level families. *Falsifiable*
by showing that some extremal strong $B_d$-free family is always weak $B_d$-free.
title: F5. Weak and strong extremal numbers differ

description:
**Statement.** With `P = (9,28)` on `E_55`, `log den x(kP) ∼ 2 ĥ(P) k²`, and consequently the
set `S(P) = {ℓ prime : ∃ k, ℓ ∣ den x(kP)}` has natural density one among the primes.

**The key insight is** that the exact `2`-adic law already proves *linear* growth of one
valuation along one sub-orbit (`v₂ = v + 2k`), which is the degenerate case of the canonical
height asymptotic; upgrading `k ↦ 2^k` to all `k` is what converts linear growth in `log` into
the quadratic law.

**Why now?** `mordell_55_point_infinite_order` removes the only hypothesis such a statement
needs (non-torsion), and it is proved here without heights — so the height asymptotic is now a
statement about an object already known to be infinite rather than a conditional one.
title: C4. Quadratic growth of the denominators, and density one

description:
**Conjecture.** For each fixed degree `d`, the number of primitive Selberg-class functions of conductor at most `Q` is bounded by a polynomial in `Q`, after specifying an equivalence relation that removes duplicate presentations.

The key insight is that Chinese-remainder factorization makes the degree-one census multiplicative across coprime conductors, suggesting that local-to-global structure should constrain global growth.

**Why now?** A rigorous multiplicative count is available for Dirichlet characters, while the finite-prefix obstruction shows exactly why an unrestricted analytic counting argument cannot establish such a bound.
title: Polynomial conductor growth in fixed degree

description:
**Conjecture.** After controlling for out-degree, the number of internally vertex-disjoint weak dependency paths through a theorem predicts deletion damage substantially better than degree centrality.

The key insight is that dense acyclic order networks can have high-degree vertices yet remain connected after every single deletion; alternate routes, rather than degree alone, determine fragility. **Why now?** The robust total-order family supplies an explicit null model against which articulation-based claims can be compared.
title: Robustness is governed by redundancy, not degree alone

description:
**Conjecture.** In every diagram-local signed path model, Alexander reciprocity is induced by an involution on admissible paths that preserves sign and sends area `a` to `c-a` for a diagram-dependent constant `c`.

The key insight is that palindromicity of a signed generating function follows from an area-reversing, sign-preserving involution; this converts a polynomial identity into a concrete combinatorial symmetry.

**Why now?** The abstract involution criterion is established, so the conjecture has a precise falsifiable target: construct the involution from crossing data and check compatibility with the forbidden region.
title: Reciprocity from path reflection

description:
Attach nonnegative weights to concepts and to preserved relations, and maximise
the weighted count over all admissible analogies. **Conjecture:** the optimal
one-sided analogy is computed by a maximum-weight partial injection (an
assignment problem), so the optimum is attained, is polynomial-time computable,
and is monotone and submodular in the weight vector.

*The key insight is* that a one-sided maximiser only needs its forward map to be
injective on the fixed set, turning fidelity maximisation into a bipartite
matching whose value is the optimum of a totally unimodular program. *Why now?*
Monotonicity in the weights is already proved, which is the hypothesis that lets
the greedy/matching machinery certify global optimality.
title: Weighted fidelity is optimised by a maximum-weight partial matching

description: One can place a ring structure on a bare set underlying a quotient only after constructing a bijection with a known ring. Such a structure would generally not be coordinatewise and would need a separate geometric naturality criterion.
title: Transport a ring structure through an explicit bijection

description: Prove that the two-sphere and a point have isomorphic trivial fundamental groups but are not homotopy equivalent, by formalizing `H₂(S²; ℤ) ≅ ℤ` and `H₂(pt; ℤ) = 0`. This would strengthen the present disconnected `Unit`/`Bool` counterexample.
title: Connected counterexample detected by second homology

description:
In the stable-Yoshida minimal setting, the universal ordinary deformation ring should be finite flat, and generically étale, over the two-variable Iwasawa weight algebra; moreover, its rank should equal the multiplicity of the corresponding ordinary Hecke component.

**The key insight is...** freeness should reflect a constant arithmetic multiplicity across weight space, while generic étaleness should follow from the vanishing of the relevant adjoint Selmer obstruction at a Zariski-dense set of classical points.

**Why now?** Freeness is already naturally transported by the `R = T` identification, leaving rank and ramification as concrete invariants that can falsify or refine the conjecture.
title: Two-variable finite-flat strengthening

description:
For centered cyclic digit prefixes, the conjecture is that statistically exceptional autocorrelation peaks are equivalent to concentration of Fourier power on characters whose phases nearly stabilize the corresponding shift, with quantitative two-sided bounds uniform in prefix length.

The key insight is that Fourier inversion turns temporal repetition into spectral concentration, while polarization turns it into low interval energy. Why now? These two exact descriptions are now available in one framework, making a sharp stability theorem a concrete target.
title: Fourier-energy characterization of digit-melody repetition

description:
**Conjecture.** For natural oracle-complete targets arising from arithmetic evaluation, every level of a suitably encoded polynomial hierarchy admits a uniform bounded-query reduction, while no corresponding unrelativized complexity-class separation follows without an oracle-elimination theorem.

The key insight is that completeness and reduction composition transfer oracle access through a class, but do not erase the oracle or imply an absolute separation such as `P ≠ NP`.

**Why now?** The one-query transfer theorem supplies the structural base on which query counts, uniformity, and oracle elimination can be studied independently.
title: Oracle-relative hierarchy transfer with explicit query budgets

description:
For directed edges with `pₙ → 0`, conjecture that the centered, variance-normalized empirical spectrum obeys the circular law whenever `npₙ` grows faster than a logarithmic threshold, while below that scale isolated rows create a nonvanishing atom at zero.

The key insight is that the same sparsity scale controlling isolated vertices also controls singularity and hence the failure of two-dimensional spectral spreading.

Why now? The finite product-law infrastructure already separates exact edge independence from asymptotic analysis, and the deterministic obstruction shows that sparsity must be studied only after the symmetry issue is repaired.
title: Sparse directed threshold for circular behavior

description:
**Conjecture.** An injective learned integral transform whose outputs satisfy a uniform analytic continuation and growth law admits a deterministic uniqueness certificate: no nonzero signal and transform code can both be supported on finite-measure sets.

The key insight is that sparse representation uniqueness can be derived from analytic rigidity rather than incoherence alone. **Why now?** The completed support theorem and the Hilbert-space Gram bound provide complementary qualitative and quantitative modules for such a certificate.
title: Sparse learned-transform uniqueness

description: For `n` independent uniform samples on the unit `d`-sphere, conjecture matching upper and lower tail bounds for the covering radius of order `(log n / n)^(1/d)`, with constants uniform over a controlled range of dimensions. Determine precisely which alternative sampling or averaged criterion removes the logarithmic factor and yields `n^{-1/d}`. **The key insight is...** the proposed bare power law likely describes typical spacing, whereas full coverage and reliable topology are governed by extreme gaps. **Why now?** Separating diameter, spacing, and coverage thresholds prevents distinct phase transitions from being conflated and gives a falsifiable correction to the original scaling claim.
title: Probabilistic `n^{-1/d}` coverage law with explicit tails

description:
**Conjecture.** Every finite sequence of signed-literal revisions has a unique normal form containing, for each atom mentioned by the sequence, exactly the sign appearing at that atom’s last occurrence; atoms never revised retain their initial status.

The key insight is that revisions at distinct atoms should commute, while contrary revisions at the same atom obey a last-write-wins law.

**Why now?** Single-step consistency preservation and the demonstrated noncommutativity of contrary revisions isolate precisely the local rewriting rules needed for a global normalization theorem.
title: Last-occurrence normal forms for revision histories

description:
**Conjecture.** Every apparent zero-work erasing demon obtained as temperature tends
to zero falls into one of two classes: either its expected running time diverges
superpolynomially, or the finite Jarzynski model loses uniform integrability and the
limiting process is not a valid finite-resource realization.

The key insight is that strict positivity fails algebraically at zero temperature,
so the obstruction must reappear as a resource divergence or a singular limit.
**Why now?** Boundary analysis pinpoints `T = 0` as the main escape hatch from the
positive-work theorem and turns that loophole into a precise asymptotic research
question.
title: Zero-Temperature Boundary Classification

description:
The lattice-point enumerator of a generalized parking-function polytope satisfies a
delete-and-contract recursion over cumulative profiles, and this recursion extends to
a valuative invariant on the associated generalized permutohedral subdivision.

The key insight is that coordinate slicing is a discrete valuation operation, while
rank deletion identifies its chamberwise contraction rule.

Why now? Small-case slice tables already display a stable recursive stratification;
an explicit gluing theorem would turn that evidence into a precise valuation formula.
title: Deletion recursion as a valuation identity

description:
**Conjecture.** In an isotropic stellar model where each collector radiates by a
Stefan–Boltzmann law at its own temperature under a fixed material budget, the
net-power-maximizing swarm splits its material into equal-temperature collectors,
and the optimal common temperature is the unique root of an explicit balance
between intercepted flux and re-radiated power.

The key insight is that intercepted power is linear in area while thermal
rejection is convex in temperature, so the joint optimum couples the equal-area
principle of this cycle with a one-dimensional convex temperature trade-off.

**Why now?** The area side of the optimization (equal allocation) is now on firm
ground; supplying an explicit radiation law closes the loop without disturbing the
resource-accounting layer, yielding a fully constrained extremum.
title: Joint area–temperature power optimization

description:
`contraction_code_independence` shows that uniqueness of semantic fixed points
makes all diagonal codes agree across unrelated presentations.  Conjecture: the
same conclusion holds for guarded endomorphisms of ultrametric or
domain-theoretic semantics (Banach fixed points in complete ultrametric spaces,
or unique fixed points of guarded recursive definitions), and moreover the
resulting canonical value is computable as the limit of the diagonal iterates
of *any* code.

*The key insight is* that presentation transport is canonical while code choice
is not; uniqueness is the exact hypothesis that collapses the second source of
ambiguity, and guardedness is its syntactic shadow.

*Why now?* The Lipschitz case is proved with no isomorphism hypothesis
whatsoever, so the statement is already in the strongest possible "unrelated
codes" form and can be ported verbatim to any uniqueness principle.
title: Uniqueness from guardedness in ordered and metric domains

description:
> **Conjecture.** The information-theoretic bound `K ≥ r` for *linear* Fourier
> sampling degrades to `K = Θ(√r)` — and no further — for *adaptive*
> measurements that may depend on earlier outcomes; i.e. adaptivity buys exactly
> a birthday-square-root and never more.

*The key insight is* that `dft_sample_count_ge_period` is proved by a pure
dimension count, which is insensitive to adaptivity, whereas Pollard rho's
`Θ(N^{1/4})` is exactly a birthday bound; the conjecture says these two numbers
