are the two ends of a single interpolation and that the randomness barrier
(barrier 8) *is* the adaptive shadow of the DFT bound.

*Why now?* Both endpoints are formalised in this cycle — the dimension bound in
`DFTSampleBound.lean`, the exponential barrier `exp(x/4)` in
`ResourceClassification.lean`, and the worst-case blindness statement
`arithmetic_trajectory_blind` in `RandomnessBarrier.lean`, which already
separates the provable worst case (`√N`) from the birthday heuristic
(`N^{1/4}`) — so the missing piece is a single interpolation theorem rather than
two independent lower bounds.

**Falsifier.** An adaptive sampling scheme determining the period of every
period-`r` signal with `o(√r)` measurements.

---
title: C3. Sample/query duality for period finding (`SampleQueryDuality`)

description:
**Conjecture.** Every free witness that recovers a residue/order coordinate `r ≤ N` to
accuracy `o(1/r²)` is, as a function of `r`, within `O(1/N²)` of a *multiplicative*
function of `r`; the "spectral vs. CRT-multiplicative" distinction therefore lives in the
*computation*, never in the witness value.

*The key insight is* that exact rounding forces the witness to agree with `1/r` (or an
invertible reparametrisation of it) to accuracy `1/(2r²)`, and `1/r` is multiplicative —
this is exactly what `heatReturn_approx_multiplicative` proves for the heat kernel.

*Why now?* This cycle turned a qualitative classification label into a quantitative,
checkable statement; the general version needs only an abstract "recovery ⇒ proximity to
`1/r`" lemma, which our rounding lemma `round_one_div_of_close` already contains in germ.
title: C5. Witness-value multiplicativity is not an accident: a classification dichotomy

description:
**Conjecture.** For every seed, `k*(ctx) / (d·ctx/32) → 1` as `ctx → ∞`, and the
additive deficit `d·ctx/32 - k*` stays bounded by one grid step at every rung. Concretely:
at `ctx = 4096` and `8192` the seed-2 deficit is again exactly `32`, never `64`.

*The key insight is* that a bounded additive drift against a geometrically growing knee is
asymptotically invisible: the ratio law is exact in the limit and the deployable speedup
collapses to the guaranteed `8×` (`KneeDrift.kneeRatio_tendsto_one`,
`KneeDrift.speedup_tendsto_eight`). What the programme calls a systematic sub-linear break
is, if this conjecture holds, a *vanishing correction to an exact law* — the strongest
possible rescue of the product law, and one that also predicts the `9.1×` best case is a
transient.

*Why now?* The conjecture's asymptotic half is already a theorem for the modelled ladder;
what is open is whether the measured deficits stay at one step. Two further doublings
decide it.

---
title: C3. The vanishing-drift conjecture

description:
**Conjecture.** Let a normalized integral transform send compactly supported inputs to holomorphic functions on a connected complex domain, with a uniform growth bound determined by the input support. There is a quantitative lower bound on the transform's mass outside every measurable set of prescribed finite measure, depending only on the growth bound and the set's measure.

The key insight is that the qualitative identity principle proved in this cycle should admit a stable replacement through propagation-of-smallness estimates. **Why now?** The qualitative support obstruction and its exact regularity boundary have been isolated, leaving growth control as the single missing quantitative ingredient.
title: Quantitative analytic-continuation uncertainty

description:
**Conjecture.** Adjoining distinct positive and negative zeros to the transreal carrier admits a conservative total arithmetic in which reciprocal is an involution on every value, nullity remains absorbing, and the ordinary real field embeds as precisely the quotient identifying the two signed zeros.

The key insight is that the failure of double reciprocal at negative infinity is not caused by infinity itself, but by the loss of sign when both infinities map to one ordinary zero. **Why now?** The reciprocal boundary calculation isolates this as the only obstruction visible in the four-constructor model, making a minimal completion concrete and testable.
title: Signed-zero completion and genuine wheel involution

description:
**Conjecture.** A reflective fixed-point code admits a monotone interpretation in every complete Heyting algebra if and only if each occurrence of its bound variable has positive variance. Moreover, failure of positivity is witnessed by a two-element algebra.

The key insight is that the same variance discipline governing recursive types also governs Knaster–Tarski semantics for self-referential provability. **Why now?** The syntax–semantics boundary is explicit: unrestricted codes have been separated from the guarded fragment, making both directions of the criterion testable.
title: Positivity as the exact semantic frontier

description:
For pairs of developments whose principal interfaces use inequivalent abstraction layers, every semantics-preserving migration path incurs an intermediate source-length overhead of at least a fixed positive fraction of the smaller endpoint length.

The key insight is that the first boundary crossing is unavoidable; the open issue is whether interface adapters impose a uniform quantitative penalty there. **Why now?** The boundary-crossing theorem reduces the conjecture to measuring a single class of cross-interface transitions rather than all intermediate states.
title: Quantitative adapter-valley conjecture

description:
**Conjecture.** For every positive initial value, the globally additive-avoiding greedy trajectory is eventually an arithmetic progression, with its common difference determined by the additive semigroup generated by the initial segment.

The key insight is that the forbidden set is a finite restricted sumset whose residue-class profile may stabilize even while its diameter grows. **Why now?** The explicit successor bound shows that all choices occur in a short moving interval, making residue stabilization a concrete and falsifiable mechanism rather than an unconstrained asymptotic claim.
title: Stability under changing the initial value

description:
**Conjecture.** If candidates avoid all sums of exactly `r` prior terms, with repetition allowed, then the greedy trajectory from one is eventually periodic modulo `r` and has linear growth.

The key insight is that an `r`-fold sum of a single stable residue class occupies one residue class, potentially leaving a neighboring class permanently admissible. **Why now?** Pair-sum avoidance demonstrates that a global exclusion rule need not force quadratic growth; varying the arity tests which part of the linear behavior is genuinely structural.
title: Higher-order additive avoidance

description:
**Conjecture.** If definite answers must always be sound and an oracle must answer on at least a fixed positive fraction of every sufficiently rich arithmetic benchmark, then no computable oracle attains the requirement uniformly over all length bounds.

The key insight is that abstention ceases to be vacuous only when soundness is paired with an explicit lower bound on coverage.

**Why now?** The three-valued model already isolates abstention and counts it as failure, so alternative precision-and-coverage scoring rules can be compared without ambiguity.
title: Sound abstention under a coverage constraint

description:
**Conjecture.** Among all monotone self-observation operators on a fixed complete
lattice, those whose emergent state equals their least fixed point are precisely
the continuous ones; equivalently, "finite rounds of observation suffice" is not
merely sufficient but *characterises* continuity on lattices rich enough to
carry a limit level.

The key insight is that the discontinuous witness fails the finite-suffices
property in the sharpest possible way — its emergent state is a fixed point of no
iterate — suggesting that the implication "finite-suffices ⇒ continuous" holds in
full generality, upgrading a one-directional theorem to an equivalence.

Why now? Having both the positive theorem (continuous ⇒ finite-suffices) and an
explicit failure in the discontinuous case, the remaining converse is the natural
and testable completion of the picture.
title: Continuity as the exact frontier of finite self-knowledge

description:
For a defect rate whose budget at scale `a` grows sublinearly, `Q(t) ≤ D₀ + κ t^α`
(`0 ≤ α < 1`), the family of bounds `L ≤ (m/a)(π + Q(L)/a)` proved in `anec_domain_bound`,
optimized over the free scale `a > 0`, yields `L ≤ C(m, α)·(D₀ + κ L^α)^{1/(1-α)}`, and
the envelope is attained by an explicit oscillating curvature profile.

**The key insight is** that the scale `a` in the Prüfer angle is a genuinely free
parameter: the theorem is a one-parameter *family* of bounds and the physics lies in its
envelope, not in any single member — `EnergyShortfall.lean` is the special case `a = √(mε)`
and already shows how much the right choice of scale buys.

**Why now?** `anec_domain_bound` takes `a` as an argument and
`myers_bound_with_shortfall` demonstrates the pattern for one fixed scale; the remaining
step is to minimize a smooth function of one variable and to build the matching profile
from the `tanSol` / `riccatiSol` blocks already formalized.

**Falsifiable by:** a defect profile with sublinear budget whose exact blow-up time
exceeds the optimized envelope.

---
title: Conjecture A (Optimal scale selection in the ANEC bound)

description:
**Statement.** For any three points of the upper half-plane not on a common
geodesic, the region bounded by the three connecting geodesics has hyperbolic
area `(π - (α+β+γ))/κ`, where `α, β, γ` are the `angleBetween` angles of the
tangent vectors of the sides.

*The key insight is* that the ≥ one-ideal-vertex case proved here is already the
whole theorem: an arbitrary triangle is the difference of two triangles with an
ideal vertex at `∞`, obtained by extending one side to the boundary, so the
identity follows by additivity of the slicing integral plus a single
angle-addition identity at the shared vertex — no new analysis is required, only
bookkeeping of which region is added and which subtracted.

*Why now?* The three ingredients that used to be missing are in place: the
exact antiderivative `arcsinChord`, integrability across the singular
endpoints, and a definition of interior angle that is provably conformally
invariant (`angleBetween_smul_left/right`).

**Falsifiable form.** Compute the area of the triangle with vertices `i`, `2i`
and `1 + i` numerically; the conjecture is refuted if it differs from
`π - α - β - γ` for the numerically computed angles.
title: Conjecture A — full Gauss–Bonnet in the half-plane, all vertices finite

description:
The explicit triad over `ZMod 12` uses evaluation-preserving equivalences of
three three-constructor syntaxes.  Conjecture: for the free graded model on a
family `F`, the group of evaluation-preserving automorphisms is isomorphic to
the group of permutations of `F` fixing the chosen fixed-point assignment,
times the stabiliser of the literals; consequently two graded triads over the
same `F` are equivalent iff their fixed-point assignments agree, and the number
of inequivalent triads over `Fin n` with `|F| = m` is computable in closed form.

*The key insight is* that the free graded model is determined by nothing but a
choice function selecting one fixed point per endomorphism, so classification
of triads reduces to classification of such choice functions.

*Why now?* `exists_table_of_fixed_points` builds the free model explicitly and
`geb_triad_second_value` shows that different choices give genuinely different
diagonal witnesses (`0` versus `3`), so the moduli problem is nonempty and
finite.
title: Maximal *graded* triads with genuine domain morphisms

description:
**Conjecture.** At matched sparsity `k/L`, the selection gap of the measured profiles
obeys `gap(ctx) ≍ c·(k/N_eff(ctx))^{1/2} − k/L`, so with `N_eff ∝ ctx^{0.86}` the gap
decays like `ctx^{-0.43}` and reaches zero — the uniform-attention rigidity point of
`SelectionDilution.uniform_of_topMass_eq` — at a finite, computable context.

*The key insight is* that `SelectionExchange.selection_gap_split_eq` makes the gap an
exact invariant of self-similar refinement, so **any** decay is a measurement of the
failure of self-similarity, and the Cauchy–Schwarz cap
`SelectionDilution.topMass_sq_le_card_mul_sumSq` converts the measured effective support
directly into the achievable gap.

*Why now?* The measured gaps (`+5.3, +5.9, +1.7`) and the two measured
effective supports (`291.16, 526.39`) already over-determine the two constants; a single
`ctx = 4096` run tests the prediction, and a gap of zero would be the strongest possible
negative result about data-free attention pruning.
title: C2. The dilution exponent: the selection gap decays like `k/N_eff`

description:
**Statement.** Every integer `m ≥ 3` is a sum of exactly three anti-Fibonacci numbers.

*Status update (this cycle).* The order-`4` version is now **proved unconditionally** in
`Catalog/Computation/AntiFibonacciLagrange.lean`: `sum_four_iff` shows that `m` is a sum of
four anti-Fibonacci numbers iff `m ≥ 4`, and `sum_three_iff_sq_add_sq_add_sq` reduces the
remaining order-`3` question to "`8m - 21` is a sum of three squares".  What is left open
is therefore exactly the three-squares input.

**The key insight is** that `antiFib n = 1 + T(n-1)` with `T` triangular, so the claim is
exactly Gauss's *Eureka* theorem "every natural number is the sum of three triangular
numbers", shifted by `3`; equivalently, by the proved reduction, that every `8m - 21 ≡ 3
(mod 8)` is a sum of three squares.  Combined with the proved two-term criterion this
would give a complete additive picture: two terms fail on a set of positive density
(proved), three terms always succeed, four terms always succeed (proved).

**Why now?** Mathlib already has the three-squares theorem's cousin (sum of four squares)
and the two-squares classification; Gauss's triangular theorem follows from the
three-squares theorem `8m + 3 = x² + y² + z²`, whose formalisation is the single missing
ingredient and is actively within reach of the existing quadratic-forms API.

**Falsifiable:** a single `m` requiring four terms refutes it; scanning `m ≤ 10⁶` with the
proved `O(1)` membership test is a cheap check.

description:
**Conjecture.** Among groups of order at most 2000, the multiset of composition factors together with the directed incidence data of complemented chief factors separates substantially more isomorphism classes than composition factors together with derived length and nilpotency class.

The key insight is that the order-six collision is caused not by missing factor sizes, but by missing information about how factors act on one another. A compact extension fingerprint should therefore be a more chemically meaningful “valence shell” than a single integer.

**Why now?** The factor-ledger obstruction precisely identifies what the first axis remembers and the order-six example isolates the smallest missing interaction. This makes a finite, falsifiable census comparison possible.
title: Extension fingerprints refine composition columns

description:
There exists a decidable, aperiodically pruned binary search whose lower and upper normalized dimensions are any prescribed rational pair `0 ≤ a < b ≤ 1`, while its finite-scale estimates attain neighborhoods of both endpoints infinitely often.

The key insight is that alternating long periodic blocks should independently control lower and upper exponential growth rates. **Why now?** Exact periodic dimensions and exact complete-period estimates supply the blocks needed for a constructive oscillation theorem.
title: Oscillatory search spectra

description:
**Conjecture.** For every real `c > 0`, there exists a permutation `σ` of the natural numbers such that `p_{σ(n)}/p_n → c`.

The key insight is that the prime number theorem turns this into an asymptotic matching problem with target index scale `σ(n) ∼ cn`; global bijectivity may be achieved by sparse corrections whose relative displacement tends to zero.

**Why now?** The dense limit-one core shows that finite constraints are harmless, allowing a construction to be assembled in long blocks while preserving any prescribed finite prefix.
title: Realization of every positive limiting ratio

description:
There are optimal universal constants relating concurrence to the metric distance from a normalized state to the Segre variety of product states, for both Euclidean and Fubini–Study metrics.

**The key insight is...** concurrence is the norm of the defining quadratic equation of the Segre variety, so it should control transverse distance while degenerating predictably along tangent directions.

**Why now?** The exact determinant criterion identifies the algebraic zero set, while the unit-interval bound supplies the global normalization needed for sharp estimates.
title: Quantitative distance from the product-state variety

description:
**Conjecture.** Every maximal geodesic of the metric
\(\cosh(y)^{-2}dx^2+\cosh(x)^2dy^2\) is defined for all real time.

The key insight is that degeneration of the horizontal coefficient at large
\(|y|\) is coupled to rapid growth of the vertical coefficient at large \(|x|\),
so conserved energy may prevent finite-time escape even though neither coordinate
coefficient is uniformly comparable to the Euclidean metric. **Why now?** The
metric is known to be smooth and positive definite everywhere, and its exact
coefficient structure is explicit enough to turn completeness into quantitative
ODE estimates.
title: Global completeness of the anisotropic plane

description:
**Conjecture.** For a time-indexed network observed through a causal channel, any causal decoder achieving per-time distortion budgets \(D_1,\ldots,D_T\) must collect directed information at least the logarithm of a sequential covering number; equality holds for a class of memoryless network evolutions and product observation channels.

The key insight is that ordinary covering counts ignore the order in which information arrives, whereas a causal observer can only refine the set of compatible histories along a filtration.

**Why now?** The proved \(Tn^2\) exact-reconstruction bound gives the terminal, zero-distortion endpoint against which a genuinely sequential rate law can be calibrated.
title: Causal surveillance and directed information

description:
**Conjecture.** For each fixed dimension, there is an explicit finite classification of minimal axis-moving piece configurations that force mate, and the minimum required material is monotone nondecreasing with dimension.

The key insight is that each additional axis creates new escape directions that must be blocked independently, turning mate into a finite covering problem for the Chebyshev neighborhood.

**Why now?** The sharp contrast between two-rook mate in dimension one and lone-rook escape in every higher dimension provides the first exact boundary case and a testable base for the classification.
title: Dimension–Material Mate Classification

description:
For the conjugation-symmetric multiset of nontrivial zeros with ordinates of absolute value at most `T`, determine the asymptotic behavior of the symmetrically ordered sum of reciprocals, including multiplicity. Test whether it converges, remains bounded, or has a main term after the real contribution from each conjugate pair is isolated.

The key insight is that the classical zero count grows on the scale `T log T`, while reciprocal weighting and conjugate pairing substantially alter the scale of the resulting sum.

Why now? The separation-and-counting transfer theorem identifies exactly which analytic estimates must be sharpened and exposes why the originally proposed `log T / log log T` bound does not follow from zero counting alone.
title: Correct asymptotic scale of the reciprocal-zero harmonic

description:
**Conjecture.** Suppose candidates carry an ordinal-valued rank and every proper pruning step strictly decreases the multiset extension of that rank. Then monotone contracting elimination reaches a greatest fixed kernel by transfinite iteration, with stabilization below the successor of the initial multiset rank.

The key insight is that finite cardinality is only one well-founded measure; replacing it by a multiset ordinal should preserve the termination architecture while admitting finitely represented infinite arenas.

**Why now?** The finite proof already factors through a generic well-founded termination principle, exposing the exact interface at which ordinal or multiset measures can replace cardinality.
title: Well-founded infinite-state extension

description: The current Moore-machine model returns the observation at the final state after a finite input history. Natural extensions include Mealy outputs at every transition, infinite streams, probabilistic transition kernels, nondeterministic systems, and approximate equivalence under a metric on outputs. Each requires a corresponding bisimulation theorem and an analysis of when equivalence remains decidable.
title: Add richer interaction semantics

description:
**Conjecture.** There is a sharp polynomial weight exponent for which the
alternating binomial transform extends to a bounded involution on the resulting
weighted sequence space, and this exponent matches the decay threshold in the
Báez–Duarte criterion.

The key insight is that finite binomial inversion is exact, but infinite
inversion is controlled by the interaction between Pascal growth and sequence
decay. **Why now?** The finite involution isolates the sole unresolved issue as
continuity under completion, making a functional-analytic formulation precise.
title: Weighted Banach-space involution

description:
Let `qₙ` be the probability that two uniform elements of `Sₙ` generate either `Aₙ` or `Sₙ`. Then
   \[
   \lim_{n\to\infty} q_n=1
   \quad\text{and}\quad
   \exists C>0\;\exists N\;\forall n\ge N,\;1-q_n\le C/n.
   \]
   Formalizing `qₙ` would connect the catalog's `Sₙ`-only count to the standard random-permutation formulation of Dixon's theorem.
title: Alternating-or-symmetric generation

description:
**Conjecture.** On a connected complex with an orientation local system whose weights
are all odd, twisted developability is equivalent to vanishing of the twisted periods
together with the vanishing of a single class in `A / 2A`.  In particular over a
2-divisible group (`ℚ`, `ℝ`, `ZMod k` with `k` odd) twisted developability is
detected by periods alone, and `mobius_periods_insufficient` has no analogue.

*Falsifiable:* a connected twisted complex over `ℝ` with vanishing periods but no
height field.
title: Twisted classification over 2-divisible coefficients

description:
`symmetryGroup_subgroupPattern` realizes every subgroup for a *free* translation
action.  Conjecture: realizability survives the loss of freeness for the
quarter-turn action — for every `p ≥ 3` and every subgroup `H ≤ QuarterTurns`
there is a pattern `f : ZMod p × ZMod p → Bool` with
`symmetryGroup QuarterTurns f = H`.  *Refutation:* a `p ≥ 3` and a subgroup
(necessarily one of `⊥`, the half-turn subgroup, `⊤`) realized by no pattern.
Failure at `p = 1` is immediate — the single cell forces `⊤` — so the bound
`p ≥ 3` is part of the claim.
title: N3. Realizability for a non-free action

description:
`card_pattern_glide` counts the patterns invariant under a single glide
reflection `γ(t, n) = (t + p/2, -n)` on the `p × q` torus with `p` even: there
are `2 ^ (p q / 2)`, since `γ` is fixed-point free
(`fixedBy_glide_eq_empty`).  Conjecture: for the larger group generated by `γ`
together with *every* time shift — the toroidal analogue of the wallpaper group
`pg` — the orbits are exactly the pitch pairs `{n, -n}`, so the capacity is

    2 ^ ((q + t(q)) / 2),   t(n) = gcd(2, n),

independently of `p`.  *Refutation:* an even `p` and a `q` where a brute-force
count differs, i.e. where the glide and the shifts fail to merge two cells with
the same pitch class.  For `q = 3` the prediction is `4` patterns for every even
`p`.
title: N4. Capacity of the toroidal "pg" group

title: Beyond the resolved one-sided transfer question

description:
Cycle 6 also re-examined Conjecture 9 and expects it to be **false as stated**.
The group ring `ℤ[ℤ/3]` already contains the six units `±1, ±g, ±g²`, so the
Klein four-group of `O` is *not* the largest finite oriented unit group; and
since `ℤ[ℤ/6] ⊗ ℚ` decomposes into the rank-zero fields `ℚ, ℚ, ℚ(ζ₃), ℚ(ζ₆)`,
the unit group of `ℤ[ℤ/6]` should be finite, contradicting "infinite as soon as
`k ≥ 5`".  The corrected conjecture is: `ℤ[ℤ/k]^×` is finite exactly when every
divisor `d` of `k` lies in `{1, 2, 3, 4, 6}`, i.e. when `k ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4, 6}`.
This is stated here as a prediction, not a theorem; no part of it has been
formalised.
title: Critic's note on Conjecture 9

description:
**Conjecture.** Let `p` be a prior on orderings and let the sorter be allowed a free
side-information register correlated with the input (a "catalyst" that must be returned
unchanged).  Then the expected retained history is still at least `H(p)` bits, and equality
holds iff the prior is dyadic; in particular catalysts cannot beat
`PriorSorter.entropy_le_expectedComparisons`, and the one-comparison slack of
`exists_priorSorter_within_one_comparison` is unavoidable for non-dyadic priors.

The key insight is that a returned-unchanged catalyst cannot change the Kraft budget of the
transcript code, so the Shannon bound should survive verbatim, while the sharp equality case
(dyadic priors) is the equality case already isolated in the catalog's
`expected_length_eq_entropy_iff`. **Why now?** The prior-sensitive floor and its
one-comparison achievability are both proved, so the only remaining question is whether
auxiliary correlated resources move the floor — a clean yes/no with a concrete dyadic
boundary.
title: Prior-sensitive history is incompressible below the entropy, even with side information

description:
`Novelty/TransferPreorderRealization.lean` classifies the realizable consistency-transfer
preorders `i ≼ j :↔ ⊢ Con i → Con j` for the tag-sensitive theories.

**Conjecture.**  For every realizable total preorder `R` with no strict chain of length
`N + 1`, and for every reflection-depth vector `r` bounded by the rank function of `R`,
there is a consistent GL theory whose transfer preorder is `R` and whose per-tag
reflection depths are `r`.  Hence the transfer preorder and the reflection-depth vector
are *independent* invariants: neither constrains the other beyond the inequality
`r i ≤ rank R N i`.

**The key insight is** that the transfer preorder only sees the truncated heights
`min N (c i)` — the *accessibility* cut points — while reflection depth only sees the
valuation cut point, so conjecture 1 should upgrade automatically to the preorder level
by composing with the rank representation `totalPreorder_iff_rank_representation`.

**Why now?**  The classification of transfer preorders and the exact reflection spectrum
are now both theorems; the only missing link is the combined semantics of conjecture 1.

*Falsified by* a realizable preorder `R` and an admissible `r` that cannot be realized
simultaneously.
title: Reflection depth is invisible to the transfer preorder

description:
**Conjecture.**  Replace binary quadratic forms by binary *cubic* forms of
discriminant `Δ` (Davenport–Heilbronn / Bhargava cubic rings).  Then the vector
of representation numbers of `N` by the reduced cubic forms of discriminant `Δ`
is **not** a residue dial for any `Δ` with more than one `GL₂(ℤ)`-class, because
the associated `S₃`-extension is non-abelian — yet it is still factor-blind in
the sense that the observation depends only on the ideal class of `N`, not on the
individual factors.

*The key insight is* that the collapse proved here has two independent causes:
abelianness (which makes the dial readable) and multiplicativity (which makes it
blind); cubic forms remove the first but not the second, so they should provide a
clean separation of the two barriers.

*Why now?*  The `ResidueDial` abstraction of this project is stated for an
arbitrary index type and an arbitrary family of predicates on `ℤ`, so it applies
verbatim to cubic forms; only the finite `decide` computations change.

**Lean shape.**
`def cubicRepr (a b c d : ℤ) : ℤ → Prop := fun N => ∃ x y, a*x^3 + b*x^2*y + c*x*y^2 + d*y^3 = N`, then `theorem cubic_not_dial : ¬ ∃ (d : ResidueDial m ι), …` in the style of `no_residueDial_23`.
title: C5. Beyond quadratic: cubic dials

description:
**Conjecture.** With respect to the hyperbolic area `dx dy / y²`, the moduli space of tori has
finite total area `π/3`, and for `0 < ε ≤ 1` the area of the `ε`-thin part is exactly `1/ε − c`
for an explicit constant `c`, so

    area {sys ≥ ε} = π/3 − 1/ε + O(1)   as ε → 0 ,

with the error term coming only from the two corners of the fundamental domain.  In particular
the thick part exhausts the finite total area, and the counting function of `SL(2, ℤ)`-orbits of
tori with `sys ≥ ε` inside a ball of radius `R` grows like `area · e^{R}`.

*The key insight is* that the compactness statement `isCompact_fdThick` already identifies the
thick part with the *truncated* fundamental domain `𝒟 ∩ {Im ≤ 1/ε}` — and on that region the
hyperbolic area integral is elementary, `∫ dx dy / y²` over a vertical strip, so the whole
computation reduces to `∫_{√(1−x²)}^{1/ε} dy/y²` and a single arcsine.
*Why now?* Before this cycle the thick part was known only up to a metric comparison; now it is
a concrete compact region with explicit boundary (`isCompact_fdThick`, `sys_eq_one_div_im_of_fd`),
which is exactly the input an area computation needs, and Mathlib's integration API can evaluate
the resulting one-dimensional integrals.
