   *expanding* monotone updates and `OrderHom.lfp`, modeling saturation-style
   algorithms (adding candidates until closure). The dual bridge
   `lfp = ↑(closure kernel)` should follow the same pattern.
title: Least fixed points and the dual game

description:
For a class `{p_θ}` the minimax pointwise redundancy is **exactly** `log₂ Cₛ`
with `Cₛ = ∑ₓ sup_θ p_θ(x)` (`shtarkov_minimax`), and

* memoryless class over alphabet `A`: `Cₛ ≤ (n+1)^{#A}`, binary case `Cₛ ≤ n+1`;
* first-order Markov: `Cₛ ≤ #A·(n+1)^{#A²}`;
* binary memoryless lower bound: `Cₛ ≥ √n/4`, i.e. `≥ ½ log₂ n − 2` bits;
* deterministic ("one decompressor per file") class: `Cₛ = #X`, price `= n` bits;
* the price is additive over independent blocks (`price_prodClass_add`), and
  only *sub*additive when the blocks share a parameter
  (`shtarkovSum_tiedProdClass_le`), which specialises to subadditivity of the
  memoryless price in the message length, `Cₛ(n₁+n₂) ≤ Cₛ(n₁)·Cₛ(n₂)`
  (`iid_price_subadditive`) — so `log₂ Cₛ(n)/n` converges by Fekete.

So a specialised decompressor can move only `Θ(log n)` bits out of the message
for a parametric class, and *zero* bits for an unrestricted class. The gate of
the research plan is met (the Rissanen rate is matched from below), and the
verdict is: specialisation pays only when the data class is genuinely
low-complexity relative to the data.
title: Answer this cycle produced (context for the conjectures)

description:
For every finite decimal word and every prescribed finite vector of lag correlations compatible with that word, construct both a transcendental real and a quadratic irrational sharing the word whenever the algebraic class permits the same prefix. The conjecture is that no statistic depending on a fixed finite prefix can distinguish transcendence from algebraicity with certainty.

The key insight is that finite musical data constrain an interval of real numbers, not the arithmetic nature of an individual tail. Why now? This obstruction would give a rigorous boundary for all attempts to infer deep arithmetic properties from finite sonifications.
title: Prefix-prescription obstruction theorem

description:
Find the least integer `N` such that the coefficient functions through degree `N` of the 194 McKay–Thompson series uniquely recover every irreducible Monster character and the multiplicities of all graded pieces determined up to that degree. A falsifying outcome would be two distinct nonnegative multiplicity tables with identical classwise traces through degree `N`.

**The key insight is...** recovery is an injectivity problem for a truncated character-evaluation operator, and positivity plus integrality may force injectivity substantially earlier than unrestricted linear algebra predicts.

**Why now?** The abstract reconstruction theorem identifies injectivity as the exact boundary, making ranks, integral kernels, and positivity cones of finite truncations directly testable.
title: Finite coefficient threshold for character recovery

description:
Every normalized two-qubit state with concurrence one lies in the local-unitary orbit of a Bell state, and equality in the determinant norm bound is equivalent to orthogonality and equal norm of the two coefficient rows.

**The key insight is...** equality must hold simultaneously in the triangle inequality and both quadratic product bounds, forcing rigid phase and norm relations.

**Why now?** The sharp upper bound is established, and its proof exposes the exact inequalities whose equality cases must be classified.
title: Classification of all sharp determinant maximizers

description:
**Conjecture.** For every pair of integers `g ≥ 3` and `r ≥ 3`, there is a finite network with no cycle shorter than `g` whose emotional chromatic number exceeds `r`; moreover, such examples can be chosen so that the first positive chromatic evaluation occurs sharply after a quantitatively long zero interval.

The key insight is that local tree-like friendship geometry need not constrain the global positivity threshold of proper emotion assignments.

**Why now?** The minimal-positive-value law turns the classical high-girth/high-chromatic phenomenon into a testable statement about an explicit sequence of vanishing evaluations.
title: High-girth networks with unbounded emotional diversity

description:
**Conjecture.** For every finite relational signature and finite model, there is a finite modal language with graded modalities whose theories classify pointed models exactly up to isomorphism; moreover, the least required modal depth is bounded by the number of worlds and is attained by an infinite family.

The key insight is that truth invariance supplies one direction automatically, while finite characteristic formulas may provide the converse and quantify the observational cost of recovering structure.

**Why now?** The transport theorem isolates the exact induction principle that a characteristic-formula construction must reverse, and finite models make the depth bound falsifiable by exhaustive families.
title: Orbit-complete observational languages

description:
**Conjecture.** The stated transreal multiplication is associative on the entire carrier, and it is the unique commutative associative extension of real multiplication satisfying nullity absorption, the signed infinity rules, and `0 · (±∞) = Φ`.

The key insight is that the nullity classification reduces all difficult associativity cases to sign multiplication and the zero-infinity boundary. **Why now?** A complete exceptional-case classification is available, so uniqueness can be attacked by a finite table argument coupled to ordinary real sign algebra.
title: Maximal associative totalization

description:
**Conjecture.** For every rational expression over transreal variables, there is a finite stratification by polynomial sign and vanishing conditions such that the expression is either an ordinary rational function or one of `+∞`, `-∞`, and `Φ` on each stratum.

The key insight is that nullity can arise only from null input or zero-infinity multiplication, and all other exceptional outputs are controlled by signs. **Why now?** The multiplication classification and exact finite division theorem provide the local rewriting rules needed for a structural induction on expressions.
title: Exceptional-ideal normal forms

description:
**Conjecture.** Adding positive reflective fixed points to an intensional dependent type theory with normalization preserves canonicity for closed natural-number terms and is conservative over judgments not containing reflection or fixed points.

The key insight is to stratify reduction so that ordinary dependent computation cannot inspect reflective evidence, while guarded unfolding remains productive. **Why now?** The syntactic proper-extension theorem isolates the new constructors; the next test is whether their operational rules preserve the metatheory of the embedded fragment.
title: Conservative embedding of dependent type theory

description:
**Conjecture.** Among contracting updates on a finite powerset, synchronous iteration always stabilizes, but the terminal fixed point is greatest below every input if and only if the update satisfies a fixed-point preservation condition strictly weaker than full monotonicity.

The key insight is that contraction alone controls termination, whereas monotonicity was used only to preserve arbitrary fixed subsets; isolating the weakest replacement should classify when an implementation computes the intended semantic kernel.

**Why now?** The present separation between stabilization and greatest-kernel semantics makes it possible to search for exact boundary axioms rather than treating monotonicity as an indivisible implementation requirement.
title: Counterexample classification beyond monotonicity

description: The literal claim that one fixed proof exceeds every computable bound has the wrong quantifier order and is formally refuted. A viable noncomputable replacement is a Busy-Beaver function for proof search: as the statement-size budget grows, the maximum shortest proof length may dominate every computable function, subject to a suitable sound and sufficiently expressive formal theory. Formalizing this requires computably enumerable syntax, a proof checker, consistency/soundness assumptions as theorem parameters, and undecidability machinery.
title: Busy-Beaver rather than a single dominating proof

description:
**Conjecture.** Let `R` be a Euclidean domain and let `β ∈ R` have finite residue ring. If a complete residue digit set contains zero and admits a strictly decreasing Euclidean digit-extraction map outside a finite exceptional set, then every element of `R` has a canonical finite base-`β` expansion; uniqueness is equivalent to uniqueness of residues at every extraction step.

The key insight is that existence and uniqueness separate cleanly: descent proves termination, while residue injectivity peels equal expansions one digit at a time.

**Why now?** Negabinary arithmetic supplies the complete one-dimensional model, while complex bases provide immediate nontrivial test cases over `ℤ[i]`.
title: Negative-base uniqueness over Euclidean domains

description:
Conjecture that there is an exponent `θ<1` such that, for every sufficiently large `T`, the
window `[T,T+T^θ]` contains conductors `m,n` with `φ(m)≤T<φ(n)`, and that this remains true
after restricting to prescribed squarefree factorization patterns.

**The key insight is...** composite conductors turn monotone prime activation into an
intermittent multiplicative process, while deformation stability guarantees that every
zero-reflecting order parameter detects the same crossings.

**Why now?** The response law has been removed as a confounding variable; the remaining
question is a concrete short-interval problem about Euler's totient and controlled
factorization types.
title: Totient intermittency in short conductor windows

description:
**Conjecture.** Every taxicab number `N` factors as `N = m³ · N₀` with `N₀`
cube-free, and the representation count of `N` equals that of its cube-free core
`N₀`; consequently the *primitive* taxicab numbers (cube-free `N₀`) already carry
all the representation-count information.

The key insight is that the scaling map proved in this cycle is a bijection
between representations of `N₀` and representations of `m³ N₀` that preserves the
ordering `a ≤ b`, so cube factors contribute nothing new and can be stripped.

Why now? The scaling theorem `scaled_reps_card` supplies exactly the injection
needed for the easy direction; the open content is the reverse inclusion — that
scaling by a cube produces *no additional* representations — which would reduce
the whole theory to cube-free numbers.
title: Multiplicative obstruction and a cube-free core

description:
The proved bound `binom(N,k) ≤ N^k` is robust and directly yields the
`log₂ N` bits-per-spike ceiling. A sharper next theorem is

`binom(N,k) ≤ (e N / k)^k`,

followed by two-sided estimates from Stirling's formula. For a fixed active
fraction `k ≈ ρN`, this should connect sparse neural capacity to binary entropy:

`log₂ binom(N,ρN) ≈ N H₂(ρ)`.

That formulation would quantify one-percent coding precisely rather than merely
substituting `k = N/100` into a polynomial bound.
title: Sharpen the sparse-capacity asymptotics

description:
Every `f : TRⁿ → TR` satisfying `TropIIA` and `TropPareto` is *separable*:
there are maps `g₁,…,gₙ : TR → TR`, each monotone with `gᵢ(⊤) = ⊤`, such that
`f x = ⨁ᵢ gᵢ(xᵢ)` and `⨁ᵢ gᵢ(c) = c` for every `c`.  Moreover `f` is diagonally
idempotent iff every `gᵢ` satisfies `gᵢ(c ⊙ c) = gᵢ(c) ⊙ gᵢ(c)`, and tropically linear iff
every `gᵢ` is a translation `c ↦ aᵢ ⊙ c`.

Evidence: `distortedRule = x₀ ⊕ φ(x₁)` of `TropicalSocialChoiceNonlinear.lean` has exactly
this shape with `g₀ = id`, `g₁ = φ`, and `profile_decomposition` shows that any additive
rule is determined by its values on the scaled unit profiles `c ⊙ eᵢ`, i.e. by the `n`
functions `gᵢ(c) = f (c ⊙ eᵢ)`.  The open content is that no further compatibility is
forced between the `gᵢ`.

Falsifiable: an additive unanimous rule (necessarily on `n ≥ 2` voters) that disagrees with
`x ↦ ⨁ᵢ f (xᵢ ⊙ eᵢ)` at some profile.
title: Conjecture A (Separable normal form for additive unanimous rules)

description:
By C4 the point group descending to the `p × q` torus with `p ≠ q` is the Klein
four-group `{diag(±1, ±1)}`.  Conjecture: the number of patterns invariant under
all four of its elements is

    2 ^ ( (p + t(p)) * (q + t(q)) / 4 ),   t(n) = twoTorsionCard n = gcd(2, n),

since Burnside adds `p*q`, `q*t(p)`, `p*t(q)` and `t(p)*t(q)` fixed cells.
*Refutation:* a pair `(p, q)` where a brute-force count differs — equivalently a
cell fixed by a coordinate sign change that the parity bookkeeping misses.
This is the rectangular counterpart of the proved `card_pattern_quarterTurn`, and
would complete the capacity table for every planar point group that descends.
title: N1. Capacity of a rectangular torus under its full descended point group

description:
`capSysN n` is consistent, minimally sound, and refutes the uniform reflection rule
exactly at iteration depth `n`: it proves `□^{n+1}⊥` and refutes `□^n ⊥`.

**Conjecture (depth-graded reflection hierarchy).**  For every `n ≥ 1` the *restricted*
reflection rule "`⊢ □ φ` implies `⊢ φ` for all `φ` of box-depth `< n`" holds in
`capSysN n`, while it fails at depth `n`.  Hence 1-consistency stratifies into a
strictly increasing chain of conditions, each strictly stronger than the minimal
soundness condition `⊬ □⊥` that is *equivalent* to the negative independence half.

*Falsified by* a formula of box-depth `< n` provably boxed but unprovable in
`capSysN n`, or by a proof that the depth-`n` rule holds.
title: Depth-graded failure of reflection

description:
**Status of part (b) of the previous version of this conjecture:** *proved*.
The three-poset bound `U(n) ≥ 3n - ⌈n/2⌉ - 3` (asymptotically `5n/2`) is now
`three_poset_le_minUniversalSize`, obtained by playing the `n`-chain, the
`n`-antichain and the disjoint union of two chains against each other.  What
remains open is the following pair of statements.

**Statement.**  (a) `U(4) = 8`; equivalently, no seven-point poset contains all
four-element posets (all 219 labelled partial orders on four points).  (b) The overlap method is *exhausted* at order `n log n`: for every
family `P₁, …, P_k` of `n`-element posets, `kn - Σ_{i<j} s_{ij} = O(n log n)`,
where `s_{ij}` is the size of the largest common induced subposet of `Pᵢ` and
`Pⱼ`.  Hence every improvement of the lower bound beyond `n log n` must come
from counting, not from overlaps.

**Status.**  The matching *lower* half of (b) is now proved: some family attains
order `n log n` (`log_mul_le_six_mul_minUniversalSize`).  What is open is the
upper half — that no family does better — and part (a).

**The key insight is** that by Dilworth/Erdős–Szekeres any two `n`-element
posets have a common induced subposet on `Ω(log n)` points (a chain or an
antichain of that size occurs in both), so the pairwise overlaps grow at least
logarithmically while the family contributes only `n` per poset — the
optimisation therefore saturates at `k ≈ n / log n`.

**Why now?**  `CommonInducedBound`, `card_inter_images_le` and the three-poset
instance are formalised, so (b) is a statement purely about the extremal
quantity `s_{ij}`, and (a) has its upper half `U(4) ≤ 8` already kernel-verified
in `FourPoints.lean`; only the nonexistence half is open.
title: C2.  `U(4) = 8`, and the exact strength of the overlap method

description:
`sturm_zero_count_floor` is sharp for `k ≡ ε/m`.  Conjecture: it is *only* sharp there —
if a solution of `y'' = -k y` with `k ≥ ε/m` on `[0, T]`, `T = n·π√(m/ε)`, has exactly `n`
zeros in `(0, T]`, then `k ≡ ε/m` on `[0, T]` and `y` is the sine model up to scale and
sign; moreover a `δ`-approximate version holds, with `∫(k - ε/m)` controlled by the
excess of `T` over the last zero.

**The key insight is** that the Wronskian comparison of `nonpos_of_length_pi` degenerates
to an equality exactly when `y'' + (ε/m) y ≡ 0` on the block, so rigidity propagates block
by block, and the stability layer of `AlmostRigidity.lean` supplies the `δ`-version of
"a non-negative quantity has zero integral".

**Why now?** The two ingredients — the sharp block statement and the quantitative
equality principle — are both formalized in this cycle; what is missing is only the
bookkeeping that concatenates the blocks through a focal point.

**Falsifiable by:** a non-constant `k ≥ ε/m` whose solution still has exactly
`⌊T/(π√(m/ε))⌋` zeros on an interval where the floor is attained.

---
title: Conjecture C′ (Equality case of the oscillation count)

description:
**Status of the base case.** The *qualitative* nonabelian statement was proved in
this cycle: `Nonabelian.nonabelian_discrete_poincare` shows that for any group
`G`, a transition cochain on a connected nerve comes from a global relabelling
iff its monodromy around every closed walk is trivial, and
`perm_monodromy_obstructs_global_labelling` (with the realised example
`exTransition_no_global_labelling`) gives the `k`-class instance.

**Statement (open).** For a `k`-class classifier with continuous score vector
`s : E → ℝ^k` and a cover with overlap scale `δ`, the following are equivalent:
(i) every region admits a local `L∞` certificate of radius `δ` for its argmax
class; (ii) the permutation monodromy of the label-transport cochain is trivial
on every loop of the nerve.  Moreover, when the monodromy is nontrivial, the
certified radius of some region is at most `δ`, witnessed by a point where two
class scores tie.

**The key insight is** that the binary equivalence proved here
(`local_certificates_glue_iff_global` together with
`holonomy_obstructs_uniform_certificate`) is the `k = 2` case of a statement in
which "sign change" is replaced by "argmax change", and the intermediate value
theorem is replaced by a tie-point argument on the difference of two coordinates.

**Why now?** Both halves already exist separately: the nonabelian gluing theorem
is proved, and the analytic tie-point argument is a two-coordinate instance of
`exists_boundary_point_near`.

**Falsifier.** A `3`-class cover with trivial monodromy but no global certificate
at radius `δ` — e.g. produced by an argmax that changes without any pairwise tie
inside a region — would refute the equivalence.
title: C4. Metric multi-class monodromy (the nonabelian certificate theorem)

description:
**Conjecture.** For every braid word `w ∈ B₃` whose exponent sum is `e ≠ 0`, the
order of the reduced Burau image `r_a(w)` over `ℤ/N` equals
`c(w) · ord_N(a^{e/ gcd}) ` for a word-dependent constant `c(w) ≤ 6`; hence
*every* braid word (not just `σ₁σ₂`) is an order-finding instance, and no choice
of word escapes barrier 6/8.

*The key insight is* that `Burau.bm_cube` identifies the centre `Δ² = (σ₁σ₂)³`
with the scalar `a³`, so the order of any word is controlled modulo the centre —
the quotient `B₃/Z(B₃) ≅ PSL(2,ℤ)` is virtually free, and the scalar part is the
only place where `a` can hide.

*Why now?* `Burau.orderOf_bm` proves the case `w = σ₁σ₂` exactly
(`orderOf = lcm(3, ord a)`), and `Burau.lcm_dvd_card_burauSubgroup` shows the
group order inherits it; the general word case is the same computation done
along the Zassenhaus filtration.
title: C3. Braid words versus order-finding: an exact equivalence

description:
**Conjecture.** In `exists_small_multiple_dvd_den` the bound `4ℓ` can be improved to `2ℓ + 1`
without any group-theoretic input, and to the Hasse bound `⌊ℓ + 1 + 2√ℓ⌋` once the reduction
map is realised as a group homomorphism.

*The key insight is* that the factor `2` in the current bound comes solely from the `2`-torsion
branch of the collision lemma, where `n − m` is only known to satisfy `2(n − m) ∈ ker`; ruling
out that branch by a direct examination of `y ≡ −y (mod ℓ)` removes the factor entirely.

*Why now?* The collision lemma is already case-split exactly along that branch, so the argument
needs one extra case rather than a new framework, and the computed indices for `ℓ < 120` on
`E_55` never exceed `ℓ + 1 + 2√ℓ`, so the sharper bound is consistent with all data.
title: D1. The `4ℓ` bound can be replaced by `2ℓ + 1`, and then by `ℓ + 1 + 2√ℓ`

description:
Order density alone is insufficient. The rational line is densely ordered but disconnected. For a linear order with its order topology, connectedness requires a strong order-completeness condition in addition to density. Surreal numbers have a different obstruction: their non-Archimedean hierarchy creates clopen additive cuts.

Given `x < y`, the proof constructs a positive surreal `ε` such that

`n ε < y - x`

for every natural number `n`. The set

`{z | ∃ n : ℕ, z < x + n ε}`

is both open and closed, contains `x`, and excludes `y`. This separates every pair of distinct points.
title: Why density and “no gaps” do not prove connectedness

description:
**Conjecture.** Every effective machine model admitting universal simulation and diagonal coding has a relativized jump operator whose iterates escape all corresponding finite oracle levels.

The key insight is that hypercomputation changes the base degree but does not remove diagonal self-reference; it relocates the next undecidable problem one level upward.

**Why now?** The abstract jump-transport theorem separates the universal persistence argument from the model-specific construction, leaving a precise existence problem for each stronger model.
title: Concrete relativized jump towers for stronger computation

description:
**Conjecture.** Every sound reflective theory able to represent substitution and a guarded negative fixed point contains a closed proposition that is true and unprovable, without postulating an external diagonal operator.

The key insight is that the diagonal sentence should be synthesized from the fixed-point constructor itself once substitution is representable. **Why now?** The external diagonal theorem establishes the logical endpoint, while the modal fixed-point grammar identifies the missing internal construction precisely.
title: Diagonal incompleteness from internal fixed points

description:
**Conjecture.** For a recursively axiomatized, sound base theory equipped with the appropriate oracle predicates, level `n + 1` proves a canonical consistency sentence for level `n`, while level `n` proves neither that sentence nor its negation under standard incompleteness hypotheses.

The key insight is to encode proof search as a halting question relative to the current oracle and then separate external soundness assumptions from internally expressible consistency.

**Why now?** Strict computational growth and non-idempotence already identify the required diagonal pattern; what remains is to transport it through a faithful Gödel coding of syntax.
title: Relative consistency is visible one level above but not at its own level

description:
**Conjecture.** For each fixed leaf number `a`, the number of restrictions to an `a`-leaf set arising from unrooted binary phylogenetic trees is exponentially smaller, in the exponent, than the crude count of arbitrary families of subsets of those leaves. Moreover, this saving can be expressed through a canonical encoding by compatible quartet signatures.

The key insight is that edge splits of a tree are pairwise compatible, whereas the powerset bound treats them as independent bits. A canonical compatible encoding should expose the information discarded by that crude estimate.

**Why now?** The restriction algebra and its universal powerset bound isolate compatibility as the only missing ingredient in the counting layer. This gives a precise benchmark against which a sharper state count can be measured.
title: Compatibility-sensitive state compression

description:
**Conjecture.** There is an explicit recurrence based on four rounds of compatible-signature refinement whose terminal value bounds the leaf number sufficient to force an `n`-leaf common agreement subtree among `k` unrooted binary phylogenetic trees.

The key insight is that each refinement round should remove one layer of dependence—leaf placement, split compatibility, tree identity, and family identity—so that four nested exponential losses suffice.

**Why now?** The abstract quartet-transfer theorem already shows that any such MAST bound immediately bounds the common-quartet threshold. What remains is a quantitative compatible-tree argument, not additional threshold logic.
title: Fourfold exponential bound from iterative signature refinement

description:
**Conjecture.** The Generalized Continuum Hypothesis is equivalent to the
statement that, for every infinite set `X`, each subset of the power set
`𝒫(X)` is either of size at most `#X` or of full size `2^{#X}` — a single
dichotomy scheme uniform over all `X`.

The key insight is that Cantor's "countable or continuum" dichotomy for subsets
of the reals is the `X = ℕ` instance of a scheme whose universal quantification
over `X` is exactly GCH, mirroring how the pointwise `CH ↔ ℵ₁ = ℶ₁` lifts to the
hierarchy-wide `GCH ↔ ∀ o, ℵ_o = ℶ_o`.

Why now? The `X = ℕ` case is proved this cycle as an equivalence with CH, and
the hierarchy-coincidence theorem already supplies the transfinite induction
machinery needed to iterate the argument up the power-set tower.
title: The reals-dichotomy generalizes to a beth-dichotomy at every power set

description:
The two-state switch is nonempty, finite, fully sound, and refutes
"consistent ⟹ realizable" with the finite constraint set `{on, off}`.

**Conjecture (no finite completeness).**  Every finitely presented operational
semantics (finite world type, decidable satisfaction) whose language contains at
least two mutually exclusive observation constraints is incomplete for the
assumption-plus-ex-falso proof system: some finite consistent constraint set has no
realization.

*Falsified by* a finite, decidable semantics with mutually exclusive observables in
which every consistent finite constraint set is realizable.
title: Realizability gap for finitely presented operational semantics

description:
**Conjecture.**  For every `0 ≤ ε < η` and every perturbed trajectory
(`|uₙ₊₁ − tropicalFlow m η uₙ| ≤ ε`), the limit superior of `|uₙ − m|` is at most `ε`,
and `ε` is attained: `sup over trajectories of limsup |uₙ − m| = ε`.  Moreover the
*loss* excess satisfies `limsup (L(uₙ) − L(m)) = n_samples · ε` for a sample whose
median has full one-sided multiplicity.

*The key insight is* that the clipped update is an exact contraction to the minimizer
in one step from distance `≤ η`, so the perturbation cannot accumulate: the only
surviving error is the last one, which is why `perturbed_distance_bound` needs `max ε`
and not `max 0`, and why `perturbed_ball_bound_sharp` saturates the bound.

*Why now?*  The finite-`n` bound and its sharpness are proved; the remaining step is to
turn them into an exact asymptotic radius and to transfer it through the proved
`l1Loss_lipschitz` bound to the loss.

---
title: Perturbed descent has a sharp asymptotic radius equal to `ε`

description:
**Conjecture.** For a finite-time sorting protocol executing `d` binary comparisons with
per-comparison relaxation time `τ`, the dissipation identity
`⟨W⟩ − F = kT · D(p ‖ p^R)` (proved, `dissipated_work_eq_relEntropy`) is bounded below by
`kT · Var(W) / (2 (kT)² + C d τ⁻¹)`, so that the *product* of the excess work and the total
protocol time `dτ` is bounded below by an absolute multiple of `Var(W)`.

The key insight is that our proof extracts the excess from the strict `log x ≤ x − 1` defect
at each trajectory; second-order expansion of that defect converts the divergence into a
variance, which is the quantity a finite-time protocol cannot suppress. **Why now?** The
exact divergence identity removes all ambiguity about the equilibrium term, so any
speed-versus-dissipation trade-off must live entirely in the second-order remainder, which is
already isolated in the proof.
title: A fluctuation–depth uncertainty relation

description:
**Conjecture.**  If two hints `h₁, h₂` have invariance groups `Γ₁, Γ₂` then the
joint hint `(h₁,h₂)` has invariance group `Γ₁ ∩ Γ₂` and usable bits
`log₂(|S|/|Γ₁ ∩ Γ₂|)`; in particular two `t`-bit hints with the same invariance
group are worth `t` bits together, not `2t`.  Cycle I proves only the upper
bound `t₁ + t₂` (`worstCost_pair_ge`).

*The key insight is* that hint composition is intersection of symmetry groups,
so redundancy between hints is measurable *a priori* — a designer can tell
whether a second leak is free before measuring anything.

*Why now?*  It is the direct group-theoretic dual of `worstCost_pair_ge` and
needs only the orbit machinery of C1.
title: C4. Composite hints: is the bit budget exactly additive on symmetric sets?

description:
**Conjecture.** For every seed and every width, the smallest `k` at which the
flip becomes a no-op equals the smallest `k` at which single ablations become
no-ops, **plus one**.

*The key insight is* that a flip removes twice the coordinate that an ablation
removes, so under any saturating gate the two thresholds are `(k−1)g ≥ T` and
`(k−2)g ≥ T` — mathematically forced to be adjacent
(`self_sufficient_iff_gain`, `sign_robust_iff_gain`), which turns the observed
k = 2 sign-sensitivity / k = 3 sign-robustness pair into a general prediction
rather than a coincidence of one seed.

*Why now?* The prediction is decided by the already-proposed seed-trait test
(NET-29's dependent k = 1 seeds s = 14/15 at E = 23): if the "+1" law holds,
those seeds must show flip-sensitivity at exactly one width above their
ablation-sensitivity width.
title: C3 — Sign-robustness has its own width, one above self-sufficiency

description:
**Statement.** Let `f : ℕ → ℕ` satisfy `f 0 = 1` and have minimal period modulo every
`m > 0` equal to `pisanoAnti m = if Odd m then m else 2m`.  Then `f = antiFib`
whenever `f` is a polynomial sequence of degree `≤ 2`.

**The key insight is** that the proved characterisation `isPeriodMod_iff`
("`p` is a period iff `m ∣ p` and `f p ≡ f 0`") uses only the *first difference being
linear*; conversely, a period function equal to `m`/`2m` forces the second difference to
be constant and equal to `1`, pinning the sequence.

**Why now?** The characterisation of periods is already formalised, and the converse is a
finite linear-algebra argument over `ZMod m` — no new analytic input is needed.

**Falsifiable:** exhibit a non-quadratic `f` with the same period function.

---
title: C2. The anti-Fibonacci "Pisano-type" period determines the sequence

description:
**Statement.** If a ReLU network `ℝ¹¹ → ℝ^{m₁} → ℝ^{m₂} → ⋯ → ℝ^{m_L}` is injective, then
`mₖ ≥ 22` for **every** `k`, not just `k = 1`.

**The key insight is** that the image of the first `k−1` layers contains, inside each
activation region, a full 11-dimensional affine patch, and the local-rank lemma
`card_activeRows_ge` applies verbatim on that patch; what is missing is a *global* probe
argument replacing the antipodal directions `±su`, since the patch is only a cone.

**Why now?** This cycle proved the `k = 1` case unconditionally
(`no_injective_network_of_narrow_first_layer`) and isolated the exact obstruction
(`exists_antipodal_probes` needs a full linear space, not a cone). Either a cone version of
the duality count or an explicit two-layer counterexample with `m₂ = 12` settles it.

**Falsifier.** An injective two-layer ReLU network `ℝ¹¹ → ℝ²² → ℝ^{m₂}` with `m₂ < 22`.

---
title: Conjecture C — depth cannot beat `2n` at *any* layer

description:
* **Fourier interpolation**: for *arbitrary* equal-size `A, B ⊆ Z/pZ` and any prescribed data `g`,
  there is a **unique** signal vanishing off `A` whose transform matches `g` on `B`. This is
  deterministic compressed sensing with no genericity hypothesis on the sampling pattern.
* **Restricted surjectivity and injectivity**: the two inequality regimes of the same statement.
* **Rank of an arbitrary minor**: total nonsingularity in rank form — every rectangular `A × B`
  minor has rank exactly `min |A| |B|`.
* **Zero counting** — the "fundamental theorem of algebra for the DFT": a nonzero `f` has `f̂`
  vanishing at strictly fewer than `|supp f|` frequencies.
title: Cycle 3 — the linear-algebraic face of Chebotarev

description:
**Conjecture.** Among all operators `r : Set (Literal Atom) → Literal Atom →
Set (Literal Atom)` satisfying "success" (`l ∈ r B l`) and "consistency preservation",
`revise` is the unique one satisfying the frame law of `reviseSeq_frame`
(`p.1 ≠ l.1 → (p ∈ r B l ↔ p ∈ B)`); equivalently, the frame law plus success characterizes
`revise` outright, with consistency preservation a consequence rather than an assumption.

*Falsifiable content.* A second operator with success and the frame law that differs from
`revise` on some state — necessarily differing only in whether `opposite l` is retracted.
title: Failure of the frame property for non-local revision operators

description:
**Conjecture.** For a fixed finite complex and a fixed *integral* increment field
`ω`, the class of coefficient groups over which the induced field becomes developable
is exactly the class killing one finitely generated obstruction group
`O(X, ω) ≤ H¹(X; ℤ) ⊕ (torsion from twisting)`.  Concretely the Penrose triangle
`ω ≡ 1` is developable over `A` iff `3 ∈ A` is `0`, and the Möbius unit field iff
`1 ∈ 2A`.  (The two extreme cases are proved; the general statement is open.)
title: Coefficient dependence of impossibility

description:
For `p` odd let `D₄` act on `ZMod p × ZMod p` by the four rotations of
`QuarterTurns` together with the four reflections `(t,n) ↦ (n,t)`,
`(t,n) ↦ (-n,-t)`, `(t,n) ↦ (-t,n)`, `(t,n) ↦ (t,-n)`.  Each reflection should
fix exactly `p` cells, so Burnside predicts `(p + 1)(p + 3) / 8` orbits and

    capacity = 2 ^ ((p + 1) * (p + 3) / 8).

*Refutation:* an odd `p` (say `p = 7`, predicted `2 ^ 10`) where the count
differs.  Note the prediction agrees with the proved rotation-only value at
`p = 3` (both give `8`) but is strictly smaller from `p = 5` on, so the two
statements are independent.
title: N2. Capacity under the full dihedral group of a square torus

description:
The proof of `ratConic_pos_empty_of_isSquare_disc` yields more than emptiness.  In the primitive
square-discriminant case, with `a = f² - e²`, `b = e f`, `gcd(e,f) = 1`, the *inhomogeneous* line
`b m² - a m n - b n² = c` with `0 < |c| ≤ b` has all of its solutions with `m, n > 0` bounded by

  `f m + e n ≤ |c| ≤ e f`,  hence  `m ≤ e` and `n ≤ f`,  hence  `max(m,n) ≤ b`,

and the only unbounded case is `c = 0`, which is the pair of asymptotes `e m = f n`.  So a
square-discriminant conic degenerates in a completely controlled way: `c = b` is empty, every other
small `c` gives a set of size `O(d(|c|))` inside the box `[1,e] × [1,f]`.

**The key insight is** that the factorization `(e m - f n)(f m + e n) = c` bounds the *second*
factor by `|c|` as soon as the first is nonzero, and the second factor already dominates both
`f m` and `e n`.

**Why now?**  The factorization and the parametrization are formalized inside
`ratConic_primitive_empty` and `factored_conic_no_pos_solution`; only the bookkeeping of a general
right-hand side `c` remains, together with the `c = 0` degeneration.
title: Sub-conjecture C (Sharp bound in the square-discriminant case)

description:
**Statement.**  For every amplitude tensor `a` and every `ε > 0`,
`max_{|t| ≤ ε} ‖hyperdet (pert a t)‖ ≥ ε⁴`, with equality for some `ε` if and only if
`pertPoly a = X⁴`, i.e. iff the four exceptional parameters all coincide at `0` — which happens
exactly on a codimension-`4` subvariety containing the zero tensor.

**The key insight is** that the discrete five-node estimate proved here is a lossy substitute for
the maximum-modulus principle: the leading coefficient of a monic quartic is the mean of
`p(εω) ω̄⁴` over the circle, so `max_{|t| = ε} |p| ≥ ε⁴` exactly, and the equality case is the
equality case of the mean-value inequality.

**Why now?**  The rate is proved, only the constant is off by the explicit factor `32/3`
(measured in `ComputationalEvidence.md` §10.2); closing it needs the circle version of the same
computation plus the standard `Complex.circleIntegral` API, and the equality analysis then feeds
directly into the stratification picture of Cycle 3.
title: C1. The optimal genericity constant is `1`, attained only at the degenerate stratum

description:
**Conjecture.** The unique positive root `t*` of `|log(1 + t i)| = 1` satisfies
`t* ∈ [1.229, 1.2291]`, and `t*` is transcendental.

*The key insight is* that `t*` is the unique positive solution of the
transcendental equation
`(log(1 + t²))² / 4 + arctan(t)² = 1`,
which couples the real and imaginary parts of a single complex logarithm. The
interval refinement is within reach of the present method — the same reduction
identities with higher-precision certified enclosures of `log 2` and `π` — while
transcendence would presumably require a Schanuel-type input; even irrationality
appears open.
title: C2. Sharp two-sided algebraic bounds for the scalar root

description:
`concatGame_not_comm` shows lives do not commute. Conjecture: they commute exactly on the
*additively principal* scale, i.e.

```lean
theorem concat_comm_iff (G H : SurvivalGame) :
    (concatGame G H).value = (concatGame H G).value ↔
      ∃ a : Ordinal, ∃ m n : ℕ, G.value = ω ^ a * m ∧ H.value = ω ^ a * n
```

**The key insight is** that `α + β = β + α` for ordinals holds precisely when `α` and `β` are
natural multiples of a common additively principal ordinal, so the survival-theoretic question
"does the order of two lives matter?" has a complete Cantor-normal-form answer.

**Why now?** `concatGame_value` reduces the question to ordinal arithmetic, and Mathlib's
`Principal (· + ·)` API (already used here for `ω²`) supplies exactly the needed absorption
lemmas.

---
title: Conjecture D — Concatenation asymmetry is the only obstruction to a commutative theory

description:
`value_eq_iff_orderIso` shows the survival value is a complete invariant of the clock. The
strategic refinement conjecture: two games have the same value iff Mortal's forcing powers agree
*uniformly under refinement*, i.e.

```lean
theorem value_eq_iff_forall_forces (G H : SurvivalGame) :
    G.value = H.value ↔ ∀ K : SurvivalGame, ∀ β : Ordinal,
      (extBy G K).MortalForces β ↔ (extBy H K).MortalForces β
```

**The key insight is** that `extBy_value` turns refinement into left multiplication, so the claim
becomes: ordinals are separated by left multiplication together with `≤`. This is false for a
single test multiplier (`2 · ω = 1 · ω`), so the quantifier over all `K` is essential — the
conjecture is a statement about which distinctions survive a non-cancellative operation.

**Why now?** The negative example `not_forall_lt_extBy_value` isolates precisely the failure of
cancellation, so this conjecture is the sharp repair of the naive claim, and every ingredient is
already formalized.
title: Conjecture E — Value is a complete invariant for *strategy* equivalence, not just clocks

description:
`capSysN n` and the block theories satisfy Löb's axiom for *all* formulas, yet fail
reflection above their depth.  Löb's rule (`⊢ □a → a` implies `⊢ a`) is the reflection
rule in disguise.

**Conjecture.**  For every consistent GL theory `S` and every `d`, the depth-`d`
reflection rule is *equivalent* to the depth-`d` Löb rule ("`⊢ □_i a → a` implies `⊢ a`
for every `a` of box depth `< d`"), and both are equivalent to the statement that `S`
has no "phantom top world" below depth `d`: for every `a` of box depth `< d`, if `a`
holds at all worlds of the canonical model of `S` that are seen from somewhere, then it
holds everywhere.

**The key insight is** that the failure of reflection in a finite-height model is caused
by exactly one world — the top one — being invisible from inside the model, and that the
box depth is precisely the resource a formula needs in order to notice it; the block
family shows that this "distance to invisibility" can be tuned freely.

**Why now?**  `depthReflection_fails_of_inconsistency_height` shows the failure is always
witnessed by an iterated boxed falsum, which is the Löb witness; and the block family
provides, for every value of the parameter, a model where the equivalence can be tested.

*Falsified by* a consistent GL theory obeying the depth-`d` Löb rule but not the
depth-`d` reflection rule (or conversely).

---
title: A depth-graded Löb principle

description:
**Conjecture.** For every `r ≥ 4` the density of pairs `(N, a)` with
`ord_N(a) = r` for which the fundamental bin is *not* the largest non-DC bin of
the value signal is bounded away from `0` as `N → ∞`; in fact the fundamental's
rank grows like `Θ(r)`.

**The key insight is** that the residues `aˣ mod N` behave like an equidistributed
sequence with respect to the additive characters of `ℤ/r`, so the value signal's
spectrum is asymptotically flat and the fundamental has no structural advantage —
it is the *comb*, not the exponential, that produces sharpness.

**Why now?** The order-4 slice is already exactly solvable
(`|V̂(1)|² = (v₀-v₂)²+(v₁-v₃)²` versus `|V̂(2)|² = (v₀-v₁+v₂-v₃)²`, formalised for
`N = 15, a = 7` in `SpectralHiding.lean`), and the measured density there is
`0.366` over `N < 500` (see `ComputationalEvidence.md`). The general statement
needs only Weyl-sum bounds for exponential sequences modulo `N`.

---
title: C2. Peak-picking failure is generic, not exceptional

description:
*For every base `b` and every digit length `n ≥ 2`, the kernel of the digit
functional `w ↦ Σ w_{ij} b^{i+j}` on `n × n` integer matrices contains
`(n-1)²`-many independent vectors of squared norm `2`, and consequently every
rank-one target has a non-rank-one companion solution at squared distance `≤ 8`.*

**The key insight is** that the `2 × 2` commutator `[[0,1],[-1,0]]` generalises to
all "anti-diagonal transpositions" `E_{i,j+1} - E_{i+1,j}`, whose count grows
quadratically while their norm stays constant — the target's norm grows, the
noise does not.
**Why now?** The `2 × 2` case is fully proved in `Round7DigitLattice`
(`exists_spurious_solution`); the general case is the same identity indexed by a
larger family, and it would turn the "target sits at the Gaussian heuristic"
measurement into a theorem for all dimensions.
title: Conjecture D (lattice non-isolation in all dimensions)

description:
**Conjecture.** For `ℓ ≥ 5` with `ℓ ∤ N` and `P` of infinite order, the apparition index `m`
of `MordellDenominators.apparition_index_pos_le` equals the order of the reduction of `P` in
`E(F_ℓ)`; in particular `m ≤ ℓ + 1 + 2√ℓ`, and `m ∣ #E(F_ℓ)`.

*The key insight is* that the collision lemma proved in cycle 6 is exactly injectivity of the
reduction map on the quotient by the kernel, so upgrading `4ℓ` to the Hasse bound only requires
identifying the pigeonhole target with the group `E(F_ℓ)` rather than with the set of its
points — i.e. building the reduction group homomorphism, not new arithmetic.

*Why now?* The chord-arithmetic core (`dvd_den_chord_abstract`) already handles every case the
homomorphism would need, including the `2`-torsion branch; the missing step is bookkeeping,
and the computational table in `ComputationalEvidence.md` confirms `m = ord(P mod ℓ)` for all
`ℓ < 120` on `E_55`.
title: C1. The apparition index equals the order of the reduction (Hasse-sharp bound)

description: The development uses binary code length under an injective encoding, which captures the counting core of incompressibility but is computable rather than genuine prefix-free Kolmogorov complexity. A stronger continuation should define a prefix-free universal machine, partial evaluation, shortest-program complexity, and the invariance theorem up to an additive constant.
title: Formal-machine Kolmogorov complexity

description: Replace classical `Prop` predicates in the semantic diagonal theorem by computable Boolean predicates. The naive diagonal is then computable only relative to a sufficiently strong evaluator, leading naturally to Turing jumps and oracle-relative discovery.
title: Replace classical `Prop` predicates in the semantic diagonal theorem by computable Boolean predicates.

description:
In the calculus of `MindToolsCalculus.lean`, let `d(a)` be the least
`Deriv.size` of a derivation of `a → a`. The `S`–`K`–`K` derivation gives the
upper bound `d(a) ≤ 16·size(a) + 15` (proved: `Deriv.identity_size`; e.g.
`d(atom 3) ≤ 79` against a conclusion of size `9`). Conjecture: this is exact,
`d(a) = 16·size(a) + 15`, so the standard derivation is size-optimal, and hence
the optimal proof-size overhead of the trivial theorem `a → a` is linear in the
statement with slope exactly `16`. *Falsifiable* by exhibiting one formula `a`
with a shorter derivation of `a → a`.
title: Conjecture B (minimal derivation size in the Hilbert calculus)

description:
For every family of theories `tools : ι → FormalSystem S` that is ordinal-ranked
in the sense of `OrdinalRanks`, the induced strength order embeds into a
well-founded forest whose width can be arbitrary; more precisely, every
well-founded partial order arises (up to isomorphism) as the strength order of
some family of extensional theories with an ordinal rank. Cycle 2 proves the
antichain case (`exists_ordinalRanked_antichain`, of every size). *Falsifiable*
by a well-founded partial order that is provably not realizable as
`(Stronger, tools)` for any ordinal-ranked family.
title: Conjecture D (no ordinal rank separates apprehension from strength)

description:
Let `g` be a diagonal operator and `T` a finite base theory, and let
`iterLimit g T = ⋃ n, iter g T n` be the limit of the reflection hierarchy of
`MindToolsReflection.lean`.  Conjecture: for every diagonal `g` the limit is
never reached by any finite stage and moreover the *transfinite* continuation
`iter g` past the limit is again strictly ascending — i.e. for every ordinal
`α` there is a theory in the hierarchy of rank exactly `α`, so the ordinal
ranks of `OrdinalRanks` are attained rather than merely bounding.  Proved so
far: strictness of every finite step and of the limit
(`stronger_iterTool_of_lt`, `stronger_iterLimit`).  *Falsifiable* by a diagonal
operator whose transfinite iteration stabilises at some countable stage, which
would show that ordinal ranks over-measure the hierarchy.
title: Conjecture E (reflection hierarchies are never finitely based cofinally)

description:
**Conjecture.** For the true zeta ordinates, the limit `lim_{T→∞} Σ_{0<γ≤T} 1/(1/4+γ²)` proved to
exist in `Convergence.lean` (under the ordinate bound calibrated numerically to `a ≈ 9.79`)
equals `1 + γ_E/2 − log(2√π)`, and the truncation error satisfies the two-sided bound
`c₁ log T / T ≤ Σ_{γ > T} 1/(1/4+γ²) ≤ c₂ log T / T` with `c₁, c₂ → 1/2π`.

*The key insight is* that the conjugate-paired series is a **positive** series, so Abel summation
against the counting function `N(T)` converts the Riemann–von Mangoldt asymptotic directly into a
two-sided tail estimate, with no cancellation to control.

*Why now?* `tail_bound_of_separated` already gives a one-sided `1/(a²N)` bound from a telescoping
argument, and the numerics in `ComputationalEvidence.md` show the true decay is `log T/T`; the
only missing ingredient is a formalised Abel-summation lemma against a counting function.
title: The renormalisation constant is the Riemann–von Mangoldt main term

description:
**Conjecture.** Let `P ∈ ℚ[X]` with `P(0) ≠ 0` and let `S` be a sub-multiset of the complex roots
of `P`.  Then `Σ_{r ∈ S} 1/r ∈ ℚ` **iff** `S` is a `ℚ`-rational divisor, i.e. a nonnegative
integer combination of full Galois orbits, *except* for the sporadic coincidences produced by
vanishing partial power sums.  Degree 2 is proved (`quadratic_singleton_chord_rat_iff`); degree 3
with Galois group `S₃` is the first open case, and `A₄`/`S₄` quartics the first case where the
exceptional coincidences can be enumerated.

*The key insight is* that `Σ_{r ∈ S} 1/r` is the value at `0` of the logarithmic derivative of the
sub-product `∏_{r∈S}(X−r)`, so rationality of the chord is a statement about the field of
definition of a *factor* of `P`, not about individual roots.

*Why now?* `harmonicSum_eq_neg_deriv_div` makes the chord a coefficient ratio of the sub-product,
which converts the question into one about factorisations over number fields — exactly the setting
where Lean's `Polynomial`/`IsSplittingField` API is usable.
title: Rationality of a sub-multiset chord is a Galois-orbit condition

description:
**Statement.** For every `t` with `2 ≤ t < 10^6` and `t ≠ 3003`, `Singmaster.mult t ≠ 8`.

**Status.** Proved, in the stronger form
`Singmaster.mult_le_six_of_lt_million`: every such `t` occurs *at most six* times, so
`Singmaster.mult_eq_eight_iff_of_lt_million` gives `N(t) = 8 ↔ t = 3003` on `[2,10^6)`
and `Singmaster.mult_le_eight_of_lt_million` gives the Singmaster bound with the
conjectured optimal constant `8` on that range.  A by-product is
`Singmaster.mult_24310 = 6`, the one value of `A003015` below `10^6` that the earlier box
search could not reach.

**The key insight was** to stop quantifying over `t`.  The refined reflection
decomposition `N(t) = 2 + 2·#(left interior occurrences) + #(central occurrences)`
(`Singmaster.mult_eq_two_add_two_mul_leftInt`) plus column uniqueness means that a
multiplicity above six needs *two* left interior occurrences with column `≥ 3` and the
same value — a coincidence between two positions, not a property of a number.  There are
only `320` positions with column `≥ 3` and value below `10^6`, and comparing all `320²`
pairs in the kernel (`Singmaster.bigCols_pair_search`) shows the only coincidence is
`C(15,5) = C(14,6) = 3003`.

**Next step.** The same pair search at `10^9` or `10^{12}` is a purely quantitative
extension (the number of positions with column `≥ 3` grows like `B^{1/3}`), and the
column-`2` bookkeeping is already uniform in `B`.
title: 6b. `3003` is the unique number of multiplicity eight below `10^6` — resolved*

description:
`ImmortalityStructure.refinementStable_opow_iff` settles stability inside the scale `ω ^ a`.
The general statement should be:

```lean
theorem refinementStable_iff_cnf (o : Ordinal) :
    RefinementStable o ↔ o = 0 ∨ ∀ e ∈ (CNF ω o).map Prod.fst, ω ≤ e
```

i.e. `ω · o = o` exactly when every Cantor exponent of `o` is infinite.

**The key insight is** that `ω · o = o` is a *purely local* condition on the leading behaviour of
`o`: multiplication by `ω` shifts each Cantor exponent `e` to `1 + e`, and `1 + e = e` is
equivalent to `ω ≤ e`, so stability is a tail condition, not a size condition.

**Why now?** Mathlib carries `Ordinal.CNF` with its induction principles, and the `ω ^ a` case is
already proved here, which fixes the exact form of the general criterion and its proof skeleton.

---
title: Conjecture B — Refinement stability is exactly Cantor-normal-form tail condition

description:
**Statement.** For `v₂(H p) = s < t = v₂(H q)`, the number of units with
`orderOf u ∣ lcm(H p, H q)` equals `2^{min(t−s,1)} · H p · H q / 1` — more
precisely `#{u : ord u ∣ L} = gcd(2 H p, L) · gcd(2 H q, L)`, and this exceeds
`φ(N)/4` by exactly the factor `2^{[s<t]}·2^{[t<s]}`.

**The key insight is** that the count is a product of two gcds because the CRT
projection is an isomorphism (proved) and, in a cyclic group of order `n`, the
number of solutions of `x^d = 1` is `gcd(d, n)`.

**Why now?** `card_both_squares` and `projPair_bijective` already reduce the
count to a two-factor cyclic computation; the missing ingredient is the standard
`gcd` root-count, which Mathlib is close to supplying.
title: C4 (Quadrant equidistribution off the dial). The unbalanced case has a computable defect.

description:
**Conjecture.** Every node satisfies `d_P(m,n) ≤ 2·log₂(m) + O(1)`; combined with the
proved lower bound `m ≤ 2^(d+1)` this makes Price depth `Θ(log m)`, and hence
`d_P = Θ(log N)` at the `N`-node, matching the observed `≈ 1.4·log₂(p+q)`.

*The key insight is* that the Price parent halves `m` when `m` is even and halves `n`
when `m` is odd, and the parity of `m` cannot stay odd twice in a row along a descent
once one tracks `(m mod 2, n mod 4)`: a two-step potential `Φ = log₂(m·n)` decreases by
at least `1` per two steps. *Why now?* `price_parent` is formalised with all four cases
explicit, so the potential argument is a direct induction; this would upgrade
`price_level_gt_fermat` from "level width beats Fermat" to a *complete* cost model of the
Price tree.
title: C2. Price depth is `Θ(log m)` — a matching upper bound

description:
**Conjecture.** For all `k ≥ 1`: `I_pair(2^k) = (4/3)(1 − 4^{−k})`; in particular the
capacity of a cyclic 2-group channel is bounded by `4/3` bits and converges to it.

*Status:* proved for `k ≤ 4` (`Ipair_two_pow_law`), numerically confirmed to `k = 6`.

**The key insight is** that for `n = 2^k` the type is the 2-adic valuation, and the
valuation of a sum is `min(v(x), v(y))` unless the valuations agree — so the conditional
law `Π_c` depends on `c` only through `v(c)`, giving a self-similar recursion between
level `k` and level `k − 1` whose fixed point is `4/3`.

**Why now?** The recursion is visible in the enumerated occupation tables (each level
reproduces the previous one with one extra state of half the mass), so the induction step
is a finite identity between two explicit dyadic entropies.
title: C2. The 2-adic growth law and its limit

description:
**Conjecture.** With `m` the apparition index of `ℓ ≥ 5` (good), for every `n` with `m ∣ n`,
`v_ℓ(den x(nP)) = v_ℓ(den x(mP)) + 2·v_ℓ(n/m)`, and `v_ℓ(den x(nP)) = 0` otherwise.

*The key insight is* that the formal group at `ℓ` makes `z = -x/y` a coordinate on which
multiplication by `k` acts as multiplication by `k` up to higher order, so the only growth of
the `ℓ`-part along the progression comes from the `ℓ`-part of the multiplier.

*Why now?* Cycle 3 already proved the invariance `v_ℓ(den x(2P)) = v_ℓ(den x(P))` for odd `ℓ`,
which is the case `ℓ ∤ k` of the law; the general case needs only the `ℓ ∣ k` step, and the
tables show the predicted jumps (`v₇ = 2` throughout the progression `2ℕ`, jumping at `n = 14`).
title: C2. Exact valuation law: `v_ℓ(den x(nP)) = 2·v_ℓ(e_m) + 2·v_ℓ(n/m)`

description:
**Statement.** With `C(N)` the proved counting function, the fractional discrepancy
`θ(N) = C(N) - √(2N) ∈ [0,3)` is equidistributed in `[0,1)` after the natural
normalisation `θ(N) mod 1`.

**The key insight is** that `C(N) = ⌊(√(8N-7)+1)/2⌋ + 1` exactly (proved), so `θ(N)` is a
deterministic function of the fractional part of `√(8N-7)/2`, and equidistribution of
`√n mod 1` is a classical Weyl-type result.

**Why now?** The exact closed form removes all combinatorial noise; what remains is a
pure equidistribution statement about `√n`, for which Mathlib now has Weyl-criterion
infrastructure.

**Falsifiable:** compute the empirical distribution of `θ(N)` for `N ≤ 10⁸`; a visible
bias refutes it.

---
title: C3. Exact second-order counting law: `C(N) = √(2N) + θ(N)` with `θ` equidistributed

description:
**Conjecture.** For each ordinal `o`, a type has cardinality below `ℵ_{o+1}`
exactly when it admits a surjection from, or an injection into, a set of size
`ℵ_o`; the whole aleph hierarchy is recoverable from a graded family of
"smallness" predicates on types, one per stage.

The key insight is that the characterization of `ℵ₁` by countability is not a
special feature of the countable case but a shadow of the successor operation:
"below the successor" always means "at most the predecessor," and the predecessor
relation can be exposed as a definable predicate on types at every level.

Why now? The stage-1 case is settled here in the sharp form "below `ℵ₁` iff
countable," and the successor arithmetic used in its proof is uniform across the
hierarchy, so the general graded predicate is within reach.
title: Countability predicates characterize every successor cardinal, not just the first

description:
**Conjecture.** For all coprime `m, n ≥ 1`: `I_pair(mn) = I_pair(m) + I_pair(n)`.

*Status:* proved here for `12 = 4·3`, `10 = 2·5`, `15 = 3·5`, `14 = 2·7`, `20 = 4·5`,
`18 = 2·9`; verified numerically for every coprime splitting with `mn ≤ 40`.

**The key insight is** that the type map factors through the CRT isomorphism
`ℤ/mn ≅ ℤ/m × ℤ/n` as `T = T_m · T_n` with `gcd(T_m, T_n) = 1`, so the *unordered*
type pair of a semiprime is recoverable from the two component unordered pairs together
with the matching data, and the matching ambiguity is exactly cancelled by the
conditioning on the norm class in each factor.

**Why now?** All the pieces are in place: the Euler-φ type law is proved in general
(`typeCount_eq_totient`), the entropy of a counting distribution has a closed counting
form (`Hlist_eq`), and the conjecture is an equality of two finite sums that only needs a
measure-preserving bijection — no analysis.
title: C1. The CRT-additivity theorem (general form)

description:
**Conjecture.** For a piecewise-linear surface equipped with a specified projection and depth-order relation, realizability of a Penrose-type cyclic beam configuration is equivalent to acyclicity of the induced depth-order cocycle after subdivision.

The key insight is that a Penrose triangle is not determined by the topology of its underlying loop; its impossibility comes from projection-dependent depth inequalities that accumulate around that loop. **Why now?** Gauge-invariant additive holonomy supplies a rigorous template, while the explicit projection and order data remove the ambiguity that blocks a smooth-manifold statement.
title: Piecewise-linear Penrose semantics

description: Prove `HadwigerCase 2`: every finite graph with no proper two-coloring has a `K₃` branch-set minor. A concrete route is to formalize the odd-cycle characterization of non-bipartite graphs and contract an odd cycle to three branch sets.
title: The triangle case

description: The product/union theorem in `Tropical.CornerLocusProduct` remains valid when the ordered additive group is weakened to a cancellative ordered additive commutative monoid, provided both finite term families attain minima everywhere.
title: Product corner locus without group inverses

description: Define the manifold `ℝ × ℝ³`, a smooth ship worldline, `rₛ`, and a smooth compactly supported (or rapidly decaying) shape function. Package `metricB` as a smooth Lorentzian metric tensor and derive its inverse and determinant.
title: Smooth spacetime model

description:
Both sides of the comparison are now closed-form Lean theorems
(`addEnergy_sidon`, `addEnergy_sidon2`), so the conjecture is exactly the statement that
the exponent-two computation is *extremal*, a finite convexity problem over the
distribution of `r`, not a new Fourier estimate.
title: Both sides of the comparison are now closed-form Lean theorems

description:
**Conjecture.** Let a family of positive linear aggregators be conjugated by logarithmic dequantization and converge locally uniformly to a tropical aggregator. If the classical dependence systems are eventually ultrafilters, then the limiting tropical support is a singleton; conversely, every tropical projection arises from such a stable family.

The key insight is that logarithmic sum-exp converges to tropical maximum, but ultrafilter-valued dependence should prevent two coefficients from surviving at the same exponential scale.

**Why now?** This supplies a precise, testable meaning for a “classical limit,” which cannot be asserted until the deformation, topology of convergence, and dependence semantics are fixed.
title: Dequantization stability of decisive coalitions

description:
**Conjecture.** The function sending each ordinal `o` to the least ordinal `f(o)`
with `ℶ_o ≤ ℵ_{f(o)}` is a normal, strictly increasing function that is the
identity precisely under GCH, and its deviation from the identity is a faithful
measure of how far cardinal exponentiation departs from succession.

The key insight is that `ℶ_o ≥ ℵ_o` always holds while equality is exactly GCH,
so the "index shift" required to dominate the beth tower by the aleph tower
quantifies the failure of GCH stage by stage rather than as a single global
assertion.

Why now? Both bounding facts — `ℵ_o ≤ ℶ_o` in general and equality under GCH —
are in hand, so the shift function `f` is well-defined and its normality can be
attacked with the same limit-stage supremum arguments used here.
title: The gap between the aleph and beth hierarchies is itself an ordinal-indexed invariant

description:
**Conjecture.** The continuum can equal `ℵ_o` or `ℶ_o` only when `o` is a
successor ordinal or `0`; it can never coincide with a limit stage of either
hierarchy, because the continuum has uncountable cofinality while every limit
stage inherits the cofinality of its index.

The key insight is that placing the continuum in the hierarchy is constrained not
only by size (the CH inequality) but by cofinality: `ℶ₁ = 𝔠` sits at a successor
stage, and König's theorem forbids `𝔠` from being a countable-cofinality limit
such as `ℵ_ω`.

Why now? The identity `ℶ₁ = 𝔠` is established here, and the cofinality tools that
already rule out `𝔠 = ℵ_ω` in the surrounding development extend verbatim to the
beth hierarchy through its limit-stage supremum description.
title: Cofinality obstructs the continuum from landing on limit stages of either tower

description:
**Conjecture.** Every element of the Selberg class is uniquely determined by a finite arithmetic packet drawn from a countable alphabet, provided the packet is allowed to encode an effective global rule for all unrecorded Euler factors rather than merely their omission.

The key insight is that countability follows immediately from faithful countable coding, while finite samples alone fail even for bounded convergent Dirichlet series.

**Why now?** The precise obstruction has been isolated: the missing theorem is not analytic uniqueness from the full coefficient sequence, but a rigidity principle recovering that sequence from finite arithmetic instructions.
title: Faithful arithmetic coding of the Selberg class

description:
**Conjecture.** The identity and ordering of the ten most reused named theorems vary substantially across algebra, analysis, topology, and combinatorics, even after normalizing for domain size and theorem age.

The key insight is that global prominence may be an aggregation artifact produced by mixing dependency networks with different vocabularies and foundational conventions. **Why now?** The failure of acyclicity to enforce hubs makes stratified, falsifiable ranking comparisons necessary.
title: No universal historical hub list

description:
**Conjecture.** For every finite electorate, a normalized tropical aggregator has an ultrafilter of dependence sets if and only if its unique irredundant tropical support has cardinality one.

The key insight is that the dependence sets of a minimum of several coordinates form the principal filter generated by its support; this filter is an ultrafilter precisely when that support is a singleton.

**Why now?** The current results establish both endpoints—singleton support gives dictatorship, while two-coordinate support gives a non-dictatorial weak aggregator—so the conjecture asks for the structural equivalence interpolating between them.
title: Ultrafilter support as the exact Arrow threshold

description:
Capacity alone does not provide a decoder. Future work could define encoders and
decoders for one-hot, constant-weight, and error-correcting sparse codes, prove
round-trip correctness, and compare decoding complexity with energy and noise
tolerance.
title: Efficient decoding

description:
**Conjecture.** For any integer `a ≥ 2`, the walk with generators `{± a^t : t ≤ M_a}` on
`Z/rZ` (with `gcd(a, r)` arbitrary) has all nontrivial eigenvalues `≤ 1 − 1/(M_a + 1)`,
and the corresponding recovery `round(1/p_n(e)) = r` holds at `n = 8 (M_a+1)²`; moreover
the constant degrades exactly like `log a`, so `a = 2` is optimal among all lacunary bases.

*The key insight is* that the doubling lemma is really an *`a`-adic drift* lemma: the
circle distance is multiplied by `a` at every step until it exceeds `r/(2a)`, so the arc
one lands in is `[r/(2a), 1 − r/(2a)]` and the negative-cosine window shrinks with `a`.

*Why now?* Our `cdist_double` / `cdist_pow_two` proofs are entirely arithmetic and
generalise verbatim with `2 → a`; the only new ingredient is the cosine sign on the
narrower arc.  Falsifiable computationally for `a = 3, 5, 10` in minutes.
title: C3. Lacunary base-`a` walks: gap `Θ(1/(M_a + 1))` with `M_a = ⌈log_a r⌉`

description: Conway-style generalized Collatz maps can encode universal computation. Their undecidability does not transfer automatically to the fixed `3n+1` map. Formalizing the precise boundary would be a useful cross-domain result.
title: Investigate generalized Collatz systems

description:
*Let `x` be any finite integer stream of length `n ≥ 8` produced by iterating an
affine map of `ℤ³`.  Then the Berlekamp–Massey linear complexity of `x` is at
most 4, and the minimal polynomial computed from the first 8 symbols determines
the affine map up to conjugacy.*
title:
Let `x` be any finite integer stream of length `n ≥ 8` produced by iterating an
affine map of `ℤ³`.

description:
For richer data sheaves where compatible
   local data may fail to extend globally, define Čech cochains for a finite
   cover and connect nonzero obstruction classes to failed integration. The
   dependent-record sheaf proved here has unconditional gluing after overlap
   agreement, so its higher obstruction theory is correspondingly simple.
title: Cohomological obstructions

description: The present development does not decide paracompactness. A promising route is to study whether the clopen finite-step partitions generated by infinitesimals refine arbitrary open covers locally finitely. Conversely, a counterexample may come from a proper-class-like hierarchy of cofinality levels represented inside the fixed universe.
title: Paracompactness

description:
**Conjecture.** There are $\varepsilon > 0$ and $n_0$ such that for all $n \ge n_0$ there is a
weak $B_3$-free family $\mathcal F \subseteq 2^{[n]}$ with
$|\mathcal F| \ge (3+\varepsilon)\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$, and likewise a strong
$B_3$-free family of that size.

*Status.* The framework pins down what has to be beaten: three consecutive layers, and nothing
else of a symmetric nature. The improvement cannot come from adding sets to a layer family
(layer families are maximal: adjoining any set whose size lies outside the window creates a
strong copy), and cannot come from a level family or from a permutation-invariant family at
all. Hence such a construction must break the symmetry of the cube. *Falsifiable*: a proof of
$\mathrm{La}(n,B_3) \le 3\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor} + o\bigl(\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}\bigr)$
refutes it.
title: F3. The headline bound: an $\varepsilon$-gain for the three-atom cube

description:
The explicit arithmetic `PAsys pa qft` proves `Con(QFT₀) → Con(PA)` from the single
interpretation axiom `□_pa ⊥ → □_qft ⊥`.

**Conjecture.**  Over the GL calculus `Thm pa Ax`, the reflection sentence
`Con(qft) → Con(pa)` is derivable from an axiom set `Ax` consisting of *boxed-falsum
implications only* if and only if `Ax` already contains (or derives) the transfer
implication `□_pa ⊥ → □_qft ⊥`.

*Falsified by* an axiom set of that shape, plus a derivation of the reflection
sentence, together with a GL model validating `Ax` in which `□_pa ⊥ → □_qft ⊥` fails.
title: Exact reflection strength of the interpretation axiom

description: Prove `∀ k ≤ 5, HadwigerCase k`. In the indexing used here, the endpoint `k = 5` asserts that every non-five-colorable finite graph contains a `K₆` minor; its formal proof should explicitly identify where the Four Color Theorem is used.
title: Known cases through six colors

description:
Formalize a bounded-depth decryption
   circuit and show that the somewhat homomorphic evaluator can evaluate it on
   encrypted secret-key bits.  This would discharge the abstract
   `refresh_correct` field from concrete cryptographic hypotheses.
title: Bootstrappable decryption circuit

description: Investigate orbit-dependent transforms separately from the one-step cutoff sum. A rigorous implication between an orbit hitting-time estimate and a spectral estimate would require precise definitions and directional proofs; it should not be treated as an automatic equivalence.
title: Investigate orbit-dependent transforms separately from the one-step cutoff sum.

description:
Construct the 194 normalized McKay–Thompson series in a common analytic setting and prove that their class-indexed product has a pole of exact order 194 at the infinite cusp, with no cancellation in its leading coefficient. This sharply distinguishes a product over conjugacy classes from a product over group elements.

**The key insight is...** normalized principal parts aggregate additively under finite products, so the indexing convention leaves an observable signature in the pole order.

**Why now?** Exact class tables and replicable formulas provide finite input data, while the algebraic factorization theorem identifies the single analytic condition—control of the regular factors—needed to lift the result to genuine series.
title: Class-indexed pole order for the Monster

description:
For a bipartite coefficient matrix of arbitrary finite dimensions, normalize
the Hilbert norm of its second exterior power. Conjecture that its zero locus
is exactly rank one and that its sharp maximizers are precisely matrices with
equal nonzero singular values on their support. The two-row Lagrange identity
proved in this cycle is the first nontrivial case.
title: Exterior-power hierarchy

description: Prove `HadwigerCase 3`: every finite graph with no proper three-coloring has a `K₄` branch-set minor. This should be tested through a formal reduction to the classical low-order Hadwiger theorem rather than finite enumeration.
title: The four-clique case

description: Instantiate the continuous-linear-observable connector using integration against finite regular Borel measures, yielding a moment-determination theorem: agreement on the EML coordinate algebra implies equality of measures.
title: Measure-theoretic corollary

description: Under the same setup, prove that `consensus N' < consensus N` if and only if there is a set open for every old channel but not open for the new channel. Either implication can be falsified by a finite topological-space counterexample.
title: Strictness criterion for channel addition

description: Extend the linear neural-manifold theorem to smooth maps. The appropriate target is a local rank bound for the image of a smooth behavioral parametrization, with explicit hypotheses distinguishing image dimension, tangent rank, and the dimension of the image's linear span.
title: Extend the linear neural-manifold theorem to smooth maps.

description: Develop a finite enumeration only after specifying what “topologically distinct cake” means. Cherry positions vary continuously, so literal enumeration is impossible unless configurations are quotiented by a precise equivalence or discretized.
title: Develop a finite enumeration only after specifying what “topologically distinct cake” means.

description:
For a polyhedral map the sheet number is constant on each
chamber of a suitable subdivision of the target. Combining this with orientation data should give a
purely combinatorial degree, computed as a signed sheet count, together with a wall-crossing formula
relating the counts of adjacent chambers across the discriminant.
title: Degree theory for polyhedral maps

description:
— Stirling closes the $47$-versus-$49$ gap | **Split verdict.** Structural half **closed**: the missing lower bound $16^r \le \binom{2r}{r}^2(4r+1)$ is proved by induction through the recursion $(r+1)\binom{2r+2}{r+1} = 2(2r+1)\binom{2r}{r}$ (slack exactly $1$), giving the sandwich $4^r/\sqrt{4r+1} \le \binom{2r}{r} \le 4^r/\sqrt{3r+1}$, the exact $r^{-1/2}$ defect rate $\delta_r\sqrt r \in [1/(2\sqrt5),\,1/(2\sqrt3)]$, non-summability of the defects, and the Stirling-improved rate $2p(1-p)(4p(1-p))^r/((2p-1)\sqrt{3r+4})$. Numerical half **refuted**: *no* bound dominating the sharpened rate can certify $1\%$ at $47$ seeds, because the sharpened rate itself already exceeds $1/100$ there while the truth does not. |
| **D2** — the dichotomy under contamination | **Closed in finite-sample form**: for contamination level $c$ below the breakdown number, the achievable readings of the $m$-th rung are *exactly* the clean readings in $[Q(m-c),\,Q(m+c)]$ — the bracket is attained at both ends, so the maximal bias equals the clean spread and the breakdown number is the level at which that spread stops being finite. |
| **D3** — every offset rung has its own generating function | **Closed**: for each fixed offset $k$, the off-centre ladder started at its smallest ensemble sums to exactly $1 - p^{2k+1} = (1-p)(1 + p + \cdots + p^{2k})$, i.e. the conjectured $(1-p)R_k(p)$ with $R_k$ the geometric polynomial of length $2k+1$; $k = 0$ recovers the earlier cycle's $1-p$. |
title: — Stirling closes the $47$-versus-$49$ gap | Split verdict.

title: Define `bsearchRange`, a binary search returning the maximal index

description:
**A refuted guess, recorded because the refutation is informative.** The natural
first conjecture was `d(z₁,z₂) = log max(g, N/g) + O(1)`: "balanced factorisations
give distant witnesses". It is **false**. At `N = 52565 = 5 · 10513` the two nodes
sit at distance `d = 2.568` while `log max(g, N/g) = 9.26`. The correct parameter
is the pivot deficit `N − P`, not the factorisation balance; a large factor
guarantees a large *deficit-divisibility*, not a large deficit.
title: A refuted guess, recorded because the refutation is informative.

description:
**Graded modalities do not close the resolution gap** — a *refutation*
  (`Catalog/Probability/GradedResolution.lean`).  With the counting semantics
  `gsat` ("at least `k` successors of positive probability satisfy `φ`"), graded
  truth is invariant under exact analogies (`gsat_transport`), but it is *blind on
  deterministic systems*: any two deterministic constant-atom systems, on arbitrary
  finite world sets and with arbitrary successor functions, satisfy exactly the same
  graded formulas at every pair of worlds (`det_graded_iff`).  Hence "two self-loops"
  and "one 2-cycle" are graded-equivalent yet non-isomorphic (`gap_persists`): a
  finite language of graded modalities does **not** classify finite pointed models up
  to isomorphism, refuting Conjecture 1 of the root direction and the `k = 1`
  separation claim of Conjecture 4.  What does separate the pair is the
  self-reference observation `0 < step s s` (`loopObs`), which is itself invariant
  under exact analogies (`loopObs_transport`, `loop_separates`) — the missing
  resolution is a fixed-point phenomenon, not a multiplicity phenomenon.
title: Graded modalities do not close the resolution gap

description:
**N1 (cohomology of the whole nerve complex) — CLOSED in its structural half.**
  `DatabaseNerveTriple.finrank_H1_nerve_triple` extends the Betti law to a nerve
  with triple overlaps: `dim H¹ + #sources + rank d¹ = #overlaps + #components`,
  so `dim H¹ ≤ b₁` always (`finrank_H1_nerve_triple_le`), with equality exactly
  when the triangle relations are vacuous.  The predicted collapse is verified on
  the smallest interesting instance:
  `triple_overlap_kills_obstruction` proves `dim H¹ = 1` for three sources
  compared cyclically and `dim H¹ = 0` once their common triple overlap is
  recorded.  What remains open is the identification of `dim H¹` with simplicial
  `H¹(N; 𝕜)` for an arbitrary abstract simplicial nerve, restated as **P1**.
title: N1 (cohomology of the whole nerve complex) — CLOSED in its structural half.

description:
*"`minHeads` of a block-diagonal task is the sum of the blocks' head counts."* — **True**
   (`minHeads_blockTask`). The proof is that the output span of the block task is the internal

title: "`minHeads` of a block-diagonal task is the sum of the blocks' head counts."* — True

description:
**N2 (sharp two-sided threshold) — CLOSED, with a corrected parameter.** The
  conjectured parameter `k²(1−r)²` is wrong in the dense regime (it diverges
  while the failure probability saturates at `1`).  The correct parameter is the
  binomial tail `tail(k,r) = P[Bin(k,1−r) ≥ 2] = 1 − r^k − k(1−r)r^{k−1}`, and
  the two-sided bound is proved exactly:
  `(1−1/q)·tail ≤ 1 − base(k,q,r) ≤ tail` (`one_sub_base_ge_tail`,
  `one_sub_base_le_tail`), hence
  `(1 − tail)^n ≤ P(sheaf) ≤ (1 − (1−1/q)·tail)^n` (`sheafProb_sandwich`),
  `P(sheaf) ≤ exp(−n(1−1/q)·tail)` and `P(sheaf) ≥ 1 − n·tail`.  The transition
  therefore happens at `n·tail(k,r) ≍ 1`, and in the sparse regime
  `C(k,2)(1−r)²r^{k−2} ≤ tail ≤ C(k,2)(1−r)²` recovers the pair bound.
title: N2 (sharp two-sided threshold) — CLOSED, with a corrected parameter.

hyperprime" fails (`exists_primeFree_galaxy`), and even "prime-carrying
galaxies are dense" fails (`no_prime_galaxy_between`: no galaxy strictly

the wrong invariant.  The surviving conjecture is multiplicative:
title: Two successive versions of this conjecture are now refuted

description:
**Walls are flats of the support matroid.**  Since the walls are the loci
  `x i − x j = δ j − δ i`, the arrangement is a weighted braid (type `A_{n−1}`)
  arrangement, whose matroid is the graphic matroid of the complete graph on
  `S`.  `closedCell_subset_wallSet_iff` proves that the walls containing the
  cell of `T` are exactly the pairs `(i, j)` with `i, j ∈ T`, i.e. the edge set
  of `K_T`: the flat spanned by the cell.  `closedCell_eq_star_inter` exhibits
  the star of any `i₀ ∈ T` — the `|T| − 1` equations `x i + δ i = x i₀ + δ i₀`,
  `i ∈ T` — as a spanning set of that flat, cutting the cell out of the chamber
  of `i₀`; by `closedCell_ssubset` no proper subcoalition suffices, so the star
  is a basis.
title: Walls are flats of the support matroid.

coefficient growth beats the geometric decay, so the strict chain of
`truncation_chain` must terminate at a computable order rather than continue
forever.  **Why now?**  All the analytic ingredients — the two-sided tail
estimates `abs_tail_le_two` and `abs_tail_ge` — are already formalised and are
stated for arbitrary coefficient bounds; only the geometric majorant needs to be
replaced by a factorial one.
