description:
**C1 (`K_Schur ≤ 2·C_opt` for every family) — REFUTED, and not just for the constant `2`.**
  `AsaiLargeSieve.schur_row_gap_unbounded` (in `AsaiSchurGap.lean`) shows that for *every*
  constant `K` there is a family whose Gram matrix is Hermitian positive semidefinite — a
  rank-one family `v = (1, ε, …, ε)` with `ε = 1/m` and `m³` copies of `ε`, i.e. a single
  form — with an admissible large sieve constant `C = 1 + m` (`largeSieve_rankOne`) and Schur
  row `1 + m²` (`schur_row_rankOne`).  So `K_Schur / C_opt` is unbounded, and positivity of
  the Gram matrix alone gives no constant-factor comparison.  The case `K = 2` is recorded as
  `schur_row_not_le_two_mul_largeSieve`.
title: C1 (`K_Schur ≤ 2·C_opt` for every family) — REFUTED, and not just for the constant `2`.

description:
Let `σ(n)` be the stopping time of `n` under `T_3` and define the *orbit
transform* `G ω N = Σ_{n≤N} e(ω σ(n)/log n)`.  Then `G ω N / N` converges for
every `ω` to the characteristic function of the limiting distribution of
`σ(n)/log n`, and the Collatz conjecture restricted to `[1,N]` is *equivalent*
to `σ` being everywhere finite, i.e. to `G` being well defined — whereas no
statement about `F a ω N` has this property (by Conjecture 3 / the proved
blindness theorem).
title:
Let `σ(n)` be the stopping time of `n` under `T_3` and define the *orbit
transform* `G ω N = Σ_{n≤N} e(ω σ(n)/log n)`.

  `ℓ ∣ #E_{j0}(𝔽_p) ↔ p ≡ ℓ − 1 (mod ℓ)` for all `ℓ ≥ 1` and all `p ≡ 2 (mod 3)`,

description:
Formally: for i.i.d. symmetric coefficients, `P(cure | E) = 1 − 2^{-E}` for
`E ≤ D` and `1` for `E > D`, so no `E` in the fragile range has probability `0`
or `1`.
**The key insight is** that `separable_eosOf_iff` makes the cure event a
*maximum-of-coefficients* event, and maxima of independent coordinates are
monotone in the number of coordinates — the shift is a max-stability phenomenon,
not a capacity phenomenon.
**Why now?** `separable_eosOf_iff` and `margin_bound_sharp` already pin the
event exactly; only the product-measure bookkeeping remains, and the untested
`E = 24` arm is a direct empirical test of the predicted strict monotonicity.
title: Formally: for i.i.d.

description: If theories `U` and `T` are mutually faithfully interpretable over PA and PA verifies preservation of falsum proofs in both directions, then `Con(U)` is PA-independent exactly when `Con(T)` is PA-independent. A single verified pair of interpretations for which only one consistency sentence is independent would refute this conjecture.

description:
Using the already computed Christoffel symbols,
   formalize the coupled ODE
   for affine geodesics. The assertion that geodesics are piecewise exponential
   and trigonometric should first be tested: the smooth coefficients do not
   change formula at the diagonals, so literal piecewise behavior is not

description: Introduce parameterized optical fields whose zeros trace curves in three-dimensional space, and prove conservation of total local winding under deformations that neither create nor destroy boundary zeros.
title: Singularity motion

description:
**FiniteField.lean** *(settles the global half of the former Conjecture 1)* — the Gaussian
  product `∏_{i<k}(q^m - q^i)`, the closed product formula
  `poincare R k n q · ∏_{i<k}(q^k - q^i) = ∏_{i<k}(q^n - q^i)` over an arbitrary commutative
  ring and with no hypothesis `k ≤ n`, and the **point count of the Grassmannian**

  (`card_grassmannian_eq_poincare`), obtained by a fibration over the space of independent
  `k`-tuples.
title: FiniteField.lean

description:
**C2, discrete case.**  `π₀` is defined (`Components`), shown invariant under equivalence
  (`componentsEquivOfEquivalence`), trivial for connected 1-types
  (`subsingleton_components_of_connectedAt`), and shown to be a *complete* invariant of
  discrete (totally disconnected) 1-types:
  `discrete_equivalence_iff_nonempty_equiv : Nonempty (Discrete α ≌ Discrete β) ↔ Nonempty (α ≃ β)`.
  The general case (arbitrary groupoids) is restated as N2 below.
title: C2, discrete case.

description:
**Correction to old Conjecture 5.** The "no threshold at all" claim is *false* at the
  level of the parametrised quartic: the closed window `[8/9, 1]` is a genuine spectral
  stability band. What survives is the conditional statement: *whenever the Euler
  parameter exceeds `1`*, the collinear configuration is unstable, with no further
  threshold and a real growth rate. The remaining physical input is Conjecture 5′ below.
title: Correction to old Conjecture 5.

description:
**Torsor half: TRUE, as an exact characterisation.** `torsor_iff_abelian` —
  the compensating class is unique for every target and candidate **iff** the
  group is abelian.  `nonabelian_two_nonconj_compensators` produces explicit
  non-conjugate compensators from any non-commuting pair, `perm3_not_torsor`
  instantiates this in `S₃`, and `compensator_multiplicity_jump` shows the
  compensator count actually *jumps* between candidate classes.
title: Torsor half: TRUE, as an exact characterisation.

description:
* *Non-i.i.d. walks.* Replace the memoryless step law by a Markov chain on the three moves.
  The harmonic measure should become a Gibbs measure on the boundary rather than a product
  measure, with entropy the Markov entropy and dimension the corresponding ratio; ray rigidity
  should survive with the transition matrix as the invariant.
* *Arithmetic multifractality.* Study the spectrum of local dimensions of the harmonic measure
  with respect to the *hypotenuse* metric rather than the 3-adic one; the entropy–metric gap
  suggests a genuinely nontrivial multifractal spectrum.
* *Harmonic measure of subtrees.* The Pell spine of pure middle moves and other periodic rays
  are natural distinguished points of the boundary. The local behaviour of the harmonic
  measure near such points, and the associated conformal / Patterson–Sullivan theory of the
  hyperbolic embedding, are open.
* *Groupoid and hyperbolic-embedding refinements.* Relating the harmonic measure to the
  natural conformal density on the limit set of the embedded tree would explain the constant
  `2/3` structurally rather than numerically.
title: *Non-i.i.d.

description: Define a dovetailed proof-search algorithm, prove that every valid finite derivation is eventually checked, and distinguish the number of candidate strings inspected from the number of distinct theorems emitted.
title: Effective enumeration rather than bare countability

description:
**C3 (a matching lower bound for multi-block AFEs) — PROVED, in a stronger form.**  For an
  AFE whose blocks are spectrally separated (pairwise disjoint coefficient supports, e.g. a
  dyadic decomposition) the whole AFE collapses to a single Dirichlet polynomial
  (`AsaiSecondMoment.afe_eq_linForm_aggregate`) whose coefficient mass is the sum of the
  blockwise masses (`sum_normSq_aggregate_of_disjoint`).  Hence the lower bound
  `(D − eN)·∑_j |w j|²‖A j‖²` (`secondMoment_disjoint_lower`), the removal of one factor `J`
  from the flagship bound (`secondMoment_disjoint_uniform`), their combination into an exact
  order `≍ D·∑_j |w j|²‖A j‖²` when `2eN ≤ D` (`secondMoment_disjoint_order`), and the dyadic
  case used in the paper (`dyadic_support_disjoint`, `secondMoment_dyadic`: the bound is
  `C · W · B`, with no `J`-dependence).  All in `AsaiSecondMomentLower.lean`.
title: C3 (a matching lower bound for multi-block AFEs) — PROVED, in a stronger form.

description:
Call `s(T)` the minimum over all proper 2-colourings of `T` of the smaller colour class.  Then
for every tree `T` and all `n ≥ s(T)`,
```
exBip n T ≥ (s(T) - 1) * (n - s(T) + 1),
```
with equality for all sufficiently large `n` **iff** `T` has a vertex whose removal disconnects
`T` into components each of order `< s(T)` (equivalently, iff no "blocky" construction beats the
wide one).
title: Call `s(T)` the minimum over all proper 2-colourings of `T` of the smaller colour class.

description:
**Pruning half: FALSE.** `nonabelian_no_pruning` — in *any* group, for any
  target `σ` and any candidate `p`, the element `q = p⁻¹σ` compensates.  Since
  `classCompatible_conj_left/right` show the relation depends only on the two
  conjugacy classes, the fibre always projects **onto** all of `Cl(G)`: a
  non-abelian Artin channel prunes exactly nothing either.  The group-theoretic
  no-pruning barrier is therefore not an artefact of commutativity.
title: Pruning half: FALSE.

description:
The three failures worth recording. (a) *Value-level* features (top-bit balance,
adjacent differences) of a **short** window are still **not** covered: the two windows
differ as integer sequences (122 vs 124 high bits), so their nullity is empirical, not
proved — this was a "needs a different definition" failure, and §14 of the file supplies
the definition and settles the full-period case; the truncated case (`m ≪ d`) is what
Conjecture 1 now asks for.
(b) An unconditional "no polynomial-length window sees smoothness" statement is out of
reach because it quantifies over all computations; Conjecture 3 replaces it by a
symmetry statement that is provable. (c) Attempts to lower-bound `ord_N(2)` by
computation fail (`orderOf` is not decidable in practice); the working route is the
divisor argument used in `ord_two_1019_ge`, and Conjecture 4 turns it into a general
tool.
title: The three failures worth recording.

description:

description: Define the cubical set whose vertices are `Fin n → Bool`, whose edges are single toggles, and whose higher cubes are sets of mutually independent toggles. Prove that its realization is contractible, while selected discrete subspaces (such as the one-choice cookie fiber with no substitution edge) realize `S^0`.

description:
prove the sharp bound `R_min ≥ 1/2`.  A promising route is a *strip* argument: for
  `R < 1/2` consecutive cells of a path are king-neighbours and each crossing of a
  lattice line `x = K` forces both endpoints within `R` of the line; a counting argument
  in a two-row strip gives `2` cells per column against the `1/R > 2` hops per column
  needed to advance one column.  The difficulty is to rule out paths that drift in both
  coordinates.
title: prove the sharp bound `R_min ≥ 1/2`.

title: Syndrome-graph counterexamples

For finite--cofinite events `A ⊆ B`, prove

title: Strict monotonicity classification

description:
**Conjecture.** The mod-2 obstruction is the first term of a full congruence filtration:
for every `k ≥ 1` the reduction of the Berggren group mod `2^k` is a proper subgroup of
`GL(2, ℤ/2^k)`, and the resulting inverse limit is a proper open subgroup of `GL(2, ℤ₂)`
whose abelianization is exactly ℤ/2 — so ℤ/2 is the *only* anyon charge the tree can ever
carry, at every level of the congruence tower.

*The key insight is* that braiding must preserve every congruence-level charge, so a single
surjection onto an abelian quotient at level `2` propagates upward and pins the whole
profinite completion. **Why now?** The level-2 case is already formalized
(`berggren_mod_two`, `charge_mul`, `braid_pair_charge_eq`), and Mathlib's `ZMod` and
`Subgroup.closure_induction` machinery makes the induction on `k` mechanical.
title: Direction 1 — Congruence Obstruction Hierarchy for Berggren Braiding

description:
**Conjecture.** The Berggren group is a *thin* subgroup of `GL(2,ℤ)`: infinite index, yet
Zariski-dense, with the counting exponent of hypotenuses along depth-`d` words governed by
`log 9 / log(3+2√2)` — the ratio the two-sided depth bound `(d+2)² < c ≤ 5·9^d` already
brackets.

*The key insight is* that the two extreme spines (polynomial `A`-spine, exponential
`B`-spine) are the extremal geodesics of a hyperbolic word metric, so their exponents bound
the group's critical exponent from both sides. **Why now?** The extremal spines are proved
and explicit (`aSpine_hyp`, `bSpine_recurrence`), so what remains is a counting argument
rather than a search for the right objects.
title: Direction 2 — Silver-Ratio Pell Spine as a Thin-Group Certificate

description:
**Conjecture.** Any braid representation whose matrix entries lie in ℤ[1/√2, i] and which
is generated by matrices of finite order lands inside the Clifford group; hence no
arithmetic braid representation over the Berggren spectral field is dense in `U(2)`, and
universality requires leaving the field ℚ(√2, i) (e.g. Fibonacci anyons over ℚ(√5)).

*The key insight is* that the Clifford condition is a *closed* algebraic condition on the
conjugation action on Pauli matrices, so it survives limits and constrains the whole closure
of the generated monoid. **Why now?** The `Cliff` set, its closedness, its containment of
the Ising generators, and the exclusion of `T` are all already formalized
(`isClosed_cliff`, `isingMonoid_le_cliff`, `tgate_not_cliff`).
title: Direction 3 — Clifford Ceiling for Arithmetic Braid Representations

description:
**Conjecture.** Replacing the silver unit `3+2√2` by the golden unit `(3+√5)/2` — i.e.
using a tree of *Markov* or Fibonacci-type triples instead of Pythagorean triples — yields
a generator pair satisfying the braid relation whose image *is* dense in `PU(2)`,
reinstating the moonshot in a different arithmetic.

*The key insight is* that density of a braid representation is governed by whether the
associated quantum dimension is a non-Clifford algebraic number, and `√5` is, while `√2` is
not. **Why now?** The negative side has been isolated exactly to the field: the obstruction
proofs here (integrality, Clifford closure) are field-theoretic and transfer verbatim as
tests for the golden case.
title: Direction 4 — Fibonacci Escape from the Pythagorean Tree

description:
**Conjecture.** The two-sided bound `(d+2)² < c ≤ 5·9^d` is sharp in the strong sense that
the number of depth-`d` triples with hypotenuse below `X` is `Θ(X^{1/2})` for the
polynomial sector and `Θ(log X)` for the exponential sector, giving a two-regime complexity
dictionary: "circuit depth" in the tree is logarithmic in the hypotenuse exactly along the
Pell spine and square-root-like along the linear spine.

*The key insight is* that the tree's word metric is bi-Lipschitz to `log c` only on the
hyperbolic sector, and the parabolic `A`-spine is precisely the locus where this fails.
**Why now?** Both extremes are already proved attained, so the remaining step is a counting
estimate interpolating between them.

description:
**Conjecture.** Every radius-one rule over a finite alphabet whose global map is an
involution on every finite cycle is, up to conjugation by a permutation of the alphabet and
spatial reflection, of *marker-twist* form
`g a b c = τ_{P(a,c)} b`, where `P` is a predicate on the outer cells and `τ_·` a family of
involutive permutations of the alphabet each fixing the letters that make `P` visible in
the output.

Of the 1 800 ternary reversible rules, exactly **82** are involutive; the counterexample
families of this cycle (`signRule`, `twistRule`) are all of marker-twist form, and
`twistRule_selfDecoder` is precisely the statement that the marker survives the update.

*The key insight is* that an involution must let the decoder read the marker *after* the
update, so the twisting permutation is forced to fix the marker letters — a purely local
fixed-point condition that converts a dynamical constraint (involutivity on all cycles)
into an algebraic one on a family of permutations.

*Why now?* `Core.lean` already contains the exact tool that makes the forward direction
routine (`globalMap_involutive_of_selfDecoder`), and `cycleBijective_conj` gives the
conjugation action under which the classification is to be stated; only the converse
(involution ⇒ marker form) is open, and it can be tested exhaustively on the 82 ternary
involutions before being attempted in general.

---
title: Direction 2 — Marker-Twist Universality for Involutive Rules

description:
**Conjecture.** The maximal *minimal decoder window* of a reversible radius-one rule over an
alphabet of size `q` equals `2q` for all `q ≥ 3` (and is `1` for `q ≤ 2`).

Measured distribution for `q = 3`: windows `1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6` occur for
`18, 72, 774, 576, 216, 144` rules — maximum `6 = 2·3` (`ComputationalEvidence.md`, §4).
The Lean file `InverseRadius.lean` proves the first nontrivial instance: `gTwist` has a
window-4 decoder and provably no window-3 decoder and no radius-one inverse.

*The key insight is* that a decoder window of size `k` is a *deterministic pushdown* of the
pair graph: unreadable letters force the decoder to postpone its decision, and each
postponement consumes one of the `q - 1` "ambiguity classes" that a reversible rule can
maintain, so the window can grow only linearly in `q`, never exponentially.

*Why now?* Both the upper-bound mechanism (`cycleBijective_of_decoder4R`: a window-`k`
decoder proves reversibility at all lengths simultaneously) and the lower-bound mechanism
(`gTwist_no_window3_decoder`, an exhaustive finite refutation) are already formalised and
generalise verbatim to arbitrary `k`; the missing piece is a single uniform
`cycleBijective_of_decoderK` lemma.

---
title: Direction 3 — Inverse-Radius Growth Law

description:
**Conjecture.** The number `R(q)` of reversible radius-one rules over an alphabet of size
`q` satisfies `R(q) = q! · f(q)` with `f(2) = 3`, `f(3) = 300`, and `f` is
*not* polynomial in `q`; moreover every reversible ternary rule lies in the orbit of an
explicitly describable list of marker-twist and affine rules under the group of order 12
generated by alphabet permutations and spatial reflection.

`R(2) = 6 = 2!·3` and `R(3) = 1800 = 3!·300`.  The `3·q!` single-coordinate rules (three
window positions times `q!` permutations) are always reversible, so `f(q) ≥ 3` with
equality exactly at `q = 2`.

*The key insight is* that reversibility is invariant under the two symmetries already
formalised — `cycleBijective_conj` (relabelling the alphabet) and `cycleBijective_reflect`
(reversing space) — so `R(q)` is a sum of orbit sizes of a `q! × 2` group action, and
computing `R(4)` becomes feasible by enumerating orbit representatives rather than all
`4^64` tables.

*Why now?* The exact pair-graph criterion makes a single reversibility test cost `O(q⁶)`
bit operations, and the symmetry group cuts the `q = 4` search by a factor of ~48; the
formal side already has the invariance lemmas, so an enumeration result could be certified
by a Lean-checked criterion rather than trusted code.

---
title: Direction 4 — Exact Enumeration and the Orbit Structure of `R(q)`

description:
**Conjecture.** No reversible radius-one cellular automaton over a small alphabet can be a
secure round function: if the inverse has decoder window `k`, then `t` rounds have inverse
window at most `k + 2(t-1)`, so the inverse of the `t`-fold map is again a cellular
automaton of radius `O(t)`, and the resulting cipher admits a chosen-ciphertext local
inversion attack of complexity linear in the state size, uniformly in `t`.

*The key insight is* that reversibility of a CA is *hereditarily local*: composition adds
radii, so unlike an SPN, whose inverse becomes global after a few rounds, a reversible CA
never escapes a linear-in-`t` inverse radius — the very property that makes such automata
attractive (cheap invertibility) is the property that destroys diffusion-based security.

*Why now?* The formal ingredients are in place: `cycleBijective_of_decoder4R` shows how a
window-`k` decoder certifies invertibility at all sizes at once, and the composition of two
decoders is a decoder of the summed window; making the attack statement precise turns a
folklore warning about CA-based cryptography into a theorem with an explicit constant.

**Conjecture.**  For every wolf count `k ≥ 2` there is a rational function `R_k` of degree
`⌈(k-2)/2⌉` over degree `⌈(k-2)/2⌉` such that, for every odd population `n ≥ k`,

`n · (k · surv n − failProb (n−k) k) = R_k(n)`,   with   `R_k(∞) = C(k,2) = k(k−1)/2`.

The first five instances, found by exact rational computation, are

**The key insight is** that the defect recursion
`(v+k+3)·D(v+2,k+1) = (k+1)·D(v+1,k) + (v+2)·D(v,k+1)` is *free of the survival product*:
the union-bound term cancels identically because the survival ladder and the population
ladder step in lockstep, so on the odd-population fibre — where the `surv`-valued
inhomogeneity is absent — the recursion closes inside the field of rational functions of
`n`, and the degree can only grow by one every two steps.

**Why now?**  We have just proved the exact `k = 2` and `k = 3` cases
(`failProb_two_wolves_odd`, `failProb_three_wolves_odd`), proved the sharp upper bound
`n·D ≤ C(k,2)` for all `k` (`defect_scaled_le`), and verified the shape of `R_4, R_5, R_6`
in exact arithmetic.  The only missing ingredient is a closed recursion for the coefficient
vectors of `R_k`, which the defect recursion supplies directly.

*If true*: the odd-population game is solved in closed form for every fixed `k`, and
`n·D → C(k,2)` follows immediately, upgrading `defect_scaled_le` from an inequality to an
asymptotic equality.  *If false*: the defect must carry a transcendental (Wallis-type)
component even on the odd fibre, which would be a genuinely surprising asymmetry.

description:
**Conjecture.**  On the *even*-population fibre no such rational description exists: for
every `k ≥ 3` the scaled defect satisfies

`n · (k · surv n − failProb (n−k) k) = S_k(n) · surv (n−2)`

with `S_k` rational and `S_k(∞) = c_k > 0`, so that the even-population defect is
`Θ(n^{-1/2})` and is *not* a rational function of `n`.

The first cases, proved this cycle, are `S_2 = 0`, `S_3 = 1`, `S_4 = 4`
(`defect_two_wolves_even`, `defect_three_wolves_even`, `defect_four_wolves_even`).

**The key insight is** that the two parity fibres of the recursion are not symmetric: the
odd fibre is fed by boundary data at `v = 1` (the "one villager left" absorbing state,
where `failProb = 1` exactly), whereas the even fibre is fed at `v = 0`, whose value
`k·surv k − 1` still carries the survival product — so the Wallis irrationality survives on
one fibre and is annihilated on the other.

**Why now?**  The three base cases are already theorems, and `defect_recursion` reduces the
general statement to an induction on `k` alone.  Combined with Direction 1 this would give
a complete two-fibre solution of the game.

*If true*: the parity dichotomy is not merely a difference of constants but a difference of
*arithmetic type* — rational on one fibre, Wallis-transcendental on the other.
*If false*: some `k` has a rational even-fibre defect, which would force a hidden algebraic
relation among the central binomial coefficients.

title: Direction 2 — Wallis Obstruction on the Even Fibre

description:
**Conjecture.**  Consider the family of information-free games in which, after a day that
misses a wolf, exactly `d ≥ 1` villagers are removed at night.  Then the population drops
by `d+1` per round, the conserved quantity is the population mod `d+1`, and the rescaled
wolf-win probability has exactly `d+1` distinct subsequential limits
`c_0, …, c_d` with

`c_j / c_0 = Γ-quotients of the form Γ(1 − j/(d+1))/Γ(1 + j/(d+1))`,

specializing at `d = 1` to the ratio `π/2` proved this cycle.

**The key insight is** that the survival product along a step-`(d+1)` ladder is a ratio of
Gamma functions by the Gauss multiplication formula, and the parity (more precisely, the
residue class mod `d+1`) selects which shift of the Gamma argument appears — the Wallis
`π/2` being the reflection-formula value at `d = 1`.

**Why now?**  The `d = 1` case is fully proved (`parity_constant_ratio`,
`tendsto_parity_ratio`, `not_tendsto_scaled_failProb`), and the proof factors entirely
through the identity `surv n · surv (n+1) = 1/(n+1)` (`surv_mul_succ_gen`), whose
step-`(d+1)` analogue is an immediate telescoping computation.  Mathlib now contains enough
`Real.Gamma` API to close the resulting limit.

*If true*: the `π/2` gap is one member of a Gamma-valued family, and "parity" is revealed as
a shadow of the reflection formula.  *If false*: the `d = 1` case is exceptional, which
would point to a hidden extra symmetry of the alternating day/night structure.

description:
**Conjecture.** `greedySeq n = Θ(n³)`; more precisely there is `c > 0` with
`greedySeq n ≥ c·n³` for all large `n`, so the cubic upper bound proved here is tight in
order of magnitude.

The key insight is that the cubic upper bound is exactly the strength of *counting* the
obstruction set `sidonBad A` (`≤ |A|³` elements), so a matching lower bound must be a
*dispersion* statement: the obstruction set has to be shown to be spread out over an
interval of length `≍ max A` rather than clustered, and the greedy rule guarantees the
spreading because each new element is chosen minimal.

**Why now?** `greedy_valid_gt` removed the ordering restriction that previously made the
greedy step a local statement; with the unordered criterion `isSidon_insert_of_avoid` the
obstruction set is a genuine subset of an interval and can be attacked by counting
collisions `c + d − b = c' + d' − b'`, which is a finite Sidon-type condition already
formalised in the catalog.

sandwich (degree `h` below, degree `2h+1` above) is off by exactly one unit of degree at
each end, and the truth is the arithmetic mean.

The key insight is that the weighted obstruction set `bhBad` has `≍ n^{2h}` elements but
only `≍ n^{2h−1}` distinct values, because the weight-`d` families for `d ≥ 2` are
lower-dimensional; counting *values* rather than *tuples* should move the exponent.

**Why now?** `bhBad` and `card_bhBad_le` are formalised with the weight parameter explicit,
so the refinement is a purely combinatorial recount inside an existing definition rather
than a new development. The numerical data (A046185, A046186) is consistent with

description:
Cycle 3 shows that a *single* member of size `k` can force nothing better than
`|F| ≤ (2^{k−1}+1)·deg`, and that this is attained.  **Conjecture: for a union-closed family
in which every nonempty member has size at least `k`, the best possible abundance ratio
degrades exactly like `2^{k−1}+1`, i.e. the extremal family `insert A (A.erase a).powerset`
is the unique extremiser up to isomorphism.**  The key insight is that the extremal family is
a power set with a single "cap", so extremality is a statement about how much of a Boolean
lattice can sit below one cap.  Why now?  Both sides are already formalised, so uniqueness is
the only missing ingredient, and it can be probed by enumerating extremisers on `Fin 4`.
title: Direction 2 — The `2^{k−1} + 1` law as a Frankl obstruction

description:
`frankl_of_card_le_four` is proved by "two distinct nonempty members give degree ≥ 2".
**Conjecture: `m` distinct nonempty members of a union-closed family always produce an element
of degree at least `⌈log₂(m+1)⌉ + 1`, and consequently Frankl's conjecture holds for all
families with at most `2^t` members by induction on `t`.** The key insight is that minimal
nonempty members behave like the singleton in Frankl's classical argument, and unions with a
minimal member are injective on the family.  Why now?  The chain case
(`frankl_of_chain`) is the extreme case of this statement and is already proved; the general
case needs only a quantitative version of the same minimality argument.
title: Direction 3 — Frankl for families of bounded size, beyond four

description:
The averaging criterion (`exists_abundant_of_large_totalSize`) needs average member size
`≥ n/2` and needs no union-closedness; union-closed families can sit far below that (see
`averaging_criterion_not_necessary`).  **Conjecture: there is a constant `c < 1/2` such that
every *union-closed* family whose members average at least `c·n` has an abundant element, and
`c` can be taken to be `1/4`.**  The key insight is that union-closedness itself pushes total
size upward — the closure of any family contains all its joins — so the averaging threshold
should be strictly weaker for union-closed families than in general.  Why now?  Total size is
already related to degrees by the formalised double-counting identity
`sum_deg_eq_totalSize`, so the conjecture is exactly a question about the minimum of
`totalSize` over union-closed families with no abundant element.
title: Direction 4 — Average size versus abundance: a threshold phenomenon

   has `m_k = ⌊√N⌋` (observed on 283/283 non-squares `N ≤ 300`).  This is the
   only unproved hypothesis of `cf_period_end_quotient`, and it is the
   integral shadow of the classical purely-periodic expansion of
   `⌊√N⌋ + √N`.
title: Period-end normal form

description:
Generalize bounded geometric defect to
   `G(n) = o(n)` and prove zero logical and protected-entropy rates directly via
   the same normalized Singleton estimate.
title: Sharper asymptotics

description: For some finite fields and parameters with `2e > n-d-1`, there is a received vector admitting at least two distinct degree-at-most-`d` candidate polynomials within `e` disagreements, so unique reconstruction cannot be extended beyond half the Reed–Solomon minimum distance.
title: List-decoding failure beyond half distance

description: Combining Conjectures 1 and 2 with an admissible `k`-tuple of diameter `246` yields arbitrarily large translates containing at least two primes.
title: Sieve-to-prime-cluster implication

description: Use Möbius inversion to pass from rooted walks to primitive cycle counts. This would turn the local coefficient formula proved here into the full graph analogue of the prime-power explicit formula.
title: Use Möbius inversion to pass from rooted walks to primitive cycle counts.

description: Study invariance under refactoring. Adding wrapper lemmas can change both dependency counts and proof lengths, so a robust statistic should quotient or penalize such transformations.
title: Study invariance under refactoring.

description:
After quotienting global phase, conjecture that each level `0<c<1` is a smooth
homogeneous space of fixed diffeomorphism type. The endpoint `c=1` has a larger
stabilizer, while `c=0` is the Segre stratum; the exact maximizer theorem now
identifies one of the two singular endpoints algebraically.
title: Interior level-set topology

description:
in this cycle: `exists_block_dvd` shows that a
non-admissible pattern is realised at most finitely often (never, past `p > q`), and
`constant_gap_run_dvd` is the special case of constant patterns.  The open half is the
existence direction, a barcode restatement of the Hardy–Littlewood/Dickson prime
`k`-tuple conjecture.
title: in this cycle: `exists_block_dvd` shows that a

description:
Prove idempotence of `tropicalConvexHull` and package
   it with the already established monotonicity and extensivity results as a
   closure operator.
title: Closure-operator API

description:
The map `s ↦ cost(closure of s)` is modular on
   dependency-closed sets (proved: `cost_merge_add_cost_inter`) but is
   conjectured *strictly submodular* on arbitrary generating sets; if so, greedy
   library construction is a `(1 − 1/e)`-approximation of the champion.
title: Submodular closure cost

description: Introduce the first-order radial system, compute its Jacobian at equilibrium, and prove oscillatory linearized solutions with frequency squared `2k/(mr²)`. The present theorem uses positivity of the effective second derivative as the standard energetic stability criterion.
title: Formalize linear stability dynamically

description: Replace pairs of scalar resources by vectors in an ordered cone. A positive linear functional should yield a generalized barycenter theorem, while equality under an exposed supporting functional should force every positively weighted component into the same exposed face.
title: Ordered-cone generalization

description:
Extend the proved Rips-simplex dichotomy to chain groups
   and prove explicitly that reduced homology vanishes in positive dimensions in both regimes.
title: Formalize simplicial homology

description: Model cooking and verification costs as nonnegative random variables. Prove expectation and concentration analogues under an almost-sure positive lower bound on total verification cost; explicitly distinguish the expectation of a ratio from the ratio of expectations.
title: Uncertain timings

description: Define `M_N = ∏_{n < N} S^n`, prove `M_{N+1} ≃ M_N × S^N`, and construct the genuine inverse sequence with coordinate-forgetting bonding maps. Its inverse limit should recover the countable product. This gives a non-discrete inverse-system formulation of the same object.
title: Finite-stage approximation

description: Construct affine monoid algebras `ℤ[M]`, glue them over fan faces, and identify the resulting scheme with the toric variety attached to the fan.
title: Toric realization

description: For a genuine Chaitin-style direction, define prefix-free machines, halting domains, and finite Omega approximants. Prove monotonicity and convergence first; machine-dependent randomness or uncomputability requires substantial computability and algorithmic-information infrastructure.
title: For a genuine Chaitin-style direction, define prefix-free machines, halting domains, and finite Omega approximants.

description:
The genuinely unbounded assertion that these are
   all class-number-one imaginary quadratic fields requires deep analytic number
   theory. It must not be inferred from `max_of_heegner_list`, which only computes
   the maximum of an explicitly supplied finite set.
title: Stark–Heegner theorem

description:
For all `P,Q` with more than one element,
   \[
   \dim(P^+\times Q_+)\le \dim(P\times Q)+1.
   \]
   The formal theorem `proposition_2_2_uniform` shows that this bound, together with its order-dual application and bounded-poset additivity, implies Conjecture 1.
title: Opposite-endpoint augmentation bound

description:
State any power-law claim with finite-range error
   bounds and coding assumptions.  A relation to Hausdorff dimension requires a
   separately defined metric space of proofs or proof trees and an invariance
   theorem connecting that metric to the chosen encoding.
title: Length distributions

description:
Both halves are already formalised separately: the commutation theorem for `2k+1`
monotone curves, and the breakdown theorem for `2k+1` samples.  Composing them is the exact
statement a deployment guarantee needs — "one bad seed cannot move the reported knee" — and it
is the fourth-seed experiment's formal content.
title: Both halves are already formalised separately: the commutation theorem for `2k+1`

description: For every imaginary quadratic field of class number at most `4`, construct a singular modulus generating its Hilbert class field and prove that its minimal polynomial has degree equal to the class number and splitting field unramified over the quadratic base field.
title: Explicit imaginary-quadratic generators

description:
Replace the one-vertex feasibility model by a cost
   function on variables and minimize total cost subject to `k`-colourability of the induced
   graph on unspilled vertices. The counterexample shows that degree alone cannot solve this
   optimization problem.
title: Formalize weighted spill cost

description:
**Relative cohomology tied to the classifier.** Replace cohomology of the
  bare weight space by a relative or constructible sheaf whose restriction
  maps depend on class labels, margins, and activation regions. Investigate
  whether its obstruction classes characterize failure to glue local
  certificates.
title: Relative cohomology tied to the classifier.

description:
Whenever `vmin < vmax`, the chord produced by
   `exists_affine_chord` at `x` may be chosen with `value i < value j`; equivalently every
   hull velocity has a subgradient that is a genuine chord slope. This is the single
   missing step of Conjecture 2 above.
title: Nondegenerate chord selection

description: If a graph predicate is reconstructible from `SameDeck`, then the predicate obtained by applying it to graph complements is also reconstructible. This should be formalized as a general theorem and instantiated for every reconstructed class in the catalog.
title: Complement transfer for reconstructible predicates

description: Generalize optional choices from `Bool` to finite ingredient-state types. Fibers then have cardinality equal to the product of coordinate cardinalities, while methods become actions of finite permutation groups or cyclic groups rather than Boolean parity.
title: Non-binary substitutions

description:
On configurations `ℤ → α`, formalize
   radius-one global maps and prove that every single-coordinate permutative
   rule has an inverse which is again a radius-one cellular automaton, with the
   same explicit opposite-shift formula established here for finite cycles.
title: Infinite-configuration extension

description: A regular exponential family is flat for its exponential and mixture connections, while its Fisher metric may have nonzero Levi-Civita curvature. Formalize these connections and state projective-flatness claims with explicit connection coefficients.
title: Separate dual flatness from Levi-Civita curvature

description:
Extract an executable colouring algorithm from a perfect
   elimination ordering and prove that it uses exactly the clique number of registers.
title: Certified greedy allocation

description: Equip corner loci with rational polyhedral complexes and prove that scheme-theoretic bend support recovers their underlying topological spaces.
title: Polyhedral geometry

description: For every commutative ring `R`, every `n : ℕ`, and `a b : R`, define the `n + 1` parameters `a^i b^(n-i)`. Their product is conjectured to equal `(a*b)^(n*(n+1)/2)`. A counterexample is any ring, `n`, `a`, and `b` for which these two explicit products differ.
title: All symmetric powers and their central characters

description: Formalize that the representing probability measure is unique, using polynomial moments on the compact convex set of density matrices.
title: Uniqueness of the mixing measure

description: Establish existence and uniqueness for the logarithmic central-force ODE away from the origin, classify turning radii using the effective potential, and determine which exceptional energy-angular-momentum pairs, if any, yield closed noncircular trajectories.
title: Study global bounded orbits

description:
Between the exponential `2^n`
   (independent) and linear `n + 1` (chain) baselines, the number of usable
   sub-libraries of a random dependency DAG with edge density `p` is conjectured
   to be `exp(Θ(n / (1 + pn)))`, with the crossover at `p ≍ 1/n`.
title: Candidate-count phase transition

description: Given an actual finite recipe dataset and a declared flavor map, construct fibers or tolerance neighborhoods reproducibly. Only after specifying a distance, threshold, and simplex rule should one compute persistent homology or compare cuisines.
title: Measured flavor maps

description: The proved model is exactly quadratic in speed. Investigate how bubble radius, wall thickness, shape profile, and any ship-mass coupling alter the scaling. The proposed `E ~ M vₛ c` law is not established by the standard fixed-profile density formula.
title: Energy scaling

description: Model connectomes with exactly `m` active synapses, whose state count is `choose (synapseSlots N) m`, and derive entropy bounds for their minimum description length. This would distinguish dense worst-case connectomes from biologically sparse families.
title: Sparse biological constraints

description: For a connected groupoid with vertex group `G`, prove that natural-isomorphism classes of self-equivalences are in bijection with the outer automorphism group `Out(G)`. The claim is falsifiable by computing both sides for finite cyclic and symmetric groups.
title: Unpointed self-equivalences of a `K(G,1)`

description:
Conjecture: no sound calculus for all
   `TempFrame`s proves the negation of “not provable now and provable at some later
   stage.” The two-world model underlying `proof_gain_is_satisfiable` is a concrete
   countermodel to any such proposed refutation.
title: Non-refutability of proof gain

description: Package unit complex phases as `Metric.sphere (0 : ℂ) 1`, package each radius-`r` three-sphere as a subtype of `ℂ × ℂ`, and prove that the induced group action is free for every `r > 0`: if a phase fixes one sphere point, then that phase equals `1`.
title: Freeness of the full circle action on every nonzero sphere

description:
Study spacetime diagrams rather than only fixed points.  Turing completeness
  concerns unbounded evolution, while a fixed-point locus discards transient
  and propagating behavior.
title: Study spacetime diagrams rather than only fixed points.

description:
Define a height-bounded representation
   predicate and prove search certificates for historically difficult targets.
   Keep the certificate-generating computation separate from the small kernel-
   checked theorem that validates each displayed identity.
title: Bounded certified searches

description: If `s` locations are marked erased and the remaining received shares contain at most `e` errors, then degree-at-most-`d` reconstruction is unique whenever `n ≥ d + s + 2e + 1`; the bound is sharp under the same field-size feasibility conditions.
title: Erasures-and-errors tradeoff

description: Generate a `RingCon` from all term-deletion equations and prove its functor-of-points vanishing set agrees with `bendVanishingSet`.
title: Bend congruence quotients

description: Enrich `SearchInstance` with an exploration order, failed-branch costs, and terminal nodes. The present non-determination theorem shows that these semantic data are necessary before dimension can imply proof-search time or shortest-proof length.
title: Search policy and cost

description:
`which_factor_wall_general` gives `I(class N ; F(class p)) = 0` for a semiprime and *any* statistic
`F`; `last_factor_wall` proves `I( h(u)·v ; F(u) ) = 0` for any aggregate `h` of the other factors,
and `kfactor_wall` instantiates it at `N = p₁⋯p_{k+1}` for every `k`.
title: C5 / C7 (wall half) — which-factor independence *(closed)

description: Formalize a circuit or Turing-machine model that computes `piBit n`, separating storage complexity from computation complexity.
title: Uniform generation problem

description: π and e do not have bounded partial quotients established by the proposal, while √2 does. A theorem connecting decimal digit consonance to continued-fraction coefficients would require a precise statistic and substantial new number theory.
title: Clarify the continued-fraction claim

description:
Package the Kronecker symbol `n ↦ (D/n)` as a Mathlib
   `DirichletCharacter`, including the prime `2` and composite moduli. Prove its conductor is
   `|D|` for fundamental `D` and connect evaluation at odd primes to `quadraticColor`.
title: Global Dirichlet characters

description: Replace the unsupported genus-only `O(√g)` claim by bounds involving block length `n`, area, injectivity radius, and bounded local geometry. Determine hypotheses under which `d = O(√n)` or hyperbolic-surface tradeoffs can be proved.
title: Correct asymptotic variables

description:
The two easy halves are *proved*: closure under subgraphs
(`TriangularForest.IsTriangularForest.mono`, `IsTriangularForest.comap`) and closure under
1-sums (`TriangularForest.isTriangularForest_oneSum`).  Subdivision/suppression is the missing
operation and is not available in Mathlib.
title: The two easy halves are *proved*: closure under subgraphs

description:
The present theorem assumes a
   chordal graph via an explicit perfect elimination order. A compiler-facing development
   could define dominance, SSA live ranges, and prove that the resulting interference graph
   admits such an order.
title: Connect perfect elimination orders to SSA construction

description:
Mathlib has the unique factorisation of `ℤ[i]` (`GaussianInt` is a
`EuclideanDomain`), and `range_toGaussian` already identifies `PTriple` with the square-norm
submonoid, so the conjecture becomes a statement about prime factorisations with even
exponents — reachable with existing API.
title: Mathlib has the unique factorisation of `ℤ[i]` (`GaussianInt` is a

description: Develop an appropriate notion of local idempotent semiring and prove that stalks of the localized structure sheaf are local.
title: Stalk locality

description: Define trajectories in `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)`, angular momentum, and the central-force ODE. Prove conservation of energy and angular momentum, then derive the effective radial equation rather than taking it as the starting model.
title: Derive the reduced equations from planar mechanics

description:
The two extreme cases `t = 0` and `t = m` are already proved tight
(`corradi_tight_of_pairwiseDisjoint`, `corradi_tight_of_constant`), and the
rigidity theorem tells us precisely which combinatorial object must be built for
intermediate `t`; nothing else in the argument is missing.
title: The two extreme cases `t = 0` and `t = m` are already proved tight

description:
Two contexts and six seeds already separate the three rungs of a three-seed
ladder, and a single `ctx = 4096` cell distinguishes the two candidate low-tail families by
exactly one grid step: `320` (constant ratio) versus `288` (affine), proved as
`KneeQuota.lowtail_prediction_32x`.
title: Two contexts and six seeds already separate the three rungs of a three-seed

description: Missing rate zero lies in this range, and complete data forces a tie between methods that preserve observations. Any valid performance theorem must specify a stochastic model and should use non-strict or expected-risk comparisons.
title: A distribution-free claim that sheaf imputation is always strictly better for `r < 0.5` and more than ten features

description:
(`TriangularForest.completeGraph_not_decomposesIntoTwo_six`).  Randomised search finds
matching covers for all `n ≤ 11`.  Open: a construction for general `n`.
title: (`TriangularForest.completeGraph_not_decomposesIntoTwo_six`).  Randomised search finds

description: Formalize finite base-golden-ratio expressions with binary digits. Because `φ² = φ + 1`, unrestricted expansions are not unique; impose the standard no-consecutive-ones normalization and connect coefficients to Zeckendorf representations.
title: Phinary arithmetic

description:
Pairwise overlap events commonly share columns
   and therefore need not be independent. Formalize the dependency graph and
   derive exact probabilities or rigorous upper/lower bounds instead of an
   unconditional product formula.
title: Constraint dependence

description: For the constructed Hilbert class field `H/K`, prove that extension of ideals sends every nonzero fractional ideal of `𝒪_K` to a principal fractional ideal of `𝒪_H`. Equivalently, prove that the induced homomorphism `Cl(𝒪_K) → Cl(𝒪_H)` is zero.
title: Principal ideal theorem

description:
The certificate reformulation just proved turns the problem into an
edge-set-quantified property, which is the precise input format of the MSO transfer theorems;
and the sparsity bound `e ≤ 3(n-1)` for decomposable graphs already bounds the instances that
need to be considered.
title: The certificate reformulation just proved turns the problem into an

description: Prove that the general Artin reciprocity map, specialized to `K = ℚ` and a cyclotomic extension, agrees on every rational prime coprime to the conductor with the catalog map sending a residue-class unit to the automorphism `ζ ↦ ζ^p`.
title: Compatibility with cyclotomic reciprocity over `ℚ`

description: Before attempting a universal constant for arbitrary convex bodies, formalize an available dimension-dependent lower bound. This would validate the full geometric interface without presupposing the unresolved dimension-free step.
title: Dimension-dependent bounds

description:
**Minimax as a theorem, not a pair of facts.** State the game explicitly as a
  two-player zero-sum game and prove `value = 0` via a genuine minimax equality
  (e.g. from Mathlib's convexity/`sInf`–`sSup` interchange), rather than the
  matched upper/lower bounds provided here.
title: Minimax as a theorem, not a pair of facts.

description: Define finite alternatives, strict linear orders, voter profiles, social welfare functions, Pareto unanimity, independence of irrelevant alternatives, and dictatorship. Prove Arrow's theorem combinatorially on that domain.
title: Formalize the actual Arrow domain

description:
Prove equivalences between normalized max-plus,
   min-plus, and projective formulations of tropical convexity.
title: Convention comparisons

description:
The planar case is already an equality, proved and cross-checked
numerically (Section 3 of `ComputationalEvidence.md`); the only missing
ingredient is the inclusion–exclusion over the subspace lattice in dimension
`k ≥ 3`, where the current data show the naive formula fails.
title: The planar case is already an equality, proved and cross-checked

description:
Investigate algebras generated by interval cells together with
   infinitesimal atoms.  Compatibility constraints must be checked carefully: equal mass for every
   real point does not by itself determine interval masses.
title: Larger event algebras

description: Replace injective encodings by bounded-distortion codes and prove covering-number lower bounds. This is the appropriate framework when an upload need only preserve selected functional observables rather than every synaptic bit.
title: Approximate and lossy reconstruction
Investigate genuine asymptotics.

description:
Replication at 1.5B parameters, at longer contexts, and across a broader corpus, to establish
whether the retention bands and the size of the gap are stable properties of trained attention or
artefacts of one model and one context length.
title: Scale and corpus robustness

description:
The convolution of two log-concave finitely
   supported sequences of nonnegative integers with no internal zeros is log-concave.  (The
   combinatorial core of Conjecture 2, and reusable well beyond this thread.)
title: Log-concavity of the uniform convolution

description:
For a partition `λ ⊢ n`, compare the number of
squarefree monic polynomials with irreducible-factor degrees `λ` to the number of
permutations with cycle type `λ`, and derive a quantitative `O_n(1/q)` discrepancy.
title: Factorization type distribution

description: Add finite 2-dimensional CW or simplicial complexes, incidence maps, edge lengths, bounded face size, and bounded vertex degree. Prove that the present `CellularCode` is induced by their cellular chain complex.
title: Geometric cellulations

description:
The present development proves the standard
   clopen-basis certificate for dimension zero. If a covering-dimension API is
   added to Mathlib, connect that certificate to the library's formal Lebesgue
   covering dimension.
title: Formal covering dimension

description: Represent Eve's coherent interaction with all transmitted systems and an ancilla. Formalize purification, deferred measurement, symmetrization, and a justified reduction from coherent attacks to a tractable attack class.
title: Arbitrary quantum attacks

description:
> For every `n`, `d` and every `A ⊆ 𝔽₂ⁿ`, the odd-intersection probability in the **flat**
> model equals `oddProb n (d+1) A · 2^{n(d+1)} / #{independent (d+1)-tuples}` up to a factor
> `1 + O(2^{d-n})`; consequently every bound proved here transfers verbatim to `d`-flats.
title: > For every `n`, `d` and every `A ⊆ 𝔽₂ⁿ`, the odd-intersection probability in the flat

description: Formalize a finite probability space and prove the union bound directly for arbitrary civilization events. The present product formula specifically encodes independence, while Markov’s inequality only needs a nonnegative count.
title: Dependence without independence

description: Refine `bekensteinBits` using a dimensional-quantity library, so radius, energy, action, and velocity cannot be mixed incorrectly. Concrete bounds could then be derived from explicitly stated empirical assumptions.
title: Physical units and constants

description: There is a tropical S-pair construction on finite polynomial families such that a family is a Gröbner basis on a finite divisor-closed test set exactly when every S-pair whose support lies in that test set reduces to zero.
title: Finite tropical S-pair criterion

description: Equip invariant patterns with probability distributions and prove Shannon-entropy bounds. The current exact cardinality theorem gives the uniform-capacity value but does not formalize probabilistic musical entropy.
title: Entropy beyond support size

description: Under positive mass, coupling, and radius, define the uniform circular solution and verify the vector ODE. This would turn the algebraic critical-point result into an existence theorem for an actual trajectory.
title: Construct the circular trajectory explicitly

description: Keep astronomical assumptions outside the mathematical theorem: observational estimates of candidate counts and biological filter probabilities require data and cannot be established by pigeonhole arguments alone.
title: Empirical separation

description:
Exhaustively classify the smallest chordal graphs for which a
   maximum-degree spill fails, with the exhaustive search reflected by a kernel-checked finite
   theorem rather than an external computation.
title: Minimal counterexamples

description:
Connect the analytic divergence hypothesis to the combinatorial hypotheses needed for
   completeness of every tail. The theorem `stronglyComplete_iff_eventually_complete_tails`
   then turns this into strong completeness directly.
title:
Connect the analytic divergence hypothesis to the combinatorial hypotheses needed for
   completeness of every tail.

description:
If `x` lies in the interior
   of a maximal affine piece of `μ.rate`, the supporting tilt `θ` of
   `exists_affine_chord` is unique; the tilt is non-unique exactly at the breakpoints of
   Conjecture 1.
title: Uniqueness of the supporting tilt at a non-breakpoint

description: The present independence result uses semantic soundness. Separate consistency, 1-consistency, and omega-consistency, and formalize the original Gödel and Rosser arguments under their standard weaker hypotheses.
title: Sharper consistency assumptions

description: The predicate `TwinPrimeGaps.ArbitrarilyLargePrimePairs 246` holds. Together with the proved reduction `liminf_primeGap_le_246_of_maynard_output`, this gives `Filter.atTop.liminf TwinPrimeGaps.primeGap ≤ 246`.
title: Unconditional bounded-gap endpoint

description:
There is a strict hierarchy of hints for semiprimes:
`φ(N)` ⟹ factorisation (proved) ⟹ `λ(N)` ⟹ ... ⟹ `g` ⟹ nothing,
and `g` sits strictly below `λ(N) = lcm(p-1,q-1)` in the sense that there are
infinitely many pairs of semiprimes with equal `g` and different `λ`.
title:
There is a strict hierarchy of hints for semiprimes:
`φ(N)` ⟹ factorisation (proved) ⟹ `λ(N)` ⟹ ...

description:
If the period is odd then
   `x² − N y² = −1` is soluble, i.e. `N` is a sum of two coprime squares.  This
   project proves the obstruction direction only
   (`negPell_prime_factor_ne_three_mod_four`).
title: Converse of the negative-Pell dichotomy

description:
Fix chord extraction,
   transposition normalization, treatment of repetitions, metric, filtration convention,
   coefficient field, aggregation statistic, train/test separation, and uncertainty estimates.
title: Specify the empirical protocol before testing genre claims

description:
`cdet` satisfies a cofactor expansion
   along the first column for *any* matrix; for right-quantum matrices one expects the full
   set of quantum Cramer identities and a quantum Jacobi ratio theorem.
title: Laplace expansion and Cramer-type identities

description:
Formalize "many nearly-periodic
   components": a partition of the vertex set into parts each with small
   periodicity ratio, with guarantees in terms of the higher eigenvalues of the
   rotated Laplacian.
title: Almost-periodic decompositions

description:
For SSA/chordal interference graphs, test `χ = ω`, not
   `χ = max(Δ+1,ω)`. Record maximum degree separately as a general upper-bound parameter; it
   does not determine the exact chromatic number.
title: Correct the empirical target

description:
Formalize only accurately sourced historical FLT criteria involving Fibonacci–Wieferich
   primes. Such criteria are subtler than an equivalence with FLT itself; the counterexample at
   exponent 3 rules out that naive formulation.
title:
Formalize only accurately sourced historical FLT criteria involving Fibonacci–Wieferich
   primes.

description:
Classify fibers over `Z/p^r Z`, count their
   cardinalities, and prove compatibility of solutions under reduction. This
   would turn the qualitative local statements into finite local-density
   factors.
title: Prime-power local theory

description: Derive the orbit count from fixed-point counts via Burnside's lemma. This would connect geometric generators (translations, rotations, reflections, and glides) to computable pattern capacities.
title: Burnside counting

description: Define the renormalization-group differential equation and turn the positive linearization calculation into a local stability or instability theorem, with the direction of RG time stated explicitly.
title: Stability as a dynamical statement

description:
Establish
   completeness or identify incomplete directions. If completeness holds,
   develop consequences such as uniqueness of geodesics between points and
   convexity of squared distance.
title: Sectional/geodesic consequences of nonpositive curvature

description:
Study proper scoring rules, where reported probabilities replace a single
   randomized Boolean action.
title:
Study proper scoring rules, where reported probabilities replace a single
   randomized Boolean action.

description:
Compare the proved
   parameters against the quantum Singleton bound using the number of physical
   edge qubits `N=n·2^(n-1)`, rather than using the cube dimension `n` as though it
   were block length.
title: Add quantum-code bounds with the correct block length

description: Investigate whether a genuine dark predicate exists under the exact external reading of `PA ⊬ T(n)`. Compare this with the numerical existence property and witness properties of fragments such as HA and constructive arithmetic.
title: Investigate whether a genuine dark predicate exists under the exact external reading of `PA ⊬ T(n)`.

description:
Package `LocalSection` as a
   presheaf on the poset of column subsets, prove the identity and composition
   laws for restrictions, and derive the sheaf condition from the concrete
   gluing theorem.
title: Restriction maps and a bundled sheaf

description:
Relate `rotEnergy` to the eigenvalues of the actual
   matrix `D − A_om` in `Matrix.IsHermitian` form, and prove
   `λ_min ≤ periodicityRatio` as a statement about `Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvalues`.
title: Spectral side

description:
*True but hard*: multivariate tropical rational calculus. The pairwise-sum product
  rule `tmax_add_tmax` generalizes verbatim, but the median/sharpness argument does not:
  in `ℝ^d` the `L¹` minimizer is a coordinatewise median only for separable losses.
title: True but hard*: multivariate tropical rational calculus.

description: Test candidate examples from nonstandard models, Rosser-style constructions, and recursively inseparable sets. Every candidate must include a proof that PA proves the existential and a metatheorem excluding every standard named instance.
title: Test candidate examples from nonstandard models, Rosser-style constructions, and recursively inseparable sets.

description: Add mean subtraction and variance normalization, prove invariance under shifts and positive rescaling, and then compose this nonlinear normalization with the learned affine stage already formalized.
title: Full layer normalization

description: Add the shift map on streams, its induced map on compatible threads, and a conjugacy theorem. Extend from the full binary shift to subshifts of finite type presented by finite transition graphs.
title: Formalize symbolic dynamics

description: Formalize finite truncations of `-ζ'/ζ`, whose coefficients are the von Mangoldt function. Its frequencies still include prime powers, but its support encodes primes in a mathematically correct way.
title: Prime-sensitive signal

description: Distinguish locality notions. IIA is pairwise informational separability, not locality in the topology of a smooth manifold; any geometric reformulation must prove an equivalence rather than identify them by analogy.
title: Distinguish locality notions.

description: Define Chebyshev distance and prove `dependencyCone t p` equals the square of radius `t` around `p`. This improves the current coarse bound from `9^t` to the exact `(2t+1)^2` distinct input cells.
title: Sharper geometric light cone

description: Formalize compact sequence domains, continuous sequence-to-sequence maps, and a genuine uniform universal-approximation theorem using an available neural-network or Stone–Weierstrass development.
title: Continuous universality

description: Add block-length-dependent confidence, smoothing, authentication, and leakage terms. These distinguish the proved asymptotic threshold from the lower tolerable QBER of practical finite blocks.
title: Finite-key rates

description:
`Σ_g |X^g|^k = (B_k + Σ_P (m_P − 1))·|G|`
    (`bell_defect_eq`): the excess of a moment over its Bell floor is `|G|` times the number of
    *extra* orbits per pattern, and it vanishes exactly for `k`-transitive actions
    (`sum_patternMultiplicity_sub_one_eq_zero_iff`).

---



## Open conjectures for the next cycle



### Conjecture E′ (the fibre spectrum is a strictly finer invariant)

*The vector `(m_P)_P` of pattern multiplicities separates pairs of actions that the scalar moment
`Σ_g |X^g|^k` cannot; and `m_P = 1` for all `P` with exactly `j` blocks iff the action is
`j`-transitive (the block-graded refinement of the fibrewise criterion).*

The key insight is that the fibrewise criterion now proved treats all patterns at once, whereas the
transitivity hierarchy is graded by the number of blocks: restricting attention to the patterns
with `j` blocks should isolate exactly `j`-transitivity inside the `k`-tuple data, giving a
spectrum of invariants between the moments.

Why now? The decomposition, the fibrewise criterion and the exact defect formula are proved
(items 18–19), and cycle 3 also shows the scalar moment cannot separate actions (item 15), so the
only thing left to test is whether the refined vector can.



### Conjecture F (Bell defect bounds the failure of transitivity)

*The Bell defect `D_k(G,X) := Σ_g |X^g|^k − B_k|G| ≥ 0` satisfies: `D_k = 0 ⇒ D_j = 0` for `j ≤ k`
(proved), and quantitatively `D_2 > 0 ⇒ D_k ≥ c_k · D_2` for an explicit combinatorial constant
`c_k` depending only on `k`.*

The key insight is that the defect counts non-singleton fibres of the orbit-to-pattern map with
multiplicity, and a failure of 2-transitivity is inherited by every longer tuple by padding with
repeated coordinates, which multiplies the excess by a controlled partition count.

Why now? Non-negativity, the implication `D_k = 0 ⇒ D_j = 0`, and now the exact formula
`D_k = |G|·Σ_P (m_P − 1)` (item 19) are theorems; only the quantitative propagation between
different `k` is open, and it is now a statement about fibre sizes rather than about moments.



### Conjecture G (how much labelling an injective aggregate must spend)

*Every injective aggregate `A : (Fin m → QLaurent) → QLaurent` that is additive in each argument
must spread the coefficients over at least `m` pairwise disjoint infinite sets of exponents; in
particular no such aggregate has image contained in the series supported on a set of density
`< 1/m`.*

The key insight is that cycle 3 identified symmetry as the obstruction, so what remains is a
counting bound: injectivity forces the aggregate to reserve, for each index, an infinite family of
independent coefficient slots, which is exactly what the interleaving construction does with the
residues mod `m`.

Why now? The dichotomy (interleaving injective, every symmetric aggregate non-injective) is proved;
the missing piece is a lower bound showing interleaving is not just *an* answer but essentially the
*only* shape of answer.

description:
This sub-conjecture
   of the previous cycle is settled in the form `eventually_exists_dense_no_cube`
   (`CubeSharp.lean`) together with `exists_proper_cube_of_density_int` (`CubeProper.lean`):
   properness had to be added on **both** sides, since a `δ`-dense set always contains short
   progressions and hence *degenerate* cubes of every dimension.  What remains is the
   second-order term: the avoidance condition costs `(d+1)·log n` (one parameter per
   generator plus the base point) while the existence condition costs `2^d log(4/δ) + 2d`,
   so the critical `d` is determined only up to an additive `log₂(d) + O(1)`.  Conjecture:
   the truth is the existence side, i.e. for every `ε > 0` every `δ`-dense `S ⊆ [n]`
   contains a proper cube of every dimension `d ≤ (1 − ε)·log₂(log n / log(1/δ))`, and some
   `δ`-dense `S` contains none of dimension `d ≥ (1 + ε)·log₂(log n / log(1/δ))`.
title: (cube dimension is sharp — now a theorem, up to `log log log n`)

description:
**Status update.**  The composite-`m` attainment conjectured earlier in this
thread is now a theorem (`extremal_collision_value_general`): the mixture of a
uniformly random bijection (mass `1 - 1/m`) with a uniformly random constant
(mass `1/m`) is *exactly* `2`-universal for every `m` and attains `1/m`.  What
remains open is whether the extremal family is *strongly* `2`-universal.

**Conjecture.**  For every `m ≥ 2` the bijection–constant mixture is pairwise
independent: `P(h x = u, h y = v) = 1/m²` for all `u, v` and all distinct keys
`x, y`.  Consequently the extremal value `1/m` is attained inside the class of
strongly `2`-universal families for every `m`, not only for primes.

The key insight is that pairwise independence for the mixture reduces to the
permutation count `|{σ : σ x = u, σ y = v}| = (m-2)!` for `u ≠ v` together with
the vanishing of the bijection branch on the diagonal, i.e. to elementary
counting rather than to field structure; the prime hypothesis in
`affine_pairwiseIndependent` is an artefact of the construction.

**Why now?**  `mix_exactly2Universal` and `mixLaw_prob_constant_branch` already
reduce every mixture probability to a pair of `Finset` cardinalities, so only
the permutation counts are missing.

title: Strong universality of the extremal mixture

description:
**Conjecture.**  For a `k`-wise independent family (`k ≥ 3`) and `n` keys, the
probability that some `k` keys land in the same bucket is at least
`1/m^{k-1}`, and this is sharp — attained by the degree-`(k-1)` polynomial
family over `ZMod p`.

The key insight is that the reverse Markov argument survives verbatim once
`X` counts ordered `k`-tuples: the expectation is `n^{\underline{k}}/m^{k-1}`
and the trivial bound is `X ≤ n^{\underline{k}}`, so the ratio is again
independent of `n`; only the sharpness construction changes.

**Why now?**  `collisionProb_ge_of_pairwise_lower` is already stated with an
abstract per-pair lower bound `δ`, so the `k`-tuple version needs only a
`Finset` of `k`-tuples in place of `offDiag`.

description:
**The key insight is** that the hump of the uniform-mixture residual is not a
property of the pair `(power law, Dickman surrogate)` but a property of the
*exponent*: the algebraic log-slope `(1 - (b-1)x)/(x(1+x))` and the exponential
correction `1/(e^x - 1)` become tangent at a single critical `b_c`, above which
no sign change survives.  The bracket `(11/10, 3/2)` is proved; unverified
root-finding puts `b_c ≈ 1.1605`, and the reported bootstrap interval
`[0.991, 1.218]` straddles it.  **Why now?**  Both endpoints of the bracket are
theorems (`uniformResidual_peak`, `uniformMixtureResidual_strictAntiOn`), so the
remaining task is the tangency system — a two-equation, two-unknown problem in
elementary transcendental functions — and it converts a numerical observation
into a decidable experimental target.
title: Critical exponent for mixture-hump onset

description:
The criterion itself was closed during the cycle: a sweep attains the maximal effective
dimension $2^{|P \setminus \{2\}|}$ **iff** the numbers $p - 1$ over the odd primes of $P$ have
pairwise distinct subset products, and the prime set $\{3,7,13\}$ shows that the criterion bites,
since $(3-1)(7-1) = 13-1$. What remains open is the arithmetic classification. **The key insight
is** that the effective dimension of a divisibility sweep is not a property of $P$ at all but of
the multiset $\{p-1\}$ as a *multiplicative Sidon system*, so the question becomes: for which
sets of odd primes are the subset products of $p-1$ distinct, and what is the density of such
sets among all $k$-subsets of the first $n$ primes? **Why now?** Selection-corrected inference
over cell sweeps needs the effective count, and with the criterion settled the remaining question
is a clean multiplicative-combinatorics problem, testable exhaustively for small $k$.
title: A. Which prime sets have distinct subset products?

description:
All exact statements above concern *whole* periods. In a truncated window $[0, N)$ with $N$ not a
multiple of $L$, the count deviates from $N\kappa(\sigma)/L$ by a boundary term. **The key insight
is** that inclusion–exclusion writes the deviation as a signed sum of at most $2^{|P|}$ fractional
parts, so the discrepancy is bounded by a constant depending only on $|P|$ — never on $N$ — and
the sharp constant should be $2^{|P|-1}$, attained at a window end aligned with the extremal cell.
**Why now?** Every finite-sample estimate of a cell rate uses truncated windows, so the sharp
boundary constant is exactly the deterministic part of the error budget that a calibrated null
must not absorb.

(The no-go direction proposed for this slot in-cycle — exact independence of a cell from every
coprime-measurable statistic — was closed during the cycle and now appears above as an established
theorem rather than a conjecture.)
title: B. Sharp discrepancy of cell counts in partial windows

**The key insight is** that `horocycle_preserving_iff_translation` is really the

description:
**Conjecture.** On the simplex of a finite sample space, a totally symmetric
3-tensor field that is (i) natural under all Markov embeddings and (ii) annihilated
at every point admitting a weight-preserving sign-reversing involution is a
constant multiple of the Amari–Chentsov tensor.

The key insight is that our involution theorem produces an explicit, purely
combinatorial family of *zeros* of any admissible tensor, and zeros at a
Zariski-dense set of symmetric points plus naturality should be enough to pin the
tensor down without the usual representation-theoretic machinery.

**Why now?** `amariCubic_eq_zero_of_involution` gives the zero set in closed
form, and finite Markov embeddings are combinatorial maps between finite index
sets — the whole statement lives in a category the catalog can already express.
title: Chentsov uniqueness from the involution collapse

description:
**Conjecture.** For a binary graphical model on a graph `G` with pairwise
features, the Amari–Chentsov tensor component `C_{eee}` for an edge feature `e`
factors as `p_e (1 − p_e)(1 − 2 p_e)` and the *mixed* component `C_{ef g}`
vanishes whenever the features `e, f, g` lie in three distinct connected
components — with the converse failing precisely at triangles.

The key insight is that `cum3_binary_feature` and `cum3_mixed_product_eq_zero`
are the two extreme cases (one feature; independent blocks) of a single
inclusion–exclusion statement about third cumulants of indicator features, whose
combinatorics is governed by the cycle structure of `G`.

**Why now?** Both extremes are now formal theorems with a shared proof
(`cum3_expand` plus factorisation), so the interpolating statement is a
combinatorial bookkeeping problem over subgraphs rather than new analysis.
title: Skewness dichotomy for graphical (Ising-type) models

description:
**Conjecture.** A linearly ordered abelian group `G` with order topology is sequentially
discrete (every convergent sequence is eventually constant) if and only if the positive cone
has uncountable coinitiality; and `G` is zero-dimensional iff its archimedean equivalence
classes are non-trivial at every scale.

*The key insight is* that the two proofs given here for `Surreal` never used anything
surreal-specific beyond `exists_pos_lt_seq` and the dyadic halving `2·h_{n+1} = h_n`, so
they should axiomatise into a clean equivalence for divisible ordered groups.

*Why now?* The `Surreal` proofs already isolate exactly these two hypotheses; abstracting
them costs only a re-parametrisation and yields a Mathlib-ready general theorem.

**Test.** State the two directions for `[LinearOrderedAddCommGroup G] [DivisibleBy G ℕ]`
and re-run the present proofs with `powHalf` replaced by an abstract halving sequence.
title: Direction 3 — Sequential discreteness as an axiom-free characterisation

description:
**Conjecture.** Weighting each `(layer, head)` cell by its measured *load-bearingness* (the
end-task degradation caused by corrupting that cell's attention) turns the unweighted aggregate
bound `2√(H·B·∑ₕ SSEₕ)` into a strictly smaller weighted bound, and the front-high/mid-low `R²`
profile is *anti-correlated* with load-bearingness — cells that are easy to predict are the ones
that matter least.

**The key insight is** that the aggregation step is a Cauchy–Schwarz inequality with uniform
weights, and any nonuniform weighting that is negatively correlated with the residual variance
strictly improves it — so measuring load-bearingness converts P3 from a description into a
budget-allocation rule.

**Why now?** `head_aggregate_gap_le` and `heterogeneity_strictly_improves_bound` supply exactly
the unweighted inequality and its strictness criterion; the ablation that measures the weights is
the experiment already scheduled as "next" in the round.

**If true:** cache budget should be allocated per layer by residual variance, not uniformly.
**If false:** uniform budget allocation is optimal and the depth structure of `R²` is a red
herring for deployment.

description:
**Conjecture.** There is no non-trivial translation-invariant, countably additive Borel
measure (real- or surreal-valued) on `Surreal` giving finite non-zero mass to some clopen
monad; equivalently, `Surreal` supports no Haar-type integration theory.

*The key insight is* that `Surreal.not_isCompact_of_mem_nhds` kills the usual construction
of Haar measure from compact neighbourhoods, while zero-dimensionality
(`Surreal.exists_isClopen_subset_of_mem_nhds`) means any candidate measure is determined by
its values on monads — and monads at one scale split into a proper class of monads at
smaller scales, forcing mass `0` or `∞`.

*Why now?* The clopen basis and the non-compactness obstruction are both formalised, so the
statement can be attacked directly as a theorem about finitely additive set functions on the
Boolean algebra generated by monads.

**Test.** Formalise the monad Boolean algebra and prove: a translation-invariant finitely
additive `μ` with `0 < μ(monad 0 1) < ∞` yields a contradiction from a proper-class
partition of `monad 0 1`.
title: Direction 2 — Surreal-valued Haar measure obstruction

description:
**Conjecture.** No pseudo-metric, and more generally no countably generated uniformity, can
metrise the surreal line; consequently a "surreal key space" admits no distinguisher based on
a countable family of statistical tests: any adversary using countably many neighbourhoods of
the true key gains no advantage over one using a single monad.

*The key insight is* that `Surreal.not_small_of_nhds_basis` upgrades non-metrisability into a
statement about *test families*: a countable test family is subsumed by one clopen monad,
which is the exact analogue of "computational indistinguishability at a fixed scale".

*Why now?* The character bound is already formalised for arbitrary small index types, which
is precisely the strength needed to quantify over adversaries indexed by a set.

**Test.** Formalise a distinguisher as a map into `Bool` measurable with respect to the

contrast direction is not an observable: it is built from the two hypothetical predictors
themselves, so a physically realisable test must correlate against a direction in the span of
*measurable* covariates, and the loss is exactly the cosine of the angle between that span and
the contrast direction.  **Why now?** With the optimum pinned exactly, the residual question is
a single projection estimate, and the recorded response `w` already provides one measurable
direction achieving `0.008` out of the optimal `0.0141…`, i.e. cosine `0.5657` — a concrete

description:
*(The previous cycle's Direction 4 — an infinite family of parity witnesses — is now proved:
`halving_obstruction_family`, together with the completeness statement
`isSidon_insert_iff_avoid`. What follows replaces it.)*

**Conjecture.** For every `n ≥ 4` the greedy set `greedySet n` is *not* a perfect difference
set: reduced modulo `q = n² − n + 1` its differences never cover all nonzero residues. The
Singer family and the greedy family intersect only in the degenerate range `n ≤ 3`.

The key insight is that a perfect difference set is an algebraically rigid object — Singer
sets come from the action of a Frobenius-type cyclic group on a projective plane — while the
greedy rule is purely order-theoretic and locally minimal, so the two selection principles
should be incompatible beyond the trivial cases; the leftover residues should be forced by
the rigidity result `greedy_valid_gt`, which pins each greedy value as the least admissible
one rather than an algebraically distinguished one.

**Why now?** The base cases are already formalised (`greedySet_three_perfect` shows
perfection modulo `7` at `n = 3`, `greedySet_four_not_perfect` shows the residue `5` is
missed modulo `13` at `n = 4`), and the exact step criterion `isSidon_insert_iff_avoid` gives
a handle on which residues a greedy extension can create, which is precisely what an
induction on `n` needs. Numerically the conjecture holds for every `n` up to `9`, with an
increasing number of missed residues.
