description:
**Conjecture.**  For every wolf count `k ≥ 1` and every population `n`, the quantity
`n · (failProb (n−k) k / k)²` lies strictly below `1` when `n` is even and at or above `1`
when `n` is odd — that is, the separator `1 = √(2/π) · √(π/2)` proved for `k = 1`
(`failProb_sq_parity_even`, `failProb_sq_parity_odd`) governs *every* wolf count, at every
finite population, with no asymptotics.

**The key insight is** that the separator is exactly the geometric mean of the two limiting
constants (`parity_constants_geometric_mean`), and the identity
`surv n · surv (n+1) = 1/(n+1)` says the survival ladder is *self-reciprocal* about that
mean — a symmetry that the union bound preserves up to the `C(k,2)/n` defect, which is
precisely the size needed for the inequality to survive division by `k`.

**Why now?**  The `k = 1` case is proved by a purely rational certificate, and
`defect_scaled_le` supplies exactly the quantitative control on `failProb / k` needed to
propagate the argument to general `k`.  The remaining step is a comparison between
`C(k,2)/(kn)` and the gap `1 − n·surv n²`, both now explicitly bounded.

*If true*: the parity dichotomy holds pointwise, not just asymptotically, for the whole
family — an unusually strong form of a "two expansions" statement.  *If false*: there is a
small-`n`, large-`k` window in which the union-bound defect overwhelms the separator, and
locating it would pin down the exact regime of validity of the inclusion–exclusion
heuristic.

description:
Computationally (see `ComputationalEvidence.md`) the humor/rating correlation is
`+0.97` below a surprise threshold and `−0.97` above it, with a global correlation of
only `+0.04`. The conjecture is that this threshold is not a psychological accident but
the point where the submodular valuation stops being *supermodular on the diagonal*: a
rating functional `R` that is a concave increasing transform of a submodular valuation
necessarily monovaries with the valuation on a down-set and antivaries on its
complement, and the crossover is the unique maximiser of `R`.

**The key insight is** that an inverted-U rating curve is exactly what a *concave*
utility applied to a *submodular* surprise valuation must look like, so the empirical
Wundt curve is a theorem about concavity, not a fact about people.
**Why now?** Both halves are now formalised: submodularity is proved here, and
Chebyshev monovariance machinery is in Mathlib, so the crossover statement can be
attacked directly.
title: Wundt Threshold for Submodular Valuations

description:
**Conjecture:** the map `domain ↦ knee-curve` has finite image over natural text
domains at fixed model and context, and the number of deployment entries needed
for a fleet is the interval-cover number of that image — so fleets never need
more than `⌈(k_max − k_min)/(δ+1)⌉ + 1` cache sizes, with equality only for
arithmetic ladders.
*The key insight is* that the covering side of our min–max is greedy and
anchor-free, so the fleet cost depends only on the spread of knees, never on how
many domains sit inside it.
*Why now?* The three-domain table is already `{12, 16}`; adding LaTeX-heavy
math, code-with-comments and non-English prose is a direct falsification test of
"finite image, small spread".
title: D4 — Sparsity classes are a coarse quotient of domains

description:
**Conjecture.** The model-level knee equals the maximum of the per-head knees up to a
bounded additive defect, and the defect is controlled by the spread of the per-head
head-mass totals: `k*(Σ heads) ≤ max_j k*(head j)` always (proved), with equality unless
one head carries a vanishing share of the total mass.

The key insight is that the pass inequalities add, so aggregation can only be limited by
the worst head, while the *mediant* structure of retained mass prevents a large gap
unless the mass shares are extremely unequal. **Why now?** This is exactly the P2
measurement the round dropped in the crash-recovery rewrite; the theorem says the
per-layer/per-head stats block is not a nice-to-have but the only way to explain a
model-level knee mechanistically.
title: Per-Head Knee Spectrum and the Worst-Head Law

description:
Can a tiny predictor, trained to forecast the next row's top-`B` set from the prefix, close the
gap? It cannot in the worst case — a learned head is still a causal policy and so is covered by the
impossibility theorem — but the sharp empirical question is whether it reduces the *measured*
defect. This is the cleanest test of whether the deployed gap is estimator-limited or
information-limited on real text.
title: Learned importance heads

description:
**Conjecture.** For every odd prime `m`, the Chebyshev-type coefficient
`A_m(t)` (`A₀ = 0`, `A₁ = 1`, `A_{n+2} = t·A_{n+1} − A_n`) factors as
`A_m(t) = Ψ_m(t) · (−1)^{(m−1)/2} Ψ_m(−t)`, where `Ψ_m` is the minimal
polynomial of `ζ_m + ζ_m⁻¹`, and moreover `A_{m−1}(t) + 1 = Ψ_m(t) · R_m(t)`
with `R_m` coprime to `Ψ_m` modulo every prime `p ∤ m`. Consequently `Ψ_m` has
a root mod `p` iff `p ≡ ±1 (mod m)`, for all odd prime conductors at once.

*The key insight is* that `A_m` is the "order-`m` locus" of the trace map on
`SL₂`, and the two factors correspond to the two ways an order-`m` element can
arise, `ζ + ζ⁻¹` and `−(ζ + ζ⁻¹)`; the second condition `A_{m−1} = −1` is
precisely what discards the `−` branch.

*Why now?* `TraceOrder.cheb_root_iff` already reduces the arithmetic to these
two polynomial identities, and they were verified and proved by `ring` for
`m = 5, 7, 11` (`TraceOrder.golden_iff`, `TraceOrder.cubic_seven_iff`,
`TraceOrder.quintic_eleven_iff`). In each case the Bézout identity between the
two spurious factors turned out to be *integral* (denominator 1), which is the
uniform statement one has to prove. Only the uniform-in-`m` factorisation is
missing; it is a statement about `ℤ[t]`, not about primes, so it is within
reach of a resultant computation.
title: Chebyshev Factorisation of the Real Cyclotomic Tower

description:
**Conjecture.** For composite `N` coprime to `p`, a companion matrix
`!![t, −1; 1, 0]` over `𝔽_p` has exact order `N` iff `N` divides the exponent of
the cyclic group generated by a suitable Frobenius eigenvalue — concretely, iff
`N ∣ p − 1` or `N ∣ p + 1`. The union `N ∣ p²−1` used in the prime case is
*strictly larger* than `(N ∣ p−1) ∨ (N ∣ p+1)` once `N` has two prime factors,
so the criterion genuinely changes shape at composite level.

*The key insight is* that for prime `m` the group `⟨u⟩` of order `m` must sit
inside either `𝔽_p^*` or the norm-one subgroup of `𝔽_{p²}^*`, and for composite
`N` it can straddle the two, splitting as a product.

*Why now?* `TraceOrder.exists_companion_order_iff` is stated and proved for odd
primes `m` only because primality is used twice (Cauchy's theorem and a
coprimality step); both uses are localisable, so the composite case is a
refinement of an existing proof rather than a new one. It is also the exact
statement needed to move from prime conductors to conductors such as
`m = 9, 15, 16`, i.e. to the full real cyclotomic tower.

description:
**Status of the ambient problem.** The *finiteness* of the test is no longer open: this
cycle proves in Lean that cycle-bijectivity over an alphabet with `q` letters is decided by
the cycle lengths `1, …, q⁴` (`cycleBijectiveA_iff_upTo`, ternary form
`cycleBijective_iff_upTo_81`).  What remains open is the sharp constant.

**Conjecture.** The bound can be lowered from `q⁴` to `q²`: a radius-one rule is bijective
on every finite cycle as soon as its global map is injective on the cycles of length
`1, 2, …, q²`; and `q²` is attained for `q = 2`.

Exhaustive computation gives maximal first-failure length `4 = 2²` for `q = 2` and `8` for
`q = 3` (`ComputationalEvidence.md`, §3), against the proved bound `q⁴ = 81`.  The affine
sharpness theorem `affine_eight_test_sharp` realises the value `8` in Lean, so for `q = 3`
the truth is pinched between `8` and `9`.

*The key insight is* that in the splicing argument the pigeonhole is currently run over all
`q⁴` pair-graph states, whereas a difference between the two configurations can only be
transported through the states that are *reachable while the difference persists*; counting
those states — a pair `(x,x')` with `x ≠ x'` together with one shared context letter —
gives roughly `q²` instead of `q⁴`, which is exactly the conjectured bound.

*Why now?* The whole infrastructure is in place and machine-checked: `HasCollision`
converts an injectivity failure into a periodic pair of sequences, `periodic_loop` and
`collision_of_loop` perform the splice, and `exists_small_collision` runs the induction.
Improving the constant is a matter of replacing the pigeonhole set, not of redoing the
argument, and it would make the exhaustive `q = 4` classification computationally
realistic.
title: Direction 1 — Quadratic Cycle-Length Barrier

description:
**Conjecture.** Because the value bound `δ_V` is additive and unamplified, value
caches remain quality-neutral (`< 1%` PPL) down to 2 bits, and the first
significant loss appears at 1 bit, where `δ_V` becomes comparable to `‖v‖_∞`.

*The key insight is* that the proved value term never interacts with the query
norm or the depth, so the only scale it can be compared against is `‖v‖_∞`
itself — the breakdown must occur at `δ_V ≈ ‖v‖_∞`, i.e. at one bit.

*Why now?* K16/V4 measured `+0.17%`, far below any plausible cliff; the model
predicts the *next* two arms (V2, V1) exactly, and one of them must fail if the
theory is right.
title: Value quantisation is free at 2 bits, and 1 bit is where it breaks

description:
`share_sub_inv_card_le_relClusterSD` is a deterministic bound at a fixed profile.  What a
future gate needs is the *typical* floor when clusters are drawn from the hypotenuse
distribution.  **The key insight is** that the max/mean ratio of hypotenuse cluster sizes
grows like a divisor-type function, so the design effect should grow like a power of
`log`, not stay bounded.  **Why now?** The exact bootstrap variance identity is proved, so
a distributional statement can be phrased as a statement about `∑ (xᵢ − x̄)²` alone.
title: Distributional floor, not just worst-case floor

description:
**Conjecture.** Perplexity damage under key quantisation is governed not by the
worst-case margin but by the *mass* of tokens whose margin is below
`2‖q‖₁δ_K`: `ΔPPL/PPL ≈ C · P(margin < 2‖q‖₁δ_K)` with a model-independent `C`.

*The key insight is* that `strictTop_of_margin` is a per-token certificate, so the
aggregate loss is a measure of the certificate's failure set, and the softmax
`ℓ¹` bound `e^{2η} − 1` controls the damage each failed token can contribute.

*Why now?* The two ingredients (per-token certificate, per-token damage bound)
are both formal theorems in this cycle; only the aggregation step is missing,
and it is a statement about one measurable distribution.
title: Margin-mass criterion replacing worst-case margin

description:
**Conjecture.** For a sweep set `S` whose smallest passing point is `g` and whose largest
failing point below `g` is `p`, the true knee lies in `(p, g]`, and for *every* `t` in
that interval there is a monotone profile matching all measurements on `S` with knee `t`.
Hence a sweep determines the knee iff `g = p + 1`.

The key insight is that a monotone profile is free inside a grid hole, so the resolving
power of a sweep is the fineness of its consecutive gaps *around the crossing*, not its
overall density.  Why now? The `p = 12`, `g = 20` case is fully proved in both directions
(`Net62.true_knee_bracket`, `Net62.bracket_tight`); the general statement is the same
construction with `S` abstract.
title: Tight hole brackets for arbitrary sweeps with gaps

description:
**Conjecture.** The Dedekind completion of the surreal line (adding all gaps such as `On`
and the infinitesimal gap) is a compact, connected, non-metrizable linear continuum in which
`Surreal` embeds as a dense, totally disconnected, nowhere-locally-compact subspace; and
`Surreal` itself is a Baire space.

*The key insight is* that our clopen cuts are exactly the gaps of the surreal line, so total
disconnectedness measures the abundance of gaps, and completing the order must restore
connectedness while destroying first countability at every point.

*Why now?* `Surreal.smallerPart` gives an explicit, formalised supply of gaps, which is the
hard half of building the completion.

**Test.** Formalise the cut completion of `Surreal` for small families, prove density of the
image, and prove that a countable intersection of dense open sets in `Surreal` is dense using
`exists_pos_lt_seq`.
title: Direction 4 — Gaps, Dedekind completion and the Baire property

description:
**Conjecture.** If a knee chain `k(1) < ⋯ < k(r)` lies in `[1, N]`, a doubling sweep
reports at most `clog₂N + 1` distinct values, so for `r > clog₂N + 1` at least
`r − clog₂N − 1` reported "plateaus" are artifacts; moreover the number of *genuine*
strict increases such a sweep can certify equals the number of octaves the chain meets,
minus one.

The key insight is that the information content of a coarse sweep is bounded by the size
of its grid inside the window, independently of the model, so flatness claims (such as
the `{16, 16}` size-invariance reading) are counting artifacts until the octave count is
checked.  Why now? `card_verdicts_dyad_le` gives the bound and `read_strictMono_reflect`
the reflection principle; only the chain-level bookkeeping remains.
title: Octave-collapse bound on certifiable chain length

description:
**Conjecture.** Let `stair b j = 2^b(2^j − 1)` be the NET-47 knee family.  A doubling
sweep reads `stair b j` as `2^(b+j)` for all `j ≥ 2`, with relative overstatement
`2^j/(2^j − 1) → 1`; and an arithmetic sweep of step `d` resolves *every* rung of the
weight-`n` ladder iff `d ∣ 2`, since the `2`-adic valuation of `stair b j` is exactly `b`
and the ladder contains the rung with `b = 1`.

The key insight is that binary staircases are simultaneously as far as possible from the
dyadic grid and highly divisible, so they separate the two grid families sharply.  Why
now? `Net62.stair_dyad_read` proves the first clause; the ladder-wide statement combines
it with `KneeStaircase.factorization_two_stair`, already in the catalog.
title: Staircase knees are dyadically invisible

description:
**Conjecture.** For any finite family of context-stable heads the merged budget equals the maximum
of the per-head budgets exactly — not merely up to the sandwich between the smallest and largest
per-head knee — and is therefore independent of the number of heads.

**Test.** Measure per-head knees separately and check that the model-level knee coincides with the
worst head's, across head counts and context lengths.
title: Head-count invariance of the budget

description:
**Conjecture.** For a fixed `S₃` cubic field with discriminant `D`, the empirical mutual
information computed from the primes below `X` satisfies
`|I_X(p mod |D| ; T) - 1| = O(X^{-1/2 + ε})` under GRH, and `O((log X)^{-A})` unconditionally.

*The key insight is* that the mutual information is a smooth function of the four class
frequencies, so the Chebotarev error term transfers to the information with the same exponent up
to a constant depending only on `|G|`.

*Why now?* The catalog's `ChebotarevGeodesic*` files already formalise an error-exponent calculus
(`HasErrorExponent`, `exponent_of_inverse_transform`), which is exactly the interface needed to
turn a density error into an entropy error.
title: C4. A quantitative Chebotarev-with-error version of the one-bit theorem

description:
**Conjecture.** Let `K/ℚ` be a Galois number field of conductor/discriminant
data `d`, and let `T(p)` be the decomposition type of an unramified prime `p`.
The channel `p mod m ↦ T(p)` is fully pinned (`I = H(T)`) for some modulus `m`
if and only if `K/ℚ` is abelian. For non-abelian `K` — the first case being an
`S₃` cubic such as `X³ − X − 1` — every residue channel satisfies
`I(p mod m ; T) < H(T)` strictly, with a computable positive deficit.

*The key insight is* that full pinning is exactly the assertion that the type
map factors through `(ℤ/m)ˣ`, which by Kronecker–Weber is exactly abelianness;
information theory therefore *detects* class field theory.

*Why now?* `CyclicCubic.MI_of_deterministic` and `CyclicCubic.MI_le_right`
turn "fully pinned" into "the label is a function of the residue", a purely
combinatorial predicate that can be tested by `decide` on any finite modulus.
The negative half for `S₃` cubics is a finite computation for each `m`, so the
first counterexample-free evidence is one afternoon of `decide` away.
title: Pinning–Abelianness Dichotomy

description:
**The key insight is** that a hinge law has three parameters but a flat measured
prefix supplies only inequalities, so a measurement grid that starts below the
hinge cannot identify the slope — it can only bound it below.
**Why now?** `hinge_prediction_discriminates` shows the two admissible fits of
the current 1.5B data separate at exactly one point (20 vs 21 keys at 4096), so
one octave of extra data upgrades a lower bound into an identification. The
conjecture to formalise: for a hinge with floor `f`, the slope is identifiable
from a grid iff the grid contains at least two points strictly past the hinge.
title: Slope Identifiability of Hinge Budget Laws

description:
**Conjecture.** For number fields `K₁, K₂` with Galois groups `G₁, G₂` and coprime discriminants,
the compositum has `I(class ; residue) = log₂ |G₁^ab| + log₂ |G₂^ab|`; the visible information is
additive while the total type entropy is *sub*additive, so the hidden fraction grows.

*The key insight is* that `(G₁ × G₂)^ab = G₁^ab × G₂^ab`, so the abelian ceiling is additive by
`uEnt` of a product read-out, whereas conjugacy classes multiply only up to the class-fusion of the
product group.

*Why now?* The catalog already contains a CRT/product law for the cyclic type channel
(`Shared.CyclicTypeChannelProduct`, `Shared.CyclicTypeChannelCRTLaw`); this direction merges that
line with the abelian-ceiling theorem proved here.
title: C3. Multiplicativity of the visible bits over composita

description:
**Conjecture.** Conjugation by `cayleyMat` carries `SL(2,ℝ)` isomorphically onto
`SU(1,1)`, and under this isomorphism the trace trichotomy `|tr| < 2 / = 2 / > 2`
matches exactly the three normal forms `discPar t`, the diagonal rotation
`diag(e^{iθ}, e^{-iθ})`, and the hyperbolic `!![cosh r, sinh r; sinh r, cosh r]`,
with the parabolic case characterised intrinsically by `discHoro`-invariance.

**The key insight is** that `discPar_normSq_key` (`|den|² - |num|² = 1 - |w|²`) is the
defining `SU(1,1)` form identity written for one element; promoting it from the
parabolic family to all of `SU(1,1)` turns three separate case analyses into one
quadratic-form statement.

**Why now?** `discriminant_dichotomy` already separates the elliptic and parabolic
cases in the disc model; only the hyperbolic branch is missing, and its normal form is
a two-line matrix computation of the same shape as `discPar`.

---
title: Full trichotomy in the SU(1,1) picture

description:
**Conjecture.** Let a demon be an infinite decision tree with an almost surely finite
stopping time `N` (rather than a tree of some finite depth `n`), every node dissipative at
`ΔF`.  Then the three displayed stopping-time bounds hold verbatim, and moreover
`E[total work] ≥ ΔF·E[N]` requires no integrability hypothesis beyond `E[N] < ∞`.

The stopping-time theorem covers every tree of *some* finite depth, uniformly in that
depth, which already forces the conclusion for the truncations `N ∧ n` of an infinite tree.
The open content is the passage to the limit: is `lim_n E[W_{N∧n}] = E[W_N]`, or can a
demon smuggle work into the tail?  We expect uniform integrability to fail exactly when
`E[N] = ∞`, which would make this the horizon-free counterpart of the `T → 0` analysis in
§5.

*Falsifiable:* an infinite tree, all nodes Jarzynski compliant, with `E[N] < ∞` and
`E[total work] < ΔF·E[N]`.
title: Almost-surely finite demons with no horizon at all

description:
**Conjecture.** The critical key bit-width `b*` at which perplexity departs
from control satisfies `b* = log₂(‖q‖₁ R / m) + Θ(1)`, where `m` is the median
top-1 logit margin of the model and `R` the key range; in particular `b*` shifts
by exactly one bit when the query norm doubles.

*The key insight is* that the proved criterion
`2‖q‖₁R/2^b < m` is logarithmic in the amplification, so the cliff is a
*threshold in bits*, not a smooth degradation — a doubling of `‖q‖₁` must be paid
for with exactly one extra key bit.

*Why now?* `decision_preserved_of_key_bits` and `four_bits_destroy_the_decision`
already bracket the threshold from both sides at one scale; instrumenting
`llama.cpp` for `‖q‖₁` and the margin distribution turns the bracket into a
prediction that a single sweep can refute.
title: Query-norm law for the cliff location

description:
**Conjecture.** For pseudo-orbits of the parameter-four logistic map that remain a certified distance from the critical point, a product of local derivative envelopes yields an exponentially smaller shadowing budget than the uniform factor `4^N`, and this adaptive budget is asymptotically sharp on periodic itineraries.

The key insight is that the interval-wide Lipschitz constant four discards orbit information; local derivative products retain the actual itinerary-dependent amplification.

**Why now?** Forward invariance and the global certificate are established, providing a baseline against which a local, itinerary-sensitive refinement can be quantitatively compared.
title: Adaptive logistic-map shadowing beyond the global factor four

description:
**Conjecture.** There is an explicit family of polynomial-size propositional certificates whose shortest paths to normal form under any fixed finite local, conclusion-preserving refinement basis have superpolynomial length.

The key insight is that a small final certificate need not imply a short route to it; local simplification can be obstructed by globally distributed redundancies.

**Why now?** The distinction between well-foundedness and quantitative normalization time is exposed by the audited cost model. Candidate families can be built from repeated substitution, shared lemmas, and forced commuting conversions, giving concrete lower-bound instances.
title: Superpolynomial refinement distance for propositional certificates

description: For a fixed exact cyclotomic realization of the Fibonacci braid matrices, determine the characteristic polynomial of \(\rho(\sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_3)\) and prove that at least one eigenvalue is not a root of unity. This is falsifiable by an exact finite-order computation. **The key insight is** that a non-torsion eigenvalue makes the full integer-power orbit injective and therefore certifies an infinite image. **Why now?** The abstract infinitude theorem identifies precisely the matrix-level fact that must be supplied, while avoiding unreliable floating-point order tests.
title: Exact infinite-order certificate for the three-generator product

description:
**Conjecture.** Let a real polynomial causal return map preserve a closed interval. If it has a fixed point whose derivative has absolute value below one, then every initial state in the immediate basin of that point generates a history converging to a unique self-consistent history within that basin. Basin boundaries are formed by critical or repelling periodic points.

The key insight is that global contraction is stronger than the causal mechanism requires; consistency may be selected locally by a dynamically invariant basin. **Why now?** The global theorem isolates contraction as the decisive ingredient, while the polynomial counterexample shows exactly why a domain-sensitive replacement is needed.
title: Local basin Novikov principle for polynomial feedback

description:
**Conjecture.** Let a finite candidate system be governed by a monotone contracting parallel update. Any fair asynchronous execution that removes only candidates rejected by the current parallel update terminates at the same greatest fixed kernel as synchronous iteration.

The key insight is that monotonicity should turn every fair deletion schedule into a refinement of the same descending fixed-point computation, while fairness prevents a permanently rejected candidate from surviving.

**Why now?** The sharp synchronous stabilization theorem and greatest-kernel characterization isolate exactly the two invariants—descent and maximality—that an asynchronous confluence argument must preserve.
title: Order-independent asynchronous elimination

description:
**Conjecture.** If an implementation deletes one currently rejected candidate at a time, never reintroduces candidates, and eventually selects every continuously rejected candidate, then it performs at most the initial number of candidates in total, regardless of selection order.

The key insight is that serial execution changes the number of rounds but not the strict-cardinality ranking: every effective operation spends one unit of a finite deletion budget.

**Why now?** The concrete least-candidate example attains the abstract bound, showing that a linear estimate is both plausible and sharp rather than an artifact of parallel iteration.
title: Fair serial deletion with a linear total-deletion bound

description:
**Conjecture.** There is a uniformly defined operator on partial functions whose value at an oracle is the diagonal halting predicate relative to that oracle, and it satisfies both jump inequalities at every oracle. Its finite iterates therefore realize the strict order embedding established by the abstract hierarchy.

The key insight is that one universal relativized evaluator should supply both directions: direct simulation gives reducibility to the jump, while self-application and Boolean complementation give strict nonreducibility.

**Why now?** The order-theoretic consequences have been isolated from coding details, so the remaining task has a sharply defined interface: construct one operator and establish exactly two inequalities.
title: A concrete relativized jump realizes every abstract level

description:
Let two prefix-free encodings of the same deductive system translate into one another with additive length overhead at most `b`. Conjecture that their level-`ε` critical indices differ by at most `b`, after correcting for the two alphabet entropies.

The key insight is that a bounded recoding distorts metric balls only by a bounded radial shift, so a threshold should move rather than disappear.

Why now? The entropy–density separation identifies exactly which observables must be compared, while the critical-index theorem isolates monotonicity and a positive crossing level as sufficient hypotheses.
title: Quasi-invariance of critical indices under efficient recoding

description:
For a finitely generated deductive calculus, suppose cumulative derivability counts are submultiplicative up to a polynomial factor and have exponential growth rate strictly below the ambient language. Conjecture that a logarithmically smoothed density is eventually antitone and that every fixed positive level has a transition window of width bounded independently of the cutoff.

The key insight is that submultiplicativity should suppress oscillations that are invisible to exponential growth rates but currently obstruct an intrinsic threshold.

Why now? The existing boundary analysis shows that exponential sparsity alone gives convergence but not a sharp finite crossing; controlling oscillation is the precise missing ingredient.
title: Threshold windows for submultiplicative derivability counts

description:
**Conjecture.** In any extensional dependent calculus with an internal code type closed under dependent products, a decoding operation that represents every predicate on codes entails a fixed point for every endomorphism of truth values.

The key insight is that the dangerous ingredient is not self-membership alone but point-surjective semantic evaluation, which converts diagonal substitution into a universal fixed-point principle.

**Why now?** The predicate-space diagonal obstruction identifies a compact interface whose derivability can be tested independently across proposed impredicative calculi.
title: Impredicative Self-Coding Forces a Lawvere Fixed Point

description:
**Conjecture.** If a self-observation operator is strictly progressive below its
least fixed point — every non-fixed state moves strictly upward and the moves do
not accumulate short of the fixed point — then the least fixed point is the
*unique* fixed point, and iterated self-modelling from any starting state, not
only from the least one, converges to it.

The key insight is that the pre-fixed-point bound (the emergent state lies below
every fixed point using monotonicity alone) already forces uniqueness the moment
one rules out plateaus: the only obstruction to a single global self-image is a
second, higher fixed point, which strict progress forbids.

Why now? The separation established here between the monotone-only bound and the
continuity-driven fixed point property shows exactly which extra hypothesis
(progress, not mere monotonicity) is responsible for uniqueness, making the
contraction refinement a clean next step.
title: Uniqueness of the emergent state under contraction

description: Formalize null, weak, dominant, and averaged energy conditions and identify exactly which fail for classes of shape functions.
title: Energy conditions

sequence alone (not of the model's loss) has retained quality bounded by the
demand-quantile curve, so no policy can beat the knee; and the gap to the oracle

*The key insight is* that our exact tail criterion `knee_le_iff_tail_small`

*Why now?* It would unify NET-61 (`λ = 0` optimal) with NET-70 (domain-invariant
knees) under a single tail-counting bound, and both halves are now formalised.

description:
**Conjecture.** For every certificate tree, augmenting redundant-restatement elimination and named-lemma inlining with a finite family of commuting conversions yields a confluent terminating rewrite system. Consequently, every certificate has a unique normal form up to renaming of hypothesis leaves.

The key insight is that termination has already been separated from uniqueness: natural-valued descent supplies the former, while local diamond properties could supply the latter through a confluence theorem.

**Why now?** Concrete refinement is known to preserve conclusions and strictly decrease audited cost, so the remaining question has a sharply testable form: classify all critical pairs and determine whether they join.
title: Confluence of audited certificate refinement

description:
**Conjecture.** For regularized logistic regression, empirical natural gradient is insensitive to feature covariance conditioning only while the empirical Fisher remains uniformly comparable to the loss Hessian; outside that regime, the rate degrades according to the generalized eigenvalue spread of the Hessian–Fisher pair.

The key insight is that cancellation is controlled by metric–curvature matching, not by the Fisher condition number in isolation.

**Why now?** The diagonal matched model proves exact cancellation and exposes generalized mismatch as the minimal falsifiable parameter for numerical and theoretical comparison.
title: Logistic regression under metric mismatch

description:
Fix `q` and `m`. Conjecturally, every sufficiently long word contains a scattered length-`m` motif with `r` pairwise disjoint occurrences at a threshold asymptotic to `c(q,m)r`, where `c(q,m)` is strictly below `q^m m` for `m ≥ 2`.

The key insight is that large fibers already force multiplicity among aligned blocks, while a disjoint scattered-occurrence theorem could compress the threshold by exploiting many possible embeddings. **Why now?** The established fiber hierarchy provides a precise baseline against which any genuine subsequence gain can be measured.
title: Multiplicity phase transition for repeated genetic motifs

description:
For every prefix-free encoding of a finite derivation family, at least a `1 - 2^{-c}` fraction of derivations require code length at least `log₂ N - c`, where `N` is the family size and the fraction is measured uniformly. A weighted analogue should hold with cardinality replaced by source entropy and code lengths constrained by Kraft mass.

**The key insight is...** the finite pigeonhole obstruction should persist quantitatively when equal-size code bins are replaced by prefix-free weighted cylinders.

**Why now?** The exact count of all shorter binary descriptions supplies the sharp finite endpoint from which a weighted theorem can be developed.
title: Kraft-weighted incompressibility on derivation trees

description:
**Conjecture.** Every state in the stabilized winning region has a least iteration rank, and this rank equals the minimum worst-case capture time among all cops' strategies from that state.

The key insight is that the first table containing a state records the outer existential choice of a cops' move followed by the worst robber response, which is precisely a minimax recurrence. **Why now?** Bounded-horizon correctness already gives one direction; extracting least ranks would turn a yes/no recognizer into a strategy and optimal-capture-time certificate generator.
title: Rank functions as capture-time certificates

description:
**Conjecture.** For finite-type pure pro-spectra, reflection from degree `-n` to degree `n` induces an equivalence after stabilization completion, and this equivalence preserves Euler characteristic, finite component cardinality, and equivariant coindex excess simultaneously.

The key insight is that reflection is an even suspension, while coindex excess is invariant under equal source-target suspension; completion should promote these matching numerical laws to an equivalence of stabilized objects.

**Why now?** Stagewise reflection and exact coindex translation are both available, so the remaining question is whether their agreement is merely numerical or arises from a universal completed object.
title: Completion invariance under two-sided stabilization

description:
**Conjecture.** Under polynomial-overhead mutual simulation, completeness for every reduction-closed language class is preserved, provided both substrates support reduction precomposition with polynomial cost.

The key insight is that completeness combines two independent invariances: transport of bounded decision procedures and closure under semantic precomposition.

**Why now?** These mechanisms have been proved separately in the exact setting, making their asymptotic interaction a sharply formulated next target.
title: Reduction completeness independent of architecture

description:
**Conjecture.** If a state contains both signs of one atom and omits a literal over a distinct atom, then every revision history avoiding that distinct atom preserves omission of that literal, regardless of how often the contradictory atom is revised.

The key insight is that revision is local to one complementary pair, so unrelated coordinates should satisfy a frame property.

**Why now?** The two-atom countermodel establishes the base case, and the local definition of revision makes the proposed persistence law sharply testable by induction on histories.
title: Persistent non-explosion under irrelevant revision

description:
Replace evaluation-preserving equivalences by retractions, embeddings, or bisimulations. Conjecture that embeddings preserve fixed points in one direction, retractions lift them under an explicit coherence law, and bisimulations preserve only observational equivalence of `Y` values rather than literal equality.

The key insight is that exact isomorphism yields equality because both arguments of evaluation are preserved simultaneously; weakening either preservation law should produce a graded notion of fixed-point transport.

Why now? The current naturality theorem gives the strongest endpoint, from which each coherence condition can be removed independently and tested by counterexample.
title: Naturality under weaker simulations

description:
**Conjecture.** The globally additive-avoiding greedy trajectory beginning at one is exactly the odd sequence: its term at index `n` is `2n+1`.

The key insight is that all sums of two earlier odd values are even, while the immediately preceding even candidate is forbidden as the sum of the initial one and the current value. **Why now?** The existence and growth-ceiling results isolate precisely the local admissibility argument needed for an induction, and the initial computations expose the parity invariant.
title: Exact classification of the repaired trajectory

description:
*"A softmax layer with `N` keys has uniform error `≥ c/N` on the identity."* — **False.**
   `SoftmaxResolution.no_universal_softmax_resolution_bound`. The construction is explicit: the
   logit gap `log((x+ε)/(1+ε−x))` makes the two-key head compute `(x+ε)/(1+2ε)`. The
   pigeonhole invariant behind the hard bound (`finitely many realizable outputs`) simply has
   no soft analogue: softmax weights move continuously and the realizable set is an interval.
title: "A softmax layer with `N` keys has uniform error `≥ c/N` on the identity."* — False.

description:
**Conjecture.** Extend `windowSum_pairedOrdinates_eq_zero_iff` beyond the critical line: for any
conjugation-symmetric zero multiset contained in the strip `0 < Re ρ < 1`, `Re H(T) > 0` whenever
the window is nonempty, with the explicit bound `Re H(T) ≥ 2σ_min/(σ_max² + T²)`.  Consequently a
*certified numerical upper bound* on `H(T)` would exclude zeros in the window — a computationally
checkable route to zero-free windows.

*The key insight is* that each conjugate pair contributes `2 Re ρ/|ρ|²`, which is positive
throughout the critical strip, so the statistic can never cancel and its size is a certificate.

*Why now?* `inv_add_conj_inv` already isolates the contribution of a conjugate pair as
`2 Re ρ/|ρ|²`, and the critical-line case is proved; only the uniform bound over the strip
remains.
title: Off-line zeros are detected by the window statistic

description:
**Conjecture.**  For every cost stream (not just replicate/alternating ones), an optimal
schedule exists that changes decoder state at message `i` only if the state it enters is
optimal for at least `D` of the next messages; and this "commit for `D` messages" rule is
optimal within an additive `D` bits.

*The key insight is* that all sharp results so far — `optCost_replicate_eq`
(`n·r + min(D,n)`), `beats_generic_iff` (break-even exactly at `n = D`), and the block law
(`min(2D, L)`) — express the same trade-off: a switch is worth it iff the coherent run it
serves is at least as long as the delta.

*Why now?*  The exact block optimum shows mixed policies can beat both pure policies
(see §3 of `ComputationalEvidence.md`), so a *provable* greedy/threshold rule with an
additive-`D` guarantee is the natural next theorem, and it is directly testable against
the DP.
title: C2. Optimal adaptation schedules are hysteretic, with threshold exactly `D`

description:
**Conjecture.**  If a shared decompressor serves `K` domains with prefix-free patches, then
the *average* patch length is at least `log₂ K − O(1)`, and hence the average break-even
stream length over domains is `Ω(log K)`; no reparametrisation (LoRA rank, sparsity
pattern, quantisation) can beat this without shrinking the number of reachable domains.

*The key insight is* that `exists_expensive_patch` is a pigeonhole statement about the
patch alphabet itself, and Kraft's inequality upgrades a worst-case counting bound to an
average-case one.

*Why now?*  `log_delay_before_gain` and `total_patch_overhead` already give the worst-case
and aggregate versions; the missing ingredient is Kraft's inequality for the patch code,
a self-contained formalization target.
title: C3. The `log K` warm-up delay is unavoidable *on average*, not just in the worst case

description:
**Statement.** Call a layer `δ`-equivariant if its weight matrix is within `δ` (entrywise) of
the hyperoctahedral-equivariant subspace. Then every `δ`-equivariant injective ReLU layer on
`ℝ¹¹` has frame lower constant `α = O(δ²)`; equivalently, approximate hypercube symmetry
forces an approximate information bottleneck with an explicit modulus.

**The key insight is** that `hyperoctahedral_rigidity` shows the equivariant subspace is
`1`-dimensional (scalars), so an equivariant-plus-perturbation layer is a scalar map plus a
`δ`-small operator, and the scalar part contributes nothing to distinguishing percepts after
rectification along the flipped coordinates.

**Why now?** The exact rigidity statement (dimension `1` versus `121`) is now proved, which
turns the qualitative "symmetry destroys 11-dimensional processing" slogan into a perturbation
question with a well-posed constant.

**Falsifier.** A family of `δ`-equivariant injective layers with frame constant bounded below
independently of `δ`.

---
title: Conjecture D — symmetry/losslessness incompatibility is quantitative

description:
Define a pitch-interval histogram counting pairs whose digit values differ by a prescribed number of semitones, independently of their temporal separation. Under the stated ten-note chromatic map, the conjecture is that octave counts are identically zero, while any temporal lag-12 effect is unrelated to octave incidence.

The key insight is that sequence position and pitch distance are orthogonal coordinates and should never share the word “lag.” Why now? The present analysis shows that the original octave interpretation is structurally incompatible with a digit alphabet of width ten.
title: Temporal-lag and pitch-interval separation

description:
**Conjecture.** Let `N(n)` be the number of successful prefixes of length `n` in a finitely branching search language, and suppose `N(n+m) ≤ N(n)N(m)` with `N(n) ≥ 1`. Then the normalized logarithmic growth rate exists and equals the infimum of the finite-scale rates. Under a compatible ultrametric and a finite-type extension condition, this rate also equals the Hausdorff dimension of the infinite successful-path boundary.

The key insight is that the exact additivity proved for finite profiles should be replaced by subadditivity, while the relative-entropy normalization remains unchanged. **Why now?** The finite multiscale composition law identifies precisely which quantity must survive when exact self-similarity is weakened.
title: Entropy dimension for genuinely submultiplicative search languages

description:
**Conjecture.** A nonconstant geodesic can pass through the origin at most once.

The key insight is that the zero-curvature locus is a single point rather than a
phase boundary; a second visit would create a geodesic loop whose interaction with
strictly negative curvature away from the origin should be rigid. **Why now?** The
isolated zero and strict negativity of every sectional quotient off the origin
have been identified, reducing the question to existence, uniqueness, and global
control of the geodesic flow.
title: A unique passage through the flat point

description:
**Conjecture.** For every relational set universe, quotienting set-codes by equality of membership observations produces an extensional universe that is universal among all extensional targets preserving and reflecting membership observations.

The key insight is that failed Extensionality is not an alternative membership law; it is nontrivial kernel data for the observation map. A universal property would turn the extensional shadow from a useful construction into a canonical reflection.

**Why now?** The kernel characterization and extensionality of the represented observation shadow isolate exactly the equivalence relation that the quotient must collapse.
title: The extensional shadow as a universal quotient

description:
**Conjecture.** If deterministic machines and witness verifiers are each mutually simulable with polynomial overhead, then any language separating deterministic from witness computation on one substrate yields a separating language on every equivalent substrate without changing its extensional membership predicate.

The key insight is that a separation witness should be a property of a language and resource regime, not of the material architecture used to recognize it.

**Why now?** Equality of the two classes is already known to transport under exact equivalence; transporting explicit nonmembership under polynomial rescaling is the next falsifiable strengthening.
title: Robust separation witnesses across heterogeneous verifiers

description:
**Conjecture.** Every length-191 snake in `Q_9` is equivalent, under coordinate permutation, translation, and path reversal, to one of the 131 reported classes.

The key insight is that fixing an initial transition pattern should break the full cube symmetry, after which chordlessness and the distance-two constraints may force a finite collection of canonical extensions.

**Why now?** Repeated searches found exactly the same 131 classes, making this a sharply falsifiable classification statement with a finite certificate target rather than an open-ended optimization claim.
title: Completeness of the dimension-nine census

description:
**Conjecture.** For consistent finite states `B, C` with `assigned B ⊆ assigned C`, the
minimal length of a history `ls` with `reviseSeq B ls = C` equals `|C \ B|`, and any minimal
history is a permutation of the list of literals of `C \ B`.

*Falsifiable content.* A pair `B, C` reachable by a strictly shorter history than
`|C \ B|`. The construction in `reachable_of_assigned_eq` gives the upper bound `|C|`; the
sharpened bound and the rigidity of minimizers are open.
title: Optimal-length histories and a normal-form metric

description:
`hvzk_pmf` fixes the challenge `c` before sampling.  Conjecture: for every function
`C : G → ZMod q` (a verifier choosing the challenge from the commitment), the honest
transcript distribution `r ↦ (g^r, C (g^r), r + C(g^r)·x)` is **not** in general equal to any
witness-free simulator's output distribution — concretely, there exists `q`, `x` and `C` for
which no simulator matching `hvzk` exists, while for every *constant* `C` one does.  This
would formally separate honest-verifier ZK from malicious-verifier ZK inside the catalog's
framework.
title: C2. Perfect HVZK survives adaptive challenge choice but not adaptive statement choice

description:
**Conjecture.** For a one-parameter family of input distributions `p_t` on a fixed verifier,
`t ↦ condEntropyW f p_t` is smooth and its second derivative at a regular point is the
difference of the input and output Fisher informations; in particular the Jensen defect grows
quadratically in the deviation of the fiber-size profile from regularity, with the Hessian
given by the fiber-size variance.

*The key insight is that* `jensen_defect_eq_zero_of_regular` identifies the zero set of the
defect exactly, and a non-negative smooth function vanishing on that set must be
second-order there, so the defect is a genuine (squared) distance from regularity rather than
an unstructured slack.

*Why now?* The identity and its zero set are proved, and the numerical table in
`ComputationalEvidence.md` §9 already exhibits the quadratic scaling on profiles `(k,1)`;
falsification only requires one profile where the defect grows linearly.
title: C″. Fisher-type second-order refinement of the defect

description:
Extend `RepresentsDiagonal` to depth `k`: a table represents the composite
`f ∘ (x ↦ eval x (eval x x))` and its higher analogues.  Conjecture: depth-`k`
representability of `F` holds iff every `f ∈ F` has a point of period dividing
`k` under some auxiliary transformation, so the spectrum stratifies into a
strictly increasing chain whose `k`-th level over `Fin n` has cardinality
`n^n - #{f : f has no point of period dividing k}`, and the chain is strict for
every `n ≥ 3`.

*The key insight is* that the depth-1 argument consumes the semantic
endomorphism exactly once, which is precisely why pointwise fixed points — and
not the generated monoid — control representability; increasing the depth
should trade fixed points for periodic points in a controlled way.

*Why now?* The depth-1 spectrum is now a proved equivalence with an exact
finite count, so any deviation at depth `k` is immediately measurable against
`n^n - (n-1)^n`, and the `Fin 3` monoid counterexample supplies the smallest
domain where strictness can be tested exhaustively.
title: A relative obstruction spectrum for *iterated* self-application

description:
Let `A_S = {a : Σ aᵢ ≤ S}`.  Then the *regret of the best single ridge parameter*
against the Wiener optimum, in the worst case over `A_S`, is governed by the
capacity gap:

```
sup_{a ∈ A_S}  [ inf_λ filterRisk(a,b,ridge λ) - noiseFloor(a,b) ]
      ≍  b · ( logDet(a*, b) - effDim(a*, b) )   for the maximising a*.
```

**The key insight is** that both the ridge deficiency and the capacity gap
measure the same thing — the spread of the numbers `aᵢ/(aᵢ+b)` around their mean
— so an inequality between two symmetric concave functionals should be provable
by the same tangent-line technique used in `noiseFloor_le_flat`.

**Why now?** Round 6 supplies all three quantities in formal form (`filterRisk`
for ridge, `noiseFloor`, `logDet`) plus the tangent-line machinery
(`tangent_identity`); the conjecture is the first quantitative link between
information-theoretic capacity and the *suboptimality of a hyperparameter
family*, rather than of an estimator.

**Falsifier:** a spectrum with a large capacity gap but ridge-optimal risk (or
vice versa), e.g. found by optimising over `Fin 3` spectra numerically.

---
title: Conjecture D4 (Capacity is the exact price of adaptivity)

description:
**Conjecture.** For a boundary-dependent seed, the `zeroN` retention decays like
`base/(gain·k)`; equivalently `k · retention(k)` converges and the retention
series over widths diverges (`retention_asymptotic`, `not_summable_retention`).
A single positive-width read therefore determines the whole profile
(`retention_profile_determined`).

*The key insight is* that if the answer path mixes a width-independent internal
drive with `k` equal boundary contributions, then retention is a Möbius
(fractional-linear) function of `k`, and Möbius functions are rigid: one value
plus the fixed point at `k = 0` pins the rest.

*Why now?* The round's own numbers already put this under stress: fitting
`gain/base` at `k = 2` predicts `k = 3` retentions of `0.672 / 0.877 / 0.732 /
0.866` against measured `0.704 / 0.901 / 0.710 / 0.744` — good for seeds
`13, 14, 15`, **badly off for seed `17`** (see `ComputationalEvidence.md`).
**Test:** measure `k = 4` for seeds `15` and `17`. Harmonic decay predicts
retention `≈ 0.65` for `s = 15`; a second boundary channel switching on at
`k = 3` (the natural repair for `s = 17`) predicts a visible kink instead.

---
title: C3. The harmonic law: `k · retention(k) → base / gain`, with one known outlier

description:
**Conjecture.** Replacing the fixed sweep `{32, 64, 96, …}` by a bisection on the bar
crossing yields, for the same compute, a two-seed bracket of width `≤ 8` at
`(d = 4, ctx = 1024)` — i.e. the true knees of the two seeds are separated (or merged)
at resolution far below `32`, and the resulting fine-grained knees satisfy
`k*(s2)/k*(s1) ∈ [0.70, 0.80]` rather than the coarse `0.75` forced by the grid.

*The key insight is* `KneeFluctuation.oneStepFluctuation` together with
`KneeLaw.true_knee_mem_Ioc`: a step-`s` grid identifies a knee only inside a window of
width `s`, and a one-step difference can be manufactured by an arbitrarily small change
in the underlying threshold, so the entire observed effect could be a quantisation
artefact — *unless* the windows are disjoint, which is a resolution question.

*Why now?* The disjointness of `(64, 96]` and `(96, 128]` is proved
(`KneeLaw.net44_true_knee_windows`), so the seeds do differ; what is unknown is by how
much, and bisection answers that with `log₂(32/8) = 2` extra sweep points per seed.

---
title: C2. Adaptive grids collapse the bracket: bisection to a two-seed knee of width 1

description:
**Conjecture:** two domains have equal knees at *all* gates iff their demand
multisets have equal upper-tail counting functions, and equal knees on a gate
*window* of width `w` iff the counting functions agree on the corresponding
count band.  Hence "MATH-READS-AS-PROSE" is testable with a single tail
histogram, without any sweep.
*The key insight is* that the knee is an order statistic, so agreement of knees
on an interval of gates is exactly agreement of the inverse distribution
function on the corresponding interval of ranks.
*Why now?* It converts a 6-point sweep per cell into one histogram per corpus,
making the 7B cell and the non-English domains affordable.
title: D2 — Knee stability is equivalent to tail-exchangeability

description:
**Conjecture.** The pair `(H(T), I(T ; residue)) = (H(T), log₂ |G^ab|)` determines `G` among all
transitive subgroups of `S₅`, but fails first at degree `6`, where two non-isomorphic groups share
both invariants.

*The key insight is* that `H(T)` sees only the class-size multiset while `I` sees only `|G^ab|`, so
the conjecture reduces to a finite check of the transitive group tables — a genuinely decidable
question with a sharp expected boundary.

*Why now?* Both invariants are now theorems rather than measurements, so the classification
question is finite and formalisable; degree `≤ 5` is already within reach of `decide`-style
enumeration of `Perm (Fin 5)` subgroups.

description:
**Conjecture.** For any symmetric labelling channel — one whose ordered joint
law satisfies `w(n, (i,j)) = w(n, (j,i))` — the ordered and unordered channels
carry identical mutual information, so the "which factor is which" bit is
always exactly `0` bits, however large its own entropy is. In particular no
side-channel of this form can ever help factor a semiprime.

*The key insight is* that the swap symmetry is an automorphism of the joint
distribution fixing the residue coordinate, so the extra label ordering is
independent of the observation conditionally on the unordered pair.

*Why now?* The conductor-7 instance is proved
(`CyclicCubic.which_factor_information_zero`, resting on the exact symmetry
`CyclicCubic.countOrd_swap`), and it is proved there by computation rather than
by symmetry — replacing that computation by the structural argument would give
the general theorem immediately.
title: Exchangeability Erases the Which-Factor Bit

description:
Define `d(φ) = (|A| + |B|) − twoSided(φ)`. **Conjecture:** `d` is a genuine
premetric on analogies whose zero set is exactly the equivalences, and it obeys a
composition inequality `d(ψ ∘ φ) ≤ d(ψ) + d(φ)`, making analogies with this cost
into a Lawvere-style enriched structure.

*The key insight is* that two-sided maximality already characterises bijections,
so the residual `d` measures precisely the failure of surjectivity on each side,
and failures can only accumulate additively under composition. *Why now?* Both
the exact zero-set characterisation and the preservation of perfection under
composition are in hand, giving the triangle inequality's two endpoints.
title: The two-sided score metrises the "distance from equivalence"

description:
In the setting of `softMin_sandwich_of_gap`, let `m` be the number of pivotal voters, `Δ`
the gap to the next-best cost and `m₁` the number of voters attaining that next-best cost.
Then

`t · e^{tΔ} · [ (min y − log m / t) − softMin s t y ] → m₁ / m` as `t → ∞`.

Evidence: the two-sided bound `0 ≤ error ≤ (q/m) e^{−tΔ}/t` is proved
(`softMin_sandwich_of_gap`), with `q = #(s \ pivotal)` the total number of non-pivotal
voters; the conjecture replaces `q` by the number `m₁ ≤ q` of *second-best* voters and
asserts that the bound is asymptotically attained.

Falsifiable: a profile for which the limit exists and differs from `m₁ / m`, or fails to
exist.  Note `softMin_eq_of_pivotal_eq_self` already gives the degenerate case `q = 0`
exactly.
title: Conjecture D (Exact asymptotics of the dequantisation error)

description:
The representable density over `Fin n` tends to `1 - e⁻¹`.  Conjecture: for the
category of finite semantic domains with a fixed extra structure (monoid
actions, partial orders, metric quantisations), the representable density
converges to a structure-dependent constant, and this constant is a complete
invariant separating the structures: e.g. monotone endomorphisms of a finite
chain have density `1` (every monotone self-map of a finite chain has a fixed
point) while permutations have density `1 - e⁻¹ + o(1)` in the derangement
sense.

*The key insight is* that the obstruction is quantitative: `e⁻¹` of all
semantic dynamics is permanently outside self-applicative syntax, and this
proportion is computed from the fixed-point predicate alone, so it should vary
predictably when the ambient class of endomorphisms is restricted.

*Why now?* `card_maximal_representable_family` and
`representable_density_tendsto` give the unrestricted baseline in closed form,
so restricted classes can be compared to a proved reference value.
title: Density laws as an invariant of the semantic category

description:
**Conjecture.**  The inequality `N_eff ≤ 8·A·ctx + 4` of
`effSupport_le_eight_amplitude` is saturated up to a factor `2` by trained rows:
`N_eff/(A·ctx) ∈ [4, 8]` at every measured cell, where `A = δ/32` and `δ` is
read off the accuracy budget of the sweep.  Combined with the depth-independence
of `A`, this predicts that `N_eff` is *the same function of `ctx` at every
depth*, so the residual depth drift `46.6 → 50.2 → 52.7` must be a head-profile
effect of size `O(1)` positions and must **saturate**: `N_eff(d)` at `ctx = 128`
should stay below `56` at `d = 32` and `d = 64`.

*The key insight is* that the tail amplitude bounds concentration from one side
and Cauchy–Schwarz bounds it from the other, so a two-sided window for
`N_eff/(A·ctx)` is available without any new modelling hypothesis — the same
double-bracket strategy that closed C1.

*Why now?*  `amplitude_ge_of_effSupport` already converts each logged `N_eff`
into a lower bound on `δ` (`1.33, 1.44, 1.52, 1.16` across the grid); the spread
of those four numbers *is* the tightness measurement, and it is small.
title: E2.  The concentration ceiling is tight: `N_eff ≈ 8·A·ctx`, not merely `≤`

description:
**Conjecture.**  Every exactly 2-universal family on `n = m` keys has
`P(max bucket load ≥ 2) ≥ 1/m`, and moreover
`E[max load] ≥ 1 + (m-1)/m²`; the affine family attains both, so a 2-universal
family cannot be "balanced with high probability" in a stronger sense than the
collision bound already dictates.

The key insight is that the maximum-load event contains the collision event,
so the converse bound transfers, while the expectation statement needs the
fibre-square inequality `fiber_sq_lower_bound`, which is already available and
gives the deterministic floor `∑_v c_v² ≥ n²/m`.

**Why now?**  Both ingredients (`Collides` and `fiber_sq_lower_bound`) exist in
the development; the missing piece is only a definition of the load random
variable and its comparison with `X`.

title: Load-balancing converse: the maximum bucket load

description:
**Conjecture.** There are explicit integers `q`, `n₀`, and a rational constant `c > 3` such that for every `n ≥ n₀`, a labeling into a finite vector space produces a weakly `D₆`-free family in `2^[n]` of cardinality at least `c` times the largest middle-layer cardinality.

The key insight is that interval exclusion is deterministic; only the lower bound on the number of selected sets requires probabilistic rank estimates. Replacing asymptotic error terms by explicit Gaussian-binomial inequalities should therefore yield a finite threshold.

Why now? The closure obstruction and positivity of the gain numerator have been isolated, leaving a sharply defined quantitative counting problem.
title: A finite, explicit improvement over three middle layers

description:
**Conjecture.** There is an absolute constant `C` such that snakes of lengths `L` in `Q_m` and `K` in `Q_n` can be combined into a snake in `Q_(m+n)` of length at least `(L+1)(K+1) - C(L+K)`.

The key insight is that Cartesian products naturally create long grid walks, and all offending chords are localized near changes between factors. A bounded family of separator coordinates may repair those interfaces without destroying the multiplicative main term.

**Why now?** Record searches currently proceed dimension by dimension. A successful product theorem would turn isolated records into systematic lower bounds in higher dimensions and would explain which transition motifs transfer across dimensions.
title: Product constructions with bounded chord repair

description:
**Statement.** `∃ C, ∀ t ≥ 2, Singmaster.mult t ≤ C`, and in fact `C = 8`, attained
only at `t = 3003`.

**The key insight is** the reduction proved here as
`Singmaster.two_mul_rows_card : mult t ≤ 2 * (rowsOf t).card`: since a row can carry a
given value at most twice (`row_solutions_le_two`), Singmaster's conjecture is
*equivalent* to a bound on the number of **rows** meeting the value `t`.  That
reformulation removes the column bookkeeping entirely and turns the problem into:
"how many `n` can satisfy `C(n, k_n) = t` for some `k_n`?"

**Why now?** `two_mul_rows_card` is proved and sorry-free, so the conjecture can now
be attacked in the row-only formulation; every partial result about
`(rowsOf t).card` immediately transfers to `N(t)`.

title: "two rows suffice" form

description:
`sum_sq_sub_self_add_ne_zero` shows `Σ(xᵢ² − xᵢ) + c = 0` forces `c = −2k`, `k ≥ 0`.  The
substitution `xᵢ(xᵢ−1)/2 = Tᵢ` turns solvability into "write `k` as a sum of `n` triangular
numbers", so `n = 1` gives the triangular numbers, `n = 2` the sums of two, and `n ≥ 3` should be
unconditional.

*The key insight is* that the `n ≥ 3` case is Gauss's *Eureka* theorem, equivalent to the
three-squares theorem for `8k + 3`, which is the only genuinely missing input: the reduction
itself is `omega`-level once the triangular substitution is formalised.

*Why now?* The reduction is independent of the missing arithmetic, so `n = 1` and the *reduction*
for general `n` can be closed immediately, isolating the three-squares theorem as a single
well-delimited formalisation target.

title: Conjecture E′ (Eureka threshold, restated)

description:
**Statement.** Let `T : ℕ → β` be any statistic that is eventually periodic with period `P`
(not necessarily a character: think of `p mod P`, of Hamming weights of residues, of any table
lookup). Then on a hint class mod `m` the statistic takes at most `P / gcd(P, m)` values, and
every attacker strategy combining the hint with `T` has candidate-set shrink factor at most
`P/gcd(P, m)`; the *only* way to break the bound is aperiodicity.

**The key insight is** that the master bound never used multiplicativity, Kronecker
reciprocity, or even that the dial values are `±1` — only periodicity — so the barrier is a
statement about *conductors*, not about characters.

**Why now?** The master bound and its sharpness are already established for an abstract
periodic dial; the remaining work is to replace "periodic" by "eventually periodic" and to
quantify over the attacker's strategy as a decision tree, which is exactly the finitary
zero-information machinery already available.
title: Conjecture A (Conductor-budget conservation for *all* periodic side channels)

description:
**Conjecture.** For every polynomial `f ∈ Z[X]` inducing a permutation `σ_f` of
`Z/NZ`, the cycle count satisfies
`#cycles(σ_f) = (1/L) ∑_{k<L} #Fix(f^{∘k})` with
`#Fix(f^{∘k}) = #{x : N ∣ f^{∘k}(x) − x}`, and each fixed-point count is
computable from the resultants `Res(f^{∘k}(X) − X, ·)` — so *no* polynomial
permutation readout can carry information beyond a family of gcds of the form
`gcd(N, g(a))` with `g` a fixed integer polynomial, i.e. beyond the
derived-modulus barrier already established in
`Physics/DerivedModulusNoGo.lean`.

*The key insight is* that `card_fixedPoints_eq_gcd` is not special to
multiplication: it says the fixed-point count of any map is a gcd with `N`, and
orbit counting then turns every "cycle-structure attack" into an average of gcd
probes.

*Why now?* Both halves already exist formally in this catalogue: the Burnside
half is proved here, the resultant/derived-modulus half in
`DerivedModulusResultant.lean`. Only the interface is missing.
title: C2. The Burnside identity is the *complete* accounting of every polynomial map

description:
**Conjecture.** In the saturating channel the effective clip level `T` is not a
seed-independent constant but satisfies `T ≍ g_max`, the largest exclusive
coordinate of the arm; equivalently, self-sufficiency is governed by the
*dimensionless* ratio `(k−1)·g / T` and not by `(k−1)·g`.

*The key insight is* that `self_sufficiency_monotone_in_gain` proves the
opposite of the observed trend at fixed `T` — larger coordinates should be
*more* self-sufficient — so the measured s = 13 arms (largest coordinates of
their width, `0.701` vs `≤ 0.660`, and the only dependent ones) refute a
seed-independent clip, and the only conservative repair is a clip that grows
with the coordinates.

*Why now?* The magnitude→dependence hint now holds at two widths for one seed;
the ratio form is testable with the same ~24 arms/width already scheduled for
the magnitude trend, at no extra training cost, and it converts a
seed-idiosyncrasy into a measurable scalar.
title: C1 — The clip level co-scales with the exclusive coordinate magnitude

description:
Landau-type constant

**Statement.** `#{m ≤ N : m = antiFib a + antiFib b} ~ K · N / √(log N)` for an explicit
Landau–Ramanujan-type constant `K`.

**The key insight is** the proved equivalence "representable ⟺ `8m - 14` is a sum of two
squares": the counting problem transfers verbatim to the classical Landau problem on an
arithmetic progression, so the density is *not* `0` in the crude sense but decays like
`1/√log N`.  Our proved `2/9` lower bound on the non-representable set is the first
quantitative step in this direction.

**Why now?** The reduction is formalised; the remaining input is the Landau–Selberg–Delange
asymptotic, which is the natural next analytic target for Mathlib's Dirichlet-series API.

**Falsifiable:** the ratio `#{representable m ≤ N}·√(log N)/N` should stabilise; if it
drifts to `0` or `∞`, the conjecture is wrong.

description:
**Conjecture.** There is an absolute constant $c > 0$ such that for all $\varepsilon > 0$ and
all large $n$, every weak $B_3$-free family $\mathcal F \subseteq 2^{[n]}$ with
$|\mathcal F| \ge (3+\varepsilon)\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$ satisfies
$\min_S |\mathcal F \,\triangle\, \mathcal L(S)| \ge c\,\varepsilon\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$,
the minimum being over all sets $S$ of levels. More generally the same should hold with
$\mathcal L(S)$ replaced by any permutation-invariant family.

*Status.* The degenerate case $\mathcal F = \mathcal L(S)$ is a theorem (a level family never
exceeds the central-layer bound), so the conjecture is precisely a robust, quantitative version
of it: an $\varepsilon$-gain must not merely break the symmetry of the cube, it must break it on
a positive proportion of the middle layer. *Falsifiable* by a weak $B_3$-free family of size
$(3+\varepsilon)\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$ that differs from some level family in
$o\bigl(\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}\bigr)$ sets.

*Remark (a related claim we deliberately do not conjecture).* One might guess that no gain is
possible from families of *bounded width*, i.e. contained in $d+t$ consecutive layers for
constant $t$. Since the known $\varepsilon$-constructions for $B_d$ with $d \ge 4$ appear to
live on a bounded number of layers, we expect that guess to be false, and record it only as a
question: for which $t$ is the maximum size of a weak $B_d$-free family inside $d+t$
consecutive layers equal to the sum of the $d$ largest of those binomial coefficients? The case
$t = 0$ is the layer construction; the case "$t = 1$, one extra set" is the maximality of layer
families.
title: F6. Stability: an $\varepsilon$-gain forces a large distance from every level family

description:

title: Exact constants in the exponential regime

description:
The key insight is that order-consistency is a *checkable* property of a prefix together with a
candidate ranking: it does not require the future row, only a certificate that no inversion of the
candidate ranking can be large. Any such test must be conservative — the impossibility theorem
forbids a complete one — but a conservative test is already valuable, because it licenses adaptive
budgets: evict aggressively on certified prefixes and fall back to a conservative cache on the
rest. The research question is how much of a real corpus certifies, and at what budget.
title: Certifiable prefixes: an online test for when pruning transfers

description:
**Conjecture.** For the pooled train/test window population of a fixed model, the ANOVA ceiling
`1 - SS_within/SS_tot` lies below `0.5`; consequently no content head, however deep, exceeds
`R² = 0.5`, and the measured linear `0.329` already captures more than two thirds of what any
content function can achieve.

**The key insight is** that `SS_within` is measurable directly — it needs only repeated key
contents across windows and no model of the predictor — so the ceiling of the entire nonlinear
class can be *measured* rather than searched for.

**Why now?** `Rsq_le_intrinsic_ceiling` plus `intrinsic_ceiling_attained` make the ceiling an
exact supremum, and `ssWithin_eq_zero_of_injective` identifies precisely the pooling regime in
which the measurement is meaningful.

**If true:** the nonlinear arm of the roadmap can be cancelled on quantitative grounds.
**If false:** a deep content head is worth building, and the relational ceiling (D1) becomes the
binding constraint instead.

title: D3. Nonlinear probe ceiling on the pooled window population

description:
**Conjecture.** Let `χ : (ℤ/m)ˣ → L` be a finite labelling that factors through
a quotient group, and let `N = pq` be a semiprime with `p, q` independent
uniform. Then the information the residue `N mod m` withholds about the
unordered label pair is *exactly* one label entropy:
`H(pair) − I(N mod m ; pair) = H(L)`.

*The key insight is* that multiplication is a group homomorphism, so the joint
law of `(pq mod m, {χ(p), χ(q)})` is a coset-fibred distribution whose fibres
are translates of a single one — the lost coordinate is a whole label, never a
fraction of one.

*Why now?* The conductor-7 case is now a theorem,
`CyclicCubic.semiprime_deficit_eq_type_entropy`, with the deficit equal to
`log₂3 − 2/3` on the nose; the coincidence of "deficit" and "type entropy" is
too exact to be an accident, and the general statement is a finite-group
computation that the existing `MI` API supports verbatim.
title: Deficit Quantisation for Multiplicative Label Channels

description:
*For all `r, s` with `r + s ≤ |X|` the spectrum satisfies `t_{r+s} ≥ t_r·(t_s − r)`, and more
precisely `t_{r+s} ≥ t_r · (number of orbits of injective `s`-tuples avoiding a fixed injective
`r`-tuple)`.*

The key insight is that `descFactorial_injOrbits_one_le` is the case `r = 0` of a relative
statement: cutting an injective `(r+s)`-tuple into its first `r` and last `s` coordinates gives a
fibration of the top fibre at level `r+s` over the top fibre at level `r`, whose fibres are the
orbits of the stabiliser on injective `s`-tuples in the complement.

Why now? The maps `dropOrbit` and `shrinkOrbit` already realize the "forget coordinates"
direction, and the orbit–stabiliser theorem used in `descFactorial_dvd_card_of_kTransitive`
supplies the relative count; only the bookkeeping between the two is missing.
title: Conjecture M (a full multiplicative hierarchy)

description:
Fix an audit statistic `f` with `𝔼_p f = 0`, `Var_p f = 1`. Then the PTX mix-in is detectable
by `f` at sample size `n` iff `γ ≥ c/√n` up to constants, i.e. there is a sharp threshold
`γ_n ≍ n^{-1/2}` separating "statistically invisible mix-in" from "detectable drift", while
the reward-induced part contributes only at `β^{-1}n^{-1/2}`.

The key insight is that the two drift scales `γ‖d − p‖₁` and `MAD/β` interact with the
`n^{-1/2}` statistical noise floor to produce a *two-dimensional* phase diagram in `(γ, β)`
whose boundary is a hyperbola `γ ≈ MAD/(β‖d − p‖₁)` — below it, the reward drift dominates
the pretraining drift. Why now: both scales are now proved with explicit constants, so the
comparison is a finite computation rather than a modelling guess.
title: Conjecture D (phase transition in γ for the audit-detectability of the mix-in)

description:
**Conjecture.**  For odd `p ≠ q`, `N = pq`, `s = p + q`, the number of solutions
of `x² − s x + N ≡ 0 (mod 2^t)` equals `2^{min(v₂(p−q)+1, ⌊t/2⌋)+1}` for
`t` large, in particular it saturates at `2^{v₂(p−q)+2}` and never grows with
`t` beyond that.  The computed table (`ComputationalEvidence.md` §6) shows
saturation at `8` for `v₂(p−q)=2` and `16` for `v₂(p−q)=3`.

*The key insight is* that the trace hint's sub-bit behaviour is not a constant
`3`-bit tax but a function of a single 2-adic invariant of the secret pair, so
the "hint deficit" of a family can depend on the secret and not only on the
hint — a genuinely new axis in the taxonomy.

*Why now?*  `sq_congr_iff` (cycle I) already reduces the whole question to a
2-adic valuation bookkeeping over `ℤ`, which `omega` plus induction on `t` can
carry.
title: C2. The 2-adic root explosion is governed by `v₂(p − q)`

description:
**Conjecture.** A single seed-2 run at `ctx = 4096` reports a knee in `[416, 448]`. A
report `≤ 384` instead refutes the `ctx = 2048` amplitude window, and a report `≥ 480`
refutes both seed-2 windows in favour of the seed-1 amplitude.

*The key insight is* that the three surviving amplitude hypotheses have predictions at the
next rung that are pairwise separated by at least one full grid step
(`KneeAmplitude.next_rung_three_way_separation`) — unlike the `224`-vs-`256` reading,
which is not robust at its own resolution (`KneeDrift.net46_seed2_knee_not_robust`). This
is the first cell of the programme where the grid can actually adjudicate.

*Why now?* The separation theorem is proved and needs no new theory; only the run is
missing.

---
title: C2. The decisive-context conjecture

description:
Identify the strongest seed class for which empirical orbit measures converge to the
arcsine invariant measure, and characterize the periodic, preperiodic, and other
exceptional seeds excluded from that class.

The key insight is that angle doubling transfers the question to binary expansions,
where normality and periodicity can be stated precisely.

Why now? Fixed and absorbing orbit counterexamples show that “regardless of initial
condition” is untenable, while the semiconjugacy indicates the correct almost-everywhere
replacement.
title: Invariant-measure theorem with sharp exceptional set

description:
**Conjecture.** For fixed positive integers `d` and `Q`, only finitely many primitive Selberg-class functions have degree `d` and conductor at most `Q`.

The key insight is that a countable universe need not have finite conductor slices; finiteness requires an additional arithmetic rigidity or compactness principle.

**Why now?** Fixed-modulus Dirichlet characters provide a complete degree-one model in which the corresponding analytic family is both faithful and finite, giving a concrete base case for testing higher-degree analogues.
title: Finite fibres at bounded degree and conductor

description:
**Conjecture.** There is an explicit `c > 0` with
`#{n ≤ N : T^[k] n ≥ n for k = ⌊½ log₈ N⌋} = O(N^{1−c})`.

**The key insight is** that the two error terms in the counting bound now decay
at *different* exponential rates in `k` — the dyadic failure density like
`(243/256)^{k/5}` and the threshold term like `8^k/N` — so a single choice
`k ≍ log N` balances them and produces power savings, whereas with the old
Chebyshev bound `1/(4δ²k)` only `O(N/log N)` was available.

**Why now?** Both ingredients are theorems in this cycle
(`noncontracting_density_pow_le` and `nondescending_density_bound_general`); the
remaining work is the elementary but fiddly choice of `k = k(N)` with floors and
logarithms. The special case `N = 64^k` is already proved
(`nondescending_density_at_scale_decay`).
title: C4. Polynomial-savings natural density

description:
because they measure different functionals

**Conjecture.** P(cure) at training time is governed by the *number* of
exclusive coordinates the optimiser can recruit (knee at `k = 3`), while
eval-time sufficiency is governed by the *saturation margin* `(k−1)g − T`
(knee at `k = 2`); consequently forcing `g` up by a factor `≥ 2` at `k = 1`
(e.g. by rescaling the boundary column at initialisation) should buy eval
sufficiency at `k = 1` without buying training reliability.

*The key insight is* that the two knees are separated by exactly one
coordinate, which is what a margin-versus-count distinction predicts, and the
Lean thresholds make the margin functional explicit and manipulable.

*Why now?* It is the cheapest available discriminator between "k = 2 is
special" and "the margin is special", and it needs one inference-time rescale
plus one training run per seed.
title: C4 — Training-time success and eval-time sufficiency have different knees

description:
**Conjecture.** A third seed at `ctx = 1024` reports a knee `k*` with
`k* / 8 ∈ (12, 14]` — i.e. `k* ∈ {112, 128}` on a step-16 grid — rather than `96`.
Equivalently, the seed-2 `ctx = 1024` cell, not the `ctx = 2048` cell, is the outlier of
`KneeAmplitude.seed2_no_common_amplitude`.

*The key insight is* that the two seed-2 rungs are **not** two instances of one drifting
constant: their amplitude windows `(8, 12]` and `(12, 14]` are disjoint, so exactly one of
them can be generated by a multiplicative law, and the round's "systematic" reading is
provably unavailable. The conflict is a two-point obstruction, and one more measurement at
the *earlier* rung resolves which point is anomalous.

*Why now?* The obstruction is already proved (`seed2_no_common_amplitude`) and each rung
is separately explainable (`seed2_each_rung_explainable`), so the experiment is a genuine
fork with two live branches rather than a confirmation run.
