title: C1. The amplitude-conflict conjecture (highest value)

description:
The claim
   that 163 is the unique natural `n` for which `exp (π * sqrt n)` is within
   `10⁻⁶` of an integer needs careful qualification and a counterexample search.
   Any rigorous theorem should specify a bounded range or add structural
   hypotheses. Equidistribution heuristics make an unrestricted uniqueness claim
   particularly implausible.
title: Do not treat the proposed uniqueness statement as established

description:
**Conjecture.** There exists a positive constant `ε₅` such that the largest weakly `D₅`-free family in `2^[n]` has size at least `(3 + ε₅)` times the largest middle-layer cardinality for all sufficiently large `n`.

The key insight is that forbidding five, rather than six, intermediate elements requires the top layer to detect two exceptional rank values; a successful construction must recover the resulting density loss through a second correlated invariant.

Why now? The four-layer rank construction explains exactly why the direct one-invariant modification loses density, narrowing the search to coupled rank, nullity, or quotient-space statistics.
title: The unresolved five-element-width diamond threshold

description:
Fix a finite corpus of statements and charge each theory for both source length and the transitive size of its dependency closure. Among theories proving the entire corpus, the mature shared library has maximal dependency-adjusted fitness.

The key insight is that extensive reuse can outweigh the local cost of general abstractions once dependencies are charged only once. **Why now?** The finite maximum principle identifies exactly what remains empirical: a fixed comparison class, a reproducible cost model, and complete theorem-coverage measurements.
title: Dependency-adjusted global champion conjecture

description:
For any theory language permitting conservative addition of independently stated consequences at sublinear marginal source cost, raw theorem-per-line fitness has no global maximum on the unrestricted class of expressible theories.

The key insight is that a global champion is meaningful only after fixing theorem identity, admissible dependencies, and a bounded comparison universe. **Why now?** The finite existence result and the documented unbounded boundary case together isolate normalization as the decisive hypothesis, turning a vague universality claim into a sharp falsifiable dichotomy.
title: No universal maximum without resource normalization

description:
**Statement.** For every linear-plus-ReLU layer on `ℝ¹¹` (odd dimension) there is a nonzero
percept `v` and `λ ≥ 0` with `relu(Wv) = λ v` whenever `W` has nonnegative entries; and the
odd-dimensional invariant-direction theorem extends to the *nonlinear* rectified setting via
a fixed-point argument on the percept sphere.

**The key insight is** that `relu ∘ W` maps the nonnegative orthant of `ℝ¹¹` into itself when
`W ≥ 0`, so Brouwer's theorem on the (odd-dimensional) simplex yields an invariant ray, while
`exists_invariant_percept_11` gives the linear shadow of the same phenomenon.

**Why now?** The linear odd-dimensional statement and its dimension-2 counterexample are
proved, so the exact boundary of the phenomenon is known; Mathlib's Brouwer fixed-point
machinery makes the nonlinear extension reachable.

**Falsifier.** A nonnegative `11 × 11` matrix `W` for which `relu(Wv) = λv` has no nonzero
solution.
title: Conjecture E — the parity dividend has an architectural payoff

description:
A binary fork can never yield more than one bit (`mutualInfo_bool_le_log_two`), and the ceiling is
reached exactly when the observable determines the fork *and* the fork is balanced
(`capacity_attained_iff`).  For `Sₙ` (`n ≥ 2`) the sign is balanced, so the capacity is attained,
and `sign_capacity_attained_iff` shows it is attained by exactly two forks: `sign` and `¬sign`.
title: C2 — capacity *(closed)

description:
Conjecture that if every endomorphism in a designated semantic class has at most one fixed point, then all diagonal codes for the same endomorphism yield one common value, even when the codes themselves are unrelated by a domain isomorphism. Seek natural ordered or metric semantic domains where this uniqueness follows from contraction or guardedness.

The key insight is that the present construction separates two sources of ambiguity: presentation transport is canonical, but arbitrary universal codes need not choose the same fixed point.

Why now? The fixed-point factorization proves invariance along structure-preserving maps and precisely exposes uniqueness as the missing hypothesis for global code independence.
title: Choice independence from unique semantic fixed points

description:
**Conjecture.** For every `X` large, the number of squarefree sum-of-two-squares
parameters `d ≤ X` for which `E^d` has rank one is at least `c · X / (\log X)^{1/2}`
for an explicit constant `c = c(E) > 0`.

*The key insight is* that the count of sum-of-two-squares integers up to `X` already
has the Landau order `X / (\log X)^{1/2}`, and the rank-one proportion from
Conjecture 2 is positive, so the two effective inputs multiply.

*Why now?* The infinitude of the parameter set is established; upgrading it to an
effective window only requires attaching the (already conjectural) positive
proportion, isolating a single missing analytic estimate.
title: Effective infinitude with a height window

description:
**Conjecture.** A finite hyperreal projection-valued measure with finite matrix entries descends under entrywise standard part to an ordinary projection-valued measure if and only if its projections are pairwise orthogonal up to infinitesimal operator norm and its total projection is infinitesimally close to the identity.

The key insight is that polynomial identities defining projections and orthogonality should survive standard part, while approximate hypotheses capture the natural measurement errors of non-Archimedean states.

**Why now?** Scalar standard-part normalization and support collapse are established; the next falsifiable step is to determine exactly which matrix identities survive observation.
title: Standard-part projection-valued measures

description:
**Conjecture.**  Define the knee `k*(m,p) := min {k : 1 - P(cure at k) ≤ 1/2}`.  Then in the
model `⌈log_p m⌉ ≤ k*(m,p) ≤ ⌈log_p (2m)⌉`, so the empirically observed "reserve ≥ 4 exclusive
dimensions" rule is the statement `m ≈ 8–16` obstruction modes at `p = 2`.

*The key insight is* that the two-sided envelope proved in `cureProb_deficiency_two_sided`
already pins the deficiency between `p^{-k}` and `m p^{-k}`, so the knee can only move by an
additive `log_p m`, never by a multiplicative factor — a threshold *location* result even
though there is no threshold *sharpness*.

*Why now?*  Both envelope inequalities are theorems; the remaining work is a monotone-inversion
lemma for `k ↦ m p^{-k}`.
title: C2. The knee is at `k = ⌈log_p m⌉` — a formal "design rule"

description:
**Conjecture.** For every seed and every width `k ≥ 3`, the single-coordinate
flip is a no-op; at `k = 2` the flip read is *equivalent* to the whole-block read
(`flip` hits ⟺ boundary-dependent), with no false positives or negatives.

*The key insight is* that on a block read collectively the flip costs exactly
`2·a` of aggregate drive while the whole-block ablation costs `k·a`, so the flip
threshold is `(k-2)·a`: it degenerates to the `zeroN` threshold precisely at
`k = 2` (`flip_iff_selfSufficient_at_width_two`) and becomes strictly weaker for
`k ≥ 3` (`flip1_noop_of_width_three`). At the arithmetic layer sign flips are
*always* free (`resolves_neg`), so sign sensitivity can never be a capacity
effect.

*Why now?* The round observed `flip = 0 %` in all 12 arms at `k = 3` and
`−7 … −25 %` in 4/4 dependent arms at `k = 2` — precisely the predicted
degeneracy. **Test:** run `k = 4` and `k = 5`. The conjecture forbids *any*
flip effect at `k ≥ 3`, and predicts that a two-coordinate flip at `k = 4`
behaves like a one-coordinate flip at `k = 2`.

---
title: C2. Sign-sensitivity is a boundary-case artefact of `k = 2`, not a mechanism

description:
**Conjecture.**  Across the whole measured grid, the product of the measured
knee and the median held-out logit margin, `k*(d, ctx)·m(d, ctx)`, is constant
to within `±15 %` once divided by `4·L·B·A·ctx`; equivalently the dimensionless
number `k*·m/(4·L·B·A·ctx)` lies in `[1, 2]` at every cell — the window that
`margin_law_theta` proves it must occupy if the margin channel is the operative
one.  A cell landing outside `[1, 2]` — in particular a cell with a *large*
margin but an unchanged knee — falsifies the margin channel there and points
instead to a hard mass requirement.

*The key insight is* that `margin_law_upper` and `margin_law_lower` bracket the
same quantity from both sides, so the conjecture is not a fit with a free
constant: the admissible window is closed, of width exactly a factor `2`, and is
fixed before any measurement.  The window itself is now a theorem
(`knee_margin_window`: `k*·m/(4·L·B·A·ctx) ∈ [1, 2]` whenever the margin channel
is the operative one), so the conjecture is exactly the empirical claim that the
measured cells fall inside it.

*Why now?*  The margin is the one quantity in the mechanism that the harness
never logged; `netB_margin_channel_lower_bound` shows one extra logging line
(median margin at the knee) already decides the question at the measured cells,
with no retraining.
title: E1.  The margin is the *only* free parameter of the knee: `k*·m` is a cell invariant

description:
For finite columns and normed value spaces,
   define a loss between partial observations and global sections. Prove that
   minimizing over global sections is equivalent to minimizing subject to all

   suitable finiteness, compactness, or coercivity assumptions.

description:
**Conjecture.** For a concrete syntax of first-order arithmetic with a standard-model satisfaction relation, every length-bounded fragment has a finite exact truth table, but there is no single computable procedure whose restrictions produce all of these tables uniformly.

The key insight is that each finite stage is harmless while uniformity across all stages can encode the full unbounded truth problem.

**Why now?** Exact finite tabulation and diagonal non-enumeration have been separated cleanly, making the missing uniformity condition precise enough to target by a reduction.
title: Arithmetic truth as an unbounded limit of bounded truth tables

description: Prove both directions of the precise statement: a surreal has a representative of finite birthday iff it lies in `Surreal.dyadic`. The forward direction should induct on a numeric pre-game's birthday and identify the simplest dyadic strictly between its finite sets of dyadic options. This requires a formal “simplest dyadic in an interval” theorem.
title: Classify every finite-birthday surreal

description:
NET-67 reports "increments set by scale"; NET-70 reports `+4` from 512 to 1024
for both prose and math.  **Conjecture:** the map `ctx ↦ knee(ctx)` satisfies
`knee(2c) = knee(c) + δ(c)` with `δ` depending only on the model, not on the
domain, and `δ` is itself the knee of the *conditional* demand profile of the
newly visible positions.
*The key insight is* that the extra context contributes an independent block of
demands, so the quantile of the concatenated profile shifts by the quantile of
the increment block — a cocycle identity for `knee` under context doubling.
*Why now?* Two contexts already pin the additive shape; a third (4096) would
falsify or confirm the cocycle, and the formal shift law `knee_shift` is already
in place to state it.
title: D3 — The increment law is a translation cocycle

description:
**C1 (settled, in a stronger form).**  Every character-weighted circle count is either
  identically zero (odd weights, `circleSumC_eq_zero_of_odd`) or a sum of exactly two Jacobi
  sums against the quadratic character (`circleSumC_eq_jacobiSum_add`), whence

title: C1 (settled, in a stronger form).

description:
**Conjecture C (sharper silent-error constant) — PROVED.**
  `AlmostLosslessTunableMarkov.lean` generalises the Markov step to an arbitrary
  threshold (`card_badMassC_lt`, sub-conjecture C1) and splits the key space
  with any pair `1/c₁ + 1/c₂ ≤ 1` (`exists_tunable_good_key`).  With
  `c₁ = 1+η`, `c₂ = 1+1/η` this yields
  `exists_tunable_almost_lossless_scheme`: silent corruption
  `≤ (1+η)·δ·|l|/M` and failure `≤ δ + (1+1/η)·|l|/M`, cost exactly `|l|`.  The
  silent constant can therefore be pushed to the first-moment optimum `1`; the
  cycle-2 theorem is the case `η = 1`.
title: Conjecture C (sharper silent-error constant) — PROVED.*

description:
**Conjecture D (coordinatewise block decoding is optimal) — converse half
  PROVED.**  `block_cost_ge_of_coordinatewise` shows that `b` independent
  coordinate decoders that are correct on an `n`-symbol codebook are forced, on
  some product input, to spend `≥ b·log₂ n` queries in total, matching the
  `b·(log₂ n + 3)` cost of the sorted block decoder.  What is *not* proved is
  that a non-coordinatewise decoder cannot do better; see Conjecture G below.
title: Conjecture D (coordinatewise block decoding is optimal) — converse half

description:

  non-vacuous by `sparse_hypotheses_satisfiable`.
title: Sparse corpora never approach the binomial ceiling.*

description:
**Conjecture B (a `T`-wise independent family with a short key) — PROVED.**
  `AlmostLosslessPolyFamily.lean` realises the degree-`T` polynomial family
  `h_c(x) = c₀ + c₁x + ⋯ + c_T x^T` over `ZMod p` with `K = p^{T+1}` keys.  The
  missing counting step (sub-conjecture B1) is
  `polyEval_injective_of_agree_on_points`, proved from
  `Matrix.det_vandermonde_ne_zero_iff` rather than from polynomial-degree
  bookkeeping: coefficient vectors agreeing at `T+1` distinct points coincide.
  Hence `card_poly_constrained_le` (at most `p` keys satisfy a `T`-fold

  the separation `poly_key_exponentially_shorter : p^{T+1} < p^p`.
  `polyHash_universal2_one` records coherence with cycle 1 at `T = 1`.
title: Conjecture B (a `T`-wise independent family with a short key) — PROVED.*

description:
An earlier form of this conjecture asserted
> `expCost ≤ B·(1 - frac Found) + (B+1)/2 · frac Found`.  That is **false**: a
> succeeding seed may have witness index `B-1`, so the conditional average of a
> succeeding seed is not bounded by `(B+1)/2`.  The `j = 1` case that survives
> the correction is now the theorem `expCost_le_of_first_probe`.  The conjecture
> below is the corrected, still-open generalisation.
title: An earlier form of this conjecture asserted

description:
**C3 (the ratio `2/3` is optimal for one-query located searches) — refuted.**  The
  general one-query scheme is formalized as `Bishop.searchGen`; it preserves the
  enclosure invariant (`Bishop.searchGen_enclosing`) and contracts by
  `max β (1−α)` (`Bishop.searchGen_width_le`).  `Bishop.trisection_not_optimal`
  instantiates `α = 2/5, β = 1/2`, contracting by `3/5 < 2/3`.  The corrected sharp
  statement is `Bishop.one_query_contraction_gt_half` (every one-query ratio exceeds
  `1/2`) together with `Bishop.exists_one_query_contraction_lt_half_add` (ratios

(`shtarkovSum_eq_one_iff`), so any genuinely new source makes the price strictly
positive, and the price is monotone in the class (`price_reindex_le`).  What
remains is the quantitative form.  If `S'` is obtained from `S` by adding one
source `p_new`, then
`Cₛ' − Cₛ = Σ_x (p_new(x) − maxLik_S(x))⁺`, and this is strictly positive unless
`p_new ≤ maxLik_S` pointwise.  *The key insight is* that the Shtarkov sum is
the `ℓ¹`-norm of a pointwise supremum, so its increments measure exactly the
mass on which the new model strictly dominates the old envelope — a

bounds (`shtarkovSum_sigma_le`, `le_shtarkovSum_sigma`) are in place, so the
statement is a pointwise `max` computation; if true it turns the price of
universality into a submodular set function on model libraries, which would make
greedy decompressor-library design provably near-optimal.

many corner-disjoint violating rectangles, each contributing deviation energy at essentially disjoint
locations. Summing over a maximum family of such witnesses should yield a bound
sup |A|^2 <= |R| - c*w(R), where w(R) is the maximum number of corner-disjoint non-box witnesses,
interpolating towards the multiplicative losses observed for the agreement family (where the true
optimum is exactly half the Cauchy-Schwarz value at every depth).

**Bounded entanglement / higher rank.** Replacing product coins by states of Schmidt rank at most r
across a chosen cut, the Cauchy-Schwarz optimum becomes the sum of the r largest squared singular
values, and one expects a gap unless the resonance set is a union of r disjoint boxes. Rank at most r
forces the vanishing of all (r+1)x(r+1) minors, so the minor-versus-pattern comparison should
generalise, with an (r+1)-dimensional analogue of the rank-one minor inequality.

**Multi-cut strengthening at depth n.** The depth-n theorem transports the bipartite gap along a
single register cut. A resonance set may be non-box at several registers simultaneously, and the
deviation energies harvested at different cuts are generically distinct. Combining k cuts should give
a constant of order k/7, producing gaps that grow with the depth for genuinely global targets.

**Extremal combinatorics of the gap.** Determining which non-box set of size m minimises
m - sigma_1^2 would replace the size-dependent factor m/(3m+1) by the exact extremal function. The
exhaustive scan of all subsets of small grids suggests the minimiser is always the L-shape, embedded.

**Beyond the Euclidean metric.** The distance identity underlying the proof is specific to the
l^2 geometry. Analogues in l^p geometry, or with relative entropy replacing squared distance to the
product family, would connect the rigidity gap to information-theoretic separability measures.
title: Structure-dependent gaps

description:
It would upgrade "the cost of internal soundness is one loop"
(`soundnessExt_sound_iff`, `iterExt_selfLoop_ncard`) into "the cost is *nothing* for
the old theory", i.e. a genuine conservativity theorem for tangled hierarchies — the
formal counterpart of Hofstadter's claim that strange loops do not corrupt the levels
they sit above.
title: It would upgrade "the cost of internal soundness is one loop"

description:
`RLHF.localZeta_curvature_eq_variance` identifies
   the curvature of the `p`-factor as a variance; conjecture the exact total curvature
   `∫_{−∞}^{∞} Var_{k log p}(s) ds = A log p` for the `A`-truncated factor, and hence that the
   total curvature of the truncated Euler product over `p ≤ P` is `∑_{p ≤ P} A_p log p`, a
   Chebyshev `θ`-type sum.  The variance-flow identity `RLHF.integral_tiltVar` reduces this to
   the two endpoint limits of the tilted mean.
title: (Curvature mass of an Euler factor)

description: Formalize the relevant hypotheses for central potentials and distinguish: all bounded orbits closed, one closed orbit, local stability of a circular orbit, and commensurability of linearized frequencies. These are different claims, and the logarithmic potential separates them sharply.
title: State a precise Bertrand-theorem comparison

description: Replace the full Boolean cube by a predicate encoding incompatibilities, allergies, ingredient availability, or flavor-preservation constraints. The induced subcomplex can have nontrivial topology; compute connected components and cycle ranks for concrete finite predicates.
title: Constrained recipes

Combine with the existing
   `Catalog/Pythagorean/BerggrenCompleteness.lean` to show that the leg-square
   factorizations obtained from the Berggren subtree rooted at a triple with leg `a`
   enumerate exactly the factorizations of `a²`, linking tree depth to divisor

title: Full Berggren generation

description:
: `IsSidon A ↔ IsSidon (A.image (· + t))` and,
   for `u` a unit, `IsSidon A ↔ IsSidon (A.image (u * ·))`.
   *Status: **closed in cycle 4** — `isSidon_image_add_right` and `isSidon_image_unit_mul`.

title: Translation- and dilation-invariance

description:
For every `m ≥ 1`, the renormalized product `q^m · Π f i` of `m`
    normalized series realizes **exactly** the series of order `0`
    (`renormalized_prod_iff_orderTop_zero`); the pole order is the only obstruction, and the
    factorization is never unique (`factorization_not_unique`).
title: Conjecture C, closed

description: From any dark predicate `T`, tagging a hidden witness by `Fin k` constructs a level-`k` dark predicate for every finite `k`. Thus levels 1, 2, and 3 require no successively stronger independence principles. On a fixed predicate, level `l` implies every lower level `k ≤ l`.
title: The proposed strict hierarchy collapses

description:
The valuation ladder is the first step past squarefree periods: refining $p \mid v$ to
$v_p(v) = e_p$ leaves the numerator $\prod (p-1)$ frozen and multiplies the denominator by a pure
power. The natural next question is the analogue of the coprime no-go theorem for valuation cells
at auxiliary scales that are *not* coprime to the refined period, where the interaction is
expected to be governed entirely by the greatest common divisor of the two periods — quantifying
exactly how much positional information a divisibility statistic can carry when the scales are
allowed to interact.
title: C. Valuation cells at non-coprime auxiliary scales

description:
over `ℤ`: if `|A+A| ≤ 3|A| - 4` then `A` lies in an
   arithmetic progression of length `|A+A| - |A| + 1`.  This alone would upgrade the main
   theorem from "`A`, `B` progressions" to "`A`, `B` of doubling `< 3`", which is the
   regime where the union bound is genuinely tight.
title: Freiman's `3k-4` theorem

description:
**The key insight is** that the endpoint-matched tilt cancels the mismatch size $d$ from the
stationarity equation $d/(1+x) + b = 0$, leaving $1 + x^\star = (u-l)/(\log(1+u)-\log(1+l))$, the
logarithmic mean — a *universal* location depending only on the window. **Why now?** The present
cycle proves the two-sided trap GM < LM < AM, and also proves the *existence* half for an arbitrary
strictly convex curvature excess; what remains is to show the same *location* pinning survives when
the baseline mismatch is an arbitrary smooth curvature excess rather than a pure exponent shift,
which would turn "peak in the right half" into a decisive, model-free falsifier for any leakage
explanation.
title: Direction 1 — Log-mean pinning of curvature-leakage artefacts

description:
**The key insight is** that the sign of the second-derivative mismatch, not its size, decides
whether an endpoint-matched residual bumps or dips. An over-curved baseline yields a strictly
concave residual with exactly one interior maximum; an under-curved baseline yields a convex
residual with no interior maximum for any tilt whatsoever; a matched baseline yields a residual that
is flat after edge calibration. Turning this into a full dichotomy theorem — with the mirror
statement for interior minima — would classify the first-order pathologies of residual shapes
completely and give a one-line sign test on residual curvature as a diagnostic for baseline
misspecification.
title: Direction 2 — Curvature-signed dichotomy for residual shapes

description:
The original form of this direction — "a base-3 window sees deeper than a base-2 window" —
was **refuted inside this cycle**: `universal_depth_null` shows that *every* rational-scale
truncation `⌊(a/b)(m/n)⌋` fails at the very first letter past the inversion, because the
boundary `5/2 + 2k` is *attained* by an admissible state and truncation is right-continuous.
So the surviving question is about a different sensor class.

**The key insight is** that what a sensor really needs is not finer scaling but *Euclidean
steps*: the pair `(⌊m/n⌋, m mod n)` is one step of the Euclidean algorithm and already
determines strictly more letters than any single truncation.  **Why now?** The universal
null fixes the exact failure mode (attained boundaries), and a `t`-step Euclidean sensor is
precisely what resolves them, so the conjectured hierarchy "`t` steps ↔ `Θ(t)` letters" is
now the sharp question — and it is the one that prices an attack, since `t` full Euclidean
steps already cost the scan.
title: D2. Euclidean-step hierarchy (after the universal null)

description:
**The key insight is** that `b = 1` is not cosmetic: it separates finite from
infinite total window mass, and the bootstrap interval straddles it, so the
present experiment is provably unable to decide a qualitative property of the
positional layer.  **Why now?**  `windowMass_tendsto_finite` /
`windowMass_tendsto_atTop` make the dichotomy formal, so a re-run whose CI
excludes `1` converts a statistical statement into a proved qualitative one.
title: Exponent-one dichotomy as a decidable experimental target

description:
**Conformality is a hierarchy, not a single obstruction.**
  `strict_hierarchy_of_local_conformality`: for every level `m ≥ 2` there is a corpus in
  which every clique of at most `m` theorems has a common document while some clique of
  `m + 1` theorems does not.  The catalogued three-theorem example is the case `m = 2`.
title: Conformality is a hierarchy, not a single obstruction.*

description:
**Conjecture.**  Refining `ordPatterns n` by the number of *descents* of the
ordered pattern (positions where the block order drops) refines the Fubini
number into the Eulerian-like triangle `∑_j A(n,j)·2^j`-style statistics; more
precisely `#{r ∈ ordPatterns n | r has exactly j distinct values} = S(n,j)·j!`
(proved) refines further, over the descent statistic of the induced word, into
the second-order Eulerian numbers.

The key insight is that `card_fibre_ordPatterns` identifies each fibre with
`Equiv.Perm (Fin k)` *canonically*, so any permutation statistic on `Perm (Fin
k)` transports to a statistic on faces, turning the Fubini identity into a
`q`-analogue with no new geometry required.

**Why now?**  The fibre bijection is already constructed and proved bijective in
`Fubini.lean` (`card_fibre_ordPatterns`); adding a statistic only requires
checking that the bijection is statistic-preserving, which is a pointwise
computation on `rank`.

---
title: Eulerian Refinement of the Fubini Fibration

description:
Every `A/B ∈ ℝ(x)` is a finite sum of a polynomial and
   terms `(αx+β)/Fᵏ` with `F` monic irreducible of degree `≤ 2`. Combined with
   `RischIrred.quadratic_pow_has_log_arctan_primitive` and
   `RischSplit.singlePole_integrable` this immediately yields Conjecture A′.
title: Real partial fractions

description:
Chebotarev's theorem that every square submatrix of the `p × p` DFT matrix
is nonsingular, which in turn follows from a resultant/Vandermonde computation over `Q(ζ_p)`
using the irreducibility of the `p`-th cyclotomic polynomial — machinery that Mathlib already
contains (`Polynomial.cyclotomic_irreducible`, `IsPrimitiveRoot`).
title: Chebotarev's theorem that every square submatrix of the `p × p` DFT matrix

description:
**Conjecture.** For `Surreal.{u}`, the character of every point equals the cofinality of
the class `On` of ordinals of `Type u`; formally, a family `B : ι → Set Surreal.{u}` of
neighbourhoods of `c` is a basis only if `ι` surjects onto a cofinal family of ordinals, so
"character = `On`" in the proper-class sense.

*The key insight is* that `Surreal.exists_pos_lt_family` bounds the character from below by
every small cardinal, while the archimedean-monad basis `Surreal.monad c d` bounds it from
above by the class of scales `d`, and scales are classified up to archimedean equivalence by
ordinals through the `ω^y` normal form.

*Why now?* Both halves are already formalised in this cycle; what is missing is Conway
normal form (`ω^y` exponentiation) in Mathlib, which is a self-contained addition.

**Test.** Formalise the map `d ↦ leading exponent of d` and prove that monads at
archimedean-equivalent scales coincide; then show a basis must meet every archimedean class.
title: Direction 1 — Exact character of the surreal line

description:
**Conjecture.**  Let `G ≤ Sym(X)` act diagonally on `Xⁿ`. Then the kernel
pattern is a complete invariant of the `G`-orbits *for every* `n ≥ 1` if and
only if `G` is `|X|`-transitive, i.e. `G = Sym(X)` (for finite `X`); for
`t`-transitive `G` the pattern is complete exactly on tuples with at most `t`
blocks.

The key insight is that `exists_perm_of_pat_eq` builds the required permutation
by extending a bijection between the two value ranges, and the number of values
that must be matched is precisely the number of blocks — so transitivity degree
and block count are the same parameter viewed from two sides.

**Why now?**  `pat_not_complete_of_trivial_group` already proves the extreme
case, and the general statement needs only the block-count bookkeeping supplied
by `card_reps` and `patternsWith`.

---
title: Kernel Completeness Beyond the Symmetric Group

description:
**Conjecture.** Fix a window `[1, N]` and a budget of `r` sweep points.  The sweep set
minimising the worst-case *additive* overstatement `max_k (read k − k)` is the arithmetic
grid of step `⌈N/r⌉`, while the sweep set minimising the worst-case *multiplicative*
overstatement `max_k (read k)/k` is the geometric grid of ratio `N^{1/r}` (rounded to
integers).  In particular the doubling grid is optimal for the wrong loss function, which
is exactly why it misreports knees by up to a factor `2` while costing only `log₂N`
points.

The key insight is that the two grid families in this round are not "coarse versus fine"
but *optima of two different loss functions*, so the NET-62 discrepancy is a statement
about which error the harness should minimise.  Why now? `card_resolved_arith`,
`card_resolved_dyad_le` and `dyad_overstates` already quantify both grid families; the
optimisation needs only an exchange argument on gap lengths.
title: Budgeted grid optimality: additive versus multiplicative error

description:
The construction `C_k = ∏_{v<k}((v+2)²+1)` provably delivers `k` hits but measurably
delivers far more (`C_3 = 850` carries `14`).  **The key insight is** that the scaled
family only sees one primitive triple per factor, while the true count is multiplicative
in the primes `≡ 1 mod 4` dividing `C_k`, so the gap between the proved and true bound is
itself a clean arithmetic function.  **Why now?** `exists_hypotenuse_multiplicity` gives a
formal skeleton into which a Gaussian-integer factorisation count can be dropped without
redoing the distinctness argument.
title: Sharp multiplicity growth for the scaling construction

description:
**C3: closed.** Union dilution is sharp — every dilution factor `c ∈ (0,1)` is
  attained exactly by an honest two-class binary channel with a class-blind
  admixture, so the achievable factor set is precisely `(0,1]`: the inequality
  "CM shadow ≤ inert-class channel" is universal, and no constant `< 1` improves
  it.
title: C3: closed.

description:
Model scores in `ℕ → Fin 2` (Cantor space)
   and study shift maps, iterated-function systems, and invariant compact sets. A Cantor
   attractor must be assumed or generated by explicit contracting branches; it does not
   follow from continuity and total order alone.
title: Cantor dynamics with honest hypotheses

description: Construct a Tarskian hierarchy with a truth predicate at each level for lower-level sentences. Prove the consistency of the acyclic stratification relative to the base semantics, then identify the exact diagonal obstruction introduced when a reference edge closes a cycle.
title: Stratified truth

description:
We proved that mixing *curves* traps the knee between the constituent knees.
Concatenating *corpora* is a different operation: the demand multisets add.
**Conjecture:** for the union of two workloads with window counts `n₁, n₂`,
`knee(union, g) ≤ max(knee(D₁, g₁), knee(D₂, g₂))` whenever
`g ≤ (n₁g₁ + n₂g₂)/(n₁+n₂)`, with equality iff one demand multiset dominates the
other in the tail region.
*The key insight is* that the union's agreement curve is the `n`-weighted
average of the constituents', so the quantile of the union is squeezed by the
constituents' quantiles at *shifted* gates.
*Why now?* Barrier (c) of NET-70 lists "one corpus mix" as the main external
limit; a proved concatenation law removes the mixing ratio from the deployment
argument entirely.
title: D1 — Sub-additivity of the knee under corpus concatenation

description:
**The key insight is** that a knee read on a coarse grid is the least grid point
above the true knee, so a sweep with spacing `d` over-reads by at most `d - 1`
(`kneeMul_bounds`), which is exactly the NET-66 read of 20 against the NET-67
read of 18 (`coarse_grid_reads_twenty`).
**Why now?** Every cell in the campaign is measured on a grid; the conjecture is
that the *entire* discrepancy history between rounds is explained by spacing,
i.e. all previous readings are consistent with a single underlying curve once
each is replaced by the interval `[read - d + 1, read]`. This is testable
retroactively, without new experiments.
title: Grid-Resolution Correction for Knee Measurements

description:
**The key insight is** that "additive keys per context doubling" is not a
property of a distribution but a differential relation between the tail exponent
and log-context: for exponential tails the equivalence is exact
(`exp_tail_le_iff`, `kneeCts_lamAt`, `rate_of_increment`).
**Why now?** The natural conjecture is that the equivalence extends to any tail
family `T(k) = φ(λ k)` with `φ` strictly decreasing: the knee is affine in `j`
with slope `s` iff `λ_j = φ⁻¹(δ)/(s(j+1))`. Proving this would make the law
independent of the exponential ansatz, which is currently the weakest modelling
assumption in the chain.
title: Rate–Increment Duality for General Tail Families

description: After defining lifting and substitution for de Bruijn variables, prove that substituting a closed well-scoped code into a code scoped under one binder produces a closed well-scoped code. A single well-scoped input pair yielding an ill-scoped result refutes the conjecture.
title: Scoping is preserved by capture-avoiding substitution

description:
Because entropy alone cannot certify
   a budget, a deployable pipeline must fit `(C, r)` in `1 - M(k) ≤ C rᵏ` and
   report the two-sided sandwich `g²/E ≤ k* ≤ N`. Quantifying the fit's
   uncertainty and propagating it to the budget is the natural next step.
title: A tail-exponent measurement protocol

description:
**The key insight is** that the additive law and the decay-rescaling law are *not*
alternative fits of the same curve — they are the linear and the ceiling-of-a-quotient
branches of one two-parameter family, and the branches are numerically indistinguishable
exactly while the admissible exponent window
$\bigcap_d \big((P_d-1)/C_d,\; P_d/(C_d-1)\big)$ stays non-empty; that window is empty
from $d = 3$ on.

**Why now?** The impossibility of any rescaling model fitting both the context-512 cell
and a 24-reading at context 4096 is already proved, so the experiment is fully
pre-registered: a 4096 code reading of $24$ kills the multiplicative mechanism, and any
reading $\le 23$ kills the additive law. No further theory is required to run it.
title: D1. Additive base, multiplicative decay: the 4096 decision

description: Specify a reproducible encoding of MIDI onset grids, tolerance rules, symmetry detection, and a statistical null model before testing distributional claims. The claim about 1000 patterns cannot be verified without a supplied corpus and classification protocol.
title: Corpus methodology

description:
Formalize counting functions for admissible and
   represented integers in symmetric intervals. The established `7/9` local
   proportion is a natural baseline, but any assertion that all admissible
   integers are globally represented must remain explicitly conjectural.
title: Density conjectures

description:
`stability` gives a Lipschitz bound on
   the history as a function of the loop. Upgrade to differentiability of the
   solution map `p ↦ history(p)` (implicit-function theorem for fixed points) and
   study bifurcations as the contraction rate approaches `1`.
title: Parametrised families and bifurcation

description:
Both regimes are proved unconditionally here
(`sum_card_V4_of_isSquare_three`, `sum_card_V4_of_not_isSquare_three`), together with the
reciprocity input for the classes `1, 5, 7 mod 12`; the general statement needs only the
factorisation of `ψ_n` over `ℚ(N)` plus the same fibre-counting bijection factor by factor.
title: Both regimes are proved unconditionally here

description:
For the PTX-augmented optimum `q*_{β,γ}` with `γ > 0`,
`‖q*_{β,γ} − p‖₁ = Θ(γ·‖d − p‖₁) + Θ(σ_p(r)/β)` as `β → ∞`: the pretraining mix-in
contributes a `β`-independent drift toward `d`, so `lim_{β→∞} q*_{β,γ} ≠ p` unless
`d = p`, while the *reward-induced* part of the drift still obeys the `σ/β` law proved
in cycle 2.
title: For the PTX-augmented optimum `q*_{β,γ}` with `γ > 0`,

description:
* **Chebotarev's theorem on the minors of the prime-order Fourier matrix**: *every* minor of the
  prime-order DFT matrix is nonsingular. Established from scratch by an order-of-vanishing
  argument: the integer polynomial `F(X) = det(X^{a_i b_j})`, shifted to `G(X) = F(X+1)`, has all
  coefficients below `N = k(k-1)/2` equal to zero, and `(∏_{j<k} j!) · G_N = V(a)·V(b)` is a
  product of two Vandermonde determinants. If `F(ζ) = 0` then `Φ_p(X+1) ∣ G`, and `Φ_p(1) = p`
  forces `p ∣ G_N`, contradicting `p ∤ V(a)V(b)`.
* **The additive uncertainty principle** itself.
* **The exact converse**: *every* splitting `|A| + |B| = p + 1` is realised by some `f` with
  `supp f = A` and `supp f̂ = B`.
* **Sparse recovery and threshold sharpness**: `k`-sparse signals are determined by any `2k`
  frequencies, and `2k` is optimal for every sampling pattern.
* **Failure at modulus four**: primality is not decorative.
title: Cycle 1 — the bound and its arithmetic input

description: Define finite-orbit and asymptotic Lyapunov exponents using extended real values, then derive exponent `-∞` for a superattracting cycle from `criticalOrbit_multiplier_zero`. This gives a precise replacement for the proposed finite cosine formula at centers.
title: Lyapunov conventions

description: For the seven canonical interval representatives formalized in `SonicCounterpointCategory.lean`, the reflexive-transitive closure of `CanonicalMotion` is total: every interval reaches every other interval. A single unreachable ordered pair refutes this claim.
title: Seven-state strong-connectivity conjecture

description:
In every elementary topos formalized
   with exponentials and a classifier `Ω`, prove that the Heyting implication on `Subobject X`
   agrees, under characteristic maps `X ⟶ Ω`, with the implication morphism
   `Ω × Ω ⟶ Ω` induced by the exponential universal property.
title: Internal implication versus classifier exponentials

description:
Replace "avoid pairwise sums" with "avoid
   sums of `r` earlier terms". Conjecture: the greedy trajectory becomes an
   arithmetic-like progression whose partial sums are polynomial in `n`;
   identify the polynomial and its connection to figurate numbers.
title: Generalised avoidance moduli

description:
Attach to each node a weight reflecting its word, e.g. $q^{|w|}c(w)^{-s}$, producing a two-variable
zeta function $Z(q,s)$. Its analytic structure interpolates between the pure counting problem
($q=1$) and the pure branching problem ($s=0$, where $Z(q,0) = \sum_k(3q)^k$), and its singular
locus should contain both the line $s=1$ and the silver curve $3q\lambda^{-s}=1$ — reconciling the
two answers as different features of a single object.
title: Direction 6 (weighted, two-variable zeta functions)

description:
Construct a finite list of all fundamental
   discriminants satisfying `|D| ≤ 1000`, prove soundness and completeness of that list,
   and derive the exact count in Lean. This is the missing part of the proposed bounded test;
   no unchecked count is asserted here.
title: Certified bounded enumeration

description:
The block argument turns counting bounds into divergence rates. Refining the block ratio and the
counting constants would yield explicit two-sided bounds on $\liminf$ and $\limsup$ of $N(H)/H$,
narrowing the interval $[1/50, 2]$ towards $1/(2\pi)$ by purely elementary means.

title: Direction 5 (effective residues from the block method)

A uniqueness theorem for reachable minimal models would precisely identify the substrate-independent information retained by the Lifebox semantics.
title: Minimize finite person models

Identify $Z(s)$ explicitly as a sieved Epstein zeta function of the quadratic form $m^2+n^2$ and
continue it to the whole plane, locating trivial zeros and a functional equation if one exists. The
unsieved form $4\zeta(s)L(s,\chi_4)$ has a functional equation; the sieve is a finite Euler-factor
modification at $2$ together with a $1/\zeta(2s)$-type factor, and both should transport.

Investigate which results require

title: Separate finite and infinite notions

title: The syntax equivalence restricts to guarded closed formulas

Model local physical laws as relations on assignments
   around a finite directed cycle. Existence of a globally consistent assignment then becomes a
   finite constraint-satisfaction theorem. Compactness could extend this to infinite causal
   networks.
title: Constraint-based self-consistency

description:
*A group with `D_k = 0` and `|G| < 2·|X|^{\underline k}` is sharply `k`-transitive, hence for
`k ≥ 4` belongs to the classical list (symmetric, alternating, Mathieu).  Consequently, for
`k ≥ 6` the equation `D_k = 0` has no solutions with `|X| > k + 2`.*

The key insight is that `descFactorial_dvd_card_of_kTransitive` turns defect zero into a
divisibility statement, and an order bound below twice the falling factorial forces the quotient
to be `1`, which is sharp transitivity — a purely arithmetic route into the classification.

Why now? Both ingredients (`bellDefect_eq_zero_iff` and the divisibility bound, the latter
repaired in this cycle) are now theorems in this thread.
title: Conjecture N (spectral rigidity and the classification)

description:
*With `M_{k,j} = S(k,j)·t_j·|G|` the graded moments, the exponential generating function
`Σ_k M_{k,j} x^k/k!` equals `t_j·|G|·(e^x − 1)^j / j!`, so the whole moment family of a `G`-set is
determined by the `|X| + 1` numbers `t_j` through the classical Stirling generating function.*

The key insight is that the rank collapse `m_P = t_{rank P}` factors the doubly indexed family
into a purely combinatorial factor and a purely group-theoretic one, so the analytic structure is
inherited verbatim from the Stirling numbers of the second kind.

Why now? Both factors are theorems (`patternMultiplicity_eq_injOrbits_rank`,
`card_orbits_eq_sum_stirling`), and the moment–spectrum equivalence proved in this cycle says the
generating function loses no information — it would connect this thread back to the analytic
(moonshine) side that motivated it.
title: Conjecture O (a graded moment generating function)

description:
Conjecture: for `q ≥ 2` the sequence `k ↦ binom(n,k)_q` is strictly increasing for `k ≤ n/2` and
log-concave, and consequently `G_q(n) ≤ (n+1) binom(n,⌊n/2⌋)_q`.  Falsifiable at `q = 2, n = 4`
(`1, 15, 35, 15, 1`).
*The key insight is* that the two Pascal recursions proved here (`gaussBinom_pascal` and
`gaussBinom_pascal'`) give an induction on `n` in which the ratio of consecutive entries is
controlled by `(q^{n-k} - 1)/(q^{k+1} - 1)`, an explicit monotone quantity.
*Why now?*  Both recursions are available in `ℕ` without any field-theoretic detour, so the

description:
**Conjecture.**  Let `A ⊆ ℕ` with `#A = m + 1` and let `f, g` be functions with values in `A`
whose power sums agree for all `k < m`.  If their value distributions differ then

`|p_m(f) - p_m(g)| ≥ ∏_{a ∈ A} ∏_{b ∈ A, b > a} (b - a) / D_A`

for an explicit `D_A` depending only on the nodal weights — i.e. the top-index gap is
quantised, with the interval case `A = {0,…,N}` giving the known bound `N!`.

*The key insight is* that the count difference is an integer multiple of the nodal weight
vector `w_a = ∏_{b≠a}(a-b)⁻¹` (proved for `w` up to the kernel classification in
`NearMissGeneralNodes` and constructed explicitly here as `intWeight`), so the top moment
lives in the lattice generated by `1/w`.

*Why now?*  `powerSums_below_card_insufficient` produces the extremal witness for every `A`;
the matching lower bound would show that the witness is not merely an example but the
minimiser, generalising the catalog's `factorial_le_powerSum_gap` beyond intervals.

The key insight is that the map `β ↦ q*_{β,γ}` is a smooth curve in the exponential family

in disguise.

number) into a lattice invariant (the subgroup lattice), and the lattice remembers strictly more.
*Why now?*  All three counts (cyclic, elementary abelian, coprime products) are available, so the
degree multiset can be computed for every abelian group of order `< p^3`.

description:
Every index-two subgroup of any group is the kernel of a surjection
   onto `C₂` (`charOfIndexTwo`, `ker_charOfIndexTwo`), and its odd-prime successor is now
   settled too: a *normal* subgroup of prime index `p` is the kernel of a surjection onto
   `C_p` (`exists_surjective_char_of_prime_index`) and exactly `p − 1` surjective characters
   share that kernel (`card_surjective_chars_with_ker`). **New successor (C1b):** drop
   normality — for `p` the smallest prime dividing `|G|`, every index-`p` subgroup of a
   finite group is normal, hence *every* connected degree-`p` covering of a `K(G,1)` with
   `p = min(primes dividing |G|)` is regular and character-theoretic; the falsifiable form
   is that a non-regular connected degree-`p` covering forces a prime divisor of `|G|`
   smaller than `p`, tested by `G = S₃`, `p = 3` (one non-regular triple covering, and
   `2 < 3`).  **C1b is now settled in both directions**
   (`normal_and_exists_char_of_index_eq_minFac`, and
   `minFac_lt_index_of_not_normal` together with the `S₃` witness
   `nonRegular_prime_degree_forces_smaller_prime`).  **New successor (C1c):** for a finite
   group `G` and a prime `p ∣ |G|` that is *not* minimal, the number of conjugacy classes
   of non-normal index-`p` subgroups is `(n_p(G) − 1)/p`-controlled by Sylow counting —
   concretely, the conjecture is that this number is `0` exactly when every index-`p`
   subgroup contains a normal subgroup of index `p`, and the falsifiable form is to exhibit
   a group where the non-normal classes outnumber the character-theoretic ones.
2. **(C2a — settled)** `ℤ²` has exactly three subgroups of index two and exactly four of
   index three, so the torus has `σ(2) = 3` double and `σ(3) = 4` triple coverings
   (`torus_three_double_coverings`, `torus_four_triple_coverings`), all of whose total
   spaces are tori. **New successor (C2b):** every connected finite covering of the torus
   has total space a torus, i.e. every finite-index subgroup of `ℤ²` is isomorphic to `ℤ²`
   — provable from the fact that a finite-index subgroup of `ℤ^k` is free abelian of the
   same rank — and the degree-`n` count is `σ(n)`, with `n = 4` (`σ(4) = 7`) the next
   checkpoint.  **C2b is now settled**: `torus_finite_index_subgroup_mulEquiv` (every
   finite-index subgroup of `ℤ²` is a copy of `ℤ²`),
   `card_index_n_subgroups_torus_sigma` (the count is `σ(n)` for every `n`) and
   `card_index_four_subgroups_torus` (`σ(4) = 7`).  **New successor (C2c):** for `K(ℤ^k,1)`
   with `k ≥ 3` the number of connected `n`-sheeted coverings is the coefficient
   `∑_{d₁ d₂ ⋯ = n}` of the lattice zeta function `ζ(s)ζ(s−1)⋯ζ(s−k+1)`, i.e. the number of
   finite-index sublattices of `ℤ^k` of index `n`; the falsifiable form is the first case
   `k = 3`, `n = 2`, where the prediction is `7` sublattices of index two — testable by the
   same character argument that gives `p + 1` for `k = 2`, since index-two sublattices of
   `ℤ^k` are the nonzero mod-two characters, `2^k − 1`.

description:
**Conjecture E (the key-length hierarchy) — PROVED, and by a different
  mechanism than conjectured.**  The coding-theoretic route suggested in cycle 2
  is *vacuous*: at relative distance exactly `1 − 1/M` the Plotkin double count
  degenerates to `N(N−1) ≤ N²`, and the Cauchy–Schwarz second-moment count
  degenerates to `n/M ≤ n`, so neither yields any bound.  What works is
  **integrality**: the number of keys on which two symbols collide is a natural
  number `≤ K/M`, so `K < M` forces every hash function to be injective.
  `AlmostLosslessKeySharp.lean` proves `universal2_key_ge_codes`: a nonempty
  2-universal family that compresses at all (`M < n`) has `K ≥ M` keys — the
  advice is at least as long as the codeword.  Consequences:
  `universal2_key_ge_max : K ≥ max(M, log_M n)`,
  `universal2_key_pow_bound : n ≤ M^c → n ≤ K^c` (so at constant rate the key
  space is polynomially large and `poly(log n)` keys are impossible, refuting
  cycle-1 Conjecture 5 as predicted), and `universal2_key_length_ge` in bits.
  The bound is attained: `linHash_key_count_optimal` shows *every* 2-universal
  family compressing `(ZMod p)²` into `p` codewords needs `≥ p` keys, which the

  cancellation is no longer a constant exponent map, but a *pigeonhole involution*
  (`ParityGap.permCoeff_eq_zero_of_pigeonhole`): the `S`-values that are multiples of `a`
  outnumber the classes of `T`-values modulo the subgroup generated by `b`, so every permutation

description:
Conjecture: for `q ≥ 2` and a prime `ℓ ∤ q`, the `ℓ`-adic valuation of `binom(n,k)_q` equals the
number of carries when adding `k` and `n-k` in base `d`, where `d` is the multiplicative order of
`q` modulo `ℓ`, plus a correction term counted by `v_ℓ(q^{d}-1)`.  Falsifiable at
`q = 2, ℓ = 5, n = 6, k = 3`, where `binom(6,3)_2 = 1395 = 3² · 5 · 31` and the order of `2`
modulo `5` is `4`.
*The key insight is* that `qFactZ_mul_qBinom` expresses `binom(n,k)_q` as an exact quotient of
`q`-factorials, so the valuation question becomes a counting question about the multiples of `d`
in an interval — the same combinatorics that proves Kummer's theorem.
*Why now?*  The exactness of the division (`gaussBinom_eq_qBinom`) is the hypothesis every
valuation argument needs and was the missing ingredient before this cycle.

description:
**Conjecture.**  For the nodes `0, …, N`, the `ℓ¹`-norm of the inverse row at the node `0`
is `lebesgueConst N 0 = N + 1`, and more generally
`lebesgueConst N v = C(N, v) · ∑_{k} …` is bounded by `2^N`, with the maximum attained at
the middle node.

*The key insight is* that `L_0 = ∏_{j=1}^{N} (1 - X/j)` has coefficients of alternating sign,
so the `ℓ¹`-norm of its coefficient vector is `|L_0(-1)| = ∏_{j=1}^{N}(1 + 1/j) = N + 1`;
sign alternation is exactly the statement that the elementary symmetric functions of the
positive nodes are positive.

*Why now?*  `count_eq_of_powerSums_close` already converts any bound on `Λ_N(v)` into an
*exact* recovery threshold `ε < 1/Λ_N(v)` for noisy power sums; a closed form for `Λ_N`
turns that qualitative robustness statement into a usable error budget.
title: C1. The Lebesgue constant of the interval nodes is exactly `2^N`-free: `Λ_N(0) = N + 1`

description:
**Conjecture.**  For every `N` and every `v ≤ N` there are bounded functions `f, g` and an
`ε > 0` with `|p_k(f) - p_k(g)| ≤ ε` for all `k ≤ N` and
`|count_f(v) - count_g(v)| ≥ c · Λ_N(v) · ε` for an absolute constant `c > 0`.

*The key insight is* that the extremal input for the `ℓ¹`-`ℓ^∞` duality bound used in
`count_sub_le_of_powerSums_close` is the sign pattern of the inverse row, which is realised
by the positive/negative split of the nodal weight vector — exactly the construction already
formalised as `posPart` / `negPart`.

*Why now?*  Together with C1 this would pin the conditioning of power-sum inversion
completely, turning `count_eq_of_powerSums_close` from a sufficient criterion into a sharp
threshold.
title: C3. Noisy inversion is optimal: a matching lower bound for the stability estimate

description:
**Conjecture.**  Two diagonalisable rational matrices `A, B` (not assumed diagonal) whose
eigenvalues are natural numbers `≤ N` and which satisfy `tr(A^k) = tr(B^k)` for all `k ≤ N`
are conjugate over `ℚ̄`, and in fact have equal characteristic polynomials.

*The key insight is* that `count_eq_of_traces` already gives equality of eigenvalue
multiplicities for the diagonal representatives, and the missing step is only the transfer
from a diagonalisable matrix to its diagonalisation — a statement about `Matrix.IsDiag`
conjugacy rather than about power sums.

*Why now?*  `exists_equiv_of_powerSums` supplies precisely the index-set bijection needed to
build the conjugating matrix, so the remaining work is packaging rather than new
mathematics; it would upgrade the spectral corollary from diagonal matrices to the class
that actually occurs in applications.
title: C5. Trace rigidity for non-diagonal matrices with spectrum in `{0,…,N}`

description:
The same analysis applies to any Möbius-type tree of arithmetic objects: the Stern–Brocot tree of
rationals, the Markov triple tree, and trees of solutions to other Pell-like and Vieta-jumping
equations. In each case one may ask whether the branching/growth heuristic gives the right abscissa.
The prediction implied by the present work is that it never does when the tree bijects onto a
lattice of full dimension.

description:
**Conjecture.** For two scores drawn from any absolutely continuous distribution over rankings
of `n` keys, the probability that their retained-mass ordering is constant across all budgets
`1 ≤ B ≤ n` tends to `0` as `n → ∞`; the expected number of crossings grows like `Θ(log n)`.

**The key insight is** that retained mass differences are partial sums of a mean-zero exchange
sequence, so sign changes are recurrences of a random walk, and recurrence counts are
logarithmic.

**Why now?** `net58_no_uniform_budget_ordering` shows one crossing exists; upgrading existence
to genericity is the natural next step, and it directly governs how many budgets a benchmark
must report before a policy comparison can be trusted.

**If true:** single-budget policy comparisons in the KV-eviction literature are statistically
meaningless.  **If false:** a single well-chosen budget suffices and benchmarks can be cheaper.
